0 Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable amid excess liquidity on Thursday."It's very busy today but people are holding onto their paper because they are anticipating a fall in the treasury bill rate today because the market is in surplus," one dealer said.He said discount houses
0 were buying the central bank paper at 22.49 percent, the same as overnight, and selling at 22 percent from 22.25 percent.NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at Wednesday's 23.5 percent level and sold at an unchanged 22.75 percent, while call money was quoted at
0 its previous 22 percent rate.Bankers' acceptance bills were being bought at 22.75 percent, also unchanged from overnight and were selling at 22 percent compared to 22.50. The market opened in surplus of Z$600 million versus Z$223 million previously.-- Emelia Sithole, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 27/8/9</
1 Zimbabwean police said on Thursday they were investigating an unregistered Harare-based get-rich-quick savings club promising members huge returns on deposits into its and a chain of other bank accounts."We have no comment, except to say we are investigating," a police official said in answer to queries about the club which
1 has drawn the attention of Zimbabwe's financial markets.Zimbabwe's Central African Building Society (CABS) has closed the club's account where thousands of people had deposited their subscriptions.Organisers of the Richer 2000 Club were unavailable for comment on local press allegations that the club was dubious.To register, reports say, a person must
1 deposit a total of Z$300 into six accounts of Z$50 each, including the Richer 2000 Club, before being given five certificates to sell to new members who must continue the chain.A member could reap Z$68,000 in two months in return, the report said.-- Cris Chinaka, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52
2 Analysts raised a toast on Thursday to South African Breweries Ltd's plan to tap the market for up to some two billion rand to finance the drinks giant's burgeoning overses expansion.In a brief statement the group said it would explore the possibility of issuing for cash ordinary shares worth up
2 to five percent of the existing issued ordinary and automatically convertible preference shares."The issue will be received very positively. SAB is a highly rated company," said one analyst.Another commented: "I don't think they will have problems getting the shares away. SAB has been one of the most internationally traded (South
2 African) shares."They speculated that it would be pitched at or slightly below its current share price of 131.75 rand, unmoved at 0900 GMT. The market expects SAB to raise at least 1.5 billion rand and possibly the full two billion.Analysts said the cash would likely be used to fund the
2 expansion of the group's beer arm, not its smaller hotels or retail divisions.SAB, with brand names like Castle and Lion, dominates its home beer market with a 97 percent market share. In order to grow, it has expanded rapidly into other African states and further afield into Europe and China."There
2 is no way that, in the medium to long-term, South Africa would be able to sustain the type of growth SAB has seen recently. They have to go overseas to get that," said Zelda Zaayman, analyst at Silvis, Barnard, Jacobs, Mellet &amp; Co.SAB has bought controlling stakes in the state
2 breweries of Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique and is negotiating to buy Angola's. It has also established itself Hungary, Romania and, most recently, Poland.Further afield the firm has 55 percent of the Shenyang brewery in north east China.Analysts said SAB would probably use the cash in a mixture of activities, combining
2 new ventures with reinforcing existing plants. "It most likely will be a combination of acquisition and investment in existing opportunities," said Tom de Trafford, analyst at Simpson McKie.Analysts said it was unlikely SAB would seek to enter new markets, such as Latin America, and would instead build on extending its
2 already existing base in central and eastern Europe and China."I think we will probably see more of the same in places where they they have already built up a presence," de Trafford said.Analysts were split as to exactly where the emphasis of the new investment would be. Zaayman said the
2 firm would seek to expand in Europe and, for the moment at least, keep a watching brief on investment in its Chinese operations."I expect they will look at more breweries in Hungary, Romania and Poland...I don't think that in China they will be that aggressive in the short-term," she said.In
2 May, when SAB bought a 27.5 percent chunk of Polish brewer Lech Browary Wielkopolski, the firm said that it would see further investment opportunities in that country.But another analyst said the firm may seek to plough a sizeable chunk of the cash into China, hoping to capitalise early on its
2 massive market potential, despite the difficulties of a market where consumers have not traditionally drunk beer."It's got fantastic growth," the analyst said.Company officials were not immediately available for comment.-- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003</

9 Slovak steel maker Zeleziarne Podbrezova a.s. will launch a five-year, 800 million crown bond issue on Thursday, lead manager Slovenska Sporitelna a.s. said.A senior Sporitelna official told Reuters the bond will carry an annual fixed coupon rate of 12.1 percent. The issuer has reserved the right to repurchase the issue
9 after three years at the rate of 101 percent, the official said.The bond, the funds of which will be to restructure the companies' debts, will be traded on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE)."This is one of several steps towards our financial restrusturing, perhaps the last one this year, but not
9 the final," Marian Kurcik, Zeleziarne finance director told Reuters.Zeleziarne Podbrezova is Slovakia's major steel pipe producer. It exported two-thirds of its last year's production to western Europe.VUB, Slovakia's largest commercial bank, is the co-lead manager of the issue.Three other Slovak banks - Banka Slovakia, Priemyselna Banka and Istrobanka - co-managed
9 the issue.Sporitelna's treasurer Ivan Benda said Sporitelna had lead managed "five or six" bond issues so far, including one billion crown issue for petrol fules distributor Benzinol a.s. last spring, and 1.5 billion crown issue for energy utility Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. last year.-- Tatiana Vacova, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687</

16 The Budapest office of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday that an IMF report issued in Washington should not be read as an expression of concern about Hungary's yen-based bond issues.The statement from Mark Allen, IMF senior representative in Hungary, said a Reuters report drawing on information from
16 the IMF's International Capital Markets Report "could be read as implying that the IMF was concerned about the yen bonds issued by the National Bank of Hungary (NBH)."This is absolutely not the case," the statement said."The Fund believes that Hungarian government policies are such as should give full confidence to
16 international financial markets," the statement continued.It noted that Hungary has sharply reduced its fiscal and current account deficits and "substantially reduced its gross and net external debt and prepaid a number of borrowings".The IMF's Washington report, cited by Reuters, questioned whether investors adequately understood the risks entailed in some bond

32 to be waged on three fronts - wages, fiscal policy and supply side policy - in order to stimulate exports and retain the crown's strength."Exports need to be stimulated if the foundations for stable and sustained growth are to be established, and if the currency is to be preserved at
32 current levels over the longer term."The Czech Republic is running a large trade deficit and its current account deficit could reach 5.7 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.On Thursday, Czech business daily Hospodarske Noviny quoted Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy as saying the current account deficit could reach crisis proportions
32 sometime next year if current trends continue.But the report said the central bank's foreign currency reserves -- nearly $13 billion in July -- should be sufficient to steady the market in the event of a run on the crown."Even if the currently bullish support for the Koruna (crown) evaporates, the
32 Czech Republic should still have sufficient foreign exchange reserves to steady the market."However, the investment bank said the government needed to take firm action to improve economic fundamentals, which would in turn help exports, if a devaluation is to be avoided in the longer term.While praiseworthy of the crown, the

45 The British government on Thursday decided to put its full-scale beef cattle cull on hold in a move certain to spark a clash with the European Union over the mad cow crisis."The new scientific evidence available means that further work is needed on appropriate culling strategies," a spokesman for Prime
45 Minister John Major said after a two-hour meeting of ministers at his Downing Street residence.Major acted after reviewing the latest evidence from a group of Oxford University scientists who argued that the disease would die out naturally within five years and that mass culling was unnecessary."For the present, the governmment
45 is not proceeding with the selective cull but will return to cull options in the light of the developing science and of discussions on the certified herd scheme," Major's spokesman added.But the European Union has refused to budge on the issue.It says Britain should carry out an agreed plan to
45 slaughter up to 147,000 cattle most at risk from the debilitating disease.At a European Union summit in Florence in June, Major agreed with other European leaders that Britain would impose a cull and other measures in return for a gradual lifting of the worldwide ban on British beef exports.After Major
45 met with Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg, Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke and other ministers, the premier's spokesman was at pains to stress that the Florence agreement had not been broken."This is not a departure from the Florence framework which states that the UK eradication plan "shall be adapted if necessary in
45 the light of scientific and epidemiological developments'."The export ban was imposed in March after Britain admitted a possible link between Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) and Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, a deadly human equivalent.After the Florence deal, Major had said he expected the EU to start lifting the ban within five months but
45 this confident prediction found little backing from other EU countries.Officials said Hogg returned from talks with EU farm ministers in Brussels this week once again convinced they would not lift the ban any time soon.The pressure Major is under was illustrated earlier on Thursday when he met a delegation of

51 The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) on Thursday unveiled an alliance with Japanese-controlled information technology company ICL to develop a commercial online Internet service.The venture, which has the working title BBC Online, will provide a BBC-branded web service and is targeted for launch on the global computer network in early 1997.It
51 will be built around popular BBC radio and television programmes and magazines and will cover news, sport, information and entertainment."This will play an absolutely vital role in stimulating consumer acceptance (of the Internet) and moving forward to greater interactivity," BBC Worldwide chief executive Bob Phillis told a news conference.The project
51 between BBC Worldwide, the corporation's commercial arm, and ICL, controlled by Japan's giant Fujitsu Ltd, will initially run until the end of 1999.ICL chief executive Keith Todd said his company was investing "many millions of pounds" in the venture.ICL is funding the venture as BBC Online is subject to regulations
51 that ensure no public money is used to finance any of BBC Worldwide's commercial ventures.The BBC will supply the creative content while ICL will be responsible for providing the systems integration services, as well as technical expertise.The project aims to provide fast and simple Internet access through a BBC-branded software
51 package and access service. Access will also be available through managed services such as CompuServe and America Online AMER.O.Todd said the content would initIally be heavily based on text and graphics, but Phillis said the aim was to add audio and visual services as technology advanced.Phillis said the service would
51 at first be tailored for a British audience but he expected it eventually to be marketed internationally. There are plans to carry advertising and charge a subscription for premium services.The deal is part of the BBC's efforts to expand its commercial activities and lessen its dependence on the licence fee,
51 a tax which must be paid by anyone with a television set.Net benefit from commercial ventures was 77 million pounds in 1995/96, a sum dwarfed by the 1.8 billion pounds raised by the licence fee charged to all Britons with a television.BBC director-general John Birt last month called for an
51 above inflation hike in the annual licence fee, which currently stands at 89.50 pounds ($140) for a colour service. 52 were expected to cut back on the slaughter programme or introduce measures to protect the domestic beef market.Major's London office expected to be able to give some details of the ministers' discussion later on Thursday.If they decide to cut back on the cull, Britain could once again come into conflict

52 scientific veterinary committee 10 days ago and should not serve as an excuse to delay the cull.Roger Freeman, the minister in charge of seeing measures to eradicate the disease are implemented, welcomed the commission's decision to review the new study.But he said Britain was still looking for a fast easing

52 to a rapid lifting of a ban on British beef exports.After the Florence deal, Major said he expected the EU to start lifting the ban within five months but this confident prediction found little backing from other countries in the bloc.Officials said Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg returned from talks with

57 Kevin Maxwell, youngest son of media tycoon Robert Maxwell, whose death in 1991 led to the collapse of his business empire, will not face a second trial on fraud charges, a judge ruled on Thursday.Judge John Buckley said a further trial "would be unfair, so unfair as to amount to
57 an abuse of power of the court", adding that he had come to the clear view that the proceedings served no further public interest.The judge later agreed verdicts of "not guilty" should be recorded on all outstanding charges against Kevin and his three fellow defendants.He ordered their costs -- around
57 30 million pounds ($46 million) in Britain's most expensive criminal case this century -- paid from state funds.The judge's ruling ended five years of controversy over hundreds of millions of pounds which were found missing from Maxwell company pension funds after Robert Maxwell disappeared from his yacht in the Atlantic
57 Ocean."It is an enormous victory for commonsense and humanity. I'm enormously relieved, immensely relieved and delighted," an ecstatic and clearly stunned Kevin told a pack of reporters outside the court."It's a hell of a moment. Quite clearly this was a very powerful and uncompromising judgement. Thank God he stopped it."In
57 January, Kevin, his brother Ian Maxwell, and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of conspiring to defraud pension funds after an eight-month trial."My immediate reaction is not one of anger or bitterness and I don't want to use words like vindictive or vendetta -- let other people do that,"
57 said Kevin.Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) sought to bring charges in a second trial against Kevin Maxwell, Trachtenberg, and two former Maxwell executives, Albert Fuller and Michael Stoney.All had proceedings stopped against them under the ruling.The judgement brings into question how the SFO, set up to deal with major financial
57 fraud, will act in the future."We have reached the end of the legal process," said SFO director George Staple in a statement. "The law does not provide any avenue of appeal. There are serious implications for the prosecution of the largest and most complex criminal cases."Sources close to the SFO
57 said the judge's decision would put it in an impossible position when it came to tackling the largest and most important frauds and reopen the debate over whether juries are qualified to hear complex fraud cases.The judge said that the factor that had influenced him most was, "(that) the essential
57 criminality of the prosecution's case was before the jury in the first trial.""Broadly speaking, if any jury was going to convict in this case, surely it would have been on the pension counts (at the first trial)," he told the court.Kevin Maxwell, 37, had taken his case before the judge
57 to argue that the impending second trial was "oppressive".At a news conference, Kevin thanked the judge and said he would not consider a lawsuit against the prosecutors. "I have an absolute horror of litigation," he said. "I have no intention of going into a court of law."Lawyers expressed surprise when
57 the SFO said it wanted a second trial and many said the organisation was trying to salvage its own reputation but, on Thursday, the judge said the verdict in the first trial must now be accepted."In a notorious case, people looking on will have their own theories, some better informed
57 than others. But, since we have a jury system we should all accept their verdicts," Buckley said. "In the Maxwell case that is overdue. I accept the jury's verdict. These proceedings are stayed."Kevin became Britain's biggest bankrupt in 1992 with debts of over 400 million pounds ($630 million at current
57 rates). He was released from bankruptcy in 1995.Kevin -- whose ambition in life had been to follow his father -- always denied conspiring to defraud by misusing pension fund money to prop up the indebted companies.He said his father, whom he has described as as bully, used pension funds just
57 like any other assets in his corporate empire -- as a source of cash to be moved from one company to another.Kevin told the first trial that he and his brother had merely obeyed their father's orders.</

61 monthly industrial trends survey found only 17 percent of the 1,217 UK companies surveyed said total orders were above normal while 26 percent said they were below -- a negative balance of nine percent. This is a slight improvement on August when the balance of firms was minus 10 percent
61 which in turn was distinctly less gloomy than the minus 22 percent reading in the July survey."The improvement in demand seen over the past few months is encouraging, although manufacturers continue to be hampered by weak exports," said Sudhir Junankar, CBI associate director of economics.A negative balance of 11 percent
61 of firms said export demand was worse than normal. But that represents an improvement on August, when the balance was minus 14 percent. Manufacturers' expectations were more encouraging. A positive balance of 20 percent of firms expected output to increase markedly over the next four months -- a small deterioration
61 in sentiment from August when the balance was 22 percent.The outlook means few firms expect to be able to pass on higher prices. As many firms expect the trend in prices to be down as up. "The news on prices is much better as companies expect the unchanged trend in
61 domestic prices to continue in the coming months," Junankar said. "This is promising, as it is likely to exert downward pressure on overall inflation over the short-term."The overhang in manufacturers' stocks continues to be a problem but is slowly being unwound, the CBI said. A positive balance of 14 percent
61 of firms said stocks were more than adequate, but that reading is the lowest since August 1995."With companies starting to make inroads in their stocks of unsold finished goods, the output increases predicted in this survey suggest that manufacturing industry in the UK is poised to recover," Junankar said.The monthly
61 trends survey canvassed 1,217 manufacturing companies, representing 50 industries and accounting for about half of the UK's manufactured exports and output of some two million employees.-- Mike Peacock, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5109</

63 Studies on African villagers have confirmed the value of eating fish -- but it takes a lot of fish to affect health, Italian researchers reported on Friday.The study, by Dr Paolo Pauleto and colleagues at the University of Padua, found that Tanzanian villagers who ate a fish-based diet had lower
63 blood pressure and lower cholesterol than their mostly vegetarian neighbours.They said their findings confirmed controversial research in the 1980s that found "Eskimos" in Greenland had low rates of heart disease despite a diet consisting almost entirely of meat and fish. The Eskimo results gave birth to a Western obsession with
63 fish oil.Pauleto's group compared two groups of about 1,200 Bantu villagers living in Tanzania."One group live on the shores of Lake Nyasa and their diet includes large amounts of freshwater fish; the other group live in the nearby hills and have a vegetarian diet," they wrote in the Lancet medical
63 journal."After adjustment for age, sex and alcohol intake, the fish-consuming group had lower mean blood pressure." Only 2.8 percent of fish-eaters had high blood pressure, compared to 16.4 percent of those who did not eat fish.Cholesterol levels were also lower in the group that ate fish and the fish-eaters had
63 higher levels of omega-three fatty acids, which are linked to lower rates of heart disease.Fish is a rich source of omega-three fatty acids. Other sources are soya oil, linseed oil and nuts -- all rare in the African diet.They said the communities were very similar, so that comparisons would be
63 scientifically accurate. Obesity was unusual in both groups and both ate about 2,100 calories a day.The vegetarians had less fat and protein in their diet and got most of their energy from grains like maize or rice. They also drank more beer.The fish-eaters ate three to four fish a day
63 -- between 300 and 600 grams (10 and 20 ounces) compared to an average of 400 grams a day of meat or fish eaten by Greenland natives. The fish supplied 60 percent of all fat eaten by the Bantus.The researchers said their findings were surprising as other studies have shown
63 that people who take fish oil supplements may actually have higher blood pressure. But they noted that the Bantu villagers were being tested on a lifelong diet, while the supplement studies reflected a short-term change in diet."Our findings confirm that the favourable risk factor profile originally described for Eskimos living
63 on a diet rich in omega-three polyunsaturated fatty acids is real, and not overestimated," they concluded.</
64 Cancer patients want to know as much as possible about their disease and do not appreciate being "spared" the truth, British doctors said on Friday.Dr Paul Symonds and colleagues at the Western Infirmary in Glasgow surveyed 250 patients and found that 79 percent of patients wanted as much information as
64 possible, 96 percent wanted to know they had cancer."Most patients also wanted to know the chance of a cure (91 percent) and about side-effects of treatment (94 percent)," they wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal.They found a trend for patients from more affluent areas to want more
64 information and those from deprived areas to want less. Only 15 percent did not want any information and six percent wanted only good news."Not being told what is wrong with them is the most common complaint that patients make about the medical profession," they said. "There is evidence that many
64 doctors in Britain fail to tell patients if they have cancer."Such good intentions were aimed at not alarming or depressing the patient, they said."Using the word "cancer', with all its implied connotations, is stressful for both doctors and patients and there may be many reasons why doctors avoid communicating bad
64 news," they added.A second study said patients did not appreciate efforts by their families to keep bad news from them, either.John Benson, a general practitioner in Cambridge and Nicky Britten of Guy's Hospital in London interviewed 30 cancer patients about what doctors should tell their families.They found that although sometimes
64 relatives ask the doctor to keep a cancer patient in the dark about his or her illness while keeping the family quietly informed, the patients themselves would not want this."All subjects wished doctors to respect their views rather than those of their family, should they differ," they wrote.</
65 A decline in the proportion of Danish boys being born could be due to chemicals that affect male fertility, a researcher reported on Friday.Henrik Moeller of the Danish National Research Foundation checked Danish birth records as part of an investigation into theories that hazards to male reproduction were increasing.He said
65 in a letter to the Lancet medical journal that fewer boys than girls had been born in recent decades. The proportion of boys to girls peaked at around 1950 and fell precipitously after that.Moeller noted that many pesticides produced chemicals that mimicked the effects of the female hormone oestrogen, while
65 others suppressed the production of male hormones."It is possible that environmental or other agents with toxic properties on the male reproductive system could lead to low male:female ratios," he wrote."One such agent, the nematocide dibromochloropropane, is known to reduce the sperm count and lead to an excess of females in
65 the offspring of exposed men."Researchers have found conflicting evidence of the effects of chemicals on men and their fertility. Studies over the past four years found declining sperm counts in Denmark, Paris and Scotland, but no decreases in Finland, the French city of Toulouse and New York.</
66 Go ahead and have a big piece of chocolate along with that glass of red wine -- they're both good for you, U.S. doctors advised on Thursday.Both treats contain phenols, chemicals believed to help stop arteries from clogging up."The pleasant pairing of red wine and dark chocolate could have synergistic
66 advantages beyond their complementary tastes," Andrew Waterhouse and colleagues at the University of California at Davis wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.Phenols are antioxidants that prevent the "rusting" of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs), which are the so-called bad fat component of cholesterol.When LDLs oxidise they turn into a
66 plaque that can block arteries, causing heart disease.Waterhouse's group, knowing that chocolate has natural preservatives that stop the fat in it from going rancid, tested chocolate to see how it compared to red wine, known to contain high levels of phenols.They found quite a lot. "A cup of hot chocolate
66 containing 7.3 grams (two tablespoons) of cocoa could have 146 mg total phenol, whereas a 41 g (1.5 ounce) piece of chocolate would have 205 mg total phenol," they wrote."For comparison, a standard 140 ml (five ounce) serving of red wine contains about 210 mg total phenol."They said the effects
66 would need to be proven in people, but if they did, chocolate could be a significant source of the healthful chemicals.</

76 Leaders of the Welsh Anglican church on Thursday voted by the narrowest of margins to lift the ban on women becoming priests.The Church in Wales, which was the only Anglican church in Britain still barring women from the priesthood, approved the move by just one vote at a tense meeting
76 of its governing body held in Lampeter, south Wales.A bill to allow women priests just reached its necessary two-thirds majority among lay members and the clergy.The six Welsh bishops were all in favour of the reform following changes made by the Church in England, Scotland and Ireland. 76 England approved the ordination of women in 1992.The vote will allow nearly 80 Welsh women deacons to become priests.Of the Anglican communion's 37 self-governing churches around the world, 17 ordain women priests. 76 Rev Alwyn Rice-Jones, said continued opposition to women priests would leave Welsh Anglicans isolated and split within the Church."We will simply slide backwards and nobody will be prepared to listen to us. 76 another as they celebrated the breakthrough.Many had threatened to leave the Welsh Church and move to England because of their frustration at not being ordained.Many have been deacons since 1980, when the Church in Wales first opened its doors to women clergy.</

91 British fraud trials are set for a radical shake-up after the failure of a second trial against Kevin Maxwell, youngest son of late media baron Robert Maxwell, a source close to the Serious Fraud Office said on Thursday.Judge John Buckley's closed the final chapter in the five-year Maxwell saga by
91 refusing the SFO's attempt to press ahead with a second trial against Kevin Maxwell.George Staple, director of the SFO, said after the ruling that it had "serious implications for the prosecution of the largest and most complex criminal cases".Kevin and his brother Ian were acquitted in January after an eight
91 month trial and Judge Buckley said that to continue with a second trial against Kevin would "serve no further public interest". He later recorded a not guilty verdict."To pursue them (these proceedings) in the face of the jury's unanimous (not guilty) verdict in the first trial would test both the
91 public's confidence and the integrity of the system," he said.Staple said the charges relating to alleged faud against pension funds, banks and other institutions had been split to make them more manageable for a jury but the ruling meant "very serious charges will not now be heard".While the SFO is
91 expected to lobby for a change in the way large fraud trials are conducted, calls for radical changes to the SFO and even its disbanding are likely following the ruling.Britain's opposition Labour party said "serious questions must now be asked about the future operations of the SFO".Among the options under
91 consideration are modifying the jury trial system for complex fraud trials, with either specially selected jury members or a tribunal which could assess a large, complex case in one go, the source close to the SFO said.The practice of severing, or dividing up charges into separate, more manageable, trials, would
91 have to be reviewed in the wake of the Maxwell trial, the source said, adding that in deciding to go ahead with the second trial, Staple had weighed up all the views and had made a "brave decision".But the judge said he could not allow it to proceed because of
91 the cost involved, the strain on the defendants and their families and for fear of suggesting to the public that the authorities did not accept the verdict of a jury.The SFO was set up in 1988 to prosecute serious or complex financial fraud, but has been widely criticised for failing
91 to secure convictions in some notable cases.It has strongly defended its record and says its overall conviction rate is around 63 percent. Of 150 trials to date, involving 338 defendants, 213 have been convicted."We feel that our conviction record speaks for itself, it is a respectable record. We are dealing
91 with some of the most difficult and complex cases in the criminal justice system," an SFO spokeswoman told Reuters.But despite the SFO's record the public perception of the SFO rests with its high-profile failures.These include the acquittal of George Walker in 1994 for an alleged fraud against creditors and shareholders
91 in leisure group Brent Walker and the Blue Arrow trial which lasted a year and ended with acquittals for all the defendants.The SFO maintains it has had some high-profile successes, citing the conviction of Peter Clowes in the Barlow Clowes case and four trials which have led to convictions in
91 the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) fiasco.But concerns over the cost of such cases are likely to rouse most public condemnation when the final bill for the Maxwell trials, including more than 20 million pounds ($31.19 million) in legal aid, is finally known. (Legal aid is taxpayers' money
91 provided to poor citizens to fund a legal defence).The SFO spokeswoman on Thursday confirmed its own investigation and prosecution had cost in the region of 11.3 million pounds, with 300,000 pounds spent since January. ($1=.6412 Pound)</

98 commercial value the demands really amounted to only "one percent of the business issue" and suggested that the demand was being made by Richard Branson's Virgin Atlantic only to prevent a deal being done."I think those who are saying that are saying we don't want a deal at all,'" Greenwald
98 said.Failure to agree an open skies pact would block the proposed alliance between Virgin's arch rival British Airways and American Airlines.Virgin has been a vociferous opponent of the controversial BA-American pact, complaining that it would dominate the British transatlantic market with more than 60 percent of all flights.Under the alliance,
98 BA intends to coordinate its 244 flights a week from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with all of American's 238 flights a week from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.BA and American argue their deal will lead to greater competition because it will only go ahead if Britain and
98 the U.S. agree to establish an "open skies" free market.But talks between government negotiators broke down last month. U.S. airlines want BA to give up some of its 38 percent share of runway slots at London's Heathrow airport to give them room to compete and to be allowed "fifth freedom"
98 rights to fly from Britain to third countries.On the British side, BA says it should not have to give up slots while Virgin wants British government negotiators to press for "cabotage" rights which would allow British airlines to fly domestic routes within the United States and to be allowed to
98 own U.S. airlines.U.S. law bans foreign airlines operating in the U.S. and limits foreign ownership of a U.S. airline to a 25 percent voting stake.Virgin later denied it was simply trying to block an open skies deal to scupper the BA-American alliance."If a deal is done with the American prize
98 being Heathrow and onward rights to Europe and the rest of the world, then the least the UK consumer can expect is to be able to have the opportunity to fly onwards with a British carrier in the U.S., just as U.S. consumers would expect to do the same in
98 Europe," said a company spokesman.If the rules are changed Virgin has vowed to start up services in the U.S.But Greenwald said in reply to questions about Virgin's new plan that if Branson wanted to set up in the U.S. and fly domestic routes he should gain access by taking a
98 25 percent stake in a U.S. carrier which would also spread the risks."I don't see that is an issue," he said. "More power to him if he thinks he can swim with the sharks like Herb Kelleher (founder of pioneer low-cost carrier Southwest Airlines). That's a very tough market."He said
98 outright cabotage rights were unlikely to be granted by the U.S. government because U.S. airline workers were so opposed to seeing foreign airlines come into their home market, unless a pan-European aviation treaty was agreed with the U.S."The U.S. unions are crazed over the cabotage issue. It is a highly
98 political issue. The only way I can see it being resolved is to have it (agreed) between the whole of Europe and the whole of the U.S."Virgin's spokesman said: "We would expect them as a U.S. carrier not to want competition in their own market. To us it's a major
98 issue. If cabotage is there we pledge to take it up."Currently only BA, United American and Virgin can operate U.S. services out of Heathrow but United and Virgin both say Heathrow is so overcrowded they could not compete against BA and American without more runway slots."In terms of seat share
98 the number one and number two airlines serving the United Kingdom are proposing to merge in a market that is already effectively closed to competition," Greenwald said in his speech on Thursday.</

102 traditional criteria as cost of capital, cost of raw materials and transport. Publishing the survey, attached to a BT/MCI Global Communications report, the groups said that by the year 2000, telecommunications would be worth more than $650 billion and would account for 2.37 percent of world GDP."It is clear that
102 telecommunications competition encourages investment by foreign companies," said Sir Peter Bonfield, BT's chief executive."The UK experience has shown that competition is good for customers and good for the UK economy and we would encourage national governments to open their markets to reap the benefit of increased investment". Gerald Taylor, the
102 president and chief operating officer at MCI, urged business people and governments to recognise "the crucial role that competitive communications plays not only in successful global expansion, but also in the development of national economies"."The challenge we are issuing today is to ensure that communications issues, including global deregulation, remain
102 high on the agenda for the entire business community," he said.An estimated 50 million people will use the Internet this year, double 1995 figures, the report added, and business and retail transactions on the net are estimated to reach $21 billion by 2000.Telecoms traffic is also expected to surge. While
102 the world spent nearly 60 billion minutes on the phone last year, in 2000, this could rise to 95 billion minutes, according to the report. BT/MCI Global Communications Report, 1996/97, was published in the third anniversary year of the creation by BT and MCI of their Concert alliance -- one
102 of three alliances of global carriers.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4017</
103 High costs levied by managing agents in particular have eroded Lloyds of London's competitiveness and should be reduced, an agency representing the insurance market's backers, known as Names, said on Thursday."These costs have grown substantially over the last 20 years and have destroyed any competitive position that Lloyd's had in
103 relation to its competitors in the 1960s and 1970s," members' agent Christie Brockbank Shipton (CBS) said in its September newsletter.Around 40 percent of a Name's gross return is lost in one form or another to Lloyd's and market agents, CBS said, adding that Names have done little or nothing to
103 challenge the charges, despite general recognition in the market that they are too high.The largest single element of costs charged by agents is the approximately 15 percent taken by managing agents as a profit commission on Names' profits, CBS said."Unless something is done to reduce the costs for Names and
103 corporate investors then Lloyd's is in danger of becoming an unattractive investment," it added."These are quite astonishing figures and bear no comparison with other forms of business let alone the costs that shareholders are required to bear as investors in insurance company stocks."CBS said that Lloyd's should create a climate
103 in which market forces could drive down costs, while Names' representative bodies and others should bring pressure to bear on syndicates and managing agents to cut charges.It also called for an end to managing agents and syndicates charging costs separately.The problem of costs should not be ignored, CBS said, adding,
103 "it is Lloyd's collective problem which will continue to hinder Lloyd's recovery until something is done about it."-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769</

106 Charter airline growth potential is being impeded by inadequate airport facilities, air traffic control delays and poor ground handling standards despite carrying over 50 percent of intra-European air traffic, said Marcel Pisters, director general of the International Air Carrier Association (IACA).He told an IATA conference that moves by the European
106 Commission to liberalise ground handling facilities that were "very disappointing".A proposed directive was being watered down by "so many possible exemptions," he explained, that it did nothing for non-scheduled airlines. IACA represents 41 European charter carriers.There was too much emphasis on major gateways and a lack of investment and planning
106 at many of Europe's tourist-receiving airports.Other moves by Brussels to alleviate airport congestion through the introduction of a so-called "monetised secondary trading" system encouraging the buying and selling of arrival and departure slots by airlines was another sources of concern, he said.It would impede market entry and place cash-rich scheduled
106 airlines in a dominant position at important charter hubs.European plans to end duty-free privileges on airline sales in June 1999 was another blow to operators dedicated to providing low-cost services to the leisure segment of the air transport market and would be resisted."As non-scheduled airlines," said Pisters, "we rely on
106 such inflight sales to a greater extent than scheduled airlines and our profitability will be affected to a much greater degree."The charter airline body was also vigorously opposing state handouts to national flag carriers: "We have to compete on a playing field that is less than level," he said, "when
106 you take into account the vast sums of cash being injected into these airlines with the blessing of the European Commission."Our association continues to pressure governments and the Commission to outlaw such capital injections," he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017</

129 The legal side of the Maxwell saga may have finally closed on Thursday with the release of Kevin Maxwell from any further charges, but British pension fund experts say the case has left indelible marks on the industry.Both Kevin Maxwell and his brother Ian, sons of tycoon Robert Maxwell who
129 disappeared from his yacht in 1991, were cleared in January this year of conspiracy to defraud the Maxwell group pension funds. More than 400 million pounds ($600 million) went missing. "The whole occupational pension movement in the UK has been deeply affected by the Maxwell affair," said Anne Robinson, director
129 general of the National Association of Pension Funds (NAPF). "The Pensions Act was subsequently designed to ensure that such problems would never happen again."The saga has had most effect on occupational or company-run pension schemes, but the Financial Services Act, which regulates the selling of private pensions and pension advice,
129 was also affected by the Maxwell affair.The exact implications of the Pensions Act will not be known until April next year when it comes into force.A spokesman for Legal &amp; General noted that the Maxwell scandal "kickstarted the Goode Committee and Report, which looked at what could and couldn't be
129 done by pension fund managers and what various roles and responsibilites were".Robinson added that since the Goode Report, the Minimum Funding Requirement (MFR) and the rule that one third of company scheme trustees must be member-nominated had been introduced.A new pensions Ombudsman and an Office of Pensions Regulatory Authority (OPRA)
129 are stll to be set up in 1997.Fund managers said that pre-Maxwell, neither companies nor employees paid much attention to in-house pension schemes. Companies took on the investment risk, effectively promising employees a certain return at retirement, without realising what it was costing them or exploiting the facility to attract
129 staff.Employees knew that to leave a company scheme early jeopardised full final payment but accustomed to state support, they hardly realised how important pension provisions were. Nor did they imagine how company funds could be so mis-used.Now, with less government social support and greater labour mobility, employees are being forced
129 to take greater responsibility for their investments and financial future."The balance has shifted from the company to the trustees of pension funds," said Robinson. "There is quite a complex system of checks and balances which they are required to monitor and understand. It can't be taken as lightly as before
129 -- trustees can be personally fined or sent to jail if they are negligent."The Legal &amp; General spokesman said increased costs following the new legislation, especially for smaller firms, had made many review their current pension schemes and possible alternatives.Ideas like group personal pensions, a collection of individual personal pensions,
129 are being considered. They are a type of money purchase arrangement where final pension depends on defined contributions (what the employee puts in) rather than defined benefit (relation to final salary).Kenneth Inglis, chairman of Fleming Investment Management, confirms new interest in this area. "Following the recent Pensions Act, businesses are
129 increasingly concerned about controlling the costs of managing their pension schemes...more and more are looking to money purchase pensions rather than traditional final salary pensions."Money purchase assets could reach 50 billion pounds in the next 10 years, providing cover for more than one million people.But the NAPF's Robinson said the
129 new legislation was only half the battle. "We are most concerned that some provision for independent custody of assets is included, which it is not at present," she said.She would also like greater simplicity and clarity in the rules. "We have all the legislation but the way it has been
129 enacted is very prescriptive. We want more people to come in to occupational pension schemes but they need simple, clear explanations of what they have to do." ($1=.6412 Pound)</

136 The following is the complete text of the minutes of the July 30 monthly monetary policy meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George:The Chancellor of the Exchequer and the Governor of the Bank of England met, together with officials, on 30 July,
136 to review monetary developments.Monetary and Economic Developments2. Latest monetary and economic data (reviewed by officials before the meeting) provided further evidence of weaker cost and price pressures. While output data showed growth remaining below trend, recent indicators of business confidence and consumer demand were more buoyant.Inflation Indicators3. Underlying inflation (RPI
136 excluding mortgage interest payments - RPIX) was unchanged in June, at 2.8 per cent. All-items RPI inflation fell by 0.1 percentage point, to 2.1 per cent, as recent mortgage rate cuts continued to take effect.4. Most other price and cost indicators confirmed that inflationary pressures remained weak:- the oil price
136 had fallen to $18.9 per barrel, and non-oil commodity prices had continued to decline; but sterling's effective exchange rate index fell by nearly 2 per cent over the period since the last meeting, to stand at 85.1;- total non-oil import prices fell by 0.8 per cent in the three months
136 to May compared to the previous three months; and non-EC import prices fell by 0.3 per cent in the three months to June;- producer input prices for manufacturing (excluding food, beverage, tobacco and petroleum industries) fell again in June, by 1.3 per cent; and compared to a year ago they
136 were 4.7 per cent lower. The CIPS survey input price indicator also fell sharply in June;- producer output prices for manufacturing (excluding FBTP) rose by 0.1 per cent in June; and the annual inflation rate fell to 2.0 per cent, from 2.4 per cent in May. The CBI survey output
136 price expectations balance was little changed;- the annual growth rate of underlying average earnings fell to 3.5 per cent in May, down from 3.75 per cent in April;- IRS median pay settlements were unchanged at 3.0 per cent in June.Monetary and Financial Indicators5. No new M0 data had been published
136 since the last meeting, although provisional and partial information suggested that growth had fallen back again following the sharp rise in June. Both M4 and M4 lending grew by 0.7 per cent in June, down from 0.8 per cent in May. The 12-month growth rates for M4 and M4 lending
136 rose slightly to 10.0 per cent and 9.4 per cent respectively.6. No new data on house prices were available since the last meeting. Housing market transactions had started to recover; particulars delivered (which lag actual transactions) in the three months to June were 4.7 per cent up on the previous
136 three months, although only 1.7 per cent up on a year earlier.7. Short-term interest rates were little changed in the US since the last meeting, but had fallen slightly in Germany, and risen slightly in Japan. Official rates had been reduced in Italy. UK short-term interest rates were little changed.
136 Forward interest rates implicit in short-sterling futures contracts were also little changed for September 1996, but had fallen (by up to 20 basis points) for longer maturities.8. 10-year bond yields in the US had risen by around 10 basis points, but had fallen by over 10 basis points in Germany,
136 and were little changed in Japan. In the UK, yields on conventional gilts were little changed at all maturities. Since the 3 July meeting inflation expectations implied by the gilt yield curve (calculated by the Bank from the difference between the yields on conventional and index-linked bonds) had risen slightly
136 for both 5 and 10 years ahead.Activity Indicators9.Overseas data indicated that US activity remained strong, and there were further signs of recovery in Japan. Activity indicators in Germany remained mixed:- in the US the June employment numbers were again strong, and unemployment had fallen to 5.3 per cent - the
136 lowest rate since June 1990. Industrial production rose by 0.5 per cent in June, following a rise of 0.5 per cent in May also;- in Japan industrial production rose by 2.4 per cent in May, following a rise of 3.2 per cent in April;- in Germany industrial production rose by
136 1.0 per cent in May; but business confidence fell back sharply in June, and unemployment rose slightly.10. The preliminary estimates of UK GDP growth in 1996 Q2 showed that whole economy and non-oil GDP grew by 0.4 per cent and 0.3 per cent respectively. Annual whole economy GDP growth in
136 Q2 was 1.8 per cent, down from 1.9 per cent in Q1. Services output was estimated to have grown by 0.7 per cent in Q2, and was 2.7 per cent higher than a year earlier.11. Other output data were consistent with growth overall below trend; but consumer indicators were again
136 strong, and survey information pointed to more buoyant business confidence:- manufacturing output was unchanged in May. However, in the three months to May it was 0.4 per cent higher than a year earlier. Total industrial production rose by 0.8 per cent in May, and in the latest three months was
136 up 1.2 per cent on a year earlier;- all major business surveys were more buoyant. The June CIPS survey and July CBI survey both showed an increase in output and new orders' indicators. The BCC survey was also stronger;- retail sales rose by 1.3 per cent in June, and figures
136 for April and May were also evised up. In the three months to June sales were 2.7 per cent higher than in the same period a year earlier;- survey indicators in the retail sector also remained strong: consumer confidence rose slightly, and in the June CBI Distributive Trades Survey the
136 balance of retailers expecting higher sales remained at a high level by historical standards;- claimant unemployment fell by 14,300 in June, and unfilled vacancies at Jobcentres rose by 13,000. Summary of discussion12. The Governor said that the data that had become available since the 3 July meeting served to reinforce
136 the prospect of weak inflationary pressures in the short run on the one hand, but increasing strength of domestic demand - especially consumption - in the period ahead on the other. In that context the Bank's August Inflation Report would point to a somewhat greater upside risk to the inflation
136 target by the spring/summer of 1998 than was projected in the May Report.13. Immediate cost and price pressures remained weak in June. Producer input prices, in particular, again had fallen (to 2 per cent below their level of a year earlier, or -4.7 per cent ex FBTP) helped by the
136 temporary appreciation of sterling; and output prices had risen by only 0.1 per cent (a rise of around 2.25 per cent on the year, excluding excise duties), with the survey evidence suggesting that they would remain subdued over the next few months at least. Underlying earnings growth had edged downwards
136 (to 3.5 per cent in the year to May), and pay settlements remained just below 3.5 per cent in June on the Bank's 3-month employment-weighted average. Although claimant unemployment had continued to decline, and job vacancies to increase, the LFS suggested that the demand for labour had not been rising
136 in the spring. Retail price inflation had not fallen as the Bank had expected in June (RPIX, RPIY and the headline rate were all unchanged from May, at 2.8 per cent, 2.3 per cent and 2.1 per cent respectively) partly because of food and household goods prices - with the
136 summer sales perhaps starting later this year. The Bank nevertheless continued to expect that RPIX would resume its fall in the autumn - to below 2.5 per cent - before it began to pick up again in the course of next year.14. The Governor noted that further ahead, the inflation
136 prospect depended on the speed and strength of the upturn in demand and activity. New data on this, as well as all the main surveys since the last meeting, had been relatively strong. This made the preliminary estimate for GDP growth in Q2 (+0.4 per cent, or +0.3 per cent
136 for non-oil GDP) disappointingly weak. In part this was explained by the fall in agricultural output as a result of the BSE crisis - without which output growth would in fact have picked up, again led by the services sector.15. As it was, retail sales volumes (helped by sales of
136 summer clothing) were very strong in June - up 1.3 per cent - and the April and May figures had been revised up to give a 1.3 per cent quarterly rise over Q1 and a 2.7 per cent rise over Q2 last year. There had also been a significant improvement
136 in both the CBI's Distributive Trades and the consumer confidence surveys. And, although Halifax house prices had fallen modestly in June, the underlying recovery of demand in the housing market appeared intact, with a modest improvement in turnover, net lending, new commitments and the number of site visitors over the
136 past 2-3 months. Business confidence too appeared to be improving, to judge from the quarterly CBI and BCC surveys, as well as the earlier survey of Purchasing Managers.16. The latest money and credit data remained consistent with the prospect of rising nominal demand growth later this year and next. Narrow
136 money growth remained at 7 per cent year-on-year, and faster on a 3- or 6-month annualised basis. And there was little sign in the June data of any significant deceleration in the underlying growth of either broad money or M4 lending - both rising at about 9 per cent on
136 a 3-month annualised basis to June. First estimates of the sectoral breakdown of money and credit in Q2 showed that individuals' deposits had continued to rise strongly, as had ICCs' deposits, although OFIs' deposits had risen more slowly than in Q1 (when they were inflated by the introduction of the
136 gilt repo market). Consumer credit had also grown strongly in Q2 despite a more moderate figure for June.17. The Governor concluded that, taken as a whole, the evidence since the last meeting suggested more clearly than before that the pick-up in demand - driven by household demand - that we
136 had all been expecting was now beginning to occur. On that basis the Bank saw no justification for further policy stimulus. In fact, as the Chancellor knew, the Bank would prefer short-term rates at 6 per cent. It was possible that this month's data exaggerated the underlying acceleration of demand.
136 But the opposite risk was that if the acceleration continued through the summer and into the autumn it would become increasingly difficult to moderate.18. 136 the year was undiminished. In his view, this was to be welcomed but needed to be seen against the background of below trend growth in recent quarters. The preliminary figures for GDP in Q2 were a little disappointing and surprising, though perhaps distorted downwards by a one-off BSE effect on

136 a year earlier, and followed a run of more disappointing data. Retail markets also remained very competitive, with little sign of upward pressure on margins. 140 As Finland hovers on the brink of entry to Europe's exchange rate mechanism, many analysts here believe the perceived medium-term economic or political benefits of bringing the markka into the current ERM regime are illusory.The luxury of huge 15 percent ERM fluctuation bands makes the chosen central exchange rate little
140 more than a symbolic target. As a result, there is little or no exchange discipline or currency-risk reduction inherent in the existing system.Moreover, many analysts believe that maintenance of 15 percent ERM bands alone will not be sufficient to satisfy the Maastricht criterion on exchange rate stability prior to European
140 monetary union. Hence, the political imperative of entering the ERM quickly is also notional at best."An ERM with 15 percent bands is of no practical value and and it's not even clear whether its necessary or sufficient for qualification for EMU," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS
140 Ltd.Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is pushing for a peg, in a bid for tight links with the EU to ensure closer political connections with the west for Finland, which joined the EU in 1995 after decades in the shadow of the former Soviet Union.But the central bank has been
140 reluctant, with officials voicing concerns that a link may expose the markka to speculative pressures and fuel volatility.The markka rallied to 2.99 per mark early on Thursday, its strongest level in nine months, as speculation about the exact timing of ERM entry intensified.The chairman of the Bank of Finland's board
140 of parliamentary supervisors IIkka Kanerva said ERM entry was unlikely this month, putting the market focus on early October as likely date for a joint lira and markka ERM fixing.Yet, analysts questioned the logic of trading on back of speculation about the entry level."The focus on the central rate in
140 a 15-percent-band system is a little misplaced," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "With such wide margins of error it's hard to see why ERM entry would change anyone's investment decision within Finland or toward Finland."Even if Finland attempts to informally target narrower 2.25 percent bands,
140 that some analysts believe will be necessary to satisfy the EMU criteria, the chances of holding the erratic markka in those bands over two years is slight, they said."In our view, the 2.25 percent rule will be used by the EU as a way of identifying the countries who will
140 have the least problem with fixed exchange rates and moving to EMU in 1999," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch.That would exclude Spain and Italy, for example, from the first move to EMU, even if they do manage to meet a relaxed interpretation of the other Maastricht criteria,
140 he said."Finland would have severe problems holding a narrow band regime for long, mainly because it is subject to strong exchange rate shocks that do not effect the rest of the European core," said Prendergast.The Finnish economy, and hence the competitiveness of the markka, is heavily dependent on volatile commodity
140 prices, with paper and pulp products accounting for about 40 percent of its export revenue.This is a stark contrast to the core European currencies to which Finland intends to peg the markka closely. In 1994 and 1995, for example, the markka was one of the strongest currencies in the world,
140 in contrast to exchange rate weakness against the German mark elsewhere in Europe.Conversely, the markka's devaluation against its European currency unit peg in 1992, prior to its later flotation, was a precursor to the exit of sterling and the lira from the ERM later that year.Moreover, neighbouring Sweden is Finland's
140 biggest trade competitor for pulp products and it is currently deeply divided about the merits of joining either the ERM or EMU."Finland is to Sweden what Ireland is to the UK, for example, and it is hard to imagine the markka not being heavily influenced by the swings of a
140 floating Swedish crown given such trade interdependence," said Meggyesi at Deutsche.Even as Finnish industry chiefs protest the recent rise of the markka, analysts say Finland's strong current account surplus, balanced budget and low inflation argue for an even stronger markka right now. Deutsche argues for an equilibrium level as low
140 at 2.85 per mark, for example.But Von Maydell at UBS said that while there may be a good case for saying a central rate about 3.00 per mark is fair value right now, that may not be the case over the full course of the economic cycle.--London newsroom +44 171

149 was batsman Rahul Dravid's gritty innings of 46 which won acclaim as the performance of the match by judge Sir Garfield Sobers.While Dravid, who has amassed 175 runs at an average of 58 in the series so far is quickly making a name for himself, English umpire David Shepherd, considered
149 one of the best adjudicators in the world, smudged his fine reputation with two poor decisions which had Pakistan reeling after just six overs."We lost the game when we lost the first three wickets," Pakistan captain Wasim Akram said later.Two of the three dismissals to leave Pakistan 16-3 came from,
149 at the very least, questionable decisions.Aamir Sohail (1) and Ijaz Ahmed (0) both appeared to miss deliveries from paceman Venkatesh Prasad by the proverbial mile, but when wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia gloved the ball and the Indians went up to appeal, they got the caught behind decision they wanted from Shepherd.While
149 Pakistan were never really in the match during their innings, India, skilfully captained by 23-year-old Sachin Tendulkar, made the most of their good fortune.India had struggled early after winning the toss and deciding to bat as Akram and his opening partner Waqar Younis bowled with clever variation, managing to move
149 the ball in the air and off the seam.At 14-2 in the fifth over, the situation looked awkward, but Dravid and his partner Mohammad Azharuddin (38), who had constructed a record 161 run partnership in match two, added 74 to steady the rocky boat.Akram picked up four for 35 as
149 the last four Indian wickets fell for just four runs (corrects from two runs), but 191 was going to be a challenging target on the Toronto turf.The controversial umpiring decisions did not detract from India's exceptional bowling performance. 151 week and coach Rodney Eade said his main attacking player would take the field.The other semifinal sees North Melbourne take on Brisbane at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday afternoon.North Melbourne, who finished second behind the Swans on the AFL table, must win to avoid the very real possibility of
151 the AFL final being played without a team from Melbourne for the first time.Monday sees the annual Brownlow Medal awards ceremony for the best and fairest player in the AFL.Rugby league is also one week away from its grand final, with two relative bolters through to the semifinals this weekend.St
151 George have performed well beyond expectations after the club lost several key players in the Super League battle and barely survived a possible merger with Sydney City at the start of the season.Last Saturday's upset win over Sydney City put the over-achieving St George through to a semifinal against North
151 Sydney on Saturday.Bookmakers have Norths as slight favourites although the possibility of another giant-killing performance by the confident Dragons can never be discounted.Sunday's semifinal sees minor premiers Manly up against Cronulla, who disposed of Brisbane last weekend.TENNISIt's also do-or-die time for Australia's Davis Cup tennis players, who take on Croatia
151 in Split starting on Friday.Australia must win to make it back into the elite world group of the Davis Cup after being relegated to the regional section of the tournament for the first time when they lost to Hungary last year.Non-playing captain John Newcombe has hinted he'll stand down if
151 Australia lose. His cause wasn't helped when doubles specialist Todd Woodbridge pulled out with an unspecified illness, breaking up his very successful partnership with Mark Woodforde.Jason Stoltenberg and Mark Philippoussis will play singles while Pat Rafter will partner Mark Woodforde in the doubles.With Croatia fielding world number four Goran Ivanisevic,
151 Australia must win the doubles to have a realistic hope of taking the tie.CRICKETAn important development in Australian cricket will take place in an unlikely place when the Victoria state side travel to Darwin for a 10-day session of practice matches from Friday.The tour will be the first prolonged hit-out
151 for leg-spinner Shane Warne since Australia's main strike bowler had surgery on the ring finger of his bowling hand in May.Warne was included in Australia's squad for the tour to India which starts on October 1, as was captain Mark Taylor, who is recovering from surgery to correct a back
151 problem.Australian Cricket Board officials have said Warne and Taylor must prove their fitness before they go on the tour.-- Sydney Newsroom 612 9373-1800</
152 Australia have threatened to cancel a test against Wales in December unless England are added to the Wallabies' European tour, a newspaper reported on Thursday.The Australian Rugby Union (ARU) issued the ultimatum after a request to play England at Twickenham was rejected by their British tour hosts, the four home
152 unions.ARU chief executive John O'Neill has adopted a tougher stance after suggesting two alternative dates, November 2 or 16, for the test against England in a bid to resolve the dispute."The ARU would reserve its position as regards its commitment to other matches currently on the itinerary," O'Neill was quoted
152 as saying in The Australian on Thursday.Australia added a test against Wales in Cardiff on December 1 to their original tour schedule after a request from Welsh officials, The Australian said. Originally, the eight-week tour only involved tests against Scotland, Ireland and Italy."It would have to be a board decision
152 but we'd look at cancelling the Wales test and going back to the original programme. I don't think we're being unreasonable," O'Neill said.Australia first suggested December 7 as the date for playing England at Twickenham. The Four Home Unions Tour Committee refused the idea, saying it was too late to
152 re-schedule a match against the Barbarians at Twickenham scheduled for the same day.By adding England to the fixture list, Australia would complete their first grand slam tour of Great Britain since 1984.O'Neill said financial considerations lay behind the push to include England on the itinerary."We're not ashamed to say there
152 are financial objectives and I just think these people need a big jolt. We all have enormous challenges to face in the professional era," he said.O'Neill said Australia had been caught out by the deterioration in relations between the home countries after England broke ranks by signing an individual television
152 deal.Their stance, which infuriated the Welsh, Scottish and Irish unions, threatened for a time the future of the annual Five Nations competition."The others don't want to help England at all, even if that means they get hurt (financially) in the process," O'Neill said.Australia's tour begins in October in Italy, where
152 the Wallabies will play a one-off test against their hosts, before heading to Britain.</

155 Morocco's 10,000 metre world record holder, Salah Hissou, said on Thursday he was determined next year to break the 5,000 metre record held by Ethiopian Haile Gebreselassie.Hissou told the Moroccan news agency MAP that his time of 12:50.80 in the 5,000 metres this year motivated him to go for the
155 record of 12:44.39 set by the Ethiopian in Zurich in 1995.The 24-year-old Moroccan, who took the bronze medal in July Olympic Games in Atlanta, set his 10,000 metres record in Brussels last August with a time of 26:38.09.Hissou, dubbed the "New Prince of the Desert" and seen by national coach

156 Haarlem, The Netherlands, Sept 19- Canterbury tennis professional Alistair Hunt faces his biggest ever test tomorrow when he meets Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek in his opening match of the Davis Cup tie between New Zealand and Holland here.It will be a giant leap for the 23-year-old to make on the
156 indoor court here in Haarlem.Hunt is more used to facing players with three digits in their rankings, rather than the single figure of Krajicek -- now ranked eighth in the world. But Hunt is in the best form of his career, having risen to 294th in the world after winning
156 both the singles and doubles of the British satellite circuit last month.However he knows facing Krajicek will be a different world."He's a great player, no doubt about it," Hunt told NZPA."But you can't look at that, all I have to really do is play the best I can."You can't think
156 about who the guy on the other side of the net is. If you have to do it, you have to do it sometime, and now is the best time." Hunt will face Krajicek, the Dutch No 1 in the second match tomorrow, hoping that New Zealand's No 1 Brett
156 Steven will have given the Kiwis the best possible start.Steven, now ranked 81st after a two-month lay-off following the birth of his son Ryan, will play Dutch No 2 Jan Siemerink in the opening rubber.That would appear to give Steven an advantage, but Siemerink, ranked 29th, will be no pushover.And
156 Steven admits his own lead-up form is not good."My form has been terrible this week,'' said Steven, who has particularly struggled with his serve. "I haven't played much so I can't get too uptight about it. I just hope it clicks on the day."Steven has not played since losing to
156 Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch in the first round of the Olympic tournament in July.But he had other things on his mind -- on the eve of the match he was told his wife Heather was about to give birth.After losing his Olympic match, he raced home for the birth and had
156 not played since, even missing the US Open.Now his family life has settled a little, Steven has his mind back on tennis. "It's not a worry any more," he added. "You get to the stage where you just want to play."It's frustrating not to be in great form, but hopefully
156 it will come together."New Zealand's chances of upsetting the Dutch hinge on Steven, although non-playing captain Jeff Simpson doesn't want more pressure on his top player."I don't want him to think like that," Simpson said."He hasn't played much this year but when he has, he has played well."I just want
156 him to go out and play as well as he can." New Zealand arrived in Haarlem by beating South Korea to win their Asia-Pacific qualifying zone in April.The Dutch came into this world group qualifying tie courtesy of a surprise loss to India.The winner of this tie will progress to
156 the elite world group.Dutch non-playing captain Stan Franker is cautiously confident of his side's chances, but won't be experimenting outside the Krajicek-Siemerink combination, who will also play Saturday's doubles against Steven and Hunt. Krajicek will also be playing his first match in Holland since winning Wimbledon in June to become
156 a national hero, but Dutch eyes will be on him.</

159 Canada and China on Thursday signed an understanding that Canada will retain its consular presence in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule next July."Our continued presence in Hong Kong ensures that we can keep on providing consular services to Canadians who live, travel or do business
159 there," Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said at a meeting with China's Foreign Affairs minister Qian Qichen.He also said the two countries agreed in principle on a deal to grant Hong Kong residents visa-free access to Canada after the handover. He said he hoped to have a final agreement in
159 a matter of weeks and there was an indication that once an agreement is in place the Chinese government will support it."In my discussion with the minister we agreed in principle about the visa-free access and the freedom of movement," Axworthy said. "The only issue that really remains is what
159 we need to establish as a procedure for removals and we are presently negotiating that with the Hong Kong government."Qian was scheduled to meet Canadian Immigration Minister Lucienne Robillard on Thursday to discuss the agreement.The so-called "right of removal" would guarantee Canada the right to send people with Hong Kong
159 passports back to Hong Kong if Canada had to deport them.Later, in a luncheon speech at the Institute for International Affairs and the Alliance of Manufacturers and Exporters of Canada, Qian said China's policy toward Hong Kong will remain unchanged. "The long-term stability and prosperity of Hong Kong are fully
159 guaranteed," he said.He said China would strictly fulfil the commitments it made in the Sino-British Joint Declaration. "The current socio-economic system and way of life in Hong Kong will remain unchanged. Likewise, the laws previously in force in Hong Kong will basically be maintained."Qian said foreign economic interests in Hong
159 Kong "will be taken care of."Earlier in the day, Qian said Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien will make a brief visit to Shanghai this autumn, during which the two governments will sign a contract on the introduction of the Candu heavy water nuclear reactor technology from Canada in a Chinese
159 nuclear power plant."This is a new beginning for the economic, trade and technological cooperation between the two countries," he said.Canada and China also signed an understanding that provides for the extension of the consular territories of Canada's diplomatic representation in China and the Chinese representation in Canada.</
160 Rain delayed harvest on the western Prairies as well as bleached some of the cut crops while combining advanced in the east, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in its crop report for the week ended Sept 18.British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley saw another 1.5 to
160 2.0 inches of rain in the past week then clear skies earlier in the past days which brought overnight lows of 0 to -3.0 Celsius. Rain was forecast to resume into the weekend. Ten percent of the crop was combined.Alberta's crops were rated six percent very good, 47 percent good
160 and 47 percent fair. Rain delayed harvest progress with 50 percent done in the north, 70 percent in the south. Harvest was expected to be delayed by seven to 10 days. Yields were seen average.Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt was rated seven percent very good, 61 percent good and 32 percent fair.The
160 northwest region's harvest was halted by rain and needed two weeks of good weather to be completed. Ninety percent of crops were swathed and 40 percent combined.North central Saskatchewan saw scattered showers delay the harvest. Ninety-five percent of crops were swathed, 30 percent combined. Ergot was reported to be the
160 primary downgrading factor but the extent of the downgrade was not yet known.Northeast Saskatchewan swathed 80 percent of crops but only cut 10 percent of flax. Forty percent of crops were harvested with flax at five percent combined.Southwest Saskatchewan rated 69 percent of crops as good, 23 percent fair and
160 eight percent poor. Two inches of rain halted harvest progress and caused downgrading due to bleaching. Wheat and durum was 75 percent combined, oats and barley 85 percent, canola 97 percent and flax was 45 percent combined.Southeast Saskatchewan rated crops 73 percent good, 20 percent fair and seven percent poor.
160 Swathing was 80 percent done, wheat, durum and oats were 45 percent combined. Canola and barley were 65 percent harvested, flax 40 percent. Wheat midge and rain bleaching caused downgrading.Eastern Saskatchewan and western Manitoba rated 89 percent of crops as good, 11 percent as fair. Showers delayed harvest and the
160 region needed two weeks to near completion. Sixty five percent of cereals were combined, 50 percent of canola and 25 percent of flax was harvested. Yield were above average but not bumper.Manitoba's harvest advanced well on good weather. Yields were slightly above average and grades were average.-- Gilbert Le Gras
