162 The Canadian government said on Thursday it introduced a bill in parliament that would permit Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc, to hold a broadcasting license and compete with cable TV companies.Industry Canada said the bill amends a 1968 prohibition which prevented Bell from entering the broadcasting business.Under the
162 amendment, Bell and its Stentor partners will be able to provide broadcasting distribution services once the rules for competition in local telephone services, including tariffs to enable companies and others to launch competitive local telephone services, have been implemented."The convergence of technologies means that companies which previously focused on either
162 telecommunications or broadcasting now want to offer integrated services,' said Industry Minister John Manley. "The real winners are consumers, who will ultimately have a coice in who provides their services."The government announced its intention to amend the Bell Canada Act in August with the release of the Convergence Policy Statement,
162 which cleared the way for cable companies to compete in each other's core businesses.-- Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100</
163 Canada's venerable public broadcaster, the CBC, announced on Thursday it was cutting 2,500 jobs and eliminating all U.S. programmes in an attempt to reinvent itself with a much smaller budget.The Canadian Broadcasting Corp. released long-awaited details on how it would cope with the hundreds of millions of dollars shred from
163 its government subsidies."We must move quickly," CBC President Perrin Beatty told reporters. "The bulk or our reductions must be implemented within the next six months or our checks will bounce."The CBC said the drastic new measures would reduce its operating budget by C$127 million ($92.7 million) by 1998. The CBC,
163 with its sprawling television and radio broadcasts in French and English, has already announced a series of other measures that would pare more than a third from its C$1.4 billion ($1 billion) budget by 1998.The Canadian government has contributed nearly two-thirds of the CBC budget in the past, but the
163 government's scramble to rein in its own troubled finances has led to deep cuts in funding for the CBC.The CBC, once similar in makeup to Britain's BBC, has turned increasingly to American situation comedies as well as big name sporting events to make up for lost federal revenues.As CBC became
163 more commercially oriented, some have called for abolishment of the public broadcaster as it appeared to be competing with private broadcasters to stay on the air.Others sought CBC to return to its roots. It was established as an act of Parliament in 1936 with a mandate to protect and promote
163 the fragile Canadian identity from the American cultural giant to the south.CBC developed programmes such as its classic "Hockey Night In Canada" on television and its public affairs show "As It Happens" on radio to tell Canadians what was happening in their own country.Beatty said the new plan would return
163 it to its roots with elimination of American shows. But it will also include more advertising. For the first time, the CBC's flagship evening news show, the National, will run advertisements.CBC did not announce the closing of any local television stations, but instead spread the cuts across the board, forcing
163 all departments to deal with substantially reduced resources.American programming will be gone from both prime time and day time schedules by September, 1998 and will be replaced by other shows created in-house or with more co-productions with private firms."In the future we will live or die on our Canadian productions."

166 Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson introduced amending legislation on Thursday which would double the potential liability for oil spills."The amendments introduced today will substantially raise a shipowner's liability in the event of an oil spill or other maritime incident," Anderson said in a statement."And in the case of a spill,
166 shipowners will also be responsible for the costs of reasonable measures to repair oil spill damage to the environment."The legislation would amend the Canada Shipping Act to more than double the amount available to Canadian claimants in an oil pollution incident to C$270 million from about C$120 million.The statement said
166 current provisions are based on a 1957 convention but the liability limits set out then have been eroded by inflation.Canadian rules for maritime liability would now be harmonized with those of other maritime nations, it said.Anderson also introduced into Parliament's House of Commons a bill which sets a clear legal
166 framework, for the first time in Canada, for compensating passengers involved in a marine accident.-- Randall Palmer, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613-235-6745)</
167 Countries bordering the Arctic Ocean inaugurated a joint council on Thursday to protect the region's fragile environment from tundra to polar bears while allowing sustainable economic development."The Arctic and its future are too big for one country, one government or for one conference every few years," Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd
167 Axworthy, chairman of the conference, said in a statement ahead of a signing ceremony.The vast Arctic lands are sparsely populated but some environmental experts suggest they suffer disproportionately from pollution and other activities of man. "The Arctic is an environmental early warning system for our globe," Canadian Environment Minister Sergio
167 Marchi said. "The Arctic Council will help deliver that warning from pole to pole."The group links Canada, Dennmark (responsible for Greenland), Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden and the United States. It seeks to build on the joint Arctic Environmental Protection Strategy, providing a permanent forum for governments to draw up
167 common guidelines and strategies to protect the environment in the face of development.Norwegian Deputy Environment Minister Bernt Bull said governments cannot just say no to all economic development -- whether mining or oil exploration -- but environmental issues must be considered simultaneously. Otherwise, he told Reuters, "the pressure for short-term
167 profits might limit the alertness on environmental issues."The World Wide Fund for Nature, known in North America as the World Wildlife Fund, said it welcomed the council but would closely monitor its activities to ensure environmental protection is strengthened.WWF's Norway-based Arctic specialist Peter Prokosch said that despite a higher polar
167 bear population as a result of an international protection treaty, scientists were worried that it might be starting to face risks of sterilisation."Scientists have found PCB levels on a level which bring gray seals in the Baltic to sterilisation," he said, referring to the poisonous pollutant polychlorinated biphenyl. In the
167 North Atlantic, the bowhead whale population has been reduced to 200 or 300 from thousands early in the century, requiring particular vigilance and study, he added.One challenge is to encourage environmental protection in Russia, which circles half the Arctic but which poses enormous risks as the country plunges into less-regulated
167 economic development. "They (previously) had the notion that nature was able to withstand anything," Bull said.The environmental group Greenpeace urged the group to work with natives to tackle potential catastrophic climate change."There are more striking climate changes taking place in the polar regions than any other place on the planet,"
167 Greenpeace spokesman Kevin Jardine said in a statement. The group said it was concerned about international transport of toxic pollutants and threats to northern fisheries.The chair and the secretariat of the council will rotate every two years among the eight states, beginning with Canada. Ministers will meet every two years.</

172 Population growth and problems with water management in Asia should drive up demand for grains steadily in coming decades, Worldwatch Institute's director Lester Brown said on Thursday."The rate of population growth in some central Asian states is higher than in India, so there will be an increasing need to import
172 grain," Brown said in a speech to the Winnipeg Chamber of Commerce.Brown, whose 1995 book "Who Will Feed China?" predicted China may import 200 million tonnes of grain a year by 2030, said aquifers in north China and India's Punjab were dropping. "Northern India's facing the same problem as China.
172 The Punjab, the breadbasket of India, is experiencing a steady depletion of its underground water and it will be faced with some substantial irrigation cutbacks," Brown said.Another source of demand for water comes from urbanization where expanding cities such as Beijing and Los Angeles compete with surrounding rural areas for
172 water use, he said."In a country like China, the loss of irrigation water translates into the need for additional grain imports," Brown said. "To import a tonne of wheat is to, in effect, import 1,000 tonnes of water." Southern China has also been losing rice crop land to urban sprawl
172 with increases in yields unable to make up the loss, Brown said."China can import a lot of grain but who can supply them? No one can on that scale," Brown said.Kazakhstan, a traditional supplier of grain to Russia, may need to import grain in coming years as would other central
172 Asian republics such as Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan due to rapid increases in population growth, he said.To meet such demand, production will have to continue rising in major exporters. Argentina could double its grain exports to 24 million tonnes from 12 million in coming years and Ukraine may also expand
172 grain output, Brown said.(Gilbert Le Gras 204 947 3548)</

174 Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Thursday launched a retooled government agency designed to boost sales of Canada Savings Bonds and other retail debt products.Martin also said the government will be making changes to the 50-year old Canada Saving Bonds program, including extending the length of time the bonds pay
174 a guaranteed minimum interest rate.The finance minister said the changes are being made to halt a decline since 1987 in sales of Canada Savings Bonds, which are sold to individuals and are not traded. The agency now administering sales of retail debt will be know as Canada Investment and Savings.
174 The agency was formed last year as the Canada Retail Debt Agency with the goal of boosting retail debt product sales.Among the changes being considered for the Canada Savings Bond program are pricing the bonds to carry a minimum guaranteed interest rate for up to a decade. The bonds now
174 carry a guaranteed rate for a maximum of three years.The agency is also lauching a pilot program with some companies to reduce the workload involved in offering Canada Savings Bonds to employees through payroll savings. Canada Investment and Savings will also be reducing administration demands on financial institutions for Canada
174 Savings Bonds sales of less than C$1,000, said Martin. A pilot program will also be established to make sales of less than C$1000 of the bonds available through some post offices.Martin said the bonds, which are held by about seven million Canadians and account for about C$30 billion of the
174 national debt, represent "a special anchor" in turbulent global financial markets.This year Canada Savings Bonds go on sale from Tuesday October 15 until Friday, November 1.-- Jeffrey Hodgson (416) 941-8105, e-mail: jeffrey.hodgson@reuters.com</

177 Liberalise more quickly or stagnate further was the message to emerge from a summit on Nigeria's economy on Thursday.Hundreds of businessmen and officials of the military government gathered in the capital Abuja in the search for policies to reform the economy and achieve long term growth.While there was emphasis on
177 government investment in infrastructure most recommendations were geared toward reducing government involvement in business and encouraging outside investment.Previous summits are credited with having influenced military ruler General Sani Abacha into carrying out a "guided deregulation" policy over the past two years."We are going to write a report to reflect all
177 the recommendations, and don't be surprised if after even a week they will be prepared for implementation," Ibrahim Ida, economic advisor to the president told journalists after the meeting.Despite the billions which Africa's most populous nation has earned through crude oil sales its economy has spiralled into ever deeper decline.Economic
177 policies have often stifled rather than accelerated growth as succesive military governments abruptly changed priorities."The time of direct government involvement in business is over and by the same token the time has passed when the private sector looked up to government for all the infrastructure needed for business," said Abacha
177 in a speech on Wednesday.A total of 16 separate groups debated areas of macroeconomic policy, trade and investment in both the long and short term. Next month a book will be produced containing all the recommendations."The military are not exactly experts in these fields, but at least if they are
177 listening to us then some of our ideas might filter through and bear fruit," said one private sector delegate who preferred not to be named.While economic liberalisation has swept much of the continent, Nigeria has kept more firmly to interventionist policies.Although the government has liberalised foreign exchange, and repealed controls
177 on external investment it has still paid little more than lip service to other areas.Hindering a Medium Term Economic Plan, essential for talks on rescheduling a $32 billion debt, are the dual exchange rate, interest rate caps and subsidies on fuel and fertiliser.Finance minister Anthony Ani told delegates the government
177 was ready to abolish the dual exchange rate and fertiliser subsidy, even going as far as to suggest eventual divestment from oil production.But at the same time he spoke of continued commitment to developing the steel industry, into which an estimated $8 billion have been ploughed without result.Delegates, among them
177 government ministers, said they recognised the need for revitalised privatisation or at least for competition to be permitted in key areas."What we see today is a serious attitude and development on key issues that is dramatically different even from previous summits," said Freddy Scott, one of the organisers.</

178 on a minibus taxi near Rumonge, 75 km (45 miles) south of the capital, according to an army spokesman.Archbishop Joachim Ruhuna, whose body was found by troops on Tuesday after he was said to have been killed in a rebel ambush last week, was buried in Gitega in central Burundi
178 on Thursday.State radio reported his burial but gave no further details.The army and the military-appointed government have blamed Hutu rebels for the murder, but they have in turn accused the Tutsi-led army of carrying out the attack.Ruhuna, a Tutsi who had criticised extremists on both sides of Burundi's ethnic divide
178 for perpetuating violence, was the most senior cleric killed in three years of massacres and civil war between rebels and the military.More than 150,000 people, most of them civilians, have been killed since renegade Tutsi soldiers killed the country's democratically elected president, a Hutu, in 1993.Buyoya was installed by the
178 army after the overthrow of Hutu president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya in July. The ex-president has been holed up in the U.S. ambassador's residence since then.Rukingama said the military government had offered talks to the rebels but had been rebuffed with vows of intensified armed struggle.</

185 to discourage the government from human rights violations and political oppression.Bushnell told a gathering of the American Business Association (in Kenya): "It must be improved trade that we must look at, to improve opportunities for growth for Kenya."But she also spoke of good governance and accountability.Central Bank of Kenya Governor
185 Micah Cheserem told Bushnell her emphasis should be trade between the two countries and a focus on governance to be on accountability and transparency."The relations (between Kenya and the U.S.) on political issues should be of advisory nature," Cheserem said.Cheserem said Kenya's annual per capita income of $250 was the
185 highest in the East African region but was a trickle compared to $25,880 in the United States.He said that despite poor intra-African trade, 49 percent of Kenya's exports were to African countries, mainly Uganda and Tanzania. The second largest market was the European Union which bought 32 percent of Kenyan
185 exports."The U.S. buys a dismal 3.0 percent of our exports compared to the 4.0 percent share it has in our imports," he said.Cheserem said gross domestic product (GDP) growth had picked up from a low of 0.2 percent in 1993 to 4.9 percent in 1995 and was now estimated at
185 6.0 percent in 1996, 7.0 percent in 1997 and 8.0 percent in 1998."Kenya's economic prospects have never been better. 185 of up to 9.0 percent.Cheserem said Kenya's reform agenda included reduction of the budget deficit and its eventual elimination, limiting government borrowing from the central bank, rehabilitating and upgrading infrastructure and privatisation of state companies.He said current investor concerns were dilapidated and inadequate infratructure, especially power supply, poor roads, inefficient
185 railways and inadequate water supply.He said investors were also wary of insecurity, corruption at many levels in government, weak and corrupt judicial system and uncertainty caused by frequent political tensions."But we are doing something about this," he said.</

204 accustomed to Western aid and the result was an unsustainable external debt: "We do not want aid that we cannot pay back, we need to improve two-way trade."Africa's external debt is estimated at around $317 billion."We strongly believe our mission will only be accomplished through accelerated economic growth rates. 204 aid has not eradicated and will not eradicate poverty in Africa," he added."We have great potential and opportunities. 204 the root cause of civil unrest and power struggles mainly as poverty."Many of the Africans who have left to live in the West are economic refugees. 204 Cheserem said."The prospects for Africa's 700 million people can only get better," he said, referring to economic reforms in much of the continent and sustained economic growth rates averaging 5.0 percent recorded last year in the continent.Africa's people make up 12 percent of the world population but the continent's gross

204 countries have high population growth rates which outstrip economic growth and overstretch existing services, economic and political problems lack homegrown solutions, leadership pays attention to politics more than economics, media cherishes negative publicity," Cheserem said.Cheserem said privatisations and launching of stock exchanges raised avenues for trade while liberalisation removed avenues

205 and annualised rate of nine percent in the three months to June after a fall of 1.5 percent in the first quarter.This turnabout was due to an acceleration in real private consumption expenditure and a sudden sharp increase in inventory accumulation, the Bank said in its Quarterly Bulletin.Private consumption expenditure
205 rose four percent in the second quarter from three percent in the first, with household spending on consumer goods and services jumping 13.5 percent."Higher purchases of transport equipment, motivated strongly by expectations of future price increases that may arise from the depreciation of the exchange rate of the rand, were
205 primarily responsible for the sharp increase in real consumer spending on durable goods," it said.Real gross domestic fixed investment slowed down from an annualised seven percent in the first quarter, but remained relatively high at 5.5 percent in the second quarter.Private sector fixed investment, which had declined progressively from 8.5
205 in the third quarter of 1995 to three percent in the first quarter of 1996, reverted back to 6.5 percent growth in the second quarter.All major sectors saw an increase, except mining, with agriculture prominent. 231 Deep water around western and southern Africa offers significant oil production and revenue opportunities, extending well into the next century, British Petroleum Co Plc said on Thursday."The possibility that we have in mind is that future production opportunities lie off Africa in the deeper water," David Bamford, head of BP's
231 sub-Saharan Business Unit said at the Africa Upstream 1996 conference.But he said that the key to developing these resources was improving the relationship between major oil companies and national oil companies (NOCs)."The single most important thing to delivering that is the quality of the relationship between major oil companies like
231 ourselves and the NOCs. This is the key, the heart," he said.Sub-Saharan Africa in particular offered significant deep water oil production possibilities, which were achievable but by no means certain, and whose development lay with the application of advanced technology, Bamford said.Deep water zones were those lying between 200 metres
231 and 2,000 metres and were provinces which contained billions of barrels of oil and several giant fields.He cited world examples as being the Campos Basin offshore Brazil -- a direct analogue of what might exist offshore sub-Saharan Africa -- and the Mississipi Canyon area of the Gulf of Mexico.Bamford said
231 development of such resources should aim for production four years after discovery and therefore the industry should find ways to speed up the execution of the risky exploration period."I predict that there is need for little other than incremental progress to deliver developments out to 2,000 metres water depth...out to
231 1,500 metres most milestones have been achieved or are achievable, though not inexpensively."From 1,500 metres to 2,000 metres some innovations are required and costs will certainly go up sharply. However, this should not be seen as a barrier but considered simply a question of striking the right risk-reward balance," he
231 said.Bamford added that geophysics and drilling technology was advancing at a rapid pace and so allowed talk of exploiting resources at vast depths beneath the sea.Major oil companies had a "pretty poor profile" with regard to world exploration and development -- indulging in selective truth telling and treating the people
231 of countries they operated in carelessly, Bamford said."We in BP believe the key to progress in our industry is to seek relationships, activities and projects that have at their heart the mutual advantage of all sides," he said.-- Melanie Cheary, Cape Town newsroom +27 21 22 2358</

236 Hundreds of Nigerian businessmen and officials from the military government gathered in the capital Abuja on Thursday to discuss ways to reform the country's stagnant economy.Delegates to the "Economic Summit" were to debate macroeconomic policy, trade and investment in the long and short term before making recommendations to the government.Previous
236 summits are credited with influencing Nigeria's military ruler, General Sani Abacha, to carry out a "guided deregulation" policy over the past two years."The time of direct government involvement in business is over and by the same token the time has passed when the private sector looked up to government for
236 all the infrastructure needed for business," Abacha said on Wednesday.Despite the billions which Africa's most populous nation has earned through crude oil sales, its economy has spiralled into ever deeper decline.Economic policies have often stifled rather than accelerated growth as successive military governments abruptly changed priorities."The military are not exactly
236 experts in these fields, but at least if they are listening to us then some of our ideas might filter through and bear fruit," said one private sector delegate who preferred not to be named.While liberalisation has swept much of the continent, Nigeria has kept more firmly to interventionist policies.Although
236 the government has liberalised foreign exchange and repealed controls on external investment, it has paid little more than lip service to other reforms."The key changes we've had since 1993 were recommended by the economic summit and are already having a major impact," Ibrahim Ida, economic adviser to the president, told
236 reporters.Hindering a medium-term economic plan, essential for talks on rescheduling a $32 billion debt, are the dual exchange rate, interest rate caps and subsidies on fuel and fertiliser.Finance Minister Anthony Ani told delegates the government was ready to abolish the dual exchange rate and fertiliser subsidy, even going as far
236 as to suggest eventual divestment from oil production.But at the same time he spoke of continued commitment to developing the steel industry, in which an estimated $8 billion has been invested over the last 20 years without concrete results.Delegates from the private sector are pushing for the stalled privatisation programme
236 to be restarted or at least for competition to be permitted in key areas."We urge that the private sector be allowed to operate...even in areas such as telecommunications, power and oil refineries, where outside privatisation seems untouchable," said Pascal Dozie, president of the Nigerian Stock Exchange."The private sector should be
236 allowed to participate even if only to force existing parastatals (state-owned companies) in these areas to improve their service quality," he added.</

240 The central National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) said on Thursday it had cut interest charged by commercial banks on loans and deposits to stimulate investment.The NBE said in a statement it had reduced interest on commercial bank loans to 10.5 percent from 16 percent and had cut interest on deposits
240 to 7.0 percent from 10 percent. The changes were effective from September 16, it said. The central bank said the reduction in bank loans was meant to inspire more people to turn to commercial banks for loans, promote bank deposits and spur investment."The new policy was also aimed at discouraging
240 those who simply deposit money in banks and live on interest to think about investment on any business venture," the bank said.Ethiopian economists and bankers said the new interest policy was bound to drastically affect newly established private banks with small capital that survived on interest from loans.Three private banks
240 have been launched in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa and have established branches throughout the country since Prime Minister Meles Zenawi's government liberalised the country's financial system in 1994.These include the Awash Bank, the Dashen Bank and Bank of Abyssinia. All are fully owned by Ethiopian shareholders.</

250 Divisions between Serb and Moslem leaders have already begun to emerge in Bosnia's peacetime collective presidency only a day after election results were announced.International mediators are struggling to forge an agreement about where the three-member presidency should meet, the wording of an oath of office and other basic issues.The Serb
250 member of the newly-elected collective presidency, Momcilo Krajisnik, said on Thursday he wanted joint institions to work but staked out positions in clear opposition to his Moslem rival, Alija Izetbegovic.Krajisnik finished second in the presidential voting behind Izetbegovic, who will serve as the chair of the presidency after winning the
250 largest number of votes in Saturday's poll.The hardline Serb nationalist told a news conference he rejected a ruling by international election organisers that Izetbegovic should serve a two-year term as chairman."You have noticed that one of my partners in the presidency has already shown bad will and tried to represent
250 himself as the chief of a body in which he is only first among equals," Krajisnik said.The Serb leader insisted the post should rotate between the three members every eight months.He also said the three members should discuss whether the candidate with the most votes should hold the post first
250 in the rotation.The exact oath Krajisnik would take as a presidency member had not been resolved either, he said.On Thursday, Izetbegovic said no official meeting of the presidency could take place until Krajisnik took an oath to Bosnia's constitution."The approach I should take to my duties is still not agreed,"
250 he said.Carl Bildt, the international High Representative to Bosnia, had discussed the issue with presidency members, Krajisnik said."There should be definitive statements which will oblige the members of the presidency to act according to the law."Krajisnik, who has openly opposed reunifying Bosnia, repeated his demand that the presidency convene in
250 industrial suburbs straddling the boundary separating the Serb and Moslem- Croat federation.He also mentioned Pale, the mountain village 16 km (nine miles) outside Sarajevo that serves as the Serb government seat, as a possible site."It should be in Sarajevo but in a place where the security of all the participants
250 can be guaranteed."Bosnian Moslems have ruled out the Serb proposal, saying meeting on the inter-entity boundary line would symbolise the division of Bosnia, violating the spirit of the Dayton treaty.Sworn enemies during 3-1/2 years of war, Izetbegovic and Krajisnik have yet to meet since election results were reported but the
250 Croat member, Kresimir Zubak, held talks with both men on Thursday.Asked if the Bosian Serbs had given up their goal of sovereignty, Krajisnik said Serbs had settled for a "realistic" compromise.Krajisnik acknowledged the Bosnian Serbs had wished for independence or union with neighbouring Serbia, but insisted they were satisfied with
250 the "limited sovereignty" granted by the Dayton peace agreement."We have been working for future generations. We created peace and the Serb republic, and what future generations will do -- that is their right."</
251 Peace coordinator Carl Bildt said on Thursday he would welcome authorisation from the U.N. to apply sanctions if needed to push nationalist factions into sharing power in post-election Bosnia.The three main Moslem, Serb and Croat parties who led their communities through war won clear victories in Saturday's general elections run
251 under provisions of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty signed by all sides.Bildt said it may take more than moral persuasion to get communal leaders genuinely committed to joint rule."We need to beef up the structures of civilian implementation of the Dayton accords and we are having a dialogue on that,"
251 Bildt, the international High Representative in Bosnia, told a news briefing."Will there be some sort of sanctions instrument given by the Security Council for the next few years? I don't know. But I would certainly be in favour of that, a wider or more graduated sanctions instrument."I need to have
251 in our arsenal some additional measures," he said, to rebuild Bosnia's multi-ethnic society torn apart by the very nationalist factions that were re-elected on Saturday.Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic, leader of the Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA), Momcilo Krajisnik of the Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and Croat HDZ party leader
251 Kresimir Zubak won the three seats on a new collective presidency.The SDA, SDS and HDZ will also dominate a new Bosnian parliament and assemblies in two semi-autonomous entities, the Federation (Moslem-Croat) and Serb Republic, according to near- complete returns released on Thursday.The Bosnian presidency is to govern by consensus while
251 quorum majorities will suffice in the assemblies. But legislation can be blocked by one national faction perceiving "a threat to the vital interests of its people".This provision was written into the Dayton treaty to prevent domineering by one side -- but could be exploited by separatists to paralyse joint government,
251 critics say.Once the elections are certified, expected next week, the presidency must convene to start appointing a cabinet.Bildt said that in talks he had earlier this week, Izetbegovic, Krajisnik and Zubak had all pledged to work together. But disputes over crucial symbolic issues broke out ominously on Thursday.Krajisnik told Bildt
251 he wants the presidency to convene right on the boundary line between the RS and Federation, a line the Serbs treat as an international border.Moslem leaders want the venue in Sarajevo, the Bosnian capital besieged but not taken by Serb forces in the war, accusing Krajisnik of trying to nip
251 unity in the bud.In the Serb "capital" Pale, Krajisnik told reporters Serb leaders could not feel safe in downtown Sarajevo.He also said he had never agreed to Izetbegovic serving as head of state in the presidency -- as the top vote getter -- for the first two years, instead of
251 rotating with Serb and Croat members earlier.The Bosnian oath of office was also problematic, he said.Earlier, Moslem-led Bosnian state radio quoted Izetbegovic as saying formal talks within the new presidency would begin when Krajisnik was prepared to "swear on the Bosnian constitution".Zubak said on state television he had already had
251 informal talks with Krajisnik. Asked if Krajisnik was ready to join the presidency, Zubak said: "That's indisputable. He's ready to work on something he signed up to and he told me that."With counting almost finished, the SDA was polling 54.3 percent of the vote for two-thirds of the 42 seats
251 in a new House of Representatives reserved for candidates from Federation territory, or half of Bosnia.The HDZ, the SDA's uneasy partner in a pre-election Federation government, had tallied 23.4 percent.In the race for seats allotted to parties running in the Serb Republic entity, the separatist SDS was way ahead with
251 54.4 percent. Biljana Plavsic of the SDS was elected Serb entity president with 65.1 percent of the ballots.</

256 (92 ft) long grave is dug into a hillside in the remote and mountainous region.Investigators dressed in blue overalls worked amid the overpowering stench of rotting flesh, to clear away topsoil and uncover the pile of corpses.War Crimes prosecutors believe the bodies are those of Moslems killed as they fled
256 the Serb conquest of Srebrenica last year.The town had been declared a U.N. "safe area" for Moslems, although Serb forces siezed it in a major offensive and forced the population to flee into the hills.While thousands of women and children survived, some eight thousand Moslem men and boys are missing.The
256 investigators believe conquering Serbs forces either cut them down as they tried to sneak to safety, or rounded them up and executed them before burying the bodies in mass graves.In Pilica, the unearthed bodies had been randomly thrown on top of one another to form a heap some 3 metres
256 (10 ft) deep.The investigators zipped the remains into body bags before storing them in refrigerated containers for transport to a makeshift morgue in Moslem-controlled Kalesija.There, forensic scientists will try to identify the victims and determine the cause of death in their hunt for clues to convict the people accused of
256 ordering the alleged massacres.Haglund said there was evidence that the bodies had been bound with cloth. 256 way now," he said.Haglund's team, from the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, has finished exhumations at three other grave sites -- Cerska, where they found 160 bodies, Nova Kasaba which contained 33 bodies, and Lazet which had 160.Haglund refused to be drawn on the number of bodies there
256 may be in the Pilica grave before the exhumation was completed.Autopsy and examination were expected to continue for another month and a half, he said adding that "Pilica may well be the last site that we will look at in this form this season."</

292 Ukrainian officials said on Thursday that neutron radiation readings had risen considerably inside the Chernobyl nuclear plant's ruined fourth reactor and called for new efforts to rebuild the "sarcophagus" housing it.Viktor Baryakhtar, vice-president of Ukraine's Academy of Sciences, told Ukrinform news agency that readings of neutron activity in the cracking
292 steel and concrete "sarcophagus" covering the reactor had risen by five to 110 times this week.Independent experts said even those readings posed no immediate danger, 10 years after the reactor caught fire and exploded in the world's worst civil nuclear disaster.President Leonid Kuchma, who has pledged to close Chernobyl by
292 the year 2000, expressed concern over the state of the sarcophagus at talks with an envoy of the G7 wealthy countries, one of the chief paymasters in financing the shutdown.Baryakhtar, Kuchma's top nuclear adviser, described the increased readings as a "chain reaction" which had lasted from four to five hours
292 on Monday."This is a rather dangerous phenomenon which has been observed three times this year," he told Ukrinform."The main reason is leakage under the sarcophagus of rainwater, which speeds up neutrons. The only way to avoid these instances is to build a new structure around the sarcophagus without delay."One independent
292 report this week said neutron radiation readings twice normal levels had been recorded inside the "tomb" hurriedly erected around the reactor after the 1986 disaster.But it said rises of tens of thousands times the norm would be required to cause a new nuclear reaction.Baryakhtar's statement, and its appearance on Ukraine's
292 official news agency, appeared aimed at pressing for quicker action in replacing the sarcophagus."Such levels are still well below anything constituting a danger but it is important to understand just what is happening inside there. It all must be explained," Patrick Michaille, a French nuclear safety expert in Ukraine, told
292 Reuters."If levels continue to be abnormal that makes the problem of the sarcophagus more urgent. The Ukrainians are clearly trying to draw attention to this. But even if more money is allocated that does not necessarily deal with the problem."Ukraine's top negotiator on closing Chernobyl, Environment Minister Yuri Kostenko, initially
292 suggested on Wednesday that the readings were caused by faulty equipment.But he later said that, if the levels proved correct, they required quick investigation which Ukraine could not afford.At a meeting attended by G7 ambassadors, special envoy Claude Mandil handed Kuchma a letter from French President Jacques Chirac, the current
292 G7 chairman, responding to Kiev's plea to speed up promised aid and grants of about $3 billion.A spokesman said Kuchma expressed concern to Mandil about delays in financing construction of two unfinished reactors at other power stations "and the 200 tonnes of nuclear fuel under the sarcophagus. I expect clear
292 decisions on this from G7."Kuchma was also meeting a senior official of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which is negotiating a separate financing accord on Chernobyl.Ukraine has complained that Western efforts have focused on restructuring the former Soviet republic's energy sector and do not recognise a new sarcophagus
292 as an urgent priority.A Franco-British plan devised three years ago to build a new structure has been all but abandoned as too expensive and the winner of a new tender for a less complex project is expected to be announced next month.</

302 been very active during the last two weeks, but tariffs have not changed."Tariffs were stable. Forwarders do not want to lose clients by increasing them," Vins said.He said the company had shipments of between four and seven tonnes of cargo a week. "It's a good volume," Vins added.Lilia Sirbu, manager
302 director of Icaros International Cargo Service, said clients were more active in September tha in the two previous months. "We have many new orders," she said, adding the market would be most active by the year end."Competition between freight-forwarders is sharp now. I do not beleive that tariffs will increase,"
302 Sirbu said, adding that clients often suggested tariffs and forwarders agreed with them.Igor Mordvinov, Burlington Air Express Moscow senior sales manager, said tariffs were unchanged compared with mid-August."But we see the market as very active after the summer holiday slumber," he said.Mordvinov said the market activity was expected to peak
302 during the next three months."We see lower tariffs if this happens," he said.Mordvinov also said his company had signed a few big contracts with clients. He declined to name the firms and volumes of future shipments.But Grigory Portenko, sales manager of Logimix, Air France cargo agent, said his firm's orders
302 had been steady in the summer. "We have a stable level of cargo operations irrespective of the summer holidays period," he said.Chief cargo manager Vladimir Pavlov of Soby, a cargo agent for Aeroflot and Vnukovo Airlines, said his company had stable export shipments.Meanwhile, Ilya Maslennikov, a sales manager of forwarder
302 Eruslan, said sales volumes were sharply down at Sheremetyevo airport due to rigorous customs clearance rules."Customs tariffs are higher here than around the world," he said, adding that many companies try to avoid delivery of its cargoes through the airport's cargo terminals. "They prefer to use trucks to carry cargoes
302 from Helsinki to Moscow or find other airports," he added.Maslennikov said the market became very active in the last two weeks. "We have many orders for export, but absolutely no import deliveries. Our storage area in Sheremetyevo is empty now," he said.Many forwarders see the development of transit deliveries to
302 internal Russian destinations as very promising.Vins said the majority of air cargo business was moving from Moscow to Russian provinces."Lufthansa saw this tendency an is developing its network of routes in central Russian regions, the Urals and Siberia," he said.Vins said that his company had some big shipments to China
302 and Hong Kong. "Shipments from Moscow to U.S. destinations were stable, he said. Export shipments had picked up in the last two weeks although Vinlund Air had more import deliveries earlier.Mordvinov said his company planned shipments to Tunis and Cairo later this month. "Russian companies want to carry machinery to
302 Egypt and equipment to recently opened joint ventures in Tunisia," he added.Sirbu said shipments for Europe of excise stamps for cigarettes, which were produced in Europe for Russian firms were stable.She also said flights from Amsterdam to Moscow with flowers had stable load factors. "We see growing flower deliveries from
302 Columbia and Ecuador to Russia next few months," she said.Chris Lewis, manager for Chapman Freeborn Russia, also said deliveries of flowers from South America were very active in recent weeks. "Delta and KrasAir carried many flowers," he said, adding that there was a big demand for deliveries of this cargo
302 in Russia.--Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520</
303 Civilians working in the cash-strapped Russian armed forces and the defence industry launched a series of protests on Thursday against chronic wage delays.The actions, which Itar-Tass news agency said included a one-day warning strike by workers servicing Russia's nuclear submarines, follow a long build-up of tension in the military, which
303 is owed billions of dollars by the state."The armed forces of the Russian Federation seem to be reaching a critical point in their overstretched patience," the presidential newspaper Rossiskiye Vesti said on Thursday."Sociological surveys show that...the military is extremely unhappy with its current situation and is sliding towards the dangerous
303 state where it could take unpredictable actions."Tass said employees of the Northern Fleet logistics services and enterprises providing technical support to the nuclear submarine force staged a one-day warning strike.Many workers had not received their wages since April, Tass said. It did not say how many employees took part in
303 the action, which was organised by a local trade union.The agency had said on Wednesday that a trade union conference in the northern naval base of Severodvinsk decided to launch a strike at docks servicing nuclear submarines next Monday.It was not clear whether Thurday's labour action was a substitute for
303 the announced strike which the union had said would involve up to 15,000 workers.Tass said in a separate report that civilian employees of the Pacific Fleet based in Vladivostok also went on a one-day strike on Thursday.In Moscow civilians working in the armed forces held a protest action in front
303 of the government headquarters, carrying placards saying, "Give us a peace of the pie!" or "Russia needs an army".Tass quoted the union's leader Spartak Orzhavin as saying that the government owed the army more than six trillion roubles ($1.2 billion) in overdue wages.The liberal opposition daily Nezavisimaya Gazeta said this
303 was only a fifth of the state's debt to the armed forces.Security council secretary Alexander Lebed has drawn attention to the crisis and lobbied for funding to be further increased in next year's budget."The armed forces are in a financial crisis. If measures are not taken urgently it could have
303 irreversable consequences for national security," he wrote in a letter to President Boris Yeltsin which was published on Friday.</

305 the bank was in talks with clients on nine level-one ADR issues, two private placements and the prospective level three listing.Sturdy said the timing of the level-three issue, which raises new capital and requires strict disclosure of a company's financial performance, would depend on market conditions."It could be before the
305 end of the year," he said, but declined to name the company.Several Russian companies, including high-profile firms such as LUKoil and Chernogorneft, have issued level one ADRs, which are intended to increase liquidity in a stocks but do not raise new capital.The Bank of New York is depositary bank to
305 many issues.Mosenergo has made a private placement of treasury stock.Russian banks also plan to issue ADRs, which allow foreign investors to gain access to underlying shares without domestic settlement problems, but need central bank approval first.Sturdy said some 23 percent of Mosenergo shares were held in ADR form, 22 percent
305 for LUKoil and 14 percent for Seversky Tube Works."I think that is a very positive sign of the interest across the globe in investing in Russian stocks," Sturdy said.Companies which have announced plans for ADRs include Unified Energy System and Irkutskenerg."There is a relatively large number of companies which are
305 either in a position to appeal to international investors or have the potential to do so with continued management changes or better economic conditions," he said.--Nigel Stephenson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520</

309 Firms listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange recorded slightly better earnings in August for the second month in a row, a tendency that could help keep the bourse mood positive, analysts said on Thursday.But they said investors would best wait for the earnings rally to continue to the end of
309 the year."The August results are a continuation of last month since they're better than the first half, which could mean the start of a trend, but it's hard to say what will happen by the end of the year," said Pawel Hominski of Magnus brokerage.Analysts had said uninspiring May and
309 June earnings had hastened July's downward correction that followed the bourse's 90-percent surge this year. Weaker earnings over the first four months had been blamed partly on this year's harsh winter.Analysts said there was always the danger that auditors would pare preliminary profit reports, as happened with three main-market firms
309 for 1995 earlier this year."There could still be many nasty surprises," said Jacek Dzierwa, Polish Equity Analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.But Dzierwa said the bourse could rise by at least another 10 percent this year, helped by better earnings and especially by the arrival of capital from foreign investment
309 funds.Firms showing good results tended to rise on the bourse on Thursday, such as the two top gainers, furniture maker Forte and paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn.Thursday's biggers losers Espebepe and Remak plunged by or near the maximum 10 percent after publishing weak August earnings.Analysts liked Cieszyn and rival paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw
309 in the longer term, though said Wroclaw looked cheaper at the moment and warned that the fourth quarter was a tough time for the industry.Analysts also favoured banks, which continued to show good results, and tyremakers Debica and Stomil Olsztyn, though Stomil was cheaper especially after its 9.1-percent plunge on
309 Thursday after its lower August profit.Debica recorded its highest monthly net profit in August but did so on financial rather than operational gains.Analyts said that among sectors containing small-cap stocks, textile firms were seen rebounding upon a better business cycle in Germany, but meat firms could be stung by higher
309 fodder prices.-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700</

310 this year would likely be 10 million tonnes above last year's official 63.4 million tonnes.First Deputy Agriculture Minister Vladimir Shcherbak, quoted by Interfax, gave the same estimate earlier this week, which is below official government forecasts of 75-77 million tonnes.Gridasov said cold weather, rain and a lack of fuel and

343 a second term as head of the country, which regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991.Political commentators said the vote was too close to call although Meri is seen as the favourite.Meri's closest rival is Arnold Ruutel, 68, a silver-haired former senior Communist and one of the
343 leaders of the country's drive to win back its independence.Ruutel was Meri's only rival through the three rounds of parliament voting in what was a rerun of the 1992 election, when Meri beat Ruutel although the latter won a national vote."There are five candidates and it seems to me that
343 there will be a second round of voting," said Rein Toomla, a political scientist at Tartu University.The electoral college includes 101 members of parliament and 273 local government representatives. It has two votes on Friday. If both are inconclusive, parliament will vote again."If Meri and Ruutel win through to the
343 second round, it seems that Meri has the better chances," Toomla said.Right-winger Tunne Kelam, 60, like Ruutel a deputy parliament speaker, is seen as the strongest new challenger.His pedigree is as a pro-independence nationalist who worked outside the Soviet system rather than within as Ruutel did.Kellam says Meri may be
343 the president today but he is the leader of the future while Ruutel is yesterday's man.Meri, a charismatic former film director, is seen as an eloquent spokesman for Estonia but has earned the anger of parliament for over-stepping the bounds of what is supposed to be a largely ceremonial role.The
343 main criticism is that he signed a deal with Russia in 1994 on the withdrawal of Russian troops from Estonia without consulting parliament. Critics say the agreement left too many former Soviet military pensioners in Estonia.The Estonian media has also been working itself into a frenzy over allegations that Meri
343 worked with the KGB, the feared Soviet security police.The allegations were given new impetus on Wednesday when high-profile opposition politician Edgar Savisaar, a former prime minister and interior minister, urged Meri to step down and said he had proof the president worked with the KGB.Meri has consistently denied the allegations.Critics
343 also say Meri has interfered with legislation affecting Estonia's large Russian minority, resented by some Estonians as remnants of a colonising power.But Western diplomats have applauded Meri for being more liberal than some of his nationalist colleagues.The only female candidate in the presidential race, Siiri Oviir, is deputy leader of

347 Russian oil refiners are eyeing costly upgrades to make the lighter products that export markets favour, but they may find it hard to find the cash.Hydrocrackers and fluid catalytic crackers -- expensive, sophisticated plants that produce lighter material like gasoline, naphtha, diesel and jet fuel -- are rare in Russia,
347 where heavy fuel oil makes up around 40 percent of output.Most Russian refiners use less sophisticated processing technologies, and only three percent of capacity comes from cracking processes, well below Western levels."There's just a screaming need for secondary capacity," said a senior Western energy consultant in Moscow. "But who's willing
347 to invest in a Russian refinery?"Boston Consulting Group says that by 2000, new capacities in Russia could include 254,000 barrels per day (bpd) of catalytic cracking and 131,000 bpd of hydrocracking, both used to produce expensive, high-octane fuels.The increases, and boosts to other processes, could bring Russia's products output to
347 5.9 million bpd by 2000 from a current 5.2 million -- but the analysts said they would not mean heavy product output falls by the wayside."You will clearly increase light products capacity, but you also at least maintain the heavy products," said Boston Consulting Group Vice-President Charbel Ackermann. "It's not
347 a substitution or reduction for heavy capacity."Oil sources said Russia's 28 major refineries had collectively put in 28 formal requests to international lenders and banks for loans for upgrades -- but money has not flowed in."Lots are talking about it, but few are actually doing it," said Bechtel International Inc.
347 Vice-President Robert Parker.In one of many plans dependent on full financing, Russia's Kirishi refinery has said it hopes Chevron will help install a $750 million hydrocracker.The Yaroslavl refinery, north of Moscow, is getting a $60 million catalytic cracking unit to boost gasoline output, while the Angarsk refinery in Siberia is
347 working with M. W. Kellogg on a $70 million plan for a fluid catalytic cracking unit.The Fuel and Energy Ministry said the Omsk refinery, in Siberia, would get a catalytic reforming plant by 2000, and that ABB Lummus Global was working on plans to help the Perm, Samara, Angarsk and
347 other refineries install catalytic crackers.Rif Usmanov, chief engineer at the Ufa refinery in southern Russia, said the plant's catalytic cracking facility, completed in March, would produce two million tonnes of gasoline and diesel a year (about 40,000 bpd).An engineer at the Ryazan refinery south of Moscow said revamping of a
347 catalytic cracking unit to raise capacity to 24,000 bpd would continue into 1997."A lot of projects are merely adjusting the heights of the columns and tinkering with other things," said energy specialist Peter Houlder at CentreInvest consultancy in Moscow. "But most of these are not $200-$300 million projects."Some question the
347 timing of the proposed upgrades, saying transport costs to Europe will squeeze margins too much."A lot of ambition is geared on the basis of exporting product to Europe, which I don't think is that logical," Parker said. "Continental Europe is surrounded by state-of-the-art, high-tech refineries and sophisticated distribution."But the economy
347 in Russia's Volga and Urals regions, where heavy industry is in steep decline, is not picking up quickly and may not be able to absorb new products output soon."With the domestic market's limited absorption capacity, you'll still see an inclination to export heavy," Ackermann said.</

355 bank.Consumer prices fell 0.2 percent in August, the first decline since Russia began its economic reforms in January 1992. Double-digit monthly inflation was common in the early years of the economic transformation.Those high inflation rates helped foster a mentality of non-payments as firms and individuals delayed paying bills because they
355 knew the value would go down month by month.The attitude still exists in the new, low-inflation Russia, where workers strike because they have not been paid for months and the government, itself a debtor to firms and regions, struggles to raise tax revenue.Economists say companies have money, but prefer to
355 use it on the high-yielding market for government securities than for mundane things like paying bills. 355 said Jochen Wermuth, head of the Finance Ministry's Economic Expert Group, referring to companies like Gazprom, which have traditionally been viewed as above the law."If there are no holy cows, revenues will come this autumn."He said officials were determined to get tough on companies which did not pay their bills.Finance

355 this week in Moscow and will report back to Washington in time for the IMF's early October annual meetings.Wermuth said tax collection, especially VAT collection, had been rising in August.He said new regulations that firms pay VAT and excise duties when they deliver goods should boost revenues further.Firms previously paid

369 waging rhetorical war when they breezed to victory in their respective fiefs in Saturday's elections, devised by the U.S. authors of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty to put Bosnia on track to gradual reunification.But despite the mutual loathing left over from 43 months of siege, slaughter and mass expulsions, these
369 elections are seen as less likely to spawn war, at least in the near term, for one crucial reason -- international engagement.In 1990-91, world powers were so preoccupied by the Gulf Crisis and the dissolution of the Soviet Union that they hardly noticed the disintegration of Yugoslavia's multi-national state and
369 society until it was too late.Today, however, there are NATO peacekeeping troops and an army of international peace agencies stationed in Bosnia to spur its factions into the kind of power-sharing arrangements they once discarded at such terrible cost.In 1990, three parties crystallised around the constituent nations of Bosnia --
369 Christian Orthodox Serbs, Roman Catholic Croats and Slav Moslems -- as Yugoslavia's communist system yielded to democratic pressures.Moslems founded the Party of Democratic Action (SDA) under Izetbegovic, a former prisoner of conscience under communism.The Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) formed as the Bosnian branch of Croatia's ruling national party. The Serb
369 Democratic Party (SDS) appeared as the sister of a party seeking statehood for rebel minority Serbs in Croatia.The SDA, HDZ and SDS coalesced for short-term political ends, upsetting a reform League of Communists bloc in the November 1990 elections.The victorious bloc formed a collective presidency of two members for each
369 community and one for everyone else.But the need for consensus rule had become a euphemism for political stalemate, as in the Yugoslav federal government after the death of strongman communist leader Josip Broz Tito in 1980.The SDS and, less openly, the HDZ, were fixated on one goal -- autonomy for
369 Bosnia's minority Serbs and Croats en route to union with "Mother Serbia" and "Mother Croatia".They wanted to pre-empt what they claimed would be tyranny exerted by the more numerous Moslems as the balancing framework of Yugoslav socialism crumbled in an explosion of long-repressed nationalist movements.The SDS emerged as little more
369 than the paramilitary vanguard for the president of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, in his campaign to group all Serbs scattered through then-Yugoslavia in one "Greater Serbia".In April 1991 the SDS declared an autonomous entity in north Bosnia where most Bosnian Serbs lived. 369 presidency and parliament.With the Milosevic-controlled Yugoslav federal army (JNA) arming a Bosnian Serb takeover of parts of Bosnia where defenceless Moslems and Croats also lived, the HDZ found temporary common cause with the SDA.The SDA and HDZ sponsored a referendum for the independence of Bosnia. Bosnian Moslems and Croats, almost
369 two-thirds of the 4.3 million population, voted yes, while Serbs boycotted.Serb forces, bristling with JNA weaponry, reacted by laying siege to Sarajevo, overrunning wide swathes of Bosnia and beginning a systematic expulsion of non-Serbs. The war began.At the end of 1992, the Croats dropped their political mask and declared a
369 sovereign entity in Croat-populated southwest Bosnia, driving out its Moslem minority.Bosnia is still at odds with itself today. 377 times this week in the "sarcophagus" covering the reactor. But independent experts say much higher rises - tens of thousands times the norm - would be needed to cause a new nuclear reaction. "This is a rather dangerous phenomenon which has been observed three times this year," Baryakhtar, President Leonid
377 Kuchma's top nuclear adviser, told Ukrinform."The main reason is leakage under the sarcophagus of rainwater, which speeds up neutrons. 377 for quicker action, with foreign support, in replacing the cracking steel and concrete structure hurriedly erected after the explosion and fire at Chernobyl in 1986.Ukraine's top negotiator on closing Chernobyl by the year 2000, Environment Minister Yuri Kostenko, initially suggested on Wednesday that the readings were caused by faulty equipment.

408 Valentin Tsvetanov said.The BCC manages state equity in domestic commercial banks.Only Bulbank, Bulgaria's most stable bank, will remain state-owned under the government's plans, he added."Bulbank is the only institution representing Bulgaria in the international financial community," Tsvetanov said.He declined to give further details on the sell-off plans but said they
408 included Balkanbank and Economic Bank, which were on an unofficial list of banks slated for closure or special supervision that has recently circulated in local media.The other five banks expected to be sold are Biohim Bank, Bulgarian Post Bank, Hebros Bank, Express Bank and United Bulgarian Bank.Economic Bank has the
408 largest share of debts to foreign creditors among the seven, amounting to around $150 million.The seven banks, several of which are suffering severe liquidity problems, were recapitalised three months ago with dollar-denominated government securities at a total cost of $400 million.All the banks had a negative capital to assets ratio
408 before the government conducted the recapitalisation operation, which was part of a funding agreement clinched with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in July.The banks' shares will not be offered publicly as the government is keen to attract strong foreign investors, Tsvetanov said."So far we have not discussed the possible sell-off
408 of Mineralbank," Tsvetanov added, referring to the state-owned institution that the central bank is currently trying to shut.The Sofia city court is expected to rule on the insolvency suit against Mineralbank on September 25.Commenting on the chances of selling state banks to serious foreign investors, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov earlier
408 on Thursday sounded a cautious note."Garbage should be thrown away, not sold," he told reporters.-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145</

412 If Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan loses his bid for re-election in Sunday's first round ballot, it will not be because voters didn't buy his pre- election promises.In fact, Ter-Petrosyan doesn't promise much of anything."The president doesn't believe in propaganda. 412 just because it might sound pretty," said Hamlet Gasparyan, his campaign press secretary.His main opponent, former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan, has pledged to raise living standards, but Ter-Petrosyan has told his countrymen to expect no miracles."There are people who are promising to make your lives better. If you believe them,
412 then please vote for them," he told one group of rural voters recently.The 50-year-old academic and former Soviet-era dissident, cuts an aloof image unusual for Caucasus leaders.Television in Azerbaijan is a daily soap opera of President Haydar Aliyev's activities, while Georgia's Eduard Shevardnadze keeps in touch with live weekly radio
412 interviews.But the wavy-haired, chain-smoking Ter-Petrosyan was never a member of the Soviet Communist Party. He rarely addresses the nation on television or radio. He has given one press conference in two years, and almost never agrees to press interviews."He is a man of science. He doesn't speak empty words. It
412 is just not his nature," said Tigran Mansuryan, a famous Armenian composer and a longtime Ter-Petrosyan confidante.Political scientist Suren Zolyan says Ter-Petrosyan came to prominence in Armenia largely on his strength as an orator."By keeping a cool distance, he portrays himself as above politics, as above party institutions. So although
412 he is the president, he thus creates an aura of a tsar or king who can't be blamed for problems and without whom Armenians cannot live."There is ample evidence the recipe works.Many of his rank-and-file backers seem more enamoured with his charisma than with his programme."I love him very much.
412 He is our president, he is a real man," said 26-year-old accountant Gazancha Goyan, who admitted she didn't know much about Ter-Petrosyan's politics.Ter-Petrosyan has survived five years in power despite an unresolved war with neighbour Azerbaijan and biting economic problems in the landlocked country which also borders Iran, Turkey and
412 Georgia.He is on his fourth prime minister over that time span. Three, including Manukyan, left office at least in part as scapegoats for one economic, political crisis or another.Manukyan has won popularity with an aggressive campaign which promises to relieve the poverty affecting most Armenians.Ter-Petrosyan has kept a low profile,
412 although worried advisers have stepped up his schedule in advance of the vote.But the enigma won out again at a big election rally in central Yerevan on Wednesday.Dancing girls performed and one ally after another stood on a lighted stage to sing his praises. His government members stood at attention,
412 applauding enthusiastically.But the president leaned passively up against a back wall and puffed on a cigarette, almost oblivious to the fanfare."Unfortunately I cannot see your faces in the glare of the lights, my friends, but please consider that I am speaking with each one of you as an individual," he

414 year.While traders say a return to such volumes is some way off, they forecast imports could begin recovering next year, as domestic confectionery manufacturers begin to boost output."This year, we are likely to buy the same amount of cocoa beans as last year, but we do not exclude that 1997
414 purchases could be larger," said a senior Babayevsky confectionery factory official, who declined to provide figures.An official from the State Statistics Committee said Russia imported 32,200 tonnes of cocoa beans in the first seven months of this year, a five percent rise from year-ago levels."Imports of cocoa beans could rise
414 next year, whereas purchases of Western-made output containing cocoa could fall," one Moscow-based trader said. 414 year. 414 is going well in Russia," said a Nestle's source in Moscow who declined to be named.Alexander Pavlov, head of the Food Industry Department at the Agriculture Ministry, said he expected output of domestic chocolates to rise by eight percent in 1997 due to confectionery plants' remodernisation plans and changing consumption
414 trends."Our chocolate wasn't considered bad in the past, before this massive influx of foreign sweets," Pavlov said."But Russia does not grow cocoa beans, and if there are plans to produce more Russian chocolate, then there must be higher cocoa imports."Imports of cocoa beans and derivatives by the Soviet Union, including
414 Russia, which accounted for 75 percent of the country's buying, varied from 150,000 to 180,000 tonnes a year before the country collapsed in 1991, traders say.The Nestle's source said one strong point at domestic sweets' makers was packaging chocolates in bright gift boxes for holidays."In fact, now there are big

416 ballot, but neither are expected to do well.Observers hold little faith in Armenian opinion polls. 416 a big surprise if Ter-Petrosyan didn't take it in the first round," said a Western diplomat.A second round between the top two candidates will be held in two weeks if no candidate wins 50 percent of the vote.Landlocked Armenia became a textbook case of chaos and misery when the Soviet
416 empire began to break up, going to war with neighboring Azerbaijan over the enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh and suffering near total economic collapse as Soviet-era trade ties collapsed and Azerbaijan closed the frontiers.But battlefield defeats in the enclave forced Azerbaijan to accept a ceasefire which has held for more than two
416 years, although there is no sign of a lasting solution to the conflict.Most of Armenia's 3.5 million people are still poor, but the economy has began to recover from a dismal base and a once-notorious power shortage has been somewhat alleviated.The wavy-haired Ter-Petrosyan, who disdains what his aides call "election
416 propaganda," has run a campaign which portrays him as a guarantor of peace and stability but emphasises the many difficult problems ahead."All of our economic and social problems are temporary and one day our nation will overcome them," he told a rally of 10,000 supporters in Yerevan's central square on
416 Wednesday evening. 416 and says it is impossible for anyone not directly linked to Ter-Petrosyan's "clan" to do serious business or invest in Armenia."Oh, you can open an ice cream parlour if you want, that they will tolerate," he said earlier this week. "But try anything bigger and immediately you will begin having
416 problems."Some 2.4 million people are elegible to vote on Sunday.
