426 Armenians often refer to their country as "our much-suffering land".A journey across the small, landlocked former Soviet republic from north to south leaves no doubt why.The winner of Sunday's presidential election faces the herculean task of ending a devastating war with neighbouring Azerbaijan and lifting most Armenians out of miserable
426 poverty.Four candidates are on the ballot, but only two, President Levon Ter-Petrosyan and former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan, have a real chance of victory."I don't know anything about politics, but I know that life here is bad. No money, no jobs," said 42-year old Ashot, manning a kebab stand along
426 a dusty road in the north of the country, just over the border from Georgia."At least I have the pigs," he says, pushing chunks of pink meat on to greasy metal skewers and placing them on a makeshift grill.Workers in state jobs often receive salaries of as little as 4,000
426 dram ($10) a month. The minimum pension is 2,000 dram.Ter-Petrosyan, a 50-year-old academic known for his aloof, intellectual approach to government, is regarded by political observers as the favourite to win a new five-year term.But he faces a stronger than expected challenge from Manukyan, who accuses him of running a
426 "mafia-clan type country" and promises to raise living standards quickly. Manukyan has won the backing of three other candidates who dropped out of the race."If the vote isn't falsified, then Ter-Petrosyan will lose in the first round," physicist Manukyan, 50, told Reuters in an interview at his campaign headquarters in
426 central Yerevan.He said it was impossible for anyone not directly linked to Ter-Petrosyan's "clan" to do serious business or invest in Armenia."You can open an ice cream parlour if you want, that they will tolerate," he said, puffing on a cigarette. "But start anything bigger and you will have problems
426 immediately."Ter-Petrosyan, who has dominated Armenia's political landscape since independence five years ago, has generally shrugged off Manukyan's broadsides as populist electioneering."Manukyan just tells people what they want to hear. The president does not believe in lying to people, so he tells them the truth -- that things will continue to
426 be difficult," said Hamlet Gasparyan, the president's campaign press secretary.Both will be trying to clear a 50 percent hurdle to claim a first-round win. If neither does, they will face a run-off.The drive towards the capital Yerevan, along desert roads bordered by parched mountains, is a trek through towns lined
426 with darkened, dilapidated buildings and dormant traffic lights.Armenia, with few domestic power resources, has suffered a chronic power shortage since the Soviet Union collapsed and other republics began charging hard currency for gas and oil. People are without electricity for days on end.One town on the road is Spitak, epicentre
426 of a giant earthquake in December 1988 which killed more than 25,000 people. Most were entombed in shoddily built high-rise apartment buildings that collapsed like packs of cards.Eight years on, new apartment blocks dot the town's skyline but the government has still been unable to build new housing for around
426 half of the survivors of the disaster. Weeds poke out from leftover rubble bulldozed into piles years ago.The Metsamor nuclear power plant, closed after the quake, is visible on the city skyline. Officials reopened it this year, saying they had no choice, given the desperate power situation.Cranes tower over the
426 capital Yerevan itself, but most of the giant arms have been motionless since Armenia was dumped into deep economic crisis by war with Azerbaijan for control of the Armenian-populated region of Nagorno-Karabakh.Armenians now control the enclave, which was part of Azerbaijan under borders drawn up in Soviet days.The result of
426 Sunday's election is far from clear.Khachik, a father of three hawking blocks of butter and bags of coffee in Yerevan's central bazaar, is characteristic of people who blame Ter-Petrosyan for the economic mess."I was a specialist in a jewellery factory here, and now I sell this junk to buy bread.
426 Look at this market. Lots of these people have higher education. Now we are a people with no future. If it isn't the president's fault, then whose is it?"Ter-Petrosyan can point to improving economic indicators as evidence that life is getting better.Inflation is under control and industrial production has been
426 rising for months, albeit from a low level.Yerevan is full of private shops and restaurants.But observers say the key to truly reviving the economy lies in ending the long-running conflict with Azerbaijan.The conflict was already under way over Nagorno-Karabakh in 1988 and the Christian Armenians achieved stunning victories against the
426 Moslem Azeris until a ceasefire came in 1994.The war has closed off traditional export and import routes through Azerbaijan and Turkey, which has supported its fellow Moslems by sealing the Turkish-Armenian border.Mediation and negotiations to find a lasting solution to the conflict have led to no concrete results.Azerbaijan says it
426 will use future revenues from huge new offshore oil projects to rearm and retake the territory unless a solution can be found to preserve its territorial integrity."This is without a doubt absolutely the most crucial problem facing the country. Without a real settlement to the war there is no way
426 to get the economy going," said one Western diplomat.Armenia's only open borders are through Georgia, whose infrastructure is in poor shape, and Iran."Unfortunately there is no way that we are going to see a resolution of Karabakh in the next year," the diplomat said. "In 18 months they may agree
426 some sort of framework, but the prognosis is not optimistic," he said.</
427 Beware of fire, flood and ill fortune in Romania, says the best local advice. Most probably you will not be insured against calamity.Romania is slowly dismantling its state insurance monopoly but it has built little by way of a commercial safety net for individuals and companies walking the tightrope of
427 risk.Under pressure to open up the financial industry to outsiders, the government has scrapped communist-era mandatory insurance cover for property and vehicle passengers.Car owners must choose third-party insurance themselves from October and state property cover mostly expires next year.That has cleared the way for more foreign competition and an explosion
427 in the domestic insurance industry -- but so far interest has been slight, leaving former state monopoly holders to prospect for most of the market."The market has great potential but is not exploited enough," said Emil Boldus, president of the National Union of Insurance and Reinsurance Companies (UNSAR). "We need
427 the financial strength and knowledge of big foreign companies."Business should boom in a country with 23 million people, rising car ownership and the continuing privatisation, albeit sluggish, of thousands of state companies. But without the appropriate legal architecture, growth is forecast as small.More than 40 insurers have opened over the
427 past six years, but few are solid enough to stand up to state-owned ASIROM, which controls more than half the business and held the monopoly on compulsory insurance.The overall insurance market remains thin, taking only some 0.4 percent of gross domestic product. Theft, pension, crop and health insurance are almost
427 entirely unavailable.With minimum equity requirements unchanged since 1991, the total capital of insurers operating in Romania was only 77 billion lei ($23.87 million) at the end of 1995."The present capital requirement is ridiculous. There are plenty of players on the market but most of them are undercapitalised," said Boldus.Anyone with
427 around $8,000 in his pocket can set up an insurer in Romania, said Boldus, adding that less than a third of local insurance companies had the 1.0 billion lei in capital that would take them close to minimum western standards."There are some 160 so-called brokers but I doubt more than
427 10 are what an insurance broker is supposed to be," he said.The insurance supervisory body OSAR acknowledges the need to raise present capital requirements by at least 10 times but says the move has to be stipulated by a new law."The insurance market will then crystallise, we will see mergers
427 and switches of activity. Only 10 or 15 companies will be left, but they will be solid," said Nicolae Crisan, head of OSAR.With companies aware of the scope for growth, competition is fierce, with some firms slashing premiums below profitable levels, compromising financial safety and risking the scandals that have
427 dogged other parts of the country's finance industry.Total premium incomes almost doubled to 290 billion lei last year from 164 billion in 1994, while profits of insurance companies rose to 51 billion lei from 48 billion."Most insurers just want more premiums and that's why they are low. Insurers don't really
427 care whether they can cover the risks they take," said Valentin Tuca, manager of Marsh &amp; McLennan's local branch.Analysts say few insurers put their gains into reserves and a lack of capital strength has forced most companies to seek reinsurance abroad, using up the bulk of collected premiums -- especially
427 from aviation and maritime policies.Aviation insurance premium incomes tripled to 9.6 billion lei last year but some 85 percent flew abroad for reinsurance.In a bid to reduce premium outflow the law asks Romanian insurers to seek cover among local players. Only if three refuse can insurers then resort to international
427 markets."What we need in this market is a (local) reinsurer," said Crisan.Some big international insurers have dipped their toes in the Romanian market.Italy's Assicurazioni Generali Spa and American International Group Inc operate joint ventures and market sources say ING Group, which has businesses across central Europe, will soon enter the
427 life insurance field.Income from life insurance rose to 31.5 billion lei last year, 67 percent up in real terms from 1994, but such policies take up only 11 percent of the market.Some analysts say major foreign involvement will only follow the privatisation of state giants ASIROM and ASTRA, underwriter of
427 hard currency policies, but the sale of such precious state assets will be a long time coming.Tougher supervision and a greater awareness of the need for insurance are also essential if the market is to take off."This market hasn't had to cope with big problems so far as the private
427 sector is still underdeveloped and major industrial risks still go uninsured," said Tuca.Industry experts say the insurance law should be amended to give the OSAR the right to influence premiums and to counter potential dumping practices by large companies.Analysts say most state company managers have failed to grasp the importance
427 of insurance."No one has made them take such policies in the past. And their managers now bear no responsibility in case of accidents if they haven't thought to cover the risks," one source said. ($1=3226 Lei)</
428 Venezuela's former President Carlos Andres Perez tasted his first day of freedom in over two years on Thursday relishing the return to the public limelight.Drummed out of office in May 1993 to face corruption charges shortly before the end of a second five-year presidential term, the charismatic Perez gave early
428 warning that he intended to make the most of his new-found freedom."I am not going to be written off or buried. I am not going to become one of those library books which are taken out occasionally to be consulted," he told a news conference.The first Latin American leader to
428 be convicted of corruption, Perez maintained that the charge that he misappropriated $17 million in state funds was politically motivated.But he said he would waste no time dwelling on the past. "I don't have any intention to seek revenge ... my conscience is clear," he said.Hundreds of cheering supporters swamped
428 the Social Democratic leader early on Thursday morning when he stepped from the luxurious colonial residence that had been his jail since July 1994. He previously spent two months in a prison.Perez had breakfast with Central American leaders, including former Honduran President Rafael Callejas, and visited the grave of his
428 daughter, Tais, who died while he was under house arrest.Perez, 73, whose second government was rocked by price riots and two military coup attempts, heads to his home state of Tachira on Friday to "renew my contact with the people."An apparently unquenchable thirst for publicity saw Venezuela's most famous ex-convict
428 give at least 60 interviews on Wednesday. Even during the relative seclusion of house arrest Perez maintained a high public profile through regular press interviews and, more recently, chats on the Internet.But his plans to renew his international profile were put on ice by Attorney General Ivan Dario Badell, who
428 said he would seek to have him barred from leaving Venezuela while investigations go on into alleged joint foreign bank accounts with close friend Cecilia Matos.In a political career spanning five decades, Perez was no stranger to controversy and he still provokes polarised reactions among Venezuelans.But while his every move
428 on Thursday was accompanied by a small band of fervent supporters, most bystanders appeared unmoved by his return to the limelight."He just likes the publicity. It's a show, that's all," said security guard Hernan Guzman as he watched Perez's supporters cheer their leader.</

430 Former President Carlos Andres Perez, Venezuela's most controversial politician, completed two years of house arrest on Thursday and received a jubilant welcome by hundreds of supporters outside his Caracas home.Drummed out of office in May 1993 to face corruption charges for misuse of public funds shortly before completing a second
430 five-year presidential term, the flamboyant and charismatic Perez said he planned a quick return to public life."I feel happy among this crowd that shows how Venezuelans feel", he told hundreds of friends and cheering supporters at the gate of the luxury colonial residence above the capital which had been his
430 jail since July 1994. He had previously spent two months at the Caracas low security Junquito prison."I'm back on the streets and that's on the streets that we shall seek peace for Venezuela and solutions to the country's woes", the 73-year-old social democrat leader said.The first Latin American leader to
430 be convicted of corruption, Perez has maintained that he was wrongly convicted for misappropriating $17 million in state funds.The first Venezuelan to win two presidential elections, Perez has survived jail, exile and two coup attempts during a political career spanning five decades. No stranger to controversy, Perez provokes polarised reactions
430 from Venezuelans.An oil boom during his first government from 1974-79 brought unprecedented wealth to the South American country and raised his international profile as a champion of Third World interests. But his dramatic fall from grace left his reputation in tatters.Perez's first taste of freedom, officially set to begin at
430 midnight, was brief and chaotic as he was literally swept out by a tide of supporters and journalists surrounding him.He only took two paces from his front gate and though obviously determined to explore his new-found freedom was turned back by the sheer weight of the crowd estimated at nearly
430 1,000."Out of the way, let me get out," he shouted, as photographers and TV cameramen jostled for the best spot.His appearance was greeted with spontaneous renditions of the national anthem and cries of "freedom, freedom".Supporter Armando Medina, who travelled nearly seven hours from the central city of Barquisimeto to witness
430 Perez's return to freedom, said he was convinced the former leader would quickly spring back onto the political arena."This is only the beginning, this man is not going to stay idle", he said.Perez's path to political redemption will start on Friday with a tour of western Venezuela, beginning with his
430 home state of Tachira on the Colombian border, where he still commands considerable support.</

437 With an estimated 80 to 90 percent of Brazil's 1995/96 soybean crop sold, the trade has now begun in earnest to make advance sales of its 1996/97 crop, so-called green soybeans, traders and brokers said."We reckon 20 percent of the coming harvest has already been sold," said one leading Parana
437 state based broker. "Most cooperatives and traders are now making green soybean sales."A leading Rio Grande do Sul broker said he was recommending clients to sell some of the crop, either for the domestic or export market, because the price is so good. "The price is really fantastic," he said.
437 "If we'd have had these prices three to four years ago people would have gone crazy with advance crop sales.""The current problem is lack of available funds in the market, especially among export customers," he said.Green soybean sales, traditionally popular in Brazil, but which lack any guarantee, fell out of
437 favor over the last two years due to farmers' debt problems, which led to cases of non-delivery of the soybeans to contracted customers. For the coming soybean season, however, most farmers are in a far improved situation due to the government's drawing up of debt securitisation programmes with producers, and
437 this year's long run of favorable domestic and international prices.The national soybean price, a composite average, was quoted at $17.06 a 60-kilo bag on September 19, some $3 above the price of just one month previously.Prices at Rio Grande port for sale delivered to crushers reached 19.20 reais ($19) this
437 week, dipping slightly at the week's end to 18.80 reais ($18.61), said broker Brasoja. At Paranagua port Alianca Corretora reported sales of soybean delivered to crushers at 18.50 reais ($18.31) per 60-kilo bag on September 19, while green soybeans were fetching 16.50 reais ($16.34) for April 1997 delivery.Traders and brokers
437 estimated Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop may be up to 15 percent bigger than this year's, reaching some 27 million tonnes, giving plenty of scope for producers wishing to sell green soybeans.Planting is expected to begin during October. The numbers of soybean futures contracts traded on Sao Paulo's futures exchange Bolsa
437 de Mercadorias e de Futuros (BM&amp;F) has meanwhile grown relatively slowly since the contract's launch in late 1995.In the month of August 1996, 2,042 soybean futures contracts were traded on the BM&amp;F, worth 13.4 million reais ($13.27 million), an exchange spokesman said.Trade sources said they feel the Brazilian soybean market
437 is not sufficiently large to support a full-level futures market. "The trade is worried price distortions could arise between the futures market and the cash market, especially as liquidation in the futures contract is via a cash index rather than product," one broker said."That's why the trade prefers green soybean
437 sales, even despite the lack of guarantees," he said.For what remains of Brazil's 1995/96 crop, traders and brokers described the Brazilian market as continuing nervously quiet in view of the soycomplex price fluctuations in Chicago.Only isolated sales are now taking place from the current year's crop, they said.This follows a
437 flurry of activity earlier in the week immediately following the government's elimination of the state-level ICMS tax on exports and interstate sales of soycomplex products, they said. -- Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151</
438 Argentina's biggest union group, the Central Labor Confederation (CGT), said Thursday its 36-hour general strike on September 26-27 would go ahead as planned.CGT Secretary-General Rodolfo Daer, who will lead a march on President Carlos Menem's Casa Rosada government house in Buenos Aires, vowed that workers would "take the Plaza de
438 Mayo by storm," referring to the landmark plaza where the planned demonstration will take place. The CGT, in the past an ally of the Peronist government, is staging its second general strike in two months to protest the country's 17 percent unemployment rate, government austerity measures and Menem's attempts to
438 make labor laws more flexible.In a speech to regional unionists, Daer said workers would "no longer put up with austerity for austerity's sake.""There are starvation pensions, poverty-line salaries and no stability or security for workers," said the new CGT chief. Menem's labor bill, which is expected to be sent to
438 Congress this week, proposes scrapping collective pay deals and swapping redundancy payments for an unemployment insurance scheme with employer contributions. Menem threatens to push it through by decree if Congress puts up a fight.The union protests escalated this week after Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said he wanted pay deals
438 to make a proportion of workers' wages variable, "taking into account the economic conditions of each company."The minister said Thursday he would also like the bill to include modifications in working hours and vacations. 446 had matured and would start looking at anti-trust cases with more emphasis on international law and with greater complexity. 446 buyout, but set conditions to stop Colgate snapping up a 77 percent share of the Brazilian toothpaste market overnight.Colgate must either refrain from selling the Kolynos toothpaste brand in Brazil for four years, licence it to a third party over a 20-year period, or sell the brand to a competitor
446 with a less than one percent market share. "The ruling represents a change in Cade in that we no longer want to adopt a simplistic position of yes or no," Silva said. She said the decision was taken in close consultation with international anti-cartel norms and with the U.S. Department
446 of Commerce."We are on the path to becoming civilized," she said.The ruling was welcomed by the U.S. personal hygiene giant, which purchased Anakol in 1995. The Brazilian operation accounts for $760 million of the total buyout and the Kolynos brand, with a 50 percent market share in Brazil, is the
446 icing on the cake. 446 were distributed in Brazil, said Colgate would reply to Cade within the 30-day limit and was hopeful about satisfying Cade's conditions. 446 region and also other emerging markets."The decision does not affect any other plans of the company," she said.Silva noted that the buyout not only gave Colgate a 77 percent share of the Brazilian toothpaste market, but also 75 percent of all of Mercosur, grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. 446 the biggest market of the four, the ruling in Brazil would naturally have an impact on Colgate's activities in the other countries, she said.Cade has come under the spotlight in recent months with rumoured attempts by the government to exert greater influence on its rulings. 446 was wholly independent.-- Brasilia newsroom 55-61-2230358</
447 Honduras on Thursday launched an ambitious development plan that would require $18 billion in investment.Among the proposals is a "dry canal" to link container ship ports on the Atlantic and Pacific with a high-speed rail. Similar plans also are being discussed in Nicaragua, Mexico and Colombia.President Carlos Roberto Reina on
447 Thursday signed an executive agreemment authorizing a local foundation to begin studies and seek financing for the projects. One potential source of financing is the Interamerican Development Bank, which would be willing to provide credit to private developers, bank representative Federico Alvarez said at a ceremony announcing the plans.The so-called
447 Great National Transformation Project, proposed by the local private sector, was described by President Reina as something that "cannot be postponed in order to promote development and fight poverty." The plan calls for projects to be developed by the private sector, both local and international, while the government creates the
447 macroeconomic, fiscal and legal incentives to attract capital. Apart from the dry canal, proposals include a huge tourist, commercial and industrial zone at Trujillo and Castilla on the Atlantic Coast to be built over the next 10 years. The foundation would promote the construction of highways and airports throughout the
447 country.Among the proposals is to use the U.S. Army base at Palmerola in the center of the country, currently home to 500 U.S. troops, as a private air terminal. Other concessions under the plan include two large hydroelectric plants, an African palm cultivation project, new banana plantations, mine exploration and
447 reforestation to boost the timber industry. Corporate taxes would be lowered and import and export taxes eliminated. The Honduran constitution would be reformed to expand land-ownership rights for foreigners and privatize the pension system.Miguel Facusse, a Honduran investor and major backer of the project, said at the unveiling ceremony that
447 the plan could be executed in two phases over the next 10 years, with the first phase costing $6 billion and the second $12 billion."We're talking about a substantial change of economic and social strategy aimed at stopping poverty," Facusse said.-- Gustavo Palencia, Tegucigalpa bureau, (504) 39 28 85</

450 The Mexican Senate on Thursday unanimously approved a so-called "antidote" to the U.S. anti-Cuba law known as Helms-Burton, a Senate spokesman said."It was approved unanimously, everyone voted in favour," Senate spokesman Ernesto Martinez said, referring to a Senate vote of 118-to-0. "It was just sent to the Chamber of Deputies
450 (lower house)."The antidote law would fine Mexican companies that allow themselves to be sanctioned by the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which seeks to discourage investment in Cuba, a Senate bulletin said.Mexico, along with other U.S. allies like Canada and the European Union, have condemned Helms-Burton as a violation of international law
450 because it seeks to punish third countries for investing in the Communist-ruled island.Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday he expected a retaliatory bill introduced on Monday against the Helms-Burton law to pass quickly, but he hoped the bill would never be needed."These are ugly measures," Eggleton told
450 reporters at a meeting. "I hope we will never be implementing it. It's an antidote legislation."His bill would let Canadians countersue in Canadian courts to recover damages awarded by U.S. courts under Helms-Burton. It would also allow Canada to issue "blocking" orders declaring that judgments handed down under any objectionable
450 foreign law would not be enforced in Canada.Helms-Burton allows U.S. firms to sue foreign companies that "traffic" in properties that were confiscated by Cuba after Fidel Castro came to power 37 years ago. U.S. officials say there are only a handful of companies worldwide in that category.The Mexican consortium Grupo
450 Domos, which plans to operate telephone service in Cuba, has been identified as one of those companies.Mexico is particularly sensitive to any perception that the United States is meddling in the affairs of its Latin American neighbours.According to modifications in the antidote law made by the Mexican Senate on Wednesday,
450 Mexican companies would be fined the equivalent of 100,000 days of the minimum wage for submitting to any sanctions from foreign countries, or about $300,000 at present.The proposed Mexican law applies to any foreign country but was written in direct response to the United States and its Helms-Burton law.Mexican companies
450 would be fined about $150,000 for providing information about themselves to U.S. courts in cases related to Helms-Burton.They would be fined about $3,000 for failing to inform the Mexican foreign ministry that they are being targeted for sanctions by the U.S. law.</

499 The Mexican Senate on Thursday is expected to approve a so-called "antidote" to the U.S. anti-Cuba law known as Helms-Burton, a Senate spokesman said on Thursday."It will be discussed today and it is expected that the law will be approved and sent to the Chamber of Deputies (the lower house),"
499 Senate spokesman Victor Hugo Figueroa told Reuters. The antidote law would fine Mexican companies that allow themselves to be sanctioned by the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which seeks to discourage investment in Cuba, a Senate bulletin said.Mexico, along with other U.S. allies like Canada and the European Union, have condemned Helms-Burton
499 as a violation of international law because it seeks to punish third countries for investing in the Communist-ruled island. Helms-Burton allows U.S. firms to sue foreign companies that "traffic" in properties that were confiscated by Cuba after Fidel Castro came to power 37 years ago. U.S. officials say there are
499 only a handful of companies worldwide in that category.The Mexican consortium Grupo Domos, which plans to operate telephone service in Cuba, has been identified as one of those companies. According to modifications in the antidote law made by the Mexican Senate on Wednesday, Mexican companies would be fined the equivalent
499 of 100,000 days of the minimum wage for submitting to any sanctions from foreign countries.At the current minimum wage of 22.60 pesos per day, that fine would be 2.26 million pesos, about $300,000.The proposed Mexican law applies to any foreign countries but was written in direct response to the United
499 States and its Helms-Burton law. Mexican companies would be fined 50,000 days of minimum wage (1.13 milion pesos, about $150,000) for providing information about themselves to U.S. courts in cases related to Helms-Burton.They would be fined 1,000 days of minimum wage (226,000 pesos, about $3,000) for failing to inform the
499 Mexican foreign ministry that they are being targeted for sanctions by the U.S. law.-- Dan Trotta, Mexico City newsroom, (525) 728-9507</

505 Mexico's infrastructure development bank, Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Publicos (Banobras), plans to make a rare incursion into the international capital markets with a U.S. dollar five- to seven-year bond worth about $250 million, officials said."We are planning to launch another bond issue in the forthcoming weeks," assistant director
505 Carlos Sotomayor told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.The bank sees a spread of about 350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, he said, with Morgan Stanley as lead manager. The government development bank has only gone to the global markets twice in the 1990s, placing five-year bonds both times.The first
505 time was a $100 million Eurobond issue in 1991 that came due in August this year. The second time was another $100 million issue in 1993 that matures in October 1998."The objective of Banobras is that we do not want to just refinance the bond issue that matured in August,
505 nor to pay off the one that matures in 1998," said Sotomayor, assistant director for international operations. "What we plan to do is have a funding structure in place for the long-run." The bank expects to be busy in the markets next year as well, going to the markets to
505 place medium-term notes, officials said.Much of the bank's activity is acting as an agent of the federal government, negotiating and channeling funds from organizations such as the Inter-American Development Bank and the World Bank to infrastructure projects in Mexico.The bank is known for extending long-term credits for infrastructure projects, especially
505 to state and municipal governments. Banobras also takes on the risk in a percentage of the projects.Many development projects were put on hold during the turnover of the federal administration in 1994, hurting Mexico's infrastructure sector even before the recent downturn of the economy."The bank's growth was halted for a
505 year and half and now the bank has several projects that we would like to launch, so the bank has a plan to overhaul its funding strategy," Sotomayor said. Banobras arranges its funding in the dollar sector and in the peso sector."We do not have a primary deposit base of
505 funds. Our main reserves come from the capital markets and money markets," he said.The development bank hopes to extend the terms of its placements and sees the new private pension funds scheduled to come into force next year, known as Afores, as an aid in placing its peso-denominated paper. The
505 longest term for its peso paper is three years, with the bulk in the short end of the curve from one to six months."But with the measures that the Mexico government has taken, we are very bullish that in the near future we will see extended tenors, and we could
505 go with tenors of five to even seven years in pesos," said Sotomayor."One main factor will be the Afores. It is a natural market for Banobras to fund itself in pesos," he added.When asked if the market would be ready to accept seven-year peso-denominated paper, Sotomayor said, "I think we
505 could even go longer. As time goes on, I think that Banobras will be able to raise funds in longer tenors."-- Mexico City newsroom 525 728 9559E-mail at robert.kozak@reuters.com</

530 government officials and 11 top businessmen, made no statement to waiting reporters.As his plane was approaching Mexico, a passenger jet of German airline Lufthansa had to return to Mexico City after authorities received a bomb threat, an airport official said.No bomb was found after the plane made a safe landing,
530 the official told Reuters. There was no indication of who had made the threat, although the government has attributed a spate of bomb threats in several cities in recent weeks to the leftist rebel Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR).The EPR denies making the threats and says they are part of a
530 government disinformation campaign against them.Kohl was due to meet President Ernesto Zedillo on Thursday and to receive the keys of Mexico City from Mayor Oscar Villareal before visiting on Friday the central city of Puebla, where German auto firm Volkswagen has a large production plant and will make its new
530 Beetle car.Kohl was then scheduled to travel to the eastern Yucatan peninsula to visit the city of Merida, Maya ruins at Chichen Itza and the holiday resort of Cancun before leaving Mexico on Saturday.High on Kohl's agenda was the issue of free trade talks due to begin in October between
530 Mexico and the European Union, which Mexican officials hope will allow their country to diversify its trade links, now heavily weighted towards the United States."Germany has been an important motor for seeking the accord with the European Union," Mexico's deputy Foreign Minister Juan Rebolledo said earlier on Wednesday.Bilateral trade between
530 the two countries in 1995 was $3.2 billion, making Germany Mexico's biggest EU trading partner, although Mexico is keen to reduce its trade deficit of almost $2.2 billion with Germany.Despite the Mexican peso crisis of late 1994 and ensuing deep recession, German investment in Mexico last year rose to $3.15
530 billion from $2.61 billion in 1994."For us it is not only important that the established companies have expansion plans, but also to attract new companies," Rebolledo said.</

533 Former Venezuelan President Carlos Andres Perez walked free on Thursday from his Caracas home after more than two years under house arrest.Forced out of office in May 1993 to face corruption charges eight months short of completing a second five-year presidential term, the flamboyant Perez said he planned a quick
533 return to public life."I am happy", he told hundreds of friends and cheering supporters on the doorstep of the luxury colonial residence above the capital which had been his jail since July 1994. He had previously spent two months at the Caracas low security Junquito prison."I'm back on the streets
533 and that's on the streets that we shall seek peace for Venezuela and solutions to the country's woes", he added.The first Latin American leader to be convicted of corruption, Perez has maintained that he was wrongly convicted for misappropriating $17 million in state funds.A 73-year-old social democrat and the first
533 Venezuelan to win two presidential elections, Perez has survived jail, exile and two coup attempts during a controversial political career spanning five decades.</
534 Three multinational logging companies from Asia have moved into the Brazilian Amazon, raising fears that the already growing rate of deforestation in the planet's largest rainforest may be about to speed up.Malaysia's WTK Group, one of the world's biggest timber firms, is completing its purchase of 741,300 acres (300,000 hectares)
534 of forest up the remote, winding Tapua River, seven days by boat from the city of Manaus. An official said the firm was also doubling capacity at a Manaus sawmill it owns."We are very hurt by the criticism. We haven't cut down a single tree yet," said WTK representative Tu
534 Twang Hing in response to claims that his and other Asian firms plan to log on a scale not yet seen in Brazil.Environmentalists say the arrival of the multinationals, combined with government plans to pave a highway to Venezuela to bring goods to the Caribbean and overseas markets, shows development
534 of the Amazon is shifting into top gear."This is test of the government," said Carlos Miller of the environment group Vitoria Amazonica. "Brazil must advance with sustainable development and strengthen its regulatory ability."Logging is a major force driving destruction of the Amazon. Eleven percent of Brazil's Western Europe-sized chunk of
534 the forest has been cleared and the rate is speeding up. During 1994, 5,750 square miles (14,896 square km) were cut down, up from 4,298 square miles (11,130 square km) in 1991.The government's Environmental Institute (Ibama) admits its efforts to control the notoriously negligent local timber industry have been flawed.
534 A recent survey of 34 logging sites in Paragominas, the Amazon's biggest timber center, found that not one met requirements of the International Tropical Timber Organization, to which Brazil has agreed to comply by 2000.A swoop this year by Ibama found 31,000 cubic metres (1.095 million cubic feet) of illegally
534 felled timber floating down the Purus River towards waiting sawmills."Multi-million-dollar investments in the Amazonian logging industry would spell disaster as things stand," Ibama chief Eduardo Martins said. "We don't want that kind of invesment."Martins said that as well as WTK, Samling Corporation also of Malaysia, and Fortune Timber, owned by
534 the Chinese government and Hong Kong investors, have bought bankrupt local companies. Other deals have been stalled when the would-be buyers discovered they were being offered Indian lands.An Ibama document put at 11.1 million acres (4.5 million hectares) the amount of Amazon land now owned by the multinationals and said
534 the Asians' upgrading of local sawmills would lead to a five-fold jump in timber felled to produce plywood."We're extremely worried because (the Asians) work with very powerful technology," Miller of Vitoria Amazonica said.WTK and Samling have logged massively in Malaysia's Sarawak region where critics say massive ecological damage has been
534 inflicted on tropical forests. Both have concessions across the Far East. But, as Asian governments tighten their forestry laws and local forest resources dwindle, the multinationals have inevitably turned to the Amazon rainforest, which is estimated to hold a third of the world's tropical timber but accounts for only two
534 percent of the international tropical timber trade.The World Resources Institute, a New York policy research center, warned in 1995 that concessions offered to Asian loggers in Surinam, on Brazil's northern border, meant between 25 and 40 percent of that nation's land could be logged. The report said Surinam risked losing
534 "its forests and getting shattered biodiversity, ruined fisheries, eroded soil, displaced populations and perhaps ethnic strife in return."Richard Bruce, a forest economist hired by WTK to draw up its application to log Jurua, argued the levels of concern caused in Brazil over the arrival of the Asian logging firms might
534 lead to improvement in enforcement of forestry rules. "You'd be crazy to think we won't have government inspectors all over us after all the uproar," he said.And that is precisely what the government intends to do, Martins of Ibama said. Every existing logging permit-holder in the Amazon region is being
534 checked to see if their timber really does come from areas authorized for logging and not from protected Indian lands. So far, 80 percent of permits have been found to be "irregular."Martins pledged that timber produced by the Asians would be inspected. He also said stricter new laws on forest
534 clearing, combined with a two-year ban on new projects to fell rare mahogany and virola trees, would slow deforestation.But environmentalists said they were waiting to see if the government lives up to its promises to get tough with loggers."The problem is a lack of enforcement," said Garo Batmanian, head of
534 the World Wildlife Fund in Brazil. "Just changing the law without a systematic and comprehensive strategy will simply not work."</

546 Shell Australia Ltd said it wants to integrate the huge North West Shelf and Gorgon gas projects off northwest Australia and that talks with its partners would soon enter a "constructive" phase.Shell, a part owner in each project, dismissed as absurd the option of developing Gorgon as a stand-alone project
546 with its own greenfield liquified natural gas (LNG) plant, and said it was working to jointly develop Gorgon and the North West Shelf. "It's been our contrivance for the last year to bring it (Gorgon) in," Shell Australia chief executive Roland Williams told Reuters in an interview late on Thursday
546 night."I believe we can look for quite constructive discussions on this now." Williams did not give a timetable for a decision."Everybody wants to do the right thing. We have got to try and understand each other," he said.Shell owns a sixth of the North West Shelf project, which has a
546 total production capacity of 7.5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) through its LNG plant on the Burrup Pensinsula. The other partners are The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the MiMi consortium, Chevron Corp, British Petroleum Co and Woodside Petroleum.Shell also owns two-sevenths of the nearby Gorgon gas field, which has
546 the capacity to produce 6 MTPA but is still subject to feasibility studies. The other partners are Chevron, Texaco Inc and Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd.Shell and other main players in the two projects are under pressure from the Western Australia state government to decide soon on the future development
546 of the state's LNG industry. "There's no question we must expand," Williams said, adding that he and the visiting chairman of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group's committee of managing directors, Cor Herkstroter, spoke to Western Australia premier Richard Court in Perth this week."The Japanese market want that capacity and we have
546 a wonderful position there, so Shell is absolutely 110 percent behind the need to expand capacity in Western Australia," he said. But, Williams added, "It is frankly absurd in building another LNG plant on the north sea front of Western Australia." "Our attitude to Gorgon is very straight forward. For
546 God's sake don't go and waste the money building another grass-roots plant in Western Australia. We've got one of the best in the world at the Burrup Pensinsula," he said."You can pipe all the gas in there."Japanese gas and power utilities take the bulk of North West Shelf LNG and
546 have agreed to buy an additional 6.8 MTPA from next decade, paving the way for a A$5 billion expansion of the North West Shelf project to double capacity at the Burrup plant.The extra capacity would start to come on stream in 2003 and reach around 14.7 mtpa two years later,
546 Williams said. The North West Shelf and Gorgon partners should optimise the resources, developing the lowest-cost reserves first, he said."On the Burrup Pensinsula we have world's nicest LNG plant and offshore we have wave after wave of gas. We can produce gas from there I think till the end of
546 the next century."What you do is to optimise your up-front economics," Williams said. "You take obviously the cheapest gas to liquify earliest, because if you are going to put in A$5 billion into an investment, you are looking for the best cash flow in the first year of operation. Gorgon
546 will go into there, and we are very happy to cooperate on that...." The MiMi partner in the North West Shelf project is a 50-50 joint venture between Mitsui &amp; Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp.-- Melbourne Bureau 613-9286-1421</

549 Three earthquakes jolted New Zealand's lower North and upper South Islands overnight but there were no reports of damage, seismologists said on Friday.The biggest was a moderate quake of 5.6 on the Richter scale near the South Island spa town of Hanmer -- just 20 km (12 miles) from where

571 Sumitomo Corp said on Thursday that losses from a massive copper trading scandal have soared to $2.6 billion from the $1.8 billion it originally estimated and said it is pressing authorities for criminal charges against the man it holds responsible.The statement came in a revision of the trading group's earnings
571 forecast. The company said it revised its group net forecast for 1996/97 to show a loss of 147 billion yen ($1.34 billion) from a profit of 24 billion yen ($220 million).The trade house announced on June 13 that it had suffered huge losses from unauthorised copper trades and blamed the
571 long-time head of its copper trading division Yasuo Hamanaka, whom it promptly fired.The company said on Thursday it planned no further changes to the copper loss estimate and said it had closed out most of the loss-making copper positions."As a result of our liquidation up to now, there still remain
571 some positions, including both short and long positions, but the liquidation of uncovered positions is nearly complete," Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara told a news conference."Accordingly, there is almost no risk remaining and it is our judgment that we will not again revise the estimated loss we have announced today," he
571 added.Traders and financial analysts had questioned Sumitomo's previous loss estimate, saying it appeared to be much too low given the company's huge exposure in the market and a sharp fall in copper prices since the scandal broke.Sumitomo said Hamanaka had for more than a decade deceived the company, his losses
571 snowballing more than 40-fold as he tried to cover an initial 6.5 billion yen off-the-books loss with more secret trades. At the current exchange rate of 109 yen to the dollar, that would be $59.6 million.Miyahara said Hamanaka conducted as many as 2,000 unauthorised deals in a single year and
571 forged or doctored documents to cover his tracks, according to an in-house investigation by a 60-strong task force that was still sifting through 2,000 cardboard boxes full of documents.He declined to comment on whether Hamanaka had cooperated with the company's investigation.Investigators from Britain and the United States are also looking
571 into the affair, the biggest financial scandal in history.In Washington, congressional hearings into the affair opened on Wednesday. An official with the U.S. Federal Reserve said the crisis appeared to be confined to Sumitomo and had not spread to any other financial firms.Japanese authorities, meanwhile, have been reluctant to step
571 into the case, arguing that since all of the questionable trades took place overseas, there would have been no violation of Japanese law.Sources said recently that a criminal investigation has been launched into whether Hamanaka broke any laws by defrauding the company.But some of those allegedly linked to his trades
571 say the accounts in question were fully authorised by senior Sumitomo officials."What we want to prove most at the moment is that the company was not involved with Hamanaka's unauthorised copper trading," Miyahara said.Hamanaka, a 26-year veteran of Sumitomo, has kept largely silent about his activities since his dismissal, staying
571 at his modest suburban house near Tokyo and saying only that he would give his side of the story at a later date.</

622 Britain and China buried a festering four-year dispute over Hong Kong on Thursday, signalling an eagerly awaited thaw in their frosty relationship in the countdown to the handover of the colony next year.British and Chinese diplomats told reporters at the conclusion of three days of negotiations in Beijing that agreement
622 had been reached over a container terminal delayed since 1992 by bickering over the terms of the contract.Signs that the two sovereign states were finally putting their differences behind them were sure to be greeted with relief in Hong Kong, which has been forced to watch from the sidelines as
622 its future is determined in far-away capitals.British negotiators said no accord had been concluded on another high profile issue -- arrangements for the ceremonial handover of Hong Kong -- but team leader Hugh Davies expressed cautious optimism that it was only a matter of time.Asked by reporters whether he thought
622 remaining differences over a Sino-British ceremony could be reached next week, Davies said: "I am cautiously optimistic an agreement can be achieved."Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen and his British counterpart, Malcolm Rifkind, were scheduled to meet in New York next week.In 285 day's time -- at midnight on June 30,
622 1997 -- Britain is to return its colony to China under the terms of a treaty reached by London and Beijing in 1984 without reference to Hong Kong's six million people.The ensuring 12 years of transition have been turbulent ones for Hong Kong with Britain and China frequently at loggerheads
622 to the dismay of the tiny but wealthy community.The dispute over a ninth terminal for Hong Kong's container port, the world's busiest and a source of pride in the economically vibrant colony, flared when China objected to the award of the contract by private treaty rather than tender.More ominously for
622 Hong Kong's sophisticated business sector were Beijing's political objections to the inclusion of Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd in the consortium.Beijing accused the Hong Kong government of rewarding Jardine, a pillar of the British establishment since the colony was founded, for supporting Governor Chris Patten's electoral reforms, the object of bitter
622 Chinese opposition.Patten's reforms, announced shortly after his arrival in 1992 as Hong Kong's 28th and last governor, caused an already cool relationship to deteriorate dramatically.But the container terminal settlement, aided by Jardine agreeing to give up its role as consortium leader, will be regarded as the latest in a series
622 of signals suggesting that China is seeking cooperation rather than confrontation.Beijing's hardline stance is perceived to have eased in recent weeks, beginning with Foreign Minister Qian's surprise announcement last month that China was prepared to tolerate dissenting views within the Selection Committee being formed to choose Hong Kong's future leaders.The
622 signs of a more moderate line were reinforced when China said it was willing to consider a dialogue with Hong Kong's Democratic Party, which Beijing has cold-shouldered.In what was regarded as the final clincher, the Chinese official in charge of Hong Kong affairs said publicly he would be willing to
622 shake Patten's hand at the handover.The official, Lu Ping, had pointedly snubbed Patten, whom China has dubbed a criminal for ten thousand years and a political prostitute, for sponsoring the democratic reform.</

623 said, adding each naval vessel on coastal patrol watches over a sea block almost 300 miles (482 km) long and 200 miles (321 km) wide."North Korea's situation is similar to ours," he said, noting North Korea has about 760 combat and support ships and some 90 submarines, including 50 midget-class
623 submarines.Wednesday's infiltration was made easier by the removal of barbed wires barricades along the coast designed to keep out North Korean frogmen."The majority of our ground forces are deployed in the frontline," an army officer said. 623 forces. 632 fast-growing economy in recent years, investors frequently complain about red tape and an inadequate legal and regulatory framework.A draft of the amendments, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, showed that under new regulations the government would be required to issue investment licenses and decisions within two months from
632 the date of application instead of three months.The draft listed several areas where foreign investment would be encouraged, those where it was to be prohibited and those where 100 percent foreign-owned enterprises would be banned.Telecoms, insurance, auditing and electricity generation and distribution were included in the last of the three
632 categories.Foreign investment in exploitation of forest products, wood processing, broadcasting, television and cinematography would be banned.</

652 Taiwan said on Thursday it would open its door wider to businessmen from China despite Taipei's official attempts to cool local firms' fever to invest in the mainland.The economics ministry issued a statement saying it had decided to ease rules to allow visits by China businessmen.Current rules allow senior executives
652 and technical staff from mainland companies to apply to visit Taiwan for business purposes for a month, with the option to extend the visit for a second month.The relaxed rule will allow middle-level executives and technical staff to visit for business functions or training.They will be eligible to stay in
652 Taiwan for one month to visit or attend meetings, or for three months for training. Extensions under these terms are not allowed.The move is expected to expand economic and trade exchanges across the Taiwan strait, the statement said.Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with China since the end of
652 the Chinese civil war in 1949, when the Nationalists fled to the island.Despite the ban, indirect commerce has flourished since the late 1980s, when political tensions began to thaw. About 30,000 Taiwan companies have poured more than US$20 billion into China so far.Last week, Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui accused China
652 of using commerce as a political lever against the island and Taiwan's top economic policymaker told local businessmen it was time to slow their investment projects in the mainland."Communist China is trying to use our people to coerce our government and use commerce to achieve political coercion, in order to
652 pressure our government," Lee said."Faced with this situation, we must uphold the principle of exercising restraint and avoiding rashness in order to handle the current cross-straits relations," he added.Though all investments in China must be government approved and routed indirectly through Hong Kong or other countries, Taiwan remains concerned that
652 its economy may become too dependent on China -- and hence politically vulnerable.President Lee said in August the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market to avoid over-dependence on the mainland for investment.Taiwan's President Enterprises said on September 12 it had abandoned plans to

676 1995, market sources said.An increase of $1.00 or $2.00 in oil prices would normally be considered a potential problem to any economy, more so that of a net importer like Thailand, analysts told Reuters.Thailand buys crude oil mainly from the Middle East and some from the Far East. The specifications
676 of Middle East crude oil serve as a basic design for Thai refineries.Despite the political and economic volatility of the Middle East, Thai policy makers say they still view oil prices from the region to be relatively stable.Thailand's oil import bill in 1995 was 115.2 billion baht (US$4.6 billion), compared
676 with non-oil imports of 1.67 trillion baht.Paul Alapat, an economist with Lehman Brothers, said rising oil prices could worsen Thailand's fragile trade and current account deficits, already among the highest in the region.Thailand's 1996 current account deficit is officially expected to total 7.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). Lehman,
676 however, expects the deficit to be 8.5 percent of GDP, after 8.1 percent in 1995."It (the rise in oil prices) is bad for sentiment. But we do not plan to revise our current account deficit forecast for Thailand yet," Alapat said.Thailand's economy has slowed sharply this year, with some private
676 analysts expecting GDP growth to slow to just over 6.0 percent from the 8.6 percent posted in 1995.Arporn Chewakrengkai, chief economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said higher oil prices were already factored into the group's economic forecasts, but warned Deutsche was likely to revise up the inflation forecast if oil
676 prices rose steeply.Recent Iraq-U.S. tensions have given rise to fears about which way oil prices might trend in the near future."Our forecast for 1996 inflation is 5.7 percent. 676 Supapol, president of SCB Research Institute, said there were sufficient stocks held in Thailand to weather the effects of any immediate rise in oil prices."The effect could be delayed or reduced. 676 to rise," he said.(US$1--25 baht)</

696 claimed the lives of some 400 haemophiliacs, police said.The arrests follow nationwide raids last month of offices of Osaka-based Green Cross which were spurred by a murder complaint filed by the family of a deceased AIDS patient.The investigation took a new turn on Wednesday when the family filed a similar
696 complaint against a former Health Ministry official -- the first such formal complaint against a public official.The move could open the way for investigations into the alleged role of the government in the scandal, analysts said.A lawyer for the family asked prosecutors in Osaka to act against Akihito Matsumura, who
696 headed the ministry's Biologics and Antibiotics Division from 1984 to 1986. 696 though he knew unheated products could be contaminated with HIV.In a separate development, prosecutors said they had indicted the former head of a ministry AIDS research team who was arrested last month.Takeshi Abe was charged on Wednesday with professional negligence resulting in the death of a haemophiliac patient knowing that

704 of the companies are small, commercial trading firms which are not suitable for listing," said a stock analyst with Shenyin &amp; Wanguo Securities."But the problem involves millions of investors, prompting the central government to take measures to solve it.""The problem has been on the agenda since early last year," said
704 an economist with China Financial Trust and Investment Co. 704 of the 90 have been listed, including Cai Hong Display Devices in Shanghai and Chongqing Traditional Chinese Medicine in Shenzhen.A CSRC notice issued on Tuesday last week said the securities authorities planned to list 32 more of the companies before the end of next year, prompting the Shanghai and Shenzhen
704 domestic A share markets to fall sharply on the day.Shenzhen's A share index tumbled a further 5.32 percent on Wednesday this week, while Shanghai A shares lost 2.04 percent in part on rumours A share listings would be accelerated, brokers said.The criteria used for determing which companies should be listed

713 Chinese conglomerates are emerging as the new powerhouses of Hong Kong's corporate scene, ready to take on the mantle of the old "hongs" who dominated the territory during British colonial rule.A dramatic shift in the landscape is under way as Britain prepares to hand Hong Kong back to China next
713 July 1."The whole picture in Hong Kong is changing," said Ching-ju Yeh, senior investment manager at HSBC Asset Management."The impression is that for some of the traditional old names, the influence will start to decline and new names from China are getting a much higher profile," she said.Changes in Hong
713 Kong's business environment have already been anticipated by investors and China-related shares have been snapped up eagerly this year on expectations these firms will flourish when Hong Kong becomes their home turf."Institutional investors are hedging themselves against a drop in influence from the British-related companies, which were the historical landlords
713 of Hong Kong, and increasing their weightings in red chips," said Charles de Trenck, senior analyst at Kerry Securities."There is a re-rating of China-related shares because of the handover. 713 backing from China.Some of Hong Kong's hongs -- the old name for large trading houses -- go back to the founding of the British colony in the mid-19th century.Names such as Jardine Matheson &amp; Co, Butterfield and Swire, Wheelock Marden and Hutchison Whampoa wielded great influence in the affairs of
713 Hong Kong.But the territory will be handed back to China at midnight on June 30, 1997 and the return to Chinese sovereignty will allow the rise of companies like CITIC Pacific Ltd, Guangdong Investment Ltd, China Resources Enterprise Ltd and Shanghai Industrial, analysts said."The companies with Chinese background or capital

713 environment of Hong Kong compared with other mainland cities, these companies are likely to compete for the economic advantages currently enjoyed by the established players," it said."CITIC Pacific and Guangdong Investment are likely to emerge as influential conglomerates in the territory post 1997."Analysts said the rapid rise of these China-backed
713 firms is likely to be boosted by valuable asset injections by influential state-owned parents.Although it is hard to say just how wealthy the parents are, they said backing from a provincial government assures financial support and access to important business."Some of the influential concept stocks like Guangdong Investment and Shanghai
713 Industrial will definitely emerge. 713 fall," he said.CITIC Pacific, the Hong Kong branch of Beijing's official foreign trading arm China International Trust and Investment Corp, has become a role model for emerging Chinese firms.The company has already ascended to blue chip status and its assets have swelled through acquisitions and asset injections.Other companies are expected
713 to follow suit and Guangdong Investment, also a blue chip, is well on its way.Controlled by Guangdong province, Guangdong Investment engages in investment holding, hotel ownership and management. 713 array of businesses ranging from brewing to property to cold storage. Its shares have risen about 74 percent this year."It's being regarded as a conglomerate in the making. 722 rush to leave the country by sea and air during a two-month amnesty period granted to illegal workers that expires on September 30.The law, which comes into effect on October 1, imposes stiff penalties on illegal aliens or workers who violate labour laws."The first launch left yesterday with 200 people
722 on board," said K.V. Shankar, the secretary general of the privately funded association in Dubai.Originally five small, open-decked cargo boats had been hired to make the four-day trip across the Arabian Sea. But after the first launch left on Wednesday, with a bucket as its toilet, the association pulled the
722 plug."For humanitarian reasons there will be no more launches, but a ship holding 2,000 people is due to leave on September 28," said Shankar, whose group organised Wednesday's sailing."The boats were not in very good condition," said Shankar, adding: "It is torture travelling with the open deck, the toilets, everything."Many
722 illegal expatriates have been leaving the UAE by air for weeks, but no figures on their numbers are available.Diplomats expect up to 200,000 expatriates will have left by the end of the August-September amnesty period, in which violators can legalise their stay or leave the country.The UAE has said foreigners
722 who do not have permits to reside in the emirates or who work for employers other than their sponsors -- a widespread practice -- would be severely penalised and deported. The practice has always been illegal but the new law imposes harsher punishment.From October 1, illegal workers and their employers
722 face hefty fines and jail sentences if they are caught.Foreigners, mostly from the Indian subcontinent but also from the Philippines and other southeast Asian states, make up 75 percent of the UAE's 2.4 million population.UAE officials have said illegal aliens pose a security threat to the country.But business executives and
722 newspapers say the departure of large number of labourers could take its toll on businesses, which rely on low-paid foreign workers.India's Ambassador, Murladhir Menon, said over 30,000 Indian nationals had applied for so-called "out-visas" and "the stream of people applying for these permits to leave is continuing".But he said that
722 because many could not afford the 800 dirham ($220) airfare, he had asked the Shipping Corporation of India to send boats to help bring the workers home.Joseph Angeles, charge d'affaires at the Philippines Embassy in Abu Dhabi, said some 3,500 people had sought help from the embassy since the amnesty
722 began, but said it could just be the tip of the iceberg."There might be a huge number of people who come in when the deadline draws nearer," he said.</

724 U.S. ground troops belonging to a 3,000-strong force were deploying in Kuwait on Friday under orders to head into the desert with battle tanks close to the Iraqi border to deter threats by Baghdad."There are a lot of Kuwaitis who are going to sleep better tonight because the First Cav
724 (U.S. Army 1st Cavalry Division) is here," said U.S. Ambassador to Kuwait Ryan Crocker. "This is a tremendously important deployment for the Kuwaitis."The first 230 of the U.S. troops arrived on Thursday in oil-rich Kuwait, where the United States has already deployed eight hi-tech Stealth bombers and Patriot launchers for
724 fear of Iraqi Scud missile attacks against neighbours.They are part of Washington's huge military build-up in the Gulf where the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise arrived on Thursday to join another carrier battle group. Seven U.S. ships in the region are capable of firing Tomahawk cruise missiles.The latest Iraq-U.S. confrontation erupted
724 in late August when President Saddam Hussein's forces intervened to help a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq against a rival Kurdish group.Washington retaliated by firing 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq on September 3 and 4 -- a move which most 1991 Gulf War Arab allies
724 failed to support, describing it as a violation of Iraq's sovereignty.The U.S. troops are making the long flight to Kuwait from Texas on commercial aircraft equipped with chemical and biological warfare detectors, protective suits and masks."We are here to deter war...We are trying to send a signal and that signal
724 (to Iraq) is 'We are ready'," U.S. Army Colonel Robert Pollard told reporters on Thursday night.He flew in with the first batch of soldiers. A second flight was expected in Kuwait late on Thursday night with the rest of the 3,000 arriving over the next few days, U.S. officers said.The
724 first contingent, some looking tired and jet-lagged, were to drive 28 U.S. pre-positioned main battle tanks (MBT) and other military hardware stored at a facility in north Kuwait, Camp Doha, into the desert late on Thursday night.Over the next few months, U.S. officers said, the troops will join 1,200 U.S.
724 soldiers, who came to Kuwait before the current standoff erupted, in exercises just south of Iraq.A total of 4,000 U.S. soldiers, including 150 women in combat support units, 1,600 MBTs, armoured fighting vehicles (AFV) and other heavy weaponry will take part in the war games.If Washington orders more troops to
724 come to Kuwait they will draw similar pre-positioned heavy armour from U.S. warships in the region and other storage facilities in Gulf Arab states.The MBTs and AFVs are not air conditioned, a tropicalised specification which most Gulf Arab states include when ordering such hardware mainly from Western arms makers."They just
724 asked how hot is this compared to Texas," Pollard said of the first question posed by arriving soldiers as they loaded their vehicles with hundreds of boxes of bottled water."God, I wish," said one soldier when asked if his M1A1 MBT was air-conditioned. Some of the soldiers fought in the
724 1991 U.S.-led coalition which freed Kuwait of a seven-month Iraqi occupation.Officers said the temperature inside MBTs and AFVs when in the desert reaches 65 degrees Celsius (150 Fahrenheit) in September.Western diplomats said that without serious provocation from Baghdad the likelihood of a strike on Iraq was now slight."He (Saddam) continues
724 to flex his muscles," said Kuwait-based Pollard. "Therefore we have to continue to deploy our forces... First to keep the peace in the region, secondly to protect (U.S) national interests in the region."</
725 Control of aircraft noise and pollution will dictate airport development in future, an expert from Europe's Airports Council International (ACI) told a seminar in the Moroccan city of Casablanca on Thursday.Dr Callum Thomas told the international meeting the airport industry faced increasing environmental pressures which would continue to mount and
725 influence future development of airports around the world."This could in theory result in all travel between a number of major cities in Europe being made by TGV (high speed) trains and not aircraft...," Thomas, president of ACI's Swiss-based environment committee, told delegates."Environment is therefore seen as the key to future
725 development," he said, adding: "Disturbance caused by aircraft noise is the single most important issue of concern to European airports."The standard of living amongst residents of Europe is very high with the result that their tolerance of noise is low and accordingly aircraft noise has created some of the most
725 marked constraints upon airport development."Some European airports had to close at night, with a further 50 having restrictions on their use then.Other pollution, particularly in densely-populated Europe, included that of the air, water and soil, while airport waste management was becoming increasingly important.He said "at least 18 European airports regularly
725 measure air quality with a further eight planning monitoring programmes in the near future."Pointing to costs involved, he said a $15 million drainage strategy had been recently completed at one British airport."Over 40 airports have or are about to undertake major surveys of waste management systems," he said.Despite social and
725 economic development coming from airport expansion, and increasing demands for air travel as people became more affluent, there was less tolerance of disturbance and pollution."This is a paradox which senior managers at major airports across Europe have to understand and resolve...," he added.</

749 The Clinton administration Thursday unexpectedly rescinded a controversial waiver that would have let the District of Columbia bypass a five-year limit on benefits under a new welfare reform law.Officials at the Department of Health and Human Services insisted they had been forced to withdraw the waiver after discovering the District
749 had not met technical requirements.But Republicans, angry about President Clinton's decision to grant the waiver just three days before he signed the sweeping welfare measure, had threatened to bring legislation to the floor of Congress to overturn it.The welfare law, signed by Clinton last month, ends a six-decade federal guarantee
749 of aid, limits most benefits to five years and requires recipients to work after two years. It gives states block grants to design their own welfare systems."I think on further reflection they (the administration) probably determined that it wasn't a very good idea for several reasons," said Florida Republican Rep.
749 Clay Shaw, a main author of the welfare measure."It was sort of an 'in your face' to the Congress: after we passed the bill and before the president signed it they let the District of Columbia opt out of the work provisions for 10 years, absolutely gutting the bill," he
749 said.Michael Kharfen, a spokeman for the HHS, said that after reviewing the waiver, officials discovered the District had not complied with a requirement for a public comment period.He said the decision was not a response to Republican complaints, adding, "there's certainly been a lot of discussion about the D.C. waiver
749 and we reviewed it again and then identified this flaw."But in a one-sentence statement released through his press secretary, Washington Mayor Marion Barry said it was politics at work: "HHS succumbed to pressure from the Republicans on Capitol Hill."More than half of the children in the District get some public
749 aid. The percentage of the population receiving welfare is one of the highest nationwide.The 10-year waiver would have let the District exempt welfare recipients from the five-year limit on benefits if they were trying to find work and could not.At the insistence of Republicans, states with waivers already in place
749 were allowed to continue running their welfare programs under the new law. Shaw said Republicans will take a close look at the other waivers.The law already allows states to exempt up to 20 percent of their population from the time limit.Unlike a majority of states, the District had not moved
749 aggressively before the law was passed to implement a welfare reform plan. It submitted a waiver in August, which was granted by the administration in a matter of days.There is concern that the District may become a magnet for welfare recipients as nearby states like Virginia and Maryland pass tough
749 welfare reform plans.Because the new law provides block grants, rather than automatically increasing funding when case loads rise, that could spell problems for the financially strapped District.</

760 A Texas jury decided in favour of Baxter International Inc. in lawsuits over breast implants which four women said left them with "silicone poisoning," lawyers and company officials said Thursday.The Dallas County jury of six women and six men deliberated for nearly two days before returning Wednesday with a 10-2
760 decision in favour of the company, a unit of Baxter International Inc.The four plaintiffs, whose cases were consolidated for the four-week Dallas trial, underwent implant surgery between 1977 and 1981.All said their implants later ruptured and had to be removed. They alleged they have "silicone poisoning" and suffer from fatigue,
760 joint pain, rashes and muscle aches.The jury rejected those claims after reviewing the women's medical records during deliberations.Baxter has never made or sold breast implants but its alleged liability stemmed from its 1985 merger with American Hospital Supply Corp, which once owned implant manufacturer Heyer-Schulte Co. Heyer-Schulte no longer exists.Plaintiffs'
760 attorney Zoe Littlepage said she and her four clients were disappointed by the verdict. She told jurors during the trial that the women were given implants without adequate testing."The truth is that breast implants are harmful," she said. "This company made these four women an experiment."Thousands of women have sued
760 Baxter and other silicone breast implant makers, saying the implants led to connective tissue diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. A settlement was reached in a class-action lawsuit involving hundreds of thousands of women last fall, but many recipients dropped out to file individual lawsuits.Baxter, which is based in Deerfield, Ill.,
760 said in a statement it has won 20 breast implant verdicts and lost two. Of those two, one is on appeal and Baxter was granted a new trial in the other. Two other cases have ended in mistrial.The Dallas jury in the four-week trial decided that breast implants made by
760 Heyer-Schulte were properly manufactured, designed, tested and inspected and that adequate warnings about the products were given.</

762 Western Resources Inc., which holds a 24.3 percent stake in ADT Ltd., said Thursday it opposes Republic Industries Inc.'s planned acquisition of the security firm.The opposition by the Topeka, Kan.-based utility is just the latest stumbling block for the controversial transaction, which already has generated concern on Wall Street.Western said
762 it disclosed its opposition in a filing made to the Securities and Exchange Commission last Friday."We are opposing that transaction. We believe that Republic stock is much too volatile to give Western any real benefit," said Western spokeswoman Michel Philipp.Originally valued at $5 billion when it was announced July 1,
762 the deal's price tag declined sharply just weeks later when Republic's stock price sank below $20 per share. As announced originally, the deal was based on a price of $26 for each share of ADT common stock.Since then, Republic and ADT reportedly have been haggling over new terms for the
762 deal. Republic has confirmed that negotiations were continuing, but has declined to specify the nature of the talks. 762 slipped 25 cents to $20.25 on the New York Stock Exchange and Western Resources gained 12.5 cents to $29, also on the NYSE.Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based Republic declined to comment on Western's opposition to the deal. 762 not divulging its opposition strategy.She noted, however, that one possible method would be for Western to acquire a larger chunk of ADT stock.
