871 The typical mutual fund investor owns shares in three different funds, according to the Investment Company Institute. For many of these investors, that includes two or more funds that invest in equities.That's a good idea: Investing in a number of stock funds can increase the diversification of a portfolio, and
871 thereby reduce its overall level of risk. It's more likely that a single investment will hit the skids than two will at the same time.But you can't just pick a couple of funds and assume that your investments are diversified. Some mutual funds walk nearly in lock step with each
871 other.For example, Fidelity's massive Magellan and Contrafund have provided very similar returns in recent years. They've even held many of the same stocks, although that might change following former manager Jeff Vinik's departure from Magellan.One result of the two funds' similarities has been a high degree of correlation between their
871 returns. At times, that was in favour of investors. For example, in 1995, Magellan and Contrafund turned in nearly identical 36.8 percent and 36.3 percent returns, respectively, thanks to their similar strategies. But investors who chose both funds gained little diversification.A little-used statistic called "R-squared" can help you ensure that
871 your portfolio is well-diversified. It represents the percentage of a fund's performance that can be explained by the returns of another fund or index.For example, at the end of 1995, Fidelity Magellan had an R-squared of 94 percent with Contrafund, meaning the fund giants' returns tracked each other quite closely
871 during the previous three years.Fidelity Capital Appreciation would have been a better choice for a Magellan investor in search of diversification. The two funds recently posted an R-squared of only 31 percent.Even international equity funds sometimes provide less diversification than investors expect. For example, Templeton Growth and Templeton World each
871 recently had a relatively high R-squared of 62 percent with the Standard &amp; Poor's 500 index, according to Morningstar Mutual Funds. In fact, seven Templeton international equity funds recently had R-squareds of 47 percent with the S&amp;P 500.Some international funds do provide a greater level of diversification. For example, GAM
871 Global (800-426-4685; $10,000 minimum investment; 5 percent load; 15.4 percent recent three-year annualized return) recently had an R-squared of only 9 percent with the S&amp;P 500. Fontaine Global Growth (800-247-1550; $500 minimum; no load; 21.2 percent, three-year annualized return) posted an R-squared of 12 percent with the index.Investors in search
871 of still greater levels of diversification might turn toward Japan. The six international mutual funds that had the lowest R-squareds with the S&amp;P 500 all are Japan-specific funds. Each posted an R-squared with the S&amp;P 500 of less than 1 percent.The funds included G.T. Global Japan Growth (800-824-1580; $500 minimum;
871 4.75 percent load; 1.5 percent three-year annualized return) and T. Rowe Price Japan (800-638-5660; $2,500 minimum; no load; -2.6 percent three-year annualized return).But keep in mind that a single country fund, such as a Japan fund, likely will carry more risk than a diversified international offering.It's also possible to increase
871 your equity fund portfolio's diversification without heading overseas.For example, Premier Strategic Growth (800-554-4611; $1,000 minimum; 4.5 percent load; 16.8 percent three-year annualized return), an aggressive growth fund, has an R-squared of only 1 percent with the S&amp;P 500 index.Small-cap fund Govett Smaller Companies (800-225-2222; $500 minimum; 4.95 percent load; 10.6
871 percent three-year annualized return) has a correlation of 6 percent with the S&amp;P 500. Another low-correlation fund is Merger Fund (800-343-8959; $2,000 minimum; no load; 11.6 percent three-year annualized return), which compiles a unique portfolio of stocks that seem likely to benefit from merger and acquisition activity. Merger has an
871 R-squared of 11 percent over the past three years.But low correlation alone isn't enough to make a fund worth an investment. For example, Oak Hall Equity has an R-squared of only 8 percent with the S&amp;P 500, thanks in large part to significant gold-stock holdings. But the fund's return ranks
871 it in the bottom 5 percent of all small-cap funds over the past three years -- not the sort of diversification that's worth seeking out.(EDITORS: Clint Willis is a free-lance writer who covers financial issues for Reuters. Any opinions in the column are solely those of Mr. Willis.)</

886 Bermuda-based reinsurer Mid Ocean Ltd has adopted a shareholder rights plan that would protect shareholders against unsolicited takeover offers.The company said the plan, which would exempt the existing holdings of EXEL Ltd, which has a 29.8 percent stake in Mid Ocean."The rights are intended to enable all Mid Ocean shareholders
886 to realize the long-term value of their investment in Mid Ocean," chief executive Michael Butt. "They will not prevent a takeover of Mid Ocean. However, the rights plan should encourage anyone seeking to acquire Mid Oean to negotiate with the board prior to attempting a takeover," he said.A Mid Ocean
886 spokesman on Thursday declined comment on why the company decided to adopt the rights plan at this time.However, the insurance industry has been among the hottest sectors in the merger market and the Bermuda market saw its first bidding war this summer when ACE Ltd and IPC Holdings Ltd made
886 rival offers for Tempest Reinsurance Holdings Ltd. Under the plan, each holder of ordinary shares at the close of business on October 1, 1996 will receive a distribution of one right for each class A ordinary share held. Each right entitles the holder to purchase from Mid Ocean one class
886 A ordinary share at an initial purchase price of $140.The rights will become exercisable and will detach from the class A ordinary shares a specified period of time after any person has become the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares. They also will become
886 exercisable and detach from the class A ordinary shares after any person has commended a tender of exchange offer, which if consummated, would result in any person becoming the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of the common shares.Parties, such as EXEL, owning 20 percent or more of the
886 common shares of Mid Ocean on the date the plan was adopted would not cause the rights to become exercisable. If anyone becomes the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares, other than EXEL, each right will entitle the holder other than the acquiring person,
886 to purchase for the then applicable price Mid Ocean common shares having a value of twice the purchase price. If, following an acquisition of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares, Mid Ocean is involved in certain mergers or other business combinations or sells or transfers more than
886 50 percent of its assets or earning power, each right will entitle the holder to purchase for the then applicable price common stock of the other party to such transaction having a value twice the purchase price.At any time after a person has acquired 20 percent or more, but before
886 anyone has acquired more than 50 percent, of the company's ordinary shares, Mid Ocean may exchange all or part of the rights for common shares at an exchange ratio of one class A ordinary share per right, subject to rights holders delivering to the company an amount in cash equal
886 to the par value of each class A ordinary share to be received.Mid Ocean may redeem the rights at a price of $0.01 per right at any time prior to a specified period of time after a person has become the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of its
886 common shares. The rights will expire on October 1, 2006, unless earlier exchanged or redeemed.</

894 The unconscious human brain is capable of registering subliminal messages flashed on a screen but not well enough to follow commands like "Eat popcorn," research psychologists said on Thursday.The experiments established that the brain can perceive a simple subliminal message, which can very briefly influence subsequent conscious perception.But from what
894 the researchers have learned so far it appears the message must be an extremely simple one and the effect lingers for about a tenth of a second, not long enough to influence or manipulate behaviour."'Think' is too strong a word for what the unconscious can do -- it can analyse
894 meaning of a single word," said University of Washington psychologist Anthony Greenwald, whose findings appear on Friday in the journal Science. His research also fits into the larger ongoing debate between cognitive psychologists like himself and the psychoanalytic ones.Cognitive ones believe the unconcious mind is rather limited, if not downright
894 dumb. The psychoanalytic ones share Sigmund Freud's belief that the unconscious mind is capable of complex and powerful mental operations.Greenwald's experiment involved flashing a string of 15 consonants, followed by a word or name, and then another string of consonants across a computer monitor, forming what Greenwald called a "subliminal
894 sandwich."Then a word or name -- without the accompanying nonsense letters -- was flashed on the screen. The subject in the experiment had to determine whether it was a male or female name or a pleasant or unpleasant word.When the "sandwiched" word was in the same category as the single
894 word display, the subject recognised and categorized the word more quickly than if it was not. The subliminal "priming" sped up the recognition of subsequent words.For instance, if "David" was in the sandwich, the subject was quicker to recognise the category of "Kevin" than to do the same for "Sarah."
894 The mind was "primed" to see and recognise a boy's name.When names or words were presented without the sandwich preceding them, response time was 0.5 or 0.6 second. With the "priming," subjects could respond in 0.4 second, he said."It's like swinging at a fast ball -- you do better when
894 you know where it's coming from," Greenwald said. "The subliminal sandwich is like a hint of where the fastball is coming from. They can't see it but they get that subliminal hint and they start leaning, male or female."In his experiment, the priming effect was too brief to lend itself
894 to any significant conditioning or manipulation.If further research shows such subliminal responses could "accumulate and work like a conditioning procedure," it could have some potential for advertising or influencing behaviour, but Greenwald said he doubted it would go undetected in an era when videos could be viewed frame by frame."It
894 is potentially usable for manipulation but not in the 'Drink Coca-Cola,' 'Eat popcorn' sense," he said.He said his prior research also showed that self-help tapes that boast of subliminal messages do not work, although they might have a placebo effect. People who think they are being taught subliminally to lose
894 weight or concentrate may, in fact, lose weight or concentrate better, he said.</

900 Two tickborne diseases first recognised in the past decade have struck more than 600 people, killing more than a dozen of them, federal health officials said Thursday.The U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said the two emerging illnesses, transmitted through the bite of an infected tick, have caused
900 at least 13 deaths. The diseases can cause fever, headache, muscle aches, chills, sweating, nausea and vomiting.There have been more than 400 known cases of human monocytic ehrlichiosis (HME) since it was first identified in 1986 and about 200 cases of human granulocytic ehrlichiosis (HGE), first recognised in 1993. Not
900 all state health departments track the new diseases, so the actual number of cases is probably much higher."The diseases are remarkably similar" but are caused by slightly different species of erhlichia bacteria, epidemiologist James Childs of the CDC's National Centre for Infectious Diseases said. "The infection affects blood cells and
900 blood chemistry but also takes up residence in other organs," he said.The CDC estimated that HME was at least as common as Rocky Mountain spotted fever, which affects about 800 people every year. HME has been confirmed in 30 states, mostly in the southeastern and south central regions. HGE has
900 been confirmed in Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Wisconsin and New York.The two new ailments can usually be treated with antibiotics, "but it sometimes becomes more complicated," Childs said. "In a few cases we've seen chronic or persistent infection," he said.People infected with the diseases do not always develop a rash. When
900 they do, it is not necessarily at the site of the tick bite by which the infection was spread, the CDC said.The most common tickborne ailment is Lyme disease, which causes 10,000 to 11,000 cases per year and is not generally considered life-threatening.The CDC said tick bites could be prevented
900 by wearing light-coloured clothing to make it easier to see crawling ticks, tucking pant legs into socks, conducting regular body examinations and using insect repellent.Attached ticks should be promptly removed using forceps. Removing ticks by hand carries the risk of infection through cuts in the fingers. After a tick is
900 removed, the bite site should be cleaned immediately with a disinfectant, the health agency said.</

904 Frederick Forsyth, one of the Cold War's most famous thriller writers, has decided to retire, he said in an interview to be published next month.Forsyth, 58, a former Reuters and BBC correspondent who shot to fame 25 years ago with the publication of "The Day of the Jackal" about an
904 attempt to murder Charles de Gaulle, told Sky magazine his ninth thriller, "Icon," will be published this month and "I just feel this is it.""I've done nine books, add to that the anthology of short stories, 'No Comebacks,' which is 10 books, a nice round figure," he told the magazine.

907 A breath test for the bacteria that cause peptic ulcers was approved on Thursday by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the test's maker said.The test, manufactured by Nashville, Tennessee-based Meretek, involves drinking the diagnostic drug Pranactin and exhaling into a collection device, which is then sent to the company's

911 The World Bank arm that supports private enterprise said Thursday its help for developing countries is strongly in demand, although other investors were increasingly picking up part of the load.The International Finance Corp. said total financing in the year ended June 30 hit a record $3.2 billion, up from $2.9
911 billion in fiscal 1995.At a briefing to unveil its annual report, IFC Executive Vice President Jannik Lindbaek told reporters he expected total financing this year would be up 8 percent to 10 percent.This was somewhat slower than in recent years, he said, noting that over the past five years total
911 financing by the agency has doubled as countries around the world rushed to embrace the free enterprise system."We see that in some of our important countries, alternative sources of financing have become available, so we are less important to some of these countries," he said. "We're talking about Eastern Europe
911 and some parts of Asia."At the same time, he said the IFC was launching a new initiative to expand its activities in smaller and poorer nations, targeting some 16 countries it said were undergoing particularly difficult transitions to market economies.They included Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cambodia, countries in the Eastern Caribbean,
911 Central Africa, as well as the Slovak Republic and the West Bank and Gaza.But the IFC made clear that it was working to ensure that it did not get into the way of private capital moving into developing country markets, consulting extensively with the private sector to reduce investment conflicts.This
911 was good news at the Institute of International Finance, which separately reported its annual forecast showing that net private investment in the major emerging markets will reach a record $225 billion this year, up from $208 billion in 1995.The group, which provides economic analysis for commercial banks and other financial
911 institutions, said it was critical that the International Monetary Fund and World Bank work closely with the private sector so they don't get in each other's way.Moreover, IIF Managing Director Charles Dallara said it might be better for the international financial institutions to walk more softly during crisis rather than
911 mobilise huge bailouts as was done for Mexico at the start of last year.The new information on global investment comes in conjunction with the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, which begins next week.</

920 A new Vermont property tax law that sets how municipalities and the state split the cost of preserving open space has pit neighbor against neighbor, while a panel set up to help resolve the issue has clashed."That's the whole riff, who's going to pay the bill," said Edward Hasse on
920 Thursday. He is Vermont's Commissioner of Taxes and chairs the panel, which was set up by Gov. Howard Dean.The current use tax program helps ensure that the owners of open spaces, such as forests and farms, are assessed at low rates, though on an across-the-board basis the state's property taxes
920 are fairly high.The problem of how much the state and municipalities should pay was brought to a boil by a bill approved by the legislature on its last day in May, which Dean signed into law. Two towns, Darnard and Bridgewater, have refused to put it into effect, and state
920 officials said it is a major campaign issue.Under the legislation, the state makes a contribution to towns whose tax rates rise more than 1.8 cents per $100 of assessed value in 1995.However, the law obliges all property owners in towns -- from mobile home owners to businesses -- to pay
920 the shortfall left after the state makes its contribution.Previously, the landowners who elected to participate in the current use tax program made up the difference. Last year, the state paid $9.7 million for the program, about 68 percent of its cost. Vermont's annual budget is about $700 million.The tax rates
920 in 1996 are expected to rise above the 1.8-cent limit in many towns because their budgets have climbed, and property values have been reappraised.And enrollment in the current tax use program likely will climb. While a number of landowners, who represent 44,000 acres, opted out of the program this year,
920 the tax department is seeing a lot of of new applications for 1997.Landowners figure that if they will have to pay for part of the taxes on their neighbors' open land, they might as well participate in the program. "So the impact is going to be felt even greater for
920 the 1997 tax season," Snow said.However, the new law also has encouraged some owners of open spaces, like forests and lands, to drop out of the current tax use program because they find it hard to incur their neighbors' wrath."They said they want to walk down the street holding their
920 head high, they don't want their neighbors to pay their taxes," Snow said, saying that was the reason some landowners told the tax department they were leaving the program.And some towns and landowners who are not in the program might wish to encourage development as a way to lower the
920 property tax burden. "So it behooves everybody to develop their town...nobody will get a (tax) break," Snow said, explaining that was a worst-case scenario.The governor extended the deadline for the task force's recommendations by about two weeks to September 30, although local officials want to be sure the voters have
920 a chance to make their views known in the November 5 elections.Despite the clash among the panel members, with state officials seeking greater contributions from municipalities, which their representatives are resisting, the Commissioner predicted that it would find a way to resolve the issue."We're going to decide one way or
920 another on September 30," Hasse said, explaining he anticipated that it would take until around October 10 to draft the final report for Dean.--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1654</

936 The Florida Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that a British ex-socialite who faces the electric chair for murdering two business rivals deserved a new hearing because of possible prosecutor misconduct and a breach of judicial ethics.In a unanimous ruling, Florida's high court ordered an evidentiary hearing to determine the validity
936 of charges posed by attorneys for Krishna Nanan Maharaj that prosecutors withheld information and knowingly allowed perjured testimony.Maharaj, once Britain's second-biggest racehorse owner and a millionaire fruit importer, was sentenced to death in 1987 for the murders a year earlier of Derrick Moo Young and his son, Duane Moo Young,
936 who were gunned down during a meeting with Maharaj in a Miami hotel.Maharaj faces death in Florida's electric chair for the slayings, which took place after a bitter dispute over a property deal between Maharaj and Derrick Moo Young in which each accused the other of extortion, bribery and theft
936 of hundreds of thousands of dollars.In addition to ordering a rehearing, the court criticised Miami Circuit Judge Leonard Glick, who presided over the case despite an apparent conflict of interest. Glick, who was the supervisor of prosecutors handling the case, denied Maharaj an evidentiary hearing in 1995. The high court
936 ruled that he should have recused himself from the case because of his relationship with the attorneys.The case will be returned to the Miami circuit court, where a different judge will hear evidence to determine if a new trial or sentencing hearing is warranted. The hearing must be conducted within
936 90 days.Jim Lohman, a Tallahassee attorney representing the Bar of England and the Wales Human Rights Committee in the Maharaj case, said Florida law generally requires an evidentiary hearing when a defendant raises disputed issues of fact that bear on the validity of the conviction."Those allegations were abundantly raised by
936 Mr. Maharaj in the trial court," Lohman said. "The trial court denied him an opportunity for an evidentiary hearing. Obviously, the trial court was wrong in doing so."Maharaj moved to Britain from Trinidad in 1960, driving a truck before building what would become "Chris Foreign Foods," a multi-million dollar fruit
936 import and distribution business.His appeal had received wide support in Britain, where his supporters included more than 100 members of Parliament.</

941 Florida hopes a new publicity campaign will put some teeth into a longstanding message to tourists and residents alike -- don't feed the alligators.With 14 million people and a million alligators, Florida is logging more and more complaints about gators that crawl into neighbourhood canals and lakes, backyards and occasionally
941 swimming pools, a state spokesman said on Thursday.Florida's information campaign, due to begin within two months, aims to teach people that alligators are a part of the landscape in the Sunshine State, said Henry Cabbage, spokesman for the Florida Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission."Gators belong in Florida," he said.
941 "The idea is to teach people how to peacefully coexist with alligators."Under the slogan "Welcome to Our State. You Might See Some Alligators Here," a campaign of posters, brochures and public service announcements will start in Florida and expand to eight other Southern states where alligators live and breed.Florida records
941 about 13,000 nuisance calls and averages 18 attacks on humans annually, Cabbage said. There have been 220 documented alligator attacks, six fatal, since 1948.Many of the people who call to complain about pesky alligators do not understand that the creatures are simply doing what alligators do, he said."Usually an alligator
941 wouldn't be a problem if people would learn to treat them like a wild animal. Don't feed them, don't try to pet them and don't get close to them."Cabbage recalled the story of a Florida zookeeper who stopped a tourist who was lifting a little boy over a fence so
941 he could set the child down on a 12-foot (3.5-metre) alligator and take a picture.Alligator were declared an endangered species in 1966 but were removed from threatened lists in the mid-1980s after Florida populations were successfully regenerated.</

954 A number of international free trade agreements are likely to result in higher U.S. exports of agricutural products and healthy job creation in rural America, according to a U.S. Department of Agriculture senior economist."Recently, the weaker dollar and the U.S. support of multilateral trade liberalization, which worked to open other
954 countries' agricultural markets, resulted in strong exports for U.S. products," Bill Edmondson, economist with the USDA Economic Research Service, said in a research paper. "This trend of agricultural trade growth will likely continue in the future and will have economic impacts in rural America," Edmondson said.Edmondson presented the paper on
954 U.S. agricultural trade and the Midwest economy at a one-day conference held on Wednesday by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.The conference is part of the Chicago Fed's year-long research project on various aspects of the Midwest economy.Edmondson noted the research work on the agricultural exports/employment relationship has so far
954 focused on the national level, leaving aside the specifics of the Midwest. "Because the U.S. rural and general economy is extremely diverse, differences in various regions make broad generalizations difficult," Edmondson said. "The mix of farm and processed food products produced in the (Chicago Fed) district, however, suggests that this
954 district should be favorably affected by such an expansion."Edmondson said trade ageements such as the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) or the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and the creation of the World Trade Organization (WTO), should contribute to a more competitive agricultural sector. Edmondson noted the
954 economy and labor markets of rural U.S. regions have been affected in the 1980s by "volatility of export markets.""During the 1990s, however, these markets have been expanding rapidly and prospects for more exports are good considering the GATT, WTO, and regional pacts such as NAFTA," Edmondson said.The USDA economist estimated
954 that if all agricultural products imported in 1995 had been produced domestically, "56,000 more workers would have been needed in the five states (of the Chicago Fed District)." However, Edmondson's paper shows that "even if one takes the extreme assumption that all import-related jobs replaced domestic jobs, the Chicago Fed
954 region was 87,700 jobs better off after agricultural trade in 1995."Edmondson also expected the share of agriculture-related jobs to increase versus the region's average as the volume of high-value products -- such as poultry, processed foods or fruits -- increasec compared with basic commodities like grains.-- 212-859-1666</
955 The International Monetary Fund opened a site on the Internet Thursday providing information about the types of economic data available in 18 member countries."For a long time we have been trying to press countries to report to us on a more timely basis, more information, and based on good statistical
955 systems," said Jack Boorman, director of the IMF's policy and review department.The 1994-95 Mexican peso crisis highlighted the need for timely and accurate data about developing countries, Boorman told a news conference.The site does not include the countries' actual data -- that may come later -- but it lists contacts
955 for obtaining the information."Good statistical citizenship helps to inform markets," Boorman said. "The whole purpose of this system is to help that process, to make sure that markets are getting better data in a timely way."The Internet address of the site is http://dsbb.imf.org. It lists information such as the frequency,
955 schedule and types of economic and financial data released on a regular basis by the countries which have subscribed to the fund's "Special Data Dissemination Standard."The countries on the site are Argentina, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Peru, the Philippines, Singapore, Slovenia, Switzerland, Thailand, Britain
955 and the United States.By next week, information about another eight countries is expected to be added. 955 Columbia, Iceland, Israel, and Lithuania.The special standard is being phased in over two years. countries agreed to meet the standards by Dec. 31, 1998.Discussions are continuing with other countries that have not yet agreed to subscribe, including Germany, said John McLenaghan, director of the IMF statistics department.IMF officials said the
955 site could eventually include direct links to countries' data or other kinds of information."We're starting something which, while it has a very specific content and frame at the present time, has potential for going in directions that none of us perhaps quite see at the present time," Boorman said.</

958 U.S. manufacturing exports from the Midwest grew at a rapid pace over the past decade despite a stronger -- not a weaker -- dollar, according to economists at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago."The conventional wisdom was...that the sharp depreciation of the dollar during the period 1985-1987, and a gradual
958 depreciation of the dollar since then, materially contributed to Midwest manufacturing industries' ability to compete in export markets," Chicago Fed economists Jack Hervey and William Strauss said in a research paper. "The common perception is that the dollar has recorded a secular depreciation during the past 25 years. But has
958 it really?" Hervey and Strauss questioned in the paper they presented at a day-long conference on "Global Linkages to the Midwest Economy" held at the Chicago Fed on Wednesday.The conference is part of a year-long Chicago Fed research project on the Midwest economy.Hervey and Strauss noted that, since the United
958 States abandoned the gold standard in 1971, the dollar has declined against some currencies, appreciated against others or remained stable against a third group. The Chicago Fed economists argued that, to better assess the export/dollar relationship, it would be useful to look at the dollar's performance versus a specific basket
958 of currencies representing the main export markets of any given U.S. region."The premise underlying construction of a regional dollar index maintains that there are differences in the foreign markets, or export shares, served by different geographical regions of the United States," Hervey and Strauss said.The economists noted that about 43
958 percent of the Midwest's exports of manufactured goods go to Canada, 13 percent to Mexico, 13 percent to Europe and five percent to Japan. Nationwide, 23 percent of U.S. exports of manufactured goods go to Canada, 17 percent to Europe, and about 10 percent to Mexico and Japan."The export data
958 strongly suggest that Midwest exporters of manufactured goods depend substantially more heavily on foreign markets in which the dollar has actually appreciated in recent years -- Canada and Mexico -- relative to U.S. exporters of manufactured goods overall," Hervey and Strauss noted.In their study, the economists chose aggregate exchange rates
958 adjusted for inflation differentials between the United States and 44 countries importing U.S. goods. "Contrary to the common perception, the real dollar did not continue a depreciating trend following the large gyrations recorded during the 1980-1987 period, at least for the Midwest," Hervey and Strauss found. "The aggregate Midwest export-weighted
958 real dollar index shows an appreciating trend for the entire period 1974-1996."Meanwhile, the annual dollar value of manufactured goods exported from the Midwest rose more than fivefold between 1969 and 1991, Hervey and Strauss estimate.The Chicago Fed economists concluded the increased competitiveness of U.S. manufacturers was achieved despite the dollar's
958 appreciation in their main export markets."Given the foreign markets Midwest manufacturing is active in, it would appear that this increased competitiveness has been accomplished without the help of a depreciating dollar exchange rate, as conventional wisdom has often contended," Hervey and Strauss said.-- 212-859-1666</

979 Japan's banking system is not likely to suffer a meltdown, especially now that the Japanese government has stepped in to bail out debt-ridden housing lenders, said experts at a conference on the future of Japan's banking system which took place on Wednesday.But financial deregulation, in the wake of the political
979 backlash to the rescue, may soon prod Japan's banks to model themselves after U.S. and European financial institutions, speakers at New York's Japan Society gathering said. "Japanese banks, if they hope to play in global markets, must adopt a more Western style of management," said Akira Kondoh, director and general
979 manager of Sumitomo Bank Ltd in New York.The recent passing of legislation to prop-up the housing loan corporations -- or jusen -- barely puts a dent in the bad loan problem, which has rocked Japan's financial markets and shaken global investors.But the banks have deep enough pockets to absorb these
979 non-performing loans, experts said. "This is not a debilitating problem, it's not going to take down the whole financial structure," said Ethan Penner, president Nomura Asset Capital Corporation.Estimates of non-performing loans haunting balance sheets of Japan's financial institutions range from $100 billion to $450 billion, experts said.Public anger over the
979 taxpayer bailout and at the bankers has prompted various plans for reform, restructuring and further deregulation. It has also led the Ministry of Finance, which regulates banking, to draw up a reorganization plan, the unveiling of which is expected any day. Just as the Depression-era walls separating banking and securities
979 underwriting in the U.S. slowly crumble, the division between investment banking and commercial banking in Japan may be reviewed again, said experts."Basically, I think we need more deregulation of the industries," said Shuzo Nakamura, Deputy Consul General and Head of Finance Division, at Japan's New York consulate."The banks need to
979 compete better with other financial industries...and other industries need ... to have access to the things that are normally allowed to banks," he said. Nakamura said in the past Japanese securities firms have had limited access to the foreign exchange markets, which have been the domain of large commercial banks.
979 At the same time banks need access to capital markets so they can compete better with the securities firms.The Japanese parliament may take up measures to aid the lowering of some barriers in 1997.Legislation to further relax regulation on foreign exchange markets is being drafted and may be submitted to
979 the Diet next year for approval, Nakamura said.-- 212 859 1667</

981 Municipal bond issuers that are hoping for a "handy-dandy check list" from SEC on how to avoid securities fraud charges better think again, a prominent bond lawyer told attorneys meeting here Thursday."The Securities and Exchange Commission will, I am confident, steadfastly refuse to tell local officials exactly how to avoid
981 liability under the federal securities law," Dean Pope, a partner with Hunton &amp; Williams in Richmond, said in a keynote address at the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop.Bond lawyers who advise local governments "have a responsibility to point that out to local officials," Pope told the 1,000 lawyers
981 attending the three day-meeting.SEC officials agreed last week to meet soon with municipal bond groups about their concerns with the agency's aggressive municipal enforcement program.SEC has brought 20 enforcement actions involving the muni market since SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt took office. Most involved charges against bond underwriters, financial advisers and
981 other professionals.Earlier this year, however, SEC brought its first enforcement action against a general purpose issuer, Orange County, Calif. And the agency has other issuer probes in the works.Alarmed by the trend, issuer representatives say SEC is overstepping its authority. They argue they do not have the same expertise and
981 funds as corporations to avoid lawsuits.But Pope said it is "completely unrealistic" to expect SEC to consider "fraud any less fraudulent" when committed by a municipality."A local government that disguises its financial problems to avoid embarrassing its mayor is no less a target of the SEC than a corporation attempting
981 to manipulate its stock price," Pope said.Pope urged bond lawers to give municipal clients "common-sense steps" to avoid fraud charges. He also recommended that bond lawyers and their clients send questions to Government Finance Officers Association, which is developing guidelines on how localities can avoid fraud.Pope said press reports that
981 SEC may bring charges soon against Orange County's former bond counsel highlights a growing problem for bond lawyers.Bond counsel traditionally are not responsible for disclosure, but many local government officials incorrectly think otherwise, Pope said. "It is in the interest of both ourselves and our clients to clear up misunderstandings,"
981 he said.Pope said a lawsuit Orange County brought against the former bond counsel raises another issue -- when should a bond counsel go over the head of the day-to-day client to elected city boards?The bond counsel only was permitted to contact the county attorney on disclosure matters, Pope said. Yet
981 the lawsuit damns bond counsel for failure to report certain matters to the county board," Pope said. "I offer no easy answers for this thorny problem," Pope said.But, he added, "It now seems, however, extremely dangerous to accept a limitation on your right to discuss matters with the elected officials
981 of the public body you are representing."Pope said SEC's probe of Orange County also raises questions about whether public officials must read disclosure documents."Common sense suggest(s) that elected officials should certainly read at least the basic disclosure document," he said. That way they can question statements that do not make
981 sense or they know are wrong, Pope said.In other comments, Pope predicted that conflicts of interest in the muni arena probably will get a lot of attention from regulators in the coming year."SEC has given us ample warning that any whiff of conflict is a prime subject for disclosure," Pope

982 Richard Chirls, a partner with Orrick, Herrington &amp; Sutcliffe in New York, said in a keynote speech at the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop.Chirls was referring to a July 19 IRS ruling that gives issuers of advance refunding bonds the option of entering into "closing agreements" with IRS
982 to head off possibly having interest on their bonds declared taxable.Municipalities would have to agree to pay the Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest on that figure under the IRS procedure, which triggered a howl
982 of protest from municipalities nationwide.IRS yesterday announced it was extending the one-year deadline for entering closing agreements indefinitely while it reviews the controversial procedure. 982 Washington to fess up to their sins" in response to the closing agreement program.He added that issuers "have to recognize that if they go to Washington they have to bring a check with them. And they are not going to want to bring that check unless it is backed up
982 with the support of the people who participated in the transaction."And that joint contribution to the federal (government) is just not going to happen," Chirls said."So, I just don't think there's much going on here to get too excited about," Chirls said. 982 extensive litigation by issuers against dealers."The train to the 21st century will be a litigious one" for municipal market participants, Chirls said.On another front burner issue, Chirls criticized U.S. Sen. 982 Senator Moynihan," Chirls said."It's federal meddling into areas that are a local affair. 986 Telephone records show that President Clinton's former political adviser Dick Morris was in regular contact with Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott, the New York Post reported Thursday.Morris resigned in August after a supermarket tabloid reported he had had a year-long relationship with a call girl and had allowed her to
986 listen to his phone conversations with Clinton.The newspaper said Morris kept a back channel open with Lott even after he was reprimanded last February for leaking secret budget polling data to the presidential election campaign of Clinton's Republican opponent, Bob Dole.It quoted an unidentified source familiar with telephone records from
986 the Jefferson Hotel in Washington, where prostitute Sherry Rowlands said she visited Morris, as saying he called Lott at least 27 times between January and July."They pitched back and forth (proposals) from here when we were trying to get a budget," Lott's spokeswoman, Susan Irby, was quoted as saying. She
986 told the newspaper some of the calls might have been made to Lott's aides and not the senator.By contrast, only one call was made to the Democratic Senate leader, Tom Daschle of South Dakota, the Post said.</

992 The CIA pulled the plug on its Internet site on Thursday after a hacker broke in and posted a message declaring it the "Central Stupidity Agency."CIA officials said their World Wide Web home page was not linked to mainframe computers containing spy secrets or other classified national security information."There is
992 no way to access internal CIA information from this home page," said Rick Oborn, an agency spokesman.He said the site was tampered with on Wednesday night and had been shut down by the agency on Thursday morning while a task force tried to prevent another break-in.The unidentified hacker turned the
992 home page of the Central Intelligence Agency, a bastion of spy technology and computer wizardry, into a crude parody."Welcome to the Central Stupidity Agency," it read. A picture of an unknown man replaced that of CIA Director John Deutch and fictional links offered "News from Space" and "Nude Girls." The
992 text also read "Stop Lying."No stranger to covert action, the CIA played down the possibility that it was the victim of a cyber-era foe of the trenchcoat-and-dagger type that it had battled in Cold War back alleys."If there is any major enemy who wanted to do us damage, this is
992 not anything that causes us great concern," the spokesman said, adding that he had no idea of the culprit's identity.He termed the attack "malicious" and said he was not shrugging it off. The site, visited about 120,000 times a week, would be restored when the agency's technicians were confident they
992 had "cleaned it up," officials said.The spy agency has formed a task force to look into how the page was penetrated and how to prevent a recurrence, they said.The web site (http://www.odci.gov/cia) showcases spy agency press releases, speeches and other publicly available data including the CIA's World Fact Book, a
992 standard reference.The attack resembled one that forced the Justice Department to close its Web site for a few days last month after hackers turned it into the "Department of Injustice," inserting a swastika and picture of Adolf Hitler.The incident highlighted the vulnerability of Internet sites and drove home the need
992 for multiple layers of security to prevent manipulation of data."You want people to visit, you want them to interact, but you don't want them to leave anything behind," said Jon Englund of the Information Technology Association of America, a trade group of leading software and telecommunications firms.Ben Brandenberg, the Justice
992 Department's chief spokesman, said his department had reopened its home page (http://www.usdoj.gov) after taking unspecified "reasonable measures" to secure it from hackers.But there were no guarantees that the fixes would prevent repeat attacks, he said, adding: "This is a hazard of the information age.""If you make it bullet-proof, you make
992 it useless to the public. We are determined to keep it open," Brandenberg added.</

997 The International Finance Corporation Thursday said strong developing country financing growth continued last year but the pace will moderate slightly as others help take up the cause of private development.The World Bank affiliate that helps private enterprise in the developing world said total financing in the year to June 30
997 hit a record $3.2 billion against $2.9 in fiscal 1995.At a briefing to unveil its annual report, IFC Executive Vice President Jannik Lindbaek told reporters he expected total financing this year would be up eight to 10 percent.Lindbaek said this was somewhat slower than in recent years, noting that over
997 the past five years total financing by the agency has doubled as countries around the world rushed to embrace the free enterprise system."We see that in some of our important countries, alternative sources of financing have become available, so we are less important to some of (them)," he said, adding:
997 "we're talking about Eastern Europe and some parts of Asia." At the same time, he said the IFC was launching an initiative to expand its activities in smaller and poorer nations, targeting some 16 countries it said were undergoing particularly difficult transitions to market economies.They included Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cambodia,
997 countries in the Eastern Caribbean, Central Africa, as well as the Slovak Republic and the West Bank and Gaza."We are devoting increased resources to small and medium-sized enterprises," Lindbaek said, adding: "We continue to pioneer in new sectors and countries."The IFC also said it is working hard to ensure it
997 does not get in the way of private capital moving into developing markets by extensive consultation with the private sector.The IFC said its focus remained on meeting the needs for building private infrastructure, such as roads and bridges, as well as supporting private capital market development.In its catalyst role, it
997 said syndications with financial institutions last year reached $4.8 billion, a staggering 88 percent increase over 1995.The increase, including loans, equity deals and syndications, was 47 percent higher than 1995.It approved projects in 68 countries last year, including some 71 for sub Saharan Africa, the largest for any region.</

1002 Six electricity suppliers have been chosen for a one-year pilot program to provide retail power to four Massachusetts towns, part of the state's move toward a deregulated power market, officials said Thursday.The program, set up by Massachusetts Electric, owned by New England Electric System, is set for a January 1,
1002 1997, launch. The six participants are; AllEnergy Co, a venture between New England Electric System and Eastern Enterprises ; Enova Energy of San Diego; Northeast Utilities (NU), NU affiliate Northfield Mountain Energy; a venture between Wheled Electric Power in Boston and Cynergy in Ill., and Working Assets Green Power of
1002 San Francisco.Steven Rothstein, head of Environmental Futures, a private company that Massachusetts Electric hired to select the suppliers and the programs, said the pilot will allow up to 10,000 residential and small commercial customers to choose their electricity supplier. Mass Electric already has a separate pilot program for industrial users."We
1002 think that, depending on which supplier the customer chooses and which program they use, there are potential savings of 10 to 15 percent," Rothstein said.He added that with little publicity, his group had already received calls for more information on the pilot from more than 3,000 customers in the participating
1002 towns of Lynn, Lawrence, Northampton, and Worcester."Mass Electric knows that deregulation is coming. It's expected in early 1998...This is a year-long program. It starts in January. That will allow them to see how it will work on an experimental basis," Rothstein said.Sorting out customer billing from a variety of power
1002 generators will be one of the main tests of the program.Though customers will be able to chose their suppliers, Mass Electric will still manage the transmission and distribution of electricity on the local grid.-- Leslie Gevirtz, Boston bureau</
1003 Rules that enhance the functioning of markets do more to foster prosperity than political institutions, Cleveland Federal Reserve President Jerry Jordan said on Thursday.Days before Fed policy makers are scheduled to meet, Jordan said he would not comment on recent economic data or inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy. Instead,
1003 his address to a conference sponsored by The Cato Institute, a conservative think-tank, focused on broad historical themes.Jordan said the 20th century featured contests of ideas in the arenas of politics and economics. In politics, the conflict was between dicatorship and democracy, he said. In economics, the competition was between
1003 centrally controlled economies and free markets."The contest is over," Jordan noted. In the 21st century, democracy and markets will prevail, he said."We may be entering the golden age of capitalism ... One lesson nobody can miss is that political organizations affect prosperity," Jordan said. "Some enhance prosperity and some hinder
1003 it."Jordan said the successful public policies are those that enhance the effectiveness of markets. He said those policies include deregulation, denationalisation (privatisation), tax-reform and tax-reduction."The relative size of the government sector is shrinking everywhere in the world," Jordan said.Jordan said the job of central banks is to pursue sound money.
1003 When the value of money remains stable, it ensures that resources will not be wasted and encourages savings and investment, Jordan said.In an inflation-prone environment, businessmen try to protect profits by raising prices, Jordan said. In a stable money environment, businessmen focus on increasing efficiency and productivity, he said.Queried about
1003 the impact of electronic money, Jordan said that central banks can stabilise the value of money even when it is issued by private agencies rather than the government.--Ellen Freilich, 212 859-1660</

1008 Defence Secretary William Perry leaves on Friday for Scandanavia on a trip that will include NATO talks on a new Bosnia peacekeeping force and the signing of an agreement to stop Soviet nuclear contamination of the Arctic.He will go first to Finland, Sweden and Denmark for bilateral military talks, then
1008 to Norway for discussions with NATO and Russian defence ministers on whether an international peacekeeping force should be sent to Bosnia again next year.Perry will wind up the 10-day trip on Sept. 29.No final Bosnia decision will be made at the informal Wednesday and Thursday NATO meeting in Bergen, Norway,
1008 but defence chiefs will begin laying the groundwork for an expected go-ahead by political leaders in December.Western officials say they expect a new international military force will replace a current NATO-led peacekeeping force of over 50,000 in Bosnia next year. But Washington says it has made no decision on participation
1008 in such a force.Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodinov will attend a special session at the NATO meeting. On Thursday, Rodinov, Perry and Norway's Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo will sign an agreement under which the three nations will cooperate to halt and perhaps even clean up nuclear and other waste dumped
1008 by Russia's military in the vast Arctic.A U.S. military spokesman, who asked not to be identified, said the Russian military had dumped 16 nuclear reactor compartments in the Arctic region, six with fuel on board."The principal purpose of the AMEC (Arctic Military and Environmental Cooperation) agreement is to change the
1008 environmental conditions in the Russian Arctic region," the official said, adding that Norway was especially concerned because of its close proximity to Russia.The official said the contamination was not considered widespread or dangerous but the agreement was aimed at halting such practices as nuclear and oil dumping. It will include
1008 joint development of containers for interim storage of spent nuclear fuel and work on technology for treatment of liquid as well as solid radioactive waste.Although no final plans have been made, the signing is expected to be followed in the near future by a meeting with senior Russian military officials
1008 in Murmansk, Russia.A senior U.S. defence official said Perry looked forward to private talks with Rodinov on continued U.S. bilateral and other cooperation with Russia that grew out of close ties between Perry and former Defence Minister Pavel Grachev.Grachev was sacked by Russian President Boris Yeltsen this summer in a
1008 domestic shakeup over the military's handling of the bloody civil war in Chechnya.The Perry-Rodinov talks will include "the general state of NATO-Russia relations, the continuation of Russian cooperation within IFOR (the Bosnia peace implementation force) and development of an expanded scope for bilateral military programmes and other activities involving Russia
1008 and the United States," the official added.Before the NATO meeting, Perry will visit Helsinki on Saturday, Stockholm on Sunday and Copenhagen on Monday for bilateral talks with government and defence leaders.In Copenhagen on Tuesday morning, he will take part in a Baltic defence seminar hosted by Danish Defence Minister Has
1008 Haekkerup and including Defence Ministers Michael Portillo of Britain, Volker Ruehe of Germany and others, U.S. officials said.</
1009 The United States is continuing to work toward an agreement on International Monetary Fund gold sales, but is not clear when a pact can be reached, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Thursday."We continue to work toward that end," he told reporters after a speech to the President's Export Council.
1009 "Whether that will get done in the near future or not, I do not know."The IMF on Wednesday endorsed stepped-up aid for the world's poorest nations, including debt relief. But it stopped short of spelling out how it planned to pay for that.Rubin said that the United States believes that

But most U.S. voters so far are focusing on other matters.A recent Reuters poll found voters ranked the character and integrity of the candidates fourth most
1015 important on a list of 10 issues, behind education, the economy and crime.Just over 50 percent agreed that President Bill Clinton lacked a firm core of beliefs, while 45 percent disagreed.Still, in some three dozen follow-up interviews with voters who took part in the poll, many who expressed doubts about
1015 Clinton's character said they would vote for him anyway.Questions about Clinton's character derive from such matters as extra-marital affairs alleged to have happened when he was governor of Arkansas, his entanglement in the failed Whitewater real estate deal of the same period and his evasion of the Vietnam-era military draft
1015 as a university student.Those issues were all raised in the 1992 presidential campaign and did not seem to hurt him much then.Dole supporters are bitter about this and say it shows the country's morals are in decline. But Democrats and many independents say a man's private life is his own."I
1015 don't understand why the character issue is ignored. I think it's a big deal. I just don't know why people don't feel it's important," said Darryl Lee, a college instructor from Hilliard Ohio.That reaction -- "I can't understand it" -- is typical of the feelings of many Dole supporters."I really
1015 don't know how to explain it," said Robert Williams, a retiree from Murphysboro, Illinois. "I'm aggravated people aren't looking at Clinton's character. It says something about America.""This is the highest office in the country. A man should have some kind of character even to be considered," he said.Said Mary Bowen,
1015 another retiree from Columbus, Ohio: "I figure the American people will have lost if Clinton wins. They will have lost their sense of honour. We Americans sure have gone a long way down."Several voters said Dole should attack Clinton's character more aggressively. "I don't know why Dole can't attack Clinton
1015 and his administration, the number of his Cabinet members who have been under indictment," said Virginia Collins, a retiree from Benicia, California.On the other side are those -- the majority, by every indication -- who call Clinton's character flaws irrelevant.Their view is summed up in the phrase "nobody's perfect."Gary Drys,
1015 an undecided voter from Southgate, Michigan, said he would be looking at several factors in making up his mind, but Clinton's character would not be one of them."I'm not bothered by the allegations and scandals," Drys said. "Nobody's perfect, everybody makes mistakes. As long as he hasn't done anything crooked,
1015 it has nothing to do with running the country."Carole Baker, a factory labourer of Boyne City, Michigan, dismissed the Clinton character issue in a few terse words. "He's just human. It's nobody's business," she said.Rosalind Reider, a legal secretary from Southfield, Michigan agreed. "Most of the scandals have been overblown
1015 by the media. His sex life should be private, between him and his wife. It doesn't affect his presidency."Some Clinton backers wish he would be discreet in his personal life and express doubts about Hillary Rodham Clinton's role in the complex Whitewater financial deals, long under investigation by a special
1015 prosecutor and Congress."Whitewater -- I think Hillary is the big cheese there. She's always been an aggressive woman. But I feel that as a public figure, Clinton should be careful with his personal life," said Joyce Sloder, assistant manager of a dry cleaner in Mahomet, Illinois.In many ways Clinton's perceived
1015 character weaknesses are balanced by Dole's age of 73. Sloder was one of many voters who said bluntly of Dole, "He's too old."Susan Sosnowitz, a homemaker in the Bronx, New York, said she had backed Ronald Reagan, who was president well into his seventies, but worried about voting for someone
1015 Dole's age."I liked Reagan very much, but look what happened to him," she said, referring to the Alzheimer's Disease that has struck his since his retirement. "The same thing might happen to Dole. I think he's a little too old."</

1017 While Federal Reserve leaders seem as vigilant as ever for inflation omens, current economic and political conditions rule out an interest rate hike at next Tuesday's policy meeting, former Fed officials said.Whether the Fed has kept its focus on preemptive strikes against inflation or shifted to a new theory advocating
1017 more tolerance of price growth during economic expansions, recent data suggest no action is needed, ex-Fed officials said. "Both approaches come up with the same conclusion. There's no indication that inflation is heating up or out of control and the Fed can live with the current situation," said former Fed
1017 Governor Robert Heller.The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets next Tuesday and Fed alumni expect no increase in the 5.25 percent federal funds rate, already 2.65 percentage points above the core Consumer Price Index over the last 12 months. "I really don't see any immediate pressure to act. We've got
1017 a pretty balanced economic picture, with no sectors that are really overloaded," said Heller, now executive vice president at Fair Isaac and Co in San Rafael, California.At an annual monetary policy conference last month in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, central bankers debated a new theory dubbed "opportunistic disinflation" that seeks to
1017 overload progress toward lower inflation in times of economic weakness.This differs from a traditional Fed policy geared toward slowing the economy through higher interest rates when spurts in growth threaten to stoke faster inflation. While some Fed officials may consider the new theory during current policy deliberations, the central bank
1017 remains committed to squashing inflation whenever it appears, said former Fed Governor John LaWare."I don't think the Fed has taken its eye off the inflation concern," said LaWare, now with the Alliance for the Commonwealth in Boston.Like Heller, LaWare sees the economy slowing on its own in coming months as
1017 consumer spending and auto sales taper off. "My personal view is the third quarter will be slower than the second and the fourth quarter is liable to be significantly slower," LaWare said.Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew a robust 4.8 percent in the second quarter, well above the 2.0- to 2.5-percent
1017 range many economists consider the maximum without faster inflation.But many analysts forecast GDP growth well below 3.0 percent in the third quarter, which would minimize any increase in inflation. That scenario would also help the Fed avoid falling behind inflation as it has in many previous economic cycles, LaWare said."In
1017 the past the Fed has always worried: 'Did we wait too long to tighten?' I really don't see that happening this time," he added.With the economy sending only modest inflation signals, the November 5 presidential and Congressional elections take on added significance as the Fed debates interest rates, ex-officials said.
1017 While current Fed leaders vehemently deny politics influence monetary policy, the departed officials maintain the closeness of the elections will help convince FOMC members to hold off on raising rates next week."There's nothing in it for them to do it now," said Michael Belongia, University of Mississippi professor, who worked
1017 for 10 years as an economist at the St. Louis Fed.If Fed leaders find it necessary to raise interest rates, FOMC meetings on November 13, eight days after the elections, and December 17 offer more politically palatable timing."I would be very surprised if the Fed does anything about interest rates
1017 before the election," LaWare said. "That would just open them up to all kinds of (political) attacks."-- 212-859-1664</
1018 International Monetary Fund opened a site on the Internet Thursday providing information about the data dissemination practices of 18 member countries.The site lists information such as the frequency, schedule and types of economic and financial data released on a regular basis by the countries, which have subscribed to the fund's
1018 "Special Data Dissemination Standard."The site does not include the countries' actual data, although it lists contacts for obtaining the information. "For a long time we have been trying to press countries to report to us on a more timely basis, more information, and based on good statistical systems," Jack Boorman,
1018 director of the IMF's policy and review department, said at a press briefing here.The Mexican peso crisis highlighted the need for timely and accurate data about developing countries, Boorman added."Good statistical citizenship helps to inform markets," Boorman said. "The whole purpose of this system is to help that process, to
1018 make sure that markets are getting better data in a timely way." The countries on the site are Argentina, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, malaysia, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Peru, the Philippines, Singapore, Slovenia, Switzerland, Thailand, the United Kingdom and the United States.By next week, information about another eight countries
1018 is expected to be added. Those countries are Croatia, France, Hungary, Japan, Poland, South Africa, Sweden and turkey. Another eight countries have subscribed to the data standard but are not ready to go online. Those are Austria, Australia, Belgium, Chile, Columbia, Iceland, Israel, and Lithunia.The special standard is being phased
1018 in over two years. Subscribing countries agreed to meet the standards by December 31, 1998.Discussions are ongoing with other countries that have not yet agreed to subscribe, including Germany, John McLenaghan, director of the IMF statistics department, said.IMF officials said the site could eventually include direct links to countries' data
1018 or other kinds of information."We're starting something which while it has a very specific content and frame at the present time, has potential for going in directions that none of us perhaps quite see at the present time," Boorman said.--Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312</

1021 despite news that Pemex recently restarted two units at the Cactus plant that were undamaged in the July 26th blaze. Roberts said he hoped Glickman would change the rule before the final version was published, saying he expected 8.3 million acres would be removed from the program under the proposal."It baffles me how a Secretary of Agriculture from Kansas could come to the conclusion that the erosion
1027 and wildlife benefits of the past 11 years should be discarded so easily over vast areas of the central United States," he said.Deputy Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger told the hearing the department hoped to keep the program at the 36.4 million acre maximum set by Congress by enrolling more fragile
1027 land to replace acreage that was removed. Roberts slammed USDA for delay, saying that under the best circumstances, farmers would not know the contents of the final rule until January to March next year, too late for spring planted crops.Rominger told reporters the department had written the regulation as fast
1027 as possible after the farm bill was passed, but faced other farm bill priorities such as implementation of the new law's market transition payments.He said farmers who had CRP acres expiring at the end of this month were still able to extend their contracts, which he said gave them an
1027 extra year to decide whether to re-enroll the land.</

1039 New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough said Thursday he does not see bank reserves falling to a point where they would impair the Federal Reserve's ability to conduct monetary policy.Asked whether he saw reserves falling to a point where it would be difficult to conduct monetary policy, McDonough
1039 replied "no I don't, I think the main effect of sweep accounts has already been seen and it has not caused us problems in managing monetary policy."McDonough told a conference on electronic money and banking that if banks' reserves ever got that low then the Fed might have to come
1039 up with some different methodology, for example paying interest on reserves.He said that a Group of Ten report had concluded that the likely evolution of electronic money would not be so rapid as to have a significant effect on the ability to carry out monetary policy."Thus far we have always
1039 been able to figure out a way to conduct monetary policy and to be able to accomodate the creativity in the financial services sector, and I have every reason to think we will be able to do that in the future," McDonough said.</

1055 House and Senate negotiators reached agreement Thursday on two key health care reforms -- to expand insurance coverage for mental illness and to give new mothers the option of a 48-hour hospital stay.Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle told reporters the agreement provided for both to take effect Jan. 1, 1998.
1055 But no agreement was reached on a Senate-passed plan to provide federally-funded health care for children of veterans with spina bifida, he said. While health plans will not be required to cover mental illness, those that do will no longer be permitted to set lower maximum coverage amounts for mental
1055 health treatment. If there is no lifetime limit on physical care, none will be permitted on mental health care. The compromise exempts companies with 50 or fewer employees.Health insurers will be required to offer new mothers and their babies at least a 48-hour hospital stay after a normal birth and
1055 a 96-hour stay after a Caesarean section. They will also be banned from offering any cash or rebates to women who choose a shorter hospitalization.Both provisions had passed the Senate with broad bipartisan support but had not cleared the House. Earlier this week the House endorsed the health care reforms,
1055 but senior Republicans objected that the issues had not been thoroughly studied.The delay in the effective date until January 1998 was designed to give Congress time to review the issues and possibly revise the laws next year.</

1062 Total world inventories of silver bullion and coins, excluding metal held by governments, are probably between 780.3 million and 1.08 billion ounces, CPM Group said in its third-quarter 1996 Silver Review."The single most important issue concerning the outlook for silver prices is how much metals exists in unreported inventories of
1062 bullion and coins," CPM managing director Jeffrey Christian said.From 1990 to 1995, silver inventories have been drawn down by about 827.2 million ounces, according to CPM. Investors, who have been net sellers of silver from their holdings since 1989, have sold about 790.2 million ounces of silver on a net
1062 basis since 1989.This year, another 195.2 million ounces of silver inventories are expected to be used in jewelry, photographic papers and film, silver decorative objects and a range of industrial products."The question facing the silver market is how much silver still exists in inventories around the world and how much
1062 longer the silver market can continue to live off these stocks," Christian said. "There is no definitive answer to these questions, given the secrecy that surrounds silver ownership and the lack of comprehensive physical records," Christian said.The CPM Group study presents a range estimates as to how much silver is
1062 in these inventories, broken down into various locations, bullion coins and inferred and unreported inventories in individual countries.A sizable portion of the unreported silver is believed to be held in the vaults of Wilmington Trust Co in Delaware.Wilmington Trust has been approved as a licensed COMEX silver depositary, effective Jan
1062 1, 1997.Before that, Wilmington Trust will begin reporting the amounts of silver is has in its vaults that are eligible and suitable for COMEX delivery.--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk 212-859-1641</

1067 The European Union reverted to granting subsidies to its main grain exporters for the first time in more than a year on Thursday, farm officials said.It agreed to assist commercial exports of 237,470 tonnes of wheat to a world grain market where prices are now sagging below European levels after
1067 soaring to records earlier this year.Subsidies were suspended in early 1995 and the EU even imposed a tax on exports for a while when global market supply tightened as grain stocks fell to 20-year lows.But several regions including the EU have reported bumper harvests this year, prompting the return to
1067 subsides.This time round, however, the EU has tried to steer clear of a trade spat by granting fewer subsidies than expected, after warnings of retaliation by the United States if it doles out too much."This is not as big a sale as we expected. They obviously don't want to start
1067 undercutting the United States," a Geneva-based grain trader said.The EU and U.S. are among the biggest suppliers of wheat and competed savagely up to the mid-1990s by throwing billions of dollars in aid to help exports, driving down world prices.Each side blamed the other for starting a price war.In a

1080 champion of free trade, was seeking EU acceptance of a range of issues to be tackled at the Singapore meeting.He was anxious to assure the ministers that he was not seeking a mandate to begin a new round of trade negotiations, rather take existing deals further.An EU official said Brittan's
1080 proposals had been well received by the ministers, but it was clear they were concerned to protect their domestic industries and markets.EU sources said Portuguese trade minister Fernando Freire Sousa warned that Lisbon was not prepared to jeopardise its textile and garment industries and urged the EU not to make
1080 further concessions to exporters from developing countries.But his was a rare dissenting voice from an audience that generally embraced Brittan's philosophy.Brittan told a news conference he was prepared to come up with a new European offer to try rekindle interest in a global agreement on telecoms.Negotiations for an agreement, due
1080 to be settled next year, have stalled because of Washington's dissatisfaction at offers from Europe and Japan to open their markets to U.S. products.Brittan said the EU was unlikely to make a big issue of labour standards at the Singapore meeting, believing instead that the International Labour Organisation was the
1080 best forum for dealing with the issue.Developing nations, particularly those from Asia, are concerned that Western demands for international labour standards will reduce their competetive edge.British Trade Minister Ian Lang urged the Commission to step up efforts to conclude the Information Technology Agreement between the EU, U.S. and Japan, saying

1083 NATO planners are developing a "super" Partnership for Peace to embrace countries likely to be left out of the first wave of expansion of the alliance, its Secretary-General and Western diplomats said on Thursday.With the Western alliance likely to accept some former communist countries into its fold next year, diplomats
1083 say some non-aligned nations and unsuccessful NATO candidates may join a tighter grouping of would-be members and affiliates.Russia could also join this intensified Partnership for Peace -- dubbed "PfP-Two", "Enhanced PfP" or "PfP Plus" -- which aims to boost non-members' military cooperation and political contact with NATO, a U.S. diplomat
1083 told Reuters."Let's include the Russians," said Derek Shearer, U.S. ambassador to Finland.The plan aims to demonstrate to Russia that NATO is not belligerent and ease the concerns of countries that may fall into a security "grey zone" after the alliance expands."A 'PfP Plus' should generate the necessary reassurance that the
1083 security of an enlarged NATO and its partners remains closely linked," said NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.Of the 27 current members of the PfP scheme aimed at uniting former European foes, Shearer said between 15 and 20 could join a super PfP, which could involve specific liaison officers and working groups
1083 and would be based on charters."It's just a notion of enhancing PfP to show where we're going in Europe," he said.The scheme builds on a milestone speech by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in Stuttgart earlier this month in which he outlined a vision of a New Atlantic Community
1083 which would erase former Cold War barriers.Christopher spoke of forming a New Atlantic Partnership Council based on a charter between NATO and Russia and said the alliance should involve non-members in the PfP programme.NATO's Solana, in a speech to the international institute for strategic studies (IISS), said the current scheme
1083 was already the most successful military cooperation programme in Europe's history."But (it) has to be upgraded and deepened to reflect the new situation which will exist after NATO enlargement," he said."This could entail, among other things, offering interested partners greater involvement in NATO military planning, activities and structures as well
1083 as in consultations with the alliance."Czechoslovakia, Hungary and Poland are widely regarded as top of the list for inclusion in an expanded NATO. Other former Soviet Bloc states including the Baltic countries, Romania and Bulgaria are less likely to make it into the first round."You don't want them feeling this
1083 means 'no' forever," Shearer said.The scheme could also embrace non-aligned and neutral countries -- Finland, Sweden and Austria -- which do not currently seek NATO membership, offsetting concerns that NATO expansion may be seen as re-creating "zones of influence".For instance, Finland, Sweden and the three Baltic states, Estonia, Latvia and
1083 Lithuania, have said expansion in central Europe may leave former Soviet satellites in a security void which, under some circumstances, Russia could try to fill."We want to see the avoidance of the grey area by the development of a super-PfP," another Western diplomat said.With Europe still in transition from the
1083 Cold War period, the plan aims to let countries address threats like terrorism and drug-trafficking, which are now more likely causes of instability than invasion, diplomats said.</
