1412 at or near the site they are being treated for their underlying disease and overcome resistance to patient referral by specialists.Neurex said it expects these studies to be initiated soon, widening the clinical trial centers working on SNX-111 and providing further support for a filing with the FDA for chronic

1427 U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Thursday that he does not see any signs of inflation heating up."I don't see evidence of it," he told reporters following a speech to a Treasury Department confernce on electronic money.Rubin also said he expects Treasury to launch its first issue of inflation-indexed debt
1427 early next year. Rubin pointed to a variety of reasons why he expects U.S. inflation to stay low -- large excess capacity in Europe, excess capacity in Japan, globalization and technological advances.He called U.S. economic growth solid."Wages are going up, but inflation has not been reignited," he added.Asked if that
1427 meant that the administration was at odds with the Federal Reserve, Rubin declined comment. Some Fed officials are pushing for higher U.S. interest rates because of fears that the pickup in wage growth will spur inflation. Rubin said he saw a "fair chance" that Treasury's plan to issue inflation-indexed bonds
1427 might increase U.S. savings.Treasury expects to announce "in the reasonably near future" the terms and other details of its first issue, he added.That would pave the way for the first issue of the new type of debt early next year.</

1429 Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Thursday the United States must avoid "inappropriate regulation" of electronic money in order to allow the free flow of innovation.Speaking to a conference on the future of electronic money, the term used to describe commerce that is largely transacted by computers, Rubin said a
1429 goal was to support its development and to make sure people feel confident about it."The last thing we want to do is to unnecessarily impede the development of innovations which are going to be so beneficial to our economy and our society," he said.But he said electronic money poses difficult
1429 consumer protection issues, including avoiding monopoly, ensuring that adequate information to make choices was available, security was maintained and that issuers were financially sound.There also were issues of counterfeiting, money laundering, piracy, civil fraud and the activities of computer hackers that merit attention, Rubin added.Nonetheless, he said: "Government should protect
1429 consumers to the extent possible and enforce the law, but tread as lightly as possible." Rubin announced at the conference, organized by the Treasury Department, that a consumer electronic task force was being set up to investigate issues arising from new payments systems.He said the task force will include respresentatives
1429 from the Federal Reserve Board, the Federal Deposit Insurance Cop. the Federal Trade Commission and Treasury.</

1431 Neoprobe Corp on Thursday said it signed a deal under which U.S. Surgical Corp gained exclusive worldwide sales and marketing rights for Neoprobe's RIGS products for surgical cancer detection.The agreement, which excludes Korea, Thailand, Taiwan and Singapore, became effective September 18, Neoprobe said. 1431 the majority of which will be paid upon U.S. and European marketing approval of RIGScan CR49, Neoprobe's first RIGS product, for surgical detection of metastatic colorectal cancer.No exchange of equity is involved in the agreement, Dublin, Ohio-based Neoprobe said.In an interview, Neoprobe president David Bupp said the the company expected
1431 to file with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the fourth quarter, with final approval possible in 1997's third quarter. Final European approval could come in the first half of next year, he said. Neoprobe retains primary responsibility for product development and manufacturing.U.S. Surgical will provide surgeon training and
1431 professional education worldwide for RIGS products, upon marketing approval, and will help fund future research.It also has has options on future RIGS surgical detection products for the next five years, Neoprobe said.Bupp said future products would include those for the detection of breast, prostate and upper gastro-intestinal cancers. Bupp said
1431 Neoprobe will book sales of the products, with U.S. Surgical getting a "sales commission" in the form of a percentage of revenues. He declined to give the percentage.In a statement, Norwalk, Conn.-based U.S. Surgical said it expects the deal to be accretive within the first year.The RIGS system works by
1431 injecting patients with Neoprobe's low-energy radioactive drug that targets cancer cells. 1431 of $600 million for the colorectal product.Under the deal Neoprobe will know get information on RIGS customers, who will be potential buyers for the company's future therapy products, Bupp said. 1432 a control valve that was left valve partially open by the lightning strike.The problem valve caused the main feed pump to fail, which in turn, tripped the unit out of service, she said.Comanche Peak 2 could begin dispatch power to the regional grid later today, Nichols said."It usually takes 24
1432 to 36 hours to return to full output," she said.The adjoining Comanche Peak 1, which was unaffected by the Wednesday's lightning storm, was operating fully at its 1,150 MW capacity.Texas Utilities had no trouble meeting its electricity demand due to unseasonably cool temperatures in the northern and central Texas regions,

1460 with no caveats, Holland said in his order."At this point, it is clear that the least complicated and least costly means of providing plaintiffs with some meaningful security for timely payment of their judgment is an automatically reneweable, irrevocable letter of credit" issued by one of more of the banks
1460 with which Exxon does business, he said.The letter must assure payment of the fine within 60 days of a mandate issued by the court of appeals, Holland said."That's exactly what we wanted," said Dave Oesting, a lead attorney for thousands of fishermen, Alaska Natives, property owners and others who sued
1460 Exxon over the Valdez disaster.A letter of credit issued by one or more banks insulates the plaintiffs from any future Exxon financial problems, he said, adding that was the security plaintiffs were seeking."I want a divorce from Exxon," he said.Wednesday's order was one of the final steps in the complicated
1460 Exxon Valdez litigation, which involved trials in federal and state courts and settlements with various groups.The $5 billion punitive fine was ordered by a U.S. District Court jury, which ruled in 1994 that Exxon and its former supertanker captain, Joseph Hazelwood, had been reckless in their actions leading to the
1460 1989 oil disaster.In addition to issuing the largest punitive fine ever assessed against a corporation, the jury ordered Exxon to pay $287 million to compensate an estimated 10,000 commercial salmon and herring fishermen for spill-related losses.Oesting said he expected Holland to enter formal judgment on the verdicts and settlements soon,
1460 paving the way for payment or an Exxon appeal. Exxon has vowed to attempt to have the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals overturn the trial outcome.The disaster occurred on March 24, 1989, when the Exxon Valdez supertanker grounded on a reef in Alaska's icy Prince William Sound and spilled 11

1461 trade deficit as a percentage of GDP is considerably lower now than it was in the worst years of the 80s.""If we continue with our strategy of deficit reduction, one of the benefits ... is that it is likely to be associated with a reduction over the long run in
1461 the trade deficit," he said. The Commerce Department said earlier on Wednesday that the U.S. trade deficit soared in July to its highest level in more than eight years as imports surged and foreign sales shrank for a second straight month.The steep 42.6 percent jump in the July deficit to
1461 $11.68 billion from $8.19 billion in June was caused partly by weaker sales of U.S.-made commercial aircraft, as well as brisk demand for Japanese cars and costlier oil."Next month could be one way or another," Stiglitz said. "You just don't put a lot of emphasis on any one month's data."

1465 The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday endorsed stepped-up aid for the world's poorest nations, but stopped short of spelling out how it planned to pay for that.The decision, announced by IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, effectively left open the question of whether the Fund would sell some of its gold
1465 to help the world's poor."The IMF is fully ready to assist its low-income members well into the next millenium," Camdessus said in a brief statement. 1465 gold if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.Wednesday's decision by the IMF board puts the proposal on the
1465 back burner for now. Although the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee may take up the issue again at a meeting on September 29, an agreement at that time seems unlikely. Camdessus said in his statement that the IMF board had reached "understandings" to ensure stepped-up IMF assistance to the world's poorest
1465 countries.The board, which first met on the issue last Friday then took it up again today, discussed two inter-related initiatives to help poor countries -- beefing up its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) and participating in a multilateral debt relief plan.ESAF, which lends money at virtually no interest charge to
1465 the world's poorest nations, would be the vehicle through which the IMF would take part in the latter initiative. "I am pleased to announce that the executive board has reached understandings to ensure permanent continuation of the enhanced structural adjustment facility ... and allow the IMF to participate in the
1465 ... initiative for the highly-indebted poor countries," Camdessus said in his statement.He added that he warmly welcomed the "cooperative spirit" in the board that made the understandings possible.An IMF spokesman declined to elaborate further.</

1469 Senior economic advisor to conservative New Democracyparty leader Miltiadis EvertTHE GREEK ELECTIONS AND THE ECONOMYThe snap elections of September 1996 have been prompted by the fact that the economic policy of the ruling party has reached a dead end.While the convergence program predicted a fall of inflation to 5.0 percent
1469 by the end of 1996, with concomitant falls in interest rates, the outcome is likely to be three percentage points higher, 8.0 percent at best.This failure is extremely serious, as the main strategy of the convergence program was based on the fall of nominal interest rates, given that every fall
1469 in interest rates by one percentage point reduces the borrowing requirememnt of the general government by about 0.8 percent of GDP.Given this year's overrun, a fall by more than 5.0 percentage points is actually required. This amounts to 1.5 billion drachmas, and is clearly unattainable, even if taxation were to
1469 rise sharply and all margins for reductions in government reductions in government expenditure were exhausted.Given this situation the government decided to go for early elections. Having failed to bring about a substantial increase in the primary surplus of the general government, the PASOK government has exhausted all the margins that
1469 were created by the policy of 1990-93 period.These margins have allowed inflation to fall from 23.9 percent in November 1990 to 10.2 percent in March 1994 and 8.5 percent in August 1996, the borrowing requirement of the general government to fall from 14 percent in 1989 to 11.2 percent in
1469 1993 and about 9.0 percent in 1996 and the public debt to GDP ratio to be stabilised at about 111 percent of GDP in 1993.New initiatives are now required after the lack of underlying progress in 1994-96. New Democracy, the opposition party, has a program centred around reductions in primary
1469 expenditure, privatisations and better use of the EU Community Support Framework.On the other hand, the socialist PASOK party promises to keep government expenditure roughly at the same levels. Therefore, the only way to reduce the deficit with a PASOK government would be higher tax rates.</

1484 Euro-MP Edward McMillan-Scott said the parliament's 173 Christian Democrat and Conservative members backed the call.He said they were "profoundly concerned" about recent developments in Turkey, including the arrest of deputies, the treatment of political prisoners, government repression of the media and its stance on certain issues of foreign policy.Seven of
1484 the parliament's eight political groups are backing a joint resolution, due to go to a vote on Thursday, which demands an immediate block on all EU aid to Turkey, bar funding for projects to promote democracy and respect for human rights.The EU plans to set aside 375 million Ecus ($470
1484 million) between 1996 and 2000 to help Turkey put in place a customs union with the 15-member bloc.Turkey is also eligible for substantial financing from the EU's MEDA programme, through which 410 million Ecus have been made available for the bloc's Mediterranean neighbours in 1996.The EU could allocate as much
1484 as 842 million to this group of countries in 1997.</
1485 The pilot of a Swissair jumbo jet suffered two heart attacks over Russia on Wednesday night, forcing the plane to make an emergency landing in Helsinki, the airline said on Thursday.The pilot of the Boeing 747 was taken to the Helsinki University Central Hospital while the 258 passengers spent the
1485 night in a hotel, a spokesman for the carrier said.A hospital spokesman declined to specify the pilot's illness, but added he was in stable condition and in no grave danger.The pilot suffered an initial heart attack some four hours after the plane left Zurich, bound for Beijing.The plane's co-pilot took
1485 over the controls after the attack, while the pilot was attended to by a doctor on board.After the pilot suffered a second heart attack, Swissair decided to make an emergency landing in Helsinki.The passengers will continue their journey to Beijing later today with a new crew, the Swissair spokesman added.</

1488 British construction-to-cables group BICC Plc made a 170 million pound ($265 million) cash call to investors on Thursday, just one month after reporting a plunge into first half loss.The company unveiled plans for a 2-for-11 rights issue of new shares at 270 pence per share to help fund investment opportunities
1488 worth more than 200 million pounds ofIt also said it was likely to maintain the final dividend at 8.5 pence per share, taking the year's total to 12.5 pence."The time is right to focus on the future development of the business and significantly accelerate the pace of its investment to
1488 facilitate faster growth," chairman Viscount Weir said.The group plans investment of around 140 million pounds in optical fibres, Brand-Rex data communications cables and high voltage cabling.An extra 40 million is earmarked for the Asia-Pacific region and 35 million for equity investment in infrastructure projects which require private finance both in
1488 Britain and abroad.Chief executive Alan Jones said investment was needed and, with gearing levels at around 80 percent, a cash call was considered the best option."I've been under pressure from our managing directors to make some investments," he said.The money will be focused in the higher-margin products on the cable
1488 side of the business, adding extra capacity in key regions.Jones said the investment would make the group's base "much more sound" and better able to withstand fierce pricing pressures and competition in the mass cable market.BICC has undertaken a strategic shake-up for the past year in an effort to make
1488 itself more dynamic. In August it reported a half-year loss of two million pounds, skidding from a 60 million profit last year due to restructuring costs.Analysts expressed concern then that as national utility and telecom companies were privatised, cosy relationships with cable suppliers would end.They felt the tough pricing climate
1488 could continue for up to two years, leading players like BICC to concentrate on higher margin products.BICC shares fell 2.5 pence after the news to 314 pence by 1410 GMT. ($1=.6412 Pound)</
1489 By Nicholas Doughty, Diplomatic CorrespondentNATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Thursday the alliance would have to remain engaged in Bosnia beyond the end of this year, probably with a smaller military force that would include U.S. troops.Solana's comments, in an interview with Reuters and in a speech in London, are
1489 the latest and clearest signal that a continued Western military presence will be needed to shore up the fragile peace in Bosnia -- despite last week's elections.Under the terms of the Dayton peace agreement, the one-year mandate of the current NATO-led peace force of some 55,000 troops runs out in
1489 December.While some Western countries have mentioned the possibility of leaving a smaller force in place next year, perhaps numbering 20,000 troops, the subject is sensitive in the United States ahead of presidential elections there on November 5."I believe that the international community, including NATO, must remain engaged in Bosnia beyond
1489 this first year...," Solana said in a speech to the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) in London."On the security side, there may well be a requirement for a continued military presence in Bosnia...albeit smaller and for a strictly limited term."A new force would "assist progress towards stability in the
1489 region and provide an environment of security while durable institutions are established and the parties fully assume their responsibilities".Solana told Reuters that the subject would be discussed at a meeting of defence ministers in the Norwegian city of Bergen next week, but that no decisions would be reached there by
1489 the 16-nation Western alliance.Solana said he thought most countries would be "generous enough to continue" if a continued military presence in Bosnia were needed. But the deployment would have to include U.S. forces and would be limited to no more than one year."I don't think if there is a follow-on
1489 force of some nature...it will be longer than a year. The responsibility is now with the parties."European allies insist that Washington take part in any continued deployment to avoid a repeat of the transatlantic rows that marred Western policy during the Bosnian war."I do think the countries which have been
1489 participating should continue," Solana said. Asked if that also meant U.S. participation, he replied: "Sure".President Bill Clinton originally promised that U.S. troops would be in Bosnia for no longer than a year but U.S. officials say privately that is almost certain to change -- although not before the November presidential
1489 election.Britain and others have warned against an indefinite commitment of troops to Bosnia, saying that it is now time for the Serbs, Croats and Moslems to rebuild their country and work together after last week's elections.Solana's comments suggested that Bosnia will get one more year of stability, enforced by Western
1489 troops, to give peaceful cooperation a chance.The alliance has already agreed that it will not start major troop withdrawals until delayed municipal elections have taken place, probably in November or December.NATO decided on Wednesday to set up a new headquarters in Bosnia, ostensibly to oversee the year-end withdrawal. But it
1489 could also have the dual role of pulling out existing troops while coordinating a smaller replacement force.</
1490 Kevin Maxwell, youngest son of media magnate Robert Maxwell, whose death in 1991 led to the collapse of his business empire, will not face a second trial on fraud charges, a judge ruled on Thursday.Judge John Buckley said a further trial "would be unfair, so unfair as to amount to
1490 an abuse of power of the court", adding that he had come to the clear view that the proceedings served no further public interest.His decision effectively ended five years of controversy over hundreds of millions of pounds (dollars) which were found missing from Maxwell company pension funds after Robert Maxwell
1490 disappeared from his yacht in the Atlantic Ocean."It is an enormous victory for commonsense and humanity. I'm enormously relieved, immensely relieved and delighted," an ecstatic and clearly stunned Kevin told a pack of reporters outside the court."It's a hell of a moment. Quite clearly this was a very powerful and
1490 uncompromising judgement. Thank God he stopped it."In January, Kevin, his brother Ian Maxwell, and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of conspiring to defraud pension funds after an eight-month trial."My immediate reaction is not one of anger or bitterness and I don't want to use words like vindictive or
1490 vendetta -- let other people do that," said Kevin.Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) sought to bring charges in a second trial against Kevin Maxwell, Trachtenberg, and two former Maxwell executives, Albert Fuller and Michael Stoney.All had proceedings stopped against them under the ruling.The judgement brings into question how the SFO,
1490 set up to deal with major financial fraud, will act in the future."We have reached the end of the legal process," said SFO director George Staple in a statement. "The law does not provide any avenue of appeal. There are serious implications for the prosecution of the largest and most
1490 complex criminal cases."Sources close to the SFO said the judge's decision would put it in an impossible position when it came to tackling the largest and most important frauds and reopen the debate over whether juries are qualified to hear complex fraud cases.The judge said that the factor that had
1490 influenced him most was, "(that) the essential criminality of the prosecution's case was before the jury in the first trial.""Broadly speaking, if any jury was going to convict in this case, surely it would have been on the pension counts (at the first trial)," he told the court.Kevin Maxwell, 37,
1490 had taken his case before the judge to argue that the impending second trial was "oppressive".At a news conference, Kevin thanked the judge and said he would not consider a lawsuit against the prosecutors. "I have an absolute horror of litigation," he said. "I have no intention of going into
1490 a court of law."Lawyers expressed surprise when the SFO said it wanted a second trial and many said the organisation was trying to salvage its own reputation but, on Thursday, the judge said the verdict in the first trial must now be accepted."In a notorious case, people looking on will
1490 have their own theories, some better informed than others. But, since we have a jury system we should all accept their verdicts," Buckley said. "In the Maxwell case that is overdue. I accept the jury's verdict. These proceedings are stayed."The investigation and first trial set the record for the most
1490 expensive criminal case in Britain this century with final costs estimated at around 30 million pounds ($46 million).Kevin became Britain's biggest bankrupt in 1992 with debts of over 400 million pounds ($630 million at current rates). He was released from bankruptcy in 1995.Kevin -- whose ambition in life had been
1490 to follow his father -- always denied conspiring to defraud by misusing pension fund money to prop up the indebted companies.He said his father, whom he has described as as bully, used pension funds just like any other assets in his corporate empire -- as a source of cash to
1490 be moved from one company to another.Kevin told the first trial that he and his brother had merely obeyed their father's orders.</

1492 Six elder statesmen of Britain's ruling Conservatives united on Thursday to warn Prime Minister John Major to hold firm against increasingly vocal demands from the party's right wing to oppose European integration.In a letter to the Independent newspaper, the six, headed by former Prime Minister Edward Heath, wrote: "To countenance
1492 withdrawal from the European Union would be to court disaster."The letter was published the day after Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind delighted the so-called Eurosceptics with a warning that the EU's plan for a single currency could split the bloc for the foreseeable future.Party officials rushed to deny that the contrasting
1492 tone of the two contributions to the European debate signalled civil war had broken out again in the party over relations with Brussels.Anxious to play down internal rows with a general election due by next May, party chairman Brian Mawhinney insisted all wings of the party were united."Both Mr Rifkind
1492 and the grandees as you call them were reaffirming and being supportive of the government's position," he told a questioner at a news conference.Mawhinney was asked repeatedly by journalists whether the Conservatives might change their wait-and-see attitude and rule out joining a single currency in the next five-year parliament.He declined
1492 to answer the question directly but insisted: "The position of the government is quite clear."Three of Rifkind's Foreign Office predecessors -- Lord Peter Carrington, Lord Geoffrey Howe and Douglas Hurd -- signed the letter which said: "For us now to rule out British membership of a single currency would be
1492 to betray our national interest."Howe denied on BBC Radio that he and his colleagues were causing splits in the party."We are not creating the division. The truth is that all those who have led the Conservative Party from the days of (former war leader Winston) Churchill onwards have been clear
1492 about the need for Britain to be involved in Europe,"The other signatories were Lord William Whitelaw, who was deputy prime minister under Margaret Thatcher, and Sir Leon Brittan, one of Britain's EU Commissioners. Thatcher is flag-bearer for the Euro-sceptic right-wingers.In an attempt to hold his party together, Prime Minister John
1492 Major has said he will decide whether to join a single currency when the full plan for it is developed -- after the next election. He has also pledged a referendum on the issue.John Redwood, one of the leading right-wing contenders to succeed Major, supported Rifkind's warning."I say three cheers
1492 for Malcolm Rifkind for beginning to set out our stall," Redwood, who last year challenged Major for the party leadership, told Channel Four television."I think the foreign secretary has looked at the damage this scheme is now doing and has looked at the strong opinion in the Conservative Party, which
1492 is that we want a common market and not a common government."</

1500 As Finland hovers on the brink of entry to Europe's exchange rate mechanism, many analysts here believe the perceived medium-term economic or political benefits of bringing the markka into the current ERM regime are illusory.The luxury of huge 15 percent ERM fluctuation bands makes the chosen central exchange rate little
1500 more than a symbolic target. As a result, there is little or no exchange discipline or currency-risk reduction inherent in the existing system.Moreover, many analysts believe that maintenance of 15 percent ERM bands alone will not be sufficient to satisfy the Maastricht criterion on exchange rate stability prior to European
1500 monetary union. Hence, the political imperative of entering the ERM quickly is also notional at best."An ERM with 15 percent bands is of no practical value and and it's not even clear whether its necessary or sufficient for qualification for EMU," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS
1500 Ltd.Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is pushing for a peg, in a bid for tight links with the EU to ensure closer political connections with the west for Finland, which joined the EU in 1995 after decades in the shadow of the former Soviet Union.But the central bank has been
1500 reluctant, with officials voicing concerns that a link may expose the markka to speculative pressures and fuel volatility.The markka rallied to 2.99 per mark early on Thursday, its strongest level in nine months, as speculation about the exact timing of ERM entry intensified.The chairman of the Bank of Finland's board
1500 of parliamentary supervisors IIkka Kanerva said ERM entry was unlikely this month, putting the market focus on early October as likely date for a joint lira and markka ERM fixing.Yet, analysts questioned the logic of trading on back of speculation about the entry level."The focus on the central rate in
1500 a 15-percent-band system is a little misplaced," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "With such wide margins of error it's hard to see why ERM entry would change anyone's investment decision within Finland or toward Finland."Even if Finland attempts to informally target narrower 2.25 percent bands,
1500 that some analysts believe will be necessary to satisfy the EMU criteria, the chances of holding the erratic markka in those bands over two years is slight, they said."In our view, the 2.25 percent rule will be used by the EU as a way of identifying the countries who will
1500 have the least problem with fixed exchange rates and moving to EMU in 1999," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch.That would exclude Spain and Italy, for example, from the first move to EMU, even if they do manage to meet a relaxed interpretation of the other Maastricht criteria,
1500 he said."Finland would have severe problems holding a narrow band regime for long, mainly because it is subject to strong exchange rate shocks that do not effect the rest of the European core," said Prendergast.The Finnish economy, and hence the competitiveness of the markka, is heavily dependent on volatile commodity
1500 prices, with paper and pulp products accounting for about 40 percent of its export revenue.This is a stark contrast to the core European currencies to which Finland intends to peg the markka closely. In 1994 and 1995, for example, the markka was one of the strongest currencies in the world,
1500 in contrast to exchange rate weakness against the German mark elsewhere in Europe.Conversely, the markka's devaluation against its European currency unit peg in 1992, prior to its later flotation, was a precursor to the exit of sterling and the lira from the ERM later that year.Moreover, neighbouring Sweden is Finland's
1500 biggest trade competitor for pulp products and it is currently deeply divided about the merits of joining either the ERM or EMU."Finland is to Sweden what Ireland is to the UK, for example, and it is hard to imagine the markka not being heavily influenced by the swings of a
1500 floating Swedish crown given such trade interdependence," said Meggyesi at Deutsche.Even as Finnish industry chiefs protest the recent rise of the markka, analysts say Finland's strong current account surplus, balanced budget and low inflation argue for an even stronger markka right now. Deutsche argues for an equilibrium level as low
1500 at 2.85 per mark, for example.But Von Maydell at UBS said that while there may be a good case for saying a central rate about 3.00 per mark is fair value right now, that may not be the case over the full course of the economic cycle.</

1546 Robert Maxwell was one of Britain's most powerful tycoons who built a media and publishing empire almost single-handed and dealt ruthlessly with enemies.A bully at home, he made his large family suffer -- both before and after his death -- through his lust for deal-making and love of grandiose gestures.Five
1546 years after his body was found floating in the Atlantic Ocean, mystery still surrounds the circumstances of his death and the loss of millions of pounds from Maxwell company pension funds.On Thursday, Maxwell's youngest son Kevin was told he would not face a second trial on fraud-related charges, clearing his
1546 name and ending legal attempts to get to the bottom of one of the biggest corporate collapses in recent British history.Robert Maxwell's reputation and business methods came under the microscope during and earlier eight-month fraud trial of Kevin and his brother Ian. They were both acquitted in January of conspiring
1546 to defraud pension funds."Basically he was a man possessed by business. It consumed his whole life," Kevin said of his father during the trial."He wasn't motivated by money, he was motivated by power."Robert Maxwell was capable of being extremely charming, likeable and generous. He also bullied his employees and family,
1546 the court heard."He was somebody for whom the law was a weapon to be used, like every other weapon in business. He would stretch the law as far as it could go to achieve his business ends," Kevin said.Robert Maxwell, born Jan Lodvik Hoch on June 10, 1923, was the
1546 son of Jewish peasants from the Czechoslovakian province of Ruthenia, one of the poorest parts of Europe.He escaped the Nazi Holocaust which claimed his relatives, went to Britain and emerged from World War Two with a British army medal for gallantry.Although he had little formal schooling, Maxwell's lack of education
1546 did not stop him from building and controlling an empire with two major public companies and 400 private firms.In 1971 a Department of Trade and Industry report said Maxwell was "not a person who can be relied upon to exercise proper stewardship of a publicly quoted company".But he clawed his
1546 way back. By the 1980s he was a huge success, famous for his girth, big cigars and a flamboyant lifestyle including a luxury yacht and a helicopter."Given his weight and bulk he could and would dominate every meeting he attended," said Kevin.Colleagues and associates claimed he controlled his directors and
1546 employees by shouting and pounding his fists."He was capable of dealing with complex issues one after the other very quickly and able to make decisions quickly. He combined, I have to say, a bullying technique with a separate technique of enormous charm," said Peter Walsh, the chief auditor of the
1546 Maxwell companies.Maxwell's long-suffering French-born wife and mother of his nine children, Elisabeth, described him as a power-crazy man who was particularly strict with his offspring.Although he groomed his children to help him with his business he resented any initiative they took."Bob wanted to keep his finger on the pulse. He
1546 couldn't bear to have any power taken away from him," she told the court.Maxwell exercised unilateral control over his companies for years. He used pension funds as liquid cash to invest in other businesses and invested funds from some of his companies into others, a practice called "self-investment".In the year
1546 before he died at the age of 67, Maxwell had relinquished much of the running of his main businesses to Kevin, while he cultivated ties with heads of state and other dignitaries.Maxwell's debt-laden businesses unravelled after he went over the side of his yacht on November 5, 1991, and was
1546 found floating dead off the Canary Islands.A pathologist who conducted an autopsy said in a statement read in court it was unlikely he committed suicide and the cause of death was probably drowning."It is more likely that he fell involuntarily into the sea either as a result of accident accident
1546 or homicide," said Dr Jehuda Hiss.London physiology lecturer Dr Jane Ward suggested that the death could have resulted from micturition syncope -- fainting while emptying the bladder. Kevin said his father, a light sleeper, frequently relieved himself over the side of the yacht when he woke up during the night.Maxwell
1546 was given a hero's funeral in Jerusalem before being buried on the Mount of Olives.But weeks after his death fraud detectives discovered 400 million pounds ($632 million) in company pension fund assets were missing.</

1550 A strongly "Euro-sceptical" speech by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind split the ruling Conservative party on Thursday, just two days before key European negotiations on a future single currency.Rifkind's warning of the dangers of monetary union, in a speech to mark the 50th anniversary of Winston Churchill's vision of a
1550 United States of Europe, delighted Conservative right-wingers who want Britain to rule out membership of EMU.But it drew an angry response from some of the party's most influential elder statesmen who have appealed to Prime Minister John Major not to turn his back on European co-operation.In a letter in Thursday's
1550 Independent newspaper, six Tory grandees including three of Rifkind's predecessors at the Foreign Office wrote: "For us now to rule out British membership of a single currency would be to betray our national interest."Up to now Britain has pursued a policy of delicate balance, refusing to say whether or not
1550 it will sign up to EMU (Economic and Monetary Union), but insisting on its right to join in the preparatory negotiations.But the picture Rifkind painted on Wednesday of Economic and Monetary Union splitting apart the European continent has boosted the confidence of his party's right wing who now see Rifkind
1550 firmly on their side in a bid to keep Britain out.The row is certain to surface again at the Conservative Party's annual conference in October and could weaken the stance of Major's pro-European finance minister Kenneth Clarke at EMU negotiations this weekend in Dublin, Ireland.Britain was always going to be
1550 sidelined at Saturday's meeting of European finance ministers and central bank chiefs.Britain is still arguing internally about the whole concept of monetary union, while the powerful Franco-German alliance is forging ahead towards EMU and just wants to clear up details.Added to the furore over mad cow disease, with Britain now
1550 calling into question a pledge to kill off suspect cattle, Britain's position on Europe is looking increasingly isolated.One of the main points on the Dublin agenda is to put the finishing touches to a Stability Pact, a scheme to ensure that EMU members stick to tough anti-inflationary policies not only
1550 before they sign up to union but afterwards as well.The pact was originally inspired by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and has now been firmly embraced by France.Also on the Dublin agenda are plans to link a future single currency to currencies outside EMU, a further development of Europe's existing
1550 Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).After being unceremoniously ejected from the ERM in 1992 after a huge run on the pound, Britain will stress its view that countries cannot be forced to join "ERM II".But Clarke and central bank governor Eddie George are also expected to assure partners that even if Britain
1550 stays out it will not seek competitive advantage by devaluing sterling.George's deputy Howard Davies has stressed Britain will stick to tough anti-inflationary polices. "Indeed our policy as an 'out' would be broadly the same as that of the European Central Bank," he said last week.Another issue the Bank of England
1550 is likely to address at least informally at Dublin Castle is a growing row over plans for an interbank payments system once EMU has begun.To the alarm of the British financial community, French and German banks are pushing for limits on the access banks in countries outside EMU can have
1550 to the system, known as TARGET.But Davies this week demanded that all European nations should have equal access to market liquidity whether they sign up for EMU or not and said moves to prevent this may be illegal.</

1567 The amount of passenger traffic has declined substantially in recent years amid continuing anarchy in the former Soviet Union's air transport industry, the International Air Transport Association (IATA)'s area specialist Horst Herlemann said.He told an IATA conference on Wednesday that figures collated by Russia's interstate aviation authority (MAK) show air
1567 traffic volume in 12 of the 15 states of the former Soviet Union (FSU) slumped to 89 billion passenger kilometres in 1995 from 156 billion in 1992.MAK receives data from all CIS states (except the three Baltic Republics) but Herlemann said there was "no more reason to believe in the
1567 quality of post-Soviet statistics than in the quality of Soviet statistics."From Belarus to Kyrgyzstan, the collection of aviation data was flawed, he added.Under the old Soviet system "the plan was law and had to be fulfilled by all means including the manipulation of data. The mechanism of self-deception worked quite
1567 well, not only in the Soviet Union but also in its satellites," he said."MAK has repeated difficulties in verifying or even obtaining material from individual civil aviation bodies which are not efficient and, as one might expect, not very reliable," Herlemann added.eAdding to this chaos was the fact that in
1567 Russia alone there were over 400 registered airlines and in the Ukraine another 150 although most of them did not actually fly."Gone are those happy times when Aeroflot's regional offices would dutifully report what the plan proposed." he added.Since many airlines and airports were still organised as one unit and
1567 liable to be assessed for tax on the basis of any statistics they submitted, Herlemann said, "the chances of receiving honest figures are small."And as air traffic control services were also assessed on the basis of flights reported, a similar problem existed there.Thus the FSU operates a route system "which
1567 has almost no economic rationale,.....It is mostly arbitrary and still reflects to a large extent the Soviet organisation of domestic air transport," he said.If market-based aviation is to exist in the FSU, this approach has to end, he added."Route efficiency has to be measured...and decisions to serve a destination based
1567 on unbiased market research.It was impossible for every state of the FSU to have its own fully-fledged national airlines serving the world "or even the former union."He added: "The last five years of aviation in the FSU have made it clear that this approach is extremely costly and the results
1567 uncertain. Solutions have to be found and quickly," he warned.IATA sources says the FSU has inherited an elaborate aircraft inspection system but its rules and procedures are now frequently violated or ignored, leading to a serious decline in air safety standards.With so many under-utilised aircraft available, there were many fly-by-night
1567 operators breaching flight regulations and intimidating inspectors (and their families) when they try to intervene. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017</
1568 Kevin Maxwell, the son of media tycoon Robert Maxwell who disappeared from his yacht in 1991, will not face a second trial on a charge of fraud, a judge ruled on Thursday.Judge John Buckley said a further trial "would be unfair, so unfair as to amount to an abuse of
1568 power of the court".His decision effectively ended five years of controversy over hundreds of millions of pounds which were found missing from Maxwell company pension funds after Robert Maxwell's death.In January, Kevin, his brother Ian Maxwell, and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of conspiring to defraud pension funds
1568 after an eight-month, multi-million-pound trial.Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) sought to bring charges in a second trial against Kevin Maxwell, Trachtenberg, and two former Maxwell executives, Albert Fuller and Michael Stoney.The judge on Thursday announced his decision to stay any further proceedings before reading out his judgment.Kevin Maxwell, 37, had
1568 taken his case before the judge to argue that the impending second trial was "oppressive".The decision to stay any further proceedings was a blow to the SFO, which came under fierce attack for failing to secure a conviction at the first trial.Lawyers expressed surprise when the SFO said it wanted
1568 a second trial and many said the organisation was trying to salvage its own reputation.Critics also said that cases of this kind should be decided by judges, since it was clear a jury could not grasp the financial complexities involved.The investigation and first trial set the record for the most
1568 expensive criminal case in Britain this century with final costs estimated at around 30 million pounds ($46 million).Kevin Maxwell, Trachtenberg and Fuller were then charged with dishonestly using shares in language firm Berlitz International as collateral for loans while Stoney faced charges of dishonestly falsifying accounts.Kevin became Britain's biggest bankrupt
1568 in 1992 with debts of 406.8 million pounds ($631 million at current rates) after he lost a lawsuit filed by liquidators who were trying to recover missing pension funds. He was released from bankruptcy in 1995.Kevin -- whose overrriding ambition in life had been to follow in his father's footsteps
1568 -- always denied conspiring to defraud by misusing pension fund money to prop up the indebted private Maxwell companies.He said his father, whom he described as as bully, used pension funds just like any other assets in his corporate empire -- as a source of cash to be moved from
1568 one company to another whenever he deemed necessary.Kevin told the first trial that he and his brother had merely obeyed their fathers' orders.Witnesses at the first trial said Kevin had basically taken over running his father's businesses by 1991 as Robert Maxwell eased away from corporate matters and sought new
1568 status as a statesman.Robert Maxwell's body was found after he disappeared off his yacht in the Atlantic Ocean near the Canary Islands in November 1991.</

1571 OPEC's Vienna-based Secretariat in a monthly report revised down its estimate for world demand on OPEC crude next year by 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 24.9 million, OPEC news agency said.The report said the Secretariat says the call on OPEC crude in 1997 is likely to remain unchanged from
1571 this year, despite world rising demand. "An upward revision in non-OPEC supply of 200,000 bpd has led to a downward revision in the balance for OPEC oil in 1997 to 24.90 million bpd, compared with 25.10 million bpd in last month's report," said OPECNA."This balance is the same as that
1571 of 1996, which means that there will be no additional oil available for OPEC, despite the expected demand growth of 1.5 million bpd for 1997," the report said."That is, the growth in demand will be matched by similar growth in non-OPEC supply."OPEC headquarters said it now projected average non-OPEC supply
1571 at 45.74 million bpd next year, 280,000 bpd higher than in last month's preliminary estimate and up from 44.26 million bpd in 1996.The Secretariat forecasts global demand for 1997 at 70.63 million bpd, up 1.5 million or 2.2 percent from this year's 69.12 million and unchanged from last month's report.

1587 weight and then build sugar content," the report said.Although there were still some areas such as north Germany which could benefit from more moisture, the weather in August had enabled most West European beet crops to make up some of the ground lost during the early stages of the season,
1587 it added. 1587 and Ireland were all showing good growth rates compared with previous seasons, although at differing levels, the report said.It added that the weather during the harvest itself would still have a major bearing on the eventual outcome, especially with some of the longer running campaigns such as Britain. 1587 was not so bright in Eastern Europe, where a lack of inputs and poor organisation were key factors that could amplify the impact of poor weather, Czarnikow said."Despite the better progress that good weather has brought to western Europe there has not been the same optimism for late improvements in
1587 the east," it said."In both the Ukraine and Russia the summer has been dry but the lack of resources to provide counter-measures has meant that these conditions cause far greater damage than in an equivalent western context."Delays had been occurring in many Russian growing areas and the additional rains that

1603 The Suez Canal is offering a discount of between 20 and 25 percent on tolls for containerised cargo passing through the canal on journeys between the Mediterranean and the Jordanian port of Aqaba.The reduction will come into effect on Friday and aims to help the canal compete with routes opened
1603 between Aqaba and Israeli ports since the Israeli-Jordanian peace treaty in 1994.Ahmed Ali Fadel, the director of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), said the canal would offer a 20 percent reduction up to $22,500 for containers that docked at Aqaba or at any non-Egyptian Mediterranean port.There will be a 25
1603 percent reduction up to $27,500 for containers travelling between Aqaba and Egyptian Mediterranean ports.Fadel said that to qualify for the reduction vessels would have to present to the canal a certificate from the port of Aqaba and a letter from the captain quantifying the amount of containerised cargo shipped or
1603 docked from there.A canal source said the reduction was to head off stiff competition from the land routes between Jordan and Israel.Egypt, which became the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979, fears canal business will drop because of the Israeli-Jordanian peace and shippers using Israel's Mediterranean
1603 ports of Haifa and Ashdod for the region.The SCA agreed the cuts in principle earlier this year but was waiting for Jordan to cut stevedoring charges at Aqaba.</

1657 Construction starts on new homes and apartments climbed unexpectedly in August to the highest level in nearly 2-1/2 years, the Commerce Department said Thursday.The building rate increased 4.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.525 million units -- the highest rate since March 1994, when it was at
1657 1.531 million, and well above Wall Street economists' forecasts of a 1.445-million-unit building rate.In addition, the department revised upward its estimates for building activity in both June and July, indicating the housing market entered the second half with brisk momentum despite generally higher long-term interest rates.The unexpectedly strong figures sent
1657 the inflation-sensitive 30-year U.S. Treasury bond off half a point, or $5 per $1,000 face value. Its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, climbed to 7.06 percent, from 7.01 percent Wednesday."This is a wake-up call," said Veronika White, senior economist at First Union Corp. "Given this number, the chances
1657 are greater than 50 percent for a rate hike on Tuesday," she said, referring to next week's meeting of the Federal Reserve's Open Markets Committee to review whether higher interest rates are needed to cool the economy."This is one of the best leading indicators you have for forecasting the economy
1657 two quarters out," said Alan Ruskin, research director at I.D.E.A. Inc. "It is indicative of an economy that's unlikely to slow dramatically into the first quarter of 1997."There were some signs that the building rate may ease later in the year, as applications for new building permits fell 4.4 percent
1657 last month to a rate of 1.393 million after rising 3 percent in July.The department revised its estimate of July housing starts to an annual rate of 1.46 million from a previously reported 1.455 million and said June construction was at a stronger rate of 1.49 million a year, instead
1657 of 1.474 million.Housing starts were expected to level off in the summer because of the increase in long-term mortgage rates since the beginning of the year. Analysts said high levels of consumer confidence and strong job growth meant any easing in housing would be modest but did not foresee the
1657 continuing pickup in August building.Construction starts on new single-family homes jumped in August by 8.3 percent to a rate of 1.238 million a year after a 5.5 percent decline in July. The August starts rate on single-family homes also was the highest since March 1994, when it was at 1.28
1657 million.Building of apartments dropped in August by 9.5 percent to a rate of 287,000 following a 12.8 percent increase in July.Regionally, the only area where building declined in August was in the Midwest, where starts fell 2 percent to a rate of 342,000.Starts in the West surged 13.5 percent to
1657 378,000 a year and in the Northeast they gained 7 percent to a rate of 138,000. Construction in the South, the nation's biggest housing market, picked up 2.8 percent to a rate of 667,000.</

1662 Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole tumbled off a stage on Wednesday while shaking hands with a line of voters but a doctor said he suffered only a minor scratch and haemorrhage on his eye."It's fairly noticeable, but essentially nothing more than ...just a bruise," said Dr. Rudy Manthel, an opthamologist
1662 who examined Dole after he arrived in Las Vegas from Chico, California, where the fall took place."By tomorrow it'll probably feel a lot better and the next couple days it will go away completely," he said.At a campaign rally in Chico, a decorative, unattached stage railing Dole had reached out
1662 to for support gave way and he fell to the ground, his tumble broken by a group of news photographers.Dole grimaced as he fell from the platform, which was about 3 1/2 feet (100 cms) high, but quickly got to his feet with some assistance from security personnel.Dole, who was
1662 given two Purple Heart medals for severe wounds sustained in the Second World War, then immediately began his speech, saying, "I think I just earned my third Purple Heart going over the rail, but you can always say I've fallen for Chico."After the speech, Dole was greeting supporters when a
1662 reporter asked him if he was shaken by the fall. He said, "Yeah, a little bit, it woke me up."He told reporters travelling with him on his plane, "I'm really not stiff at all. I thought I might be...It's a wonder I didn't get hurt there."A reddening was evident in
1662 Dole's left eye, and the candidate later said he had poked the eye with a finger as he fell.Dole continued as scheduled to Las Vegas, where he was to spend the night before a campaign appearance on Thursday, and was examined in his hotel room by Manthel.Manthel told reporters he
1662 examined Dole for about half an hour and found that Dole had scratched the lining over the white of his eye, and ruptured one or two blood vessels. The injury probably was caused by direct contact to the eye."There really was no other complaints," Manthel said. There were no signs,
1662 for example, of fractures or injuries to the brain, he said.Manthel said he had prescribed eye drops to relieve any pain, and also prescribed an antibiotic.Dole spokesman Nelson Warfield said there were no signs of injuries elsewhere on Dole, who landed on his back on the right side of his
1662 body, where he was wounded in the war.He said Sheila Burke, a longtime Dole aide and registered nurse, had examined the area and there was "no indication of any kind of damage."Speaking of Dole's quick recovery, Warfield said of the 73-year-old candidate, "This should put to rest the age question
1662 once and for all. If Bob Dole can take a tumble like that and hop right back up on his feet and deliver a great speech, he is strong enough to be president and go a couple of rounds with Mike Tyson too."While Dole was travelling to Las Vegas, he
1662 went to the back of the plane to look at a Reuters photograph of his fall and re-enacted how he had leaned on the rail that gave way. Studying the picture, he quipped, "My hair stayed alright. I had enough hair spray on."When asked by a reporter if the fall
1662 meant a bad campaign day, Dole answered, "I got up, didn't I?"</

1664 Shuttle Atlantis edged ever closer to the Russian space station Mir on Wednesday to give space endurance champ Shannon Lucid a ride home.The shuttle, carrying Lucid's replacement and thousands of pounds of supplies, was due to dock with Mir at 10:13 p.m. CDT (0313 GMT on Thursday) as the two
1664 craft soar high above Russia.The shuttle's final approach ended a three-day chase through space that began early on Monday with a pre-dawn blast-off from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre.The astronauts caught their first glimpse of the sprawling Russian space complex from a distance of 52 miles (84 km)."We can see Shannon
1664 smiling from here," joked shuttle skipper Bill Readdy.The shuttle was running nearly seven weeks late on its promise to return Lucid to Earth. The 53-year-old mother of three arrived at Mir in March and was due home in early August, but rocket problems, a threatening hurricane and a scheduling clash
1664 with an unmanned rocket delayed the shuttle's planned July 31 launch.As the shuttle closed in, Lucid was tending a crop of wheat in a miniature space greenhouse when a ground controllers advised her the shuttle's docking was imminent."I sure hope so," was her response.Lucid's mission, the second of seven planned
1664 U.S. astronaut tours of duty of Mir, is the longest ever by a woman and a record for an American.The shuttle crew planned to hover 150 feet (46 metres) from Mir before inching in towards the station's 6.5 feet (two meters) diameter docking port.Readdy will have to negotiate his way
1664 through the station's forest of delicate, electricity generating solar panels, including a newly installed panel that will hang 14 feet (four metres) from the shuttle's nose. A final nudge from the shuttle's manoeuvring jets will link the two spacecraft. Motors will then draw the craft together and seal the docking
1664 ports.If all goes according to plan, the hatches between the two craft will swing open at about 12:39 a.m. CDT (0539 GMT) on Thursday.Joining Readdy on Atlantis are pilot Terry Wilcutt and mission specialists John Blaha, Tom Akers, Jay Apt and Carl Walz.Blaha, a 54-year-old former fighter pilot, will remain
1664 aboard Mir with Russian cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Kaleri until Atlantis returns in January to retrieve him.The two spacecraft, weighing 535,480 lbs (242,900 kg), will remain joined in space for five days while the astronauts transfer thousands of pounds of equipment and supplies to and from Mir.Atlantis is due
1664 to return home on Sept. 26, ending Lucid's record-breaking 188-day stay in space.</

1667 The U.S. Army on Wednesday began deploying more than 3,000 troops to the Gulf as part of the Clinton administration's latest moves to guard against further military action by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.Almost 300 soldiers from the 1st Cavalry Division and sophisticated satellite equipment were flown from the Fort Hood
1667 army base in central Texas for Kuwait on a commercial jet and a C-5 military cargo plane.Two more flights were to take 700 troops out early on Thursday.Officials said the staggered deployment of about 3,000 troops from Fort Hood, the U.S. Army's largest base, would be completed over the next
1667 two or three days, with each flight to Kuwait taking from 17 to 22 hours.Most of the heavy equipment was already in place in Kuwait so the arriving troops would quickly get down to military exercises."They are ready, they are prepared and they are excited," said Maj. Mary Ann Cummings
1667 as the first group of 217 soldiers took off on Wednesday morning. Seventy-three more went out on an afternoon flight with the satellite equipment.But several family members were critical of President Bill Clinton's handling of the deployment. They said he had failed to explain the deployment, unlike in 1991 when
1667 President George Bush sent hundreds of thousands of troops to the Gulf War."Bush told us why. Clinton hasn't told us. I know he can't tell us everything but he hasn't told us why," said Pauline Ketchum, just before her husband Steve, a radar specialist, left.Ketchum said she was a political
1667 independent but would not now vote for Clinton.Others said many relatives of the soldiers wondered whether the deployment was dictated more by domestic politics than security interests."A lot of people think this is a political thing because of the elections," said Edye Holman, who cooked up hot dogs and sausages
1667 at a dawn farewell event for the soldiers and their families.Defense Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday the deployment was to augment enforcement of "Operation Southern Watch," which is the patroling by air of southern Iraq."We will not tolerate any threatening actions against our air crews and ... any that
1667 they take we will respond (to) very sharply," Perry told reporters. But he said Iraq had in recent days stopped threatening allied warplane, reducing the chances that further U.S. military action would be taken soon.The U.S. military launched cruise missile strikes against air defense facilities in southern Iraq two weeks
1667 ago after Iraq moved against Kurds in the north. President Clinton said he ordered the new troop deployment last weekend.The formal mission of the Fort Hood troops was to provide training for Kuwaiti forces, but officials said they could be used in any new military action against Iraq. About 1,200
1667 ground troops were already in Kuwait before the latest Gulf crisis began and they have stayed in place. It was Iraq's invasion of Kuwait that sparked the 1991 Gulf War.Clinton, who also ordered the expansion of a "no-fly zone" excluding Iraqi warplanes in southern Iraq, said on Tuesday his policy
1667 was designed to "keep Saddam Hussein in a box and limit his ability to threaten his neighbors."The Fort Hood troops deployed on Wednesday hugged their spouses and children in emotional farewell ceremonies before being moved to a holding area and boarding their planes."I have faith in God and I'm just
1667 going to get over there and do what I have to do," said Staff Sgt. Dennis Garrett.About 45,000 troops are stationed at Fort Hood, which lies just outside Killeen in central Texas, about 120 miles (190 km) south of Dallas.</

1671 U.S. demand for petroleum products rose just 0.5 percent in August from a year ago to 18.13 million barrels per day (bpd), the American Petroleum Institute said on Wednesday.Demand, as measured by deliveries, rose for distillates, jet fuel and residual fuel but dropped for gasoline.U.S. oil imports continued their steep
1671 climb, with crude imports up 7.2 percent to 7.973 million bpd and petroleum product imports up 8.9 percent to 1.769 million bpd, API said in its monthly report. But matching EIA's tally, API reported distillate stocks at 109.7 million barrels, down 16 percent from a year ago.Total gasoline deliveries fell
1671 1.7 percent from a year ago to 8.045 million bpd, defying expectations."Strong economic growth and the moderation in prices over the past several months suggest that actual consumption would have risen around 1 to 1.5 percent for the month," API said.Jet kerosine demand rose 6.4 percent to 1.601 million bpd,
1671 while residual fuel demand rose 3.1 percent to 845,000 bpd.Refinery use at 94 percent of capacity in August was on par with last year's level, but rose 135,000 bpd from July.Total petroleum stocks at the end of August stood at 964.5 million barrels, down 5.7 percent from August 1995, although
1671 crude stocks were up 1.4 percent to 312.2 million barrels.U.S. crude production, including condensate, dipped 0.7 percent to 6.405 million bpd in August from a year ago. Deliveries of distillates -- heating oil and diesel -- grew 3.3 percent to 3.143 million bpd.Distillate imports stayed around 200,000 bpd, where they
1671 have been since May. From January through August, distillate imports, which came mostly from the western hemisphere, averaged 230,000 bpd, up 20 percent from last year, API said.While the U.S. Energy Information Administration this week warned that distillate stocks were low, API noted that refinery yields of distillate in August
1671 "were the highest in at least twenty years for this time of year" despite a loss of output from the closed Marcus Hook refinery in Pennsylvania.</

1724 have flown together in space twice before, floated in each other's arms, wearing wide grins.Atlantis, with six astronauts and thousands of pounds (kilos) of supplies aboard, docked at Mir at 10:13 p.m. CDT on Wednesday (0313 GMT on Thursday)."Atlantis and Mir are shaking hands," said Readdy as the metallic petals
1724 of the two docking ports slipped together."You make that look easy," radioed mission control's Bill McArthur.Electric motors then drew the two ports together, completing the docking process and making an air-tight seal.Readdy had to negotiate his way through the station's forest of delicate, electricity generating solar panels, including a newly
1724 installed concertina-like array that hangs just 14 feet (4.2 metres) from the shuttle's nose.The shuttle's arrival at Mir, its fourth visit, ended a three-day chase through space that began early on Monday with a pre-dawn blastoff from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre.Lucid has been waiting for her ride home since early
1724 August. 1724 former Vietnam fighter pilot. 1735 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe International Monetary Fund on Wednesday endorsed stepped-up aid for the world's poorest nations, but stopped short of spelling out how it planned to pay for that.The decision, announced by IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, effectively left open the controversial question of whether the IMF would
1735 sell some of its gold to help the world's poor."The IMF is fully ready to assist its low-income members well into the next millenium," Camdessus said in a brief statement after a lengthy IMF board meeting.Camdessus, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, had proposed selling
1735 5 million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.Camdessus said
1735 the board had reached "understandings" to ensure a permanent continuation of the IMF's Enhanced Structural Adjustment loan Facility (ESAF) and its participation in a multilateral debt relief plan for poor nations.But he did not say how that would be accomplished and an IMF spokesman declined to elaborate.ESAF, which lends money
1735 to the world's poorest countries at virtually no interest charge, faces a roughly $3.5 billion financing gap from the years 2000 to 2004.Bilateral contributions from major countries are expected to fill at least some of that gap. But Camdessus and his allies have argued that would not be enough and
1735 that a modest amount of gold sales would be necessary.Under their proposal, the IMF would use the income generated from investing the proceeds of the gold sales to help finance the ESAF."When you get finished with all the modalities, it's the only way to do this," U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert
1735 Rubin told reporters earlier on Wednesday while the IMF was still meeting.This was the IMF's second meeting in less than a week to discuss ways to help the world's poorest countries. The board failed to reach a consensus on selling gold at a meeting on Friday.Camdessus said the discussions had
1735 taken place in a "cooperative spirit."Finance ministers and central bank chiefs that make up the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee are expected to discuss the gold sales question when they meet in Washington on Sept. 29.But an explicit agreement looks unlikely at that time.</
1736 In a patch of prairie ringed by refineries and dotted with oil wells, a dozen squat little birds walk gingerly out of their holding pen and into a world they have never seen.They do not know it but these birds known as Attwater's prairie chickens represent the last, best hope
1736 for their nearly extinct species. Raised in captivity, they are being released on a nature preserve here on Galveston Bay 40 miles (64 km) southeast of Houston to try to re-establish a wild prairie chicken population that is almost gone.Their survival is crucial because scientists estimate that there are only
1736 42 prairie chickens left in the wild and another 80 in captivity. A century ago, an estimated one million of the birds ranged along the vast coastal prairies of Texas, Louisiana and northeastern Mexico.The near-demise of the prairie chicken is primarily the work of man. Once their natural range covered
1736 millions of acres (hectares) along the Gulf of Mexico but land development and degradation radically reduced the area where the birds can live, said Jim Bergan, a biologist for the Nature Conservancy of Texas, an environmental group that owns the Texas preserve.Prairie chickens, which are members of the grouse family,
1736 need a lot of open, unspoiled prairie to survive. They move about feeding on bugs and seeds and use different parts of the prairie during the year as they go through their annual cycle of breeding, nesting and raising their young.Squeezed by man's encroachment, the birds are running out of
1736 both land and time. Groups such as the Nature Conservancy, with help from the private sector, are in a pitched battle to save them, but the outcome is far from certain because no one knows if attempts to re-establish a wild population will work.A year ago, 13 prairie chickens raised
1736 in captivity were released at a federal refuge near Eagle Lake, Texas, 50 miles (80 km) southwest of Houston. Only two of them survived for last spring's mating season.Early in August, seven of the birds were placed on the Texas City preserve. Less than three weeks later, two were dead,
1736 one killed by a wildcat, another by intestinal problems. Even under the best of conditions, the Attwater's prairie chicken does not live much more than three years."We've got a long, uphill battle. There are so many things we don't know the answer to, so many things beyond our control," Bergan
1736 said.The 12 birds released most recently, all three months old, appeared less than excited about their new home. Staying low in the knee-high grass, they huddled near the opening of the pen where food pellets were spread to entice them out.If the birds make it, they will join a wild
1736 population of 10 prairie chickens already on the preserve. Only two other groups are known to exist in the wild, 14 on the refuge near Eagle Lake and 18 on private land near Corpus Christi, Texas.The Attwater's prairie chicken, when full-grown, is about the size of a standard chicken but
1736 looks like a large quail. Its brown and white feathers enable it to melt easily into the underbrush where only the most dedicated predator can find it.The birds are a favourite of bird experts because of the elaborate mating ritual known as "booming" they perform each spring on the open
1736 prairie. It is so named because of the long, low sounds -- akin to that of blowing into a soft drink bottle -- made by male birds trying to attract females.The Texas City preserve is one of several that conservation groups and government agencies plan to string along the Gulf
1736 Coast. They will not be contiguous, but the hope is that the birds will fly from one to the other, creating new populations along the way, and eventually establish themselves in larger wildlife refuges in the area.The Texas City preserve would seem an odd place for an endangered species to
1736 make its last stand, given its proximity to the vast complex of refineries and petrochemical plants that line the banks of Galveston Bay and the Houston Ship Channel. Pipelines transporting petroleum products to and from the plants crisscross the land.The refuge was given to the Nature Conservancy last year by
1736 Mobil Corp., which ran cattle and pumped oil and natural gas on the land for many years. But Bergan said the birds seem unruffled by the smoke-belching plants. In fact, he said, Texas A&amp;M University scientists said the prairie chickens here are among the most vigorous they have found."They start
1736 'booming' earlier in the season and stay at it longer than birds in other places," he said.</

1778 a rise in prices around 1999 or 2000."Aluminium, used mainly in transport, packaging and construction, slumped on Monday to a 2-1/4 year low of $1,414 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME). Prices have since edged up slightly to between $1,420-1,425 a tonne on Thursday.Martin forecast an average aluminium
1778 price of $1,650 a tonne between 1996 and 2005.Of the metal's three main markets, Martin said transport was projected to grow at the fastest rate of around three percent per year up to 2005 with gains in market share in engine blocks, cyclinder heads and suspension parts, radiators and wheels.But
1778 consumption in packaging would likely be restrained by substitution and he predicted an annual growth rate of 0.5 percent."Aluminium in packaging faces significant threats from PET bottles in North America. In fact packaging applications in this market will probably decline," the analyst said.Modest growth was seen in the building sector
1778 in the main markets of North America and Europe, but a decline in Japanese housing would limit shipments there. Demand growth in construction was forecast at about 0.9 percent per year to 2005.Primary aluminium consumption in the main markets of North American, Japan and Europe was expected to grow at
1778 below the three percent per year forecast for global consumption over the ten year period due to a faster growth rate for recycled metal.Latin America and Asia -- excluding Japan -- would be the star performers with primary growth seen at three percent and 4.5 percent respectively, Martin said.Primary consumption
1778 in the Western world was forecast at 22.2 million tonnes by 2005, an increase of 4.7 million tonnes from 1995 levels. Meanwhile, world smelting capacity was predicted to rise by around 4.6 million tonne by 2005, including some 900,000 tonnes in capacity "creep"."Generally speaking those regions who already have to
1778 import a large amount of their requirements -- Europe, Japan and other Asia -- will see this requirement grow strongly over the forecast period," Martin said.European import requirement was expected to rise to 2.3 million tonnes in 2005 from 1.4 million tonnes in 1995. Japan's imports would rise about 400,000
1778 tonnes to around 2.8 million tonnes in the 10 year period."On the other hand Africa, Latin America and the Middle East are expected to significantly increase their exportable surpluses," he said.Exports from so-called "East bloc" countries were expected to decrease due to strong growth in demand outpacing growth in production,
1778 especially in China and eastern Europe."China's import requirement should double to around 500,000 tonnes by 2005," Martin said. "Sluggish growth in CIS primary consumption and a new smelter in Kazakhstan will result in little change in CIS exports over the forecast period."As a result net exports from the "Eastern bloc"
1778 were projected to fall on an annual basis by around 500,000 tonnes to 2005.--Tanya Pang, Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41</

1780 Germany's 16 state interior ministers met on Thursday to set a date to start sending home 320,000 Bosnian civil war refugees who have taken shelter here.Despite pressure from human rights groups who say many parts of Bosnia are neither ready nor safe enough to take the refugees back, the ministers
1780 appeared ready to agree on October 1 as the starting date for a gradual repatriation programme."Now that the civil war is over and it is again possible to live in and especially rebuild the homeland, our temporary guests must return," federal Interior Minister Manfred Kanther told Berlin's Info Radio."We could
1780 never take in so many refugees again if we didn't always make clear that this is not a programme of immigration by the back door, but help in need."The vast majority of the refugees are Moslems driven out of their homes mostly by Serbs but also by Croats.The United Nations
1780 High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) has singled out 22 regions suitable for refugees to return to -- but added that this only applied to returnees from the ethnic group which was dominant in those areas.By and large refugees from former Yugoslavia have been received sympathetically by ordinary Germans, many of
1780 whom remember the ravages of war.The Bosnians, many of them staying with friends or relatives in Germany, have not aroused resentment in the same way as refugees from further afield who still apply for asylum at a rate of well over 100,000 a year and are often branded as spongers
1780 by hardline rightwingers.However, even federal states which have until now urged that the Bosnians should be allowed to stay longer have started pushing for a definite timetable, under pressure from overstretched local and municipal budgets.The states agreed tentatively in January that a gradual return should begin on July 1, starting
1780 with single people and childless couples, but then agreed with Bonn not to start before October 1.Now a consensus appears to be emerging that the programme will not rigidly follow family categories, but instead focus more on returning specific ethnic groups to areas where they will be safe."We have to
1780 take account of individual personal circumstances and -- this is the most important thing -- be sure that people are only returned to areas where this is possible from the security point of view," Max Stadler, interior policy spokesman of the liberal Free Democrats, told NDR television.Politicians of all shades
1780 accept that the repatriation programme will take two years.Even if permits allowing the refugees to stay are no longer renewed from October 1 onwards, many will not expire for another three months, and Bonn is unlikely to try to force refugees home in the depths of the Balkan winter.But the
1780 setting of a date will provide a starting signal that means the refugees will be available for repatriation at short notice when conditions are considered suitable.Politicians also admit that by sending refugees only into areas populated by their own ethnic group, they are in effect cementing the ethnic cleansing which
1780 last December's Dayton peace agreement was intended to counteract."The process of ethnic separation is regrettable, but I have met no one who has said it can be changed in the foreseeable future," Bavarian interior minister Guenter Beckstein told the Sueddeutsche Zeitung daily.</
