1783 The Chairman of the German parliament's European Affairs committee, Norbert Wieczorek, said on Thursday that he feared parts of the the French budget were against the spirit of the European Union's Maastricht treaty.Wieczorek voiced doubts about the French government's use of a one-off payment of 37.5 billion French francs from
1783 France Telecom to cut the central state deficit and enhance its credentials for joining European Monetary Union (EMU)."It is certainly unusual," Wieczorek told Reuters in Dublin after addressing an Irish parliamentary committee."It is a one-time item and to have included that in their calculations as a normal item is not
1783 in the spirit of the (Maastricht) Treaty."Wieczorek, who is also currency union expert for Germany's opposition Social Democrats, said the decision to rely on the France Telecom payment diminished the French budget deficit by 0.4-0.5 of a percent and was a cause of concern in Germany.Asked if this concern was
1783 shared in official circles, Wieczorek said the German government would have to debate that with the French in private.But he pointed to comments by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday, before the French budget was unveiled, that Germany and France had agreed to meet the 1997 deficit limit for entry
1783 into EMU without resorting to "window dressing" schemes.The Bundesbank has not commented on the French budget but the European Commission said on Thursday that the plan to include the France Telecom payment appeared compatible with the Maastricht treaty rules "at first sight".Some European analysts have expressed concern that the French
1783 budget is an accounting exercise to smooth France's entry into EMU without meeting the Maastricht criteria on their strictest terms.The Maastricht Treaty requires that countries proceeding to the European single currency have a general government deficit not exceeding three percent of GDP although a small and temporary excess will be
1783 permitted.Wednesday's French budget brings the deficit down from a targeted four percent of GDP this year.</

1799 and the electronic system at the same time," said Alexander van Drooge, head of public relations at the EOE.The proposed system, Switch, aims to give the EOE a competitive edge over its rivals by combining the versatility of the open outcry system with the speed of a screen system.Originally scheduled
1799 to begin in mid-1996, the new system will not begin until an unspecified time next year.The impracticality of market makers shouting on the floor and keying in numbers at the same time has forced the EOE to put forward two plans to members.The first is to split option trading into
1799 screen trading for small transactions and open outcry for large orders. The EOE would rely on arbitrage to narrow any differences in prices.The second system would employ EOE overseers to fit best offers to best bids, whether on the screen or the floor."We expect the members to decide in a
1799 couple of months," said van Drooge.The EOE said it will bring in changes gradually and expected to introduce the electronic delivery of orders by the end of the year. However, the fundamental changes to the trading system will not take place until 1997."We cannot say how long it will take.

1806 NATO planners are developing a "super" Partnership for Peace to embrace countries likely to be left out of the first wave of expansion of the alliance, Western diplomats said on Thursday.With the Western alliance likely to accept some former communist countries into its fold next year, diplomats say some non-aligned
1806 nations and unsuccessful NATO candidates may join a tighter grouping of would-be members and affiliates.Russia could also join this intensified Partnership for Peace -- dubbed "PfP-Two" or "enhanced PfP" -- which aims to boost non-members' military cooperation and political contact with NATO, a U.S. diplomat told Reuters."Let's include the Russians,"
1806 said Derek Shearer, U.S. ambassador to Finland.The plan aims to demonstrate to Russia that NATO is not belligerent and ease the concerns of countries that may fall into a security "grey zone" after the allance expands.Of the 27 current members of the PfP scheme aimed at uniting former European foes,
1806 Shearer said between 15 and 20 could join a super PfP, which could involve specific liaison officers and working groups and would be based on charters."It's just a notion of enhancing PfP to show where we're going in Europe," he said.The scheme builds on a milestone speech by U.S. Secretary
1806 of State Warren Christopher in Stuttgart earlier this month in which he outlined a vision of a New Atlantic Community which would erase former Cold War barriers.Christopher spoke of forming a New Atlantic Partnership Council based on a charter between NATO and Russia and said the alliance should involve non-members
1806 in the PfP programme.His speech "was specific and important because the secretary made clear that Russia should be included in discussions of the European security architecture", Shearer said.Czechoslovakia, Hungary and Poland are widely regarded as top of the list for inclusion in an expanded NATO. Other former Soviet Bloc states
1806 including the Baltic countries, Romania and Bulgaria are less likely to make it into the first round."You don't want them feeling this means 'no' forever," Shearer said.The scheme would also embrace non-aligned and neutral countries -- Finland, Sweden and Austria -- which do not currently seek NATO membership, offsetting concerns
1806 that NATO expansion may be seen as re-creating "zones of influence".For instance, Finland, Sweden and the three Baltic states, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, have said expansion in central Europe may leave former Soviet satellites in a security void which, under some circumstances, Russia could try to fill."We want to see
1806 the avoidance of the grey area by the development of a super-PfP," another Western diplomat said.With Europe still in transition from the Cold War period, the plan aims to let countries address threats like terrorism and drug-trafficking, which are now more likely causes of instability than invasion, diplomats said.</

1825 Germany's independent cable television operators, shackled for over a decade to Deutsche Telekom AG's network monopoly, said on Thursday they were contemplating breaking the chain in light of deregulation.Until now, only Deutsche Telekom was allowed to build public communications networks, leaving independent cable TV operators the option of connecting individual
1825 homes to the cable network in their street.But that weakness could turn out to be a major strength as independent operators control two thirds of the 16 million subscribers that receive programming over Telekom's cable TV network."Should the independent cable operators seek an alternative carrier, Deutsche Telekom would not be
1825 able to refinance investments in its own cable network," said Bruno Baumann, president of the Federation of Independent Cable Network Operators (ANGA).Baumann presented the challenge with a 90-page study containing proposals for modernising Telekom's broadband cable TV network to transform it into a digital superhighway bringing high-speed Internet access to
1825 millions of homes.The study, conducted by ANGA and the ZVEI Electronics Industry Association, calls for a joint effort between independent operators, equipment makers and Deutsche Telekom to upgrade the cable TV network."ANGA members alone plan to spend at least five billion marks by the year 2000 to expand their networks,"
1825 said Baumann.Deutsche Telekom's cable TV network currently is used largely for one-way broadcast of television programming and has capacity for around 30 channels. Digital compression technology will allow Telekom to broadcast up to 150 channels over the network to 50 percent of subscribers late next year. Further investment would boost
1825 that figure to 95 percent later.But Baumann said that its proposals go much further than what Telekom has planned so far and could result in as many as 400 channels over the cable TV network that currently has the potential to hook up to over 20 million homes.The cable is
1825 also much faster for Internet surfers than even Telekom's high-speed Integrated Services Digital Network.Using cable modems, it is possible to transmit a 10 megabyte file in just 13 seconds over the cable network as opposed to 93 minutes with a 14,400 baud modem over an ordinary phone line, Baumann said.One
1825 of the central conflicts between Telekom and the independent cable operators is how to allow cable users to interact with programme providers.What is needed is a so-called return channel that would allow users to send commands back to programme providers to order goods, send electronic mail, choose a programme or
1825 call up a page on the Internet.Telekom wants to use its ISDN network as the return channel. It has invested huge sums in building the ISDN network into the largest in the world, subsidising its expansion with 200 million marks in rebates to new customers this year. But that is
1825 not in the interests of the independent operators."We want the return channel in the cable network, otherwise there's nothing in it for us," said Baumann.The independent cable operators are seeking discussions with Telekom. If these do produce the desired results, then they will seek talks with Telekom's new competitors like
1825 Vebacom or Mannesmann.Should they hook up with the newcomers, a mighty alliance could be formed granting the new phone companies direct access to millions of homes. For this reason, it is likely that Telekom will find a way to cooperate with the cable operators.</

1831 "comprehensive" highlights will be broadcast on free terrestrial television.The call is included in a report, adopted by 213 votes to 140, which makes a series of recommendations designed to guarantee a future in Europe for state-funded television.The MEPs fear public TV will not survive the increasing competition from commercial channels.According
1831 to the report, drafted by British Socialist Carole Tongue, the state-funded channels' share of European Union audiences has plummeted from 82 percent in 1984 to 46 percent in 1994.The report says public service broadcasting should continue to receive support from the EU and national governments, so that it can continue
1831 to fulfil its role as a promoter of European culture and new talent, and a provider of unbiased information."We are in danger of witnessing a trend towards a society of those who can afford the privilege of impartial information and those who can't, those who can afford to watch our
1831 national sporting treasures and those who can't," Tongue said during a debate on Tuesday.Euro-MPs demanded an increase in funding for public service channels with a pan-European remit, like ARTE and EURONEWS.They asked the European Commission to sanction public funding for state channels "provided they strictly fulfil their public service obligations",
1831 and allow them to bid jointly for television rights without contravening new EU rules on media concentration.For their part, public TV channels should make a commitment to improve their accountability to the public, become more independent from governments and strictly respect their obligation to broadcast a majority of European programmes,
1831 parliament said.Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann told MPs on Tuesday that the public could be informed just as well by the new, private TV channels as by public TV."If you have got a monopoly, you can't be serving the interests of democracy," he insisted, adding that if public service broadcasting was
1831 as good as Carole Tongue made out, then she need have no fears for its future.</

1837 compensation for three offshore oil platforms destroyed by U.S. warships in two attacks in 1987 and 1988.The U.S, which ran naval patrols in the Gulf to protect international shipping during the final stages of the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war, says the 1955 Treaty of Amity covers only commercial and consular affairs.It
1837 says the attacks in October 1987 and April 1988 were legitimate military responses to attacks on a U.S. frigate and a Kuwaiti tanker sailing under the U.S. flag.Mohammed Zahedin-Labbaf, leading the Iranian delegation, said the U.S. attacks had been groundless. "It (the U.S. position) implies that attacks on the platforms
1837 were part of a series of hostile engagments between Iranian and U.S. forces, whereas it is Iran's position that these were unprovoked attacks on civilian, and commercial facilities."He said the court's jurisdiction to rule on the matter was clearly established by the treaty."What Iran has brought before the court is
1837 purely a legal case arising out of very particular incidents - and one that is grounded in specific provisions of the Treaty of Amity, which Iran maintains the United States has breached by attacking the oil platforms," he told the court.Seyed Mostafa Zeinoddin, head of legal affairs at the National
1837 Iranian Oil Company, rebutted remarks from U.S. navy commander Ronald Neubauer earlier this week that the platforms were being used as military facilities.The U.S. in opening its submissions on Monday said the platforms were used to identify, track and target ships for attack, serving as staging and supply bases for
1837 the Iranian helicopters and small boats used in such attacks.Zeinoddin said the platforms had been previously been targetted by the Iraqis and for that reason had small security detachments to support oil workers, adding that having bases on intallations packed with oil and gas made little military sense."The small number
1837 of security personnel on these platforms were simply there to act as lookouts, to provide early warning of attacks and to provide some comfort and support to the oil company personnel in the light of Iraqi attacks," he said."Such platforms are quite small and are packed with complex equipment. 1837 is not feasible to install missiles or any other sophisticated military equipment on such small areas and totally impractical to use them as a base for attacks," said Zeinoddin.He said the attacks caused massive economic damage, not only in the immediate loss of oil revenues but also in the huge
1837 cost of rebuilding the platforms, the costs which were still being felt by Iran today.The International Court of Justice, the main judicial organ of the United Nations which settles disputes between states in accordance with international law, is hearing submissions from Iran and the U.S. to determine whether it has
1837 jurisdiction in Iran's claim for compensation.Iran dropped a case at the International Court of Justice over the shooting down in July 1988 or an Iran Air airliner by a U.S. warship after Washington agreed to compensate the families of the 248 Iranians on board who were killed.</

1884 Pope John Paul, starting a four-day visit to France on Thursday that will test his shaky health, dodged controversies about his trip and said his thoughts were with the suffering and the poor.On his last foreign trip before entering hospital for an operation to remove his appendix next month, the
1884 Pontiff walked unaided down the steps of his airliner after it landed at Tours, western France, to be greeted by President Jacques Chirac.Amid heavy security, he left the airport in a bullet-proof car but switched to his Popemobile in central Tours to wave to sparse lines of wellwishers who braved
1884 rain to cheer him.The 76-year-old Pontiff looked alert and more robust than on a visit to Hungary two weeks ago. Tours is the first stop of a gruelling trip that will take him to Brittany, Vendee and the eastern city of Reims.In his first speech on a trip including 21
1884 public appearances, the Pope skirted controversies in France over the role of the Church in a modern secular state and opposition to his strict moral teachings on issues such as birth control."I am mindful of the fact that French society faces many problems as, for example, an economic crisis which
1884 is also the case for many countries throughout the world," the Pope said after meeting Chirac in Tours in the Prefecture building."My thoughts go first to all those who are suffering trials of all sorts, particularly those who must bear with poverty, to those who are victims of prejudice, or
1884 bias, those who lack security and those who are ill," he said.On his sixth visit to France, including a trip to the Indian Ocean island of La Reunion, the Pope praised French aid to developing countries in a "long tradition of solidarity and fraternity for their fellow men"."These gestures of
1884 friendship must be accompanied on the part of the Western world by a new attitude, refusing to take advantage of these poor nations simply for the goods they produce," he added.He also hailed French Catholics' dialogue with the country's large Moslem and Jewish communities.Neither the Pope nor Chirac, accused of
1884 violating a 1905 law separating Church and State by helping fund the visit, used France's traditional Catholic title of "eldest daughter of the Church". The Pope used the title on his first visit in 1980.Chirac said France was "proud of its roots" as a nation that blended secular traditions of
1884 the 1789 Revolution, respectful of religious freedom, with a history of spirituality. 1884 during the trip.Sixty-seven groups including anarchists, freemasons and a police trade union are planning a rally in Paris on Sunday, when the Pope will be in Reims, to protest at the Pope and back the secular ideals of the 1789 French Revolution.The Pope will be in Reims for the 1,500th

1904 Germany's Volkswagen AG said on Thursday that its 1996 west European commercial vehicle sales through August rose 13 percent to 112,000 units, raising its market share to 11.8 percent from 11.1 percent.VW, which is Europe's largest carmaker, said the gains were due to the introduction of new truck models as
1904 VW's sales gains outpaced overall European market growth of four percent.Bernd Wiedmann, chief executive of Volkswagen's commercial truck unit, said at the IAA truck exhibition that VW domestic truck sales through August rose despite a drop of two percent in domestic sales of vehicles weighing up to six tonnes."Our target
1904 for this year and the coming years is to maintain and extend our market leadership in Europe," he said. "In addition, we shall be working actively to build up our position in the new markets of central and eastern Europe."He said the Wolfsburg-based carmaker had 31.3 percent of the German
1904 light commercial truck market through August compared with 29.6 percent in the year-ago period.Wiedmann said he expected sales at the VW commercial truck unit, now structured as a separate brand within the VW group along with Audi, VW passenger cars, SEAT and Skoda, in 1996 to total about 10.5 billion
1904 to 11 billion marks ($7.3 billion).He also expected VW European commercial vehicle production to total about 205,000 units compared with 155,000 in 1995 and for VW's European truck sales in 1996 to reach 6.7 billion marks compared with 5.9 billion marks in 1995.But Wiedmann said VW was not pleased with
1904 its performance in the large truck segment where VW sells its LT delivery trucks and L80 heavy truck platform vehicles.The first-generation LT delivery van achieved a market share of four percent in its final year of production, a figure he said was "totally unsatisfactory from our point of view"."We have
1904 set for ourselves an extremely ambitious target with the new LT," he said, adding VW wants to sell at least 40,000 of the vehicles in 1997 and 1998 for a market share of about 10 percent in Europe for the 2.8 to 5.6 tonne class.The new LT van was launched
1904 in June and the entire new product line will be available by the start of 1997, he said.In eastern and central Europe, Wiedmann said VW was "yielding positive results" following an increase in production capacity at a plant in Poznan, Poland, which led to a 22 percent increase of deliveries
1904 to customers.In Asian markets, Wiedmann said total VW commercial vehicle deliveries rose 55 percent in the first eight months of 1996.In the North and South American markets, Wiedmann said deliveries of VW light commercial vehicles, trucks and busses topped 200,000 vehicles so far in 1996, about nine percent above year-ago
1904 levels.VW said it estimated the worldwide commercial vehicle market at about 15.5 million vehicles, of which 13.6 million have a gross weight of up to six tonnes.Wiedmann said the light commercial vehicle market was "an area that is growing out of proportion to the passenger car market" and would reach
1904 18.1 million vehicles by the year 2000.VW said its Caddy city delivery van, in its first sales year, controls 20 percent of the commercial vehicle market in Europe and about 19,000 units have been delivered.For its larger Transporter, Caravelle and Multivan products, he said VW has a 28 percent market
1904 share in Europe following a thorough model revision at the start of 1996.--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.508 German Marks)</

1910 and D'Amato Bill -- which seek to quash trade with Cuba and Iran and Libya respectively -- was likely to go to WTO arbitration."I don't want to see it ... I don't like to see it, but I think it will happen," he said.Ruggiero, attending a meeting of European Union

1912 International Business Machines Corp. said Thursday it is offering a voluntary buyout programme to an unspecified number of its U.S. employees as it seeks to rebalance the skills of its work force.An IBM spokesman said the Armonk, N.Y.-based computer giant was offering the buyout to certain support staff in various
1912 businesses nationwide. He said employees who decide to accept the deal will leave IBM by the end of the year."We are not giving any figures on the number of people we are offering the programme to," said an IBM spokesman. "We simply do not know how many will accept."The spokesman
1912 pointed out that even with the buyout plan, IBM expects its U.S. personnel to grow in 1996, from 110,000 staffers in 1995, as the company builds up its computer services business. IBM had 225,000 employees worldwide at the end of 1995."The key is the total number of U.S. employees at
1912 the end of 1996 will be greater than the 110,000 we had at the end of 1995," the spokesman said.Only employees who have been with IBM for more than five years are eligible, because in recent years the company has been hiring experienced people with critical skills.Analysts said the move
1912 is aimed at getting 6,000 to 10,000 employees worldwide out of its slower growth areas.Layoffs are likely before the end of the year if not enough employees accept the buyout offer, they added. Others may also be offered jobs at IBM's faster-growing units, such as its services business, which has
1912 added about 10,000 staff this year and plans to add 4,000-5,000 more before year end, they said.Analysts do not expect a charge for the buyout plan, because IBM has told analysts to include $800 million for restructuring costs into their financial models this year.IBM's stock was unchanged at $124.50 on
1912 the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.</

1916 Sports sponsors are increasingly targeting "ambush marketing" in Europe by companies that muscle in on events without paying sponsorship fees, a legal expert said on Thursday.The top lawyer at ISL Marketing AG, a Swiss-based marketing and sponsorship company, said sports sponsorship was becoming a huge business and sponsors wanted to
1916 protect their investment."Ambush marketing is very much foul play," Meena Sayal told an annual conference of the Incorporated Society of British Advertisers, a trade body with 300 members.She said ISL, which works with sports federations on sponsorship deals, got help from lawyers, local police and trading standards officers to prevent
1916 companies from "hitchhiking a free ride" at the Euro 96 football championship this spring.The ISL also launched a pan-European campaign to raise awareness of the official sponsors of Euro 96.Sayal described Nike Inc, the world's biggest athletic footwear maker, as a case study of a company that wrongly targeted consumers
1916 outside Euro 96 games, since it was not an official sponsor.She said Nike had committed an "own goal" because of criticism it subsequently received for its alleged ambush marketing."What are the risks to a company that wants to see itself as a global player when federations see it as an
1916 ambush marketer? We see it for Nike as an own goal," Sayal said.But Nike was unrepentant.A spokesman for Nike UK Ltd, the UK subsidiary of U.S.-based Nike Inc, told Reuters there was nothing wrong with targeting consumers near Euro 96, as long as Nike didn't claim to be a sponsor."It's
1916 really a more cost-effective way to reach the consumer, rather than paying through the nose to become a sponsor," Graham Childs said on Thursday."Sometimes we do the official route (and become sponsors) and sometimes we don't...If consumers go to an event, they're fair game," Childs said in a telephone interview.

1918 South Africa is likely this year to approve the purchase of four second-hand British Upholder class submarines, the biggest post-apartheid weapons purchase, government and political sources said on Thursday.The acquisition programme, dubbed "Project Wills", is amongst 145 listed in a secret military capital expenditure programme, which Reuters has seen.The purchase
1918 is expected to cost 2.07 billion rand over the next decade and will overtake an alternative plan to revamp the country's three small and aged French Daphne class vessels.The project is described as "the opportunistic purchase of second-hand submarines" from the British navy.Tony Yengeni, chairman of parliament's powerful standing committee
1918 on defence, said his committee had asked the defence ministry for a special briefing on the project on October 9.He said legislators wanted capital projects delayed until the completion of a defence review next year, but accepted that some deals might need to be decided sooner."The question is whether we
1918 should wait until the review process is finished, in which case these subs would have been sold to someone else, or whether we should go ahead now."I understand we would get them relatively cheaply because they are second-hand," he said.A source in the ruling African National Congress (ANC) told Reuters
1918 that the deal would be approved and that the navy would be told to go ahead immediately."In this case, the decision is not to wait, but to go for it," the source said.An opposition party source confirmed that the defence committee was likely to give the defence department permission to
1918 go ahead with the deal.The sources said government would also restart a stalled 1.6 billion rand project to buy four naval corvettes in time for its inclusion in the March 1997 budget.The diesel-electric submarines were built by VSEL for the Royal Navy in the early 1990s at a cost of
1918 around one billion pounds ($1.55 billion), but saw only brief service.They are now laid up in VSEL's Barrow yard awaiting sale.Helmut Roemer Heitman, correspondent in South Africa for Jane's Defence Review, said the purchase would significantly bolster South Africa's navy, which has been reduced to a few old mine-sweepers, a
1918 handful of Israeli fast patrol boats and two supply ships."They are not the world's sexiest submarines, but South Africa would be getting four for the price of one," he said.$=4.49 rand</

1920 European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Thursday that any decision to alter a cull of British cattle should be based on collective European scientific findings."The European Commission is a scientific organisation ... any decision to change the cull would be scientifically based," he told a news conference
1920 at the end of an EU trade ministers meeting.Brittan was responding to a question which suggested the Commission -- the EU's executive -- had done a U-turn in its policy regarding British proposals to reduce a planned cull of 147,000 cattle as part of a plan to eradicate mad cow
1920 disease.He said any decision to alter the cull should be made by European scientists, who should take advantage of all research available to them.The European Commission, denying on Thursday that it was backtracking, said the new evidence, based on computer studies, showing mad cow disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy or
1920 BSE -- would die out naturally in five years, had been referred to its scientific veterinary committee.Europe has been battling to restore confidence in beef since March when the British government created a massive health scare by saying that BSE could be transmitted to humans.British ministers were meeting on Thursday
1920 to consider whether to stick with the cull programme or scale it back.Fearing a parliamentary rebellion from ruling party members opposed to the full cull, Prime Minister John Major and his colleagues were expected to cut back on the slaughter programme or introduce measures to protect the domestic beef market.</

1922 The European Commission said on Thursday that it had not changed its policy on a plan to kill up to 147,000 cows in Britain most at risk of developing mad cow disease."Suggestions in the British press today that there has been a U-turn by the Commission...are not true," Commission agriculture
1922 spokesman Gerard Kiely told a news briefing.The European Commission eased pressure slightly on Britain by agreeing on Wednesday to examine the new evidence, based on computer studies, showing mad cow disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy or BSE -- would die out naturally in five years.But Kiely said the evidence by
1922 Oxford University scientists had been passed to the EU's scientific veterinary committee 10 days ago.He added that the report would be studied but should not be used as an excuse for delaying the cull.On Tuesday EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told a meeting of EU farm ministers that he was
1922 disappointed that Britain was planning to revise the selective slaughter plan and at the lack of progress since the Florence EU summit in June.The report contained nothing new in that people knew the disease would die out early next century, he said."That aspect of the information...is not new and is

1924 The European Union is lining up export subsidies for its wheat for the first time in a year, but believes a return to grain price wars with the United States is unlikely.Analysts said the EU might bring back subsidies as soon as Thursday when it holds a weekly grain auction,
1924 to dispose of a larger-than-expected crop which has made up for recent shortage."I think you will see Brussels sell some wheat today, maybe up to 300,000 tonnes, and to do this there will be some kind of export refund (subsidy)," a European grain trade analyst said.Subsidies which once caused bitter
1924 trade clashes across the Atlantic have disappeared from the grain market for more than a year as warnings of scarcity drove prices to historic highs.The subsidies were replaced in December with a tax, making it harder for exporters to sell and providing a windfall in revenues for the EU's Commission
1924 headquarters in Brussels.But acknowledging that world wheat and barley prices have fallen sharply in recent weeks, the EU finally scrapped the export tax on Wednesday and is now offering the chance to bid for export subsidies to keep its grain shipments moving.Uppermost in the Commission's mind is the fear that
1924 by exporting too little, a big crop this year could fill up the EU's near-empty grain silos too quickly.The EU faces what could be a record grain harvest of up to 200 million tonnes this year, up more than 10 percent from 1995, after farmers expanded sowings to cash in
1924 on a price boom.Wheat prices peaked near $300 per tonne in April, before sliding to their present $160 per tonne as harvests rolled in.As a top supplier alongside the United States, the EU has signalled it wants to export more in the crop year to next June.But it is drawing
1924 back from any hint of confrontation with its old trade foe.Guy Legras, director general for agriculture at the Commission, a veteran of past trade clashes with the United States, believes a new spat caused by undercutting each others' prices is in neither side's interest."We will align ourselves to wheat prices
1924 in the United States," he told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.From the mid-1980s, Washington and Brussels competed savagely for wheat sales by throwing billion of dollars in subsidies at exports while encouraging their farmers to keep growing more. Prices spiralled down to some $80 per tonne by 1994. Each
1924 blamed the other for starting a price war.Washington has promised to fight "fire with fire" if necessary to meet EU competition but is reserving judgement on whether to go aahead and subsidise its own exports once more.But Republican senator Richard Lugar on Thursday urged the Clinton Administration to put forecful
1924 pressure on Brussels to make sure the European subsidies do not happen.The EU subsidies are available in a grain auction held each Thursday in Brussels. Traders bid for the refund they need to close the price gap between Europe and the rest of the world, where farmers are less protected
1924 and prices are usually lower.But the 15 EU states -- in practice usually guided by the Commission -- can reject the bids if they think they are too steep.In the secretive world of grain, the weekly ritual is seen as a game of cat-and-mouse between the EU and market middlemen
1924 over how much a subsidy should be worth. If the Commission guesses the market wrongly and forks out a bigger subsidy than a trader needs to close a grain deal, the rest is pure profit.</

1935 As Finland hovers on the brink of entry to Europe's exchange rate mechanism, many analysts here believe the perceived medium-term economic or political benefits of bringing the markka into the current ERM regime are illusory.The luxury of huge 15 percent ERM fluctuation bands makes the chosen central exchange rate little
1935 more than a symbolic target. As a result, there is little or no exchange discipline or currency-risk reduction inherent in the existing system.Moreover, many analysts believe that maintenance of 15 percent ERM bands alone will not be sufficient to satisfy the Maastricht criterion on exchange rate stability prior to European
1935 monetary union. Hence, the political imperative of entering the ERM quickly is also notional at best."An ERM with 15 percent bands is of no practical value and and it's not even clear whether its necessary or sufficient for qualification for EMU," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS
1935 Ltd.Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is pushing for a peg, in a bid for tight links with the EU to ensure closer political connections with the west for Finland, which joined the EU in 1995 after decades in the shadow of the former Soviet Union.But the central bank has been
1935 reluctant, with officials voicing concerns that a link may expose the markka to speculative pressures and fuel volatility.The markka rallied to 2.99 per mark early on Thursday, its strongest level in nine months, as speculation about the exact timing of ERM entry intensified.The chairman of the Bank of Finland's board
1935 of parliamentary supervisors IIkka Kanerva said ERM entry was unlikely this month, putting the market focus on early October as likely date for a joint lira and markka ERM fixing.Yet, analysts questioned the logic of trading on back of speculation about the entry level."The focus on the central rate in
1935 a 15-percent-band system is a little misplaced," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "With such wide margins of error it's hard to see why ERM entry would change anyone's investment decision within Finland or toward Finland."Even if Finland attempts to informally target narrower 2.25 percent bands,
1935 that some analysts believe will be necessary to satisfy the EMU criteria, the chances of holding the erratic markka in those bands over two years is slight, they said."In our view, the 2.25 percent rule will be used by the EU as a way of identifying the countries who will
1935 have the least problem with fixed exchange rates and moving to EMU in 1999," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch.That would exclude Spain and Italy, for example, from the first move to EMU, even if they do manage to meet a relaxed interpretation of the other Maastricht criteria,
1935 he said."Finland would have severe problems holding a narrow band regime for long, mainly because it is subject to strong exchange rate shocks that do not effect the rest of the European core," said Prendergast.The Finnish economy, and hence the competitiveness of the markka, is heavily dependent on volatile commodity
1935 prices, with paper and pulp products accounting for about 40 percent of its export revenue.This is a stark contrast to the core European currencies to which Finland intends to peg the markka closely. In 1994 and 1995, for example, the markka was one of the strongest currencies in the world,
1935 in contrast to exchange rate weakness against the German mark elsewhere in Europe.Conversely, the markka's devaluation against its European currency unit peg in 1992, prior to its later flotation, was a precursor to the exit of sterling and the lira from the ERM later that year.Moreover, neighbouring Sweden is Finland's
1935 biggest trade competitor for pulp products and it is currently deeply divided about the merits of joining either the ERM or EMU."Finland is to Sweden what Ireland is to the UK, for example, and it is hard to imagine the markka not being heavily influenced by the swings of a
1935 floating Swedish crown given such trade interdependence," said Meggyesi at Deutsche.Even as Finnish industry chiefs protest the recent rise of the markka, analysts say Finland's strong current account surplus, balanced budget and low inflation argue for an even stronger markka right now. Deutsche argues for an equilibrium level as low
1935 at 2.85 per mark, for example.But Von Maydell at UBS said that while there may be a good case for saying a central rate about 3.00 per mark is fair value right now, that may not be the case over the full course of the economic cycle.</

1943 were part of a series of hostile engagments between Iranian and U.S. forces, whereas it is Iran's position that these were unprovoked attacks on civilian, and commercial facilities."He said the court's jurisdiction to rule on the matter was clearly established by the treaty."What Iran has brought before the court is
1943 purely a legal case arising out of very particular incidents - and one that is grounded in specific provisions of the Treaty of Amity, which Iran maintains the United States has breached by attacking the oil platforms," he told the court.Seyed Mostafa Zeinoddin, head of legal affairs at the National
1943 Iranian Oil Company, rebutted remarks from U.S. navy commander Ronald Neubauer earlier this week that the platforms were being used as military facilities.The U.S. in opening its submissions on Monday said the platforms were used to identify, track and target ships for attack, serving as staging and supply bases for
1943 the Iranian helicopters and small boats used in such attacks.Zeinoddin said the platforms had been previously been targetted by the Iraqis and for that reason had small security detachments to support oil workers, adding that having bases on intallations packed with oil and gas made little military sense."The small number
1943 of security personnel on these platforms were simply there to act as lookouts, to provide early warning of attacks and to provide some comfort and support to the oil company personnel in the light of Iraqi attacks," he said."Such platforms are quite small and are packed with complex equipment. It
1943 is not feasible to install missiles or any other sophisticated military equipment on such small areas and totally impractical to use them as a base for attacks," said Zeinoddin.He said the attacks caused massive economic damage, not only in the immediate loss of oil revenues but also in the huge
1943 cost of rebuilding the platforms, the costs which were still being felt by Iran today.The International Court of Justice, the main judicial organ of the United Nations which settles disputes between states in accordance with international law, is hearing submissions from Iran and the U.S. to determine whether it has
1943 jurisdiction in Iran's claim for compensation.Iran dropped a case at the International Court of Justice over the shooting down in July 1988 or an Iran Air airliner by a U.S. warship after Washington agreed to compensate the families of the 248 Iranians on board who were killed.</

1944 has been made towards democratisation," the parliament said in a resolution.Euro-MPs said that since January 1996, when the customs union came into force, Turkey had fomented tension by actions such as "provocations in the Aegean Sea and Cyprus and aggression in northern Iraq".Parliament only approved the creation of the customs
1944 union last December after the Ankara government had given explicit guarantees that it would take positive action on human rights, democratisation, Cyprus and the plight of the Kurds.Turkey's failure to honour these obligations was "in conflict with the letter and spirit" of the customs union and other EU-Turkey accords, parliament
1944 declared.All EU aid to Turkey should therefore stop immediately, bar funding for projects to promote democracy and respect for human rights, said the resolution, which was backed by six of the parliament's eight political groups.The EU plans to set aside 375 million Ecus ($470 million) between 1996 and 2000 to
1944 help Turkey put the customs union in place.Turkey is also eligible for substantial financing from the EU's MEDA programme, through which 410 million Ecus have been made available for the 15-member bloc's Mediterranean neighbours in 1996.The EU could allocate as much as 842 million Ecus to this group of countries

1945 and D'Amato Bill -- which seek to quash trade with Cuba and Iran and Libya respectively -- was likely to go to the WTO to settle."I don't want to see it ... I don't like to see it, but I think it will happen," he said.Ruggiero, attending a meeting of
1945 European Union Trade Ministers, said settling international disputes was precisely what the WTO was created for."Some think that if there is a dispute, you should blame the WTO. But the fact that the WTO is where the disputes are heard shows that it is working," he said.The EU and U.S.
1945 have been at odds for months over the Helms-Burton Act and D'Amato Bill, and the European Commission is considering escalating its grievances with the WTO.If this happens, a WTO disputes settlement panel would decide whether the EU's complaints that the laws were extra-territorial are justified.Outlining his ambitions for the WTO
1945 ministerial meeting in Singapore in December, Ruggiero said it was important to keep the agenda focussed on the progress the organisation had made in wrapping up global deals left over from its predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.He said the so-called "new issues" -- which include labour standards
1945 and environmental concerns -- should be put aside or tackled at a differant forum.Ruggiero, speaking the day after a tyre-factory closure here was blamed partially on cheaper imports from Eastern Europe, said trade liberalisation almost always created rather than cost jobs.The German rubber giant Continental AG announced on Wednesday that
1945 it was closing its Semperit tyre factory in Ballyfermot with the loss of over 600 jobs."This unfortunate matter is one for the Irish government or the EU," Ruggiero said. 1945 against pushing controversial issues too far, saying this could merely polarise the West from developing nations.</

1949 Britain's M4 money supply growth shot up to 9.4 percent in the year to August, the Bank of England said on Thursday, and consumer credit continued to increase.Economists said the sharp 9.4 percent pick-up in broad money growth, above the government's three-to-nine percent monitoring range, showed Britain's economy was steaming

1949 firm economic recovery," said Jonathan Griggs, economist at Barclays Bank."The UK will look like one of the strongest economies in the world as we go into the pre-election countdown and I think the bias in interest rate markets has to increasingly shift towards...a pre-emptive hike."Thursday's figures came just a day
1949 after August retail sales were shown to have leapt 1.0 percent, taking the three-month rate of growth to its strongest level in eight years and reviving memories of the late 1980s boom.Griggs supported the line taken by Bank of England Governor Eddie George. Minutes of the July 30 meeting with
1949 Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke showed George wished to see official interest rates at 6.00 percent, not 5.75.In those minutes George said money supply growth, often seen as a harbinger of future inflationary pressure, was consistent with rising demand growth this year and next.The UK Treasury said the growth
1949 in August M4 was in part due to special factors, particularly the takeover of the National &amp; Provincial building society by British bank Abbey National and subsequent payouts made to N&amp;P account holders.But economists said the N&amp;P takeover was offset by a fall in gilt repos included in M4.They said
1949 the bounce in M4 growth, after it's tumble to 9.0 percent in July, merely confirmed what most UK data have been singing from the rooftops -- Britain's economy is growing fast as consumers queue up to spend."The overall tone of the data is firm enough to keep the Bank of
1949 England convinced that base rates should be six percent and not 5.75," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.But he added that there was little chance of that in the near future. With elections to be held by May 1997 and the ruling Conservative government trailing badly in opinion
1949 polls, Clarke will come under intense political pressure to boost his party's flagging fortunes.That could involve rate cuts and/or tax cuts at the November budget.Figures released by the Building Societies Association (BSA) at the same time as M4 showed Britain's housing market, a key part of the economy's recovery, continues
1949 to prosper.Although new mortgage approvals fell slightly to about 3.6 billion pounds in August, the underlying trend remains powerfully upwards.BSA director-general said gross advances on a seasonally adjusted basis were down only a little on July, signalling the strongest performance since 1990. 1950 domestic auto sales. 1951 A strongly "Euro-sceptical" speech by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind split the ruling Conservative party on Thursday, just two days before key European negotiations on a future single currency.Rifkind's warning of the dangers of monetary union, in a speech to mark the 50th anniversary of Winston Churchill's vision of a
1951 United States of Europe, delighted Conservative right-wingers who want Britain to rule out membership of EMU.But it drew an angry response from some of the party's most influential elder statesmen who have appealed to Prime Minister John Major not to turn his back on European co-operation.In a letter in Thursday's
1951 Independent newspaper, six Tory grandees including three of Rifkind's predecessors at the Foreign Office wrote: "For us now to rule out British membership of a single currency would be to betray our national interest."Up to now Britain has pursued a policy of delicate balance, refusing to say whether or not
1951 it will sign up to EMU (Economic and Monetary Union), but insisting on its right to join in the preparatory negotiations.But the picture Rifkind painted on Wednesday of Economic and Monetary Union splitting apart the European continent has boosted the confidence of his party's right wing who now see Rifkind
1951 firmly on their side in a bid to keep Britain out.The row is certain to surface again at the Conservative Party's annual conference in October and could weaken the stance of Major's pro-European finance minister Kenneth Clarke at EMU negotiations this weekend in Dublin, Ireland.Britain was always going to be
1951 sidelined at Saturday's meeting of European finance ministers and central bank chiefs.Britain is still arguing internally about the whole concept of monetary union, while the powerful Franco-German alliance is forging ahead towards EMU and just wants to clear up details.Added to the furore over mad cow disease, with Britain now
1951 calling into question a pledge to kill off suspect cattle, Britain's position on Europe is looking increasingly isolated.One of the main points on the Dublin agenda is to put the finishing touches to a Stability Pact, a scheme to ensure that EMU members stick to tough anti-inflationary policies not only
1951 before they sign up to union but afterwards as well.The pact was originally inspired by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and has now been firmly embraced by France.Also on the Dublin agenda are plans to link a future single currency to currencies outside EMU, a further development of Europe's existing
1951 Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).After being unceremoniously ejected from the ERM in 1992 after a huge run on the pound, Britain will stress its view that countries cannot be forced to join "ERM II".But Clarke and central bank governor Eddie George are also expected to assure partners that even if Britain
1951 stays out it will not seek competitive advantage by devaluing sterling.George's deputy Howard Davies has stressed Britain will stick to tough anti-inflationary polices. "Indeed our policy as an "out' would be broadly the same as that of the European Central Bank," he said last week.Another issue the Bank of England
1951 is likely to address at least informally at Dublin Castle is a growing row over plans for an interbank payments system once EMU has begun.To the alarm of the British financial community, French and German banks are pushing for limits on the access banks in countries outside EMU can have
1951 to the system, known as TARGET.But Davies this week demanded that all European nations should have equal access to market liquidity whether they sign up for EMU or not and said moves to prevent this may be illegal.</

1952 market is continuing to thrive.The latest jobless claims report showed greater strength than many Wall Street economists had expected. 1952 ended Sept. 7, the latest period for which the data are available.Among the largest were California, with a drop of 2,744 initial jobless claims, Michigan, with 2,400, New York, with 1,621, and Tennessee, with 1,442.Michigan reported fewer layoffs in all industries, while Tennessee saw fewer layoffs in the transportation equipment,
1952 food, textiles and apparel industries.California and New York had no comment.Labour said one state, Ohio, reported an increase in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Sept. 7 week. Ohio, which reported a rise of 1,148, reported layoffs in the transportation equipment industry.</
1953 Construction starts on new homes and apartments climbed unexpectedly in August to the highest level in nearly 2-1/2 years, the Commerce Department said Thursday.The building rate increased 4.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.525 million units -- the highest rate since March 1994, when it was at
1953 1.531 million, and well above Wall Street economists' forecasts of a 1.445-million-unit building rate.(May be bylined Glenn Somerville)In addition, the department revised upward its estimates for building activity in both June and July, indicating the housing market entered the second half with brisk momentum despite generally higher long-term interest rates.There
1953 were some signs that the building rate may ease later in the year, as applications for new building permits fell 4.4 percent last month to a rate of 1.393 million after rising 3 percent in July.The department revised its estimate of July housing starts to an annual rate of 1.46
1953 million from a previously reported 1.455 million and said June construction was at a stronger rate of 1.49 million a year, instead of 1.474 million.Housing starts were expected to level off in the summer because of the increase in long-term mortgage rates since the beginning of the year. Analysts said
1953 high levels of consumer confidence and strong job growth meant any easing in housing would be modest but did not foresee the continuing pickup in August building.Construction starts on new single-family homes jumped in August by 8.3 percent to a rate of 1.238 million a year after a 5.5 percent
1953 decline in July. The August starts rate on single-family homes also was the highest since March 1994, when it was at 1.28 million.Building of apartments dropped in August by 9.5 percent to a rate of 287,000 following a 12.8 percent increase in July.Regionally, the only area where building declined in
1953 August was in the Midwest, where starts fell 2 percent to a rate of 342,000.Starts in the West surged 13.5 percent to 378,000 a year and in the Northeast they gained 7 percent to a rate of 138,000. Construction in the South, the nation's biggest housing market, picked up 2.8
1953 percent to a rate of 667,000.</

1954 would be limited to "experienced telecommunications operators".He told Reuters that reforming Telecom topped the list of needy reforms in Sri Lanka's creaking infrastructure and was absolutely essential for a country canvassing foreign investment to generate jobs."Without reforming Telecom, Sri Lanka will go into the 21st century as one of the
1954 very few countries which cannot provide telephones even on payment," he said.Sri Lanka's privatisation programme was set up under the Public Enterprise Reform Commission on March 1, 1995.High points so far, include Royal Dutch Shell groups purchase of a controlling stake in Colombo Gas Co and Alpha Airports Group plc's
1954 purchase of a stake in airport duty-free operator Orient Lanka in early 1996.The privatisation of 23 plantation firms started in late 1995, while Airlanka, the ailing national carrier, was restructured by a Chase Manhattan-led consortium.Sri Lanka now has 226,200 direct telephone lines for a population of 18 million people, with
1954 a waiting list for about another 300,000 lines, analysts say.Asirwatham said the sale of the 35 percent stake would be completed by the end of this year.Restructuring Sri Lanka Telecom matches up with the government's stated goal of reforming non-profitable and badly managed public enterprises."Where a total or partial sell-off
1954 is not feasible, the government will try to end most monopolies by encouraging competition and reform others by injecting efficient management," Asirwatham said.The sale of the Telecom stake was recommended by a consortium led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, commissioned by the government in April to restructure the state firm.Other consortium
1954 members were Sri Lankan co-ordinators Development Finance Corporation, technical consultants Deloitte Touche Tomatsu International, and international legal consultants Slaughter and May.Analysts speculated that a 35 percent stake and management of Sri Lanka Telecom could enrich state coffers by about 15 billion rupees ($268 million).Sri Lanka Telecom's post-tax-profit in 1995 was
1954 1.82 billion rupees and it employed 7,750 at the end of March this year.Asirwatham also brushed aside fears that the unionised labour force would oppose reforms.($1=56 rupees).</

1961 The Bank of Cyprus-Greece said on Thursday its first half profit rose 27.6 percent to 2.173 billion drachmas from 1.703 billion in the same period a year earlier.It experienced a 24 percent growth in deposits which grew to 92.7 billion drachmas while loans rose 29 percent to 113.2 billion. Its
1961 total assets increased by 36 percent reaching 190.8 billion."The bank's international expertise and modern approach to banking have sealed its five-year dynamic presence in Greece," it said.The Bank of Cyprus presently has a network of eight branches in Greece and plans to open three new branches in 1997. Its administrative
1961 headquarters will soon move to newly acquired premises at Leoforos Alexandras in Athens. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4</
1962 Investment bank Salomon Brothers expects the markka to join the EU's exchange rate mechanism at a central parity within a 3.02-3.07 range against the German mark."This week's Bank of Finland action and recent rhetoric suggests that a markka ERM entry will take place in coming weeks," Salomon economist Wike Groenenberg
1962 said in a newsletter published on Wednesday.She said the Bank of Finland's repeated currency interventions suggested that Finnish authorities did not want to join ERM at a rate stronger than 3.0 against the mark.She noted, however, that the real-trade-weighted markka is about seven percent below its long-term average."The average exchange
1962 rate over the last year is 3.06 markka per mark, while the average since January amounts to 3.08," she said.The impact of ERM entry on the yield curve would probably be small, she said, as ten-year bonds already appear to be close to fair value with yields only 60 basis
1962 points above German yields.-- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11</

1966 The Finnish markka will not be linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism in September, Ilkka Kanerva, chairman of the Bank of Finland's board of parliamentary supervisors said on Thursday.Speaking to reporters after a regular supervisory board meeting, Kanerva said that for various reasons it would not be possible to decide
1966 to link the markka to ERM during the coming September 21-22 weekend nor the weekend of September 28-29.He declined further comment on the timetable. Any decision to peg the markka to ERM must pass the board of parliamentary supervisors. The markka has been floating since September 1992. "(Any linkage) was
1966 never intended for this weekend," Kanerva said. "The essential people are not around to make the decision," he added.When asked whether a link would be possible the weekened of September 28-29, Kanerva said: "Actually it (that weekend) has been out of the question for a long time."The International Monetary Fund
1966 and World Bank annual meeting is held in Washington from September 24 to October 3.Asked whether it was possible that the markka would not be linked to the ERM at all, Kanerva said: "In principle that is possible."The next regular Bank of Finland supervisory board meeting is scheduled for October
1966 7.-- Helsinki newsroom + 358 - 0 - 680 50 240</

1972 O.70 0.70LON-BAH O.85 0.85 AFRICALON-JNB 1.69 1.68 SCANDINAVIALON-STO 0.7O 0.70LON-CPH 0.65 0.65 LATIN AMERICALON-SAO 2.06 2.05*The rates quoted in this report were obtained by Reuters journalists on confidential basis from a range of airlines, large forwarders and smaller air cargo agents based at the three main London airports.*All prices quoted
1972 in sterling.*The tariffs represent average rates calculated from a range of prices and are indicative or current market activity.Ex-UK air cargo rate rises not seen this year, earmarked forAprilBy Helen HillLONDON, Sept 17 (Reuter) - The usual round of October general rates increases look unlikely as carriers remain reticent to
1972 push the rates up. Next April looks to be the preferred month for any inceases, a Reuter survey showed.An All Nippon Airlines spokesman said the rates would remain stable, adding the market is 'not quite ready'. April next year may be the time ANA looks for an increase, he added.Korean
1972 Airlines cargo manager, Frank Smith, said he is extremely cautious about any autumn increases, adding that April looks more likely.A spokesman from leading freight forwarder, MSAS, Doug Overett, was more adamant about the prospect of rates rises. "Many think the market could not take any rates rises, it is not
1972 a strong enough market to squeeze any more from", he added.Ray Disson, UK cargo manager of Emirates Airline, said the carrier will probably not increase rates to Dubai in October because Emirates had increased rates on the route for the last three years.Some carriers have bucked the trend, American Airlines
1972 has put increases in place and German carrier Lufthansa is considering some increases.John Smith, UK cargo manager of American Airlines, added that a five percent increase had been added to all routes. Demand is very strong, he said, "we would not put prices up unless we were confident".Lufthansa's UK marketing
1972 manager, Ruediger Helm, said Lufthansa has increased its "Flash' express tariffs by six to seven percent on August 1.But as regards general cargo he added, "we are evaluating rates increases but a dramatic increase would not be right'. After the first quarter of the year activity levelled off a little,
1972 he said.Most carriers claim to be looking for stability in the market. United Airlines UK cargo manager, Peter Chase, said United is another carrier preferring to take a more cautious approach to rates rises.However, he commented, United reviews rates twice a year and would prefer to see stability in the
1972 market."We would prefer to create a stable base from which people can operate and we would actually prefer to look at the rates once a year and retain them on an annual basis."Concerning market activity, most report that September has seen a pick-up as the summer season draws to a
1972 close and people return to work.But in all markets, the condition cannot be described as booming, though most say it is in line with their expectations.Barry Gibson of Singapore Airlines (SIA) said so far business to Asia is positive, following the usual August slown-down because of the holidays and factory
1972 closures.SIA had quite severe payload restrictions because of high passenger loads and weather conditions in the summer, he said. Already the airline is able to carry around five tons per flight more than it could in the summer, he said.SIA is another carrier that will not be introducing increases, it
1972 too is looking to next April for rises,he said.Business to north east Asia seems to have shown the biggest pick-up in business. An ANA spokesman said the Japanese carrier already had all of its space booked on Monday for the following weekend and the outlook was good for the coming
1972 weeks. From the UK he was confident the carrier would be above budget, he added.He put the upturn in business volumes down to the UK's favourable exchange rate. But he admitted business inbound from Japan was not quite so buoyant.Korean Airlines in the UK was even more optimistic.Frank Smith, UK
1972 cargo manager said September was in line with expectations and the airline was ahead of this time last year. He added that he was way above budget.He added that despite the busy market he too remains very cautious about any rates rises because the European Continent is not as buoyant
1972 as the UK market.Rates have remained exceptionally stable to the Asian market, showing little signs of changing. Rates to Korea and Australia have edged up slightly to 1.83 stg and 2.05 stg a kg respectively.Most air cargo players operating in the UK-U.S. market have looked forward to the return of
1972 winter schedules as summer charters travelling to popular holiday destinations have created a glut of capacity on certain routes.Kevin Durnin of Viking Freight, representative of Leisure International Airways, said outbound business is difficult especially because of the competition generated because of holiday traffic.Rates have been dumped, market sources said, especially
1972 to destinations such as Orlando and Atlanta during the summer. One shipper requested a 0.35 a kg rate on a 6.5 ton shipment to Atlanta, said one source.However, John Smith, cargo manager of American Airlines, said he felt confident enough in the market and for that reason the carrier had
1972 implemented rates rises.Demand has remained strong to the U.S., he said, though competition on price and quality has remained tough.United Airlines Peter Chase said there are signs of an upward trend this month, although it has not been as rapid as the carrier would have liked, he admitted.He said that
1972 business was not quite as good as last year although he admitted, 1995 was an exceptional year for many. Last year, manufacturers went through a re-stocking programme, he said. Chase added that he expects the fourth quarter to be reasonable but not the boom it was in 1995.U.S. rates are
1972 fairly stable even though a lot of spot-rate activity has being taking place. Rates to Los Angeles have fallen to 0.69 from 0.71 per kg and New York has gone up slightly from 0.60 to 0.61 per kg.In the Middle East market ex-UK, carriers say September has seen a "small
1972 pick-up'. A Gulf Air spokesman said activity has increased slightly and that he is expecting a stable fourth quarter.Disson of Emirates said this year is as good as last year. However, there is more spot-rate activity in the market this month, with even the larger carriers getting involved in some
1972 very competitive pricing, he said.Africa is again generating a lot of interest in the market in the UK as German carrier Lufthansa introduces a weekly DC8 freighter from London Gatwick to Nairobi and Virgin Atlantic prepares to launch its South African service.Lufthansa's Helm said Africa is an interesting market and
1972 not only for the perishables industry. Semi-finished and finished goods are increasing traffic to Africa, he added.People are buying more in Africa and there is much more confidence in southern Africa, especially, which has led more companies to set up production plants in the country, he said.Latin America demand remains
1972 strong, with airline's travelling at full capacity. Paul Ryan, of Varig Brazilian Airways, said Sao Paulo and Rio are full. Shipments for the many automobile manufacturers based in Brazil are generating a lot of business, he said.Rates to Sao Paulo remain strong and are showing an upward swing to 2.06
1972 stg a kg. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017</

1981 of the court". His decision ends five years of controversy over money which was found missing from Maxwell company pension funds after Robert Maxwell's death. In January, Kevin, his brother Ian Maxwell, and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of conspiring to defraud pension funds after an eight month,
1981 multi-million pound trial.Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) sought to bring charges in a second trial gainst Kevin Maxwell, Trachtenberg, and two former Maxwell executives, Albert Fuller and Michael Stoney.The judge on Thursday announced his decision to stay any further proceedings before reading out his judgment. 1981 before the judge to argue that the impending second trial was "oppressive".</

1984 IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it assigned a claims settling ability rating of AA to UAP Provincial Insurance Plc. The company, based in Kendal, is a multi-line non-life insurer operating throughout Britain. It is primarily an underwriter of small to medium-sized commercial risks and personal lines,
1984 IBCA said."The company's published underwriting results have shown losses in the past. However, a very conservative technical reserving policy had, to an extent, masked the true underwriting position, while above average operating costs have also contributed to the underwriting deficit," IBCA said.Action by management to control expenses is underway, the
1984 rating agency said. Union des Assurances de Paris is the parent company of UAP Provincial."A carefully managed investment portfolio has generated income and capital gains that contributed to a return-on-equity that has consistently bettered the UK market average since 1990," IBCA said. "UAP Provincial's technical reserving philosophy is conservative, with
1984 reserves steadily strengthening year on year."The company's liquidity is good and the 1995 solvency margin of 72.4 percent is assessed as very satisfactory for the size and nature of the business, the agency said. "It is IBCA's view that the company possesses a balanced portfolio underpinned by sound underwriting discipline."Multi-channel
1984 distribution and diverse product lines provide a degree of protection from some of the competitive pressures that prevail in the UK market, reflected in good 1996 interim results that are ahead of target."The recent listing on the London Stock Exchange of UAP Provincial's holding company, Sun Life &amp; Provincial Holding
1984 Plc, improves the financial flexibility of the group and raises its market profile," IBCA said.--International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6784</
1985 British ministers met on Thursday to review a cull of up to 147,000 cattle most at risk from mad cow disease after new scientific evidence suggested the mass slaughter was unnecessary.Fearing a parliamentary rebellion from ruling party members opposed to the full cull, Prime Minister John Major and his colleagues
1985 were expected to cut back on the slaughter programme or introduce measures to protect the domestic beef market.But such a move could bring Major once again into conflict with his European Union partners who introduced an export ban on British beef in March to reassure panicky consumers.The European Commission eased
1985 pressure slightly on Britain by agreeing on Wednesday to examine the new evidence, based on computer studies, showing mad cow disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy or BSE -- would die out naturally in five years.But the European Commission's chief spokesman said it was unlikely that the export ban could be
1985 eased quickly."The report is saying that the BSE disease will go away by itself in a number of years," Nikolaus van der Pas told the BBC."The ban is there because BSE is there, so as long as BSE is there it is unlikely that the ban will go." The ban
1985 followed a British government admission that humans might contract the fatal CJD brain disease from eating BSE-infected beef.Roger Freeman, the minister in charge of seeing measures to eradicate the disease are implemented, on Thursday welcomed the Commission's decision to review the new study.But he said Britain was still looking for
1985 a fast easing of the ban, adding: "We are fulfilling our side of the bargain and in return we wanted an early lifting of the ban in stages."At the heart of the debate is anger in London that a deal hammered out by Major with his partners at the European
1985 Union summit in June has failed to lead to a rapid lifting of a ban on British beef exports.After the Florence deal, Major had said he expected the EU to start lifting the ban within five months but this confident prediction found little backing among other EU countries.Officials said Agriculture

1986 high stablility and predictability of revenues, the improvement of the Flemish Community's budgetary performance and a manageable debt burden," S&amp;P said."The Flemish government's cost-containment strategy, in combination with the strength of the diverse economic base are expected to support the financial performance and the gradual reduction in the debt burden,"
1986 the agency said. 1986 much related to industrial activities.""With 26 percent of employment in 1994, the industrial sector remains important and accounts for 70 percent of the Belgian industrial employment. 1986 in recent years."The future budgetary performance will rely largely on moderate expenditures which are not easy to cut," it said.S&amp;P said it will look for continued improvement in the budgetary performance and for a reduction in debt, currently manageable at 73 percent of revenues.--International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041</

1992 take several days for the market to digest the news, which could be interpreted many ways, analysts said."It's bullish on the face of it, since it removes some uncertainty, but I don't think we should get too carried away," Bahr said.Sumitomo did not say how much copper had been liquidated
1992 and it could refer to passing positions on to banks, he said.The question of physical stocks was unclear, but if the firm has loosened its hold on LME stocks, that would be bearish for the market since more supplies would be available, Bahr said. If prices breached $1,950, resistance was

1993 A sharp acceleration in UK broad money in August adds to the list of data showing strong economic growth and potential inflationary pressures, playing into the hands of the Bank of England which wants higher interest rates."M4 remains strong in August. It has again pushed above the monitoring range and
1993 is reflecting a possible danger to inflation. The next move in rates is likely to be up, not down," said Philip Shaw, group economist at Union Plc.M4 grew 9.4 percent in the year to August compared with 9.0 percent in the year to July. Several special factors were at work
1993 during the month, but analysts said they broadly offset one another.The Treasury focused on the 900 million stg boost to M4 prompted by the merger of National &amp; Provincial building society with Abbey National Plc. That was completed in August and led to special payouts to N&amp;P savers and mortgage
1993 holders."That is equivalent to around 0.1 percent on M4 growth in the year," said Shaw.But the fall in gilt repos included in M4 during the month partially offset this. "A fall in gilt repo was a key factor and helped to disguise strong personal sector borrowing," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior
1993 economic adviser at BankAmerica.In August, gilt repos fell by 400 million stg to 8.6 billion stg and reverse repos fell by 1.2 billion stg to 13.5 billion.The figures will prove unhelpful to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke if he is seeking to cut rates in the run-up to the
1993 general election, which must be held by May 1997.And they will strengthen the hand of the Bank of England which wants to see base rates back up at 6.0 percent from their current level of 5.75 percent. "They play into the hands of the governor and add to the great
1993 majority of evidence in the past few weeks suggesting the economy is picking up strongly," said Shaw.The data shows the flourishing consumer sector is driving growth upward. Latest figures showed retail sales in August running at levels last seen in the 1980s consumer boom.A breakdown of the M4 lending figures
1993 by the British Bankers' Association showed consumer credit continued to grow strongly in August. It was up 453 million stg in the month, down slightly from July's massive rise of 556 million stg, but still above the recently monthly average rise of 405 million stg. Building Society Association figures covering
1993 the same month showed demand for mortgages remained strong in August, reinforcing growing evidence of a revival in the housing market.Net new approvals fell slightly in August to 3.643 billion stg from 3.781 billion in August.Adrian Coles, BSA's director-general, said the latest figures represented good news for the housing market."These
1993 figures provide the clearest indication that the housing market is returning to health, with the stronger-than- expected levels of lending over the summer period pointing to further improvements for the rest of the year." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7715</

2019 Six elder statesmen of Britain's ruling Conservative Party urged Prime Minister John Major on Thursday not to yield to increasingly vocal right-wing demands to oppose European integration."To countenance withdrawal from the European Union would be to court disaster," the six, headed by former prime minister Sir Edward Heath, said in
2019 a letter to the Independent newspaper.The letter was published a day after a speech by Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind in which he delighted the so-called "Eurosceptics" on the right-wing of the party with a warning that the EU's plan for a single currency could split the bloc for the foreseeable
2019 future.Three of Rifkind's Foreign Office predecessors -- Lord Carrington, Lord Howe and Douglas Hurd -- also signed the letter, which said: "For us now to rule out British membership of a single currency would be to betray our national interest."The other signatories were Lord Whitelaw, who was deputy prime minister
2019 under Margaret Thatcher, and Sir Leon Brittan, one of Britain's EU Commissioners."We have to find the confidence as a nation and as a people to make a success of our European destiny. The British instinct is to lead, not walk away," the letter said.The move by the six signalled that
2019 the long-running feud between pro- and anti-European Conservatives was set to continue despite the imminence of a general election, which must be held within the next eight months.Earlier, John Redwood, one of the leading right-wing contenders to succeed Major, had lavished praise on Rifkind for his speech, delivered in Zurich.Rifkind
2019 told his Swiss audience the single currency plan would split the EU in two since about half its nations would not qualify to join."We should not proceed down a path of integration faster or further than our people are prepared to go," he said."I say three cheers for Malcolm Rifkind
2019 for beginning to set out our stall," said Redwood, who unsuccessfully challenged Major for the party leadership last year."I think the foreign secretary has looked at the damage this scheme is now doing and has looked at the strong opinion in the Conservative Party, which is that we want a
2019 common market and not a common government," Redwood told Channel Four television.Major's premiership has been dogged by internal party disputes over Europe which have helped to give the opposition Labour Party a lead of some 20 points in opinion polls.In an attempt to hold his party together, Major has said
2019 he will decide whether to join a single currency when full details of how it would operate are clear -- after the next election. He has also pledged a referendum on the issue.His hesitancy is in marked contrast to the keenness with which most other EU leaders, especially German Chancellor
2019 Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac, are pressing for a single currency to come into force in 1999.</
