2039 Mordechai Vanunu might be forgiven for thinking the world had forsaken him.Lauded by activists the world over for daring to reveal details of Israel's top secret Dimona nuclear plant, Vanunu now sits alone in a tiny cell with no prospect of early release from an 18-year sentence."The agent who helped
2039 end the Cold War is still in the cold," he lamented in a poem written last year.But as the 10th anniversary of his arrest approaches on September 30, campaigners around the world are uniting in a bid to persuade Israeli authorities to free him.In the forefront is veteran anti-nuclear activist
2039 Professor Joseph Rotblat, winner of the 1995 Nobel Peace Prize."I find it hard to understand that a civilised country like Israel could keep a man in solitary confinement for 10 years. It is an act of barbarism," Rotblat said in an interview.The Israeli technician was sentenced to 18 years solitary
2039 confinement in 1986 for spilling his country's nuclear secrets. Friends worry about the effect of the incarceration on Vanunu and say he is showing signs of paranoia and depression.Vanunu hit the headlines when he gave London's Sunday Times newspaper photos and details of Dimona, which foreign analysts say has produced
2039 at least 200 atomic weapons.The enraged Israelis, who have never admitted they can make atomic weapons, hit back quickly.In an episode which could have come straight from the pages of a lurid thriller, Israeli intelligence used a blonde agent to lure Vanunu from Britain to Rome, where he was kidnapped,
2039 drugged and shipped home to be tried.Rotblat said Vanunu had been disproportionately punished, especially considering the treatment meted out to Soviet spy Klaus Fuchs, whose information enabled Moscow to detonate its first nuclear weapon in August 1949."Without his information the Russians simply could not have built the nuclear bomb. Fuchs
2039 was sentenced to 40 years in jail, where he worked as a librarian, and was released after nine. It was quite humanitarian," said Rotblat."Compare this to Vanunu: people knew about Israel's nuclear capacity in any case. What he said did not damage anyone. By comparison with Fuchs his treatment is
2039 unimaginable."Rotblat appealed to Israel to release Vanunu when accepting his Nobel award last year. Sources in Norway said Vanunu himself had been nominated for the Peace Prize over the last couple of years.Israel says it cannot free Vanunu ahead of time because he has threatened to reveal more about Israel's
2039 nuclear programme.But campaigners say the Israelis are worried Vanunu will give more details about his kidnapping and thereby prove the operation broke international laws.The main focus of the September 30 campaign will be in the United States, where protests are planned in 10 cities from Los Angeles to Washington.Coordinator Sam
2039 Day said a cage representing Vanunu's cell would be placed outside the Israeli embassy in the capital."There is a great feeling of outrage around world against Vanunu's continuing imprisonment. We see him as prisoner of conscience and not a spy," Day said by telephone from Minnesota."We also want to send
2039 a message that it is by consent of the U.S. government that Israel has a secret nuclear weapons programme," added Day.He said he was increasingly worried by Vanunu's recent letters."He is very impatient about efforts around the world (to free him). He thinks we should be doing more to build
2039 a fire under the government of Israel. The letters seem a little paranoid at times, as if the whole word is out to get him."Protestors in Canada will hold vigils and collect petitions in Winnipeg and Toronto on September 30."I believe it is of importance for the world to know
2039 where nuclear weapons are and to eliminate them as soon as possible. Vanunu provided a service to Israel and the rest of the world," organiser Mordecai Briemberg said from Vancouver."Any movement like this must depend on heightened public awareness and more awareness of the double standards which allow Israel to
2039 do things which other countries can't do."Campaigners will also stage rallies in Britain and New Zealand, which has banned nuclear weapons from its territory since 1987."We believe he was just another peace worker following his conscience and would have hoped that most of us, if we'd had the same amount
2039 of courage, would have done likewise," event coordinator Arthur Quinn said from Wellington.</

2056 Australia and New Zealand on Thursday sealed the merger of their air transport systems into a single A$5.0 billion (US$4.0 billion) aviation market.Under the single aviation market agreement, airlines of both countries have unrestricted rights to fly anywhere in the other country."The arrangement will create a new market worth an
2056 estimated A$5.0 billion and covering more than 31 million passengers a year, by bringing together the domestic travel markets of each country and the trans-Tasman market which links them," Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said.Sharp said he hoped the increased competition from the new market would spark fare cuts of
2056 at least five percent."I'd like to think the figure would be greater, but I would be reluctant to speculate," he said.Sharp said there would be no limit on the number of airlines from either country that could operate services within the single aviation market.The agreement, which comes into force on
2056 November 1, did not include rights for New Zealand carriers to fly beyond Australia, but Sharp said the governments were now considering the move."We are very aware of the interest that New Zealand has in this and we are now negotiating with the New Zealand government over beyond rights," he
2056 said, adding that Australian air operators would also be consulted.Single aviation market discussions began in 1992, but Australia's former Labor government transport minister Laurie Brereton cancelled the plan shortly before it was due to come into effect in 1994.Brereton cited the single aviation market's impact on the value of the
2056 Australian national flag carrier Qantas Airways Ltd, then 75 percent government-owned, as the reason for the last-minute decision.Australia's new Liberal-National government promised before it won this year's March 2 election to restore the deal."We have restored our relationship with New Zealand and repaired the damage done by the previous government's
2056 last minute axing of the agreement," Sharp said.To be eligible to operate in the single market, airlines are required to have at least 50 percent ownership and effective board control by nationals of Australia, New Zealand or both.Two-thirds of the board, including the chairperson, must also be Australians, New Zealanders
2056 or both. The airlines must have a head office and operational base in Australia or New Zealand.Approved carriers are Ansett New Zealand, Air New Zealand, Ansett Australia and Qantas Airways.Air New Zealand is buying Australian transport group TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett's domestic Australian operation.Rupert Murdoch's media firm
2056 News Corp, which holds the other 50 percent in Ansett Australia, will assume full ownership of the New Zealand domestic operator, Ansett New Zealand.Ansett Australia welcomed the move, saying it also expected the agreement to result in lower fares."Ansett has always supported the concept of a single aviation market, so
2056 we welcome the decision of both governments to open the trans-Tasman market," spokeswoman Jane Corbett-Jones told Reuters."We see competition on that route or any route as being beneficial to passengers and carriers alike," she said.(A$1 = US$0.79)</

2121 An export slowdown, low efficiency and deteriorating savings could prevent South Korea from meeting its economic growth targets this year, but the nation still intends to join the OECD, a finance official said on Thursday.Finance Minister Han Seung-soo said South Korea still hoped to join the Organisation for Economic Cooperation
2121 and Development (OECD) despite criticism that entry was premature."Although there are many people who think that because of the current economic difficulties we should postpone our entry, I think the government will push, if invited, to enter the OECD," Han told the Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club.The Paris-based OECD is expected
2121 to announce on September 26 its decision on whether to invite South Korea into the club of rich nations."If Korea had opened its door a hundred years ago like Japan, our economic situation would be much better today," Han said."By opening up thirty years ago, we've grown fast, whereas North
2121 Korea, by closing its door and trying to have its own self-contained economy, is in shambles. We should learn from these historical lessons."This week, the head of a major opposition party called for a postponement of South Korea's plan to join the organisation by two or three years to give
2121 the economy a chance to recover.Han said the economy was expected to grow at an annual rate of about seven percent in 1996. Earlier this year, the Bank of Korea had forecast an annual growth rate of 7.5 percent rate for 1996, against growth of 9.0 percent in 1995."This year's
2121 current account deficit is predicted to surpass $15 billion compared to the earlier forecast $11-$12 billion and is not likely to improve significantly in the near future," the minister said.Some research institutes have predicted the shortfall could reach as high as $20 billion.Han partly blamed cyclical problems for the slowdown.
2121 Corporate profits have been hit by sliding prices in major export items such as semiconductors, steel and petrochemicals.But structural problems, including high interest rates and wages, low efficiency and falling savings rates, were also weighing on growth, he said.</
2122 Japan's ruling coalition agreed on Thursday to convene an extraordinary session of parliament on September 27, paving the way for widely anticipated general elections next month.Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who is also president of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), won agreement on the date of the special parliament session from
2122 leaders of the two other coalition parties, Shoichi Ide of the New Party Sakigake and Tomiichi Murayama of the Social Democratic Party.Politicians, in frequent leaks to the domestic media over the past two weeks, have said Hashimoto would dissolve parliament on the first day of the session and hold general
2122 elections on October 20.But Sakigake head Ide emerged from the meeting saying Hashimoto did not specifically mention a parliamentary dissolution or election date. Under the constitution, elections must be held within 40 days of a dissolution of parliament.Most observers say the prime minister, who has the sole right to dissolve
2122 parliament, is balancing competing demands from the LDP, which is keen on early polls, and its coalition partners, who want to put off elections until next year.Polls are not mandated until July 1997, but the LDP favours going before voters as early as possible before April, when an unpopular rise
2122 in the consumption tax, approved by the Hashimoto government, takes effect.The Social Democrats and Sakigake want more time because they are locked in a bitter row over how to regroup for the coming polls, which will be held under a revised electoral system thought to favour large groupings.A public opinion
2122 survey this week by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a leading financial daily, gave the LDP the highest approval rating with 22.4 percent, while Sakigake scored just 1.2 percent and the Social Democrats 3.7 percent."It is not proper to call a special parliament session just in order to dissolve it," Murayama
2122 said after the coalition meeting.Hashimoto, who has said he will set an election date after settling a dispute with the southern island of Okinawa over U.S. military bases, is helping his junior partners save face by remaining non-committal about the poll date.The Okinawa issue, Hashimoto's thorniest political problem, eased last
2122 week when the island's governor agreed to renew leases for U.S. military bases on the island in exchange for fresh efforts to cut back the bases and $45.8 million fund for Okinawa's economic development.The main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), which has called for elections since the three-party coalition took
2122 power with Murayama as prime minister in 1994, indicated it was spoiling for a showdown at the ballot box."The New Frontier Party welcomes an early election and wants to make it clear that the government wants elections because it has run into a dead end in terms of policy-making," Shinshinto
2122 secretary-general Takeo Nishioka told a news conference on Thursday.With all parties trying to lure voters with calls for cutting red tape and taming Japan's powerful bureaucracy, analysts have said the main focus of the contest will be the effect of electoral reforms introduced in 1994.Designed to correct a system in
2122 which thinly populated rural districts enjoyed vastly more clout than urban areas, the new system features a mix of first-past-the post constituencies and proportional representation.Many politicians predict a showdown between the LDP and Shinshinto over which can win an outright majority in the 500-seat Lower House and name the next
2122 government -- or win more seats than other parties then lure small parties into a coalition.</

2124 South Korean security forces on Thursday killed six North Korean infiltrators as they ruthlessly hunted down the last of around 20 agents who slipped into the country on Wednesday by submarine.Three were cut down by automatic fire as they crouched by a stream to drink water, according to military sources
2124 in the east coast city of Kangnung.A fourth infiltrator standing guard for his colleagues slipped away, they said.Later, another three were killed by security forces, a defence ministry spokesman said in Seoul. He gave no details.On Wednesday the bodies of 11 North Koreans were found huddled together on top of
2124 a mountain situated close to a beach where they landed. 2124 their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.Long lines of troops cradling rifles snaked over rugged mountain terrain around Kangnung to hunt for the last two agents believed to be still on the run. 2124 as an act of "military provocation" at a cabinet meeting, a presidential spokesman said."This is not a simple spy case. 2143 A "borderless" strategy in Southeast Asia has boosted the performance of Digital Equipment and improved its inventories, senior company official J. Graham Long said on Thursday."The approach we've developed about a year and a half ago was to go after this territory in a borderless fashion. The growth has improved
2143 considerably," said Long, vice president for the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) region. The "borderless" programme means Digital's partners in Southeast Asia and developing countries like Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh pay the same price for products.The contracts they sign with Digital are also valid in all the countries,
2143 Long told Reuters in an interview.He said it also meant Digital could also support its partners' programmes across borders. ASEAN comprises Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam."Our overall business revenue grew 40 percent to US$400 million," for the financial year ended June 1996, Long said. "For two years,
2143 we had flat growth in workstations. We implemented this strategy and then we grew 250 percent year to year. This year, we're going to double this business," he said.The company's Alpha range of products grew 55 percent.Long said Digital was aiming to increase revenues by 30 percent a year in
2143 the region for the next three years and to improve profits by 50 percent this fiscal year. He declined to give profit figures. Orders for the first quarter ending this month were expected to be better than the same period last year, compared to a weaker quarter expected by Digital
2143 on a worldwide basis, he said.Long said the "borderless" strategy was unique to Digital's Southeast Asian business and began when the company saw its partners, selling hardware or software, were expanding geographically as ASEAN moved towards eliminating intra-regional trade tariffs.Digital's inventories in the region have also been cut. "Now we're
2143 carrying one-third less inventory than we have before, compared to 18 months ago and we've gotten rid of redundant inventory," said Long.Digital has centralised stocks at its Singapore plant and closed down warehouses in other ASEAN countries. It is now working on developing a central order desk out of Singapore,
2143 Long said.He said competitors could adopt a similar strategy, but saw Digital with an edge from being the first to do it."The competition would have to break down barriers that took us one and half years to break," he said. "Actually, we would encourage any vendor of size to implement
2143 a borderless strategy. We would lose some competitive advantage, but it would be good for the industry. It would be one way to bring IT solutions to developing countries faster."Digital would focus on three areas of business in the region -- high-end Unix systems, Windows NT technology and Internet/Intranet business.Its
2143 strong performance in the region has captured attention at group level, Long said. There was now greater pressure to keep doing better to help bolster the company's earnings on a worldwide basis, he said. For fiscal year 1995/96, Digital reported a loss of US$111.8 million on a worldwide basis.</

2147 Asia's oil importers are fretting over increasing crude oil prices as they begin to feel the sting of rising import bills.They are worrying about their balances of payments and are concerned about higher inflation as increasing prices are passed on to the customer, analysts said on Thursday."Compared with 1995, crude
2147 prices this year are nine to 10 percent higher," said former OPEC secretary general Subroto."The higher prices will certainly put pressure on the balance of trade and balance of payments of consuming countries," Subroto, who now heads a private energy think-tank in Indonesia, told Reuters.Vishvanath Desai, the Asian Development Bank's
2147 energy industry director, said the impact of oil prices was declining thanks to improved energy efficiency, conservation and the use of alternative fuels."In the early 1980s, when oil prices were very high, countries here paid 30-40 percent of their export earnings to import oil," Desai said. "But today, nobody has
2147 to pay more than 15-20 percent at the most."Benchmark Brent crude prices jumped in early September with the explosion of tension between the United States and Iraq to a post Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel. At the end of August, it was $18.63 a barrel. Now, as tensions
2147 ease, it is $22.15.Subroto said he expected prices to remain high until the end of the year because a United Nations/Iraq oil deal has been put on hold because of Iraq's incursion into northern Kurdish areas.Baghdad had been due to sell oil worth $2.0 billion over six months to pay
2147 for food and medicines as an exemption to an embargo resulting from the 1991 Gulf War. Such sales would have pushed crude prices down.How long oil prices will stay high is of special interest to Japan. Official figures show its August crude import bill rose 53.8 percent from a year
2147 earlier, mainly due to higher prices.Crude oil made up 8.9 percent of overall imports last year. "It is a big chunk and we are keeping very careful watch over the global crude oil trade and price movements," a Finance Ministry official said.Economists said the price rise could deepen South Korea's
2147 snowballing trade deficit and spiralling inflation. Crude imports account for more than eight percent of its imports -- 12.4 percent when oil products are included."South Korea is likely to end up the biggest victim in Asia of strong oil prices," said Shin Hoo-shik, a senior economist at the private Daewoo
2147 Economic Research Institute in Seoul.Higher crude prices will hurt India, too.India's external trade as a percentage of GDP is a low 22.6 percent and oil accounts for 21 percent of imports. "The base on which you have to finance oil imports is narrow," said Sanjeev Sanyal, an economist at Crosby
2147 Ltd.Ramdeo Agarwal, research head at Motilal Oswal Securities, said Indian industry was still reeling from an oil product price rise in July. "Even to think of another price hike is nerve-shattering," he said. "It will be very bad at a time when the economy itself is slowing down."China has cut
2147 crude imports since the Iraqi crisis pushed up prices, industry sources said. Chinese officials dismissed any real impact of higher prices on its economy.Economists and government officials were divided over the impact on Thailand. The rise has been "acceptable" and would not harm the economy, said senior official Metta Banturngsuk.But
2147 Lehman Brothers economist Paul Alapat said higher prices would further jeopardise Thailand's trade and current account deficits, both among the highest in the region.Sri Lanka, wholly dependent on imports, is looking at a higher trade deficit. Analysts said they expected higher prices at the pump when the government, faced with
2147 a ballooning budget deficit, presents next year's budget on November 6.For net crude exporters Indonesia and Malaysia, higher prices are better news."Indonesia will receive around $600 million for every dollar increase above the price envisaged in the budget," said Baharuddin, director of state-owned oil company Pertamina."However, 47 percent of this
2147 will be swallowed by crude purchases to feed our refineries."High oil prices will boost Indonesia's GDP growth because "the industrial sector that uses raw material from oil-based products will grow too," said senior official Miranda Gultom.Malaysia could earn around $3.6 billion from oil exports at current prices, up from sales
2147 worth an estimated $2.64 billion in 1995, analysts said.But since oil accounted for only 3.6 percent of exports in 1995, that would only have a marginal impact on GDP, said Rajeev Malek, economist at Jardine Fleming.</

2153 Recent U.S. hedge funds' aggressive short-squeezing has left the Japanese government bond (JGB) market in chaos, overshadowing the future of the market's new settlement system due to start next month.Many market players said the funds' activity pushed some market participants to the verge of failing to deliver necessary cash JGBs
2153 at settlement, which has never before happened.Failure to deliver bonds is strictly forbidden in Japan's settlement system, unlike many other countries where failure is overlooked if a fine is paid.The hedge funds' activity centred around the September JGB futures and the cheapest cash JGBs deliverable against the September contract, namely
2153 the 161st and the 163rd 10-year JGBs. Cash delivery for the September is due on Friday.A record 2.3519 trillion yen ($21.5 billion) worth of the September contract is due for settlement through delivery of cash JGBs, according to the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).Some said those funds would receive about 1.8
2153 trillion yen ($16.5 billion) worth or about three-fourths of the total JGBs to be delivered.Many traders said CS First Boston Ltd seems to be receiving much of the cash delivery against the September contract, trading on behalf of the hedge funds.One official at CS First Boston said he was aware
2153 of such market talk but declined to comment, citing client confidentiality.While the hedge funds are said to have huge long positions in the 161st and the 163rd JGBs through cash delivery of the September contract, they have been borrowing an enormous amount of the same JGBs, bond traders said.Some traders
2153 said the funds have borrowed about 500 billion yen ($4.58 billion) worth of the 161st JGBs, and the same amount of the 163rd JGBs.As the outstanding amount of these two JGBs are about 700 billion yen ($6.42 billion) each, the hedge funds have a virtual monopoly over them, some traders
2153 said.Reflecting an extreme shortage of these JGBs, their repo rates (lending fees) have shot up in the last couple of weeks. Some said the repo rate for the 161st JGBs went over 30 percent of the face value in the offshore market, compared with 0.2-0.3 percent about a month ago.Some
2153 dealers complained the recent movement in the market was close to manipulation, as those who amassed and hoarded the cheapest JGBs were lending these bonds to helpless market players who were short of them, at extremely high rates.They said this kind of activity could have been illegal if it had
2153 been in the United States.The whole incident also highlighted the lack of liquidity of the JGB market, dealers said. "Some people might have placed too much trust in the liquidity of the JGB market," said a dealer at a Japanese bank.The lack of liquidity is a serious problem particularly at
2153 a time when the market is launching the rolling settlement system, said Yoshiki Fujioka, manager of the Yen Bond Derivative Department at Credit Lyonnais.The JGB market on Thursday began rolling settlement, called T plus seven, in which every transaction is settled seven business days after trading from October.Those who go
2153 short in specific bonds have to borrow them on the repo market and therefore liquidity of the repo market is a prerequisite for smooth settlement, traders said.Up until Wednesday, cash JGBs trading was settled once every five days. Thursday marks the first day of the new system, with dealing on
2153 Thursday settled on October 1. ($1-109 yen)</

2162 Sanyo Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday that its "capital adequacy" ratio at the end of September was estimated about 170 percent.Japan's Securities and Exchange Law requires brokerages to disclose the ratio, which indicates their financial health. The ratio is that of net capital and latent profits on securities holdings
2162 against risk-weighted assets and potential losses from securities business.A ratio of below 150 percent is considered an early warning level and if it falls below 120 percent, financial authorities can order brokers to improve their operations.</

2169 Japan's three ruling coalition parties will finalise an outline on how to reform the country's powerful Finance Ministry next week, a senior coalition lawmaker said on Thursday."We hope the plan would be something that we can boast about ahead of widely expected general elections," said Shigeru Ito, head of the
2169 coalition's special task force on MOF reforms.The special task force, which ended seven months of deliberations today, left the thorny issue of how to separate the inspection function from the ministry to senior policymakers to decide. The senior policymakers, who are scheduled to meet on September 24, would also decide
2169 whether to separate the budget-forming function from the ministry. The outline will be endorsed by the coalition parties on September 25, Itoh said."I personally feel the reforms must be drastic," he said.The ministry, long viewed as the pinnacle of Japan's elite bureaucracy, has come under fire for its handling of
2169 problems in the nation's banking industry and has been urged to change its system of trying to deal with banking crisis internally.The task force agreed to several options in separating the inspection function of the financial industry from MOF. One option was to set up a body completely independent from
2169 the ministry while another was to set up an entity which the ministry would still have some influence over, he said."Many of the task force members said they did not want half-hearted reform (of separating the inspection function from MOF)," Itoh said.However, the task force agreed to streamline the ministry's
2169 functions by merging its banking and securities bureaux into one. The international finance bureau will remain as it stands now, but consideration should be given to incorporating part of its function to the newly merged bureau, he said.</

2227 Japanese banks are asking regulators to open the door for them to tap directly into Japan's huge business of selling and managing mutual funds.Banks are keen to use their extensive branch networks to directly sell mutual funds, called investment trust funds in Japan, to depositors throughout the country and to
2227 diversify the range of businesses they offer.Although banks have investment trust affiliates these have few branches, and banks themselves are not allowed to sell or manage such funds.Rather than managing the funds, the banks are eager to sell the variety of investment trust funds available to individuals in order to
2227 earn commissions."In the United States, outstanding mutual funds total nearly 200 trillion yen ($1.829 trillion). But in Japan, they are only about 50 trillion yen ($457.46 billion)," said an offical at a major commercial bank."The figures show Japan's investment trust market has the potential to grow much bigger," he said.The
2227 popular perception in Japan is that ordinary individual investors show little interest in trusts as they are poorly run.However, the bank official said the slowness in sales of investment trusts was due to insufficient sales efforts by brokerages.Poor returns on stock investments have also kept small investors away from the
2227 funds, industry sources said."I don't think major Japanese brokers are serious about selling investment trusts offered by bank affiliates," the bank official said. "We think we are quite good at managing the trusts, so we need the effective sales channel."Banking sources said the banks' long-established credibility could help polish the
2227 image of investment trusts.Most of Japan's investment trusts are managed by brokerages' subsidiaries and sold via stock sales staff at brokerages.To boost competition and attractiveness of the trusts, the Finance Ministry allowed banks to join the investment trust management business through their affiliates in 1993.The ministry also took steps in
2227 late 1994 to improve the performance of the investment trusts and increase their transparency to attract more small investors. But data from the Investment Trusts Association show net assets of stock investment trusts have continued to fall since the early 1990s.Net assets of stock investment trusts totalled 13.53 trillion yen
2227 ($123.79 billion) at the end of July, down from 45.55 trillion yen ($416.74 billion) at their peak at the end of 1989, when Tokyo's Nikkei stock average hit a record 38,957.44. On Wednesday, the Nikkei closed at 21,156.75.Takashi Tamaki, chairman of the Regional Banks Association of Japan, has said the
2227 industry group would ask the government to implement deregulation, including of sales of investment trusts at bank branches. His remarks follow similar requests which Japan's 10 biggest banks made to the government in August.The Securities and Exchange Council, an advisory body to the finance minister, is expected to examine the

2302 Japan's ruling coalition agreed on Thursday to convene an extraordinary session of parliament on September 27, a move politicians have predicted will lead to general elections next month.Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who is also president of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), won agreement on the date of the special parliament
2302 session from leaders of the two other coalition parties, Shoichi Ide of the New Party Sakigake and Tomiichi Murayama of the Social Democratic Party.Politicians have predicted that Hashimoto will dissolve parliament on the first day of the session and call general elections for October."We have agreed to convene an extraordinary
2302 parliament session on September 27," Ide told reporters after a meeting of the coalition leaders.Ide said Hashimoto did not specifically mention a parliamentary dissolution at the meeting. The prime minister has the sole right to dissolve parliament.Under the Japanese constitution, elections must be held within 40 days of a dissolution
2302 of parliament.Polls are not mandated until July 1997, but Japanese media have reported that Hashimoto has already decided to call general elections on October 20.Many in the LDP want elections as soon as possible, but the two smaller parties, embroiled in a dispute over how to contest the polls, want
2302 more time, analysts say."It is not proper to call a special parliament session just in order to dissolve it," Murayama said after the coalition meeting.In the past week, Hashimoto has reiterated earlier statements that he would set an election date after settling a dispute with the southern island of Okinawa
2302 over U.S. military bases.The Okinawa issue, the thorniest political problem his government faces, eased last week when the island's governor agreed to take steps to renew leases for U.S. military bases on the island, ending a bitter one-year standoff with Tokyo.Hashimoto pledged fresh efforts to cut back the bases and
2302 set up a five billion yen ($45.8 million) fund for Okinawa's economic development if Okinawa governor Masahide Ota eased calls for a total pullout of U.S. forces, which are seen by Tokyo as a bulwark of regional security.Analysts have said the main focus of what is likely to be a
2302 mostly issue-free election will be the effect of drastic reforms in the electoral system introduced in 1994 to balance a system in which thinly populated rural districts enjoyed vastly more clout than urban areas."I assume the public now want a stable government. The LDP has now secured about 287 candidates
2302 for the general elections," LDP Secretary-General Koiichi Kato told reporters on Wednesday. The LDP has 206 seats in Japan's 511-seat Lower House of parliament.Meanwhile, the main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) looks ready for an early election."The New Frontier Party welcomes an early election and wants to make it clear
2302 that the government wants elections because it has run into a dead-end in terms of policy-making," Shinshinto Secretary-General Takeo Nishioka told a news conference on Thursday.</

2316 sister for the past 20 years. He told Reuters in a recent interview that he bought the land from a friend for about 30 yen (27 cents at current exchange rates).A long-dormant sovereignty dispute over the uninhabited islands, called the Senkakus in Japan and the Diaoyus in Chinese, erupted in
2316 July after the right-wing Japan Youth Federation erected a lighthouse on one of the islands.The move angered Taiwan and China, which each challenge Japan's claim to the islands, and sparked anti-Japanese protests.Kuribara said his family did not give the group approval to build the lighthouse, and dismissed its presence as
2316 unnecessary to protect ships in the area. He refused to say whether he would take any action against the group.The head of the right-wing group said last week that there was a "tacit" agreement between the group and the Kuribaras."It has nothing to do with me," Kuribara said of the
2316 furore. "I didn't have the faintest idea that it would become such a big issue."Kuribara was speaking at his home outside Tokyo where he runs a hall used for wedding receptions.China and Taiwan have condemned the construction of the lighthouse and demanded its immediate removal. China has charged that Tokyo
2316 is conniving with the right-wingers.Kuribara accused the Japanese government of failing to clarify its sovereignty over the islands to the international community."Unless the government takes a firm stand, our ownership of the islands will be jeopardised," he said."We can't let go of our hold on the islands," he said. 2316 we do so, we will become traitors to the country."Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.The Taiwan government also claims ownership of the islands, saying they are under the jurisdiction of the northeastern
2316 Taiwanese county of Ilan.Japan was given control of the islands in 1972 by the United States, which had administrated the islands along with Okinawa since the end of World War Two.Kuribara himself owns the biggest of the five uninhabited islands, His younger brother owns two other isles and his sister
2316 owns another.Kuribara said he bought the islands for 30 yen (27 cents) from his friend about 20 years ago.The family's ownership of the islands was confirmed by local government records. 2316 he was able to acquire the islands at such a low price, he said: "You see the islands are far more isolated than the Galapagos."</

2322 Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, aiming to transform itself from a phone firm into a multimedia superpower, will launch a new network business in January to tap explosive demand for computer communications.The telecoms goliath also plans to open up its network for use by rival Internet access providers and leased-line
2322 providers, partly to counter support for the government's proposed break-up of the company.The new service, called the Open Computer Network (OCN), will be a data transmission network giving users access to the Internet and private lines for computer communications.The network will provide a platform for NTT to move into new
2322 areas, such as software and cross-border services. Japanese law currently limits NTT's operations to domestic services.The system will use routers, which cost only a small fraction of conventional telephone exchange systems used in voice communications. NTT will spend only 12 billion yen ($110 million) on the project during its first
2322 year."The OCN service is the mainstay of our next-generation multimedia business," said Masamichi Tanabe, NTT's senior vice president in charge of multimedia services. "Inquiries (about the OCN) are flooding in. We need to respond to our customers' demands for low-cost international network services."He said NTT hopes eventually, through affiliates, to
2322 launch businesses such as security-related applications on the OCN.The new network will also pose a serious threat to existing Internet and leased-line providers that use more expensive systems such as telephone exchanges.NTT will charge 30,000 yen ($275) to 40,000 yen ($366) a month for a 128 kbps (kilobits per second)
2322 OCN line. Leased lines of that speed using telephone exchange systems cost 280,000 yen ($2,568) a month for Osaka-Tokyo services.Though five times as fast as a conventional phone line, 128 kbps is a comparatively low speed for computer communications."We are concerned. There are a lot of customers who would prefer
2322 such a cheap service (as OCN) even if it's of lesser quality," said a spokesman at Japan Telecom Co, an NTT rival."Considering its brand image and the strength in the local call market, NTT will be able to acquire half Japan's Internet access service market," said Goldman Sachs analyst Eric
2322 Gan.According to industry estimates, Japan's Internet access service market totaled 25 billion yen ($229 million) in 1995, and will balloon to between 200 billion yen ($1.83 billion) and 300 billion yen ($2.75 billion) in 2000.Moreover, the OCN service is expected to strengthen NTT's earnings structure by boosting profits from local
2322 calls and sales of high-speed digital connections.Gan expects profits from local calls to catch up with those from long-distance calls within two years, buoyed by users utilising the OCN to access the Internet and other communications services through their personal computers.Long-distance services now account for roughly 75 percent of NTT's
2322 parent operating profits, Gan said.A more important concern for NTT, however, is the pending government decision, expected during a parliament session due to begin next February, on whether to split up the company.Officials at NTT are eager to give the impression that they will cooperate with other firms and allow
2322 open access to the OCN, and to avoid stirring up fears that they are trying to gain monopolistic advantage in information services. Such fears would refuel the calls for an NTT break-up.Tanabe says competing firms will be able to use OCN's local loops at low rates to launch their own
2322 services. "We have no intention of becoming the sole winner in this OCN business."But some industry officials are sceptical, saying NTT may forget this open philosophy once the break-up debate ends."NTT will have to go slowly, at least in the beginning, so as not to take away too much revenue
2322 from existing operators," said Kiyohisa Ota, an analyst at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc. ($1=109 yen)</

2354 A new rolling settlement system began on Thursday for transactions in Japanese government bonds (JGBs) to reduce risks in settlement, an official at Japan Bond Trading Co said on Thursday."Beginning with JGBs traded on September 19, deliveries will always take place seven days after the transaction date, rather than eight,
2354 nine or even 10 days, which used to be the case," said Akio Kimura, director at Japan Bond Trading Co, the largest inter-dealer broker in Japan.JGBs traded on Thursday will be settled on October 1, he said. Under the new system, settlement will take place every business day, rather than
2354 on fixed dates, as was the practice earlier.JGB settlement formerly took place on fixed dates -- the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and 30th of each month -- and it took from seven to 11 business days to settle JGB transactions.The adoption of rolling settlement will lessen risk by reducing
2354 the amount of money involved on a particular settlement day and by shortening the time lag between trade and settlement, said Kimura of Japan Bond Trading. "Under the old system, there could only be six settlement days in a particular month. The new system may have as many as 20
2354 settlement days each month, so there will be less concentration of funds," Kimura said.As for the shortening of the time lag between trade and settlement to reduce risk, the eventual goal is to achieve "T+3," or settlement on the third day after the transaction."Our goal is to achieve T+3 by
2354 April of next year," Kimura said. In the Eurobond market, transactions are settled three days after a deal and U.S. Treasuries are settled one day after the transaction.</

2370 Japan's claim to small disputed islands in the East China Sea dates back to January 1895 when the government formally declared the Senkaku Islands, called the Diaoyus in Chinese, part of Okinawa Prefecture.The territory lies in the East China Sea, west of Japan's Okinawa island, northeast of Taiwan and east
2370 of China's southeastern Fujian coast.It is now uninhabited but until the 1940s could boast a dried fish factory on one of its larger islands.With the signing of the San Francisco Peace Treaty in 1951, Japan was deprived of all of its territories seized since 1895, including Taiwan, Korea, and southern
2370 Sakhalin.The U.S. trusteeship of the Ryukyu Islands, the current Okinawa Prefecture, was permitted indefinitely, and the Senkaku Islands, registered as part of Okinawa, were also under the jurisdiction of U.S. forces until Okinawa's return in 1972.During the U.S. occupation of Okinawa, the islands were used for military drills by U.S.
2370 forces.In 1971, Taiwan and China both officially claimed the islands as theirs, but neither China nor Japan brought up the issue in 1972 when the two nations issued the landmark China-Japan joint communique.Japan ceased diplomatic relations with Taiwan following the communique, recognising only the communist government.When Japan signed a peace
2370 treaty with China in 1978, Deng Xiaoping, the then vice-premier of China, said the territorial issue between the two countries "will be shelved until the next generation comes up with a solution".But the Japanese government claimed there was no pending territorial issue regarding the Senkaku Islands.In the same year, a
2370 first makeshift lighthouse was set up by a Japanese ultra-rightist group on the largest of the islands, called Uozuri-jima in Japanese.The first major flare-up on the issue of sovereignty, which had been dormant for many years, came in 1988 when the same rightist group Nihon Seinen Sha (Japan Youth Federation)
2370 rebuilt the lighthouse and sought official recognition.Taiwan had been particularly strong in voicing its protest, which made Japan back down and leave the application for official recognition of the lighthouse pending "out of diplomatic considerations", according to a Maritime Safety Agency spokesman.Japan lodged a formal protest in 1992 when China
2370 claimed the disputed islands by enacting the Law of the People's Republic of China on its Territorial Waters and Their Contiguous Areas.In the law, China claimed the South China Sea and much of East China Sea, which includes the Senkaku Islands, as "contiguous areas".The United Nations Convention on the Law
2370 of the Sea -- adopted by the General Assembly in November 1994 to nudge countries with rival territorial claims to settle them -- only sparked renewed rivalry.In July, the rightist group built its third lighthouse in the smaller of the islands, owned by a family in Saitama Prefecture north of
2370 Tokyo.The Japanese government has continuously maintained that it was not involved in, nor would it endorse, any private activity taking place on privately owned property.</

The men had all been shot through the head in what authorities said was a mass suicide.One other North Korean was flushed out of
2373 hiding on Wednesday, leaving eight unaccounted for in the most serious infiltration drama since the 1960s.Communist espionage agents from North Korean have in the past chosen suicide over capture.A defence ministry spokesman in Seoul said the fugitives were apparently trying to flee home across the land border."Villagers have reported that
2373 some suspected infiltrators asked them about roads leading to the Taebaek mountains," he said. The mountain range straddles the heavily fortified border, sealed since the 1950-53 Korean War.South Korean President Kim Young-sam denounced the infiltration as an act of "military provocation", the domestic Yonhap news agency reported."This is not a
2373 simple spy case. I regard it as a kind of military provocation," Yonhap quoted Kim as telling a cabinet meeting."Despite food shortages, the reason why North Korea sent armed infiltrators is that they still have not given up their ambition to reunify Korea by force," Kim was quoted as saying.The
2373 head of the Agency for National Security Planning, Kwon O-kie, was quoted as saying the incident amounted to "infiltration by armed guerrillas".Troops with sniffer dogs combed mountains and beaches around Kangnung after a dusk-to-dawn curfew was lifted on Thursday. The submarine remained stranded on rocks.The North Korean captured on Wednesday
2373 was quoted by local media as saying the vessel drifted into Southern waters after developing engine trouble.His dead colleagues were members of the crew, not trained saboteurs, Lee Kwang-soo, 31, was quoted as saying.Troops who boarded the abandoned grey craft found automatic guns and ammunition along with canned food and
2373 shoes.The incident has further raised tensions between the two hostile neighbours who face each other across the world's most heavily fortified border.Pyongyang has not commented on the drama, one of the deadliest since 1968 when 31 North Koreans reached the presidential Blue House in Seoul.Twenty-eight were killed in a gunbattle
2373 in which 34 Southern troops, police officers and civilians also died.Earlier this year, armed North Korean troops staged illegal exercises in a border buffer zone, and following that scare U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean head of state Kim Young-sam made a peace overture to Pyongyang.They proposed four-way talks,
2373 also including China, but North Korea has yet to respond.However, there had been hopeful signs that Pyongyang was being lured out of its hostile isolation in its desperation for help to ease a food crisis.</

2375 South Korean finance minister Han Seung-soo said on Thursday the country was not expected to meet its 1996 economic targets because of an export slowdown, high costs and low efficiency.(Corrects year in headline and first paragraph from 1997)"It will be rather difficult to attain the economic performance that we had
2375 initially forecast earlier this year," Han told members of the Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club.Economic growth in 1996 has been revised to around seven percent from a real 9.0 percent a year earlier.The consumer price index grew by 4.4 percent in the first eight months of the year, close to the
2375 target of 4.5 percent for the whole year. And the current account deficit is now predicted to surpass $15 billion from an originally forecast $6.4 billion. Han said the shortfall "is not likely to improve significantly next year". Han said cyclical problems were partly to blame. Corporate profitability has been
2375 hit hard by sharp drops in the prices of major export items.But he said the root problem was structural."Our wages have been increasing at a faster rate than in competing countries, and the corporate financial burden grows larger as high interest rates continue," Han said.Interest rates are among the highest
2375 in the world with benchmark three-year yields are now at 12.11 percent and wages growth has been in double-digits for several years. Han added that logistical costs and land prices in South Korea were considerably higher than those in most other countries and government regulations were hobbling business."These structural problems
2375 have been manifest for many years, but the recent depreciation of the yen and the drop in major export prices have made them more conspicuous as major obstacles to our economy's progress," Han said.He said the government would stress economic stability by curbing inflation and boosting corporate health. Han said
2375 joining the OECD would help accelerate Korean economic deregulation and improve economic structural problems.Despite criticism over Korea's entry into the OECD as premature, Han said the government "stands firm in our pursuit of accession to the OECD".-- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647</

2381 China's military authorities have blocked the promotion of a general after he was accused of sexual harassment by a woman soldier, Chinese sources said on Thursday.General Qu Cong has been transferred back to the Guangzhou Military Zone in the southern province of Guangdong after the soldier, a member of the
2381 Uighur minority in restive northwestern Xinjiang, accused him of sexual harassment during a trip to North Korea, the sources said.Qu and the soldier, whose identity was withheld in the rare expose of sexual harassment in China, were members of a Chinese military delegation that visited North Korea recently, said the
2381 sources who asked not to be identified.Qu had initially been designated for promotion to chancellor of the Liberation Army Art Academy, the sources said.His promotion was blocked after Jiang Zemin, chairman of the powerful Central Military Commission and general secretary of the ruling Communist Party, ordered commission member General Yu
2381 Yongbo to look into the scandal and placate Xinjiang."Xinjiang was very dissatisfied," one of the sources said.The general tried to force the soldier to have sex with him, but she resisted, the sources said."If (the victim) were not Uighur and were Han Chinese, nothing would have happened," a second source
2381 said.Uighurs are a Moslem Turkic people indigenous to Xinjiang, a region that borders Afghanistan, Pakistan and three former Soviet central Asian states of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. They speak a language closely related to Uzbek.While China has no qualms about crushing a separatist movement in Xinjiang, it says it has
2381 poured billions of dollars to develop the region and that Uighurs are a privileged class, enjoying preferential treatment in school and employment.Xinjiang has a long history of ethnic unrest and has been hit by sporadic pro-independence bombings and assassination attempts in recent months.During a recent trip to Xinjiang, General Zhang
2381 Zhen, a vice-chairman of the commission, said soldiers should "serve as models for the unity of various nationalities"."If the unity...of various nationalities is firm like a rock, there is no difficulty that cannot be overcome and any plot aimed at destroying the stability and development of Xinjiang is doomed to
2381 failure," Zhang was quoted as saying.Chinese Premier Li Peng was in the restive region this month to break ground for the construction of a railway, which he said would boost the confidence in the Communist Party among ethnic minorities.The railway would help to narrow the gap between the wealthy eastern
2381 and impoverished western parts of China, Li said at the ground-breaking ceremony in Korla city.In May, China ordered tighter border controls in the region to prevent the smuggling of weapons and subversive materials from neighbouring Moslem states. It also ordered a crackdown on campuses in the sprawling region.In the same
2381 month, separatists wanted for an attack on a Moslem leader and a government adviser were shot dead in a gunbattle.</

2383 Floundering gasoline retail prices are expected to eat away at Japanese oil companies' profits for the third consecutive year, industry analysts say."The oil industry's profits have slumped from a peak to their worst ever in a matter of years," Toshinori Itoh, a senior analyst with private think-tank Daiwa Institute of
2383 Research (DIR) said."Not only are gasoline retail prices still weakening, but margins for kerosene and gas oil are also falling," he said.Itoh expects combined current profits at seven Japanese refiners -- Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, 5004 T Koa Oil Co Ltd, Cosmo Oil Co Ltd, Fuji
2383 Kosan Co Ltd, General Sekiyu KK and Japan Energy Corp -- to plunge an average 52.23 percent in fiscal 1996/97 ending March 31 compared to a year earlier, to 34.4 billion yen ($315 million).This compares with the seven firms' combined current profits of 175.96 billion yen ($1.61 billion) in fiscal
2383 1993/94.Current profit is pre-tax profit including losses or gains on investments. Most refiners are due to announce their mid-term company results in October.In 1993/94, leading refiner Nippon Oil Co posted current profits of 42.3 billion yen ($388 million). Itoh forecasts Nippon Oil's current profits for 1996/97 at four billion yen
2383 ($36.6 million).Refiners have been battling in vain to boost oil product retail prices, partly by keeping refinery operations low and oil product stockpiles tight.A new wholesale price system introduced by leading refiners this April, which brings kerosene and gas oil prices higher, is also meeting stiff opposition from retailers and
2383 consumers."Refiners had been counting on gasoline retail prices to recover this year, but prices have weakened further," Takashi Kawai, an analyst with the Nikko Research Center Ltd said.The retail price of gasoline, formally the pillar of refiners' income, has been falling since mid-1994, when the industry grew certain that deregulation
2383 of the oil product imports was inevitable.Anticipating a flood of cheap imports, refiners rushed to build gasoline stations and encourage dealers to slash retail prices in a desperate attempt to secure market share.Last April, oil product imports were liberalised and refiners lost their monopoly on imports of oil products, such
2383 as gasoline, kerosene and gas oil.In addition to the poor oil product retail market, rising crude oil prices have also dealt a crippling blow to the industry, analysts said."Refiners have not been able to pass on higher costs deriving from strong crude prices and a weaker yen against the dollar,
2383 to the retail stage," Nikko's Kawai said.During the period from April to August, leading refiners raised their wholesale prices by about 1.5 yen ($0.013) per litre reflecting higher crude prices and a weaker yen against the dollar. But during the same period, retail prices dropped by about two yen ($0.018)
2383 to a national average of 105 yen ($0.96) per litre.In August 1995, the national average gasoline retail price was 113 yen ($1.04) per litre, and 120 yen ($1.10) in August 1994."Refiners will be in a very serious situation if high crude prices prevail and retail prices do not recover," Itoh
2383 said.Unlike western major oil companies which develop a large quantity of their own crude and profit from higher crude prices, Japanese oil firms do not benefit from strong crude prices, especially when retail prices are easing.Crude oil developed by Japanese oil firms overseas accounts for only an estimated 15 percent
2383 of Japan's total crude imports, Kawai said. Japan imported 266.83 million kilolitres of crude oil in calendar 1995, official statistics show. ($1=109 yen)</

2407 Once sellers of raw materials to the industrialised world, Southeast Asian countries are now rapidly-industrialising "Tigers" with no thought of turning backSome are further along the road than others, but all talk more about the pace than the direction of development even though some, like communist Vietnam, are just beginning.Malaysia
2407 and Indonesia have made impressive strides. In Thailand progress has been slower while the Philippines is still suffering from the economic legacy of profligate former president Ferdinand Marcos.MALAYSIA DOUBLES MANAUFACTURING OUTPUTNowhere has the change been more dramatic than in Malaysia, once a purveyor of rubber, tin and palm oil, now
2407 among the world's largest producers of semiconductors.The share of primary commodities in the economy has fallen by more than half to around 20 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) over the last decade. That of manufactured goods has more than doubled to about 31.5 percent, Malaysia's Economic Report for 1995/96
2407 says."I think the industrialisation process is well under way. From nowhere, it has become the world's leading maker of semiconductors. There is no looking back for Malaysia," said Liew Yin Sze, economist with J.M. Sassoon &amp; Co in Singapore."There is fairly consistent decline in dependence on commodity exports. It has
2407 happened everywhere."Economists say a key factor in the transformation was a recession between 1985-87 in the OECD countries, which caused a sharp drop in prices of tin, rubber and palm oil -- then Malaysia's primary exports.The Malaysian economy went into a tailspin. The impact was so severe, another racial conflict
2407 between Malays and ethnic Chinese of the type which traumatised the country in the late 1960s looked likely.A series of dramatic economic policy changes by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who opened up the country to foreign investment and privatised state-owned companies and infrastructure projects, pulled it back from the brink.The
2407 response was huge. Malaysia's economy has been growing since at more than eight percent a year.Under Mahathir's Vision 2020 programme to make Malaysia a fully industrialised nation by that year, economists say GDP growth will have to be maintained at that level.Sassoon's Liew said that although manufacturing now dominated the
2407 economy, this would change as it moved toward more capital intensive, high-technology and service-oriented industries.THAILAND NEEDS MORE HUMAN RESOURCESIn Thailand, economists say the government will have to work harder on human resources, infrastructure and an outdated tax system to ensure a transformation to full industrialisation.With little virgin land to be
2407 opened up to farming and the prospects of a dramatic improvement in agricultural prices slim, dependence on primary exports must decline."Inadequate infrastructure is one of the major constraints," said Supavud Saicheau of the Phatra Research Institute. "And about only one third of our workforce finishes high school."Thailand has good industrial
2407 potential, particularly in the automobile industry and in electronic products, said Chalongphob Sussangkarn, president of the private Thailand Development Research Institute."But the government will have to chip in much more before that can happen," he said.Thailand's transition from agriculture economy to industrialised economy began to show in 1985 when manufactured
2407 goods exports first exceeded primary commodity exports.Another crucial step took place in 1993 when medium-to-high-tech products made a splash and started to replace exports from labour-intensive industries as the economy's growth engine.To maintain traditional strength in commodities in an increasingly diversified economy, Chalongphob said Thailand must cultivate niche markets.For example,
2407 instead of trying to increase all rice exports, Thailand should focus only on top quality grades such as fragrant rice, he said. Exotic fruit sales were another potential growth area, he added."We cannot just sell average agricultural products which other countries with cheaper labor can catch up very soon," Chalongphob
2407 said. "We should try to make some of our primary commodities high-value luxury goods."INDONESIA DIVERSIFIES ECONOMY, LESS DEPENDENT ON OILIndonesia has also progressed quickly in the last three decades in transforming a mainly agriculture-based economy towards a more industrial economy, economists said.Industrial production contributed some 24.3 percent of GDP in
2407 1995, compared with 9.2 percent in 1989. Agriculture's contribution to GDP has declined steadily to 17.2 percent last year from 49.3 percent in 1969, the government says."The structure of our economy has changed a lot. You don't have to look far. Just comparing 1973 and now there has been a
2407 very significant change," said Miranda Gultom, an economist attached to the Ministry for Economics and Finance.The Indonesian economy is more diversified now, with the manufacturing sector making up about one-third of GDP, followed by the agricultural sector and service industries.Christianto Wibisono of the Centre for Business Data, said, however, there
2407 was still much to be done because Indonesia had many advantages in certain sectors which could be developed."We should have the fifth largest paper industry in the world based on the potential we have. We should manufacture more value-added products than exporting raw materials," he said."We are still behind Thailand
2407 in terms of export ability. Our economy is still very much resources-based. The government needs to encourage industries which could add more value to our products," Wibisono said.He said Indonesia should focus on industries with a natural base here rather than those needing a high level of imports."The high import
2407 contents have made our export products uncompetitive," he said.Economists said another important structural change was the declining dependence on oil exports to finance the budget.From 1984/85 to 1996/97, income from the oil sector, as a proportion of total government revenues, diminished to an estimated 18 percent from more than 65
2407 percent, while income from taxation had grown to 70 percent from 30 percent.PHILIPPINES LAGS DUE TO MARCOS ERA "HAEMORRHAGE"The Philippines is perceived to have lagged in the transition to industrialisation, which Joey Salceda, research director at SBC Warburg in Manila, attributed to "financial haemorrhages" during the rule of late president
2407 Ferdinand Marcos.He said the hangover of debt left by Marcos had dashed Manila's dream of keeping pace with others in the region."Commodity exports from the Philippines, ranging from copper, gold, sugar to coconut oil, between 1974 and 1980 really boomed. It could have made the country the first tiger in
2407 Southeast Asia if it had been able to wisely use its export receipts while building up its industries," Salceda said.</

2410 Troops with sniffer dogs combed mountains and beaches in South Korea on Thursday for up to nine North Koreans after 11 of their companions were shot dead in the most serious infiltration since the 1960s.A dusk-to-dawn curfew was lifted and thousands of armed troops and police who cordoned off the
2410 search area overnight began moving in on their prey.Authorities believe around 20 North Koreans landed on Wednesday in a submarine, now stranded on rocks near the east coast city of Kangnung, in a flagrant breach of an armistice agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War and sealed the division of
2410 the peninsula.Bloodsoaked bodies of 11 North Koreans were found huddled together at the top of a mountain on Wednesday, apparently shot by their leader who then turned the gun on himself.Communist espionage agents from North Korean have in the past chosen suicide over capture.No sightings of the fugitives have been
2410 reported since Wednesday night, when two of them burst into a villager's home and stole food and cigarettes after brandishing a pistol.Soon after that, news reports said two North Koreans exchanged gunfire with their pursuers in a 15-minute skirmish near Kangnung's airport.Rain lashed much of South Korea overnight, and with
2410 helicopters and a reconnaisance plane joining the search the capture of the North Koreas, dead or alive, appeared to be only a matter of time.One infiltrator who was captured alive was quoted by local media as saying the submarine drifted into Southern waters after developing engine trouble.His dead colleagues were
2410 members of the vessel's crew, not trained saboteurs, Lee Kang-soo, 31, was quoted as saying.South Korean authorities maintain the incident was a deliberate provocation, and it has further raised tensions between the two hostile neighbours who face each other across the world's most heavily fortified border.Troops who boarded the abandoned
2410 grey craft, now bobbing helplessly in the shallows, found automatic guns and ammunition along with canned food and shoes.Pyongyang has not commented on the drama, one of the deadliest since 1968 when 31 North Koreans reached the presidential Blue House in Seoul. 2410 34 Southern troops, police and civilians also died.Earlier this year, armed North Korean troops staged illegal exercises in a border buffer zone, and following that scare U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean head of state Kim Young-sam made a peace overture to Pyongyang.They proposed four-way talks, also including China,
2410 but North Korea has yet to respond.However, there had been hopeful signs that Pyongyang was being lured out of its hostile isolation in its desperation for help to ease a food crisis.Over the weekend several hundred foreign investors were feted at a North Korean free-trade zone. South Korea boycotted the
2410 event in a row over invitations, but on Tuesday a faxed message to South Korean Foreign Minister Gong Ro-myung attempted to patch up the quarrel by inviting a Southern delegation to the Rajin-Sonbong zone for an exclusive look.Previous bouts of North Korean sabre-rattling have been interpreted by North Korea watchers
2410 as deliberate attempts by Pyongyang hardliners to sabotage detente moves.</

2441 The fare at Ali's Restaurant, situated in a Cyprus territorial vacuum, reflects the main elements of the island's division; the food and beer are Turkish, the mineral water is Greek and the bill is in Cyprus pounds.As you approach the restaurant on a barren plateau bright yellow lights strung on
2441 trees bounce eerily up and down in the breeze to the soft strains of Turkish music. Waiters stand to attention in front of the arches of a converted house."You want jeans?" asks an eager young Turkish Cypriot waiter. "I get you some from there," he said, pointing towards a village
2441 discernible its lights about a mile north.Few Greek Cypriots visit the restaurant, located between the mixed community village of Pyla in the United Nations controlled buffer zone, and the Turkish-held village of Pergamos in the south eastern part of Cyprus.Located within the sprawling British military base of Dhekelia, seventy percent
2441 of Ali's clients are British servicemen.The tasty dishes are prepared by a chef from the Turkish town of Adana.Ali's Restaurant is perched on a rocky plateau overlooking Pyla, a village home to 850 Greek and 350 Turkish Cypriots, declared a UN-controlled buffer zone since the Turkish invasion in 1974.Tension has
2441 risen considerably on the island in the past month following the killings of two Greek Cypriots in the buffer zone. Last week a Turkish Cypriot sentry was shot dead at his post close to the ceasefire line.Until then, Ali's was used as a pick-up point for hundreds of Turkish Cypriots
2441 taken to the government-controlled south every morning to work."After the troubles they are not going anymore," said Yousouf, the Turkish Cypriot waiter.To its north is the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, declared nine years after the 1974 invasion, which followed a short-lived coup in Nicosia inspired by the military regime ruling
2441 Greece.The north, where some 30,000 mainland troops are based, is recognised only by Ankara. To the south lies the government-controlled part of Cyprus.Residents of Pyla, whether they are Greek or Turkish Cypriots, tend to view strangers with a liberal dose of suspicion. They don't like to talk, and they do
2441 not like questions."We have never had any problems with the Turkish Cypriots," said one Greek Cypriot resident. "If we do have problems they will start from the foreigners, the mainland Turks," he said.Macedonia is the Greek Cypriot coffee shop in the village square. Turkish Cypriots have their own coffee shop,
2441 apparently unnamed, on the other side of the square.A group playing poker on the Turkish side were non-committal."I don't speak English," said one bearded Turkish Cypriot, trying to hide a grin, his eyes firmly fixed on the cards he was holding.Another was more outspoken. "No, we do not get on
2441 well. I cannot work, I can't go to work," he exclaimed, throwing down the cards and walking off.Minefields lie on either side of a narrow road leading to the village cordoned off with rusty barbed wire.Taking photographs in the village is forbidden and, to preserve the peace, flags are only
2441 allowed to be flown at schools or on national holidays.Being one of the few bicommunal villages on the Mediterranean island is not all it is known for. Smuggling from the Turkish occupied north to the south is reported to be rampant in the area.Activity in Pyla is monitored by Turkish
2441 sentries on the top of a rocky hill overlooking the village. One of them never moves. It is a plastic cut-out."People mingle and there are cases of intermarriage," said Chief Superintendent Liam Quinn, a member of the Irish Civilian police force stationed in Pyla. "We do not have any problems."In
2441 the privacy of their homes, some Greek Cypriot women sit and have coffee in the morning with their Turkish Cypriot neighbours."Nothing has changed for us, we still go to their house, they still come to ours," said one Greek Cypriot woman.Greek Cypriot Kyriakos Karkides, 91, has lived in Pyla all
2441 his life. "We haven't stopped talking to each other," he said. "I have Turkish friends who come and see me all the time."</

2444 The Bundesbank said on Thursday that German M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 8.7 percent in August, up from 8.6 percent in July.The growth was stronger than expected.Most economists had predicted M3 growth would have slowed again in August, following a steady downward trend seen in recent
2444 months.Economists had predicted an annualised rate of eight percent from 8.6 percent in July. Forecasts ranged from 7.9 percent to 8.2 percent. The Bundesbank is aiming for M3 growth between four and seven percent this year.Separately, the Munich-based ifo economic research institute reported a modest pick-up in business confidence in
2444 August, broadly in line with expectations.The Ifo business climate index for west Germany rose to 94.4 from a revised 94.0 which was previously reported as 94.1, Ifo said in a statement. Most economists had predicted a figure of about 94.5.German bonds dropped quickly in response to the M3 news on
2444 the assumption that it made a further cut in German interest rates less likely. There has been some speculation that a further cut in German rates was possible later this year.But the subsequent news that business confidence had risen only modestly confirmed that the economic upturn remained fragile, and bonds
2444 quickly pared their losses.Klaus Baader, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London told Reuters Financial Television: "The (M3) number is not a major catastrophe, but the process of rapid convergence toward the growth target (four to seven pct) has been interrupted. Reaching the target after this will be an uphill struggle."The Bundesbank
2444 targets M3 money supply growth as its main monetary policy indicator on the grounds that it provides a guide to future inflation.</
