2451 For the fourth consecutive year, China and its supporters on Wednesday blocked moves in the General Assembly to consider U.N. membership for Taiwan.As in previous years, the move to put the issue on the agenda, sponsored by 16 mostly Caribbean, Central American and African countries, was defeated without a vote
2451 after a long debate in the assembly's steering committee.The proposal was introduced by the Solomon Islands and strongly opposed by China's ambassador. Delegates from 38 countries opposed the item while 17 spoke in favour.Assembly President Razali Ismail of Malaysia ruled that because of the views expressed, the item would not
2451 be recommended for the assembly's agenda.During the debate, a dirigible "blimp" with "Taiwan" inscribed on its side hovered near the United Nations.A paddle steamer adorned with the slogan "Welcome Taiwan to the U.N." cruised New York's East River alongside the U.N. complex while a pro-Taiwan demonstration took place a few
2451 hundred yards (metres) away.The United States also rejected a donation of $160,000 (2.5 million Taiwanese dollars) offered to the financially pressed world body by a group called "Taiwan International Alliance." Hsiu-lien Annette Lu, its president, maintained the funds were raised by 40,000 Taiwanese.It was not accepted because a U.N. spokesman
2451 said it was "not a bona fide donation" but an attempt to publicise the Taiwan cause.When China's Nationalist government retreated to Taiwan in 1949 after defeat by the Communists in a civil war, it continued to hold China's U.N. seat. But it was expelled by the Assembly in 1971 and
2451 the seat given to Beijing, which considers Taiwan a renegade province.China regards any bid to give the island U.N. membership as an intolerable encroachment on its sovereignty and interference in its internal affairs. It suggests the sponsors are motivated by economic inducements.The sponsors of the move, which referred to "Taiwan,
2451 Republic of China," wanted the assembly to discuss the matter and set up a committee to consider it further.They did not seek to unseat Beijing but said the present situation left the more than 21 million inhabitants of Taiwan, an economic powerhouse, without representation in international bodies.Introducing the item in
2451 the committee, the Solomon Islands' ambassador, Rex Horoi, said much had happened since the 1971 decision which reflected "the passions of the Cold War.""On Taiwan the Republic of China has been transformed into a vigorous democracy based upon a powerful trading economy -- 14th largest in the world -- that
2451 helps to produce a gross national product and a per capita income that rank 19th and 25th globally," he said."At this point in its history, can the United Nations afford to deprive itself of what the Republic of China on Taiwan would bring to the table?" he asked.China's ambassador Qin
2451 Huasun said Taiwan "has been a part of the Chinese territory since ancient time." He blasted the "very small number of member states instigated by the Taiwan authorities" who he said were trying to create "two Chinas" or "one China, one Taiwan" in the United Nations."We wish to advise these
2451 countries to rein in at the brink of the precipice and refrain from further erroneous moves against international law and the U.N. Charter ... Otherwise, they are bound to be cast aside by the Chinese and all justice-upholding people in the world," Qin said.</
2452 United Nations economists said on Thursday that world growth had stalled and warned that anti- inflationary policies in richer countries could spark popular reaction against open trade and a return to protectionism.The U.N.'s Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), in its annual survey of the global scene, also found that
2452 while leading emerging economies in Asia were still growing rapidly they faced a mounting challenge from lower-wage countries."The slowing down of growth in the world economy is likely to continue during the remainder of 1996," UNCTAD's Trade and Development Report said.The overall growth rate for the current year would not
2452 exceed the 2.4 per cent in 1995, already a drop from 1994's 2.8 per cent that was scored as the global economy was emerging from three years of recession.UNCTAD suggested that policies pursued in the drive among major members of the European Union to meet conditions for economic and monetary
2452 union (EMU) were partly responsible for the loss of steam.The commitment to reach the targets for the launch of a single European currency in 1999, while fostering growth and employment, "presents a daunting challenge," it said."The budget cuts undertaken to meet the (EMU) convergence conditions....are exerting downward pressure on the
2452 growth of output, and therefore on the very budget receipts needed to meet the fiscal targets."There was, it added, "scope for further monetary relaxation on pursuit of the twin goals of convergence and growth."While noting that the United States and Britain had been able to combine wage and price stability
2452 with falling unemployment, the report said there was a real risk of deflation in most developed economies if monetary policy continued to focus on fighting inflation and governments on cutting budgets.The U.S. experience of maintaining growth, in the face of assertions that the economy was overheating, "confirms that fears of
2452 inflation have been exaggerated," it declared.In Europe, it said, there was a risk that job losses and lower real wages, especially in low-skill occupations, would be blamed on imports as well as on the drive towards EMU."High unemployment thus risks increasing resistance to policies directed toward achieving important objectives --
2452 monetary union in Europe and the full integration, through trade, of developing countries in the world economy," it added."The bright point in the short-term outlook is the continued resilience of developing countries to external shocks, including the stagnation in a number of industrialised economies, and their ability to maintain recent
2452 trends in the growth of both their output and their trade."These economies were less dependent on trade with the North "because successful industrialisation in the South has opened up new opportunities for South-South investment and trade."But, it added, "the current outlook is not all rosy". In several East and South-East
2452 Asian countries export growth seemed to be faltering, partly due to the emergence of new competitors.Serious balance-of-payments deficits difficulties could arise "if competition from low-wage countries draws foreign investment away from South-East Asia," UNCTAD warned.Africa, the report said, was expected to return growth of 3.1 per cent this year, its
2452 highest of the decade -- partly due to a boom in export earnings from higher commodity prices and partly to greater political stability in many countries.But the region would need to sustain faster growth for some time to bring per capita incomes to their level of 20 years ago.Latin America,
2452 slowly recovering from the effects of the Mexican financial crisis at the end of 1994, appeared set for some recovery in 1996 with output likely to be up 2.4 per cent after a fall of 0.7 per cent in 1995."For most countries in the region, the challenge in the period
2452 ahead is to sustain rapid growth while consolidating recent significant progress in the fight against inflation and limiting external balances," UNCTAD said.</

2469 The powerful Franco-German axis is all set to steamroller its way through this weekend's meeting of European finance ministers in Dublin, Ireland, forging a precise path to long-term fiscal stability in Europe.German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and his French counterpart Jean Arthuis are heading for Dublin secure in the knowledge
2469 they hold the same position on all key agenda points.After a preparatory meeting on Tuesday, the two countries made clear the lasting stability of the single currency was paramount and that every effort must be made to secure this.Strengthened by the approval of controversial spending cuts by Paris and Bonn
2469 in recent days, the two ministers and their central bank heads will no doubt seek to inspire other European nations to rein in spending to approach the Maastricht ideals."The Franco-German position is sealed," said Alison Cottrell, international economist at PaineWebber in London. "They have a few Ts to cross and
2469 a few Is to dot, but it is basically there. Both want to keep the momentum going."The officials agreed this week that the so-called stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline within Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was essential for the Euro's success and that a second exchange rate mechanism was
2469 needed to group non-EMU currencies.They also said the legal framework of the currency's launch should allow those who wish to transact in the Euro to do so from January 1, 1999, but force no one to do so until 2002.Motivation to maintain convergence efforts is essential, as states which wish
2469 to join EMU in 1999 must meet the Maastricht Treaty's targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budget deficits and public borrowing in the decisive 1997 year.But with that crunch year now drawing alarmingly close, observers have detected a subtle change in the hardline language used at Europe's core.Germany, still
2469 insistent that the economic criteria in the Maastricht Treaty must not be softened, has nonetheless become wary of pushing its view that the Maastricht reference level of three percent of gross domestic product is an absolute maximum.Responding to fears that nations will adopt wholesale window-dressing to make 1997 budgets look
2469 good -- whatever the consequences for 1998 and beyond -- the new buzzwords on fiscal discipline are 'long-term', 'durable', 'sustainable'."We are agreed that long-term budgetary discipline is seen as indispensible by both Germany and France if the stability of the Euro is to be guaranteed," Arthuis told reporters after Tuesday's
2469 Franco-German summit, echoing a comment from Waigel.Both Cottrell and Thomas Mayer, senior economist at Goldman Sachs, saw this stance as an attempt to dim the spotlight which has been placed on 1997 alone, so going back to the spirit of the Maastricht convergence criteria rather than focusing exclusively on detail."It
2469 could well be that the politicians are seeing they are manoeuvring themselves into an awkward position...with some countries only trying to get the cosmetics right," Mayer said."This is a very important shift to emphasis on the Treaty. I think they moved too far in stressing one particular year... which was
2469 almost counterproductive. Looking at numbers alone cannot be consistent with the spirit of the Treaty," he added.Cottrell added that too much emphasis on the numbers could pose problems if nations such as Italy and Spain -- which most economists say are not yet ready for EMU -- somehow managed to
2469 squeeze their 1997 budgets into a three percent straitjacket.But Werner Becker, senior economist for European issues at Deutsche Bank Research in Frankfurt, said Tuesday's comments at least made clear that Europe's pacesetters did not themselves intend to cheat excessively to meet the Maastricht goals."Those worries have been largely dispelled," he
2469 said, welcoming that the two countries at the heart of European integration had obviously recognised that budget discipline was of no value unless it could be maintained long-term."A stability pact shows willingness to maintain these ambitious goals long-term. It is needed primarily for psychological reasons...but it is nonetheless very important
2469 that its measures are effective," he said.</

2477 Consistency and continuity will be the watchwords for the Netherlands' presidency of the European Union, starting on January 1, 1997, the Foreign Ministry has said said in its 1997 budget memorandum."The six months of the Dutch presidency cannot and must not be viewed in isolation," the ministry said.The document noted
2477 that the Dutch presidency coincides with several major EU projects: completion of the inter-governmental conference (IGC); the third phase of economic and monetary union (EMU); budget reform; changes in the agricultural and structural funds and negotiations on the admission of new members.The ministry said the EU's internal agenda was likely
2477 to be dominated by the IGC, which it noted was scheduled to be concluded in mid-1997.It said the IGC could conclude during the Dutch presidency or the Luxembourg presidency which follows it.The ministry said the IGC should result in a balanced document which would enable the EU to take a
2477 step forward."The new treaty should, on the one hand, give the Union greater strength, effectiveness and democracy."The text of the new treaty should also be written more clearly to make it more accessible to EU citizens, it added.The European Union could not afford to stick with the status quo because
2477 yesterday's solutions could not be applied to tomorrow's problems, the ministry said.Enlargement of the EU made changes in the composition of EU institutions essential, otherwise the EU would become less efficient with every new member.The second and third pillars established under the Maastricht Treaty were not functioning well and also
2477 needed to be reformed, the ministry added.Apart from the IGC, the Netherlands views preparation for the third phase of economic and monetary union as one of the key priorities during the Dutch presidency.Negotiations on budget reform and reform of agricultural policy and the structural funds are not due to start
2477 until after the IGC, but initial, exploratory talks could be held during the Dutch presidency, the ministry said.The creation of more jobs and the completion of the EU's internal market would also be important themes during the Dutch presidency, it added.Cooperation with the countries bordering the Mediterranean would be given
2477 an important place on the agenda while peace and reconstruction in Yugoslavia would remain one of the most important concerns in the area of foreign and security policy.Peace in the Middle-East, reforms in Central and Eastern Europe and transatlantic relations would also be high on the foreign and security policy
2477 agenda, the ministry said.The government plans to send further details of its plans for the Dutch presidency to parliament in October.</

2483 COREPER agreed a compromise on Wednesday to extend European Union rules allowing shipbuilding aid until December 31, 1997, in the absence of an international deal to scrap most support to the sector, an EU source said.The agreement by the Committee of Permanent Representatives means there will be no extraordinary Industry
2483 Council on Friday."The Council will not take place," the source said, adding the issue would be an "A" point on the September 27 Telecoms Council.No other details were immediately available.The issue was a problem because the United States has so far not ratified an accord brokered in 1994 by the
2483 Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.The EU had to decide whether and for how long to extend its 7th shipbuilding directive, 90/684/EEC, which allows aid of up to nine percent of contract value.The Council decided last year that current aid rules would apply in the absence of the OECD deal,
2483 but only until October 1, which is why the EU now had to take a new decision.In July, the Commission proposed legislation COM(96)309 to enable the EU to extend the directive until the end of 1998 or the entry into force of the international agreement.However, some member states believe that
2483 is too long while for example Finland would like the EU to scrap its aid now, even without ratification of the OECD deal. Finland will vote against the compromise in COREPER, the source said.Officials have earlier stressed that as soon as the OECD accord takes force, the EU rules would
2483 lapse automatically.The OECD agreement would eliminate all direct shipbuilding subsidies except social aid and, within certain ceilings, aid for research and development.But the deal, which was originally due to enter into force in January, faces ratification problems in the United States.The Republican-controlled House of Representatives endorsed it on June 13,
2483 but adopted amendments that would delay key sections by 30 months, leading the Clinton administration to warn the agreement might not be ratified.U.S. shipyards argue they have not had enough time to adjust to the commercial era after the loss of military contracts at the end of the Cold War.The
2483 EU, which represents about 20 percent of the world shipbuilding market, ratified the OECD agreement in December, saying it would help improve market access for its shipyards.</

2488 German repo rate, adding that the Bank would want to show financial markets it believed the government's budget was credible.The intervention rate is 3.35 percent and the German repo rate is 3.0 percent. 2488 of approval to yesterday's budget," said Credit Lyonnais economist Iain Lindsay."For them not to move at all would be a spit in the face," added Sean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.The Bank of France's monetary policy council will hold a regular meeting on Thursday morning.Other analysts argued a
2488 weaker French franc, which fell nearly a centime against the mark on Wednesday, would make it difficult for the Bank to act so soon after the budget.They also saw the Bank's failure to lower call money on Thursday morning as a sign the Bank would wait until markets stabilized before
2488 making its next move.Call money, which the Bank uses as a third unofficial rate, has not moved since it was lowered by 1/16 percentage point to 3-7/16-9/16 percent on August 23.Another factor seen tying the Bank's hands was strong growth in August German M3 money supply released on Thursday morning."Since

2490 The Bundesbank said on Thursday that German M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 8.7 percent in August, up from 8.6 percent in July.The growth was stronger than expected.Most economists had predicted M3 growth would have slowed again in August, following a steady downward trend seen in recent
2490 months.Economists had predicted an annualised rate of 8.0 percent from 8.6 percent in July. Forecasts ranged from 7.9 percent to 8.2 percent. 2490 a further cut in German interest rates less likely. 2490 the growth target (four to seven per cent) has been interrupted. Reaching the target after this will be an uphill struggle."The Bundesbank targets M3 money supply growth as its main monetary policy indicator on the grounds that it provides a guide to future inflation.</

2507 by public borrowing.An overhang from July also influenced August M3."Among the seasonally adjusted components of money supply, sight and savings deposits with a three month notice period expanded strongly again in August," the Bundesbank said. 2541 Painting a bleak picture of life in Tajikistan, the United Nations said it intended to send a humanitarian relief mission to the former Soviet republic to increase the current level of assistance."The people of Tajikistan are faced with an acute crisis," said Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali in a report to the
2541 Security Council released on Wednesday.Because of continuing heavy fighting in several areas, he said thousands of civilians have been displaced and many needed aid "to meet their basic survival needs."Although the cereal harvest is expected to be larger this year than last, Tajikistan will continue to need foreign help for
2541 basic foods. Diarrhoea outbreaks are common and typoid epidemics and malaria were reported totally out of control.Since independence in 1992, the central Asian state of 5.7 million people, has suffered a mosaic of clan and regional rivalries, in which tens of thousands of people were killed, 600,000 were displaced and
2541 another 300,000 fled the country.The report described a ceasefire agreement reached in July as a failure. Fighting continued in the central Tavildara area and increased in the the Garm district to the north.In addition tension was is high on the Tajik-Afghan border and U.N. military observers have been restricted by
2541 both sides from inspecting dangerous areas, it said.Boutros-Ghali called on the government and the rebels to resume direct contacts and said his special representative, Gerd Merrem of Germany, would help set up such a meeting.The U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) comprises 94 people, including 44 military observers.Last month,
2541 after weeks of fighting with rebels, government troops took control of the strategically important town of Tavildara, 120 miles (193 km) east of the capital of Dushanbe.Boutros-Ghali said that in Tavildara itself, about 15 percent of the town haf been completely destroyed and nearly all residents had fled.</

2543 than a diplomat and a statesman."In different periods, different emphasis is put on these jobs," she said, adding that it was essential at this time that a new secretary-general be foremost an administrator.This did not mean electing a bookkeeper "but someone who has a vision about reform and is not
2543 dragged into it kicking and screaming but who sees reform as a very high priority."The United States has angered numerous diplomats, especially those from France, Russia and China, in announcing through the press it would block Boutros-Ghali's bid for re-election. 2543 as well as Britain, have veto power on the Security Council, which chooses the secretary-general.Albright emphatically denied a widespread belief among delegates that the U.S. campaign against Boutros-Ghali arose from presidential politics to meet Republican criticism of most activities of the United Nations. 2543 few defenders, and payment of the $1.6 billion American debt to the United Nations has been delayed."The issue here is this is not an issue of presidential politics ... we want to make sure our tax dollars are spent properly," she said. "I am sure my country is not alone."In
2543 the past year, the United Nations has sliced off or left vacant 900 jobs, which Albright has credited to the American Undersecretary-General Joseph Connor, who in turn has supported and praised Boutros-Ghali for the programme.But the latest debacle in the United Nations, which has angered Albright as well as British
2543 envoys, involves the dismissal of 37 employees who were given three months notice after their jobs were cut and they could not be placed elsewhere in the bureaucracy.The General Assembly's budgetary committee directed Boutros-Ghali to delay the dismissals. 2543 make those tough decisions."If the 73-year-old Egyptian diplomat does leave his post, African nations, backed by China, insisted another African replace him. 2543 Kofi Annan of Ghana, the U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping, and Salim A. Salim, chairman of the Organisation of African Unity. 2543 Security Council last month to rebuff Albright's efforts to begin finding a replacement now.</

2545 Greece's erratic foreign policy, which has often infuriated its allies, will keep moving towards a solidly pro-Western stance whoever wins elections on Sunday.Extreme policy swings, unilateral ultimatums and maverick positions against prevailing Western policies will become relics of the past, diplomats and foreign policy analysts say.Socialist Premier Costas Simitis and
2545 conservative challenger Miltiades Evert would both work to improve relations with Balkan neighbours, restore credibility with Western partners and keep troubled relations with Turkey from boiling over."I don't see any dramatic differences. They have the same overall goals but would implement policies differently," said Thanos Veremis, director of the Hellenic
2545 Foundation for European and Foreign Policy.The concerns of either leader would be EU relations, EU or U.S. initiatives on Cyprus and problems with Turkey, with whom Greece came close to war in January.Both Simitis and Evert would try to see the world through EU eyes and separate foreign policy from
2545 the unpredictable populist antics which have dogged Greek politics since a military junta fell in 1974.This would be especially true if Simitis, 60, a passionless law and economics professor, won. He took over as premier this year from late party founder Andreas Papandreou -- the man the West loved to
2545 hate."Simitis has shown no interest in submitting foreign policy to the whims of the Greek mob. He is determined and cool, and he has done almost everything right as far as the European Union is concerned," a Western diplomat said.Evert has toyed with nationalism during the campaign but this was
2545 to steal votes from the tiny Political Spring party, and he would drop this approach quickly if elected, diplomats predicted.For most of the past 20 years Greece has tweaked the nose of its EU partners and the United States -- its major arms supplier -- or uttered a flat "drop
2545 dead" in foreign policy disputes.Papandreou, who ruled throughout the turbulent and fiercely anti-American, anti-EU 1980s, seemed to delight in infuriating his Western allies."The old man (Papandreou) was a great problem. He saw the whole of foreign policy through the prism of domestic politics and left-wing populism," said Veremis.Papandreou vowed to
2545 shut U.S. bases and to quit the EU and the NATO military alliance. He never did, but many Greeks loved his David versus Goliath show.On a more sinister note, he hobnobbed with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi and communist dictators in Eastern Europe, and he refused to extradite Arab and Palestinian
2545 guerrillas to stand trial in Western countries for alleged attacks on civilians.While his allies sat in muted fury, Papandreou explained he believed in a balanced foreign policy. At home he told adoring crowds that Greece took orders from nobody.When he returned to power in 1993, one of his first moves
2545 was to slap a trade embargo on the neighbouring former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia.EU partners, already upset with Greece's out-of-step Balkan policy, erupted in rage and took Athens to the European Court to try to have the embargo lifted.The 1990 to 1993 conservative government of former premier Constantine Mitsotakis fared
2545 little better with Western allies.His foreign minister, young Harvard Business School graduate Antonis Samaras, set EU partners' teeth on edge with persistent and ponderous lectures on Greek and Balkan history.He disrupted EU affairs for two years with demands that Macedonia, the only Yugoslav republic to win independence peacefully, change its
2545 name. Whatever the merits of his case, his style led some EU allies to brand Greece a Balkan bully.But diplomats say Greece appears to be entering a new era, leaving behind the outpouring of emotion of the 1980s after the military junta fell and the confusion in the Balkans in
2545 the early 1990s after communism crashed."The flamboyant, even reckless, go-it-alone approach was popular and emotionally satisfying for many but it left Greece isolated and weak internationally," another EU diplomat said.Both Evert and Simitis have realised that nationalism, domestic populism or adventures in the region would hurt Greek interests and both
2545 believe careful lobbying of EU partners is the best way forward, the diplomats said.A priority for either will be rearming the military. Defence ministry officials have put a $10 billion price tag on the arms package they would like and both politicians have identified NATO ally Turkey as the potential
2545 enemy."Our defence policy is our ability to deter Turkish threats. The main factor in this is our armed forces and upgrading our armed forces personnel, development and armaments," Simitis said during the campaign.Diplomats said that if Simitis wins he might dump outspoken Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and replace him with
2545 George Papandreou, son of the late premier and a key Simitis supporter.Evert was likely to name Peter Moliviatis, a distinguished diplomat and former ambassador who helped steer Greece into the European Union in 1981.</
2546 IKEA, Swedish home furnisher to the masses, is moving into China.As the international household goods market shrinks, the world's biggest furniture retailer is targeting Asia.In its home markets the low cost, no nonsense IKEA, has been forced to start cutting prices to support its market share and is looking eastwards
2546 to bolster sales.Birger Ljung, outgoing managing director of IKEA retail in Sweden, said the group already had stores in Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan and four in Hong Kong but from October this year he will spearhead a new drive into China."We are gradually moving east," Ljung, IKEA's new managing director for
2546 China, told Reuters."We have been in Asia for quite a while as a purchasing organisation but not in any great force as a retailer, being a European retailer of European origin."But the general idea is that if we can do business in other countries we can do business in China,"
2546 said Ljung who will be based in Shanghai.Since IKEA was set up in 1958 by Ingvar Kamprad, a farmer's son from Smaland in southern Sweden who is still chairman of the company, its success has been phenomenal.Now with 130 self-service stores in 28 different countries, the IKEA group in the
2546 year to August 31, 1995, had a turnover of over $5 billion.In 1995 it employed over 30,000 staff to sell its range of 11,400 products, some self-assembly, usually from out-of-town warehouses.Germany was the company's biggest market in 1995, accounting for 29.9 percent of sales revenue, followed by Canada and the
2546 United States combined with 13.6 percent then Sweden with 10.6 percent."But the whole home decoration market has now been reduced," said Ljung who has been with IKEA for 18 years. "We want to improve our market position so we are growing out in a pretty aggressive way."We need to focus
2546 on China as longterm -- maybe Japan and Korea as well -- as this part of the world's growing in every way."We already have some contacts in China as we do some buying there but the main idea is that we'll design the products then go out to the market
2546 and find manufacturers to work for us and sell from there."He said he was not yet sure if IKEA would jointly or wholly own its production facitilies. No date has yet been set for the opening of the first Chinese store and no sales targets set.Ljung said it was unlikely
2546 IKEA would introduce a new range especially for the Chinese market with 95 percent of its stock the same the world over.Its latest range, PS, launched last month, is characterised by block colours and rounded shapes in natural wood and chrome, inspired by the 1960s and 1970s.Ljung said the organisation
2546 and products of IKEA, which now has its international headquarters in Denmark, reflects the down-to-earth attitude of founder, 69-year-old Kamprad."Functional objects for flatter not fatter wallets," is one of Kamprad's much quoted mottos.Now living in Lausanne, Switzerland, Kamprad remains known for his thriftiness.He made headlines in Swedish newspapers in 1992
2546 when it was revealed that his claim for travel expenses to attend an interview at a Swedish television station showed he had taken a bus to the studio.Although he has three sons, Kamprad in 1980 handed the ownership of IKEA over to a Dutch charitable foundation, Stichting Ingka, so the
2546 company could never be the victim of a hostile takeover or split up after his death.He has, however, reportedly left his sons Habitat, the British-French "lifestyle" shop set up by designer Sir Terence Conran, which IKEA bought four years ago for 78 million pounds.Kamprad's reputation came under a cloud in
2546 late 1994 when a Stockholm newspaper found his name in archives of the pro-Nazi activist Per Engdahl with whom he was friendly in the 1950s.Kamprad wrote a letter of apology to all his employees, saying he was naive and young at the time when he admired Engdahl's anti-communist view, and
2546 he now bitterly regretted these links."I did not link them at all with Nazism. Only some years later did I understand that it was a big mistake," he said in the letter, referring to his action as "youthful sins".</

2556 A "borderless" strategy in Southeast Asia has boosted Digital Equipment's performance and improved its inventories, senior company official J. Graham Long said on Thursday."The approach we've developed about a year and a half ago was to go after this territory in a borderless fashion. The growth has improved considerably," said
2556 Long, vice president for the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) region.The "borderless" programme means Digital's partners in Southeast Asia and developing countries like Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh pay the same price for products.The contracts they sign with Digital are also valid in all the countries, Long told Reuters
2556 in an interview.He said it also meant Digital could also support its partners' programmes across borders. ASEAN comprises Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam."Our overall business revenue grew 40 percent to US$400 million," for the financial year ended June 1996, Long said."For two years, we had flat growth
2556 in workstations. We implemented this strategy and then we grew 250 percent year to year. This year, we're going to double this business," he said.The company's Alpha range of products grew 55 percent.Long said Digital was aiming to increase revenues by 30 percent a year in the region for the
2556 next three years and to improve profits by 50 percent this fiscal year. He declined to give profit figures.Orders for the first quarter ending this month were expected to be better than the same period last year, compared to a weaker quarter expected by Digital on a worldwide basis, he
2556 said.Long said the "borderless" strategy was unique to Digital's Southeast Asian business and began when the company saw its partners, selling hardware or software, were expanding geographically as ASEAN moved towards eliminating intra-regional trade tariffs.Digital's inventories in the region have also been cut."Now we're carrying one-third less inventory than we
2556 have before, compared to 18 months ago and we've gotten rid of redundant inventory," said Long.Digital has centralised stocks at its Singapore plant and closed down warehouses in other ASEAN countries. It is now working on developing a central order desk out of Singapore, Long said.He said competitors could adopt
2556 a similar strategy, but saw Digital with an edge from being the first to do it."The competition would have to break down barriers that took us one and half years to break," he said."Actually, we would encourage any vendor of size to implement a borderless strategy. We would lose some
2556 competitive advantage, but it would be good for the industry. It would be one way to bring IT solutions to developing countries faster."Digital would focus on three areas of business in the region -- high-end Unix systems, Windows NT technology and Internet/Intranet business.Its strong performance in the region has captured
2556 attention at group level, Long said. There was now greater pressure to keep doing better to help bolster the company's earnings on a worldwide basis, he said.For fiscal year 1995/96, Digital reported a loss of US$111.8 million on a worldwide basis.</

2574 South Korean finance minister Han Seung-soo said on Thursday the country was not expected to meet its 1997 economic targets because of an export slowdown, high costs and low efficiency."It will be rather difficult to attain the economic performance that we had initially forecast earlier this year," Han told members
2574 of the Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club.Economic growth in 1996 has been revised to around seven percent from a real 9.0 percent a year earlier.The consumer price index grew by 4.4 percent in the first eight months of the year, close to the target of 4.5 percent for the whole year.
2574 And the current account deficit is now predicted to surpass $15 billion from an originally forecast $6.4 billion. Han said the shortfall "is not likely to improve significantly next year".Han said cyclical problems were partly to blame. Corporate profitability has been hit hard by sharp drops in the prices of
2574 major export items.But he said the root problem was structural."Our wages have been increasing at a faster rate than in competing countries, and the corporate financial burden grows larger as high interest rates continue," Han said.Interest rates are among the highest in the world with benchmark three-year yields are now
2574 at 12.11 percent and wages growth has been in double-digits for several years.Han added that logistical costs and land prices in South Korea were considerably higher than those in most other countries and government regulations were hobbling business."These structural problems have been manifest for many years, but the recent depreciation
2574 of the yen and the drop in major export prices have made them more conspicuous as major obstacles to our economy's progress," Han said.He said the government would stress economic stability by curbing inflation and boosting corporate health.Han said joining the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) would help
2574 accelerate Korean economic deregulation and improve economic structural problems.Despite criticism over Korea's entry into the OECD as premature, Han said the government "stands firm in our pursuit of accession to the OECD".-- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647</

2579 to help the world's poor."The IMF is fully ready to assist its low-income members well into the next millenium," Camdessus said in a brief statement.IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, had proposed selling five million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold
2579 if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.Wednesday's decision by the IMF board puts the proposal on the back
2579 burner for now. 2579 which first met on the issue last Friday then took it up again today, discussed two inter-related initiatives to help poor countries -- beefing up its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) and participating in a multilateral debt relief plan.ESAF, which lends money at virtually no interest charge to the world's
2579 poorest nations, would be the vehicle through which the IMF would take part in the latter initiative."I am pleased to announce that the executive board has reached understandings to ensure permanent continuation of the enhanced structural adjustment facility ... and allow the IMF to participate in the ... initiative for
2579 the highly-indebted poor countries," Camdessus said in his statement.He added that he warmly welcomed the "cooperative spirit" in the board that made the understandings possible.An IMF spokesman declined to elaborate further.</

2591 Loewen Group Inc., the target of a hostile takeover bid by rival funeral home operator Service Corp. International, said Friday it agreed to acquire Rose Hills Co. Inc. of Los Angeles for $240 million.Vancouver, British Columbia-based Loewen is teaming up with Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund L.P. of
2591 New York, to acquire the cemetery and mortuary operations and assets of Rose Hills Co. and The Rose Hill Memorial Park Association.Rose Hills Memorial Park is the largest cemetery in North America, and its mortuary serves more families annually than any other one in the United States.Loewen, North America's second-largest
2591 funeral home company, said the Rose Hill deal was in the works before Service Corp. launched its unsolicited $43 a share bid, worth $2.8 billion, on Tuesday.Houston-based Service Corp. is North America's biggest funeral home company and a fierce rival of Loewen.Loewen founder and Chairman Ray Loewen said Rose Hill
2591 will immediately boost the company's earnings."This transaction ... is part of Loewen's long-term growth plan to acquire strategic operators consisting of larger urban properties as well as small, family-owned funeral homes and cemeteries," Loewen said in a statement.The Rose Hill deal, coming a few months after Loewen acquired Prime Succession
2591 Inc., may play a role in getting a sweeter offer from Service Corp., analysts said.Last June, Loewen and Blackstone joined forces to buy Prime Succession, the largest privately held funeral home operator in the United States, for $320 million."I'm hard-pressed to think from any standpoint that this is negative. It's
2591 good for Loewen on its own and it's good for Service if it wins the day," said David Brodie, an analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy.Loewen gets an immediate earnings boost and can buy Blackstone's majority stake in Rose Hill in four years."They could say, 'These things are going to kick
2591 in with a good return four years down the road, so we've got extra future growth, so stick with us,'" Brodie said.But Rose Hill also makes Loewen a more attractive target and may help prompt a sweeter offer. Analysts said Service Corp. was rumored to be a rival bidder for
2591 California company.In a interview, Service Corp. President William Heiligbrodt downplayed the Rose Hill purchase, saying it's "no real victory" for Loewen shareholders."We don't see how that's a 'win' situation," Heiligbrodt said, adding that its offer makes sense for shareholders of both companies. He declined to say if Service Corp. would
2591 pursue a hostile takeover, but noted that "we usually try to finish the things we start."When asked about a possible role for Loewen's top managment if a friendly deal were completed, he said "we'd certainly like to talk about that."Loewen and Service Corp. have been bitter rivals in gobbling up
2591 small independent funeral home operators across North America. Loewen said its board will meet some time over the next few days to decide whether to fight to bid.Blackstone officials said Friday that they had not been approached by Loewen to help mount a defense."We're nowhere near to talking about what
2591 our role would be, if any, if they decided to launch any kind of defense," Blackstone spokesman Howard Lipson said."Other than to say, 'Look guys, we think you're terrific. If your plans call for something that involves private equity, we hope you think of us,' and I know they would,"
2591 Lipson said.Under the terms of the deal, Loewen and Blackstone will form a new company to acquire the Rose Hills operations.Loewen will integrate its 14 funeral homes and two combination funeral home/cemetery operations in California's Los Angeles and Orange counties into the new company.Loewen operates 931 funeral homes and 271
2591 cemeteries across the United States and Canada.Blackstone and its affiliates will be the major shareholders and control the board of directors in the new venture. But Loewen will have the option to buy Blackstone's interest after four years.The deal is expected to close by mid-December.</

2596 * TSE volumes heavy due to triple witching expiry * 14 sectors evenly split * 94 million shares traded worth C$1.36 billion Toronto stocks ended at record highs for a fifth straight session on Friday, while triple witching expiry spurred a day of heavy trading on Canada's biggest stock market.The
2596 TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 11.44 points to 5287.47, surpassing the previous record close set on Thursday.The index also recorded a new intra-day high of 5289.26.Just over 94 million shares were traded worth C$1.36 billion. Triple witching is the quarterly period when options, futures and options on futures all expire.
2596 Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 462 to 443 with 268 issues flat. Toronto's 14 sub-groups were evenly split. The strong side was led by consumer products, conglomerates, technology and financial services."Bank stocks have been doing well. There is some expectation that the Bank of Canada may lower rates again and that
2596 will help interest sensitive stocks," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.The TSE weakest groups included gold and precious metals, transportation and communications. Analysts said investors will be watching the bond market next week and its reaction to the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Tuesday.---

2600 company controls 50 percent of the AK/CJ property, about 100 km southeast of Lac de Gras where Dia Met Minerals Ltd is partnered with BHP Minerals Inc to build the first diamond mine in North America. Its partners are Glenmore Highlands Inc with 40 percent and Camphor Ventures Inc with
2600 10 percent."It would be easier to have a 90-10 set-up," Shatzko told Reuters after the company's annual meeting."In the next 30-60 days, it would be a good idea to look at that kind of arrangement," he said. Glenmore officials were unavailable for comment on merger prospects.Shatzko said Mountain Province expects
2600 a takeover offer from a major partner next year after bulk sampling is completed at the AK 5034 kimberlite pipe. He said company's that have shown a preliminary interest include RTZ Corp Plc, De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd."De Beers would be the favored candidate,"
2600 he said.After a "highly successful" 100-tonne mini bulk sample was completed earlier this year at the 5034 pipe, a C$20 million bulk sample of between 3,000 and 10,000 tonnes is planned for next spring, company president Jan Vandersande told shareholders.The bulk sample will attempt to substantiate Mountain Province's current estimates,
2600 which say the 5034 pipe contains "at least 20 million tonnes grading 3 carats per tonne" for a total value of between US$1.8 billion and US$3 billion.In addition, C$4.0 million is slated for exploration outside of the 5034 on the AK and CJ claim blocks. Mountain Province's share of all
2600 exploration costs is 50 percent.Mountain Province's largest declared shareholder is Societe Generale, a Paris-based financial institution with 20.12 percent of the issued shared as of April 25, 1996.-- Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100</

2602 Canada is expected to pump unprecedented volumes of crude oil to the United States over the next decade amid increasing competiton among shorthaul suppliers to the world's largest oil-consuming nation.But cost and reliability will determine whether it beats out other producing nations for a bigger slice of market share, industry
2602 experts say. A projected jump in Canadian heavy crude oil volumes shipped to the key U.S. Midwest refining region on newly-expanded pipelines next year is expected to cause a short-term glut, said Steve Kelly, an oil market analyst with Purvin &amp; Gertz Inc.But that should mean more competitive pricing for
2602 the gooey Canadian crude in the market, Kelly said."Short-term, the price will fall and that should encourage more consumption in the region to the extent that people can take in that heavy crude," Kelly said. The volume of Canadian oil shipped to U.S. refineries has skyrocketed over the past decade.
2602 In 1995, Canada pumped 1.41 million barrels per day to the U.S., compared to 468,000 bpd in 1985, figures from U.S. oil analyst Bonner and Moore Associates Inc show.But the massive increase allowed Canada only to maintain a 14 to 15 percent share of total U.S. imports. The main source
2602 of U.S. oil imports, and Canada's principal competition, is Mexico and the rest of Latin America, which accounted for around 35 percent last year. Crude output from the region also is expected to grow and is expected to continue to compete for the market share lost by Middle East suppliers
2602 since the Gulf War. Analysts said increases in pipeline capacity to the U.S. from Canada -- including a possible total of 250,000 bpd in expansion space on the IPL Energy Inc system to the U.S. Midwest and a further 170,000 bpd to Wyoming on the new Express Pipeline -- should
2602 also aid in cementing Canada's reliability in the eyes of U.S. refiners. Packed-full pipelines over the past few years meant a sometimes crippling rationing of space on IPL, which threatened Canada's competitive position against other imports, said Bob Laidlaw, manager of crude oil marketing for Alberta Energy Co Ltd, which
2602 is a 50-50 partner with TransCanada PipeLines Ltd in the Alberta-Wyoming Express project."But I really believe that issue is going to be behind us," Laidlaw said. "It's a good idea to expand the pipeline capacity and have the availability to get it there, but it will still be competing," said
2602 Chuck McSpadden, vice-president of market analysis for Bonner and Moore in Houston. "It's going to be quality-for-quality, price-for-price type competition."With multibillion-dollar moves to boost oil drilling, production and pipeline space from western Canada, the country stands to bolster its total output to 2.31 million barrels by 1998 from a projected
2602 2.16 million this year, according to figures from Canada's National Energy Board. And because of static Canadian consumption levels, any increase in production is expected to be pumped southward to the U.S., Kelly said. Current exports are just over half of total output.Production of Canadian light oil, previously thought to
2602 be on the wane, has bucked a long-term two-percent decline trend and increased over the past five years, thanks to a boom in drilling activity and better technology, the NEB said.Synthetic light oil production from the Canada' burgeoning oil sands industry is projected to rise by about five percent annually,
2602 although a recent spate of new projects could boost the figure over the next five years, it said.But of total gains, conventional heavy oil production is projected to make up the lion's share as more projects are announced, large reserves tapped and production costs fall with new horizontal drilling and
2602 production technology.Today, heavy oil prospects are being "drilled up like a pin cushion," said Martin Molyneaux, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp in Calgary.But Kelly warned that a glut in the U.S. Midwest could sway some producers to mothball higher-cost heavy oil projects, lowering some production forecasts. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau

2606 Blackstone were in a similar deal last June to acquire Prime Succession Inc, the largest privately owned funeral home operator in the United States, for US$320 million. 2608 Royal Bank of Canada said on Friday that it will arrange C$3 billion in financing for Nav Canada 's acquisition of the Canadian civil air navigation system from the Canadian government.The three-tranche facility will provide the initial funding for the acquisition until Nav Canada phases in its capital markets financing,
2608 the bank said.Some of the financing arranged by the bank will cover Nav Canada's day-to-day needs after the acquisition is completed. Nav Canada is a non-share capital corporation with exclusive rights to Canada's air traffic operations. Royal Bank said the financing was divided into two Canadian domestic tranches of between
2608 C$750 million and C$1 billion each and an international tranche of between C$1 billion and C$1.5 billion.The total financing would not exceed C$3 billion, the bank said.The domestic tranches will be revolving with maturities of 30 months and five years respectively, with the international tranche having an initial availability of
2608 364 days with a five-year term out. The pricing is governed by a six-part grid reflecting the rating of Nav Canada. As a non-share capital corporation, Nav Canada has members, rather than shareholders or other equity holders.One member is appointed by the Canadian government, two by user groups representing commercial
2608 air carriers and business aircraft operators and one by unions representing the company's employees. Other aviation interests are represented by 126 non-voting associate members. The acquisition is expected to close in October. Nav Canada will have more than 6,000 employees operating from seven area control centers, two terminal control units,
2608 44 control towers and 86 flight services stations in Canada. Nav Canada will be able to levy user fees for its services to meet its current and future financial requirements, such as debt service and reserves for future expenditures and contingencies.The company will move to fund its operations entirely through
2608 user fees within the first two years of closing of the acquisition. During this transition period the Canadian government will pay the company up to C$1.44 billion in revenues it collects through the present Air Transport Tax to supplement the user fee structure being implemented.-- Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100</

2612 A Canadian jazz star whose music is rooted in the sounds of Cuba begins an abbreviated U.S. tour on Saturday, saying her career is threatened by U.S.-Cuban political tension.Toronto-based saxophonist and flutist Jane Bunnett, who has been playing in Cuba for more than a decade, said she is an indirect
2612 victim of the controversial U.S. Helms-Burton law, which seeks to punish foreign companies that invest in Cuba.Helms-Burton, which was signed by President Bill Clinton in March after Cuban MiG fighters downed two private planes piloted by Cuban-Americans, does not target culture.But Bunnett said in a telephone interview she is convinced
2612 fear of anti-Cuban sentiment prompted U.S. concert promoters to cancel five of her concerts at colleges set for this month. All five were canceled shortly after the bill was passed.The tour begins on Saturday in Wausau, Wisconsin, with the other U.S. dates set for Rochester, New York, and Chicago. Bunnett
2612 will tour with the 16-piece Cuban band Oba-Ilu. She had been slated to release a CD with Oba-Ilu but that plan was also scapped shortly after Helms-Burton became law."Helms-Burton isn't supposed to affect cultural and sports activities -- it's primarily dealing with business," said Bunnett, who won a Juno Award,
2612 Canada's version of the Grammy, for her 1992 recording "Spirits of Havana." Her latest CD, "The Cuban Piano Masters," was released in August."I think people just panicked," she said. She said she had to scramble to add Canadian cities to the tour to make up the lost revenue and the
2612 Chicago venue had to be changed after the Cuban-American promoter received bomb threats.Martha Woods, who booked the tour for New York-based Jonathan Wentworth Associates, said it was impossible to link Helms-Burton with the cancellations. She said promoters had not signed on the dotted line and two educational services that were
2612 part of a group planning to bring in the band got "cold feet."The Canadian government has been a vocal opponent of the Helms-Burton law, which includes a provision to bar senior executives of foreign firms entry into the United States if they are found to be "trafficking" in property confiscated
2612 by the Castro government after Cuba's 1959 revolution.The same week the U.S. concerts were scrapped, a record deal with Sony Music's Canadian division, which was to release a CD recorded in February by Bunnett and Oba-Ilu, fell through at the 11th hour, Bunnett said."It was pretty important for the deal
2612 to be working along with Sony in the U.S.," she said. "The lawyers had come up with a mutual contract that was pretty much ready to be signed. So I find it strangely coincidental."But Randy Sharrard, Sony Music Canada's director of special marketing, said the company's abandonment of the deal
2612 was "a business decision" and not due to Helms-Burton."Basically it was a matter of numbers and it had nothing to do with politics," Sharrard said. "It was basically a coincidence that it all happened at the same time."</

2641 the first phase of development and the facilities will include 12 high-speed, 50 ton capacity container cranes, Han-Padron said.Support facilities include systems to supply ships with fuel and water, container repair facilities, storage facilities for 500 refrigerated containers on 50 hectares of land. 2641 as many as 12 ships at a time, Han-Padron said.</

2669 Hughes Electronics Corp's buyout of PanAmSat Corp is another aggresive move by Hughes into high growth data and communications services and gives General Motors Corp further reason to sell the rapidly changing company."This purchase tells me that this entity isn't long for the General Motors mix of business because they're
2669 going into businesses that are just not a part of GM," said John Modzelewski, an analyst at PaineWebber Group Inc. Hughes agreed to buy PanAmSat on Friday in a deal worth $3 billion. The companies will merge their satellite services into a new public company using the PanAmSat name.For months
2669 Wall Street has speculated that GM may want to spin off Hughes, which the automaker acquired in 1985 for more than $5 billion. Hughes Chairman Mike Armstrong has suggested in the past that he would prefer his company to operate independently.At a news conference in New York, Armstrong declined to
2669 speculate on a possible spinoff. Hughes has been diversifying in recent years away from its traditional staple as a maker of satellites and missiles into high growth consumer services such as DirecTV, its consumer satelite television operation."It's clear to everybody that the value of Hughes is becoming less and less
2669 what it was just a year or two ago," Modzelewski said. "This was a defense company that was going to link up with Delco and we were going to have aerospace technology make its way into GM cars." Modzelewski said Hughes' traditional defense business coupled with automotive unit Delco account
2669 for some 85 percent of profits, while the high growth space and communications side accounts for almost half of the company's value."What they're trying to do is push into some real high growth areas where the cost is a function of what the benefit is to you," Modzelewski said."Selling satellites

2691 the companies' projections were "highly speculative."The commission said, however, that it would allow the firms to file no earlier than January 1, 1997 an application to show that competition will deprive them of the opportunity to earn a fair return on their regulated assets.The companies argued that because of the
2691 introduction of competition into local phone markets, their shareholders would be denied an opportunity to earn a fair return on investment, amounting to a violation of their claimed constitutional protection against uncompensated "takings" of property. 2691 impacts," proceedings dealing with major components of a revised regulatory program, such as universal service and equal access rules, had not been completed.The commission said it would be premature to determine now whether the new regulatory program will adversely affect rates of return. 2691 be too speculative," the commission said.The commission said it would allow the companies to submit evidence that CPUC policy has resulted in investor losses.</

2695 U.S. utilities on Friday poured cold water on an idea by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to require all transmission line owners to file a capacity reservation tariff by the end of 1997.The commission had thought a capacity reservation tariff might be the best way to promote efficient use of
2695 the electric grid as power markets became more competitive under the FERC's open transmission access rules that went into effect in July.With a reservation tariff, transmission users would have to book firm rights between specific points on the grid instead of booking space based on total load requirements. While the
2695 commission believed that the capacity reservation system would allow all market participants to know how much and where capacity was available at any time, utility officials told FERC the system might not work that way."Moving to a CRT (capacity reservation tariff) is neither technically feasible nor economically desirable," said Charles
2695 Bayless, CEO of Tucson Electric Power Co, who represented the Edison Electric Institute at a FERC conference on the proposal.FERC hoped that reservation rights would help spur a secondary market for trading transmission capacity.But utility officials said trading physical transmission rights could complicate coordination of power production and transmission operations
2695 which are already complex."The proposal ... to create a reservation system and tradeable rights based on specific physical performance would be extremely difficult to implement and could have undesirable consequences, particularly the creation of stranded transmission costs," said Paul McCoy, a vice president of Commonwealth Edison Co, unit of Unicom
2695 Corp. Industry officials also warned that any new tariff designed to allocate transmission capacity should only be put in place after utilities have set up independent system operators with authority to redispatch power and manage trading of capacity rights.A capacity reservation tariff would likely spur power producers to overbook transmission
2695 capacity so that they are guaranteed space during peak demand periods, said John Odom, an engineer at Florida Power Corp, a unit of Florida Progress Corp.Overestimates of the capacity needed would lead to inefficient use of transmission space, he said.Utility officials and a state representative urged the commission to let
2695 states and regional power pools experiment with new approaches for allocating transmission capacity, instead of imposing a single, untried tariff on all utilities in the next 15 months.</

2708 Putnam Berkley Group, Inc. ; Simon &amp; Schuster, Inc. ; and Random House, Inc. The FTC said it did not reach any decision on whether there were any violations of antitrust law, but concluded that public interest would be best served by terminating the cases rather than expending resources to

2720 Barclays de Zoete Wedd Government Securities expects the Federal Reserve to raise the discount and federal funds rates by 50 basis points each next week -- a minority view tied to the firm's forecast of heightened inflationary risks."There is a need for monetary policy to be very aggressive to avoid
2720 a flare-up in inflation," said BZW senior economist Waldo Best. "We are closer to a flashpoint in inflation."Best cautioned that, if the Fed does not move relatively aggressively on rates promptly, "the flare-up would be much more accentuated." The Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24. The last
2720 Fed move took place on January 31 when the central bank shaved off 25 basis points from the discount and funds rates amid signs the U.S. expansion may be faltering."We think the Fed will raise the funds rate and the discount rate by 50 basis points," said Best who works
2720 on monetary policy forecasts with BZW chief economist Steve Ricchiutto."If they do 50 basis points, there is a very good chance they might not have to do anything else if the economy begins to decelerate going into the first quarter," Best added. Best said BZW's inflation models point to a
2720 marked acceleration in the inflation pace in the near future with the Consumer Price Index likely to rise at an annual rate of 3.5 percent in the coming months due to a "combination of higher labor costs, energy prices and food prices.""Our inflation models has all three arrows pointing in
2720 the same direction," Best added.In a Reuter survey, 17 out of 30 economists see a rate hike next week. Only BZW expects a 50-point dual move. Five other firms -- Aubrey Lanston, DLJ Securities, Lehman, MFR, and Standard &amp; Poor's -- see a 25-point dual rate hike. Eleven other firms
2720 see only a 25-point hike on the funds rate next week. Seven firms expect a move on November 13 -- the first FOMC meeting after the U.S. presidential elections -- while six do not call for a move this year.If BZW's rate forecast proves correct, Best expected the long end
2720 of the Treasury market to rally as "there would be the reestablishment of the Fed's credibility regarding fighting inflation.""We believe there is definitely a faction at the Fed that believes they should have tightened by now. One (50-point) move would reestablish cohesion within the FOMC," Best said. Best said a
2720 50-point tightening would allow the economy to run its course into 1997 free of inflationary risks and give the Fed time to reassess its policy in the second quarter.According to BZW, another factor arguing in favor of an aggressive rate hike now is the reemergence of a "bubble" in the
2720 U.S. stock market.Best -- who noted the perception of BZW's foreign clients is that the Fed is getting too lenient on inflation -- expected a 25-point funds rate hike to translate into a moderate Treasury market selloff "because no one believes you can get away with one single 25-point tightening
2720 move."The absence of a Fed move, Best said, would trigger a long-end selloff on the perception the Fed is losing its anti-inflation focus.-- Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666</

2733 About 17,223 megawatts (MW) of nuclear generated electricity, just over 17 percent of the nation's nuclear output, is currently shut for maintenance and refueling, according to a Reuter survey of plant operators."The fall is a low demand period (for electricity), the peak demand is through the course of the summer,"
2733 said Gene Gorzelnik, spokesman for the North American Electric Reliability Council (NERC).Nuclear power plants typically shut down for about 45 days every 18 months to refuel and conduct any needed maintenance or upgrades. This work in turn is usually set for the "shoulder", or low-demand months of May and September."Generally
2733 speaking, the spring or fall would be the best time for outages just because electricity loads are not likely to be as high," said Diane Park, spokeswoman for Entergy Corp.The absence of a huge piece of the nation's power generation complex was having predictably little impact on electricity prices, which
2733 traders and brokers said were at some of their lowest levels in weeks due to mild weather.September is seen as the prime time for outages, when temperatures are too cool to require air conditioning but not yet cold enough to trigger heating demand."In September the days are still long enough
2733 that people aren't using their lights, they're turning the air conditioner off," said one Mid-West power marketer. 2736 against other investment companies including Dean Witter, Travelers Group's Smith Barney, and Lehman Brothers, a Delaware attorney experienced in limited partnerships told Reuters. 2736 considered undervalued "because there's no public market for LP units and they are sold at a very low price. This provides an opportunity for speculative funds to acquire partnerships cheaply." 2736 three Liquidity Fund LP plaintiffs, had "a contractual right to the lists under the applicable Partnership Agreements" but not a statutory right.Jacobs said that contractual right overrode his finding that Donaldson did not have a "proper purpose" under Delaware law for wanting to seeing the lists.According to court papers, Donaldson
2736 said he wanted to see the lists to determine whether to increase his investment in the partnerships through a tender offer. But Jacobs said that in trial Donaldson admitted "that if any tender offer were to be made, it would be conducted not by the plaintiffs directly but rather by
2736 an as-yet-to-be-created $50 million investment fund."Jacobs said Donaldson's funds were liquid but insufficient to mount a tender offer."The plaintiffs have no plans to use the lists to increase the value of their investments" but are using a combined five percent interest in the PaineWebber partnerships as a "legal vehicle to
2736 obtain the lists" and make them available "to the investment fund in return for an equity participation in that fund, should it ever be created."A PaineWebber spokesman could not be reached for comment. 2782 A slim majority of economists expects the Federal Reserve to raise official interest rates by 25 basis points on Tuesday, but foreign exchange experts said the dollar will need more aggressive rate action to bolster its fundamental outlook.The dollar is currently discounting a 25-basis point tightening in the 5.25 percent
2782 federal funds target rate. It may take a bigger hike or an increase in the discount rate, as sought by regional Fed banks, to give the dollar an added lift, experts said. "Fifty (basis points) would probably be enough to push the dollar through the top of the technical trading
2782 range," said John Nelson, senior vice president of foreign exchage trading at ABN-AMRO Bank. "But I think an interest rate hike of 25 points is definitely priced in and 50 is probably partially priced."Seventeen of 30 economists in the latest Reuters poll said the Fed is likely to raise short-term
2782 interest rates at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next week. All but one of the 17 predicted a 25-basis point rate hike. The poll followed news this week that eight of 12 district Fed banks are pushing for a higher discount rate, which is currently set at 5.0
2782 percent. But the results were largely unchanged from a September 6 poll in which 16 of 30 experts predicted higher rates.If Fed policy makers do deliver a discount rate hike Tuesday, it might buttress the dollar by broadcasting a concern that festering wage pressures require a dose of stronger medicine.
2782 "Meaning they are signaling more of a longer-term need for higher rates, the discount (rate) would have more of an impact than just a 25-basis point hike (in the federal funds target rate)," said Mark Gargano, manager of foreign exchange at First Union National Bank.The Fed last adjusted interest rates
2782 on January 31, when it lowered the discount rate and fed funds rates by 25 basis points each.The dollar has gyrated in the last week while market players became overloaded by myriad Fed action scenarios. After low inflation and weak retail sales data buoyed bonds and depressed the dollar late
2782 last week, Tuesday's news about the regional Feds refueled bets on a credit tightening."It rekindled the expectations," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist at Bank of Montreal in Chicago. "Itreally does confirm ... the regional banks are far more hawkish on inflation than the Fed governors themselves. I'm not sure
2782 whether it is anything different from that, or whether they are laying the groundwork for something," he added. Any U.S. rate hike is expected to boost the dollar more versus currencies in Europe, where rates are falling, rather than against the yen.Japanese deposit rates are expected to remain stable in
2782 the foreseeable future, traders said."Rate spreads, in essence, should favor the U.S. because you've got European (rates) dropping and U.S.(rates) rising, so spreads should be widening dramatically," Gargano said.However, the technical picture is more important than the interest rate outlook for the dollar right now, some traders said.Marc Chandler, senior
2782 currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, agreed. "Whether the Fed moves 25 basis points or not is not, in the scheme of things, a bullish or bearish factor," he said.But, Nelson added that "the absence of an interest rate hike would probably put the dollar under some pressure."-- 212-859-1667</

2794 Danish governments bonds, with their currency stability and generous spreads over Bunds, continue to offer good value to investors seeking shelter from the vicissitudes of European Monetary Union, analysts said.Denmark's robust economic fundamentals qualify it, along with Ireland and Luxembourg, to join a single European currency by meeting strict Maastricht
2794 convergence criteria.However, Denmark's 1993 EMU opt-out provision gives Danish government bonds something of a safe-haven status in the runup to monetary union in 1999, analysts said. "One of the things we've been looking for is for Denmark to outperform other European countries given its fundamentals," said Julie Grandstaff, vice president
2794 of global fixed income at Bailard, Biehl and Kaiser.The Danish ten-year government bond has maintained a spread of 90 to 100 basis points over its German counterpart over the past several weeks, she said."In terms of the yield curve, certainly the ten-year sector would do well. The current spread there
2794 is about 97 basis points with a yield of 7.13 percent," she said. Denmark's low inflation rate -- about 2.0 percent -- suggests a net yield of about 50 basis points over German Bunds, she added.With a projected 1996 budget gap of 1.7 percent of gross domestic product compared with
2794 an EMU target of 3.0 percent, Denmark meets most of the EMU convergence targets, said Marc Chandler, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell."Their budget deficit as a percentage of GDP is among the lowest in Europe," he said. Giving Danish bonds added appeal is the fact that the Danish
2794 currency has remained within a stable, narrow band against the German mark, helping to limit currency risk, said Michael Perelstein, managing director at MacKay Shields.The crown has traded as low as 3.87 against the mark in recent weeks, but has generally maintained a level around 3.85 in the recent past,
2794 analysts said."It's basically like saying Denmark is like a sector in the German bond market that pays 90 (basis points) over comparable German governments, so it becomes a real buy," Perelstein said. Analysts said the crown's low volatility appeals to investors looking to trade in interest rate differentials, selling marks
2794 and buying Danish paper.Denmark initially rejected the Maastricht Treaty in an historic "no" vote in a referendum in June 1992.It later voted narrowly in favor of the accord but only after the Danish government secured special opt-out provisions on monetary union and other key clauses."The European Union has said three
2794 countries meet the Maastricht criteria. Denmark is one of them, but their political will is questionable," Chandler said.Executives of Denmark's two largest banks said earlier this week that Denmark's opt-out of EMU could have a beneficial effect on Danish bonds.A common European currency could reduce opportunities for currency speculation, encouraging
2794 a flow of speculative funds into Denmark, narrowing spreads between Danish bonds and their European counterparts, they said.N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1662</

2806 Recurring rumors that Saddam Hussein is a big oil futures player are not backed up by the facts, according to U.S. intelligence and regulatory officials.The theory, which has surfaced over the years when Iraq has been at the center of Middle East turmoil, is that Saddam Hussein and his Baghdad
2806 cronies play oil futures markets, particularly the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), via Swiss accounts controlled by third parties. "We have looked into the rumor and found that there is no evidence to substantiate it," said a Langley, Virginia-based U.S. official familiar with government intelligence on Iraq.The view from intelligence
2806 sources is backed up by futures market regulators and experienced brokers on the exchange.Though there has long been light-hearted talk among oil traders and diplomats of how the inner circle in Baghdad could benefit financially from its political and military actions, that speculation has taken on a more serious tone
2806 in recent months as oil price volatility has run at its highest level since the end of the Gulf War. In the wake of protracted negotiations between Baghdad and the United Nations over a limited lifting of oil sanctions, The New York Times' ran a 'Foreign Affairs' column in August,
2806 couched as an idea for a novel, which mused at length about how Saddam Hussein could use foreknowledge of his diplomatic positions to benefit from their effect on oil prices. Last week, following the oil market turmoil caused by Baghdad's incursion into protected Kurdish zones and the U.S. military response,
2806 the respected Journal of Commerce quoted an unnamed United Nations official as saying that Baghdad "is believed to be playing the futures market for some easy money.""They can play the oil futures market and make money out of nothing," the U.N. official told the newspaper.But regulatory investigation of futures market
2806 activity both before and after major market-moving events in Iraq turned up nothing suspicious, according to officials. "I can assure you that when Surveillance saw (the big Iraq-related price moves) they looked into it," said John Phillips, spokesman for the Commodities Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in Washington, the regulator for
2806 U.S. futures exchanges including the NYMEX. He explains that all NYMEX trades must be carried out by members of the exchange and they must report to the CFTC details of any futures position of 300 contracts or more in any one month, covering 300,000 barrels, or about $7 million worth
2806 of oil at current prices. The CFTC's Surveillance committee meets weekly and examines closely any unusual activity. The market and the firms trading in it the weeks prior to and following the latest crisis were examined closely and no suspicious trading was found, sources confirm. There have been similar exercises
2806 previously when markets were roiled, they add.To conceal trades of significant enough size to make it worthwhile to Baghdad "would be damn near impossible," said Phillips of the CFTC. "There has never been an entity which has come up that you are not aware of who they are." To make
2806 $1 million from the threshold reportable position would require a move of more than $3 a barrel in Friday's oil price, a huge move.And Baghdad would have to get the direction right. When it signed its deal to partially lift U.N. sanctions on May 20, an event which would be
2806 expected to result in lower oil prices, oil futures ended up nearly $2 a barrel that day. "You are constantly hearing about conspiracy theories, whether it is Saddam Hussein having a trading account or whatever," said Tom Blakeslee, a trader at Minneapolis-based Cargill Investor Services Inc., one of the largest
2806 international commodities firms."For it to make any difference to him he would have to trade in such huge size that we would know. Frankly, I don't believe it. I don't think he is moving troops around and betting futures on it; I think he's got bigger goals," said Blakeslee.</
