3180 Independent monitors said on Friday more than 100 percent of the maximum possible electorate apparently voted in Bosnia's elections and they demanded an investigation before results were certified.After days of exhaustive number-crunching of preliminary figures provided by international election supervisors, the monitors concluded the voter turnout was "improbably high".The three
3180 main Moslem, Serb and Croat nationalist parties that dismembered Bosnia in war and agreed to peace in late 1995 under Western pressure romped to election victories in their respective domains last Saturday.Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem, won the senior seat of a new tripartite presidency, narrowly defeating a Serb
3180 separatist who, with a Croat, took the other two seats.The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which organised the vote, and an OSCE-affiliated observer team reported that the elections -- for a presidency, parliament and regional assemblies -- were generally free of irregularities.But the International Crisis Group (ICG), a
3180 respected private agency monitoring the peace process, said its own inquiry turned up discrepancies that cast serious doubt on the integrity of the elections."Something stinks big time here. All three sides come out of these elections looking pretty black," a Western official familiar with the ICG probe told Reuters."The Moslems,
3180 in particular, may have stuffed ballot boxes big time because they were so desperate to have Izetbegovic beat (Serb candidtate Momcilo) Krajisnik."OSCE official Nicole Szulc said its experts were examining their figures in view of the ICG report. "We take these allegations very seriously. Clearly something's wrong somewhere," she said.U.N.
3180 figures used by OSCE planners put the total of eligible voters at 2.91 million -- 1.34 million in their original homes, 675,000 displaced within Bosnia and 900,000 refugees abroad. Preliminary final OSCE figures said 2,431,554 ballots were cast.But ICG deputy director John Fawcett said significant numbers of people did not
3180 vote, meaning there could not possibly have been 2.43 million valid ballots under the "one man-one vote" principle.Quoting OSCE figures, he said only 641,000 of the potential 900,000 refugee voters registered to vote, reducing the maximum possible voter pool to 2.66 million.In this case, if 2.43 million voters cast ballots
3180 for the presidency, turnout would have been 91.4 percent."To put these figures into context, turnout in the 1990 elections was 74.4 percent when only 2.33 million voted," he said. This was before tens of thousands of war casualties and the displacement of more than 1.5 million people.Fawcett said the initial
3180 calculation of a 91.4 percent turnout, a plateau historically equalled only in the rigged one-party elections of communist countries, rose to 103.9 percent when other key factors were considered:-- Only 14,700 people crossed Bosnia's internal communal boundaries to vote in former home areas out of a potential of about 150,000
3180 who did not register to vote absentee.-- A maximum of 98,400 out of 123,000 Bosnian Serb refugees now in Yugoslavia returned to vote in person, OSCE figures said, although Bosnian Serb authorities estimated only 37,000 actually came back.-- Of 260,000 Moslem and Croat refugees from Serb terrain, and now living
3180 in states other than Yugoslavia, who registered to vote absentee, only about 100,000 appeared to have voted."If these highly conservative assumptions are correct, the maximum number of voters should have been 2,341,100, which would give a voter turnout of 103.9 percent," said Fawcett.He said the ICG calculations did not account
3180 for the estimated five percent of the electorate who tried to vote but could not because their names were missing from voter registers.Diplomats said there was only one confirmed case of ballot- box stuffing but security and technical standards were so lax in some polling areas that abuses were inevitable.ICG
3180 director Sir Terrence Clark said municipal elections planned for November would have no credibility unless the OSCE overhauled registration procedures for refugees abroad and corrected voter lists in Bosnia.</

3194 Azerbaijan issued its first Treasury bills on Friday, in a bold step by the oil-rich but economically-strapped country to tap the government paper market for much-needed cash.The National (central) Bank said five billion manats' worth of one-month T-Bills were auctioned at an average discount of 7.58 percent, producing an average
3194 annualised yield of 31.18 percent.Investors, mainly newly-authorised dealers, snapped up the entire issue of short-term paper, giving the state coffers 4.87 billion manat in revenue.The former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan sits on huge oil reserves in its sector of the Caspian Sea and has attracted billions of dollars in foreign
3194 investment from Western and Japanese oil consortiums.But its economy is in shambles after seven years of a debilitating war with Armenia over the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh enclave and economic reforms have lagged behind those in most former Soviet republics.Gross domestic product shrank 17.2 percent last year after a 21.9 percent slip
3194 in 1994, and industrial output showed similarly steep declines.There is a rudimentary two-tier banking system, with nearly 250 small banks. 3272 price growth because of several structual problems Poland faced.He said the wage growth mechanism which indexes salaries to price growth created a direct link between the two and hampered government attempts to lower the inflation.Inflation was also fuelled by unreformed sectors of the economy, which often increase prices to compensate
3272 for high costs instead of modernising, he said. @"Often an enterprise that is not able to reform tries to push the resulting costs onto its prices...(and) many of these sectors and industries have some monopoly power or enjoy protection," Rodlauer said.-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700</

3282 NATO's mission in Bosnia may have finally answered the question: what is the alliance for now the Cold War is over?In less than a year the alliance that won the East-West confrontation without firing a shot in anger has moved from peace enforcer to peace supervisor in a mission unthinkable
3282 during the Cold War.When Bosnians voted last Saturday, NATO troops policed roads, patrolled polling stations and escorted ballot boxes to counting centres. The 55,000 soldiers ensured the vote passed off smoothly.In sharp contrast to the United Nations, which left Bosnia with its credibility in tatters, NATO has used the Balkans
3282 to enhance its reputation and confirm itself as the European continent's pre-eminent security organisation.The only criticism stems from its failure to arraign indicted war criminals, particularly the Bosnian Serbs' wartime leader Radovan Karadzic and his army commander Ratko Mladic.Supporters of NATO say that task was deliberately left out of its
3282 mission aims and will be fulfilled only when there is sufficient political will in national capitals.Senior NATO officials say the challenge for the alliance now is to build quickly on the Bosnian experience, particularly links forged with former enemies who participated in the NATO-led peace Implementation Force (IFOR)."We have to
3282 show IFOR was not just a one-night stand," said one senior NATO official."The challenge is not just getting Bosnia right, but making NATO a permanent feature of the new security landscape now taking shape in Europe."That begins next week when NATO defence ministers gather in Norway for the first formal
3282 discussion of what sort of force to leave in Bosnia when the current mandate expires in December.Western allies accept that a force has to stay in order to prevent conflict and give the Dayton peace accords time to take root, but its exact size, mandate, duration and composition are yet
3282 to be agreed.Many countries, however, want it to take another step in the direction of a "new NATO".Germany has indicated it may commit ground troops and a more flexible, less U.S.-dominated command structure, with Russian participation, could be used.Former Warsaw Pact enemies, such as Poland and Hungary, see close cooperation
3282 in the force as a way of strengthening their case for full NATO membership early next year -- an issue which will require a new NATO-Russia deal on European security."We want the follow-on force to be as ground-breaking as IFOR," the official added.Despite earlier warnings of "mission creep", officials say
3282 the most powerful military alliance ever assembled did far more than just provide the security blanket to allow Saturday's polls to take place. It as good as ran the elections.NATO's military were closely involved in the detailed planning process, making available its hi-tech infrastructure to poll organisers from the Organisation
3282 for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).Robert Frowick, the head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, described NATO's effort as "brilliant" and said the polls would not have been possible without its presence.Finally let off the leash in the summer of 1995, the alliance used air strikes to force the
3282 Bosnian Serbs to pull back their heavy guns and end the 3-1/2 year siege of Sarajevo.Then it broke new ground, assembling the biggest ground force seen in Europe since the end of World War Two to police implementation of the Dayton peace agreement -- the alliance's first "out of theatre"
3282 operation.Diplomats say the failure of the international community to head off the wars in former Yugoslavia and then stop them highlighted the importance of transatlantic unity. For much of the fighting, western Europe and the United States were divided."When we spoke with one voice, we got things done. That is,
3282 I think, the lesson," Carl Bildt, the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, has told Reuters.NATO is the only organisation which formally brings the United States and the Western allies together and has the military capability to enfore its writ. The critics who questioned its relevance after the collapse of
3282 communism now remain silent.The alliance's high-profile role in Bosnia has coincided with the end of talk of a separate European security role outside the alliance, fashionable within the European Union until it failed to make any impact on the war on its doorstep."NATO is the only show in town, we
3282 are all now agreed on that," one alliance ambassador says.</

3305 A rusted ferris wheel towers lifelessly over the ruins of Agdam, an Azeri city which exists on world maps but is almost devoid of normal life.The city once had a population of 100,000 Moslem Azeris, but it was overrun by Christian Armenians in 1993 as part of a drive by
3305 the Armenian forces to create a huge buffer zone around the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh in western Azerbaijan.Agdam was the base from which Azeri forces launched deadly missle attacks against Armenian-held towns and villages in the Karabakh enclave. Its capture became a symbol of Armenian success on the battlefield over
3305 Azerbaijan.The conflict, frozen for more than two years by a ceasefire forced on a reluctant Azerbaijan after military defeats, casts a shadow of uncertainty over the tinderbox Caucasus region, rocked by ethnic unrest since the Soviet Union began to fall apart.Azerbaijan and Armenia have been fighting for eight years over
3305 mountainous Karabakh, which Soviet map-makers placed in Azerbaijan even though most inhabitants were ethnic Armenians -- traditional enemies of Turkic Azerbaijan.The war started when the local Armenians demanded to be administered from the Armenian capital of Yerevan. Thousands of people died before the ceasefire was declared.No one disputes that Armenians
3305 from the Karabakh region did most of the fighting, but arms and logistical support from the Yerevan government were crucial.The war is the most serious issue facing both countries and is a major factor in Sunday's Armenian presidential election, essentially a two-way battle between incumbent Levon Ter-Petrosyan and former prime
3305 minister Vazgen Manukyan.The Armenians looted Agdam clean after capturing it, removing anything made of metal and selling it as scrap.Now walls of worthless bricks line the town's wide, derelict streets. An eerie silence hangs in the air, punctuated by Armenian soldiers racing by in military vehicles or the rumble of
3305 lorries full of the junk metal some still come to scavenge.Armenians like Razim Tsaturyan, a 42-year-old who fought in Karabakh until the ceasefire, trek into Agdam only to look for salvage or to collect fruit."I'm just going down to gather some pomegranates for my kids," he said, hitching a ride
3305 with a journalist into Agdam from his home in the regional Karabakh capital of Stepanakert."There is almost nothing left to take here, right down to the nails and bolts."Looting and burning has been the rule for all sides in the myriad Caucasian wars of the past few years.Stepanakert also still
3305 shows the scars of the conflict. Dozens of buildings were destroyed or damaged by shrapnel from the notoriously innacurate rockets.Azerbaijan's government has made it clear it will use new oil revenues from lucrative offshore projects to rebuild its army and retake what it has lost by force if necessary."Time is
3305 not on the Armenians' side," said a Western diplomat in Yerevan.Presidential candidates Ter-Petrosyan and Manukyan have been trying to take credit for successes on the battlefield, but neither has produced a clear idea of how to end the dispute.Nagorno-Karabakh, home to 170,000 ethnic Armenians, has run itself as an independent
3305 state for five years, but its leaders make no secret of the fact that their real goal is union with Armenia."Every Armenian in their soul wants the two parts of our Armenian nation to be united... We understand that politically this is more difficult, so independence for us is a
3305 compromise," Karabakh "foreign minister" Arkady Gugasyan told Reuters.Gugasyan accuses Azerbaijan of using the talks to buy time and rearm to try to start the war anew.Azerbaijan says it is willing to offer Karabakh "autonomy" but Gugasyan says Baku has yet to say what this might entail."We are not going to
3305 give up our practical independence, including the right to have our own army. Maybe we can find some sort of mutual cooperation, but we will never agree to be ruled by Azerbaijan. That would be suicide," he said.Thousands died during the fighting and many Azeri refugees face the prospect of
3305 yet another winter in tents.But even if Azerbaijan eventually agrees to some sort of autonomy for Karabakh, it will never agree to the loss of the territories around, including cities like Agdam.Gugasyan says there is no intention of holding the towns forever but says his government wants security guarantees before
3305 giving them up.Political analysts say Armenia, whose trade routes have been severed by the conflict and an Azeri blockade, will be severely handicapped unless it can find a way out of the war.But they say both Manukyan and Ter-Petrosyan owe their political survival to the nationalist movement born in the
3305 late 1980s that demanded Armenia control the region, and they cannot politically afford major concessions to the Azeris.</

3323 Regional Agricultural Union of Agave Producers.Added Beas, "We can't let them keep putting sugar in tequila."Benjamin Garcia Duran, plant manager for Tequila Cuervo, which exports its product under the Jose Cuervo brand name, said if blockade extends past Friday, it would affect production by "100 percent.""Each day of the stoppage

3336 Like an old scar that never heals, talk of a devaluation of the local peso currency has erupted again in Argentina.The debate was triggered by powerful businessman Jorge Born, who said recently the current convertibility system makes Argentine companies less competitive abroad."Average wages in dollars are too high," said Born,
3336 head of the multinational Bunge y Born. He was joined in calling for an exchange rate change by two former government advisors, the leader of the center-right Democratic Center Union party Alvaro Alsogaray and economist Guillermo Calvo, although each had different formulas."The time is approaching when pressures will require a
3336 solution to the problem that must be tackled together by economists, businessmen and the government so as not to alarm the population," said Alsogaray. The Argentine peso has been pegged at parity to the dollar by law since April of 1991 under the convertibility plan designed by former Economy Minister
3336 Domingo Cavallo, which guarantees virtually full backing of the currency in gold, dollars and bond reserves.Convertibility was highly successful in taming once runaway inflation, which this year will be around zero percent, but some analysts say it prevented Argentina from becoming a leading exporter. Market sources told Reuters a powerful
3336 U.S. bank based in Argentina was conducting research into the possible repercussions of a devaluation of up to 30 percent.As rumours spread this week, President Carlos Menem came out denying "any possibility of a devaluation."Most analysts think the exchange rate has distorted relative prices, favoring producers of goods sold only
3336 in the country and hurting exports.But although there is a near-consensus regarding the disease, the cure is shrouded in controversy. "A nominal devaluation is not the solution. It would create such chaos that it would be impossible for it to affect real variables," said economist Juan Carlos de Pablo, a
3336 staunch supporter of the convertibility plan.In a similar vein economist Aldo Abram of consultants Proeco said: "If relative prices are really distorted, the way out is not a devaluation but a deregulation of the markets and flexibilization of labor laws."The government recently proposed sweeping labor reforms. For his part leading
3336 economist and former economy minister Roberto Alemann warned: "Even the mere hint of a devaluation would leave banks without a single peso deposit."Government economists dismiss talk that exports are suffering, noting they have surged to $21 billion in 1995 from $12 billion in 1991 and could reach $28 billion this
3336 year.Critics of peso-dollar parity say exports still account only for eight percent of gross domestic product against an average 16 percent in other Latin American countries.But even the harshest critics agree a devaluation is made more difficult by the fact that three million people have dollar debts and public utility
3336 rates are fixed in dollars."This is the poison pill that Cavallo left us and will be suffered by all Argentines," said economist Eduardo Conessa. "A devaluation would cause savers to go broke and many Argentines would be unable to pay their utility bills."-- Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0654</

3385 Aiming to solve the problem of weak financing for Mexico's water treatment plants, government officials and private sector experts are studying a plan that would allow local governments to issue bonds.There are a number of daunting barriers to overcome, however, including a lack of standardized financial information, officials said. "It
3385 is something that we are working on. There has been a group formed in the bank to see if these (water) organizations can place bonds in the future...," said Alfredo Navarrete Martinez, the associate director of finances for Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Publicos, also known as Banobras.Banobras is
3385 the Mexican development bank charged with providing long-term credits and support to infrastructure projects, including water treatment.Mexico has decentralized its water and waste-water treatment authorities over the past few years into "organismos de aqua," which are run mainly by states and municipalities."The bank has been looking at this from the
3385 start as a medium- and long-term project. We don't believe that we can succeed in three or six months, rather it is something that will take more time," Navarrete said in an interview.The aim is help municipalities reduce their financing costs, and allow markets to make a realistic evaluation of
3385 the risk of lending to the municipalities.The development bank is looking at a number of issues, such as whether demand for the paper would be great enough to ensure liquidity, and whether the bonds might be able to have tax free status such as many municipal bonds do in the
3385 United States. At the moment, the most likely paper that would be issued would be medium-term, about three years to begin with, an official with Banobras said."We are half-way through. One thing that will help is the Afores, (the planned private pension plan) next year," the official said."Also it is
3385 important to look at tax implications. The way we have seen it in the United States, is that it is attractive for certain investors. That is something we are exploring as well. It is not just issuing the paper," he said.There are other issues that have been raised as well.For
3385 example, only 10 to 20 of the Mexican water organizations would likely meet the criteria to have their debt rated, one recent report said.There are also legal roadblocks to having states or local governments issue foreign denominated debt, but some suggestions, such as the creation of trusts, have been put
3385 forward that might allow borrowers to skirt those barriers.Various federal ministries would also have to sign on.There are other potential difficulties to overcome. "What we have found is that there isn't standardized information about the public finances of the municipalities," said Navarrete.What is clear is that there is a need
3385 for this type of financing, though."We have supported the (bond) proposal, and we think that it one of the best options for financing, which is one of our main problems, along with high interest rates," said Ricardo Garza Blanc, president of the industry umbrella group, Empresas de Agua y Saneamiento
3385 de Mexico, which represents about 320 water groups in Mexico.-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559. E-mail at robert.kozak@reuters.com</

3401 Heat and humidity blanket Chapare's mountains in central Boliva with vegetation so thick the rainforest appears to be a lost paradise.But government troops torching a makeshift laboratory while military helicopters fly overhead on a recent patrol are testimony to this region's most profitable crop, cocaine, and the fact that Chapare
3401 is no paradise, lost or found.One cocaine lab has been destroyed but for officials of the military's anti-drug battalion, UMOPAR, victory is short lived. "Many people just move on and start again if they are chased away," the unit's commander Luis Caballero said.Chapare is the world's second largest producer of
3401 coca leaf and third largest producer of cocaine paste, which is later purified and sold mostly in America's inner city streets. Colombia and Peru account for the rest.Why, after years of concerted international efforts that cost governments billions of dollars, do drug kingpins continue to hold their ground? And why
3401 has Bolivia, which in the past produced just coca leaf, the raw material for cocaine, advanced to producing cocaine almost ready for consumption in the form of "paste" and "base"?A half-hour ride from UMOPAR near Chimore hamlet followed by a 30-minute walk through the thick tropical forest of Chapare goes
3401 a long way to answer those questions.First, the robust coca plant yields four crops of leaf a year. The rich soil and the heat and rain are all it needs during its 10-year lifespan. And the labs, unlike the more elaborate sites common in Colombia, can be erected quickly by
3401 a few men for perhaps as little as the price of two grams of cocaine in New York.These labs require no chemists either -- just a few barefoot campesinos crushing coca leaves in a plastic container with water fetched in buckets from one of the myriad streams crisscrossing Chapare. There
3401 is no electricity or running water. Machetes, buckets, shovels, some sticks and a piece of cloth used for sifting are their simple tools.Nor do the labs have roofs or walls. "Cocaleros," cocaine workers, open up a narrow path in the jungle with machetes and clear a 25-by-10 foot (eight-by-three metre)
3401 area. The thick vegetation makes them invisible from a short distance away.Then come the "precursor chemicals" -- a sophisticated term for nothing more than gasoline (petrol), lime, baking powder and sulphuric acid.More and more, Bolivian labs are now going one step further and producing cocaine base -- the last step
3401 before cocaine is ready for consumption -- which is smaller in volume and has a much longer lifespan than the paste.These labs each produce up to four kilos of paste or base a day and net the Cocaleros $450 to $500 per kilo. The further away from Chapare, the higher
3401 the price becomes -- $1,000 per kilo after it is purified and taken to the border, $9,000 in Brazil, between $17,000 and $25,000 in Miami, Caballero said.Some 40,000 families from the Aymara, Quechua and Guarani aborigine groups grow coca and help produce about 170 tonnes of cocaine paste a year.
3401 But most is confiscated and burned, so the Chapare's net yield is some 60 tonnes a year, he added.Manpower in the area is any businessman's dream come true -- cheap, plentiful, loyal, highly mobile. Bolivian campesinos, who rank among the poorest in Latin America, will readily grow coca and then
3401 crush it with their feet in a tub for a handful of Bolivianos, mindless of the health hazards posed by the chemicals, army officials say.Many live in clusters of one-room wooden huts standing on poles above the ground. This gives the cocaine workers plenty of mobility. If the army destroys
3401 their crop, as is often the case, they just move with their families, their few hogs and other scant belongings a little further into the jungle by another stream and build a new hut. Lookouts for cocaine workers set off firecrackers when they see military vans approaching, giving them ample
3401 time to flee.Caballero said his 270-strong battalion set up 13 years ago has burned nearly 2,300 labs so far this year. That comes down to almost 10 labs a day and reveals the odds the troops are up against with just a few trucks and four helicopters.The government, sometimes with
3401 backing from United Nations agencies, is promoting alternative crops such as pineapples, bananas, palm hearts and citrus. In some cases it compensates peasants who willingly give up growing coca with money and gives them seeds, cows and technical assistance.But many peasants find four crops a year, paid for in cash
3401 and free of sanitary controls, invoices and credit lines, hard to beat. It is also clear that poor people barely making a living off the land find it hard to discuss alternative crops -- or anything else, for that matter -- with armed rural patrols or their associates.Asked for comment,
3401 a woman holding a baby in her arms, one of about a dozen hut dwellers standing by a dirt road as troops filed by, replied "I know nothing, sir. They just come here in the trucks. ... I know nothing."</

3467 small scale mining, were biased against the commercial mining industry."The proposed modifications of the IRR go against the letter and the spirit of the Mining Act which encourage the exploration, development, utilisation, and conservation of our country's natural resources," Disini told participants of the forum.</

3480 region's surplus."The new Dalian refinery will have a bigger impact on the market" than new refineries elsewhere in Asia which have flooded and depressed the market since July, a Japanese trader said.The Dalian West Pacific Petrochemical Co, China's largest joint venture refinery set up to export gasoline, is by owned
3480 by Total SA of France and several Chinese companies, including state oil giant SINOCHEM.Sources close to the venture said the 100,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Dalian refinery would start trial runs at the end of September and should be exporting 40,000 bpd by the end of the year.The refinery's start up date,
3480 originally scheduled for May 1995, has been delayed several times and the sources could not give a firm date when the refinery would start commercial operations.Traders said the possibility of fresh gasoline supplies made the outlook for November and December uncertain.New refining capacity in Asia has added to a regional
3480 surplus. Thailand alone is estimated to have started exporting up to 43,000 bpd since July.Traders said they had been moving some of the surplus to South and East Africa, Australia and South America."It is interesting how quickly the region as a whole has reacted to the surplus," a trader in
3480 Singapore."Cargoes have been moving out, Saudi Yanbu import barrels have been shut off and refiners in Asia have cut runs. The supply side has been taken care of," he said."It is now a regular trend that cargoes from our region are going elsewhere," said another trader.But traders said if additional
3480 Chinese supplies hit the markets at the end of the year, it might not be so easy to find buyers.They said sales outside the region were possible up to October, because prices in the Mediterranean and the United States were higher.But with peak summer demand tailing off, there are already
3480 concerns about oversupply in the United States and gasoline prices fell sharply in New York on Thursday.The October contract on the New York Merchantile Exchange settled 1.74 cents lower at 61.32 cents a gallon after falling as low as 60.40 cents during the day.Singapore prices have firmed because of the
3480 sales outside the region, with the price of a barrel of gasoline rising by around $2.00 since mid-August to more than $23.00 on Thursday.They could go still higher, closing the gap with prices in Europe and the United States, making Dalian's exports a depressing market factor, the traders said.</

3498 A flood of domestic A share listings is pulling down the overall quality of China's stock markets and undermining their development, analysts said on Friday.A total of 121 new A share companies have listed on the exchanges in Shanghai and in Shenzhen since the start of 1996, raising the total
3498 of listed companies by about 40 percent.But the companies listed this year are on average much smaller than those listed previously, which analysts said tended to make the market much more speculative.The 68 new firms on the Shanghai stock exchange have on average only 27.1 million listed shares, against an
3498 average of 52 million shares for listed firms as of the end of 1995.In Shenzhen, the 53 firms listed this year have on average 24.5 million listed shares against 66.2 million for listed firms at the end of 1995."Listing of a large number of small companies has damaged the healthy
3498 development of the markets," said one stock analyst with China Financial Trust and Investment Co. "This has also increased speculation in the market.""Small firms are making the overall quality of companies on the two markets deteriorate," said another analyst with Shenyin &amp; Wanguo Securities. "One of the major reasons is
3498 the existence of the share issue quota system."Domestic share issues in China are decided by quotas that are distributed to provinces, major cities and industrial bureaux, with companies fighting ferociously to get the precious right to issue shares, stock analysts said.In distributing the quota, some local governments or the bureaux
3498 divide it up between several companies to please them all rather than give all the shares to one big, high-quality firm and annoy the others, they said.In the early years after China revived the stock markets in 1990, most listed companies were small, making the market extremely speculative and subject
3498 to wide fluctuations.In 1993 and 1994, Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges selected major Chinese companies for listing, such as Shanghai Petrochemical Co and Maanshan Iron and Steel Co, to help improve the company composition."The latest batch of small firms has made company composition on the two markets deteriorate," said a
3498 broker with China Guotai Securities. "Cases of irregularities have also arisen, with firms competing for a slice of the quota system."</

3536 Traffic Safety Administration 30 years ago and the publication of Nader's 1965 book, "Unsafe at Any Speed," which helped raise public awareness about safety issues.Since then, the government has been involved in setting standards on everything from seat belts to speed limits. 3536 requiring automobile makers to notify car owners if their cars were found to harbour safety-related defects.A spokesman for the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said officials there were not in a position to comment on the Nader report because they had not yet seen it."We haven't had a chance to
3536 see the report so we wouldn't be able to say anything about it," the spokesman said.Nader credited the Clinton administration with extending passenger car standards to vans and light trucks and improving child restraint safety rules, among other changes.But the report criticised as too modest standards intended to reduce head
3536 injuries. 3536 1980."Nader predicted that motor vehicle fatalities inevitably would accelerate with the revocation of the 55 mile per hour national maximum speed limit.He also faulted the media for deserting automobile traffic safety issues, dwelling instead on recent airline crashes."Yet the same number of people killed in one of those crashes are
3536 killed on the highway almost every day and barely a peep is heard," Nader said.According to NHTSA data, the number of automobile-related fatalities stood at about 16 per 100,000 people in 1995. 3545 New York City might be well known for its towers of glass and steel, but trees outnumber skyscrapers more than 500 to one, officials announced Friday.The city's first-ever tree census ended with a flourish and a drumroll as Parks Commissioner Henry Stern counted the last of the 500,000 trees that
3545 line New York's 30,400 blocks.The census data will help save ailing trees and determine where to plant more, he said. "If we know where they are, we can take better care of them," he said.The six-month census found the city's most common trees are the hardy London plane and the
3545 Norway maple.Growing in a forest, they would fill 2,860 acres (1,150 hectares). Planted in a row 20 feet (seven metres) apart, they would stretch 1,893 miles (3,046 km).The city's 500,000 trees compare with its roughly 900 buildings taller than 100 feet (30 metres), said the Real Estate Board.The census cost
3545 $75,000 in tax dollars, officials said. Another $15,000 came in private donations, and volunteers contributed 14,000 hours of labour.Some might argue the city could have saved time and effort. The 500,000 matches an earlier estimate drawn from aerial photographs, the Parks Department said.Or they could have guessed. Asked at random
3545 to estimate the number of trees in the city, a man walking his dog in the borough of Queens said, "If I had to guess, I'd say 500,000."A precise number of trees will be calculated in a few weeks from the census data, the Parks Department said.</

3547 to committee efforts to depose the Air Force officers who dismissed negligent homicide charges against the two F-15 fighter pilots.A family member said the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations was looking into allegations by relatives of some of the 26 Americans and foreign officers killed in the accident that a
3547 coverup allowed the two F-15 fighter pilots to escape prosecution.A Senate source confirmed the investigation but would not say if evidence of a coverup has been found."What I am concerned about is that you have general officers who are covering this thing up," retired Air Force Col. 3547 in an interview. "When you cover something like this up then somebody else is going to die for the same stupid reason."His daughter, Air Force 2nd Lt. Laura Ashley Piper, was among the 26 people killed when the two U.S. F-15 fighter planes mistakenly identified two U.S. Black Hawk helicopters
3547 as Iraqi Hinds in the "no-fly" zone in northern Iraq and shot them down with missiles.The Air Force said it stands by its investigation which led to dismissal of negligent homicide charges against the two F-15 pilots. Higher commands reviewed and approved the action.Senate investigators hit the legal snag when
3547 they tried to depose and take sworn statements from the Air Force judicial officers who dismissed the charges against the pilots.Deputy Secretary of Defence John White told the subcommittee in a letter Sept. 3 that Congress "has no judicial function or review authority" in the case.White said Congress's deposition of
3547 such officers "poses a grave risk to the integrity of the military justice system" because judicial officers in the future would have to worry about "possible congressional criticism and public censure."The Senate subcommittee's chairman, Sen. William Roth, a Delaware Republican, must now decide whether to subpoena the Air Force officers
3547 or drop his effort to get their testimony.They include Maj. Gen. Eugene Santarelli, the 17th Air Force commander who dismissed the charges, and Col. Edward Starr, the Article 32 investigating officer who recommended the charges be dismissed. An Article 32 investigation is similar to a civilian grand jury hearing.The Air
3547 Force said in a statement in December 1994 that a charge of negligent homicide was dismissed against the lead pilot, Capt. Eric Wickson, because "evidence revealed Wickson made a reasonable mistake, under the circumstances, in misidentifying the Black Hawks as Iraqi helicopters."It said the second pilot, Lt. Col. Randy May,
3547 had been charged with negligent homicide because initial evidence indicated he gave only a vague answer when Wickson asked if he also recognised the helicopters to be Iraqi Hinds.But it said that charge was dismissed against May because "evidence convinced the investigating officer and Santarelli that May, as wingman, followed
3547 proper procedures in yielding control of the action to his lead pilot."Piper said he believed there was a coverup, including immunity from prosecution for Wickson, so that all blame could be put on him and then neither pilot would be prosecuted.But the Air Force said Wickson was given immunity only
3547 from being prosecuted on the basis of his own testimony. It said he could have been prosecuted with any other evidence.</

3568 be reached in the Security Council on a new secretary-general."What we want to do now is to have countries begin to look seriously at alternative candidates, and ... in October to have the Security Council set up a timetable and a process both for receiving nominations, considering them and eventually
3568 voting," Lyman said.As a veto-holding permanent member of the Security Council, the United States has the power to prevent Boutros-Ghali being re-elected.But its opposition to him has received little support so far from other countries, some of which believe Clinton has sacrificed him to his own re-election campaign against Republican
3568 challenger Bob Dole.Many Republicans, and some Democrats, look askance at the United Nations in general, and Boutros-Ghali in particular, seeing the world body as a free-spending bureaucracy dominated by Third World countries hostile to the United States.While some reforms have begun, Lyman said that for them to "really be carried

3568 Friday with Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia and would raise it with other foreign ministers in New York next week."I think most countries understand that we are serious about our position and will not change it," he said.Lyman said that over the coming year the United States would continue
3568 to push for a reduction of its U.N. dues, including agreement to a 25 per cent cap imposed by Congress on the U.S. contribution to the peacekeeping budget.At present the United States pays just over 30 per cent of U.N. peacekeeping costs. It pays 25 per cent of the U.N.

3580 Paul Maco, director of SEC's office of municipal securities, on Friday urged municipalities that do structured financings to make sure they are not creating new securities that must be registered with the commission."There may be more than one security in ... structured financings," Maco told bond lawyers meeting here for
3580 the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop."(That) means you have to find an exemption for each one" under the federal securities laws, Maco said."You start throwing different types of contractual arrangements for exempt securities together, you might end up with a package that is slightly different from the pieces
3580 you put in," Maco said."And you may have merged with something that no longer has an exemption" under the securities laws, Maco said.Maco added that when municialities start "pulling" securities together, they may end up with "something called an investment company."That may be the case "even though you don't have
3580 a board of directors floating around or a fund manager," he said."The definition of an investment company is very liberal," Maco said."We've been seeing" some confusion in this area, Maco said. "We hope you keep this in mind when you find yourself with a client. Remember, there's more to the
3580 securities laws than just disclosure (issues)."--Vicky Stamas, 202-898-8314</

3597 Space marathon woman Shannon Lucid worked out on Friday to prepare for her long-awaited return to Earth and the crushing pull of gravity.Lucid jogged on a treadmill in Mir's bus-sized core module as the Russian space station Mir and shuttle Atlantis circled, linked together, 245 miles (394 km) above the
3597 Earth. She was to exercise for two hours a day for the remainder of her flight to counteract the wasting effect of weightlessness, NASA's chief flight director Lee Briscoe said.The 53-year-old biochemist is nearing the end of a six-month tour on Mir, the longest space flight by a woman and
3597 a record for an American. She told ABC TV's "Good Morning America" on Thursday that she was anxious to see her husband, two daughters and son."I'm looking forward to having my family around. We're going to sit, we're going to talk," she said.Her stay on Mir was extended by nearly
3597 seven weeks because of shuttle booster problems, threatening hurricanes and scheduling difficulties. Her place on Mir was taken on Thursday by John Blaha, a 54-year-old former Vietnam fighter pilot, who joined the Mir crew of cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Kaleri for a four-month stay.Blaha asked mission control to tell
3597 his wife that he felt right at home after just one night aboard the station."Pass along to Brenda for me that life on the Mir is fantastic," he radioed controllers in Houston. "I've had a lot of fun in the last day, meeting my crewmates, talking to them and eating
3597 with them," he told ABC later. "I'm looking forward to the stay."Blaha is the second of six U.S. astronauts who will staff the orbiting outpost into 1998. NASA began joint manned missions with Russia in 1994 to prepare for an international space station that the two nations plan to start
3597 constructing in late 1997."This is a fantastic programme that we are doing with the Russians," Blaha said. "It's a good start to an international space station and for space exploration in the future."Briscoe said the joint U.S.-Russian crew had accomplished about half of their 6,000-pound (2,700 kg) cargo transfer. Atlantis
3597 carried food, water and equipment for the station and will bring the results of scientific experiments and obsolete equipment back to Earth.Atlantis is due to leave Mir on Monday and return to Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Thursday, ending a 188-day mission for Lucid.</

3609 World surgar production in 1996-97 should be 121.4 million tonnes and world sugar consumption -- not adjusted for unrecorded trade -- should be 119.5 million, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.An apparent surplus of 1.9 million tonnes disappears after adjustments for unrecorded trade, USDA said in a Situation and Outlook
3609 summary.The world production forecast is up 1.2 million tonnes from the earlier forecast published in the June summary, and 1.5 million tonnes below the revised estimate for the global 1995-95 crop, USDA said. Global sugar consumption for 1996-97 -- not adjusted for unrecorded trade -- was forecasted up 2.8 million
3609 tonnes from the revised estimates for the previous year, USDA said.World sugar trade in 1996-97 was forecast at 34.9 million tonnes, or about 29 percent of forecasted production.U.S. imports should be 2.74 million tonnes, USDA said, making the United States the second top importer and at the highest level since
3609 1983-84.Sugar imports are expected to remain strong in the Russian Federation at 3.2 million tonnes, while China's import were seen sliding to 2.4 million tonnes from an estimated 2.5 million the previous year.Ending stocks for 1996-97 should be 23.4 million tonnes, slightly below last year. The forecasted stocks-to-use ratio at
3609 19.1 percent would be down 20.3 percent from last year.Sugar use continues to expand in Latin America, and Asia should use 42 million tonnes, up 23 percent since 1990-91.Among the world's leading exporters, better crop prospects in Australia, Brazil, Cuba, South Africa and Thailand should allow those countries to increase
3609 exports.India also likely will be a major exporter, but exports from Ukraine will drop to 1 million tonnes, USDA said.The summary said raw sugar prices have been trading below the spot price and are likely to remain weak into the fall.</

3614 Recurring rumours that Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein is a big oil futures player are not backed up by the facts, according to U.S. intelligence and regulatory officials.The theory, which has surfaced over the years when Iraq has been at the centre of Middle East turmoil, is that Hussein and his
3614 Baghdad cronies play oil futures markets, particularly the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), via Swiss accounts controlled by third parties."We have looked into the rumour and found that there is no evidence to substantiate it," said a U.S. official familiar with government intelligence on Iraq.The view from intelligence sources is
3614 backed up by futures market regulators and experienced brokers on the exchange.Though there has long been lighthearted talk among oil traders and diplomats of how the inner circle in Baghdad could benefit financially from its political and military actions, that speculation has taken on a more serious tone in recent
3614 months as oil price volatility has run at its highest level since the end of the Gulf War.In August, in the wake of protacted negotiations between Baghdad and the United Nations over a limited lifting of oil sanctions, The New York Times' ran a "Foreign Affairs" column couched as an
3614 idea for a novel, which mused at length about how Saddam Hussein could use foreknowledge of his diplomatic positions to benefit from their effect on oil prices.Last week, following the oil market turmoil caused by Baghdad's incursion into protected Kurdish zones and the U.S. military response, the respected Journal of
3614 Commerce quoted an unnamed United Nations official as saying that Baghdad "is believed to be playing the futures market for some easy money.""They can play the oil futures market and make money out of nothing," the U.N. official told the newspaper.But regulatory investigation of futures market activity both before and
3614 after major market-moving events in Iraq turned up nothing suspicious, according to officials."I can assure you that when surveillance saw (the big Iraq-related price moves) they looked into it," said John Phillips, spokesman for the Commodities Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in Washington, the regulator for U.S. futures exchanges, including the
3614 NYMEX.He explains that all NYMEX trades must be carried out by members of the exchange and they must report to the CFTC details of any futures position of 300 contracts or more in any one month, covering 300,000 barrels or about $7 million worth of oil at current prices. The
3614 CFTC's Surveillance committee meets weekly and examines closely any unusual activity.The market and the firms trading it in the weeks before and following the latest crisis were examined closely and no suspicious trading was found, sources confirmed. Similar procedures were followed when markets were roiled, they added.To conceal trades large
3614 enough to make it worthwhile to Baghdad "would be damn near impossible," said Phillips of the CFTC. "There has never been an entity which has come up that you are not aware of who they are."To make, say, $1 million from the threshold reportable position would require a move of
3614 more than $3 a barrel in Friday's oil price, a huge move.And Baghdad would have to get the direction right. When it signed its deal to partially lift U.N. sanctions on May 20, an event which would be expected to result in lower oil prices, oil futures ended the day
3614 nearly $2 a barrel higher."You are constantly hearing about conspiracy theories, whether it is Saddam Hussein having a trading account or whatever," said Tom Blakeslee, a trader at Minneapolis-based Cargill Investor Services Inc., one of the largest international commodities firms."For it to make any difference to him, he would have
3614 to trade in such huge size that we would know. Frankly, I don't believe it. I don't think he is moving troops around and betting futures on it," said Blakeslee. "I think he's got bigger goals."</

3626 This year's U.S. corn harvest may not offer immediate relief to end-users pinched by tight stocks as farmers opt to store new crop grain in hopes of higher prices, analysts and merchandisers said."We can have a nine-billion-bushel crop but it's not going to get into the channels," said Joe Miller,
3626 market analyst at the Indiana Farm Bureau."I have not talked to a farmer yet who said he would sell his corn for $3.00," he added. "If this stuff goes into the (storage) bin you're going to have to pay to get it out." On average, farmers sell seven to eight
3626 percent of new crop corn in September and 10 to 17 percent in October, said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities, an Iowa-based grain marketing and merchandising firm. "This year we're probably one-third behind (normal levels) nationally," he said.With current futures prices at the Chicago Board of Trade down more
3626 than $2.00 from July's record high of $5.54-1/2 per bushel, farmers had little incentive to sell, Miller noted.Corn for delivery against CBOT December futures closed up 3/4 cent at $3.14-1/4 a bushel Friday. Some producers were concerned about crop conditions after below-normal summer temperatures and the threat of an early
3626 frost put late-planted plants in jeopardy.And with abundant, inexpensive grain storage space available and enough money in the bank to last a few months, farmers were unlikely to sell as much new crop corn as they would in a typical year, said Dave Armstrong, analyst with The Chicago Corporation."Farmers are
3626 in pretty good financial shape, they can stand to wait," he said. This year's tight stocks forced end-users to buy virtually every kernel of old crop corn, leaving elevator storage bins empty. In addition, U.S. agriculture policy brought an end to government grain storage which freed up even more room.A
3626 Nebraska merchandiser said his elevator's bins were empty for the first time in 16 years. An Illinois dealer said he had never seen empty bins before this year."We're probably 8 million bushels behind normal," the Illinios dealer said, referring to typical grain purchases for this time of year. In anticipation
3626 of tight new crop supplies, some end-users have turned to the futures markets in hopes of securing the grain at a lower price, Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) data indicate.As of Sept. 10, the CFTC Commitment of Traders report showed commercials held long positions in corn of 776 million bushels
3626 and were short 636 million bushels."The commercial typically this time of year is short," Roose said. "The commercial is long (this year) because he is still covering his end-usage until new crop comes in."But below normal summer temperatures have slowed crop development and delayed harvest, meaning commercials will have to
3626 wait longer than normal for new crop supplies.--Chicago Newsdesk 312-408-8749</

3636 Federal health officials on Friday proposed guidelines for transplanting animal tissue and organs into humans, one of the most complex cutting edge issues in modern medicine."Xenotranplants" hold out hope for patients who are getting sicker or dying as they wait for suitable human donor organs. But scientists fear introducing animal
3636 viruses into humans with potentially disastrous effects.That risk may be even higher with transplant patients whose immune systems are suppressed and who therefore are less able to mount a response to foreign microbes.Yet the benefits could be huge. Some 48,000 people are on waiting lists at any given time in
3636 the United States alone. The 5,000 people who donate organs each year after death do not meet the demand.Organ transplant is only one aspect. Scientists are also studying whether certain animal cells could cure diseases like diabetes or even control a cancer patient's pain."We want to protect the public and
3636 patients from potential risks while not impeding research into these promising new treatments," Food and Drug Commissioner David Kessler said as the draft guidelines were printed in the Federal Register for 90 days of public comment.Cross-species transplants, whether cells or whole organs, are reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration.
3636 The new recommendations include animal safety screenings to minimise the risk of transferring diseases, a fear that has been underscored by the AIDS epidemic.HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, is widely believed to have originated in monkeys and somehow made its way into the human population, although not through a
3636 transplant.The guidelines would require doctors to take blood cell and tissue samples from the animal and the human recipient for future public health study if needed. A national data base or registry would be established for public health research purposes and there would be requirements about monitoring the patients and
3636 careful selection of the doctors and researchers.There have already been a few cross-species transplants. A baby received a baboon heart in California several years ago but died. Last year an AIDS patient received a baboon bone marrow transplant. The transplanted cells apparently did not take, but the patient is alive
3636 and doing well.Other scientists and biotechnology companies are exploring whether they can genetically modify animal organs such as pig livers for human transplants, either as a replacement for a failing human organ or to keep a patient alive long enough to wait for a human replacement.Researchers are also testing whether
3636 they can treat Parkinson's Disease with foetal pig nerve cells, whether foetal calf adrenal cells implanted into the spine can help control end-stage cancer pain, and whether pancreatic islets from pigs could help treat insulin-dependent diabetes.The guidelines were drawn up jointly by the FDA, the National Institutes of Health and
3636 the Centres for Disease Control in consultation with leading scientists. The topic of xenotranplantation has also been vigorously analysed and debated at research centres and in the top medical journals."This guideline represents the consensus of physicians and scientists regarding the best way to move ahead in the field of xenotransplantation,"
3636 Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala said.Once the regulations are finalised, they can be updated as scientific knowledge advances.</

3644 International Business Machines Corp. will extend health benefits to the domestic partners of gay and lesbian employees, making it the largest U.S. company to date to adopt such a policy.A spokeswoman for the world's largest computer maker said Friday the company would extend health coverage to same-sex domestic partners during
3644 its annual enrollment period between Oct. 1 and Oct. 31.The benefits cover health, dental and vision plans offered by the company and would take effect July 1, 1997, IBM spokeswoman Melinda McMullen said.She said the policy change brings the Armonk, N.Y.-based company into line with its own written policy of
3644 non-discrimination that has included sexual orientation since 1974.The spokeswoman also said the move was designed to keep IBM competitive with other high-tech firms with such policies, including Microsoft Corp., Apple Computer Inc. and Hewlett-Packard Co."The competition to attract and retain a high-quality workforce is fierce in the high technology business,"
3644 the spokeswoman said. "So it made sense from a competitive business standpoint as well."A legal group that represents gays and lesbians welcomed the IBM move."Big Blue is in good company with nearly 500 employers that offer similar benefits," Lambda Legal Defense and Education Fund spokeswoman Peg Byron said. "Popular culture
3644 and many in the private sector recognize that lesbians and gays should have equal treatment and Congress will catch on soon."The IBM policy does not cover unmarried heterosexual couples who live together because they have the option of marriage."What we require of all our employees is proof of commitment. The
3644 acknowledged proof of committment among heterosexuals is marriage," the IBM spokeswoman said.Last week the U.S. Senate, by a wide margin, passed a bill that would deny recognition of same-sex marriages. On the same day however, it narrowly defeated a bill prohibiting employment discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation.In the
3644 absence of laws allowing gays and lesbians to marry, IBM said it would require employees with same-sex domestic partners to present a notorized affidavit that they are involved in a committed relationship, living in the same household, and that their finances are interdependent.McMullen noted that such documents were unlikely to
3644 be entered into lightly, since they have been used as evidence in some so-called palimony cases recently. She said very few employees were expected to benefit from the policy change.IBM also extended its health benefit plans to cover employees who care for a dependent child, even if the employee is
3644 not a biological or adopted parent of the child.For example, an aunt would be covered if she had taken into her house a niece or nephew. Young people up to 23 years old who are financially dependent on an IBM employee would qualify.</

3666 The near-term credit outlook for computer hardware manufacturers calls for overcast skies as companies adjust to escalating competition and a shift to more open systems technology, corporate debt analysts said.The longer-term scenario, however, is bright as demand for new technology is expected to remain at lofty levels.The apparent paradox, corporate
3666 pundits said, is almost a trademark of the industry. Experts said the nature of the high-technology market itself, characterized by stiff price competition, short product life cycles and high investment requirements, makes firms more susceptible to earnings and cash flow volatility.And nothing shakes corporate debt investors more than uncertainty about
3666 future revenues."The first question is: Why am I going to lend money to a company ... mainly if I don't know if that company is going to survive?," said Martin Fridson, high-yield market analyst at Merrill Lynch and Co Inc. Analysts also said that, among other things, the recent growth
3666 of the Internet worldwide computer network has forced the industry to quickly move from proprietary to lower margin, more commodity-oriented open systems technology.Analysts said such phenomena affect the high-technology sector in general, but hardware makers in particular."The same forces apply to hardware and software. But they're accentuated in hardware because
3666 the technology cycle is faster," said Molly Toll-Reed, director and high-tech analyst at credit rating agency Standard and Poor's. "The need to roll out new products is accentuated in hardware ... You can't stop developing products in software either, but you don't have to be rolling out a new product
3666 line every nine months, like you do at hardware," she added.Analysts said Apple Computer Inc, the Macintosh computer manufacturer, has become a clear-cut example of how abrupt shifts in the marketplace can deteriorate a firm's credit outlook and erode investor confidence."Apple had a proprietary system and the industry moved away
3666 from proprietary hardware platforms ... Apple didn't move on a timely basis," Toll-Reed said. "They moved over the last year or so to try to license their system and open it up to broader usage ... but it's coming too late. Failure to adapt to industry changes kills anybody, including
3666 Apple," she added.Apple entered the long-term corporate debt market in February 1994, when S&amp;P granted the firm an A-minus rating.Since then, the company was downgraded to BBB in August 1994, to BB-minus in January 1996 and to its current junk bond rating of B-plus with a negative outlook, following several
3666 quarters of losses. "It just shows that if you're behind the curve in the technology wave, you can quickly get swamped," said Kingman Penniman, high-yield investment analyst at KDP Investment Advisors Inc.Apple is not alone. Unisys Corp also shares the same B-plus rating from S&amp;P with a negative outlook.Analysts said
3666 the higher business risk profile of the technology sector forces companies to keep very conservative balance sheet structures and sizable cash balances. Thus, they added, the ability to quickly shift direction and adopt new standards is seen as key for the companies to keep their heads above water."Past success does
3666 not guarantee future success in an industry in which annual growth rates sometimes exceed 50 percent," Toll-Reed said.Besides, analysts at S&amp;P estimate that after worldwide growth of 25 percent in 1995, global PC industry growth is expected to moderate to the high teens this year.The U.S., which accounts for 40
3666 percent of the worldwide market, led the slowdown in the first half of 1996. However, the 14 and 12 percent growth rates experienced in the domestic PC industry in the first and second quarters, respectively, are very healthy by most standands, keeping most analysts bullish over the long term.Due to
3666 the sector's volatility, most high tech hardware manufacturers that decided to issue debt ended up doing so in the speculative, high-yield market.A close look at S&amp;P's credit ratings chart shows that eight of the 11 covered companies have been granted a "stable" outlook, including giants like International Business Machines and
3666 Hewlett-Packard Corp. Two firms have negative outlooks, while only one has captured S&amp;P's heart and received a positive outlook rating -- Dell Computer Corp, a consumer-direct PC vendor."Sucessful companies will continue to evaluate -- and change, if needed -- their cultures, cost structures, product lines, response time and marketing focus
3666 to effectively implement their business strategies," Toll-Reed said. 3692 European finance ministers were due to start talks in Dublin on Friday determined to push forward plans for a single currency despite doubts over the ability of the Franco-German alliance to meet conditions for monetary union.The meeting, coming amid an intense scramble by EU governments to bring their 1997 budget
3692 deficits in line with the Maastricht treaty, will focus on three important technical areas of economic and monetary union (EMU), the plan to have a common currency among qualifying European Union countries.The Dublin agenda focuses on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline among EMU participants, a new exchange rate
3692 mechanism (ERM) linking the single currency to non-members, and the legal underpinnings of monetary union.The talks in Dublin Castle, which start in earnest on Saturday, are seen as essential for keeping the considerable political momentum behind EMU on course, powered largely by Germany and France.But recent criticism by some German
3692 economic officials of France's questionable accounting tactics in its 1997 budget plans threatened to overshadow what many hope will be a successful weekend.At issue is the French government's use of a one-off payment of 37.5 billion francs ($7.30 billion) from France Telecom, the state telecommunications company, to cut the state
3692 deficit and bring it in line with the Maastricht treaty's requirement.Norbert Wieczorek, chairman of the German Parliament's European Affairs Committee, said on Thursday he feared parts of the French budget were against the spirit of the treaty.Other German officials have also voiced criticism over the use of such funds in
3692 France's budget.However, EU monetary affairs commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday that France's proposal appeared to be in line with accepted EU accounting rules."It seems to me that this operation is in line with the principles of national accounting...which are defined, known and agreed by all member states," de
3692 Silguy told a news conference.Among the three topics on the agenda, the Stability Pact has been cast as the centerpiece of the meeting, with recent progress on the issue by the EU's monetary committee setting the stage for a comprehensive deal later this year.The committee, a secretive group of national
3692 treasury and central bank officials, reached a compromise last week that would punish EMU members which run deficits above three percent of gross domestic product.Several details remain unresolved -- the size of fines, when they would take effect, and a better definition of the economic circumstances under which a country's
3692 poor finances would be overlooked. But the Dublin meeting is expected to give its blessing to what has been accomplished so far.German finance minister Theo Waigel's initial proposal for a Stability Pact was considered by many as too severe and out of step with what was politically feasible.Yet his desire
3692 to put more bite into the current sanctions process focused attention on a dominant worry -- for a single currency to ultimately work, national budget policies must be kept under control in a credible way.Regarding a new ERM, ministers and bankers are likely to nod through the vision emerging from
3692 the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to a European Central Bank (ECB).Alexandre Lamfalussy, the EMI's head, will outline a system which is voluntary, establishes the single currency as an anchor and gives the ECB an influential voice in realigning the value of currencies under pressure.But specifics, such as the width
3692 of the trading bands for non-EMU currencies, or the limits on how much the ECB would spend to support them should they come under speculative attack, are to likely to be kept vague.Lastly, there is the tricky issue of implementing a legal framework for EMU in advance of its expected
3692 1999 start date.While considerable progress has been made in clarifying the legal aspects of a single currency, such as the contractual rights investors will have after it is launched, the Maastricht Treaty only allows such a framework to come into force in 1999.For many in the financial markets this is
3692 much too late. The task for the ministers and central bankers is to find a way around this hurdle. ($1=5.139 French Franc)</

3746 The Vespa, the much-loved motor scooter that did for transport in post-war Italy what the Model-T Ford car did for the United States, celebrated its 50th birthday in style on Friday with a hip new look.Piaggio, the family-owned firm that has been turning out Vespas since 1946, launched two new
3746 models of the cult classic complete with new environmental features for the 21st century."The Vespa was the Italian product that introduced Italy to the world," said chairman Giovanni Alberto Agnelli."The challenge we face is to reinterpret not just the legend but also the function of the Vespa in today's post-industrial
3746 society," he told an anniversary news conference attended by more than 500 journalists from around the world.Traditionalists need not fear. The Vespa has not lost an ounce of the "dolce vita" appeal glamorised by Audrey Hepburn and Gregory Peck in the 1952 movie "Roman Holiday".If anything, the retro-style has been
3746 given a boost with sleeker styling and a new range of colours -- including pastel tones and the olive green of the original Vespas.Contours on the new 50cc Vespa ET2 and 125cc Vespa ET4 are rounder, the saddle is bigger and more comfortable and some original features, including slanted letters
3746 spelling out Vespa -- "wasp" in Italian -- on the front, have been reintroduced.The structure is still made of steel, not plastic.But the 50cc model boasts the world's first fuel-injection two-stroke engine, making it the only scooter to meet European Union rules on exhaust and noise emissions for the year
3746 2000.The 125cc version has a new "clean" four-stroke engine. Both models purr rather than buzz and are automatic, ridding the rider of the hassle of kick-starting or changing gears.The new-generation Vespas run on lead-free petrol, rather than a mixture of petrol and oil, meaning the company can now target North
3746 American markets where its old scooters failed to meet rules on emissions.Piaggio, which leads the European scooter sector and is fourth worldwide behind Japanese giants Honda, Suzuki and Yamaha, says it cost 35 billion lire ($21 million) and took three years to develop the new Vespas in an ever tougher
3746 market."We're behind some of our objectives because the market has contracted a bit but turnover is higher than last year," said spokesman Enea Nepentini. The company is related to Italy's carmaker Fiat, controlled by the Agnelli family.The original Vespa was the brainchild of Enrico Piaggio, the son of an entrepreneur
3746 whose aviation factory was bombed out of business at the end of World War Two."I want a vehicle that puts Italy on two wheels, but I don't want the usual motorbike," said Piaggio, who saw the scooter -- which had been around since the 1920s without success -- as a
3746 potentially mass-market product to get the factory going again.The first Vespa, designed by engineer Corradino D'Ascanio who invented the world's first fully-functional helicopter, was launched in April 1946. Its shape earned it the famous name."It looks just like a wasp!" history records Piaggio as exclaiming when he saw the buzzing
3746 contraption with its "head", narrow waist and flared back tapering to a point.The Vespa soon became an affordable, sturdy means of transport for whole families, giving young people their first taste of independent travel. Enthusiasts caught the bug. One, Giorgio Bettinelli, has been right around the world on a Vespa
3746 and there are clubs in 23 countries from Japan to Finland.The new-look Vespas broadly got the thumbs-up from motoring journalists and aficionados attending the launch.Even Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who is better known for riding a bicyle, said he was a fan. 3751 Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, outlining Moscow's vision of post-Cold War European security, said on Friday stationing NATO's military might closer to Russia's borders was "absolutely unacceptable".In an address to the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), Primakov said Moscow had no right of veto if former
3751 Soviet bloc members wanted to join the Western military alliance."However, Russia finds it absolutely unacceptable that NATO's military infrastructure should come closer to its territory," he said in a closed-door speech to the OSCE's permanent council.A translation of his address was later made available to reporters.Primakov, who was due to
3751 meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana later on Friday, was repeating Moscow's position stated in June when he suggested a limited expansion of NATO to the east may be acceptable if no troops or weapons were stationed on the territory of the new members.Ex-Warsaw Pact states the Czech Republic, Hungary and
3751 Poland are front-runners to join NATO, probably next year.Post-Cold War collective security could collapse if new lines of division emerged in Europe, Primakov said."Unfortunately, a trend toward this eventuality does exist. In our opinion, the intention to expand NATO to the east will reinforce it," he added.Primakov said political leaders
3751 were beginning to understand the emergence of three problems - the transformation of NATO, special relations between Russia and the 16-member Atlantic alliance and its expansion."We are for the consistent consideration of these inter-related problems," he said.He made no reference in his speech to proposals put forward by U.S. Secretary
3751 of State Warren Christopher earlier this month to draw up a new charter defining NATO's ties with Russia or an enhanced Partnership for Peace programme to include countries not accepted into the alliance in the first wave of new entrants.Outlining his own vision of a future pan-European security structure, Primakov
3751 said the 53-member OSCE, whose members include most of Europe, the United States and Canada, was uniquely positioned to be strengthened into the continent's main security body."The model should envisage counteraction against an entire range of threats, both military and terrorist, as well as challenges in the economic, ecological, humanitarian
3751 and other fields," Primakov told OSCE ambassadors.He said the new security model should be discussed at the OSCE summit in Lisbon in December and called for a treaty to set up the new body to be ready at the next summit in 1998.Primakov went on to suggest that all organisations
3751 involved in security policy should have an input in a restructured OSCE -- the United Nations, NATO, the Council of Europe, the European Union, the Western European Union (the EU's defence arm) as well as the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)."The OSCE is the only really universal organisation of European
3751 states. In addition, it embodies the deep linkage of interests between the European and North American states."</

3774 federal government put an end to the ongoing political drama in Gujarat by dismissing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ministry. The decision came in the wake of reports of violence and bedlam in the state Assembly as the BJP government rushed through the confidence vote on Wednesday. The prime minister,
3774 following a report by the state governor, called a cabinet meeting which decided to impose president's rule in the state and keep the assembly in suspended animation. A presidential proclamation was later issued after the prime minister met the president to apprise him of the cabinet's decision.----The Economic TimesCABINET NOD
3774 FOR $500 MLN STATE BANK GDR ISSUEThe Cabinet Committe on Foreign Investment (CCFI) cleared the proposed $500-million global depository receipt issue of the State Bank. Together with that, CCFI also cleared the proposals of Hughes Ispat, Reliance Telecom and Jindal Power. However, CCFI turned down a proposal from a securities
3774 firm. The committee has decided against allowing foreign investment in the service sector. The Hughes Ispat proposal entailed hiking the foreign equity in the company, currently at 40 percent (eight billion rupees) to 49 percent. The Reliance Telecom proposal is for an increase in the paid-up capital and foreign equity
3774 to 9.13 billion rupees and 4.11 billion rupees.----MARUTI'S 15 BLN RUPEE EXPANSION GETS NOD AS SUZUKI YIELDSThe government scored a point against Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp as the Maruti Udyog Ltd board okayed a 15 billion rupee expansion programme without dilution of equity. The board has approved the contentious programme
3774 for expansion of production capacity by 100,000 units a year. While Suzuki was keen on tapping the equity route, the government was adamant that the expansion programme should be financed through debt.----MODILUFT CONSIDERS RAISING $100 MLN EXTERNAL BORROWINGCash strapped ModiLuft is planning a $100 million external commercial borrowing (ECB) as
3774 a way out of its financial problems. The $100 million ECB is about to go through with a European group of banks. Sources say the Delhi-based airline is in talks with a London-based consortium of banks to finalise the borrowings. The proceeds from the ECB will be used to finance
3774 the airlines plans to acquire aircraft and fulfil some of its working capital needs.----ITOCHU PLANNING TO RAISE STAKE IN PATSPIN TO 18 PCTThe $175 billion Itochu Corp of Japan is planning to raise its stake in Patspin India Ltd from 12 to 19 percent. Patspin is a 1.5 billion rupee
3774 GTN Textile group company. The Japanese giant has received approval from the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to hike its stake, sources said. However, the Indian company has no plans to issue shares or other instruments on a preferential basis to enable Itochu increase its stake.----Financial ExpressMINISTRY FOR CHANGES IN TAKEOVER
3774 CODEThe Finance Ministry has proposed changes in the draft takeover code prepared by the bourse regulator. The ministry is not in favour of its recommendation seeking to exempt the requirement of a public offer for acquisitions made through rights issues. The ministry fears that promoters and raiders may use this
3774 route to acquire stakes in companies at the cost of small shareholders. The ministry is also opposed to allowing shareholders holding above 10 percent stake to acquire a differential percentage of shares from the market without attracting the mandatory public offer requirement.---- DONORS PLEDGE $7 BLN TO INDIAMultinational and bilateral

3780 accused of involvement in a 1981 airline hijacking.His sister shunned his militancy and, when democracy returned after Zia's death in a plane crash, led the PPP to victory in a 1988 election.
