3786 India should implement a phased decontrolling of its oil sector by the year 2002, a government-appointed panel said on Friday.Reforms of the hydrocarbon sector should be launched in three phases, with total deregulation of upstream and downstream sectors by the year 2000-2002, the Strategic Planning Group said in its report.It
3786 said the government should announce its decision to deregulate the sector within the specified timeframe and appoint a panel to suggest ways to restructure prices.The group, headed by the highest-ranking civil servant in the ministry of petroleum and natural gas, submitted its report to Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda
3786 on Thursday.A summary of the report was obtained by Reuters on Friday. The group, set up last year, included experts from the public and private sectors.As part of economic reforms launched in 1991, the government has opened domestic oilfields for exploration by private and foreign participation. It has allowed free
3786 import and marketing of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), kerosene and lubricants and cut import duty on oil products.The group said the first phase should begin between 1996 and 1998 and cover rationalisation of the tariff structure, deregulation of natural gas pricing and of of furnace oil and bitumen, and partial
3786 decontrol of the marketing.It suggested removal of subsidies on high speed diesel and cut in subsidies on kerosene, LPG and input for fertilisers.Reforms between 1998 and 2000 should include pricing of indigenous crude on the basis of the fob price of comparable imported crudes, rationalisation of royalty and cess, and
3786 reduction of subsidies on kerosene, LPG and input for fertilisers.The report said the final phase in 2000-2002 should cover deregulation of aviation turbine fuel, high speed diesel and motor spirit and total deregulation of upstream and downstream sectors of the oil sector."In order to provide the right signal to private
3786 investors, government should make a policy pronouncement declaring its intention to deregulate the hydrocarbon sector within the speicfied time-frame," it added.The panel said the government should also announce appointment of an experts' group on the import tariff reforms.It said the success of the reform programme would largely depend on efficient
3786 management of the transition period and pursuing a transparent policy."With appropriate levels of domestic taxes, import tariffs, cess and royalties, it is entirely feasible that the reform package is budget-neutral," it said.The group said the decontrol would increase efficiency and reduce the cost by setting up a competitive and investment
3786 friendly market structure."In order to achieve the primary objective of securing oil supplies to meet the future growing demand, it would be absolutely necessary to move towards a market-driven price mechanism and to free the petroleum sector from APM (administered price mechanism)."</

3791 by state-run distribution companies, environmental regulations and cost of generation of power.The government was promoting the practice of competitive bidding to attract private investment to set up power generation capacities, Deve Gowda said.The demand for power was growing by an average of nine percent every year, and India needed to
3791 add 142,000 megawatts of power generation capacity by 2007, he said.Officials say roughly 40 million rupees ($1.1 million) are needed to create one megawatt of capacity.Deve Gowda said he would convene a meeting of state chief ministers to discuss the question of reforming loss-making state electricity boards (SEBs) and discuss
3791 a shortfall in power generation. He did not mention any date."We are strongly on the reform and liberalisation route," Deve Gowda said. "We have to cover a large ground."India is welcoming foreign investors in the power sector under a five-year-old economic reform programme, but the poor financial health of the
3791 SEBs, who would pay for the electricity generated, worries investors.Deve Gowda assured private power producers, who made recommendations to the government at the end of the seminar, that he would seriously consider their demands.They asked for an automatic approval of power projects that will cost up to 40 billion rupees.

3819 India's short-term interest rates have fallen in the past six months due to slower industrial demand but long-term rates are seen remaining at current high levels, bankers and analysts said on Friday."Demand for long-term funds exceeds supply," former Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor S. Venkitaramanan told Reuters. "This will
3819 keep interest rates high."Short-term rates have come down sharply due to poor demand from industry, analysts said. Bank credit fell by 16.44 billion rupees ($460 million) to 2,688.63 billion between March 29 and August 30, 1996, according to latest RBI figures.Further, RBI cuts in cash reserve requirements in April and
3819 July this year freed 93 billion rupees to banks.Primary market yields on 91-day treasury bills have fallen to around 10 percent from 13 percent in March while commercial paper is now priced around 13 percent against 17 to 18 percent.Prime lending rates have also eased with some banks slashing rates
3819 by up to 100 basis points in less than three months.State-run banks, who dominate the banking industry with more than 80 percent of total bank advances, announced a 50 basis point cut in prime rates in July.Industry leader State Bank of India (SBI) announced a second 50 basis point cut
3819 to 15.5 percent per annum earlier this month. Two other state-run banks have announced similar cuts and others are expected to follow suit.Analysts said long-term interest rates, however, show no signs of easing with term-lending financial firms borrowing at an effective cost of over 17 percent for maturities above 20
3819 years.Leading companies like Larsen &amp; Toubro and Tata Iron and Steel Company recently raised funds for 10 years and more at rates in excess of 17 percent."Even the government is unable to significantly cut rates on its long term stock (government securities)," an analyst said."Last June, it issued 10-year stock
3819 at 13.85 percent against 14 percent in 1995."But last week's six-year stock issue flopped with just over 50 percent subscription despite 13.82 percent yield," he added."Government borrowings convey a strong signal to the rest of the financial market," a senior official at India's leading term lender, Industrial Development Bank of
3819 India (IDBI) said."At the moment the signals are that interest rates will remain at the current level."The current paradox of banks facing declining credit disbursals and being forced to cut interest, while term lenders and corporates borrow at high rates may be due to structural rigidities within the financial system,
3819 Venkitaramanan said."We also have to realise that this may be a temporary phenomenon," he said. "As industrial activity picks up in the busy season (October to April), demand for credit will rise and even short-term rates will go up."The solution lies in attracting foreign capital inflows into the country, analysts
3819 said."Basically, our requirements cannot be met though domestic sources," said Aashish Pitale, analyst at ICICI Securities and Finance Company. The recent government decision to allow foreign insitutional investors to set up funds to invest exclusively in Indian corporate was an important step in this regard, he said.(1$ = 35.71 rupees)</

3839 A Pakistani official said on Thursday he hoped to convince the International Monetary Fund to resume stalled lending programmes during talks in Washington later this month."We are taking a package of measures for the discussions and hope we will be able to reach an agreement," said V.A. Jafarey, finance adviser
3839 to Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto."They (the IMF) will review our estimates of the budgetary situation," he told a news conference.Jafarey said the discussions planned for September 28 would focus on reviving a stalled $600 million standby loan and an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF).The IMF withheld payment of an $80
3839 million tranche of the standby loan, due to have been disbursed in June, pending a review of Pakistan's budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).Jafarey said Pakistan had completed its own review of the budget figures, but declined to give details of any revisions.He said Pakistan still wanted to cut the fiscal
3839 deficit to four percent of gross domestic product from more than five percent in 1995/96, despite some adjustments in revenue collection plans.Jafarey described Pakistan's foreign exchange position as satisfactory, with cash reserves of $1.4 billion and gold deposits worth about $800 million.He said the trade deficit in the first two
3839 months of 1996/97 had narrowed to a provisional $500 million from $630 million in the year-ago period. Exports had risen 14.9 percent, but imports only by 1.6 percent, he added.Pakistan's trade gap grew to about $3 billion last year from $2.25 billion in 1994/95.The IMF halted a three-year, $1.5 billion
3839 ESAF programme in 1995 after Bhutto's government failed to meet agreed targets for deficit reduction and tariff reform.</
3840 The White Fly cotton pest in Pakistan's main cotton growing belt of Multan in the central province of Punjab is causing a health scare for humans, doctors and officials in the area were quoted on Thursday as saying.The official APP news agency said this was the first time the pest
3840 had been found in the region's residential areas and said the authorities had "hardly made any headway in checking the problem which has so far proved to be an open threat to human health ".It quoted Multan district health officer, Dr Mohammad Riaz, as saying the existance of the pest
3840 in residential areas was unusual and that health officials were discussing ways to fight it.If the fly drops into a human eye, it causes inflammation with severe itching, APP quoted doctors as saying.Riaz advised motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians to use sunglasses to protect their eyes from the small white insect.Multan
3840 Municipal Corporation administrator Rana Naseer Ahmed said anti-fly and anti-mosquito spraying was being carried out in open spaces such as parks, green areas and ponds.But APP quoted experts as saying such steps were insufficient as the fly was resistant to such sprays.</

3843 British Airways Plc. said it filed a motion in Manhattan federal court Friday asking the judge to dismiss an antitrust suit brought by USAir Group Inc. over the British carrier's proposed alliance with American Airlines.USAir has "been unable to identify a single substantive provision of the 1993 agreement (between USAir
3843 and British Airways) that Brtish Airways has purportedly broken."British Airways' motion to dismiss claims that USAir has "a case of corporate amnesia" and that it "forgets" its previous chairman calling the deal "perfectly acceptable."Arlington, Va.-based USAir, British Airways' existing trans-Atlantic partner, filed suit in July saying the proposed alliance between
3843 British Airways and American Airlines would monopolise air travel between the United States and Britain.It also charged the new alliance would undermine its own relationship with British Airways.British Airways said it believed the suit was a tactic by USAir to rengotiate that agreement.USAir said British Airways' motion to dismiss, a
3843 standard tactic in lawsuit, was "posturing."The USAir suit alleged that British Airways forced it to relinquish three routes, but British Airways countered in its motion that a consent decree with the U.S. Deparment of Justice compelled the move for anti-trust concerns.The motion claimed that the suit was based on the
3843 "frustration" of USAir management that British Airways has a new partner. "Disappointment and frustration, however, do not give rise to recognisable legal claims," the filing said.</
3844 Hughes Electronics Corp. agreed to buy satellite operator PanAmSat Corp. for $3 billion in cash and stock that will merge the two companies' satellite services operations, Hughes announced Friday.Under the agreement, Hughes Electronics' Hughes Communications Galaxy (HCG) business will merge with Greenwich, Conn.-based PanAmSat to create a new company called
3844 PanAmSat Corp., the companies said.Hughes, a General Motors Corp. unit which has been aggressively moving into high-growth data and communications services, will become a global leader in satellite services, Wall Street analysts said."It's an excellent idea for Hughes," said analyst Cai Von Rumohr of Cowen &amp; Co.The new company will
3844 combine HCG's fleet of 10 communications satellites for the U.S. market with PanAmSat's international fleet of four communications satellites.PanAmSat has four satellites under construction and HCG has three in development. All are planned for launch through 1998. PanAmSat and HCG had combined 1995 revenues of about $500 million.Under terms of
3844 the agreement, PanAmSat shareholders will get a total $1.5 billion in cash and 28.5 percent of the new company. Hughes Electronics will own 71.5 percent of the new company immediately after the merger.Mexican media giant Televisa, which had been trying to sell its 40.5 percent stake in PanAmSat, said Friday
3844 it expects to receive about $600 million in cash and an equity interest of about 8.5 percent as result of the deal.Analysts said the deal gives GM another reason to sell Hughes, which has changed direction since the automaker acquired it in 1985 for more than $5 billion.Hughes has been
3844 going into "businesses that just are not a part of GM," said John Modzelewski, an analyst at PaineWebber Group Inc.For months Wall Street has speculated GM may want to spin off Hughes. Hughes Chairman C. Michael Armstrong has hinted he would prefer his company operate independently. At a news conference
3844 in New York Friday, he declined to speculate on a possible spinoff.HCG is a leading provider of commercial video, voice and data satellite communications services in the United States. Its Galaxy fleet serves premier cable and broadcast television programmers, with access provided by HCG's Galaxy Network Operations unit in Long
3844 Beach, Calif."By combining Hughes' and PanAmSat's strengths in domestic and global satellite communications, we will be bringing a new level of service to our customers throughout the world," said Armstrong. "Satellites have proven to be one of the most effective and competitive ways to communicate, whether by voice, computer, fax
3844 or video, by anyone, from anyplace, at anytime to anywhere on the planet."Hughes has been diversifying in recent years away from its traditional staple as a maker of satellites and missiles into high-growth consumer services such as DirecTV, its consumer satelite television operation."It's clear to everybody that the value of
3844 Hughes is becoming less and less what it was just a year or two ago," analyst Modzelewski said. "This was a defence company that was going to link up with (auto electronics unit) Delco and we were going to have aerospace technology make its way into GM cars."Under the deal,
3844 PanAmSat shareholders will have three options for payment with respect to the about 100 million outstanding shares of PanAmSat common stock.The companies said they will be able to choose between $30 in cash, one share of new PanAmSat common stock, or half a share of new PanAmSat common stock and
3844 $15 in cash.The new PanAmSat Corp.'s corporate headquarters will be in Greenwich, Conn., with domestic operations based in Long Beach and international operations based in Greenwich.The deal requires government review and approval of the Federal Communications Commission, which are expected to be completed within six to 12 months. Although it
3844 is subject to PanAmSat shareholder approval, PanAmSat shareholders owning in excess of 90 percent of the voting power have agreed to vote in favour of the transaction, the companies said.PanAmSat stock fell 12.5 cents to $27.625 Friday on Nasdaq, and GM Hughes, which trades separately from the automaker's stock, slipped
3844 $2.50 to $60.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.</

3847 International Business Machines Corp. said Friday it will extend health benefits to the domestic partners of gay and lesbian employees, making it the largest U.S. company to date to adopt such a policy.A spokeswoman for the world's largest computer maker said the company would extend health coverage to same-sex domestic
3847 partners during its annual enrollment period between Oct. 1 and Oct. 31.The benefits cover health, dental and vision plans offered by the company and would take effect July 1, 1997, IBM spokeswoman Melinda McMullen said.She said the policy change brings the Armonk, N.Y.-based company into line with its own written
3847 policy of non-discrimination that has included sexual orientation since 1974.The spokeswoman also said the move was designed to keep IBM competitive with other high-tech firms with such policies, including Microsoft Corp., Apple Computer Inc. and Hewlett-Packard Co."The competition to attract and retain a high-quality workforce is fierce in the high
3847 technology business," the spokeswoman said. "So it made sense from a competitive business standpoint as well."Gay rights groups hailed IBM's move."It's a monumental step forward," David Smith, communications director for the Human Rights Campaign, a prominent gay rights group, said in a telephone interview. "IBM's stature in the business community
3847 sends a signal to other companies that it is not only the right thing to do, it makes bottom-line business sense."At the Lambda Legal Defence Fund, which represents gays and lesbians, spokeswoman Peg Byron said, "Big Blue is in good company with nearly 500 employers that offer similar benefits. Popular
3847 culture and many in the private sector recognise that lesbians and gays should have equal treatment and Congress will catch on soon."The IBM policy does not cover unmarried heterosexual couples who live together because they have the option of marriage."What we require of all our employees is proof of commitment.
3847 The acknowledged proof of committment among heterosexuals is marriage," the IBM spokeswoman said.Last week the U.S. Senate, by a wide margin, passed a bill that would deny recognition of same-sex marriages. On the same day however, it narrowly defeated a bill prohibiting employment discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation.In
3847 the absence of laws allowing gays and lesbians to marry, IBM said it would require employees with same-sex domestic partners to present a notarized affidavit that they are involved in a committed relationship, living in the same household, and that their finances are interdependent.McMullen noted that such documents were unlikely
3847 to be entered into lightly, since they have been used as evidence in some so-called palimony cases recently. She said very few employees were expected to benefit from the policy change.IBM also extended its health benefit plans to cover employees who care for a dependent child, even if the employee
3847 is not a biological or adopted parent of the child.For example, an aunt would be covered if she had taken into her house a niece or nephew. Young people up to 23 years old who are financially dependent on an IBM employee would qualify.Smith said IBM's decision came at an
3847 opportune time following Congress's action.The marriage ban "is one example of how homosexuals do not get the same benefits as heterosexuals," he said. "The domestic partnership programmes (at IBM and elsewhere) are a way of equalising the workplace for gay people, providing equal benefits for equal work."</

3849 Russia's U.N. envoy said on Friday that Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali should be able to establish quite soon whether conditions in northern Iraq were safe enough to begin implementing a delayed "oil-for-food" plan.But Boutros-Ghali, in an interview with Reuters, was more cautious, saying that the situation in northern Iraq was still
3849 not clear and that technical problems remained.Asked repeatedly when he thought the programme might be implemented, the secretary-general said he did not know if it would be next month or before the end of the year."We still have not a clear assessment of the situation," he said. "We still have
3849 difficulties to implement this."Boutros-Ghali put the plan on hold after Iraqi troops recently entered the Kurdish-inhabited northern region of Iraq, delaying deployment through the country of U.N. personnel required to carry out the programme.But Russia's ambassador Sergei Lavrov, in a separate briefing for journalists, said: "I believe that the secretary-general
3849 is well in a position to establish quite soon whether safe conditions exist in northern Iraq."He said Security Council members, at a monthly lunch with Boutros-Ghali, had discussed the "oil-for-food" plan under which Iraq would be allowed to buy $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine
3849 and other necessities to offset the effects of U.N. trade sanctions in force since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.Lavrov said there were still reports of "isolated fighting in villages" in northern Iraq, but "the personnel which is required and the deployment of which has been delayed, we were assured could
3849 be there in a matter of a few days.""The implementation process is under way, as the secretary-general assured us," he said, adding that some technical procedures still had to be completed.Boutros-Ghali said he had received a long letter from Iraq's Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf saying he wanted "to send

3851 NEW YORK, Sept 20 - The dollar posted modest gains against major currencies Friday as currency traders squared their books before European finance ministers meet this weekend in Dublin, Ireland, and the Federal Reserve convenes on Tuesday.The talks in Dublin Castle, which start in earnest on Saturday, are seen as
3851 essential for keeping considerable political momentum behind launching a single European currency in January of 1999.The meeting comes amid an intense scramble by European Union governments led by Germany and France to bring their 1997 budget deficits in line with the Maastricht Treaty criteria for economic and monetary union.Some currency
3851 traders were optimistic that the Dublin talks would yield progress. As a result, the German mark weakened against the dollar and other European currencies because the mark would become less important as a safe haven currency if monetary union came into being."As time goes on, it seems like the countries,
3851 France and Germany, seem to be determined to try and get their budgetary matters in accord with Maastricht targets," said Tom Benfer, director, foreign exchange at Bank of Montreal."So people feel the convergence is going to happen eventually. So that's why the mark was sold off in overnight trading."The French
3851 franc had soared to a two-month high against the mark Friday, but the German currency managed to cut its losses against the franc and other currencies including the dollar in New York.In late New York trading, the dollar stood at 1.5160 marks late Friday, up from 1.5136 marks late Thursday.
3851 The dollar traded at 109.96 Japanese yen, up from 109.44 yen.Speculation about whether the Fed will hike interest rates on Tuesday to head off any inflationary pressures also has preoccupied the foreign exchange market. Higher rates tend to help the U.S. currency by making dollar-denominated deposits more attractive to foreign
3851 investors.Early in the week, a Reuter report that eight out of 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested an increase in the discount rate, now at 5 percent, heightened expectations that the central bank might decide to raise rates at Tuesday's meeting of its policy-setting Federal Open
3851 Market Committee.By Friday, currency traders had largely priced into dollar exchange rates the possibility that the Fed may increase rates by one-quarter percentage point, traders said.In light of this view, there was some reluctance to sell or "short" dollars and a preference to buy or be "long" dollars before Fed
3851 policy-makers meet on Tuesday."Given the Dublin meeting and given the FOMC meeting on Tuesday, it's difficult to find a reason to be short dollars," said David Durrant, a senior currency strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc.In other trading, the British pound rose moderately to $1.5557 on Friday from $1.5532 on Thursday. The
3851 dollar fell to 1.2390 Swiss francs from 1.2428 francs and to Canadian $1.3670 from C$1.3705.</

3859 from the trans-Atlantic dialogue."The trans-Atlantic dialogue involves a group of business leaders from both Europe and North America working to find ways to lower barriers, harmonise standards and reduce the cost of trade. 3859 Barshefsky said.The idea of an information technology agreement was endorsed this spring at a meeting in Japan of the trade ministers of the European Union, Canada, United States and Japan. 3867 International Business Machines Corp. will extend health benefits to the domestic partners of gay and lesbian employees, making it the largest U.S. company to date to adopt such a policy.A spokeswoman for the world's largest computer maker said Friday the company would extend health coverage to same-sex domestic partners during
3867 its annual enrollment period between Oct. 1 and Oct. 31.The benefits cover health, dental and vision plans offered by the company and would take effect July 1, 1997, IBM spokeswoman Melinda McMullen said.She said the policy change brings the Armonk, N.Y.-based company into line with its own written policy of
3867 non-discrimination that has included sexual orientation since 1974.The spokeswoman also said the move was designed to keep IBM competitive with other high-tech firms with such policies, including Microsoft Corp., Apple Computer Inc. and Hewlett-Packard Co."The competition to attract and retain a high-quality workforce is fierce in the high technology business,"
3867 the spokeswoman said. "So it made sense from a competitive business standpoint as well."A legal group that represents gays and lesbians welcomed the IBM move."Big Blue is in good company with nearly 500 employers that offer similar benefits," Lambda Legal Defence and Education Fund spokeswoman Peg Byron said. "Popular culture
3867 and many in the private sector recognise that lesbians and gays should have equal treatment and Congress will catch on soon."The IBM policy does not cover unmarried heterosexual couples who live together because they have the option of marriage."What we require of all our employees is proof of commitment. The
3867 acknowledged proof of committment among heterosexuals is marriage," the IBM spokeswoman said.Last week the U.S. Senate, by a wide margin, passed a bill that would deny recognition of same-sex marriages. On the same day however, it narrowly defeated a bill prohibiting employment discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation.In the
3867 absence of laws allowing gays and lesbians to marry, IBM said it would require employees with same-sex domestic partners to present a notorized affidavit that they are involved in a committed relationship, living in the same household, and that their finances are interdependent.McMullen noted that such documents were unlikely to
3867 be entered into lightly, since they have been used as evidence in some so-called palimony cases recently. She said very few employees were expected to benefit from the policy change.IBM also extended its health benefit plans to cover employees who care for a dependent child, even if the employee is
3867 not a biological or adopted parent of the child.For example, an aunt would be covered if she had taken into her house a niece or nephew. Young people up to 23 years old who are financially dependent on an IBM employee would qualify.</
3868 European Union plans for a common currency are expected to receive a solid push forward this weekend when EU finance ministers and central bank governors gather informally in Dublin.The meeting, coming in the middle of an intense scramble by EU governments to bring their 1997 budget deficits in line with
3868 the Maastricht treaty, will focus on three important and rather technical areas of economic and monetary union (EMU), the plan to have a common currency among qualifying European Union countries.The three areas, including a budget stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline among EMU participants, a new exchange rate mechanism (ERM)
3868 linking the single currency to non-members, and the legal underpinnings of monetary union are all scheduled for discussion.While Saturday's talks in Dublin Castle are seen as essential in keeping the considerable political momentum behind EMU on course, EU ministers and monetary officials have sought to play down what might emerge
3868 from the session."This will be a work-in-progress meeting. I am not expecting any dramatic or earth-shattering announcements to come out of it," Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn told a news conference Tuesday.Quinn's measured view was echoed by other officials."I would expect that they present a positive picture of recent developments,"
3868 said one EU monetary official. "Anything else is really not justified."Among the three topics, a budget stability pact is being cast as the centrepiece of the meeting, with recent progress on the issue by the EU's monetary committee setting the stage for a comprehensive deal later this year.The committee, a
3868 secretive group of national treasury and central bank officials, reached a compromise last week that would punish EMU members which run deficits above 3 percent of gross domestic product.While several details remain unresolved -- the size of fines, when they would take effect, and a better definition of the economic
3868 circumstances under which a country's poor finances would be overlooked -- there is the expectation that Dublin will give its blessing to what has been accomplished so far.</

3906 The Justice Department's examination of Microsoft Corp. entered a new phase on Thursday when the company said investigators were seeking additional information about the software giant's business practices.The request, which was announced after the market closed, marked the first time in over a year that the Justice Department had sent
3906 a written request to Microsoft for information.The U.S. government has been investigating Microsoft for more than six years for alleged anti-trust practices but critics claim a 1994 settlement was little more than a slap on the wrist.Microsoft's senior vice president for law and corporate affairs, William Neukom, said the company
3906 would cooperate with the federal agency, adding the facts would show Microsoft was competing "vigorously and legally" and that the competition was benefiting consumers.In Washington, the Justice Department declined to comment on the request other than to say its investigation into Microsoft was continuing and nothing had changed.The request, coming
3906 after many experts had regarded the investigation as dormant, took some observers by surprise.However, Neukom said the latest Justice Department request appeared to be prompted by "complaints from competitors which are reminiscent of allegations that were thoroughly reviewed in the past."Microsoft, which supplies the operating system used in 80 percent
3906 of the world's computers, has been a frequent target of criticism. Microsoft officials declined to say Thursday where the latest complaints had come from, but the company has recently become embroiled in a bitter battle with upstart software company Netscape Communications Corp.Last month, Mountain View, Calif.-based Netscape -- whose dominance
3906 of the market for Web browsers is threatened by Microsoft -- accused its arch-rival of anti-competitive behavior and urged the Justice Department to take action.Gary Reback, outside antitrust counsel for Netscape at Wilson, Sonsini, Goodrich &amp; Rosati, called the inquiry a good first step."On one hand, I would say it's
3906 about time. On the other hand there's still time for the government to do some positive thing for consumers," he said.Unlike the government's earlier investigation into Microsoft's control of computer operating system software, Reback said the stakes were much higher now that the software giant had set its sights on
3906 the Internet."Before we've been talking about monopolization of particular segments of desktop computing," he said. "Here we're talking about monopolization of the Internet."The Internet is going to be as important to our lives as the telephone has been and the television combined," he said."It's the way we're going to get
3906 news, deal with our banks and buy baseball tickets and everything else. And so if one company ends up dominating that through illegal practices, consumers would really suffer and that's what's really motivating the government here."Among other things, Netscape has accused Microsoft of making written offers to computer makers, Internet
3906 service providers, large corporations and others on condition that rival browsers would be less accessible than Microsoft's.Netscape said the offers consisted of payments or discounts on the Microsoft desktop operating system or payments in the form of "real estate" on the Windows 95 screen.Microsoft officials have called the Netscape complaints
3906 a public relations ploy."As a company and as an industry we've been through this before," a Microsoft spokesman said. "We are not going to be distracted by this latest request."Netscape is hardly the first company to take on Microsoft. Most notably, Apple Computer Corp. unsuccessfully sued the software giant, accusing
3906 it of copying its Macintosh operating system for Microsoft's Windows system.Neukom said Thursday that it was disappointing that Microsoft's competitors "continue to seek government intervention in the competitive process rather than concentrating on improving their products."Microsoft has had numerous squabbles with the government over the years, most notably the company's
3906 decision in 1995 to abandon its planned acquisition of personal finance software maker Intuit Inc. after the Justice Department threatened to challenge the deal in court.</
3907 The U.S. Senate passed a bill late Wednesday that would outlaw various forms of computer mischief and increase penalties on repeat offenders.The National Information Infrastructure Protection Act extends existing laws to cover private computers used in foreign or interstate commerce or communications and adds penalties for government employees who misuse
3907 confidential information."Computer crime is on the rise and these steps are needed to help us fight it," said Sen. Patrick Leahy. The Vermont Democrat introduced the bill with Republican Senators Jon Kyl of Arizona and Charles Grassley of Iowa.On Thursday, the Central Intellingence Agency closed its World Wide Web page
3907 after an unknown hacker defaced the site, following a similiar break-in at the Justice Department's Web site in August.And earlier this month, some computers on the Internet were virtually shut down by hackers transmitting vast streams of bogus data. Public Access Networks Corp, the oldest public Internet system in New
3907 York, said attacks on its computers began Sept. 6 and are nearly impossible to trace. The bill that passed the Senate would fill gaps in current law by amending existing criminal statutes and clarifying definitions that apply to hacking, Senate staffers said.For example, the bill broadens the definition of damage
3907 to specifically include physical injury and threats to public health or safety.The measure, endorsed by the Justice Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, now goes to the House.Rep. Robert Goodlatte has introduced a companion measure, but with little time left in the current session the Virginia Republican's bill might
3907 not reach the floor for a vote.--Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312</

3947 Hughes Electronics Corp and PanAmSat Corp agreed to merge their satellite services operations into a new public company. PanAmSat shareholders will get $1.5 billion cash and 28.5 pct of the new company. PanAmSat shareholders have three options for exchanging their shares for either cash or stock. Grupo Televisa S.A. will
3947 buy back options related to PanAmSat Spanish-speaking ventures. A full text of the press release follows.---PRESS RELEASE-------------------------------NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 20, 1996--Hughes Electronics Corporation and PanAmSat Corporation (NASDAQ:SPOT) today announced they have agreed to merge their respective satellite services operations into a new publicly held company.Under the terms of the agreement,
3947 the Hughes Communications Galaxy (HCG) business of Hughes Electronics will be combined with PanAmSat to form a new public company to be named PanAmSat Corporation. In connection with the transaction, PanAmSat stockholders will receive an aggregate of $1.5 billion in cash and 28.5 percent of the new company. In addition,
3947 Grupo Televisa S.A. will repurchase PanAmSat's options to obtain equity interests in Spanish-speaking direct-to-home ventures in the Americas and the Iberian Peninsula. Immediately after the merger, Hughes Electronics will own 71.5 percent of the new PanAmSat.PanAmSat stockholders will have three options to receive payment with respect to the outstanding shares
3947 of PanAmSat common stock: $30 in cash, one share of new PanAmSat common stock, or 1/2 share of new PanAmSat common stock and $15 in cash. These options will be subject to proration based on the total consideration described above.The transaction requires government review and receipt of other approvals, including
3947 that of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission, which are expected to be completed within six to 12 months. Although the transaction is subject to PanAmSat shareholder approval, PanAmSat shareholders owning in excess of 90 percent of the voting power have agreed to vote in favor of the transaction.Frederick A. Landman,
3947 48, the current president and chief executive officer of PanAmSat, will be president and chief executive officer of the new company. Other members of the executive management team will be Lourdes Saralegui, current executive vice president of PanAmSat, and Carl Brown, senior vice president of Hughes' Galaxy Satellite Services. Jerald
3947 F. Farrell, president of Hughes Communications, Inc. (HCI), will continue as HCI president and will serve as the executive overseeing the transition of the two organizations. Personnel reductions are not expected at either operation as a result of the merger. "By combining Hughes' and PanAmSat's strengths in domestic and global
3947 satellite communications, we will be bringing a new level of service to our customers throughout the world," said C. Michael Armstrong, chairman and chief executive officer of Hughes Electronics. "Satellites have proven to be one of the most effective and competitive ways to communicate, whether by voice, computer, fax or
3947 video, by anyone, from anyplace, at anytime to anywhere on the planet."The new company will combine HCG's fleet of 10 communications satellites for the U.S. market, with PanAmSat's international fleet of four communications satellites. PanAmSat has four satellites under construction and HCG has three satellites in development, all of which
3947 are planned for launch through 1998."The strategic combination creates the premier commercial provider of global satellite-based communications services," said Landman. "The new PanAmSat will provide its customers with a unique, one-stop shopping resource for U.S. and international satellite services, and will be poised to pursue exciting new opportunities in satellite
3947 communications."When the merger is completed, the new PanAmSat Corporation will consist of about 500 employees working at facilities within the United States and offices throughout the world. The corporate headquarters of the new PanAmSat Corporation will be in Greenwich, Conn., with its domestic operations based in Long Beach, Calif., and
3947 international operations based in Greenwich. PanAmSat and HCG had combined 1995 revenues of approximately $500 million.HCG is the leading provider of commercial video, voice and data satellite communications services in the United States. The Galaxy fleet serves premier cable and broadcast television programmers, and 24-hour customer support and uplink access
3947 is provided by HCG's Galaxy Network Operations unit in Long Beach, Calif. HCG also offers a full range of technical support from its dedicated engineering staff in Long Beach and satellite tracking stations in Fillmore, Calif., Castle Rock, Colo. and Brooklyn, N.Y.PanAmSat is the world's first private-sector company to provide
3947 global satellite services. It offers satellite-based video and data communications services to more than 300 customers worldwide. The Company currently operates a global satellite system: PAS-1 and PAS-3 over the Atlantic Ocean region; PAS-2 over the Pacific Ocean region; and PAS-4 over the Indian Ocean region. With its additional planned
3947 launches through 1998, PamAmSat will operate multiple satellites in each ocean region worldwide. The next scheduled PanAmSat launch will deploy the PAS-6 satellite over the Atlantic Ocean region in December.The earnings of Hughes Electronics Corporation are used to calculate the earnings per share attributable to GMH (NYSE symbol) common stock.

3968 Dimitris Tsovolas seems more like a mischievious imp than the giant killer who may stop socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis from winning Sunday's election.He has been a radical populist lawyer, a socialist finance minister, a convicted felon and now he seems to be pulling the electoral carpet out from under
3968 Simitis' feet.Tsovolas, 54, who quit the socialists last year, has Simitis running scared and has siphoned off a substantial block of votes with his reputation as a working class hero."Tsovolas is the socialists' biggest problem. He is the big unknown, the "X" factor in the equation of this election," said
3968 MRB polling expert Christina Badouna.His Democratic Social Movement (DHKKI), set up in December, has a solid five percent in opinion polls -- almost every vote taken from Simitis' Panhellenic Socialist Movement (PASOK)."Tsovolas focused his campaign on the grassroot socialist populists, the lower income earners, the less educated and all those
3968 who are angry with both major parties," said political commentator John Loulis.Simitis called the early election confident of a strong win and convinced that his personal popularity would even bring over voters from the conservative opposition.But conservative leader Miltiades Evert mounted a vigorous campaign. He appears to have rallied his
3968 supporters and headed off a large-scale defection to Simitis.That one-two punch by Evert and Tsovolas has been Simitis' worst nightmare. 3968 targets while Tsovolas lays down a passionate stump speech.A skilled courtroom lawyer, Tsovolas's campaign style and politics come from the early radical days of Andreas Papandreou, one of Greece's most loved politicians and skilled speakers.That has helped him connect with the PASOK old-guard while Simitis has alienated some leftists with
3968 vows to create a "New PASOK" -- a modern party eschewing Papandreou's populism and enforcing stringent economic targets.Simitis appears to have understood only late in the campaign that Tsovolas had successfully painted him as a neo-conservative who would cut back on Papandreou's vast welfare state."Simitis and his cohorts are transforming
3968 the socialists from a movement of the disenfranchised to a movement of hustlers pursuing neo-conservative policies and betraying the people," he told a campaign rally.Tsovolas was Papandreou's finance minister from 1985 to 1989 and became something of a Robin Hood figure for responding with gusto to Papandreou's public order to
3968 "Give it all away".He was charged along with Papandreou in a $200-million bank embezzlement scandal in 1989 but rejected his mentor's order to stay away from the televised trial.Instead he mounted his own passionate defence, facing down the austere supreme court judges and perhaps saving the skin of the absent
3968 Papandreou, who was eventually acquitted.Tsovolas's courtroom flare confirmed his standing among many leftists, who saw the case as little more than a right-wing show trial.He was convicted and ordered jailed for two years -- PASOK paid a fine instead -- and he had his political rights suspended for three years
3968 -- preventing him from running in 1993.He was pardoned by parliament after the socialists returned to power in October 1993 but broke formally with the socialists after Simitis and his reform group took control.</

3978 Prospects of an early lifting of a European ban on British beef sales vanished on Friday after the government bowed to domestic political pressure and shelved a cull of up to 147,000 cattle most at risk of mad cow disease.Farmers' leaders welcomed the decision but it drew an icy response
3978 from the European Union, which had insisted on a full-scale cull as part of a deal with Britain aimed at a gradual easing of the crippling embargo imposed in March."As long as they do not meet the pre-conditions and until we have a working document from them which we can
3978 carefully check, then an end to the export ban is simply not a possibility," European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said.British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said London had called off the selective cull, which is in addition to a rolling programme to destroy 450,000 cattle a year over the age
3978 of 30 months, because of fierce opposition in parliament."Any minister who wanted to get the cull order through the House of Commons would have to be able to persuade the House of Commons that member states would be able or willing to ... lift the ban. And many members of
3978 parliament are deeply concerned," Hogg told BBC radio.Prime Minister John Major, who must call an election by May, has a majority of just one in the 651-seat lower chamber. He would have faced certain defeat had the cull been put to a vote.Major said new projections by Oxford University scientists
3978 that mad cow disease would die out within five years, with or without a cull, also justified the government's decision."I don't think anybody wishes to see a cull take place which is unnecessary and economically wasteful," Major told reporters."I would ask for a rational debate, rational consideration," Major added. "No
3978 more hysterical overreaction so that gradually we can restore the confidence that I believe should never have been lost in British beef."The European Union imposed the ban after British scientists discovered a probable link between mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), and the invariably fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, which
3978 rots human brains.Major said suspension of the cull did not mean he was tearing up a deal struck at an EU summit in Florence in June. "It was perfectly clear within the Florence agreement that if new evidence arose we had to consider that evidence," he said.Hogg did admit, however,
3978 that Britain could no longer hope for the ban on beef exports, worth 500 million pounds ($780 million) a year before the crisis erupted, to be lifted by November as Major had hoped after the Florence agreement.Asked whether the ban would still be in place in five years' time, Hogg
3978 added: "It depends on member states. There is a process which enables the ban rapidly and substantially to be lifted, but that depends on member states."He said the strategy now would be to get the ban lifted first on so-called certified herds -- cattle primarily fed on grass that have
3978 no record of BSE. Such a plan, if agreed by the EU, would be likely to start in Northern Ireland.Sir David Naish, president of the powerful National Farmers' Union, said he would meet European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler later on Friday to put Britain's case."Our Scottish and our Ulster (Northern
3978 Ireland) colleagues do have many more herds that have had no BSE cases, and I hope we can help persuade Commissioner Fischler that this is a way to start the lifting of the beef ban," he told BBC radio.Members of the ruling Conservative Party from farming constituencies, who had threatened
3978 to vote down the cull when parliament debates it next month, were pleased by the news.But former prime minister Sir Edward Heath, a fervent pro-European, said: "It will be interpreted widely that the British government reached an agreement at Florence and has now overthrown that agreement unilaterally."</

4009 be temporary.In the wake of the merger which created Pharmacia &amp; Upjohn Inc last year and plans by Switzerland's Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG to get together as Novartis, analysts are reluctant to put their heads above the parapet and say a merger or takeover won't happen."Never say never," said
4009 an analyst at a merchant bank who asked not to be named, but he added that in the immediate future "it doesn't make sense."With a ballooning price tag of around $30 billion, analysts said Zeneca may well be safe from any predator other than the cash-rich Swiss group Roche AG,
4009 which is still smarting from losing its number one position at home to Novartis.Yamaichi international analyst Erling Refsum said the bid talk was effectively acting a "poison pill," actually protecting Zeneca from takeover.And a merger, such as with Bayer's complementary pharmaceutical and agrochemical operations, also appears to be ruled out
4009 by scarcely concealed hosility to the idea among Zeneca's management."It is a case of do Zeneca want to merge?" the merchant bank analyst said, adding that a merger was unlikley to offer anything better than the annual 15 percent pretax profit growth rates predicted for the company.But another analyst at
4009 a U.K. brokerage, who also asked not to be identified, said the problems facing Zeneca were in the longer-term as it competed with giants like Novartis, whose R&amp;D spend had actually gone up."It really means that for a medium-sized player like Zeneca it will be hard to get the new
4009 products developed and through as fast as other major players can," she said.She added that even at current levels Zeneca was not expensive given its product portfolio and pipeline. 4010 to hamper the realisation of the crude oil reserves target," says the report, Inside Nigerian Oil, published by Petroguide.Nigeria National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) accounts for 58 percent of Nigerian crude exports through joint venture companies with Western oil companies, but it has consistently failed to find its share of investment
4010 on time. 4010 set up escrow accounts in Nigeria so that their investments can be monitored."The government and people of Nigeria are not getting their fair share out of the joint venture arrangemnents for petroleum exploration and production," said Etete in August.He said anomalies and inequalitites which made Nigeria the "laughing stock of
4010 the international oil industry" must be eliminated.But Inside Nigerian Oil says, "Companies operating the joint ventures with NNPC do not receive NNPC cash calls as and when the same fall due, which severely decelerates crude oil production, and results in increased interest charges to the government.".Because of late payments, the
4010 report says NNPC has been asked to concede some of its equity to its joint venture partners, including subsidiaries of Royal Dutch/Shell, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp, Agip Spa and Elf Aquitaine.One way of coping with the cash shortages was to sign production sharing contracts with foreign oil companies, which allocate
4010 all funding requirements to the foreign partners. Inside Nigerian Oil says this is now the government's favoured method of foreign oil company participation.-- Tom Ashby, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8145</

4025 The dollar hit a two-month peak against the mark in Europe on Friday and volatile London shares retreated sharply from an opening rally which took them to a new record high.A weaker mark saw the dollar rise to a morning high of 1.5186 marks before some profit-taking dulled its advance.Dealers
4025 said most activity had been between the mark and other European currencies, particularly the french franc, which was being bought heavily against the mark following the publication of the French budget. Generally speaking, dealers said, interest rate jitters were still overhanging the currency markets with the main topic of conversation
4025 being next week's U.S. rate-setting Federal Open Markets Committee meeting. Many analysts expect a 25 basis point (quarter percent) rise in the Fed funds rate.Leading British and German shares opened higher on Friday -- London breaking records -- ignoring another choppy day on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Average
4025 closed down again.But British stocks had retreated into negative territory by late morning after their brief rally, which traders said was related to futures and options.The quarterly futures and options expiry is important because market players have to decide whether to take any profits or losses on their positions or
4025 to "roll over," or take new positions, in the next contract period.The expiry is often associated with unsually high levels of market volatility as traders and investors bet on market moves through the next three months, using derivatives which often set the pace for the rest of the stock market.The
4025 blue chip FTSE 100 index had jumped to a new best of 3,994.1, a rise of 19.8, beating its previous best of 3,987.7 set on Thursday.In Frankfurt, German shares were bullish, almost one percent up at midday, holding onto higher levels attained earlier on the knock-on effect from their own
4025 futures expiry trade. Dealers said the market was also supported by the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.But French shares were at their lows for the day with dealers saying the market was drifting amid lack of consensus over its direction.CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMTThe dollar was at 1.5170
4025 marks and 109.80 yen compared with 1.5139 marks and 109.40 yen in Europe late on Thursday.STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMTThe Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 9.2 points at 3,965.1In Paris, the CAC-40 share was down 8.64 points at 2,073.54The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt
4025 was up 21.66 at 2,646.10. PRECIOUS METALSGold fixed at $382.50, compared with its close in London on Thursday of $382.85. Silver was weaker at $4.95.</

4028 European minor metal traders were initially cautious to news that major antimony producer China is to slash annual production by 20 percent, with opinions divided on the next price direction."It's wait and see at the moment...we have had similar moves by the Chinese in the past," one London trader said.Others
4028 agreed, saying at present they were unprepared to move European antimony prices significantly but would closely eye further developments from a country that has around 50 percent of the world's known reserves."Its like a dripping tap which in all probability is likely to be turned off soon," another antimony trader
4028 said."My feelings this time round is that the Chinese will try to rigidly reinforce the proposed production cuts."According to the China Daily newspaper the cuts would be implemented following rises in both domestic and international production, while prices for antimony have fallen over the last two years. "As a result,
4028 the state wants to limit production," it quoted the National Production Union for Antimony as saying.Antimony is added to alloys to increase their strength and hardness and can be also utilised as a fire retardant and in some batteries.Traders believe the announcement followed a meeting of the Chinese Antimony Producers
4028 Association held recently in Hunan. Several traders, referring to the proposed state intervention to curb production, remain unsure if the government could fully enforce the cuts."Most of the antimony mines and smelters are in the southern provinces of China," one noted.He said, compared to the north, the south of China
4028 was more Westernised with many of the antimony facilities leased from the Chinese government by private enterprise."This should make any cuts hard to enforce," he said. Stock levels in China are hard to pin down, although traders believe they are at high levels, both inland and at exit ports, following
4028 the recent flooding which caused transport problems.Antimony's next price move is likely to be dictated by consumer demand. "At the end of the day it's all down to how the consumers react," one trader said. Some believed they would now be tempted to cover at current levels in anticipation of
4028 a price spike, but others said they would also adopt a wait-and-see attitude.Antimony is currently hovering around $2,500 a tonne, a significant psychological level, according to some traders. "A break of $2,500 could see a dive towards $2,200, but if consumers cover prices could easily bounce," one trader said.The price
4028 had been as high as $5,900 in Novemeber 1994, but since the start of 1996 prices have fallen from levels of around $3,400. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8075</
4029 British Prime Minister John Major said on Friday the British government had suspended a cull of up to 147,000 cattle because it could have been unnecessary or uneconomic. "I don't think anyone wishes to see a cull take place that is unnecessary and economically wasteful. I hope we can discuss
4029 these matters rationally with the European Union and reach a rational and proper decision. And that is what we are seeking to do," Major told reporters. The government's decision to suspend the cull effectively dashed any hopes of the European Union agreeing to an early lifting of its ban on
4029 British beef sales.Farmers' leaders welcomed the decision but it drew an icy response from the EU, which had insisted on a full-scale cull as part of a deal with Britain aimed at a gradual easing of the crippling embargo imposed in March. "As long as they do not meet the
4029 pre-conditions and until we have a working document from them which we can carefully check, then an end to the export ban is simply not a possibility," European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said.</

4036 The British unit of European rail supplier ABB Daimler-Benz Transportation (Adtranz) unveiled its latest family of tilting trains for the UK passenger railway market on Friday, claiming they could cut trunk journey times."Adtranz is developing a family of diesel and electric tilting trains specifically for the UK, built on the
4036 proven technology of the Swedish X2000 intercity trains and Germany's VT611 inter-regional diesel train," it said in a statement.Such trains would allow up to 30 percent faster speeds through existing track curves, "significantly reducing journey times" even before infrastructure improvements are carried out. Seven countries already have tilting train fleets
4036 and another eight have them on order, but neither Adtranz nor any of its competitors have broken into the British market.The company believes the much-maligned West Coast intercity route linking London with Manchester and Glasgow would be an ideal starting point for its marketing efforts.The line, which is to be
4036 upgraded over the next few years in a complex 1.0 billion pound project led by infrastructure owner Railtrack Plc, has contraints due to its twisting tracks, outmoded signalling systems and power restrictions.Adtranz's plan is to offer its trains ahead of improvements. John Vale, Adtranz business development manager, told a conference
4036 on the future of the West Coast line in Manchester on Friday that new trains soon would make good strategic sense.A signalling project currently under way involving Siemens, Britain's GEC, Westinghouse and Adtranz is intended to deliver a new signalling system that will permit higher train speeds and more capacity."The
4036 next step in the strategy needs to be the train. But a train which is already proven and is sufficiently flexible to give immediate benefits whilst able to capitalise on the infrastructure improvements as they are implemented," he said. Adtranz is making its pitch against the background of this year's
4036 total change in Britain's business of train operating.All the country's 25 passenger operating companies, of which Intercity West Coast is one, are being privatised to franchisees through contracts of seven or more years.Meanwhile, Railtrack, floated this spring, is evolving a market-based capital raising function for new projects and train builders
4036 are looking for customers among either the privatised operators or the three big leasing companies already in place.A key feature of Vale's paper was his assertion that new trains would lead to immediate revenue benefits at a level comparable to the reduction in journey time.He said the introduction of the
4036 X2000 in Sweden had lifted the market share of rail over air on the trunk route between the main cities of Stockholm and Gothenburg by cutting 25 percent off the rail journey time with only minor track improvements.Between London and Glasgow, where West Coast trains compete with airlines and the
4036 rival East Coast trunk rail line, Adtranz sees potential to cut the journey time from five hours to four.Adtranz was formed by merging the rail units of Germany's Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss-Swedish ABB.-- Andrew Huddart, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8716</

4048 35/40 points recently, the quota is expected to reduce western hemisphere raws availability and balance the expected increase in output."The central Americans this year seem to have been scooped up by the U.S. quota," said one broker."Although it's slightly down on last year it looks as if there is going
4048 to be a pretty good U.S. quota. It's going to be quite tight," he said.The U.S. Agriculture Department recently set the sugar import quota for the 1997 fiscal year at 2.3 million tonnes, with 1.7 million tonnes to be allocated immediately and the rest hinging on reviews set for January,
4048 March and May.Brazil, along with the Philippines and the Dominican Republic, are to receive quota certificates allowing them to ship up to 25 percent of their quota during each quarter, and unentered allocations may be carried into other quarters.The three producers are the largest quota holders among three or four
4048 dozen nations.The U.S. requirement will take advantage of the expected production increase in north Brazil, which brokers said was probably the only origin to be delivered against New York's October contract.Trade sources said while it was still too early to gauge the exact size of the north Brazilian crop, a
4048 total cane crush of 48.5 million tonnes is expected, producing 3.35 million tonnes of sugar and 1.75 million in exports."One never knows with Brazil how much will actually come out, with the requirements for domestic (needs) and alcohol," said one physical sugar trader.However, in its latest report Czarnikow Sugar said
4048 north Brazil could set a new sugar production record in 1996/97, exceeding last year's record of 3.54 million tonnes raw value.Exports from the region could soar once the government finally removed a 40-percent tax on the remaining 20 percent of permitted sugar exports, it said.Some brokers suggested that South Africa's
4048 bumper crop could compete with north Brazil as the country is well placed geographically to supply raws to both west and east hemispheres.But others said South African sugar was unlikely to be delivered against October and availability would be limited at best for the remainder of the year."The South Africans
4048 are getting towards the end of their season so they certainly won't be involved in the tape," said one London trader.Although north Brazil's crop will be mainly raw sugar, most of the small amount of 45 ICUMSA whites is said to have been bought in advance by European trade houses."There's

4059 Chocolate like red wine contains phenols, chemicals believed to help stop arteries from clogging up, U.S. doctors advised on Thursday."The pleasant pairing of red wine and dark chocolate could have synergistic advantages beyond their complementary tastes," Andrew Waterhouse and colleagues at the University of California at Davis wrote in a
4059 letter to the Lancet medical journal.Phenols are antioxidants that prevent the "rusting" of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs), which are the so-called bad fat component of cholesterol.When LDLs oxidise they turn into a plaque that can block arteries, causing heart disease.Waterhouse's group, knowing that chocolate has natural preservatives that stop the fat
4059 in it from going rancid, tested chocolate to see how it compared to red wine, known to contain high levels of phenols.They found quite a lot. "A cup of hot chocolate containing 7.3 grams (two tablespoons) of cocoa could have 146 mg total phenol, whereas a 41 g (1.5 ounce)
4059 piece of chocolate would have 205 mg total phenol," they wrote."For comparison, a standard 140 ml (five ounce) serving of red wine contains about 210 mg total phenol."They said the effects would need to be proven in people, but if they did, chocolate could be a significant source of the

4062 Prospects of an early lifting of a European ban on British beef sales vanished on Friday after the government bowed to domestic political pressure and shelved a cull of up to 147,000 cattle most at risk of mad cow disease.Farmers' leaders welcomed the decision but it drew an icy response
4062 from the European Union, which had insisted on a full-scale cull as part of a deal with Britain aimed at a gradual easing of the crippling embargo imposed in March."As long as they do not meet the pre-conditions and until we have a working document from them which we can
4062 carefully check, then an end to the export ban is simply not a possibility," European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said.British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said London had called off the selective cull, which is in addition to a rolling programme to destroy 450,000 cattle a year over the age
4062 of 30 months, because of fierce opposition in parliament."Any minister who wanted to get the cull order through the House of Commons would have to be able to persuade the House of Commons that member states would be able or willing to ... lift the ban. And many members of
4062 parliament are deeply concerned," Hogg told BBC radio.Prime Minister John Major, who must call an election by May, has a majority of just one in the 651-seat lower chamber. He would have faced certain defeat had the cull been put to a vote.Hogg said, however, that the decision, taken at
4062 a two-hour meeting late on Thursday, was also justified by new projections by Oxford Univeristy scientists that mad cow disease would die out within five years with or without a cull.The European Union imposed the ban after British scientists disclosed in March a probable link between mad cow disease, or
4062 Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), and the invariably fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, which rots human brains."The position of the Commission has not changed," Jacques Santer, president of the European Commission, told Reuters Television in Brussels when asked about the British decision.Major's office said suspension of the cull did not mean the government
4062 was departing from the framework of a deal struck at the European Council in Florence in June. This deal allowed the eradication plan to be "adapted if necessary in the light of scientific and epidemiological developments".Hogg did admit, however, that Britain could no longer hope for the ban on beef
4062 exports, worth 500 million pounds ($780 million) a year before the crisis erupted, to be lifted by November as Major had promised after the Florence agreement."We will not be seeing the ban lifted by November," Hogg said.Asked whether the ban would still be in place in five years' time, Hogg
4062 added: "It depends on member states. There is a process which enables the ban rapidly and substantially to be lifted, but that depends on member states."He said the strategy now would be to get the ban lifted first on so-called certified herds -- cattle primarily fed on grass that have
4062 no record of BSE. Such a plan, if agreed by the EU, is likely to start in Northern Ireland.Sir David Naish, president of the powerful National Farmers' Union, said he would meet Fischler later on Friday to put Britain's case."Our Scottish and our Ulster (Northern Ireland) colleagues do have many
4062 more herds that have had no BSE cases, and I hope we can help persuade Commissioner Fischler that this is a way to start the lifting of the beef ban," he told BBC radio.Members of the ruling Conservative Party from farming constituencies, who had threatened to vote down the cull
4062 when parliament debates it next month, were pleased by the news.But former prime minister Sir Edward Heath, a fervent pro-European, said: "It will be interpreted widely that the British government reached an agreement at Florence and has now overthrown that agreement unilaterally." 4067 increasing unease about pensions products and selling methods employed by the industry," OFT Director General John Bridgeman said."People are now more worried about living too long to provide a comfortable retirement than they are about dying early."The OFT announcement came just as a court told Kevin Maxwell, son of disappeared
4067 tycoon Robert Maxwell, that he would not have to face a second serious fraud trial.The decision draws a line under five years of controversy surrounding some 400 million stg which disappeared from Maxwell company pension funds.In January Kevin, his brother Ian and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of
4067 conspiring to defraud the pension funds.The 1995 Pensions Act, drafted largely as a result of the Maxwell affair, is due to come into effect in April 1997.The final report from the OFT inquiry, scheduled for publication in the first half of 1997, will cover an analysis of actual or potential
4067 "detriment" to consumers in general and particular groups such as women who have taken career breaks.It will also seek how such losses can be addressed and avoided in the future and make any necessary recommendations to ministers, regulatory bodies, the industry and consumers.A further aspect will be a comparison with
4067 other pensions industries internationally.Bridgeman said an important source of information will be responses gathered from consumers who have had both favourable and unfavourable experiences with the sale and performance of pension products.This will be used in the final report but OFT will not be able to take up any individual
4067 case or complaint. Views will also be sought from the industry, regulators, consumer groups and other government and self regulatory organisations.-- Caroline Allen, London newsroom +44 171 542 6414</

4101 Morocco's economy has gathered steam after a slow start, with Gross Domestic Product (GDP) forecast to rise by more than 10 percent this year after a catastrophic drought sent it plunging by 7.6 percent in 1995."I am optimistic because the results are favourable. There is a net improvement in the
4101 balances. And the ratios, as you can see from the figures, are positive," Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj told Reuters on Friday.Kabbaj, confirming figures given to the cabinet on Thursday and carried on the official news agency MAP, said in reference to GDP: "We hope to go over 10 percent growth
4101 this year."He had told the cabinet the economy was characterised by "positive financial indicators" such as an increase of global monetary reserves to three billion dirhams ($344.8 million) at the end of July 1996.According to the figures, public savings were up to 5.7 billion dirhams, a rise of 2.6 billion
4101 compared with end of August 1995, while revenue from company taxes was up by about 45 percent and income tax revenue was up by more than 10 percent.Kabbaj also told the cabinet that after stagnation in the first half of the year, total credits of 3.6 billion dirhams had been
4101 granted in July. These, with loans from state banks, were mainly for farming and construction, including the hotel sector."Bank deposits recorded an important increase, reaching 3.7 billion dirhams in July after a fall during the first six months of this year," he said.Kabbaj earlier this month had dismissed rumours of
4101 a possible devaluation of the dirham, saying "we have no plans to devalue our national currency".All economic indicators showed "the resumption of economic activity", he said, including the main indicators on the Casablanca bourse.Forty-six companies are listed on the bourse, whose traded volume on Thursday totalled 48.5 million dirhams.The Casablanca
4101 stock market has seen increasing activity as Rabat's privatisation plans have gone ahead, with 114 state enterprises slated to be sold off by the end of 1998 when the programme was launched in 1993. So far, more than 40 firms have been sold.Earlier this month, the country's ONA Group bought
4101 controlling stakes in four mines for the equivalent of $75 million. Next month, the state plans to float 30 percent of the FERTIMA feriliser firm on the bourse at 120 million dirhams ($13.7 million).But there are shadows hanging over future exports to the European Union, which took three-quarters of Morocco's
4101 important citrus fruit exports in 1995.Farmers in this North African country of 27 million people have been angered by an EU decision they said last week would cut their exports of citrus and tomatoes and expose them to unfair competition from EU members like Spain.Agriculture and food products in the
4101 first five months of this year, the latest figures from the official Office des Changes, made up 37 percent of Morocco's total exports.This was dominated by citrus fruit exports valued at 1.309 billion dirhams, compared with 838 million in the first five months of 1995. ($1 = 8.7 dirhams)</

4103 Turkish bureaucrats, economists and businessmen gave contrasting reactions on Friday to a government plan to pool public revenues to help poor state institutions and better control state funds.Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday a central cash management system would be set up to enable state companies which need money
4103 to tap revenues made by profit-making state institutions and firms.Gazi Ercel, governor of the central bank, said the plan would enable the government to control money from one centre."The system will make it possible to monitor public accounts simultaneously and from one centre," he told a meeting. "Movements of state
4103 funds will easily be controlled," he said.But economist Erhan Isil said the plan, prepared by four state banks, would contravene the rules of free market economic policy Turkey adopted in the 1980s."Taking the monetary management of the state economic enterprises, which are commercial and industrial institutions, into the central state
4103 is diametrically opposed to the concept of market economy," he wrote in the economic daily Dunya.He said the government plan, yet to be approved after cabinet debates, did not clarify whether non-profit state institutions would be included in the system."The government had better prepare a management system for the cash
4103 flow of its institutions, which fluctuates according to seasons," he said.The plan will not allow money making state companies like petrochemicals producer Petkim and petroleum marketer Petrol Ofisi to invest their profits or excess cash in financial instruments, mainly in repurchase agreements, or repo.Repo, the trading of t-bills with maturities
4103 from overnight up to 32 days, is an attractive short-term financial tool for small- and large-size investors who do not have to pay income tax for their returns.Erbakan said the system would reduce the treasury's borrowing requirement. The treasury borrows mainly to close the deficits of government institutions and companies.Electricity
4103 producer TEAS and distributor TEDAS, postal services PTT, oil refiner Tupras and coal producer TKI are among biggest loss-making state companies whose losses amount to trillions of lira.Under the plan, part of the government's two revenue-raising packages, a state company which needs cash can draw money from the common pool
4103 instead of resorting to the treasury's borrowed funds.Erbakan said the plan would not disrupt the implementation of the individual budgets of each government company.But the Ankara Industrialists and Businessmen's Association (ASIAD) said the plan would create problems when budgets were prepared by parliament with varying priorities for each government institution."Prorities
4103 may clash during the preparation of the budgets of key institutions in the defence, agriculture and other sectors," it said in a statement.$=90,400 Turkish lira</

4119 Israel said on Friday it would tighten its entry ban against Palestinians from the West Bank and Gaza Strip ahead of and during Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement."During Yom Kippur and the weekend before it Palestinian entry will not be permitted from Judea and Samaria (West Bank) and
4119 Gaza beginning from today at 1600 (1400 GMT) until Tuesday 0400 (0200 GMT)," an army spokeswoman said."Urgent humanitarian cases will be permitted entry."Israel barred the nearly two million Palestinians of the territories from entering Israel after the first in a series of Islamic militant suicide bombings in March and February
4119 that killed 59 people in Israel.The closure bars thousands of Palestinians from livelihoods in Israel and is condemned by them as collective punishment.Over time, Israel gradually eased the closure allowing nearly 40,000 Palestinians to return to work. These people will be barred from Israel during the tightened closure.Yom Kippur runs
4119 from Sunday evening through Monday evening.</
4120 Morocco's gross domestic product (GDP) will increase by more than 10 percent by the end of 1996, the official MAB agency said.This follows a GDP fall of 7.6 percent last year, and earlier forecasts of around 11 percent rise for this year.Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj presented the forecast to a
4120 cabinet meeting late on Thursday night, MAB said. He said global monetary reserves had increased to three billion dirhams ($344.8 million) at the end of July 1996 while public savings had reached 5.7 billion dirhams, a rise of 2.6 billion dirhams compared with the end of August 1995.After a period
4120 of stagnation in the first six months this year, total credits of 3.6 billion dirhams had been granted in July to the farming and housing sectors."Bank deposits recorded an important increase, reaching 3.7 billion dirhams in...July after a fall during the first six months of the year," Kabbaj was quoted
4120 as saying.All economic indicators showed "the resumption of economic activity", he said, including the main indicators on the Casablanca bourse. ($1 = 8.7 dirhams) -- Rabat newsroom - 212-7-726518</
