4133 Reform Party candidate Ross Perot said he would file his lawsuit on the presidential debates on Friday, but his attorney said the suit would be submitted on Monday."We'll file the legal papers today," Perot said, but attorney Jamie Raskin, dean of American University Law School, said through an assistant that
4133 "The suit will be filed on Monday ... by 5 p.m."Asked to explain the discrepancy, Raskin's assistant Anna Kelly said by telephone, "It was a mistake. I guess he (Perot) was not informed."Perot gave no details in two television interviews, saying he wanted his case against the Commission for Presidential
4133 Debates to unfold like the Saturday serials of his childhood.The panel recommended excluding Perot from the debates, saying he had no chance of winning the presidency.The two major candidates are still negotiating the timing and format of the debate series. But Perot challenged Republican Bob Dole to "meet him in
4133 St. Louis," where the first debate originally was to take place Sept. 25."I will be in St Louis the night of 25th, I'll see that the arena is ready," he said on NBC's "Today" show. "It'll be interesting to see if he can show up and debate me."Moments later on
4133 ABC's "Good Morning America," he seemed ready to break into song as he quoted the lyrics from the Judy Garland musical: "Meet me In St. Louis, Meet me at the fair."Dole's spokesman Gary Koops responded, "We are in a meeting with the Clinton campaign on Saturday to continue discussion on
4133 the one-one-one debates between Bob Dole and Bill Clinton. And we look forward to having our one-on-one debates on with Bill Clinton."Perot said earlier he would seek a court order to delay the debates until a decision is made on his participation. He maintained he would have won in 1992
4133 if people voted their consciences and ignored news reports that he could not win.Perot said a poll by the "big media" that was "never reported" showed that he was actually the top candidate in the 1992 race with Clinton and President George Bush. Perot won 19 percent of the popular
4133 vote but no electoral votes that year. Polls show him with only around five percent currently.Saying he was being deprived of access to television, and that voters were being manipulated, Perot added, "We probably need to bring in poll watchers from Bosnia and Haiti for this election, it's that bad."</

4137 Westinghouse Air Brake Co., North America's largest manufacturer of air brakes, said Thursday it acquired Vapour Corp. from Mark IV Industries Inc. for about $65 million.Vapour is the leading U.S. manufacturer of door systems for transit rail cars and metropolitan buses, with about 575 employees in Chicago, Montreal and London.The
4137 purchase price includes $63 million in cash and $2 million in potential payments tied to future sales targets.Westinghouse Air Brake said a large portion of the projected increase in revenue is expected to come from new contracts for Vapour to provide door systems for the London Underground, a project that
4137 has already begun.The deal is not expected to affect earnings per share for the remaining four months in the fiscal year, which ends Dec. 31, the company said. It is expected to contribute to earnings beginning in the first quarter of 1997.Wilmerding, Pa.-based Westinghouse Air Brake makes air brakes and
4137 related equipment for locomotives, railway freight cars and passenger transit rail vehicles.Westinghouse's stock fell 25 cents to $11.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange. Mark IV edged down 12.5 cents to $21.375, also on the NYSE.</

4143 President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore rumbled through the Pacific Northwest on a bus tour on Thursday, urging voters who helped give control of Congress to Republicans two years ago to throw them out on Election Day.Increasingly confident of their chances of being re-elected Nov. 5, Clinton and

4147 Municipal bond broker dealers will increasingly feel the squeeze as the internet and other electronic trading systems allow buyers and sellers to cut out the middleman, the fixed-income manager for Raymond James &amp; Associates Inc predicted."A lot of our customers will be purchasing securities without talking to our brokers," Raymond
4147 James Senior Vice President Van Sayler told the Miami Bond Club Wednesday night. "The growth in the use of internet technologies is fantastic."Direct trading systems have already made major inroads in the stock market through on-line trading and through direct trading systems such as Instinet, Sayler said.The municipal market has
4147 lagged because of logistical problems, namely the sheer volume of issues and issuers. Only 20,000 to 30,000 different stocks are traded, while there are more than 1.3 million CUSIPs in the muni marketplace."In a year or two, that issue is going to be gone," Sayler said.Increasingly sophisticated databases will not
4147 only solve the volume problem, but will enable customers to retrieve information that is now only available to broker-dealers, including spreads and the identity of the seller.By typing in criteria such as the state, maturities and coupon rates they are looking for, buyers will be able to retrieve lists of
4147 available bonds and buy them directly from the seller, Sayler said.The result will be more consolidation within the industry. He predicted the biggest firms would survive, along with "boutique firms" that carve out niche markets, but that "There's going to be fewer in the middle."Firms that survive will do so
4147 by cutting their own transaction costs. In that regard, brokerage firms will follow the trend already seen in commercial banking, Sayler said."To talk to a broker, you're going to have to pay a fee the way some banks are charging a fee to talk to a real live teller," he

4148 the effect," a U.S. producer source said. "It all has to be taken with a grain of salt."Antimony prices have plunged to their lowest levels since 1993 to 1994. Metal prices are down over $1,000 since last summer to about $2,500 per tonne, with oxide at $2,650. The slide finally
4148 provoked Chinese Antimony Producers Association to announce a 20 percent cut in production.A U.S. trader who spoke to those attending the meeting said the Association was focusing on "reigning in" the smaller producers who were selling as much metal as they could to generate revenue.China is the world's dominant supplier,
4148 accounting for about 50 to 55 million pounds of the 60 to 65 million pounds consumed by the United States each year, industry sources said. "China is talking its book - prices are lousy. It's a gigantic poker game," a U.S. consumer said.U.S. industry sources said if China's intention was
4148 real, it would take 90 to 120 days to have any effect. "There is a lot of material in Hong Kong and on the water," a source said.Traders cautioned that China has threatened to cut minor metals production before to prop up prices, most notably in tungsten and bismuth, all
4148 without much success.Chinese producers were saying that antimony prices of $3,500 a tonne were below their production costs, and had even attempted last summer to set a price floor of $4,800 a tonne. Part of the problem faced by the Chinese is that the remnimbi is now fully convertible, making
4148 black market sales at inflated prices difficult, a trader said. "But the mines are also being starved of cash flow, which will probably mean there will be a price spike in six months to a year," he added.Demand from the plastics sector for flame retardants - the biggest consumer -
4148 which uses oxide is said to be particularly weak. "I think the problem is less on the supply side than on the demand side," traders said.Some industry sources said that since the last price spike, antimony may have lost market share to cheaper substitutes in fire retardants which is why
4148 demand is so weak.-- Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-859-1646</
4149 Reliance Bancorp Inc said Friday it has adopted a shareholder rights plan, declaring a dividend of one preferred-share purchase right for each outstanding share of the company's common stock.Initially, each right will entitle stockholders to buy a 1/100th interest in a share of a new series of preferred stock of
4149 the company at an exercise price of $60.The rights would be exercised only if an individual or group acquired 10 percent or more of the company's common stock, or made a tender offer that would result in it acquiring 10 percent or more of its common stock. The rights dividend
4149 distribution will be payable to shareholders of record on October 3. The rights are to expire 10 years later, on October 3, 2006.Reliance Bancorp is the holding company for Reliance Federal Savings Bank and has assets of $1.8 billion. The company said it was taking the step to protect the
4149 interests of its stockholders in the event of a hostile takeover bid. It said the plan was not adopted in response to any specific pending bid.If that were to occur, each right, unless redeemed by the board of directors at a price of $0.01 per right, would entitle its holder
4149 to purchase a number of shares of common stock with a market value equal to twice the exercise price of the right - or, at the company's option, 1/100th of a share of the new series of preferred stock, Reliance Bancorp said.</

4152 The advent of electronic money is not expected to have any major macroeconomic effect in the medium term, U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Friday."I do not anticipate in the near and medium term significant macro-economic effects," Summers told reporters following a speech to a conference on electronic
4152 money sponsored by the Treasury Department.Some analysts have speculated that the Federal Reserve's ability to conduct monetary policy may be undermined by the issuance of electronic money over the Internet or elsewhere. Others have suggested that the Fed and Treasury could lose profits from seigniorage -- the income earned by
4152 currency issuers because currency pays no interest to holders.Summers though played down both those concerns. He noted that much U.S. currency is held abroad and said electronic money is unlikely to substitute for that anytime soon.As for monetary policy, it already works indirectly through open market operations, he noted."As we
4152 move from credit cards to debit cards to stored value cards, I think the Fed will continue to have the ability, by operating in the government securities market, to have a substantial influence on the level of interest rates," Summers said.He saw macroeconomic benefits to be gained from the advent
4152 of electronic money and stored value. If, like credit cards, they make it easier for consumers to purchase goods during economic downturns, then they can act as a stabilizing force on consumption."To the extent that these technologies and the Internet make markets more competitive, they will tend to ... be
4152 a force against inflation," he added.</

4155 A U.S. Treasury Department official reiterated Friday the need for new legislation that would resolve uncertainty about the scope of a legal amendment governing certain types of derivatives transactions.The Treasury amendment of 1974 was meant to allow banks and other big dealers to keeping trading such instruments as foreign exchange
4155 forward contracts outside the expanded reach of futures regulation."It has historically been Treasury's position that legislation is needed," Deputy Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson told a futures and securites industry conference. Anderson said the amendment, part of a broad U.S. law covering commodity futures trading, needs to be changed so that
4155 it clearly gives futures regulators the authority to police certain foreign exchange market deals.The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has maintained that the amendment already gives it jurisdiction to do so. But Anderson raised questions about whether the futures regulatory agency has any authority over foreign exchange transactions.The uncertainty has dogged
4155 the market and drew harsh criticism last month from the General Accounting Office, the auditing arm of Congress. Indiana Republican Richard Lugar and Vermont Democrat Patrick Leahy offered a bill early this week that would modify the current law governing futures markets. They characterized the proposal as a starting point
4155 for reforming laws next year.The lawmakers have given the Treasury and the CFTC until the end of this year to reach an agreement on how the Treasury amendment should be interpreted."I think we have a good chance of coming to agreement on it," Anderson said. He maintained that an upcoming
4155 Supreme Court case on one interpretation of the amendment "won't answer all the uncertainties" or deal with all the issues.</

4159 likely across southern Iowa, northern Missouri, central Illinois, northern Indiana and northwest Ohio.Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, said these temperatures should produce scattered frost in low-lying areas, but clouds or wind could limit the breadth of the frost. In areas of frost there will be crop damage, but Burgio
4159 said the large portions of the corn and soybeans should survive the cold and continue to develop. 4159 30 across the northern half of the Midwest."If they (maps) are verified, temperatures will be below freezing across large portions of the corn belt, north of I-70 (Interstate 70 highway)," he said of the Sept 29-30 forecast. 4159 the Midwest, meteorologists said.During the past 24 hours, the western Midwest received 0.35 to 1.00 inch rain. The rain should move into the eastern Midwest Saturday and Sunday and bring 0.25 to 1.00 inch with 60 to 70 percent coverage.Next week should be mostly dry, but Gesser said more rain
4159 was likely from September 27 to 29.Texas to Nebraska should be dry until early next week, which will allow farmers to resume winter wheat planting, said Burgio.--Chicago newsdesk 312-408-8720--</

4162 California voters are about evenly divided on a ballot initiative that would limit the ability of local governments to impose fees, assessments and taxes, according to a survey released on Friday.After they were read a summary of the initiative's official description, 37 percent of likely voters said they were inclined
4162 to support Proposition 218, according to the Field Institute poll.The non-partisan Field Institute said 38 percent were inclined to vote against the measure, while 25 percent said they were undecided.Before survey respondents were read a summary of the initiative, just one in nine voters said they had heard or read
4162 anything about Proposition 218, the Field Institute said.Proposition 218 would require that a majority of local voters in an election approve any increase in general taxes. It would also limit local government's use of fees and assessments.According to some municipal analysts, the initiative could have a devastating effect on local
4162 government finance.The proposition was sponsored by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, which downplayed the significance of the Field poll."The only thing of value the Field poll discovered is that 89 percent of the voters polled haven't yet heard of Proposition 218 -- which isn't surprising since voters haven't started focusing
4162 on any of the ballot measures," said Joel Fox, president of the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association."All the survey research we've conducted in recent months shows the vast majority of California voters -- over 70 percent of those polled -- want the right to vote on new local taxes, assessments and
4162 fees. And this is precisely what Proposition 218 provides," Fox said."When voters begin focusing on the issues and learn more about Proposition 218, we're confident it'll enjoy widespread support from a winning majority of voters who want more control over the local taxes they pay," Fox said.The Field Institute survey
4162 was conducted between August 29 and September 7 among a representative statewide sample of 416. Of this group, 291 were deemed likely voters in the upcoming November general election.The margin of error from the overall voter sample was plus or minus five percentage points. The margin of error for the
4162 likely voter sample was six percentage points.--Adam Entous, 415-677-2511</
4163 A top SEC enforcement official urged municipalities and their lawyers Thursday to play it safe when deciding whether to disclose a new piece of information to investors about a municipality's finances."Why would you even want to take a chance?" Colleen Mahoney, deputy director of enforcement at the Securities and Exchange
4163 Commission, told a workshop at the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop here on Thursday."If you are wringing your hands, I would think you'd want to err on the side of disclosure rather than non-disclosure," Mahoney said.She added, "It is always better to make the tough call than to
4163 try to play it cute."Mahoney was responding to a workshop participant who asked what is the worst thing that can happen to an issuer if it incorrectly opts not to disclose information.Mahoney also was asked whether SEC's enforcement staff makes allowances for the fact that many municipalities do not have
4163 the same internal accounting controls as corporations to detect fraud."It's not a yes or no answer," Mahoney said. "We recognize that some issuers are operating in a difficult context.""A bad system may explain why the information was not what it needed to be," she said. But an important question, she
4163 said, is whether local officials were reckless in not knowing about system flaws.Earlier today, Dean Pope, a partner with Hunton &amp; Williams in Richmond, told lawyers that many of their early fears about the new provisions of SEC's municipal disclosure Rule 15c2-12 were "exaggerated."He said issuers generally are pledging to
4163 make only those disclosures specifically required by the rule. "This approach, I believe, is indisputably correct, and is in the best interest of your clients," Pope said in a keynote address at the NABL conference.Pope said once bonds hit the secondary market, disclosing ongoing events about the issuer "continues to
4163 be the great unknown.""Few of our clients have had much experience with it," he said.Pope turned to SEC's probe of Denver International Airport bonds. To what extent should bond professionals rely on forecasts in financings for airports, hospitals, retirement communities, and utility systems? Pope asked."Is every risk that is ever
4163 raised in project planning a risk that must be" disclosed, Pope asked. "How relevant is the fact that, despite large shifts in market value, the bonds have never defaulted?"He said Denver is a reminder that for high profile, political projects there is an "inherent tension" between providing investors with bad
4163 news and "glowing" reports.On May 2, an SEC administrative law judge ruled that Thorn, Welch &amp; Co., formerly Thorn, Alvis, Welch Inc, failed to tell investors in seven tax-exempt bond deals that the deals were structured so as to violate tax laws and threaten the tax status of the bonds.Judge
4163 Brenda Murray revoked the firm's broker-dealer registration and ordered it and its president John Thorn to pay over $1 million in fines.Pope said, "I believe that when we are wearing the hat of bond counsel, Thorn Alvis doesn't change what we do at all. We still apply the standards that
4163 we have been taught to apply in giving opinions," he said.SEC in January 1995 filed its first "pay-to-play" case against Terry Busbee, an elected official of the Escambia county, Florida, Utilities Authority, and Preston Bynum, who worked for bond underwriter Stephens Inc.Both defendants agreed to settle the charges.Pope said the
4163 case reflects SEC's "not terribly convincing" position that "any kind of political bribe in connection with retention of underwriters is a material event to be disclosed.""Guilty pleas meant this assertion was not judicially tested," he said.He said there is "substantial doubt" as to whether the SEC can prevail with this
4163 position in futures cases.--Vicky Stamas, 202-898-8314</

4170 Hughes Electronics Corp. said Friday it agreed to buy satellite operator PanAmSat Corp. for $1.5 billion in cash and an additional amount of stock in a $3 billion deal that will merge the two companies' satellite services operations.Under the agreement, the Hughes Communications Galaxy business of Hughes Electronics will merge
4170 with Greenwich, Conn.-based PanAmSat to create a new company called PanAmSat Corp., the companies said.PanAmSat shareholders will get a total of $1.5 billion in cash and 28.5 percent of the new company. Hughes Electronics, a unit of General Motors Corp., will own 71.5 percent of the new company immediately after
4170 the merger.The new company will combine HCG's fleet of 10 communications satellites for the U.S. market with PanAmSat's international fleet of four communications satellites. PanAmSat has four satellites under construction and HCG has three satellites in development, all of which are planned for launch through 1998.PanAmSat and HCG had combined
4170 1995 revenues of approximately $500 million.PanAmSat shareholders will have three options for payment with respect to the approximately 100 million outstanding shares of PanAmSat common stock. The companies said they will be able to choose between $30 in cash, one share of new PanAmSat common stock, or 1/2 share of
4170 new PanAmSat common stock and $15 in cash.PanAmSat's stock closed Thursday at $27.75 on Nasdaq, and GM Hughes, which trades separately from the automaker's stock, ended at $57.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.HCG is a leading provider of commercial video, voice and data satellite communications services in the United
4170 States. Its Galaxy fleet serves premier cable and broadcast television programmers, with access provided by HCG's Galaxy Network Operations unit in Long Beach, Calif."By combining Hughes' and PanAmSat's strengths in domestic and global satellite communications, we will be bringing a new level of service to our customers throughout the world,"
4170 said C. Michael Armstrong, chairman and chief executive officer of Hughes Electronics."Satellites have proven to be one of the most effective and competitive ways to communicate, whether by voice, computer, fax or video, by anyone, from anyplace, at anytime to anywhere on the planet."Corporate headquarters of the new PanAmSat Corp.
4170 will be in Greenwich, Conn., with domestic operations based in Long Beach, Calif., and international operations based in Greenwich.The deal requires government review and approval of the Federal Communications Commission, which are expected to be completed within six to 12 months. Although it is subject to PanAmSat shareholder approval, PanAmSat
4170 shareholders owning in excess of 90 percent of the voting power have agreed to vote in favour of the transaction, the companies said.</

4184 A document hidden in a presidential library, two Romanians who got lost sightseeing and chilling Congressional testimony from a former Czech general may be lifting the veil off some of the darkest secrets of the Korean War.Did North Korea keep hundreds of Americans prisoner after the end of the Korean
4184 War in 1953? 4184 the families of 8,000 men listed as missing in the Korean conflict are asking, and the answers they are getting are widely disparate.To Republican Congressman Robert Dornan, whose House of Representatives Military Personnel sub-committee has been holding hearings on the issue, the answers to all the questions are a simple
4184 and stark "Yes."The conservative congressman told Reuters this week that he planned to fly to North Korea later this year to try to convince Pyongyang to free the remaining Americans he believes are there -- a number he estimates at about 15."I will press these people to come clean. There

4184 men were captured in the war. Recently a North Korean defector claimed in a newspaper interview to have seen elderly white and black men in a secret prison camp and to have been told the same thing.But Defence Secretary William Perry says there is no evidence that North Korea is

4184 said he was involved in transferring a group of American POWs from Vietnam to Russia for experiments that would test chemical and biological war agents and the effects of atomic radiation.Not everyone believes Sejna, who now works for the U.S. Defence Intelligence Agency. 4187 writers.Hunter agreed expansion would mean new "costs to the alliance -- modest costs" for new offices at Supreme Allied Command Europe headquarters in Belgium, communiciations and possible start-up costs for headquarters in new countries permitted to join NATO in its first post-Cold War enlargement.But he stressed that countries joining NATO

4187 first new countries to join the 16-member alliance.RAND, in its recent study, said expansion of NATO -- whose core is a promise to defend member nations if they are threatened -- could cost an extra $42 billion over 15 years. That sum would rise to $100 billion if NATO troops

4200 In some places ants covered in chocolate are a culinary delicacy. Donnie Tucker prefers his ants steamed, but he is not out to tempt palates.The 49-year-old entrepreneur bills his ant steamer as an environmentally friendly way of controlling one of the southeastern United States' most troublesome pests, the red fire
4200 ant. "We're cooking them in the ground," he said. "I love killing them -- especially when you kill 100,000 at one time."Tucker sold his plant nursery in 1995 to purchase Cherokee Manufacturing Inc, in Centre, Alabama, where he has produced a dozen fire ant steamers. The machine, which looks like
4200 an industrial-sized cappuccino maker on wheels, is powered by a 12-volt battery charged by a kerosene burner.Most people living in the southeast and Puerto Rico where the ant is rife would agree with Tucker that the only good fire ant is a dead one. A cousin of bees and hornets,
4200 the fire ant emits a painful formic acid and proteins that can produce a fatal allergic reaction in an unlucky few like Alabama state Sen. Finis St. John, who died in 1984 from bites sustained while working on his Cullman County farm.In addition, the ants' mounds, some a foot (30
4200 cm) high, can damage hay mowers and other equipment. And each year the ants do millions of dollars of damage to the agriculture industry, killing calves, chickens, even prize emus and ostriches that can cost their owners $10,000 each.Both the red (solenopsis invicta) and black (solenopsis richten) fire ants arrived
4200 in the port of Mobile in 1918 as stowaways from South America, where disease and predators kept their numbers low. The red ant hails from Grosso, Brazil, while the less ubiquitous black variety left behind relatives in Uruguay and Argentina in the 1930's.Demonstrating his device on a mound in a
4200 neighbour's backyard, Tucker uses a metal probe to pump boiling hot water into the bowels of the ants' cavernous colony. Larvae that look like grains of rice bubble to the top and several dozen female worker ants try to climb the probe to sting Tucker, but the hot metal makes
4200 them hop off.Because disturbing the mound tells the ants to move their immobile queen, "you try to go right down to the bottom and fill it up as quickly as possible," Tucker said. "If the mound is rebuilt within two days, we know we didn't get the queen."A few days
4200 later, workers are still stacking thousands of their dead cohorts in piles on the top of the mound, now a mere sinkhole. Similar piles of ant corpses reveal other previously hidden entrances to the colony.The patent for the steam method of killing ants was actually obtained by a Kentucky man
4200 in 1994. Tucker heard about the process from his uncle Zack Taylor who built a prototype machine, and in December 1995 he and business partner John Dorsett made improvements on the device and signed a licensing agreement so they could begin offering Zacks's Fire Ant Control System.Tucker and Dorsett do
4200 not consider the ants their main enemies in this project. They are more concerned about their business rivals -- manufacturers of fire ant pesticides."We're taking on the wealth of the world, the chemical people," said Dorsett, who hopes people will see the device as an environmentally safe alternative to chemicals,
4200 which can kill birds, crabs and other wildlife along with the ants.Industrial models will cost about $2,500, but Tucker plans to offer a $400 version that a homeowner can store right next to the backyard grill.Steve Hill with United Industries Corp. in St. Louis, which manufactures Spectricide fire-ant pesticide, said
4200 his business was not yet running scared from the steamer. "It sounds a little far-fetched. It sounds too unwieldy and too expensive for the average Joe," he said.</

4238 Alain Juppe's centre-right government on Wednesday.Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP), Societe Generale, CCF and Credit Lyonnais all said they were cutting their base lending rates to 6.55 percent from 6.75 percent effective Monday.The base rate is the rate at which banks lend to their best customers but rates to other
4238 clients usually follow in the same direction making it generally cheaper for French companies and consumers to borrow money.Economists said that even if the move was limited, it was one more boost that could bolster consumer and corporate morale and eventually deliver the consumption and investment rise which the government
4238 was counting on."It's more symbolic than effective on the economy," said ABN Amro economist Philippe Brossard in Paris.Base lending rates applied to a relatively limited amount of funding, he noted. 4256 Belgian francs, rather than at the end of the day as is currently done.But under plans drawn up by the Frankfurt-based European Monetary Institute (EMI), the system will also be used after EMU starts in 1999 to send monetary policy signals to the market.ELLIPS, or Electronic Large Value Interbank Payments

4262 A former president of the German Bundesbank, Helmut Schlesinger, said Europe's currency union should begin as planned at the end of the decade, even if less than half of all nations will be ready to join in 1999.Echoing a recent wave of more optimistic assessments that the planned currency union
4262 will be launched on January 1, 1999 as nations still struggle to meet entry criteria, Schlesinger said that at least six nations should be able to pass the test."It seems likely that EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) will begin in 1999 with six to ten member states," Schlesinger wrote
4262 in an article published in this week's edition of the The Economist.Schlesinger, who guided the Bundesbank through turbulent times between 1991 and 1993 when both Britain and Italy left the European Exchange Rate Mechanism, shrugged off calls for a delayed EMU start to give nations more time to qualify.While Schlesinger
4262 concedes a wider circle of membership would be preferable, he argued that it is impossible to forecast when more nations would pass the entry test. "Bearing this in mind, there are no good reasons for postponement."To join the union, nations must show stable exchange and moderate inflation rates and meet
4262 deficit and debt criteria whose reference values should be three percent and 60 percent of gross domestic product respectively.At a time when many nations, including Germany, risk exceeding both the deficit and debt reference values, Schlesinger urged that the leeway for evaluating the criteria, enshrined in the Maastricht Treaty, must
4262 remain intact."The trouble is that considerations of this kind are difficult to translate into simple numerical formulae," Schlesinger said, adding, "it is important that...a certain discretionary leeway should remain, enabling other economic considerations to be taken into account."Political leaders will determine in 1998 which nations will be eligible to join
4262 the union after reviewing their 1997 economic data.Schlesinger, remembered as a hardline Bundesbank president never permitting the bank to swerve from its main goals of keeping the mark stable and battling inflation, also warned policy makers against undermining EMU with words and actions.The entry criteria will be effective only if
4262 they are wholly endorsed by finance ministers and used in support of their government policies, Schlesinger said."Ministers should not be devoting staff time to circumventing measures by setting up shadow budgets or shifting expenditures to quasi-private-sector or state-owned banks and enterprises," Schlesinger warned.Similarly he urged policy makers to use more
4262 discretion when firing off comments about EMU. "How is confidence in the euro to be gained if those responsible for it find it difficult to say a good word about it," Schlesinger asked.In the past, markets have been particularly sensitive to a raft of negative comments on EMU. But now
4262 Schlesinger said that financial markets appear more convinced that a number of member states will be ready to go ahead with monetary union.--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525</

4272 Can the Roman Catholic Church expect its bishops and priests to remain celibate in a fast-lane modern world filled with temptations?That is the thorny question raised yet again by the case of a Scottish bishop who fathered a child with one woman when he was a priest 15 years ago
4272 and disappeared with another, divorced, woman this month."This is a terrible blow to the Church because an individual in the highest level of responsibility...has totally betrayed his trust," Archbishop John Foley, head of the Vatican's communications department, told Reuters Television.The saga of Bishop Roderick Wright is only the latest sex
4272 scandal to rock a Church whose bishops and priests Pope John Paul insists must remain chaste.Wright is at least the fifth Catholic bishop to resign in the past six years over acknowledged or alleged affairs. In 1992 Irish Bishop Eamonn Casey also resigned after admitting that he too had fathered
4272 a son.The media has made it more difficult for the Church to sweep such cases under the carpet, as they had done for centuries.It is impossible to determine the number of clerics -- many of them often working and living in lonely conditions -- who have violated their chastity vows.
4272 Foley said many priests were under "tremendous stress" in modern society.In 1990, a study said as many as a third of Roman Catholic priests in the United States were sexually active.It was compiled by A.W. Richard Sipe, an ordained Catholic priest and professor at Johns Hopkins University for the book
4272 "A Secret World: Sexuality and the Search for Celibacy".The Roman Catholic Church demands celibacy in order to foster single-minded devotion to God and the ministry.But some Catholics believe that allowing priests to marry -- as is permitted in most other Churches such as the Anglican and Lutheran Churches -- would
4272 reduce the risk of sex scandals."The spate of cases that have emerged over the last few years about priests and bishops in sex relations is another sign that celibacy just doesn't work," said Frances Kissling, president of the Washington-based Catholics for a Free Choice."Celibacy should be optional. We had married
4272 priests for almost the first 1,000 years of the Church. Most of the apostles were married," she told Reuters on Friday.Celibacy is a discipline and not a dogma. Thus, it can be overturned or modified by a future Pope or Church Council.Britain's Cardinal Basil Hume said the Church could stop
4272 losing many excellent candidates for the priesthood if it relaxed its celibacy ruling."It is not divine law. It is Church law, so any Pope or General Council could change it," he told BBC Radio on Tuesday.But Foley, the Vatican archbishop, said: "It is within their power to do so. It
4272 is very unlikely that they would."When the Pope visited the United States last year, Catholic scholar Richard Schoenherr, author of "Full Pews and Empty Altars", said that unless celibacy is abandoned, there will be too few priests in the 21st Century to minister to Catholics.Joaquin Navarro-Valls, the chief Vatican spokesman,
4272 tried to control the fallout from the Wright affair on Friday."The problem is not whether the Pope thinks celibacy should remain," said Navarro-Valls, who is travelling with the 76-year-old Polish Pontiff in France. "It is not a personal doctrine. It is a doctrine of the Church."In the Bible, Christ refers
4272 to "eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven" and St Paul says "he who is unmarried (can) care for the things that belong to the Lord".The earliest formulation of the discipline of celibacy in the Church did not appear until the Council of Elvria, some three centuries after Christ's death.The first
4272 written universal law making celibacy a must was enacted by the Second Lateran Council in 1139 and the 1563 Council of Trent ruled definitively on the matter.</

4292 From mad cows to a single currency, from the way Europe takes decisions to its plans for security policy, Britain is sounding a discordant note in the European Union and testing its partners' patience to the limit.Long viewed from the continent as one of the most reluctant of European states,
4292 Britain has been accused this year of finding new levels of isolation in the EU under its Conservative Prime Minister John Major."The psychological climate (has) deteriorated dramatically, undermining whatever residual goodwill towards John Major and his ministers still existed," Peter Ludlow, director of the Centre for European Policy Studies, writes
4292 in a new study.Britain responds to such criticisms by noting that the EU has adopted many British views on issues such as trade and subsidiarity -- devolved decision-making -- and by arguing that being a partner does not mean having to agree all the time."Britain has an alternative vision for
4292 Europe.... It is a vision based on choosing carefully the stepping-stones toward closer cooperation; not jumping blindly toward ever greater integration, flailing for footholds that may prove precarious or illusory," Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said this week.But clashes between London and its partners have become commonplace.The latest storm centres on
4292 Britain's decision to put off a cull of cattle most at risk from mad cow disease -- a slaughter Major agreed with fellow EU leaders at a June summit in Florence in exchange for a promise from his partners to consider lifting the worldwide ban on British beef exports.Major backpedalled
4292 on Thursday because he saw little chance of winning approval for the cull from a parliament dominated, vocally at least, by so-called Euro-sceptics, a group of British Conservatives leery of closer European integration.The EU, in turn, dismissed any notion of lifting its beef export ban until Britain met already agreed
4292 terms.To obtain the Florence compromise in the first place, Britain had launched a campaign of non-cooperation that infuriated its partners, leaving some threatening to pay London back at a later date.Ludlow and others note, however, that Britain's go-it-alone action over beef is only one of a number of areas where
4292 it is at odds with its partners.At the inter-governmental conference (IGC), the EU's treaty review designed to prepare the bloc for the entry of new members from eastern Europe and the Mediterranean, Britain has staked out positions quite contrary to the general trend.It has, for example, refused any reduction in
4292 the power of member states to veto EU decision-making. Although others plan to defend their veto in specific areas, most accept that some moves towards more majority voting will be needed in a larger Union.On security policy, London -- as a major player -- has insisted that any move to
4292 a common European defence must be completely outside the EU.Sweden and Finland, two neutrals that might have been expected to support such a stand, deserted in favour of a coordinated EU policy for dealing with humanitarian and peacekeeping activities.France, the only significant military power in Europe other than Britain, remains
4292 a strong advocate of a European defence structure.Britain's main positions at the IGC -- listened to politely by its partners -- have been calls for power to be returned to nation states and for the EU Court of Justice to be reined in.Most other EU states are more interested in
4292 a further pooling of sovereignty than in stepping back from integration.Britain also remains on the outside in the drive for a single currency. Having secured an opt-out, Major's government is now torn over whether and when to use it.Ludlow suggests that hopes in London that it would become the champion
4292 of countries left outside the single currency foundered on the unwillingness of the others to follow.The split between London and the rest has many in Europe assuming and hoping that Major will lose the next British election to what they believe will be a more cooperative Labour Party. 4292 then, says Ludlow, not all will be well in cross-Channel relations."Although the atmosphere will almost certainly be more cheerful," he writes, "the basic conclusion is that the British will face a long march back to the heart of Europe." REUTER</

4330 Central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Friday Belgium might use foreign exchange reserves generated by previous gold sales to help cut its national debt.Gold sales in the past five years have left the central bank with 236 billion francs in the form of foreign exchange reserves on its books,
4330 on which the government receives interest."I do not exclude that in order to make our balance sheet more transparent...it might be that a part of this capital gain should be used, without influencing the deficit, to reduce the gross debt," Verplaetse told Reuters Financial Television."This is not window dressing, it
4330 is a real transaction. We will reduce our public debt in foreign currencies for that amount," he said.Verplaetse said the Belgian government aimed to cut its debt to gross domestic product ratio by 10 percent between 1993-97.Belgium's debt, the highest in the European Union, was 137.9 percent of GDP in
4330 1993 and is forecast to fall to 131.8 percent of GDP by the end of 1996."(The reduction) will be done firstly by reducing the budget deficit, by selling some public assets and by better management of the public debt," Verplaetse said.Belgium's 1997 budget, currently being negotiated by ministers, is due
4330 to be presented to parliament on October 1.At present the Belgian National Bank's statutes prevent its gold being used directly to help cut the debt, although a small fraction, around 2.75 percent, can be used to mint and sell commemorative coins, the proceeds from which go directly to the Treasury.Since
4330 the law on the gold reserves was drawn up in 1987 a little over two percent of the gold has been used in this way."We have important gold assets. In the last years we have sold some and the capital gain we got is a liability of the central bank
4330 the counterparty of which is foreign currencies on which the government receives interest," Verplaetse told RFTV.Under the Maastricht Treaty rules for economic and monetary union (EMU), countries joining a single current must have brought their debts to 60 percent of GDP or be approaching that level at a "satisfactory pace."Belgium's
4330 net debt, which forms the greater part of the gross debt as defined for the purposes of Maastricht, was 9,828 billion Belgian francs in August, of which roughly 970 billion was held in foreign currencies.Verplaetse said that although the debt was high, it was more than compensated by the country's
4330 high national savings rate.Belgium already meets other criteria in the Treaty on inflation, long-term interest rates and exchange rate stability.The government has said its main objective is to make sure Belgium fully qualifies by reducing its public deficit to below the EMU target of three percent of GDP by the
4330 end of 1997.The deficit is forecast by the central bank to be around 3.1 percent of GDP at the end of 1996.Including the 236 billion franc capital gain on recent gold sales, the National Bank's foreign exchange reserves amounted to 408 billion francs on September 16.In addition the bank held
4330 the equivalent of 173 billion Belgian francs in gold bullion.-- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710</

4336 excise duties should be brought more closely into line - COM(95)285.Having failed to get European Union governments to agree to harmonise national excise duties as part of the internal market programme, the European Commission persuaded them to introduce minimum rates of duty on tobacco, alcohol and mineral oils from 1993.MEPs
4336 failed to agree whether or not to recommend sticking to the current 57 percent minimum level of taxation on cigarettes, or whether excise duties on hand-rolling tobacco should be increased to the same level as the duty on cigarettes.Instead, they asked the Commission to examine whether the taxation system produced
4336 serious distortions of competition and, if necessary, come up with proposals for improving it.Cigarette prices should be increased to similar levels throughout the EU, for health reasons and to prevent possible distortion of competition, parliament said in a report drafted by German Christian Democrat Karl von Wogau.The report urged the

4336 fraud and illicit production.But they were unable to agree on a proposal to tax wine and beer, like spirits, according to their percentage content of alcohol, or to a zero rating for wine.As a compromise they recommended, if not convergence then at least an attempt to prevent a widening of
4336 the difference in rates on wine, beer and spirits.MEPs were also unable to decide whether high excise duties on wine, while useful to combat over-production and alcohol abuse, were appropriate at a time when the sector is particularly exposed.They asked the Commission to come up with a report on the
4336 issue within a year.Parliament threw the ball back into the Commission's court when it came to mineral oils too.Von Wogau's report highlights three problems with the current wide difference in prices for motor and heating fuel oils.The absence of taxation on natural gas and coal is distorting the internal market
4336 in heating fuel; the low cost of heating gas oil in Luxembourg and Belgium is diverting orders from France and Germany and leading to fraud; and cross-border shopping for low-cost petrol and diesel in Luxembourg is on the increase.MEPs urged the Commission to examine ways of using excise duties as
4336 fiscal intruments to encourage environmental protection, cleaner energy and transport, and a switch away from taxation on labour.Less polluting products should be subject to more favourable rates of duty than other fuels, parliament said.</

4362 As European Union governments struggle to meet the budgetary preconditions of economic and monetary union (EMU), questions are being raised over whether they are being a bit fast and loose with their figures.With most struggling to bring their deficits near three percent of GDP next year -- the Maastricht treaty's
4362 requirement -- every opportunity is being taken to squeeze out extra money through a variety of means, some of which are considered controversial.The most notable case has been that of France. The French government plans to use a whopping 37.5 billion francs ($7.4 billion) in its budget accounts next year
4362 through the process of privatisating France Telecom.This one-off item has so far received a cautious response from the European Commission, with Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Thursday saying the French proposal probably conformed with EU rules.An eventual opinion by the Commission will be forwarded to EU finance ministers
4362 for final consideration.Economists, however, say the French plan is an ingenous piece of accounting, well within the bounds of EU law but at odds with what one would consider budgetary rigour."It's perfectly acceptable within Maastricht, but it is not in the spirit of the treaty," says Bruce Kasman, economist at
4362 J.P. Morgan in London.While such tinkering can be of crucial importance in helping a government raise revenue, in this particular case the decision may also throw light on the political momentum behind EMU, experts say.Germany, which has argued forcefully for strict adherence to Maastricht, has so far not criticised Paris
4362 for its inventive application of EU laws. Some think such reticence suggests an ironclad political committment between the two countries to push EMU forward."The fact that you're not hearing screaming from on the part of the Germans says the political commitment is very strong," adds Kasman.Evidence of this type of
4362 accounting has also been seen in the latest budget plan from the Netherlands. The Dutch government this week unveiled a 1997 budget which will help reduce its outstanding debt to an expected 76.2 percent of GDP.Under Maastricht, countries wishing to qualify for EMU must have their debt levels "sufficiently diminishing"
4362 and "approaching" the 60 percent reference value.But a large percentage of next year's budget improvement will be due to the drawing down of an obsolete government cash reserve held at the Dutch central bank.Analysts say countries which are marginally on the edge of meeting the treaty's deficit and debt criteria
4362 are most likely to use such accounting tactics.Spain, in particular, was cited as one such potential candidate.European Commission officials say they fully recognise how such maneouverings could be interpreted as slight-of-hand accounting and not in accordance with proper rules.But they also note that a final judgment on France's proposal must
4362 be made in accordance with the law, otherwise they would face sharp criticism from other countries whose deficits are on the verge of meeting Maastricht."We are well aware of the criticism we would face if we acted in a way that was less than credible," said one official.</
4363 Like an uninvited guest, the question of who will and who won't make it into European monetary union in 1999 will lurk at the edge of the party when Europe's finance ministers meet in Dublin this weekend.It is a question few ministers will talk about publicly, but which threatens to
4363 create a north-south divide -- between rich northern European states poised to join a single currency first and Mediterranean countries determined not to be left behind.The practicalities of monetary union and relations between the 'ins and outs' "would really threaten the coherence of the European Union," CS First Boston economist
4363 Sean Shepley said. "That's why Spain and Italy are desperate to get in."The issue is becoming more pressing as the EU tries to work out the nuts and bolts of exactly how monetary union will be run, with finance ministers in Dublin to consider, among other things, a special council
4363 of ministers which will oversee Economic and Monetary Union and exclude non-members.In theory, Maastricht treaty fiscal and economic standards should weed out countries with weaker economies.But as the 1997 deadline approaches for judging which countries qualify for EMU in 1999, everyone is making a last dash to the finishing line
4363 with one-off measures which comply with the letter if not the spirit of the Maastricht treaty.France set the tone earlier this week with a budget which relies on a one-off transfer from France Telecom to cover future pension liabilities to get its deficit down to the required three percent of
4363 gross domestic product in 1997.Now Spain is going all out, with a 1997 budget due next week meant to cut its deficit/GDP ratio to three percent.That in turn is making Italy panic about being left out of the first wave of EMU, and it is hoping its plans to get
4363 the deficit to 2.99 percent of GDP -- albeit a year late in 1998 -- might help it to talk its way in.None of that matches Germany's vision of a core of rich northern countries with stable currencies which would underpin the new "euro" currency when it replaces the mark
4363 in 1999.German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said this week he thought the single currency would probably begin with five to seven members.Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet hinted last week who he thought should join first, according to minutes of a closed-door parliamentary hearing."He insisted on the fact that the credibility
4363 of the single currency was largely supported by the stability seen for nine and a half years in exchange rates of seven countries in the European Monetary System Exchange Rate Mechanism (France, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Denmark and Austria)," the minutes said.But economists say it is hard to see
4363 how a country like Spain could be excluded if it does meet Maastricht standards.France's own creative accounting has left the field wide open for other countries to follow suit, economists say.One option would be to convince some countries they would be better off waiting a few years, rather than submitting
4363 their economies to the rigours of monetary union too soon.Countries with too high inflation rates would lose competitiveness from early EMU entry, while EMU members would face higher interest rates due to the damage to the euro's credibility, Trichet was quoted as saying last week.Marie Owens-Thomsen, economist at Banque Internationale
4363 de Placement (BIP), said one deterrent might be a rebound in German growth, which would lead to higher German interest rates, forcing up rates in the rest of the euro zone."That could put the Mediterranean countries in the same kind of policy dilemna that they were in after German unification,"
4363 she said. Germany's decision to jack up rates after unification forced up rates and squeezed economies everywhere in Europe.But barring that, the political risks of being left out of a currency club that is taking on ever more institutional form as monetary union approaches might be too big to accept."At
4363 the end of the day they all have a vote each. I don't see how they can be motivated to vote against themselves," Owens-Thomsen said."Politically it is difficult to be convinced you are not going to lose from being outside," Shepley said. "What you have to start looking for is

4383 long-term effect of such a move would be disasterous ... because of inflation," he said.Gehrig also said there were limits on the amount of expansion that the SNB could allow, but did not specify those limits except to say the SNB continued to observe its medium-term monetary expansion goals.He said
4383 the SNB meanwhile would continue providing the economy with enough liquidity, and at money market rates, to fuel an improvement."We will basically continue on the same path as we have been," Gehrig said.Speaking to reporters here during a meeting of the Swiss Bankers Association, he said that a sustained drop
4383 in the franc over a longer time period would pose a "disasterous risk" to Swiss price stability."I do not think it would be appropriate to say we should push the franc significantly down and then we are out of the problem," Gehrig said.Gehrig did not specify how much the franc
4383 would have to weaken before it posed a significant danger to price stability.The Swiss franc was weakened slightly versus other currencies in recent weeks after peaking at four-month highs against the dollar in late July.It traded at 1.2425 francs to the dollar this morning. The dollar had slipped as low
4383 as 1.1840 francs at the end of July.The SNB has said in the past that is worried about an overvaluation of the franc, which hurts Swiss exports. It has in the last two months worked to keep money market rates low, hoping to discourage speculative demand for the franc.Inflation in
4383 Switzerland is currently near zero, and some SNB officials view prospects of deflation, rather than inflation as the greatest risk.Earlier this week, the Swiss government reported that the country's gross domestic product in the second quarter fell by 0.9 percent, its sixth straight quarterly decline measured against the previous quarter.Gehrig
4383 said the SNB would continue to provide money market liquidity for the time being, saying such moves were aimed at helping the economy.He was optimistic that the Swiss economy would rebound in the coming three to four quarters.Asked about the prospects for a recovery in the Swiss economy, Gehrig said:
4383 "I am reasonably optimistic for the next three to four quarters."($1.00 = 1.2425 Swiss francs)</

4392 The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) should make the most of an oil revenue windfall by keeping quiet about its output quota violations and let surging demand quietly absorb the extra barrels, OPEC delegates and oil analysts say.The 11-member cartel would be ill-advised to remonstrate publicly with its biggest
4392 quota violators, they say, or formally raise its production ceiling to take advantage of a surprisingly high oil price.World benchmark North Sea Brent crude oil, looking set to average about $19.50 a barrel this year, or $2.50 more than in 1995, should bring in an extra $20-$25 billion in OPEC
4392 export revenues this year."OPEC should just sit back, enjoy the high oil price, not plan anything and go with the flow," said veteran OPEC watcher Vahan Zanoyhan, senior director at the Petroleum Finance Co. (PFC).A public OPEC row could stampede jittery futures markets to skim the top off the price
4392 if oil traders believe such a spat could fracture the once-mighty cartel."They're getting so much more revenue at the moment. They don't want to jeopardise that by having an open row about quotas because it could destabilise the market," said Leo Drollas, chief economist at the Centre for Global Energy
4392 Studies (CGES).OPEC delegates from several key member states, including those of the influential Gulf, hope that a meeting next week in Vienna of the group's quota compliance committee is a brief, inconsequential affair.They will urge committee chairman, Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, not to make good on a promise for
4392 a "very specific programme" to deal with overproduction."We would advise Mr Aghazadeh to not make much about the quota problems. In fact, we question the logic of even holding this meeting. The market is absorbing OPEC supplies with no problems," said an industry official from an OPEC Gulf member.On Wednesday,
4392 Aghazadeh will meet fellow committee members -- OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman and ministers from Nigeria and Libya -- to compare official production figures with those from independent monitors which consistently show OPEC over its mandated quotas.Analysts say nearly every member is producing as much oil as it can --
4392 with the notable exception of the world's largest producer Saudi Arabia. Collective output is about 800,000 over a ceiling set at 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd).But the high price seems to vindicate a decision by OPEC ministers in June to keep quiet about quota busting and not cut production
4392 to make room for a return of Iraqi exports under a United Nations oil-for-food scheme.In June, OPEC raised its ceiling to 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) to reflect a rise of 700,000 bpd in Iraqi output expected when the U.N. plan was implemented.But that plan has been put on
4392 hold following the military confrontation between Baghdad and Washington and traders do not expect a resumption in Iraqi exports before the end of the year.That delay along with other Middle East tensions, unexpected shortfalls in non-OPEC oil supply and strong demand ahead of the northern winter has driven oil prices
4392 to post-Gulf War highs."We have long predicted oil prices would be strong this year because of lower than expected non-OPEC production and good demand. It looks like we were right," said a Gulf source familar with Saudi oil policy.So successful was OPEC's "do-nothing" decision in June, that if prices stay
4392 at current levels the group looks poised to leave matters well alone once more when ministers next meet in late November."With the threat of Iraq's return always on our shoulders and the uncertainity of price movements, we really should not do anything radical in November. To increase the ceiling and
4392 then come down is bloody difficult," said an OPEC delegate from a Gulf country.</

4395 The European Union on Friday flatly ruled out any lifting of a worldwide ban on British beef exports after London decided to shelve plans for a cull of cattle most at risk from mad cow disease.Not mincing words, the EU farm commissioner and the farm ministers of France and EU
4395 president Ireland all said Britain must abide by an EU summit deal reached in June designed to defuse the so-called "beef war".Foreign Ministers Klaus Kinkel of Germany and Herve de Charette of France also said lifting the ban was now out of the question.Resurgence of the six-month-old crisis is likely
4395 to inflame an informal meeting of EU farm ministers beginning on Sunday in Killarney, Ireland. It was otherwise intended to focus on ways to restore battered consumer confidence in beef.Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler was first out of the blocks in attacking the British government's decision, which came late on Thursday
4395 evening."As long as they do not meet the pre-conditions and until we have a working document from them which we can carefully check, then an end to the export ban is simply not a possibility," Fischler told the European Parliament.He said that Britain was still bound by its agreement at
4395 the summit in Florence to slaughter up to 147,000 cattle as part of a plan that would eventually lead to the EU lifting its worldwide ban on British beef exports.The British government decided to suspend the planned cull because of research suggesting that mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy
4395 (BSE), would die out in five years.Irish Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates warned Britain that there were no prospects of lifting the ban and that its farmers would be the biggest losers if it abandoned the cull.But he told Irish national radio he would strive to resolve the impasse during the
4395 informal farm ministers' meeting in southwest Ireland.Britain's partners were adamant.Kinkel, whose country has been the most concerned about a threat to humans from BSE, said:"A unilateral change by the British government is...not acceptable. The main priority is the health of the consumer. The ban on importing British cattle, beef and
4395 other products will remain in force."French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur told French radio: "The embargo remains, I'd like to add that I am going to ask for checks to be increased."British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said London had called off the selective cull because of fierce opposition in Britain's parliament.The
4395 British government has been repeatedly at odds with its EU partners since admitting in March that a fatal, brain-wasting disease could be caught by humans who ate BSE-infected beef.In Killarney, Fischler is due to present proposals for an EU meat-labelling scheme aimed at reassuring shoppers about where the beef has
4395 come from and how it was produced.Beef promotion schemes, especially on foreign markets, and incentives for farmers to rear their herds in fields on grass rather than in sheds on compound feeds will also be discussed.The Commission's chief spokesman, Nikolaus van der Pas, said in a statement that the Commission
4395 would stick to the Florence framework which was based on the latest scientific evidence.But he added that EU scientists would assess the latest studies, one by Oxford University and another which shows that BSE can be passed from cows to calves. But it would take until at least mid-October before
4395 any conclusions could be drawn.Van der Pas held out a ray of hope for farmers with grass-fed herds which were free of BSE."The Commission remains open to discuss possibilities that may exist for a relaxation of export restrictions for animals from certified herds possibly on a regional basis," he said.Northern
4395 Ireland is pressing strongly for the ban to be lifted on its grass-fed herds, saying it has an effective computer system to track the origin and feed of all its cattle.</

4397 towards European economic and monetary union (EMU).Soon after markets digest the results of that meeting, they will be confronted with a Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, where many expect a U.S. interest rate rise.By the end of the week, attention is set to turn to an International Monetary
4397 Fund/World Bank summit, which begins on Saturday and runs through the following week. On the data front, the week is relatively light, with a smattering of Japanese and U.S. figures likely to be the main features."The first and obvious focus is the FOMC," said George Magnus, senior international economist at
4397 UBS. "The U.S. market is pretty much priced for a modest rise in the funds rate."Elizabeth Legge, senior economist at Bankgesellschaft Berlin, said an increase of 25 basis points in the federal funds rate, currently 5.25 percent, would not have a major impact on markets given the degree to which
4397 it has been discounted."If more, it might have some impact on the dollar but I'm not even sure of that because the dollar has got so geared up for a hike," she said.Bal Sandhu, European strategist at Kleinwort Benson, said Wall Street and European stock markets, which have been bullish,
4397 as well as the dollar, all were in state of pre-FOMC tension."That's going to be the driving force. It's all going to revolve around whether Wall Street can take any prospective rate hike on the chin," he said.The big issue at the weekend Ecofin meeting is a so-called Stability Pact,
4397 which many analysts expect will be agreed in some form. The pact is designed to set sanctions to ensure countries continue to observe strict fiscal criteria after EMU begins.But as with the FOMC meeting, analysts said a great deal of the EMU saga has been absorbed by markets."European markets have
4397 got a lot of this already in their sails," said Magnus, noting how so many European bond spreads were trading at or near historic lows against Bund yields."Maybe the markets would respond in a negative way if the stability pact emerged without any teeth, but the word is that there
4397 will be some form of (fiscal) provisions," Magnus said."The strong performance of the European markets of the last three to four weeks is in contrast to the U.S. and it reflects that the markets are taking EMU even more seriously than they were before," he said.Britain has a monetary meeting
4397 scheduled for Monday but analysts say there is next to no chance of an interest rate cut after data showing vibrant consumer activity in the past week.Final second quarter gross domestic product data are due on Tuesday for Britain, followed by trade figures on Thursday.The U.S. has existing home sales
4397 for August on Wednesday, durable goods on Thursday and final Q2 GDP on Friday.In Japan, Friday will be a big day with consumer price, unemployment and retail sales statistics all scheduled.But analysts said that with authorities keeping a lid on call money rates, the market appears immune to anything other
4397 than GDP data or the closely watched "tankan" survey by the Bank of Japan, neither of which are due."As long as the economic numbers are reasonably in line with expectations the impact will be fairly small," Legge said.</

4428 of ministers which will oversee Economic and Monetary Union and exclude non-members.In theory, Maastricht treaty fiscal and economic standards should weed out countries with weaker economies.But as the 1997 deadline approaches for judging which countries qualify for EMU in 1999, everyone is making a last dash to the finishing line

4428 of the single currency was largely supported by the stability seen for nine and a half years in exchange rates of seven countries in the European Monetary System Exchange Rate Mechanism (France, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Denmark and Austria)," the minutes said.But economists say it is hard to see
4428 how a country like Spain could be excluded if it does meet Maastricht standards.France's own creative accounting has left the field wide open for other countries to follow suit, economists say.One option would be to convince some countries they would be better off waiting a few years, rather than submitting
4428 their economies to the rigours of monetary union too soon.Countries with too high inflation rates would lose competitiveness from early EMU entry, while EMU members would face higher interest rates due to the damage to the euro's credibility, Trichet was quoted as saying last week.Marie Owens-Thomsen, economist at Banque Internationale
4428 de Placement (BIP), said one deterrent might be a rebound in German growth, which would lead to higher German interest rates, forcing up rates in the rest of the euro zone."That could put the Mediterranean countries in the same kind of policy dilemna that they were in after German unification,"
4428 she said. Germany's decision to jack up rates after unification forced up rates and squeezed economies everywhere in Europe.But barring that, the political risks of being left out of a currency club that is taking on ever more institutional form as monetary union approaches might be too big to accept."At
4428 the end of the day they all have a vote each. I don't see how they can be motivated to vote against themselves," Owens-Thomsen said."Politically it is difficult to be convinced you are not going to lose from being outside," Shepley said. "What you have to start looking for is
4428 something that can be provided to these countries," he added.</

4435 As European Union governments struggle to meet the budgetary preconditions of economic and monetary union (EMU), questions are being raised over whether they are being a bit fast and loose with their figures.With most struggling to bring their deficits near three percent of GDP next year -- the Maastricht treaty's
4435 requirement -- every opportunity is being taken to squeeze out extra money through a variety of means, some of which are considered controversial.The most notable case has been that of France. The French government plans to use a whopping 37.5 billion francs ($7.4 billion) in its budget accounts next year
4435 through the process of privatisating France Telecom.This one-off item has so far received a cautious response from the European Commission, with Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Thursday saying the French proposal probably conformed with EU rules.An eventual opinion by the Commission will be forwarded to EU finance ministers
4435 for final consideration.Economists, however, say the French plan is an ingenous piece of accounting, well within the bounds of EU law but at odds with what one would consider budgetary rigour."It's perfectly acceptable within Maastricht, but it is not in the spirit of the treaty," says Bruce Kasman, economist at
4435 J.P. Morgan in London.While such tinkering can be of crucial importance in helping a government raise revenue, in this particular case the decision may also throw light on the political momentum behind EMU, experts say.Germany, which has argued forcefully for strict adherence to Maastricht, has so far not criticised Paris
4435 for its inventive application of EU laws. Some think such reticence suggests an ironclad political committment between the two countries to push EMU forward."The fact that you're not hearing screaming from on the part of the Germans says the political commitment is very strong," adds Kasman.Evidence of this type of
4435 accounting has also been seen in the latest budget plan from the Netherlands. The Dutch government this week unveiled a 1997 budget which will help reduce its outstanding debt to an expected 76.2 percent of GDP.Under Maastricht, countries wishing to qualify for EMU must have their debt levels "sufficiently diminishing"
4435 and "approaching" the 60 percent reference value.But a large percentage of next year's budget improvement will be due to the drawing down of an obsolete government cash reserve held at the Dutch central bank.Analysts say countries which are marginally on the edge of meeting the treaty's deficit and debt criteria
4435 are most likely to use such accounting tactics.Spain, in particular, was cited as one such potential candidate.European Commission officials say they fully recognise how such maneouverings could be interpreted as slight-of-hand accounting and not in accordance with proper rules.But they also note that a final judgment on France's proposal must
4435 be made in accordance with the law, otherwise they would face sharp criticism from other countries whose deficits are on the verge of meeting Maastricht."We are well aware of the criticism we would face if we acted in a way that was less than credible," said one official.</

4436 say some non-aligned nations and unsuccessful NATO candidates may join a tighter grouping of would-be members and affiliates.Russia could also join this intensified Partnership for Peace -- dubbed "PfP-Two", "Enhanced PfP" or "PfP Plus" -- which aims to boost non-members' military cooperation and political contact with NATO, a U.S. diplomat
4436 told Reuters."Let's include the Russians," said Derek Shearer, U.S. ambassador to Finland.The plan aims to demonstrate to Russia that NATO is not belligerent and ease the concerns of countries that may fall into a security "grey zone" after the alliance expands."A 'PfP Plus' should generate the necessary reassurance that the
4436 security of an enlarged NATO and its partners remains closely linked," said NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.Of the 27 current members of the PfP scheme aimed at uniting former European foes, Shearer said between 15 and 20 could join a super PfP, which could involve specific liaison officers and working groups
4436 and would be based on charters."It's just a notion of enhancing PfP to show where we're going in Europe," he said.The scheme builds on a milestone speech by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in Stuttgart earlier this month in which he outlined a vision of a New Atlantic Community
4436 which would erase former Cold War barriers.Christopher spoke of forming a New Atlantic Partnership Council based on a charter between NATO and Russia and said the alliance should involve non-members in the PfP programme.NATO's Solana, in a speech to the international institute for strategic studies (IISS), said the current scheme
4436 was already the most successful military cooperation programme in Europe's history."But (it) has to be upgraded and deepened to reflect the new situation which will exist after NATO enlargement," he said."This could entail, among other things, offering interested partners greater involvement in NATO military planning, activities and structures as well
4436 as in consultations with the alliance."Czechoslovakia, Hungary and Poland are widely regarded as top of the list for inclusion in an expanded NATO. 4436 Lithuania, have said expansion in central Europe may leave former Soviet satellites in a security void which, under some circumstances, Russia could try to fill."We want to see the avoidance of the grey area by the development of a super-PfP," another Western diplomat said.With Europe still in transition from the
4436 Cold War period, the plan aims to let countries address threats like terrorism and drug-trafficking, which are now more likely causes of instability than invasion, diplomats said.</

4448 granted to shipyards.EU industry ministers decided in 1995 that current aid rules would apply in the absence of the OECD deal, but only until October 1, which is why a new decision now needs to be taken.In July, the Commission proposed legislation to enable the EU to extend the directive
