4449 quota violators, they say, or formally raise its production ceiling to take advantage of a surprisingly high oil price.World benchmark North Sea Brent crude oil, looking set to average about $19.50 a barrel this year, or $2.50 more than in 1995, should bring in an extra $20-$25 billion in OPEC
4449 export revenues this year."OPEC should just sit back, enjoy the high oil price, not plan anything and go with the flow," said veteran OPEC watcher Vahan Zanoyhan, senior director at the Petroleum Finance Co. (PFC).A public OPEC row could stampede jittery futures markets to skim the top off the price
4449 if oil traders believe such a spat could fracture the once-mighty cartel."They're getting so much more revenue at the moment. They don't want to jeopardise that by having an open row about quotas because it could destabilise the market," said Leo Drollas, chief economist at the Centre for Global Energy
4449 Studies (CGES).OPEC delegates from several key member states, including those of the influential Gulf, hope that a meeting next week in Vienna of the group's quota compliance committee is a brief, inconsequential affair.They will urge committee chairman, Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, not to make good on a promise for
4449 a "very specific programme" to deal with overproduction."We would advise Mr Aghazadeh to not make much about the quota problems. In fact, we question the logic of even holding this meeting. The market is absorbing OPEC supplies with no problems," said an industry official from an OPEC Gulf member.On Monday,
4449 Aghazadeh will meet fellow committee members -- OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman and ministers from Nigeria and Libya -- to compare official production figures with those from independent monitors which consistently show OPEC over its mandated quotas.Analysts say nearly every member is producing as much oil as it can --
4449 with the notable exception of the world's largest producer Saudi Arabia. Collective output is about 800,000 over a ceiling set at 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd).But the high price seems to vindicate a decision by OPEC ministers in June to keep quiet about quota busting and not cut production
4449 to make room for a return of Iraqi exports under a United Nations oil-for-food scheme.In June, OPEC raised its ceiling to 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) to reflect a rise of 700,000 bpd in Iraqi output expected when the U.N. plan was implemented.But that plan has been put on
4449 hold following the military confrontation between Baghdad and Washington and traders do not expect a resumption in Iraqi exports before the end of the year.That delay along with other Middle East tensions, unexpected shortfalls in non-OPEC oil supply and strong demand ahead of the northern winter has driven oil prices
4449 to post-Gulf War highs."We have long predicted oil prices would be strong this year because of lower than expected non-OPEC production and good demand. It looks like we were right," said a Gulf source familar with Saudi oil policy.So successful was OPEC's "do-nothing" decision in June, that if prices stay
4449 at current levels the group looks poised to leave matters well alone once more when ministers next meet in late November."With the threat of Iraq's return always on our shoulders and the uncertainity of price movements, we really should not do anything radical in November. To increase the ceiling and
4449 then come down is bloody difficult," said an OPEC delegate from a Gulf country.</
4450 Prospects of an early lifting of a European ban on British beef sales vanished on Friday after the government bowed to domestic political pressure and shelved a cull of up to 147,000 cattle most at risk of mad cow disease.Farmers' leaders welcomed the decision but it drew an icy response
4450 from the European Union, which had insisted on a full-scale cull as part of a deal with Britain aimed at a gradual easing of the crippling embargo imposed in March."As long as they do not meet the pre-conditions and until we have a working document from them which we can
4450 carefully check, then an end to the export ban is simply not a possibility," European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said.British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said London had called off the selective cull, which is in addition to a rolling programme to destroy 450,000 cattle a year over the age
4450 of 30 months, because of fierce opposition in parliament."Any minister who wanted to get the cull order through the House of Commons would have to be able to persuade the House of Commons that member states would be able or willing to ... lift the ban. And many members of
4450 parliament are deeply concerned," Hogg told BBC radio.Prime Minister John Major, who must call an election by May, has a majority of just one in the 651-seat lower chamber. He would have faced certain defeat had the cull been put to a vote.Hogg said, however, that the decision, taken at
4450 a two-hour meeting late on Thursday, was also justified by new projections by Oxford Univeristy scientists that mad cow disease would die out within five years with or without a cull.The European Union imposed the ban after British scientists disclosed in March a probable link between mad cow disease, or
4450 Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), and the invariably fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, which rots human brains."The position of the Commission has not changed," Jacques Santer, president of the European Commission, told Reuters in Brussels when asked about the British decision.Major's office said suspension of the cull did not mean the government was
4450 departing from the framework of a deal struck at an EU summit in Florence in June. This deal allowed the eradication plan to be "adapted if necessary in the light of scientific and epidemiological developments".Hogg did admit, however, that Britain could no longer hope for the ban on beef exports,
4450 worth 500 million pounds ($780 million) a year before the crisis erupted, to be lifted by November as Major had promised after the Florence agreement."We will not be seeing the ban lifted by November," Hogg said.Asked whether the ban would still be in place in five years' time, Hogg added:
4450 "It depends on member states. There is a process which enables the ban rapidly and substantially to be lifted, but that depends on member states."He said the strategy now would be to get the ban lifted first on so-called certified herds -- cattle primarily fed on grass that have no
4450 record of BSE. Such a plan, if agreed by the EU, is likely to start in Northern Ireland.Sir David Naish, president of the powerful National Farmers' Union, said he would meet European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler later on Friday to put Britain's case."Our Scottish and our Ulster (Northern Ireland) colleagues
4450 do have many more herds that have had no BSE cases, and I hope we can help persuade Commissioner Fischler that this is a way to start the lifting of the beef ban," he told BBC radio.Members of the ruling Conservative Party from farming constituencies, who had threatened to vote
4450 down the cull when parliament debates it next month, were pleased by the news.But former prime minister Sir Edward Heath, a fervent pro-European, said: "It will be interpreted widely that the British government reached an agreement at Florence and has now overthrown that agreement unilaterally." 4457 A Labour government would want to decide sooner rather than later whether or not to join a single European currency, Peter Mandelson, a key aide to British Opposition leader Tony Blair, indicated on Thursday.Mandelson, Labour's campaigns strategist, told the Foreign Press Association that, if Labour wins power it will decide
4457 on economic grounds whether or not to join monetary union.But he added: "If you pinned me down on timing, I'd be bound to say that Britain with a Labour government would want to maximise its influence in shaping that union if we chose to become members of it." Mandelson reaffirmed
4457 Labour policy that no decision should be taken now on whether or not to join monetary union.The ruling Conservatives have a similar policy and Mandelson said he could not imagine Prime Minister John Major abandoning it. To rule out membership of a single currency in the life of the next
4457 parliament, as right-wing Eurosceptics demand, would split the party and cause cabinet resignations.Mandelson, expressing a personal opinion as vice-chairman of the European Movement, said he thought a referendum on Britain's membership of the European Union might be both "inevitable and desirable" to settle the issue. Mandelson said a Labour government
4457 would not be stampeded into a single currency to help fulfil German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's European ambitions. Nor would it stay outside for bogus reasons of nationalism.Labour would weigh the economic arguments and would want to be satisfied that economic and monetary union (EMU) was sustainable and not "a leap
4457 in the dark," Mandelson said.He firmly rejected any dilution of the criteria for EMU to maximise the number of countries that join, saying it would be a recipe for an unsustainable union. Mandelson said Labour was much more united over Europe than the Conservatives, but admitted the question of a
4457 single currency would pose the party economic and intellectual problems.On other issues, he reaffirmed that the Labour leadership had no plan to sever its structural links with Britain's trades unions, but said he could not speculate on how their relations would evolve in the years ahead. He said he was
4457 not complacent about the general election, due by next May, and forecast Labour's 20-point lead in opinion polls would narrow as disgruntled Conservative voters returned to the fold."It was ever thus and ever will be," he said.-- London newsroom 44-171-542 7767</
4458 Britain's Prince Charles on Thursday launched a major assault on intensive farming methods and the genetic engineering of foodstuffs, saying man's desire for cheap food had caused immense damage to the environment."It is difficult to over-emphasise the significance of what has been unwittingly destroyed in only two generations," he said
4458 in a speech to the 50th anniversary meeting of the Soil Association, the governing body of Britain's organic movement."We have burdened ourselves and our children with the task of rebuilding what we have destroyed. I fear it may take them most of their lifetimes to do so. And the cost,
4458 both for us and for them, will be immense," he said in remarks released before delivery.The heir to the throne, in his first major speech since divorcing Princess Diana last month, called for a more sustainable approach to growing food with more emphasis on usuing natural low-intensive methods.Charles has been
4458 farming organically at his Highgrove estate in the west of England for the last 11 years.He said there was no such thing as cheap food, since people were paying twice for what they ate -- once to subsidise farming through taxes and again to repair the damage.He took care not
4458 to blame farmers, saying they had been encouraged to produce as much as possible as cheaply as possible by successive governments over the last 50 years."But the prevailing mood...has been that man can dominate Nature and win, that human beings are not only at the top of the food chain,
4458 but that manipulation and domination of the natural world is somehow our destiny, even our duty," he said."That, I think, is where things have gone wrong," he added, saying lessons should be learned from mad cow disease, or BSE, which started when farmers began feeding their cattle feed made from
4458 ground-up sheep."We see the consequences of treating animals like machines, seeking ever greater 'efficiency' and even experimenting -- catastrophically, as we now know -- with totally inappropriate fuels...with which to "power' them," he said."Perhaps BSE will come to be seen as one example, albeit a very expensive and damaging one,
4458 of how nature hits back when we violate her laws," he said.Genetically modifying organisms to boost food production was also dangerous."Apart from certain medical applications, what actual right do we have to experiment, Frankenstein-like, with the very stuff of life? We live in an age of rights -- it seems
4458 to me that it is about time our Creator had some rights too."</

4478 British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said on Friday that the decision to suspend a beef cull agreed in June with the European Union was made for scientific and domestic political reasons."Members of parliament would certainly not approve the (cull) order which in terms of science is not easy to justify,"
4478 Hogg said. Hogg said Thursday night's decision by ministers to put a plan to cull up to 147,000 cows on hold was right because of new scientific evidence that mad cow disease could die out by 2001 and that the disease might be transmitted from mother to calf.He told BBC
4478 radio said the Florence agreement in June said any cull decision should be made on "scientific and objective" and it also created the mechanism that new scientific evidence could be brought forward for discussion. "Any minister who wanted to get the cull order through the House of Commons would have
4478 to be able to persuade the House of Commons that member states would be able or willing to ... lift the ban. And many members of parliament are deeply concerned," he said."We need positive evidence that the Europeans are able to deliver what they say that they will deliver because
4478 I have to satisfy the House of Commons on that."Prime Minister John Major's government has a one-seat majority in the 651-seat lower house. A parliament debate on the culling policy is expected next month.</

4487 Silver prices sunk lower on Thursday and flirted with the psychological $5.00 an ounce level, dragging down the rest of the precious metals.Gold's losses were limited, however, and it closed in London just $0.50 lower than on Wednesday at $382.85 an ounce."Gold isn't doing too badly," one dealer said.The gold
4487 market was anticipating a price surge after speculators took positions favouring a go-ahead for the sale of International Monetary Fund gold which failed to materialise.Prices eased last week after U.S. investment funds took short positions ahead of IMF meetings on the plan, playing on fears prices would drop if fresh
4487 gold supply hit the market.But the IMF has failed so far to agree a plan to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves to aid poor countries."At some point the funds are going to have to react. And then everyone's going to cover like crazy," a dealer said,
4487 adding that the gold price could soar to $388 an ounce.Silver's position had also weakened over the past week as prices hovered within 10 cents above the $5.00 level. A sell-off on New York's futures market on Thursday afternoon took it sharply lower, to close at $5.01 per ounce, down
4487 eight cents.Palladium, a rare white metal used in the electronics, auto and dental industries, followed silver lower to test its key $120 an ounce support level. It ended at $119.55, down $1.60.Platinum also shed gains from a rally the previous day to end $2.20 lower at $388.70.Some analysts were concerned
4487 that weakness in silver and platinum might undermine a recovery in the gold price."Silver at around $5.00 and platinum at $390 makes many people very nervous," one analyst said."Expectations for gold to move higher in a better demand environment depend on the behaviour or silver and platinum," he added, emphasising
4487 that falls in either of these metals could erode gold's upward potential.Analysts noted that in the longer term, gold was moving into the peak demand season, covering Christmas buying in the West and post-monsoon and wedding buying in Asia.</

4490 defied efforts to make him reduce derivative holdings three weeks before the collapse.Leeson, now serving a six-and-a-half year jail term in Singapore, ran up almost $1.4 billion of losses in unauthorised derivatives trades. 4490 the end of January 1995 as Leeson escalated his trading.In one conversation, equity derivatives trading head Mary Walz admitted to Ron Baker, the bank's head of derivatives trading, that she did not fully understand the reasons Leeson was giving for not cutting his trading on Simex, the Singapore Futures Exchange,
4490 and on the Osaka Securities Exchange.She was quoted as saying: "What happened today is that Nick doubled the size of the Simex position... It's very bad. I really don't know how it happened."In late July, German and British authorities dismissed a report claiming Leeson stashed 53 million marks ($35.53 million)
4490 in German bank accounts before Barings collapsed.Barings was later rescued by Dutch financial giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep.</
4491 Eight months after debuting as one of Britain's nascent multi-utilities, Hyder Plc is keeping its water and electicity core but looking to its infrastructure expertise for future extra dividend growth, according to chief executive Graham Hawker."Our regulated businesses have the potential to continue providing strong dividend growth in the medium
4491 term. However we want to use our substantial skill base in a way which ensures long term superior returns," Hawker said in an interview.Pricing for Britain's privatised water and electricity firms is set by industry watchdogs Ofwat and Offer respectively, with the next reviews due in the year 2000.Hyder was
4491 formed when Welsh Water took over South Wales Electricity (Swalec) in an 872 million pound ($1.36 billion) deal which was completed in January.The company has already predicted cumulative cost savings from both the merger and ongoing cuts of 275 million pounds by the turn of the century, with eight million
4491 pounds coming through in the first year.EXPANSION FROM INFRASTRUCTUREHawker is clear that the company will focus on its strengths in water and electricity and expansion will come from its growing infrastructure consultancy business, Hyder Infrastructure Developments, formerly known as Acer."That's what we are good at, we are good at handling
4491 businesses which many would consider boring old utilities and the regulation that goes with being a monopoly," he said.For Hyder, utilities would also cover areas such as transport infrastructure, he added.Cost cuts from the merger will help Hyder to sustain dividend growth and although Hawker is not making any firm
4491 commitments, indications are that last year's 11 percent real term rise is a level the company would like to maintain.Analysts have been led by Hyder's suggestion that it has a track record of not paying out dividend increases it does not regard as sustainable.But it is in the infrastructure business
4491 internationally that the company sees the possibility for long term generation of additional profit growth.WELSH INTERNATIONALHyder, named from the Welsh word for "confidence" and the Greek for water, reports in both English and Welsh but considers itself an "international Welsh company", Hawker said."We are determined that our broader infrastructure investments
4491 will be materially income-generating by the year 2000. We need shareholder confidence in this, so we must be able to make money out of them," he said.In the year ending March 31, 1996 Hyder saw turnover of 138 million pounds from its infrastructure business out of a total 757 million
4491 pounds but operating profits amounted to just 1.4 million pounds out of a total 140.6 million pounds.The former Acer business provides engineering and environmental consultancy and is seen by Hawker and his team as a way of identifying high quality infrastructure investment opportunities to use the company's basic skills.In Australia,
4491 it was instrumental in developing the scheme for the 900 million pound by-pass road system for Melbourne, where in addition to the design fees, Hyder now has a 6.5 percent stake in the concession to build and operate the road."It is important to understand that Hyder won't take on the
4491 construction. That is better left to construction companies," Hawker said."But we are good at procuring construction, that is something we do every day in our water and electricity business," he added.He said Hyder would look internationally but would focus on projects where it felt it had a competitive edge.COY ON
4491 LARGE SCALE INVESTMENTSWithin Britain, Hawker is coy on the subject of another large scale investment after the acquisition of Swalec. 4491 telecommunications company in which it inherited a 30 million pound 40 percent stake through Swalec.The company also aims to take part in trials to supply gas to domestic customers ahead of liberalisation of the market in 1998. 4491 already supplying water and electricity.But it would also be a defensive move, he added, to protect its existing electricity supply business from encroachment by either gas supply companies or electricity firms pushing gas.CUSTOMERS SHOULD ALSO HAVE REWARDSAll of this should add up to benefits for shareholders, but customers should also
4491 reap rewards, Hawker said.He points out that customers have benefited from cost savings over the last five years, with rebates and price increases below regulatory limits.In addition, Hyder is spending 38 million pounds of voluntary investment on the environment over and above the one billion pounds committed by the water
4491 utility business."We have consistently gone the extra mile with customers," he said, adding that environmental concerns from Welsh water consumers had been taken into account in the company's plans.Hawker says the company's belief is that it should act in a way that balances the interests of its various constituents and
4491 that this in the end will secure shareholder value."Successful companies are those that provide the services or products that customers desire at prices which represent value for money and monopolies should be no exception," he said.POLITICAL FOOTBALLSThat view comes in the face of much public criticism of the industry in
4491 general over "fat cat" salaries for directors, high-priced takeovers and the failure of some water companies to maintain non-essential supplies during last summer's drought.Opposition politicians have also hit out at the emergence of multi-utilities such as Hyder, United Utilities and Scottish Power.They see these mergers as indications that the Conservative
4491 government's privatisation has merely allowed private companies to reshape the utility sector to their own advantage.The Opposition Labour party has vowed to curb the perceived excesses by imposing a "windfall" tax on the firms if it wins power in a general election, which must be held by May 1997.The market
4491 view is that the proposed tax is largely reflected in the share price already.Hawker suggested an election would bring one clear benefit for utilities."Peace. 4493 withdrawal by the carrier from all scheduled passenger services.World never mounted much of a threat to SAA Cargo, said Langeveldt, but European carriers have applied downward pressure on U.S.-South Africa rates throughout the year."They were more competition for us than the direct carrier on the route," he said in a
4493 telephone interview from New York.Rates slid, said Langeveldt, though he declined to say by how much or where SAA Cargo's rates now stand."Any adjustments in rates were done more to counteract the marketing efforts of the European carriers," he said.Citing Atlanta as an example, European carriers have set a spot
4493 pricing floor there by charging about $3 per kg for shipping to South Africa.The same airlines get as little as 50-55 cents per kg for a transatlantic shipment, so chasing South African traffic is an effective yield raising strategy for them, said Langeveldt.With the onset of the fall peak, demand
4493 for space ex-North America is strong. 4493 increased demand from European customers, he said."I think the volumes of cargo are going to increase (this fall), and who knows, we might be able to adjust our rates slightly upwards," said Langeveldt.The amount and timing of a rate increase has not been determined, he said.World's pullback marked the second

4495 Population growth and problems with water management in Asia should drive up demand for grains steadily in coming decades, Worldwatch Institute's director Lester Brown said on Thursday."The rate of population growth in some central Asian states is higher than in India, so there will be an increasing need to import
4495 grain," Brown said in a speech to the Winnipeg Chamber of Commerce.Brown, whose 1995 book "Who Will Feed China?" predicted China may import 200 million tonnes of grain a year by 2030, said aquifers in north China and India's Punjab were dropping."Northern India's facing the same problem as China. The
4495 Punjab, the breadbasket of India, is experiencing a steady depletion of its underground water and it will be faced with some substantial irrigation cutbacks," Brown said.Another source of demand for water comes from urbanization where expanding cities such as Beijing and Los Angeles compete with surrounding rural areas for water
4495 use, he said."In a country like China, the loss of irrigation water translates into the need for additional grain imports," Brown said. "To import a tonne of wheat is to, in effect, import 1,000 tonnes of water."Southern China has also been losing rice crop land to urban sprawl with increases
4495 in yields unable to make up the loss, Brown said."China can import a lot of grain but who can supply them? No one can on that scale," Brown said.Kazakhstan, a traditional supplier of grain to Russia, may need to import grain in coming years as would other central Asian republics
4495 such as Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan due to rapid increases in population growth, he said.To meet such demand, production will have to continue rising in major exporters. Argentina could double its grain exports to 24 million tonnes from 12 million in coming years and Ukraine may also expand grain output,
4495 Brown said.(Gilbert Le Gras 204 947 3548)</

4505 By Russell Barton (ABC TV Political Editor)One most unkind observer of John Howard's first major overseas trip this week labelled it "pygmy diplomacy".Nowhere is the contrast between Howard and his predecessor, Paul Keating, more stark than in the field of foreign relations.Keating, once overseas, seemed to expand into an even
4505 larger-than-life figure, not afraid to lecture world leaders on everything from trade to town planning.It was high risk but when it scored it hit some big targets.In the process Keating developed genuinely close friendships with a number of key world players.Howard, however, as soon as he's away from the safety
4505 of his home ground seems to shrink into a stiff and awkward travelling salesman uncertain of his product.The thrust of his foreign policy is to lower the risk, to provide a smaller target, in essence to back away from innovation and, therefore, from advancement.This flows from the coalition's pre-election policy
4505 which was redolent with questioning of foreign treaties, cutbacks in foreign aid (including the abolition of the DIFF scheme which Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer is now trying to backfill with ad hoc schemes) and a general loathing of the Keating style.But low risk is not risk free.Howard's speech this
4505 week to the Jakarta welcoming banquet hosted by President Suharto is a case in point."We do not claim to be Asian," he said."Neither do I see it as a matter of balancing out interests in Asia against or with our interests in the rest of the world.""Neither do I see
4505 Australia as a bridge to Asia and the West as sometimes suggested."This was directed at his Australian audience, rather than the Indonesians.It was supposed to further distinguish John Howard from Paul Keating.But the department of foreign affairs had not seen this key section of the speech.Had it gone to the
4505 department for advice, Howard's office would have been alerted to the contradiction this would present to the recent push to establish Australia as a commercial bridge to Asia, a promotion aimed at attracting European companies to establish their regional head offices here.The following day the prime ministerial spin team were

4507 Australian resources giant The Broken Hill Proprietary Co on Friday announced a 23 percent drop in first quarter net profit, blaming a strong Australian dollar for exacerbating the impact of weak copper and steel markets.The steel, petroleum and copper giant reported a net profit of A$287 million for the three
4507 months to August 31, down from A$372 million a year earlier.The result was within market expectations.Managing director John Prescott put a brave face on lower result, claiming the company was set to improve. "What we have to do is to strengthen those foundations in the short term by improving our
4507 near-term performance," he said."That's going to require a great deal of effort, a great deal of intensity. It must be done," he said in a pre-recorded interview prepared by the company. Prescott later declined to discuss the financial outlook for the current quarter.Analysts have been trimming back their BHP earnings
4507 estimates due to weaker copper prices and a flat steel market. However, although the result was within market expectations, it was not enough to stop BHP's share price falling. By the close of Friday's dealings, BHP shares were five cents down at A$16.04. The stock has fallen about 15 percent
4507 since May."I tend to feel that overall the result hasn't changed our outlook for the company ... that things will be a little bit subdued while the steel markets and copper markets are subdued," one Sydney-based analyst told Reuters.BHP results were largely hit by copper, a metal in which BHP
4507 invested heavily earlier this year before copper prices plummeted on the Sumitomo copper trading scandal in May. Prescott said the full impact of the alleged rogue trading already had passed through the market but he noted confidence was yet to return."We believe the fundamentals for the copper market are somewhat
4507 better than the market pricing indicates," he added.BHP's copper division reported a 56 percent fall in net profit to A$85 million for the first quarter, despite increased copper sales.BHP became the world's second largest copper producer when it bought the U.S.-based Magma Copper Co for US$2.4 billion in January. While
4507 Prescott was forced to admit the Magma business had posted a loss for the quarter, he did not quantify it and said the group had set aggressive targets for cost savings in its copper and other divisions.Quarterly profits fell 38 percent to A$90 million at BHP Steel, the troubled division
4507 which hobbled the group's financial performance for fiscal 1995/96.The company noted that despite a flat Australian market for steel during the period, signs of improving domestic steel demand were emerging. BHP's total sales rose a marginal 2.7 percent to A$4.84 billion in the quarter. Sales growth was constrained by a
4507 stronger Australian dollar, which rose to an average 79 U.S. cents from 73 U.S. cents a year earlier.BHP noted that a one cent increase in the Australian dollar cuts about A$35 million from its bottom line.Of the four key divisions -- steel, petroleum, copper and minerals -- only the petroleum
4507 group increased profit.-- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435</

4512 The Australian dollar finished a downbeat week on a minor upbeat note as the resilience of support defeated repeated attempts to extend the correction.The day's range was only 30 basis points but within that the price action was choppy as sizeable sell orders from Japanese and Chinese banks eddied with
4512 buying linked to a samurai issue and direct from local corporates.The bulls were carrying the day at the close but had yet to pierce offers at US$0.7920, which had capped the currency since its fall from atop 80 cents last week, and without such a break the dollar would remain
4512 vulnerable to a relapse to US$0.7810. By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the dollar was making threatening gestures at US$0.7915/20 having advanced from Thursday's late US$0.7890/95 level despite repeated setbacks.That was still short of its US$0.7962/67 finish Friday last week, but comfortably above the US$0.7860 week low.Traders said the firmer tone
4512 was largely a result of buying for a 20 billion yen dual currency samurai bond for Denmark, which came on top of a similar sized issue for NSW Treasury on Thursday. That helped the dollar inch up to 86.82/92 yen from 86.33/43 late Thursday, but remained well down on last
4512 Friday's 87.63/73 close. The samurai bonds were welcomed by dollar bulls who have been concerned by a sharp slowdown in the pace of issues.The sudden reticence of Japanese investors was thought to be partly due to the proximity of the half year end there and partly to concerns the U.S.
4512 would soon be raising rates while Australia eased, thus eating into the dollar's yield premium.The U.S. Federal Reserve meets next Tuesday to decide on policy and most analysts here are tipping a 0.25 point hike in the 5.25 point funds rate, although they expected the vote to be a very
4512 close one. In contrast, most think the Reserve Bank will cut domestic rates by 0.5 point to 6.5 percent by year end. Such a scenario would narrow the Australian dollar's yield premium on two and three year bonds -- the typical time scale for dual currency samurais -- to virtually
4512 nothing and make US$ samurais much more attractive to Japanese investors.The local currency derived indirect support from a firmer US$/yen which rallied on the back of strong U.S. housing data and rises in the price components of the Philadelphia Fed survey of business conditions.However, such signs of upbeat U.S. growth
4512 have conflicting implications for the local unit since it makes it a little more likely the Fed will hike rates at its policy meeting next week. But strong U.S. growth was bullish for the AUD in the longer run since it promised to underpin recoveries in Japan and Europe and
4512 eventually produce the sort of synchronised world upturn which would boost the demand for, and price of, commodities.The dollar tends to track commodity price trends over time as commodities make up over 60 percent of Australia's exports and the currency is seen as a commodity play by many investors.All this
4512 has convinced some analysts the local dollar could weaken toward 77 cents by year end if the Fed hikes and the RBA eases as feared, but should rebound to 80 cents in 1997 as stronger world growth drives commodity prices higher. On the technical front a week of tight consolidation
4512 had left the currency with a slight upward bias, although analysts emphasised it would have to clear US$0.7950 resistance to restore some semblance of credibility to the uptrend so badly tarnished by last week's 3/4 cent dive.In trade weighted terms it edged ahead to 58.2 from 58.0 late Thursday.There were
4512 no domestic data today and little next week to provide direction, but the new RBA governor Ian Macfarlance was speaking at an economists conference on Wednesday and anything he said would be closely analysed. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 373 1800</

4534 New Zealand risks unfettered power price increases when it throws the switch on its new wholesale electricity market next month, aluminium producer Comalco New Zealand Ltd warned on Friday.Managing director Kerry McDonald said the new market, which will become fully operational on October 1, was unbalanced in favour of power
4534 generators and seriously flawed. "There are serious problems with it. It has the potential to damage our (Comalco's) position, it has the potential to damage the position of all of the consumers in New Zealand," McDonald told Reuters in an interview.Comalco NZ, a unit of Australia's Comalco Ltd and New
4534 Zealand's largest consumer of electricity, resigned from the New Zealand Electricity Market (NZEM) on Thursday."A key issue with our resignation is we're putting up our hand and saying very clearly: 'look, this is going down an unsatisfactory path'," McDonald said. "It's very important that consumers generally become quite strongly focussed
4534 on the issue, because otherwise they're going to wake up one morning and find their power bills are a hell of a lot higher than they were expecting."He said there were "significant risks" of electricity prices rising and consumers being unable to do anything about it."And there's a signficant risk
4534 that at some time in the future, the market may be manipulated," he said. Developing competition between all electricity market participants is at the heart of the new market. In contrast to the cost-based methods of the past, prices are to be discovered on the basis of the equilibrium between
4534 supply and demand.But electricity purchaser and consumer groups have voiced concerns that the proposed market rules will allow the two state-owned generators, Contact Energy and Electricity Corp of New Zealand (ECNZ), to act unilaterally to push market prices above a competitive level, otherwise known as gaming. "I am not saying
4534 that ECNZ (the largest generator of electricity in New Zealand) is going to game the market or use its dominant position, but the market should not be set up so that there is the opportunity for that," McDonald said.He said the development of the market rules had left the structure
4534 "quite unbalanced"."What you want is a market in which buyers and sellers can interact in a very even-handed way -- neither side can dominate. If there's potential to undermine or influence the market, then it should be roughly balanced between either side. "What you've got now is a situation in
4534 which consumers fulfill a relatively weak role in the market. They are bidding in quantity and those quantities are aggregated, so no individual consumer really has an influence on the overall picture. It really is as simple as that."McDonald slammed the market's structure, saying it was not conducive to efficiency."Because
4534 of the complexity and the cost structure of the market, I don't believe that there are adequate incentives on the market to reduce its costs and operate efficiently." He said it was possible that other market participants would follow Comalco's lead in resigning from NZEM, but stressed that Comalco did
4534 not want to see the new market fail."What I want to see is changes to the constitution and processes of the market, so that we can influence change towards a more efficient market, rather than seeing a whole range of people pull away from it."Earlier this month, the anti-monopolies Commerce
4534 Commission said it had no jurisdiction to pass judgement over the proposed market rules, which market operator EMCO (Electricity Market Company) had submitted for authorisation. However, the monopolies watchdog said it did not believe the rules would lessen competition.--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746</

4542 One week into the serious part of the general election campaign and already the new proportional representation system has thrown up a major surprise.Politicians are talking as much to each other as they are to the electorate. And not (just) because public meetings are badly attended.The adoption of German-style mixed
4542 member proportional representation heralded, the pundits said, political niche marketing. Parties, so the wisdom went, would run positive campaigns emphasising their platform and voters could, at last, focus on a policy mix they wanted and fashion a truly representative legislature.Now this is not to say voters haven't spent a great
4542 deal of toil on the parties' respective policies, but if you judged the campaign so far you would have to say the single outstanding question has been "who will deal with whom?" The issue has been simmering in the stand-off between natural allies Labour and the five-party left-wing Alliance grouping.
4542 The Alliance will talk coalitions but only before the October 12 election. Labour, and every other party of significance, will only talk coalitions when the make-up of the House is determined.But this week it has become the underlying theme of almost every major political event. So we saw National launch
4542 its campaign warning of the "gloom gang" to its left: Labour, the Alliance and economic nationalist New Zealand First. NZ First leader Winston Peters countered with talk of the "toxic trio" of National, the Christian Coalitio and free-market Act New Zealand.Alliance leader Jim Anderton again tried to get Labour to
4542 the pre-election bargaining table to establish a broad agreement on common policy. Labour leader Helen Clark once more rebuffed him (much to the chagrin of Alliance strategists who fear increasing isolation and a backlash from the electorate if they refuse to join a government -- or worse -- fail to
4542 bring down the existing conservative government).Anderton's olive branch was, as Alliance press secretary John Pagani said, "our last box of chocolates" in the wooing of Labour.Similarly, the public divisions between the left and right of New Zealand First are about who feels comfortable with a Labour- Alliance axis and who
4542 would prefer National despite personal animosities between Prime Minister Jim Bolger, Peters and others. In the cheap seats centrist United Party, currently in coalition with National, fulminated about the "extremism" of a National-ACT-Christian Coalition government and indicated it was unlikely to get into bed with ACT.In all this position-taking, former
4542 Labour leader Mike Moore's decision to return from backbench purdah and accept the long-standing offer of the trade and foreign affairs spokesmanship was a key event.It came only hours after Peters resurrected his promise of a ministry of all talents (but whose policy?) in which Moore would be offered trade.
4542 Labour managed to "spin" the Moore acceptance as a positive for the campaign -- as undoubtedly it is. In a relatively inconclusive week it helped Labour shine. New Zealand First and the Alliance fared less well and the National government was almost invisible.But Moore's decision has a number of other
4542 ramifications.Firstly, it enables him to claim some of the credit for any improvement in Labour's fortunes in the last three weeks on the hustings. Secondly, it will allow him to absolve himself of blame for Labour going into a campaign divided against itself. But thirdly, and most importantly for the
4542 shape of the next government, it builds a bridge to New Zealand First. Moore is on excellent terms with New Zealand First, and as much as his star rises the likelihood of major concessions by Labour to the Alliance diminishes.His move took Labour by surprise at a time when many
4542 in its left wing were privately concerned at Clark's hardline rejection of Anderton's advances.Lastly, it positions Moore on the frontbench for the inevitable leadership challenge should Labour make a poor showing. Moore supporters are disproportionately represented in winnable eletorate seats, Clark's on the list. Given Labour will be struggling to
4542 win any list seats on current polling, then the balance of power in the caucus will swing to the right and Clark's silently anointed successor Steve Maharey will have a hard job mustering the numbers.Despite the fracturing and realigning that has already taken place, the abiding impression is that all
4542 this chat is not just about coalition building. It is also about party formation. The parties themselves have yet to complete their transition to the new electoral system.</

4553 The Australia-New Zealand business council on Friday praised progress in trans-Tasman economic relations but said significant issues remain on the agenda.New Zealand council chairman Kerry McDonald, speaking ahead of a three-day conference on Ausrtalian and New Zealand business competitiveness, told a briefing of journalists that the process of developing trade
4553 relations had come a long way under the Closer Economic Relations (CER) agreement. "So we do tend to talk now about the unfinished business, which is still pretty significant," he said. Top of the list of issues were rules of origin, investment and tax."Rules or origin; the problem is the
4553 50 percent domestic content requirement," McDonald said."Australia has been very reluctant at the official level to make progress on that. They're saying this is a multilateral issue and must be dealt with in terms of multilateral processes that are already under way. "Now both the Australian and New Zealand business
4553 communities are saying 'no', it's an issue that should be dealt with more quickly, even if it's on an interim basis."McDonald said there was also negative sentiment surrounding tax issues."It's not credible to talk in terms of a common tax system for Australia and New Zealand, but it's things like
4553 the transfer of franking credits -- that is the critical issue," he said. "If you've got cross-border investment, then it's silly to have non-transferability of franking credits." He said work was being done to look at the the tax treatment of foreign investors, who were currently "quite clearly disadvantaged."There were,
4553 for example, offshore shareholders in New Zealand companies whose earnings had to come back into New Zealand, go through the New Zealand tax system, and then go back into their own home-base tax system. "It's a major disincentive to invest in New Zealand," McDonald said.There was now a very high
4553 volume of investment between Australia and New Zealand and the council was keen to see an umbrella framework agreement put in place. "There's a double tax agreement, which is a key document, but it's limited in it's scope, and there's no obligation on either side to maintain a particular standard
4553 of behaviour in relation to those cross-border investments," McDonald said."So we are very keen to see some sort of framework agreement in place. Obviously the end result is that we want...New Zealand investment to be treated in Austrlia as if it were domestic investment, and the same coming the other
4553 way."He said there had already been some discussion on the question of an investment agreement between the two countries. "My understanding is that discussions have to go some way yet before it's clear that there is a basis for an agreement."The important thing is that between (New Zealand Finance Minister)
4553 Bill Birch and (Australian Treasurer) Peter Costello, there is now some meeting of the minds on seeing what can be done in this area."McDonald said the change of government in Australia had brought a "new view, vision, willingness to discuss issues", but added: "Perhaps it's unfortunate that the bureaucracy in
4553 Canberra doesn't completely change at the same time as the government does, because there are still, we perceive, pockets ...that are pretty resistant on a number of key issues."The three-day conference in Auckland, starting on September 25, would look at the question of competitiveness: how the two countries had done
4553 over the last 10 or 20 years, how they were positioned now, and what their future prospects were."The whole purpose of CER is to make Australia and New Zealand more competitive with the rest of the world, not just to improve trade between the two countries," McDonald said.--Wellington Newsroom (64

4557 Friday, of whom some abstained. 4557 a population of about 100,000, is made up of 171 islands scattered just west of the international dateline. 4566 A massive search for North Korean infiltrators who landed by submarine in South Korea moved to an area of mine shafts on Friday after fierce gunbattles raged through the night.Security forces believe several agents are holed up around disused coal mines in rugged mountains near the east coast city of
4566 Kangnung.The agents are the remnants of a squad of heavily armed infiltrators that landed on Wednesday.State television withdrew an earlier report that four had been found dead on Friday.An army officer pleaded with the men to surrender and save their lives in messages shouted through a loud-speaker mounted on the
4566 back of a jeep."You are surrounded. If you abandon your weapons and surrender you can live. Most of your colleagues have been shot to death. 4566 far, 18 are confirmed to have been shot dead and one captured alive.A military officer in Kangnung said security forces had found hollows in the ground where several agents may have spent the night."I heard gunfire all night and grenades exploding," said local resident Chang Choon-taik.Five or six helicopters were
4566 flying over the area, which is saturated with armed troops and located about 17 km (10 miles) from a beach where the agents landed.South Korean authorities have described the most serious infiltration since the 1960s as a military provocation. 4566 1950-53 Korean conflict ended in a truce.On Thursday, troops shot dead seven agents and displayed their bullet-riddled bodies dressed in South Korean-made blue jeans and sneakers.In Washington, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher urged "all parties" to avoid further provocative action. 4566 on the brink of famine following devastating floods and has appealed for international aid.The United States is part of an international consortium providing the North with nuclear power plants as part of a deal to end the country's suspected nuclear weapons programme.In South Korea, the public has reacted with anger
4566 and anxiety to the infiltration. 4566 ammunition to hardliners in Seoul, who oppose any concessions to the North.South Korea and the United States are trying to entice Pyongyang to talks, along with China, to work out a peace pact to replace an armistice that sealed the division of the Korean peninsula in 1953.</

4571 A massive search for North Korean infiltrators who landed by submarine in South Korea moved to an area of mine shafts on Friday where fierce gunbattles raged through the night.So far, 18 infiltrators out of about 20 who landed on Wednesday have been shot and killed -- 11 in an
4571 apparent mass suicide. One has been captured alive.State television reported one infiltrator had signalled surrender on Friday by waving white clothes, but other news reports quoted military authorities denying this.An army officer in the east coast city of Kangnung said there may be two or three North Koreans holed up
4571 around an area of disused coal mines in rugged mountains.He said security forces had found hollows in the ground where several agents may have spent the night."I heard gunfire all night and grenades exploding," said local resident Chang Choon-taik.Five or six helicopters were flying over the area, which is saturated
4571 with armed troops and located about 17 km (10 miles) from the beach where the infiltrators landed.South Korean authorities have described the most serious infiltration since the 1960s as a military provocation. North and South Korea have been technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean conflict ended in a truce.Thousands
4571 of troops and police have been combing through undergrowth and tall grass to try to flush out the last of the North Koreans.On Thursday troops shot dead seven agents and displayed their bullet-riddled bodies dressed in South Korean-made blue jeans and sneakers.In Washington, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher urged
4571 "all parties" to avoid further provocative action. The United States has 37,000 troops stationed in the South."We wish that all parties would refrain from taking further provocative actions," Christopher told a news conference.Asked if the incident could affect efforts to provide Pyongyang with nuclear technology and humanitarian aid, he added:
4571 "Obviously the episode is a matter of concern but the facts are so murky."He said it was impossible to assess the long-term impact of the incident.North Korea is on the brink of famine following devastating floods and has appealed for international aid.The United States is part of an international consortium
4571 providing the North with nuclear power plants as part of a deal to end the country's suspected nuclear weapons programme.In South Korea, the public has reacted with anger and anxiety to the infiltration. Some blame the navy for failing to detect the 34 metre (111 feet) submarine and worry the
4571 country is vulnerable to attack from its arch-enemy to the north.Political analysts said the incident may have damaged the chances of peace on the Korean peninsula by giving ammunition to hardliners in Seoul, who oppose any concessions to the North.South Korea and the United States are trying to entice Pyongyang
4571 to talks, along with China, to work out a peace pact to replace an armistice that sealed the division of the Korean peninsula in 1953.South Korean President Kim Young-sam is under increasing pressure from the rightwing of his ruling New Korea Party to take a tough line with Pyongyang.The latest
4571 security scare will limit his ability to take initiatives, such as offers of aid, to improve the atmosphere and smooth the way for talks, the analysts said.</

4594 Buyers and sellers of kerosene are gambling big on the North Asian winter in the build up to the peak demand fourth quarter, traders said on Friday.Consumers banking on a mild winter have held back on buying kerosene, used for heating and jet fuel, reckoning on buying cheaper later. Sellers
4594 counting on a severe winter are building stocks, they said.No one is betting 100 percent on the winter weather, but sellers are counting on the absence of exports from the United States and seasonal demand to keep the market tight.Buyers, who built up stocks over the summer, are hoping regional
4594 refinery expansions will tilt the supply balance in their favour.Last year, the Japanese winter was very cold and the price of kerosene delivered there shot up to a record $37.00 per barrel.Sellers are betting on that happening again and have up to 4.0 million barrels stockpiled in Abu Dhabi, Singapore
4594 and Guam, traders said.Kerosene prices in Singapore, a benchmark for other regional markets, averaged $22.80 per barrel in 1995. But so far this year they have averaged $26.95 -- 18 percent higher. Prompt kerosene was assessed on Thursday at around $30.00 per barrel."We think its overpriced. It's too expensive to
4594 buy right now," one major Japanese importer said."We think the winter is not going to be so cold," he said in explaining why Japanese importers were not yet buying their winter stocks.At this time last year, at least two major companies had signed up most of their winter requirements. This
4594 year, only one one company has partially covered its demand, traders said.Japanese refiners are leaving their options open, either to import or produce more kerosene, depending which is more economical, a trader said.Japan's reluctance to buy forward for the winter was also due to large purchases in the summer, traders
4594 said.The country's July imports, at 149,000 kilolitres (kl), were double of those in July 1995 and boosted stocks at the end of July to 3.04 million kl. 4594 1995 and February 1996.During the same period, South Korea imported 20.225 million barrels, but this year will import less as it has already secured 6.7 million barrels through term contracts and has expanded refining capacity, traders said.By November, capacity will have been raised to 2.44 million barrels per day (bpd)

4603 Japanese refiners are facing strident demands from gasoline station owners to change their oil product wholesale pricing system so it better reflects domestic market conditions, oil industry sources said."Under the new system, refiners are making profits while retailers are losing money," said Hiroshi Kawane, vice-chairman of the National Federation of
4603 Petroleum Commercial Associations, an oil product retailers' group."Prices set under the new system do not reflect the domestic retail market," Kawane told Reuters.Leading Japanese refiners introduced a new wholesale pricing system in April when restrictions on oil product imports were lifted because they believed liberalisation would lead to a flood
4603 of cheap imports.Liberalisation caused Japanese refiners to lose their virtually exclusive right to import oil products.Although most Japanese refiners have stuck to the new system, General Sekiyu KK said it had stopped using the system because it was not functioning."After four months of implementation, we realised the wholesale pricing system
4603 was unrealistic," a General Sekiyu spokesman said. "We could not allow the retailers to suffer."Traditionally, Japanese oil companies kept gasoline prices high while keeping the price of kerosene and gas oil at low levels.The new system -- designed to reflect international oil product and crude prices as well as currency
4603 fluctuations -- lowers the price of gasoline while raising those of kerosene and gas oil to better reflect global markets.Also in April, refiners announced they would drop the practice of guaranteeing retailers a rebate if prices fell below a certain level as a result of market competition.Industry sources expect this
4603 move will eventually force many of Japan's 60,000 gasoline stations, which together sell 50 million kilolitres of the fuel a year, out of business.In the past two years, during the run up to market deregulation, gasoline retail prices in regions where stations are close together, plummeted on expectations of cheap
4603 imports.The average national gasoline retail price has dropped 17 yen (15 cents) per litre since early 1994 to 105 yen (95 cents).Tax accounts for about 56 to 57 yen (51 to 52 cents) of the retail price.Gasoline retail prices have fallen since April under the new system, contrary to expectations
4603 they would recover in regions where they had fallen too sharply.Kawane said the new pricing system has failed to stop the price cutting war, partly because refiners affiliated to foreign oil firms, such as Esso Sekiyu K.K, and Mobil Sekiyu K.K., have not adopted the system and keep their prices
4603 below those of major Japanese refiners.Esso Sekiyu, an affiliate of Exxon Corp, for example, sets its gasoline wholesale price about four to five yen (cents) below major Japanese refiners, he said.A spokeswoman for Esso Sekiyu said the company made it a policy not to reveal its wholesale price.Nippon Oil Co
4603 and Idemitsu Kosan, the top two domestic refiners, have repeatedly made clear their determination to continue the pricing system.Industry analysts, however, said refiners would most likely review the system. "Refiners are expected to have no choice but to review the system soon," said Toshinori Itoh, senior analyst with private think-tank
4603 Daiwa Institute of Research."Refiners should also take into consideration price differences according to regions," Itoh said.A Ministry of International Trade and Industry official said: "We give the new system high marks, and we think it should be kept." ($1 = 110 yen)</

4613 Singapore's exports, lifeblood of a vibrant economy, dropped more sharply than expected in August and leading economists said on Friday it could be six months before a full recovery.Total exports fell 4.4 percent year-on-year after a 6.7 rise in July, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said.It said non-oil domestic exports
4613 fell 6.3 percent to Singapore $7.01 billion (US$5 billion) in August in nomimal terms year-on-year after rising 6.3 percent in July. The drop in non-oil domestic exports was worse than even the most pessimistic forecast.Eight economist polled by Reuters earlier in the week had predicted an average year-on-year fall of
4613 0.8 percent for August. The actual forecasts had ranged from a rise of 3.5 percent to a fall of 4.5 percent."The figures were clearly below market expectations," said Ng Bok Eng, regional economist at Deustsche Morgan Grenfell. "Those who have called for a recovery in the fourth quarter or even
4613 in the first quarter of 1997 might be too early." "I think we are probably close to the bottom of the cycle now, even though any kind of meaningful recovery will probably not be seen until the second quarter of next year," said Liew Yin Sze, economist at brokerage J.M.
4613 Sassoon.The TDB blamed the fall in exports on the slowdown in global demand for electronics and related products as well as an oversupply of semiconductors.Electronics account for almost half Singapore's total industrial output and around 60 percent of non-oil exports. "The slowdown was reflected in our key markets, mainly U.S.,
4613 EU (European Union), Malaysia, Japan and Hong Kong," the TDB said.Eddie Lee, regional economist at Vickers Ballas, said the greater than expected decline in exports pointed to a basic problem in the rapidly-evolving electronics industry.By the time something is made it may be out of date and hard to sell,
4613 leaving manufacturers with stocks they have to figure out what to do with. Lee said he expected the third quarter to be the weakest of the year, though when a recovery might take place was open for debate."It is a question of timing. In this industry, the turnaround can be
4613 very quick when it comes. I still expect a slight pick up by Christmas but manufacturers will remain very cautious."Lee also said the electronics slowdown was cyclical and not structural. "Global computer demand is still on a structural uptrend with penetration levels very low outside of the U.S." And despite
4613 the slowdown, there is no shortage of foreign investors willing to put their money into Singapore.Foreign investment commiments for the first half total S$3.8 billion and should meet the government's full year target of S$8 billion, up from last year's S$6.8 nillion, Lee said.US$1 = S$1.41</

4660 A Ministry of Finance official and an official for the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said on Friday they are aiming to further shorten the settlement period for Japanese government bonds (JGBs)."At the earliest, we would like to start 'T plus three' in April 1997," Kaname Seki, vice-chairman of the
4660 Japan Securities Dealers' Association, told Reuters Financial Television.Under a "T plus three" system, deliveries of JGBs take place three business days after the transaction date.Japan has just shortened the settlement period to "T plus seven" for JGB transactions made from September 19. Hiromichi Tanigawa, director of the MOF securities bureau's
4660 bond market office, said shorter settlement periods were desirable, because there would be less chance of unpredictable events occuring before settlement."Unpredictable events which take place in the time between trade and settlement can lead to unexpected risk," Tanigawa said.Examples of such unpredictable events would be earthquakes, or sudden bankruptcy on
4660 the part of trading counterparts, he said.</

4662 The Indonesian navy will continue to patrol waters around the gas-rich Natuna islands in the South China Sea following military war games in the area, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday."Marine security operations around the islands can be mounted at any time by the navy's Western Fleet," the
4662 news agency quoted Navy Chief-of-Staff Vice-Admiral Arief Kushariadi as saying.He said several destroyers and other warships had been ordered to remain in the waters around the Natunas to protect a multi-billion dollar gas extraction project.The Natuna field, some 680 miles (1,100 km) north of Jakarta off the northwest coast of
4662 Kalimantan, is estimated to contain 210 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of natural gas, of which 45 TCF is thought to be recoverable commercially.Indonesia recently questioned a Chinese maritime map that showed the Natunas as part of Chinese territory. 4662 belonged to Indonesia.A major 12-day military exercise at the Natunas, involving 19,525 personnel from all branches of the armed forces, 54 aircraft and 27 warships, ended on Thursday. 4662 armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung told reporters during the exercise.He denied the exercise was a show of force, however.Indonesia's state-owned oil company Pertamina owns 24 percent of the Natuna gas project, the U.S. Mobil Corp 26 percent and the U.S. Exxon Corp 50 percent.</

4672 their summit meeting here.Howard arrived in Japan on Wednesday for a four-day visit after winding up a three-day tour of Indonesia.It is his first major Asian tour as prime minister and has been closely watched as a barometer as to whether his coalition government born in March will be less
4672 committed to Asia than its predecessor."We have been able to establish a very good relationship with Australia so far and it should remain so," Hashimoto told the same news briefing. "We were able to establish a very good relationship. I can now safely say that we can discuss any issue
4672 at any time over the telephone."Japan is Australia's biggest trading partner and the third-largest foreign investor in the country. 4672 support for China's bid for World Trade Organisation membership and Japan's attempt to become a permanent member of the United Nation's Security Council."Both of us agreed how important it was to engage China, how important it was, on proper conditions, that China would become a member of the World Trade
4672 Organisation," Howard said."Australia and Japan have very similar views in relation to the need to properly and appropriately engage China not only in World Trade Organisation but more generally," he added.On Thursday, Howard told business executives here that Japan and Australia shared an interest in the closest possible engagement of
4672 China in regional and global affairs -- as a responsible partner.Australia is now in a fresh row with China after Howard said he would meet Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, who is on a two-week visit to Australia, after returning from his trip to Japan.Howard hopes to meet

4706 Malaysian conglomerate Renong Bhd's near doubling in annual earnings failed to excite most industry analysts despite beating market forecasts, analysts said on Friday.Much of the profit surge reflected the sale of land in southern Johor state, the analysts said, adding that Renong's cash position remained weak and net profit would
4706 have run within expectations if proceeds from the land sale were excluded.The infrastructure developer announced after the market closed on Thursday a net profit of 407.11 million ringgit for the financial year to June 30, 1996, against 207.83 million ringgit in the previous year.Analysts had forecast net profit of between
4706 360 million to 390 million ringgit.Earnings per share rose to 23.6 cents from 12.6 cents."The 23.6 cents was some 40 percent above the consensus estimate of 16.9 cents," said Jupiter Securities in a morning report on Friday. "Its excellent results could inject a new lease of life into other main
4706 Board companies," it said.But other analysts were not as enthusiastic. "The profit numbers are good, but much of the gains are from the proceeds of the sale of land in Johore," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage.Earlier in the year, Renong sold about 1,060 hectares of land in Johor
4706 to companies involved in the construction of the second causeway link to Singapore. The proceeds were about 270 million ringgit.Renong's 64 percent subsidiary, Prolink Development Sdn Bhd, is the developer of the 10,000-hectare site in Johor."The profits are not really representative of the group's cash situation," said the foreign brokerage
4706 analyst."Their real cash earnings are a lot less than the profit figures suggest," he said. "Around 70 percent of the cash proceeds (from the land sale) will not be collected until three years from now."Ami Moris, vice-president of dealing at Capitalcorp Securities said: "Renong also has a considerable debt situation,
4706 amounting to roughly 17 billion ringgit."The interest payments on this are going to begin to eat heavily into Renong's long-term earnings prospects, she said. Most analysts contacted by Reuters said if proceeds of the land sale were factored out of the profit figures, operationally the group performed within their expectations.HLG
4706 Securities said in a commentary: "Revenue and profit jumped due to aggressive recognition of Prolink land sales. Most other associate and subsidiary income was as expected."Renong subsidiary United Engineers (M) Bhd performed within expectations at the half-year mark, HLG said.HLG Securities said they are recommending a long-term buy on Renong

4718 Southeast Asian exports will bounce back from this year's sudden decline, but economists warned on Friday the recovery will be patchy and fail to match the heady rates of the past two years."The extent of the slowdown in the first half this year will limit the upside for the full
4718 year, but demand conditions should improve in 1997," ING Barings said in a report.Around the region, exports growth slumped to seven percent in the first half of the year, compared with a 30 percent increase last year. First improvements are expected to surface in early 1997, but economists warned that
4718 the complex nature of Southeast Asian trade dictates an uneven regional recovery."The only unifying theme in this case is that there isn't any," said Andrew Freris, chief economist at Salomon Brothers.A number of country-specific factors combined with an inventory correction in the United States, particularly in the electronics sector, threw
4718 Asia into a tailspin, suggesting its competitiveness is declining."The key to understanding the so-called 'Pan-Asian exports growth' decline is to appreciate different explanations apply to different countries, thus undermining the notion that there is a common trend of loss of competitiveness," Freris said.In fact, economists said many Southeast Asian nations
4718 are successfully diversifying away from low value-added, cheap labour products into higher value-added, more competitive goods.As one of Asia's most developed economies, Singapore was most affected by the U.S. electronics inventory adjustment.It is expected to report a slide in exports growth to three percent in 1996 from 13.8 percent last
4718 year, with recovery to 12.5 percent forecast next year.By comparison, both Malyasia and Thailand showed surprising resilience to the electronics slowdown despite their dependence upon the U.S. market through trade links with Singapore.In Malaysia, exports fell sharply but imports -- which in Asia tend to be export-regenerating rather than consumer-driven
4718 -- sank even more dramatically.This allowed Malaysia to improve its trade deficit to US$0.5 billion at the end of June compared with US$1.34 billion in the same period last year, which will make a positive contribution to Malaysia's forecast economic growth rate of 8.5 percent.Thai exports crashed across the board,
4718 but Asian economists said an unusually high base of comparison thanks to a bumper rice crop last year overstates the damage. Exports are forecast to rise 13.3 percent in 1997 from 9.8 percent this year.Closer examination also reveals a successful attempt at economic diversification. Weak exports of lower value-added goods
4718 obscure a rising contribution from electronic components."(This) belies the current fashionable view that Thailand may be in the throes of a structural crisis in terms of its exports composition as it loses its competitive edge against other Asian economies," Salomon Brothers said in a report.The Philippines actually bucked the trend.
4718 Although exports grew by only 19.4 percent in the first half this year compared with 33.6 percent last year, electronics exports reported a 51.4 percent increase in May as new capacity came on stream.Most of the weakness in the Philippines came from garment and coconut products, which were affected by
4718 poor weather.Economists said one Southeast Asian nation that can be accused of losing its competitiveness is Indonesia, even though exports should fall only two percent to 11.4 percent this year."Rising labour costs in Indonesia following a decade of substantial economic progress and the emergence of new players elsewhere in Asia,
4718 particularly in the textile and garments sector, have eroded competitiveness by more than the exchange rate regime can compensate," ING Barings said.Indonesia's rupiah declines between three and five percent each year, partly to support its export competitiveness.-- Hong Kong News Room (852) 2843 6441</

4750 and losers -- the ones that would expand and the ones that would contract," said Kate Newman Mack, director of research at Kleinwort Benson.LUXURY RETAILERS AVOIDED BATTERINGLuxury retailers like Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd and Joyce Boutique Holdings Ltd have avoided the battering that many Hong Kong department stores have taken,
4750 with their high income target market protected from the economic woes of middle to lower income buyers."For people who could afford to buy higher income products, the economic slowdown has impacted them less," explained Ken Chan, senior economist at Nikko Research Center (Hong Kong) Ltd."The middle end was the sector
4750 that was hit the most -- department stores and mid-range products."Dickson Concepts announced last week that its Hong Kong Seibu unit would open a new department store in the Causeway Bay district in late 1997. The retailer said in June it had agreed to acquire an 85 percent stake in
4750 Hong Kong Seibu Enterprise Co."Since Dickson's strength is in the technical side of retailing and since that was Seibu's weakest point in its operation, the Dickson people should be able to turn around Seibu. It is a good mix of management style," said Newman Mack.Upmarket clothing retailer Joyce Boutique is
4750 boosting its store area in the Kowloon district and has been adding designer names to its labels list.In February it said it had won the regional distribution rights for three new fashion labels -- Superga casual shoes, Eres Swinwear and Cutler &amp; Gross spectacles. 4750 Hugo Boss in Hong Kong in August."It's always the labels that have done very well," said Renee Tai, analyst at BZW Asia. 4750 retailers and shopping malls and away from department stores."We are seeing niche market expansion but we are not seeing the mass market expansion because of that very reason," said Morris Macleod, investment analyst at ING Barings."For the high-end products that they are marketing in some of the niche markets, they

4750 lost its focus. "It's now a big shoe store with a lot of other stuff attached," said one analyst.Lane Crawford, controlled by Wheelock and Co Ltd, posted a sharp drop in net profit for the financial year to March, down to HK$16.4 million from HK$131.7 million.It said last week it

4750 ahead of an expected recovery in retail sales late this year or early next year and while property prices were still negotiable."Dickson and Joyce are expanding at the bottom rather than the top. But you have to be good retailer to be able to afford it," said Newman Mack."If you
