5451 Arsenal's new French manager Arsene Wenger paid a flying visit to Highbury on Sunday and immediately denied he was taking over a club in crisis.Wenger, 47, who officially takes control on September 30, said he had read all the stories concerning the problems at the club but thought they had
5451 been greatly exaggerated, although he agreed there had been plenty of turmoil."The board are strong and united and know exactly what they want to do, and the team are playing very well. I think the crisis might have been around the club -- not inside the club. I do not
5451 think there is a problem with any crisis."But Wenger knows Arsenal have been making as many headlines off the pitch as they have been making on it.Despite currently lying third in the premier league after a 2-0 win at Middlesbrough on Saturday and being unbeaten for five matches, they were
5451 rocked last week when club captain Tony Adams said he was an alcoholic.The club has also been widely condemned for the way it sacked previous manager Bruce Rioch just five days before the start of the season.But Wenger, who will meet the players for the first time on Monday and
5451 accompany the team when they visit Germany this week for the return leg of the UEFA Cup match against Borussia Moenchengladbach, praised Adams for admitting his problem."My message for Tony Adams is one of respect. I know that to say what he said took a lot of courage and when
5451 people are brave and honest you have to respect them."Wenger, who is fluent in French, German, English, Italian, Spanish and speaks some Japanese, also said he intended to impose discipline on the club.Over the past 10 years Arsenal have won all the major honours in England, but they have also
5451 been involved in some major off-field scandals, including the illegal payments affair which led to ex-manager George Graham leaving the club nearly two years ago.Wenger said: "I believe in strong discipline but the strongest discipline is when players understand what the coach is trying to do. But today success on
5451 the field depends on discipline -- on the field and off it."Wenger, showing a refreshing openness not normally associated with many more guarded English managers, said he was offered the job at the beginning of August but could not join Arsenal immediately until his current Japanese club, Grampus Eight, had
5451 found a suitable replacement. His revelation was intriguing as Rioch was not sacked by Arsenal until August 12.Wenger is only the fourth overseas coach ever appointed to manage a senior English club but felt that being foreign was no disadvantage. He was excited by the thought of marrying his continental
5451 background to the demands of the English game."That is my challenge," he said. "I have studied English football for many years and although I might not know every player and every ground, I will have good people around me to assist me."I also think English football has changed so much
5451 in the past four or five years. It is much more international than it was. Who could have imagined (Fabrizio) Ravanelli or the Brazilians at Middlesbrough five years ago?"His assistant manager will be Pat Rice, an Arsenal stalwart and member of their double-winning team in 1971, who will remain in
5451 charge until Wenger returns permanently from Japan.Arsenal may not be ready to win another double yet, but Wenger believes they are a "great club" who can look forward to "It will take me a couple of months to adapt to the team and for them to adapt to me, but
5451 my message to the fans is come here and watch us and be happy."No team can always be attractive and fantastic in every match. But we have a very strong squad with some excellent technically gifted players. We might need some new players, but not yet. The challenge for me

5466 3-1 lead in their world group semifinal.The Czech Republic had kept their hopes alive by winning Saturday's doubles and Vacek looked to be on the way to squaring the tie when he moved in to a 2-1 lead after losing the first set.Vacek made the first service break of the
5466 match when he took the fifth game in the first set but the Swedish number one immediately returned the favour, breaking back and then surging ahead with another break in Vacek's next service game to take the set 6-3.Enqvist, who had never faced Vacek before, then opened the second frame
5466 with another break and appeared to have the top ranked Czech at his mercy.But then Enqvist's serve began to fail miserably while Vacek hit his stride, becoming more confident with each shot. He broke back and then overpowered Enqvist in a tie break 7-3.With a partisan crowd firmly behind him,
5466 Vacek continued to press the faltering Enqvist, watching him double fault and then miss an easy volley to give up the break needed to allow the Czech to take the third set 6-4.The two went toe-to-toe in a hard-hitting fourth set, neither surrendering a break point until the 12th game
5466 when the Swede used his blistering returns to break Vacek and win 7-5.Enqvist who's serve had failed him throughout most of the match as he double faulted 18 times, finally found the rythym in the final set, firing five of his 18 aces to overcome an early break by Vacek
5466 with one of his own in the fifth game.The break proved to be the turning point in the match as Vacek lost his temper, slamming the net twice with his racket and earning a warning from umpire Bruno Rebeuh.Vacek, who served 27 aces, could not stem the tide, giving up
5466 a break in the eighth game and allowing Enqvist to serve out the match, putting six times champions Sweden into the final. "I was very upset after the break in the fifth set. It was an emotional match, one of the toughest I have ever played. Every point was a
5466 battle," Enqvist said."I lost my timing on the serve and Daniel was putting a lot of pressure on my second serve. After a while, I began to come in after my serve to mix it up and find my rythym again."Vacek commented: "I played probably the best game of my
5466 career today, it's too bad I couldn't win such an important point for our team."I had a chance in the final set with the early break and tried to pressure him but he responded and found his serve."Victory will give Stefan Edberg, in the final year of his distinguished career,
5466 a chance to win his fourth Davis Cup trophy. Edberg closed out the tie with a 4-6 6-2 7-5 win in a shortened match over his Australian Open doubles championship partner Petr Korda, giving the Swedes a 4-1 overall score."It's tough playing after the emotional high of (Enqvist's) win but

5466 Czechs, France faced elimination after going down 2-0 in the opening singles, but came roaring back to win the three remaining matches.</

5479 Austria's Davis Cup team walked out of their World group qualifying tie against Brazil on Sunday in protest at crowd behaviour, handing their opponents a 4-1 victory.The Austrian team, furious about crowd behaviour, refused to play the two reverse singles which were automatically awarded to the home team, and said
5479 they would appeal to the International Tennis Federation.But both Austrian and Brazilian officials denied reports that death threats had been made against Austrian number one Thomas Muster.The trouble began on Saturday when Muster stormed off the court in a fit of pique during the doubles match in protest at the
5479 behaviour of the crowd and said he had been spat at.Muster, partnering Udo Plamberger, had been complaining about the crowd throughout the match, at one stage hitting the umpire's chair, and finally abandoned the rubber in the fifth set.Brazilian pair Jaime Oncins and Gustavo Kuerten were awarded the doubles by
5479 default, giving Brazil 2-1 lead."Our top player Thomas Muster felt the crowd was unfair. He was continually provoked by the crowd and he thought it was too much," said Pieter Nader, general-secretary of the Austrian Tennis Federation,Nader added Muster said he had been spat at by people in the crowd.
5479 "He is our top player, he is number three in the world and if that is what he says I believe him," he said.Luis Noriega, a spokesman for the Brazilian organisers, said Muster, who had been due to play in one of the reverse singles, had left the country on
5479 Saturday night. Austria had been offered the chance to field a substitute for Muster but declined."They alleged there was a lack of security but that's not true," said Noriega, adding that Austria could be suspended from next year's competition."There was no reason for Austria to abandon the court. The organisation
5479 was good, there were plenty of police.""If anyone spat, it was Muster. He spat blatantly on the court and made obscene gestures to the crowd. Every time there was a line call, the Austrians caused a scandal. When he left, he was pushing and swearing at everyone.""The crowd was noisy
5479 but that is the behaviour of a Latin crowd.""Muster was given a police escort to the airport which was not necessary because nobody knows who he is here."The result means Brazil, semifinalists in 1992, return to the World group after a three-year absence.With Austria refusing to carry on, the Brazilians
5479 played two exhibition matches amongst themselves to entertain the crowd.</

5481 Temperamental Austrian tennis star Thomas Muster cost his country a crucial point in its Davis Cup World Group qualifying tie with Brazil by storming off the court in the fifth set of Saturday's doubles match.The world number three abandoned the pivotal match in protest at what he claimed was bad
5481 crowd behaviour to give Brazil a 2-1 lead heading into Sunday's reverse singles.Brazil's Jaime Oncins and Gustavo Kuerten were leading Muster and Udo Plamberger 2-0 in the final set when Muster lost his cool. The Brazilians had won the first and third sets and the match ended prematurely with the
5481 score 7-6, 4-6, 6-3, 3-6, 2-0, 30-15.Witnesses said Muster, who always seems to have a gripe about something, refused to carry on because he was angry at the umpire's refusal to act over noise in the crowd while the Austrians were serving.Muster claimed several times that he could hear people
5481 in the crowd calling out his name as he served, but the chair umpire said he could not hear anything.When numerous protests by the cranky Austrian produced no satisfaction from officials, Muster stormed off court amid jeers, angrily pointing his finger at someone in the crowd.Muster had also moaned several
5481 times during the match about what he said was a small bump in the court surface.It was not known whether he would take part in Sunday's reverse singles, but Saturday's fit of pique could help propel Brazil back into the elite World Group after a three-year absence.</

5505 and Guillaume Raoux over Gaudenzi and Diego Nargiso.Pioline, ranked 17th in the world, said: "In the Davis Cup you always get a second chance. I served better today."It's easier for me to adapt to an excited crowd than to expect 6,000 people to adapt to me."The shy and sometimes brooding
5505 Pioline did not manage to get the crowd strongly behind him on Friday but they lifted him from the start against Furlan and helped him give a much more passionate performance.Pioline worked harder in the long rallies favoured by the Italian slow-court specialists and his greater mobility than on Friday

5505 hs recent form on the tour "because in the Davis Cup it's a question of life or death."In the third set Boetsch broke his Italian opponent in the first game then survived two double faults to retain his serve.Gaudenzi finally broke Boetsch in the third game only for the Frenchman
5505 to break right back, when the Italian, having at last found his length, sent a passing shot wide.The Italian's tenacity helped him break Boetsch again when the Frenchman served for the match at 5-4 and carry the set into a tiebreak.Panatta was angered by a decision by the umpire to

5524 South Africa's hopes of starting the new year with a final apartheid-free constitution improved on Sunday when President Nelson Mandela's rivals refrained from demanding a major re-write.Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi said his Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), which boycotted constitution-writing over the last 18 months, wanted informal talks on the subject
5524 with the African National Congress (ANC)."It is in the interests of the country that we have a meeting with the ruling party," he told a news conference in Ulundi in his home province, KwaZulu-Natal, at the end of a two-day summit of IFP leaders.They met to decide whether to rejoin
5524 the formal talks on the new constitution after the country's highest court rejected an earlier draft, written without the IFP and approved by parliament in May.But the IFP took no final decision on rejoining the Constitutional Assembly, and time is running out.A new version has to be submitted to the
5524 Constitutional Court by October 11 if it is to come into force in January to replace an interim constitution that was agreed during the dying days of the old apartheid regime.The IFP's failure to make up its mind this weekend increases the chances that the law will be fine-tuned by
5524 the other parties and sent back to the court on time.ANC leaders have said they are not willing to let the IFP reopen full negotiations over all aspects of the law as this could seriously delay its approval. The court also said it expected just minor amendments.Buthelezi said that was
5524 one reason for his reluctance to get involved again.His party boycotted the constitution-writing process when international mediation promised by the ANC over the parties' differences failed to materialise.The nationally strong ANC wanted a powerful central government, the regional-based IFP wanted more powers for the provinces.The Court rejected several parts of
5524 the draft law including the section on provincial powers which it said would be unacceptably weakened.But it also threw out the IFP-shaped KwaZulu-Natal provincial constitution for the opposite reason, saying it usurped central powers as if it was a separate state.IFP and ANC supporters have waged a low-level civil war
5524 for control in KwaZulu-Natal for a decade, but the fighting has died down since local elections in June.Buthelezi said the rejection of his province's constitution could stir the conflict up again."There is a lot of anxiety amongst our members that the constitution agreed to by all KwaZulu-Natal parties being thrown
5524 out will promote that state of ungovernability," he said.Political analysts said the IFP's weekend indecision showed it was internally divided and in a weak position.</

5534 Getting that long distance feeling over the Internet appears to be a rapidly growing phenomenon.Companies from small start up firms to the big chip maker Intel Corp. have been intent on getting surfers hooked on Internet chatting.For consumers it has one big drawing card: it is a lot cheaper than
5534 paying long distance tolls."I can see in the future that it's just going to grow," said Ian Pulver, author of the Internet Telephone Toolkit and editor of The Pulver Report newsletter (www.pulver.come:80/reports).Some have predicted there are already more than a million people using the Internet to make telephone calls. Pulver,
5534 however, said his best estimate has 55,000 people a week phoning over the Net, but that was up from 30,000 two months ago. He believes users will be counted in the hundreds of thousands or even millions within a few years.The idea behind Internet telephony is simple. Online, a surfer
5534 may go anywhere in the world and the only charge has usually been the monthly fee from an Internet service provider.So why not hook up a phone, and with help from some software, conduct calls at no extra charge to Tampa, Tokyo or Tuktoyaktuc. Of course, the person at the
5534 other end would have to have compatible software and be on line to make this all work.Such a concept has been enough to make devotees of Alexander Graham Bell shudder. The thought of all those Internet packets containing voices running willy nilly over the globe was not something they welcomed
5534 with open arms, or open circuits.Why anyone would want to leave the safe world of precise switching to the vagaries of the Internet was beyond comprehension for them. You might as well just string up two cans with some thread in your backyard if you wanted free talk time.But in
5534 a measure of their concern that maybe, just maybe, Internet telephony could prove to be a threat, a number of telephone firms in the United States and in Canada have appealed to regulatory authorities for -- what else -- regulations against this new phenomenon.The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission,
5534 Reed Hundt, however, said in a speech last Wednesday he was against roping in the Internet with rules from the conventional telephone world, including making Internet service providers pay long distance access charges."You don't pour new wine into old bottles and if we applied these old access rules to new
5534 technologies, you'd have every reason to whine," he said in a speech to a Washington conference.Pulver said Internet telephony probably began when startup VocalTec Ltd. of New Jersey launched a product in 1995.Internet telephony started out as a rather crude service, about as fun as communicating with walkie talkies. Pulver
5534 said it has gotten a lot better, not unlike overseas communications a few years ago when slow satellite relays caused delays in talking.A number of things have been driving its use. Not the least of all was Intel handing out free software to allow users to make phone calls over
5534 the Net, all with the aim of getting more and more people to buy personal computers.As well, Netscape Communications Corp. has included the Internet telephone program "Cool Talk," in its latest Navigator browser software -- a veritable Trojan Horse that could really spur the forces for Internet telephony.Pulver said a
5534 number of new uses will likely draw more and users into the concept. Businesses have been attracted to cheaper long distance calling methods, including sending faxes, a transaction well suited for the Internet.Corporations with Web sites might soon offer an icon where a customer could click on to have a
5534 quick conversation with a sales or technical representative to talk about a certain product.In the world of Internet games or chat rooms, adding the possibility of direct conversations could prove wildly popular too. But most of all, the idea of talking to someone new anywhere in the world for little
5534 cost will probably be key to it all."It offers the ability for people to meet others anywhere in the world, in the spirit of ham radio," said Pulver.--To comment on this weekly column:russell.blinch(at)reuters.com</

5544 question on everyone's mind: Will they or won't they?"They" refers, of course, to the Federal Reserve and the question is whether or not the Fed will increase interest rates this week in an effort to forestall inflation. In the latest Reuters poll, conducted Thursday, 16 of 30 economists surveyed said
5544 the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) would raise interest rates by one-fourth of a percentage point (25 basis points) at its September 24 meeting.Thirteen economists said the Fed would leave rates unchanged and one predicted a hike of half a percentage point.Yet, even with attention so squarely fixed upon
5544 and opinion so divided over this Fed meeting, only lately has a second question come to be addressed, namely: What difference does it make? Analysts generally expect little stock market fallout in the event of a modest increase in the federal funds rate, currently targeted at 5.25 percent, because the
5544 market has acted to discount such a move."If the Fed raises by 25 basis points, that's already priced in the market," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.Likewise, a Fed vote to leave rates unchanged is only expected to provide a short-lived, modest boost. "If there's no
5544 change, I think there will be a mild celebration," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. 5544 rise in rates, seven forecast a Fed tightening in late November, just after the U.S. Presidential elections. 5544 in the recent past.One reason is that the market is devoid of the speculative fervor that fueled a fierce small-cap rally early in the year and, by most indicators, smaller-cap stocks have yet to recoup their losses from the July correction.Another is that recent data have delivered mixed signals about
5544 the state of the economy and the spectre of inflation. 5544 outcome to settle anything at all."I don't want to make the (FOMC meeting on the) 24th the be-all and end-all," Wachtel said, "because everybody realizes this is a work in progress."</

5577 The curtain went up on Sunday on Britain's most crucial party conference season for years when Liberal Democrat activists arrived in the southern resort of Brighton to set out their general election wares.But political observers questioned whether the annual gathering of Britain's third party represents Act One of the main
5577 political drama, or a show on the fringe.For while the Labour opposition and ruling Conservatives hope to use their conferences in the following two weeks as launchpads for an election victory next April or May, the Liberals aspire merely to influence in the next parliament.At best, say political pundits, the
5577 party could win 30-40 seats in the 659-member House of Commons, and find itself the junior partner in a coalition with Labour, which would be the first non-Conservative government in Britain since 1979.Party leader Paddy Ashdown, asked on BBC television about his ambitions for the election, replied: "As many seats
5577 as we can get and as many Liberal Democrat votes as we can achieve across the country."The Liberals, who struggle against a British electoral system which benefits their bigger rivals, at present hold 25 parliamentary seats -- comparative luxury for a party which almost disappeared from the House of Commons
5577 in the 1950s.Yet although, following abysmal Conservative performances since the 1992 general election, they are now the second party in local government, their hopes for a breakthrough in national politics could be thwarted by the "Blair factor".In making his party favourite to win the forthcoming election -- it leads the
5577 Conservatives by 20 points in the polls -- moderate leader Tony Blair has stolen Liberal clothes.Labour has adopted constitutional reforms such as a bill of rights which were once the smaller party's trade mark, and has moved much closer to the Liberals' pro-European stance.But Ashdown said electors would have to
5577 ask themselves what Labour now stood for after Blair had ditched so many of its traditional socialist beliefs."What do they believe in? How deep does the Blair revolution go? People don't ask these sort of questions about the Liberal Democrats," he told interviewer David Frost.The narrowing of differences between Labour
5577 and the Liberals has pushed the smaller party down to around 14 percent in the polls from 18 percent at the 1992 general election.They are trying to fight back by being bolder than Labour -- daring for example to contemplate raising taxes to pay for higher spending on education."We are
5577 going to confront issues instead of dodging them. The notion is, for a third party in our position, an important one," said Lord Richard Holme, the party's election supremo.The party's successes in local elections in recent years is buoying the spirits of activists gathering in Brighton.If they can win parliamentary
5577 seats where they run local councils, the breakthrough will, they say, be assured.But the Liberals' opponents are dismissive, saying even many of the people who vote Liberal reject key party policies such as its support for a single European currency.Conservative Party chairman Brian Mawhinney called a news conference last week
5577 to denounce the Liberals as "a radical left-wing party committed to threatening policies".A party spokeswoman was undisturbed. "Once they would have ignored us," she said. "Now they see us as a threat."</

5587 WELLINGTON, Sept 23 - The New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) on Monday unveiled its player transfer system for the 1997 season, NZPA reports.The system received ringing endorsements from NZRFU chairman Richie Guy, All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick and All Blacks manager Mike Banks."This will shape the future of New
5587 Zealand rugby," Guy said.Speaking on behalf of All Blacks management, Banks said having a clear structure in place for player movement among provinces "will enhance what we have to do in the professional environment". The system has three basic principles.It will reward individual unions for developing young players and give
5587 an incentive for the unions to invest in "grass roots" rugby.The transfer market will be player driven. They will retain control of where they play their rugby, they cannot be forced to transfer and they cannot be prevented from transferring by their unions. The other main tenet of the system
5587 is a desire to encourage evenness of teams and competitive rugby in New Zealand. With that in mind, the system will protect unions' player strengths by keeping a check on the number of players who can move to any one union.New Zealand players are split into 12 categories for the
5587 purpose of deciding the amount of compensation payable to unions losing players.Those categories range from All Blacks test players down to players enrolled in the NZRFU rugby academy next year. Top All Blacks are rated at a maximum of NZ$125,000 for compensation purposes. Compensation payments range downwards to $2000.A union
5587 will be entitled to acquire a maximum of five players in any one year. Those five players are spilt among the categories, therefore preventing a union getting five leading All Blacks at one time.All transfers will take place in November.</

5622 the weekend following a symposium of 400 leading Yugoslav financial and economic experts at this Montenegran seaside resort. The official also rejected calls by exporting companies to devalue the dinar, now pegged at 3.3 to the German mark.Banovic denied that the central bank was under increasing pressure from the governments
5622 of rump Yugoslavia and of its two constituent republics, Serbia and Montenegro, to print new money to finance the cash-starved economy and losses."On the contrary, the federal and both republic governments are appealing for tight control of monetary policy." He admitted however that pressure on the bank to print new
5622 money was coming from commercial banks and industry."They are used to asking the central bank for help whenever they have (financial) problems," he said.In 1993 the presses worked around the clock to print new money in a desperate bid to combat international sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia for its role in
5622 the Bosnian war, driving inflation to dizzying levels of 60 percent a day. Banovic said the NBY would regulate the volume of money supply and stability of currencies and prices using available mechanisms, adding: "But we will not help the financial recovery of the banks by just printing money."The central
5622 bank's foreign currency reserves, he said, had risen by 40 million German marks since December. It had sold half a million marks to Yugoslav companies to finance imports since December 1, but had bought 540 million marks over the same period, he added.The bank does not publish regular figures on
5622 foreign currency reserves, but in mid-May they stood at $335 million. The bank was closely monitoring the rise in money supply (M1) in order to control it at the level which would preserve currency and price stability, he said.He recalled that the NBY had introduced new measures in August to
5622 maintain and slow down the rising tendency of M1 and to force banks to resolve their insolvency problem by themselves."We just want them to do their own job," he said. "They should not expect us to do something that is not our job. We believe the new measures will help
5622 currency and price stability." Banovic suggested that banks and companies short of working capital should raise it by liquidating assets such as real estate, stocks and foreign currency."They must re-establish contacts with their partners abroad and try to get credits to maintain their solvency," he added.Banovic said the NBY had
5622 rejected demands by some sectors of the Yugoslav economy currently suffering big losses for the bank to finance their production."It could ease the situation and increase production but only in the short term," he said, adding that any gains would soon be neutralised by price increases and inflation. Annual inflation
5622 in August was running at 99.2 percent.Banovic also rejected calls for changes in the dinar exchange rate by export firms who argued that the currency was overvalued.He said that according to NBY's analysis of price increases here and abroad since Belgrade introduced a drastic monetary reform in February 1994, the
5622 dinar was now undervalued by two or three percent."There is still some room left for the prices to rise and there is no reason to even contemplate changing the currenct exchange rate," Banovic said.The dinar was devalued by 70 percent in November, bringing it into line with the black market
5622 rate of 3.3 dinars to one German mark, when it real value was 2.5 dinars to the mark. The current black market rate is 3.4 dinars to the mark.</

5641 The Brazilian government plans to lay off up to 40,000 federal government workers out of a total of 540,000 under its voluntary program which is being launched in November, a newsPaper said.Brazil's minister for public administration Luiz Carlos Bresser Pereira said it was too early to say exactly how many
5641 staff would take part in the program, but it would be somewhere between 20,000 and 40,000 workers, according to O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper. "I don't think we can talk exact numbers yet," he was quoted as saying by O Estado. "I don't think, for example, that we will
5641 reach 40,000."Bresser Pereira said the aim of the program was to create incentives for staff to leave their jobs in areas where excess personnel existed.He said the government was in the final stages of defining the terms of the voluntary redundancy program which would provide compensation for federal public workers
5641 based on the number of years of employment.A further 70,000 public sector jobs which are vacant at present will be eliminated and another 20,000 positions will disappear once the current holders retire, Bresser Pereira added.The government is also still studying the closure of state- owned companies, O Estado said.Bresser Pereira
5641 said an inter-ministerial working group was studying a preliminary list of 23 state-owned firms to determine exactly how many and which companies would be shut down.-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151</
5642 Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's approval rating has dipped under 50 percent, according to a new poll released Sunday.The survey of 3,000 people throughout the country by pollster Analistas y Consultores showed that 49.6 percent approved of Fujimori's record, while 42.3 percent did not approve, and 8.2 percent held no opinion.
5642 The polls, taken from September 6-17 and with a 1.8 percent margin of error, compared to previous Analistas y Consultores' polls giving Fujimori a 54.3 percent rating at the beginning of this month and 60.8 percent in August.The poll also found that the majority of Peruvians, 55.4 percent, would not
5642 vote for Fujimori were an election to be held now, while 36.6 percent would vote for him, and 8.0 percent expressed no opinion.Fujimori, who took office in 1990 and won re-election last year with an overwhelming 64 percent of the vote, has held relatively high popularity ratings during his term
5642 due primarily to the virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reforms and strong, personalized leadership style.But his perceived authoritarianism and the administration's failure to reduce high levels of poverty and unemployment is starting to take its toll on Fujimori's popularity, analysts say.-- Andrew Cawthorne, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134</
5643 Ruling party activists opposed to the government's free-market policies rebelled at a key party convention on Saturday, demanding a return to the party's socialist roots in the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution.Through shouts, clenched fists and fiery speeches, delegates of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has governed Mexico without a break
5643 since 1929, vented their fury at the foreign-educated technocrats who they say have betrayed party principles in government.Since 1982, three successive PRI presidents of Mexico have broken with the party's left-wing, nationalistic past to encourage free markets, economic orthodoxy and foreign investment. Many rank-and-file party members have had enough."Block the
5643 way of the technocrats!" and "We need a revolutionary, nationalist spirit!" were the rallying cries heard repeatedly from the podium, received with roars of "Hard, hard, hard!" from the audience.One speaker, Rafael Garcia Vasquez, of the state of Baja California, won ecstatic applause for his accusation that by allowing the
5643 conservative opposition PAN party win its first-ever governorships over the past decade, the PRI had "done deals with the forces of reaction" and "fallen victim to the fascist right."The aggressive stance of many delegates on Saturday, the second day of the PRI's 17th National Assembly, marked a dramatic change from
5643 previous PRI assemblies, which have generally been stage-managed affairs designed to shore up the government of the day.Delegates at a session on party statutes approved a proposal to oblige future presidential candidates to be PRI militants of at least 10 years' standing who have won at least one elected job
5643 -- a rule that would have excluded President Ernesto Zedillo (himself a foreign-educated technocrat) if it had been in place for the 1994 presidential election.Analysts said the decision was likely to shatter a half-century-old Mexican tradition under which the president of the day nominates his successor from within his Cabinet.Zedillo's
5643 name was conspicuous by its absence during the first two days of the assembly, though he was scheduled to address its closing plenary session on Sunday.Delegates were far more concerned with Luis Donaldo Colosio, the PRI's original candidate for the 1994 presidential race, who was assassinated months before the election.Copies
5643 of Colosio's ideology and political proposals were handed out to all delegates, and any speaker who identified himself with the Territorial Movement, a grass-roots party organisation set up by Colosio, was cheered ecstatically.Many PRI militants believe Colosio's murder was a political plot hatched at some level of the government, but
5643 the party leadership tried to keep the delicate topic off the agenda in the interests of party unity.When Ramiro de la Rosa, from the Democracy 2000 reform wing of the PRI, accused former President Carlos Salinas of being a "thief and a murderer" responsible for Colosio's death, he was grabbed,
5643 dragged off and thrown out of the hall.A later session on party statutes broke down completely as delegates jeered a senator, Eduardo Andrade, when he accused them of creating a "dangerous impression of a break with the president of the republic," Zedillo.The committee chairing the meeting switched off the podium
5643 microphones while Andrade spoke, infuriating the senator, who attempted to snatch another microphone from the chairman.Chaos ensued as reporters invaded the stage and delegates rose to their feet to boo and whistle at Andrade, who admitted that he had been sent by the party leadership to give his message to
5643 the delegates.PRI president Santiago Onate had to rush in and suspend proceedings to allow tempers to cool before the meeting continued. But in a sign of the hardliners' strength, the group chairing the meeting was replaced with a lineup more acceptable to the rank-and-file militants.Other party meetings on Saturday were
5643 considering whether to expel Salinas, whose 1988-94 administration was the prelude to Mexico's December 1994 economic crash, and oppose the privatisation of the petrochemical industry, a Zedillo policy.</
5644 President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said in an interview being published on Sunday he was considering running for a second term, confirming that he wanted to become Brazil's first president to be re-elected.Asked if he would run in the 1998 elections if the constitution was revised to allow the possibility and
5644 the economic stability he introduced stayed on track, he replied, "I would.""I am in favour of re-election as an idea, and if the constitution were to be rewritten, I think I should have the right to stand," the president told veteran political reporter Elio Gaspari in the interview, conducted for
5644 the newspapers O Globo and O Estado de Sao Paulo.Until now, Cardoso has limited himself to discreet comments in favour of the theory of re-election, declining to say whether he wanted to emulate his Peruvian and Argentine counterparts, both of whom rewrote their respective constitutions to allow them to stand
5644 for, and win, second terms.In Sunday's interview, Cardoso continued to shy away from explicitly saying he would be a candidate in 1998. "A president can't say he wants this or that. You have to feel whether or not society is willing to accept it," he was quoted as saying.So far
5644 Brazilian society seems less than enthusiastic about re-election, which for many still smacks of the authoritarianism of the country's rule by imperial Portugal and of the 1964-85 military dictatorship. A recent poll found 62 percent of those questioned were against the idea of Cardoso's running again.Another poll showed support of
5644 just 40 percent of members of Congress, where the re-election debate is expected to begin in October with the first meeting of a lower house committee.Observers say the president faces the toughest test of his two years in power in trying to get a constitutional amendment allowing re-election through a
5644 volatile Chamber of Deputies, where his ambitions will clash with those of other would-be presidents.Cardoso himself, in an interview published on the eve of election day in 1994, said re-election would prove too hot an issue to touch during his term. "Imagine what a campaign for re-electing a sitting president
5644 would be like. He is liable to lose everything, because everyone will say he is using the state machine to get what he wants," Cardoso was quoted as saying.On the president's side in the re-election debate are the country's powerful state governors and mayors, who are also currently banned from
5644 re-election but would be granted the chance of a second term by the proposed legislative changes.In Sunday's interview, the president considered the possibility of the amendment's being defeated in Congress but said any successor would be bound to continue his policies of fiscal restraint, which have slashed Brazil's once sky-high
5644 inflation and kept Cardoso's personal approval ratings high."Like it or not, Brazil is on a clear path," he told the newspapers. "Now we are facing the possibilty of ending next year with single-digit inflation. You want to know something? I never thought I would see that day."</

5662 Australian grain prices continued to fall heavily last week as markets grimly celebrated the big world crop and traders looked for further price declines.Cash wheat prices fell by up to A$15.00 a tonne for the benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW), and while futures prices fell less than this the prospect
5662 at week's end was for a continued market slide. Australian wheat prices have now fallen by more than A$40.00 a tonne in the last three months as Australia consolidated its own big 1996/97 grain crop and as an expected poor crop in the U.S. and elsewhere gradually emerged much bigger
5662 than thought.Futures broker Ben Suttie of C, A &amp; L Bell Commodities said A$120.00 a tonne for January 1997 futures was now a prospect, against the contract's Friday settlement close of A$163.50."I think we're (prices are) going to weaken as we go into harvest. We've got a huge crop out
5662 there. Bar a frost the crop's going to be huge," he said. "(Cash) ASW delivered Newcastle (on Friday was) A$155.00 offer - A$120 here we come." Guy Allen of GrainCorp saw last week's Australian market fall as largely reflecting Australian concern over European export subsidies.Rain toward the end of the
5662 week in wheatgrowing areas added to the bearish news, he said.End users were still not coming to the market, he said.Peter Howard of New England Agricultural Traders described last week's market as an "absolute capitulation" and as having turned "extremely ugly". Feed barley had lost A$20 a tonne over the
5662 past two weeks to reach a bidding quote of A$114.00 a tonne on Friday, while the wheat market had virtually dried up with no farmers considering selling at present prices, Howard said.The sorghum market in the past week was also very thin, with old crop down A$10.00-A$12.00 to A$170 delivered
5662 Newcastle and the new crop down to about A$152.00.Some signs were emerging of consumer buying in the U.S., but the market continued to drop."Perhaps it will flop about for months," Howard said, adding that chartists were still bearish. 5662 Wheat Board's pool price revision, expected on Monday.Allen said the trade expected a cut for ASW of A$5.00-A$15.00 a tonne, with the best bet A$10.00.Suttie said pool prices were expected to be down by another A$5.00-A$10.00 after the last price cut, of A$10.00 a tonne on September 10 to A$205.00
5662 a tonne for ASW.Suttie pointed out that the ASW pool price, at A$205.00, less A$27.00 duty into store, stood at a net A$178, while at A$155.00 cash wheat was A$20-A$23 less than the pool. The AWB's indicative price for new crop ASW wheat delivered Newcastle fell by A$15.00 to A$158.00

5668 had no consultation on whatsoever," Australian Gas Association (AGA) chairman Greg Harvey told a news conference at the start of a three-day AGA gas convention."The country has to develop an interstate market. 5669 The copper price fell through the US$1,900 per tonne support level on Friday night after it failed on the upside earlier in the week as the market moved into contango. Gold and silver prices also weakened, with silver ending at an 18-month low, but oil and wheat prices firmed.The CRB
5669 index ended 0.72 points lower at 244.42.METALSLME copper prices sagged on Friday to end the week precariously hovering below $1,900 per tonne as a new wave of negative sentiment swept world metals markets.Speculative sales hit copper again crimping a rally up from $1,850 a week ago -- a level it
5669 threatened to revisit after Friday's $36 drop to the LME afternoon close exactly at $1,900.Copper weakened again by some $20 in late inter-office activity. Dealers cited an emerging contango when forward values are higher than the nearby delivery price.Copper had been in steep backwardation with spot supply commanding a premium
5669 recently when star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, sacked in June by Japan's Sumitomo Corp, was building stocks in an apparent bid to defend a high price.Traders said the fundamental picture post-Hamanaka is now clearer. Despite falling warehouse stocks and a pick-up in physical interest in Europe, the market now believes that
5669 an oversupply in copper will be the feature in 1997.In a tv interview on Sunday BHP chief executive John Prescott said he would not describe himself as bullish on the copper price and said BHP would have to learn to live with the lower prices. BHP is the world's second
5669 largest copper producer.Aluminium clawed up from Friday's new 2-1/4 year low of $1,403 on end-week covering and technical support.Traders said the market is likely to fall below $1,400 soon, with fundamentals all depressive. 5673 Australian markets, like markets around the world, will be dominated this week by the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.There is little of interest locally to distract markets from Fed watching. Wednesday's appearance by new RBA Governor Ian Macfarlane the key scheduled event on the
5673 domestic calendar.U.S. Treasuries and U.S. dollar trade was subdued on Friday ahead of the FOMC meeting with traders having either squared up or already taken their positions. The Dow Jones index closed stronger, up 20.72 points, ending three days of losses.Ahead of the FOMC meeting, trade is expected to be
5673 cautious.The outcome remains in doubt, with a hike of 25 points seen as the most likely outcome, although many analysts expect any hike to be held over until the November meeting.The local highlight is Wednesday's maiden speech by Ian Macfarlane as RBA govenor.Macfarlane will be appearing in Canberra with ex-RBA
5673 head Bernie Fraser and UK Treasury Permanent Secretary Sir Terence Burns on a panel to be chaired by Treasury Secretary Ted Evans.The topic of the panel is "Fiscal and Monetary Policy Indeterdependance and Central Bank Independence," and Macfarlane will delivered a prepared speech.While the U.S. is expected to raise rates,
5673 if not this week then in November after the Presedential election, local sentiment still favours another rate cut this year.One data release that may receive greater than usual attention given the market's bullish mood on rates is Thursday's job vacancies data for the three months to August released by the
5673 Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS)."The ABS's quarterly job vacancy series provides the most statistically reliable guide to future employment growth," Commonwealth Bank economist Tim Moloney said. "To date markets have paid it less attention than they prehaps should," he said.The stalling in the labour market was a key factor behind
5673 the RBA's decision to cut rates on July 31, and markets grow more confident of another rate cut with each sign of continuing labour force weakness. The data is expected to show a fall of about five percent, but forecasts range up to a 10 percent fall.Car registrations data for
5673 August are due on Friday. Forecasts centre on a rise of 3.9 percent for the month.BONDS: (Friday: 10 year bonds 7.97 percent, 3-year 7.08)Local bonds should start the week on a cautious note ahead of the FOMC, with the potential to continue their recent out-performance of the U.S. market.With the
5673 absence of any major local data this week, the market will be focussed on the FOMC meeting.The U.S. bond market has talked about nothing else in the last few weeks as it debated whether the Fed will tighten policy, and in that time local bonds have generally shown a tightening
5673 bias on a spread differential basis.The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread touched its lowest level in over two years last week at 106 basis points.Analysts believe that given Australia's current positive fundamentals it can ride out any storm from the U.S. if the Fed does hike rates on Tuesday.Some economists
5673 also believe that a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates may even be taken positively by U.S. Treasuries as it would be seen as a pro-active move by the Fed to contain inflation."A rate hike would show that the U.S. is very serious about inflation," said State Bank
5673 of New South Wales chief economist Hans Kunnen.Such a response would also help the local debt market."If U.S. bond yields fall, Australian bonds will follow," Kunnen said. "With inflation low in Australia and the economy stalling, bond dealers need little encouragement to buy."AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR: (Friday: US$0.7915/20, NY $0.7912/17)The Australian dollar
5673 will start the week above US$0.7900 after holding reasonably steady in New York trade, but it remains vulnerable to the downside after failing to break past resitance at US$0.7950.As with other markets, the lack of domestic data means the major event of the week is the FOMC meeting.If the Fed
5673 does hike by 0.25 point it would trim the local dollar's yield advantage and leave it very vulnerable to a possible easing in domestic policy later this year.However, dealers felt that as long as the hike was only 0.25 point, the AUD's yield advantage would still be enough to attract
5673 Japanese investor demand and should therefore limit the dollar's downside to US$0.7865 or so.If the Fed restrains itself, there was scope for the currency to re-test 80 cents again, although analysts reckoned world commodity prices were not yet buoyant enough to justify levels much above there.Macfarlane's comments on Wednesday will
5673 be dissected for any clues to his stance on monetary policy -- he is thought to be more of a hawk on inflation than his predecessor.AUSTRALIAN STOCKS: (Fri: All Ordinaries 2240.8, down 6.3)Wall Street's 20.72 point rise on Friday, ending three days of losses, should be supportive of local markets,
5673 although the All Ordinaries has under-performed the U.S. recently. The All Ordinaries lost 11.5 points over the week to Friday.While the FOMC will also give the local market a lead, metal prices remain the key for the market."The resources are likely to be the stronger influence over the short term
5673 as commodity prices are being watched very closely," one Sydney-based broker said.Copper fell again on Friday, ending under the US$1,900 per tonne support level in LME trade. Aluminium also touched a 2-1/4 year low of US$1,403, and although it managed to end at $1,412, traders said it was likely to
5673 fall below US$1,400 soon.BHP chief executive John Prescott said in a weekend tv interview he would not describe himself as bullish on the copper price. "I think it's fallen a bit further than it would have had it not been for (the) Sumitomo incident, but we have to learn in
5673 these circumstances to live with lower copper prices for some time and I'd regard any short term spikes as just that."Brokers said lack of local data and the end of the reporting season were seen keeping trade fairly quiet this week.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800</

5674 their forecast of 1996/97 total business investment.The government forecast in the budget was for a 14 percent rise in total business investment -- which consists of plant and equipment and non-dwelling construction spending.Market economists tended to come in below that forecast, although they did say the Treasury had a good
5674 track record on business investment in recent years. Of the 31 economists surveyed, only three forecast a figure stronger than the government, while another three expected the government's forecast to be met.Those at the weaker end of forecasts tended to have weaker GDP growth forecasts than the government's 3.5 percent.This
5674 fit in within recently retired Reserve Bank Govenor Bernie Fraser's statement in Tokyo earlier this month that "the main key to achieving the 3.5 percent GDP growth forecast for 1996/97 is business investment." Some eocnomists said the government forecast may have erred on the upside, as the business investment forecast
5674 could effect sentiment. A weak forecast could have undermined some confidence by creating the belief that the budget would be contractionary, economists said. 5678 A New Zealand First-led government would drive down the value of the New Zealand dollar and bring about lower interest rates, party leader Winston Peters said on Sunday."We intend to drive that dollar down in the interests of exporters -- the most critical people we need for this country --
5678 and at the same time interest rates will fall back," Peters said on Television One's "Meet the Press" current affairs programme. Peters was responding to journalists' questions about his party's proposed compulsory savings levy of eight cents in the dollar.He said he did not underestimate the difficulty some people would
5678 have in paying the levy in addition to paying off a mortgage, but said a lower dollar would cause interest rates to fall and make mortgages more affordable."That relief will be able to assist them in terms of their long-term savings capacity," he said.New Zealand was "in hock to international
5678 money" and needed to start to finance its own development. "We do intend to give the cheque back and to take the forest back," he said.New Zealand First has been running neck and neck with the Labour party for second place behind the ruling National party government in recent political
5678 opinion polls.A general election will be held on October 12.--Wellington Newsroom 64 4 4714 277 "Long-term, we have the vision of making ourselves independent," Peters said.He said New Zealand First's foreign investment policy, which would limit offshore ownership in "strategic" New Zealand assets to 24.9 percent, was non-negotiable."We understand the
5678 difference between foreign investment and foreign control. Foreign investment should be in our interest, not just in theirs."He said New Zealand First would reclaim the recently privatised Forestry Corporation from the Fletcher Challenge -led consortium which purchased it.</
5679 Commodity prices in Australian dollar terms fell during September, according to the international commodity price review, released by the National Farmers' Federation (NFF) and Dresdner Australia International.NFF's director of economic policy, Todd Ritchie, said the renewed Iraqi conflict had provoked a surge in crude oil prices during the month, but
5679 the rises masked a decline in the price of metals and lower prices for most agricultural commodities."The conflict also halted the planned sale from Australia of one million tonnes of wheat per year, which would have been allowed under the 'oil for aid' programme," he said. Rural prices in special
5679 drawing rights (SDR) terms increased marginally by 0.1 percent during September and were now 5.6 percent higher than a year ago, Ritchie said.However, in Australian dollar terms, prices fell by 1.8 percent during the month, he said.Beef prices improved slightly during September but prices fell for sorghum, barley, wheat, rice,
5679 cotton and wool, he said.Wheat prices continued to soften following a number of developments during September, including an upward revision of the estimated global wheat crop and the news that the European Union had reintroduced wheat export subsidies, he said. Wool prices have also weakened since the end of August,
5679 although there is a more optimistic outlook for demand in the first half of 1997, and beef prices are expected to remain relatively weak in the short-term, Ritchie said.Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said the SDR commodity index rose 1.2 percent during September but in Australian dollar terms it fell
5679 by 0.7 percent due to a stronger A$ during the month. "The strong appreciation over the past 12 months has resulted in the index dropping to a level 3.8 percent lower than a year ago," Henderson said. Improving prospects for growth in Japan and Western Europe, combined with a strong
5679 and resilient U.S. economy, suggested higher prices for the mining sector into 1997, Henderson said.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</
5680 Australian housing is due to be the most affordable for 10 years during the December quarter, Westpac Banking Corporation's Spring housing report shows.Bill Evans, general manager of economic strategy and planning at Westpac, said affordability was high as a result of steady wages growth."With the relationship between housing prices and
5680 wages back to where it was a decade ago and recent interest rate cuts, buying conditions (are improving)," he said.The affordability index for Australia was forecast at 151.5 in the December quarter up from a forecast September quarter level of 144.8 and a December 1995 level of 130.8.Evans said the
5680 Westpac index was derived from Australian Bureau of Statisitcs numbers which were adjusted to remove the influence of price changes in prestige properties and quality houses."Once these distortions are removed, it becomes clear that it is easier to afford a house now than at any time over the last 10
5680 years," he said.Westpac's housing report forecast an improvement in residential construction, with starts forecast to reach 120,000 in 1996 and 137,000 the year after.New South Wales and Victoria seen as the best positioned for near-term recovery, Westpac said.-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373 1800</

5682 The chief of the Royal Dutch/Shell oil group has expressed confidence that oil and gas resources in the South China Sea can be developed peacefully despite competing territorial claims.Cor Herkstroter, chairman of the oil major's committee of managing directors, made the comment during a visit to Australia where he affirmed
5682 the group's belief that the "breathtaking" opportunities in Asia outweighed potential regional problems."There could be (problems)," Herkstroter told reporters in a select media briefing before leaving the country on Saturday."But in the end everybody is interested in finding a solution I think, because if you have too many disputes then
5682 nothing (no development) will happen."So I am inclined to think something will be sorted out."Herkstroter's confidence in the peaceful development of resources in the South China Sea comes as Southeast Asian nations and the United States are reported to have expressed disquiet over the scale of China's territorial claims there.
5682 In July China called for joint development of disputed territories in the South China Sea after a political confrontation with the Philippines last year over a part of the hotly contested Spratly islands.Thought to be rich in both oil and minerals, the islands are claimed in their entirety by China
5682 and Taiwan and in part by Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Brunei.Vietnam, China and Taiwan also contest sovereignty of the nearby Paracel islands. In the gas-rich Natuna islands, off Indonesian Borneo, Jakarta staged war games this month after Beijing included the Natunas in a map of Chinese territory.But Herkstroter said:
5682 "I believe that, in this region of the world, opportunities outweigh problems by a large margin."He said the central economic theme in the region was growth, which would boost demand for oil, coal and gas."A good example is the gas industry," he told a private dinner held here earlier during
5682 his visit."The emergence of significant demand, primarily from a number of urban centres, from Jakarta in the south to Tokyo in the east and Bombay in the west, is likely to create the need for the most extensive gas pipeline network yet seen in the world." He envisaged a gas
5682 pipeline network linking fields in Turkmenistan, Iran, Siberia, Sakhalin and the South China Sea with consumption centres for the gas scattered as widely."The scale of such a network is breathtaking," he said."Many of its component parts are already being built and any energy company that sees itself as a global
5682 player...must take part."A meeting last month of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (APEC) energy officals highlighted the forecast surge in regional energy demand.They were told that US$1.6 trillion of investment capital was needed to meet this demand over the next 10 years, and that the region was shifting increasingly to natural

5683 during morning assembly, while steelworkers south of Sydney visit the biggest Buddhist temple in the southern hemisphere.As Australia's multicultural society blossoms, many people are turning away from traditional Western religions and looking towards Asia and the Middle East for spiritual enlightenment.According to the latest census, Buddhism has become the fastest
5683 growing faith in Australia, growing 300 percent between 1981 and 1991, closely followed by Islam.In 1991 there were 140,000 Buddhists. The 1996 census conducted last month is expected to show about 200,000, or one percent, of Australia's 18 million population are Buddhists.Some Buddhist leaders believe their followers will make up
5683 10 percent of the population within 50 years.The growth in Buddhism, albeit from a low base, has been largely due to migration, with a third of Buddhists born in Vietnam and 20 percent in Malaysia, Cambodia or Laos.But there is a growing list of Anglo-Celtic Australians converting to Buddhism. Tens
5683 of thousands of Australians are flocking to hear the words of Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, during his current two-week visit."Life is becoming more stressful in Australia and people are looking for a way to overcome that stress, so they are looking to practices like Buddhism," said Graeme
5683 Lyall, a 65-year-old convert and chairman of the Buddhist Council of New South Wales.Buddhists also say their godless faith fits well with Western scientific and secular perspectives, making it attractive to Australians of Christian origin."Traditional religions are finding they have conflicts with advances in science. 5683 with science as the Buddha taught there are many world systems," explained Lyall.The Dalai Lama said Buddhism has also become fashionable in Western societies. 5683 the 1991 census there were 300,000 Moslems in Australia. 5683 and Melbourne."We are seeing more and more young people coming forward and becoming more attached to Islam," said Ali Roude, chairman of the Islamic Council of New South Wales."You walk in the streets and you find young women, Moslem women, wearing the hijab as an expression of their identity and
5683 belief. 5683 at the turn of the century when thousands of Chinese arrived during the country's gold rush. 5683 But Islam's initial impact was negligible -- herds of feral camels and abandoned mosques were the only legacy.The introduction in 1901 of the White Australia policy, a racist immigration law which judged migrants on their English, saw Buddhist and Moslem numbers drop dramatically.The end of the racist policy by the
5683 early 1970s and a need for cheap labour saw Middle Eastern migrants welcomed, while conflict in Indochina resulted in Buddhist refugees.But Australians were not tolerant of either, ranking Islam and Buddhism the two most disliked faiths.Today, Australia is a multicultural society where ethnicity is protected by law."The Australian way of
5683 life encourages tolerance and respect, so it is easier to practice a non-Western religion in this country than in other countries," said Kerry Trembath, a Catholic who converted to Buddhism 10 years ago.Silma Ihram, an Anglo-Celtic Prostestant who converted to Islam and founded the Noor-Al-Houda Islamic school in western Sydney,

5683 lost touch with Islam and that religious tolerance had grown with education. "Educators now teach Islam as not such a heathen religion," Ihram said.</

5790 Egypt earned a record of more than $3 billion from tourism in the 1995-96 fiscal year, up 30.9 percent from the previous year, the government newspaper al-Gomhuria said on Sunday.Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi said in Alexandria that foreign exchange receipts from tourism amounted to just over $3 billion during the
5790 year, $710 million more than in 1994-95. The year ends on June 30.According to figures released by the tourism ministry earlier, the number of people visiting Egypt in 1995-96 was 3.620 million, 27.8 percent more than in 1994-95.Tourism in the 1995 calendar year had already matched the record-breaking year 1992.
5790 Attacks on tourist targets by Islamist militants had led to a slump in 1993 and 1994.The last attack was in March this year, when gunmen massacred 18 Greek tourists outside a Cairo hotel. But it appeared to be an isolated incident and its effect on tourist arrivals was both minor
5790 and short-lived.Tourism is Egypt's third largest source of foreign exchange, after remittances from Egyptians abroad and visible exports.</

5797 Saudi Arabia has ambitious plans to dig beneath its vast desert sands. But this time it will be searching for minerals rather than oil to boost its wealth.The world's richest oil producer already mines eight tonnes of gold a year, but its wealth of zinc, copper, bauxite, phospates, silver, iron
5797 and yet more gold are waiting to be exploited as part of a drive to reduce reliance on oil earnings of $40 billion yearly.Analysts say slow government approval for exploration licences is holding back development of the sector, which is forecast to grow faster than any other in the state's
5797 five-year plan to 2000, at an average annual real rate of nine percent."The new minister is pushing hard to develop the industry, but the Saudi government has to move faster to develop the minerals sector," said one Saudi executive."The main mining ventures are taking so much time because the mining
5797 industry is pretty new so there is plenty of red tape," said another mining executive, of the numerous projects which have been on the drawing board for years.They include four gold and silver deposits, which like other Saudi sites are likely to be developed as open-pit mines."Because they lack previous
5797 experience in these fields it is pretty natural that a mining licence should take longer than one for oil. But these have taken far too much time," he said, adding some firms had waited for over three years for a licence.The government plan for the economy up to the year
5797 2000 concedes that this discourages foreign private involvement, so far limited to Swedish firm Boliden Mineral Aktiebolag, a unit of Trelleborg."The main reasons preventing the private sector engaging in mining activities are: the long procedures involved in obtaining mining concessions, the fact that many promising mining deposits are often located
5797 in remote areas, and inadequate financial support..." the state plan says.A Saudi firm, Arabian Shield Development Co which is listed in the United States, has a mining concession for the al-Masane deposit in the southwest, but production is not due to start until late 1997.The government is taking steps to
5797 improve things. It is setting up a state-owned firm -- the Saudi Arabian Mining Co, Maadin -- which analysts say will be given some independence."This is a positive move and part of plans to diversify away from oil," said a Western diplomat in Riyadh."Now the ministry is looking at changing
5797 its approach on processing quotations to make it similar to (state oil firm Saudi) Aramco. The new arrangement will be set up in the new year. It might speed up procedures," said a mining executive.Aramco, the world's largest oil firm, has administrative and structural freedoms which few state firms enjoy
5797 in the kingdom.The Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources has also set up a committee to reassess previous mining practice and look at ways to encourage private investment of the sector.Executives said incentives for foreign investors include a five-year tax holiday and exemption from duty on main imports.But these have
5797 not been enough to lure private firms. "One important change would be if they ease the mining code to make it easier for foreign companies to seek and get mining licences. That is paramount if the sector is to prosper," said one.The state plan to 2000 speaks of eventual private
5797 sector involvement: "In the longer term, when the profitability of Petromin's precious metals activities becomes more firmly established, shares in Petromin's minerals company will be offered to private investors."Apart from private participation, executives also see a need for development of supporting infrastructure around reserves, which are widely scattered across the
5797 huge desert kingdom.Despite offers to develop a phosphate deposit in the north, analysts say the estimated $1.7 billion project is unlikely to come on stream before 2000 because of its inaccessibility."The directorate general of mineral resources is meeting firms in November to look at bids for the al-Jalamid phosphate mine.
5797 But by the time the bids are accepted and construction starts, production is unlikely for another five or six years because it is so remote," said the Western diplomat."First they have to decide how they will get phosphates to customers and ports," he added.</

5801 Oil companies may again come in for criticism as gasoline prices turn up, but refiners are also being punished by the surge in oil prices in recent weeks, analysts say.Though the major integrated oil companies make up on high oil prices what they lose on the refinery margins, those in
5801 the industry specialising on the "downstream" or refining and marketing end of the market are feeling the pinch."These are not the worst gasoline margins, but they are certainly one of the worst," said David Zinamon, director of refining and environmental affairs at consultants Petroleum Industry Research Associates.Some of those companies
5801 heavily skewed toward gasoline refining are Chevron Corp., Valero Energy Corp., Diamond Shamrock Inc., Sun Co. and Tosco Corp., analysts said.The margin squeeze can be seen on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), where gasoline futures prices have lagged badly behind the 16 percent rise in crude oil prices since
5801 early August.This week, gasoline's premium above the U.S. benchmark crude oil West Texas Intermediate fell to $2.25 a barrel -- the lowest level since October, 1994. The premium has averaged around $5 over the past two years.The reasons for the dismal gasoline margins is that refiners have been increasing their
5801 overall runs to produce more heating oil, which has seen its premium skyrocket to nearly $5 as inventories dwindled to historically low levels ahead of winter."They are going to try to lean toward making distillate (mainly heating oil) as much as possible but ... for gasoline output this will be
5801 hard," said Linda Abramo, analyst with Energy Security Analysis Inc.United States refineries generally are geared up to produce twice as much gasoline as heating oil from a barrel crude oil.The pressure on gasoline margins is likely to remain in place for some months, made worse by the fact that Europe
5801 is facing a similar situation.With heating oil stocks there also running well below typical levels, European refineries also are producing a larger surplus of gasoline."We see maybe a little blip up in October or November due to tensions between Iraq and the U.S. dying down, but we don't expect it
5801 to improve that much after that," said Abramo.</
