5805 President Bill Clinton's representatives on Saturday scrapped their hopes of including Ross Perot in presidential debates, agreeing to a one-on-one format with Republican nominee Bob Dole who had refused to share the stage with the feisty Texas billionaire.After more than nine hours of talks, negotiators for Clinton and Dole agreed
5805 to hold two 90-minute debates. The agreement also calls for one debate between Vice President Al Gore and Dole's running mate Jack Kemp.The first presidential debate will be held on Oct. 6 in Hartford, Connecticut, followed by the vice presidential match up in St. Petersburg, Florida on Oct. 9.The last
5805 presidential debate will be held in San Diego on October 16, and, unlike the previous debates, will have a town hall format that allows participants to directly question the nominees.The Clinton campaign tried to keep Reform Party candidate Perot and his running mate Pat Choate in the mix, but the
5805 Dole campaign was flatly oppossed to their inclusion, said Clinton's lead negotiator, Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor."We're sorry Mr. Perot and Mr. Choate are not in the debates, we did everything we can, but the president said there has to be debates, we cannot allow these to go by the board.
5805 They are in the best interest of the people," Kantor said.Analysts had said the Clinton campaign favoured Perot's presence in the debates because he would tend to draw votes away from Dole, which is why Dole opposed Perot's presence."I think what we have come up with is acceptable to the
5805 Dole campaign," said Dole's chief negotiator, former South Carolina Gov. Carroll Campbell. "The fact is we have one-on-one debates with the president of the United States and Senator Dole and that is what we wanted and we wanted a minimum of two of them."Cambell said the Dole camp became willing
5805 to accept the town hall format for one debate when it became clear Perot was out of the mix."We had a very substantive discussion off and on all day," Campbell, who also heads the American Council of Life Insurance, told reporters. "We did not agree on everything. We worked it
5805 out as we went along."The gregarious Clinton is widely thought to have the edge in the more spontaneous town hall-type debates, and his side argued vigorously for a format that served him well in 1992.The three cities chosen have never before hosted presidential debates. Kantor said he was "delighted to
5805 be in California anytime we can go there. We've spent some time there as some of you have noticed."Clinton holds a whopping lead in polls over Dole in the state, the biggest prize in the November election, and he has visited there dozens of times during his presidency.Negotiators said they
5805 expect to agree on moderators before Tuesday when both sides were to sign the debate agreement.The Clinton team originally wanted two debates lasting two hours each with one including Perot, and one vice presidential debate. Dole, trailing in the polls, had wanted three 75-minute presidential debates and one vice presidential
5805 debate, with Perot excluded.On Friday, Perot lodged a formal complaint with the Federal Election Commission. His campaign said it would file a lawsuit on Monday over the Commission on Presidential Debates' decision to bar him from the debates.The debate commission, which makes non-binding recommendations, last Tuesday said Perot and Choate
5805 should be excluded from debates, declaring the Perot ticket had no real chance of winning the Nov. 5 election.</
5806 The city where Little Richard was born, Otis Redding grew up, James Brown got his start and the Allman Brothers pioneered southern rock celebrated its rich musical heritage Sunday by opening a $6.5 million Georgia Music Hall of Fame.The 43,000-square-foot, three-story museum, which recreates a music festival in a small
5806 Georgia village, features more than 150 artists, including blues pioneer "Ma" Rainey, the Allman Brothers, and groups like R.E.M. and the B-52's.The music museum, funded with state and private money, has been a pet project of Governor Zell Miller for almost 20 years. Miller is giving the museum proceeds from
5806 the sale of his newly-updated book about Georgia musicians called "They Heard Georgia Singing.""The mother of the blues, Gertrude 'Ma' Rainey, was from Columbus, Georgia," Miller said. "The father of gospel music, Thomas Dorsey, is from Villa Rica, Georgia. Johnny Mercer, one of the great lyricists of all times, is
5806 from Savannah."James Brown got his start in Macon, backed by a local car dealer. Richard Penniman, better known as Little Richard, wrote "Tutti Frutti" while washing dishes at the Greyhound bus station in Macon."I am the architect of rock and roll. I am the originator. I am the emancipator. I
5806 am the man who started it all," the ebullient Richard said at the gala opening of the museum on Saturday night. The Hall of Fame opened to the general public on Sunday.Macon was also home of the Capricorn Records label, which launched the Allman Brothers Band, the Marshall Tucker Band,
5806 Johnny Jenkins and Wet Willie in the 1970s.Governor Miller said his interest in music was sparked by watching fiddlers in the north Georgia mountains. "Every time there was something in a magazine or something in the newspaper, I'd tear it out and put it in a box," he said."We've heard
5806 that story before, but we haven't seen the box," said assistant curator Deborah Besser, who stressed the museum's collection is in its early stages.While visitors can listen to a two-hour radio programme on Georgia musicians in one of the museum's small, themed rooms, most of the Hall of Fame is
5806 dedicated to displays of memorabilia, with little history or background.Among the items on display are the shoes singer-songwriter Otis Redding was wearing when he died in a plane crash in 1967, a dollhouse from the collection of country singer Brenda Lee, and the tape machine James Brown used to record
5806 his first hit, "Please, Please, Please."A gift shop selling Georgia music includes recordings by Jimi Hendrix, because the guitarist spent two years in Atlanta. There is also a museum display dedicated to southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd."They're from Florida, but Georgia claims them too," said Judy Van Zant, who lent
5806 items to the museum including musical instruments, stage costumes, and an opened bottle of Jack Daniels whiskey.The museum also highlights country, jazz and swing music and the white and black gospel music unique to the South.Organisers, who had hoped to open the museum before the Summer Olympics in Atlanta, estimate
5806 the Hall of Fame will attract 175,000 to 250,000 people annually.</
5807 Shuttle Atlantis will depart space station Mir on Monday, leaving astronaut John Blaha behind for four months with two Russian crewmates he never expected to work with.Blaha had trained for six months at Star City, outside Moscow, with cosmonauts Gennadi Manakov and Pavel Vinogradov. But just days before the two
5807 Russians were due to head for Mir in a Soyuz spacecraft, they were grounded for medical reasons.Manakov had failed a routine heart checkup, and Russian flight rules required that both men be replaced with their backups.Blaha, a 54-year-old Vietnam veteran with four shuttle missions to his credit, was devastated when
5807 NASA called to tell him the news."I knew I was going to go, but I thought it was terrible," he told Reuters before his launch last Monday. "I got to Star City in Russia. I wasn't happy. I went to a breakfast on Monday where they send the crew off.
5807 It was terrible, absolutely terrible. I wasn't in a happy mood at all."This wasn't the first time Blaha had faced a change of crew. For a year he prepared to fly with cosmonauts Vasily Tsibliev and Alexander Lazutkin, but in February they were assigned to another mission.As for his new
5807 crewmates, Valeri Korzun and Alexander "Sasha" Kaleri, they were almost strangers.A few days after hearing the "jolting" news, Blaha spent some time with Korzun and Kaleri as they prepared for launch at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan."I decided we have got to start getting happy," Blaha said. "I think it's
5807 going to work. They're both good people. They want it to work and I do. The only way to be happy is to try to be nice with each other."On Sunday Blaha appeared on television shoulder to shoulder with Korzun and said he was comfortable in his new home after
5807 just three days aboard the Russian orbital outpost."Valeri and Sasha ... have really helped me out in the last few days," he said. "I had a great night's sleep, and I feel very good on the Mir right now."Blaha, who replaces space marathon woman Shannon Lucid, will bid farewell to
5807 the shuttle crew early on Monday when the hatches close between the craft. He will be left with his Russian colleagues until Atlantis returns in January to pick him up.If Blaha doesn't get on with his crewmates, he can always retire to one of Mir's interconnected modules and watch a
5807 movie. Among the 50 videotapes he took to Mir are the "Star Wars" and "Star Trek" movies."I like space stuff," Blaha said.</

5811 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentIn old Western movies, there was often a scene where one cowboy turned to another and said, "It's quiet out there. Too quiet," just before the Indians swept over the hill.That is the way the world economy feels to some policy-makers as they prepare for the
5811 start on Tuesday of the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington.Inflation in industrial countries is low. Economic growth seems to picking up throughout much of the world. Currency markets are stable, and speculators have turned more sober.Even if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates
5811 a notch on Tuesday, as some analysts expect, the outlook for the world economy next year still looks good, IMF officials said."This is the point in time that we dig out the old adage -- complacency must be avoided," Stanley Fischer, first deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund,
5811 said.He told reporters that something inevitably would go wrong. The problem is that nobody knows what it will be.Fischer singled out Europe as one potential trouble spot as it struggles to launch European Monetary Union in 1999 against a backdrop of slow growth and sky-high unemployment."If there would be difficulties,
5811 they could be associated with the possibility that the (faster) growth we see for Europe does not happen," the senior IMF official said.Princeton University Professor Peter Kenen said Europe's inability to deal with the unemployment problem raised concern about the continent's long-term political stability."I have been amazed that their political
5811 systems have been thus far reasonably invulnerable to violent political reaction to high unemployment," he said.Another possible trouble spot cited by some analysts is East Asia, where countries such as Thailand and Malaysia are beginning to shown signs of strain from the rapid economic growth they have enjoyed in recent
5811 years.Those strains are mainly showing up in the form of huge and potentially unfinanceable trade deficits -- the same sort of problem that Mexico confronted just before its currency crisis in late 1994."There are reasons to be somewhat concerned about overheating in parts of Asia," said Charles Dallara, managing director
5811 of the Institute of International Finance, which represents about 220 banks and global investors.In many ways Asia's problems pale against those that faced Mexico two years ago before it tumbled into recession. Fischer said growth in East Asian nations was expected to slow in 1997, but to levels -- 7,
5811 8, 9 percent -- that would still be regared as a "gallop" elsewhere in the world.With the world economy seemingly on course for a good year and financial markets looking stable, policy-makers will turn their attention to less earth-shattering but nevertheless important issues relating to the IMF and World Bank.Among
5811 those up for discussion: a multibillion-dollar proposal to provide multilateral debt relief to the world's poorest nations. The IMF pledged last week to find the money to participate, and the World Bank is already on board.If the program is to work, industrial nations will need to expand the debt relief
5811 they already provide to poor nations. Money will also need to be found so that the African Development Bank can take part.Policy-makers are also likely to spend time putting the finishing touches on a series of initiatives taken after Mexico's 1994-95 crisis, including beefing up the IMF's emergency resources for
5811 handling such problems."I don't think it will be a thunder-and-lightning meeting," one international monetary official said. "But when the markets are so stable and the winds are blowing so gently, one really has to wonder what is going to upset it."</
5812 The Federal Reserve is scheduled to hold what analysts expect will be one of its more contentious meetings on Tuesday to consider raising interest rates for the first time in roughly 1-1/2 years.Arrayed on the one side: anti-inflation hawks, principally at the Fed's regional banks, who argue that the central
5812 bank needs to increase rates to keep inflation in check.On the other: the so-called doves, mostly political appointees on the Fed board in Washington, who question whether rates should be raised when the economy is slowing."There is a fundamental point of contention about how the economy's working," said James Annable,
5812 chief economist at First National Bank of Chicago. "It's a debate about how fast the economy is growing and what it means to have an unemployment rate at 5.1 percent."A slim majority of economists polled by Reuters last week -- 17 of 30 -- believes that the central bank will
5812 opt to raise short-term rates on Tuesday, with all but one of those analysts expecting a small increase of one-quarter percentage point.The decision is fraught with political and economic risks for the central bank. A rate rise -- even a small one -- would lead to higher borrowing costs for
5812 consumers and corporations.It would not be welcome on Wall Street or at the White House. Stock prices jumped to record levels on Wall Street last week, and a rate rise could dampen investor enthusiasm.And President Bill Clinton is counting on the maintenance of a trouble-free economy before the Nov. 5
5812 election to help him win another four-year term.Central bank officials admit that Tuesday's decision will not be an easy one. "It's a mixed bag," said one official, who declined to be identified. "It's more difficult than usual to pin down what's happening (in the economy)."The economy, in the words of
5812 Fed Gov. Janet Yellen, is operating in an "inflationary danger zone." But so far there is no sign of higher inflation.At 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at its lowest point in more than seven years and at a level that in the past has usually led to stepped-up wage
5812 demands and higher inflation.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies have been unable to pass through those higher labor costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Firms have enjoyed fat profit margins for 5-1/2 years of economic expansion and thus have some leeway
5812 to absorb the higher labor costs. But it is not clear how long they can go without raising prices.Much will depend of the course of the economy in the coming months, analysts said. On one hand, the economy seems strong. The jobs market is tight, and companies are stepping up
5812 production and rebuilding inventories.But there are also clear signs that growth is slowing. Retail sales have stagnated, and the housing market has weakened, although it remains healthy.Other factors are at play as well, and analysts said it is hard to see how they will pan out.If the Fed tightens credit
5812 because wages are rising, it risks giving ammunition to critics who see it as a pawn of Wall Street. If the Democrats then regain control of Congress, lawmakers may seize on the pre-election rate rise as a reason to rein in the Fed, especially the regional banks.On the other hand,
5812 some of Clinton's appointees to the Fed board may be sensitive to suspicions that they would favor the president and thus be more inclined to raise rates to prove their mettle to the markets and their colleagues."It's a good bet there will be a pretty rigorous discussion around the table,"
5812 said Chris Varvares, an economist for St. Louis-based Macroeconomic Advisers.Eight of the 12 regional Fed banks have called for a rate increase, and consensus-minded central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan may want to avoid a mutiny by them on Tuesday.In the end, the Fed's decision may be more important symbolically than
5812 economically. A small rate rise would have only a minor impact on the economy and could easily be reversed later, analysts said.But it would speak volumes about where the Fed's priorities lie, and that is why Wall Street and in Washington are watching so closely.</

5827 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentIn old Western movies, there was often a scene where one cowboy turned to another and said, "It's quiet out there. Too quiet," just before the Indians swept over the hill.That is the way the world economy feels to some policy-makers as they prepare for
5827 the start of the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington later this week.Inflation in industrial countries is low. Economic growth seems to picking up throughout much of the world. Currency markets are stable, and speculators have turned more sober.Even if the U.S. Federal Reserve
5827 raises interest rates a notch on Tuesday, as some analysts expect, the outlook for the world economy next year still looks good, IMF officials said."This is the point in time that we dig out the old adage -- complacency must be avoided," Stanley Fischer, first deputy managing director of the
5827 International Monetary Fund, said.He told reporters that something inevitably would go wrong. The problem is that nobody knows what it will be.Fischer singled out Europe as one potential trouble spot as it struggles to launch European Monetary Union in 1999 against a backdrop of slow growth and sky-high unemployment."If there
5827 would be difficulties, they could be associated with the possibility that the (faster) growth we see for Europe does not happen," the senior IMF official said.Princeton University Professor Peter Kenen said Europe's inability to deal with the unemployment problem raised concern about the continent's long-term political stability."I have been amazed
5827 that their political systems have been thus far reasonably invulnerable to violent political reaction to high unemployment," he said.Another possible trouble spot cited by some analysts is East Asia, where countries such as Thailand and Malaysia are beginning to shown signs of strain from the rapid economic growth they have
5827 enjoyed in recent years.Those strains are mainly showing up in the form of huge and potentially unfinanceable trade deficits -- the same sort of problem that Mexico confronted just before its currency crisis in late 1994."There are reasons to be somewhat concerned about overheating in parts of Asia," said Charles
5827 Dallara, managing director of the Institute of International Finance, which represents about 220 banks and global investors.But in many ways Asia's problems pale against those that faced Mexico two years ago before it tumbled into recession. Fischer said growth in East Asian nations was expected to slow in 1997, but
5827 to levels -- 7, 8, 9 percent -- that would still be regared as a "gallop" elsewhere in the world.With the world economy seemingly on course for a good year and financial markets looking stable, policy-makers will turn their attention to less earth-shattering but nevertheless important issues relating to the
5827 IMF and World Bank.Among those up for discussion: a multibillion-dollar proposal to provide multilateral debt relief to the world's poorest nations. The IMF pledged last week to find the money to participate, and the World Bank is already on board.But if the programme is to work, industrial nations will need

5831 Spurred into action by public debate about media fairness and objectivity, the biggest U.S. journalism organisation Saturday approved a new, revised code of ethics committed to "public enlightenment."The Society of Professional Journalists, wrapping up its four-day annual conference, voted to approve the new code of ethics, developed over the past

5848 EU finance ministers agreed on Saturday that a new Exchange Rate Mechanism to be set up after the launch of the single European currency in 1999 will keep the wide fluctuation bands of the current system, officials said.The new mechanism, the ERM II, will limit fluctuations between the euro and
5848 currencies whose countries are waiting to join European monetary union when their economies are ready."There is a consensus to maintain the relatively wide bands of today," French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters.The European Union was forced to widen the fluctuation bands of the existing exchange rate mechanism to plus
5848 or minus 15 percent of a central rate from 2.25 percent after a currency crisis in the summer of 1993.One delegation source said ministers had been asked whether they had any objection to maintaining the current system after the launch of the euro, and none had objected."My reading of that
5848 is that it will be plus or minus 15 percent," the source said.A European Commission spokesman said no-one had asked for bands less than 15 percent, though narrower bands were possible for countries with economies which were closely aligned to those of the euro zone.One source said details still had
5848 to be ironed out on how to set up these narrower bands, and ministers declined to confirm the new system would retain the precise limit of 15 percent."We have not finalised the bands for ERM II. We have asked for additional work to be done. We want some more clarity
5848 on how it is going to function and ensure that the new ERM will work efficiently," Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said.Commission officials also hinted countries still outside European monetary union which failed to follow sensible monetary and fiscal policies could lose the support of the future European Central Bank
5848 (ECB) if their currencies came under pressure on exchange markets.That would mean the ECB might either stop intervening to support those currencies or it would suggest a devaluation."There may be an implicit deal between respect of economic programmes in the (convergence) plan and membership of the ERM II," a Commission
5848 spokesman said.The new exchange rate mechanism will be based on the euro, with the exchange rates of countries waiting to join monetary union, the "pre-ins", fixed against it."The new system will be a system of hubs and spokes, with the euro in the centre and fairly wide bands around," the
5848 spokesman said.The ECB would intervene to defend these currencies if necessary, but would be able to stop intervention in certain circumstances."The European Central Bank and the central banks of the pre-ins can stop intervention if it would endanger the central goal which is the stability of prices," the spokesman said.European
5848 Monetary Institute head Alexandre Lamfalussy, in a confidential letter written earlier this month, a copy of which was circulating at the talks, recommended that the ECB would have the right to initiate procedures aimed at realigning currencies in ERM II if necessary.-- Dublin Newsroom 353 475 9256 211548 GMT sep

5875 Europe's top financial officials this weekend cleared key hurdles in their quest for a stability pact to control public spending once countries enter monetary union, but failed to agree exactly how the deal will work.European Union finance ministers and central bank governors said at the end of informal one-day talks
5875 in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday the broad outline of plans to punish governments that exceeded certain budget deficit limits were now in place.But specifics of the plan -- including the size of fines to be levied on offenders -- were referred to committees in the hope a consensus could be
5875 thrashed out by the end of the year.German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the architect of the plans to ensure fiscal discipline within Europe's monetary union -- set to start on January 1, 1999 -- said he was satisfied with progress although issues remained unresolved.After the meeting Waigel said, "I am
5875 satisfied. We are following exactly on the road we started on one year ago."The German minister initially proposed the concept of a stability pact as a means of ensuring that countries which pass the economic test set for entry to the single currency do not later become lax in their
5875 fiscal policies.The entry criteria for EMU laid down in the Maastricht Treaty require countries which want to meld their currencies into the Euro to meet targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budget deficits and public borrowing.The budgetary goals -- which call for annual deficits to total no more than
5875 three percent of gross domestic product and total debt of no more than 60 percent of GDP -- have proved by far the hardest for most countries to meet.This, combined with the fact that their fate on all the other criteria will be inextricably intertwined once the Euro has been
5875 established, meant there was a particular need for wideranging agreement on fiscal issues.European Union commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy echoed the views of many officials by saying this weekend that the planned stability pact was essential for the credibility of the new Euro in financial markets and with the general
5875 public.Without such a pact, overspending by one Euro member state could undermine the stability of the currency by driving up interest rates and damaging market trust in the Euro.Under the terms of the pact agreed in Dublin, countries will face sanctions if they notch up a deficit exceeding three percent
5875 of Gross Domestic Product unless they take immediate corrective action or face exceptional circumstances.French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet told reporters EU financial officials had agreed four key elements which would smooth the decision-making process and lay down clear rules on what delinquent countries could expect.Trichet said it had been
5875 agreed that the "exceptional and temporary circumstances" under which a country could exceed the three percent level without sanctions must be predefined.If these did not apply sanctions would always be levied and this would take the form of an interest-free deposit. Finally, if no action was taken, this deposit would
5875 be converted into a non-refundable fine.Ministers also said there was consensus, but not unanimous approval, on the idea that sanctions should be imposed within a calendar year of an excessive deficit being recorded.Countries would be expected to draw up their accounts for a year by the following March, and implement
5875 corrective action before the year-end, to avoid sanctions kicking in.But there was no consensus on the detail needed to flesh out the skeleton framework, leaving working parties with a large area of ground to cover by December, when ministers hope a complete pact will be ratified by a summit meeting.Officials
5875 said a German proposal calling for a deposit of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point of excessive deficit was still on the table alongside a European Commission proposal for a smaller deposit per percentage point, capped at a maximum of 0.5 percent."The type and size of (the deposits)
5875 has yet to be agreed," Waigel said.There was also no agreement on the precise definitions of exceptional circumstances -- an issue Germany sees as essential if the pact is to be applied swiftly and at least semi-automatically once a budget is exceeded.221200 GMT sep 96</

5883 European Union finance ministers have built their first bridge designed to link those in monetary union and those waiting to join by agreeing the structure of a new currency grid after the launch of the euro.Officials said the new exchange rate mechanism, the ERM II, whose broad outlines were agreed
5883 by finance ministers on Saturday, would help prevent non-members from drifting away from the euro zone when the single currency is launched in 1999."The final aim is to have all countries join the euro," French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters after an informal meeting here of finance ministers and
5883 central bankers."It is in the interests of all for as many as possible to participate," Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said.Ministers agreed the new ERM II will be based on the current system where currencies are allowed to fluctuate a wide 15 percent either side of a central rate rather than
5883 a tight grid abandoned after a currency crisis in 1993.In the new system, for which final details are meant to be ironed out for approval by EU leaders at a summit in Dublin in December, currencies will be fixed against the euro.The new currency grid is considered essential to maintain
5883 some kind of cohesion in the EU after the single currency is launched, amid worries of a divide between rich northern European countries likely to join first and any countries with weaker economies on the periphery waiting to join.Officials stressed that though the bands in the new mechanism would be
5883 wide enough to give a lot of leeway, ministers were looking at ways of giving it some bite by linking membership to respect for sound monetary and fiscal policies."There may be an implicit deal between respect of economic programmes in the (convergence) plan and membership of the ERM II," a
5883 Commission spokesman said.That could mean that the future European Central Bank (ECB) might either stop intervening to support a currency on foreign exchange markets or suggest a devaluation."The ECB should have at its discretion the right to suspend intervention if it appers that the amount of intervention would put at
5883 risk price stability in the euro area," European Monetary Institute head Alexandre Lamfalussy told reporters.Procedures are to be improved and speeded up for tracking how well countries waiting to join monetary union are bringing their economies into line with those in the euro zone."We emphasised the extent to which multilateral
5883 surveillance must be reinforced," Arthuis said.These plans, if successful, would give non-members which missed the Maastricht treaty standards in 1997 a clear goal to aim for and allow them to sell to their national parliaments the need to keep cutting public spending to reduce budget deficits.Some key questions on exactly
5883 how the ERM II will function will now have to be worked out by EU monetary officials.Ministers declined to specify a precise figure for the fluctuation bands in the ERM II.One delegation source said ministers had been asked whether they had any objection to maintaining the current system after the
5883 launch of the euro, and none had objected. "My reading of that is that it will be plus or minus 15 percent," he said.But officials will have to look at how to deal with the unlikely possibility that currencies swing 60 percent against each other -- which could only happen
5883 if one started at the maximum 15 percent above the euro and the other 15 percent below, and then reversed positions.A European Commission spokesman also said that narrower bands were possible for countries with stronger economies, though details on this too have yet to be worked out.Another key question is
5883 over the exact role of the ECB in initiating currency realignments and over how much it will have to take account of the views of the country concerned.</

5890 More than 1,000 multinational firms in the European Union will have to take concrete steps from Sunday to keep workers informed about management plans for their companies.Under a new law, commonly known as the works council directive which comes into force on Sunday, these firms will have to set up
5890 information and consultation bodies at their workers request.The European Commission said last week that about 200 companies had signed voluntary agreements with employees for setting up such bodies in a two-year grace period which lapses on Sunday.But the European Trade Union Confederation says 1,200 companies in all come under the
5890 1994 law. The directive applies to companies with more than 1,000 workers in Europe, with 150 in each of at least two countries.While companies such as Britain's Hansen and Belgium's Union Miniere signed voluntary accords at the last moment, those who did not make use of the opportunity will now
5890 feel the full requirement of the EU law."Now what's going to happen is that from the 22nd (of September) onwards all the agreements will have to be made in accordance with the directive," said Zygmunt Tyszkiewicz, the secretary general of the employers federation UNICE, which campaigned against the law.UNICE says
5890 minimum requirements under the law give workers an advantage over employers, as they know that even if negotiations on setting up a consultation body fail, they will get something thanks to the EU law."It will take that bit of balance out the agreement," said Tyszkiewicz.Under the directive an employer must
5890 launch negotiations on setting up an information body at the written request of at least 100 employees or their representatives in at least two EU countries.If the two sides cannot reach agreement within three years the EU's minimum system will apply. The minimum system will apply after six months if
5890 management refuses to negotiate.While the the union confederation ETUC has welcomed the growing number of works councils negotiated voluntarily, a spokesman said that if workers do not like the voluntary agreements -- which give companies more flexibility -- they can always abandon them.In that case employers and unions will have
5890 to come back to the negotiating table playing by the EU's rules.Under the EU minimum system the company will be obliged to inform employee representatives of all measures deemed to have a "considerable" effect on employees' interests, especially in the case of relocation, closures and collective redundancies.Britain was excluded for
5890 the law because its government negotiated an opt-out from such employment directives in the Maastricht Treaty.But union officials say at least 35 British companies set up voluntary agreements anyway.They include Barclays Plc which the banking union Unifi said on Friday would set up a works council covering its 80,000 employees
5890 across the European Union, including Britain.A Commission spokewoman said that Britain was covered "de facto" by the directive because many British workers were also included in voluntary accords signed in other EU countries.</

5894 "Quota hoppers," foreign fishing vessels which register in another country to grab part of the national quota, can be stopped within existing rules, according to European Union Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino.The problem is most acute in Britain, where around 150 foreign, mainly Spanish, vessels are registered and take 20 percent
5894 of the national fish quota.Britain has warned that the situation must be ended before agreement can be reached on proposed sharp cuts in the EU fleet aimed at saving endangered fish stocks."I think this problem is not increasing but they (the British) have to live with what they have," Bonino
5894 told Reuters in a recent interview.The combative Italian commissioner said Britain's belated start-up last year of an EU scheme to compensate fishermen for laying up vessels should help stop further quota hoppers.The scheme had been delayed by the British government's reluctance to provide funds to match EU aid."If European fishermen
5894 have bought U.K. licences or boats it's because U.K. fishermen have sold," Bonino said in her characteristically blunt style. "They sold because the decommissioning scheme was not available."Britain wanted a common market but not common rules, she said, adding that Britain did not want fish catches by quota hoppers to
5894 be counted against the national quota.Bonino pointed out that national quotas existed for milk, olive oil and other agricultural products and that fish could not be made an exception."If you want to go and buy a piece of land in Tuscany and produce olive oil it will be counted in
5894 the Italian quota," she said.Britain has said that it will demand changes to the EU treaty on fisheries quotas at an ongoing inter-governmental conference.But Bonino said this would take a long time and would be very difficult as any changes would have to be agreed unanimously.It would be quicker and
5894 easier for the British government to introduce non-discriminatory regulations on fish catch landings and social security to discourage "quota hoppers," she added.Although British-registered vessels have to visit British ports twice a year, the government has not been prepared to impose fish catch landing measures because this would create problems for
5894 Scottish boats fishing in French waters, Bonino said.Looking ahead to the next EU fisheries ministers meeting on October 14, Bonino said she was optimistic that a framework agreement could be reached on controversial proposals to reduce EU fishing capacity by up to 40 percent over six years."I'm confident that we
5894 can reach a general conclusion at the council," she said. "No member state contests that there is overcapacity...but each says its up to the neighbour to reduce."The collapse of North Sea herring fishing this summer showed the cost of mismanagement, she said, adding that member states had watered down proposals

5906 Supporters of Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza, who was killed in a shootout with police, want his Arab-born widow to lead their movement to challenge the government.They said they would offer the leadership of Murtaza's breakaway Shaheed Bhutto faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP) to
5906 his Lebanese wife Ghinwa.The decision was taken by a Central Coordination Committee meeting of the faction on Sunday in town of Larkana, two days after Murtaza and domr of his followers were killed in a gunfight with police in Karachi, capital of Sindh province.It was not immediately known whether the
5906 committee had consulted Ghinwa beforehand or whether she would be ready to accept the offer.She told reporters earlier that she would stay in Pakistan despite her husband's death but had not decided yet whether to enter politics, which has been full of controversy and tragedy for the Bhutto family.Benazir Bhutto
5906 took over the PPP leadership mantle from her father, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who was ousted as prime minister in an army coup in 1977 and executed in 1979 after a controversial conviction for conspiring the murder of a political opponent.Murtaza challenged her leadership when he returned in 1993 after 16
5906 years in self-imposed exile, mainly in Syria. He set up his rival group in March last year, but attracted no political heavyweights from his sister's mainstream party.But political sources said protest demonstrations in his home province of Sindh and some other parts of Pakistan after his death showed that Murtaza
5906 had built up a dedicated hard core of followers with considerable support.If she accepts their offer, Ghinwa, a former teacher who speaks English and French as well as her native Arabic, will become the first Arab woman to lead a Pakistani political group, although not the first foreign-born.Her Iranian-born mother-in-law
5906 Nusrat remained figurhead PPP chief after Zulfikar Bhutto's execution before she was ousted by Benazir in 1993 and her Iranian origin was never questioned.Islam's Arab heroes and heroines are revered in Islamic Pakistan as much as in their native lands.The Larkana meeting of Murtaza's faction also decided to demand the
5906 appointment of a Supreme Court judge to investigate his death rather than the provincial high court judge already named by the Sindh province government.Murtaza's supporters, accusing Benazir's husband of conspiring in the killing of their leader, clashed with police in Larkana on Sunday and prevented President Farooq Leghari from paying
5906 a condolence call on the family.They also set fire to a police van and motorcyle and stoned private vehicles in Lahore, capital of the province of Punjab, witnesses there said.Murtaza, 42, was shot and killed with six of his followers in a clash with police in Karachi on Friday night.
5906 Another of his supporters died of his wounds on Saturday.Surviving members of the powerful but divided Bhutto political dynasty came together at the family's ancestral home in Larkana to pay their last respects to Murtaza, who was estranged from his older sister for much of his turbulent life.Nusrat issued a
5906 statement, carried by the official news agency APP, saying that Murtaza's death was part of a conspiracy against the Bhutto family and denying reports that she had implicated Benazir and her husband."The vicious, malicious and the unkindest remarks attributed to me are only designed to create confusion in peoples' minds
5906 with a view to diverting attention from the real culprits whom the independent commission will identify," she said.</

5921 Pakistani stocks, already depressed by a gloomy economic outlook, plunged on Sunday in reaction to the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto, dealers said.They said Murtaza's death had fuelled political uncertainty and the market would suffer as long as doubts over the future of Bhutto's nearly
5921 three-year-old government persist.Murtaza, 42, leader of a breakaway faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party, and seven of his supporters died after a clash with police outside his Karachi home on Friday night."The situation was bad and it is getting worse," dealer Zaina Nosherwan of Taurus Securities said after the
5921 Karachi 100-share index dipped 23.29 points to close at 1,415.52.She said Murtaza's shooting indicated that the police, themselves accused of using excessive force and killing people in fabricated clashes, were unlikely to be able to control the political unrest that has tormented Karachi.Many dealers linked the killing to the government's
5921 policy of giving the police a free hand to quell militants of the Karachi-based ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).Some also expressed fear that the shooting might have been deliberately planned to destabilise the Bhutto government.Murtaza's supporters and opposition politicians have said Benazir and her husband, Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari,
5921 are directly or indirectly responsible for his death."The market will get really weak as the country seems to be heading for new heights of political uncertainty," analyst Nauman Sheikh of KASB &amp; Co said.He said most market players would adopt a wait-and-see approach while foreign investors would certainly become more
5921 cautious about buying Pakistani stocks."Things will remain murky till we can make some sense out of the worsening political scenario," Sheikh said.He said the market could shake off its blues only if the political scene stabilised and talks with the International Monetary Fund in Washington proved positive.A delegation led by
5921 V.A. Jafarey, Bhutto's adviser on finance, is due to meet IMF officials in the next few days to try to persuade them to release delayed tranches of a $600 million standby loan due in June and September.The IMF has held up disbursements because of doubts about Pakistan's implementation of agreed
5921 policies and confusion surrounding the budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).It can only resume payments once an IMF mission completes a review of Pakistan's economic performance to the satisfaction of the IMF board. No date has been set for such a mission."We don't expect positive political news, but something good from
5921 the economic front could stabilise the market," said dealer Khalid Hussain of National Investment and Finance Services.</

5924 mountain on Saturday. 5924 different expeditions attempting to conquer the 8,848-metre high (29,028 ft) mountain from the Nepali side in the autumn season, which began early in September.Bouchon, part of a French expedition to Everest, is the third Frenchman to die on the mountain's slopes since the first successful ascent in 1953. 5925 Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto faces intense pressure after her brother's death robbed Pakistan's charismatic but ill-fated political dynasty of its last adult male, analysts and newspapers said on Sunday.Murtaza Bhutto, 42, who had flirted with violence for much of his life, died in a hail of police bullets outside his
5925 Karachi home on Friday night. Police say his guards fired first.The slaying was the latest eruption of violence in Pakistan, whose support role for Western-backed Afghan guerrillas against Soviet occupation in the 1980s placed deadly weapons in the hands of rival ethnic, political and religious groups at home.Murtaza's supporters and
5925 opposition politicians have accused Benazir and her husband, Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari, of being directly or indirectly responsible for his death.Benazir, whose government was already under opposition fire for alleged corruption, misrule and economic blunders, must now cope with the political repercussions of a personal tragedy.Her government had taken
5925 pride in what it saw as its success in restoring a semblance of peace to Karachi, Pakistan's biggest city, where a struggle with ethnic militants of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) cost more than 2,000 lives in 1995.Now the leeway Benazir gave the security forces against the MQM appears to
5925 have rebounded cruelly against her."The Karachi police, a creation of the present government, has become a Frankenstein," said The Nation newspaper on Sunday.It said it would be irresponsible to blame a grieving Benazir for the death of her only surviving brother, but added: "It is inevitable that some of the
5925 responsibility for this tragic outcome of the police action would devolve on her."Dawn newspaper said there was a new priority in Karachi. "It is to check the brutality and trigger-happiness of a police force which has imbibed one overriding lesson from its drive against the MQM: to shoot first and
5925 ask questions later."Last year Murtaza formed a splinter faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP) founded by his father, former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. He was hanged in 1979 by General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq, who had toppled him in 1977.Murtaza spent 16 years in exile, mainly in Syria, at
5925 the head of Al-Zulfikar, a clandestine anti-Zia group that was accused of hijacking a Pakistani airliner in 1981.He returned to Pakistan in late 1993, soon after Benazir regained power, to face charges arising from his underground struggle against Zia. He was freed on bail after seven months. Murtaza's PPP-Shaheed (martyr)
5925 Bhutto group posed no threat to his sister's mainstream party, but security officials have said it was suspected of being behind bomb attacks that killed one person and wounded three in Karachi last week. They said his group had backing from Pakistan's arch-rival India.Murtaza denied the charge just before his
5925 death and accused security forces of planting the bombs to discredit him.Analysts say Benazir will be anxious to prevent his demise from reigniting a damaging family feud that has in the past put her at odds with her thrice-bereaved mother Nusrat.Nusrat, who has lost her husband and two sons --
5925 her youngest, Shahnawaz, died, apparently of poisoning, in France in 1985 -- has made no public comment on Murtaza's death.Pakistani commentators say that if she attacks Benazir it could spell trouble for the PPP and its grip on power.The prime minister, 44, has vowed to complete her five-year term, which
5925 expires in October 1998, saying she has no fear of unpopularity arising from harsh but necessary economic measures.So far Pakistan's powerful military has given no hint that it wants her removed, but her alliance with President Farooq Leghari, an old political supporter, has shown signs of strain.Leghari chose to air
5925 his differences with Bhutto over judicial appointments for the first time on Saturday -- just hours before Murtaza's emotional funeral in the ancestral Bhutto homeland of Larkana, in the southern province of Sindh.</

5926 pro-government fighters to defect to its side and promised them amnesty.Mullah Amir Khan Mutaqi, a Taleban spokesman at the southern Afghan town of Kandahar, told Reuters by telephone that movement leader Mullah Mohammad Omar had announced amnesty for commanders and fighters of various factions, civil servants and citizens."Those who join

5926 it helped during their guerrilla war against Soviet occupation in the 1980s.Taleban has also besieged Kabul since last October to force Rabbani's government to step down.</
5927 Tens of thousands of south Asians this week are burying hopes of a future working in the United Arab Emirates and seeking a one way ticket home before the Gulf state's immigration authorities catch up with them.Scores of Indians filed off a jetliner at Bombay airport on Saturday, one of
5927 the many planes shuttling unwanted workers out of the Emirates.Gamba Ram, an unskilled labourer, gave this phlegmatic account of their plight."Everybody had to come out because staying in the country would have caused more problems. Even though we didn't have any money we came somehow. Some of us even borrowed
5927 money to buy our tickets. We faced some difficulties but we had to abide by the rules of that country."Similar stories will be heard in other destinations round the region -- in Dhaka, Karachi, Colombo and Manila.The UAE two months ago gave foreign workers without legal documents a September 30
5927 deadline to get their papers in order or leave the country. Otherwise, they and their employers would face hefty fines and possibly jail.But many have delayed leaving until the last days of the amnesty, desperately trying to get the proper documents or waiting in the forlorn hope that the UAE
5927 would have a change of heart.Diplomats reckon that 200,000 of the 1.8 million foreigners living in the UAE will have to leave or be booted out.The jobs they held in the Emirates were low paying but provided them with a meal ticket and the chance to send some money back
5927 to the families they left behind.Often they paid huge sums of money to sometimes crooked agents to fix flights, jobs and work permits in the Gulf.A typical cross-section of people making the trek back home would probably be a Filipino or Sri Lankan housemaid, a Pakistani oilfield worker, an Indian
5927 shop assistant, and a Bangladeshi building labourer.People from the region flocked to the Gulf in the early 1970s when the Arab states began mopping up mega-bucks by exporting oil to the world.They went to build the highways and construct the modern sparkling white cites that now fringe the western Gulf
5927 -- all paid for with oil money.And for the oil industry itself they laid pipelines across the desert, and built refineries and ports.They filled jobs from the most menial to the very highly qualified. Most came from the Indian sub-continent.There are no complaints from the governments of countries affected by
5927 the UAE's clampdown. But as the Gulf economies adjust to the idea that oil money no longer buys as much, foreign workers will be increasingly nervous about their status.Indian government officials say the UAE authorities have shown some sympathy over the logistical headache of getting so many people out at
5927 once.They said there are up to 60,000 Indians working illegally in the UAE. The Indian embassy has already arranged exit visas for 40,000 of them and is fixing extra air and sea transport to fetch other stranded nationals.Half of India's migrant workers come from the southwest state of Kerala, where
5927 there are plans to establish a $196 million rehabilitation programme.Bangladesh's government says the 30,000 people it expects to be returning will have to fend for themselves, but it has asked the national airline to put on extra flights."The government has no plan as such to help or compensate the returnees,"
5927 said Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad on Saturday.The Philippines and Sri Lanka both foresee about 10,000 of their citizens, mostly maids, being ruled illegal in the UAE. But both government and employment agencies expected many will fix their documentation or make arrangements to return legally.</

5946 strongly pro-European British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.While risks still remain, particularly on the economic front and in the period between when EMU participants are chosen -- early 1998 -- and the start date on Jan. 1, 1999, there is a growing sense that the political determination of Germany
5946 and France will see the thing through.Work on technical aspects of EMU is expected to accelerate between now and December, with the European Commission and the EU's monetary committee, a group of national treasury and central bank officials, taking the lead role.On the Stability Pact, the committee was asked to

5952 Greece's ruling socialists romped home to an unexpectedly easy win over the opposition conservatives in national elections on Sunday.It was a personal triumph for Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who confidently called the vote only to see his once-strong lead shrink and opinion polls predict a neck-and-neck finish.But returns showed the
5952 socialists with a solid three-point lead in their first election without legendary party founder and three-time prime minister Andreas Papandreou at the helm.With interior ministry figures showing an irreversible lead, opposition leader Miltiades Evert conceded defeat and Simitis quickly claimed a "great victory"."The people showed they want a new course
5952 for Greece and society. This great victory belongs to all citizens who envision a better future," he said. "This victory belongs to all who believe in development coupled with social justice."Many Greeks, who had suffered a long and dull campaign, went wild on the socialist win. Cars raced through Athens
5952 with horns blarring, and white and greek PASOK banners flying. Fireworks boomed throughout the capital and people danced in the streets.With 33.5 percent of the vote counted, the socialists had 41.8 percent and the conservatives 38.7 percent. Legal experts said that would give Simitis around 162 deputies in the 300-seat
5952 parliament, a solid absolute majority.Simitis, 60, took over as premier from the ailing Papandreou in January and consolidated his power with his rise to socialist party president in June after Papandreou died.His election win cements his control over the Panhellenic Socialist Movement (PASOK), where he plans major changes, and gives
5952 him the mandate in parliament to carry out his promised reforms.A German and British-trained economist and lawyer, Simitis called repeatedly for a more democratic PASOK party. He clashed occasionally with Papandreou publicly, and in so doing created an image of being his own man.Simitis turned his back on Papandreou's passionate
5952 populism and generous campaign promises and told Greeks bluntly they could expect no more handouts from the European Union.That no-nonsense talk sent him plummeting in opinion polls and had a welter of smaller left-wing parties denouncing him as a neo-conservative.He eventually switched tactics and began recalling the glory of the
5952 Papandreou days, when Greece's vast welfare state was set up, and promising to take care of the less well-off.But Simitis is staunchly pro-European and is determined to make whatever sacrifices necessary to meet the economic targets set out by the European Union.He has also said Greece will eschew maverick stands
5952 and the unpredictable policy swings that Papandreou relished. Instead he said he would work hard and quietly with the EU and Washington to convince them of Greece's positions, especially with Turkey.Socialist officials expected Simitis to name his new cabinet on Tuesday. Rumours have already begun that he will move Defence
5952 Minister Gerassimos Arsenis and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.Arsenis has pushed for a $10 billion arms package to face off against neighbouring Turkey and Simitis is clearly unhappy with the effect this would have on EU economic targets.He may also appoint George Papandreou, son of the late premier, foreign minister. Papandreou
5952 has little experience in foreign affairs but was a key backer in Simitis's rise to power.The defeat spelled the end for Evert, who resigned as leader of the New Democracy party."I take personal responsibility for the election result. I resign as president of the party," he said in a brief
5952 televised statement.Evert, a hard-nosed former Athens mayor, took over as party leader after the conservatives were thrashed in a 1993 election but he presided from the start over a deeply-divided and unhappy group.Results showed three smaller leftist parties in parliament. The Communist Party had 5.2 percent, the Coalition of the
5952 Left had 4.9 percent and the Democratic Social Movement had 4.2.The Political Spring party of former conservative foreign minister Antonis Samaras had 2.8 percent, leaving his party out of parliament. A party needs three percent to win a seat.</

5956 The Federal Reserve is scheduled to hold what analysts expect will be one of its more contentious meetings on Tuesday to consider raising interest rates for the first time in roughly 1-1/2 years.Arrayed on the one side: anti-inflation hawks, principally at the Fed's regional banks, who argue that the central
5956 bank needs to increase rates to keep inflation in check.On the other: the so-called doves, mostly political appointees on the Fed board in Washington, who question whether rates should be raised when the economy is slowing."There is a fundamental point of contention about how the economy's working," said James Annable,
5956 chief economist at First National Bank of Chicago. "It's a debate about how fast the economy is growing and what it means to have an unemployment rate at 5.1 percent."A slim majority of economists polled by Reuters last week -- 17 of 30 -- believes that the central bank will
5956 opt to raise short-term rates on Tuesday, with all but one of those analysts expecting a small increase of one-quarter percentage point.The decision is fraught with political and economic risks for the central bank. A rate rise -- even a small one -- would lead to higher borrowing costs for
5956 consumers and corporations.It would not be welcome on Wall Street or at the White House. Stock prices jumped to record levels on Wall Street last week, and a rate rise could dampen investor enthusiasm.And President Bill Clinton is counting on the maintenance of a trouble-free economy before the Nov. 5
5956 election to help him win another four-year term.Central bank officials admit that Tuesday's decision will not be an easy one. "It's a mixed bag," said one official, who declined to be identified. "It's more difficult than usual to pin down what's happening (in the economy)."The economy, in the words of
5956 Fed Gov. Janet Yellen, is operating in an "inflationary danger zone." But so far there is no sign of higher inflation.At 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at its lowest point in more than seven years and at a level that in the past has usually led to stepped-up wage
5956 demands and higher inflation.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Firms have enjoyed fat profit margins for 5-1/2 years of economic expansion and thus have some leeway
5956 to absorb the higher labour costs. But it is not clear how long they can go without raising prices.Much will depend of the course of the economy in the coming months, analysts said. On one hand, the economy seems strong. The jobs market is tight, and companies are stepping up
5956 production and rebuilding inventories.But there are also clear signs that growth is slowing. Retail sales have stagnated, and the housing market has weakened, although it remains healthy.Other factors are at play as well, and analysts said it is hard to see how they will pan out.If the Fed tightens credit
5956 because wages are rising, it risks giving ammunition to critics who see it as a pawn of Wall Street. If the Democrats then regain control of Congress, lawmakers may seize on the pre-election rate rise as a reason to rein in the Fed, especially the regional banks.On the other hand,
5956 some of Clinton's appointees to the Fed board may be sensitive to suspicions that they would favour the president and thus be more inclined to raise rates to prove their mettle to the markets and their colleagues."It's a good bet there will be a pretty rigorous discussion around the table,"
5956 said Chris Varvares, an economist for St. Louis-based Macroeconomic Advisers.Eight of the 12 regional Fed banks have called for a rate increase, and consensus-minded central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan may want to avoid a mutiny by them on Tuesday.In the end, the Fed's decision may be more important symbolically than
5956 economically. A small rate rise would have only a minor impact on the economy and could easily be reversed later, analysts said.But it would speak volumes about where the Fed's priorities lie, and that is why Wall Street and in Washington are watching so closely.</

5957 an increase in Turkish grain output this year."We have to protect our farmers and our grain industry," Mahmut Arslan, president of the Arbel trading company, said on the eve of a second annual conference at the Mediterranean resort of Antalya.Others, however, said the decision would hit local users of corn

5957 importing foreign durum wheat, despite the higher duties which are likely to cost them some $30 per tonne."We have to import because local wheat is not satisfactory," a senior pasta industry official said as word of the imminent import tax decision spread last week.Supplies could come from Mexico, the United
5957 States, Spain, Canada or France, he said.Turkey has said it expects a bumper harvest for all kinds of wheat, including durum, of some 18 million tonnes this year, up from 15.5 million in 1995.Grain import levies were slashed two years ago to encourage imports in the wake of what were

5960 More than 1,000 multinational firms in the European Union will have to take concrete steps from Sunday to keep workers informed about management plans for their companies.Under a new law, commonly known as the works council directive which comes into force on Sunday, these firms will have to set up
5960 information and consultation bodies at their workers request.The European Commission said last week that about 200 companies had signed voluntary agreements with employees for setting up such bodies in a two-year grace period which lapses on Sunday.But the European Trade Union Confederation says 1,200 companies in all come under the
5960 1994 law. The directive applies to companies with more than 1,000 workers in Europe, with 150 in each of at least two countries.While companies such as Britain's Hansen and Belgium's Union Miniere signed voluntary accords at the last moment, those who did not make use of the opportunity will now
5960 feel the full requirement of the EU law."Now what's going to happen is that from the 22nd (of September) onwards all the agreements will have to be made in accordance with the directive," said Zygmunt Tyszkiewicz, the secretary general of the employers federation UNICE, which campaigned against the law.UNICE says
5960 minimum requirements under the law give workers an advantage over employers, as they know that even if negotiations on setting up a consultation body fail, they will get something thanks to the EU law."It will take that bit of balance out the agreement," said Tyszkiewicz.Under the directive an employer must
5960 launch negotiations on setting up an information body at the written request of at least 100 employees or their representatives in at least two EU countries.If the two sides cannot reach agreement within three years the EU's minimum system will apply. The minimum system will apply after six months if
5960 management refuses to negotiate.While the the union confederation ETUC has welcomed the growing number of works councils negotiated voluntarily, a spokesman said that if workers do not like the voluntary agreements -- which give companies more flexibility -- they can always abandon them.In that case employers and unions will have
5960 to come back to the negotiating table playing by the EU's rules.Under the EU minimum system the company will be obliged to inform employee representatives of all measures deemed to have a "considerable" effect on employees' interests, especially in the case of relocation, closures and collective redundancies.Britain was excluded for
5960 the law because its government negotiated an opt-out from such employment directives in the Maastricht Treaty.But union officials say at least 35 British companies set up voluntary agreements anyway.They include Barclays Plc which the banking union Unifi said on Friday would set up a works council covering its 80,000 employees
5960 across the European Union, including Britain.A Commission spokewoman said that Britain was covered "de facto" by the directive because many British workers were also included in voluntary accords signed in other EU countries.</

5963 in the region, Singapore will increasingly become a centre of excellence, sharing our expertise in these markets, training people and setting up sites," Jurgens said."That will be more and more our role into the future. But to be able to do that, we need a manufacturing site of a critical

5963 manufacturers will come from these state monopolies as they privatise. 5963 and Indonesia, more smokers of clove cigarettes would turn to white cigarettes or buy international brands.Jurgens said Singapore remained competitive despite its high wage and land costs due to its ability to respond quickly."Its location allows BAT to supply fast to other parts of Asia relatively cheaper than from the
5963 U.S. or Europe due to efficent harbour facilities and more regular shipping lines," Jurgens said.BAT has a stable market share of about 17 percent in Singapore.Jurgens said the company has no plans to diversify away from tobacco business. 5970 also says he had been verbally promised a lifetime contract to train the boxer by Tyson's former manager and mentor Cus D'Amato."I considered bringing him back until he sued me," Tyson said during three hours of testimony before a federal jury in Albany, New York. 5970 Rooney in 1988 after Rooney publicly commented about the boxer's failed marriage to Robin Givens. Rooney had worked with Tyson since the athlete's amateur days in 1982 until Tyson became world champion in 1988."Even right now I am not mad at him," said Tyson, looking straight at Rooney in a
5970 courtroom crowded with spectators. 5970 Monday, his lawyers filed a motion to have the case dismissed, but Chief Judge Thomas McAvoy reserved judgment, and the jurors were expected to hear more witnesses Tuesday.On the stand last week, Rooney said D'amato, Tyson's guardian, had promised him a lifetime job with a guaranteed 10 percent cut of
5970 the boxer's winnings. He said there was a tradition in the boxing industry of honouring verbal contracts and he felt betrayed.The boxer has said there was no such deal or at least none he knew about.Rooney said in his lawsuit that he was entitled to 10 percent of Tyson's net
5970 worth, which Rooney calculated at $490 million.Tyson, who apparently had written contracts with other trainers, told the court he never used "paper contracts" with Rooney.The trial of Rooney's lawsuit was postponed by Tyson's conviction in 1992 and prison sentence for the rape of a 19-year-old black beauty contestant from Rhode
5970 Island. Tyson was paroled in March 1995.Two weeks ago, Tyson stopped Bruce Seldon in one minute and 49 seconds of the first round to win the World Boxing Association (WBA) heavyweight title, his fourth victory since his parole.His next opponent is scheduled to be former champion Evander Holyfield in November.

5978 at Estoril."I was very surprised," he said. "I did not know where he was. Then suddenly he was alongside me and I could not do much to stop him getting by. It was a very brave move."Villeneuve said he had talked to his team's engineers about attempting to pass on
5978 the outside of that corner and had been warned that it was too risky."I was sure we could do it," he said. "They said they would come and pick me out of the guard rail if I tried it."Actually, if we hadn't hit any traffic I don't think it would
5978 have been possible. But I had nothing to lose. Either I beat Damon or I lost the championship right there anyway. So, it was worth it to take a big risk."Villeneuve's startling passing move on Schumacher was the highlight of his excellent drive and will give him a psychological boost

5994 Nigeria have had their ban on competing in the African Nations' Cup cut in half, effectively allowing them back into the qualifying competition for the finals in the year 2000.The Confederation of African Football (CAF) said Nigeria's original four-year suspension, imposed in February after their failure to turn up for
5994 the finals in South Africa at the start of the year, had been reduced to two years.The decision was made at a CAF executive committee meeting in Cairo at the weekend.CAF also announced the creation of an African Champions' League from next year, disqualified Burundi from the youth championship and
5994 held over a decision on Burkina Faso's hosting of the next Nations' Cup finals in 1998.The reduction of Nigeria's ban came after an appeal by both the Nigerian football association and their Congolese counterparts.Nigeria, the defending champions, refused to take part in the Africa Nations' Cup in South Africa in
5994 January after a diplomatic spat between the two countries over Nigeria's execution of writer Kan Saro-Wiwa and nine others late last year.They were slapped with the four-year ban by an indigant CAF and threatened with expulsion from the 1998 World Cup qualifiers in France but the African body later softened
5994 its stance.Nigeria will now be able to enter the qualifiers for the 2000 finals in Zimbabwe after having been excluded from the draw for the 1998 qualifiers, which kick off next month.CAF also announced the creation of an African Champions' League, modelled on the successful, and lucrative, counterpart in Europe.The
5994 competition will start next year and see the eight quarter-finalists divided into two groups with the winners going through to a two-leg final.The two earlier rounds of the competition will still be played on a two-leg knockout basis, said CAF, who hope to attractive sizeable sponsorship for the tournament."But the
5994 Champions' League will start in 1997 even without sponsors," they added in a press release issued on Monday.Burundi, who were surprise qualifiers for the last world under-20 champonship in Qatar in 1995, have been disqualified from the 1997 qualifiers because of an air embrago placed on the tiny east African
5994 country after a recent coup d'etat.Burundi were scheduled to travel to Tanzania this weekend for their first round, first leg match but teams have been unable to leave the country because of the travel ban.Earlier this month, the Burundi national team were disqualified from the 1998 African Nations' Cup qualifiers
5994 because they could not go to the Central African Republic.The CAF executive committee also studied a report on Burkina Faso's progress in organising the next Nations' Cup finals in 1998 but CAF gave no details save to announce that another delegation is to travel there "in the coming months".</

5997 Holders Orlando Pirates became the latest victims of the African Champions' Cup curse, when they were knocked out in the quarter-finals at the weekend.Their penalty shootout defeat by Shooting Stars of Nigeria in Ibadan on Saturday sees the South African team join a 27-year-long list of defending champions who have
5997 been unsuccessful in retaining Africa's top club prize.Not since Zairean club TP Englebert retained the African Champion's Cup in 1968 has a team been able to win the competition in successive years.Pirates hopes were shattered when Brendan Silent missed the vital kick in the shootout after a 1-1 aggregate draw.The
5997 match was one of 11 African club competition quarter-final, second leg ties played at the weekend.The holders travelled to Nigeria with a slim 1-0 lead after the first leg in Bloemfontein two weeks ago and lost the advantage after 55 minutes when Dotin Alatishe scored.But it was Stars' goalkeeper Abiodun
5997 Baruwa who was the hero of the afternoon with two shootout saves and a penalty of his own to see the Nigerians through 4-3 on kicks to a semifinal meeting with Algeria's JS Kabylie.Kabylie, last year's African Cup Winners' Cup victors, beat Angola's Petro Atletco 1-0 on Friday to advance
5997 2-1 on aggregate.The other Champions' Cup semifinal will involve Zamalek of Egypt, who beat COD Meknes of Morocco 4-2 on aggregate, against CS Sfaxien of Tunisia.The Tunisian team went through despite losing 3-1 away at Diaraf Dakar on Sunday with all the goals coming in a furious first half.Arab Contractors
5997 justified their billing as favourites in the African Cup Winners' Cup by reaching the semifinals at the expense of Moroccan opposition FUS Rabat.Contractors won the second leg on Friday 1-0 after a goalless draw in the first leg earlier this month.They now meet another former winner Canon Yaounde, who scored
5997 two vital away goals in a 2-2 draw away at Costa do Sol of Mozambique to progress on the away goals rule.CAF Cup holders Etoile du Sahel conceded a last minute goal against Unisport Bafang in Cameroon on Sunday but still won 4-2 on aggregate to book their berth in
5997 the final four.The Tunisian club will now have to travel further south in the semifinal where they meet Vita Club of Zaire.Zaire's immensely popular team came from two goals behind to beat Mouloudia Oran of Algeria on post-match penalties in Kinshasa on Sunday.The other semifinal clash pits Kenya Breweries, who
5997 ended Ports Authroty's dream of becoming the first club from Sierra Leone to reach the semifinal of any African club competition, against Kawkab Marrakesh of Morrocco.</

5999 Tamas Gyarfas, re-elected head of the Hungarian Swimming Federation (HSF) at the weekend, said on Monday frauds such as the "phantom" qualifying meet over which he resigned would not be repeated."I will personally see that such things never happen again," Gyarfas told Reuters after he was elected president of the
5999 HSF on Saturday by 65 votes to two.Gyarfas quit his post after allegations that half of Hungary's Olympic swimming team competed in Atlanta on the basis of a qualifying meet which never took place.When he resigned, Gyarfas said he had no previous knowledge of the affair.HSF general secretary Jozsef Ruza,
5999 who later admitted sending the counterfeit qualifying sheets, was also re-elected to his post on Saturday."Everybody involved was willing to take as much of the blame as possible," Gyarfas said, adding that he would accept his re-election as president."To leave my post at this stage would not be the proper
5999 thing to do," he said. "The federation needs to stick together."Although he described the forgeries as an "inadmissible, grave mistake" he said the fraud did not result in Hungarian swimmers taking the place of any other nation's athletes at the Olympics as each country had its own quota of places.Hungary
5999 is one of the world's top swimming nations and came away from the Atlanta Games with three gold, one silver, and two bronze medals.</
