6406 The management group poised to complete a buyout of the Toronto Sun Publishing Corp. on Tuesday said it wants to keep the company's majority stake in the Financial Post daily business newspaper.The Toronto Sun's chief financial officer, Bruce Jackson, said that despite news reports to the contrary the management group
6406 has not received an offer for the Financial Post from media mogul Conrad Black.Black's Hollinger Inc., which has a controlling stake in Southam Inc., holds about 20 percent of the Financial Post.A Canadian Press news agency report late Thursday said Southam had made an offer for the Toronto Sun's 60.2
6406 percent holding in the Financial Post."We don't have any offer for the Financial Post," Jackson said in a telephone interview, referring to the report.But he added, "Southam was in the (Toronto Sun) data room back in June or July...I believe they made an offer at that time for the Financial
6406 Post. And I think obviously there is interest there."The report of a Southam offer came as the final days ticked away ahead of Tuesday's vote by shareholders on the management group's C$16 ($12) per share bid for Toronto Sun. The management group buyout will cost about C$411 million ($301 million),
6406 before expenses.Toronto Sun owns a chain of tabloids in several major Canadian cities as well as the Financial Post stake.Debt-ridden Rogers Communications Inc. in May put its 63-percent holding in Toronto Sun on the block, which led to the takeover offer for the whole company.Jackson said despite the hefty long-term
6406 debtload the management group buyout will place on Toronto Sun, the group would prefer to keep the Financial Post."The Financial Post has a lot of upside to it. We believe it's got a really good future," Jackson said.Canadian Press quoted David Radler, Southam's associate chief executive and president of Hollinger,
6406 as saying he did not know if Southam's offer for the Post would succeed."It's in the hands of (Toronto Sun President Paul) Godfrey," Canadian Press quoted Radler as saying.Unless an 11th-hour offer materialises, Tuesday's vote will rubber-stamp the ownership transfer of Toronto Sun to the Godfrey-led management group, which will
6406 then be in full control of the Financial Post's future.</
6407 Some minor downgrades in Manitoba's spring wheat crop were expected from an outbreak of fusarium head blight, a grain quality specialist with Manitoba's largest grain handling firm said on Monday."It's not a severe outbreak where you're getting large percentages," Manitoba Pool Elevators quality control manager Derry Sager told Reuters. "You'll
6407 get some fields that may be hit a little harder than others but it's generally a No1 and No2 (Canada Western) Red (Spring Wheat) crop in southern Manitoba where the problem would be."Fusarium is caused by prolonged rain during heading stage.The fungus can produce vomitoxin which, in low levels, is
6407 tolerable, but in higher concentrations can cause nausea."We're not seeing anything big like 15 to 20 percent infected crops this year. We're seeing something very minute, either under 0.2 or not much over two percent if there is any heavier infestations," Sager said.This summer's infection appeared to be most acute
6407 in the Red River Valley, Sager said.The Canadian Grain Commission earlier this month estimated about two percent of early-harvested samples showed minor downgrading due to fusarium head blight. The CGC plans to update its estimate later this week.MPE operates the largest number of primary elevators in Manitoba at more than
6407 110.-- Gilbert Le Gras 204 947 3548</

6410 Black Sea Energy Ltd said it completed necessary agreements in Krasnodar and Moscow to form a joint venture that gives the company 50 percent interest in the rehabilitation of a large oil field in southern Russia.Black Sea, whose major shareholder is Canadian mining developer Robert Friedland, said the agreement covers
6410 the Anastasievsko-Troitskoye oil field, which has an estimated 190 million barrels in place.It said about 53 million barrels were recoverable by the joint venture. Black's Sea's partner is Krasnodarneftegaz, a company controlled by Rosneftegaz. The field, where 1,400 wells are available for rehabilitation, is connected by pipeline to Russia's main
6410 oil export terminal at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.The company plans to use Canadian technology to boost output to 26,000 barrels of oil a day from the current 12,000.The project was expected to require US$10 million for initial capital and operating costs. Startup is due later this year and
6410 includes the use of adavanced well completipon and horizontal drilling technology, Black Sea said.John Ellis, who with Friedland is s co-chairman of Black Sea, was a financial adviser to the Russian oil ministry before directing international business development for Canadian Fracmaster Ltd.Fracmaster was the first Canadian company to take oil
6410 in payment for reworking oil wells in Russia. Black Sea president Clint Hussin negotiated five joint ventures for Fracmaster. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624</
6411 Burundi authorities said on Monday sanctions imposed by neighbouring countries hurt the weak and if they were not lifted soon the country would explode.Lieutenant-Colonel Longin Minani, spokesman for the army which seized power in Burundi on July 25, said an embargo on the country since July 31 was hitting those
6411 who could least afford it."For us the sanctions have been put there unfairly," he told Reuters. "Measures...should be for the good of the population.""We do not have fertilisers. Next year what will happen?" said Minani, arguing Buyoya's government had met the demands of regional states behind sanctions by lifting bans
6411 on political parties and parliament.The sanctions imposed after Buyoya's take over of power have cut off oil imports to the landlocked country and blocked exports of coffee, its main hard currency earner.But regional leaders who imposed sanctions on July 31 also demand talks without conditions between all parties to Burundi's
6411 conflict. Buyoya says the rebels have to lay down their weapons first.Minani said rebels were being helped by neighbouring states and were continuing their activities unabated despite sanctions.In an interview published in Kenya's East African weekly on Wednesday, Tutsi military ruler Pierre Buyoya said: "If this country remains under sanctions
6411 for two or three (more) months, all is going to explode.""I say that the embargo and sanctions are destroying the peace process right now," said the retired army major, adding he was ready to negotiate a lifting of the sanctions.Meanwhile, officials from a faction of the main Hutu party, split
6411 since the army coup, said earlier on Monday they backed exiled party president Jean Minani and were committed to solving Burundi's conflict peacefully.The group made the announcement in a statement a week after another wing of the Frodebu party elected rebel leader Leonard Nyangoma as its president and endorsed armed
6411 struggle.Frodebu Secretary-General Augustin Nzojibwami said party leaders at the weekend in Bujumbura confirmed their commitment to a peaceful resolution to Burundi's conflict between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi-dominated military and supported Minani."Participants reaffirmed that there is no military solution to the Burundian conflict. Only negotiations...will bring peace to Burundi," the
6411 party said in a statement after the talks.Frodebu has been divided since the army took over and Buyoya succeeded President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya, a Frodebu member.Nzojibwami told Reuters on Wednesday several Frodebu leaders who took refuge in the German embassy in Bujumbura after the coup left their sanctuary at the weekend
6411 after Buyoya lifted the ban on political parties.The statement made no direct mention of the split within the party but former foreign minister Venerand Bakevyumusaya, who lost his post in the coup, told Reuters Minani was still the leader.More than 150,000 people -- mostly civilians -- have died in three
6411 years of violence between the army and rebels from the Hutu majority, which makes up 85 percent of the country's six million people.</

6412 Mohammed el-Sanousi, spokesman of the Sudanese armed forces, as saying."It does not help the efforts of the two countries to consolidate the concepts of security specified in the recent agreement," he added.Uganda's Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi said earlier two Sudanese MiG planes had on Sunday dropped bombs
6412 aimed at an army barracks in the northwestern town of Moyo, 16 km (10 miles) south of Sudan's border but missed their target."It is true we have been bombed by Sudan...It is surprising that even before the ink dries on the agreement we signed they are bombing us," Mbabazi told
6412 reporters."We shall not sit back and watch while our territory continues to be violated. We shall soon respond appropriately."Under the September 9 pact, mediated by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on a visit to Khartoum and Kampala, the two countries agreed to work to halt activity by rebels in the
6412 border area. Both accuse each other of supporting rebel groups.Sunday's air raid was the first since Sudanese planes bombed northern Uganda in January in an attack Khartoum said was aimed against southern Sudanese rebels."Two Sudanese MiGs came over on Sunday and dropped a number of bombs, around 10. Not all
6412 fell on Moyo and we have no reports of casualties," an aid worker, who declined to be named, said.Other aid workers said they heard from the region that the MiGs attacked at 9:30 a.m. and dropped bombs and fired rockets at Moyo but no reports of casualties or damage were

6447 South Africa expects its current account to improve in the second half of the year and has no plans to seek International Monetary Fund (IMF) assistance, officials said on Monday.Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said the country's recent success in tapping the international bond market, despite this year's sharp fall in
6447 the rand on investor jitters, showed South Africa could stand on its own feet."It's not as though we are knocking on the door of the Fund or the Bank with a begging bowl," Manuel told a news conference ahead of the 1996 IMF/World Bank meetings which start this week.Reserve Bank
6447 Governor Chris Stals said South Africa did not envisage applying for an IMF standby facility since the country did not now require balance of payments support.It had reserves to help bridge the current account deficit, plus over 15 billion rand ($3.3 billion) of unused credit facilities, Stals told the same
6447 news conference."That second line of defence (credit facilities) is still available before we come to the third line of defence which would be the IMF," Stals said.A number of factors suggested improvement in the current account from now on, including a slowdown in gross domestic expenditure, restrictive monetary policy, the
6447 expectation that bank credit extension will decline and the likely effects of the depreciation of the rand."We believe that the current account deficit will decline in the second half of this year...so far we have not seen very convincing statistics, but we still believe that the current account deficit will
6447 get smaller over the next 12 months," Stals said.Worries about South Africa's balance of payments position, and a decline in official reserves to just one month's import cover, have exacerbated concerns about the rand. It has fallen since February from 3.65 against the dollar to 4.51.The deficit on the current
6447 account for the balance of payments ballooned to 6.9 billion rand in the first half of 1996, after 12.7 billion for the whole of 1995 and 2.2 billion for all of 1994.But Manuel said the reception for South Africa's 500 million mark Eurobond launched this month showed international investors still
6447 had faith. The finance department hopes to follow with a U.S. "Yankee" bond next month and will be holding a roadshow for potential investors in the United States from October 4 to 11.Manuel said South Africa had also been holding preliminary talks on a possible World Bank loan to help
6447 its industries compete more effectively.A topic at the IMF talks of particular interest to South Africa, a major gold producer, is the IMF plan to sell five million ounces of bullion to aid poor countries. South Africa has discouraged the IMF from selling the gold, which represents some five percent
6447 of IMF reserves of gold.But Stals said he was sympathetic to helping the poorest states and sales would not unduly disrupt the market if they were gradual.Manuel, Stals and other officials head first to Bermuda for the September 24-26 Commonwealth finance ministers' meeting before attending the IMF/World Bank talks.Manuel said
6447 he was keen to compare notes with Commonwealth counterparts, including India, which is seeking to implement a budget-cutting plan similar to that unveiled by Manuel in June.($=4.51 rand)</

6497 The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday it had placed nine commercial banks under special supervision in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector. 6497 the banking system," the BNB said in a statement after a board meeting.The banks are Trade and Savings Bank (TSB), Balkanbank, Economic Bank, Businessbank, Elitbank, Slavyani commercial bank, Mollov bank, Yambol commercial bank, and Dobrudzha commercial bank, the statement said. Placing these banks under special supervision was part of a
6497 larger package of measures agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under a $580 million funding agreement sealed in July, the BNB said.Supervision, which entails ban on lending, will allow these banks to boost their capital and facilitate their sale to foreign investors.The BNB said that such negotiations have begun
6497 already with the two large state institutions Balkanbank and Economic Bank.The decision against the nine banks was taken on the eve of IMF/World Bank annual meeting where the Socialist government hopes to win a second $115 million tranche of funding which was previously delayed by the IMF due to Bulgaria's
6497 failure to meet reform targets.Bulgaria pledged to close down loss makers, including banks by end-September.This was yet another bid by the government to meet funding requirements after opening insolvency procedures through the courts against five other banks in May and June.</

6621 Mexican Finance Minister Guillmero Ortiz issued a warning to tax evaders on Monday and urged the public to view tax cheats as common thieves.Ortiz said on a radio tax talk show that it was an affront to society that certain rich Mexicans did not pay taxes when less wealthy ones
6621 did. He urged Mexicans to "see tax evaders as people stealing from the rest of society," but stopped short of asking them to blow the whistle on tax evaders.His strong message came shortly after Mexico launched a crackdown on tax evasion in response to a sharp drop in tax receipts
6621 after last year's economic crisis. Arrest warrants have been issued for several high-profile businessmen and the government has launched an aggressive media ad campaign featuring a burning match and the slogan "Don't Get Burned."Tax evasion is widely seen as a sport in Mexico and people who do not pay are
6621 praised for "accounting" skills. Ortiz estimated that 70 percent of workers do not pay income tax, many from the "informal sector" who sell goods on the streets, polish shoes in bars and wash windshields at traffic lights.Newspaper magnate Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz was the most prominent businessman to be caught
6621 in the crackdown. Ealy, who owns Mexico City's oldest daily newspaper, El Universal, is free on bail pending charges of tax fraud. Arrest warrants are out for three other businessmen.As part of the clampdown, Mexico plans to carry out 400,000 audits on companies and public servants this year, Finance Ministry
6621 spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela told reporters on Monday, hinting that the tax problem in Mexico is exacerbated by officials taking bribes not to investigate.Finance minister Ortiz said Mexico's tax collection levels were too low. Discounting tax receipts on items such as fuel sales, he said, tax inflows were not even 10
6621 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP).But he gave no indication Mexico was about to change its tax rates: a 34 percent income tax and a 15 percent value added tax under which products are taxed according to value added at each level of production and exchange."Mexican tax rates
6621 are not high," he said.The drive to capture tax cheats includes collecting information on people who buy luxury cars or take expensive flights. Tax officials are asking travel agents to supply names and addresses of clients who have traveled extensively.Ortiz said the government was pinpointing offenders who, for example, paid
6621 a few dollars in taxes but flew first-class to Paris three times. "Such scenarios do not fit together."Mexico's top business leader went one step further than Ortiz on Monday, calling for an overhaul of tax laws to give bosses more certainty about where they stand."We desperately need to look together
6621 to implement judicial certainty for companies, which would require a complete fiscal reform," Hector Larios Santillan, the chairman of the Business Coordinating Council, told reporters.</

6642 But angry at unemployment of 17.1 percent, it is fighting President Carlos Menem's drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labor laws. "The CGT is open to dialogue, but it must be understood there is no possibility of negotiating the strike," said CGT chief Rodolfo Daer, who will lead a

6642 scrap collective pay deals, swap redundancy payments for an unemployment insurance scheme, make a proportion of wages variable depending on the health of the economy and change working hours and vacations.Menem threatens to push the laws through by decree if the Congress puts up a fight. 6643 Argentina's private pension funds will be decisive in the development of the local capital markets in the years to come, a top official said."Their (the funds) participation as institutional investors within the system is crucial for the expansion of the capital markets and tends to reduce volatility," Jose Luis Pardo,
6643 president of the Chamber of Argentine Private Pension Funds, told Reuters. Speaking on the eve of the first convention organized by the Argentine private pension funds system, he forecast the system's rapid expansion. By 2000 he expects the funds to manage $20 billion against $4.2 billion now. Looking further ahead
6643 to 2010, he anticipates close to $100 billion managed by the funds."The new pension system, its dynamic, its competitiveness, the development of its services and ability to accumulate savings is provoking a strong impact on Argentina's reality," says the pamphlet introducing the 'Private Pensions, Social Certainty and Economic Growth,' convention.The
6643 funds hold out great hope for the continued reform of Argentina's economy. Neighboring Chile's private pension system created more than 10 years ago is often cited as one of Latin America's biggest economic success stories.But Pardo cautions that Argentina's system still has "a long way to go before becoming a
6643 net exporter of capital" like Chile's has become.In addition, Pardo said the recent strong performance of the private pension funds must be considered together with the slump and subsequent recovery in Latin American markets induced by the devaluation of the Mexican peso in December 1994. In the 12 months ending
6643 in the middle of this year, Argentine pension funds posted average returns of just over 20 percent."The recuperation of the various markets and the gradual reduction of country risk has to offer lower returns, so it is logical that, in the future, the average return of the system will moderate,"
6643 said Pardo.Pardo did not say he expected further lifting of the controls governing the way the funds can invest. Now, up to 49 percent of funds can be invested in stocks and recently the minimum amount allowed to be used on one stock was raised to 2.5 percent from 1.5
6643 percent.Still, "we do not expect that in the future we will be surprised with any important new investment limitations," said Pardo. Some local observers have called for larger participation by the funds in privatized companies.The private pension funds were established in August 1994 and currently have some 5.0 million members.President
6643 Carlos Menem will deliver the opening speech at the two-day conference that starts on Tuesday.-- Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0668</

6653 Mexico's monetary base is expected to spike up sharply between now and the end of the year, but analysts said the increase will be tied to seasonal demand and not by itself reflect an easing of monetary policy.Year-end demand will push the monetary base up sharply, but the government is
6653 within the signposts for growth of the money supply -- the next one coming up at the end of September. They add that, within the overall perimeters set for growth in the monetary base -- mainly notes and coins -- the central bank has begun to allow for lower interest
6653 rates. "They (the central bank) definitely are on track and they may be even better than originally expected. There is no reason to think that they will go off track with their program," said one Mexico City-based economist.At the start of the year, the central bank forecast an increase of
6653 18.0 billion pesos in the monetary base by the end of 1996 over the figure at the end of 1995.The monetary base ended 1995 at 66.8 billion pesos, but the central bank also previously forecast 63 billion pesos as its year-end starting point since they said a sharp increase in
6653 December last year was not representative. At the end of last week, the monetary base was about 60.1 billion pesos, while the central bank's forecast for the end of the third quarter was for about 450 million pesos below the 1995 year-end figure. Economists say this latitude allows room for
6653 a sharp year-end increase, traditionally tied to greater holiday spending.Santander Investment said recently that the nominal monetary base will rise 40 percent from current levels during the fourth quarter "however, this would not imply a relaxation of the monetary policy, because the expansion will be caused by a seasonally higher
6653 level of expeditures in the economy." Within that overall envelope for growth in the monetary aggregates, analysts say the central bank recently has been able to allow interest rates to drift lower.Interest rates have come down as worries over inflation have eased and as the need to spur greater domestic
6653 growth increases."It is not because the monetary base may go up in December, but I do think the central bank has adopted a policy of supporting somewhat lower levels of interest rates...," said HSBC James Capel economist Gray Newman. 6653 year, when they didn't like to admit it, but when they were much more concerned about stability in the peso and providing overall stability and they were willing to let interest rates rise," Newman said.Santander noted that the Mexican central bank started to ease after the U.S. Federal Reserve left
6653 rates unchanged following its August 20 Open Market Committee meeting.It said this shows monetary authorities are confident about the downward trend in inflation, which will lead to a drop in real rates next year when monetary policy is seen as being even Exports have led most of the growth in
6653 the economic recovery, but as the economy moves to an increase in investment spending, it becomes more sensitive to interest rates, analysts said.-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559. E-mail at robert.kozak@reuters.com</

6655 Many Salvadorans have been trading in assault rifles, grenades and rocket launchers for consumer goods in a programme aimed at reducing violence in this Central American country, organisers said on Monday."We're content because the people have responded by bringing in a large number of war weapons," David Gutierrez, chief of
6655 the Patriotic Movement Against Delinquency, which devised the "Guns for Goods" programme, told a news conference.Gutierrez said in the first week the programme collected 150 rifles, mostly M-16 and AK-47 assault rifles, along with 81 handguns, five rocket-launchers and 35 grenades plus a wide array of dynamite and C4 explosives.Thousands
6655 of Salvadorans have kept high-powered weapons since a 12-year-long civil war that killed an estimated 75,000 people ended in 1992. The government estimates 300,000 military arms were left in civilian hands, of which 140,000 have since been recovered.Guns for Goods, financed by a group of business leaders, a local Rotary
6655 Club and the Roman Catholic Church, was intended to get poor people to give up their arms in exchange for coupons to buy consumer goods such as food and clothes.For each handgun, participants receive a coupon worth the equivalent of $172, while each rifle brings a coupon worth the equivalent
6655 of $345. The programme will continue each weekend until Dec. 15 with collection sites at Roman Catholic churches in major cities.Anonymity for the participants is guaranteed and the Legislative Assembly passed a law that permits carrying war weapons to the collection sites.</

There will be reactions," said Carlos Aldana, spokesman for the Guatemalan archbishopric, which
6687 has called on Guatemalans to support Arzu's efforts to limit the army's power.Arzu and Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein told reporters corrupt elements could start threatening government officials. When Guatemala has tried to move against corrupt military officers in the past, Stein said bluntly, "they started killing judges."Unlike his three civilian
6687 predecessors from 1986 to 1995, who could not shake the army's influence on every sector of Guatemalan life, Arzu has moved decisively since January.He ordered the army to halt 36 years of counterinsurgency actions against guerrilla fighters and last week, in the most sweeping action yet, the government fired a
6687 score of allegedly corrupt officials including two generals, one of them the deputy defence minister.The top-ranking army officers, police chiefs and customs administrators who were fired are all suspected of involvement with a huge, long-established smuggling ring that officials say cheated the government out of millions of dollars a month.The
6687 anti-corruption operation last Tuesday struck at the heart of the military intelligence community, which is deeply involved with organised crime as well as with assassinations, disappearances and torture during Guatemala's dirty war.Two days later, government and guerrilla peace negotiators signed a landmark agreement to reduce the army by a third,
6687 limit the military's role to defending Guatemala from external threats and give Congress control over military intelligence.Arzu did not begin the peace process but he gave it impetus. Guerrillas and government negotiators say they will sign a definitive agreement to end the civil war by December.Not everyone is convinced everything
6687 will run smoothly."Anything is possible. There could be a backlash. ... There's still fear of (a coup) because of the history of the country," said a foreign observer in Guatemala, who did not want to be identified.On the record, most government officials and international supporters express enthusiastic support for Arzu's
6687 commitment to the peace process, which they hope will energise Guatemala's economy and stimulate foreign investment.Defence Minister Julio Balconi told Reuters the army was willing to make sacrifices for peace.Cesar Gaviria, secretary-general of the Organisation of American States, in Guatemala this week, pledged support for the fight against corruption and
6687 for implementation of the peace accords.A government-sponsored jingle on the radio chirps, "let's make a change, let's go, Guatemala," cajoling citizens to get on board the peace train. But Guatemala has yet to shake off years of terror. A one-hour blackout in almost the entire country on Thursday had Guatemalans
6687 fearing that a coup was under way. Power outages traditionally accompany coups here.Human rights leader Helen Mack, who has fought to put military officers accused of killing her anthropologist sister in 1990 on trial, fears army intimidation will keep the corruption scandal out of the courts. "The judges will obstruct
6687 the entire process in the struggle against impunity," Mack predicted.Aldana of the archbishop's office said if corrupt military officers actually go on trial, the risks the government has taken would all be worthwhile. "It is riskier to Guatemalan society as a whole not to take these measures," he said.</

6700 A Brazilian Central Bank study is garnering public attention for its dramatic trade liberalization stance and its forward look at the Brazilian economy. The document comes at a time when the government's current reform drive is losing momentum, economists say.Its author, international affairs director Gustavo Franco, is a leading thinker
6700 behind Brazil's successful 2-year-old anti-inflation drive known as the Real Plan.Franco, a Harvard trained economist, has written dozens of academic papers on the merits of economic stabilization. "But this paper is important because he wants to take a long-term view of the Real plan and move beyond stabilization," said Alvaro
6700 Manoel, director of research at Chase Manhattan bank in Brazil.Franco, who occupies the No. 2 post at the Central Bank, entitled his 45-page document "Economic Opening and Development".Economists said Franco's not-so-original prescription is simple: tear down trade barriers, force Brazilian companies to become more productive through greater competition and achieve
6700 stable economic growth. The country's new economic growth model must include wide trade liberalization, "maybe two or three times more than what we have today," Franco writes.Although Brazil has removed a host of trade barriers over the past few years, it remains a relatively closed economy. Total trade represents just
6700 15 percent of Brazil's gross domestic product, compared to 60 percent in Mexico and 30 percent in Latin America as a whole.Despite its simplicity, Franco's forward-looking focus could not come at a better time for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso. Cardoso's constitutional reforms, seen as key to the ultimate success of
6700 the Real Plan, are stalled in Congress.Cardoso reportedly liked the paper so much he made it public. Aides say the president hopes to revive some discussion of Brazil's economic reform drive, a subject that has taken second stage recently to nationwide municipal elections and debate surrounding presidential re-election.Analysts noted that
6700 Franco's treatment of unemployment as a necessary, but temporary, consequence of stabilization undoubtedly pleased the president, who has his eye on re-election in 1998. "High unemployment has been a big worry for Cardoso. Franco gives him a light at the end of the tunnel by saying continue with privatizations, speed
6700 economic opening and at first you will have unemployment but it won't be permanent," said Marcelo Allain, chief economist for BMC bank in Brazil.It also moves beyond the government's central concern over taming inflation, Allain added."It answers the basic question: Now that we have low inflation, what are we going
6700 to do? And his answer is economic growth through openness," Allain said. The document is now making its way through research departments of Brazilian investment banks, where analysts are looking for hints about any upcoming changes to Brazil's stable exchange rate policy.Franco, who is most closely identified with Brazil's exchange
6700 rate policy, has been criticized at home and abroad for maintaining a strong real in the face of large trade deficits and stagnant to modest economic growth.But based on his latest paper, economists say they do not expect any change in the system, which now allows the real to depreciate
6700 by about eight percent a year. "He doesn't want to use exchange rate policy to tackle trade deterioration and boost growth. This message is very clear," said Marcelo Carvalho, chief economist at JP Morgan in Brazil.The release of the paper by Cardoso's office has also stirred speculation over future leadership
6700 of the Central Bank. A rumor circulated earlier this week that Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola would soon be out. For the first time Franco's name cropped up as the leading contender for the post.--Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 232-4411</

6709 International proposals to bail out the world's poorest debtor nations will come under attack for not going far enough when finance ministers from the Commonwealth meet here this week.Ministers, representing most of the 53 members of the former British Empire which makes up the Commonwealth, will also look at how
6709 to stamp out money-laundering and encourage instead the inflow of legitimate private capital to prime their economies."We want to see how to get proposals on terms for debt relief improved. Terms are too tough for seriously indebted countries," Commonwealth Secretary General Humphrey Maude told reporters ahead of the September 24-26
6709 talks in this Caribbean island.All but five of the countries in the group are classed as developing economies, ranging from Asian giant India to tiny islands in the Pacific and Caribbean.Many are struggling to pay off huge debts, including to multilateral financial institutions like the World Bank and the International
6709 Monetary Fund (IMF).Commonwealth officials described the meeting as the one chance each year when developing members can join with leading economies such as Britain and Canada to lobby the international community on their behalf."We expect quite a tough debate...we hope for consensus on easing (debt relief) terms," Maude said.Their views
6709 will be taken on to Washington the following week to the annual IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington where debt relief will figure high on the agenda, including the deeply contentious question of whether to use some of the IMF's gold.Up to 20 of the world's poorest countries have been targetted
6709 as in urgent need of help but officials say in reality only two or three countries can expect quick help to pull them out of a deepening debt trap.The Commonwealth's chief concerns are that it is too difficult for many of the most needy to meet the terms for debt
6709 relief, that it takes too long for the help to arrive and that the burden for providing assistance is not fairly shared out.Commonwealth officials said they realised that it was equally important for the countries themselves to prove that they were making serious attempts to put their own economies on
6709 track.Ministers will look at ways to bring in more private investment to offset "aid fatigue" which has seen aid to developing countries slide as industrial nations focus more on how to slash their own budget deficits.That includes how to deal with the surge of flows in and out of an
6709 economy, which was held responsible for the near catastrophe that hit Mexico's economy one and a half years ago, and whose effects are still swirling the world of international finance.On the other side of the coin, the Commonwealth will press ahead with efforts to prevent illicit money coming through member
6709 countries -- several of them international tax havens -- which are used to launder to earnings of drug dealers and their like.However, officials concede that several are reluctant to do anything that would also limit banking secrecy in case it scares off more legitimate investment.</

6719 and profits would reverberate throughout the business community and discourage competition. 6719 in relation to his own somewhat intrusive brand of socialism," Shirtcliffe told Reuters."Telecom may be the icon for Mr Anderton to say we're going to control their profits. What I'd say is -- 'it may be us today, it will be you tomorrow' -- that's what I'd say to every
6719 other business," Shirtcliffe said. "It isn't just about Telecom. It's about a whole philosophy of control and regulation. These guys can't help themselves," he said. "These guys are control freaks."Shirtcliffe said New Zealand had come out of an era of being run by control freaks in the mid 1980s which
6719 had retarded growth and New Zealanders knew they could not go back a second time."Kiwis (New Zealanders) no longer want that environment."Shirtcliffe said any attempt by the Alliance or any other party in government to use the so-called kiwi share to cut residential line charges or Telecom's profits would be
6719 counterproductive. It would restrict competition and was likely to be part of a wider re-regulatory push that would hurt business.When Telecom was privatised the government continued to hold a "kiwi share" which forced Telecom to keep residential line charge increases below the inflation rate and to keep local residential calls
6719 free."The kiwi share's a two way deal. It's a contract." Shirtcliffe said, adding he did not believe Anderton understood how the kiwi share worked. "If a politician and a group of politicians want to come and fiddle with the environment, I think you've got to take it as a given
6719 that they will be dealing not just with Telecom, but with the business environment generally," he said.Telecom currently cross-subsidised its residential customers by charging higher rates for its business customers and any cut in residential rates could see business rates rise.Lower residential rates would also discourage competition in the residential
6719 market, Shirtcliffe said."If you reduce those local rental prices, how is anybody going to provide a competitive service," he said. 6723 a net 10 percent of those surveyed expected a market deterioration in the November quarter.This improved from the more than 50 percent who, in May, saw a deterioration in the August quarter. 6723 in May had turned to optimism by August.The commercial property market, overall, was expected to remain steady by 58 percent of those surveyed, while 27 percent expected an improvement and 11 percent saw a deterioration.The survey was the first conducted by the Massey University real estate analysis unit on behalf
6723 of the Institute of Valuers. 6726 New Zealand production statistics for the June quarter present a mixed picture, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.While the quarter saw falls in production of cigarettes and tobacco, beer, footwear, petrol refining and livestock slaughtering, there were significant rises in coal sales, softdrink, and gas and crude petroleum production.Marginal rises
6726 were also seen in electricity production and sawn timber.The volume of cigarettes available for consumption in the quarter fell 6.6 percent when compared to the year-ago quarter, while tobacco was 23.6 percent lower.Beer production was 3.3 percent lower than a year ago, while footwear production was down 11.3 percent.Total petrol
6726 production in the June quarter was 8.9 percent less than a year ago. Production of regular petrol rose by 9.2 percent, but this was offset by a decline in premium petrol production of 32 percent.There were 10.4 percent fewer livestock slaughtered in the June 1996 quarter than in the June
6726 1995 quarter.Coal sales were up nine percent compared to a year ago.-- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746</

6727 1996/97 total business investment. The government forecast in the budget was for a 14 percent rise in total business investment -- which consists of plant and equipment and non-dwelling construction spending.Market economists tended to come in below that forecast, although they did say the Treasury had a good track record
6727 on business investment in recent years.Of the 31 economists surveyed, only three forecast a figure stronger than the government, while another three expected the government's forecast to be met.Those at the weaker end of forecasts tended to have weaker GDP growth forecasts than the government's 3.5 percent. This fit in
6727 within recently retired Reserve Bank Govenor Bernie Fraser's statement in Tokyo earlier this month that "the main key to achieving the 3.5 percent GDP growth forecast for 1996/97 is business investment."Some eocnomists said the government forecast may have erred on the upside, as the business investment forecast could effect sentiment.
6727 A weak forecast could have undermined some confidence by creating the belief that the budget would be contractionary, economists said. 6731 logo and service stations, and building new ones, he said."We are in the process of completing our plans and making our priorities," Law-Smith said in an interview."But we are looking at a number of $5 billion. The area we are looking at is the whole of Asia, including new markets,
6731 that is China, Vietnam, Cambodia, India and Indonesia."Law-Smith also said Caltex was revamping its Asia management, putting top decision-making executives into Singapore to bring management closer to the market.He said Caltex interests in China involved areas under less government restriction, including liquified petroleum gas (LPG), lubricants, the production of asphalt
6731 for road building and retail sales of transportation fuels, especially in southern China.China has made it known it does not need foreign investment and technology in developing oil refineries, Law-Smith said. "However there is certainly room for integrated refineries and petrochemical plants down the road," he said.The company's plans in
6731 India were also focused on the LPG and lubricant sectors, Law-Smith said.He said Caltex had started discussions with several parties in India on possible investments, had done its research and analysis, and was "half-way" to making decisions.Law-Smith said Caltex has told the Indonesian government its intention and ability to enter
6731 Indonesia's refining and marketing sector to help meet growing demand, especially for transportation fuel, as the economy grows.Indonesia is keen to attract private and foreign oil companies to build export-oriented oil refineries. 6732 Jim GilchristTwo months after EVA Air entered the busy Hong Kong-Taipei sector, the Taiwanese carrier's two main rivals say there has been no significant impact on cargo volumes.Under a new commercial agreement on air services, EVA began flying 16 times a week between Taipei and Hong Kong on August 1
6732 using Boeing 747 Combi aircraft with 45 tonnes cargo capacity, McDonnell Douglas MD-11s and Boeing 767s. At the launch of the new service, EVA said it expected Hong Kong to quickly become its busiest international destination.China Airlines and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd which have flown the route for many years,
6732 both said the new competition has so far not had a noticeable impact on load factors.But China Airlines' Hong Kong cargo manager M. F. Lai told Reuters he is unhappy at EVA's "discounted" rate which is hitting yields."I'm not happy about the rate. I don't know why Eva are using
6732 such a low rate. We have talked to them face to face and asked them to increase it but their price structure remains the same. It's a difficult situation," Lai said.China Airlines rate to Taipei was HK$4 per kg until EVA began offering HK$3.50 per kg, Lai said."We were only
6732 affected by EVA during the first two weeks of their service. We don't see any negative effect since then because the market is ok but wait and see what the real effect is when the market goes down," Lai said.He called on Eva Air to raise their fares to improve
6732 profitability for all carriers on the route.EVA have so far declined to comment.Cathay Pacific Cargo's marketing and sales manager Ray Jewell also said EVA has had no significant impact."We haven't noticed any significant effect so far but it is the peak right now and things are flowing pretty well when
6732 extra capacity would not necessarily have a big impact but come the slack in January and February there may well be more noticeable effects," he said.The Hong Kong-Taipei route is one of Cathay's busiest with six freighter flights a week and nine passenger flights a day.China Airlines has five freighter
6732 flights a week and 11 passenger flights a day. Lai said his freighter flights are currently enjoying 85 percent load factor. During the slack period load factors are expected to slump to 60 percent.Other airlines which operate Hong Kong to Taipei services are Thai Airways International Ltd, Malaysia Airlines System
6732 Bhd, Singapore Airlines Ltd, Garuda Indonesia and British Airways Plc..According to new statistics from Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department, Taipei is Hong Kong's biggest trading partner importing 7,619 tonnes of air cargo and exporting 5,642 tonnes to Taipei during July.Lai also said he expects the current Hong Kong government estimate
6732 of a seven percent increase in the weight of exports from Hong Kong to Taiwan this year to be exceeded which would be good news for his airline. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017</
6733 Malaysia's announcement of a 624.5 million ringgit ($250.80 million) trade deficit for July after a surplus of 551.4 million in June was in line with market expectations, economists said on Monday.They said the deficit figure pointed to a more sustainable trend evolving after the data for the first six months
6733 showed a dramatic improvement over the previous year."The figure is in line with our own expectations. This is a return to a more sustainable trend, following the previous two months' surpluses," said Desmond Supple, an economist with research consultancy I.D.E.A. in Singapore.Malaysia's Statistics Department said in the first seven months
6733 of the year the trade gap was 1.4 billion ringgit against 6.9 billion in the year-ago period."That is a very big improvement over last year. If you annualise it for the whole year, and if the same trend continues, we expect the trade deficit to be around 2.5 billion ringgit
6733 for the year," said Ghazali Atan, economist with MBf Unit Trust Management in Kuala Lumpur.This compares with a gap of 9.2 billion ringgit last year.Most economists have lowered their full year forecast for the country's trade deficit after a low first half figure.In a poll by Reuters last week, economists
6733 from nine research houses said the trade deficit in 1996 would be an average 4.95 billion ringgit against an average 8.55 billion they had predicted in a poll three months ago.Economists said the high deficit figure in July was due to a slowdown in exports, both manufactured and commodity, and
6733 an increase in some large, one-time equipment imports not accounted for earlier.Bulky imports in the first seven months of 1996 declined by 30.7 percent, or 1.7 billion ringgit, to 3.9 billion against 5.7 billion in the same period in 1995."What these figures suggest is some of those lumpy import items
6733 are yet to impact on the trade figures, so the average monthly deficit should be around this figure over the rest of the year," Supple of I.D.E.A. said.The economists, many of whom had last year expressed worries that the fast-growing Malaysian economy was overheating, said that while they were happy
6733 with an economic slowdown, the slowing export growth was cause for concern.Nik Ahmad Fauzan, economist with Vickers Ballas in Kuala Lumpur, said while the overall figures were improving, year-on-year export growth at just 2.5 percent was low."On the whole the numbers are disappointing. I was hoping for export growth of
6733 around five percent, but it actually came out roughly half of that," he said.The economists said the ringgit's appreciation against the yen, increased gains from petroleum exports and a rise in export of electronic goods despite a worldwide slump, had helped improve the country's balance of payments in the first
6733 six months."Basically, we are just being fortunate. This (weak yen) has allowed us to do quite well despite the electronic sector being hit by some slowdown," Ghazali of MBf said."For the whole year the trend is quite optimstic. It will be helpful in reducing people's doubts about the current account
6733 deficit and prospects for the ringgit," Ghazali said.</

6737 North Korea said on Monday a submarine found stranded off South Korea last week had drifted there after engine failure, and it demanded the return of the vessel and crew, including bodies of those killed.It was Pyongyang's first direct comment on a drama that started on Wednesday when an estimated
6737 26 North Koreans came ashore on an east coast beach near the city of Kangnung.Southern forces have killed nine intruders, found the bodies of 11 believed killed by their own colleagues, captured one North Korean alive, and lost three of their men. One civilian was also killed accidentally by Southern
6737 forces as they continued hunting five North Koreans thought still on the loose.South Korea dismissed Pyongyang's explanation and maintained the intrusion was a military provocation."The North Korean explanation about the vessel is nonsense. It is not worthy of consideration," a defence ministry spokesman told a news conference. "It is nothing
6737 but North Korea's habitual deceiptful policy to defuse critism."The intrusion was a carefully planned infiltration."A statement by Pyongyang's Ministry of the People's Armed Forces carried by the Korea Central News Agency said the vessel was on a routine training mission when it developed engine trouble and ended up on rocks
6737 off Kangnung."It seemed that its crew were left with no other choice but to get to the enemy side's land, which might cause an armed conflict," the poorly-worded statement said."The South side must unconditionally return to the North the submarine and its crew including the dead bodies at once."The statement
6737 said the submarine carried no heavy weapons and there were only small arms on board.However, the South Korean Joint Chief of Staff said a rocket launcher had been found on board.North and South Korea have been technically at war since an armistice ended the 1950-53 Korean conflict and sealed the
6737 partition of the peninsula.South Korea's parliament brushed aside Pyongyang's protestations of innocence and in a rare display of political unity adopted unanimously a resolution condemning the North."The act of infiltrating armed troops by a military submarine is not simply an espionage activity but an explicit military provocation and can never
6737 be tolerated," the 299-member National Assembly declared.It called on the international community "to recognise the reality that the Cold War still persists on the Korean Peninsula and to cooperate in deterring North Korea's aggressive acts".In a veiled criticism of the military's handling of the intrusion, the resolution urged the government
6737 to take measures to respond to guerrilla operations more quickly and restore the public's trust.The mission to hunt down the intruders claimed its first civilian fatality when South Korean troops accidentally killed a man clambering up a mountain in search of wild mushrooms, a military official said.The 56-year-old man was
6737 shot in an area where gunbattles had raged sporadically throughout the night.Two South Korean soldiers were wounded and taken to hospital during the gunbattles, the official said.President Kim Young-sam visited a mortuary to pay respects to the three Southern soldiers killed in the hunt. He burned incense and paid condolences
6737 to bereaved relatives.In Kangnung, more than 5,000 citizens led by the major staged a rally to denounce the incursion, which has ruined the area's all-important tourist industry ahead of the Korean Thanksgiving holiday.South Korea is trying to drum up an international campaign against Pyongyang over the incident, one of the
6737 deadliest incursions from the North since the early Cold War. It has urged the U.N. Security Council to take action.</

6739 Singapore said on Monday it would allow at least one, and possibly two, new operators to compete head on with domestic telephone monopoly Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel).Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said a two-stage tender process would decide who would be allowed to compete against SingTel on basic telecommunications services,
6739 including local and international phone calls, from 1 April, 2000.Licences would include services for voice telephony, leased circuits, public switched message and data services, he said.Mah said preference would be given to tenderers willing to invest extensively and establish their own telecommunication infrastructure networks. Foreign companies would be allowed up
6739 to 49 percent equity participation in the new networks, he said.Industry analysts said the tender was likely to attract interest from companies around the globe anxious to get into the fast-growing telecommunications markets of Southeast Asia.British Telecommunications PLC (BT), believed by analysts to be strongly interested in investing in the

6760 coupon of 8.75 percent and were priced at 95.481 to yield 9.25 percent. 6760 above the minimum US$200 million stipulated in the exchange offer.Arranger J.P. 6760 demand because the pricing, while attractive if the Philippines redeemed the notes at the seven-year call, may not have been generous enough for 15 years.The FRNs were to pay a minimum of 175 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.More likely, however, is that investors preferred the fixed-rate bonds
6760 because they are more easily traded in the secondary market than floating paper, a syndicate manager said.The maximum aggregate amount of the fixed rate bonds to be issued is US$690 million.Dealers said the 20-year bonds were priced tightly versus outstanding Philippine paper and compared with the issues of similarly rated
6760 sovereigns. But there were good reasons to take the new bonds, they said."Part of the reason why the deal was attractive was the feeling that if you kept the Bradies, you wouldn't be able to participate in the credit improvement in the Philippines," a Hong Kong banker explained.Sources also pointed
6760 out that some banks holding onto the Brady paper are receiving a coupon lower than their funding costs, so the yield pick-up on the new bonds is attractive if not incredibly generous.The Philippine par bond due December 2017 pays a coupon of 6.25 percent. The stripped yield on the par
6760 bond is close to the 225 basis points offered on the new bond, bankers noted.Traders said the 20-year deal extends the yield curve for Philippine paper, but not everyone is sure the new bond creates a new benchmark for the country."It's an unusual maturity, and how much of a benchmark

6778 The Taiwan government's decision to raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stock shares will give the market a psychological boost but longer-term benefits may be limited, analysts said on Monday.The central bank and finance ministry announced on Monday they had agreed to raise the ceiling on foreign-held stock
6778 equity to 25 percent of total market value by the end of 1996, up from 20 percent.The two agencies, in a joint statement, also adjusted the ceiling on holdings by any single foreign investor in any one listed stock to 10 percent from 7.5 percent.Analysts said the liberalisation measures could
6778 pull the local stock index out of its doldrums temporarily, but said it would not be enough to trigger a bull run."Any news of market liberalisation is good news to investors and the market probably will react immediately," said Joe Chiou, senior analyst at Taiwan Securities Investment."However, the change is
6778 really not that big and it is not effective until the end of the year," Chiou added.Michael Hung, senior analyst for Nikko Securities, predicted Taiwan's index might see a 50-point gain on Tuesday before hitting a strong barrier at 6,500. The index lost 36.11 points on Monday to close at
6778 6,453.98."Foreign ownership in the market right now is a little less than five percent, so the rise from 20 percent to 25 percent is not going to make of a difference beyond the psychological level," Hung said.Analysts said the rise in the investment ceiling for a single foreign investor was
6778 the more significant of the two relaxations, as it may prompt major foreign investors to pour more funds into blue-chip shares."It is unlikely that overall foreign investment would ever test the 25 percent limit, but big investors like Morgan Stanley may increase weightings of certain blue-chip stocks now that the
6778 7.5 percent limit has been raised," Chiou said.Major shares in the market, especially those in the heavily weighted financial and electronic sectors, have attracted strong foreign buying since Morgan Stanley began including Taiwan in its global emerging market stock indices on September 2.Most of the 78 stocks listed by Morgan
6778 Stanley are considered blue chips, or large-capital shares with a leading performance in Taiwan's various industries.Taiwan has said it would seek to raise the foreign investment ceiling to 50 percent in June 1997 and then fully scrap the limit in December 1997.The government says it wants to turn the island
6778 into a regional financial centre like Hong Kong or Singapore by liberalising its economy to attract foreign investment and corporations' regional operation hubs.</

6784 The impending resignation of Thai Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa is unlikely to revive the country's slowing economy anytime soon, economic analysts said on Monday.Whoever succeeds Banharn will have a tough time restoring business confidence after his ruling coalition was blamed for depressing investor sentiment and triggering a bearish mood on
6784 the bourse this year, they said.Banharn was accused by the opposition of condoning corruption and economic mismanagement which it charged had sparked the Thai economy's slowest projected growth in a decade.Private economists expect the Thai gross domestic product to expand only 6.2 percent this year against 8.6 in 1995.The front-runner
6784 for Banharn's job, Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, was likely to give his ally Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan a full mandate to tackle economic problems, economists said,However, Banharn has not named a successor after his announcement on Saturday that he would quit in seven days, and his main Chart Thai
6784 Party, which controls 91 seats in the 391-seat House of Representatives, has not agreed to back Chavalit as premier.Even if Chavalit wins the premiership, analysts said intense political horse trading among the six ruling coalition partners would impede efforts to form a respectable economic team by including non-elected economists in
6784 his cabinet."A Chavalit-led government with Amnuay taking charge of the economy could not solve all problems. We need to see first who joins his economic team," said Sa-ngad Sathapatpattana of Baring Research.Sa-ngad said Chavalit, whose New Aspiration Party was the second largest in Banharn's coalition, would need to accommodate Chart
6784 Thai's political interests in return for its future backing of national budgets and major economic policies."New economic measures would not be clear cut as long as the prime minister's party is not the biggest in parliament. We are basically looking at the same old team that has run the country,"
6784 Sa-ngad said.Unelected Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda told reporters on Monday that he expected to be replaced in any new cabinet and would not make major policy decisions for the time being.Analysts said this reflected the economic disarray the government was in.Most analysts gave poor ratings to Banharn's two finance ministers,
6784 Bodi and Surakiart Sathirathai, citing their limited finance expertise and saying they had failed to display full commitments to tackling inflation and current account deficit."The pressing issue for the new prime minister is to handle serious economic problems. I don't think the business community would see a fresh economic direction
6784 as long as Chavalit still needs to share cabinet seats according to party quotas," said analyst Somyos Chaemchoi of the Thai Farmers Research Centre.Chainarong Intharameesap, chairman of business consultancy CSN and Associates Ltd, did not expect a Chavalit economic team would be more effective than its predecessor."We are trapped in
6784 the vicious circle under the quota system. Bringing in a few experts as window dressing is not going to change things," Chainarong said.</

6801 Buddhist temples in Lhasa, a temple spokesman said by telephone.The project was to repair damage caused by Red Guards to the buildings and the destruction of many of its relics during Mao Zedong's Cultural Revolution, the temple official said.China's Xinhua news agency said the central government had set aside more

6810 banned mainland Chinese from buying new foreign currency B shares.The two exchanges said that local investors must not buy any new B shares with immediate effect. They can sell B shares they hold and enjoy the rights of B share investors until they do. The exchanges did not set a
6810 deadline."The background to this is that not long ago, Shenzhen domestic investors poured money into the B share market there, and foreign funds took advantage of the situation to take profit and get out," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage."This goes completely against the original reason why the B
6810 share market was set up in the first place, and has resulted in a big outflow of foreign exchange," he added.China set up the B share market in 1992 with the aim of allowing Chinese firms to raise money from overseas investors to fund their development.The B share market in
6810 Shanghai closed slightly down on Monday but the Shenzhen B share index rose sharply despite the crackdown, with brokers saying the news had been completely digested ahead of the announcement on the basis of rumours.Shanghai's B index closed down 0.58 percent at 40.059 points and its Shenzhen counterpart rose 2.24
6810 percent to 89.32 points.A Shanghai exchange offical said that investors with existing accounts must from now on prove their overseas nationality before they can buy new B shares."The new measure will be strictly implemented," he added.A broker from Guotai Securities said trading in B shares by domestic investors over the
6810 past few months had made the foreign exchange market more confused."It has put pressure on the renminbi (Chinese yuan), especially in Shenzhen against the Hong Kong dollar," he said. 6810 mid-1997)."Brokers said the outlook for China's B share markets in the wake of the announcement was pessimistic, but added there was little risk of a wholesale sell-off because domestic investors couldn't buy and foreigners generally wanted out rather than in."Who are they going to sell to?" said Alex Conroy of
6810 ING Barings in Shanghai. "I don't see a lot of foreigners lining up to buy."Domestic investors already holding B shares were also unlikely to want to sell at the current low levels, analysts said.But the move has hurt market sentiment, and prices were expected to move lower in the near
6810 future, they added."The ban is a new blow to the B share markets, which have already been in depression for the past two years," said one stock analyst.Other brokers said major domestic institutions such as Guotai and Shenyin &amp; Wanguo Securities, which have been given special approval by the State

6812 The consumer price inflation rate in Hong Kong fell to 4.9 percent in August, its lowest level in nine years, the government said on Monday.Consumer Price Index (A), the territory's most widely used inflation measure, fell sharply from the 6.1 percent increase recorded in July."This is the lowest inflation rate
6812 recorded since July, 1987," the government said.Inflation fell across the board and was reflected in a decline in all three of the main indices, CPI(A), CPI(B) and the Hang Seng CPI. The composite CPI also fell, to 5.4 percent in August from 6.2 percent in July."Looking forward, this is a
6812 plus. Hong Kong is getting its costs under control," said Andrea Cheng, economist with Lehman Brothers in Hong Kong.Comparisons with the inflation rate at this time last year are unavailable following a rebasing of consumer price indices earlier this year.Food and housing costs showed the sharpest decline, although price increases
6812 in durable goods, meals bought away from home and miscellaneous goods also fell.Economists said the figures confirm that an economic recovery is in the wind, but warned its pace will be slow."A slow rate of inflation is a reminder that it will be a slow recovery," Cheng said. "You have
6812 to remember that inflation is a lagging indicator and this is more a reflection of a weak economy in the second half of 1995 and the first half of 1996."Eddie Wong at HG Asia said housing costs will continue to depress the inflation rate for the next six to 12
6812 months because of a peculiar Hong Kong feature called rental reversion.Housing costs, typically a major component of most Hong Kong people's pay packets, lag economic conditions by up to two years because that is the usual term of most rental agreements."The economy is picking up quite rapidly but housing costs
6812 are lagging because of rental reversion," Wong said.This feature is partly responsible for a subdued or declining rate of inflation during economic recovery in Hong Kong, Wong said."We expect inflation to remain under control even through next year," he said.-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441</

6845 dark, somewhat exotic looks, cast her in 1936 as "The Jungle Princess."Lamour won praise for her acting, but she made the biggest splash for how well she wore a sarong. She later confided to an interviewer that she was mortified when she was first asked to wear one."I had to
6845 bite my lip to keep from crying," she said. "I'd been embarrassed to wear a bathing suit in the Miss New Orleans contest, and now Paramount Pictures wanted millions of people to see me in a little strip of cloth. I'd throw a robe over my sarong on the set."Lamour's
6845 first big movie year, 1937, was mainly spent in supporting roles to other stars, but she also returned to the jungle in "The Hurricane," with John Hall, an early special effects extravaganza. In 1940 she played a gangster's girlfriend in "Johnny Apollo" and appeared in "The Road to Singapore," the
6845 first musical comedy with Hope and Crosby.It was as the foil to Hope and Crosby in the "Road" movies -- films that combined adventure, slapstick and zany humour -- that Lamour shone. Some of her other movies with them included "Road to Morocco" (1942), "They Got Me Covered (1943)," "Road
6845 to Utopia" (1946), and "Road to Rio (1947)."It was in "Road to Rio" that Hope took one look at Lamour's tight-fitting sarong and quipped: "How did you get into that dress -- with a spray gun?"Of Hope and Crosby, Lamour would later say, "Mostly they would ad lib, playing with
6845 the lines I'd worked so hard to memorise."In 1953 Paramount reunited her with Hope and Crosby in the successful "Road to Bali." She then announced her retirement to raise her two sons by advertising executive William Ross Howard III, who died in 1978 after 35 years of marriage.Lamour's husband William
6845 R. Howard died in 1978 after the couple had been married for 35 years. She is survived by their two sons, Tom and Ridgely, as well as stepson William R. Howard IV.</

6847 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe Federal Reserve will consider Tuesday whether to raise interest rates for the first time in 1-1/2 years at a meeting analysts called fraught with political and economic risks for the central bank.A slim majority of international economic experts surveyed by Reuters on Monday said they
6847 expected the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to decide to bump up short-term rates by a quarter percentage point.Arguing for a rate rise: tight labor markets, rising wages and an economy that is operating in an "inflationary danger zone" because it may have overshot its potential.Arguing against:
6847 slowing growth, quiescent inflation and looming presidential and Congressional elections on Nov. 5."We expect the Federal Reserve to increase the federal funds rate by 25 basis points (one-quarter percentage point)," said Richard Berner, chief economist at Pittsburgh-based Mellon Bank. "But the case for tightening isn't open and shut."The federal funds
6847 rate is the rate that commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans. It, along with the discount rate that the Fed charges on its loans to commercial banks, serves as a benchmark for other interest rates throughout the economy.The central bank has not changed either rate since January 31,
6847 when it cut them both by a quarter percentage point. The funds rate is 5-1/4 percent; the discount rate, 5 percent.A rate rise now -- even a small one -- would mark a reversal of Fed policy and would lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and corporations.It would not
6847 be welcome on Wall Street or at the White House. U.S. stock prices jumped to another record on Monday, and a rate rise could dampen investor enthusiasm.And President Bill Clinton is counting on the maintenance of a trouble-free economy before the Nov. 5 election to help him win another four-year
6847 term.In a sign of what is at stake politically, 78 members of Congress Monday urged the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged. All but two of the lawmakers are Democrats.In a letter to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, the group, which includes House Democratic Leader Dick Gephardt from Missouri, saw a
6847 lack of inflationary pressures and argued that a rate rise would hurt, not help, the economy."Our concern is that an increase in the interest rates will slow the economy and drag down wages and the standard of living for middle and working class families," Rep. Maurice Hinchey, a Democrat from
6847 New York, said.Also weighing in on Monday against a rate increase was the National Association of Manufacturers. "In the current economic climate, low unemployment has not translated into more inflationary pressure," the group said.The Fed itself seems split over what to do. A senior central bank official told Reuters last
6847 week that eight of the Fed's 12 regional banks had requested an increase in the discount rate, with three calling for a half point rise."It's a good bet there will be a pretty rigorous discussion around the table," said Chris Varvares, an economist for St. Louis-based Macroeconomic Advisers.</
