6850 The Federal Reserve, set on achieving long-term price stability, is close to adopting a monetary policy that would attempt to keep the government's measure of consumer price inflation within a specific target range, according to a Fed source.The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the policy, which relies
6850 on a measure of the Consumer Price Index, has been "informally adopted within the Fed."Under the policy, the Fed considers a rate of inflation of between zero and 2 percent as measured by the core rate of the CPI to be non-inflationary.The core rate of the CPI, which is prepared
6850 and released monthly by the Labour Department, excludes food and energy prices, which can cause wide fluctations in the index because of their volatility.If such a policy were adopted, it would mark the first time that the Fed was using a specific measure as a guide in setting interest rates.The
6850 Fed controls the discount rate, which is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks, and sets a target for the federal funds rate, which is the rate at which banks lend money to each other when they balance their accounts at the end of each
6850 business day.Those rates in turn determine the rates at which banks and other institutions lend money to businesses and consumers.The Fed's policy making arm, the Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet Tuesday for its latest deliberations on interest rates, and speculation about what the panel might do has
6850 led to sporadic volatility in the stock and bond markets in recent weeks.Many economists expect the Fed to raise the discount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.0 percent and to raise its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 5.50 percent.Eight of the 12 regional Fed
6850 district banks have asked the Fed to make such an increase in the federal funds rate as a means of warding off inflation.The core rate of CPI rose 2.6 percent in the 12 months ended in August, a rate that would encourage the Fed to raise interest rates under the
6850 policy described by the Fed source.When the Fed last moved on interest rates -- it cut the federal funds and discount rates by a quarter point on Jan. 31 -- it did so without dissent and with six Fed banks requesting a cut in the largely symbolic discount rate.One reason
6850 for targeting CPI is the loss of usefulness of policy references such as the monetary aggregates.Cleveland Fed President Jerry Jordan, a voting member of the FOMC, commented on the notion of a numerical target as a guideline for monetary policy as early as 1992.The Fed's current view on targeting core
6850 CPI is in line with a CPI range first spelled out by New York Fed President William McDonough in a March 21 speech.McDonough defined U.S. price stability as being in a range between 0.5 percent and 2.0 percent on CPI to allow for the upward bias believed to exist in
6850 the imperfect -- but most publicised -- measure of U.S. inflation.According to another source, New York Fed Director of Research Frederic Mishkin and Head of the Markets Group Peter Fisher contributed to formulating that range.The notion has since received the support of long-time FOMC members such as San Francisco Fed
6850 President Robert Parry.A New York Fed spokesman said the bank had no comment on the notion of a numerical target for monetary policy or the impact of McDonough's views within the Fed.The Fed is considering targeting core CPI regardless of the fate of legislation sponsored by Sen. Connie Mack, R-Fla.,
6850 that would establish price stability as the Fed's main goal and require the central bank to use a numerical target toward that goal.The Fed's existing dual mandate is to seek both full employment and price stability.The FOMC discussed Mack's bill at its Sept. 26, 1995, meeting, noting members' "initial reaction
6850 was favourable in regard to the overall thrust of the bill...(that) would restructure the monetary policy requirements to permit the Congress to carry out its oversight responsibilities more effectively."The CPI is a key issue on more than one account.A low CPI would not only help drive U.S. long-term market rates
6850 lower along with declining inflation expectations, it would also reduce government spending on a number of inflation-indexed outlays.</
6851 Ultramar Corp., seeking to expand its oil refining and marketing operations into the Southwest, said on Monday it will merge with Diamond Shamrock Inc. in a stock deal worth about $975 million.Ultramar said it will eliminate about 200 jobs, or about 1.2 percent of the combined company's workforce, as part
6851 of savings that are expected to total at least $75 million annually by 1998.The new company, to be called Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp., will have revenues of more than $8 billion and be headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, where Shamrock is now based, the companies said in a joint statement.Pete
6851 Smith, who will become the new company's chief financial officer, said the combination was expected to add about 7 percent to 8 percent to earnings immediately.Ultramar, based in Greenwich, Conn., is one of the largest home heating oil companies in North America, primarily in the northeastern United States and eastern
6851 Canada. It also markets gasoline through 360 locations in California.Diamond Shamrock is a leading refiner and marketer of petroleum products in the Southwest, including the largest-selling gasoline brand in Texas and the second largest in Colorado and New Mexico. It also takes in about $1 billion annually from convenience store
6851 merchandise.The company also produces petrochemical feedstocks and operates the world's largest commercial natural gas liquids storage facility, serving the Texas Gulf Coast area.Under the deal, Diamond Shamrock stockholders will get 1.02 shares of Ultramar for each Shamrock share they own.After the announcement, Diamond Shamrock's stock rose 37.5 cents to $30.625
6851 on the New York Stock Exchange, where Ultramar gained $1.375 to $29.875.Based on Ultramar's closing stock price, the deal would value Shamrock's 32 million shares at about $30.47 each and the whole deal would be worth about $975 million.Diamond Shamrock Chairman, Chief Executive and President Roger Hemminghaus will become chairman
6851 and chief executive of the combined company.Jean Gaulin, chairman, chief executive and president of Ultramar, will become the new company's vice chairman, president and chief operating officer.Gaulin will become Ultramar Diamond Shamrock's chief executive by the end of 1998 and will become chairman within three years thereafter, the companies said.Gaulin
6851 said the company will now delay Ultramar's plans for building service stations in California and eastern Canada. The company had planned to spend about $50 million on new stations over three years. He said most of the delays will be in California.Gaulin also said Ultramar was going ahead with plans
6851 to build about 600 convenience stores in Canada, noting that about 100 are in place.Both chief executives said the merger grew out of the companies' exchange of information over the past few years under a technology exchange agreement. This was possible because of the lack of direct competition between the
6851 two companies, they explained.The companies said the deal was expected to result in total charges of about $67 million which will be taken this year.The boards of both companies have approved the merger, which is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. The deal is expected to close at the end
6851 of this year, they said.The companies said the merged company expects to pay an annual dividend of $1.10 per share, Ultramar's current payout.The merger agreement also includes a $45 million backout fee to be paid by either company pulling out of the deal, they said.</
6852 The FBI has agreed to work with the Federal Reserve in investigating a leak of sensitive information about internal Fed recommendations for higher interest rates, Justice Department officials said Monday.They said the Fed last week asked the Justice Department for FBI assistance in the inquiry being conducted under the direction
6852 of Fed Inspector General Brent Bowen and the request had been approved."The FBI has agreed to work with the Fed to find out what happened," one official said, adding that the inquiry would try to determine the source of the leak and whether any laws or confidentiality regulations had been
6852 violated.The inquiry stemmed from a Reuters report on Sept. 17 disclosing that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested an increase in the discount rate amid mounting evidence the pace of economic expansion is likely to remain brisk in the second half of 1996.The
6852 story, written by New York-based reporter Isabelle Clary, quoted an unnamed senior Fed official. It caused bond prices to fall sharply and long-term interest rates to jump.The disclosure came ahead of the scheduled Sept. 24 meeting of the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to consider interest rate policy.Senate Banking Committee
6852 Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, wrote to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan asking for an accounting of the incident."As I know you are aware, the premature disclosure of such sensitive interest rate information can add to fluctuations in financial markets, moving rates when no immediate change was intended," D'Amato
6852 said in a copy of the letter dated Sept. 23 and released to the media."I know that you agree that these types of disclosures cannot be tolerated if we want to maintain the Federal Reserve's ability to effectively implement monetary policy," D'Amato said.Fed spokesman Joseph Coyne declined comment on the
6852 reported probe, which was disclosed Monday by the Washington Post and the New York Times. "We have nothing to say," he said. Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg also declined comment.A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Washington said, "We anticipate that if the investigation produces any evidence of criminal
6852 wrongdoing the U.S. Attorney's Office will become involved."Another official said Justice Department prosecutors would await any evidence from the FBI and the inquiry before considering further what laws might have been violated. "It is very much up in the air," the official said. "The question is what law has been
6852 broken. They don't know."A Reuters spokesman said the company had not been contacted by the FBI.</
6853 The U.S. State Department on Monday hailed the arrest of 11 Colombian Air Force personnel in connection with the discovery of heroin stashed on President Ernesto Samper's official jet, and said it did not intend to take any action in the matter."Our understanding is that Colombian law enforcement officials are
6853 taking the right kinds of steps to deal with this criminal act," deputy spokesman Glynn Davies told reporters."I don't think that there's any action that we (the United States) need to take since the Colombians seem to be pursuing this vigorously and well, and they've, as I say, made some
6853 arrests, so that's a good sign," he added.As Samper left for New York on Saturday to address the U.N. General Assembly, he was caught in a new drug scandal over heroin found stashed on his presidential jet.The embarrassing discovery on board the presidential Boeing 707 was made at the Catam
6853 military air base near Bogota during an inspection prompted by an anonymous telephone caller.Police and military officials said 7.4 pounds (3.4 kg) of heroin were found hidden in 14 small packets stashed in the nose and tail section of the aircraft at the air base where the jet was being
6853 readied for the flight to New York.The plane is owned and operated by the Colombian Air Force, and National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano has said air force personnel were among prime suspects.Military and judicial officials said on Sunday that an air force colonel, a major, several captains and
6853 a sergeant were among the 11 people who had been arrested for questioning in the scandal.The 11 were all involved in a test flight of the 707 on Friday in which it flew from Bogota to the southwest city of Cali and then on to the northwest city of Medellin
6853 before returning to Catam.Davies asserted the detention of suspects shows that it is a lie that "somehow forces outside of Colombia were responsible for planting these drugs."That "clearly is not the case, because some people have already been picked up in Colombia and their investigation's proceeding," he said.Samper, in a
6853 speech to the General Assembly on Monday, cast his nation as that of a victim and proposed setting up a "grand alliance" to fight the scourge of drugs."Colombia wants to be part of the solution," Samper said. "We do not want to continue to be demonized when, in fact, we
6853 are all victims."The U.S. State Department spokesman said Washington was glad the heroin was discovered before the plane landed in New York. "We're glad the drugs were found before they hit the streets in the United States and added to the drug problem here in this country," he said.While the
6853 arrests are good news, many questions remain, including why the drugs were hidden in the plane and whether the aim was to make a profit or a political point, he said.Samper, who has defied repeated calls for his resignation because of charges his 1994 election campaign was partly financed by
6853 the Cali drug cartel, told reporters before his departure from Colombia that the latest incident was the work of someone seeking to hurt him.Samper's U.S. visa was revoked in July because of his alleged ties to drug traffickers and as a sign of Washington's displeasure over a move by Colombia's
6853 Congress to clear him of drug corruption charges a month earlier. The travel restriction does not apply to heads of state visiting the U.N. headquarters.</

6861 The public highlight of President Bill Clinton's United Nations visit on Tuesday will be a speech applauding a nuclear test ban treaty, but most U.N.-watchers will focus on an intriguing political sub-plot.That is Clinton's crusade to dump Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali as secretary-general of the world organisation, and how the two
6861 handle personal encounters when the president visits U.N. headquarters in New York City to promote the prospective, sweeping test ban accord.Washington's commitment to ousting Boutros-Ghali is driven by widespread suspicion among Americans that the United Nations is an expensive bureaucracy that has stumbled badly in global hotspots like Somalia and
6861 Bosnia.There are sure to be smiles aplenty when Clinton and Boutros-Ghali meet, but White House officials warn against taking polite outward appearances at face value."The president has made an irrevocable decision on the need to find a new secretary-general who can more actively spearhead the reform process in the U.N.
6861 There is no backing off on that. It's a done deal," one official said.Asked at a White House ceremony if this would make for an awkward situation, Clinton said it would not. "Our position on the future of the U.N. and the secretary-general, a man for whom I have great
6861 personal respect, has been clear for many months now. So nothing's changed there. That's not new," he said.White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the administration is consulting with other nations on a replacement for Boutos-Ghali, and has no firm candidate at present.Clinton, in the midst of a soaring re-election campaign
6861 in which U.S. membership in the United Nations has not surfaced as much of an issue, will address the U.N. general assembly after signing the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty.Approved by the general assembly two weeks ago by a vote of 158-3, with India, Libya and tiny Bhutan opposed, the treaty
6861 bans nuclear explosions in the atmosphere, underground or anywhere else."The treaty fulfils a dream first espoused by President Dwight Eisenhower and given life by President John Kennedy, with the limited test ban treaty," a White House official said. "President Clinton will emphasise that it moves us significantly away from the
6861 nuclear precipice."The agreement must be ratified by 44 nations with nuclear power capability before it enters into force but the consent of eight countries is crucial.They are the five acknowledged nuclear powers -- the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China -- and three so-called threshold states believed capable of
6861 developing nuclear weapons quickly: India, Pakistan and Israel.According to a senior Clinton administration official, none of the eight countries will allow the treaty to enter into force until the other seven are ready to ratify it.India, which exploded a bomb in 1974, vows to block it from taking force. It
6861 maintains the treaty is flawed because it does not commit the nuclear powers to eventually destroy their arsenals, and in fact lets them develop more sophisticated means of testing without explosions.New Delhi is also worried about China's nuclear capability and that of its neighbour and regional power rival Pakistan, which
6861 the United States said has received nuclear weapons-making equipment from China.Clinton, who will campaign in New Jersey later on Tuesday, intends to stress the positive in his speech, officials said.In a campaign speech in California the day after the treaty was approved, he said conclusion of the pact showed that
6861 "we are making this a safer world."Clinton plans one key meeting on the fringes of his U.N. visit, a brief get-together with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto at the U.S. mission in New York. The two last met at the G7 summit in France in June."This meeting will be brief,
6861 but the leaders will touch on a range of issues we deal with together, including trade and security relations," a U.S. official said.</

6865 The Dow industrials roared back from a 53-point deficit to snare a new record, boosted by a large afternoon buy program and a turnaround in bonds, but volume was sleepy ahead of the Fed's policy meeting Tuesday."We're just seeing statistical noise in anticipation of the Fed meeting tomorrow. There were
6865 some nervous Nellies selling stock at the open and then this afternoon we had bargain-hunters," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon and Farrell. The Dow rose six to about 5895, topping last Monday's 5889.20. The broader market remained weak, with the S&amp;P 500 off fractionally to
6865 about 686. The Nasdaq Composite lost eight to about 1211. Losers outpaced gainers 7-4 on NYSE volume of about 295 million shares, the slowest so far this month. Volume was also thinned by the Yom Kippur holiday.The long bond erased earlier modest losses and rose 10/32 to yield 7.02 percent
6865 after an unidentified Federal Reserve source reassured Wall Street that the Fed remains vigilant in its inflation fight. The source told Reuters the Fed views a zero to two percent range on core Consumer Price Index as price stability. Largely due to the aggressive 1994 preemptive tightening cycle, the Fed
6865 has brought core CPI down from around 4.9 percent in 1991 -- when the expansion kicked off in the second quarter -- to 2.6 percent in the sixth year of the current cycle. Targetting core CPI as a guidline for monetary policy has been "informally adopted within the Fed," the
6865 Fed source said.Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst, said the Dow returned to record territory "as bonds came back...the Reuter story that the Fed is targetting core CPI as a guide for monetary policy and a big buy program." Biriniyi Associates said it tracked one large afternoon buy program
6865 that added 30 Dow points and then a smaller one that added 3.7 points."But today is one of those days you write off as the blank space before the news. Everyone is watching for tomorrow," Crane said.A slim majority on Wall Steet expect a modest 25 basis point tightening, according
6865 to a recent Reuter survey."If there's no change, the initial reaction for stocks will be positive, but I wouldn't be surprised to see bonds reverse course," Crane said. "A modest tightening would have stocks give up a bit in the short-run and bonds would probably move a little lower initially
6865 and then rally," he added.Few on Wall Street see a 50 basis point tightening, but expect stocks to be roiled on such an aggressive Fed move.Among special situations, Missimo, the apparel designer that went public in February, tumbled 6-7/8 to 34-1/8. It warned that third-quarter earnings would fall far short
6865 of Street expectations after unusually high production costs that hurt gross margins for men's and women's autumn sportswear collections. Merrill Lynch downgraded the stock. Templeton Russia Fund lost 1-1/4 to 21-1/2. Russian President Boris Yeltsin's doctors have recommended delaying heart surgery for Yeltsin for two months to let him build
6865 up more strength before the operation.Lehman Brothers rose 1/8 to 22-7/8 after hitting an intraday high of 24-1/4. Lehman, whose shares rose Friday amid takeover speculation, said it knew of no business reason to account for the unusual acitivity in its shares and declined to confirm or deny if it
6865 was a possible takeover candidate.Alcoa lost 1-7/8 to 58-5/8 and Alumax fell 5/8 to 32-1/2. Goldman cut the stocks to market perform from outperform.Exide Electronics rose 3-1/2 to 12-5/8 after news it won an Air Force contract with a potential value of $625 million to provide and service power supply
6865 systems.Diamond Shamrock rose 3/8 to 30-5/8 and Ultramar Corp added 1-3/8 to 29-7/8 after the companies agreed to a merger of equals in which each share of Diamond Shamrock will be converted into 1.02 shares of Ultramar.Spine Tech rose 1-5/8 to 25-3/8 after the FDA approved its BAK Interbody Fusion

6871 Reform Party presidential nominee Ross Perot filed suit on Monday to force his way into campaign debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican nominee Bob Dole.Lawyers for Perot and his running mate, economist Pat Choate, filed papers in U.S. District Court in Washington seeking an injunction to force their inclusion
6871 in presidential and vice presidential debates scheduled for next month.The lawyers said they hoped a judge would hold a hearing on their suit this week. They would argue that Perot's constitutional rights were violated when the Commission on Presidential Debates decided the Texas billionaire should not be included because he
6871 had no chance of being elected.That recommendation was effectively accepted by the Clinton and Dole camps when they agreed on final debate terms -- excluding Perot -- last weekend."Declaring the election essentially over for all candidates but two before a single debate takes place will only deepen the nation's cynicism
6871 about government," the lawsuit said.The Dole and Clinton camps agreed to hold two one-on-one televised presidential debates between their candidates on October 6 in Hartford, Connecticut, and October 16 in San Diego, California. A vice presidential debate was scheduled for October 9 in St. Petersburg, Florida.Clinton, who had originally backed
6871 Perot's demand to participate, told reporters at a White House bill-signing ceremony that Perot's exclusion was Dole's fault."We signed an agreement with the Dole campaign when it was obvious there would be no debate if Mr. Perot was involved," he said. "And I thought the American people were entitled to
6871 a debate between Senator Dole and me. So i told the people who were negotiating for me to go ahead and sign the agreement."The Perot camp has portrayed the move as an establishment effort to smother a third-party candidate who won 19 percent of the popular vote in the 1992
6871 presidential election after making a strong mark in that year's debates."We are here this morning because there is no more fundamental exercise of free speech in this country than the right to vote for the candidate of your choice," Perot campaign spokesman Russell Verney told reporters at the court.He said
6871 a Louis Harris poll found that 76 percent of voters want Perot included in the debates as he was in 1992.Perot's suit named the Federal Election Commission, which oversees campaign financing laws but has not been involved in debate preparations, as the agency that should be directed to have the
6871 Reform Party candidates included. The suit argues that the debate commission, a privately funded agency established by the two major parties in the 1980s to organise the debates, is a fraudulent entity."The Republicans and Democrats have joined to get them (the FEC) to put up a fraudulent front organisation, the
6871 Commission on Presidential Debates, to control the debates and keep third-party candidates out of the debates," Verney said.The commission recommended last week that Perot should not be invited because it felt he had no realistic chance of winning. Current opinion polls show him garnering only five or six percent backing,
6871 with Clinton solidly in the lead and Dole his only close competition.The Dole camp opposed Perot's inclusion all along because it sees him as more a threat to their candidate than Clinton.Perot has since treated Dole and the commission to the withering sarcastic tongue-lashings that are his hallmark."Now here is
6871 a guy who is supposed to be a war hero," he said of Dole, a decorated and combat-wounded veteran of World War II, in an NBC interview on Sunday. "You'd think he'd be willing to talk to another person, wouldn't you?"Perot argues that the debate commission -- which did invite
6871 him into the 1992 presidential campaign debates, where he aimed most of his fire at Clinton's rival, then-President George Bush -- does the bidding of the two major parties,</
6872 Bausch &amp; Lomb Inc. said on Monday it has completed the sale of its Oral Care Division to Conair, a maker of personal care appliances, health and beauty products, kitchen appliances and telephones.Bausch &amp; Lomb did not disclose the sale price, but said it expects to take a one-time charge
6872 of $6.3 million, or 11 cents per share, in the third quarter for the sale, which is part of the company's strategy to focus on its core eye care business.The Rochester, N.Y.-based company in January announced its intention to exit the Oral Care business.The division has sold the Interplak line
6872 of power toothbrushes for plaque removal since 1988, when Bausch &amp; Lomb acquired Dental Research Corp., the creator of Interplak. The division accounts for less than 3 percent of Bausch &amp; Lomb's total revenues.Conair, a privately held company based in East Windsor, N.J., makes Cuisinart food processors, Jheri Redding shampoos
6872 and conditioners, Conair hairdryers and curling irons, and the Southwestern Bell Freedom Phone.Bausch &amp; Lomb's stock fell 12.5 cents to $37 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.</
6873 Turkey and the United States agreed on Monday to try to curb Baghdad's role in northern Iraq and said Turkey's foreign minister had been wrongly quoted as suggesting Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein should have a free hand there.U.S. officials said the strategy now being developed by Washington and Ankara was
6873 to have the Kurds and the Turkmen minority take control of security in the Western-protected area, filling the void left by Iraq's intervention there.Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller denied that Ankara would be ready to cancel a security zone it declared this month in northern Iraq if the Iraqi president

6877 senior Kennedy said in a statement. "I know that Jack and Jackie would be very proud of them and full of love for them as they began their future together."He referred to President John F. Kennedy, assassinated in 1963, and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, the society beauty whose every move and
6877 outfit were chronicled by the world's media until her death in 1994.Fascination with the family is such that an auction of their possessions -- from golf clubs to costume jewelry -- in New York earlier this year brought unprecedented prices and attention.So the marriage of John Jr., remembered by many
6877 as the toddler who saluted his assassinated father's coffin and was once proclaimed "the sexiest man alive" by People magazine, took on added significance.The details were traditional: the bride, until recently an executive at Calvin Klein Industries, wore a long dress of pearl-coloured, bias-cut silk crepe, a veil of silk
6877 tulle and crystal-beaded silk satin sandals.The groom wore a single-breasted midnight blue wool suit with a white pique vest and pale blue silk tie.Caroline Kennedy Schlossberg, the groom's sister, was the matron of honour, with her daughters Rose and Tatiana serving as flower girls and her son Jack as ring

6888 A provision contained in the mininum wage bill signed into law last month by President Bill Clinton is causing a mini land rush by first-time farmers wanting lower-cost, federally tax-exempt loans to purchase farmland.The federal tax law change allowed for the first time the use of tax-free loans to finance
6888 farmland purchases between family members. It also doubled the amount a farmland an individual can own and still be eligible for the loans.Wayne Nelson, president of Communicating for Agriculture, a rural advocacy group that lobbied for the changes, said applications for the loans have increased in some of the 14
6888 states that operate beginning farmer loan programs. Meanwhile, other states that don't have the programs, such as Ohio and Michigan, have expressed interest in starting one, he added.David Wirth, executive director of the Illinois Farm Development Authority, which runs one of the most active tax-exempt bond loan programs in the
6888 nation, said that prior to the new law, first-time farmers could not use the loans to finance land purchases from relatives."We're getting calls every week from grandparents wanting to sell to grandchildren and couldn't use the bond program because of the related party issue," Wirth said. "Now we have another
6888 resource to help those farmers."The new law also expanded the amount of land a beginning farmer can own and still obtain a loan to 30 percent of the median farm size in the county where the land is located. Previously, the limit was 15 percent.However, the value of the land
6888 already owned by the farmer cannot exceed $125,000, according to Wirth.Under Illinois' program, the authority issues a tax-exempt agricultural bond, a subset of an industrial development bond, for a loan amount that cannot exceed $250,000, according to Wirth. The bond then is privately placed with a local bank, he added.In
6888 fact, Nelson said all loans created by beginning farmer state programs are privately placed and none are sold in the open market.The exemption from federal income tax payments on interest earned on the loans allows banks to charge lower rates. Wirth said interest rates on the tax-exempt loans average seven
6888 percent, compared to nine percent on a conventional loan.Loan proceeds can be used to purchase land and in some cases equipment, Wirth said.The amount of loans each state agency can initiate is subject to their federal private activity bond cap allocation. Wirth said his agency is restricted this year to
6888 $12 million.Steve Ferguson, executive director of Iowa Agricultural Development Authority, said the agency had been averaging 20 to 30 loan requests per month. In the wake of the bill signing, the number jumped to 225 requests, he said.The agency has already completed $19 million of tax-exempt loans this year and
6888 can go up to $24 million, which is the agency's limit under its private activity cap allocation.--Karen Pierog, 312-408-8647</

6890 a milestone in their attempt to work out which systems will be permitted under a 24-year-old arms treaty. 6890 smaller-scale "theater" systems which are not limited.Experts from the United States, Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus and Ukraine worked out a draft accord in June on lower-speed systems. 6890 as quickly as possible to complete the final agreement," Under Secretary of State Lynn Davis said.The phase one agreement specifies that all theater missile defense systems with interceptor speeds up to three km per second (1.8 miles per second) are permitted under the ABM treaty, unless they are tested against
6890 targets with speeds over five km per second (3.1 miles per second) or ranges greater than 3,500 km (2,174 miles), she told reporters.Primakov said at a joint news conference with Christopher he believed the accord would have a "positive effect" on prospects for Russia's parliament ratifying the START-2 U.S.-Russian strategic

6897 Hillary Rodham Clinton's legal billing records suggest she helped draft a sham deal under which Madison Guaranty savings and loan evaded regulations and deceived bank examiners, government banking regulators said in a report made public Monday.The supplemental report by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.'s inspector general followed a renewed investigation
6897 launched after the mysterious discovery of Mrs. Clinton's Rose Law Firm billing records at the White House last January.The records showed work done by Mrs. Clinton in the mid-1980s for Madison, which was headed by the Clintons' partners in the failed Whitewater real estate development, James and Susan McDougal.The FDIC
6897 report was made public without comment by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, and appeared to back up conclusions on the land deal made in the final report of D'Amato's Senate Whitewater Committee, which harshly criticised the first lady.The inspector general said entries in Mrs. Clinton's billing records and
6897 other evidence suggested that she and law firm partner Webster Hubbell helped facilitate payment of $300,000 in commissions to Hubbell's father-in-law Seth Ward, a "straw byer" of land owned by Madison."The method of the payment of the commissions evaded regulations designed to protect the safety and soundness of the institution
6897 and violated the integrity of its books and records," the new report said."Further, Madison Guaranty used a document drafted by Clinton to deceive federal bank examiners as to the true nature of payments to Ward."The report said that Madison apparently conceived a May 1, 1986, option agreement setting out an
6897 arrangement under which Ward was to purchase a parcel of land in a property known as Industrial Development Corp. to further the purpose of concealing from bank examiners' payments to Ward. The option was drafted by Mrs. Clinton.The report also noted that during the summer of 1988, prior to a
6897 suit by Ward against Madison, Mrs. Clinton ordered destruction of all of her files related to the IDC transaction, including a file labeled "Ward option."When the Rose Law Firm solicited legal work from the Resolution Trust Corp., the government savings and loan cleanup agency, and the FDIC, it did not
6897 disclose any information on the work done for Madison by Mrs. Clinton or Hubbell, the report said.</

6901 The Gulf Cartel drug smuggling operation moved several tonnes of cocaine a week through a safe house near the U.S.-Mexican border, police and a convicted drug trafficker said on Monday.Sitting in a citrus grove three miles (4.8 km) from the border, a modest ranch house outside Harlingen, Texas, was equipped
6901 with an underground vault and was filled with more than nine tons (eight tonnes) of cocaine when it was raided in October 1989, Dagoberto Pena, a narcotics officer with the Texas Department of Public Safety, said.Duffel bags, flour sacks and cardboard boxes stuffed with cocaine were found in the house,
6901 along with weapons, business ledgers and a confidential police report on an alleged cartel member, Pena said as testimony continued in Juan Garcia Abrego's trial on 22 counts of drug trafficking, money laundering and bribery.Garcia Abrego, a 52-year-old former cookie factory employee from Texas, allegedly headed the Gulf Cartel. Arrested
6901 last January in Monterrey, Mexico, and flown to Houston for prosecution, he faces up to life in prison and the forfeiture of hundreds of millions of dollars in illicit drug proceeds if convicted.During testimony on Monday, Alfonso Gonzalez Tristan, a labourer hired to drive and unload truckloads of cocaine and
6901 cash, said his job at the house was to "keep it clean, to help unload the money and the cocaine."Ledgers found in the raid documented shipments of about 4,000 pounds (1,800 kg) moving through the house every few days, with packages identified by the source of the cocaine and its
6901 purity.While U.S. drug agents were monitoring the smuggling operation through wiretaps and surveillance, the Gulf Cartel had ways of keeping tabs on federal investigations, Gonzalez told jurors.At one point in 1989, he said, he was told to drive to McAllen, Texas, to pick up confidential police reports supplied to the
6901 organisation by an unnamed lawyer."They paid the lawyer to provide the reports," he said through a translator. One of the confidential reports, compiled by police on suspects in criminal cases, was found inside the house when it was raided.The Gulf Cartel allegedly smuggled billions of dollars' worth of cocaine produced
6901 by Colombia's Cali cartel across the U.S.-Mexican border and was reputed to have moved up to a third of the cocaine consumed in the United States.The biggest revelation in the trial's first week was that U.S. agents, despite more than three years of continous wiretapping of the cartel's phone conversations,
6901 had no recordings of Garcia Abrego or even the mention of his name on tape. 6901 of money to buy protection and a former FBI agent testified that the drug empire was built on public corruption.News reports have linked Garcia Abrego to Raul Salinas, the brother of former President Carlos Salinas, who is in jail in Mexico City on charges he ordered the 1994 assassination of
6901 a high ruling-party official.Last week drug agents testified about the difficulties of maintaining wiretaps, because cartel insiders constantly changed phone numbers and residences as they shuffled money and cocaine between Mexico and the United States.Moving into rented homes and apartments, the drug dealers would try to blend in to their
6901 surroundings. 6901 into a mobile home in the driveway.</

6905 The government's budget deficit widened in August to $41.83 billion, a 23.6 percent increase from the $33.85 billion shortfall posted a year earlier in August 1995, the Treasury Department said Monday.Last month's deficit also was far higher than July's shortfall of $27.1 billion.One reason cited by the Treasury for the
6905 big monthly gap was that pay to military members as well as veterans' benefits and supplemental security income payments that were scheduled for Sept. 1 were accelerated to Aug. 30.Since Sept. 1 was a Sunday, the checks were mailed out on the preceding Friday to avoid delays to recipients, which
6905 had the effect of boosting government spending in August.Total spending in August was $141.83 billion, an increase from the $130.99 billion of outlays made in July and up from $130.49 billion spent in August 1995.Income, mainly from taxes, dropped in August to $99.99 billion from $103.89 billion in July but
6905 exceeded the $96.64 billion the government took in during August 1995.Despite the big deficit in August, the government remained well on its way to once more shrinking its red-ink total for the full year.During the first 11 months of fiscal 1996 that ends on Sept. 30, the budget deficit totalled
6905 $143.96 billion. That was down 16 percent from the $171.11 billion total posted in the first 11 months of fisal 1995.September typically brings a surplus in the monthly budget.As a result, the Clinton administration is forecasting the deficit for the full 1996 fiscal year will drop to $116.75 billion from
6905 fiscal 1995's deficit total of $163.87 billion.</

6907 Households could save one-third of the electricity they use for lighting if they replace their incandescent lightbulbs with compact fluorescent bulbs, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Monday.Using fluorescent lights instead of the inefficient incandescent lights could save homes almost 32 billion kilowatthours of electricity a year, EIA said.But it

6911 The Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it filed insider trading charges against the former chairman of Tyson Foods Inc. and a friend in connection with the poultry company's purchase of Arctic Alaska Fisheries Corp. in 1992.In a civil complaint filed in federal district court in Arkansas, the SEC alleged
6911 that Frederick Lee Cameron, bought Arctic Alaska shares based on a tip he received from his friend, Donald John Tyson, then chairman and majority shareholder of Tyson Foods.Springdale, Ark.-based Tyson Foods is the nation's biggest poultry processor with sales of $5.5 billion last year.Arctic Alaska is a Seattle-based seafoods processor
6911 that was traded at the New York Stock Exchange before being acquired by Tyson Foods in the $212 million deal.Simultaneously with the filing of the complaint, Tyson and Cameron agreed to settle the charges, without admitting or denying the SEC's allegations, the agency said.Pending final court approval, the defendants consented
6911 to be permanently enjoined from violating anti-fraud provisions of federal securiies laws, the SEC said.Cameron also agreed to forfeit $46,125, the alleged illegal profits, and pay interest totalling $18,153. Both Cameron and Tyson also agreed to each pay a civil penalty of $46,125, the SEC said.Tyson, 66, lived in Fayetteville,
6911 Ark., at the time. He now resides in Miami, the SEC said. In late May and early June 1992, he took a trip with Cameron, 62, and a National City, Calif., resident, to Britain.During the trip the food company official allegedly communicated with his office about the on-going negotiations with
6911 Arctic Alaska and participated at a board meeting on May 29 by phone.According to the SEC lawsuit, Cameron bought 9,000 shares of Arctic Alaska at $6.625 a share or $59,625 on June 2, 1992, after receiving information from Tyson about the pending acquisition.In doing so, Tyson violated his company's insider
6911 trading policy and breached his fiduciary duty to Arctic Alaska shareholders, the SEC contended.Cameron sold the shares on June 16, the day the deal was announced, at $11.75 a share or $105,750, making a profit of $46,125, the SEC alleged.</

6922 Some 13.7 million acres now enrolled in the Conservation Reserve would not meet at least one of the criteria for entry under new Agriculture Department rules, an analysis said Monday.The analysis by the Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute at the University of Missouri said the stricter erodibility requirements proposed
6922 n the rules would preclude at least some land from re-enrollment.USDA proposed the new rules last week. They would not take effect until after a 45-day period for comment and suggested changes. Land would be required to have an erodibility index of at least eight to be eligible in the
6922 future or meet some other standard such as being devoted to wellhead protection or a filterstrip.FAPRI said about three million acres that did not have an erodibility index of eight but were devoted to those practices.The think tank said 73 percent of the CRP land in Missouri met the erodibility
6922 index test.It listed other states as Iowa 69 percent, Texas 63 percent, Kansas and Illinois 61 percent, North Dakota 57 percent, Indiana 55 percent, South Dakota 53 percent, and Oklahoma 51 percent.States with high percentages of land meeting the erodibility test were Wyoming 98 percent, Kentucky 90 percent, Colorado 89
6922 percent, Tennessee 83 percent, Wisconsin 78 percent, Montana 77 percent and Nebraska 74 percent.Contracts on 24 million acres expire by fall 1997.FAPRI based its estimates on a sampling of CRP land.</

6931 The Canadian Auto Workers' decision on Monday to bargain next with General Motors Corp. suggests the United Auto Workers will now move on to Chrysler Corp. and save tough job security issues at GM for last.If that is the case, it could set up a fall showdown between the UAW
6931 and GM, the world's largest automaker, that some analysts fear could end up in a strike."The word I'm trying to get out to suppliers is be prepared," said Donna Parolini, whose Troy, Mich.-based International Business Development Corp. consults with auto suppliers.UAW officials have not notified Chrysler or GM which company
6931 will be the second bargaining target, representatives of both automakers said Monday. A union spokesman said a decision on which company would be next has not been made.But CAW President Buzz Hargrove said Monday he is certain UAW President Steve Yokich will not pick GM next."We have a clear understanding
6931 between myself and Mr. Yokich of the UAW that we will not do anything to interfere or harm one another in our efforts to put together a 1996 collective agreement," he said.The UAW, which represents nearly 400,000 hourly auto workers in the United States, last week reached a tentative agreement
6931 with Ford Motor Co.. The union typically gets an agreement with one of Detroit's Big Three and then applies those terms as a pattern to the remaining two.The UAW's three-year pact with all automakers expired Sept. 14. The union extended the deadline at Chrysler and GM while it negotiated at
6931 Ford. But in a break with tradition, Yokich has continued subcommittee discussions at Chrysler and GM. It is possible, analysts have said, that Yokich will continue to talk with remaining two simultaneously.Analysts said GM and the UAW will have the most trouble reaching a new labour accord because union job
6931 security concerns clash directly with the company's determined efforts to sell unprofitable parts plants and reduce headcount.That view was reinforced by the Ford-UAW deal, which guarantees the company will keep 95 percent of its UAW hourly workers through the three-year agreement, unless a severe market downturn occurs."The real reason you
6931 push GM to last is they have the most difficult issues," said Paul Ballew, chief economist in the Troy, Mich., office of industry consultant J.D. Power and Associates.An independent study by Harbour &amp; Associates released last May concluded GM needed to shed about 33,000 workers from its assembly, stamping and
6931 powertrain operations to reach the productivity levels of Ford and Chrysler.Ballew, like other industry analysts, also believes GM and the CAW could be headed for a strike. Chrysler, in a deal reached last week with CAW bargainers, promised to add jobs, increase wages and replace any job that it contracts
6931 out with a similar job at one of its Canadian plants.Analysts said there is no way GM can accept those terms. For that reason, GM executives are evaluating how to stockpile parts and best brace for a strike in Canada, Parolini of International Business Development said.GM spokesman Tom Klipstine said
6931 the automaker's assembly operations are still trying to recoup light vehicle supplies lost during the Dayton, Ohio, strike in March that crippled North American production. He said the company is not building up inventory to brace for a strike."We basically have been in a position of playing catch-up," he said.</

6949 or plane, was pulled off with a sense of privacy rarely accorded America's most famous family. "The people here are nice enough that they felt they would like to treat people as they would like to be treated," Brinko said.Life was far from normal on Monday on this exclusive island

6949 fortified by the British to prevent Spanish incursion into the coastal waters of Savannah, Georgia, and Charleston, South Carolina. 6949 at the remote north end of the island."It's very simple. I'm surprised they used it," said Zachary Kirkland, a park ranger at Cumberland Island National Seashore, which owns the church. 6951 Trash and sewage -- two municipal headaches around the world -- could become a valuable source of water and fertiliser for farmers, researchers said on Monday at a World Bank conference.The result would be more food and fewer worries about overflowing landfills, they said. It could also mean less disease
6951 if farmers had "cleaner" water supplies instead of the polluted water now used for irrigation in parts of the world."We have seen them (waste products) as a problem, not a solution," said Anders Wijkman of the U.N. Development Programme in asking that recycling be part of government planning.Only a small
6951 part of the organic waste generated in cities now is turned into compost or other products that would boost farm productivity. The World Bank estimated more than five million people die each year from diseases caused by improper garbage and sewage disposal.Along with describing beneficial uses, researchers warned that care
6951 must be taken to insure there were no plant or human health risks from recycling munincipal wastes. Wijkman, for example, said householders would have to sort their trash to keep harmful items out of organic waste headed for compost.A $520 million sewage treatment project in Santiago, Chile, was cited as
6951 an example of how to turn a pollution problem into a benefit for city dwellers and farmers. Other case studies looked at using Los Angeles sludge as a crop fertiliser and using "renovated" sewage water for industrial plants in Madras, India.For years, farmers downstream from Santiago often had no choice
6951 during the dry summer months than to use river water tainted with city sewage to irrigate fruits, vegetables and other crops. The crops then became a link in the spread of typhoid."The spillovers from pollution in the city of Santiago have come back to haunt the city," said Carl Bartone,
6951 a World Bank enviromental specialist, who outlined plans to build three wastewater treatment plants for Santiago.In Madras, industrial use of purified wastewater eased the demands for water in a city short on water supplies.Kenny Evans, who uses sewage sludge as fertiliser on an Arizona farm covering 22 square miles (5,698
6951 hectares), was among three speakers who said high standards must be set to prevent use of material containing harmful metals, plant-killing organisms or microbes that would sicken people.</

6962 The Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it filed insider trading charges against Donald John Tyson, former chairman of Tyson Foods Inc, and a friend in connection with Tyson Foods' acquisition of Arctic Alaska Fisheries Corp in 1992.In a civil complaint filed in a federal district court in Arkansas, the
6962 SEC alleged that Tyson's friend, Frederick Lee Cameron, bought Arctic Alaska shares based on a tip he received from the then chairman of the food company. According to the SEC complaint, Cameron bought 9,000 shares of Arctic Alaska at $6.625 a share or $59,625 on June 2, 1992 after receiving
6962 word from Tyson about the pending acquisition.Cameron sold the shares on June 16, the day the deal was announced at $11.75 a share, for $105,750, making a profit of $46,125, the SEC alleged. Simultaneously with the filing of the complaint, Tyson and Cameron agreed to settle the charges, without admitting
6962 or denying the SEC's allegations, the agency said.Pending final court approval, the defendants consented to be permanently enjoined from violating anti-fraud provisions of federal securities laws, the SEC said.Cameron also agreed to forfeit $46,125 -- the alleged illegal profits -- and pay interest totalling $18,153. Both Cameron and Tyson also
6962 agreed to each pay a civil penalty of $46,125, the SEC said.</

6970 The Federal Trade Commission recommended Monday that Congress tighten consumer confidentiality laws to help stop credit fraud and identity fraud.It said current law did not bar credit bureaus from releasing identifying consumer information, yet such data might facilitate identity fraud, credit fraud or other illegal activities.The agency said its proposal
6970 was a response to many consumer complaints and to inquiries by members of Congress, particularly Senator Richard Bryan, a Nevada Democrat.It said the complaints concerned commercial services that provide identifying information about individuals for a fee.The agency said that according to recent press reports, at least one tracking company currently
6970 furnished an individual's name, maiden name, aliases, prior addresses, telephone number, and birth month and year.It said the tracking service had also furnished Social Security numbers.The agency said in a letter to Bryan that fraud concerns outweighed the limited legitimate uses of this information for locating individuals.It recommended that the
6970 Fair Credit Reporting Act be amended to provide confidentiality for a person's maiden name, Social Security number, prior addresses and date of birth, so this information would be released only to those with a legal release for obtaining it.</

6986 President Clinton signed into law on Monday a $265.6 billion defence bill calling for more spending than he wanted but strengthening federal "anti-stalking" laws that he strongly supports.The law, a blueprint of U.S. military spending priorities for the year beginning Oct. 1, provides money for a three percent military pay
6986 raise and for destroying thousands of nuclear weapons from the former Soviet Union.It also calls for $11 billion more spending than Clinton had sought, including $950 million for military housing and readiness and $780 million for improved National Guard and reserve artillery and rockets.Clinton, running for re-election against Republican Bob
6986 Dole, chose to highlight the bill's domestic aspects, signing it in a White House ceremony flanked by the families of two women who were victims of stalkers.One of the women, Sharon Wiggs, was stalked and killed by her former boyfriend's brother in 1992.In a provision sponsored by two Republicans, Texas
6986 Senator Kay Bailey Hutchison and California Congressman Ed Royce, the law makes it a federal crime for a stalker to cross state lines with the intention of harassing or injuring someone. It also makes it a crime to stalk victims on federal property, including military bases and government offices."Today we
6986 say loud and clear if you stalk and harrass, the law will follow you wherever you go, and if you are the victim of stalking and want to build a new life somewhere else, you will have the full protection of federal law," Clinton said.The emphasis on anti-stalking measures fits
6986 squarely with Clinton's efforts this election year to stress issues that appeal to women, whose support for the president exceeds that by men by double-digit margins.Nationally, Clinton holds leads of around 15 percentage points over Dole in opinion polls with six weeks left before the Nov. 5 election.Although Congress sent
6986 Clinton a bill with more military spending than he wanted, it also stripped the legislation of several items to which he strenuously objected. These included provisions that would have undermined his policy of allowing gays to serve in the military and required the dismissal of military personnel with the virus
6986 that causes AIDS.Known in congressional jargon as an "authorization" bill, the legislation does not actually force the administration to spend the $11 billion it did not seek. Congress first authorises spending and then passes separate bills that "appropriate" the money for them.</

6998 Economic policymakers from the Group of Seven industrial nations will take care to avoid disrupting the tranquility of the currency market when they converge on Washington later this week.Since falling to a record low against the German mark and a post-World War II drop vs. the Japanese yen in early
6998 1995, the dollar has rebounded and enjoyed a period of unusually limited volatility.The dollar's rise followed an April 1995 call by G7 ministers for an "orderly reversal" in the greenback. With the dollar safely back near 110 yen and 1.50 marks, economists agree this orderly reversal has occurred.To the chagrin
6998 of volatility-hungry currency traders, G7 policymakers, gathering this Saturday on the fringes of the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings, will do all they can to maintain this equilibrium."I think the general view is that central banks and finance ministries are pretty comfortable with the exchange rate relationships
6998 the way they are," said Robert Hormats, vice chairman at Goldman, Sachs &amp; Co. "They will do everything they possibly can to avoid rocking the boat."Since March of this year, the dollar has traded in a relatively narrow band between 1.47 and 1.55 marks, remaining marginally above the 1.50 level
6998 in recent weeks. The dollar has traded in a 105- to 110-yen range since May and has been above the 100-yen level since October of 1995.The dollar's strength against the Japanese currency has been a source of concern to U.S. automobile manufacturers, who have voiced their displeasure as the dollar
6998 has reapproached 110 yen in recent weeks.Little sympathy is expected from U.S. officials however, who are unlikely to waver from Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's "strong dollar" mantra, regardless of whether their desired dollar reversal has already taken place.The Clinton Administration's stance toward the carmakers was demonstrated last week when Commerce
6998 Secretary Mickey Kantor indicated that recent dollar strength against the yen did not appear to be hurting car sales."If people are looking for a statement saying the orderly reversal is ended, we won't see anything like that," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics."The U.S. does not want
6998 to be sidetracked by U.S. producers' calls for a lower dollar," he added. "I think they will welcome the (dollar) move so far, say exchange rates are more in line with economic fundamentals, but not give any indication there has been an overshoot."If any one country calls for the dollar
6998 to strengthen from its current levels it will be France, economists said. In an effort to meet strict Maastricht criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) France has adopted tight fiscal measures.A stronger dollar vs. the franc would help French exports and overall economic growth, thus easing the pain of
6998 weaker government spending. Gains in the dollar against the French franc would make French exports cheaper in dollar terms."The only country that would really welcome a stronger dollar is France because it would help the French growth outlook considerably," Chris Iggo, international economist at Barclays Bank.Germany, which would also benefit
6998 from dollar strength in the runup to EMU, could echo French calls for a stronger U.S. currency, but is unlikely to push hard for such a move, economists said.In the absence of exciting currency pronouncements, economists predicted G7 policymakers will focus on ensuring continued recovery in the world economy, while
6998 touching on the success of last year's Mexican rescue plan."Certainly compared to the G7 meetings last year, things are looking quite a bit brighter," said Barclay's Iggo. "The U.S. economy continues to do well, Germany and Japan are past the worst and there is no currency instability.""It's steady as she
6998 goes. I think that will be the message," he added.</
6999 Lifting millions of rural people around the world out of poverty is a key to ensuring a secure food supply and protecting the environment, officials of the World Bank said on Monday."We are concerned that there is total inadequate interest in rural poverty around the world," Andrew Steer, director of
6999 the bank's Environment Department, said at a briefing before the bank's annual conference on the environment this week.The conference in Washington will focus on ways to improve living conditions in rural areas, which contain about 75 percent of the world's poor, and how that can help improve conditions in urban
6999 areas, restore the environment and fight poverty."It is not that the rural poor should be helped before the urban poor. The problems of both must be addressed, but the rural poor must not be forgotten in the global rush to modernization," Ismail Serageldin, the bank's vice president for Environmentally Sustainable
6999 Development, said in a statement."A thriving rural economy will generate benefits far beyond the boundaries of any local area," he said."From the beginning of the industrial age, down to the amazing advances of the East Asian countries of the 1980s, a strong rural economy has been a necessary pre-condition for
6999 strong national economic growth."More than 800 million people go hungry every day and more than 500 million children do not get enough food to fully develop physically and mentally, and most of those live in rural areas, the bank said."There is a sort of seduction going on as world food
6999 prices have tended to be fairly low, that therefore things are under control with regard to food," Steer said."Even when food supplies are fairly ample" the desperately poor in food-producing areas go hungry, he said.Effective rural development is the best means to fight hunger, increase food production and protect the
6999 environment, the bank said.Food supplies must double by 2025 to meet population growth, meaning far more will have to be produced from the same or a smaller share of land, the bank said. That raises a potential for more hunger and environmental devastation."If agriculture is not intensified, in an environmentaly
6999 appropriate fashion, then the sheer expansion of the population and its requirement will lead to the destruction of the world's forests from slash-and-burn farming of poor, small holders who barely feed their families," Serageldin said.</

7001 NEW YORK, Sept 23 - Standard &amp; Poor's Corp Monday said it lowered its rating on Columbus City School District, Ohio, $26.6 million G.O. bonds to single-A'-plus from double-A'-minus.The downgrade is due to deterioration in the district's financial position over the past three years, resulting in increased short-term borrowing to
7001 balance operations.The Columbus City School District encompasses about 67% of the city of Columbus (triple-A' G.O. rating). The city continues to enjoy strong growth through annexation of developing areas outside the school district, benefiting greatly from the expansion of the employment base through its municipal income tax. School district revenues
7001 consist mainly of property taxes (61% of total revenues) and state aid (36%). Tax base growth of the district has been flat over the past decade, averaging less than 2% a year since 1989. Ohio law precludes the district from capturing inflationary increase in tax revenue, leaving the district dependent
7001 on state aid increases in the absence of real property tax base growth.Lower state aid due to declining enrollments and slow property tax revenue growth contributed to consecutive operating deficits totaling a combined $32 million in fiscals 1994 and 1995. The general fund balance totaled a negative $17.2 million on
7001 a GAAP basis at June 30, 1995. On a cash basis, the general fund balance totaled $6.9 million (2.0% of expenditures) after various accounting adjustments. Budget cuts totaling $12.7 million and a spending reserve borrowing of $13.6 million in short term notes, representing the use of the subsequent year's tax
7001 receipts, enabled the district to balance the fiscal 1996 budget. The ending general fund balance on a cash basis at June 30, 1996, totaled $8.6 million, or 2.3% of the district's $353 million operating budget.Additional budget cuts of $28 million, including layoffs of 260 employees, and $14 million of spending
7001 reserve borrowing authority was necessary to balance the fiscal 1997 budget, which projected revenue growth of 4.2%. A 5.5 mill permanent property tax levy is on the November 1996 ballot, representing the district's first levy election since 1991. If passed, the levy is projected to generate about $36 million annually,

7002 The public highlight of President Bill Clinton's United Nations visit on Tuesday will be a speech applauding a nuclear test ban treaty, but most U.N.-watchers will focus on an intriguing political sub-plot.That is Clinton's crusade to dump Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali as secretary-general of the world organisation, and how the two
7002 handle personal encounters when the president visits U.N. headquarters in New York City to promote the prospective, sweeping test ban accord.Washington's commitment to ousting Boutros-Ghali is driven by widespread suspicion among Americans that the United Nations is an expensive bureaucracy that has stumbled badly in global hotspots like Somalia and
7002 Bosnia.There are sure to be smiles aplenty when Clinton and Boutros-Ghali meet, but White House officials warn against taking polite outward appearances at face value."The president has made an irrevocable decision on the need to find a new secretary-general who can more actively spearhead the reform process in the U.N.
7002 There is no backing off on that. It's a done deal," one official said.White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the administration is consulting with other nations on a replacement for Boutos-Ghali, and has no firm candidate at present.Clinton, in the midst of a soaring re-election campaign in which U.S. membership
7002 in the United Nations has not surfaced as much of an issue, will address the U.N. general assembly after signing the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty.Approved by the general assembly two weeks ago by a vote of 158-3, with India, Libya and tiny Bhutan opposed, the treaty bans nuclear explosions in
7002 the atmosphere, underground or anywhere else."The treaty fulfils a dream first espoused by President Dwight Eisenhower and given life by President John Kennedy, with the limited test ban treaty," a White House official said. "President Clinton will emphasise that it moves us significantly away from the nuclear precipice."The agreement must
7002 be ratified by 44 nations with nuclear power capability before it enters into force but the consent of eight countries is crucial.They are the five acknowledged nuclear powers -- the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China -- and three so-called threshold states believed capable of developing nuclear weapons quickly:
7002 India, Pakistan and Israel.According to a senior Clinton administration official, none of the eight countries will allow the treaty to enter into force until the other seven are ready to ratify it.India, which exploded a bomb in 1974, vows to block it from taking force. It maintains the treaty is
7002 flawed because it does not commit the nuclear powers to eventually destroy their arsenals, and in fact lets them develop more sophisticated means of testing without explosions.New Delhi is also worried about China's nuclear capability and that of its neighbour and regional power rival Pakistan, which the United States said
7002 has received nuclear weapons-making equipment from China.Clinton, who will campaign in New Jersey later on Tuesday, intends to stress the positive in his speech, officials said.In a campaign speech in California the day after the treaty was approved, he said conclusion of the pact showed that "we are making this
7002 a safer world."Clinton plans one key meeting on the fringes of his U.N. visit, a brief get-together with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto at the U.S. mission in New York. The two last met at the G7 summit in France in June."This meeting will be brief, but the leaders will
7002 touch on a range of issues we deal with together, including trade and security relations," a U.S. official said.</

7005 Municipalities in North Carolina and Virginia should see no credit impact from Hurricane Fran because their underlying economies are strong and they will receive substantial state and federal disaster aid, Moody's Investors Service said Monday.The hurricane swept through eastern North Carolina and southwest and central Virgina Sept 5 and 6,
7005 causing widespread damge that is expected to total in the billions of dollars.However, the rating agency said, "The approximately 100 debt ratings of municipalities in the affected states are not expected to be significantly impacted."Hardest hit were Wilmington, Wrightsville Beach, New Hanover County, Raleigh and Wake County in North Cartolina,
7005 and in Virginia, Danville and communities in the Shenandoah Valley.Moody's said its ratings in the region are mainly general obligation and essential purpose revenue bonds, and certificates of participation backed by absolute and unconditional pledges to pay debt service."Most of the affected municipalities have established economic bases, which are expected
7005 to recover in a reasonable period from the storm's short-term disruption," Moody's said. "Most communties maintain good finances and liquidity and therefore can support extraordinary expenses."The rating agency said general revenues are comprised mainly of property taxes and state aid, which should not be significantly affected by the storm."Losses from
7005 decreases to collected sales taxes and other economically sensitive revenue sources, which comprise a relatively small share of revenues, are likely to be temporary, and support for essential purpose revenue bonds also should not be materially affected," Moody's said.Additionally, the rating agency said, large portions of the two states have
7005 been declared federal disaster areas, entitling them to Federal Emergency Management Administration money.Most property damage from wind and fallen trees is expected to be covered by private insurance, while businesses and residents who were not fully insured will be able to seek federal low-interest loans.State emergency preparedness officials are already
7005 coordinating with federal officials to facilitate that funding, Moody's said.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</

It follows another lawsuit filed last year by the Minneapolis branch of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
7014 and the parents of several school children enrolled in Minneapolis public schools."The common ground between our lawsuits would be both lawsuits are seeking to hold the state responsible under the constitutuion," said John Shulman, a Minneapolis attorney representing the NAACP.In the St. Paul case, school officials claimed that the concentration
7014 of poverty in that city has put the district in a "unique financial bind" because of its inability to get funding referendums passed."In allocating resources and other assistance for schools, the state has failed to take sufficient account of the substantially greater services needed to provide adequate educational opportunities for
7014 our students," said St. Paul Public School District Board of Education chair Mary Thornton Phillips in a news release.According to a spokeswoman for the district, 64 percent of the district's $348 million annual budget comes from Minnesota. However, the lawsuit does not indicate how much more state money is needed
7014 by the school district to ensure students receive an adequate education, the spokeswoman added.A spokesman for the Minnesota Attorney General's Office said last week that the St. Paul school lawsuit was under review.Meanwhile, the NAACP's case charged that school children in Minneapolis are deprived of an adequate education because their
7014 schools are segregated and that the education offered in those schools in unequal to education provided in suburban Minneapolis school districts.Shulman said the lawsuit seeks injunctive relief in the way the school district is set up and operated in addition to state funding.He added that a Hennepin County District Court
7014 judge has ordered the plaintiffs and the state to explore the possibility of mediation. The judge has also forwarded certain questions pertaining to the case to the state supreme court in order to give the trial court guidance, Shulman said.--Karen Pierog, 312-408-8647</

7017 Reform Party presidential nominee Ross Perot filed suit on Monday seeking federal government backing for his bid to force his way into campaign debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican nominee Bob Dole.Lawyers for Perot and his running mate, economist Pat Choate, filed papers in U.S. District Court in Washington
7017 essentially asking an injunction against debates already scheduled that would exclude Perot, and demanding that he and Choate be included in any debates that are held.It was not clear when the court would proceed with the lawsuit although speculation centred on Thursday as a possible date for the hearing of
7017 arguments.The Dole and Clinton camps agreed over the weekend to hold two one-on-one televised presidential debates between their candidates on October 6 in Hartford, Connecticut, and October 16 in San Diego, California.In so doing, Clinton gave up his support of Perot's demand to be included and yielded to Dole, who
7017 opposed participation by the feisty Texas billionaire, and to the recommendation of a private bipartisan debates commission that the clash be limited to the two major party candidates.The two campaigns also agreed to hold a vice presidential debate on October 9 in St. Petersburg, Florida, but limit it to Vice
7017 President Al Gore and Republican Jack Kemp.The Perot camp cried foul, portraying the move as an establishment effort to smother a third-party candidate who won 19 percent of the popular vote in the 1992 presidential election after making a strong mark in that year's debates."We are here this morning because
7017 there is no more fundamental exercise of free speech in this country than the right to vote for the candidate of your choice," Perot campaign spokesman Russell Verney told reporters at the court.He said a Louis Harris poll found that 76 percent of voters want Perot included in the debates
7017 as he was in 1992.Perot's suit named the Federal Election Commission, which oversees campaign financing laws but has not been involved in debate preparations, as the agency that shoud be directed to have the Reform Party candidates included. It argues that the debate commission, a privately funded agency established by
7017 the two major parties to organise the debates in the 1980s, is a fraudulent entity."The Republicans and Democrats have joined to get them (the FEC) to put up a fraudulent front organisation, the Commission on Presidential Debates, to control the debates and keep third-party candidates out of the debates," Verney
7017 said.The commission recommended last week that Perot should not be invited because it felt he had no realistic chance of winning. Current opinion polls show him garnering only five or six percent backing, with Clinton solidly in the lead and Dole his only close competition.The move to exclude Perot was
7017 pressed by the Dole camp, which sees the feisty Texan as more a threat to their candidate than to Clinton. The Clinton camp yielded in return for Dole concessions on other debate terms.Perot has since treated Dole and the commission to the withering sarcastic tongue-lashings that are his hallmark."Now here
7017 is a guy who is supposed to be a war hero," he said of Dole, a decorated and combat-wounded veteran of World War II, in an NBC interview on Sunday. "You'd think he'd be willing to talk to another person, wouldn't you?"Perot argues that the debate commission -- which did
7017 invite him into the 1992 presidential campaign debates, where he aimed most of his fire at Clinton's rival, then-President George Bush -- simply does the bidding of the two major parties, which founded it."They (the established parties) do not want to discuss the issues that will determine this country's future,"
7017 Perot said in the NBC interview. "They don't want to talk about the debt, the deficit, they don't want to talk about setting the highest ethical standards for the White House and the Congress."</
7018 The U.S. Federal Reserve is scheduled to hold a pivotal meeting Tuesday to consider raising interest rates for the first time in about 1-1/2 years.At issue is whether the U.S. economy is robust enough to reignite inflation -- which would call for a rate hike to keep prices in check
7018 -- or whether a rate increase would instead stifle a struggling economy.A majority of economists polled by Reuters last week -- 17 of 30 -- believes the central bank will opt to raise short-term rates Tuesday, with all but one of those analysts expecting an increase of 0.25 percent.Even a
7018 small rate hike would lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and corporations, putting a damper on Wall Street and Main Street. President Bill Clinton, too, would balk at any brakes on the economy that would reduce his chances of a victory in the Nov. 5 election.Conflicting signs about the
7018 economy's health present strong arguments for both camps in the Fed -- the anti-inflation hawks, mainly at the Fed's regional banks, and the so-called doves, mostly political appointees on the Fed board in Washington.At a seven-year low of 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at a level that has historically
7018 led to higher inflation and demands for higher wages.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Firms have enjoyed fat profit margins for 5-1/2 years of economic expansion
7018 and thus have some leeway to absorb the higher labour costs. But it is not clear how long they can go without raising prices.While the job market is tight, and companies are stepping up production and rebuilding inventories, retail sales have slowed and the housing market has weakened.If the Fed
7018 tightens credit because wages are rising, it risks giving ammunition to critics who see it as a pawn of Wall Street. And if the Democrats then regain control of Congress, lawmakers may seize on the pre-election rate rise as a reason to rein in the Fed, especially the regional banks.On
7018 the other hand, some of Clinton's appointees to the Fed board may be sensitive to suspicions that they would favour the president and thus be more inclined to raise rates to prove their mettle to the markets and their colleagues.Eight of the 12 regional Fed banks have called for a
7018 rate increase, and consensus-minded central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan may give in to avoid a revolt Tuesday.In the end, the Fed's decision may be more important symbolically than economically. While a small rate rise would have only a minor impact on the economy and could easily be reversed later, it
7018 would clearly signal the Fed's priorities, and that is why Wall Street and Washington are watching so closely.</
