7026 Economic policymakers from the Group of Seven industrial nations will take care to avoid disrupting an agreeable state of currency market tranquility when they converge on Washington this week.Since falling to a record low against the mark and a post-World War II trough versus the yen in early 1995, the
7026 dollar has rebounded and enjoyed a period of unusually limited volatility.The dollar's rise followed an April 1995 call by G7 ministers for an "orderly reversal" in the greenback. With the dollar safely back near the 110 yen and 1.50 mark levels, economists agree this orderly reversal has occurred.To the chagrin
7026 of volatility-hungry currency traders, G7 policymakers, gathering Saturday on the fringes of the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings, will do all they can to maintain this equilibrium."I think the general view is that central banks and finance ministries are pretty comfortable with the exchange rate relationships the
7026 way they are," said Robert Hormats, vice chairman at Goldman, Sachs &amp; Co. "They will do everything they possibly can to avoid rocking the boat." Since March of this year, the dollar has traded in a relatively narrow band between 1.47 and 1.55 marks, remaining marginally above the 1.50 level
7026 in recent weeks. 7026 to strengthen from its current levels it will be France, economists said. 7026 government spending."The only country that would really welcome a stronger dollar is France because it would help the French growth outlook considerably," Chris Iggo, international economist at Barclays Bank.Germany, which would also benefit from dollar strength in the runup to EMU, could echo French calls for a stronger U.S. currency,

7034 By Nicholas Doughty (Diplomatic Correspondent)The United Nations, facing huge debts and a leadership crisis, launched its annual debate on Monday in a sombre mood as countries lined up to appeal for urgent reform of the world body."A stalemate persists, an uncomfortable stalemate that leads to a feeling of ... insecurity
7034 about the future of the United Nations," Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Palmeira Lampreia told the 185-nation General Assembly.The annual U.N. assembly session brings together presidents, prime ministers and foreign ministers to discuss conflicts and problems from trade to the environment. The debate lasts three weeks.With much fanfare, world leaders
7034 called for political and financial reforms of the organisation at last year's celebrations to mark the U.N.'s 50th anniversary.Various committees were set up, but one year later there is no agreement on key reforms and the United Nations is still owed nearly $3 billion in unpaid dues, more than half
7034 by the United States.A U.N. spokeswoman said on Monday that Washington had just paid $40 million, a fraction of what it owes. The United States has demanded faster reforms if it is to pay up, an attitude described on Monday as intimidation by Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland.To the
7034 annoyance of many other nations, Washington has also blocked the appointment of Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali for the customary second five-year term.The United States says a more vigorous reformer is needed to lead the United Nations into the 21st century.Discussions on reforms, including the issue of which countries should become new
7034 permanent members of the powerful U.N. Security Council, are bogged down in regional rivalries.Most countries agree the United Nations must do something to try and restore the brief "golden age" of true cooperation that it enjoyed immediately after the end of the Cold War.But there is no real agreement about
7034 how reform should be achieved, and the United States is in the middle of an election campaign in which the United Nations is regularly vilified by conservative Republicans as an enemy of U.S. interests.Angola, Argentina, the former Soviet republic of Georgia and others laid out different views on reform in
7034 the debate's first session on Monday. U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov speak on Tuesday.Norway's Brundtland, often mentioned as a potential successor to Boutros-Ghali, said reforms must nevertheless be pushed through to keep the United Nations relevant."We are not served by protracted denials of the world
7034 as it is," she told the assembly."We must go from words of intention to deeds," said Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura.There are currently five permanent members of the U.N. Security Council who each have veto power -- the United States, Russia, China, France and Britain. Wealthy Germany and Japan
7034 are prime candidates to join them, but there is far less agreement on candidates from the developing world.The financial crisis has led Boutros-Ghali and others to warn that the United Nations faces bankruptcy. But after the failure of U.N. peacekeeping in Bosnia and Somalia, many countries are now wary of
7034 using the institution in conflict resolution -- one factor that could reduce U.N. bills.One of the few real achievements of the 51st U.N. General Assembly will be the signing of a global treaty banning nuclear tests. The United States, Russia and other nuclear powers are due to sign the Comprehensive
7034 Test Ban Treaty on Tuesday, followed by other nations.However, India's objections to the treaty and its refusal to sign could mean the agreement never enters into force.</

7072 The French government pledged on Monday higher taxes and cost curbs would reduce deficits in the welfare system, which has run deep into the red less than a year after a big debt write-off meant to put it back on its feet.The independent social security accounts commission said the welfare
7072 deficit would reach 51.6 billion francs this year -- by far overshooting a government target of 17 billion francs -- but down from 67.4 billion francs last year.It warned that the deficit would reach 47.15 billion next year if no new measures were taken.Labour Minister Jacques Barrot told a news
7072 conference however that new measures, including higher excise duties on alcohol and tobacco, a reform to payroll charges and spending curbs, would bring the deficit to 29.7 billion next year."Between the forecast and the 29.7 billion francs, there is a margin in which political will must intervene," Barrot, who will
7072 present a welfare bill to parliament next month, said.The social security system -- which uses mostly payroll charges to fund healthcare, pensions and family benefits -- is run separately from the central government budget and has long been the weak link in efforts to reduce France's public deficit.Founded in 1945
7072 and co-managed by the employers' federation and trade unions, it has defied in recent years all government attempts to restore it to balance as generous healthcare spending and high unemployment have eaten into revenues.Earlier this year, the government carried out the second debt write-off in just over two years to
7072 lift the burden of paying debt service charges from the social security system.It set up a new welfare debt repayment fund, CADES, to take on the debt and imposed a flat 0.5 percent tax on virtually all income, the RDS, to repay the debt.But weak growth, which left unemployment at
7072 a record high of 12.5 percent, has wiped out all the gains from those changes.Barrot said 90 percent of the deficit overshoot this year was due to a much lower than expected rise in total wages, from which payroll charges are deducted.He also argued that if the government had not
7072 already taken strong action to curb healthcare spending, this year's deficit would be nearer 90 billion francs.The Force Ouvriere trade union, however, blamed the government's austerity drive, saying it had squeezed economic growth and hit employment, reducing revenues for the welfare system.It said it had long argued the problem was
7072 one of insufficient revenues rather than overspending."The priority given to the massive reduction of public deficits in order to meet Maastricht treaty criteria is creating serious problems for employment. It is not enough to be ready (for monetary union). We have to think about what state we will be in
7072 when we get there," it said in a statement.Economists also questioned the credibility of the government's targets."The social security funding gap has been the Achilles' heel of French fiscal policy since 1993, and is likely to remain so next year," Morgan Stanley economist Eric Chaney said.Barrot stressed however the government's
7072 aim was to restore the welfare system to breakeven. He said there was no question of debt repayment fund CADES taking on extra debt to finance the new deficit as it was prevented by law from doing so.State bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations and the French Treasury would ensure
7072 the welfare system's immediate cash flow needs were met and the government would review the situation in the spring, he said.</

7102 Dublin meeting, triggering wide-selling which carried Bunds lower.Concerns about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who faces heart surgery, also depressed sentiment.The Dublin meeting marked a big step toward monetary union with the finance ministers agreeing in principle on a stability pact to enforce budgetary discipline among future members

7102 not a lot of good that can come from EMU," said Brian Clapp, bond market analyst at Stone &amp; McCarthy in London. 7102 that may favour faster economic growth and job creation at the expense of price stability.But German debt markets got a second blow as a result of the meeting as other European markets likewise found little in the Dublin gathering to raise their own hopes for a speedy monetary union.Bond markets
7102 outside Germany such as Italy and Sweden have benefited from the increasing likelyhood of EMU which is expected to bring lower inflation rates and greater fiscal restraint throughout Europe.Some economists, such as Adolf Rosenstock at the Industrial Bank of Japan in Frankfurt, believe EMU and the fiscal responsibility that will
7102 come with it will eventually be viewed positively by German bond investors.But worries about watering down EMU criteria will continue to keep Bunds warry of EMU for some time.</

7122 EU's Social Protocol, from which Britain has an opt out.He decided to act after getting positive feedback from most EU states on the need for a European initiative in this area, Nolan said.At the same time, the Commission has been unable to break a longstanding deadlock between EU states over
7122 a related proposal to allow firms to set up as "European companies" and will propose that it be referred to a group of experts, she said.The European Company Statute -- along with proposals for a European association, European cooperative society and European mutual society -- has been blocked for many
7122 years by a dispute between EU states over provisions on worker participation.Germany has fought to apply its own system of "co-determination" for workers, while Britain wants no mandatory rules.But Commission proposals for breaking the impasse have met with some resistance, especially from Germany, because they would apply general EU rules
7122 on worker "consultation" -- rather than "participation" -- to the new entities.EU member states -- who are coming under increasing pressure from industry to allow companies to set up under EU rather than national law -- generally support the idea of referring the question to a group of high-level experts,
7122 EU officials said.EU trade unions and employers have negotiated one accord under the Social Protocol so far, covering parental and family leave, which was then turned into EU law.</

7136 Like Banquo's ghost, Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's future hovers over the 51st General Assembly session, where few countries were expected to mention publicly the subject of his re-election.But unlike the specter in Shakespeare's "Macbeth," the U.N. secretary-general is invited to the procedings, defying the United States by declaring his intention to
7136 seek another five years when his current term expires in December.With kings, presidents, prime ministers and foreign ministers gathering at the United Nations for the next three weeks, beginning on Monday, no one knows who will lead the world body next year or what the nearly bankrupt organisation is supposed
7136 to do.For Washington, how the United Nations operates, rather than what its tasks are, is foremost, beginning with the search for a new secretary-general who would concentrate on restructuring the world body."What we want to do now is to have countries begin to look seriously at alternative candidates ... in
7136 October to have the Security Council set up a timetable and a process both for receiving nominations, considering them and eventually voting," Princeton Lyman, the U.S. assistant secretary of state for international organisations, said on Friday.But so far no formal process has begun and none is expected until after the
7136 Nov. 5 U.S. presidential election. Most delegates believe opposition to Boutros-Ghali is politically motivated, and the council last month rebuffed efforts by U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright even to discuss the issue.According to Russia's U.N. ambassador, Sergei Lavrov, the majority of the 15-seat council believes "November is the good time to
7136 start discussion of the substance of the issue."But Albright, who announced in December that Boutros-Ghali must go, said flatly that "the administration will not change its mind, if re-elected. 7136 statesman, one "who is not dragged into (reform) kicking and screaming."To many analysts, Albright apparently believes Congress will never agree to pay the $1.6 billion in arrears the United States owes to the United Nations without some radical change, such as a new secretary-general.Conversely, with Congress' refusal to pay the
7136 huge debt crippling the world body, American authority has been so undercut that other U.N. members are ready to turn down many initiatives suggested by Washington.China, which also has veto power, has given notice that if Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian, is not re-elected it would support another candidate from Africa, and
7136 if that fails a candidate from another developing nation.By this logic, all women mentioned for the job -- Irish President Mary Robinson, Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland and U.N. 7136 Shahani, who has declared her candidacy.Among the African candidates mentioned most frequently are Kofi Annan of Ghana, the U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping, and Salim A. Salim, chairman of the Organisation of African Unity. In addition, Hamid Algabid of Niger, the head of the Islamic Conference, has announced his candidacy.Deciding who
7136 should lead the organisation will not resolve the issue of where its focus should be. Peacekeeping, once the centre of its activities, has dwindled to 25,000 soldiers from more than 70,000 two years ago.Boutros-Ghali himself is philosophical about the direction of the United Nations. "It took around 10 years to
7136 agree about the rules of the Cold War, to manage the Cold War and the institutions to apply those rules," he said, mentioning the creation of NATO in 1949 and the Warsaw Pact in 1955."In our case, we are still at the beginning and the member states don't know what
7136 role they want from the United Nations," he told Reuters last week. "Now we are living in a crisis of the United Nations -- its ups and downs."</

7159 Four gunmen attacked a Sunni Moslem mosque in the Pakistani city of Multan on Monday, killing at least 20 people and wounding many more, police said.Hundreds of enraged protesters later assaulted police outside the mosque, chanting slogans against them and against militant Shi'ite Moslems held responsible for the killings.Witnesses said
7159 crowds threw stones at several Shi'ite homes and a Shi'ite place of worship in the same area, and blocked the main Multan-Bahawalpur road with burning tyres."The people are understandably very agitated," said police deputy superintendent Mirza Maqbool Beg at the scene.The shooting followed the killing on Sunday night of a
7159 leader of the militant Shi'ite Sipah-i-Mohammad Pakistan (SMP) group in Bahawalpur, about 95 km (60 miles) south of Multan.Shi'ite sources in Islamabad said Qamar Haider, described as a divisional commander of the SMP, had been shot dead by unidentified gunmen while sitting in his shop.The mosque attack occurred three days
7159 after Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza was shot dead in the southern city of Karachi when police clashed with his guards.It was the latest in a bloody feud between religious militants in Pakistan. Shi'ites account for about 15 percent of the country's 130 million people, most of whom
7159 are Sunnis.Witnesses in Multan said three gunmen burst into the Al-Khair Mosque in the densely-populated Mumtazabad area and opened fire as the congregation was offering dawn prayers. They escaped in a white car driven by a fourth man.Shahid Ansari, a local councillor, said his father had been in the mosque,
7159 frequented by supporters of the militant Sunni Ahl-e-Hadith organisation, but had escaped unhurt."He told me that as soon as the worshippers kneeled in prayer, the gunmen opened up with automatic weapons, firing from three sides," he said. "The shooting went on for five minutes and there was blood and bits
7159 of flesh all over the mosque."Ambulances ferried casualties to the city's main Nishtar hospital. Police said nearly half the dead were boys studying at a religious school attached to the mosque. The official news agency APP said 19 of the wounded were aged 16 or under.The mosque was run by
7159 the hardline Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group, to which Ahl-e-Hadith is affiliated.Sectarian tension has been especially acute in the populous Punjab province, where Multan and Bahawalpur are located.The SMP's leader, Shi'ite Murid Abbas Yazdani, was shot dead at his home in Islamabad on September 12.Gunmen killed 12 people in an
7159 SSP procession in Karachi on August 14. Up to 18 Shi'ites died four days later in an attack on a community meeting near Mailsi, in Punjab.</

7169 Four gunmen attacked a Sunni Moslem mosque in the central Pakistani city of Multan on Monday, killing 20 people and wounding 56, ambulance sources said.The attack followed the killing on Sunday night of a leader of the militant Shi'ite Moslem Sipah-i-Mohammad Pakistan (SMP) group in Bahawalpur, about 95 km (60
7169 miles) south of Multan.Shi'ite sources in Islamabad said Qamar Haider, described as a divisional commander of the SMP, had been shot dead by unidentified gunmen while sitting in his shop.The mosque attack occurred three days after Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza was shot dead in the southern city
7169 of Karachi in a shootout between his bodyguards and police.It was the latest in a bloody feud between religious militants in Pakistan. Shi'ites account for about 15 percent of the country's 130 million people, most of whom are Sunnis.Witnesses in Multan said three gunmen burst into the Al-Khair Mosque in
7169 the mainly Shi'ite-populated Mumtazabad area and opened fire as the congregation was offering dawn prayers. They escaped in a white car driven by a fourth man.Shahid Ansari, a local councillor, said his father had been in the mosque, frequented by supporters of the militant Sunni Ahl-e-Hadith organisation, but had escaped
7169 unhurt."He told me that as soon as the worshippers kneeled in prayer, the gunmen opened up with automatic weapons, firing from three sides," he said. "The shooting went on for five minutes and there was blood and bits of flesh all over the mosque."Ambulances ferried casualties to the city's main
7169 Nishtar hospital. Rescue workers listed the names of 20 dead. Hospital doctors said 56 people had been wounded.Witnesses said the relatives of three of the dead had removed their bodies from the hospital without waiting for a post-mortem and recited funeral prayers outside the mosque, joined by thousands of mourners.Angry
7169 protesters blocked the main Multan-Bahawalpur road with burning barricades after the killings, witnesses said.Police said the mosque, one of the biggest in the southern district of Mumtazabad, was controlled by the hardline Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group, to which Ahl-e-Hadith is affiliated. A religious school is attached to the mosque.Sectarian
7169 tension has been especially acute in the populous Punjab province, where Multan and Bahawalpur are located.The SMP's leader, Shi'ite Murid Abbas Yazdani, was shot dead at his home in Islamabad on September 12.Gunmen killed 12 people in an SSP procession in Karachi on August 14. Up to 18 Shi'ites died
7169 four days later in an attack on a community meeting near Mailsi, in Punjab.</

7175 entire team of investigators handling the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha bribery case. Sources said the CBI move was aimed at thwarting the selective information leakage and disorder among the lower level officers of the team. Since the Delhi high court had expressed its unhappiness over the progress of the case and
7175 even indicated summoning CBI director Joginder Singh, the agency had decided to streamline the team of investigators, sources added.----The Economic TimesCHUTE FOR 100 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY IN COAL MINING LIKELYThe government is likely to allow 100 percent foreign equity investment in coal mining despite resistance from the Communist Party of
7175 India (Marxist). The government has, however, assured the detractors that public sector coal companies would not be privatised. Sources said private investment would be invited for unexplored coal blocks. 7175 TO REPORT SHARP DROP IN SALES GROWTHAfter three years of galloping growth, the corporate sector is likely to report a slowdown in growth of sales and net profit in the first half of the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). This was revealed by the research conducted by The Economic Times Investment Bureau.
7175 The research said the average growth in turnover of the companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index (excluding Industrial Development Bank of India, Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India and State Bank of India) would be between 9-10 percent compared to 24 percent last year.----NO IN-PRINCIPLE OKAY
7175 FOR ISSUESThe Bombay Stock Exchange has decided to refuse in-principle approvals to companies for getting their scrips listed on the exchange. 7175 to prevent recurrence of defaults. 7175 NORMS FOR COAL, GAS PROJECTSThe government plans to allow automatic approval for foreign direct investment of up to 74 percent in power generation and distribution. Hydro-electric power projects and distribution of power from them would also fall in this category. The power ministry's move to include the conventional power sector
7175 in the automatic list has been accepted by the industry ministry. The automatic approval would be allowed for power projects using gas, coal, lignite and liquid fuels as feedstock.----</

7179 Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, grieving for her slain brother, faced the task on Tuesday of halting sectarian unrest after a bloody attack on a Sunni Moslem mosque and the killings of two Shi'ite Moslem leaders.Bhutto, beset by political, economic and personal troubles, was expected to return to Islamabad after three
7179 days of mourning in Karachi and the Bhuttos' home district of Larkana.Apart from her brother's death and religious tension, she must also cope with a newly assertive President Farooq Leghari, who on Monday demanded a parliamentary probe into corruption.Leghari, once seen as a loyal Bhutto ally, made clear that he
7179 did not agree with her assertion that existing mechanisms were adequate. "The time for action has come," he said in a letter to both houses of parliament.Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza died in a clash with police in Karachi on Friday. She called his death a conspiracy against their family, but
7179 has not identified the culprits."Murtaza's enemies are involved in conspiring against the family," Bhutto, flanked by her wailing mother Nusrat and sister Sanam, told mourners at her Karachi residence on Monday.Bhutto, at odds with her brother while he was alive, described him as a fighter for democracy and said a
7179 provincial judicial inquiry would discover the truth about his death."Our paths were different but our blood was the same. Our destiny was one - Islam, Pakistan, democracy and equality."The government must try to prevent further outbreaks of violence after attackers killed 21 worshippers at a Sunni mosque in the Punjab
7179 provincial city of Multan on Monday.Troops in armoured vehicles patrolled Multan after angry crowds stoned Shi'ite neighbourhoods and attacked police.Gunmen killed a hardline Shi'ite leader in the town of Bahawalpur, 95 km (60 miles) south of Multan, on Sunday night and shot dead another just hours after the mosque attack.Sunni
7179 and Shi'ite militants have waged a bloody vendetta in Pakistan for several years. Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of the country's 130 million people, most of whom are Sunnis.Tension is running high over the death of Murtaza Bhutto, 42, who had led a splinter faction of the ruling Pakistan
7179 People's Party (PPP), known as PPP-Shaheed Bhutto.The PPP-Shaheed Bhutto group, accusing the police of deliberately ambushing Murtaza and his companions, has called for nationwide protests against the government for Thursday.Police fired bullets and teargas to disperse pro-Murtaza demonstrators in the Bhuttos' home town of Larkana in the southern province of
7179 Sindh on Monday, wounding two.</
7180 Sitaram Kesri, chosen by senior leaders on Monday as provisional president of India's Congress party, is a veteran who was jailed many times during India's struggle for independence.Former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on Saturday as the president of India's oldest party. Kesri, 76, will be stopgap chief until
7180 a party plenary next month.Rao quit after a court asked him to testify in a case of criminal conspiracy involving a businessman who claims he paid $100,000 to a friend of Rao in 1983 in a failed bid to win a state contract.Rao says he is innocent but resigned to
7180 help his party, which has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947.Kesri was a staunch follower of Mahatma Gandhi and has a stature that inspires awe even among senior Congressmen. His name was proposed by Rao himself.As a student, Kesri, who comes from the mineral rich
7180 but economically backward state of Bihar, quit studying to join the freedom movement. Jailed by the British, he even refused parole to attend his father's funeral rites.Many believe that Kesri's roots in the movement and his amiable disposition could help him bind togther the party which led India to freedom
7180 but now stuck finds support dwindling.In a party which rivals say is too strongly oriented towards the Hindu upper castes and the rich, Kesri has been an outspoken supporter of job quotas in government as affirmative action to help low castes. 7230 Once a political monolith, India's Congress party has lost clout with the demise of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty and the maturing of the nation's democracy, analysts and historians said on Monday.But while the resignation of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao as party leader is an embarrassing blow to Congress, the
7230 party identified with Indian independence and non-alignment will remain a major political force, they said."I don't think you can write off Congress," said Rasheed Talib, a veteran independent political commentator.The party was grappling on Monday with fallout from Rao's weekend decision to step down after a court upheld a summons
7230 ordering him to appear in a criminal conspiracy case.Senior leaders were set to gather on Monday evening to choose a stop-gap leader to carry the reins until the party's plenary body meets, probably before the year end.Formed in 1885, Congress has ruled India for nine-tenths of the nation's history since
7230 independence in 1947.Synonomous with Indian nationalism, it has been the political home for Mahatma Gandhi, the nation's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, his daughter Indira Gandhi and her son, Rajiv Gandhi.Congress has spent only four years out of power since 1947, and, helped by a wave of sympathy following Rajiv
7230 Gandhi's assassination at the hands of a suicide bomber, rebounded in 1991 to recapture control after 18 months on the sidelines.But despite broad support for Rao's foreign policies and free-market economics, Congress was thrown out of office in general elections ended in May in its worst ever showing.During Rao's five-year
7230 tenure, the party was undermined by intra-party rivalries and corruption scandals.Ironically, Mahatma Gandhi had called for the dissolution of Congress after freedom was won.The nation's spiritual founding father, who dominated the organisation for many years before independence, believed the vast, umbrella organisation was not needed in a democracy.But Congress remained
7230 the dominant political party for 30 years after independence, underpinned by its broad geographical reach, its association with the nationalist movement and its charismatic leaders, Nehru and Indira Gandhi.Eventually Congress's strengths -- centralised leadership and a penchant for domineering chiefs -- proved weaknesses as Indira Gandhi was routed in the
7230 1977 general election.More generally, Congress's base among the lower castes and the Moslem minority has eroded with time.The dynasty has faded, although a segment of Congress still turns to Rajiv Gandhi's widow, Sonia, for direction. But she is not expected to enter the political fray.New parties have sprung up to
7230 defend the dispossessed, and the Moslems have deserted Congress in a large numbers, accusing the party of failing to protect them against communal violence.Many Sikhs, too, left Congress. They accuse it of sparking anti-Sikh riots in 1984 after Indira Gandhi was gunned down by Sikh bodyguards."Congress has lost support because
7230 its factions have become separate parties," said Ashis Nandy of the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.Congress polled 28.8 percent of the vote in recent general elections -- the first time it fell below 30 percent.But Nandy said one fifth of the electorate continued to be die-hard Congress supporters,
7230 giving it a solid base, and it had the advantage of occupying the political centre between right-wing Hindu nationalists and a range of left-wing parties."Congress provides the natural point of gravitation for a sizeable segment of the Indian people," Nandy said.Its ability to rebound will depend largely on its choice
7230 of leader, analysts said."Congress needs a sharp, surgical operation," Vinod Mehta, editor of Outlook magazine said. "It needs to demonstrate it realises the follies of the past and choose a man who can take the party in new directions."</

7240 Bangladesh has begun a massive hunt for rats that annually eat and destroy enough grain to feed three million people, government officials said on Monday.They said Agriculture and Food Minister Begum Matia Chowdhury formally launched the month-long drive on Sunday, during which farmers will be taught rat-killing techniques. Successful rat
7240 killers will be rewarded with cash and crops.Agriculture officials say up to 450,000 tonnes of paddy in the field are lost to rats each year, enough to feed up to three million people.The rodents also destroy substantial quantity of grains in the warehouses, they said without giving details.Bangladesh is almost
7240 self-sufficient in foodgrains with annual production of around 20 million tonnes, according to official figures. The country's population is about 118 million.Rat killing has become an annual event in predominantly agricultural Bangladesh in recent years. Some 2.54 million rats were killed last year, agriculture officials said.</

7244 An outbreak of encephalitis has killed at least 115 people in 15 districts in Nepal in last five months, a government official said on Monday."A total of 624 people have been affected by the disease," Benu Bahadur Karki, head of Nepal's epidemiology department told Reuters while confirming a report published
7244 in the state-owned daily Gorkhapatra.The newspaper said the disease was caused by mosquitoes and had mainly affected districts of Jhapa, Morang, Rupandehi and Banke, all bordering with India.Banke in west Nepal with 25 victims was worst hit.A patient affected by encephalitis germs usually suffers from high fever, severe headaches and
7244 drowsiness and dies in five days, doctors said.Karki said the authorities were helpless as there was no special drug for the disease and hospitals outside the capital, Kathmandu, were ill-equipped to counter the epidemic.</

7246 Sri Lankan forces pounded Tamil Tiger positions on Monday in the government's latest bid to break into the rebels' northern stronghold but met heavy resistance, military officials said.At least 30 government soldiers had been killed in the offensive, the officials said."The army is spreading out from their last-held positions," an
7246 official told Reuters. "We're meeting heavy resistance. About 50 soldiers have been wounded."Troops who had consolidated positions around the northern road juction town of Paranthan launched the fresh push toward Kilinochchi on Sunday after a lull of more than a month.It was not immediately clear if the 30 dead included
7246 11 soldiers killed on Sunday."We heard reports of heavy shelling starting on Saturday night and going on till Sunday morning," a United Nations official in the northern town of Vavuniya told Reuters.The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's
7246 north and east, accused the troops of attacking civilians."The armed forces are directing their attack on civilian concentrations which are scattered around the intended path of the army's advance," it said in a statement."From early in the morning air force bombers are flying regular sorties, bombing civilian concentrations and attacking
7246 fleeing civilians," it said.Most of an estimated 150,000 people in Kilinochchi had evacuated the town since the military first launched its offensive in July but many lived on the outskirts of the town.On the first day of the new offensive, soldiers at Elephant Pass at the neck of the northern
7246 Jaffna peninsula poured onto Paranthan to reinforce attack forces.The Tigers set up positions at Kilinochchi, entry point to their jungle territory of Wanni, earlier this year after the army recaptured Jaffna peninsula.The rebels had ruled the peninsula for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.Despite security forces'
7246 air strikes and shelling from tanks and artillery, the rebels fought back using mortars, rockets and automatic rifles, killing the 11 soldiers and wounding many others, including a lieutenant colonel in the Armoured Corps.The extent of rebel casualties was not immediately known but a military officer said: "The LTTE must
7246 have suffered heavy casualties because of air and artillery strikes."Jaffna is now separated from the mainland by a big chunk of rebel-held territory that reaches from Kilinochchi to Vavuniya, 70 km (44 miles) south of the town.The army has said it wants to reopen the main highway connecting Jaffna and
7246 Colombo which passes through rebel-controlled Wanni.Opening the road would let the military supply the Jaffna peninsula more easily and cheaply than the aircraft and ships it now uses.The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire
7246 garrison of 1,400 men.It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war and the army launched an offensive soon afterwards but its southward advance from Jaffna had been stalled near Kilinochchi.Diplomats said there had been a lull in the war recently partly because the army had exhausted itself after
7246 a thrust towards Kilinochchi in July.They said about 30 percent of the military's strength of 100,000 troops were held in Jaffna since its recapture of the peninsula last April to maintain security there.</

7254 The revamped 30-share benchmark sensitive index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) could help attract more funds to India from global fund managers, investment firm Birla Marlin Securities said on the weekend."It could encourage allocation of more funds to India," Mukarram Bhagat, the firm's head of research.A study on the
7254 revised index by Birla Marlin analyst K.R. Sudhakar said volatility in the new index would be much lower compared to the earlier index."Given the low volatility, the risk perceptions of the investors would be lower than before," Sudhakar said.The required rate of return on equity investments in India would also
7254 fall as the risk perception comes down, he said."Fund managers allocating country exposure levels may rework allocation, taking into account the lower volatility and hence, reduced risk levels," the study said.The study was based on statistics for the old and the revised sensex for the period May 1994 to May
7254 1996 on the basis of returns obtained from the BSE, it said."As on 16 August 1996, the market was trading at 11.2 percent 1996/97 (April-March) earnings (Marlin estimates) of the new index," the study said."This means that the market benchmark has become cheaper with a lower risk portfolio."The BSE revamped
7254 the 30-share index last month to make it more representative of changes in market capitalisation in recent years.The new index has several large state-run firms which were listed on the exchange after the government divested some of its holdings as part of the economic reforms launched in 1991.-- Bombay newsroom

7260 California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday signed far-reaching legislation to open the state's $21 billion electricity market to competition and slash consumer rates by 20 percent by the year 2002."We're doing more than signing a new law, we are shifting the balance of power in California," Wilson, a Republican, said
7260 at the bill signing ceremony in San Diego. "We've pulled the plug on another outdated monopoly and replaced it with the promise of a new era of competition."The state Legislature approved the deregulation plan in late August. Lawmakers described the measure as "historic" and a "model" for the nation since
7260 dozens of other states are considering similar proposals.The sweeping measure will restructure the electric industry in California, ending the utility monopoly on generation and opening the market to competition so that retail customers can choose among electric energy suppliers.The bill has the support of the large utilities that would be
7260 affected most, Pacific Gas and Electric Co., Enova Corp.'s San Diego Gas and Electric, and Edison International's Southern California Edison.Supporters said deregulation would stimulate the state's economy, save schools over $123 million by the year 2002, ensure a reliable source of power and provide safeguards against widespread power outages.Critics said
7260 the plan was a bailout for utilities.The legislation lays out a five year transition period during which the industry will be opened to competition.Residential users and small commercial businesses are guaranteed a rate reduction of 10 percent starting January 1, 1998, followed by another 10 percent reduction by 2002.Currently, California's
7260 electrical rates are 40 percent higher than the national average -- 50 percent higher than Texas, 65 percent higher than Nevada and 120 percent higher than Oregon.To help the investor-owned utilities better compete as the generation market opens, the utilities will be compensated for certain "stranded" costs, such as nuclear
7260 power plants, that would not be economical in a competitive market.The legislation authorises the California Infrastructure Bank to issue up to $10 billion in revenue bonds to help the utilities pay off their stranded costs.By issuing the bonds through the state bank, the utilities will obtain more favourable interest rates
7260 on the debt. State taxpayers would have no obligation or financial exposure.The bond financings will provide substantial savings to the utilities, which will be passed on to the customers.</

7270 The Federal Reserve, set on achieving long-term price stability, is close to adopting a monetary policy that would attempt to keep the government's measure of consumer price inflation within a specific target range, according to a Fed source.The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the policy, which relies
7270 on a measure of the Consumer Price Index, has been "informally adopted within the Fed."Under the policy, the Fed considers a rate of inflation of between zero and 2 percent as measured by the core rate of the CPI to be non-inflationary.The core rate of the CPI, which is prepared
7270 and released monthly by the Labour Department, excludes food and energy prices, which can cause wide fluctations in the index because of their volatility.If such a policy were adopted, it would mark the first time that the Fed was using a specific measure as a guide in setting interest rates.The
7270 Fed controls the discount rate, which is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks, and sets a target for the federal funds rate, which is the rate at which banks lend money to each other when they balance their accounts at the end of each
7270 business day.Those rates in turn determine the rates at which banks and other institutions lend money to businesses and consumers.The Fed's policy making arm, the Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet Tuesday for its latest deliberations on interest rates, and speculation about what the panel might do has
7270 led to sporadic volatility in the stock and bond markets in recent weeks.Many economists expect the Fed to raise the discount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.0 percent and to raise its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 5.50 percent.Eight of the 12 regional Fed
7270 district banks have asked the Fed to make such an increase in the federal funds rate as a means of warding off inflation.The core rate of CPI rose 2.6 percent in the 12 months ended in August, a rate that would encourage the Fed to raise interest rates under the
7270 policy described by the Fed source.When the Fed last moved on interest rates -- it cut the federal funds and discount rates by a quarter point on Jan. 31 -- it did so without dissent and with six Fed banks requesting a cut in the largely symbolic discount rate.One reason
7270 for targeting CPI is the loss of usefulness of policy references such as the monetary aggregates.Cleveland Fed President Jerry Jordan, a voting member of the FOMC, commented on the notion of a numerical target as a guideline for monetary policy as early as 1992.The Fed's current view on targeting core
7270 CPI is in line with a CPI range first spelled out by New York Fed President William McDonough in a March 21 speech.McDonough defined U.S. price stability as being in a range between 0.5 percent and 2.0 percent on CPI to allow for the upward bias believed to exist in
7270 the imperfect -- but most publicised -- measure of U.S. inflation.According to another source, New York Fed Director of Research Frederic Mishkin and Head of the Markets Group Peter Fisher contributed to formulating that range.The notion has since received the support of long-time FOMC members such as San Francisco Fed
7270 President Robert Parry.A New York Fed spokesman said the bank had no comment on the notion of a numerical target for monetary policy or the impact of McDonough's views within the Fed.The Fed is considering targeting core CPI regardless of the fate of legislation sponsored by Sen. Connie Mack, R-Fla.,
7270 that would establish price stability as the Fed's main goal and require the central bank to use a numerical target toward that goal.The Fed's existing dual mandate is to seek both full employment and price stability.The FOMC discussed Mack's bill at its Sept. 26, 1995, meeting, noting members' "initial reaction
7270 was favourable in regard to the overall thrust of the bill...(that) would restructure the monetary policy requirements to permit the Congress to carry out its oversight responsibilities more effectively."The CPI is a key issue on more than one account.A low CPI would not only help drive U.S. long-term market rates
7270 lower along with declining inflation expectations, it would also reduce government spending on a number of inflation-indexed outlays.</

7279 The British government Monday set up a watchdog to try to get pornography off the Internet.Safety-Net, which is being financed by the industry, will have a hotline to which callers can report suspected illegal material and will contact police if necessary.It will publish a "legality indicator" or rating for each
7279 public access area on the Internet known as a Usenet news group. The rating will indicate whether the group normally contains illegal or pornographic material and what kind.Internet users can contact the hotline to complain about material received from anyone via an automatic telephone, mail, e-mail or facsimile.Safety-Net operators will
7279 try to see where the material came from, contact the authors and ask them to remove it. They can ask the relevant service provider to take action and pass details to the British Police National Criminal Intelligence Service (NCIS)."We at the Home Office (interior ministry) made it clear to the
7279 Internet providers some time ago that action was needed to deal with obscene material on the Internet," Home Office Minister Tom Sackville said."Some of the material which is available, including pictures of sex acts involving children, is totally unacceptable under the law."Science and technology minister Ian Taylor said Safety-Net would
7279 act as a warning system to alert the public."As this is an international network, we have to do something to try to eliminate illegal use of it -- the abuse of the Internet by a few perverts," he told BBC radio."Government and the Internet industry have been working hard to
7279 come up with proposals that can offer real protection to net users while preserving free speech and recgonizing the value of the net for work, education and leisure," Taylor added in a statement.</
7280 Seymour Cray, considered the father of the supercomputer, was in critical condition on Monday with massive head injuries suffered in a car accident, a hospital spokewoman said.Cray, 70, was injured on Sunday when his car was hit by another car and rolled over. Physicians operated on to relieve pressure on
7280 his brain, Penrose St. Francis Health Services spokeswoman Kate Brewster said on Monday."He's still listed as critical but unstable. His vital signs are not stable," Brewster said.Cray founded supercomputer company Cray Research in 1972. Supercomputers, which can process massive amounts of data at high speed, were the talk of the
7280 1980s but lost their luster with the advent of personal computers and workstations, which became the choice of engineers and scientists.Cray Research spun off Cray Computer, based in Colorado Springs. The two were not related. Cray Computer filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in March 1995 after it was unable
7280 to sell $20 million worth of stock to replenish its coffers.Supercomputers were used by the Department of Defence but the end of the Cold War diminished the need for them, making it impossible for another supercomputing company to survive, analysts said.</

7282 The Securities and Exchange Commission Monday charged a Gaithersburg, Md., company with fraud for falsely claiming it had developed a device that could accurately predict a person's blood sugar content.In a civil complaint filed in a federal district court here, the SEC alleged that Futrex Inc. made the claims in
7282 a private financing drive that raised $1.85 million in 1994 and in a proposed initial offering of common stock in 1995 that aimed at raising $18 million.The offering documents were distributed to nearly 20,000 potential investors but Futrex later postponed the IPO.The SEC said that in both efforts, Futrex and
7282 its president, Robert Rosenthal, claimed that Futrex' hand-held "Dream Beam" analyser could measure and accurately predict a person's blood glucose level by passing infrared light through the finger. Rosenthal is also a defendant in the case.The SEC is seeking injuctions against further securities law violations by the defendants, an order
7282 that Futrex offer to compensate the investors in the private placement and civil monetary penalties against Rosenthal.Futrex and its lawyer were not available to comment.In its lawsuit, the SEC alleged that no Futrex employee has ever reviewed or analysed any data to support the claims that the Dream Beam analyser
7282 actually works.The SEC alleged that Futrex, in offering documents for its proposed public offering, claimed that a 1991 study it conducted at Mount Sinai Medical Centre found that another device it had developed was "technically feasible."The SEC said the claim was false and misleading because Rosenthal used data selectively to
7282 make the pitch believable and the study itself did not involve any attempt to use the infrared analyser to predict blood glucose levels.Between 10 and 20 units of the device cited in the study, Futrex 9000, were sold abroad but most of those were returned, the SEC said, adding the
7282 devices were not capable of measuring blood glucose levels.The fact that the devices were returned was not disclosed in the stock offering documents, the SEC said.The SEC also alleged that field studies said to have been made in 1994 and 1995 by the company were false and misleading and that
7282 data generated by the 1995 tests was useless because of manufacturing defect in all the Dream Beams.But Rosenthal ordered his staff to proceeed with the tests to avoid the embarrasing disclosure of the manufacturing defect to participants in the studies, the SEC said.In some meetings with prospective investors, Rosenthal allegedly
7282 demonstrated that a Dream Beam showed his correct blood glucose level. But the demonstrations were staged to deceive potential investors, the SEC said.</
7283 French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen said Monday its profit fell by more than half in the first six months of 1996 as a brutal price war in France took a heavy toll on the domestic car industry.The company's net attributable profit fell to 602 million French francs ($117.2 million) in
7283 the first half from 1.22 billion ($237.6 million) in the same period last year.Analysts found the results disappointing but not surprising.Peugeot's French rival, Renault SA, earlier this month reported a huge drop in first-half profit to 158 million francs ($30.8 million) from 1.76 billion ($342.7 million) and predicted a loss
7283 for the year.French carmakers are struggling in a tough environment as their home market has turned into the biggest battleground of a fierce price war among European and U.S. manufacturers.Foreign carmakers are attracted by the rapid growth of French car sales, buoyed by the state's new-cars-for-old incentive scheme, and the
7283 high costs of French companies.Car sales in France rose 7.4 percent in the first eight months of the year, but foreigners took the lion's share of the increase, registering a combined 20 percent sales gain."Foreigners have become very aggressive. For them France is a foreign market and they can even
7283 afford to lose money here because for them it's a strategic issue," said a car analyst at a French brokerage house.Foreign companies, notably Italy's Fiat, have benefited from the French incentive scheme, which has tended to favour sales of smaller cars with smaller profit margins.PSA Peugeot Citroen said in a
7283 statement its first-half performance was also hurt by the franc's strength relative to other currencies such as the Italian lira and British pound."In this context, PSA Peugeot Citroen sought the best balance between unit margins and volumes," in a bid to maintain market share while limiting the erosion of its
7283 profit margins, the company said.The Peugeot group has withstood the ravages better than its domestic rival Renault, which now looks to be the weakest of Europe's big six carmakers. Analysts say the Peugeot group has tighter control over its costs and a clearer strategy.Peugeot said revenues rose 3 percent to
7283 89.04 billion francs ($17.3 million) as it enhanced its product mix and sold more expensive models in its line-up, including the Peugeot 406 sedan launched last fall.</

7286 Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday that the future single European currency would not automatically be stable against the dollar and would have to earn its reputation."The European central bank must earn this reputation (for stability)," Tietmeyer said in the text of a speech for a reception sponsored by
7286 German vehicle maker Mercedes-Benz AG at the IAA truck exhibition in Hanover."That can under the circumstances take a while because credibility can mostly not be built overnight," he said.Tietmeyer also said he hoped the new currency, to be called the Euro and which is slated for launch in January 1999,
7286 would not fluctuate against the yen and dollar as much as the mark currently does."There is the hope that the Euro will not fluctuate as much as the mark," Tietmeyer said in the speech."How far this hope will be fulfilled is hard to predict," he added, noting that the stability
7286 of the new currency will be pegged to solid monetary and fiscal policies.In addition, he again pushed for a detailed stability pact to secure public budgets once the new currency is launched.European officials meeting in Dublin at the weekend cleared key hurdles in their quest for a stability pact to
7286 control public spending once countries enter monetary union, but failed to agree exactly how the deal will work."It cannot be allowed that, after the start of currency union, countries put their feet up on the table in terms of stability policies because of the lack of effective sanctions," Tietmeyer said.Referring
7286 to the results of the Dublin meeting, Tietmeyer said: "There are still a few important questions left open."Tietmeyer warned that fiscal criteria for entry into currency union should not be seen as less important than other requirements set out in the Maastricht Treaty."One should not say that the fiscal criteria
7286 should be less important. Experience shows that sooner or later slack finances endanger monetary policy," Tietmeyer said."That also applies for currency union. If anything, price stability lends itself to yet higher interest rates," he said.Tietmeyer also said German companies would have the least to win in terms of interest rates
7286 with the new currency.He said that the earlier privilege of having their home currency viewed as a reserve currency would be lost against competitors from currency member countries.</

7288 reponded, pointing to his Coke. 7288 15 years ago lunchtime drinking was much heavier," said Michael Sternberg, co-owner of Sam &amp; Harry's, a Washington, D.C., steak house. "In a fine dining restaurant like ours, part of having a nice lunch is having a glass of wine. We also do a few scotches, a few martinis, here
7288 and there."Rob Hoover, president of Sprint Staffing &amp; Workforce USA, Tampa, attributed the decline to "the desire to be alert at work and an awareness among corporate executives of the impact drinking has on your health.""Drinking is rare at the lunches I attend," Hoover said. 7288 much work I did in the afternoon."Jeff Becker, vice president of alcohol issues at the Washington-based Beer Institute said there was definitely less drinking at lunctime."People are drinking less spirits at lunch and I think we and the wine people have definitely benefited from that. 7288 lunch probably only half the time," Becker said.Besides concerns about after-lunch performance, tax changes have also played a role."Nobody wants a drunken executive in the afternoon," explained Dr. Cleaves Bennett, of Health Care Partners, Los Angeles, and author of "Control Your High Blood Pressure Without Drugs" (Doubleday). 7288 recalled Rick Mohr, of Steelcase, the Grand Rapids, Mich., office furniture maker. 7288 to outsalad the other person. But there's been a backlash that everything's unhealthy. 7292 Economic policymakers from the Group of Seven industrial nations will take care to avoid disrupting the tranquility of the currency market when they converge on Washington later this week.Since falling to a record low against the German mark and a post-World War II drop vs. the Japanese yen in early
7292 1995, the dollar has rebounded and enjoyed a period of unusually limited volatility.The dollar's rise followed an April 1995 call by G7 ministers for an "orderly reversal" in the greenback. With the dollar safely back near 110 yen and 1.50 marks, economists agree this orderly reversal has occurred.To the chagrin
7292 of volatility-hungry currency traders, G7 policymakers, gathering this Saturday on the fringes of the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings, will do all they can to maintain this equilibrium."I think the general view is that central banks and finance ministries are pretty comfortable with the exchange rate relationships
7292 the way they are," said Robert Hormats, vice chairman at Goldman, Sachs &amp; Co. "They will do everything they possibly can to avoid rocking the boat."Since March of this year, the dollar has traded in a relatively narrow band between 1.47 and 1.55 marks, remaining marginally above the 1.50 level
7292 in recent weeks. The dollar has traded in a 105- to 110-yen range since May and has been above the 100-yen level since October of 1995.The dollar's strength against the Japanese currency has been a source of concern to U.S. automobile manufacturers, who have voiced their displeasure as the dollar
7292 has reapproached 110 yen in recent weeks.Little sympathy is expected from U.S. officials however, who are unlikely to waver from Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's "strong dollar" mantra, regardless of whether their desired dollar reversal has already taken place.The Clinton Administration's stance toward the carmakers was demonstrated last week when Commerce
7292 Secretary Mickey Kantor indicated that recent dollar strength against the yen did not appear to be hurting car sales."If people are looking for a statement saying the orderly reversal is ended, we won't see anything like that," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics."The U.S. does not want
7292 to be sidetracked by U.S. producers' calls for a lower dollar," he added. "I think they will welcome the (dollar) move so far, say exchange rates are more in line with economic fundamentals, but not give any indication there has been an overshoot."If any one country calls for the dollar
7292 to strengthen from its current levels it will be France, economists said. In an effort to meet strict Maastricht criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) France has adopted tight fiscal measures.A stronger dollar vs. the franc would help French exports and overall economic growth, thus easing the pain of
7292 weaker government spending. Gains in the dollar against the French franc would make French exports cheaper in dollar terms."The only country that would really welcome a stronger dollar is France because it would help the French growth outlook considerably," Chris Iggo, international economist at Barclays Bank.Germany, which would also benefit
7292 from dollar strength in the runup to EMU, could echo French calls for a stronger U.S. currency, but is unlikely to push hard for such a move, economists said.In the absence of exciting currency pronouncements, economists predicted G7 policymakers will focus on ensuring continued recovery in the world economy, while
7292 touching on the success of last year's Mexican rescue plan."Certainly compared to the G7 meetings last year, things are looking quite a bit brighter," said Barclay's Iggo. "The U.S. economy continues to do well, Germany and Japan are past the worst and there is no currency instability.""It's steady as she
7292 goes. I think that will be the message," he added.</

7297 Canada's flamboyant former Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau once said his country's relationship with the United States was like a mouse being in bed with an elephant.Until this year that metaphor was an apt description of the Bank of Canada's relationship with the U.S. Federal Reserve. Canada's central bank has had
7297 little latitude in the past decade to uncouple its monetary policy from the Fed's even when the state of the economy warranted it. But with the Fed's rate-setting Open Market Committee meeting tomorrow, and the scene set for a U.S. interest rate hike, many Canadians believe the traditional relationship between
7297 the two central banks is about to change."They (the Bank of Canada) clearly have enough flexibility and credibility that they can set their own course to a considerable extent, much more than in the past," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research for TD Securities Inc.If the Fed raises U.S.
7297 short-term rates tomorrow, few market watchers expect the Bank of Canada to follow suit. There is little fear that financial markets will punish the Canadian bank for standing pat in the face of a U.S. rate rise, as it did in late 1994.The Bank of Canada's newfound independence from the
7297 Fed has been years in the making. The reasons for it include declining government deficits, the country's first current account surplus in 12 years and an inflation record that is the envy of the industrialized world. "I think we've paid the price in terms of tough fiscal policy, tough trade
7297 policy and tough monetary policy so we can conduct our made in Canada monetary policy," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers. "If it's justified by fundamentals, I think the markets will accept it,"A drop in government borrowing is cited as the biggest reason for the increase
7297 in the Bank of Canada's independence from the Fed. Both federal and provincial governments have cut spending sharply over the past three years to control deficits that spiked sharply upward during the last recession. Finance Minister Paul Martin confirmed last week that the budget deficit for 1995/96 would come in
7297 under C$30 billion -- well under his original C$32.7 billion target and down from a peak of C$42 billion in 1993/94.Seven of Canada's 10 provinces are expected to balance their budgets this year.Declining government borrowing helped contribute to Canada's first quarterly current account surplus in 12 years last month. The
7297 current account is a measure of a country's balance of payments with the rest of the world. Analysts said Canada's 12-year record of current account deficits was largely the result of interest payments to foreign bondholders.Bolstered by improved economic fundamentals, the Bank of Canada earlier this year began to move
7297 its monetary policy away from that of the Federal Reserve. The two countries' economies then seemed to be going in different directions.The Fed put through its last rate cut on January 31, then held rates steady amid indications that the U.S. economy was running near full capacity. In Canada, however,
7297 economic growth remained sluggish and economists calculated the country had an output gap of about 3.0 percent.The Bank of Canada responded by cautiously lowering Canadian short-term rates by a total of 125 basis points in a series of moves independent of any action by the Fed. The cuts brought the
7297 country's key Bank Rate down to 4.25 percent.As the Bank eased, the Canadian dollar remained steady and money market rates followed -- confirmation of the Bank's independence from Fed policy. "I think that is clear evidence we have room to set our own monetary policy," said Mark Chandler, senior economist
7297 with Goldman Sachs Canada. "This idea that Canada can't have an independent monetary policy, I don't think it holds water."Now that the Bank of Canada has room to maneuver on domestic monetary policy, investors are questioning what the next move by the Bank will be.For the most part, analysts agreed
7297 the Bank would remain focused on its stated policy goal of keeping the inflation rate, now about 1.4 percent, in a 1.0-3.0 percent range. Market watchers reckoned the Bank of Canada was at or near the bottom of its interest rate easing cycle. The Bank has reduced rates by 400
7297 basis points since May 1995 and there are indications, such as increases in employment, that the cuts are beginning to take effect.The Bank is now awaiting further data on the economy rather than risk losing its hard-won credibility with further cuts."I think if they wanted to (ease) they could, but
7297 I don't think the conditions justify it and I don't think they think conditions justify it," said Goldman's Chandler. Looking ahead six months, Chandler said it was possible the Bank of Canada could begin raising short-term interest rates, partly in response to a growing Canadian economy and partly in reaction
7297 to expected U.S. rate hikes."I think it's quite clear we're setting our own monetary policy," said Chandler. "That doesn't mean that Canadian rates won't go up."-- Reuters Toronto Bureau 416-941-8100</

7361 Ashland Inc President Paul Chellgren said he expects to stay the course at Ashland Inc after becoming the fourth chief executive officer in the 72-year old company's history next week.That strategy includes a decision made several years ago to steer growth capital away from the diversified oil refining and marketing
7361 company's refining operations, said Chellgren, who is set to become chief executive on October 1 and slated to add the title of chairman in January 1997. Refining capital expenditures will be held to the level of depreciation as part of the company's plans to invest 75 percent of its capital
7361 in its chemicals, construction, Valvoline lubricants and other non-refining businesses by 2000, up from about 65 percent in 1995."I think there's going to be a lot of continuity and consistency in that (strategy)," Chellgren said.Ashland has a modest production-sharing pact in Nigeria, where it produces about 20,000 barrels of oil
7361 per day, but nearly all the oil fed into its 355,000 barrel per day U.S. refineries is acquired under contract or on the spot market. Chellgren said Ashland -- an active buyer of crude this year from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve -- can obtain all the oil it needs
7361 in the highly efficient world oil markets. "Having your own crude supply as a pure refiner-marketer in some ways is perhaps a little bit less important today as it was ten or fifteen years ago," he said.In recent years, Ashland has obtained about 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) under Middle
7361 Eastern contract, 100,000 bpd from Canada and 120,000 bpd from domestic and foreign spot purchases, he said. "These markets are increasingly transparent and perfect and you can get the volumes, you just have to pay the price," he said.As Chellgren takes the helm, Ashland will be paying that price in
7361 the short run. Tensions in the Middle East fueled a run-up in crude prices that was expected to trim earnings for the fourth quarter ending September 30, he said.But as those tensions fade and oil prices move lower, Ashland sees long-term advantages for its three U.S. refineries, which are located
7361 in the Midwest. Additional pipeline capacity into the Midwest, particularly Mobil Corp's decision in particular to reverse a crude pipeline from Chicago to Ohio, will increase the flow of Canadian crude."When they did that, we could get Canadian crude to our two southern refineries -- Canton (Ohio) and Cattletsburg (Ky.)
7361 -- and that's been important to us. In essence that Canadian crude has meant we are buying less offshore crude," he said.</

7368 U.S. households with direct access to the Internet via an Internet Service Provider (ISP) outnumber homes where computer users reach the Internet via a commercial online service, according to a new study.Market research firm Odyssey said its latest Homefront survey, released Monday, found that 48 percent of households surfing the
7368 Internet from home are using an ISP, while 35 percent use a commercial online service for Internet access. The research firm said the findings represent a sharp turnaround from six months ago, when it found 54 percent of at-home Internet surfers used commercial online services. Six months ago, only about
7368 30 percent of home computer users gained access to the Internet via Internet Service Providers according to Odyssey.In its latest study, the survey found that 14 percent of U.S. households are now on-line.The study showed America Online's market share rose to 18 percent of the home PC market, up from
7368 14 percent in January.CompuServe Corp held 5 percent of the home PC market, down a point from January. CompuServe's recently introduced WOW! family-oriented service accounted for another one percent of the market. International Wireless's Prodigy users accounted for four percent, down from five percent.The market for direct Internet access remains
7368 extremely fragmented, the market researchers said.Even the most popular home consumer Internet service provider, Netcom On-Line Communications Inc, has only captured 8 percent of the ISP market, Odyssey said.AT&amp;T Corp's WorldNet, the second most popular direct Internet access service, has attracted seven percent, while MCI Communications Corp and Performance Systems
7368 International Inc have 4 percent each. The rest of the market is divided among a myriad of smaller players.On the browser front, Odyssey's Homefront survey indicated that Netscape Communications Corp still leads in the battle for at-home surfers versus Microsoft Corp.The Netscape Navigator is more popular than Microsoft's Internet Explorer,
7368 with 54 percent of households surfing the Internet using the Netscape version, compared to 6 percent using the Microsoft browser. The survey found that the Internet is changing the way consumers evaluate a commercial online service and that the importance of proprietary content is "clearly decreasing."When asked to choose between
7368 quality of access to the Internet and quality of proprietary content, 41 percent chose quality of access to the Internet while only 29 percent deemed quality of the online service's proprietary content more important, the researchers said.Six months ago 37 percent chose content over Internet access.Odyssey President Nick Donatiello said
7368 online service providers have not risen to the challenge posed by ISPs."Commercial online services have to convince consumers that they are better on some dimension that's important, if not proprietary content, then ease-of-use, or content packaging, or customization, or something," Donatiello said."Pathetically slow Internet gateways and pricing schemes that seem
7368 to ignore the fact that they are now competing directly with ISPs just make it harder," he said.Odyssey's Homefront study is the largest in-depth national survey tracking the home computing market. Research is based on interviews with 2,000 consumers.-- Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1736</

7396 Ultramar Corp and Diamond Shamrock Inc agreed to a merger under which each share of Diamond Shamrock will be converted into 1.02 shares of Ultramar common. The transaction will be accounted for on a pooling of interests basis and is expected to be accretive to earnings. The new company will
7396 have a combined equity market value of more than $2.3 billion. Full text of the companies' statement follows.---PRESS RELEASE----------------------------------- Merger of Equals Will Create One of the Largest North American Petroleum Refiner/Marketers; Transaction Expected to be Accretive to EarningsGREENWICH, Conn., and SAN ANTONIO, Sept. 23 /PRNewswire/ -- Ultramar Corporation (NYSE:
7396 ULR) and Diamond Shamrock, Inc. (NYSE: DRM), petroleum refining and marketing companies with strong presences in different regions of North America, announced today that they have agreed to merge. In the merger of equals, each share of Diamond Shamrock will be converted into 1.02 shares of Ultramar common stock. The
7396 new company will have combined revenues of more than $8 billion and a combined equity market value of over $2.3 billion. The transaction will be accounted for on a pooling of interests basis and is expected to be accretive to earnings. The combined company will be named Ultramar Diamond Shamrock
7396 Corp. and will be headquartered in San Antonio, Texas.Roger Hemminghaus, chairman, chief executive officer and president of Diamond Shamrock, will become chairman and chief executive officer of Ultramar Diamond Shamrock. Jean Gaulin, chairman, chief executive officer and president of Ultramar, will become the new company's vice chairman, president and chief
7396 operating officer. Mr. Gaulin will become Ultramar Diamond Shamrock's CEO by the end of 1998 and will become chairman within three years thereafter. The Board of Directors will be comprised of twelve individuals, with six each coming from the boards of Ultramar and Diamond Shamrock.Ultramar Diamond Shamrock expects to pay
7396 an annual dividend of $1.10 per share of common stock, which is Ultramar's current dividend rate. "This is truly a merger of equals between two strong companies that fit together remarkably well," said Mr. Hemminghaus."By joining together, we will leverage both our companies' considerable strengths in petroleum refining and marketing
7396 and create new opportunities for cost savings and strategic expansion. The merger will position the new company for greater penetration of attractive western U.S. markets, including Arizona, California and Nevada.""This is a combination of two companies which have high quality assets and management. We will be building a new company
7396 with the best management and business opportunities from both sides. Our corporate cultures are complementary and we are all looking forward to working together," Mr. Hemminghaus said."Ultramar and Diamond Shamrock are ideal partners," said Mr. Gaulin. "Diamond Shamrock's large retail network and significant presence in the U.S. Southwest strongly complement
7396 Ultramar's refining and marketing operations in California and Canada. With such strong regional anchors, our new company has tremendous potential to expand into new markets and improve performance in existing ones.""This merger creates exciting opportunities for the shareholders of both companies," Mr. Gaulin said. "The transaction is expected to be
7396 accretive to earnings. Ultramar Diamond Shamrock will benefit from enhanced earnings growth prospects, less earnings volatility, increased geographic diversity of revenues, and significant merger savings."Cost savings related to the merger are projected to be at least $75 million annually, based primarily on the realization of operating synergies and reduction of
7396 overhead and administrative costs, with $25 million estimated to be realized in 1997 and the full $75 million to be realized each year thereafter. One-time transaction costs are estimated at $17 million, which will be booked in 1996. In addition there are approximately $50 million in transition costs, most of
7396 which will be booked in 1996. It is anticipated that approximately 200 positions will be eliminated as a result of the merger, out of a combined workforce of about 17,000 employees.The Boards of Directors of both Ultramar and Diamond Shamrock have approved the merger. The transaction is subject to approval
7396 by the shareholders of both companies, and to customary regulatory approvals. The parties expect the transaction to close at the end of this year.Wasserstein Perella &amp; Co., Inc. acted as financial adviser to Diamond Shamrock and provided a fairness opinion. Merrill Lynch &amp; Co. acted as principal financial adviser to
7396 Ultramar and provided a fairness opinion.Ultramar Corporation, headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, is a petroleum refining and marketing company which operates in California, Eastern Canada and the northeast United States. Ultramar employs approximately 4,000 people. Ultramar operates two refineries, in Wilmington, California, and in Quebec Province, with a combined capacity of
7396 250,000 barrels per day. In California, it markets gasoline through 360 locations (150 owned and operated by the company) under the Ultramar and Beacon brands. Ultramar's Eastern Canadian retail network includes 1,400 locations (of which approximately 630 are company-owned or controlled under long-term lease). In Eastern Canada, Ultramar markets gasoline
7396 under the Ultramar and Sergaz brands. Within this network, Ultramar owns and operates 110 convenience stores and plans to grow this number significantly over the next several years. Ultramar is one of the largest home heating oil companies in North America and sells heating oil to over 175,000 households in
7396 Eastern Canada and New England.Diamond Shamrock, Inc., headquartered in San Antonio, is a leading refiner and marketer of petroleum products in the Southwest, with a growing mix of related businesses. Diamond Shamrock has two Texas refineries with a combined capacity of 225,000 barrels per day, and markets gasoline and convenience
7396 store items through approximately 2,700 Corner Store, Stop N Go and Diamond Shamrock locations (1,500 owned and operated by the company) in nine states. Diamond Shamrock markets the largest-selling gasoline brand in Texas and the second largest in Colorado and New Mexico. Its revenue from convenience store merchandise approaches $1
7396 billion annually. Diamond Shamrock also produces petrochemical feedstocks and operates the world's largest commercial natural gas liquids storage facility, serving the refining and petrochemicals industries in the Texas Gulf Coast area. Diamond Shamrock has more than 13,000 employees. SOURCE Ultramar Corporation/NOTE TO EDITORS: Conference Call For The Media With Ultramar
