7624 generally is exempted from the rollback and annual increase limit, the measure would have significant fiscal effects and further erode the financial flexibility of local governments in Oregon, S&amp;P said.The long-term risk of Measure 47 for most local governments may be credit deterioration over time as a result of reduced
7624 flexibility to finance growth, S&amp;P said.Measure 47's impact could be even more significant for special districts. Unlike cities and counties, special districts' revenues typically are concentrated in property taxes, the rating agency said. --Adam Entous, 415-677-2511</
7625 Standard &amp; Poor's Corp warned on Monday that an Oregon ballot measure would reduce the likelihood of passing taxes submitted to voters and could reduce the financial flexibility of localities.Measure 46 would require approval from at least 50 percent of all registered voters for any new tax or revenue increases.
7625 The current authorization requirement is for only a majority of those who actually turn out to vote.S&amp;P said the measure, which will appear on the November ballot, could have long-term negative credit implications for municipal issuers in the state.S&amp;P said in Monday's CreditWeek Municipal newsletter that passage of Measure 46
7625 was likely to reduce the likelihood of passing tax or revenue measures submitted to the voters, as voter turnout is rarely large enough to result in majority approval by those registered.The credit implications of this measure include the potential for reduced financial flexibility in the form of both revenues available
7625 to pay for operations and the ability to meet infrastructure needs, S&amp;P sid.S&amp;P said the main effect of this measure would be to limit the ability of local government to pass general obligation bonds to fund infrastructure during a time of substantial growth in the economy.While some governments may try
7625 to substitute lease financings for general obligation debt, S&amp;P said this option is limited because governments would need to cover lease payments out of operating budgets."Credit quality could be at risk to the extent governments were to overburden operating budgets with lease payments or to the extend that needed infrastructure
7625 was not funded," the rating agency said.S&amp;P said Measure 46's language imposes the same voter approval requirement on general obligation bond's authorized since November 1990. This retroactivity may or may not be upheld in court, the rating agency said. --Adam Entous, 415-677-2511</

7642 study by the investigative arm of Congress warns of profound consequences of relaxing the 200-year old laws that give the Postal Service a monopoly on the delivery of letters. 7677 Germany, the bastion of stability policies, has convinced Europe of the urgent need for a pact to ensure public budgets are kept in check once a single currency is launched in 1999.Its concern now is to make sure that the framework deal thrashed out at last weekend's meeting of European
7677 finance ministers in Dublin is fleshed out with clear definitions and penalties which give the pact real deterrent value.German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the architect of the original plans for a stability pact on fiscal issues, said he was satisfied with the meeting's outcome and added on Monday that he
7677 saw no major problems gaining agreement on the details."With a bit of good will, I see no more insurmountable problems," Waigel said in response to a question at a political party meeting in Munich.Europe's ministers and central bank governors agreed in Dublin that countries participating in monetary union must keep
7677 their budget deficits below three percent of total economic output or face sanctions.If they then failed to address the problem, the "sanction" funds deposited in a European account would be converted into a fine and transferred to EU budgets, the officials agreed.The German delegation's insistence that it was pleased with
7677 the results of the Dublin talks seemed to many observers there nonetheless to mask some irritation that progress in nailing down the pact had not been quicker.The finer points of the plan -- which will be crucial to its effectiveness -- were simply referred to working committees ordered to seek
7677 a consensus in the next few months.The questions of the size of the sanctions or fines and of precise definitions for "exceptional and temporary" circumstances which would allow a country to acceptably exceed the specified deficit limit were left open.While this weekend's agreement on the basics convinced financial markets on
7677 Monday that Europe is serious in its EMU intentions, economists say tough sanctions will be essential in harnessing market credibility for the Euro."The sanctions have to be such that they are visible," said Thomas Mayer, senior economist at Goldman Sachs in Frankfurt."It has to be a sizeable amount of money.
7677 The pact will not present a credible threat if the sanctions or fines are a small amount of money which a government could do without."Germany, which has presented by far the most hardline conditions for the way it believes the pact should operate, will now have to try to push
7677 these through in discussions of European experts in the build-up to a December summit meeting.But it has found strong opposition for some of its ideas.On the size of sanctions and fines, a German proposal calling for a deposit of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point of excessive deficit
7677 is still on the table.But it may lose out to a European Commission proposal for a a more lenient deposit of 0.1 or 0.2 percent of GDP per percentage point of excess, capped at a maximum of 0.5 percent.EU sources also say many believe Waigel's proposal that a country should
7677 be considered in the exceptional circumstance of heavy recession only after its economy had shrunk by two percent or more is unacceptably strict.Some argue that it is even an error to try to decide in advance what the "exceptional circumstances" may include -- which the Germans view as essential if
7677 the pact is to have any sort of fast "semi-automatic application"."Exceptional means precisely that it could not be defined in advance," one EU source said.But Mayer also believed it was important to establish a clear definition in advance."An exceptional circumsance must be in excess of a normal small recession, which
7677 ought to be covered by the normal fluctuation in deficits," he said.</

7685 this year, revised from a forecast of a fall of 0.4 percent on August 20.Swiss institutes and banks have dropped 1996 GDP projections for growth of around one percent at the start of the year, with recent estimates hovering at zero growth to a 0.5 percent fall.BAK's forecast for 1997

7686 Nine out of 10 women are still alive five years after breast cancer treatment, according to a new study presented by cancer experts on Monday.Speaking at a conference on cancer in Vienna, Professor Harry Bartelink, Head of Radiation Oncology at Netherlands Cancer Institute, said the preliminary results of the study
7686 showed breast cancer treatment was achieving impressive survival rates.The study, conducted in 35 countries, involved over 5,500 women who all received a combination of radiotherapy and conservative surgery for tumours up to five cm (two ins) in diameter."That we are able to prevent local recurrences in 92 percent of our
7686 patients after five years in so many countries in Europe, that is a breakthrough," he told Reuters.But he warned it was unlikely the survival rate for women 10 years after treatment would ever be as good as for five years, because the disease often recurs after 15 to 20 years.One
7686 European woman in 10 develops breast cancer.Bartelink told delegates at the European Society of Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology conference that previous trials revealed similar survival rates, but those tests had such variations between centres that a new quality control programme had to be set up.He said the overall survival rate
7686 had improved by 20 percent with the new study, and the control rate by 15 percent.In the latest trial, the patients were divided into two groups, one receiving an extra radiotherapy boost dose and the other no additional dose.He said in two years long-term patient follow-up should show whether the
7686 radiotherapy boost dose increased survival chances even more than the current 92 percent rate."In the meantime, it is clear the combination of radiotherapy and conservative surgery offers women effective treatment for breast cancer," he said.The radiotherapy, given as a small daily dose over six weeks, produced virtually no side-effects, he
7686 added. The psychological burden of having the disease was the worst part."These results give hope to both patients and doctors," he said, but noted it was important to establish quality controls across Europe so the disease could be properly monitored.In a separate study, experts found that smoking in lung cancer
7686 patients reduced the effect of radiation treatment."Cancer patients who are smokers should be told that giving up smoking can improve their chances of survival," said Dr Cai Grau at Denmark's Aarhus University Hospital Oncology Department.Smokers had less oxygen in their blood, which was needed for a good response to radiotherapy,
7686 he said.Another new study found small or single doses of radiotherapy provided effective relief for terminally ill cancer patients, with no severe adverse effects."Despite this, there are still many patients in Europe who are not being offered small doses of radiotherapy as part of their palliative care," said Jens Overgaard,
7686 Professor of Oncology at Aarhus University.Radiotherapy was not being made available to patients simply because many health professionals were not aware of its benefits, but it was a good, low-cost treatment, he said.</

7694 period.On a positive note, it said the results of the August survey showed the first signs of slowing decline in western Europe and that production continued to grow in North America."In western Europe stocks are finally coming into line with actual demand," IISI said in a statement.British production rose 6.4

7707 Britain and France occupied defeated Austria from 1945 to 1955.Washington and Britain feared Moscow might launch an invasion from the eastern sector of Austria under its control to seize the whole of the country as a satellite.Soldiers from both countries hid scores of weapons depots in western and southern Austria

7728 The European Union's three Nordic members, with different currency policy pasts and varying degrees of economic strength, are all debating possible closer links with the bloc's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).Like other European countries, Denmark, Sweden and Finland are considering their options as the 15-nation EU prepares for the final stage
7728 of economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999."The link is that monetary union is approaching," said economist Wike Groenenberg at investment bank Salomon Brothers (corrects name of bank from Morgan Stanley).Denmark, already in the present ERM which limits fluctuations between participating currencies, has decided not to join monetary union and
7728 will instead seek a close relationship with the planned single currency.Copenhagen therefore takes keen interest in a new currency mechanism, dubbed "ERM2", which will be set up to link countries outside EMU with the euro currency, saying the crown should trade within narrow bands.Finland, determined to be among the first
7728 to join monetary union, may decide soon to link the markka to the current ERM as it seeks to fulfil all the requirements laid down in the EU's Maastricht treaty for taking part in the single currency.In Sweden, Central Bank governor Urban Backstrom last week injected new life into fading
7728 market speculation about possible ERM membership, listing potential benefits of such a move, even though he reiterated that entry was not topical now."I believe that the time is ready to start discussing this issue because Sweden has become an increasingly stable country," Backstrom told Reuters during the weekend meeting of
7728 EU finance ministers and central bank heads in Dublin.Reacting to his remarks, Morgan Stanley's Groenenberg said: "His comments were rather strongly worded in favour of Sweden joining the ERM."Finland and Sweden, whose currencies are floating, only joined the EU last year while Denmark is a member since 1973.There was consensus
7728 at the Dublin meeting, which laid the foundations for critical areas of monetary union, on the outline for the new ERM.Ministers agreed that it should be voluntary and include relatively wide trading bands for currencies outside EMU.However, Denmark -- one of only a few EU countries which currently qualify for
7728 monetary union -- could enter with narrower fluctuation bands than the standard ones.Economy Minister Marianne Jelved, who had expressed concern ahead of the meeting, said she was satisfied with the talks."It seems like we can get a bilateral agreement between the ECB (the future European Central Bank) and the Danish
7728 National Bank and government," she told Reuters.Jelved had earlier said she liked the way the ERM worked before the currency turmoil of 1993 when it had fluctuation margins of 2.25 percent up or down for most participating currencies. The bands are now 15 percent.Finland is widely expected to join the
7728 present ERM soon.There was even market speculation that this would happen during the weekend meeting in Dublin but Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto told Reuters the issue had not been discussed.Any decision to join the ERM seems to be further away in neighbouring Sweden even if Backstrom said he personally believed
7728 such a move would be desirable later.ERM membership could underscore Sweden's increased economic stability and also further demonstrate its determination to continue with a policy aimed at low inflation and sound public finances also if it opted to stay outside EMU, he said.But he said it was important to have
7728 support in the Swedish society for any decision to join the ERM, which currently groups 10 of the EU's 15 member countries. "We will see how that discussion is developing," he said.Backstrom noted that there were critical voices in the current Swedish debate and he suggested that Sweden could not
7728 join ERM if there was strong opposition.</

7751 The International Labour Organisation (ILO) on Monday criticised working conditions in agriculture, singling out pervasive use of child labour, long hours, low wages and slack safety standards.Despite growth in agricultural production, millions of farm workers earn a subsistence-level living while being exposed to pesticides and other hazards, the United Nations
7751 agency said in a hard-hitting report.The ILO, which promotes social justice and labour standards, called for greater opportunities for collective bargaining to improve conditions in the sector.The report, "Wage Workers in Agriculture: Conditions of Employment and Work", will be discussed by government officials, employers' groups and workers' representatives from 30
7751 countries who opened a week-long meeting in Geneva on Monday.Child labour is pervasive among agricultural wage workers and can reach 30 per cent of the workforce in some countries, according to the 97-page report. Farm workers are also exploited through bonded labour."We are talking about 400 to 500 million wage
7751 workers in agriculture. That is one-sixth of the world's labour force," Philippe Egger, author of the report, told a news briefing.The report said: "Hours of work tend to be long, often over 45 hours per week. The conditions of transport of agricultural workers in several countries are appalling and need
7751 urgent attention."The presence of child labour in agriculture, either recruited directly or a part of a family team for a full day's work, is widespread."There is a trend away from permanent forms of employment to more casual and seasonal employment with little or no social protection. Occupational injury compensation in
7751 agriculture is often limited or insufficient, or both," it said.While global trade in agricultural commodities has grown by roughly three per cent a year throughout the last decade, the benefits have been unequally distributed, according to the ILO.Representation of wage workers by workers' organisations in agriculture was very weak. "There
7751 is very little collective bargaining," Egger said."Our findings show one worker in two in the agricultural sector in wage employment is in poverty. In 40 per cent of countries that we have documented, workers cannot earn enough to sustain themselves, let alone their families," he added.Egger said agriculture was a
7751 hazardous occupation. ILO findings showed that in three out of four countries, the rate of fatal injuries in agriculture was above the overall average.The report said pesticide poisoning in some countries accounted for up to 14 per cent of all occupational injuries in the agricultural sector and 10 per cent
7751 of all fatal injuries."There should be a much stronger application of basic rights of workers, the ILO fundamental human rights standards, to this category of workers," Egger told reporters."We would like to see much stronger emphasis on collective bargaining to enable workers and employers to collective negotiate terms and conditions
7751 of employment. This is a standard ILO recipe, but it is something not happening at all or very little in the agricultural sector," he added.</

7755 The U.S. army on Monday said it has begun notifying about 1,100 soldiers and their family members that an army dental hygienist at a German post has tested positive for the HIV virus that causes AIDS.The hygienist, who provided routine care at the Hanau medical clinic near Frankfurt from February
7755 1995 to June 1996, was removed from direct patient care and sent back to the U.S., the U.S. army medical command in Germany said.His name and sex were not given,About 300 soldiers treated by the technician were now serving in Bosnia and neighbouring countries as part of Operation Joint Endeavor
7755 and another 300 soldiers and family members have returned to the U.S.Counselling sessions and tests for the deadly virus were being offered to people who were treated by the person concerned at the Hanau clinic, about 15 miles east of Frankfurt.An army spokeswoman said about 270 patients have so far
7755 come to the Hanau clinic since the announcement was made on Saturday, with 130 being confirmed as having been treated by the technician."There has been no hysteria," army spokeswoman Barbara Slifer said. 7755 initially tested positive for the HIV virus, which causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, in May and was removed from direct patient care. 7755 being confirmed positive, Slifer said.U.S. military commanders downplayed the significance of the incident, saying in a statement that "risk assessment officials have determined that the patient risk of contracting the virus from an HIV-infected healthcare provider is zero"."The scope of the dental hygienist's practice included only basic-level dental hygiene duties,
7755 further reducing the likelihood of exposure of the virus to a patient," it said.The army also said the soldier always wore gloves, mask and gowns and used sterlized instruments during patient care.The army noted a report by the U.S. Centre for Disease Control that said the only known case of
7755 the transfer of the HIV virus from a healthcare provider to a patient was in 1990 in Florida.A study of more than 22,000 cases showed no case of the virus being transmitted since 1991.</

7760 A possible merger between Sweden's two largest commercial banks, S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken, is an intriguing idea but hardly realistic, banking analysts said on Monday.Swedish business daily Dagens Industri (DI) reported at the weekend that the two banks had entered into "tentative" merger talks in recent weeks which would create a
7760 Nordic banking giant.Both banks declined to comment on the article, which was based on the comments of an unidentified source.Even so, shares in the two banks moved ahead strongly in an otherwise weak bourse on Monday as the market digested the news. At 1100 GMT S-E-Banken was 1.50 crowns higher
7760 at 60.50 crowns and Handelsbanken was up 4.5 at 159 crowns."He (DI's reporter) is probably right that the two managements have been talking to each other, but from there it's a long way to a full-blown merger. There are some massive obstacles," one banking analyst said.The appeal of a merger
7760 is evident. The two banks have a combined total of 732 branch offices in Sweden, and analysts said around a third of these could ultimately be axed.This would mean considerable potential for cost-cutting in an industry that is already extremely cost-efficient in an international perspective. With lending margins under pressure,
7760 this would be a welcome route to higher profits.Not only that, the volume advantages would be considerable. The two banks command 40 percent of the Swedish lending market, and Handelsbanken in particular has substantial interests in other Nordic countries.However, size could prove to be a disadvantage, one Swedish banking analyst
7760 said."A market share of 40 percent is pretty difficult to defend. This is a classic case of the whole being less than the sum of its parts," he said.But anlaysts said the main hurdle to the creation of a Nordic banking giant with a combined balance sheet total of over
7760 1,100 billion crowns ($166 billion) would be an unusually severe clash in the corporate cultures of the two banks.S-E-Banken falls firmly within the domain of Sweden's mighty Wallenberg dynasty, which controls or exerts a powerful influence in companies ranging from telecoms giant Ericsson to investment group Investor, which in turn
7760 controls a sizeable proportion of Swedish industry.Handelsbanken in turn has its own "sphere", which incorporates forestry group MoDo and industrial holding company Industrivarden.Merging the two banks would turn the structure of Swedish business and industry upside down, and the problems would not end there.Handelsbanken's traditionally conservative, cost-conscious approach to banking
7760 and its decentralised structure would be hard to marry with S-E-Banken's more adventurous but highly centralised structure.Then there is the problem of ownership. Initially, Handelsbanken would account for around 60 percent of the equity capital of the new bank, but S-E-Banken would hardly be willing to enter an alliance on
7760 unequal terms.Add the frictions caused as thousands of employees are made redundant and a probably sceptical attitude from competition authorities, and the attraction of a merger recedes further.In fact, there is at least one strong indication the problem will never arise.The Stockholm Stock Exchange, which has right of access to
7760 any information that could potentially move share prices, said it would not act on the report."We have received such information and we see no reason to take any measures," spokesman Hans Edenhammar said. ($1=6.61 crowns)</

7786 Europe's top financial officials this weekend cleared key hurdles in their quest for a stability pact to control public spending once countries enter monetary union, but failed to agree exactly how the deal will work.European Union finance ministers and central bank governors said at the end of informal one-day talks
7786 in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday the broad outline of plans to punish governments that exceeded certain budget deficit limits were now in place.But specifics of the plan -- including the size of fines to be levied on offenders -- were referred to committees in the hope a consensus could be
7786 thrashed out by the end of the year.German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the architect of the plans to ensure fiscal discipline within Europe's monetary union -- set to start on January 1, 1999 -- said he was satisfied with progress although issues remained unresolved.After the meeting Waigel said, "I am
7786 satisfied. We are following exactly on the road we started on one year ago."The German minister initially proposed the concept of a stability pact as a means of ensuring that countries which pass the economic test set for entry to the single currency do not later become lax in their
7786 fiscal policies.The entry criteria for EMU laid down in the Maastricht Treaty require countries which want to meld their currencies into the Euro to meet targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budget deficits and public borrowing.The budgetary goals -- which call for annual deficits to total no more than
7786 three percent of gross domestic product and total debt of no more than 60 percent of GDP -- have proved by far the hardest for most countries to meet.This, combined with the fact that their fate on all the other criteria will be inextricably intertwined once the Euro has been
7786 established, meant there was a particular need for wideranging agreement on fiscal issues.European Union commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy echoed the views of many officials by saying this weekend that the planned stability pact was essential for the credibility of the new Euro in financial markets and with the general
7786 public.Without such a pact, overspending by one Euro member state could undermine the stability of the currency by driving up interest rates and damaging market trust in the Euro.Under the terms of the pact agreed in Dublin, countries will face sanctions if they notch up a deficit exceeding three percent
7786 of Gross Domestic Product unless they take immediate corrective action or face exceptional circumstances.French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet told reporters EU financial officials had agreed four key elements which would smooth the decision-making process and lay down clear rules on what delinquent countries could expect.Trichet said it had been
7786 agreed that the "exceptional and temporary circumstances" under which a country could exceed the three percent level without sanctions must be predefined.If these did not apply sanctions would always be levied and this would take the form of an interest-free deposit. Finally, if no action was taken, this deposit would
7786 be converted into a non-refundable fine.Ministers also said there was consensus, but not unanimous approval, on the idea that sanctions should be imposed within a calendar year of an excessive deficit being recorded.Countries would be expected to draw up their accounts for a year by the following March, and implement
7786 corrective action before the year-end, to avoid sanctions kicking in.But there was no consensus on the detail needed to flesh out the skeleton framework, leaving working parties with a large area of ground to cover by December, when ministers hope a complete pact will be ratified by a summit meeting.Officials
7786 said a German proposal calling for a deposit of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point of excessive deficit was still on the table alongside a European Commission proposal for a smaller deposit per percentage point, capped at a maximum of 0.5 percent."The type and size of (the deposits)
7786 has yet to be agreed," Waigel said.There was also no agreement on the precise definitions of exceptional circumstances -- an issue Germany sees as essential if the pact is to be applied swiftly and at least semi-automatically once a budget is exceeded.</

7803 Big B Inc., the drug store chain, said Monday it has rejected the latest takeover offer from Revco D.S. Inc., calling the $332 million bid inadequate and not in its best interests.Earlier this month, Revco, the nation's largest chain of drug stores, offered $15 a share in cash for the
7803 family-owned company after its initial offer in August of $14 per share was turned down.In the latest twist to the hostile takeover, Big B said it would consider other offers and will explore alternatives to maximize shareholders' value.Big B has said that it has already received inquiries from other interested
7803 parties, who were not identified.The company's board of directors has authorised Big B to provide confidential information to interested parties who enter into a confidentiality agreement, it said in a statement.The company said it has made no decision to sell the company but will consider appropriate offers.With 397 units throughout
7803 the nation's southeastern states, the Bessemer, Ala.-based drug store chain has had a tough time competing in the cost control environment of managed health care and against huge discount retailers.Big B has been hurt by shrinking profits, and Wall Street analysts say the company has little chance of staying independent.In
7803 a defensive play, Big B also said it has adopted a shareholder rights plan to distribute, as a dividend, one right for each share of common stock held by shareholders of record on Oct. 3.Under certain circumstances, if an individual or group were to acquire 10 percent or more of
7803 the company, or otherwise tried to gain control of the company, the rights would allow stockholders to acquire discount shares of common stock.The rights plan is to expire June 30, 1997, or earlier under circumstances that were not specified.Big B said Monday that it rejected the offer in part because
7803 of advice from Robinson-Humphrey Corp. Inc., its financial adviser, that the bid was financially inadequate.A Revco spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call seeking comment.Big B's stock was up 37.5 cents at $16.625, while Revco was up 12.50 cents at $25.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.</
7804 The U.S. Federal Reserve is scheduled to hold a pivotal meeting Tuesday to consider raising interest rates for the first time in about 1-1/2 years.At issue is whether the U.S. economy is robust enough to reignite inflation -- which would call for a rate hike to keep prices in check
7804 -- or whether a rate increase would instead stifle a struggling economy.A majority of economists polled by Reuters last week -- 17 of 30 -- believes the central bank will opt to raise short-term rates Tuesday, with all but one of those analysts expecting an increase of 0.25 percent.Even a
7804 small rate hike would lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and corporations, putting a damper on Wall Street and Main Street. President Bill Clinton, too, would balk at any brakes on the economy that would reduce his chances of a victory in the Nov. 5 election.Conflicting signs about the
7804 economy's health present strong arguments for both camps in the Fed -- the anti-inflation hawks, mainly at the Fed's regional banks, and the so-called doves, mostly political appointees on the Fed board in Washington.At a seven-year low of 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at a level that has historically
7804 led to higher inflation and demands for higher wages.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Firms have enjoyed fat profit margins for 5-1/2 years of economic expansion
7804 and thus have some leeway to absorb the higher labour costs. But it is not clear how long they can go without raising prices.While the job market is tight, and companies are stepping up production and rebuilding inventories, retail sales have slowed and the housing market has weakened.If the Fed
7804 tightens credit because wages are rising, it risks giving ammunition to critics who see it as a pawn of Wall Street. And if the Democrats then regain control of Congress, lawmakers may seize on the pre-election rate rise as a reason to rein in the Fed, especially the regional banks.On
7804 the other hand, some of Clinton's appointees to the Fed board may be sensitive to suspicions that they would favour the president and thus be more inclined to raise rates to prove their mettle to the markets and their colleagues.Eight of the 12 regional Fed banks have called for a
7804 rate increase, and consensus-minded central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan may give in to avoid a revolt Tuesday.In the end, the Fed's decision may be more important symbolically than economically. While a small rate rise would have only a minor impact on the economy and could easily be reversed later, it
7804 would clearly signal the Fed's priorities, and that is why Wall Street and Washington are watching so closely.</
7805 U.S. households with direct access to the Internet via an Internet service provider (ISP) now outnumber homes where computer users reach the Internet via a commercial online service, according to a new study.Market research firm Odyssey said its latest Homefront survey, released Monday, found that 48 percent of households surfing
7805 the Internet from home are using an ISP, while 35 percent use a commercial online service for Internet access.The findings represent a sharp turnaround from six months ago, when it found 54 percent of at-home Internet surfers used commercial online services, the research firm said. At the time only about
7805 30 percent of home computer users gained access to the Internet via Internet service providers.The new survey found that the Internet is changing the way consumers evaluate a commercial online service and that the importance of proprietary content is "clearly decreasing."When asked to choose between the importance of quality of
7805 access to the Internet and quality of proprietary content, 41 percent chose quality of access to the Internet while only 29 percent deemed quality of the online service's proprietary content more important, the researchers said.Six months ago 37 percent chose content over Internet access.Odyssey President Nick Donatiello said this indicates
7805 that online service providers have not risen to the challenge posed by ISPs."Commercial online services have to convince consumers that they are better on some dimension that's important, if not proprietary content, then ease-of-use, or content packaging, or customisation, or something," Donatiello said."Pathetically slow Internet gateways and pricing schemes that
7805 seem to ignore the fact that they are now competing directly with ISPs just make it harder," he said.Odyssey also said its latest study showed that 14 percent of U.S. households are now on-line.The survey showed America Online's market share rose to 18 percent of the home PC market, up
7805 from 14 percent in January.CompuServe Corp. held 5 percent of the home PC market, down a point from January. CompuServe's recently introduced WOW! family-oriented service accounted for another one percent of the market.International Wireless's Prodigy users accounted for four percent, down from five percent.The market for direct Internet access remains
7805 extremely fragmented, the market researchers said.Even the most popular home consumer Internet service provider, Netcom On-Line Communications Inc., has only captured 8 percent of the ISP market, Odyssey said.AT&amp;T Corp.'s WorldNet, the second most popular direct Internet access service, has attracted seven percent, while MCI Communications Corp. and Performance Systems
7805 International Inc. have 4 percent each.The rest of the market is divided among a myriad of smaller players.On the browser front, Odyssey's Homefront survey indicated that Netscape Communications Corp. still leads in the battle for at-home World Wide Web surfers versus Microsoft Corp.The Netscape Navigator is more popular than Microsoft's
7805 Internet Explorer, with 54 percent of households surfing the Internet using the Netscape version, compared to 6 percent using the Microsoft browser.Odyssey's Homefront study is the largest in-depth national survey tracking the home computing market. Research is based on interviews with 2,000 consumers.</

7809 The proceeds of serious crime being laundered in the Cayman Islands now risk being seized by the islands' authorities under the terms of a new law, the Caribbean island group said on Monday."This legislation makes it clear that the Cayman Islands is not a place for those who wish to
7809 hide illicit proceeds," said Richard Coles, the islands' attorney general, in a statement released in London."It will also reassure those legitimate users of the financial services in the Cayman Islands that their business will not be tainted by any illicit proceeds," he added.The Cayman Islands, which passed the law late
7809 on Friday, is the first centre in the Caribbean to introduce such legislation. It is based on British law. Britain welcomed the move."This decision marks an important step in the Caymans' fight against international money laundering and will help to ensure that the Islands are not used to hide or
7809 launder illicit proceeds," a British foreign office spokesman said.The law makes it a criminal offence if a provider of financial services fails to report any suspicions that a client may be involved with or be benefiting from crime.It also allows applications to be made to the courts for an order
7809 restraining and eventually confiscating criminal proceeds, whether in the form of property or the contents of a bank account, pending prosecution.Confiscation orders made in designated nations may now also be registered in the islands and enforced by its grand court.Britain is pressing other territories to follow the islands' example as
7809 soon as possible, the statement added.</

7811 Germany, the bastion of stability policies, has convinced Europe of the urgent need for a pact to ensure public budgets are kept in check once a single currency is launched in 1999.Its concern now is to make sure that the framework deal thrashed out at last weekend's meeting of European
7811 finance ministers in Dublin is fleshed out with clear definitions and penalties which give the pact real deterrent value.German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the architect of the original plans for a stability pact on fiscal issues, said he was satisfied with the meeting's outcome and added on Monday that he
7811 saw no major problems gaining agreement on the details."With a bit of good will, I see no more insurmountable problems," Waigel said in response to a question at a political party meeting in Munich.Europe's ministers and central bank governors agreed in Dublin that countries participating in monetary union must keep
7811 their budget deficits below three percent of total economic output or face sanctions.If they then failed to address the problem, the "sanction" funds deposited in a European account would be converted into a fine and transferred to EU budgets, the officials agreed.The German delegation's insistence that it was pleased with
7811 the results of the Dublin talks seemed to many observers there nonetheless to mask some irritation that progress in nailing down the pact had not been quicker.The finer points of the plan -- which will be crucial to its effectiveness -- were simply referred to working committees ordered to seek
7811 a consensus in the next few months.The questions of the size of the sanctions or fines and of precise definitions for "exceptional and temporary" circumstances which would allow a country to acceptably exceed the specified deficit limit were left open.While this weekend's agreement on the basics convinced financial markets on
7811 Monday that Europe is serious in its EMU intentions, economists say tough sanctions will be essential in harnessing market credibility for the Euro."The sanctions have to be such that they are visible," said Thomas Mayer, senior economist at Goldman Sachs in Frankfurt."It has to be a sizeable amount of money.
7811 The pact will not present a credible threat if the sanctions or fines are a small amount of money which a government could do without."Germany, which has presented by far the most hardline conditions for the way it believes the pact should operate, will now have to try to push
7811 these through in discussions of European experts in the build-up to a December summit meeting.But it has found strong opposition for some of its ideas.On the size of sanctions and fines, a German proposal calling for a deposit of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point of excessive deficit
7811 is still on the table.But it may lose out to a European Commission proposal for a a more lenient deposit of 0.1 or 0.2 percent of GDP per percentage point of excess, capped at a maximum of 0.5 percent.EU sources also say many believe Waigel's proposal that a country should
7811 be considered in the exceptional circumstance of heavy recession only after its economy had shrunk by two percent or more is unacceptably strict.Some argue that it is even an error to try to decide in advance what the "exceptional circumstances" may include -- which the Germans view as essential if
7811 the pact is to have any sort of fast "semi-automatic application"."Exceptional means precisely that it could not be defined in advance," one EU source said.But Mayer also believed it was important to establish a clear definition in advance."An exceptional circumsance must be in excess of a normal small recession, which
7811 ought to be covered by the normal fluctuation in deficits," he said.</
7812 At least 18 people have been killed in two days of clashes between South African mine workers fighting with sticks, knives and blasting explosives, police said on Monday.They said the fighting, apparently sparked by ethnic rivalry between Pondo and Sotho workers, erupted at Buffelsfontein gold mine northwest of Johannesburg early

7823 The European Union's three Nordic members, with different currency policy pasts and varying degrees of economic strength, are all debating possible closer links with the bloc's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).Like other European countries, Denmark, Sweden and Finland are considering their options as the 15-nation EU prepares for the final stage
7823 of economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999."The link is that monetary union is approaching," said economist Wike Groenenberg at investment bank Salomon Brothers.Denmark, already in the present ERM which limits fluctuations between participating currencies, has decided not to join monetary union and will instead seek a close relationship with
7823 the planned single currency.Copenhagen therefore takes keen interest in a new currency mechanism, dubbed "ERM2", which will be set up to link countries outside EMU with the euro currency, saying the crown should trade within narrow bands.Finland, determined to be among the first to join monetary union, may decide soon
7823 to link the markka to the current ERM as it seeks to fulfil all the requirements laid down in the EU's Maastricht treaty for taking part in the single currency.In Sweden, Central Bank governor Urban Backstrom last week injected new life into fading market speculation about possible ERM membership, listing
7823 potential benefits of such a move, even though he reiterated that entry was not topical now."I believe that the time is ready to start discussing this issue because Sweden has become an increasingly stable country," Backstrom told Reuters during the weekend meeting of EU finance ministers and central bank heads
7823 in Dublin.Reacting to his remarks, Morgan Stanley's Groenenberg said: "His comments were rather strongly worded in favour of Sweden joining the ERM."Finland and Sweden, whose currencies are floating, only joined the EU last year while Denmark is a member since 1973.There was consensus at the Dublin meeting, which laid the
7823 foundations for critical areas of monetary union, on the outline for the new ERM.Ministers agreed that it should be voluntary and include relatively wide trading bands for currencies outside EMU.However, Denmark -- one of only a few EU countries which currently qualify for monetary union -- could enter with narrower
7823 fluctuation bands than the standard ones.Economy Minister Marianne Jelved, who had expressed concern ahead of the meeting, said she was satisfied with the talks."It seems like we can get a bilateral agreement between the ECB (the future European Central Bank) and the Danish National Bank and government," she told Reuters.Jelved
7823 had earlier said she liked the way the ERM worked before the currency turmoil of 1993 when it had fluctuation margins of 2.25 percent up or down for most participating currencies. The bands are now 15 percent.Finland is widely expected to join the present ERM soon.There was even market speculation
7823 that this would happen during the weekend meeting in Dublin but Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto told Reuters the issue had not been discussed.Any decision to join the ERM seems to be further away in neighbouring Sweden even if Backstrom said he personally believed such a move would be desirable later.ERM
7823 membership could underscore Sweden's increased economic stability and also further demonstrate its determination to continue with a policy aimed at low inflation and sound public finances also if it opted to stay outside EMU, he said.But he said it was important to have support in the Swedish society for any
7823 decision to join the ERM, which currently groups 10 of the EU's 15 member countries. "We will see how that discussion is developing," he said.Backstrom noted that there were critical voices in the current Swedish debate and he suggested that Sweden could not join ERM if there was strong opposition.</

7834 the bruised German unit at 1.9042 marks.The lira, which is unlikely to qualify for merger with the euro in 1999, was near two-month highs at 1004.30 per mark.The mark regained some ground later during Monday's session but remained lower compared with Friday's close in Europe."The real difference is both the
7834 politicians and the market are poring over details and conditions of EMU when it happens, not if it happens," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank.As expected, the meeting reached agreement on a budgetary stability pact to come into effect after European economic and monetary union (EMU) starts in 1999 and
7834 a post-EMU ERM II.These agreements were flagged in advance of the informal Dublin meeting and the fine details have yet to be released.Yet, analysts said the lack of dissent at the meeting and the official comments left little doubt about the committment to start EMU on time in 1999 among
7834 at least six countries."The conclusions ... don't offer us any new cataclysmic development, but what the market is being squeezed into acknowledging is that the proposals are now credible and the details are practicable," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch.For example, official comments that
7834 the ERM II would target the current broad 15 percent fluctuation bands would be seen as realistic by most players in the market, he said.Even British officials, traditionally the most sceptical EU delegation, acknowledged increased momentum toward EMU. "I get the feeling ever more clearly that it is going to
7834 go ahead," said Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Saturday.German finance minister Theo Waigel said he was satisfied with the agreement on the stability pact, crucial to convincing the German public of the stability of the new currency. "We are following exactly the road we started on one year
7834 ago," he said.France was similarly impressed by the level of agreement. "This meeting has been one of the most productive we have attended," said Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet.Traders were wary of getting over-optimistic about a process that still has several hurdles to clear, but they said there was
7834 nothing from the weekend meeting to upset the applecart."This looks like a sewn up deal and from a market point of view all the bad news seems to be factored out," said Henry Wilkes, senior trader at Switzerland's Bank Julius Baer."There's a gnawing feeling everything just looks too rosy, but
7834 the stability pact is a big thing in its favour," he said.The passing of the bulk of the 1997 European budgets without major upset has further calmed the markets in recent weeks, with the French franc more than reversing its pre-budget jitters."Credibility in EMU can be seen clearly in the
7834 Ecu's actual/ theoretical spread, which has narrowed to 0.6 percent from close to one percent in recent weeks," said Prendergast at Merrill.The Ecu spread measures the discount of market traded Ecu to its theoretical value derived from the constituent 12 EU currencies. The more likely EMU is perceived to be,
7834 the closer to par the spread moves and is often seen as a key barometer.</
7835 An overwhelming 85 percent of Chrysler Canada Ltd. workers participating in a ratification vote on Sunday voted in favor of a three-year contract that limits the company's ability to contract out jobs.About 42 percent of the 12,600 unionized members of the Chrysler Corp. unit's Canadian workforce turned out for the
7835 vote, officials at the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union said.The result, widely expected after CAW president Buzz Hargrove urged the 3,500 workers at company's assembly plants to accept the offer, sets the stage for talks with the local subsidiaries of the other two Big Three carmakers."Workers and their communities deserve
7835 to share in the success of the corporations -- this contract recognizes the contribution that workers have made to that success," Hargrove said while while announcing the result.Hargrove has said the CAW will announce Monday if it will next target Ford Motor Co. or General Motors Corp..Talks with GM, which
7835 is trying to outsource more of its production, are expected to be tough.The deal with Chrysler, reached in a last-minute session ahead of a strike deadline Tuesday, provides for about 300 new jobs and wage increases and projected cost-of-living allowances totaling 10.2 percent over three years.Chrysler has said it will
7835 replace any job it contracts out with a similar job at one of its plants. It has also promised not to sell or close any plants over the life of the contract.The union will use the Chrysler deal as a blueprint for talks with Ford and GM in a strategy
7835 called pattern bargaining, used by the CAW and its U.S. counterpart, the United Autoworkers, for decades.The UAW earlier this month settled recently with Ford, which makes it likely that the CAW will choose GM as its next target.</

7836 the world's least volatile due tosteady exports of natural gas and agricultural products. 7845 An Irish guerrilla suspect was killed on Monday during police raids said to have foiled an imminent IRA bomb attack in Britain.The dead man was wounded in a shoot-out as police officers arrested him and five other suspects. Police said he died in hospital shortly afterwards.There were no immediate details
7845 of the shooting incident or the identity of the dead man but it was certain to inflame the fragile peace process in Northern Ireland.Police said they had recovered a "very large" quantity of explosives as well as firearms and bomb-making equipment."The operation has undoubtedly frustrated a serious imminent IRA (Irish
7845 Republican Army) terrorist attack on the British mainland involving the deployment of a large vehicle bomb likely to have caused grave loss of life and massive disruption," police said in a statement.The IRA has planted a number of bombs in Britain since calling off a 17-month long ceasefire in February,
7845 citing British intransigence over the progress of peace efforts in Northern Ireland.British and Irish security sources had speculated last week that the guerrillas might be preparing to call a new ceasefire in their 25-year-long campaign to end British rule of Northern Ireland.The IRA's political wing Sinn Fein has denied the
7845 reports and Monday's police swoop suggested that the guerrillas were in fact planning another large bomb attack.Sinn Fein has been excluded from all-party peace talks that started in Belfast in June on a political settlement for Northern Ireland because of the IRA's refusal to reinstate its ceasefire.Chief Sinn Fein strategist
7845 Martin McGuiness said on Saturday the talks should be scrapped because they were going nowhere.The last IRA attacks were in June when a truck bomb exploded in the middle of the northern English city of Manchester, injuring more than 200 people. Two weeks later IRA guerrillas fired mortars at a
7845 British army base in Germany. There were no injuries.Monday's police swoop was the third major setback for the IRA this year. In February an IRA guerrilla blew himself up with his own bomb on a London bus and police later found a bomb factory at his London home.In July, British
7845 police arrested eight people and recovered bomb-making equipment sufficient for 36 bombs which they believe would have been used to target gas, water and electricity installations in London.</

7863 The Republic of the Philippines on Monday fixed the terms of its Brady exchange offer at 2.25 percent over US Treasuries for the 20-year fixed rate issue.In a statement released in London the Philippines said the clearing above the UST benchmark rate for the fixed rate bonds was 2.25 percent,
7863 the yield was 9.25 percent and the fixed rate semi-annual coupon was 8.75 percent. JP Morgan is arranging the exchange.Under the terms of the exchange, dated September 2, 1996, the Philippines is exchanging U.S. dollar-denominated series B principal collateralised interest reduction bonds, due in 2017, and dollar-denominated series A principal
7863 collateralised interest reduction bonds due in 2018, for new dollar-denominated fixed-rate bonds due in 2016.The Philippines said that because the offers to exchange the 2017 and 2018 bonds for floating rate bonds would result in issuance of less than $200 million, no floating rate bonds will be issued. However, people
7863 who submitted non-competitive offers to exchange the 2017 and 2018 issus for floating rate bonds will have the option to exchange them for fixed rate bonds at the applicable exchange value, the statement said.The issue price of the fixed rate bond is 0.95481.The maximum aggregate principal amount of fixed rate
7863 bonds to be issued is $690 million. The maximum aggregate principal amount of 2017 bonds to be exchanged is $628.093 million, while the maximum amount of 2018 bonds is $6.552 million.Settlement date is 7 October 1996, and trading in the fixed rate bonds will start today. For the 2017 bonds,
7863 the exchange value per $1,000 principal amount is $867.64, while the exchange value for the 2018 bonds is $866.33, the statement said.Invitations for offers expired on 20 September 1996. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734</
7864 Transatlantic trade will be a major factor in European oil product markets this week as the U.S. draws gasoline stocks out of the region and gas oil faces the uphill task of absorbing U.S. barrels heading into Europe.Portuguese and Tunisian purchase tenders will underpin fuel oil, traders said, while good
7864 petrochemical demand will support naphtha given the high prices for alternative feedstock LPG.Reduced European refinery maintenance, expected to run at just half of 1995 levels between September and November, should ensure current product tightness is not exacerbated.Around 350,000 bpd of capacity is set to shut in October and in November
7864 following a 600,000 barrels per day shortfall in September, the International Energy Agency recently estimated.Light oil products remain well supported because of an attractive arbitrage to the U.S. which has absorbed around half a million tonnes of September-loading gasoline and a few cargoes of naphtha.Europe's gasoline barge market, however, is
7864 well supplied, with inventory levels up on week-ago and year-ago levels.This will continue to weigh on local prices, currently at $200 a tonne fob ARA.The unusually wide spread between Eurograde and regular gasoline should remain in place, with good demand for higher octane barrels in Lavera and Poland.Trader buying has
7864 levered naphtha well above gasoline numbers, dampening refiner demand. But soaring LPG prices, largely as a result of low U.S. stocks, mean petrochemical demand for naphtha will remain strong.Strong gas oil may by the end start to feel the impact of the first of about ten north American gas oil
7864 cargoes, amounting to roughly 400,000 tonnes, heading to hit Europe. The influx might temporarily cut physical gas oil premiums $1-$2."The U.S. material could push down premiums but there's still a lot of restocking to be done in Europe and once the cold begins to bite demand can only grow," another
7864 trader said.High sulphur cracked fuel oil is likely to remain tight in both NWE and the Med with prices steady or a touch firmer. The latest Portuguese high sulphur fuel oil tender for up to 150,000 tonnes will probably be sourced from both regions. Tunisia is looking for two cargoes
7864 in October in addition to the 200,000 tonnes it tendered for from now until January.Traders thought high sulphur cargoes might rise $1-$2 over Friday's range of $109-110 fob NWE.The high to low sulphur spread could narrow this week as high sulphur rises to meet steady low sulphur levels."I see low
7864 sulphur staying steady with the spread narrowing as high sulphur rises," said a broker. An increase in low sulphur demand from the main Med buyer ENEL could be countered by Caribbean supplies. Both high and low sulphur should be able to resist softer crude unless the drop is dramatic."Fuel does
7864 have room to move down," said one trader.--London newsroom +44 171 542 8980</

7869 UK investment bank Close Brothers Group Plc aims to increase its fee earning business over the coming years, its chief executive Rod Kent said on Monday."We want to increase the fee earning businesses," Kent told Reuters in a telephone interview following the announcement of record results for the financial year
7869 to the end of July.These saw Close Brothers increase pretax profits by 33 percent to 45.1 million stg, from 34.0 million the year before.Kent said the main fee earners the group was targeting were corporate finance activity and investment management. In June Close Brothers bought Hill Samuel's corporate finance division.
7869 Kent said the new business had "got off to a marvellous start" and had retained both staff and clients.He cited a recent Hambro Company Guide which listed Close Brothers as top financial adviser in the "fastest growing clients" category. It was second in the "clients with fastest increasing earnings" division.Close
7869 Brothers' new-look corporate finance team was ranked fifth based on the number of stock market clients it advised."This transaction has really put us on the map in the corporate finance area," Kent added. Kent said the group wanted to grow its investment management business, having already built up a range
7869 of services."We would like to be relatively bigger," he said. This growth would either come through buying businesses or organically by taking on the right personnel."The question is finding the right companies and the right people," Kent said, adding that given that the stock market was at all time highs
7869 it was not the best time to go out and buy and investment management business.Commenting on the year's results, Kent said he was happy with the overall performance of the group. He said the group had reached agreement to sell its loss-making U.S. venture and was not planning to make
7869 any other overseas forays in the immediate future."We are not against international business, but the right thing has to come along. We have looked at several European markets but for one reason or another they have not been right," he added.A 17 percent increase in the group's total dividend, to
7869 10.0 pence from 8.5 pence the previous year, was "a pretty bullish signal" Kent said, adding that earnings per share had risen by only 12 percent because of a rights issue in the first half. Close Brothers' lending business had performed extremely well over the year, Kent said. Both volumes
7869 and margins were up over the period, he added.Winterflood Securities, the group's market-making operation, had a record year as a result of a bouyant stock market. Kent said the business could cope with any market changes, although the division's profits were always likely to fluctuate.-- London Newsroom ++ 44 171
7870 The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Monday it would issue a new one-month euromark interest rate futures contract on November 21, 1996.The new contract was being launched as part of the exchange's strategy for European Economic and Monetary Union, (EMU), LIFFE said in a statement.
7870 "The increased level of volatility between three-month and one-month deutschmark interest rates highlights the requirement for an additional hedging and trading tool -- a market need which will be met by the launch of this new contract," the LIFFE statement said.LIFFE said its decision to launch the new futures contract
7870 was also based on increased activity in deutschmark LIBOR-based Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) and interest rate swaps, increased issuance by the Bundesbank of short-term paper, and market and member demand. LIFFE said details of the new contract would be as follows: UNIT OF TRADING DM 3,000,000 DELIVERY MONTHS All calendar
7870 months DELIVERY DAY First business day after the last trading day LAST TRADING DAY 11.00 two business days prior to the third Wednesday of the delivery month QUOTATION 100.00 minus rate of interest MINIMUM PRICE MOVEMENT 0.01 TRADING HOURS To be advised"EMU is the greatest challenge facing European financial futures
7870 and options exchanges," Jack Wigglesworth, LIFFE's Chairman, said in the statement."Part of LIFFE's stated EMU strategy is to enhance our range of products, and, in particular, along the deutschmark yield curve."LIFFE said the new contract would trade by open outcry on the LIFFE trading floor.-- Kate Kelland, International Bonds Unit

7872 International distribution and marketing group Inchcape Plc, which has undergone a far-reaching restructuring during an 18-month period of weak profitability, said on Monday its interim results showed the start of recovery.A rebound in the "critical" business of importing and distributing mainly Japanese cars had been vital, Finance director Rod O'Donoghue
7872 told Reuters in a telephone interview."I think the real essence of this recovery is in the motors import and distribution where clearly we have had greatest difficulty (in recent times)," O'Donoghue said, adding trading margins, asset turn and return on net assets had all climbed. His comments and optimism came
7872 with a set of results that showed virtually no change in headline pretax profit, at 82.8 million stg compared with 83.3 million stg a year ago.Last year, however, exceptional restucturing charges brought the attributable interim bottom line into loss and in full-year 1995 Inchcape made a sharp total dividend cut
7872 to 10p from 15p.O'Donoghue said the interim payout for the first half, at 4.2p versus 6.0p, was in line with a more conventional approach now being taken by the group to pay a smaller interim dividend and seek to make the final dividend larger.But he said rebuilding the total payout
7872 would take time. "We've said we'll rebuild the dividend in the medium term and in anybody's jargon that's probably two to three years. That's a clear goal," he said.In the meantime, Inchcape is pressing on with its well flagged restructuring plan to divest two large non-distribution businesses by the end
7872 of this year.However, despite a high level of expectation in the share market, the company made no announcement on Monday about progress with either a trade sale of its Testing Services company or the probable demerger of insurance broker Bain Hogg.After these moves the group will have three core businesses.
7872 Inchcape's management have identified its strengths in future lying in international distribution where, O'Donoghue said, it feels the group's capabilities are the highest.At present, these interests are spread over motor importing and distribution, marketing -- including a stake in a business machines venture called Inchcape NRG -- and drinks bottling.The
7872 progress made in the first half in motors was partly offset by continued setbacks in the marketing business where weak demand squeezed returns down to unacceptable levels.O'Donoghue called marketing's 7.0 percent return on net assets "clearly too low", after 10.1 percent in 1995.In motor importing and distribution, meanwhile, the trading
7872 margin picked up to 1.4 percent in the first half compared with a trough of 0.9 percent in second half 1995."I sincerely hope we'll continue that improvement," O'Donoghue said, noting that the business aims to sustain a 2.5 percent margin, excluding currency and market factors.Motors' return on net assets tracked
7872 flat at 15.4 percent, after 15.6 percent in full year 1995, while asset turn, which reflects the speed with which cars are moved through the chain from order to delivery, improved to 11.5 times from 8.5 times.-- Andrew Huddart, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8716</

7879 Diesel oil users throughout the European Union are paying the price of a recent escalation in Middle East tension and the higher costs of producing a new grade of "greener" fuel, industry sources said.The retail price of diesel, increasingly popular with car drivers, has risen by five percent since early
7879 August, boosted by surging crude oil -- which has leapt on fears of instability in the oil-rich Gulf -- and the increased costs to refiners of making a low-sulphur grade on sale at the pumps from next month."Across the industry we've seen prices start to rise, partly as a result
7879 of the cost of product and also because people are not making enough money," said a Shell UK official.Rising costs of gasoline and automotive diesel on the European spot market has forced oil companies to pass on some of the increase to customers at the pumps, industry sources said.In Rotterdam,
7879 unleaded gasoline rose from $195 a tonne on August 1 to over $220 a tonne by mid-September. Last week it slipped back to about $200, but the cost of gas oil -- used for heating oil and diesel -- is still over $220, up from $176 on August 1.World crude
7879 prices rallied to a post-Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel earlier this month after the United States fired cruise missiles at Iraqi targets in retaliation for Baghdad's decisive intervention in Kurdish factional fighting.British consumers have felt the impact most keenly. Last autumn the country's biggest retailer Esso UK sparked
7879 a price war in response to fierce competition for market share from supermarket chains."It's well known that retail margins have been under considerable pressure for most of this year but since late July there have been several attempts by oil majors in the U.K. to reduce the losses their retail
7879 operations are seeing," said Robert Olle, director of consultants Oil Price Assessments Ltd."Just this week there was a fourth attempt to raise pump prices... which has been partially successful," he added.Elsewhere in Europe, automotive fuel retailers have been able to absorb much of the rise in gasoline prices, which are
7879 now coming down on the spot market, but the squeeze on diesel looks set to continue and pump prices may have to rise further."If I were in the retail marketing department of an oil major I would be extremely concerned about the lack of margin on diesel sales," said Olle."I
7879 would be surprised if even the big supermarket operators can live with these margins for very long."Sainsbury Plc, one of Britain's leading supermarket groups, said it raised forecourt prices across the board by a penny a litre on Thursday, the first such rise for several months.Diesel's popularity has grown in
7879 recent years, partly because it gives drivers more kilometres per litre, and now accounts for about 20 percent of the automotive fuel market in Britain, 25 percent in Germany, nearly 30 percent in Italy and almost 50 percent in France.From October 1, retailers will have to sell diesel with a

7880 Lloyds TSB Group Plc said on Monday it expected to reap cost savings of about 50 million pounds per year before tax in three years from the acquisition of the final stake in life insurer Lloyds Abbey Life (LAL).In a statement detailing the deal announced on Friday, Lloyds TSB said
7880 it expected the purchase, that values the outstanding LAL shares at around 635 pence each, to marginally boost earnings per share in 1997, excluding synergies. Lloyds TSB said the savings would be made through distribution, technology and adminstration of life and non-life bancassurance products as well as its hire purchase
7880 and leasing businesses."There will also be streamlining benefits which at this stage cannot be quanitified," the company said.The proposal, with its simplified ownership structure creating a more flexible business, created the opportunity to cut unit cost production in the combined businesses leading to a "stronger, more competitive market position and
7880 enhanced prospects for profitable growth", Lloyds TSB said. The deal by Britain's largest retail financial services company to buy the outstanding 37.4 percent stake in the insurance unit will cost around 1.22 billion stg, Lloyds TSB said.Abbey Life, which is currently quoted on the stock exchange, will remain separately run
7880 and, if the deal wins shareholder approval, three independent non-executive LAL directors will leave the board.Although the proposal would result in job cuts, Lloyds said it was aiming for voluntary redundancies and normal turnover as far as possible. Lloyds Abbey, which posted a pretax profit of 421.5 million stg in
7880 1995 and a first-half pretax profit of 259.2 million stg in 1996, has 1.435 billion stg of shareholder equity.Current trading remained "satisfactory" at both LAL and Lloyds TSB, the company said.Lloyds TSB posted a pretax profit of 2.08 billion stg in 1995 before a 425 million stg restructuring charge. 7880 year pretax profits in 1996 came in at 1.14 billion stg with shareholders' equity standing at 4.79 billion stg.Under the deal, minority LAL investors will get six Lloyds TSB shares and 2,100 pence cash for every seven LAL shares.Of the cash, 350 pence net -- 50 pence net per share

7896 Financial markets have a critical week ahead, with dealers and investors set to pounce on key decisions by European Union authorities and Federal Reserve policy makers, analysts said.EU finance ministers and central bank governors met in Dublin on Saturday for an "Ecofin" summit on moves towards European economic and monetary
7896 union (EMU).After digesting the results of that meeting, markets will be confronted with a Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, where many expect a U.S. interest rate rise.By the end of the week, attention is set to turn to an International Monetary Fund/World Bank summit, which begins on Saturday
7896 and runs through the following week.On the data front, the week is relatively light, with a smattering of Japanese and U.S. figures likely to be the main features."The first and obvious focus is the FOMC," said George Magnus, senior international economist at UBS, on Friday. "The U.S. market is pretty
7896 much priced for a modest rise in the funds rate."Elizabeth Legge, senior economist at Bankgesellschaft Berlin, said an increase of 25 basis points in the federal funds rate, currently 5.25 percent, would not have a major impact on markets given the degree to which it has been discounted."If more, it
7896 might have some impact on the dollar but I'm not even sure of that because the dollar has got so geared up for a hike," she said.Bal Sandhu, European strategist at Kleinwort Benson, said Wall Street and European stock markets, which have been bullish, as well as the dollar, all
7896 were in state of pre-FOMC tension."That's going to be the driving force. It's all going to revolve around whether Wall Street can take any prospective rate hike on the chin," he said.A big issue at the weekend Ecofin meeting was a so-called Stability Pact, designed to impose sanctions to ensure
7896 countries continue to observe strict fiscal criteria after EMU begins.But as with the FOMC meeting, analysts said a great deal of the EMU saga has been absorbed by markets."European markets have got a lot of this already in their sails," said Magnus, noting how so many European bond spreads were
7896 trading at or near historic lows against Bund yields."The strong performance of the European markets of the last three to four weeks is in contrast to the U.S. and it reflects that the markets are taking EMU even more seriously than they were before," he said.Britain has a monetary meeting
7896 scheduled for Monday but analysts say there is next to no chance of an interest rate cut after data showing vibrant consumer activity in the past week.Final second quarter gross domestic product data are due on Tuesday for Britain, followed by trade figures on Thursday.The U.S. has existing home sales
7896 for August on Wednesday, durable goods on Thursday and final Q2 GDP on Friday.In Japan, Friday will be a big day with consumer price, unemployment and retail sales statistics all scheduled.But analysts said that with authorities keeping a lid on call money rates, the market appears immune to anything other
7896 than GDP data or the closely watched "tankan" survey by the Bank of Japan, neither of which are due."As long as the economic numbers are reasonably in line with expectations the impact will be fairly small," Legge said.</
7897 John Major's wife, Norma, uses teabags more than once and likes to freeze her left-over cheese.Cherie, wife of opposition leader Tony Blair, is a dab hand at quick family meals and loves knitting sweaters.With an election less than nine months off, Britain's two main parties are using every gun in
7897 their armoury to convince voters they understand what makes the country tick, and Norma and Cherie are in the frontline in their aprons.The ruling Conservatives are convinced "First Lady" Norma is a vote-winner with middle class women because of her classic family role -- a mother of two who stayed
7897 at home supporting her husband while John climbed to the top of the political ladder.But Labour strategists think Cherie's home life is more relevant to modern Britain. They believe voters are impressed she can combine her busy life as a top lawyer with raising three children and keeping the home
7897 fires burning.In the weeks before this year's annual party conferences, when newspaper columnists will report on every hair tint and smile, the battle of the wives has been joined in earnest.Norma has given her first press interviews, six years after husband John first moved into 10, Downing Street."Domestic life suits
7897 me," says Norma, 54. Apart from squeezing the last drops out of tea bags, Norma has spent the last year working on a book on the prime minister's official country house, Chequers, which is published later this month.Norma is so good around the house that John used to ring her
7897 for help when they were first dating. "All my lights have gone off. What do I do?" John asked once when a fuse blew.Considered more politically radical than Tony, Cherie took a tentative step into the media world by editing this month's Prima, a cooking-and-hairstyles women's magazine."Sometimes I think I'm
7897 just juggling all the balls in the air and I'm amazed that they don't fall down at once," she said, lauding the efforts of working mothers and home carers. Prima readers were told Tony was very good at polishing shoes but could not be said to be "intimate" with the
7897 washing machine.While their politics, education and work experience are totally different, Norma and Cherie have a lot in common.Neither expected to be the wife of a party leader, both found press attention hard to deal with and both took a long while to adjust to the public spotlight. 7897 and families are the rocks on which they have built their lives.Major's elevation to the top job in November 1990 ended Margaret Thatcher's 11-year reign and Denis Thatcher's time in Downing Street."Everything was so new and there was nobody to give me any guidance -- it had been a long
7897 time since there had been a prime minister's wife," Norma said this month.The press could not resist snide, snobbish attacks on her naivety and her husband's ordinary background. She got "hammered" for wearing the same blue suit two days running shortly after John Major became leader, she admits now."I mean
7897 you know that's terrible, isn't it, and of course the suit was perceived to be a disaster as well. Life is full of adjustments and I think if life is going to be tolerable you've got to try and find a way to adjust to what life throws at you."Norma
7897 decided to slip into the background. She supported her husband at official and political functions but preferred to stay at home in Huntingdon, central England, rather than live with him during the week in London.The Blairs live about 20 minutes' drive from Downing Street, but Cherie says the whole family
7897 will move house if Labour, as indicated strongly by opinion polls, win the next election."Wherever Tony goes, we are going too. The most important thing is to keep the family together," she told Prima. "We want to keep life as normal as possible."That's what Norma said in 1990, and Cherie
7897 has had enough experience since her husband took charge of Labour in July 1994 to know that life will never be the same if Blair wins.The daughter of a well-known actor who starred in the television comedy series Till Death Us Do Part, Cherie was used at an early age
7897 to the pressure of fame.She once complained that she started as the daughter of someone and is now the wife of someone. The 41-year-old has given speeches at conferences discussing battered women but has resisted the temptation to give a formal interview.This has not stopped the Conservative press sniffing around
7897 her past, trying to find evidence she is a closet left-winger at odds with her husband's push to the centre ground of politics.They have had to content themselves with swipes at her dress sense -- a low point was when she turned up at a horse racing meet in pixie
7897 boots -- and her doting support for her husband in public, complete with fond gazes and an apparently rictus smile.Despite the current publicity offensive and the interest of the media in their lives, both women appear determined to avoid becoming first ladies in the U.S. mould.Cherie has been likened by
7897 Conservative newspapers to Hillary Clinton, said by some to be the power behind her husband's throne. But she says she intends to carry on working in law if Labour wins the election. She could become a judge during Tony's five-year term.Norma shudders at the thought of being like Elizabeth Dole
7897 and addressing a party convention."I can't think of anything that would make me want to do that, however much I might love him. I don't think I'd want to take a microphone and make a public declaration of it."</
