7914 The Australian government said on Monday it would allow foreign banks to issue securities on the Australian market under changes to the Banking Act."The government has decided to provide a general exemption ... to allow foreign domiciled banks to issue, in their own name, securities on Australia's wholesale capital market,"
7914 Assistant Treasurer Jim Short said in a statement.He said the measure would lower administrative costs for such banks and enhance their access to Australia's capital market. Previously, the Australian government insisted that foreign banks issue their securities in Australia through a guaranteed subsidiary company that did not include the word
7914 "bank" in its name.The aim was to minimise confusion as to what constituted a prudentially supervised banking entity in Australia, especially among retail customers.Short said the exemption would only apply to securities traded in the wholesale market and would be subject to specific disclosure requirements. Under the exemption, the securities
7914 offered must be traded in parcels of more than A$500,000 and it must be clearly stated on the securities that they were issued by a bank that is not authorised under the Banking Act.The exemption is due to take effect on Wednesday.-- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730</

7917 Australia's foreign exchange market has lost significant ground to other major centres within the region since 1989, a survey conducted by the Securities Industry Research Centre of Asia-Pacific (SIRCA) showed.The Australia Stock Exchange (ASX) has also been outpaced within the region, and only the market for interest rate derivatives exhibits
7917 a far more regionally competitive position."The evidence suggested that the relatively greater and improving liquidity in other financial centres would result in a continuing trend of regionalisation to our counterparts away from Australia," SIRCA said."This would result in further losses of liquidity in Australian markets and thus reduce or redirect
7917 savings and investment to overseas markets," the report said.SIRCA said this evidence was supported by interviews with over 35 percent of active over-the-counter participants, and of concern was a lack of concentrated government and industry action to reverse this trend.The survey, which was commissioned by the Australian Financial Markets Association
7917 (AFMA), showed that forex has grown in this period, but the market has a strong bias towards local currency transactions with volumes of 34.3 percent.The foreign exchange market of Singapore and Hong Kong display significantly higher levels of activity and can be expected to attract further participants into these markets.Although
7917 ranked ninth in the world in terms of foreign exchange turnover, Australia's world market share was only 3.0 percent compared with Singapore (ranked 4th) with a 7.0 percent share and Hong Kong (5th) with 6.0 percent.The ASX has also been steadily positive, but again the survey demonstrated that it was
7917 not keeping pace with its regional counterparts.Despite a record turnover of A$133 billion in 1995, Australia is ranked only fourth in the Asia-Pacific behind Taiwan, Korea and Hong Kong, which had a turnover of A$143 billion.However, Australia's interest rate derivatives market exhibits a far more regionally competitive position than foreign
7917 exchange, SIRCA said.The share of business undertaken with end users in Australia dwarfs that of Hong Kong and Singapore and after adjusting for the volume of Euro-yen transactions undertaken in Singapore, the volumes traded are evenly spread with Australia accounting for about one-third of the regions volumes.But a downturn in
7917 the level of domestic activity is likely to lead to substantially reduced market volumes and present a threat that participants in these markets will also gravitate towards Hong Kong and Singapore, SIRCA added.-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 373-1800</

7918 a supply surplus of 274,000 tonnes this year, growing to 290,000 tonnes in 1998.In 2000, the surplus should back-track to around 183,000 tonnes, Were said. 7918 double the 1996 estimate of 4.3 weeks.Were left unchanged from its earlier report expectations of an average copper price of US$1.01 a pound in calendar 1996, which is above the current price of about 86 cents a pound.Subsequent forecasts out to 2000, though, have been revised downward, indicating a more
7918 substantial increase in stocks than previously forecast, Were said. 7918 western world copper consumption in recent years, largely because of double counting, has led it to a 1995 consumption estimate some 137,000 tonnes below its previous figure contained in a report in March.As a result, the balance of supply and demand has shifted further into surplus through forecasts to 2000,
7918 Were said. 7940 The musky smell of joss sticks and the sight of saffron-robed Buddhist monks are becoming ever more frequent in Australia, while every Friday the Islamic call to prayer wafts across Sydney via a community radio station.In western Sydney, Australian schoolchildren in Moslem hajib headscarfs face Mecca and pray in Arabic
7940 during morning assembly, while steelworkers south of Sydney visit the biggest Buddhist temple in the southern hemisphere. As Australia's multicultural society blossoms, many people are turning away from traditional Western religions and looking towards Asia and the Middle East for spiritual enlightenment.According to the latest census, Buddhism has become the
7940 fastest growing faith in Australia, growing 300 percent between 1981 and 1991, closely followed by Islam.In 1991 there were 140,000 Buddhists. The 1996 census conducted last month is expected to show about 200,000, or one percent, of Australia's 18 million population are Buddhists.Some Buddhist leaders believe their followers will make
7940 up 10 percent of the population within 50 years. The growth in Buddhism, albeit from a low base, has been largely due to migration, with a third of Buddhists born in Vietnam and 20 percent in Malaysia, Cambodia or Laos.But there is a growing list of Anglo-Celtic Australians converting to
7940 Buddhism. Tens of thousands of Australians are flocking to hear the words of Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, during his current two-week visit."Life is becoming more stressful in Australia and people are looking for a way to overcome that stress, so they are looking to practices like Buddhism,"
7940 said Graeme Lyall, a 65-year-old convert and chairman of the Buddhist Council of New South Wales. Buddhists also say their godless faith fits well with Western scientific and secular perspectives, making it attractive to Australians of Christian origin."Traditional religions are finding they have conflicts with advances in science. Buddhism doesn't
7940 have any conflicts with science as the Buddha taught there are many world systems," explained Lyall.The Dalai Lama said Buddhism has also become fashionable in Western societies. "I think the concept of one truth, one religion, is out of date," said the Tibetan god-king.Islam has also experienced a dramatic rise
7940 in Australia. According to the 1991 census there were 300,000 Moslems in Australia. The figure today is likely to be close to 500,000.The increase in the number of Moslems has been through the growth of families -- growth reflected in the A$300 million (US$237 million) worth of marble mosques and
7940 Islamic schools in Sydney and Melbourne."We are seeing more and more young people coming forward and becoming more attached to Islam," said Ali Roude, chairman of the Islamic Council of New South Wales. "You walk in the streets and you find young women, Moslem women, wearing the hijab as an
7940 expression of their identity and belief. The more facilities we have, the more interest there is from young people to become involved."Both Buddhism and Islam have long histories in Australia.Lyall said Buddhism may date back to the 14th century when Chinese sailors reached the northern tip of Australia.But the first
7940 significant signs of Buddhism occured at the turn of the century when thousands of Chinese arrived during the country's gold rush. Lyall says an estimated 30,000 Buddhists worked the gold fields of eastern Australia. Islam came to Australia in the 1800s with Moslem camel drivers brought out to help explore
7940 the arid interior of the country. But Islam's initial impact was negligible -- herds of feral camels and abandoned mosques were the only legacy.The introduction in 1901 of the White Australia policy, a racist immigration law which judged migrants on their English, saw Buddhist and Moslem numbers drop dramatically.The end
7940 of the racist policy by the early 1970s and a need for cheap labour saw Middle Eastern migrants welcomed, while conflict in Indochina resulted in Buddhist refugees. But Australians were not tolerant of either, ranking Islam and Buddhism the two most disliked faiths.Today, Australia is a multicultural society where ethnicity
7940 is protected by law."The Australian way of life encourages tolerance and respect, so it is easier to practice a non-Western religion in this country than in other countries," said Kerry Trembath, a Catholic who converted to Buddhism 10 years ago.Silma Ihram, an Anglo-Celtic Prostestant who converted to Islam and founded
7940 the Noor-Al-Houda Islamic school in western Sydney, said it took time for her peers to accept her decision. "If you have the courage of your convictions here and are prepared to pursue them, you get a lot of respect," she said.Ihram said many of her students, who wear the hajib
7940 not only at school but at home, had lost touch with Islam and that religious tolerance had grown with education. "Educators now teach Islam as not such a heathen religion," Ihram said.</

7943 Australia will host the 1998 world gas conference to be held in Perth, Western Australia, Australian Gas Association chairman Greg Harvey said on Monday."The LNG 12 conference in Perth will be a major undertaking for the association, the North West Shelf participants and all interested companies," Harvey said in a
7943 speech to an AGA convention.The conference, a meeting place for the world's top gas producers and pipeline participants, is expected to attract about 2,000 international delegates, an AGA spokesman said. The conference is held every three years with the last conference at Birmingham, England in 1995.Harvey also said the AGA
7943 had formulated a new environmental code of practice which established principles to be adopted by the Australian industry."It covers practices for new development projects and operating and maintenance activities. Reporting will commence later this year," Harvey said. He also told the convention the federal government's gas reform task force which
7943 was developing a plan for gas access to transmission and distribution systems was "fundamentally deficient.""The draft proposals are intrusive, work against comercial negotiations and will lead to adversarial situations," he said."These may not accomodate the needs of all sectors of the gas market, especially residential customers," he said."Gas market development
7943 in Australia must be conducive to high levels of private sector project development," Harvey said.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800</
7944 Australian cotton producer Colly Cotton Ltd said on Monday its cotton output forecasts in its float prospectus were conservative and would be beaten, given reasonable weather conditions."If the sun shines and everything works, we should be able to beat them," Colly Cotton managing director David Farley told reporters.Earlier, Colly said
7944 it would issue 107 million shares at A$1.00 per share and forecast production of 180,700 bales in the year to June 30, 1997. Argentinian based investor John Kahlbetzer would take up 25 percent of the issue and units of current Colly Cotton owner, Commonwealth Funds Management, would also take 25
7944 percent of the issue.Colly Cotton is forecasting a yield per hectare of between 6.9 bales and 7.8 bales in 1996 and 1997, compared with the pre-drought yield of 8.4 bales per hectare.The drought between 1992 and 1995 was the worst in over a hundred years, Colly Cotton said.Farley said Australia
7944 was now out of the drought and set for more normal production levels. "We're well out of drought. The weather outlook looks good," Farley said.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</
7945 The overall price for New Zealand wool fell in mid-September, but some wool types fared better than others, Wools of New Zealand said on Monday.Prices for superfine merino wool were up substantially, while broader micron merino and halfbred wool prices fell.In crossbreds, fleece wool prices also eased and skirtings prices
7945 were particularly volatile. The market indicator was down four cents to 476 cents on September 12, and fell a further five on September 20 to 471 cents. Wools of NZ said the trend for full length crossbred fleece had been flat over the past six months, while shorter second shear
7945 prices had lifted from their May-June levels.Finer crossbred full fleece prices ("Chinese types") were still at very low levels, which Wools of NZ said reflected a lack of consistent demand from China."There is almost no price premium at present for 33 micron good colour fleece wool over stronger 35 micron
7945 wool," it said. Auction sales of new wool in the first two months of the 1996/97 season were up one percent on a year ago, to 6,600 tonnes. Private wool sales in July were up 42 percent on last year, to 3,200 tonnes, and slipe and sheepskin sales were up
7945 74 percent to 2,300 tonnes.Exports of wool fibre from New Zealand were up 50 percent in July compared with a year ago, to 15,700 tonnes, but Wools of NZ said the increases for July 1996 could largely be explained by the clearance of carried over wool from the 1995/96 season.
7945 Meanwhile, the Wool Exporters' Council said in a statement that wool exporters were supportive of a united industry body to provide a strong and effective lobby for wool concerns.Executive manager Nick Nicholson said a sector body could include exporters, brokers, merchants and scouring interests, as well as forming closer links
7945 with growers through Wools of NZ."Growers have not been alone in feeling the financial ramifications of a depressed international wool market, with all sectors of the industry feeling the squeeze," he said. Nicholson said he had been instructed by exporters to investigate the possibility of forming such an organisation and
7945 to prepare a report for the council by February 1997.--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746</

7952 The South Australian Assets Management Corporation (SAAMC) has achieved an unaudited after-tax profit of A$72.1 million for 1995/96, up from A$66.8 million in 1994/95, Treasurer Stephen Baker said on Monday.SAAMC is responsible for the disposal of the non-performing assets of the former State Bank of South Australia, which collapsed in
7952 1991 with more than A$3 billion in accumulated losses, and other assets not transferred to the new BankSA.BankSA is now fully owned by Advance Bank Australia Ltd.Baker said in a statement that SAAMC's surpluses were the result of better than expected recovery values achieved from the winding up of the
7952 SAAMC portfolio.SAAMC's total assets, totalling A$8.4 billion in July 1994, had been reduced to A$2.9 billion, comprising property and corporate loans in Australia totalling less than A$500 million, Treasury assets of A$2.4 billion, and offshore assets totalling less than A$30 million, he said.The reduction included sales of major properties and
7952 settlement of corporate accounts totallying A$3.5 billion, he said.Baker said major assets still held by SAAMC included the 333 Collins Street property in Melbourne and the former State Bank building in Adelaide.Statutory and legal requirements would not allow a complete wind-down of SAAMC for a number of years, he said."However
7952 SAAMC's presence will be very low key, with the main tasks now being to finalise payments to creditors as they fall due, manage the wind-down of the remaining subsidiaries, provide information for the ongoing litigation currently in existence, and complete required statutory obligations," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800</

7954 MIM Holdings Ltd acknowledged on Monday its Mount Isa mine was suffering from weak copper prices but said it had no intenton of reducing output.It was also too early to predict the impact of copper on 1996/97 earnings, an MIM spokesman said.Each one U.S. cent change in the copper price
7954 on a per pound basis meant A$3.77 million to MIM's bottom line, the spokesman said.An A$500 million project to expand mine output at the Enterprise orebody near Mount Isa and to lift smelting capacity to 250,000 tonnes a year was in full swing, the spokesman said. Elswhere in Australia, MIM's
7954 51 percent-owned Ernest Henry mine in scheduled to begin operation in late 1997, producing around 85,000 tonnes of copper a year.In Argentina, MIM's 50 percent-owned Alumbrera mine should produce about 700,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a year after commissioning in mid-1997, the spokesman said.The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper on Monday
7954 quoted a senior executive of MIM as saying the base metals miner expected to make a loss from copper operations at Mt Isa mine in the current year if weak prices persist. Last month, MIM reported a net profit after abnormals for the year to June 30 of A$170.6 million,
7954 but said the Mount Isa operations recorded a loss in June.The impact of weakended copper prices had been exacerbated by a strong Australian dollar, the spokesman said.MIM is hoping to reduce the cost of producing copper at Mount Isa, which currently ranks among the third quartile of the world's producers,
7954 the spokesman said.MIM does not reveal its costs, although analysts say it averages around US$0.71 a pound at Mount Isa. This compares with costs of US$0.40 a pound or less among some of the lowest-cost producers.Outside of copper, the future for lead and zinc mining operations at Mount Isa hinge
7954 on the findings of a feasibility study looking into developing the nearby George Fisher orebody.Early indications from the study suggest the expansion would be feasible, the spokesman said.MIM shares were trading three cents down at A$1.46 a share at 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT).-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

7955 Ltd (SACBH) for the purchase of the facilities.Baker said in a statement the government would introduce legislation next month covering third-party access and regulatory issues related to the sale. 7955 effective dispute resolution procedure, was acceptable, Baker said."The ACCC has advised that it does not intend to oppose plans by the South Australian Government to sell its bulk handling facilities to SACBH," he said."However negotiations with SACBH will require that satisfactory agreement also be reached on other issues such as
7955 price," he said. 7955 first right of purchase because the future of the facilities was inextricably linked to the SACBG grain terminals.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800</

7957 MIM said its oil and gas business did not fit strategicaly with the company's focus on copper, gold, coal, lead, zinc and silver.Proceeds from the sale would contribute to the development of MIM's new projects, the company said.Santos would employ most of MIM's oil and gas workers, the company said.Santos
7957 said on Friday it was interested in bidding for MIM's oil and gas interests and would consider a number of acquisition opportunities in the next year. 7957 20 percent stake in PPL56, which takes in a 6.975 percent stake in the SE Gobe oil field and various exploration prospects in the Fold belt area in Papua New Guinea, Santos said.The sale also gives Santos a 33.33 percent holding in the Bentu PSC gas development project in Indonesia,
7957 along with stakes in exploration projects in the Carnarvon Basin offshore of Western Australia. 7957 both the Gobe Main and SE Gobe fields.Oil production from SE Gobe is expected to start in the first half of 1998, with initial production put at about 25,000 barrels of oil a day, Santos said.The Bentu project is located in central Sumatra, about 800 km northwest of Jakarta. The
7957 block, in which Santos already holds a 27.78 percent interest, contains proven recoverable gas reserves and is expected to come on stream in around 2000, Santo said.Santos said it would fund the acquisition from existing cash facilities. 7957 conditions.An MIM spokesman told Reuters MIM was considering the future of its Southwest Queensland gas well, which was excluded from the sale.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

7960 the second half of 1996. Fahey, Australia's finance minister, said wage pressures, although still present, had eased back from the high rates of last year."These developments augur well for sustaining solid economic and employment growth over the next few years," he said.Fahey also said visible improvement in the current account
7960 should be a medium term focus.He said the government's fiscal strategy should help to contain the current account deficit by raising national savings. 7960 Fahey said.Fahey repeated that the government's fiscal strategy provided an important pre-condition for interest rate cuts.</

7964 of sovereignty to the uninhabited islands, known to the Japanese as the Senkakus and the Chinese as the Diaoyus.Another protest vessel set sail for the islands from Hong Kong on Sunday.A makeshift lighthouse built on one of the islands in July by a Japanese ultra-nationalist group has rekindled a festering
7964 dispute over the islands, claimed by Beijing, Taipei and Tokyo.Pilots aborted the landing due to the overwhelming Japanese force as well as rough seas and a rocky shoreline, a Taiwan Television reporter told her station by ship-to-shore radio."We headed for the Diaoyu islands until we were only 100 metres (yards)

7964 reverts to Chinese rule next year, carried that of the communist mainland's People's Republic of China.There were no reports of violence or physical contact.Japan's coast guard, asked for confirmation, said there had been "no trouble or conflict" but that it was duty-bound to "issue warnings and ask foreign ships to
7964 move out of Japan's territorial waters"."There is no change in our response (to foreign ships)," a coast guard spokesman told Reuters by telephone from southern Okinawa, which has jurisdiction over the islands.Taiwan radio said Japanese crewmen ignored the activists' demand to "Get out of Chinese territory!" and ordered the Taiwan

7964 mainland after Japanese patrol ships frustrated earlier Taiwanese attempts to approach the islands.On Sunday, thousands of drum-beating demonstrators chanted "Down with Japanese militarism" and "Protect the Diaoyus" as they marched through Taipei streets, the latest in a series of anti-Japanese protests in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau.An effigy of Japanese
7964 Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was tied to a car and flogged during the march.Taiwan pledged on Saturday to defend the Diaoyus by force, but only as a last resort.Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.Tokyo's
7964 claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. Beijing and Taipei say Chinese claims go back centuries but both have resisted calls to expel Japan by force.Taiwan and China have been bitter rivals since a civil war split them in 1949 and the Republic

8005 China is already recovering from a sudden slide in exports earlier this year but economists said on Monday that the world's largest developing nation would be lucky to attain zero export growth for the entire year."Year-to-year it's still negative, but exports grew by 12 percent in August, which is the
8005 highest this year. For the year, I think it'll probably be at about zero," said Kevin Chan, economist with Salomon Brothers in Hong Kong.Along with other exporting nations in Asia, China suffered from weak U.S. consumer markets in the first half with particular weakness in its exports to Hong Kong
8005 and Taiwan, much of which are then re-exported to the United States.A very high base of comparison highlighted China's poor performance. This year's forecast of zero growth contrasts sharply with a 22.9-percent rise in exports from China last year, including a sudden first quarter spurt of 80 percent.China has been
8005 relatively quick to recover from the downturn, but economists warn longer-term trends are afoot that are slowly changing the face of China as an exporting nation.Foreign funded enterprises (FFEs) are catching up with, and could soon overtake, state owned enterprises (SOEs) as the primary drivers of China's export engine, and
8005 this could have implications for public policy."China's domestic exporters have been lobbying for a devaluation of the Renminbi, arguing that this will help to reduce losses and correct the trade deficit," economist Heidi Hong said in a recent ING Barings report."(But) government assistance is not justified on the grounds that
8005 SOEs are commanding a smaller share of total exports."SOEs' contribution to total exports fell to 56.9 percent in the first five months this year compared with 71.1 percent in the same period last year, ING Barings said.By comparison, FFEs' share of total exports rose to 40.9 percent against 27.4 percent
8005 last year.Even more striking, economists in Hong Kong have all noticed a foreign investment shift away from southern China in favour of cheaper parts of Southeast Asia such as Vietnam.Economists said there are numerous reasons for the shift. Southern China's geographical location increases its vulnerability to cyclical downturns in overseas
8005 markets and regional political factors, such as strained China-Taiwan relations and unresolved Sino-U.S. trade disputes."(It is also) a result of the expansion of outward processing activities in southern China plateauing after more than a decade of massive relocation of production bases from Hong Kong and Taiwan into this area," said
8005 Hong.While economists all agree the shift is occurring, interpretations of its significance vary.Ken Chan, senior economist at Nikko Securities, said lower value-added investment is slowly moving away from southern China, but higher value added investment is increasing."Southern China will have a more difficult time but I don't think it will
8005 lose its edge. 8005 Thailand."And when you talk about labour costs, you have to look at quality as well," Kevin Chan said. "The quality may not match the costs, especially for the United States, which has strict quality control requirements, and especially in electronics."-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441</

8008 years.Dugal said Citibank's Philippine experience was replicated in most Asian countries.Myths about Asians being conservative and reluctant to leverage on future earnings were simply not true, he said."In most countries in Asia, you'll find revolving rates much in excess of 65 to 70 percent," Dugal said.The credit-revolving rate is the
8008 amount of money on which credit card users pay interest because they have not paid their dues within the stipulated time of one month.The hunger for unsecured credit has been tempered despite the fact that interest rates on revolving credit range from between 33 and 45 percent."That myth (that Asians
8008 are relectant to be in debt) has been shattered ... irrespective of cultures and ethnicity and religion, (it is) the same pattern all over Asia," Dugal said."We are talking about the global customer, whether he is in Asia or the Middle East."Dugal said of Citibank's worldwide 1995 profits of over
8008 $3.0 billion, 30 to 35 percent may have come from credit cards.He said Citibank did not have any serious multinational competitor in Asia because it was the first to enter the market about seven years ago."It is only recently that some of the multinational banks have started pan-Asian efforts, especially
8008 Amex (American Express), Chartered and recently Hongkong Bank," he said.Dugal said an important factor for the growth of credit cards was that unsecured credit was not easily available."Unofficial lenders, their rates are 50 or 60 percent and banks for some reason are not offering consumer unsecured credit at rates of
8008 25 and 35 percent, he said.He predicted banks would soon try to cash in on the unsecured loans market. "I believe (this) will happen in this market going forward," he said.</

8021 KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 - PORLA reported CPO production in August rose 12.2 percent or 88,200 tonnes to 810,550 tonnes. This is slightly higher than our estimate of 801,000 tonnes. The better production performance reflected mainly the vigorous recovery in output in East Malaysia which saw a phenomenal increase of
8021 34.7 percent or 44,300 tonnes to 172,200 tonnes. This represents half of the increase for the country. On an annual basis, production in August posted a growth rate of 15.4 percent. For the first eight months this year, production expanded 7.4 percent or 361,000 tonnes to 5.231 million tonnes. Peninsular
8021 Malaysia alone accounted for 74 percent of the increase when its output grew seven percent to 4.08 million tonnes. Latest partial data for first-half-September indicated a slowdown in the seasonal production in both the Peninsular and in East Malaysia. The performance of several major producers in Peninsular Malaysia ranged from
8021 down two percent to up five percent. For the whole country, our tentative estimate for September shows production rising moderately by some 50,000 tonnes or six percent to 860,000 tonnes. With production exceeding offtake, end August stocks of palm oil posted an increase of 45,000 tonnes to 800,900 tonnes. This
8021 compared with our estimate of 775,000 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone rose 69,500 tonnes to 472,200 tonnes. East Malaysia accounted for 51 percent of the increase when its CPO stocks rose 35,500 tonnes to 112,500 tonnes. PORLA reported smaller than expected August palm oil exports of 638,600 tonnes. This is
8021 lower than the July exports of 662,000 tonnes which was revised upward by 16,000 tonnes. We view the preliminary August exports figure as understated and would not be surprised to see an upward revision to 675,000 tonnes. Palm oil exports remain good this month and should be higher than PORLA's
8021 preliminary August figure. Indonesia took 20,000 tonnes RBD olein during September 1-20 against nothing in August. From a low of 1,024 ringgit on July 11 CPO futures advanced to 1,100 ringgit in August 9. Thereafter in KLCE, just over three weeks price surged to an intraday high of 1,268 ringgit
8021 before settling at 1,249 ringgit on September 2. This represents a gain of 225 ringgit in about seven weeks. However over the last two weeks the market had surrendered 114 ringgit or half the gains accumulated in the period between July 11 and early September. Better than expected palm production
8021 coupled with perceptions of a slowdown in offtake had generated heavy long liquidation as well as short selling by commission houses on the KLCE. We still view the price retracement as healthy and timely as it would restore the competitiveness of palm oil in the export market, not only against
8021 other oils but also against Indonesian palm oil. December CPO futures settled at 1,137 ringgit last Friday. 8054 use the 0.05 percent sulphur diesel grade for the whole country following a government mandate to curb air pollution, sources said. Thailand started using 0.25 percent sulphur diesel instead of 0.5-percent material in October last year.But market watchers said Thailand would have to pay a heavy price for the 0.05
8054 percent diesel because it is made using more sophisticated hydrodesulphurising refining units.They said it is easier and cheaper to switch from the 1.0 percent to 0.5 percent sulphur grade as it costs only about 20 cents per barrel more on a free-on-board (fob) basis.It costs 30-35 cents per barrel more
8054 to upgrade from the 0.5 to 0.25-percent grade. But the sources said PTT might have to pay double in terms of premiums on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis for the 0.05 percent grade.For example it normally pays between $1.20 and $1.50 per barrel premium, c-and-f Sri Racha, for the 0.25 percent
8054 grade, and may need to pay an additional $1.50 for the 0.05-percent grade, industry sources said.The sources said refineries in Thailand, like Thai Oil, would be able to produce the 0.05 percent grade diesel by processing very light, low sulphur crudes, which cost more. They said Thailand's Rayong and Star
8054 refineries would be able to produce this grade as well, but they would only start marketing it by the middle of 1997 as they do not have suitable storage facilities yet.This forces PTT to seek imports for the time being, but the number of regional suppliers is limited.One potential source
8054 is South Korea but it plans to start using 0.05-percent diesel by 1998, which will limit exports. South Korea aims to sell more 0.5 percent sulphur grade.Japan will switch to the 0.05 percent grade from August next year. In Singapore, only one refiner can produce 0.05 percent diesel, but one
8054 source said it was still developing storage for it.The chances of importing from Algeria and Europe were slimmer now that Europe is switching to 0.05-percent from 0.2 percent grade next month.The sources said Algerian cargoes might be absorbed by Europe as prices there are about $10.00 per tonne over values

8058 is a capitalist enclave whose economy depends heavily on casino tourism. 8058 territories and reunify by the end of the millenium.But unlike Hong Kong, Macau's assembly is not fighting for its survival beyond its 1999 handover. 8058 drew a record number of 75,093 voters to the polling stations, and a turnout of 64.49 percent, the highest since direct elections were introduced in 1976.The Macau Economic Promotion Association, headed by 46-year old property, entertainment and trading tycoon, Chio Ho Cheong, alias Chan Kai Kit, from China's Hainan island,

8058 cent of the votes. The group, which won 25.25 per cent in 1992, returned its two legislators, 49-year old social worker Leong Heng Teng and 43-year old business manager Kou Hoi In. Tea is a popular beverage in many countries in the world.Sri Lanka, the world's largest exporter, expected production to soar to an all-time high of 250 million kg in calendar
8079 1996 against the former record of 245.96 million kg in 1995, said R.L. Jurainsz, former chair of the Colombo Tea Traders Association,But tea imports by major consumers like Britain fell nearly eight percent in 1995 to 137,000 tonnes while U.S. imports slid 15.8 percent to 81,300 tonnes, FAO figures showed.
8079 "Tea export competition among exporting countries continued to intensify as demand remained weak," Hicks said.Bhasin said the excess supply made it vital that producing countries banded together and set aside a desire to boost exports in favour of a drive to boost prices."It does not require a mathematical genius to
8079 show that an indiscriminate increase in production and exports only results in a spiralling fall in tea prices and it is better to export a slightly lower quantity which can fetch a much higher price and a much bigger total revenue than to export a large quantiy at a very
8079 low price," he said. Another factor the tea industry faced was increased competition from other drinks like mineral water and soft drinks, said Rachmat Baduriddin, chairman of the Indonesian Tea Association."It's total share can be eroded drastically unless effective strategic measures are taken by the tea industry as a whole,"
8079 the official said, adding the competition would continue "to exert very strong downward pressures on the tea industry".Tea-producing nations must launch a vigorous drive to raise tea consumption locally and to develop new markets in other countries, he added. - Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)</

8120 public switched message and data services.Mah was speaking at the signing ceremony for the formation of the Singapore One Infrastructure Consortium.The consortium, by the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS), is being formed to bring wide-spread multi-media services and applications to Singapore. Mah said the tender process for the licences would
8120 be in two phases. The first would be a pre-qualification exercise held on March 1 1997. The second, for short listed candidates, would be in September 1997."The results of the main tender are expected to be announced in mid-1998. The successful licensee or licensees will have around 18 months before
8120 the licence commnencement date of 1 April 2000 to build, roll out and test their networks and services," said Mah.</

8130 Beijing is walking a diplomatic tightrope in a row with Tokyo over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea in part because Japan is a major aid donor, trading partner and investor, analysts said.China, which has fanned the flames of nationalism in recent months to fill an
8130 ideological vacuum, has thwarted any attempts to stage street protests, fearing nationalistic sentiment could careen out of control, Chinese and Western analysts said.While China does not want to be perceived as weak or unpatriotic, it faces the challenge of avoiding too many squabbles with too many diplomatic partners at the
8130 same time."The breadth and depth of the economic relationship between China and Japan ... compels the Chinese government to exercise some restraint on this issue," a Western diplomat said of the dispute over the islands -- known as the Diaoyus in Chinese and the Senkakus in Japanese.Tokyo has agreed to
8130 grant $5.27 billion in low-interest loans to Beijing over a three-year period from April, making it difficult for China to bite the hand that helps feed it.A dispute flared this month when Japanese rightists sailed to the uninhabited islands and repaired a makeshift aluminium lighthouse damaged by a typhoon last
8130 month to buttress Tokyo's claim over them.Japan effectively supported the rightists by sending patrol boats to repel private vessels from rival claimant Taiwan that tried to approach the islands, touching off anti-Japanese sentiment in China, Taiwan and the British colony of Hong Kong, which is due to revert to Chinese
8130 rule in mid-1997.Beijing and Taipei, rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, agree the Diaoyus have been China's for centuries and dispute Tokyo's claim, which dates to 1895 when Japan defeated imperial China in a war and seized the Diaoyus.Many Chinese have been slow to forgive
8130 and forget Japan's 1931-45 invasion of China. By Beijing's count, 35 million Chinese died under Japanese occupation.Attempts by Japanese politicians to whitewash Japan's atrocities and Tokyo allowing the rightists to reassert its sovereignty over the islands have only added insult to injury.The issue has ignited anger among ethnic Chinese in
8130 many places and a protest ship set sail on Sunday for the islands from Hong KongIn the face of growing anti-Japanese sentiment, Tokyo has called for calm.China has no plans to take on Japan head on."It's not in China's interests to have too many major disputes going at the same
8130 time with too many of its diplomatic partners," an Asian diplomat said.Beijing and Washington have squabbled in recent years over Taiwan, human rights, trade and alleged nuclear proliferation."If we go to war against Japan, we will fall into the trap of the United States," a retired Chinese diplomat said of
8130 calls for China to send warships to the islands.Some U.S. officials and media have portrayed China as the evil empire that could become a threat to world peace. China vehemently denies this.A Chinese official who spoke on condition of anonymity said China was as eager as Japan to put the
8130 dispute behind them.China has shunted to remote regions zealous anti-Japanese activists who planned to stage protests outside the Japanese embassy in Beijing.Beijing has difficulty understanding why Tokyo cannot rein in its right-wing groups.Also, Chinese education authorities have pacified Beijing's embattled students and stopped them from taking to the streets, fearing
8130 behind-the-scenes "black hands" could manipulate demonstrations, analysts said."China does not want to encourage ... demonstrations because they would have the potential to careen out of control," the Western diplomat said.Student-led demonstrations for democracy in 1989 ended with soldiers opening fire on protesters, tanks rolling in and heavy loss of life.
8130 China blamed the protests on "black hands"."Nationalism is the (ruling) Communist Party's weapon. But China must be careful not to cut itself," said a Chinese analyst who requested anonymity.</

8133 according to results issued on Monday.The Macau Economic Promotion Association, formed by business people, and a group formed by neighbourhood committees each won two seats in the contest for eight directly contested seats in the 23-member Legislative Assembly.The Macau Prosperity League, the Macau Construction League and the Democratic New Macau,
8133 as well as a pro-China labour group, each took one seat each. Voter turnout reached 64 percent, the highest in Macau's history.Macau's elections are only partly democratic. 8133 election by functional constituencies in a non-contest -- the number of candidates matched the number of seats.The remaining seven seats are to be appointed later by Macau's colonial governor, General Vasco Rocha Vieira.Twelve electoral groups ran in the election, representing interests ranging from labour, neighbourhood associations, business, and liberal political
8133 interests.Macau, a territory of 424,000 people, most of them ethnic Chinese, lies on the southern tip of China along the Pearl River estuary.</

8152 The Philippines, which only four years ago was enduring power cuts of up to 10 hours every day, is now basking in its highest ever generating capacity.But the country has paid a high price for the dramatic turnaround and is now looking to cheaper forms of generation.The 60-year-old state National
8152 Power Corp has power reserves of 40 percent, compared to 1992 when power deficiency levels reached 1,000 megawatts and power cuts brought industry to a virtual standstill."We are keeping a very high level of reserve, at 40 percent, because we await the commissioning of more reliable power plants. Once these
8152 power plants are in, then we can drop the reserve requirement to the usual level of 20 percent," Energy Minister Francisco Viray told Reuters.A 40 percent power reserve means that of the 4,000 megawatts required daily by the main Luzon grid, some 1,600 megawatts of power plant capacity is on
8152 stand-by. Luzon is the Philippines most populous island.Viray said 20 percent was usually regarded as a comfortable reserve and was the level maintained by most Asian countries. Reserves should normally be the equivalent of the capacity of the grid's biggest power plant, he added.But he conceded that maintaining a high
8152 power reserve level was not without costs.Most of the power plants which make up the reserves were gas turbines fuelled either by diesel or bunker fuel, Napocor system operations officer-in-charge Rolando Bacani said.Power from gas turbines costs about 2.0 pesos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) while cost of power from other types
8152 of plant range from 1.30 to 1.68 pesos per kwh."We definitely have sufficient power although we still have some transmission line limitations. The 40 percent reserve is possibly the highest in Philippine history," Bacani said.Economist and former Philippine National Oil Co chairman Benjamin Diokno said the government's energy and power
8152 agencies may have erred in overestimating the country's power needs."I think we over-reacted and that because of the mad rush to put on stream more power plants, we have over invested in fuel-fired power plants. It is turning out to be more costly for the country," Diokno told Reuters.Recognising the
8152 need to diversify energy sources, the energy department has put a lid on oil-based power plants. On August 26, Viray signed an administrative order stopping accreditations to build bunker oil-fired or diesel-fired power plants."We do not want to be too dependent on one type of fuel. We want to control
8152 the share of oil in the power generation mix. We want to diversify and the discovery of the Camago-Malampaya gas field in Northwest Palawan paves the way for the country to start a gas industry," Viray said.In a newly revised 30-year Philippine energy programme, covering the years 1996 to 2025,
8152 the Department of Energy reiterated its goal of diversifying energy sources.It envisages oil's share in the power generation mix as dwindling from its current 41.6 percent to just 8.3 percent by the year 2010. It will largely be replaced by natural gas.By 2010, natural gas will provide 19.6 percent of
8152 the power generation, from a current level of zero, followed by coal at 16.1 percent from this year's 20.5 percent. Geothermal power will fall from the current 22.6 percent to 12.6 and hydro from 15.3 to 8.6.Gas production is projected to reach 967.2 billion cubic feet in 2025 inclusive of
8152 the Camago-Malampaya gas find.The 30-year plan also discussed the entry of nuclear power after the year 2005 possibly by 2007, Viray said.This is the first time the government has considered nuclear energy since a debacle in the early 1980s over a 620-mw nuclear power plant had to be mothballed amid
8152 intense legal wranglings over alleged corruption.The energy plan requires 7.73 trillion pesos ($295 billion), of which 91 percent will be sourced from the private sector.This sum covers the entire energy sector from exploration to refining but most of the financing will be required to install 92,138 mw of power over
8152 the 30 years.Former presidential energy adviser Peter Garrucho lauds the government's efforts to diversify fuel sources."We have to have competitive power and clearly the best alternatives are natural gas, coal and geothermal," Garrucho, who is now president of First Gas Holdings Corp (FGHC), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.Garrucho
8152 said the next challenge was to set up a distribution system to bring natural gas to the market."One has to deal with difficulties in getting rights-of-way especially in a densely populated market as Manila. But really the direction of spreading it (power sources) around, going low cost is really the
8152 way to go," Garrucho added.Conversion $=26.2</

8163 Deep inside a vault near Hong Kong's border with China, a young woman in a white coat examines a freshly-made five-kg (11-lb) platinum bar."This is worth about half a million Hong Kong dollars," or US$64,000, she says casually, replacing the rough, palm-sized slab on a shelf.The woman, a local employee
8163 of the privately-owned German precious metals refiner Heraeus Ltd, Hong Kong (HLH), then indicates with a wave of her hand stacks of one-kg (2.2. lb) gold bars produced at the firm's Hong Kong factory.Like other international and local precious metal refiners based in the British colony, Heraeus is cashing in
8163 on China's dependence on Hong Kong for a steady supply of precious metals."Heraeus has increased its Hong Kong refining capacity by four times, just over the last two years," said company president Juergen Schroeter.It has invested HK$100 million in a new Hong Kong factory which spreads over 8,000 square metres,
8163 he said.Heraeus processes several hundred tonnes a year of electronic scrap containing precious metals, and under 50 tonnes a year of jewellery scrap, including shavings, cuttings and dust, Schroeter said.Heraeus-made products and services boast a large share of the Hong Kong market and are also sold to customers in the
8163 Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, Taiwan, South Korea, Indonesia and Australia, he said.Its chief rival, Britain's Johnson Matthey (JM), says the amount of gold it refines each year depends on prices."Every year we refine 20 to 30 tonnes, depending on the price of gold," said JM's Hong Kong-based sales manager Anthony Tsang.
8163 "This year I think we'll have 20 to 25 tonnes, because the price has not been very good."Precious metal chiefs are bullish about platinum because China is a market growing at their doorsteps. "We are not aware of any platinum sources within China," said Schroeter.China's platinum imports in 1996 are
8163 expected to jump more than 50 percent to about 180,000 ounces, compared to 130,000 ounces in 1995, an earlier Johnson Matthey forecast said."Richer Chinese people, particularly in Shanghai, now want to buy Japanese-style platinum jewellery instead of gold," said Tsang. He said JM's platinum jewellery sales to China had jumped
8163 from about two tonnes in 1995 to around 2.5 tonnes this year.Its total platinum sales to China were 4.5 tonnes in 1995 and will hit 5.6 tonnes this year, Tsang said.The flow of precious metals goes both ways. Hong Kong's refineries have long processed gold for the mainland, industry sources
8163 say."All (Hong Kong-based) refineries get at least some of their gold from China, especially the local refiners," one source said.China's state-determined gold prices lie behind this trade.Gold prices in China are periodically decided by the People's Bank of China and are often lower than international market prices, prompting the flow
8163 of metal over China's borders, bullion traders say."The People's Bank of China currently buys 90.0-99.0 percent purity gold at about 90 yuan (US$10.8) per gram (US$335.90 per ounce) and sells the gold to domestic manufacturers at about 105 yuan per gram ($391 an ounce) according to the World Gold Council's
8163 Shanghai representative, Helen Mao.The World Gold Council is a promotional body funded by gold mining companies worldwide.With world gold prices fluctuating between US$380 and $389 an ounce, the incentive to refine gold in Hong Kong, as opposed to selling it to China's central bank, is powerful, sources say.Gold trickling into
8163 Hong Kong from China is normally of 97-98 percent purity and gets refined to 99.99 percent purity before being sold on behalf of Chinese customers, they added."The mainland cannot crack down on this trade as no one knows what channels are used," one senior gold trader said.Gold nuggets mined in
8163 China's northeast and southwest regions flow to Hong Kong's neighbouring Guangdong Province, where gold is in hot demand.Some of that gold -- no one knows exactly how much -- finds its way into Hong Kong refineries.These refineries could be handling more and more Chinese gold as Beijing boosts state output
8163 targets but shows little sign of price reform.Annual gold production in China is set to reach 150 tonnes by the year 2000 at an average growth rate of 6.8 percent, according to an official China Daily report earlier this year.But the global gold industry has always questioned China's true output
8163 of gold.An analyst from consultants Gold Field's Mineral Services Ltd said earlier this year that China's official gold production figures for 1995, pegged at 108 tonnes, ignored "informal production" of the metal and did not take into account gold sold outside China's central bank.Offical Chinese media acknowledged last month that
8163 illegal mining using primitive extraction techniques accounted for about 16 tonnes of gold produced in 1995 above official figures.China is trying to eradicate unauthorised gold mining, closing 430 illegal gold pits between January and June this year and rounding up armed gangs involved in the business, the official Xinhua News
8163 Agency said.But China's gold market is showing more conventional signs of opening up, boosting Hong Kong refiners' and traders' confidence in a golden future."The People's Bank of China has authority to decide, according to demand, the necessity to import gold to China," said Raymond Chan Fat-chu, head of Tem Fat
8163 Hing Fung Refinery."The PBOC has also issued 300 licences to bring in raw materials, process and re-export," he said.Hong Kong remains a nerve centre for China's gold imports. The value of Hong Kong's official re-exports of gold to China in 1995 was HK$77.9 million (US$10 million), up from HK$68.0 million
8163 in 1994.Anticipating further growth in the precious metals sector, Heraeus is quietly strengthening its toe hold within China.In addition to being the first foreign joint-venture to obtain a government gold licence late last year, Heraeus is lobbying the Chinese government for a silver licence.With the licence to process gold, joint
8163 venture Heraeus Zhaoyuan Precious Metal Materials produces gold bond wires in the northeastern Chinese province of Shandong for the computer chip industry.In late 1995, the company opened Heraeus Materials Technology (HMT), a 100 percent-owned subsidiary to produce tungsten carbide balls in Shanghai for ballpoint pens.Heraeus has also expanded into the
8163 sale of precious metal products such as platinum plating of anodes and cathodes for protection against corrosion.US$ 1.00 = HK$ 7.79</
8164 It was somehow fitting that choreographer Ea Sola should bring her troupe of elderly peasant women back to Vietnam in September, just when vast areas of the country were being ravaged by tropical storms and flooding.The group's dance, "Han Han va Con Mua" (The Drought and The Rain), is a
8164 bitter-sweet testimony to their nation's fortitude in the face of calamity.A young French-Vietnamese woman who left her war-tattered country as a teenager, Ea Sola has won the approval of audiences in both Europe and North America for her production's disconcerting mix of folk tradition and modernism.But back at home, "The
8164 Drought and The Rain" has triggered consternation and acrimonious debate in art circles.In a country where poverty and stark communism have kept novel art forms at bay, it is no surprise that Hanoi audiences were more excited about a recent visit by the Belarussian ballet company than they were about
8164 13 old ladies twitching across a stage.Ea Sola's dancers are no ballerinas, it is true.Most of the women have spent their lives toiling in the paddy fields of Thai Binh, a poverty-stricken province in the north of the country. The youngest is 51 years old and the oldest, spritely for
8164 her age, is 77.Nevertheless, it was the dance's portrayal of a country still reeling in undignified pain which riled the youth newspaper Tuoi Tre so much."It's really a dull picture of the past," Tuoi Tre fumed after a performance in Ho Chi Minh City. "And the audience cannot ignore the
8164 link to the present since there was an allusion.""The sooner we stop this performance, the sooner we can end this smear and insult," it added."The Drought and The Rain" works from the base of two folk legends. The first is a figurative battle between sun and rain, of which man
8164 is the victim, and the second is the story of a bride who loses the way back to her husband.Traditional instruments accompany songs which illustrate the legends while the old ladies, barefoot and in peasant garb, perform a highly stylised routine of everyday rural gestures.Their gnarled hands claw at the
8164 air, their conical straw hats bob and weave, they stare up obsessively at the sky, they nod, they shake and they grin, toothlessly, at the audience.At one chilling moment, the women march forward and hold out photographs of fathers, husbands and sons -- martyrs of the country's wars against the
8164 French and then the Americans.Tran Van Khe, a member of UNESCO's International Music Council and one of the production's admirers, was among those who added their voices to a rebuffal of Tuoi Tre's lambasting."By this naturalism, she (Ea Sola) has depicted the harshness of drought and rain...the misery of Vietnamese
8164 women in wartime, the waiting and the heavy losses," Khe wrote in the Saigon Times Daily.Ea Sola says her dance sets suffering inflicted by war and the elements against a background of village and family tradition, of which the old women represent the resilient guardians. It is there that her
8164 work carries its message of hope.It may have received a lukewarm welcome at home, but "The Drought and The Rain" is heading off for another tour of European countries at the end of this month.For the simple women of Thai Binh -- many of whom had never even been in
8164 a car let alone an airplane before they were recruited by Ea Sola -- exposure to the western world has been a mind-blowing experience.But it takes more than luxury accomodation and Western world comforts to change the habits of generations. While they are on tour, the dancers sometimes sneak down
8164 to their hotel kitchen and cook themselves a bowl of rice.</

8182 the city was hit by a serious water shortage last summer.Mayor Walid Abu Mweis said the state-owned Israeli water company, Mekoroth, does not pump enough water to meet the needs of his city of 38,000.Only a fraction of the 6,100 cubic metres (215,400 cubic feet) of water which are supposed

8182 the West Bank.Water shortages are common in the West Bank. But the problem appears to be especially acute in Jenin this year. 8182 Authority to fix the price and deploy policemen to enforce it.Hisham Istaitiyeh, deputy director of Jenin hospital, noted a sharp rise in stomach diseases due to contaminated water. 8182 operate without water?" he said.Water shortages also affected agriculture, once the mainstay of one of the most fertile West Bank districts. 8182 say affects both Palestinians and Israelis."The area in general is short on water. 8182 said.But Palestinians said the problem lay in unfair water distribution and pointed to lush lawns and shimmering swimming pools in Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza.Palestinian researchers estimate that Israel pumps more than 85 percent of West Bank water across its border or to settlements.Israel recognised Palestinian water
8182 rights under a 1995 self-rule accord, but retained full control of water resources. Water is a key issue in future Israeli-PLO talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip."The Israeli side must learn to share water with us just like they share the air," said Zuhdi

8231 Japan's trade ombudsman is taking to the road to explain to foreign exporters how best to complain about any problems in penetrating the Japanese market.Office of Trade and Investment Ombudsman (OTO) officials are in Europe this week to tell governments and business chiefs how the department works and boast of
8231 its success since it was established in 1982.It has handled a total of 545 grievances, but the number of cases reaching it has been whittled down from around 50 a year to just two in 1996.OTO chief Yoshio Okawara told Reuters that the office would exist for as long as
8231 a perception remained that Japanese markets were unfairly closed.The office does not handle complaints regarding tariffs or other barriers that exist because of World Trade Organisation regulations or other trade agareements.But it aims to help foreign companies to understand and overcome Japanese internal regulations such as standards and certification.An example
8231 was a complaint by a U.S. mobile home maker that it was denied access to Japan. Because mobile homes were relatively unknown in Japan, officials assessed them as both vehicles and dwellings, and thus they could not be certified.The OTO, which reports directly to the Japanese prime minister eventually managed
8231 to change the law so that they could be assessed separately.The OTO says that just 149 of the 545 complaints have resulted in no change to market access. In the rest, it says, improvements have been made or misunderstandings cleared up.The United States leads the number of complaints with 164
8231 followed by the European Union with 158.Anyone -- governments, businesses or individuals -- can file a complaint by filling out a form and sending it to any Japanese Trade mission around the world.Okawara said OTO procedure had been speeded up so that the average "life" of a complaint was now
8231 less than three months."The system is not perfect...It can never be," he said. "But I believe the OTO has served a valuable role which is helping Japan's markets open to foreign goods." REUTER</

8249 Greece's socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis won his first major political gamble on Sunday, sweeping to victory in early national elections.After stumbling in his first national campaign, Simitis, 60, showed he was a quick learner by changing his tactics and coming back strong at the finish.His win marked the end
8249 of a long wait in Greece's political wilderness and then a meteoric rise to power in the past eight months.It gave him complete control over the Panhellenic Socialist Movement (PASOK), a free hand to name a cabinet of his choosing and a four-year mandate to implement his reform policies.An enigma
8249 to many, he was dubbed "the Chinese" by the media for his slight build, almond-shaped eyes and inscrutible grin."I support him. I don't know why. I just think he's the only way forward for the party and the country but I can't give you a concrete reason. It's a feeling,"
8249 a former PASOK official said.A German and British-trained economist, Simitis emerged from the socialist shadows after party founder and three-time premier Andreas Papandreou was taken ill in January.With lightning moves, he won a fight in the parliamentary group to replace Papandreou as premier. He then won the PASOK leadership in
8249 a close race after Papandreou died in June.Unpretentious but supremely self-confident, Simitis had long seen himself as the only obvious heir-apparent to Papandreou, the one-time mentor with whom he had tense relations.Papandreou named him to every cabinet but never included him in his inner circle and Simitis twice resigned from
8249 ministries because of public humiliations by the revered party founder.In the end those disputes with Papandreou gave him the image of being his own man, and enhanced his popularity with the PASOK rank-and-file when the time came to choose an heir.Simitis disliked Papandreou's flamboyant style and appeal to radical populism
8249 in formulating policy, which alienated allies and left Greece weakened internationally.His own style is dry, even tedious, and in contrast to the extrovert and fun-loving Papandreou. He is a private man who prefers to stay home with a good book.He billed himself the face of change for the 21st century
8249 but steered clear of giving details. Instead he catered to lofty dialogues on the EU, the need to work and sacrifice, and visions of Greece's potential as a Balkan and Mediterranean leader.Simitis will give the first indication of just how different his "new PASOK" will be on Tuesday when he
8249 is likely to name his cabinet.He is the son of a Piraeus lawyer and grew up in a well-off, progressive family, where the first seeds of his leftist views were sown.He left home at 18 to study law and economics in Germany and did post-graduate work at the London School
8249 of Economics. He has worked as a lawyer and taught law and economics in Germany.Simitis opposed a military junta which seized power in 1967 and was a founding member of Papandreou's PASOK when the regime fell in 1974.During the junta Simitis escaped to Germany on a false passport while his
8249 wife was arrested and put in isolation. He was convicted in absentia for his opposition to the dictators.</

8268 - Some may want to idle away their holidays on a beach in France, in a quaint Italian village or cruising a warm, azure sea.Others of a hardier ilk might plump for Norway's Spitzbergen, a wind-blasted archipelago boasting one of the harshest climates on Earth.There is most decidedly no beach
8268 here, but the tourist is free to delight at mighty ice mountains, jagged fjords and hundreds of polar bears that attack without warning.The Arctic territory offers the raw beauty of one of the last untouched wildernesses. Mobile telephones do not work here, so there is no point in bringing that
8268 icon of the plugged-in."This is a good place for a holiday," said Mike Jenkins, 47, a British telecommunications worker, gazing at the snow-tipped mountains and the frigid Icefjord."It sure looks different from London."The British capital is 3,000 km (1,900 miles) from Longyear, an old coalmine town with roads so dirty
8268 that signs advise you to take off your shoes on entering shops or public buildings.It is a bright evening in September, winter has not yet set in and snowscooters are stranded on patches of grass outside the houses of Longyear, 1,306 km (810 miles) from the North Pole.The sun shines
8268 around the clock for four or five summer months on Spitzbergen, which lies 800 km (500 miles) off North Cape, the northern tip of Norway that is the final destination for most of the few tourists who brave the far north.The islands were called Spitzbergen for their saw-teeth mountains by
8268 Dutch seafarer Willen Barents in the 16th century. But the Vikings had been to these shores hundreds of years earlier. Icelandic annals show that the Vikings called it Svalbard, or Land of the Cold Coast.Death can come quickly on Spitzbergen, either by polar bear, icy drowning or by falling into
8268 a crevice on a glacier.A Justice Ministry sign at Longyear airport says: "Svalbard is beautiful, but the Arctic wilderness can also be dangerous."Tourism in Svalbard is subject to special regulations, for instance concerning notice of travel plans and insurance cover. Enjoy your stay, but take care!"Tourists are advised to go
8268 on treks under the leadership of a guide partly because the weather changes quickly. Visitors are also advised to rent heavy-calibre rifles because of the polar bears -- gun licences are not needed."This is a boy's adventure," said Jens Krageur, 44, a Norwegian tourist. "I have been looking for this
8268 experience for 20 years."Rifles over their shoulders, Krageur and Jenkins were waiting for a ride out of town with one of Longyear's two taxis."If you want to come for the raw beauty of the landscape or go dog-sledging on a glacier in the summer, then this is the place," Jenkins
8268 said, grappling with his rucksack.Other treats include kayaking and tours of the coal mines.About 8,000 tourists visited Longyear last year, up 10 percent up from 1994. Most stayed in the settlement's three hotels but some went camping, which tourism officials say can be dangerous and is not to be recommended.Two
8268 tourists were killed by polar bears last year, including a Norwegian man who fired several pistol shots at a bear but was mauled to death on an island in eastern Spitzbergen. A Norwegian woman was fatally attacked by a polar bear on a mountain behind the Longyear church.Polar bears rarely
8268 venture into town, but in 1982 one was gunned down by a hunter on the steps of the church."For once we had a church-goer, and he was shot," one villager said.The church, which can take 100 visitors, is seldom crowded although Longyear has 1,200 inhabitants."The people who go to church
8268 on the mainland are not here," Reverend Jan Hoeifedt said. "Those who work hard making money are not the most frequent church-goers. We've had 10 to 12 people on a cold winter day and 60 to 70 on a nice summer day."But the church was full the Sunday after the
8268 August 29 crash of a Russian TU-154 aircraft. It slammed into a mountain near Longyear airport killing all 141 people aboard.The plane was flying miners to two nearby Russian settlements running coal mines under a 1925 treaty which recognised Norway's sovereignty but granted Moscow the right to exploit coal.Spitzbergen became
8268 a virtual coal mining Klondyke at the turn of the century. Among the pioneers were American John Longyear of Marquette, Michigan, who set up camp in what became known in Norwegian as Longyearbyen, or Longyear's town.Because of the archipelago's international status, Longyear is a tax-free haven. A basic selection of
8268 alcoholic beverages, including a few French and Italian wines, is on offer in a shopping centre that has popped up in the last decade with increasing tourism.In true prohibitionist Nordic fashion, however, alcohol is rationed for tourists as well as inhabitants to keep them from going on a binge in
8269 Fearing he might be forgotten by future generations, 19th century German composer Richard Wagner built a vast theatre and founded a festival devoted exclusively to his own music.It worked. Wagner not only laid the foundations of a cult in his own honour, he also established the Bayreuth Festival which has
8269 become one of the world's most sought-after cultural events with a waiting list of thousands.Americans, Japanese and French fans head the international contingent of Wagnerian devotees who head to this small Bavarian town each year.Opponents call Wagner a megalomaniac and say the festival is tainted by associations with the Third
8269 Reich. Adolf Hitler became a regular guest of his favourite composer's family, who continued the tradition after Richard Wagner died in 1883.Few Germans seem to share their qualms.Droves of visitors flock to Bayreuth each summer for the six-week event hoping to attend a performance -- regardless of the fact that
8269 they are vying for some of the world's most coveted tickets.Visitors who want to be guaranteed success must apply for tickets about six months before the festival, when tickets are allocated. Most requests are placed on a waiting list of thousands where some wait for up to 15 years."We never
8269 advertise the festival. People just come to us," said Bayreuth Festival spokesman Peter Emmerich. "The festival has been permanently sold out since the 1960s.""It's a phenomenon. The average waiting time for a ticket is seven years, but some wait as many as 15 years." Last year there were half a
8269 million requests for 58,000 tickets."It just shows you the huge demand there is for his music -- particularly today in the modern world."A few statesmen and other VIPs are invited each season. Others have to wait their turn."I've been on the waiting list for eight years," said one taxi-driver, who
8269 wore a tuxedo and bow tie during the festival in case a passenger came out early and left him a ticket for the rest of the performance.One did and he won a free seat for the last two acts of a new production of Wagner's opera The Mastersingers of Nuremberg
8269 -- so it was just as well he was properly dressed for the occasion, he said.Some locals in the town have "friends" working in the box office, on the door, in the wings. A last-minute phone call can mean a seat for that night's performance.Fans dressed in evening finery queue
8269 outside the festival box office for hours in the hope of getting returns.That having failed, they wait outside the entrance to the theatre before the performance displaying signs, such as:"It's probably impossible but I'm looking for a ticket".Some offer multiples of the original prices, which range up to 300 marks
8269 ($200) a seat -- moderate by international standards.Students volunteer to work as ushers for a pittance to see the shows. Virtually all the festival theatre's employees from cleaners to administrators are Wagner music-lovers and are there mainly for complimentary tickets to dress rehearsals.Even the singers make a sacrifice to be
8269 here by accepting a pay cut just to perform on the Bayreuth stage -- a showcase for operatic talent, where many performers have made their names."Wagner fans are obsessed. They're unlike fans of any other composer," said one of the soloists performing in this year's production of The Mastersingers directed
8269 by Wolfgang Wagner, the composer's grandson.He shook his head as a gang of autograph hunters, all aged over 60, who had tracked the singers down to their favourite pub in Bayreuth, badgered each one in turn for their signature."It's because the music gets under your skin. Once it's there you
8269 never get tired of it," said the German soloist, who has been performing at Bayreuth for 20 years.The atmosphere inside the theatre -- packed with people who have gone to ridiculous lengths to be there -- is slightly tense. A once-in-a-lifetime experience is not always a relaxed affair.Performances are long.
8269 The intervals are long too, lasting one hour during which the audience munch bratwurst and drink beer -- in this thoroughly German experience.The ultimate experience for true devotees is perhaps the Ring cycle, Wagner's longest work, a four-day marathon of four performances each no less than six hours.Visitors come armed
8269 with cough sweets and cushions since rustling programmes, wheezes, coughs and noisy fidgeting are all taboo here.The theatre, famed for its superb acoustics, is larger, with a bigger and taller stage than other opera houses built at the time. The orchestra pit is below the stage and kept out of
8269 sight so that the music appears to well up from the ground.Wagner's works were intended to fuse poetry, drama and theatre. That is why he did not call them "operas", preferring to term them "music dramas". He wrote the librettos himself based on tales of mediaeval knights and epics of
8269 Germanic tribes -- hence its popularity with nationalists -- notably the Nazis."For Germans Bayreuth is more than just a music festival, and although we have many guests from abroad, it will always be a symbol for all that is German," Emmerich said.Every year some 45,000 people visit the villa where
8269 Richard Wagner spent the last 20 years of his life, "Haus Wahnfried" -- meaning peace from delusion -- and the grave where he is buried alongside his widow Cosima and his dog.Now a museum, it is dedicated to the composer's life and works.It is full of Wagner's musical scores and
8269 models of productions going back to the festival's founding year in 1876. But it also includes objects from his everyday life."These things have nothing to do with his musical heritage. But we try to exhibit them to show that he was not a Greek god but a human being too,"
8269 said museum director Sven Friedrich, referring to the composer's clothes and personal effects."But for some Wagner fans they are more like religious reliquaries," he told Reuters, pointing to the "death sofa" which had to be encased in glass to prevent fans plucking out upholstery feathers as a keepsake. 8270 Sweden's real estate market is laying the foundations of a new structure after reemerging from the rubble left by the property collapse of the early 1990s, analysts said.Analysts said the sector had bottomed and was starting to take slow and cautious steps forward but was still trailing the rest of
8270 the stock market.But they said the new-look market is shaping up to be far more focused on the home market than before with Swedish players starting to streamline their portfolios and divest themselves of large stakes in foreign property."Swedish real estate firms need to restructure their portfolios, mainly because they
8270 are so diversified," said an analyst at Handelsbanken."After the 1980s many firms saw that they couldn't manage properties all over Europe. They have to concentrate and be good on the local market."With over 30 property companies currently listed on the Stockholm bourse, analysts said the sector was ripe for rationalisation.
8270 After that it could start to look attractive."What you'll see in the future is fewer, larger companies," a property analyst from broker Matteus told Reuters."With a lot of finance deals and mergers, once you have larger more consolidated property companies, you will probably see more foreign interest in buying."The nation's
8270 banks are leading the drive to streamline portfolios.Four Swedish banks, S-E-Banken, Handelsbanken, Swedbank and Foreningsbanken, have this year started to trim their operations, spinning off property divisions, to concentrate on their core business, banking.This move was prompted after the government late last year scrapped the heavy tax burden banks had
8270 to pay if they wanted to get rid of the property stakes they inherited.One consequence of the troubles of the loan-loss crisis that swept across the Swedish banking system in the early 1990s was that the banks found themselves with huge real estate holdings, taken over as collateral on bad
8270 loans.Swedbank's former property division, Tornet, was independently quoted on the Stockholm bourse in early May and Handelsbanken's former property company, Nackebro, was listed in June.These two companies were among the highest climbers on the bourse list in August, with Tornet climbing to 75 crowns in August from a start of
