8271 A stream of corporate corruption scandals in Germany has dented its self-image as a by-the-rules player and spurred a fresh drive to clamp down on malpractice.The government plans to introduce tighter penalties for corruption -- doubling the maximum prison term for convicted civil servants to 10 years -- and is
8271 considering blacklisting errant companies from public service contracts.Public prosecutors are pushing to be allowed to use more powerful methods to crack major corruption rings, such as tapping telephone lines and offering informants the incentive of a reduced or waived sentence.Corruption has become a hot topic in Germany in recent years
8271 but public consternation reached new heights last summer when prosecutors revealed a probe into more than 200 people at 40 companies, among them 65 past and present staff at General Motors Corp subsidiary Opel.A second big scandal emerged this year as work ended on Frankfurt Airport's second terminal. Prosecutors mounted
8271 a massive investigation into a suspected corruption network of up to 50 managers, inluding airport staff and 20 contractors.Experts say corruption has always played a quiet role in German business, but the stakes have risen dramatically, especially in the battle for major public service contracts.While a fur coat or expensive
8271 dinner might have bought success in a public tender in the 1970s, prosecutors say some government officials are now demanding cash payments of thousands or even millions of marks just for information.Reliable figures are hard to find, but prosecutors estimate the annual cost of corruption in the public building sector
8271 alone at five to 10 billion marks -- a figure which gives the cash-strapped government an added incentive for a clampdown.In the state of Hesse, which includes the business capital of Frankfurt, systematic bribery costs the state finances between 120 million marks ($79.45 million) and 170 million marks a year."Compared
8271 with France or Italy, for example, the situation is fairly limited. But that doesn't change the fact that the level of corruption here -- for our society and with our legal system -- is dramatic and emotionally unacceptable," said Frankfurt senior public prosecutor Wolfgang Schaupensteiner.Schaupensteiner heads a nine-year-old specialist corruption
8271 task force -- Germany's first ever -- and says he is deluged with work. His division has probed 1,700 corruption cases to date and brought around 340 to court."We have over 300 cases pending," he said in an interview. "Every time one of our investigators clears up one case, it
8271 leads to dozens more, like an avalanche. That shows just how widespread corruption is."In most cases this is not just the site foreman getting a backhander. There are top level people, right up to management board level, dealing very personally with bribery," he said.The Frankfurt airport case alone, where losses
8271 on overpriced contracts and payments for non-existent deliveries are estimated at tens of millions of marks, is so much broader than it seemed at first that investigations will drag on at least until 1998, Schaupensteiner said.The scandals, continually highlighted in the media, have exploded Germany's belief that its public servants
8271 and business executives were above the kind of wheeling and dealing more associated with their more chaotic Mediterranean neighbours."Controls must be sharpened if the state is not to suffer lasting damage ... But the roots are in society's moral code ... If it is viewed as chic to bribe here
8271 and cheat a bit there, a corruption-free society remains a dream," the Berliner Morgenpost newspaper said in a recent editorial.Industry groups have issued their members with guidelines on how to break chains of bribery in their organisations and improve controls, but observers say a hard core of executives views corruption
8271 as part and parcel of everyday life."Ask anyone who deals with the German building sector, for example, about an anti-corruption drive and you will just get a tired smile and a shrug of the shoulders," said Karen Hussmann, editor of Berlin-based Transparency International, a quarterly newsletter on corruption worldwide.The building
8271 industry, where cash-strapped companies struggle furiously to win lucrative public contracts, has been at the heart of most big German corruption cases. A major probe into a contruction scam in Frankfurt in the late 1980s emptied offices and sites throughout the city for months.Engineering group Siemens suffered serious embarrassment last
8271 year when it was among five companies banned from doing business in Singapore for five years after being accused of involvement in the country's biggest ever corruption ring.Prosecutors claim to have discovered hundreds of smaller scale scams involving residence permits, driving licences, market stall licences and public sector housing.Even the
8271 medical profession is not immune. Prosecutors said this July they were investigating 1,860 doctors and health executives on suspicion of accepting 33 million marks in bribes to buy overpriced replacement heart valves and other equipment.The German cabinet in June approved a draft corruption law making price-fixing deals between firms tendering
8271 for contracts a criminal offence punishable with up to five years' prison.The proposals, which should be finalised this year, also raise the penalty for bribery in business to five years from one year and impose a maximum 10 years for giving or accepting bribes or gratuities in the public service
8271 sector.Prosecutors have welcomed what they say is overdue action from Bonn but say the government should take a tougher line.Schaupensteiner is pushing for a broader definition of corruption to include the "soft-soaping" to which he says government officials are continually exposed -- a suggestion Bonn has so far rejected as
8271 impracticable.Prosecutors and other justice officials have also called for reduced sentences for individuals who inform on a corruption ring, an almost unheard of occurrence at present because of the danger of prosecution."Principles like free competition are also at stake here, not just state funds. We have to stop corporate crime
8271 and corruption from gaining a stronger foothold here," said Schaupensteiner. ($1=1.5103 Mark)</

8275 an informal meeting of the 15-nation bloc's trade ministers in Dublin last week.Brittan warned there could be no progress on an ITA unless steps are taken to include the EU in a semiconductor deal signed in July by the United States and Japan after long negotiations.The Quad meeting, which brings
8275 together the trade ministers of Canada, the United States, Japan and the EU, this Thursday to Saturday, is expected to focus on an ITA, which which aims to reduce tariffs and other barriers on a wide range of products including semiconductors, computer hardware and software as well as telephone equipment.It
8275 has been on the drawing board since the World Trade Organisation took over from the General Agreement of Tariffs and Trade last year.The WTO seeks to introduce a global rules-based system of trade instead of the previous rash of bilateral and multilateral agreements that emerged during the computer industry boom
8275 of the 1980s.On Friday, U.S. acting trade representative Charlene Barshefsky said an ITA was impossible without Europe's participation."Europe needs to demonstrate leadership here," Barshefsky told reporters on Friday in a briefing ahead of the quad meeting. 8275 and industry officlas say they are unsure of Europe's motives in moving away from a deal, saying it could be a bargaining position or reflect division within the EU.But EU officials insist there is no division, and Brittan says he wants an ITA as much as anyone. Sources say, however,
8275 he is still fuming at being excluded from July's U.S-Japan semiconductor deal.The deal puts responsibility for monitoring semiconductor sales between those countries on the industry itself. 8275 "toothless", he is nevertheless concerned European chip producers have corenered a mere three percent of the Japanese market.Japan was reluctant to sign any deal, saying its market was already operating freely with nearly 30 percent of chip sales from foreign producers.Analysts say Barshefsky, knowing the U.S. is producing at full
8275 capacity has more than 20 percent of the market anyway, was desperate for a deal to formally include in president Bill Clinton's relection campaign.Washington and Tokyo have tried to include the EU, as well as emerging chip produces such as South Korea and Taiwan, in the deal by promising to
8275 establish a Global Governmental Forum along WTO lines, but Brittan is believed to want a more formal trilateral participation.But, analysts say, the EU is expecting something for nothing. 8285 India urged the world's major tea-producing countries on Monday to restrict exports in order to boost prices in what is now a stagnant market.S.K. Bhasin, managing director of the Goodricke Group of Companies and former chairman of the Indian Tea Association, told an Asia Tea Industry conference in Singapore that
8285 world output continued to rise while consumption remained flat."I suggest that the major tea-producing countries like China, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Kenya, Malawi and Bangladesh should sit together and work out a mutually acceptable formula for the exports of tea in the coming years," Bhasin said."The first important decision needed
8285 on the part of every exporting country is to restrict its exports to a level which fetches remunerative prices," he said.Alastair Hicks, a senior Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) official, told the conference production expansion programmes in many countries would boost output to 2.81 million tonnes by 2005 from the
8285 1991-93 average of 1.91 million tonnes.In 1994, production was 1.74 million tonnes while consumption was 1.70 million tonnes. Tea is a popular beverage in many countries in the world.Sri Lanka, the world's largest exporter, expected production to soar to an all-time high of 250 million kg in calendar 1996 against
8285 the former record of 245.96 million kg in 1995, said R.L. Jurainsz, former chair of the Colombo Tea Traders Association,But tea imports by major consumers like Britain fell nearly eight percent in 1995 to 137,000 tonnes while U.S. imports slid 15.8 percent to 81,300 tonnes, FAO figures showed."Tea export competition
8285 among exporting countries continued to intensify as demand remained weak," Hicks said.Bhasin said the excess supply made it vital that producing countries banded together and set aside a desire to boost exports in favour of a drive to boost prices."It does not require a mathematical genius to show that an
8285 indiscriminate increase in production and exports only results in a spiralling fall in tea prices and it is better to export a slightly lower quantity which can fetch a much higher price and a much bigger total revenue than to export a large quantiy at a very low price," he
8285 said.Another factor the tea industry faced was increased competition from other drinks like mineral water and soft drinks, said Rachmat Baduriddin, chairman of the Indonesian Tea Association."It's total share can be eroded drastically unless effective strategic measures are taken by the tea industry as a whole," the official said, adding
8285 the competition would continue "to exert very strong downward pressures on the tea industry".Tea-producing nations must launch a vigorous drive to raise tea consumption locally and to develop new markets in other countries, he added.</
8286 An overwhelming 85 percent of Chrysler Canada Ltd. workers participating in a ratification vote on Sunday voted in favor of a three-year contract that limits the company's ability to contract out jobs.About 42 percent of the 12,600 unionized members of the Chrysler Corp. unit's Canadian workforce turned out for the
8286 vote, officials at the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union said.The result, widely expected after CAW president Buzz Hargrove urged the 3,500 workers at company's assembly plants to accept the offer, sets the stage for talks with the local subsidiaries of the other two Big Three carmakers."Workers and their communities deserve
8286 to share in the success of the corporations -- this contract recognizes the contribution that workers have made to that success," Hargrove said while while announcing the result.Hargrove has said the CAW will announce Monday if it will next target Ford Motor Co. or General Motors Corp. .Talks with GM,
8286 which is trying to outsource more of its production, are expected to be tough.The deal with Chrysler, reached in a last-minute session ahead of a strike deadline Tuesday, provides for about 300 new jobs and wage increases and projected cost-of-living allowances totaling 10.2 percent over three years.Chrysler has said it
8286 will replace any job it contracts out with a similar job at one of its plants. It has also promised not to sell or close any plants over the life of the contract.The union will use the Chrysler deal as a blueprint for talks with Ford and GM in a
8286 strategy called pattern bargaining, used by the CAW and its U.S. counterpart, the United Autoworkers, for decades.The UAW earlier this month settled recently with Ford, which makes it likely that the CAW will choose GM as its next target.</

8290 Fears that Vietnam's economy could be slipping into a deflationary spiral receded on Tuesday after the government released figures showing that consumer prices had risen for the first time since April.The General Statistics Department said prices rose 0.3 percent (Corrects from 0.8 percent) this month from August, breaking a four-month
8290 run of declines.However, the year-on-year rate of inflation fell for the sixth month in a row to 2.9 percent. This is its lowest level for about three years and compares with a rate of 17.1 percent just 12 months ago.Vietnam's economic statistics, which lack the scientific rigour of those in
8290 more developed countries, are routinely issued ahead of the period which they measure.The government, fearing that the country's fast-growing economy could be coming off the boil, has expressed disquiet in recent weeks over the decline in consumer prices."We consider that if the inflation drops too drastically then it could affect
8290 the economy in terms of business operations and production," Deputy Prime Minister in charge of economic affairs Tran Duc Luong said earlier this month.He said measures may be taken before the end of the year to prevent the inflation rate from going below zero.The governor of the central bank said
8290 in an interview at the weekend that interest rates, which have already tumbled this year, would be eased further and the local currency adjusted to bolster the economy and narrow a yawning trade gap.Foreign bankers said governor Cao Si Kiem's oblique reference to the need for "raising" exchange rates was
8290 an indication that a managed depreciation of the currency was on the cards.The official rate of the local currency, the dong, against the dollar is around 11,022. It has been around 11,000 per dollar for more than two years.Peter McLean, head of treasury at Standard Chartered Bank in Hanoi, said
8290 the monetary easing proposed by Kiem would inject dong into the market place and should ensure that inflation turns higher towards the end of the year."I think we have seen the bottom in the downturn in inflation," McLean said. "I think the inflation rate will move higher over the next
8290 few months."Bankers say the decline in consumer prices has been partially fuelled by a slowdown in foreign direct investment, a development the communist government has been reluctant to admit.However, McLean said foreign investment was likely to pick up again in the last quarter of the year because some investors had
8290 been holding back ahead of a ministerial reshuffle expected next month.</

8293 Gulfstream Aerospace Corp 's $644 million initial public offering should be well received, but aerospace analysts warn the corporate jet maker will face tough competition for its new long-range G-V aircraft within a year.Gulfstream's "going to have an excellent 1997. But you have to look beyond the first year to
8293 properly value the stock," Robert Natale, director of equity research at Standard &amp; Poors, who tracks new stock offerings said.Gulfstream's new G-V aircraft has a one-year lead on the competition, but its potential market will shrink starting in 1997 as Boeing Co and Canada's Bombardier Inc launch comparable products, some
8293 aerospace analysts said.Gulfstream has an order backlog of about 64 G-V jets, the first of which will be delivered by year-end.Randall Greene, an aerospace consultant with Aeronautical Systems in Colorado doubts Gulfstream can meet analysts' projections for sales of up to 350 to 500 G-V planes over the next decade."There's
8293 no way Gulfstream can have the projected sales they say," Greene said. "Gulfstream's pretty much dominated the high-end of the corporate jet business for 30 years or so, but that's without much competition."Most of Gulfstream's jets are sold to repeat customers. But the G-V offers "only 25 percent more performance,
8293 but a 50 percent increase in price" than the previous G-IV model, Greene said.At the hefty price tag of over $30 million, the "potential market is already smaller than for Gulfstream's earlier products. But with competition, the market really shrinks," Greene said.Gulfstream's 19-passenger G-V is also virtually identical in payload,
8293 speed and price as Bombardier's jet, analysts said. The competing aircrafts also have the same engine.Greene expects Gulfstream to sell about 150 G-V planes over the next decade, compared to total sales of about 270 G-IV planes, Gulfstream's earlier model.Wolfgang Demisch, an aerospace analyst with BT Securities, is more bullish,
8293 saying Gulfstream will benefit from the increased globalization of business and growing Asian demand."The market for long-range planes with trans-Pacific capabilities will be surprisingly good," giving both Gulfstream and Bombardier "room to co-exist," Demisch said.Demisch said he expects sales of G-V caliber products to reach up to 1,000 jets over
8293 20 years.Regardless of the long-range sales forecasts, some analysts who track new stock offerings say Gulfstream's initial stock offering will be well received by institutional investors attracted by its worldwide name recognition.John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, says Gulfstream's 28 million share offering in early October "should be hot.""But
8293 that depends what you're in there for," Fitzgibbon said. If you're in this for a flip, it's not bad.""We're pretty neutral on the deal," said Steven Tuen, an analyst with IPO Value Monitor.Gulfstream recently narrowed the expected price range for the offering to $22 to $24 a share, from an
8293 original range of $21 to $25 a share, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.Other analysts said they are concerned about Gulfstream's 18 percent (corrects from 230 percent) debt-to-capital ratio."We have an 'avoid' on this stock. 8293 will able to pull this (offering) off," Standard &amp; Poor's Natale said.Proceeds from the offering will go to Fortsmann Little &amp; Co and other selling shareholders, not back into Gulfstream - which also has become a concern for some investors.Forstmann acquire Gulfstream in 1990 through a leveraged buyout. 8293 jet maker's first attempt at a public offering failed in 1992.-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610</

8302 Bayern Munich and Parma, the last two winners of the UEFA Cup, both crashed out of the competition on Tuesday.Bayern, whose grip on the trophy was prised open by Valencia two weeks ago, finally relinquished their hold when they were eliminated 3-1 on aggregate by the Spanish side despite winning
8302 the second leg 1-0.Although Bayern won the second leg at the Olympic Stadium, they failed to turn their obvious superiority into sufficient goals. A softly-taken missed penalty by German skipper Juergen Klinsmann summed up his side's night.Bayern's only goal came after two minutes when defender Javi Navarro headed into his
8302 own net under pressure from Christian Ziege following Mario Basler's inswinging corner.If Klinsmann had converted the 15th-minute penalty, Bayern might have had a real chance of clawing back the deficit but despite going close several times -- they forced 10 corners to Valencia's none -- they could not score again."If
8302 we can't even score from a penalty then how are we expected to win ?" said dismayed Bayern president Franz Beckenbauer.Bayern captain Lothar Matthaeus added: "We missed the chance early to go 2-0 up early on -- not just from Klinsmann's penalty. We had other good opportunities too. In the
8302 second half we tried to use too much force, but we lost the tie in Valencia, not here."Parma, who won the UEFA Cup in 1995, went to Vitoria Guimaraes in Portugal holding a 2-1 lead from the first leg, but lost 2-0 for a 3-2 aggregate defeat.The Portuguese side won
8302 with goals from Vitor Paneira after 15 minutes and Ricardo Lopes, four minutes after the break.Guimaraes surprised powerful Parma with the force of their counter attack and scored two without reply to win the tie.Soon after Brazilian striker Gilmar Estevam lost a golden chance to score when Parma goalkeeper Buffon
8302 blocked his shot with his legs, international midfielder Paneira lobbed the ball over Buffon's head in the 15th minute.Striker Ricardo Lopes, whose goal was annulled when he was caught offside at the beginning of the second half, headed home in the 49th minute after the Italian defence failed to intercept
8302 a cross from the right.Striker Dino Baggio was Parma's most dangerous player but his 63rd minute header was disallowed after the referee ruled that he had fouled a Guimaraes defender.While Parma, and Bayern went out, Bayern's northern German rivals Hamburg reached the third round after an ill-tempered 2-0 win over
8302 Celtic which saw Celtic reduced to nine men and Hamburg finish with only 10.Hamburg went through 4-0 on aggregate but were helped by some suicidal Celtic tackling and some harsh refereeing which left the Scottish team with just nine men by half-time.Malky Mackay and John Hughes were each dismissed for
8302 two bookable offences, while Hamburg's Markus Schupp was sent off in the second half by Belarus referee Viktor Schuk.As well as the dismissals, Celtic lost their leading scorer, Portuguese striker Jorge Cadete, after only 13 minutes when he was carried off following a vicious foul by Hamburg defender Stephane Henchoz.Celtic
8302 manager Tommy Burns had a furious on-the-pitch argument with the referee as the teams headed towards the dressing-room at half-time. Goals from Karsten Baron (24th) and Andre Breitenreiter (50th) sealed the Germans victory.Sweden, whose part-timers have consistently embarrased England's highly-paid stars in recent seasons, did so again with Helsingborgs, most
8302 of whose players earn 300 pounds a week, knocking out Aston Villa, whose players earn about 20 times more.Helsinborgs, who scraped a 1-1 draw in England two weeks ago, prevented Villa from scoring and with the match ending 0-0 Helsingborgs won on the away goals rule.Newcastle, fielding the world's most
8302 expensive player in the form of 15 million pounds ($23.36 million) striker Alan Shearer, also lost in Sweden, going down 2-1 to part-timers Halmstads but went through 5-2 on aggregate.Despite advancing, Newcastle manager Kevin Keegan blasted his highly-paid team afterwards."We just didn't perform. We were average, right throughout the side.
8302 From front to back and back to front, nobody played well. We didn't deserve to win and the better team did win. They were the team that wanted it more and showed more enthusiasm."Just 300 fans watched Portuguese club Boavista reach the second round on the away goals rule at
8302 Benfica's 120,000-capacity stadium.Boavista used Benfica's ground for their home leg against Denmark's Odense after being banned by UEFA from playing at their own ground in Oporto.Two goals inside three minutes midway through the second half by Jasper Hjorth and Ulrik Pedersen gave Odense a 2-1 win on the night.But the
8302 aggregate score of 4-4 left Boavista winners on the away goals rule.</
8303 MIAMI, Sept 24 - Miami Dolphins star quarterback Dan Marino has a fractured right ankle and is out indefinitely, the National Football League club said Tuesday.Marino left Monday night's 10-6 loss at Indianapolis in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return. X-rays taken at the stadium
8303 and the injury originally was diagnosed as a sprain. But an MRI Tuesday revealed a non-displaced fracture."The MRI test taken today showed an acute non-displaced fracture of his (right ankle)," Dolphins trainer Kevin O'Neill said in a statement. "Proper steps are being taken to stabilise the fracture, and he will
8303 begin a course of treatment and rehabilitation."O'Neill gave no timetable as to Marino's possible return.Head coach Jimmy Johnson, however, held out hope in his weekly news conference Tuesday, saying that without complications Marino would miss the next three to four weeks.The Dolphins (3-1) have a bye week before hosting the
8303 Seattle Seahawks Oct. 6.The 35-year-old Marino was limping slightly as he came off the field following Miami's first possession. He completed 5-of-6 passes to move the Dolphins to the Colts 7-yard line before throwing two incompletions in the end zone.Marino removed his shoe and was treated on the sideline by
8303 trainers, who wrapped his foot in tape and administered an ice pack. He stayed on the sidelines until late in the first half, when he was taken to the locker room on a golf cart.Veteran Bernie Kosar replaced Marino. Craig Erickson, who played for coach Johnson at the University of
8303 Miami and was signed early in the season, is the third-stringer.</

8306 Tour of Spain leader Alex Zuelle showed signs of vulnerability after struggling to stay with his rivals in the mountain finish of Tuesday's 17th stage.Zuelle had to be helped from his bike after failing to match the searing pace set by team mate Oliverio Rincon, who raced away to victory
8306 in impressive style.Zuelle was left several seconds adrift by team mate Laurent Jalabert and fellow Swiss rider Laurent Dufaux, who both picked up bonus time after following Rincon home.Jalabert gained a provisional 18 seconds in the overall classification, leaving him one minute 10 seconds behind Zuelle, while Dufaux is still
8306 over four minutes further back after gaining nine seconds on the leader.Zuelle was still short of breath five minutes after finishing the climb, which ended at nearly 2,000 metres."It's not over until Madrid," said Zuelle, who had looked in complete control in previous mountain finishes.As in the previous stages, most
8306 of the leading riders arrived at the final climb together, but were split as Rincon made his move five kilometres from home.With Zuelle wilting, Jalabert protected his team's interests by sticking close to a dangerous-looking Dufaux."I preferred to keep my strength for later, a few seconds now doesn't mean very
8306 much. I still have to fight off people like Rominger for my place on the winner's podium," said Dufaux.Tony Rominger saw his chances of winning a fourth consecutive Vuelta all but disappear after losing nearly eight minutes in the third stage.But the Swiss rider retained a good chance of closing
8306 the three and a half minute gap to take third place, and again looked strong on Tuesday when he came in fourth, a provisional 38 seconds behind Rincon and one behind Jalabert and Dufaux.With Jalabert already reconciled to letting his fellow ONCE rider take the honours, Zuelle must remain firm
8306 favourite for the overall crown despite his problems.The riders are likely to take Wednesday's straightforward 222-km stage from Benasque to Zaragoza easily, before facing the last mountain sections of the Vuelta on Thursday and Friday.The race concludes with Saturday's time-trial and the largely flat final stage in Madrid on Sunday.</

8309 Kimiko Date, Japan's top woman tennis player and one of the most popular athletes in the country, announced on Tuesday she would retire at the end of the season, saying she had achieved all she could."I came to think that now is the limit of my strength," Date told a
8309 news conference.Date, who turns 26 on Saturday, said she first began thinking of retiring in June when the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) announced it would introduce a new, more severe, world ranking system from next year."I felt a sense of fulfilment, particularly last year and this year, because I think
8309 I played evenly-balanced matches with the top players in the world," Date said.She said she made her final decision just before the start of last week's Nichirei women's tournament in Tokyo in which she lost a tough three-set semifinal against joint world number one Monica Seles.After turning professional in 1989,
8309 Date became the first Japanese player to reach the world top 10 in January 1994 and achieved her highest ranking of world number four at the end of last year. She is currently ranked seventh.Date obtained the seventh tour victory of her career last month when she beat Arantxa Sanchez
8309 Vicario of Spain in the final of the Toshiba tournament in the United States.She won her first professional tournament in 1992.Date said the most memorable moments of her career were matches against world number one Steffi Graf.Date gained an upset win over Graf in the quarter-finals of the Federation Cup
8309 in April, leading Japan to the semifinals for the first time.Graf was also her opponent when she produced one of her best performances in this July's Wimbledon semifinals.Date reeled off six successive games to level the match at one set each before play was halted because of bad light. Graf
8309 regained the initiative the following day to win 6-2 2-6 6-3.Date said she had not decided what to do after her career ends at the WTA championship in New York in November."But I'm not announcing my retirement to get married," she said. Date has been romantically linked to a popular
8309 actor by the Japanese media.She said she had no reservations about her decision to quit tennis."I have no regrets...I was able to achieve things which I never dreamed of when I started playing tennis," she said.</

8330 St Petersburg, Russia.Competition will be in athletics, basketball, boxing, cycling (track), diving, figure skating, gymnastics, rhythmic gymnastics, swimming, synchronized swimming, triathlon, and volleyball (beach and indoor).Sports that were eliminated included archery, rowing, weight lifting, yachting, canoe-kayak, judo, team handball, wrestling, water polo, soccer, speed skating and tae kwan do."We are
8330 trying to create a marketability as well as a TV-friendly product and that's why we picked the sports that we have," said Dr Harvey Schiller, president of Turner Sports, whose president, Ted Turner, founded the Games in 1986."These are the marquee sports and that we believe garner the most interest
8330 from the public," Schiller said.More than 2,000 athletes competed in 24 different sports in St Petersburg. 8330 that will provide enough motivation to bring the world's best here," said Plant, who would not reveal how the prize money would be allocated.The first to sign up for the Games is Olympic hero Michael Johnson, who raced into the record books in Atlanta as the only man ever to
8330 win the 200 and 400 meters in the same Olympics."The good thing about the Goodwill Games in the past two that I have competed in is that they don't try to be like an Olympics," said Johnson."This is a separate and unique event," he said. "This is much more like

8344 the court, trying to establish how much money was funnelled abroad out of the reach of tax authorities, that Peter Graf had been paid between $150,000 and $270,000 a year for "services and advertising" in connection with DTB-run events in Hamburg and Berlin between 1990 and 1993.Asked if this was
8344 mostly money paid to ensure the tournaments had a big-name attraction, Sanders replied "Yes."The news weekly Der Spiegel said last weekend the widespread payment of appearance money to all top women players was an open secret.It said Steffi Graf and joint No. 1 Monica Seles each commanded between $30,000 and
8344 $400,000 to play in an event, depending on its size, with players ranked down to No. 13 receiving correspondingly less.The anecdotal examples cited by Der Spiegel from records produced in connection with Peter Graf's trial added up to a total of well over $2 million in appearance payments.While many smaller
8344 events need to pull in big stars to sell tickets, the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) has banned the payment of appearance money for fear it damages the players' competitiveness.WTA Tour rules state that "No player, agent, coach or family member shall accept money or anything of value that is given
8344 from any sources, directly or indirectly, to influence or guarantee her appearance..."The rules stipulate a fine of at least $50,000 and a ban of up to 90 days for each offence, together with repayment of the money. Organisers who pay appearance money can lose the right to stage the tournament.The
8344 Connecticut-based WTA, in a statement from chief executive Anne Person Worcester Tuesday, insisted it was "inappropriate" for them to comment on specific issues while the Graf trial was in progress."To date the Tour is not aware of any substantiated evidence of appearance money being paid to any Tour player," she
8344 said."The Tour is monitoring the ongoing trial, and if any evidence warrants further investigation, the Tour would conduct an investigation."Peter Graf is accused together with family tax adviser Joachim Eckardt of evading some $12.5 million in taxes on his daughter's earnings between 1989 and 1993. He could face a jail
8344 sentence of up to 10 years.His daughter is also under investigation, although she says she left her financial affairs to her father.</

8348 Early pacesetters Ajax Amsterdam and Grasshopper Zurich meet on Wednesday in Group A of the European Cup's Champions' League, with the Dutch side seeking to end a worrying goal drought.Ajax, winners of Europe's premier club competition in 1995 and beaten finalists in 1996, have looked dramatically off form in the
8348 Dutch first division and languish in seventh place, already eight points adrift of leaders Feyenoord Rotterdam.Transfers and injuries have decimated the team which took Ajax to European glory and won the World Club Cup but the key deficiency has been in scoring goals.With sharpshooter Patrick Kluivert sidelined with a long-term
8348 knee injury and Nigerian international Nwankwo Kanu at Inter Milan, the Dutch champions have lost their fire power.Seven league games have yielded only five goals, all at home. At the same stage last season Ajax had scored 27 goals and were well on their way to their 26th domestic title.As
8348 hopes fade fast of adding a 27th, Ajax are already looking to Europe to keep their season alive.A battling 1-0 win in Auxerre earlier this month, courtesy of Finn Jari Litmanen's 20th European goal, suggested the Dutch may have been written off too early and sets up an intriguing encounter
8348 with the Swiss who rolled over Glasgow Rangers 3-0 on the same night for their first ever Champions' League win.Like Ajax, the Zurich club's league form does not match their European exploits.They are currently third in the Swiss league with just one win in their last five games and will
8348 delay selection pending fitness tests on seven doubtful starters -- Mats Gren, Joel Magnin, Harald Gamperle, Tomasz Rzasa, Alain Geiger, Nestor Subiat and Kubilay Turkyilmaz who has a strained calf-muscle.Euro 96 striker Turkyilmaz, who scored twice against Rangers and has netted five goals in 12 Swiss league games this season,
8348 has attracted the attention of Ajax, according to Dutch reports.But Grasshopper coach Erich Vogel is adamant the player will not be allowed to leave -- at least while the side is still in Europe."It's not in our plans to give up our best attacker while we have an ace to
8348 play yet in the Champions' League," he said.Ajax welcome back skipper Danny Blind from injury but fellow international defender Winston Bogarde has joined a lengthy injury list which already sidelines John Veldman, Richard Witschge, Kluivert and Peter Hoekstra.In France a fortnight ago, coach Louis van Gaal gave five players their
8348 European debut and was rewarded with a commanding performance in which the emphasis was on defending an early lead.But, as he brings European soccer to Ajax's new super-stadium for the first time, Van Gaal will be hoping for more fizz up front to boost his side's chances of reaching the
8348 last eight for the third year in a row.History favours the Dutch, who beat the Swiss club 3-0 in Amsterdam at the same stage of the competition last season, although Grasshopper were the only side in the group to take a point from Ajax with a 0-0 draw in Zurich.Teams:Ajax

8349 President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday unveiled a monument to the composer of the hymn that is the national anthem of three African states, calling it the torch that lit South Africa's path to freedom.The ceremony at a Johannesburg cemetery, staged on the Heritage Day national holiday, honoured Enoch Sontonga who
8349 composed Nkosi Sikelel iAfrika (God Bless Africa) in 1897.The music and lyrics were adopted by Mandela's African National Congress as its official hymn at its inaugural meeting in 1912 and became the main theme of South Africa's national anthem after historic all-race elections in 1994.Political prisoners on death row sang
8349 the hymn on the eve of executions before a moratorium on hangings was instituted in 1990.Sontonga's unmarked grave was discovered only in April after a search of about 18 months. The entry in the cemetery register when Sontonga was buried in 1905 read: "Enoch, 32 years, April 19, Kaffir." Kaffir
8349 is a pejorative term for blacks."The circumstances of Sontonga's burial, in a segregated cemetery, in an unmarked grave, is a harsh reminder of the times in which the hymn was composed," Mandela said in a speech at the ceremony."We owe (this ceremony) to the countless men, women and children across
8349 the generations who carried this anthem in their hearts, in the face of bullets and the hangman's noose; in moments of terrible privation and in the joy of celebration," Mandela said.The tune is the basis of the national anthems of Zambia and Tanzania. Zimbabwe also used it as an anthem
8349 until two years ago."Nkosi Sikelel iAfrika is a prayer for crops and rain, for harvest, health and peace for all," Mandela said. "It is the torch that has lit our way."Mandela said Heritage Day, an annual holiday declared by his government after it won the 1994 election, was intended to
8349 honour those who had fought injustice and inequity so the country could "rise like the phoenix from the ashes of division and conflict."In a separate Heritage Day ceremony in the Zulu heartland province of KwaZulu-Natal, Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini urged South Africans to put their differences aside."Let us stop making
8349 ourselves the scorn of other nations," the king, clad in traditional leopard skin regalia, told a ululating crowd of about 3,000 people in the Indian Ocean port city of Durban.KwaZulu-Natal has been the scene of the worst of the political violence in which more than 20,000 people have been killed
8349 in South Africa since the mid-1980s.The violence, which has eased since the 1994 election, pitted the ANC against the Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party and members of the white-led security forces.</
8350 South African police fired tear gas and rubber bullets on Tuesday to quell a new outbreak of ethnic clashes between gold miners in which 21 have been killed in the past three days, a spokesman said.The police spokesman told reporters three miners from the gold mining area around Klerksdorp, 160
8350 km (100 miles) southwest of Johannesburg, were killed in fighting overnight between members of the Xhosa and Sotho tribes.He said the toll since Saturday midnight stood at 21 dead and 38 seriously injured. In the first clashes early on Sunday, seven miners were killed when assailants blew up their homes
8350 with blasting explosives."This morning the two groups attacked each other again and police fired tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse them. The situation is quiet now," the spokesman said.It is not clear what sparked the Klerksdorp fighting, but newspapers have reported that one group of miners had decided to
8350 avenge a colleague who was killed in a fight over a woman.The clashes have centred on the Buffelsfontein Gold Mining Company Ltd , owned by marginal mines specialist Randgold &amp; Exploration Co Ltd , which recently bought it from Gencor Ltd .In July and August about 30 miners were killed
8350 in ethnic clashes on four other mines, run by Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd .President Nelson Mandela has appointed a judicial inquiry into the fighting.Migrant labourers at most of the country's mines are accommodated in hostels segregated by ethnic group. Union leaders say the system is a legacy of
8350 apartheid but mine managers say the workers do not want to be forced to share housing with members of other tribes.</

8358 Several factors -- including "non-collegial" behaviour among banks and the central bank's own monetary tightening -- contributed to liquidity problems at Agrobanka a.s. , Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.Speaking on Czech Radio on Tuesday, Klaus said Agrobanka, which the central bank last week put under "temporary" forced administration of an
8358 undetrmined length due to illiquidty, had to look at its own behaviour also as a source of its problems.He said that the central bank's raising of its minimum reserve requirement for banks to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent earlier in the summer in an effort to reduce inflationary domestic demand,
8358 had played a role in Agrobanka's troubles."That affected the entire banking system and ... when someone is more injured and who has a fever and then breaks its leg, this is pretty, pretty bad. That's what happened also to Agrobanka," Klaus said in the radio interview.Klaus said Agrobanka "acted maybe
8358 riskier, in some ways, maybe less riskier, maybe smarter, maybe it made more mistakes", but said the bank's behaviour played a role.The Czech National Bank had said the interbank market had recently ignored trading with Agrobanka, which had close connections with the failed Kreditni Banka a.s. through its shareholder, the
8358 investment group Motoinvest.Klaus said that "such non-collegiality between banks added another drop to the whole problem".The prime minister, who has been praised for his classical liberal free-market views, defended the intervention by the central bank in Agrobanka saying liberalism does not mean "insufficient order".-- John Mastrini, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003</

8369 above the central bank's weighted mark/dollar basket, mainly on the strength of a large purchase, but then eased toward the central bank fixing of +2.80 percent."There was a huge Czech crown purchase coming through the whole morning from outside the Czech Republic, and this caused a lot of the participants
8369 on the market to be short (in crowns)," said Petr Korous at CSOB in Prague."This was a totally contrarian move," Korous added, saying it was not yet clear who was behind the large trade.The crown opened the morning just barely higher than two percent above parity of the mark/dollar basket,
8369 after the central bank's fixing at +2.61 percent on Monday.Korous said the sentiment on the market was still mostly negative as the government gets battered by the opposition about recent problems of Czech banks, repeatedly calling for the dismissal of Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.The crown had been dropping since the
8369 middle of last week when it traded more than four percent above the basket.Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his Civic Democratic Party have refused to recall Kocarnik, and have primarily blamed the Czech National Bank for lax supervision in the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. and illiquidity at Agrobanka a.s..But

8389 Quebec government-owned utility Hydro-Quebec on Tuesday defended the lucrative long-term contract under which it purchases electricity from Newfoundland's Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corp at advantageous rates.On Monday, Newfoundland Premier Brian Tobin demanded that the contract, which runs to 2041, be renegotiated because Churchill Falls will begin losing money on it in
8389 2001. Newfoundland contends that the electricity, which amounts to about 30 billion kilowatt hours annually from the 5,420 megawatt facility in Labrador, costs Hydro-Quebec only C$80 million a year, but generates revenues of about C$750 million when the utility resells it to customers in Quebec and the northeastern United States.Michel
8389 Grignon, senior vice-president of marketing at Hydro-Quebec told Reuters that the cost to Hydro-Quebec of the Churchill Falls power is roughly C$100 million a year, and he did not dispute that the Quebec utility would sell that amount of electricity for about C$750 million. But those revenues do not account
8389 for the cost of transmitting the energy to Quebec's power grid and onto its domestic and U.S. customers. In addition, Hydro-Quebec took all the financial and market risks associated with building the C$950 billion Churchill Falls generating facility in the early 1970s, Grignon said.Under the contract, negotiated before the spike
8389 in world energy prices in the early 1970s, the initial price Hydro-Quebec paid for the Churchill Falls declines over time, in part because of the risks Hydro-Quebec assumed with the project. "Since the beginning of the contract, (Churchill Falls) has made profits every year, and (had) rates of return that
8389 even Hydro-Quebec is not able to make, and this they have been making without any risk at all," Grignon said.Grignon said Churchill Falls made C$22 million of profit last year and he expects that it will continue to be profitable for the next 30 years. Newfoundland has also argued that
8389 the Churchill Falls contract accounts for most or all of Hydro-Quebec's annual net profit, which was C$390 million in 1995 and which the utility forecasts to rise to C$516 million next year. But Grignon said almost 9,000 megawatts of power in Hydro-Quebec's 30,435 megawatts of network capacity is produced at
8389 a cost that is lower than the price paid for Churchill Falls' power.Those plants were built long before Churchill Falls."The best 9,000 megawatts that Hydro-Quebec has in its park now costs less or the equivalent of Churchill Falls -- that's production and transmission costs," Grignon said. Hydro-Quebec pays Churchill Falls
8389 about 2.7 mils, or 2.7 tenths of a Canadian cent for each kilowatt hour. That rate is set to decline 2.5 tenths of a Canadian cent in 2001.Grignon said Hydro-Quebec's average transmission costs are about 1.2 Canadian cents for each kilowatt hour, while the average production cost of power, excluding
8389 the electricity supplied by Churchill Falls, is about two Canadian cents a kilowatt hour. The production cost at Hydro-Quebec's most recently commissioned megaproject, La Grande-1 in James Bay, is four Canadian cents a kilowatt hour for annual production of about 60 billion kilowatt hours, Grignon said.Although the controversy over Churchill
8389 Falls has strong political overtones involving already strained relations between Newfoundland and the separatist Parti Quebecois government in Quebec, Grignon said the further development of hydroelectric resources in Labrador can be done in a way that both provinces benefit."The whole electric industry is restructuring in North America. There will be
8389 many opportunities for developing business on a win-win situation and I think that we will be able to do that," Grignon said.-- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434</

8396 Canada's Stentor group of telephone companies said on Tuesday it has filed with the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission asking the telecommunications watchdog to stop regulating inter-exchange private line services.These services allow large customers to lease dedicated capacity from the public network to run their voice, data, video and image
8396 transmissions to their various offices across the country, from Canada to the United States and internationally through the facilities of U.S. carriers or satellite provider Teleglobe Canada Inc. Stentor said it excluded from its application its dedicated local access services such as Digital Network Access service and Local Channel services.The
8396 group said it asked the CRTC to rule by January 2, 1997 and, if the regulator agrees to the application, to get out of regulating these services by April 2 that year.Stentor, which consists of nine telephone companies, said competition in Canada's private line market is heating up, particularly in
8396 the high-capacity area. Stentor's share of the higher capacity market is roughly 50 percent, and the group said this should fall as competitors expand their reach.</

8403 Toronto Sun Publishing Corp said on Tuesday that shareholders at a special meeting approved a management group's C$16 a share bid for the newspaper company. Chairman Lionel Schipper told shareholders the deal would close on October 7 if the plan of arrangement allowing management to take the company private won
8403 court approval on Wednesday.The buyout would return Toronto Sun to its roots as a tightly held company with lots of employee involvement, Schipper said.The company will have a nine-member board, on which two members will be memed by CIBC Wood Gundy, two will be independents and two will be management
8403 appointees. The Ontario Teachers Pension Plan will appoint three members. Schipper admitted the next quarter-century may be tough. But he added that the first 25 years were hard for the Sun, which grew out of the defunct Toronto Telegram in the early 1970s, and it successfully weathered that storm."In any
8403 new company, there are always tough decisions... when you have C$250 million of debt, you have to look at things a little differently than when you are debt-free," management team leader Paul Godfrey told reporters after the meeting."We will be looking at every possibility of how we handle that C$250
8403 million in debt," he added. Godfrey did not rule out either asset sales or staff cuts. Many analysts believe Toronto Sun's debt may force it to sell its 60.2 percent holding in the Financial Post newspaper.Reports last week said Conrad Black's Southam Inc was interested in Toronto Sun's holding in
8403 the daily business tabloid. But chief financial officer Bruce Jackson on Monday said the management group had not received any bids for the asset and were interested in keeping it."I would consider every possibility...Everything is on the table but I am not going to get specific because that is unfair,"
8403 he told reporters. "We have not made any decisions yet," Godfrey said.He indicated that current plans are to keep the Sun group intact, despite the onerous debtload."We made a bid for all the assets of the Sun group and if we had any other intentions, we would have to reveal
8403 them in the information circular," Godfrey said.Godfrey was unable to confirm whether Schipper will stay on as chairman of the company. He said this is something which the team is still discussing. The management team emerged victorious in an auction Rogers Communications Inc held earlier this summer for its 63
8403 percent holding in the company.Although speculation that Quebecor Inc could step in with an eleventh-hour bid appears to have little foundation given the smooth progress of the management takeover through shareholder approval, Schipper admitted that another party has the right to make a higher offer up until the closing on
8403 October 7.-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com</

8432 Latest weekly inventory figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) suggest that the downstream oil industry is having trouble responding to a sharp switch in demand, analysts said Tuesday.The report showed that, as winter approaches, distillates stocks (mainly heating oil) were up by only around 300,000 barrels last week and
8432 actually fell in the key eastern district (PADD1) to stand almost 19 million barrels below last year's level at just above 38 million barrels. At the same time, gasoline, which traditionally sees waning demand after the early September Labor Day holiday, saw a three million-barrel rise in stocks, rising output
8432 and rising imports."What is puzzling to me is, given the picture we are discussing (of a heating oil shortage and a gasoline surplus), you would think that refiners would be shifting production towards the middle of the barrel (to make more distillates)," said Cyrus Tahmassebi, an economist and president of
8432 Energy Trends Inc. in Washington D.C. But refinery runs rose again last week, API reported, to 95.5 percent of capacity, up a half percentage point."It doesn't make a lot of sense. The economics clearly are better on the heating oil end of the barrel," said John Saucer, an oil industry
8432 analyst at Smith Barney in Houston.Possible contributory factors for the refinery industry's slowness to react to market conditions is that over the past two years while gearing up for increased gasoline production they lost some of the flexibility. Also, delayed maintenance may have inhibited their ability to respond to market
8432 conditions, Saucer said. And refiners, with their huge fixed costs, do not have many options to cut back on gasoline, their main product."There is a limit to how much you can do when generally 50 percent of how much you produce is going to be gasoline," said Marianne Kah, general
8432 manager of market analysis at Conoco, a unit of Dupont Co.The distillate production usually is around 25 percent and for most refineries the output swing possibility is between five and 10 percent. The U.S. market has the added problem of providing a market for the surplus gasoline produced in Europe.
8432 A firm distillate market there also has increased gasoline production and prices in the U.S. have looked relatively better.That was reflected in the figures where imports of gasoline last week again jumped, rising by 166,000 barrels to 507,000 barrels.The situation is expected to get worse before it gets better because
8432 of the slow response times of the refineries. "You can't just switch your slate lickety-split," said a refinery engineer at Phillips Petroleum Co in Oklahoma. "We buy crude one or two months in advance and some others up to six months in advance. You usually would assume the diesel/heating oil
8432 season wouldn't start until October and there's not a lot that people can do when you get it wrong.""It is clear that refiners are going to have to work on getting yields shifted and/or cut gasoline production," said Saucere of Smith Barney. As for the immediate market reaction to the
8432 latest report, the bullish distillate figures and a drop of more than 2.5 million barrels in crude stocks when the volatile western region (PADD5) is excluded, was expected to overshadow the bearish gasoline story.In after hours trading Tuesday November NYMEX crude was at $24.12/15 a barrel, up from $24.07 at
8432 the close when it gained 70 cents.-- New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620</

8434 A worldwide network to share information on air safety should be set up to swap and disseminate the wealth of data that already exists to make flying safer, a top industry official urged here Tuesday."We're going to have to find ways to close the door, leave the badges behind and
8434 share information about what causes aviation accidents," Edmond Soliday, vice president of corporate safety and security for UAL Corp's United Airlines told the Americas Conference on Aviation.If accident rates don't improve worldwide, the Boeing Co has projected that by the year 2015 with increased air traffic there will be a
8434 fatal air accident every eight to ten days, officials at the conference noted."We must find new ways to share information that are faster, more accurate, more comprehensive, more organized and more secure," Soliday said.One barrier to such cooperation is that many entities do not trust one another to share information,
8434 he said. Carriers do not trust their competitors or unions and nobody trusts the government, he said.Another speaker at the meeting of airline industry and public officials from throughout North and South America, Barry Bermingham, deputy assistant administrator for the Federal Aviation Administration, told of potentially dangerous quirks at some
8434 airports that "all the pilots knew about" and compensate for, but are not discussed. Eventually some of these problems have caused accidents, Bermingham said.Soliday urged the creation of some type of flight safety round table which would have no ties to any organization, manufacturer, airline or government. "The key ingredient
8434 to our success is trust," Soliday said.The Federal Aviation Administration is pushing a similar proposal it calls a Global Analysis and Information Network or GAIN."GAIN would make (safety information) available online to aviation safety researchers everywhere," said David Hinson, FAA administrator."GAIN has a lot of positive things going for it,"
8434 Soliday told Reuters, but "it rests on the expectation that people will freely give information. I think you have got to build trust before you build systems. You have got to bring people together first."Under Soliday's round table plan, information would be shared orally and "all information would remain the
8434 property of the participants. No raw data would be given up."But besides the roundtable idea, Soliday urged aviation participants to trust each other more and swap information informally."We (United) have shared our emergency response manual with at least 60 carriers," he said.</

8439 With less natural gas being injected into storage this year compared to last year, Texas could experience shortages this winter, a staff member of the Texas Railroad Commission said on Tuesday.Nationwide, storage levels appear to be back on track with 1995, but Texas gas storage this year is "not anywhere
8439 close to where it was a year ago," said David Schieck, director of head of the commission's oil and gas division."There may be some shortages," Schieck said.Texas producers have not curtailed production, but some made adjustments for over-production earlier this year, contributing to the lagging storage levels, he said.The commission
8439 estimated storage levels in the state rose slightly to 182.8 billion cubic feet (bcf) at September 15. Texas gas in storage in August was 165.1 bcf in August compared to 265.9 bcf in August 1995.The commission set October production allowables for prorated fields in the state at 2.96 billion cubic
8439 feet per day, or 93 percent of actual October 1995 production.</

8442 Brooklyn Union Gas Co, the New York-based utility, is deploying deregulated subsidiaries to boost its local market share while looking ahead at opportunities in electricity, senior company officials said."It is an appropriate move at this time as the industry moves into a deregulated environment," Robert Catell, Brooklyn Union's chairman and
8442 chief executive officer, told Reuters in a telephone interview."It gives us more flexibility and added value to shareholders." Earlier this month, the New York Public Service Commission approved Brooklyn Union's plans to reorganize its gas distribution operations and subsidiaries into a holding company, called KeySpan Energy Corp.The restructuring plan still
8442 needs SEC and shareholder approval, expected in February.Meanwhile, members of the KeySpan group, independent of the regulated Brooklyn Union utility, already have been targeting the gas market and related services in the tri-state region of New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut. William Feraudo, senior vice president in the KeySpan Energy
8442 Marketing Group, said that since late May KeySpan has picked up about 1,200 customers - mostly commerical, like diners and dry cleaners - in the New York City area.This translates into gas sales of about 1.2 billion cubic feet on an annualized basis.Most of the new customers are in territory
8442 traditionally served by neighboring Long Island Lighting Co (Lilco) and from Brooklyn Union's own 1.1 million customers. The Public Service Commission has approved 21 marketers to sell gas to former Brooklyn Union customers using the utility's existing distribution lines. Only nine of them, including KeySpan, have actually locked up contracts.Of
8442 1,100 former Brooklyn Union customers now choosing their gas supplier, about 70 percent have signed contracts with KeySpan, while KeySpan has about 45 percent of the 1,600 former Lilco customers now arranging their own suppliers.New York State so far is the only one in the Northeast to deregulate its gas
8442 market, though there are pilot programs in states like New Jersey and Massachusetts. "We haven't really hit New Jersey yet, we're planning on doing that in October," Feraudo said."As additional states in the Northeast open up, we'll study these too," Catell said.KeySpan Energy Services Inc, another member of the group,
8442 last week launched a pilot program for residential customers, hoping to attract 1,000 users within a month, Catell said.Billing will be a potentially thorny issue in this market."We think we have a significant advantage over other gas marketers, coming from a utility background," said Feraudo. Through its KeySpan Energy Management
8442 Inc, the company is also offering comprehensive energy management packages, including financing, upgrading, operating and maintaining energy units, and fuel purchasing, said Feraudo.He called the company "fuel neutral," explaining "We are not bound to gas. We very much like dual fuel systems so we can use whichever makes sense economically."KeySpan
8442 Energy Management Inc already has 25 customers and, through its recent affiliation with South Jersey Energy Co, has submitted energy management proposals to about half a dozen industrial customers in southern New Jersey. "We also see ourselves marketing electricity down the road as that market follows the gas industry in
8442 deregulation," Catell said.Efforts by the company to enter the electricity sector have been limited by the lack of an open local market."We are talking to electric partners, looking for the right combination, and think that some time in the next year we will have a partner or partners," said Feraudo.He
8442 said their initial foray into electricity would be focused on the U.S. Northeast. "It's the area we know best."-- New York Power Desk + 1 212 859 1621</

8453 The U.S. treasury may have been shorted up to $2 billion in royalties underpaid by companies for extracting oil from federal lands, according to a House panel's report released Tuesday.In a report to be considered by the House Government Oversight Committee later Tuesday, the panel chided the Interior Department's Minerals
8453 Management Service, the agency responsible for collecting royalties, for lagging in collecting underpaid amounts which may go back to 1978. The panel also said the MMS must prepare a timetable for collecting payments, and immediately determine if underpayments occurred in states beside California, where the undervaluation issue has been fought
8453 in courts for years.Royalties were based on prices posted by oil companies, which critics have said were set below market value.The panel said its estimate of potential losses was based on the high-range estimate of an Interior Department official who said undervaluation of oil from federal lands, not including California,
8453 may be as much as 10 percent The panel said that could amount to $1.3 billion, and combined that with the top-range estimate of an administration task force which said California losses could reach $856 million.The MMS has disputed the high range estimate for California, and said it would go
8453 after some $440 million in royalties it said were underpaid from federal lands there.The House panel's report said royalty underpayment was a "serious problem" that MMS has "failed to seriously address," and suggested MMS get outside audit assistance. It also said the MMS should review its existing global settlements with
8453 oil companies that are intended to resolve a range of issues, but critics said reduced the potential for royalty collections."Global settlements between the federal government and major oil companies have not protected U.S. financial interests," the report said.The MMS also should review royalty in-kind payments to see whether those also
8453 were undervalued, and should see that prices are not distorted on oil in pipelines that cross federal lands. The subcommittee report came after the Interior Department's inspector general said in nine out of ten settlements reviewed, the settlements lacked some documentation and did not give reasons why the government reduced
8453 the amount of royalties it thought it was owed.In one case, the department's watchdog said it found an unexplained $360 million gap between the MMS's estimate of the value of a disputed issue and the settlement.The inspector general's draft report was was released last month by the Project on Government
8453 Oversight, and a final report was pending. The MMS in the draft report said it was too tightly staffed to fully document their reasons for accepting lower royalties.</

8493 Accounting standards that dictate the information companies must provide to investors are falling out of step with the modern economy, a report from U.S. General Accounting Office said Tuesday.Changes in the economy "are significantly challenging the relevance of historical cost-based financial statements and the traditional audit of those statements," the
8493 research arm of Congress said.In the new economy, investors receive information more rapidly than in the past using on-line services, while companies fund their operations with complex financial instruments that can dramatically fluctuate in value, the GAO reported.Under existing rules, companies often report the initial or historic cost of their
8493 assets instead of current values."For the accounting profession to successfully move to a more modern era of auditing and provide expanded assurance services, it must more vigorously continue to address the major unresolved issues," the GAO said. The Financial Accounting Standards Board, a private body that sets accounting standards for
8493 public companies, has proposed new rules for complex instruments like derivatives. But companies have complained that the rules are burdensome and likely to confuse rather than edify investors.The GAO called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to take the lead in forging a consensus among all parties to modernize accounting
8493 standards."The SEC, given its responsibilities under federal securities laws, is in a pivotal position to assume a leadership role," the GAO said.The accounting profession could also do more to reveal fraudulent activity and prevent unexpected losses, the GAO found.Auditors should review the effectiveness of companies' internal controls, the checks and
8493 balances put in place to prevent fraudulent or unauthorized transactions, the GAO said."Effective internal controls are the first line of defense for safeguarding assets and preventing fraudulent financial reporting -- a lesson well learned from the savings and loan crisis," the GAO said. The GAO praised a recent SEC initiative
8493 to increase public participation in the accounting standards setting process. At the SEC's behest, the parent body of the FASB will include more public representatives.The GAO report, titled "The Accounting Profession, Major Issues: Progress and Concerns," was prompted by a request from Congressman John Dingell, ranking minority member of the
8493 House Commerce Committee.--Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312</

8494 face on its promotions using Whoopi Goldberg."Primarily, AT&amp;T is reacting to the effect of the Dime Lady" and a clutter of offers for telephone cards and discounts, said David Goodtree, an industry analyst with Forrester Research.AT&amp;T ad agency FCB/Leber Katz is keeping the wraps on a new ad campaign it
8494 will launch for its client next month. An agency spokeswoman, Vonda LePage, said, "I can't say if it's a celebrity or what, but we're hard at work on it and it will roll out in the middle of next month."An initial series of "teaser" ads starts on Tuesday night on
8494 network television and on Wednesday appears in national newspapers. It will attempt to underscore the simplicity of the AT&amp;T pricing plan with a tin can and string -- the kind of contraption that children play with -- using the headline: "The simplest calling plan since tin cans and a string."
8494 The upcoming advertising work that FCB is doing on AT&amp;T's image may require a bit more complexity, just because it's arriving later at the party than its main competitors. "It's hard to just throw out another celebrity -- MCI and Sprint have already done that," said one advertising executive at
8494 a Madison Avenue agency. "That formula's pretty well taken."The shear clutter of telecommunications advertising requires that ATT come up with a sharply focused advertising image for the new marketing initiative. Telephone advertising is one of the fastest-growing segments of the ad business, increasing by double digit rates annually. "It will
8494 probably be one of the strongest growth areas of the advertising business next year," said Dean Witter Reynolds analyst James Dougherty.AT&amp;T's $1-billion-a-year ad spending is spread across a variety of agencies funding a variety of products. It launched the new campaign by promising to sharpen its pitch, with Chairman Robert
8494 Allen making "decisive marketing" a major commitment, but some were skeptical."AT&amp;T has never been known for clarity of message," complained one analyst who follows media companies.</

8534 The Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady shows that the central bank will respond to inflation when it sees it, not when it is a mere blip on the horizon -- and an arguable one at that, analysts said. The Fed's decision to hold interest rates steady mildly
8534 surprised the Treasury market, where many worried that recent gains in hourly wages and a low unemployment rate were harbingers of impending inflation. The Fed, by declining to raise rates, seemed to respond with a traditional Midwest expression of skepticism -- "I'm from Missouri; show me.""You haven't seen signs of
8534 inflation in the core PPI (Producer Price Index) or the core CPI (Consumer Price Index) up until this point and that probably played an integral role in the decision," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. Elliott Platt, managing director of economic
8534 research at Donaldson, Lufkin &amp; Jenrette Securities Corp, said he was "a little surprised that the Fed did not perceive that it had to tighten."Since Platt expects second-half economic growth to slow to below 2.0 percent, he did not think the Fed needed to tighten. But Platt said the Fed's
8534 decision to leave rates unchanged shows that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and the Federal Reserve Board "clearly, clearly are actually waiting to see inflation. They're not going to make bets based on wage inflation. They're not going to be pre-emptive like they were in 1994," he said.And Platt said
8534 the next wave of U.S. economic statistics would add credibility to the Fed's steady rate policy. "People should be bullish on the fixed-income outlook and the bullishness should be confirmed in the wave of weak data that is coming up," he said. Platt cited expected weakness in the August durable
8534 goods orders report, due on Thursday. He said he expects August new home sales, due Monday, to be down 4.0 percent. The National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) September index due next Tuesday should be near 51.5 and "then on Friday (October 4), the employment report should be up only
8534 140,000 on (non-farm) payroll employment," he said.Economist Neal Soss, senior advisor to CS First Boston Corp, said the Fed made the correct decision."The Federal Reserve has told us that they are not allergic to growth," said Soss. "They are, of course, allergic to and ever-watchful for inflation -- but not
8534 to growth."Soss said so far, the evidence shows that growth continues while inflation remains invisible."When the patient's blood pressure is under control, you don't change the medication," said Soss. 8536 Federal Aviation Administrator David Hinson on Tuesday urged a group of aviation executives from North and South America to cooperate more closely on safety or risk stalling the rapid growth of air traffic."In three years, Latin America has become the number one destination for travelers from the United States," Hinson
8536 said. "We welcome this new surge of growth and the economic opportunities it creates. But this expansion will only come if we act now to increase our ability to handle it with safety and efficiency," he told the Americas Conference on Aviation. One way to improve safety is for all
8536 countries to adopt a new high technology satellite tracking system called the global positioning system, Hinson said. Ground stations for the system must be 500 miles (800 km) apart."The continental United States will be covered by this network," Hinson said. "Now it is time to think of an expansion of
8536 this network to the south, linking Central and South America."Without improvements in the aircraft accident rate, the increased traffic will bring fatal air crashes every eight to 10 days by 2015, Hinson said. "The larger the number of states using GPS, the greater the savings in time and fuel and
8536 the greater the contribution to safety," Hinson said. About 2,500 U.S. airports are equipped to use GPS.Besides safety, the environmental and economic impact of burning less fuel by using GPS will be tremendous, Hinson said. One U.S. airline estimated it would save $200 million a year on fuel if GPS
8536 were adopted worldwide. And industry-wide, the FAA estimates $3 billion to $4 billion less fuel will be burned with the adoption of GPS."Imagine the environmental impact of not burning $3 billion of kerosene," he said.</

8541 The U.S. government should stop supporting American oil companies with more than $55 billion a year in tax breaks, risk insurance, loan guarantees, and military protection for investments overseas, a consumer group said Tuesday.Oil and gas companies enjoy U.S. tax credits worth several billion dollars a year based on their
8541 foreign tax payments and tax deferrals, according to a report by Citizen Action citing government and corporate figures."The time has come to take Big Oil off welfare," said Citizen Action's energy policy director, Edwin Rothschild. The companies benefit from political risk insurance and loan guarantees provided by the government's Overseas
8541 Private Investment Corp, which currently has $1 billion in risk insurance exposure to 23 oil and gas projects, and $250 million in loan guarantees to 12 projects.However, OPIC officials said the loans and insurance are provided at no cost to taxpayers because the agency has accumulated reserves of $2.6 billion
8541 from payments by companies to cover insurance losses.By far the largest "subsidy" is the estimated $50 billion a year spent to protect the free flow of Middle Eastern oil. "Clearly, the United States' dependence on oil is a primary factor," Rothschild said at a news conference. "We stumble forward without
8541 any real policy commitment to alternative fuels."Citing the latest Internal Revenue Service data available, in 1992, oil companies with 5.6 percent of all corporate assets claimed $5.3 billion or 22.4 percent of all corporate foreign tax credits.The American Petroleum Institute defended the tax breaks, saying they "apply to all Americans
8541 and do not differentially benefit oil companies." An API spokesman added that the oil industry annually puts $25 billion worth of motor fuel taxes into the Treasury."American companies have invested more money overseas in recent years because the federal government denies them access to develop our nation's vast oil and
8541 natural gas resources, especially those located offshore and in Alaska," API said."(These restrictions) continue to harm our country economically and contribute to the rise of oil imports," it said.</
