9068 New Zealand Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Wednesday the party's spending plans would help to ease pressure on monetary policy.Cullen said there was currently "excessive" pressure on monetary policy despite surpluses being run by the conservative National Party government."Already we see, despite large surpluses, excessive pressure on
9068 monetary policy, and some of our spending will in fact ease that," he told Radio New Zealand. "If we're putting money into training, that eases the labour market. If we're putting money into housing, that eases the housing market. Reducing student fees, that has a direct impact of course on
9068 the CPI."Cullen said that Labour, while raising government spending, would still be repaying public debt and running "the strongest fiscal position of any developed country".Labour, currently the main opposition party, is running about neck-and-neck with the economic nationalist New Zealand First Party for second place behind the government in opinion
9068 polls leading up to a general election on October 12. The polls suggest a possible change of government if Labour, NZ First and the left-wing Alliance can reach agreement.-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 471-4277</
9069 New Zealand finance minister Bill Birch said on Wednesday the government hoped to exceed Treasury's forecast of three to four percent growth per year for the rest of the decade."That's at the bottom of the range that we would hope to achieve, but that's about three times the growth rate
9069 that we did achieve through the '70s and '80s and it will indeed expand the NZ economy very rapidly," he told Radio New Zealand. Birch said the government had a continuing intention of upgrading the economic framework that was working so well."That can be done without turning New Zealand on
9069 its head. We don't intend to turn New Zealand on its head, but we do intend to enhance and work on the framework of price stability, open economy, good labour market, enhancing the tax system and building the base and lowering the rates, and improving the performance of government and
9069 getting the debt down."All of those things are contributing to the growth that we're getting," he said. Birch said the current framework gave investors, manufacturers, farmers and exporters the confidence to invest and expand the economy.He said Treasury's forecasts were based on the best information available at the time.--Wellington Newsroom
9070 New Zealand political parties have largely avoided making expensive blank cheque promises in presenting fiscal projections ahead of the October 12 election, private forecaster Infometrics said on Wednesday."The parties have generally been sensitive to ensure they show the cost of the promises they make," economist Philip Wrigley said in an
9070 economic analysis of the parties' promises.The left-wing Alliance Party is the big spender with plans to boost current expenditure projections by NZ$4.8 billion in 1997/98 compared with the current National Party government. Left-of-centre Labour Party would spend $2.4 billion more and the economic nationalist New Zealand First $1.7 billion.Even the
9070 ruling conservative National Party would increase spending beyond current baselines based on recent patterns.Although the Alliance is the big spender, it also promises to be the biggest saver as a result of tax increases, with an estimated surplus of $3.7 billion in fiscal 1997/98.Infometrics estimates all parties will run surpluses
9070 for that year, with Labour having the smallest at $1.66 billion. "It gambles that much lower surpluses will support growth as well as National's plan," he said.But he warns there could be a monetary policy response from the Reserve Bank to Labour's shrinking surpluses.NZ First faces the challenge of achieving
9070 growth to pay for its spending but its plans for a compulsory pension scheme should avoid inflation pressures, Wrigley said.Plans by NZ First and the Alliance to introduce specific restrictions on foreign investment may have significant impact. Wrigley said the main question mark the Alliance faces is not over the
9070 detail of costings, but whether the economic framework it would create would deliver a prosperous economy able to generate the tax revenues its plans require.He is critical of its plan to amend the Reserve Bank Act so the central bank's targets include sustainable economic well-being and employment, together with price
9070 stability."The Reserve Bank cannout pursue all these objectives using the tools of monetary policy. Therefore, it is unlikely to achieve any consistently," Wrigley said.Labour plans to cut taxes and raise spending substantially. Only the Alliance proposes to restrict free trade and its plans to raise $1 billion via a "moderate"
9070 increase in tariffs against all countries but Australia could result in conterveiling measures.Wrigley sees conflicts within all parties' policies:* The Alliance's proposals for trade restrictions and multiple objectives for monetary policy do not accord with accepted economic principles.* NZ First has an incompatibility between its "partnership with exporters" and constraints
9070 on foreign investment. * Labour is accused of reducing flexibility in employment contracting* National proffers an ambitious growth target without suggesting reforms to achieve it.Polls suggest no party will achieve an overall majority in the election and Wrigley said "all four would have to swallow hard to accept key planks
9070 of any of the other parties".As none of the parties would rule alone, Wrigley suspects much of the fiscal policies "represent bargaining positions for post-election negotiations as much as enticements for voters".-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746</

9078 in a military coup in February 1991."There was a rumour in the market that Chatichai Choonhavan would join Banharn's coalition and be chosen as the new prime minister," said Songyos Kulvichien of First Asia Securities.Some television and radio stations also had analysts speculating that Banharn would dissolve parliament later on
9078 Wednesday. 9078 analysts said.Signs of discord over his successor appeared on Tuesday as a top adviser and elder in Banharn's Chart Thai party, which leads the ruling coalition, declared his right to the top job.Pramarn Adireksarn, whom Banharn supporters have pushed to succeed him, claimed he was in line for the top
9078 post because he was a senior Chart Thai leader and had party support.His statement frustrated some coalition members who had openly been lobbying for Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who was behind efforts to oust Banharn, analysts said.Chavalit leads the New Aspiration Party (NAP), the second largest party in the coalition."By
9078 tradition and legally, the Chart Thai party has every right and justification to pick one of its leaders to be the new prime minister," Pramarn, 82, told reporters. 9078 he said.Chavalit and other ministers attended a regular weekly cabinet meeting on Tuesday that was expected to be the last to be chaired by Banharn.The premier declined to talk to reporters."There is no progress (in seeking a sucessor) at all and I don't want to make any comment to create
9078 further confusion of the situation," a bristling Chavalit said before the meeting.Despite support for Chavalit, a close aide said the chances of his becoming prime minister were slim."As Banharn still insists he will propose someone in his party to replace him, the chances of Chavalit becoming premier are less than
9078 40 percent," said the aide, who asked not to be identified."I believe that this political standoff will possibly lead to the house dissolution."Some small coalition parties like the Social Action Party, and the Nam Thai party backed Chavalit for the premiership.Banharn has kept his silence ever since he was humiliated
9078 by his allies on Saturday. They had forced him to declare his resignation in exchange for support in a parliamentary no-confidence motion that Banharn later won.</

9126 Approval for a unit of Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa to develop and operate a container port at a former U.S. naval base in the Philippines has been upheld following a re-evaluation of the bidding.The Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority, which runs the port at the former base north of Manila, said
9126 on Tuesday it had re-evaluated all bids for the project and decided Hutchison Ports Philippines Ltd still came out the winner."The decision is subject to review by President Fidel Ramos, to whom it has been submitted," an SBMA statement said.SBMA initially awarded the contract to Hutchison, but the decision was
9126 challenged by one of the losing bidders, Philippine port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI).Ramos ordered SBMA to re-evaluate the bidding, and today's announcement was the result of that review, which SBMA said was conducted with observers from the Philippine government's Commission on Audit.ICTSI immediately said it was prepared
9126 to challenge the latest ruling, up to the Supreme Court if necessary."We still have the option of going to the Supreme Court. We can't think about that until we're there. We'll take it step by step," ICTSI chairman Enrique Razon told Reuters.SBMA rejected ICTSI's original bid on the grounds that
9126 it would violate a law forbidding monopolies in the port industry. ICTSI operates the Manila International Container Terminal, which handles 70 percent of container traffic in the country.But in its review, SBMA said it had based its decision purely on the financial returns each of the competing bidders had offered."This
9126 greatest financial return is not an arbitrary figure quoted by the bidder but should be supported by a valid or realistic business plan," SBMA said in a statement.It said it rejected ICTSI's contention that the only financial factor that should be looked into was royalty per twenty-foot-equivalent unit (TEU).In the
9126 original bidding in August, ICTSI offered the highest royalty of $58 per TEU, followed by Hutchison with $20.50 and Germany's Royal Port Services with $15.00.In its bid, Hutchison said it planned to build new wharfs at Subic in the fourth year that would effectively increase the number of ship calls
9126 at a faster pace. It also pledged to invest more than $100 million in Subic over a 10-year period.ICTSI had set the construction of new wharfs only in the ninth year and had promised fresh investment of $79 million, according to documents provided by the SBMA.ICTSI had offered a higher
9126 royalty because it would raise its rates and charges by 10 percent yearly for the first two years and 5.0 percent thereafter, the SBMA said.SBMA said it had hired three independent experts from Malaysia, Belgium and the United States who also endorsed the Hutchison plan.Subic used to be the biggest
9126 American naval base outside the United States. It was closed after the Philippine Senate refused to agree to a new treaty with Washington in 1991.It is now a flourishing economic development zone.</

9151 The South Korean cabinet on Tuesday approved a modest overall budget increase for next year, underlining the fight against inflation, but defence spending was set to rise sharply on security concerns.Budget spending for calendar 1997 was set at 67.78 trillion won ($82.56 billion) against 60.11 trillion won this year, according
9151 to a report on the budget by the finance ministry.The 12.8 percent overall increase will be the smallest annual growth in the state budget since current president Kim Young-sam took office in 1993."This reflects the government's desire to cap inflationary pressure," said Jung Hong-sang, deputy director of the ministry's fiscal
9151 policy division.The budget expanded by 15.6 percent in 1994, 16.7 percent in 1995 and 16.2 percent this year.Defence spending, the biggest single spending item, will grow by 12 percent to 14.27 trillion won from this year's budget of 12.74 trillion won.The growth in defence spending will be the highest since
9151 1993. Annual growth for defence spending was 10.7 percent in 1996, 9.9 percent in 1995 and 9.4 percent in 1994."Tension is growing on the Korean peninsula and there are few signs the situation will ease in the near future. We need to spend more to strengthen our defence capabilities," Jung
9151 said in an interview.Last month President Kim, citing "uncertainty surrounding the Korean peninsula", stressed the importance of modernising the nation's defences.Last week's infiltration of armed North Korean troops into the South by submarine has renewed nationwide concerns about the North Korean threat.When special accounts are included, the overall budget amounts
9151 to 71.6 trillion won, up 13.7 percent from this year's 62.96 trillion won.The budget assumes inflation of 4.0 to 4.5 percent next year, compared with a 4.5-5.0 percent projection for this year.Government spending will be kept at "minimum possible levels", Jung said.The government plans a freeze on hiring next year
9151 and a clampdown on the pay of senior officials. All public utility charges will be frozen in 1997, according to the budget.South Korea's economic growth is projected to slow to between 6.5 and 7.0 percent in 1997, compared with 7.0-7.5 percent this year, the ministry report said.But investment in infrastructure
9151 will be expanded steadily to strengthen the nation's international competitiveness. Transport and distribution costs in Korea are among the highest in Asia.Infrastructure investment would grow 24.4 percent to 10.14 trillion won in 1997 from 8.15 trillion won planned this year.(Conversion: $1 = 821 won)</

9154 The Philippines' recent successful debt restructuring schemes have validated international confidence in the country, officials and analysts said after the issue of its maiden 10-year bond on Tuesday.The 10-year fixed-rate Treasury bond, which fetched a coupon rate of 16 percent, was oversubscribed. The government received bids worth 9.915 billion pesos
9154 ($377 million), while the offer was worth just two-billion pesos ($76 million)."It's a success," Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said.Deputy treasurer Eduardo Mendiola said major financial players swamped the auction, pushing the coupon to 16.0 percent, just 25 basis points higher than the seven-year fixed rate bonds which were auctioned in July."We
9154 are getting better entrenched in the international capital market," said Johnny Noe Ravalo, chief economist of the Bankers Association of the Philippines.He said the 10-year peso bonds as well as the recent issue of 20-year uncollateralised Brady bonds had shown that the present economic liberalisation programmes being undertaken by the
9154 government are fully supported by foreign investors.The new uncollateralised bonds were issued on Monday as part of the government's Brady exchange programme.The Philippines issued $690 million worth of Brady bonds in exchange for $635 million worth of collateralised bonds and another $137 million outright sale of the bonds.The bonds are
9154 priced 2.25 percentage points over the benchmark U.S. Treasuries, significantly lower than Mexico's 20-year bonds which were priced 4.45 percentage points over U.S. Treasuries."It is fascinating how quickly the Philippines has improved its credit story," Peter Woicke, regional executive of J.P. Morgan for Asia, said in a statement. J.P. Morgan
9154 is the lead arranger of the Brady exchange programme."When we lead-managed the country's debut three-year Eurobond in 1993, we could not have expected that by the time that bond matured in 1996, the country would be raising 20-year money from institutional investors," Woicke added.The Philippines was shunned by the private
9154 capital market in the 1980s after it declared a debt payment moratorium in 1983.Project financing was limited to multilateral financing which started to dwindle when eastern European countries begun to restructure their economies after the fall of Communism in the late 1980s.The government used to issue Treasury bills of up
9154 to one year as investors were wary to invest beyond that due to the volatile political and economic situation.In 1992, President Fidel Ramos started a wide-ranging liberalisation programme which opened up services and manufacturing industries to foreign investors.The Bureau of Treasury started offering two-year fixed rate bonds in 1994, five-year
9154 bonds in 1995, and seven-year bonds in 1996. It has offered more than 110 billion pesos worth of bonds so far."The financial market is looking at our economic and financial system on a longer term basis ... And they see the rates going down in the long run," Treasurer Valdehuesa
9154 said. "It will take years to reap the dividends (of these projects). But we believe there is ample dividend enough in the impact of modern infrastructure on the economy as a whole -- for this will not fail to yield returns for our core businesses in the group," he said.The
9154 conglomerate's flagship Ayala Land Inc is the leader in the real estate sector.It also has stakes in the telecommunications, food manufacturing, insurance and information technology sectors."The Ayala Group is harnessing its capabilities as a group of companies to bring to bear a synergistic approach to private sector involvement in economic
9154 development," he said.Ayala said the country's current economic boom can be sustained if the policies of deregulation and liberalisation were continued."Philippine development can be sustained if we can maintain these policies of reform and institutionalise rigour in their implementation," said Ayala, a doyen of Filipino industrialists.</

9157 Rampant corruption will not engulf freewheeling Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Beijing's control in 1997, the territory's anti-graft boss predicted on Tuesday."There is no basis for such fears because we have a very good system of the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) working independently with a sound
9157 legal basis," ICAC chief Michael Leung told reporters during a business meeting."We have independent judiciary, we have Chinese cooperation to the full, so I don't see any need for pessimism in this area, because we can guarantee our operation in the Basic Law (Hong Kong's post-1997 constitution)," he said.The bustling
9157 British-ruled territory of 6.3 million people reverts to China at midnight next June 30, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.Beijing has promised Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy as a Special Administrative Region of China, but jittery Hong Kong people have expressed fears that corruption will mimic
9157 China and grow unchecked in the capitalist outpost after the handover.Corruption has spread rapidly in China as market reforms unfolded over the past two decades despite periodic crackdowns.In a survey conducted last year by the ICAC, more than 70 percent of 1,100 respondents predicted the sovereignty transfer would fuel an
9157 upsurge in corruption in Hong Kong.The survey also found 41 percent of respondents believed the anti-graft unit would be less effective due to interference from Chinese officials after the change of flag.Leung reassured Hong Kong businessmen that neither he nor the ICAC would allow themselves to be influenced by Chinese
9157 or Hong Kong officials when pursuing any corruption case in the future."Nobody can stop me from doing this lawfully," he said. "The same will apply to the Chief Executive. He or she cannot stop me from pursuing a case under the law," Leung said."I have the full legal power to
9157 pursue a case without any interference from anybody, whether it is officials in Hong Kong or in China."The graft-buster, who recently returned from Beijing after talks with the Chinese government, said China had promised its backing to keep graft out of Hong Kong after the handover."China has again pledged its
9157 strongest support to keep corruption free after 1997 and to let the ICAC continue to lead the fight against corruption," said Leung who met officials in Beijing and Guangdong province neighbouring Hong Kong last week.But Leung urged the business community to come forward if the ICAC was to succeed in
9157 stemming corruption."Our future is only as good as the strength and support this community, including yourselves, give us," he said.</

9163 South Korea on Tuesday announced a record monthly current account deficit of $3.5 billion for August, swollen by falling prices for key exports, including semiconductors, steel and petrochemicals.Bank of Korea figures showed the deficit for the first eight months of the year soared to $15.24 billion, more than double the
9163 bank's original projection of a $7 billion shortfall for the whole year.A central bank official said there was "no short-term remedy" for the deficit that private economists predicted could hit $20 billion this year.August's deficit was an increase on the July shortfall of $2.3 billion. It was also bloated by
9163 a rising invisible trade deficit, partly the result of a boom in Koreans travelling overseas on holiday."I'm getting worried," said Kim Gi-hyung, an economist at Daewoo Economic Research Institute. The trade deficit was combining with an economic downturn and the result could be recession, he said.Lee Young-man, an economist at
9163 LG Economic Research Institute, said: "Under a worse-case scenario the deficit could reach $20 billion for the whole of this year."Private economic think-tanks put the whole-year deficit at $18 to $20 billion. Last year's shortfall was $8.5 billion."We are working on the revision for the 1996 deficit forecast. Our figure
9163 will not show big differences with that of private economic institutes," said a Bank of Korea economist, who declined to be named."The huge deficit is expected to continue next year as there is no short-term remedy to improve it quickly."However, he added that at $18 to $20 billion, the deficit
9163 would be still manageable at around three percent of gross national product.Private economists predict next year's deficit at between $15.2 billion and $18 billion.Bank of Korea figures showed that international prices of semiconductors, which account for nearly 20 percent of exports, fell by 72.3 percent in August year-on-year. Prices for
9163 steel products and petrochemical goods dipped by 13.8 percent and 16.7 percent respectively."The price fall is out of our control. It cannot be solved overnight," said LG Economic Research Institute's Lee.The government is pressing a campaign to bring down costs by reducing prices and wages. It plans a freeze on
9163 government hiring next year, a clampdown on pay for senior officials and a reduction in utility charges.It is also trying to improve corporate competitiveness, partly by bringing down high interest rates.Kim of Daewoo said South Korea's reliance on imported raw materials and capital equipment made it particularly vulnerable to cyclical
9163 declines in the price of exports.Despite the seven percent fall of the local currency against the dollar this year, Korean products have been hit by a weakening yen. Korea and Japan compete against each other with similar products.Economists said the impact of the won's depreciation would show up from early
9163 next year, but the falling yen had already offset much of the potential competitive gains."We have to do something to make our products more value-added as we cannot survive by selling on price," the central bank economist said.</

9170 part of China.The dispute over the uninhabited islands flared up this month when Japanese rightists moved to buttress Tokyo's claim over them by repairing a makeshift aluminium lighthouse on one of the islands. The structure had been damaged by a typhoon last month.On Monday, Japanese patrol ships repulsed a flotilla
9170 of activists from rival claimant Taiwan and the British colony of Hong Kong, which reverts to Beijing rule in mid-1997. The activists tried to land on the islands to defy Tokyo's claim of sovereignty.Beijing and Taipei, rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, agree the Diaoyus
9170 have been China's for centuries and dispute Tokyo's claim, which dates to 1895 when Japan defeated imperial China in a war and seized the Diaoyus.The Taiwan and Hong Kong activists had vowed to remove the lighthouse, but 17 Japanese vessels backed by a helicopter thwarted eight landing attempts by placing
9170 themselves between seven fishing boats carrying the activists and the islands.Shen declined to speculate on how Beijing might react if Taiwan or Hong Kong residents were injured or killed while trying to approach the islands. "We do not wish for this to happen," he said.In New York, Japan's chief Foreign
9170 Ministry spokesman Hidehiro Hamada said on Monday that the issue was not open for discussion ahead of a meeting between foreign ministers of the two countries."The Japanese position has been made quite clear. The islands have been historically and legally an integral part of Japan... From the Japanese side, there
9170 is no dispute to discuss," Hamada said."The Chinese side knows that position... We hope this will not jeopardise friendly relations with China," he said.Shen said China had taken notice that Tokyo had repeatedly stressed the importance it attached to Sino-Japanese relations."They (Japanese) said they do not want to see Sino-Japanese
9170 relations harmed... We hope more to see action by the Japanese side," Shen said.Asked if joint military exercises China conducted this month were aimed at Japan, Shen said it was "normal" for China to conduct war games.The Shenyang Military Zone conducted the exercises at an undisclosed location on September 13-14,
9170 with the army, navy and air force seizing and defending offshore islands, the Liberation Army Daily reported on Sunday.Tokyo has called for calm in the face of growing anti-Japanese sentiment. Some Hong Kong legislators and Chinese citizens have demanded Beijing send warships to the islands.</

9177 A set of closely watched indicators released on Tuesday showed Japan's economy recovering in July, albeit slowly, despite lingering concerns over a weak consumer appetite for goods and services.The government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) announced that the diffusion index of leading economic indicators remained above the "boom or bust" 50
9177 percent line in July for a fourth consecutive month.The index of leading indicators stood at 77.8 on a scale of 100 for the month. A figure above 50 is taken as suggesting the economy will expand in the coming months.The agency said in a statement that the data confirmed that
9177 the economy was continuing to recover.The coincident index measuring economic conditions current in July, stood at 80.0 after June's 54.5, while the the lagging index, which traces economic trends in the previous few months, was at 28.6, down from 37.5 the previous month.The coincident index was above 50 for a
9177 second month in a row, while that of lagging indicators was below 50 for a fourth month."Since both (leading and coincident) indices were above 50 percent. We can translate this as meaning that the economy is still recovering," Kunji Okue, an economist at Kleinwort Benson in Tokyo, told Reuters Financial
9177 Television.The Bank of Japan echoed the view, saying in its monthly economic report released on Tuesday that companies were increasing investment in fresh plant and equipment while personal consumption showed a moderate recovery trend."Current economic situations have not offered us factors which would make the Bank of Japan consider a
9177 change in its assessment of the gradual pace of the recovery," a senior Bank of Japan official told reporters on Tuesday.The bank said in the report that housing starts remained at a high level as individuals took advantage of low interest rates and also built houses before a planned rise
9177 in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent in April."Overall, private capital spending is strong and housing investments are doing okay. The missing component is private consumption," said Yasushi Okuda, a BZW Securities economist.Okuda said that the O-157 food poisoning epidemic which swept Japan in July and August
9177 was likely to have affected consumption, adding that department and chainstore sales coming out later this week would be interesting to watch out for.Last week, the government announced that Japan's household spending fell a real 4.4 percent year-on-year in July, the biggest monthly drop since February 1981.The decline came as
9177 households cut back on purchases of fresh foods and on eating out because of the epidemic, which has killed 11 people and made more than 9,500 ill this year.Despite this, the government made it clear it would not come up with additional fiscal spending this year for the sake of
9177 the economy. Four years of heavy government spending aimed at stimulating the economy has made Japan's budgetary deficit one of the worst among major industrialised nations."Judging from indicators showing economic trends up to now, I believe we still need to be cautious about drafting a large-scale supplementary budget as a
9177 way to stimulate the economy," Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told reporters before the data was released.</

9221 Switching completely to an inactivated polio virus for vaccinations in the United States would not be cost effective but could be justified from a public health standpoint, a study said Tuesday.The naturally occurring, or "wild," polio virus has been eradicated in the Western Hemisphere. The live but weakened polio vaccine
9221 currently in use in the United States, however, carries a slight risk of causing polio, although only a handful of such cases occur each year.An advisory committee to the U.S. Public Health Service has recommended adoption of a half-and-half vaccination programme, consisting of two inactivated virus vaccinations followed by two
9221 with the live virus.Researchers at the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, in a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association, said it would cost $28 million more per year to switch completely to an inactivated vaccine, while a mix of the two would cost
9221 only $14.7 million more.The figures are beyond the estimated $11 million that would be saved by not having to pay compensation to those who get the disease from the live vaccine.Switching completely to the inactive vaccine "would not be cost-beneficial at current vaccine prices and with the current compensation awards
9221 paid to vaccine-associated paralytic (polio) cases," the report said."Although these figures are greater than those for many other public health programmes, they may be justified to assuage public concerns about adverse events associated with a government-mandated oral polio vaccine programme in the United States, where there is no disease due
9221 to wild poliovirus," it added."Continued public confidence in poliomyelitis vaccination programmes is essential to ensure the high vaccination coverage necessary to prevent epidemic transmission of imported wild poliovirus," the study said."In addition, public confidence in the safety of vaccination programmes in general may provide the additional benefit of higher vaccine
9221 coverage and more effective prevention of all childhood diseases preventable by vaccine," it said.</
9222 Men of Japanese ancestry who live in Hawaii have higher rates of Alzheimer's disease than similar men in Japan, a study said on Tuesday, raising questions about the role lifestyle and environmental factors play in the crippling disorder."Something associated with migration or with exposure to Western environmental factors has led
9222 to higher rates of Alzheimer's disease," said Lon White, chief of the National Institute of Aging's Asia-Pacific Office, who directed the study.Investigators said they looked at data on 3,734 first- and second-generation Japanese-American men living on Oahu who were born between 1900 and 1919. The men have been part of
9222 a continuing heart disease study started in 1965.The report, published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association, found that 5.4 percent of those studied had Alzheimer's disease, a degenerative condition that erases the memory and leaves victims helpless. A similar study of men living in Japan found a
9222 1.5 percent prevalance of the disease, the report said.The rate of the disease among the men in Hawaii approached that for men of European ancestry living in the United States, the study said.It has been known that Alzheimer's is more common in the Western world than in the East. In
9222 the West, the prevalance ranges from 37 percent to as high as 63 percent among those over age 85. While the way the disease attacks the brain is known, its exact cause is still a mystery.Two researchers at the University of Washington, commenting on the study in an editorial published
9222 in the same issue of the journal, called the Hawaii report a "landmark" that should encourage a search for more leads on whether lifestyle alterations influence onset of the disease."The data ... are the best yet available on the question of whether the introduction of a new environment can make
9222 a difference in the occurrence of Alzheimer's disease," the editorial said.The study also found that the risk of developing another catastrophic condition called vascular dementia, caused by a lack of blood flow to the brain that results in small strokes, was not much different among the men living in Hawaii
9222 and those in Japan, for reasons that were not clear.</
9223 Prudential Insurance Co. of America said it agreed to pay at least $410 million to settle lawsuits by policyholders claiming they were victims of deceptive sales practices.Under the settlement, about 10.7 million policyholders who bought permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995 would be eligible to apply for restitution.The
9223 settlement improves the terms of an agreement Prudential reached with a multi-state task force of insurance regulators this summer, said Melvyn Weiss, one of the lead attorneys negotiating the settlement.It provides policyholders with the potential for greater relief and makes it easier for them to qualify for it, he said.
9223 Weiss expects the policyholders to enter into a formal agreement with Prudential on Oct. 25 and a notice to class members to be sent out in November."We believe the amounts paid out under our plan are more than what would have been paid out under the original plan," Weiss said.A
9223 court hearing to determine whether or not the settlement is fair is likely to be held sometime in February or March."This settlement allows Prudential to move forward in providing the best possible service to our clients and customers" said Prudential Chairman Arthur RyanThe settlement marks Prudential's latest effort to resolve
9223 allegations that it improperly pressured unsophisticated investors to replace their life insurance policies, a practice known as churning or twisting.In July, insurance regulators from 43 states and Washington, D.C., recommended a $35 million fine and restitution programme for sales abuses by Prudential.Prudential said it will request that the remediation programmes
9223 previously accepted by the states be modified to make them consistent with the class action settlement.Prudential said discussions are being held with the remaining seven states to acquaint them with the terms of the class action settlement.Those states had opposed the original multi-state agreement because of concern that it placed
9223 the burden of proof of wrongdoing on policyholders and not the company.Complaints about abusive sales practices have plagued the life insurance industry over the past few years.Metropolitan Life Insurance Co., New York Life Insurance Co. and Allianz Life Insurance Co. of North America all have been involved in similar actions
9223 in the last two years.Metropolitan Life agreed in 1994 to pay $20 million in fines and up to $76 million in policyholder refunds to settle allegations it improperly marketed life insurance policies as retirement or savings plans.New York Life last year agreed to a national class action settlement in a
9223 dispute over dividends on life insurance policies and Allianz Life in June agreed to pay $5.1 million, including $2.3 million in restitution to settle allegations it engaged in deceptive sales practices in California.New York insurance regulators earlier this month moved to fight the industry's problems by proposing a tough new
9223 regulation to protect consumers from the inappropriate replacement of life insurance policies.The Prudential class action settlement includes general relief as well as an alternative dispute resolution process.The general relief, which includes enhanced life insurance, annuities and low-cost premium loans, is available to all policyholders who purchased permanent life insurance policies
9223 from 1982 to 1995.Prudential said it did not have an estimate of the value of the general relief to policyholders.Under the alternative dispute resolution process, policyholders could be eligible for restitution, as well as additional compensation, Prudential said.The amount Prudential will pay under the alternative dispute resolution process is not
9223 capped, but the insurer is committed to paying at least $410 million.If Prudential receives more than 110,000 legitimate claims, then it will pay out more than $410 million.Under a formula worked out in the settlement, if Prudential receives 330,000 legitimate claims, it would pay $780 million in restitution and $300
9223 million in additional compensation for a total payout of about $1.08 billion.</

9235 Charging that Switzerland grossly deceived the United States on the amount of Nazi assets it held, the head of the U.S. Senate Banking Committee asked the State Department on Tuesday to reopen negotiations with the Swiss on a 50-year-old treaty.New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato's move came as a newly
9235 discovered document in the U.S. National Archives claimed Nazi Germany not only had hundreds of millions of dollars in gold secreted in Switzerland at the end of the Second World War, but an even larger amount in other assets that included bank deposits, securities, real estate and looted art works.The
9235 May 31, 1945, document from the American legation in Bern to the secretary of state paints a sweeping picture of German investment in Switzerland but warns that the full truth may never be known because "The traditional stock-in-trade of Swiss bankers, notaries, realtors, insurance companies, attorneys, etc. is the concealment
9235 of assets."The document, obtained by the World Jewish Congress (WJC) during a search of the archives, indicates that the amount in assets -- an estimated $750 million in 1945 dollars -- was greater than what the Nazis had deposited in gold in Switzerland. Other previously secret documents estimated the gold
9235 to be worth $550 million in 1945 dollars or about $6 billion today.In 1946, after freezing Swiss assets in the United States, the United States, Britain and France reached an agreement with Switzerland to return Nazi gold and assets kept in Switzerland.Under the agreement, the three countries received $60 million
9235 in gold and was supposed to get 50 percent of the non-gold assets, an amount that worked out to $121 million over the course of seven years, according to historians. The Swiss were allowed to keep the other 50 percent of assets.This is the agreement that D'Amato said he wanted
9235 renegotiated.In a letter to Secretary of State Warren Christopher, D'Amato accused Switzerland of 50 years of deception over the amount of funds deposited in Swiss banks by the Nazis.He said, "When the allies sat down with the Swiss in 1945, in an attempt to gain possession of these looted assets
9235 in order to return them to their rightful owners, the Swiss proved to be evasive, uncooperative and outrightly stubborn when it came to giving anything back."In essence, according to our own documents, they went out of their way to deceive U.S. negotiators as to how much they retained in Nazi
9235 assets, looted or otherwise. In light of this, after more than 50 years, the Swiss must make amends and come clean."D'Amato added in his letter to Christopher, "I would ask you seek discussions with the Swiss on reopening these negotiations and provide for a proper accounting. .... Clearly the Swiss
9235 owe the Allies more than they have admitted to, yet they have managed to escape criticism for this deception for more than 50 years."The Swiss government last week promised to pay more than $800,000 to two Holocaust groups in a gesture sought by Jewish groups after Switzerland apologised last year
9235 for turning back refugees from Nazi terror.At least two tonnes s of gold looted by the Nazis remains stored in the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank and another four tonnes s in the Bank of England in London from the 1946 agreement. WJC President Edgar Bronfman has asked that this gold
9235 be made available to Holocaust survivors and other victims of Nazi persecutions.A tonne of gold is worth about $10.2 million.</
9236 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe U.S. Federal Reserve held off from increasing interest rates on Tuesday in what analysts described as a calculated gamble that the economy will slow before inflation starts to rise."Instead of raising rates, they've crossed their fingers," said Robert Brusca, chief economist for Wall Street broker
9236 Nikko Securities Inc.President Clinton hailed the central bank's decision, saying it showed that the economy was on track."I just think it shows we've got a strong economy with no inflation. I'm glad about that," Clinton told reporters during a campaign visit to New Jersey.The decision was good news for Clinton,
9236 who has been counting on a trouble-free economy in the run-up to the Nov. 5 election to help him win a second, four-year term.Wall Street's reaction was mixed. After surging in the immediate wake of the Fed announcement, share prices fell back on profit-taking following their recent record run. The
9236 Dow Jones industrial average closed 20.71 points lower at 5,874.Bond prices gained, with the pace-setting 30-year Treasury issue jumping nearly a half point, pushing the yield down to 6.98 percent from 7.02 percent Monday.Many analysts still expect the Fed to raise interest rates sometime in the coming months, possibly at
9236 its next policy meeting on Nov. 13 -- eight days after the election."If it hadn't been for the election, they probably would have raised rates," said David Wyss, of Massachusetts-based consultants DRI/McGraw Hill.As is its wont, the secretive Fed did not formally announce its decision to hold rates steady, but
9236 instead merely said that it had ended its meeting after 4-1/2 hours of talks."The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended at 1:40 p.m. (1740 GMT)," central bank spokesman Joseph Coyne said. "There is no further announcement."The bland statement hid what analysts believed was one of the more contentious meetings of
9236 the policy-making committee.Anti-inflation hawks at the Fed, particularly at its regional banks, have made no secret of their desire for higher rates to cool off the economy and head off inflation.Tuesday's decision left the federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight money at 5-1/4 percent and the
9236 discount rate the Fed charges banks for loans at five percent.The central bank has not changed either rate since Jan. 31, when it cut them both by a quarter percentage point.Fed policymakers were faced with conflicting evidence on the state of the economy when they met on Tuesday.By opting not
9236 to raise rates now, the Fed is hoping that economic growth will slow down enough on its own to head off the risk of higher inflation, analysts said.In the words of Fed Governor Janet Yellen, the economy is operating in an "inflationary danger zone." But so far there is no
9236 clear sign of higher inflation.At 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at its lowest point in more than seven years and at a level that in the past has often led to stepped-up wage demands and higher inflation.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies
9236 have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Much will depend on the future course of the economy.In the second quarter, the economy grew at a 4.8 percent clip -- its fastest pace in two years and about twice the rate
9236 most analysts reckon is sustainable on a long-term basis without fanning inflation.Growth has slowed since then, as consumer spending, which accounts for about two-thirds of the economy, has slackened.But with consumer confidence at about a six-year high, labour markets tight and wages rising, some analysts -- and Fed anti-inflation hawks
9236 -- question whether the slowdown that is on its way will be enough to keep price pressures in check.The central bank was under considerable political pressure not to raise rates Tuesday, six weeks ahead of the election.Seventy eight lawmakers -- all but two of them Democrats -- wrote to Fed
9236 Chairman Alan Greenspan on Monday contending that a rate rise now would hurt, not help the economy.And Clinton administration officials have argued that inflation remained quiescent, strongly implying that they saw no need for the independent central bank to raise rates.</

9242 Chevron Corp.'s Chevron Chemical Co. and Saudi Industrial Venture Capital Group said Tuesday they formed a 50-50 joint venture to build and operate a $650 million petrochemical complex in Al-Jubail, Saudi Arabia.In a statement, Chevron said the company will be known as Saudi Chevron Petrochemical, a Limited Liability Partnership.Construction of
9242 a grassroots 480,000 ton-per-year benzene plant and a 220,000 ton-per-year cyclohexane unit is scheduled to be completed in mid-1999.The plant will manufacture benzene from a natural gasoline feedstock supplied by Saudi Aramco.</
9243 Some American Indians are pushing to get the word "squaw" removed from dozens of streams, lakes and other geographic features across Minnesota, saying the word is offensive.But other Minnesotans say they're offended by the campaign."Squaw" offends some Indians, who say it's a French corruption of an Iroqoui epithet for vagina.Although
9243 some people in the Gopher State dispute that linguistic theory, the state legislature recently ordered that 19 place names inside lands under state control be changed, according to a Minnesota Department of Natural Resources.As a result, Squaw Point is now Oak Point. The former Squaw Creek became Fond-du-lac Creek. And
9243 two lakes named Squaw were renamed -- one Wahbegon Lake, the other Equay Lake.Residents of the town of Squaw Lake, near a body of water that once shared the same name, are resisting what they see as an attack on tradition by the forces of political correctness."Most people around here
9243 don't want it changed," lifelong Squaw Lake resident Sandra Strief said in a telephone interview Tuesday. "It doesn't mean to us what they say it means. When they say 'Squaw Lake', I just think of an Indian lady. I don't think of anything bad."</
9244 The House of Representatives on Tuesday called on the federal government to make public its records on Nazi war criminals, which have been kept secret since the end of the Second World War.The non-binding resolution, which passed by voice vote, asks that the information be made available through the Freedom
9244 of Information Act, which allows individuals to request government records."With this resolution, the House will go on record in favour of full disclosure of war crimes files, so long as the release of this information does not harm our legitimate national security interests," Representative Carolyn Maloney, a New York Democrat
9244 who was a sponsor of the measure, said.She said the Central Intelligence Agency objected to passage of a bill requiring release of the information."In passing this resolution, we honour the memory of those who died and the suffering of those who survived (the Holocaust)," she said.</

9246 Stock prices soared briefly Tuesday after the Federal Reserve decided to keep interest rates steady, but the market quickly retreated as investors assessed the implications of the central bank's move.Bonds also jumped at first before surrendering some of their gains, but the dollar drew sustained selling pressure.Shortly after 3:40 p.m.
9246 EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 40.69 points at 5,854.06 after initially gaining 35 points on the Fed's decision.The decision surprised some Wall Street analysts who had expected the central bank to raise rates for the first time in 1-1/2 years. Prior to the Fed's decision, the Dow
9246 index had hovered around unchanged."I am actually very dissapointed that the Fed didn't take a golden opportunity to nudge rates up," said Graham Tanaka, President of Tanaka Capital Management. "On a pre-emptive basis it would have been a conservative route to take."In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was
9246 up 12/32 after initially rising nearly half a point, and its yield fell to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent at Monday's close.Analysts said the stock market had already priced in a quarter-point rise in interest rates. Tuesday's declines came a day after the Dow set a closing record of 5,894.74.The
9246 Fed's decision, which had been anxiously awaited on Wall Street left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent.The central bank also held the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, at 5 percent."The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended at
9246 1:40 p.m. (1740 GMT)," central bank spokesman Joseph Coyne said. "There is no further announcement."The bland statement hid what analysts believed was one of the more contentious meetings of the policy-making committee. Anti-inflation hawks at the Fed, particularly at its regional banks, have made no secret of their desire for
9246 higher rates to cool off the economy and head off inflation.Out of 55 economists surveyed in a Reuters poll, 31 had expected the Fed to hike rates on Tuesday. Some analysts said the Fed move was justified by a lack of inflationary pressures.Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line
9246 Asset Management said, "We believe the Fed's action to leave rates unchanged is fully justified given the complete absence of inflation and a noted deceleration in economic activity during the quarter to date."Meanwhile, the dollar plunged, trading at 1.5020 German marks, down from 1.5125 marks on Monday. The currency fell
9246 to 109.20 Japanese yen vs. 109.89 yen.Currency traders said the Fed's decision to hold monetary policy steady might not inflict long-term damage to the dollar because short-term interest rates were likely to head higher before the end of the year."To me the handwriting is on the wall," said Sung Won
9246 Sohn, chief economist and senior vice president at Norwest Corp. "It's a question of when (a rate hike) comes, not if it will come."The upbeat dollar outlook was due to a belief that the central bank remained hawkish on inflation regardless of Tuesday's decision on rates, analysts said."I still believe
9246 they prefer to act early on the rate side if they have to and there will be enough of them that they'll have a consensus, I would believe, before the year is out," said Michael Faust, foreign exchange manager at Bailard, Biehl &amp; Kaiser.</

9248 Revco D.S., Inc., which has launched a hostile takeover bid for rival drug store chain Big B Inc., said Tuesday its first-quarter profits soared 71.4 percent as sales improved and operating costs declined.Revco, the nation's second-largest chain of drug stores, said its profits jumped to $14.4 million, or 21 cents
9248 a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 24, from $8.4 million, or 13 cents a share, in the year-ago period.Sales rose 9.6 percent to $1.18 billion from $1.08 billion. Comparable store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, increased 7.9 percent."Our comparable store sales increases remain strong
9248 and we continue to leverage operating expenses with a sustained focus on operating efficiencies," said D. Dwayne Hoven, Revco's chief executive officer."Our strong operating performance, coupled with the benefit of lower interest expense from reduced debt levels, yielded a very strong first quarter relative to last year's results and positions
9248 the company to deliver a record performance in fiscal 1997."Revco's operating profit rose 22.3 percent to $37.9 million from $31.0 million in the 1995 first quarter. While gross profit margins fell because of continued pressure from managed care sales, this was more than offset by cuts in the Twinsburg, Ohio-based
9248 company's operating costs.Analysts said strong cost control was the big story."(The key was) very good control of ... expense," said Philip Muldoon of McDonald &amp; Co., a Cleveland brokerage.J.P. Morgan Securities analyst Mark Husson was also impressed with expense control and said Revco had awakened from several "somnabulent" months while
9248 a proposed merger with the No. 1 chain, Rite Aid Corp., was pending.Federal regulatory antitrust concerns derailed that merger earlier this year."I think this is an aggressive business now. It's doing a lot of good work inside itself so it's not just an acquisition-driven business. This is a real live
9248 one," he said. He rates the stock a buy.Excluding a non-cash charge for amortization of goodwill, Revco had net income of $20.7 million, or 31 cents a share, in the first quarter, up from $14.7 million, or 22 cents a share, in the year-ago period.On Monday, Big B rejected Revco's
9248 $332 million takeover bid as inadequate and said it had already received inquiries from other unidentified suitors.However, Revco said it remains committed to its offer to acquire Big B, which has adopted a shareholder rights plan that would make the deal more difficult to complete.Revco, which owns 5.4 percent of
9248 Big B's stock, said it will review the terms of the Bessemer, Ala.-based drug store chain's rights plan and determine what actions to take.During the quarter, Revco opened 43 new stores, 20 of which were relocations and five were acquired stores. It closed five stores.Revco operates more than 2,200 stores
9248 in 14 Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states.Revco's stock rose $1 to $26.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.</

9251 market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on moderate volume of 239 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.The Nasdaq Composite index was up 3.03 points at 1,214.50."This is about as wait-and-see kind of a day as you can find," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at
9251 First Albany Corp. adding that the market was dominated by short-term traders rather than portfolio managers.The big question of the day was what action the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee would take on interest rates. The outcome was expected at 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).In a Reuters survey of 55
9251 primary dealers, banks and advisory firms, a slim majority of 31 forecasters said they expected the Fed to raise short-term interest rates."The message of the market today is that if the Fed does nothing or raises rates by 25 basis points (a quarter percentage point), the market will go up,"
9251 Goldman said. Edwards &amp; Sons.AT&amp;T said higher sales and marketing costs, especially in its long distance business will pressure its third quarter results, and
9251 per share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates.The sell-off in AT&amp;T depressed other long-distance carriers. 9251 cable companies, will be intense over the next three to five years," said Johnson."People often ask themselves how this manifests itself, and here you have a very good example of how competitive the communications business has become," he said.Among individual stocks, Micron Technology Inc. rose 2-3/8 to 30-3/8 after posting

9255 Consumer confidence in the economy held steady at a six-year high in September, a private research group said Tuesday, and the optimism is expected to extend into the holiday season.The Conference Board said its index of consumer confidence was at 111.8 in September, little changed from a revised reading of
9255 112.0 in August.The New York-based private research business group said its expectations component index rose in September to 100.4 from a revised 100.3 in the previous month.The survey showed consumers are "quite optimistic about the next six months," said Lynn Franco, associate director of the board's Consumer Research Centre."With consumers
9255 in high spirits, the outlook for holiday spending appears to be bright," she said."After remaining flat over the last year, consumer confidence broke out in July and is currently holding at a six-year high," Franco said.The Consumer Confidence Survey, which is based on a sampling of 5,000 households, found that
9255 the proportion of respondents who felt that jobs are "hard to get" dropped to 21 percent in September from 22 percent in August.About 27 percent of consumers say business conditions are "good," off moderately from 28.5 percent in August.The group said the percentage of respondents who expect business conditions to
9255 improve moved up to 17.3 percent from 16.1 percent.In addition to posting the national measures, the survey showed that regional confidence improved dramatically in New England, having jumped by 24 percent over the past three months. Confidence levels there had been "in the doldrums since early 1990," the Board said.The
9255 East South Central region -- including Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama and Mississippi -- was the only area to report a decline in confidence over the past three months, dropping about 1.0 percent, it said.</

9260 The blood clot-dissolving drug streptokinase is not helpful for stroke victims and may cause complications if given more than three hours after a stroke, researchers reported on Tuesday.A study involving 340 patients designed to test the efficacy of the drug in treating stroke was halted because of unacceptably high complication
9260 rates, according to researchers from the Austin and Repatriation Medical Centre, Heidelberg, Victoria, Australia.Patients given the drug was within three hours of a stroke fared virtually the same as stroke victims not given the drug, said the report published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.When streptokinase, which
9260 is often used for treating heart attacks, was given to stroke victims more than three hours after a stroke occurred there was an increase in death rates beyond what would be expected, the report said.Commenting on the study in an editorial in the same publication, Vladimir Hachinski of the University
9260 of Western Ontario in London, Ontario, said all major stroke tests with the drug "have been stopped early because of unacceptably high complication rates, and thus streptokinase cannot be recommended at this time for the treatment of acute stroke."</

9261 or sent in packages. Last year, 54 prison visitors and six employees were arrested in connection with drug smuggling."We wanted to send a message to the inmates and staff that we are not going to put up with this kind of thing," he said."They do some ingenious things, like taking
9261 the bottoms out of tennis shoes, putting drugs in and mailing them in for Christmas," said department official Joe Andrews.Monthly random tests showed percentages of positive results were significantly higher than at Ohio's other 28 prisons, said Andrews.Similar routine tests at other Ohio facilities produced an average of three to
9261 five percent, but at Mansfield the rates were as high as 19 percent, he said in a telephone interview.All 2,059 inmates were due to be tested, Andrews said. By late afternoon, 275 of 1,393 tested -- one in nearly five -- had tested positive, mainly for marijuana.Offenders would be restricted

9269 Senate.There are 53 open seats in the House, 30 of them due to Democratic retirements and 19 of those in the South where Republicans have come on strong in recent years. 9269 months as voters soured on their agenda. 9269 claim many of the 73 House freshmen Republicans are vulnerable and point to 14 Republican incumbents who they say trail their Democratic challengers.Republicans point out that Democrats trail badly in some open Southern seats and have a list of vulnerable incumbents They also have millions of dollars more than Democrats.National

9270 The Senate Tuesday approved a bill setting up a new U.S.-flag shipping subsidy plan under which the vessels would be available for carrying defence supplies during wartime.Under the bill operators of U.S.-flag ships that could be used for military supply purposes would receive $2.3 million for each ship this year
9270 and $2.1 million for each ship annually through fiscal 2005. The bill authorised $100 million a year for the payments.The bill, approved on an 88-10 vote, would replace the current programme that provides government payments to U.S.-flag operators based on the difference between the crew and operating costs of U.S.-flag
9270 vessels and foreign-flag ships.Operating American ships costs more because of higher pay and benefits and more costly regulation.The plan was assailed by a Senate foe, Sen Charles Grassley, R-Iowa, as "welfare" for shipping companies and unions but supporters said its cost would be half of that of the current programme.But
9270 Sen. Daniel Inouye, D-Hawaii, said the new plan would guarantee the Defence Department a pool of American crews and a 50-ship fleet of militarily useful ships, along with the companies' railcars, containers and other facilities."We must be able to ensure that U.S.-flag shipping is available to bring materiel and ammunition
9270 to soldiers who are defending our interests on foreign soil," said Inouye.Sen. Ted Stevens, R-Alaska, said that more than 120 U.S.-flag ships were called on to help the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf prior to the Gulf war. At the same time some foreign operators doubled their normal charter
9270 rates.Under the new plan, U.S. shipping firms would have to agree to rates established in advance for chartering in a defence emergency.The bill, which had administration support, must now be reconciled with a similar House-passed measure.</
9271 Searchers hunting for debris from downed TWA Flight 800 found what appears to be part of its centre fuel tank, a critical piece of evidence investigators have sought anxiously, officials said on Tuesday.Investigators believe the deadly July 17 explosion, which claimed the lives of all 230 people on board, was
9271 centred in the Boeing 747's centre fuel tank system.The newly recovered piece of the tank system, measuring nine feet by 13 feet (three metres by four metres), "was a piece of the area of the airplane that we're interested in," said U.S. Navy Rear Admiral Edward Kristensen, at a media
9271 briefing.Searchers also found fuel probes, possibly from the centre fuel tank, that may be significant, officials said.None of the probes found earlier were identified as coming from the centre fuel tank."We're looking for something that will tell us why the centre fuel tank exploded," said Robert Francis, vice chairman of
9271 the National Transportation Safety Board.Before this discovery, Francis estimated about 65 percent of the tank had been recovered. It held only about 50 gallons (190 litres) of jet fuel at the time of the explosion.Despite the finds, Francis conceded that the reason the Paris-bound plane exploded mid-air without warning off
9271 the coast of Long Island, New York, may never be known."Surely the possibility exists," said Francis, head of the investigation, "but I don't think people are thinking that way."Investigators maintain there are three possible explanations for the crash -- a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure.They have found microscopic chemical
9271 traces of explosives in the debris but say they lack evidence to declare that a bomb destroyed the plane.Last week investigators learned that the jet had been used to train bomb-sniffing dogs, which could account for at least some of the trace explosives they found, they said.Francis also said the
9271 search of the Atlantic Ocean floor for wreckage is winding down and could last another one to two weeks. "The returns from the bottom of the ocean are diminishing," he said.Investigators will continue to reassemble the plane in an old aircraft hangar in Calverton, New York, he said.At the site
9271 of the crash, search teams are relying most heavily on side-scanning sonar to find the last bits of the plane scattered on the ocean floor, officials said.The bodies of 213 of the 230 victims have been recovered.</

9273 policy meeting.In the half hour before the Fed said its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee had left rates untouched, bond prices climbed about one-third of a point from levels that had been nearly unchanged on the day.After the announcement, the market doubled that gain, before conceding a good portion of
9273 it.The bellwether 30-year Treasury bond closed 14/32 higher, reducing its yield to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent at Monday's close."The knee jerk reaction was the simple one in which the market rallied to news that rates are going to be held steady for a time," said Michael Moran, chief economist
9273 at Daiwa Securities America Inc."But then prices backed down from their peaks on the thought that the Fed is doing experiments with inflation and that it's not as vigilant on inflation as perhaps it should be."Short-term bill rates, which are most responsive to near-term Fed policy adjustments, fell sharply as
9273 prospects for higher official interest rates receded at least until the Fed's next policy meeting in November, analysts said.Three- and six-month Treasury bill rates fell 20 basis points and 14 basis points, respectively, closing at 4.97 percent and 5.15 percent."You'll be dealing with a 5-1/4 percent Federal funds rate until
9273 November at the earliest," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.At 5.25 percent currently, the fed funds rate -- charged by banks with excess reserves at a Fed district bank to banks needing overnight loans -- is the most sensitive indicator of
9273 the direction of interest rates.Samuel Kahan, president of A.S.K. 9273 rates steady because inflation has not accelerated.Elliott Platt, managing director of economic research at Donaldson, Lufkin &amp; Jenrette, said the big risk to the market now would be stronger-than-anticipated economic data.Platt said he expected upcoming reports on durable goods orders, new home sales and September payroll growth to be subdued,
9273 adding anything contrary to that would set the market back, he said."That's the big risk," Platt said. "Let's say the September payrolls report is strong and the next CPI is up 0.3 percent. The market could have a horrible case of indigestion which would have been mitigated by some sort
9273 of pre-emptive rate hike by the Fed. But the Fed apparently thinks it's a risk worth taking."At the close, the year bill rate fell 12 basis points to 5.40 percent. The two-year note was up 6/32 to 99-31/32, yielding 6.14 percent, the five-year note up 12/32 at 99-31/32, yielding 6.51

9278 supervisors and 100 co-workers.By comparison, government labour statistics show about one in 80 workers lost his or her job last year, the study said.Of the cancer patients in the survey, 40 percent said they missed fewer than five days work in an average month during cancer treatment. 9278 they told their employers within a week of their diagnosis, while 14 percent said they never revealed their diagnosis in the workplace.The study showed that patients and supervisors had widely different views of how cancer's side effects affected patients' job performance.Among supervisors, 85 percent cited patients' fatigue, while 58 percent
9278 of patients said they suffered from it. 9278 a family member had lost their job due to absences to care for them.Some cancer patients have responded with legal action, said the sponsors of the survey, Working Woman magazine and Amgen, a biotechnology company.Three months ago, Jane Karuschkat of Glen Cove, N.Y., who lost her job due to her
9278 cancer was awarded $70,000 by the New York State Human Rights Commission. She missed three days of work after a mastectomy and less than two days work for chemotherapy before she was fired as a legal secretary.The random telephone poll, conducted May 13 to 29, had a margin of error
9278 of plus or minus 4.5 percent.</

9304 Women who take the pill for contraception do not increase their long-term risk of breast cancer, according to a study released on Tuesday.Scientists found that women showed no increase in breast cancer 10 or more years after they stopped taking the pill, regardless of a family's history of breast cancer,
9304 ethnicity, age or country of origin."This study answers the major outstanding question we had about the pill -- does it have any persistent effect on breast cancer long after women stop taking it?" Dr. Valerie Beral, chief of the Cancer Epidemiology Unit at Oxford University in Britain, said in a
9304 statement.Beral, who led the effort to combine 54 studies on 150,000 women from 25 countries, said the results were true regardless of how long the women took the pill and what type of pill they used, but researchers observed a very small increase in breast cancer among current and recent
9304 oral contraceptive users.U.S. birth control expert Dr. Carolyn Westhoff told a news conference a possible explanation for this was that doctors who prescribed the pill were more likely to ask for mammograms, which detect breast tumours. She noted that cancer was a disease that developed over many years and that
9304 if the pill caused cancer it would not be seen immediately."This study had thousands of women in each of the different sub-groups one might have questions about and none of those particular types of women or patterns of use were associated with any risk," said Westhoff, director for family planning
9304 at Columbia-Presbyterian Medical Centre in New York.She wrote an editorial in the journal Contraception on the study, a rare collaboration by more than 200 scientists. Some of the analyses had appeared in The Lancet medical journal. It was funded by the Imperial Cancer Research Fund in Britain.</

9319 The entry of controversial activist Al Sharpton into next year's race for New York City mayor is likely to put a jolt into a campaign many have seen as ho-hum so far.While few give Sharpton any chance of defeating Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, the flamboyant black minister could emerge in the
9319 enviable position of powerbroker, political analysts said. An independent run
9319 by Sharpton could siphon off enough traditional Democratic black votes to guarantee Giuliani's re-election, analysts said.Giuliani was elected in 1993, the first Republican to hold the mayor's office in a generation. The former federal prosecutor defeated David Dinkins, the city's first black mayor, by a slim margin."Sharpton will make it
9319 a lot more interesting than it was going to be," said Michael Tomasky, a political columnist at New York magazine."He definitely shakes things up," said Democratic pollster Chris Lapetina of Global Strategy Group. "He'll get more press attention than anybody else and he's not scared to attack."Polls have shown Giuliani
9319 defeating all of the oft-mentioned challengers if the election were held now.Among his likely Democratic challengers, none well-known outside the city, are Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger, Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer, City Comptroller Alan Hevesi and Brooklyn City Councilman Sal Albanese, the first to toss his hat officially into
9319 the ring.If Sharpton, the only black among them, runs in the party primary he could strike deals with the winner in exchange for his support, Tomasky said. But a Democrat seen as beholden to Sharpton could lose more moderate votes to Giuliani and boost the mayor's chances considerably, he said."He'll
9319 have a heavy card to play, which in the end probably means the Democrats have less of a chance to beat Giuliani," Tomasky said."There will be people who might want to vote for a Democratic candidate but who will fear the influence of Sharpton," former Mayor Ed Koch said.Sharpton made
9319 an unexpectedly strong showing in 1992 in a four-way Democratic Senate primary, finishing ahead of former City Controller Elizabeth Holtzman. He was seen as having shed his more controversial image to become a credible candidate.But the ghosts of Sharpton's past will haunt him, political analysts agree, particularly his role as
9319 adviser to Tawana Brawley, a black teenager who in 1987 was found nude and covered with excrement in upstate New York. With Sharpton at her side, Brawley claimed several white men kidnapped and raped her, but the claim proved to be a hoax."He's made an effort to redefine himself but
9319 a lot of people are stuck with that old image," Lapetina said. "That's his Chappaquiddick."While no challenger has emerged as an overwhelming threat, Giuliani is vulnerable, analysts say. Admired as tenacious and independent, he has overseen a drop in crime and designed a working city budget, but his heavy-handed style
9319 has forced out several popular city figures including Police Commisioner William Bratton and Schools Chancellor Ramon Cortines and has led many to accuse him of behaving like a schoolyard bully."People don't like Giuliani in this town," said John Mollenkopf, a professor of political science at the City University of New
9319 York. "People feel for all the good he's done ... he beats up on everyone who disagrees with him."To keep his job, Giuliani must retain the coalition that elected him -- the city's few Republicans and the disgruntled Democrats who voiced unhappiness with the ineffective Dinkins."It's still a Democratic town,"
9319 Lapetina said. "If someone can come up with why voters should get rid of Giuliani, I think people will respond."</
9320 Despite the widespread belief that U.S. manufacturing is generally stronger this year, forecasts for August durable goods orders vary widely because monthly data has been volatile, economists said Tuesday.Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp, said he "guesses" data to be released Thursday will show little change in
9320 August durable goods orders. But he added that sharp variations would not surprise him that much."Remember, one order for one aircraft can skew the number significantly," Johnson said. The data is scheduled for release on Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.Johnson noted the trend for durable goods orders has been up
9320 for the year with "enormous volatility."Forecasts for overall durable goods orders by economists polled by Reuters ranged from up 2.0 percent to down 1.0 percent. The average forecast had orders down 0.1 percent in August, or off 0.7 percent excluding the volatile defense category. Lee Youngdahl, vice president and an
9320 economist at Aubrey G. Lanston &amp; Co Inc, said aircraft orders should be reflected in August's number and bolster the current trend. Orders outside transportation were more modest, he said, but not modest enough to raise concerns of weakness."The trend that's underway is one of strength when you look back
9320 in four of the past five months," he said. "The underlying trend is good. Demand remains pretty solid and inventories are at pretty low levels." James Padinha, economist at MMS International Inc., said he expects durable goods data will be unchanged in August. However, he noted that Boeing Co recently
9320 reported large aircraft orders that could skew the data upward if it is included in the August report.If the Boeing order is included in August data, Padinha said he expects durable goods orders could jump 0.5 percent."It's unlikely the whole thing will show up in August, but if it does
9320 it seems like the potential is for a surprise on the upside," Padinha said. Padinha expects the data will settle back from big gains in July. The overall trend remains strong, however, and the August data will not upset calls for firm numbers down the road, he said."The overall story
9320 is on a year-over-year basis orders are still doing pretty well," he said. "If you put recent orders in a category marked 'favors Fed tightening' or 'does not favor Fed tightening,' you'd probably have to put it in 'favors'." Defense spending, which tends to go back and forth from month
9320 to month, should rebound from a big drop in July, Youngdahl said. And outside the more volatile sectors, he said he sees no other areas that might show inherent weakness. He noted primary metals and industrial machinery have both perked up in recent months after a slow start for the
9320 year.Looking ahead, Youngdahl said he sees four to six months of an uptrend for durable goods based on expectations of rising capacity utilization rates."There is still some slack on the industrial capacity side of things, but with demand remaining good, I think the idea is factories continue to try and
9320 add capacity where they can," Youngdahl said, adding, "I would think that would tend to undergird orders going forward."Slackening consumer demand will not derail businesses from rebuilding inventories to "a reasonable level," he said.-- 212-859-1672</

9329 spot sales will be replaced by two long-term contract sales of 5,000 tonnes each in February and July 1997. A further 2,000 tonnes will be sold in a sealed bid process, with a maximum 200 tonnes available each month until the 2,000 tonnes is exhausted."For the time being this is
9329 our plan and I intend to stick to it," Connelly said.He reiterated the DLA's undertaking that 12,000 tonnes at most would be sold each year. Total nonfarm employment for
9343 August was 6.07 million, ain increase of 168,300 jobs or 2.8 percent from August of last year.Services added the most jobs, 79,700, over the year and had the second fastest growth rate, 3.9 percent. The services growth rate has been declining since October when it reached 7.3 percent. Most of
9343 the weakness has been in the business, health, legal, engineering and management groups.Trade increased by 45,700 jobs or 3 percent over the year. Construction was unchanged in recent months but has increased over the year, with two-thirds of the gains in the special trade contractor industry group.Manufacturing declined by 2,600
9343 jobs over the year, with all of the decline in nondurable goods. The transportaiton, communications and public utilities sector grew by 8,400 jobs or 2.8 percent over the year while finance, insurance and real estate grew by 8,900 jobs or 2.4 percent. Government increased by 22,000 jobs or 2.6 percent
9343 over the year.All of Florida's metropolitan areas had over the year increases. 9343 had the lowest unemployment rate, 2 percent, while Hendry County had the highest, 23.3 percent.Overall, counties with the highest unemployment rates were in the agricultural areas of central and south Florida, where seasonal increases normally occur in the summer, Jamerson said.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</
