9360 Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis mixed old-guard socialists and a new generation of party reformers on Tuesday in his "new era" cabinet at the start of a four-year term."During the formation of this cabinet, we sought to combine tested experience with the need for renewal," said a government spokesman before
9360 reading out the list.Simitis, 60, succeeded late socialist party founder and three-time premier Andreas Papandreou in January. A methodical technocrat, Simitis has vowed to reform the party and to change the erratic course of the EU's only Balkan state.His election win over the opposition conservatives on Sunday gave him a
9360 free hand to lay Papandreou's ghost to rest and stamp his own seal of authority on the party and government.Despite initial hints of radical change, Simitis stayed with tried and trusted ministers. Controversial but competent Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, who occasionally offends EU allies with his blunt comments, stayed at
9360 his post.A German and British-trained economist, Simitis has made his priority meeting strict economic targets set out by the European Union.He kept the backbone of his economic team intact, renaming Cambridge-educated National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou, who drove down inflation to single digits for the first time in 20 years.The
9360 two men have developed a close working relationship over the past eight months and Simitis effectively made Papandoniou his economic "czar", adding the finance ministry to his brief."There was always a belief that there should be one minister heading the finance and national economy ministries to ensure better coordination," said
9360 John Marcopoulos, Managing Director at Sigma Securities."The market's reaction should be positive. It didn't look forward to unpleasant surprises. I expect we will see faster action now on many pending agendas," he added.Simitis renamed Vasso Papandreou, for years a fellow party dissident, as development minister despite her confrontations with foreign
9360 investors, especially over private casinos.The only major change was the removal of defence minister Gerassimos Arsenis, an old-guard socialist who has criticised Simitis's handling of a crisis with Turkey in January.In his place Simitis named Akis Tsohatzopoulos, a Papandreou crony, but one who eventually threw his support behind Simitis.Arsenis angered
9360 Simitis with his back-room dealings to gain support for a $10 billion arms build-up. Tsohatzopoulos will cut that purchase to the bone to ensure EU economic targets are met.The only surprise was a paltry payout to George Papandreou, son of the socialist party founder, who helped turned the tide in
9360 Simitis's favour in a bruising leadership battle in June.Papandreou was named deputy foreign minister, where he will take orders from the blustering Pangalos who is renowned for his fits of temper.Political commentators said Papandreou, just 44 but wearing the most powerful political name in Greece, made his displeasure known to
9360 Simitis about his second-rank appointment.Simitis, who emerged from the socialist party shadows only recently, has vowed to push lagging Greece into line with its EU partners.But the only appointment which smacked of real reform was sending Alexandros Papadopoulos, the respected finance minister since 1993, to the interior ministry where he
9360 will try to reform a vast and hopelessly ineffective public sector administration.</

9361 with Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary the most likely candidates. The United States and its allies say they are determined to go ahead with expansion and are seeking to sweeten the pill for Russia by drawing up a special charter on ties with Moscow.But Primakov said after talks with
9361 U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Monday that the United States and Russia still had "different approaches" to the issue.In a text of his U.N. speech distributed in advance, Primakov said Russia "cannot ignore reality" and accepted that NATO would have an important place in European security. 9362 European Union negotiators said on Tuesday that most countries in the 15-nation bloc were in favour of putting the fight for jobs into the EU treaty as a way of bring the Union closer to its citizens.Noel Dorr, chairman of a group negotiating EU reforms, told reporters a majority of
9362 countries favoured legally focusing the bloc on combatting high unemployment.Opposition remained, he said, from countries fearing centralised employment planning, but he said the talks were clearly moving in the direction of writing a special employment chapter into the treaty.Sweden put forward a detailed proposal for such a chapter on Tuesday,
9362 adding to plans offered previously by Denmark, Austria and Belgium. The Irish EU presidency also has a jobs paper on the table.But negotiators said the idea continued to face opposition among heavyweights Britain, Germany and, to a lesser extent, France."With an employment chapter, we know that the fight against unemployment
9362 will always top the EU's agenda," said Gunnar Lund, Sweden's chief negotiator at the talks, the inter-governmental conference (IGC).All member states agree that lowering an unemployment rate of some 11 percent, more than twice that in the United States, is the most pressing problem facing the bloc. But there are
9362 different views on what role the EU should play."There are still countries which are not delighted with the idea," Lund told reporters.He said there seemed now to be a clearly more open attitude from France and Germany, but Danish IGC negotiator Niels Ersboell said the two countries still opposed the
9362 idea.He said Paris and Bonn did not disagree that the EU should do more to fight unemployment."The objection is about the need to inscribe this into the treaty," Ersboell said, adding that they feared such a chapter could create expectations that the EU could not live up to.Another argument was
9362 that it could create confusion about the EU's determination to stick to the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU).However, Ersboell said: "We reject these worries as completely groundless."Lund also stressed that such a chapter would not interfere with plans to create a single currency in 1999, or automatically lead
9362 to more spending.Employment policies would remain mainly a national responsibility, he added.Ersboell said Britain was against an employment chapter on principle. "They don't think this is for the European Union at all but should be a national effort," he said.According to the Swedish proposal, EU countries would commit themselves to
9362 a policy which promotes "a high and sustainable level of employment and low unemployment."Each country would adopt multi-year employment programmes and the EU would monitor the developments in each member state.To promote coordination of national policies, a special employment committee with representatives from each member state would be set up
9362 to review the employment situation.</
9363 President Bill Clinton on Tuesday signed a landmark treaty that bans all nuclear testing and called on the global community to get tougher on terrorists and drug traffickers.Using the 51st session of the U.N. General Assembly to sketch out an election-year vision of international peace and prosperity, Clinton said the
9363 countries of the world needed to cooperate against terrorism and illegal drugs because no country was immune from these menaces."Last year I asked the nations assembled here to commit to a goal of zero tolerance for aggression, terrorism and lawless behaviour. Frankly, we haven't done that yet."Real zero tolerance means
9363 giving no aid and no quarter to terrorists who slaughter the innocent and drug traffickers who poison our children and to do everything we can to prevent weapons of mass destruction from falling into the wrong hands," he said.Illustrating his determination to combat drugs, Clinton said he would provide "more
9363 than $100 million worth of defence equipment, services and training" to America's southern neighbours. This could help blunt Republican criticism of Clinton's anti-drug efforts.The White House said Clinton notified Congress on Sept. 14, and that the money would provide helicopters, patrol boats and other equipment to Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela
9363 and other nations.Clinton spoke to the U.N. delegates after making the United States the first signatory of the new Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), which is designed to end all nuclear explosions.He signed the agreement, which is expected to face a difficult fight for ratification in the U.S. Senate, with
9363 the same pen President John Kennedy used to sign a limited test ban treaty in 1963."The CTBT is the shared work of hard negotiation. Some have complained that it does not mandate total nuclear disarmament by a date certain," the president said. "I would say to them do not forsake
9363 the benefits of this achievement by ignoring the tremendous progress we have already made toward that goal."That was a veiled message to India, which exploded a nuclear device in 1974 and now vows to block the treaty from taking force. It maintains the pact is flawed because it does not
9363 commit the nuclear powers to eventually destroy their arsenals, and in fact lets them develop more sophisticated means of testing without explosions.Clinton also called for six follow-on arms control measures, including implementation of a chemical weapons treaty, a freeze on the production of nuclear bomb-making material, improving compliance with a
9363 biological weapons treaty and a ban on anti-personnel landmines.In doing so, he took an indirect swipe at Republican rival Bob Dole, who two weeks ago abruptly withdrew his support for the chemical weapons treaty, dooming U.S. ratification this year."I deeply regret that the United States Senate has not yet voted
9363 on the convention, but I want to assure you and people throughout the world that I will not let this treaty die," Clinton told the delegates.Clinton's visit to U.N. headquarters was flavored by controversy over his effort to dump Egypt's Boutros Boutros- Ghali as secretary-general of the world body. The
9363 two posed for pictures together, but the atmosphere was correct rather than cordial.Asked by reporters if they discussed Boutros-Ghali's future, Clinton said: "There was nothing to discuss. Our position is clear and it is set, and there's nothing to talk about."Clinton made no mention of the issue in his speech,
9363 saying only that his administration favoured "streamlining the bureaucracy and reining in the budget" of the UN, and that he was committed to paying past-due U.S. financial obligations to the world body.After his speech, Clinton had separate private meetings with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Saudi Arabian Foreign Minister Saud
9363 al-Faisal and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primacov. White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the situations in Bosnia and Iraq were addressed at all three meetings.</
9364 The United States and the other four declared nuclear powers on Tuesday signed a landmark treaty banning nuclear tests, with President Bill Clinton the first leader to put his signature to the pact."A major milestone has been reached on the road to making the world a safer and more secure
9364 place for generations to come," said Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali in opening the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty for signature.Clinton said the signatures of the United States, China, France, Russia and Britain and other nations were tantamount to a ban on testing even before the treaty entered into force.The world's declared nuclear
9364 powers "along with those of the vast majority of its nations will immediately create an international norm against nuclear testing -- even before the treaty formally enters into force," he said.But Russia's Foreign Minister Yvgeny Primakov warned potential nucler powers that any testing before the treaty entered into force would
9364 greatly prejudice the pact "and may compel many countries to revise their attitude to it."The landmark treaty is flawed by a provision that requires 44 potential nuclear states to ratify it through their respective legislatures. India, which has nuclear capabilities but has not deployed atomic weapons, has refused to sign
9364 "not now, not later," until the atomic powers devise a timetable for destroying their nuclear arsenals.Currently, the United States and Russia each deploy more than 7,000 warheads, France 512, Britain 464 and China 284.The treaty bans any kind of nuclear weapons explosions, whether in the atmosphere or underground. It also
9364 sets up a monitoring system to verify compliance or spot violations.Arms experts have long suspected that the insistence of Britain, Russia and China on India's acceptance during negotiation on the treaty left a loophole for future testing. British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind in his speech warned if the treaty was
9364 to be fully effective "it must command universal support."Immediately following Clinton in the signing ceremony were the foreign ministers of the four other declared nuclear states: Qian Qichen of China, Herve de Charette of France, Russia's Primakov and Britain's Rifkind. They were followed by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto of Japan,
9364 head of the only country that has been subjected to nuclear attacks -- on Hiroshima and Nagasaki at the end of the Second World War.Australia was also among the early signers, securing its place by a vigorous campaign that resulted in 158 states backing a Sept. 10 General Assembly resolution
9364 opening the treaty for signature. More than 55 countries were due to sign during the day and others over the next three weeks.Australia argues that the treaty will prevent the nuclear powers from developing more advanced and dangerous weapons and limit the ability of other states to acquire such devices,
9364 despite the ability of computer testing.In addition to the five acknowledged nuclear powers, India, Pakistan and Israel are considered threshold states exploring the development of nuclear arms.A senior U.S. official said Clinton, if re-elected, will present the treaty to the U.S. Senate for ratification early in 1997. But neither the
9364 United States nor any of the other seven governments will deposit papers of ratification until all eight are ready to do so.All five declared nuclear weapons states have imposed voluntary moratoriums on testing. The United States, Russia and Britain stopped testing between 1990 and 1992, while France and China ended
9364 blasts several months ago.The United States has conducted 1,030 explosions since its first in the New Mexico desert in 1945, followed by Russia with 715, France with 210 and Britain and China with 45 each.Clinton said he signed the treaty with the same pen that President John F. Kennedy used
9364 to sign a 1963 partial test ban treaty, which banned explosions in the atmosphere but not underground.</

9369 1980s marked the biggest banking scandal in recent French history.The French finance ministry refused to comment and the Commission in Brussels did not elaborate.But Credit Lyonnais, bailed out by the state in 1994 and again in 1995, announced without further clarification that it had postponed the release of its first-half

9387 mines and to appeal for fresh efforts to ban their production, stockpiling and use.A U.N.-sponsored conference in Geneva agreed to limit the use of some landmines in May, but stopped short of a ban because some countries argue they should remain a legitimate form of military defence."We must end the
9387 carnage caused by anti-personnel landmines -- the hidden killers that murder and maim more than 25,000 people every year," U.S. President Bill Clinton said in a speech to the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday."Today I renew my appeal for the swift negotiation of a worldwide ban on the use, stockpiling,
9387 production and transfer of anti-personnel mines. Our children deserve to walk this earth in safety."The 15-nation European Union, many of whose countries have agreed to stop exports of landmines, said on Tuesday it would give priority to dealing with the issue.Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, whose country holds the EU
9387 presidency and speaks for the bloc, said more than 110 million landmines had been sown worldwide and that they had disabled a quarter of a million people."It is an incredible and obscene irony that at a time when the United Nations ... is continuing its vital work of mine clearance,
9387 further millions of anti-personnel landmines are deployed annually," Spring said.The U.N. Security Council has asked member states to contribute to a fund that will help with de-mining in countries like Bosnia, Angola, Afghanistan and Cambodia.Millions of mines lie in these countries, often sown in uncharted areas. They continue to kill
9387 when farmers or women and children step on them, long after the conflict has ended.Many of them are designed to maim by blowing off legs or inflicting other wounds. This makes sense from a military point of view, since a wounded soldier needs others to remove him from the battlefield,
9387 further reducing troop numbers.Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura told the U.N. assembly on Monday that there were over 10 million mines in his country alone and that more than 10,000 people had been mutilated by them."My government supports all efforts towards a total ban on the production, use and
9387 export of ... anti-personnel landmines," de Moura said."The only viable solution ... is a total worldwide ban," said Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen.Following the 55-nation Geneva conference, the United States said in May it would seek a global ban on landmines by the year 2001. Almost 40 other nations
9387 support a total ban.The Geneva conference agreed to outlaw undetectable anti-personnel mines and is due to reconvene in the year 2001 to consider progress and possible further moves.But critics say the agreement encourages the use of more advanced mines which will still be permitted in the meantime.</

9402 By Nicholas Doughty, Diplomatic CorrespondentEuropean allies stepped up the pressure on Tuesday for the United States to pay its huge debts to the United Nations, saying that the world body's crippling financial crisis could not go on.Washington owes some $1.6 billion, more than half of the debt mountain that has
9402 pushed the United Nations close to bankruptcy. The United States has said there must be more radical reforms before it meets its commitments in full.U.S. President Bill Clinton promised on Tuesday that Washington would pay up.But European allies speaking at the U.N. General Assembly in New York said those countries
9402 owing money to the United Nations should pay immediately -- and without conditions.Ireland, speaking on behalf of the 15-nation European Union, said efforts to reform the United Nations were taking place "against the backdrop of a serious financial crisis."Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring did not mention the United States by
9402 name but told the U.N. assembly:"All member states have an obligation to discharge their arrears...promptly, in full and without conditions."His comments were echoed by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind."All members must pay what they owe...and promptly. The UN faces a critical year...This year must see a solution to the financial
9402 crisis," Rifkind said.On Monday, Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland -- often mentioned as a potential candidate for U.N. secretary-general -- went even further. She bluntly told the assembly that refusal to pay dues amounted to intimidation.Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov talked of the need for U.N. reform but did
9402 not address the debt question. After the United States, Russia is the biggest debtor, owing more than $335 million.Alluding to hostility towards the United Nations in the Republican-dominated U.S. Congress, Clinton blamed opponents for difficulties in paying the country's bill."We are paying our dues and we are committed to paying
9402 off our accrued obligations soon," Clinton told the assembly.Discussions on reforming the payments system for member states have made little progress since world nations called for changes at last year's celebrations to mark the 50th anniversary of the United Nations.The financial crisis comes at a time of uncertainty about the
9402 U.N.'s future role after the failure of its peacekeeping operations in Bosnia and Somalia. Discussion on other reforms of the U.N. system has also made little headway.Since Washington has blocked the appointment of Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali for a second five-year term, it is also unclear who will lead the United
9402 Nations into the 21st century.</

9407 Europe's publishing industry on Tuesday urged in-depth changes to European copyright law to ensure that companies rather then journalists hold the rights to their works in the information society."The major concern is that in many European countries, copyright is still vested in the individual creator irrespective of whether the work
9407 is created under a regular employment contract or who bears the financial risk," the European Publishers Council said in a statement.Sir Frank Rogers, Chairman of the Council, said that the publishing industry might have a social cultural, and political role, but it was none of these if it could not
9407 work as a business."None of us can perform any of these functions unless we are economically viable," he told a news conference.Kerstin Rinne, Vice-President of Sanoma Corporation in Finland, said the European Union's work on copyright in the developing information society had so far concentrated on the means of patrolling
9407 copyright, rather than the copyright concepts themselves.The publishers say the current approach leaves them ill-equipped to compete with other media players and competitors from outside the European Union."When copyrights are vested in the employees we, as publishers, face costly copyright clearance processes and multiple payments, restricted availability and use of
9407 old material...before all economic risks are taken," it said."Many European publishers are thereforce discouraged from investing in new products and services, faced with the need to secure rights for everyday business development."The EPC and other publishing groups said the EU should take over the system used in the United States,
9407 Britain and the Netherlands, where the employer holds the copyright.</

9410 Romania as they had "no effect" in containing the spread of the mosquito-borne virus.But WHO recommended tourists or business travellers to wear protective clothing and insect repellant to avoid catching the virus, whose spread is expected to decline with the start of winter. 9410 conducted by WHO at the Pasteur Institute in Paris confirmed that the patients, mainly elderly living in within 80 km (50 miles) of Bucharest, are suffering from the West Nile virus, according to the statement issued in Geneva.There is no specific drug treatment for the virus, which causes fever and

9414 France offered on Tuesday to pay farmers to let calves be slaughtered and made into animal feed in a scheme to prop up markets hit by the mad cow crisis and overproduction of beef."This is one of the first measures to control production of beef and thereby contribute to bringing
9414 markets back into balance," the Agriculture Ministry said, euphemistically calling the slaughter a "transformation process".A statement said farmers would be paid 798.5 francs ($156) for each calf up to 20 days old they decided to have "transformed". Slaughtered calves would end up as feed for other farm animals such as
9414 pigs and chickens, officials said.The French meat office OFIVAL said France was the third European Union nation, after Britain and Portugal, to introduce such a slaughter, removing the calves from markets for human consumption.The agriculture ministry says it is illegal to feed the slaughtered calves' meat to cows and other
9414 ruminants, but it is allowed in the case of omnivores.France was the first foreign country to ban imports of British beef in March after London said there might be a link between mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) and its human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease (CJD).Britain is by far
9414 the nation hardest hit by mad cow disease.But beef consumption fell sharply around the world after the announcement.OFIVAL, in charge of carrying out the slaughter, said the measures were mainly aimed at cutting the numbers of male calves born of dairy cows.The ministry set no limit on the size of
9414 the slaughter. France has an estimated four million dairy cows and more than four million calves. ($1=5.1330 francs)</

9433 President Bill Clinton on Tuesday signed a landmark treaty that bans all nuclear testing and called on the global community to get tougher on terrorists and drug traffickers.Using the 51st session of the U.N. General Assembly to sketch out his U.S. election-year vision of global security and prosperity, Clinton said
9433 nations needed to cooperate against terrorism and illegal drugs because no country was immune from these menaces."Last year, I asked the nations assembled here to commit to a goal of zero tolerance for agresssion, terrorism and lawless behaviour. Frankly, we haven't done that yet," he said."Real zero tolerance means giving
9433 no aid and no quarter to terrorists who slaughter the innocent and drug traffickers who poison our children and to do everything we can to prevent weapons of mass destruction from falling into the wrong hands."In a move that highlighted his determination to combat drugs, and that could help blunt
9433 Republican charges that he is weak on the issue, Clinton said he would provide "more than $100 million worth of defence equipment, services and training" to help America's southern neighbours fight drugs.The White House said he had notified Congress on Sept. 14 and that the money would provide helicopters, patrol
9433 boats and other equipment to Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela and other countries.Clinton addressed the U.N. delegates after making the United States the first signatory of the new Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), which is designed to end nuclear explosions in the atmosphere, underground or anywhere else.He signed the pact, which
9433 is expected to face a tough fight for ratification in the U.S. Senate next year, with the same pen President John Kennedy used to sign a limited test ban treaty in 1963."This Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty will help to prevent the nuclear powers from developing more advanced and more dangerous
9433 weapons. It will limit the ability of other states to acquire such devices themselves. It points us toward a century in which the roles and risks of nuclear weapons can be further reduced and ultimately eliminated," Clinton said."The CTBT is the shared work of hard negotiation. Some have complained that
9433 it does not mandate total nuclear disarmament by a date certain. I would say to them do not forsake the benefits of this achievement by ignoring the tremendous progress we have already made toward that goal."This was a veiled message to India, which exploded a nuclear device in 1974 and
9433 now vows to block the treaty from taking effect. India maintains the pact is flawed because it does not commit the nuclear powers to destroy their arsenals and allows them to develop more sophisticated means of testing without explosions.Clinton coupled his praise for the test ban treaty with a call
9433 for action on six follow-on arms control steps including implementing a chemical weapons treaty, freezing the production of nuclear bomb-making material, improving compliance with a biological weapons treaty and banning antipersonnel landmines.In doing so, he took an indirect swipe at Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, who two weeks ago abruptly
9433 withdrew his support for the chemical weapons treaty, dooming U.S. ratification this year."I deeply regret that the United States Senate has not yet voted on the convention, but I want to assure you and people throughout the world that I will not let this treaty die," Clinton told the delegates.His
9433 visit to U.N. headquarters was flavored by his vow to bar Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali from winning a second five-year term. The two posed for pictures soon after the president's arrival but the atmosphere was politely correct rather than warm and U.S. officials said there would be no compromise on the
9433 ouster move."Our biggest gripe against the secretary-general is, frankly, his lack of enthusiasm for reform. We don't feel that you should have a secretary-general of the U.N. going into the 21st century who has to dragged kicking and screaming into doing reform," Clinton aide Richard Clarke said.Clinton glossed over the
9433 controversy in his speech, saying only that his administration favoured "streamlining the bureaucracy and reining in the budget" of the United Nations and was committed to paying past-due U.S. financial obligations to the world body.</

9437 if it could not work as a business."None of us can perform any of these functions unless we are economically viable," he told a news conference.Kerstin Rinne, Vice-President of Sanoma Corporation in Finland, said the European Union's work on copyright in the developing information society had so far concentrated on

9437 availability and use of old material...before all economic risks are taken," it said."Many European publishers are thereforce discouraged from investing in new products and services, faced with the need to secure rights for everyday business development."The EPC and other publishing groups said the EU should take over the system used

9444 (72,000 sq yards) of floor space -- more than any European store outside Britain.Like almost no other store, KaDeWe has been a touchstone of Europe's reconstruction and renewal this century.In 1950, 180,000 people desperate to feel that they were putting the privations of World War Two and post-war reconstruction behind
9444 them came to see the store, which had been heavily bombed in the war, reopen its doors.Later they came to cherish it as a testament to the survival of West Berlin's capitalist oasis, surrounded by the grey Berlin Wall and marooned inside communist territory.And the Department Store of the West
9444 really did epitomise the riches of the West for many East Germans, too.With its steel-and-glass elegance and dizzying array of fashion, gourmet delicacies and household appliances, the store was the first place many East Berliners wanted to visit when their communist system collapsed in 1989."It is surely not too much
9444 to say that KaDeWe is a symbol of Berlin," said Karl-Heinz Schmidt, board member of KaDeWe's parent company Karstadt, at the store's opening reception."We've been coming here since we were children," said Marianne Mueller, 67, visiting KaDeWe with her husband Juergen, 69. "It was always an experience and every time
9444 I'm here, I feel like Berlin has the flair of a world city again."Reiner and Margot Schmidt, visiting the women's coats department, came from Dortmund to attend the reopening."We come to KaDeWe every time we are in Berlin, it's a tradition," said Margot. "You can feel the sense of nostalgia
9444 for the old Berlin when you're in this place. But it's even more beautiful today."The new store has moved with the times, giving itself modern trappings almost unheard-of in Germany like a free day-care centre complete with beepers for shopping parents and a restaurant with a non-smoking section.Karstadt is predicting
9444 the store's annual sales will leap 400 million marks ($270 million) to around a billion marks ($670 million in the next four years.</

9451 European Union farm ministers called for a package of urgent measures worth one billion Ecus to aid farmers hit by the mad cow crisis and to help restore consumer confidence.The package includes increasing and extending the scope of beef intervention purchases, calf slaughter and other production-reducing schemes, advancing aid payments,
9451 meat labelling, identification and promotion schemes."We are trying to come forward with the best possible solution," Irish Farm Minister Ivan Yates told a news conference after a three-day informal meeting.EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler warned that the funding of the new aid plans, which supplement an earlier 850 million Ecus
9451 package of emergency measures finalised at an EU summit in Florence in June, still had to be sorted out."We are going to have to talk an awful lot yet about how to fund the package," Fischler said.Yates, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said that member states were against
9451 the cost being financed by cuts in other sectors. He was referring to a Commission proposal for a seven percent cut in aid payments to cereals farmers.Giving details of the new package, Yates said a political agreement had been reached to ensure adequate amounts of surplus beef would be taken
9451 into intervention stores in October and at the first tender in November.Commission officials estimated around 100,000 tonnes of beef would be sold into storage during this period.An extension of intervention buying was needed because a 400,000 tonnes limit for 1996 is expected to be breached in early October and ministers
9451 don't meet again until the end of next month.Beef stocks were virtually non-existent before the mad cow crisis erupted in March when Britain said that Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) could be passed to humans who ate infected beef."If intervention hadn't been extended prices would have collapsed," said a Commission official
9451 noting that October is a critical month as farmers try to sell their herds after summer outdoor fattening.The Commission had proposed raising the intervention ceiling to 720,000 tonnes in 1996 but this was opposed by some member states, notably Germany, which argued that this was an expensive and inefficient way
9451 of reducing production.Intervention buying is also being extended to include young cattle of between seven and nine months as a medium term step to curb beef production.These two new intervention measures are due to be formally adopted in October.Ministers are due to decide at the end of October whether further
9451 measures to cut beef output, such as an EU-wide calf slaughtering scheme and reduction of carcase weights eligible for public storage, are cost-effective and controllable.At present only Britain and Portugal operate calf culling schemes.Ministers also backed bringing forward up to 500 million Ecus of 1997 beef and suckler cow aid
9451 payments into the current financial year ending on October 15, thus easing farmers severe cash flow problems.In order to help revive beef demand, which has plunged by up to 40 percent in some countries, Fischler is due to propose an Wednesday an EU meat labelling and identification scheme which will
9451 show consumers where beef came from and how it was produced.A 10-million-Ecus a year beef promotion scheme is also due to be substantially expanded in a bid to restore sales in both the EU single market and in non-EU countries.</

9461 United States, because of Emmerich's German roots."There was an enormous amount of media hype in advance about the film and especially Emmerich so it seemed a good bet that 'Independence Day' would break a lot of records," said Monica Herrin of the association of German film distributors.She said "Independence Day's"
9461 start had beaten "Jurassic Park" by nearly four million marks and it seemed likely to surpass the 90-million-mark cumulative German gross for the 1993 Steven Spielberg film."Independence Day" is a science-fiction action film about an invasion of aliens who launch a coordinated attack from enormous space ships and destroy cities

9470 Kosmo on tackling Russian military pollution in the Arctic."I have never met my new Russian colleague," Kosmo told the Norwegian news agency NTB. 9470 a closely guarded hotel in the picturesque west coast town of Bergen.Western allies accept that a force will have to stay to prevent conflict and give last year's Dayton peace accords time to take root, but its size, make-up and mandate have yet to be agreed. The issue is sensitive
9470 in the United States where presidential elections take place on November 5.President Bill Clinton originally promised that U.S. troops would be in Bosnia no longer than the current mandate for the 55,000-strong force. 9470 the country. Even with NATO mounting a big security operation, few refugees took the risk of crossing ethnic boundaries to vote in their former homes.Former Warsaw Pact states, such as Poland and Hungary, want to remain and see close cooperation in the new force as a way of strengthening their

9484 to the 13-party minority coalition."This is a decision taken under Narasimha Rao's leadership, and I agree we have to help all the forces fighting communalism," Kesri told a news conference.He was referring to the alliance linking Congress and the United Front against the rightist Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP),
9484 which in general elections in April and May emerged as the single largest party in parliament.The BJP held power for 11 days in May, but lacking an outright majority, had to step down in favour of the centre-left United Front, which had the outside backing of Congress.Rao quit as party
9484 leader on Saturday after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in a $100,000 criminal conspiracy case.His abrupt departure sent shivers through the financial markets, which were concerned that turmoil in Congress might upset the ruling balance.But Kesri's comments appeared to put those worries to rest
9484 and indicate he would pursue the policies of Rao, who as prime minister opened India's economy to foreign trade and investment."One can't distinguish me from Mr Rao," the United News of India quoted Kesri as saying.Analysts said the change in Congress leaders was not expected to affect the new government's
9484 open-market economic policies, which have been welcomed by foreign investors.Kesri said his priority would be to unify Congress, which has been hobbled by internal squabbling and splits.He also pledged to battle corruption. "I will fight corruption whole heartedly," he said.Seven of Rao's ministers quit earlier this year after being linked
9484 to a bribery scandal, and former communications minister Sukh Ram was arrested last week following the discovery of more than $1 million in cash in two of his homes.The party's top decision-making body reached into the past to choose Kesri, a freedom fighter during the independence movement, as interim leader.Kesri,
9484 who has served as Congress treasurer for 18 years, drew broad but not unequivocal support to take over the reins until the fractious party's plenary body meets to select a more permanent leader.The date of that meeting has not been set, but it was agreed that the party should await
9484 the outcome of assembly elections in India's most populous state Uttar Pradesh, which start next Monday and end on October 7.Kesri boasted the advantage of having links to Congress's heyday when it dominated the political stage. 9486 India's sickly Congress party has tapped a disciple of Mahatma Gandhi as stop-gap chief, but a fierce struggle now looms as the nation's oldest party looks for a leader to take it into the 21st century.The party's top decision-making body reached into the past to choose Sitaram Kesri, 80, a
9486 former freedom fighter during the independence movement, as interim leader on Monday to replace former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.Rao quit abruptly on Saturday after a judge ordered him to appear him in court in a $100,000 criminal conspiracy case.Kesri, who has served as Congress treasurer for 18 years, drew
9486 broad but not unequivocal support to take over the reins until the fractious party's plenary body meets to select a more permanent leader.The date of that meeting has not been set, but it was agreed that the party should await the outcome of assembly elections in India's most populous state
9486 Uttar Pradesh, which start next Monday and end on October 7.Kesri boasted the advantage of having links to Congress's heyday when it dominated the political stage. He also commands the confidence of Rao and his loyalists.Asked what his first priority would be, Kesri said he would "carry on the message
9486 of Mahatma Gandhi to wipe out tears from the eyes of the downtrodden, the poor and the oppressed."On Tuesday, Kesri said he would focus on healing Congress's deep divisions. "I will leave no stone unturned to bring about Congress unity," the Press Trust of India quoted him as saying.As a
9486 low-caste Hindu, Kesri stands out within an organisation that has traditionally been led by the Brahmin elite.He takes over just before elections in Uttar Pradesh, where Congress is pinning its hopes on an unprecedented alliance with a low-caste regional party.Congress, intended since its creation in 1885 as an over-arching organisation
9486 with a national reach, has seen its influence wane in recent years as new parties reflecting caste and regional interests sprouted.Kesri was described by The Pioneer newspaper as "a drawing room political fund raiser," reflecting his power as a party insider without an electoral base.The octogenarian with a history of
9486 heart trouble was only expected to tide over the party until a more permanent successor is chosen.Rival contenders were expected to put up a fierce fight.The Hindustan Times said Congress had reached an "uneasy consensus" in tapping Kesri as a compromise candidate.The Press Trust of India said that a "visibly
9486 agitated Rajesh Pilot," who was environment minister under Rao, had pointedly noted that the choice of Kesri was not unanimous.Pilot, 51, a member of Congress who is widely known to be interested in the leadership post, left "his stamp of dissent" at the meeting, The Asian Age said."This is his
9486 (Pilot's) style of functioning," Kesri said on Tuesday. "I am pained that Mr Pilot stood isloated in yesterday's meeting."</

9488 Sri Lankan forces halted a push into Tamil Tiger rebels' northern stronghold on Tuesday in the face of fierce guerrilla resistance, as Western aid workers reported the first civilian casualties in the fighting."The LTTE's resistance is very heavy," said a military officer at the Defence Ministry's Operational Headquarters. He was
9488 referring to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils."We are consolidating our defences, and the offensive is not going on at the moment," he told Reuters.The military, making its first major push against the guerrillas in more than a month, reported
9488 dominating an area near the town of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.But the military officer, who asked not to be named, said the troops, supported by air force bombers, artillery and tanks, were still several miles away from Kilinochchi.Defence analysts said government
9488 troops tried to outflank the rebels, who were well dug in at Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.A military spokesman said security forces killed 35 guerrillas and wounded 100 more in Monday's fighting, in which 15 soldiers were also killed and 21 wounded.This brings the army's death toll
9488 to 37 and the number of wounded to 79 in the first two days of the renewed operation."Army casualties are pretty high. This means the LTTE is fighting back very strongly," an Asian diplomat said.A spokeswoman for a Western aid team in the Wanni said a few civilians displaced by
9488 the fighting had arrived at an aid centre at Mallavi, southwest of Kilinochchi."A small number of people came in tractors and trailers," said Frances Stevenson of Medecins Sans Frontieres.She told Reuters nine people with blast wounds were admitted to a medical facility at Akkarayan, about 15 km (nine miles) from
9488 Kilinochchi.The army has said it wants to reopen the highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through a large swathe of rebel-held territory separating Jaffna and the mainland.An army major said the military suffered more casualties overnight in a guerrilla counter-attack on ground troops digging in south of the road
9488 junction town of Paranthan.Paranthan is between Kilinochchi and the Elephant Pass at the neck of the northernmost Jaffna peninsula, which was recaptured by the army from the rebels in April.The military spokesman said government troops either killed or wounded more than 200 rebels on Sunday.The LTTE questioned the military claim.
9488 The LTTE's Voice of Tigers Radio said only 13 of its fighters were killed on Sunday and two more on Monday. "The Tigers are fighting fiercely against the forces," it said.It was not possible to verify the conflicting claims as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.The
9488 military spokesman said air force Mi-24 helicopters and naval craft sank 10 rebel boats south of Vettilaikerni on the northeast coast in a separate clash, but Tiger casualties were not known.The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing
9488 almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.</

9502 Aiming to bring more order to the global market for pepper and other spices, the International Spice Group plans to launch a pepper futures exchange, the first of its kind for spices, an official said Tuesday.The exchange, to be set up in January in Cochin in southern India, will help
9502 hedge options for traders of pepper, the most widely used spice, said Fazli Husain, senior commodity marketing officer of the U.N.-backed International Trade Centre.He said the new exchange would make the international pepper market less volatile.Black pepper, which accounts for about 30 percent of all spices traded in the world,
9502 determines the value of the global spice market, which was around $2 billion last year."In the early part of this decade when the price of pepper was low, the spice market was less than $1.5 billion. The market is at today's high levels because of high pepper prices," he said.The
9502 spice group was set up in the late 1970s and supported by the Commonwealth Secretariat and the International Trade Centre. It aims to help spice-producing countries achieve sustainable growth.Husain was among some 40 overseas delegates at a symposium in Colombo this week to discuss ways to boost spice exports.India is
9502 the world's biggest spice exporter, having produced one-quarter of the 450,000 tons of spices sold in the international market last year, he said.With the exception of Brazil, the most important spice producing nations are in Asia, with India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam the most prolific producers.The United States, the
9502 largest market for spices, imported 262,743 metric tons worth $445.3 million in 1995 and European Union countries imported 195,801 tons worth $444.4 million.Husain said the main concern for the importing countries is the quality. "Not one exporting country can claim at this stage that they are giving a clean and
9502 quality product," he said.Most complaints involve pesticide residue in spices, since developing countries tend to overuse pesticides to maximize production, Husain said.Among the principal spices traded globally are pepper, paprika, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, tumeric and nutmeg."It is a growth market," Husain said. "For as long as people continue to appreciate
9502 food, there will be a growing demand for spices."</

9530 Bangladesh has the highest lead pollution in the world for part of the year, scientists at the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission (BAEC) said on Tuesday.A 17-month study by BAEC scientists detected 463 nanogram (billionth of a gram) of lead, per metre of air over Dhaka during the dry months (November-January)."Bangladesh
9530 has the highest lead pollution in world -- the figure appears to be the world's highest against 383 nanogram in Mexico city and 360 in Bombay," said BAEC's chief scientific officer, Dr. Mohammad Khaliquzzaman, who led the survey."It's alarming. Higher levels of lead are dangerous for child health", said Khaliquzzaman,
9530 who blamed the problem largely on the use of leaded fuel.In Bangladesh, all vehicles use leaded fuel because the country's only refinery is not able to produce lead-free fuel, he said.However, he said, the concentration of lead drops as the rainfall increases after the dry season."It comes down to 253
9530 nanograms during the medium railfall period (February-May) and to 160 nanograms in the peak rainy months (June-August)," Khaliquzzaman told Reuters.BAEC scientists said lead can penetrate into the lungs and subsequently into the blood. The heavy metal can also cause intellectual impairment in children,"Lead can severely impair intelligence of children, can
9530 cause respiratory problems and annemia," said doctor Mizanur Rahman, a paediatrist in Dahaka's Post Graduate Medicine and Research Hospital.Scientists and public health officials are also battling deadly water pollution in parts of Bangladesh.Up to 15 people have died in recent months in the country's southern districts due to poisoning by
9530 the high content of arsenic in sub-soil water.Authorities have hurriedly sealed many wells after water they pumped out tested "arsenic positive," doctors in the worst-affected districts said.Dr. Fazlul Huq, a civil surgeon, said patients attacked by arsenic poisoning suffered "chronic skin rashes and deteriorating health.""So far, no one seemed sure
9530 about what has led to the heavy arsenic concentration," he told reporters."The battle is on, but winning it is not that easy," said one official at the government's public health depeartment.One scientist said diarrhoea caused by polluted water was perhaps the biggest child killer in Bangladesh.</

9540 The International Spice Group plans to launch a pepper futures exchange, the first of its kind for spices, to better control the global pepper market, an official of the group said on Tuesday.The exchange, to be set up in January in Cochin in southern India, will help hedge options for
9540 traders of pepper, the most widely used spice, said Fazli Husain, senior commodity marketing officer of the U.N.-backed International Trade Centre.Husain, an advisor for the Spice Group, told Reuters that the new exchange would make the international pepper market less volatile.Husain said black pepper, which amounts to about 30 percent
9540 of all spices traded in the world, determines the value of the global spice market, which was around $2 billion last year."In the early part of this decade when the price of pepper was low, the spice market was less than $1.5 billion. The market is at today's high levels
9540 because of high pepper prices," he said.India is the world's biggest spice exporter, having sold one quarter of the 450,000 tonnes of spices sold in the international market last year, he said.Husain is among some 40 overseas delegates from 20 countries who are taking part in a symposium in Colombo
9540 this week to work out ways to boost spice exports.The group, set up in the late 1970s and supported by the Commonwealth Secretariat and the International Trade Centre, plans to assist spice producing countries to achieve sustainable growth as its priority, officials said.With the exception of Brazil, the most important
9540 spice producing nations are in Asia, with India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam being the most prolific producers and exporters.The United States, the world's largest market for spices, imported 262,743 tonnes worth $445.3 million in 1995. European Union countries jointly imported 195,801 tonnes worth $444.4 million last year, spice officals
9540 said.Husain said the main concern for the importing countries was the commodities' quality."Not one exporting country can claim at this stage they are giving a clean and quality product," he said.A majority of complaints were regarding pesticide residue in spices, arising from a developing countries' farming practice of using too
9540 much pesticide to maximise production, he said."We're imparting knowledge on using quality control from start to finish. To get producers to use less pesticide, to start using cleaning machines and to lab-test samples."He said producers had to pay attention to these factors if they wanted to carve a bigger slice
9540 of a growing spice market."It is a growth market," Husain said. "For as long as people continue to appreciate food, there will be a growing demand for spices."Among the principal spices traded globally today are pepper, paprika, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, tumeric and nutmeg.</

9578 Consumer confidence in the economy held steady at a six-year high in September, a private research group said Tuesday, and the optimism is expected to extend into the holiday season.The Conference Board said its index of consumer confidence was at 111.8 in September, little changed from a revised reading of
9578 112.0 in August.The New York-based private research business group said its expectations component index rose in September to 100.4 from a revised 100.3 in the previous month.The survey showed consumers are "quite optimistic about the next six months," said Lynn Franco, associate director of the board's Consumer Research Centre."With consumers
9578 in high spirits, the outlook for holiday spending appears to be bright," she said."After remaining flat over the last year, consumer confidence broke out in July and is currently holding at a six-year high," Franco said.However, analysts said the report had little if any impact on financial markets because it
9578 was overshadowed by the meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee.The Fed panel, which met for 4-1/2 hours, decided to leave interest rates steady.Wall Street's reaction was mixed. After surging in the immediate wake of the Fed announcement, stocks later fell back. The Dow Jones industrial average
9578 closed 20.71 points lower at 5,874.Bond prices gained, with the pace-setting 30-year Treasury issue jumping nearly a half point, pushing the yield down to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent Monday.The Consumer Confidence Survey, which is based on a sampling of 5,000 households, found that the proportion of respondents who felt
9578 that jobs were "hard to get" dropped to 21 percent in September from 22 percent in August.About 27 percent of consumers say business conditions are "good," off moderately from 28.5 percent in August.The group said the percentage of respondents who expect business conditions to improve moved up to 17.3 percent
9578 from 16.1 percent.In addition to posting the national measures, the survey showed that regional confidence improved dramatically in New England, having jumped by 24 percent over the past three months. Confidence levels there had been "in the doldrums since early 1990," the Board said.The East South Central region -- including
9578 Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama and Mississippi -- was the only area to report a decline in confidence over the past three months, dropping about 1.0 percent, it said.</
9579 Germany's largest industrial giant Daimler-Benz on Tuesday stepped to the forefront in implementing controversial new legislation to cut sick pay for employees to 80 percent from October 1.But Karl Feuerstein, the chairman of the firm's works council, told German ARD television that workers would fight the decision by refusing to
9579 work overtime and weekends.Feuerstein joined unions and some leading politicians who said companies like Daimler have no right to make such a cutback, and the bill passed by parliament earlier this month was not meant to apply to existing contracts, only future ones.But Daimler and other industrial leaders have taken
9579 a sharply different view and intend to use the legislation, part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Programme for More Jobs and Growth, to reopen talks with unions about how to cut costs."Wage contracts are not against this," Daimler said in a statement. "They are built on a legal basis which was
9579 changed as a result of this new law."Union leaders are certain to react strongly to Daimler's decision, which could encourage other leading German firms to follow suit, leading to wholesale attempts to rewrite employee contracts concerning sick pay.Daimler, which links the cutbacks with its ability to remain competitive in international
9579 markets, said it will now negotiate with its union on reducing the sick pay package, but would not say what would happen if no agreement was reached.Earlier in the day a worried Kohl called on employers and unions to avoid escalating the fight over sick pay and said the two
9579 should resolve their differences in negotiations.The sick pay law, introduced earlier this month, allows employers to pay 80 percent of wages on days when employees are off sick rather than the previous 100 percent. Sick pay in Germany currently totals 60 billion marks ($40 billion) a year.Some employers have already
9579 cancelled contracts and said they aim to move immediately to reduce sick pay.At the centre of the debate is the issue of whether the government's sick pay laws are meant to apply to existing contracts or only future ones.German Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, along with Kohl, has so far sided
9579 with workers to some extent, warning employers who hope to reduce sick pay to abide by existing contracts until they expire.But Hans Peter Stihl, president of the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce, said employers now had a firm legal basis to cut sick pay."The current contract regulations are sufficient
9579 to implement the cuts in sick pay," Stihl told a German newspaper over the weekend. Unions will probably seek court rulings, which could drag the matter out, he said.Faced with huge cutbacks in benefits, employees are preparing to take industrial action. The IG Metall union has called for labour action
9579 on October 10 to protest against moves by companies to cut sick pay."We are not looking to strike, but we will strike if forced to," said IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel at the weekend. (1=1.5124 Mark)</

9581 be as much as 10 percent below Wall Street estimates and that the pressure would continue for the rest of the year.The news sparked a sell-off in the company's stock, which is the most widely held in North America.AT&amp;T fell $5.75 to $51.50 after a delayed opening on the New
9581 York Stock Exchange, and more than 15 million shares had changed hands by the closing bell.Chairman Robert Allen said in a statement that AT&amp;T's third-quarter results appeared to be as much as 10 percent below analysts' mean estimate of 92 cents a share and that the fourth quarter will likely
9581 fall short of the mean estimate of 89 cents a share.In the second quarter, AT&amp;T earned $1.49 billion, or 92 cents a share, on revenues of $13 billion.Allen also said the company's earnings were being affected by its investments in local, on-line and wireless services as well as infrastucture to
9581 provide new communications and information services."Further, we currently believe that competitive pressures will continue for the remainder of the year, and we are intensifying our marketing efforts," Allen said.He said the company had been hurt by competition from other long-distance telephone companies."While we have succeeded in stabilising volumes and revenues
9581 at last quarter's levels, the number of customers moving between carriers is still disturbing," he said."Our research indicates that this customer volatility is due largely to price misperceptions that are frequently promoted by some competitors."In a conference call with analysts and reporters, Richard Miller, AT&amp;T chief financial officer, said the
9581 company was "taking more aggressive action on sales and marketing."Allen added, "We're greatly accelerating our expenditures."The announcement of a drop in earnings comes as AT&amp;T finishes splitting itself up in a massive restructuring.AT&amp;T will complete the spin-off of its Lucent Technologies Inc. telecommunications equipment subsidiary on Sept. 30. AT&amp;T is
9581 also spinning off its NCR Corp. computer unit.As part of the restructuring, AT&amp;T also is making a major reduction in its workforce. Allen said that reduction was "on track" and would lead to about 17,000 job cuts.Industry analysts at several Wall Street brokerages lowered their ratings on AT&amp;T as a
9581 result of the news."Mother Bell has been a sacred cow until now. This type of news is going to be disquieting," said Fahnestock &amp; Co. market analyst Alan Ackerman. "It's likely to put a lot of pressure on the stock and ruffle the feathers of many shareholders."In a separate announcement
9581 Tuesday, the company took aim at competitors with a new long-distance calling plan that would give consumers the option of a flat calling rate of 15 cents a minute at any time to anywhere in the United States.In response to AT&amp;T's statement, Sprint, a key competitor in the long-distance market,
9581 said it was gaining market share and had not suffered any similar setback to its results.Sprint, which advertises its long distance rate as 10 cents a minute, said its long-distance consumer business grew at a rate three times faster than AT&amp;T's consumer business during the first half of this year."Thus
9581 far through the third quarter of 1996, Sprint is seeing the simplicity of it's dime-a-minute message continue to drive record sales," the company said.</
9582 Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, was convicted on Tuesday on all but one count of illegally giving gifts and favours to then Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.The agricultural firm was also convicted of taking part in a scheme to funnel illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry
9582 and of two charges of wire fraud.The convictions -- the first to come out of the government's two-year investigation of the former Clinton cabinet member -- could have serious implications for pending cases in the probe and do not bode well for Espy and others still under investigation, legal experts
9582 said."Today's verdict reflects that juries are tired of what they regard as corruption in big business and government and it will give steam to the prosecutor's efforts to proceed further against other people in this matter," University of Georgetown law professor Paul Rothstein said."This gives our investigation some impetus," Independent
9582 Counsel Donald Smaltz, who is heading the widespread probe, told reporters after the verdict was announced. "Each case will be judged on its own merit ... but this should send a strong signal," he said.Sun-Diamond, whose affiliates include Sun Maid raisins, Sunsweet prunes and Diamond Walnut, had been charged with
9582 violating nine criminal counts involving illegal gratuities and illegal campaign contributions to Espy and his brother in 1993 and 1994 while Espy headed the huge agriculture agency.He resigned as a cabinet secretary in 1994 amid a swirl of accusations that he had taken illegal gifts and favours from companies his
9582 agency was charged to regulate.After deliberating for 9-1/2 hours over two days a jury found Sun-Diamond not guilty of only one of the counts, which alleged that the cooperative had paid transportation costs for Espy's girlfriend to accompany him to a conference in Greece.The government said the company, acting through
9582 its Washington lobbyist Richard Douglas, a close personal friend of Espy, used the enticements of expensive gifts and favours to Espy and his girlfriend and campaign contributions to Henry Espy to try to sway Espy on important issues.Sun-Diamond attorney Richard Hibey said the company was innocent of any wrongdoing and
9582 that the gifts, which included lavish meals, a luggage set and a weekend outing to the U.S. Tennis Open tournament in 1993, reflected the close friendship between Douglas and Espy, and nothing more. He told reporters he would recommend that Sun-Diamond appeal the conviction.Legal sources said the verdict was an
9582 important victory for prosectors, who had been accused of over-reaching their authority and of investigating relatively insignificant discretions."This is a very substantial victory for the independent counsel," said former U.S. prosecutor Joseph di Genova. "This obviously gives validation to his efforts.So far the investigation has yielded five sets of criminal
9582 indictments and charges against more than a dozen individuals and concerns including the Washington lobbyist for Tyson Foods, the huge Arkansas-based chicken processor whose chairman has long had close ties with President Bill Clinton, a former governor of Arkansas.Tyson Foods has been a focus of the Espy investigation since the
9582 start after it was learned the firm gave Espy and his girlfriend tickets to Super Bowl playoffs in 1993 and a scholarship potentially worth almost $10,000 to the girlfriend.</
9583 Stock prices soared briefly Tuesday after the Federal Reserve decided to keep interest rates steady, but the market quickly retreated as investors assessed the implications of the central bank's move.Bonds also jumped at first before surrendering some of their gains, but the dollar drew sustained selling pressure.Shortly after 3:40 p.m.
9583 EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 40.69 points at 5,854.06 after initially gaining 35 points on the Fed's decision.The decision surprised some Wall Street analysts who had expected the central bank to raise rates for the first time in 1-1/2 years. Prior to the Fed's decision, the Dow
9583 index had hovered around unchanged."I am actually very dissapointed that the Fed didn't take a golden opportunity to nudge rates up," said Graham Tanaka, President of Tanaka Capital Management. "On a pre-emptive basis it would have been a conservative route to take."In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was
9583 up 12/32 after initially rising nearly half a point, and its yield fell to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent at Monday's close.Analysts said the stock market had already priced in a quarter-point rise in interest rates. Tuesday's declines came a day after the Dow set a closing record of 5,894.74.The
9583 Fed's decision, which had been anxiously awaited on Wall Street left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent.The central bank also held the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, at 5 percent."The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended at
9583 1:40 p.m. (1740 GMT)," central bank spokesman Joseph Coyne said. "There is no further announcement."The bland statement hid what analysts believed was one of the more contentious meetings of the policy-making committee. Anti-inflation hawks at the Fed, particularly at its regional banks, have made no secret of their desire for
9583 higher rates to cool off the economy and head off inflation.Out of 55 economists surveyed in a Reuters poll, 31 had expected the Fed to hike rates on Tuesday. Some analysts said the Fed move was justified by a lack of inflationary pressures.Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line
9583 Asset Management said, "We believe the Fed's action to leave rates unchanged is fully justified given the complete absence of inflation and a noted deceleration in economic activity during the quarter to date."Meanwhile, the dollar plunged, trading at 1.5020 German marks, down from 1.5125 marks on Monday. The currency fell
9583 to 109.20 Japanese yen vs. 109.89 yen.Currency traders said the Fed's decision to hold monetary policy steady might not inflict long-term damage to the dollar because short-term interest rates were likely to head higher before the end of the year."To me the handwriting is on the wall," said Sung Won
9583 Sohn, chief economist and senior vice president at Norwest Corp. "It's a question of when (a rate hike) comes, not if it will come."The upbeat dollar outlook was due to a belief that the central bank remained hawkish on inflation regardless of Tuesday's decision on rates, analysts said."I still believe
9583 they prefer to act early on the rate side if they have to and there will be enough of them that they'll have a consensus, I would believe, before the year is out," said Michael Faust, foreign exchange manager at Bailard, Biehl &amp; Kaiser.</
9584 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe Federal Reserve on Tuesday left interest rates unchanged at a policy meeting closely watched by world financial markets.The decision, which had been anxiously awaited on Wall Street and at the White House, left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight
9584 loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent. It also left the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, unchanged at 5 percent."The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended at 1:40 p.m. (1740 GMT)," central bank spokesman Joseph Coyne said. "There is no further announcement."The bland statement hid what analysts believed was one
9584 of the more contentious meetings of the Fed's policy-making committee.Anti-inflation hawks at the Fed, particularly at its regional banks, have made no secret of their desire for higher rates to cool off the economy and keep inflation at bay.Tuesday's decision was good news for President Bill Clinton, who has been
9584 counting on a trouble-free economy in the approach to the Nov. 5 election to help him win a second, four-year term.Clinton said he thought the decision to leave interest rates unchanged showed that the economy was strong with no signs of inflation."I just think it shows we've got a strong
9584 economy with no inflation. I'm glad about that," Clinton said during a campaign visit to New Jersey.Many analysts still expect the Fed to raise interest rates sometime in the coming months, possibly at its next policy meeting on Nov. 13 -- eight days after the election.Central bank policy-makers were faced
9584 with conflicting evidence on the state of the economy when they met on Tuesday.By opting not to raise rates now, the Fed is hoping that economic growth will slow enough on its own to head off the risk of higher inflation, analysts said.In the words of Fed Gov. Janet Yellen,
9584 the economy is operating in an "inflationary danger zone." But so far, there is no clear sign of higher inflation.At 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at its lowest point in more than seven years and at a level that in the past has often led to stepped-up wage demands
9584 and higher inflation.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far, companies have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Much will depend on the future course of the economy.In the second quarter, the economy grew at a
9584 4.8 percent clip -- its fastest pace in two years and about twice the rate most analysts reckon is sustainable on a long-term basis without fanning inflation.Growth has shown signs of slowing since then. Consumer spending, which accounts for about two-thirds of economic activity, has slowed.But with consumer confidence steady
9584 at about a six-year high, labour markets tight and wages rising, some analysts and Fed anti-inflation hawks question whether the developing slowdown will be enough to keep price pressures in check.The central bank was under considerable political pressure not to raise rates Tuesday, six weeks ahead of the election.Seventy-eight lawmakers
9584 -- all but two of them Democrats -- wrote to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan on Monday contending that a rate rise now would hurt, not help the economy.Clinton administration officials have argued that inflation remained quiescent, strongly implying that they saw no need for the independent central bank to raise

9585 yesterday. The heating season has commenced," said Rothman."Refinery runs start falling off very hard beginning this week. 9585 of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and the market could have used the 700,000-800,000 bpd of Iraqi oil under the now delayed U.N. oil-for-food deal.World crude prices rallied to a post-Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel 10 days ago after the United States fired cruise missiles at Iraqi targets after

9585 nearly $5 a barrel more expensive than this time last year -- is bringing windfall revenues to OPEC despite quota busting by some members.OPEC's quota compliance committee is meeting in Vienna on Wednesday but OPEC sources say little will be done to deal with overproduction as oil prices remain strong

9588 the dollar and higher local interest rates tend to strengthen a currency, investors fled into the Japanese yen and European currencies immediately after the FOMC announced its decision Tuesday afternoon."It was a knee-jerk reaction to a slightly unexpected situation," said Robert Nelson, managing director of foreign exchange sales at Westdeutsche
9588 Landesbank Girozentrale. 9588 fell to 1.2255 Swiss francs from 1.2360, but rose to Canadian $1.3673 from C$1.3667.The dollar had spent the overnight session trapped in narrow trading ranges as market players delayed investment decisions ahead of the FOMC meeting.Some dealers blamed politics for delaying a much-needed interest rate increase, with the pressure of
9588 presidential and congressional elections only six weeks away seen persuading Fed officials to bide their time."The market needed to feel like 25 basis points (added to the current fed funds rate at 5.25 percent) was in and the Fed would do it in front of the election. Now the dollar
9588 looks a little bit soft," said Mark Gargano, managing director for foreign exchange at First Union National Bank.The dollar touched the 1.50-marks level late Tuesday and dealers expected the losses to end either at or just below that key technical level for now.But with some economists predicting the Fed will
9588 keep steady interest rates through the remainder of 1996, investors could continue to sell dollars in coming sessions."The dollar could be coming down a little more," Gargano said. 9592 The Bank of Israel Tuesday announced a 0.3 percentage point reduction in its key lending rate for October but the business sector said a sharper cut was needed to put the economy back on track.The rate cut, the third in as many months, will bring the key lending rate to
9592 an annualized 15.5 percent. Israeli banks followed suit, lowering their prime rates to 17.0 percent.The Bank of Israel attributed its decision to the low consumer price indices in the past two months and a rate of expansion in money supply that is in line with expected growth.The president of the
9592 Manufacturers Association and the head of the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce said at least another two percentage points should be cut.They said the high interest rates could lead the economy to the "brink of a crisis" and called for a programme that would include a substantial interest rate
9592 reduction, a correction in the strong shekel and a cut in the government's budget.Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel said interest rates have declined 1.5 percentage points since August. He argued that a steeper cut would not be prudent given that the capital market's inflationary expectations for the coming 12
9592 months and forecasts for inflation in 1996 are above the government's target of 8-10 percent for this year.Private sector forecasts put 1996 inflation at 11 to 12 percent."It looks now that during 1996 inflation will exceed the level set by the government," Frenkel told Reuters."I believe a more significant reduction
9592 in interest rates would have been irresponsible. It would have fuelled inflation and would not contribute to the profitability of the business sector."Frenkel said the biggest problem facing Israel was the widening current account deficit in its balance of payments."The only effective way to deal with this gap is by
9592 cutting government expenditures," Frenkel said.</
9593 Convenience is becoming a big business in food-crazed Thailand, and Kentucky Fried Chicken said Tuesday it has reaped the benefits of changing Thai eating habits and growing disposable income.The Thai market is among the fastest growing in the world for KFC, with an average annual growth of about 40 percent
9593 a year, said Hester Chew, KFC country manager for Thailand and Indochina."The whole category of fast food (in Thailand) is growing at about 30 percent a year," Chew said in an interview. "In Thailand, we have 133 restaurants and we're heading towards 150 by December or January."KFC hopes to have
9593 300 outlets in Thailand by the turn of the century, and Chew said Thailand's long-term potential is for about 500 branches.With expected revenues of about $100 million in Thailand this year, KFC is the country's largest fast-food restaurant chain with about a 36 percent market share, Chew said.The second largest
9593 is McDonald's, which has 47 outlets based mainly in Bangkok, he said.Chew said the capital city is still KFC's main growth area, but the company has also been expanding rapidly in the provinces as more Thais get a taste for fried chicken and as the restaurant adds spicy menu items
9593 adapted to the Thai palate.Fast food popularity is growing in Thailand due to a combination of factors, Chew said."Young adults and teenagers have more disposable income and are associating more with Western lifestyles," he said. "There are also more double-income families."In a country where snack-happy Thais can get a wide
9593 variety of cheap and tasty foods at roadside stalls, KFC is working hard to get consumers."The whole notion is to create convenience," Chew said. He said KFC has experimented with home delivery, especially in traffic-clogged Bangkok, and also set up an outlet at a petrol filling station for those who
9593 want to get a quick bite on the road.KFC has focused its marketing efforts on the family market, launching a children's club and decorating its restaurants to be more family-oriented with playgrounds and toys."Eating out in a restaurant, especially for young families, is an experience," Chew said. "In the States,
9593 fast food is probably the cheapest form of food -- you buy it and take it home to eat."Contrary to Western markets, like the United States, most Asian consumers prefer to eat in fast food restaurants instead of drive through or buy takeout food, he said."In Thailand, about 70 percent
9593 of people dine in, compared to about 30 percent in the States," he said. "The average seating in a KFC restaurant in the States is about 50 seats, and here it averages 150 seats."Chew said KFC hopes to make Thailand the base for the Indochina market, which is still in

9595 venture between Sonatrach and Halliburton, to develop a 60,000 barrel per day (bpd) oilfield in Hassi Berkine-Sud.Sonatrach said the 21-month project was the first stage in a plan to develop the overall Hassi Berkine-Sud field which has a potential of one billion barrels of oil.
