9595 at 1.5 billion barrels.Sonatrach and Anadarko, linked by a production sharing deal, discovered the field in the southeastern basin of Ghadames, in the Sahara, where 34 of Algeria's 207 discoveries lie.Brown &amp; Root Condor would provide equipment and services to build an array of installations, including reinjection of miscible gas,
9595 Sonatrach said."The programme comprises, among others, a network pf pipework for five oil wells, one well to inject gas, a train to produce oil with a capacity of 60,000 barrels per day," the Sonatrach statement said.Sonatrach said Brown &amp; Root Condor would also build a pressurised gas station with a
9595 capacity of 2.69 million cubic metres, a pipeline to carry the oil, and a power station.Sonatrach said Anadarko would fund the project in which six Algerian companies would be associated as subcontractors.It said 40 percent of the project cost would be in the Algerian dinar local currency.Sonatrach said it planned
9595 a second stage of developing Hassi Berkine-Sud with the building of two additional modules and the generalisation of gas injection in the field, as well as the "setting up a peripheral water injection".Algeria crude production is expected to surge with the help of several new fields, pushing Algeria oil output
9595 to about one million bpd by the year 2000, up from its current OPEC quota of 750,000.Anadarko, Spanish CEPSA, Italian Agip Spa, Petro-Canada have discovered oil and gas wells in Algeria, mostly since the cash-poor North African country liberalised more its oil and gas legislation in 1991 to attract foreign

9597 Sweden's Riksbank Tuesday signalled its growing faith in the country's nascent economic recovery in an upbeat inflation report that coincided with the 20th cut this year in the bank's key interest rate.In its latest quarterly report on economic developments and monetary policy, the central bank said inflation in Sweden --
9597 now running at just 0.6 percent -- had been held firmly in check."The prospect of inflation during 1997, as well as in the first half of 1998, being in line with the 2 percent inflation target is good," the bank said.In fact, inflation was lower than envisaged in the bank's
9597 last report, which was published in June."This is primarily because the transitory effects of falling interest rates and import prices have been greater than expected," the Riksbank said, adding that economic developments had otherwise been in line with its previous assessments.With the threat of inflation firmly banished, the central bank
9597 said the way was clear for further cuts in its key interest rate, the repo rate.This was underlined just half an hour after the publication of the inflation report, when the bank trimmed the repo rate, which is its main monetary policy tool, by a further 10 basis points to
9597 5.05 percent in what was the 20th such move this year.The repo rate has fallen by almost four percentage points from 8.91 percent in January, while the Swedish crown has steadily appreciated against the German mark and the rate of inflation has continually fallen.The main cloud on the Swedish economic
9597 horizon has been growth, or lack of it, but the Riksbank said it was slightly more optimistic in this respect too."The economic slowdown toward the end of 1995 was brief, and there has been an upturn during 1996," the bank said."A total growth rate of 3 to 4 percent for
9597 1996 and 1997 combined is still considered most probable, although today the emphasis is in the upper half of this interval."</

9599 Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole branded President Bill Clinton on Tuesday as "an old-style, dyed-in-the-wool, big-spending liberal" who would raise taxes on families while Dole promised to cut them.In a speech before business people in the nation's auto capital, Dole combined an attack on his front-running opponent with a promotion
9599 of his own economic plan centred on tax cuts, including a 15 percent income tax rate cut, capital gains tax cuts and a $500 a child tax credit."The bottom line is under our plan, a family of four making $30,000 will save $1,261," Dole said. "To some people that doesn't
9599 sound like a lot of money. But this is designed for Main Street, not Wall Street."Dole, lagging by double digits in his uphill race against Clinton, spoke before several thousand people at the Economic Club of Detroit at Cobo Hall, the same complex area where Republican Ronald Reagan was nominated
9599 for president 16 years ago and later won election partly on a plan to cut taxes across the board 25 percent over three years.In pushing his tax-cut proposals, Dole was trying to put a spark into his economic plan that public opinion polls show has not caught fire with most
9599 voters just six weeks before the presidential election Nov. 5.But Dole did not spell out in any detail how he would pay for the $548 billion in tax cuts and still carry out his pledge to balance the budget by the year 2002.He suggested it could be done by stimulating
9599 economic growth and by cutting five cents out of every dollar in spending as well as selling government property.As he has for three days now, Dole portrayed Clinton as a liberal promoting conservative policies for the election but who would propose big spending programmes and taxes if elected.During Clinton's term,
9599 Dole said, he has proposed programmes that would cost some $2 trillion and tax increases."These are not the actions of a finger-in-the-wind politician," said Dole. "These are the actions of an old-styled, dyed-in-the-wool, big spending liberal committed to a government that spends and spend and taxes and taxes."He added, "These
9599 are the actions of someone who -- once the spotlight of the campaign has been turned off -- will take every opportunity to increase the size of government -- even as he decreases the size of your wallet."Clinton denied on Monday he is a "closet liberal" and pointed to his
9599 record going back to governor of Arkansas.But Dole contended Clinton has a "tax and spend agenda" and pointed to Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt's proposal for a sales tax on outdoor equipment for outdoor recreation areas."That's a new tax on sport-utility vehicles," Dole told his audience including auto executives. "I don't
9599 have to tell you here in Detroit what that means. That's a tax on some of your most popular lines -- the Ford Explorer, the Chevy Blazer and the Jeep Cherokee.""He (Clinton) wants families to pinch their pennies so government can spend more of their money," Dole said. "I want
9599 government to pinch its pennies so families won't have to."Dole countered Clinton's claim that Dole can't cut taxes and balance the budget."I reject the words 'it can't be done,'" said Dole who said it can be done and claimed "our plan protects vital programmes such as Medicare, Social Security and
9599 defence."Clinton holds solid leads in recent polls in Michigan and two other key states, Ohio and Missouri, that Dole has on his two-day travelling schedule and which Republicans need to win.</

9645 Eclipse Surgical Technologies Inc said on Tuesday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to start a Phase II trial of its transmyocardial revascularization procedure.The trial is using the procedure as an adjunct to bypass surgery.Transmyocardial revascularization, or TMR, is a surgical procedure performed on the beating
9645 heart, in which a laser device is used to create pathways through the heart muscle directly into the heart chamber. The pathways are intended to allow improved blood flow to the oxygen-starved muscle. It is the company's second Phase II trial. The first is evaluating TMR as sole therapy for
9645 patients who are not candidates for balloon angioplasty or bypass surgery.--New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1733</
9646 AT&amp;T Corp's third-quarter results will see "pressure on the revenue line" as well as higher costs of sales and marketing, especially in its long-distance business, chief financial officer Richard Miller said.Call volume has "stabilized," at the second quarter levels, and "we're seeing pressures on the revenue line," Miller said in
9646 a telephone conference call with analysts on Tuesday morning.The call followed AT&amp;T's warning that third quarter share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates. Miller said the company is spending more on marketing. "We're taking more aggressive action on sales and marketing...The core business is still offering a great
9646 opportunity for profit.""We're greatly accelerating our expenditures," chairman Robert Allen said during the call.Asked by an analyst whether the company would be able to reach its previously stated long-term target of 10 percent earnings growth, Allen said it may occasionally miss the goal."There could always be a period the new
9646 AT&amp;T will reflect different rates of earnings growth," Allen said. 9646 short" of the "key" mean estimate of $0.89 for the fourth quarter "by roughly comparable amounts."Asked whether 1997 results would also be lower than analysts expect, Miller said it would be "premature" to talk about next year. In answer to another question, Allen said the "new" AT&amp;T was "not in
9646 an acquisition mode. Not only are we divesting major parts of the old AT&amp;T, but we're divesting other assets not strategic to our future to utilize (capital) and assets in the best possible way."AT&amp;T is in the midst of splitting into three companies, with AT&amp;T offering calling service, Lucent Technologies
9646 Inc offering telecommunications systems and software, and NCR in the computer business.Allen said AT&amp;T expected to complete distributing the remaining Lucent shares to AT&amp;T holders next week. 9646 the company, and expect earnings growth in that range," Allen said.Allen said its previously announced three-year jobs reduction plan was "on track," and would lead to about 17,000 job cuts.ATT officials said in the conference call the company was not ending its various "True Savings" discount programs. 9646 suggesting that every customer will be on one rate," one ATT official said. AT&amp;T also said on Tuesday that it will offer a single-rate, long-distance calling plan available 24 hours a day. The One Rate plan will offer consumers a flat rate of $0.15 a minute.In late morning composite trade,
9646 AT&amp;T was off 4-3/4 at 52-3/8 on volume of over 8.6 million.</

9683 Allen Reports on Restructuring,Investment Commitments and Earnings ImpactNEW YORK, Sept. 24 /PRNewswire/ -- In a letter to shareowners, AT&amp;T Chairman Robert E. Allen today reported on the status of the company's strategic restructuring and on AT&amp;T's achievements in the year since the breakup of the company was announced.Allen also described
9683 a program of decisive marketing initiatives -- including AT&amp;T One Rate(SM), introduced today -- that are intended to profitably accelerate volume and revenue growth in the company's core long- distance business.In addition, to complement long distance and capture opportunities in the fast-changing telecommunications industry, Allen reiterated AT&amp;T's commitment to invest
9683 in local, on-line and wireless capabilities as well as the infrastructure necessary to enable the company to offer customers comprehensive bundles of communications and information services.Allen said that those investments, coupled with continuing competitive pressures on AT&amp;T's long-distance business and its efforts to address them in the near term, will
9683 affect the company's third-quarter financial results."Specifically, although we do not yet know September results," he said, "it appears that third-quarter earnings will be as much as 10 percent below the mean estimate (92 cents per share for continuing operations) of key analysts who follow the company.*"Further, we currently believe that
9683 competitive pressures will continue for the remainder of the year, and we are intensifying our marketing efforts. Thus, fourth-quarter earnings will also likely fall short of key analysts' mean estimate (of 89 cents per share for continuing operations) by roughly comparable amounts," Allen said.*The full text of Allen's letter to
9683 shareowners follows: A Letter to AT&amp;T ShareownersIt was just about a year ago that we announced a strategy for unlocking the value of your investment in AT&amp;T by restructuring the company into three highly focused businesses: AT&amp;T, Lucent, and NCR.I'm pleased to report that our restructuring is on schedule. The
9683 market reacted very favorably to the initial public offering of Lucent Technologies in April, its stock has received strong support ever since, and we will be distributing the remaining shares to AT&amp;T's owners on September 30. The turnaround at NCR is well under way, and it recently reported its first
9683 quarterly operating profit since 1994. By the end of the month, we will file registration documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission preliminary to distributing NCR stock to AT&amp;T shareowners by the end of the year. Finally, we expect to complete the sale of Capital Corporation to a group of
9683 its managers and outside investors in October, possibly as early as next week.The New AT&amp;TFor its part, the new AT&amp;T is positioning itself to seize opportunities in an industry that is being fundamentally transformed by changes in technology and regulation. Capitalizing on those opportunities will require a period of investment,
9683 as I'll describe later in this letter, but I believe the steps we've already taken this year are impressive. Less than 30 days after Congress passed the Telecommunications Act of 1996, we filed to provide local service in all 50 states. We're now negotiating with the local exchange carriers in
9683 most of those states on the terms for interconnecting with their networks, and we plan to begin offering local service in targeted states before the end of the year.Our wireless services business -- already the country's largest -- has a third more subscribers than last year. And when the FCC
9683 auctioned wireless spectrum, we acquired new licenses that will more than double our national coverage, reaching over 80 percent of the U.S. population.We went from virtually nowhere in on-line services to one of the largest providers of Internet access in just six months. We're already hosting electronic storefronts on the
9683 Internet for nearly 500 businesses. And earlier this year, we took a minority equity position in the leading provider of Direct Broadcast Satellite service, DirecTV. Within nine weeks, we were offering AT&amp;T customers the best in access to home entertainment and information.Growing Our Core BusinessIn our core long distance services,
9683 business volumes have been growing at double digit rates. We have signed a number of large multi-year contracts, including some that were particularly satisfying because they were win-backs of major corporate accounts. And just last week, we announced a new offer that will give business customers one-stop customer care and
9683 consolidated billing for all their AT&amp;T services.On the consumer side of long distance, we continue to see the same challenging conditions I discussed last quarter. While we have succeeded in stabilizing volumes and revenues at last quarter's levels, the number of customers moving between carriers is still disturbing.Our research indicates
9683 that this customer volatility is due largely to price misperceptions that are frequently promoted by some competitors. To address this, we have developed a strategy intended to profitably accelerate volume and revenue growth in our consumer business.The AT&amp;T One RateWe launched a major element of that strategy just today --
9683 "AT&amp;T One Rate" responds to consumers' desire for simplicity. It is the first step in a marketing program to correct confusion about competitive claims and price misperception. Customers who subscribe to AT&amp;T One Rate will be able to make direct-dialed, long distance calls anywhere in the United States for just
9683 15 cents a minute 24 hours a day, seven days a week with no restrictions and no enrollment fee.Now, instead of wasting time comparing competing price claims, our customers can concentrate on how to make communications work best for them. We believe that lays the foundation for the integrated "bundles"
9683 of services that we will be offering in the weeks and months ahead.That's why we are determined to continue investing in the local, on-line and wireless services that, along with long distance, will make up the major elements of AT&amp;T's bundled offers -- even in the face of intense competition
9683 that continues to pressure our revenue and earnings. Indeed, we are also investing heavily in the systems and software necessary to integrate those services in a way that makes them most useful to customers.We believe that the net effect of these moves will be to clearly differentiate AT&amp;T from its
9683 competitors, fully capitalizing on the strength of the AT&amp;T brand. The Yankee Group, for example, recently reported that AT&amp;T was by far the preferred provider of combined local and long distance service.Building Long-term Shareowner ValueWe are confident these actions, and the continuing strength of our business long distance and wireless
9683 services, will build long-term shareowner value.In the near term, however, competitive pressures and our efforts to address them while continuing to invest in your business, will be reflected in our financial results.Specifically, although we do not yet know September results, it appears that third quarter earnings will be as much
9683 as 10 percent below the mean estimate (92 cents per share for continuing operations) of the key analysts who follow the company.Further, we currently believe that competitive pressures will continue for the remainder of the year, and we are intensifying our marketing efforts. Thus, fourth quarter earnings will also likely
9683 fall short of key analysts' mean estimates (89 cents per share for continuing operations) by roughly comparable amounts.I have taken the somewhat unusual step of previewing our performance prior to the close of the quarter because it has become clear that our financial results, in this critical period of industry
9683 transition, will be less than some in the investment community expect. I wanted you to understand why.At the same time, let me underscore that I have never seen a time of greater opportunity for AT&amp;T. The communicationsservices industry is undergoing fundamental change, much of which we helped shape. We intend
9683 to make the investments necessary to continue leading that change to the ultimate benefit of our customers, our employees and our owners.Robert E. AllenChairman and CEO*Please Note: This outlook on the balance of 1996 is based on our best current information. There can be no assurance, however, that actual results
9683 will not differ from this outlook. Variance could result from even further intensification of competition in our consumer business or from any of the numerous other factors that affect AT&amp;T and the industry, as described in our SEC reporting. 9690 Clarcor Inc said Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire United Air Specialists Inc in an exchange of common stock.As a result of the acquisition, United Air Specialists will become a subsidiary of Clarcor.The boards of directors of each company unanimously approved the transaction, which will be structured as
9690 a merger. Each fully diluted share of United Air Specialists will be converted into 0.36986 shares of common stock of Clarcor. The exchange ratio is subject to adjustment based on the actual number of fully diluted United Air shares at closing. United Air Specialists currently has approximately 3,270,000 fully diluted
9690 shares outstanding.Clarcor, which now has about 14,880,000 shares outstanding, will issue about 1,210,000 shares of its common stock to complete the merger. This will bring its total outstanding shares to about 16,090,000.To cover the costs of the merger, Clarcor said it expects to take a one-time charge to earnings in
9690 an amount yet to be determined in the quarter the merger is completed. Clarcor had sales of approximately $290 million and net earnings of $22.0 million for the fiscal year ended November 30, 1995. Clarcor said it expects fiscal 1996 sales to be approximately $330 million, excluding the United Air
9690 acquisition.United Air Specialists had sales of approximately $40 million and net earnings of $1.5 million for its fiscal year ended June 30, 1996.Consummation of the merger is subject, among other things, to approval by the shareholders of United Air Specialists and regulatory approvals. Clarcor said the merger is intended to
9690 qualify as a tax-free reorganization to United Air Specialists shareholders and be accounted for as a pooling of interests. The merger is expected to close in early 1997.The three largest shareholders of United Air Specialists, who collectively own approximately 50 percent, of the outstanding shares, have agreed to vote their
9690 shares in favor of the merger."The combination of Clarcor and United Air Specialists will significantly strengthen and expand our presence in the fast growing environmental and industrial air filtration industry," Larry Gloyd, Clarcor chairman, said in a statement."In addition, we will have opportunities to increase shareholder value through business synergies,
9690 such as the potential for filter cartridges manufactured by our Airguard Industries operation to be used in filter housings manufactured by UAS (United Air)," he added.Reuters Chicago Newsdesk - 312-408-8787</

9703 companies will likely post earnings growth in the high single digits in the near term, it will not be enough to ignite their stocks. To hedge his bets, he owns two of the bigger U.S. issues: Pfizer Inc, and Schering-Plough Corp, which together comprise about 2.8 percent of the portfolio.But
9703 the software/information group is all about growth, von Emster believes. The group includes companies that link up doctors, hospitals and insurers via computer and firms that offer computerized services, like monitoring hospital costs.Von Emster believes stocks in the sector will grow about 30 percent over the near term. "The stocks
9703 are underfollowed, not covered by Wall Street," said von Emster, who at age 29 is among the younger managers in the U.S. "They're in businesses where there is tremendous demand, and they can barely keep up. And we're talking about earnings growth of about 35 percent annually."Among his favorites are
9703 IDX Systems Corp, a provider of healthcare information software to doctors, at about 2.13 percent of the portfolio; and Transition Systems Inc, providing computer systems that provide clinical and financial data to hospitals, at about 1.66 percent. Overall, the fund focuses on small-cap stocks, with about two thirds under $1
9703 billion in capitalization and the other third above $1 billion.In all, the portfolio holds about 60 stocks. The top five holdings include: PacifiCare Health Systems Inc; Health Systems International Inc ; Amgen Inc ; Boston Scientific Corp ; and Serologicals Inc.Von Emster has about seven percent of fund assets in
9703 cash, down from about 25 percent in May. The curent level is just about right to cover redemptions, he said. But investor cash-outs have hardly been a problem. Von Emster said about $1 million has been flowing into the fund each day, and $100 million has poured into the fund
9703 in the last six months. Assets currently stand at about $145 million.Von Emster theorizes that in the U.S. market correction in June-July, HMOs were especially hard hit, as some companies warned of upcoming bad quarterly results. That, in turn, "spawned an overall selloff in the group," he said."Amgen and other
9703 large-cap companies went down as well," he said. "You had a 10 percent correction on solid companies with strong earnings. It was an opportunity for institutions like us to get into the market."But there were others who decided that health-care and related stocks were a safe, defensive haven.Von Esmter buys
9703 into the notion that the overall health-care industry would have continued demand and would not suffer through any business downturns."There's a flight to quality when there's a correction," he said. "Health care is viewed as a quality sector in the overall market."According to Morningstar Inc, the fund has returned about
9703 15.60 percent year to date; for 1995 it returned about 54.59 percent; and for three years it has gained 33.43 percent on an annualized basis.The average specialty health care fund has a year-to-date return of 8.48 percent, a 1995 gain of 47.20 percent, and a three-year annualized return of 23.60

9707 Despite the turbulent, rumor-ridden run-up to Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy meeting, economists are predicting only a modest reaction from U.S. markets when they finally get the central bank's decision on rates.If the Fed does hike the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, as many in the market expect, a
9707 knee-jerk sell-off is likely. But most experts expect any price drop to be short-lived, especially in the long end of the Treasury yield curve, which could ultimately benefit from a rate rise. Should policymakers decide to keep rates unchanged, a short-lived price rise would likely give way to concern at
9707 the long end that the Fed is behind the inflation curve.Worries about the possibility of hefty hikes down the road would limit any immediate gains, leaving prices relatively unchanged, economists said."I think the only way we would see a major reaction in the markets is if the Fed surprised everyone
9707 by raising rates 50 basis points," said Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets Inc. In a Reuters poll conducted last Thursday, 17 of 30 economists said they expected the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to hike rates on Tuesday. However, only one of the 17 was calling for anything
9707 more than a 25 basis point rise.Eight of the 12 regional Fed banks have submitted requests for a discount rate rise, indicating substantial pressure for tighter credit.U.S. bond and stock markets have already priced in approximately 25 basis points of tightening. But even if the Fed does not raise rates
9707 on Tuesday, many analysts feel the market will anticipate a move at the FOMC's next meeting November 13. "The belief is the Fed will either raise rates a quarter percentage point now or will do so after the election, so one way or the other you'll get the increase," said
9707 Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany .Johnson said this scenario has complicated strategy for active portfolio managers trying to gauge the impact of Tuesday's policy decision on the markets.Many longer-term investors, economists and forecasters are already looking past the meeting and asking themselves what lies ahead for monetary
9707 policy and economic growth in the fourth quarter. Currently signals are mixed. Companies are stepping up production, rebuilding inventories and hiring workers, yet retail sales remain weak.In any case, tight labor market conditions and rising wages -- the reasons many economists are predicting a hike in rates -- will not
9707 vanish on the heels of a 25 basis point fed funds boost.As a result, the Fed's decision on Tuesday may raise more questions than it answers, economists suggested."My key question is where do we go after the meeting and I think that's really the relevant issue here," said Richard Berner,
9707 chief economist at Pittsburgh-based Mellon Bank."If the Fed goes as I expect they will, it seems to me questions will immediately arise as to when the next one will be and how many more there will be," he said. "The message might be that if they don't go (on Tuesday)
9707 then the chances are greater that they will need to go more forcefully down the road."-- N.A. Treasury Desk 212-859-1673</

9716 Finnish forestry stocks were hit on Tuesday when Metsa-Serla Oy, the country's third largest pulp and paper company, warned it expected to make a loss in May-December.The company, which last year crested a cyclical boom in the industry to report bumper profits, said it would still be in the black
9716 for full-year 1996 thanks to a 318 million markka ($70.4 million) January-April profit.But it largely blamed a surprisingly sharp fall in pulp prices and particularly fine paper products for the forecast loss. It also listed other more incidental factors.Metsa-Serla said it would announce details of action to be taken to
9716 improve its competitiveness when it publishes its interim report for January-August on October 17, but a company official declined to elaborate on Tuesday."The biggest impact is indeed from fine paper prices," Metsa-Serla senior vice president Hannu Anttila told Reuters.Metsa-Serla's warning took already weak forestry shares down, but with its rivals
9716 it later trimmed losses as already bearish analysts targeted the one-off elements in its statement, limiting the damage especially to other companies.In late trading the Helsinki forestry index stood down around two percent at 2,133.27, having earlier fallen to around 2,115. Metsa-Serla was down 0.70 markka or over two percent
9716 at 31.00, off a 30.00 markka low.Metsa-Serla said several development projects and investments would lead to non-recurring expenditure of around 300 million markka, referring to restructuring at its recent German acquisition MD Papier, and the start-up of a new mill."It's probably more than just problems in the market," said Dennis
9716 Christie at Kleinwort Benson in London. "I think most people will have to revise their forecasts down quite dramatically."Nine analysts polled by Reuters in June had pointed to a full-year profit of, on average, around 800 million markka for Metsa-Serla, but the range then was already very wide at 130-1,106
9716 million markka.Metsa-Serla said prospects for its other business operations were in line with the targets set for the year.Anna-Maija Pirskanen at Merita Securities, said she would lower her 1996 forecast for Metsa-Serla, but not for other forestry groups."We have such a negative view at forestries in general, that we don't
9716 need to revise forecasts for other companies," she said, adding Merita has an underweight recommendation on forestries.But although she saw one-off factors mainly behind Metsa-Serla's warning, she said it also underlined reasons for caution in the forestry sector."This is mainly due to one-off factors, but we cannot deny that capacity
9716 ratios and paper prices have also declined," she said. 9720 Can a father take a bath with his five-year old son or daughter? Is it OK to hug your 10-year old nephew? And what if the neighbours' 12-year old daughter kisses you on the cheek when she meets you on the street?One of the consequences of the paedophile kidnap, sex
9720 and murder scandal which has rocked Belgium in the past month is that adults, especially males, have become much more nervous about physical displays of affection towards children."My husband used to go take a bath with our (four-year old) daughter. But this affair has made me think. What if she
9720 talks about it in school?" said Mieke, a 36-year old Belgian lobbyist."At my son's birthday party, one of the boys came over, gave me a hug, said 'you are my mummy' and put his head in my lap -- while other parents were there. I was petrified. Because of the
9720 Dutroux affair," said Victor, father of a five-year-old.The gruesome details of how a paedophile gang, in which Marc Dutroux is the chief suspect, kidnapped, abused and killed four girls have been headline news nearly every day since mid-August.Besides killing what faith Belgians had left in the ability of their police
9720 and courts to prevent such crimes, it has brought home the idea that atrocities like this can happen here.Despite the scandal surrounding the Dutroux case and recent discoveries in the 1991 murder of politician Andre Cools, Belgium is still a low-crime country, where drug warfare, gang violence and sex crimes
9720 make headlines because they are rare."This is terrible, it is the loss of innocence for a whole country. In my country (the U.S.) this happened a long time ago," said Nathan, 34, a New York TV producer visiting Belgium.He quoted from "Disclosure", Michael Crichton's best-selling novel about sexual harrassment of
9720 men, to illustrate how American males feel about intimacy with children:"Don't smile at a child on the street, unless you're with your wife. Don't ever touch a strange child. Don't ever be alone with someone else's child, even for a moment...At a party, don't let a little girl sit on
9720 your lap. If she tries, gently push her aside. If you ever have occasion to see a naked child, look quickly away. Better yet, leave."One long-time resident of the United States, now working in Belgium, said that while it was easy to overstate the concern in America, he had been
9720 aware of possible pitfalls as a soccer coach for eight year olds."You had to be aware that hugs and other ways of celebrating could be misinterpreted," he said.In Belgium, most men would be less apprehensive about this."When my (five-year old) son's friends come to me in the playground and want
9720 to wrestle, I wrestle with them, it is the most normal thing in the world," said a Brussels architect, 34."Children are very physical. And taking a bath with your child is the most natural thing in the world," he added.An article entitled "The Eros of Parenthood" in the U.S. magazine
9720 the New Yorker last February described how not touching children could also be a crime."What else can we make of research that tells us paedophiles tend to subscribe to...puritanical views about sex? That, within a family, harshly conservative values are a risk factor for sexual abuse. Or that sexual abuse
9720 is more likely to occur in families where there is an absence of physical affection?"Luk Goethals, 42, a bookkeeper in Ghent, agrees.He said the Dutroux case had not changed his behaviour towards children but there was a risk that the media attention about would stifle men's natural reactions to children."I
9720 hope we will be able to continue experiencing intimacy with our own children and those of our friends," he said.</

9721 of a legal loophole, the bank only supervises investment funds with a collective investment strategy.Funds of an individual nature -- where investors buy a share of a whole investment project, such as one square metre of teak trees -- can operate outside bank supervision.Newspapers said the bank would begin proceedings

9728 British Prime Minister John Major was reported to be furious with finance minister Kenneth Clarke on Tuesday after remarks by Clarke reopened a chasm over Europe that threatens to split the Conservative Party irreparably.Senior government sources were quoted by several newspapers as saying Major was "very angry" at Clarke's overt
9728 support for a single European Union currency.Major's Downing Street office said it had no comment on the reports. But senior officials studiously avoided a defence of Clarke's remarks, saying only: "The prime minister has made clear that we have a settled policy which stands."In another sign that party unity is
9728 breaking down over the issue of closer ties with the EU, a junior foreign office minister admonished Clarke, his senior in the government pecking order, saying Clarke's comments had undermined the ruling party's unity."I think the difference between Mr Clarke and some of us is that he thinks we can
9728 have a single European currency without having a federal Europe. We think... that would be an inevitable step down a road we don't want to advance down," said right-winger Sir Nicholas Bonsor."I think he will be out of line with the view of the vast majority of the party and
9728 I think it is out of line with what the government policy has been as expressed before."The government's official policy, which Major instigated to try to bridge the yawning divide between pro-Europeans and so-called Eurosceptics in his party, is that it will decide what is in Britain's interests after the
9728 single currency is launched.In an interview during a weekend meeting of EU finance ministers in Ireland, Chancellor of the Exchequer Clarke said it would be "pathetic" for Britain to wait and see how a European single currency developed before deciding whether to join."That would be the worst policy of all,
9728 of the British doing their traditional business of not be able to make their minds up and then joining late," said Clarke, seen as the most likely candidate from the Conservative Party's left wing to bid for succession to Major.Clarke's remarks provoked strong pressure on Major from Eurosceptics to ditch
9728 Clarke, the most pro-European member of the cabinet, before a general election due within eight months.Major negotiated an "opt-out" from monetary union when negotiating the Maastricht treaty in 1991. Eurosceptics want him to rule out entry into a single currency in the life of the next five-year parliament and want
9728 that pledge to be a commitment in the Conservatives' election platform.Getting rid of Clarke would be an extremely risky manoeuvre. Markets, which see him as a "safe pair of hands" and praise his careful management of the current economic upturn, would be dismayed at his sacrifice on the altar of
9728 political expediency.Pro-Europeans would be outraged. They have begun fighting back against the Eurosceptics they fear are dominating political debate. They include senior party figures like former prime minister Edward Heath and a battery of ex-ministers.The opposition Labour Party is already 20 points ahead in opinion polls. Conservative strategists are worried
9728 the European issue will dominate their party conference in early October.Home Secretary Michael Howard, one of the cabinet's Eurosceptics, heightened speculation over Clarke by carefully sidestepping a request to confirm or deny the rift between Clarke and Major."I don't think you should believe everything you read in the newspapers," he
9728 said in a BBC interview.Heath told the BBC the reports of Major's anger were part of an attempt by the Eurosceptics to "stampede" the government into a tougher policy on the single currency.Heath dismissed suggestions Clarke would quit, saying: "He won't leave the government... (I'm) quite confident because he knows
9728 he's done a splendid job and he will keep on doing it."</
9729 German and French stocks recovered their composure on Tuesday after a sharp overnight rebound on Wall Street but London slumped after a bullish start on interest rate concerns.All share and currency markets were to some degree holding their breath ahead of a decision from a key U.S. monetary policy-making meeting
9729 and bourse sentiment was not helped by another weak start by New York stocks.Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) committee would sanction a credit tightening after the meeting which began at 1300 GMT. Its outcome was not likely to be known until
9729 after European markets closed.If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.British stocks reversed their opening gains with shares in banks, a driving force behind London's recent rally, leading the FTSE index lower. HSBC, Barclays and NatWest led the retreat as fears
9729 of a U.S. rate hike prompted profit-taking.A signal from the Bank of England that it had, as expected, left interest rates unchanged after the government's monthly monetary meeting made little impact on shares. Nor did reports showing a stronger-than-expected 2.2 percent British GDP growth in the second quarter."The market felt
9729 pretty good this morning but right now it feels horrible," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage as the FTSE 100 plumbed the day's depths.Another trader said: "I would think the market would take a quarter-point hike in its stride but at the moment we just don't
9729 want to do anything."In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade higher, although volumes remained generally limited. Dealers said range trade was expected to continue in post-bourse electronic trading.The DAX index of blue chip shares ended 11.41 points higher at 2,638.45.On the Paris bourse stocks held their early gains in quiet
9729 trading ahead of the Fed decision. Brokers said a quarter-point rise in U.S. interest rates was already priced into the market.One Paris disappointment was Europe's largest steelmaker Usinor Sacilor, privatised last July. Its shares dropped after it announced first-half profits plunged by 65 percent and warned that its second half
9729 earnings would be even weaker. On the currency front, too, the mood was one of wait and see. The dollar was stuck in a tiny range by midday in Europe and dealers said all eyes were on the Fed amid confusion over what impact its decision would have on the
9729 market.A quarter-point rise in the federal funds target rate was largely discounted, but analysts were deeply divided over whether the FOMC would sanction a change in U.S. monetary policy at all.CURRENCIES AT 1345 GMTThe dollar was at 1.5142 marks and 109.73 yen compared with 1.5120 marks and 109.88 yen in
9729 Europe late on Monday.STOCK MARKETS AT 1345 GMTThe Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 9.3 points down at 3,910.4.In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 14.34 points up at 2,081.43.The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 11.41 at 2,638.45.PRECIOUS METALSGold was higher at $382.55 compared
9729 with Monday's London close of $381.25. Silver also fixed firmer at 491.00 cents.</
9730 British builder Tarmac, which staged a major asset swap with housebuilder Wimpey in February, saw half year profits plunge deeper into the red on Tuesday after being hit by a 65 million pounds ($100 million) charge.Tarmac reported a half year loss of 58.3 million pounds versus a 15.9 million loss
9730 last year. After stripping out the charge, underlying pretax profits were 6.7 million versus 29.1 million. The dividend was frozen at 3.0 pence per share.Underlying profits were at the bottom of market forecasts, due to tough markets and bad weather hitting winter projects.But Tarmac said restructuring which followed its asset
9730 swap would result in higher-than-expected savings of 35 million pounds per annum.Neville Sims, chief executive, said of the first half figures: "In a year of transition for the group, the results are neither representative of the true underlying perrformance of the businesses, nor of their potential...The outlook for the medium
9730 term and beyond is positive."Under the asset swap, Tarmac took on Wimpey's construction and aggregates units in return for its housebuilding business.The benefits have so far failed to feed through, but Sims said: "There will be increased benefit in the second half."He said he expected part of the 18 million
9730 of cost savings from the building materials business to feed through in the second half of the year. But on the construction side he warned that "there will not be much benefit before next year. You must add the full cost savings against next year's results."The total number of jobs
9730 lost under restructuring was 1,400.Commenting on the outlook, Sims said the European market was still difficult, citing France in particular.In Britain, the building materials division is suffering from low infrastructure spending and cutbacks in road building.There was also a slide in revenues from road maintenance in the first half "as
9730 local authorities wrestle with budgets", he said. But Tarmac hoped for a revival.The North American building materials arm told a better tale, reporting progress in margins.Construction also fared better, with the total order book up 15 percent and margins also improving.On group finance, debt levels rose to 511.6 million, up
9730 163.5 million, raising gearing to 66 percent. That triggered some concern within the group. Finance director Chris Bunker called it an "unacceptable level" and pledged to reduce it to 30-40 percent within two to three years.Tarmac's shares were slightly ahead after the results, up two and a half pence at
9730 96. But the verdict from analysts was divided."This was very much a transition period but they (the results) were disappointing -- construction services profits dropped nearly five million and the gearing has shot up to 66 percent. The figures are worse than expected and balance sheet much worse than it
9730 should be," said one analyst.But another was more upbeat. "The U.S. margins at eight percent are quite encouraging on the face of it. In the heavy building materials division, margins of 7-1/2 percent, down from 8.9 percent, is pretty acceptable given it includes the Wimpey business.It is a reasonably resilient

9733 British retailer Laura Ashley reported a 70 percent jump in profits on Tuesday and announced plans to expand home furnishing as part of a radical shake up under new American chief executive Ann Iverson.But the profit recovery failed to match expectations and the retailer's shares fell steeply. They stood 22
9733 pence lower at 192 pence at 1245 GMT.Pretax profits rose to 5.2 million pounds ($8.1 million) from three million. Sales fell to 156.1 million pounds from 164.6 million because of a reduction in mail order and perfume activities and the sale of Australian operations last year. Underlying sales rose by
9733 3.2 percent.The dividend was 0.4 pence a share, the first interim payment since 1989.But retail analysts were unimpressed. "The market had expected profits of six million pounds and a dividend of 0.5 pence," said one.Laura Ashley, famous for its traditionally English flowery dresses and furnishings, has begun expanding its higher-margin
9733 home furnishings business in Britain and the United States as part of a three-year recovery programme.Chief executive Ann Iverson, who took over last year, said in a statement the company's recovery was running to plan."The group remains on track through its shop expansion programme and its focus on improving product
9733 and gross margins, to achieve acceptable returns for shareholders over the next three years."Iverson, who made her name in Britain by turning around Storehouse Plc's BhS and childrenswear chain Mothercare, was hired last year to revive profits as Laura Ashley was struggling to cope with financial troubles caused by over-expansion
9733 and under-investment.The retailer is in the process of closing smaller shops and opening larger ones to display its home furnishing ranges, which have scope for bigger profits.It plans to add more than 100,000 square feet of store space in the United States this year mainly via larger format stores, finance
9733 director Jim Walsh said in an interview.In Britain, Laura Ashley is adding 33,000 square feet of space this year, opening 16 new stores and closing six. An out-of-town home furnishing store will open in Warrington in northwest England in November and another store is opening in Cardiff in south Wales
9733 next month, he said.The group also plans to expand its presence in supermarket group Sainsbury's Homebase stores, where it currently has 65 outlets, Walsh said.The group has made progress clearing out old stock and reducing costs, which fell by about six percent in the first half. Walsh said gross margins
9733 and sales were set to get a boost early next year when the first ranges from Basha Cohen, the new director of design and buying, are due to hit the shops.But he denied that the new-look fashions and fabrics would move completely away from the Laura Ashley floral prints which
9733 turned the business from a cottage industry in the 1950s into an international brand."It's taking the flower and updating it," Walsh said.($1=.6420 Pound)</
9734 British leisure and hotel company Rank Organisation Plc picked up the Tom Cobleigh chain of pubs on Tuesday, paying about two million pounds each.Tom Cobleigh, owners of 44 managed pubs in Yorkshire and the Midlands operating under the motto "Unspoilt Pubs for Nice People", is centred on the growing trend
9734 for eating out.Rank's agreed cash offer for Tom Cobleigh at 240 pence per share, values the company at 95.6 million pounds ($148.9 million). About 62 percent of Tom Cobleigh shareholders have already accepted the offer.In an interview, Rank chief executive Andrew Teare told Reuters the pace of new Tom Cobleigh
9734 pub openings would now increase. Some 16 new bars should be opened this year.Food sales in recent openings of Tom Cobleigh pubs have reached on average about 50 percent of total revenues.In the leisure sector, spending on eating out is expected to grow strongly, at some eight percent every year
9734 over the next few years.Teare said Rank expects a fast underlying profit stream from the purchase. "There is an underlying velocity in the profit streams," he said.Rank expects the deal to have a neutral impact on earnings in the first full financial year and enhance earnings thereafter.Teare said Rank would
9734 also benefit from synergies between the two companies, particularly in purchases of spirits and other alcoholic drink, where Rank is a major buyer.He said the deal would also give Rank the chance to offer eating-out facilitiies in its leisure complexes. "The one thing we don't have is an eating-out business."Rank's
9734 leisure and entertainment complexes, which include the Odeon cinema chain and Mecca bingo halls, currently rely on leasing out space to restaurant chains but the Tom Cobleigh purchase means it can run its own food outlets, said Teare."We can make substantial inroads to capture those eating-out revenues," he said. "It
9734 is a big add-on to our existing strategy."The senior management team at Tom Cobleigh, founded in December 1991 and listed on the London stock exchange in November 1995, will stay on at Rank to develop the business under the umbrella of Rank's Recreation Division.Rank was widely touted as a likely
9734 buyer of Tom Cobleigh after the pub chain acknowledged earlier this month it was in talks with potential suitors.Analysts and financiers said Rank's bid had pipped an earlier offer from Yates Brothers Wine Lodges.But Rank shares fell eight on the news to 433p as analysts doubted whether the name Tom
9734 Cobleigh would appeal country wide.Tom Cobleigh shares were 1-1/2p higher at 235p. ($1=.6420 Pound)</
9735 Police raided homes in Ireland on Tuesday as Irish and British authorities sought to capitalise on the biggest seizure of IRA arms and explosives ever made on the British mainland.The capture on Monday of 10 tonnes of explosives after dawn raids in London and the arrest of five men dealt
9735 a major blow to Irish Republican Army morale and torpedoed any chance of a new ceasefire.Police in Ireland swooped on several homes near the border with British-ruled Northern Ireland early on Tuesday but no arrests were made.One of the five men being questioned by police in London is a young
9735 Northern Irish British Airways engineer working at Britain's Gatwick airport.Transport officials said they would be reviewing already strict vetting procedures but the airline insisted the arrest in no way suggested the airport was the target for an attack.A sixth man, who was shot dead by police during Monday's raids, was
9735 believed to have been born in Britain of Irish parents.The suspects can be detained for a week without charge under anti-terrorism laws brought in to combat the IRA's guerrilla battle to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.Police, jubilant that their close co-operation with secret service agents paid such rich dividends, said
9735 they believed the IRA were within hours of launching lorry bomb attacks and targeting high profile public figures.The media speculated that IRA targets ranged from the royal family to the Channel Tunnel between France and Britain.Security experts suggested the IRA would now want to stage further attacks in a show
9735 of strength before Britain's general election, which Prime Minister John Major must call by next May."They may stage a smaller attack in the next couple of weeks to show they are still active and have not been beaten," said Professor Paul Rogers of the University of Bradford.Members of the British
9735 and Irish parliaments met amid tightened security in the city of Bath to review the slim chances of finding an elusive peace formula in Northern Ireland.The biggest casualty could be the peace process in Northern Ireland where Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, has been excluded from all-party talks.The IRA
9735 ended a 17-month ceasefire in February with an attack on London's Docklands district that killed two people. In June, a huge lorry bomb devasted the centre of Manchester, injuring 200 people in the northern English city.</
9736 European bourses generally recovered their composure on Tuesday after a sharp overnight rebound on Wall Street, which surfaced from an early 50 point dive to close slightly up.London, Frankfurt and Paris, which all closed well down on Monday and London suffering its biggest drop in two months, opened higher on
9736 Tuesday, although London fell back later.The Dow ended up 6.28 points at a record 5,894.74.But stock and currency markets were effectively holding their breath ahead of a crucial U.S. monetary policy-making meeting later in the day.Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) committee
9736 would sanction a credit tightening after the meeting (at 1300 GMT), the outcome of which would not be known until after European markets closed. If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.British stocks lost their opening gains and were trading near
9736 the day's lows by late morning as banks succumbed to a wave of institutional profit-taking and other stocks were mixed, traders said.The blue chip FTSE 100 was down 9.6 points at 3910.1 by 1100 GMT. Bank stocks HSBC, Barclays and NatWest led the retreat and decliners were in a three-to-one
9736 majority.A money-market signal from the Bank of England that it had, as expected, left interest rates unchanged after the government's monthly monetary meeting made little impact on shares. Nor did reports showing a stronger-than-expected 2.2 percent British GDP growth in the second quarter."The market felt pretty good this morning but
9736 right now it feels horrible," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage as the FTSE 100 plumbed the day's depths.Another trader said: "I would think the market would take a quarter-point hike in its stride but at the moment we just don't want to do anything."In Frankfurt,
9736 German shares held on to small morning gains ahead of the Fed meeting but volumes were generally limited and trading range seen very tight. Dollar strength continued to lend some support to stocks, dealers said, and government bonds were also slightly higher.On the Paris bourse stocks moved up from a
9736 higher opening buoyed by Wall Street. Metals, however, were hit by disappointing results from steelmaker Usinor, down two francs after reporting a 65 percent drop in first half profits. On the currency front, too, the mood was one of wait and see. The dollar was stuck in a tiny range
9736 by midday in Europe and dealers said all eyes were on the Fed amid confusion over what impact its decision would have on the market.A quarter-point rise in the federal funds target rate was largely discounted, but analysts were deeply divided over whether the FOMC would sanction a change in
9736 U.S. monetary policy at all.CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMTThe dollar was at 1.5125 marks and 109.78 yen compared with 1.5120 marks and 109.88 yen in Europe late on Monday.STOCK MARKETS AT 1100The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 9.6 points down at 3,910.1.In Paris, the CAC-40 share
9736 index was 12.95 points up at 2,080.04.The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 11.19 at 2,638.23.PRECIOUS METALSGold fixed firmer at $381.60 compared with Monday's London Gold close of $381.25. Silver was also firmer at $4.90 cents.</

9738 far sold an Oct 4-6 cargo to a northwest European refiner for Nov +3 cents a barrel.A cargo with the same dates traded at Nov parity on Monday."There seems to be more interest from refiners -- they're seeing pretty good margins at the moment," said a trader. Brent paper was
9738 also holding on to early gains with Nov Brent up 16 cents at $22.42 a barrel by 1537 GMT and the Nov/Dec intermonth spread three or four cents firmer at +49/+51 cents.Two Brent cargoes were passing through the paper chains.Other North Sea grades were also benefiting from the refinery buying
9738 spree, with Norwegian Oseberg, Ekofisk and Statfjord all moving at slightly higher premiums than the last reported deals, traders said.Oct 20-22 Ekofisk traded as high as Dated Brent +27 cents a barrel, compared with +12 cents for an Oct 4-6 cargo on Monday. 9743 European metal producer Metaleurop SA expects to post higher earnings in the 1996/97 financial year (October/September) than in 1995/96, its chairman Helmut Stodieck said on Tuesday.In a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts, Stodieck said net profits next year may rise to between 60 million and 200 million French
9743 francs, depending on the price of its two main products lead and zinc, and other factors."I see Metaleurop in the black (in 1996/97) and depending on market assumptions somewhere between 60 and 200 million French francs," he told reporters after the presentation.The lower end of the band was based on
9743 an average zinc price over the period of $1,050 a tonne, an assumption which Stodieck called "conservative." The lead price assumption at the lower end of the band was $750."My personal view is that the markets have a higher potential," he said.Prices of $1,300 for zinc and $850 for lead
9743 were used as the basis of the top end of the earnings expectations.The exchange rate basis for both earning estimates was 5.17 French francs to the U.S. dollar.For the 1995/96 financial year Stodieck said earnings were likely to be slightly below the half year net attributable profit figure of 52
9743 million francs."The (full-year) figure may come a little below this for the full year because of the problems at our Nordenham (lead) smelter," he said.Stodieck said the plant would only produce 55 percent of its 90,000-tonne annual capacity during its first full year of operations."We now have good reason to
9743 believe we have solved some of the major problems," Stodieck said.--Mike Collett-White, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057</

9747 The British Retail Consortium (BRC) said strong retail spending figures did not herald the start of an inflationary consumer boom and it urged Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to keep interest rates on hold.In a briefing for retailers, BRC chief economic adviser Andrew Sentance said inflation was likely to fall in the
9747 coming months due to a weaker trend in food prices, very low factory gate price increases and a stronger exchange rate."In the short term, these downward influences are likely to offset any upward pressure on inflation from the impact of consumer demand on profit margins," he said. BRC director-general James
9747 May said strong August retail sales confirmed the strengthening trend in consumer spending."We should not forget that this pickup in the retail sector comes after a slowdown in retail growth of just over one percent last year. There are still many negative influences on the consumer, including job insecurity, negative
9747 equity and memories of falling house prices in the recession," he said.The organisation's advice to the Chancellor of the Exchequer was to keep interest rates as low as possible and make modest tax cuts in his November 26 budget. Sentance said that as long as interest rates remained at curent
9747 levels, consumer spending should continue to grow at the present healthy rate, giving a welcome lift to economic growth.Worries that consumer-led growth would push up wages and overall inflation were premature.The pickup in consumer spending was only just beginning, whereas in the late 1980s it went on for four years,
9747 and the momentum behind it was much weaker than in the late 1980s."The recent rate of GDP growth has been sluggish...and unemployment remains high, so there is some slack to be taken up before inflationary pressures emerge," Sentance said. "The case for a rise in interest rates now is therefore
9747 weak," he added."However, as we move into 1997, and particularly after the election, some upward adjustment in borrowing costs could be justified to ensure that consumer growth is kept to a sustainable rate and does not become an inflationary threat."-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774</

9749 Sugar beet producing regions in central and eastern Europe continue to suffer from the effects of bad weather over growing areas as a more accurate picture of total production emerges as the harvest gets underway.The region's two largest producers, Russia and Ukraine, are both forecast to produce less sugar than
9749 last year due to adverse weather conditions.Sugar output in Europe's post-communist nations is widely forecast to be lower this year and was recently estimated by trade house E D &amp; F Man at 8.66 million tonnes white value, down by 289,000 tonnes from the 1995/96 crop year.UKRAINE--DROUGHT CUTS PRODUCTIONUkraine, the
9749 region's largest producer, continues on course for a lower sugar output after suffering a drought through the summer and cold rains in recent weeks."We will get about 26 million tonnes of sugar beets this year," said Leonid Bershtein, a deputy director of the Sugar Research Institute. The last harvest produced
9749 30 million tonnes."The recent rains have meant little for our beets. This year the drought had a greater influence," Bershtein said.Less than 10 percent of all beets sown had been gathered, he said, with the harvest expected to end in November.Yields for the entire crop would probably be less than
9749 20 tonnes per hectare, compared with 21.9 tonnes last year, and the real sugar content at refineries no more than 12 percent."We only have a third of the necessary fertiliser and we have absolutely no herbicides," Bershtein said. "Old equipment means that we lose about 10 percent of the harvest
9749 annually."RUSSIA--WORST CROP IN DECADESIn Russia, the beet harvest is likely to be one of the worst in decades, but industry analysts said high reserves of whites and cheap Ukrainian imports would compensate for low output."We still expect the beet harvest to total 17 million tonnes," said Mikhail Sushkov, head of
9749 the Rossakhsvyokla sugar beet producers association, adding that rain had slowed work at the beginning of the harvest.Russia's beet harvest, which is only just starting, could still be affected by bad weather, analysts said. Beet gathering is reported to be proceeding slowly and the quality of the beet harvested so
9749 far is under threat.POLAND--OUTPUT RISINGBut the outlook for Poland, the region's third largest producer, is better and this year's output is expected to rise.Despite a long winter and rainy summer, official estimates put Polish beet output at 15.5 million tonnes, 2.2 million higher than last year, which could translate into
9749 a white sugar output of around two million tonnes.Poland produced nearly 1.6 million tonnes of sugar in 1995.The first sugar beet test on September 2 showed average sugar content at 13.78 percent, down from 14.34 percent a year ago, but average root weight increased to 732 grammes from 664.Poland will
9749 hold its second and last beet test on October 7 and results are expected after October 20.CZECH REPUBLIC--DISRUPTION FROM RAINSIndustry sources in the Czech Republic said yields would probably be high compared with previous years, although recent heavy rainfall could disrupt the autumn harvesting.Czech sugar output is estimated at more
9749 than 500,000 tonnes this year after the 460,035 tonnes produced in 1995/96."The weather conditions were not as extreme as in other years, except that there was an exceptional amount of rain," said Jiri Janda, director of Prague-based refiner Prazska Cukerni Spolecnost a.s."Climatic conditions were favourable, the beet turned out well
9749 and it looks like there will be solid yields. Domestic consumption will definitely be covered," he said.But he cautioned that the final output would still be affected by weather conditions during harvest and field losses could be expected if the rains continued.HUNGARY--LOW SUGAR CONTENTHigher beet weights in Hungary are not
9749 expected to increase final sugar output to any significant degree."The roots were fattened by rains but their sugar content is very low," said a Sugar Industry Association official.Chairman Andras Angeli said while sugar yields would not be a great deal higher, more sunshine could still boost production.But according to the
9749 National Meteorology Service only a few days of continuous sunshine are forecast for mid-October.Angeli said Hungary planned to produce 460,000 tonnes of sugar this year, down from 480,000, but beet exports were likely to reach 500,000 tonnes, up from 370,000.ROMANIA--SHORTAGE OF FUNDS AND FUELRomania's beet harvest could be affected by
9749 acute shortages of funds and fuel -- and a lack of machinery, inadequate storage and transport delays are expected to cause further delays.Beet has already been lost on 23,000 hectares of the total 161,950 ha sown due to a harsh winter and late snows, but the remainder is said to
9749 be in good condition.According to the Agriculture Ministry, Romania's 1996 sugar output should reach some 250,000 tonnes after a previous 300,000 and the country might have to import about the same quantity of raw sugar to meet domestic and industry demand.Many farmers have used only 100 kg of fertiliser per
9749 hectare instead of the recommended 160 kg. Others have abandoned growing beet after factories failed to pay them in time last year.BULGARIA--YIELDS DOWN BY HALFIn Bulgaria, bad weather is expected to reduce sugar yields by almost 50 percent in a crop where the area sown to beet has been slashed
9749 to 6,000 hectares from 11,200 last year."Bad weather in the spring and plant diseases have spoiled this year's crop," said a Bulgarian Sugar Institute analyst.He estimated final sugar yield at 23 tonnes per hectare after some 40 tonnes last year.CROATIA--HARVEST DELAYEDCroatia's beet harvest, which is expected to yield some 880,000
9749 tonnes of sugar, is also being delayed by wet weather.Sugar content in all of Croatia's main growing areas in the northeast has been affected, although rains in July and August helped root growth and boosted yields, ministry officials said."The root needs sunshine and not water any more," said Andrija Kristek,
9749 head of the Sugar Beet Institute in Osijek."However, since the leaf is well preserved, the beet will not use up sugar to sprout new leaves, so its content could remain at the current 11-13 percent on average."--Compiled in London newsroom, +44 171 542 8064, with contributions from Irene Marushko in
9749 Kiev, Peter Henderson in Moscow, Wojciech Moskwa in Warsaw, Jan Lopatka in Prague, Denes Albert in Budapest, Adrian Dascalu in Bucharest, Elisaveta Konstaninova in Sofia, and Kolumbina Bencevic in Zagreb.</

9771 also hamper the success of firms operating north of the border.The poll surveyed 12 companies operating in Scotland between September 17 and 20.All 12 of the companies surveyed stated that a Scottish parliament with tax-raising powers would harm Scottish business in the short term, but this number was halved if
9771 the parliament had no authority to levy taxes.Labour, ahead in opinion polls, plans to set up a Scottish parliament if it wins the next election, but only if the Scottish people back an assembly with tax-raising powers in a referendum.Scottish businesses are worried that an increase in taxes north of
9771 the border would deter investors and make them more inclined to site their operations in other parts of Britain."A very large part of Scottish development in the last five years has been inward investment. An extra two or three pence in the pound in Scotland would simply swing the pendulum
9771 the wrong way," said one company spokesman."Paying more tax would reduce the ability to invest and would certainly make us less competitive against England, which doesn't seem to make any sense at all," he added.However, one respondent said a tax increase was not guaranteed under a separate Scottish parliament, and
9771 he felt devolution could benefit Scottish business because "most Scots would like to see some form of parliament. It would give Scotland renewed confidence in their own destiny".While tax is the main gripe for the majority of companies, other factors such as uncertainty, inconvenience and bureaucracy were also cited as
9771 reasons for opposing Labour's plans.</

9778 NATO on Tuesday opened a new naval headquarters to provide a high-speed response to crises from the Atlantic to the Baltic.The new maritime nerve centre just north of London has up to 18 frigates, destroyers and minesweepers on call to be dispatched to trouble spots.Speed is the prime motivation."We can
9778 react quickly. We have standing forces ready and available. They are a core on which we can then expand," said NATO spokesman Jonathan Worthington at the opening ceremony for the new headquarters at Northwood, near London."This will now be NATO's principal maritime headquarters this side of the Atlantic. Any crisis
9778 in this area -- we will deal with it," he added.The newly named Atlantic building, which marks the end of the first stage of NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) restructuring after the end of the Cold War, has a staff of 220 from 10 NATO countries.The ships supplied by the
9778 member states are rotated on a six-monthly basis.Their forces were already involved in NATO's Operation Sharp Guard which enforced the arms embargo against former Yugoslavia.They are now back on duty in the Atlantic but can return to the Adriatic should the situation change.The new headquarters were officially opened by American
9778 General Jack Sheehan, NATO's supreme allied commander, Atlantic.Underlining the need for NATO to adapt to its new role of co-operating with its former Warsaw Pact enemies in the Partnership for Peace programme, he said: "We can no longer afford to view NATO in East-West terms.""Collective security does work," he told
9778 the top naval brass assembled from alliance countriesAfter the opening ceremony, NATO delegates sat down with their new East European partners for a seminar on how best to tackle the maritime problems they face together.These range from fishery patrols and oil rig protection to the counter-terrorism measures and intelligence sharing
9778 needed across the continent to combat arms smuggling."Terrorism is a cross-border affair. It makes sense to try and deal with the problem together," Worthington said as the two sides met behind closed doors.Northwood is also the command headquarters masterminding Britain's new joint rapid deployment force of elite troops that can
9778 be flown speedily to the troublespots of the world.</

9783 Britain had its largest current account surplus for nine years in the second quarter of 1996 and its overall annual economic growth rate was revised up to 2.2 percent, the Office for National Statistics said on Tuesday.Official interest rates were left unchanged at 5.75 percent after Monday's monetary policy meeting
9783 between Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.The current account deficit for the second quarter showed an unexpected 457 million pound ($712 million) surplus after a deficit of 786 million in the first quarter. Financial markets had expected a second quarter deficit
9783 of around 1.2 billion pounds."This improvement was largely due to record surpluses on trade in services and investment income," the statistics office said. The current account surplus was the first for over a year and the largest since the first quarter of 1987.Gross domestic product (GDP) grew 0.5 percent in
9783 the second quarter, up from the 0.4 percent growth government statisticians had previously reported.Annual GDP growth was now put at 2.2 percent compared with the previous estimate of 1.8 percent."The figures show a healthy and sustainable economic performance," Treasury minister Angela Knight said.City economists said the figures added fuel to
9783 Bank of England Governor Eddie George's argument that interest rates should be raised to counter the risk of a future resurgence in inflation as the economy gathers steam."Monetary policy is clearly too loose," said Kevin Gardiner, an economist at Morgan Stanley.The central bank conducted routine money market operations at unchanged
9783 interest rates on Tuesday morning, indicating that Clarke, who has the final say on monetary policy, had ordered no change in official rates at Monday's policy meeting.The Chancellor has cut rates four times since December and, with a general election due by May 1997, is clearly reluctant to raise them
9783 again. He overruled the Bank of England's call at the July monetary meeting for rates to be raised to six percent."The debate will now clearly shift from possible rate cuts to whether the government can resist pressure for a rate rise before the general election," said Ian Stewart, UK economist
9783 at Merrill Lynch.A breakdown of the balance of payments figures showed a surplus on investment income in the second quarter of 3.7 billion pounds, the highest figure on record.Services showed a surplus of 1.9 billion pounds while trade in goods showed a marginally lower deficit of 3.6 billion.The revised GDP
9783 figures showed construction and a broad range of service industries growing much faster than previously thought.Alex Garrard, an economist at UBS, said recent buoyancy in retailing and signs of recovery in manufacturing suggested economic growth would pick up in the coming months."With only subdued inflation left in Clarke's stock of
9783 feasible excuses, further rate cuts are almost certainly off the agenda for the time being," he said. ($1=.6420 Pound)</

9801 The UK's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had fined UBS Ltd 20,000 stg and required the investment bank to pay costs of 8,000 stg "for matters relating to mismarking of positions".The watchdog said in a statement it had also disciplined former UBS warrants and convertibles traders
9801 James Keen and Mark Larkin following the conclusion of proceedings it instituted in June and July 1995.UBS Ltd is part of Union Bank of Switzerland. Larkin, who was head of convertibles and warrants trading at UBS, has been expelled from the SFA's register of managers, fined 10,000 stg and required
9801 to pay costs of 4,500 stg while Keen has been reprimanded, fined 2,000 stg and required to pay costs of 6,000 stg, the SFA said.UBS and Larkin settled separately with the SFA while Keen took his case to the watchdog's disciplinary tribunal.The SFA said UBS had admitted it had failed
9801 "between March and May 1994 to speedily identify and remedy the fact that a number of positions held by the convertibles and warrants desk had been mismarked". The SFA said this breached its rules on marking to market, adding that UBS had "failed to conduct its fortnightly mark reviews in
9801 a proper and effective manner".When the positions were revalued in accordance with SFA's rules, there was a divergence of 8.9 million stg between the level at which the positions had been marked and their market value, the SFA said.The watchdog said it had taken into account the prompt reporting of
9801 the mismarking, the complete cooperation of UBS with the SFA, and that "at the material time, adequate external price fixes were not available". In addition UBS had, by mid-1994, strengthened its review process on its own initiative. The fact that the divergence values "were not material in context, carried no
9801 significant business risk and did not breach UBS' capital adequacy requirements", had also been taken into account, the SFA said.It said Larkin had admitted he had ultimate responsibility for ensuring the accuracy of the marks and that he failed to ensure the positions in question were marked in accordance with
9801 SFA's rules.He had also disobeyed an instruction, between July and October 1994, not to increase positions. "He concealed the trades he undertook in breach of that instruction by failing to book them on execution and by warehousing (them) with his French counterparty," it added.The SFA said it had taken into
9801 account Larkin's full cooperation during the course of the investigations. It said he was not currently registered with it and details of the action against him had been routinely notified to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).Keen was found by the SFA's disciplinary tribunal to have applied an inappropriate
9801 marking policy in his marking of five positions and by omitting to mark three positions to market. The SFA accepted Keen's marking policy was a house policy that he was authorised to apply. This involved marking long positions at a premium over bid "to reflect short hedge positions which were
9801 also held by the desk on the basis that the positions were held as swap positions".But there was no active swap market in the securities at the time in question and the positions were not marked at their market value in accordance with SFA's rules.The SFA confirmed that, except for
9801 the matters which were the subject of the charge, its investigations into Keen's activities while employed at UBS "disclosed no other matters of concern"."In fixing the penalty the tribunal had regard to Keen's seniority on the desk and the value placed on his performance by UBS," the SFA said, adding
9801 that Keen was not registered with it.-- Alexander Smith, London Newsroom ++ 44 171 542 7719</
