9810 An upward revision to second quarter UK GDP brings economic growth perilously close to the trend rate and will lead to louder calls for a rise in interest rates, left on hold for the next month at 5.75 percent.GDP was revised up to 2.2 percent from 1.8 percent at the
9810 last estimate. Trend growth is estimated at around 2.4 percent."GDP has not been that soft to begin with this year and anecdotal and survey evidence suggests it will accelerate as the year unfolds, so monetary policy is clearly too loose," said Kevin Gardiner, UK economist at Morgan Stanley. The Bank
9810 of England has upped the ante at recent monetary meetings when Governor Eddie George said he would prefer to see rates back up at 6.0 percent.Economists said George undoubtedly made the same request at Monday's monetary meeting, but Clarke rejected the advice. This is likely to be the shape of
9810 monetary meetings in the months ahead."The debate will now clearly shift from possible rate cuts to whether the government can resist pressure for a rate rise before the general election," said Ian Stewart, UK economist at Merrill Lynch. Stewart said Clarke may be forced to rise above the political difficulties
9810 and raise the cost of borrowing as the outlook for future inflation deteriorates ahead of the election."Growth in the months ahead will show spare capacity is being eliminated and the labour market tightening further, and you can't reconcile that with a 2.5 percent inflation target."A breakdown of the final GDP
9810 figures showed output from construction and a broad range of service industries grew much faster than previously thought. Gardiner said the upward revision to service industry output was expected. "We thought there was a bit more happening in the economy than the first estimates showed. When inventories are stripped out
9810 growth is now well above trend."The slower rate of stock building in the second quarter knocked 0.9 percent off GDP, so adjusted for inventories GDP grew 1.4 percent on the quarter.Gardiner agreed a pre-election rate rise should not be ruled out. 9810 a sensible Chancellor and it could backfire if he is perceived to be bribing the electorate with tax cuts and lower rates." "I think he'll bite the bullet and raise rates by February, before the election campaign gets into full swing," said Gardiner. A general election must be held by
9810 May 1997.Second quarter current account data, also released on Tuesday, showed a surprise surplus of 457 million sterling, the largest surplus since the first quarter in 1987. 9810 HSBC Markets. "The improvement came entirely from the non-goods side. Investment income in particular has risen sharply." 9827 news agency said troops launched a major attack on positions near the remote Iraqi border in the morning.Some 20,000 soldiers, backed by aircrafts dropping bombs and U.S.-made Super Cobra helicopters, began on Monday to close in on some 250 rebels who the military said were cornered in a forest in
9827 the mountains of Tunceli province.Around 15 rebels have been killed in Tunceli in the last two days, security officials said. 9827 divert the drive against the insurgents holed up nearby, PKK rebels attacked a police post in the well-guarded town of Tunceli overnight."They tried to enter Tunceli but came across the police special forces," governor Atil Uzelgun told reporters. "They fled, leaving two dead," he said.Two members of the elite police
9827 unit were wounded.The 12-year-old conflict costs Turkey an estimated $8 billion a year and damages its image, but successive governments have refused to discuss rebel demands for self-rule. More than 20,000 people have died.Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller on Monday reiterated plans for a security zone in northern Iraq to prevent
9827 PKK infiltration from bases across the border. Baghdad and other Arab governments have condemned the proposed zone as a violation of Iraqi territory.Ciller tried to calm U.S. fears that Turkey would drop the buffer zone and instead cooperate with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein to fight the rebels in north Iraq.

9833 has been buying foreign currency frequently in the past month to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond its permitted trading band.Israeli banks estimate the central bank has injected more than a billion shekels through its interventions."Daily (monetary) auctions and other monetary instruments are being used to ensure that the interventions
9833 are not allowed to alter the base of monetary expansion beyond what we in the bank think is warranted," Frenkel said."To date (the interventions) are fully sterilised."On September 2 the central bank suspended its daily auctions for loans to commercial banks in light of excess liquidity. 9838 China is unlikely to be either a major importer or exporter of corn this year, a senior Cargill grains trader predicted on Tuesday.China, facing sharp rises in domestic corn demand due to rising meat consumption, banned exports of the grain in 1994 but its future trade plans remained uncertain, he
9838 said."We know that there are good stocks of corn in the producing provinces of the northeast but central government has shown no signs of wanting to lift the export ban imposed in 1994," Fausto Filice, responsible for non-U.S. coarse grains trading at Cargill International in Geneva, told an industry conference.China
9838 appeared to have a bigger corn crop this year but demand for feed grain was also likely to keep growing.And domestic prices were now higher than world market levels, so exports would require some form of subsidy, which Filice thought unlikely."Anything can happen in China but for the coming year
9838 I don't see China as being either a big exporter or importer of corn," he said.The International Grains Council sees China's corn (maize) output rising four million tonnes to 108 million this year.It predicts China will import two million tonnes.China's meat demand surged between 1980 and 1995 to nearly 50
9838 million tonnes from a little over 10 million tonnes, according to figures given at the conference."In China meat consumption this year will be two and a half times what it was in 1986," Filice said.Assuming projected 1997 economic growth of some eight to nine percent fed through into higher incomes,
9838 meat demand would rise even further.Filice predicted China's current per capita annual meat consumption of 43 kilos would reach 50 kilos after the turn of the century.Increased Asian demand for feed grain, driven mainly by meat as wealthier populations chose richer diets, was one of three big factors behind record
9838 corn prices this year, he said.Others were competition from the oilseeds sector for arable land at the expense of grain and past European and U.S. policies designed to shield farmers from market forces.</

9841 Donor countries have averted an imminent cash crisis at the United Nations Relief and Works Agency, but the organisation which helps millions of Palestinian refugees said on Tuesday its finances remained precarious.UNRWA Commissioner-General Peter Hansen said the donors, summoned to an emergency meeting in Jordan on Monday to tackle the
9841 agency's growing deficit, pledged an extra $14.5 million towards UNRWA's services.He said the money had staved off the most immediate threat facing health, educational and relief programmes which the agency offers to its 3.3 million registered refugees in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.But he urged
9841 the world community, especially oil-rich Arab states, to accept greater responsibility for the welfare of the refugees from two major Middle East Wars following the creation of Israel in 1948.Hansen said before Monday's pledges of support, UNRWA was eating into the last of its reserves and looked like stumbling into
9841 1997 with no working capital and enough money in hand to finance just two to three weeks' work.Officials put the overall 1996 deficit at $45 million."Now with a little bit of money in the kitty, at least we won't go bankrupt tomorrow," he told a news conference. "If all the
9841 donors pay up we will make it through the year with a little working capital."He said another $20 million of qualified pledges might materialise in the next two months, subject to parliamentary approval from the donor countries.But he said the agency, facing spiralling costs because of its rapidly growing refugee
9841 population, needed more commitment from the international community to help reverse recent austerity measures which cut UNRWA to the bone.UNRWA says the refugee population is growing by 3.8 percent a year."Children are now more than 50 in each classroom, recipients of the special hardship programme are not getting all the
9841 commodities they should, and each doctor in our clinics has 100 patients a day," Hansen said.He called on the wealthy Gulf Arab states, their coffers swelled by a recent oil price surge, to follow the contributions of the poorer Arab nations hosting the refugees.Hansen said contributions to UNRWA of Arab
9841 nations outside the host countries Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, had historically been low. But they plumbed new depths after Gulf states reduced aid to Palestinians because of their perceived support for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait."As of now Arab countries (outside host nations) bear only one percent of the burden
9841 of UNRWA," he said. "If rich Arab countries contributed 15 percent of UNRWA's budget, amounting to $60 million next year, we would not have a financial crisis."The permanent status of the refugees is due to be settled under the final stage of a Palestinian self-rule accord between Israel and the
9841 PLO.Israel disputes the number of people which UNRWA says were displaced in the 1948 and 1967 wars. Arab states say it is also resisting the right of return to Palestinians, and the election in May of right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has further dampened hopes of progress."This refugee crisis is
9841 not the same as others," Hansen said. "We have here a population that has been dispossessed, their land, identity, dignity has been taken away, and they are the third or fourth generation of refugees."</

9875 As the battle against illegal immigration into the United States rages, a study released on Tuesday shows the number of illegal immigrants in California actually declined in the early 1990s.Research at The Policy Institute of California reveals that from 1990 to 1993 the net number of undocumented aliens in the
9875 state fell to an average 125,000 annually from around 200,000 in the late 1980s. The net figure dropped below 100,000 in 1992.From 1980 to 1985 net immigration, which excludes immigrants staying in the United States for short periods before returning home, averaged about 100,000 a year. Undocumented immigrants comprised 22
9875 to 31 percent, or 1.3 to 2.2 million, of the total six million new residents who came to the state during the 1980s. California currently has a population of roughly 35 million."The net flows (of immigrants) are broadly consistent with economic factors in California and Mexico," Hans Johnson, who headed
9875 up the research group, said in an interview.The study points to the booming California economy in the late 1980's as likely spurring illegal job seekers into crossing the U.S. border. But in the early 1990s, the state's economy slipped into a deep recession, causing sharp declines in employment. And in
9875 the early 1980s, California experienced slow growth.The jobs data would seem to bolster arguments for immigration reform, many of which centre on the notion that undocumented immigrants are taking jobs from citizens.The report's unveiling comes at an awkward time for conservative politicians, including California Governor Pete Wilson, who have taken
9875 a hardline approach to undocumented immigration. They argue it is on the increase and must be stemmed to save tax-payer dollars.Congress is trying to finalise an immigration bill passed by both houses earlier this year. The key sticking point centres on a provision that would deny public education to children
9875 of undocumented aliens.President Bill Clinton has vowed to veto the bill if it contains that provision.The study "reflects the fact that proposals dealing with immigration result from politician's scapegoating immigrants to further their own political careers," said Mark Silverman of the San Francisco-based Immigrant Legal Resource centre.Along with economic factors,
9875 Johnson also cited the federal Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 as contributing to the late 1980's influx.That law made it easier for undocumented foreigners living in the U.S. to apply for legal residency status, and prompted a rise in the number of wives, children and relatives joining family
9875 members, according to researchers.Johnson said the research group does not yet have data from 1994 to present. Those numbers will be telling because the California economy has been growing again while the Mexican economy has struggled. Looking at the results of the study, Johnson said net immigration would likely rise.However,
9875 he noted funding for border patrols also has increased in those years, leading to stricter policing of the U.S. border with Mexico.</

9888 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentPolicy-making members of the U.S. Federal Reserve began meeting on Tuesday to consider whether to raise interest rates for the first time in 1-1/2 years amid an atmosphere of intense political and economic scrutiny.The meeting opened at 9:00 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) and a decision
9888 on whether or not to change rates was expected to be announced at about 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).A slim majority of international economic experts surveyed by Reuters on Monday said they expect the central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to decide to bump up short-term rates by a
9888 quarter percentage point.Arguing for a rate rise: tight labour markets, rising wages and an economy that is operating in an "inflationary danger zone" because it may have overshot its potential.Arguing against: slowing growth, quiescent inflation and looming presidential and Congressional elections on Nov. 5."We expect the Federal Reserve to increase
9888 the federal funds rate by 25 basis points," said Richard Berner, chief economist at Pittsburgh-based Mellon Bank. "But the case for tightening isn't open and shut."The federal funds rate is the rate that commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans. It, along with the discount rate that the Fed
9888 charges on its loans to commercial banks, serves as a benchmark for other interest rates throughout the economy.The central bank has not changed either rate since Jan. 31, when it cut them both by a quarter percentage point. The funds rate is 5-1/4 percent; the discount rate, 5 percent.A rate
9888 rise now -- even a small one -- would mark a reversal of Fed policy and would lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and corporations.It would not be welcome on Wall Street or at the White House. U.S. stock prices jumped to another record on Monday, and a rate
9888 rise could dampen investor enthusiasm.President Bill Clinton is counting on the maintenance of a trouble-free economy before the Nov. 5 election to help him win another four-year term.In a sign of what is at stake politically, 78 members of Congress on Monday urged the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged.
9888 All but two of the lawmakers are Democrats.In a letter to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, the group, which includes House Democratic Leader Dick Gephardt of Missouri, saw a lack of inflationary pressures and argued that a rate rise would hurt, not help, the economy."Our concern is that an increase in
9888 the interest rates will slow the economy and drag down wages and the standard of living for middle and working-class families," said Representative Maurice Hinchey, a Democrat from New York.Also weighing in on Monday against a rate increase was the National Association of Manufacturers. "In the current economic climate, low
9888 unemployment has not translated into more inflationary pressure," the group said.The Fed itself seems split over what to do. A senior central bank official told Reuters last week that eight of the Fed's 12 regional banks had requested an increase in the discount rate, with three calling for a half-point
9888 rise."It's a good bet there will be a pretty rigorous discussion around the table," said Chris Varvares, an economist for St. Louis-based Macroeconomic Advisers.</

9894 Shuttle Atlantis ended its metallic embrace of Russia's Mir station on Monday, undocking after a five-day visit to pick up one U.S. astronaut and drop off another.Atlantis departed Mir at 8:33 p.m. CDT (0133 GMT on Tuesday) as the two craft soared 245 miles (400 km) above Earth, just northeast
9894 of the Caspian Sea over the Ural Mountains."Houston, we have physical separation," said Atlantis skipper Bill Readdy as springs parted the huge spaceships."You look great. We'll see you later," radioed astronaut John Blaha, watching the shuttle pull away from one of Mir's windows. "Have a good landing. Bye-bye Atlantis."Atlantis retreated
9894 to a distance of 400-600 feet (120-180 meters) from Mir and began two circles of the orbiting complex.The shuttle astronauts trained cameras at a jumble of interconnected modules as they flew high above China, the east coast of Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Ocean."Watching this undocking and the shuttle
9894 was absolutely incredible," said Blaha. "Wow, it's a sight that I'll never forget. I haven't ever seen the shuttle from this kind of view.""Your new home looks pretty incredible too," said John Uri, a mission scientist in Houston who watched pictures of the station beamed from Atlantis.Blaha had earlier swapped
9894 places aboard Mir with NASA's space record-holder Shannon Lucid. He joined Mir crew Valeri Korzun and Alexander Kaleri for a four-month stay in space.During five days of docked operations, more than 170 items of cargo weighing 6,000 pounds (2,700 kilograms) was transferred to and from Mir. The shuttle delivered about
9894 240 gallons (900 litres) of water and replenished Mir's supplies of oxygen and nitrogen.But it was not all work during the five-day link-up, explained Atlantis astronaut Carl Walz, who sings for "Max-Q," an all-astronaut band. Walz, nicknamed "Elvis" by his fellow astronauts, sang at a meal for the Mir crew
9894 aboard the shuttle.Later the shuttle astronauts were invited over to Mir for "Russian beverages and a taste of Las Vegas," Walz said. He did not elaborate.The two crews said their goodbyes early on Monday with a final round of handshakes and hugs. The hatches between the shuttle and station swung
9894 shut shortly after 7 a.m. CDT (1200 GMT).Shannon Lucid, preparing to head home after a record-breaking tour of duty, had mixed emotions as she departed."I'm really happy and I also feel a little sad," she told reporters in a televised news conference broadcast from Mir on Monday. "This has been
9894 my home for six months. I've had a great time here, but obviously I'm very anxious to go back to my real home in Houston, Texas."For Blaha, Atlantis' departure would in some ways be a relief, he said. "We've been so busy ... I'm looking forward to the pace slowing
9894 down a little bit."Blaha is the second of seven U.S. astronauts who will continuously man the Russian orbiting complex until 1998.Atlantis is due to return to Earth on Thursday. Landing is planned at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre, but strict weather restrictions, imposed after a shuttle hydraulic power unit failed, may
9894 force a diversion to Edwards Air Force Base in California.The shuttle's touchdown will mark the end of a 188-day stay in space for Lucid, the longest by an American and a record for a woman.</

9895 on to Washington aboard the private jet of Katharine Graham, the retired publisher of the Washington Post.</

9897 Nearly half of South Carolina residents believe the state should immediately close the Barnwell radioactive landfill, which generated $90 million for school construction last year, the State newspaper reported Monday.In a poll conducted for the newspaper, nearly 50 percent opposed the operation of the low-level nuclear waste disposal site.Republicans were
9897 split on the issue, with 38 percent saying it should be closed and 36 percent preferring that it remain open. Democrats favored closing the facility 45 percent to 18 percent. Among independents, 58 percent favored closing it and 22 percent said it should be kept open.Among those who felt the
9897 facility should stay open, the money generated for education was the main reason cited.The poll suggets the landfill could become a major issue in the upcoming legislative elections.The regional landfill had been scheduled to close last year, but the North Carolina facility that was to replace it was nowhere near
9897 ready to open.Rather than leave South Carolina businesses with nowhere to dispose of low-level radioactive waste, Republican Gov. David Beasley proposed keeping the facility open and earmarking disposal fee revenues for education.Last year, the landfill generated $90 million for school construction and $20 million for scholarships.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</

9917 Privately held OptiMark Technologies Inc. said Tuesday that it has developed a new "three-dimensional" trading system that will reduce price volatility and increase liquidity in securities markets.The Colorado-based company said the Pacific Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange already have agreed to use its system, which allows traders
9917 to specify a variety of trading prices and block sizes and the degree of their willingness to trade under those differing circumstances.OptiMark said it intends to offer the system non-exclusively as an integrated transaction facility for all exchanges and distribute the service through existing vendors.The new system, which has financial
9917 backing from Dow Jones &amp; Co., will be offered first in stock markets and then in related options markets, OptiMark said.The system also will be accessible over the IBM Global Network, a private voice, data and video network operated by International Business Machines Corp., which provided the technological infrastructure for
9917 the system.The company, based in Durango, Colo., was due to unveil the system formally on Wednesday at Pace University's Third Annual Securities Industry Conference in New York.OptiMark said its system recognises that usually there is not just one price at which a trader is willing to buy or sell shares.
9917 Typically, there is a range of acceptable prices, depending on such factors as the size of the block, timing and market direction.Existing trading systems can represent a single price in a bid or offer, but these are only a crude approximation of buyers' and sellers' real intentions, the company said.OptiMark
9917 said its system will enable buyers and sellers to specify a variety of trading preferences and, based on those preferences, to find the best trade prices and block sizes to complete transactions -- while keeping traders' anonymity and trading strategies secret."Through OptiMark buyers and sellers are able to represent their
9917 intentions with visually intuitive 'satisfaction profiles' and can take advantage of the sophisticated search and matching capability of the system's supercomputer to execute entire transactions at optimal prices," OptiMark President Terry Rickard said in a statement.OptiMark said that while its technology is protected by multiple patents pending, the company's strategy
9917 is to offer the new system non-exclusively as an integrated transaction facility for all exchanges.It said the system, designed for maximum participation via an open architecture, will run over various distribution networks to both new and existing trader workstations.The company said the system will be distributed through existing market data
9917 services, including Dow Jones Telerate, which serves the financial community in 83 countries.The system will also be available non-exclusively to other network providers that wish to carry the service.IBM is providing the complete technology infrastructure to support the project, including an RS/6000 SP supercomputer that will power OptiMark, as well
9917 as software development, operations support and other integration services.</

9958 The FBI has agreed to work with the the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve, to investigate a leak about internal Fed recommendations for higher interest rates, Justice Department officials said.They said the Fed last week asked the Justice Department for FBI assistance in the inquiry being conducted under the
9958 direction of Fed Inspector General Brent Bowen and the request had been approved."The FBI has agreed to work with the Fed to find out what happened," one official said, adding that the inquiry would try to determine the source of the leak and whether any laws or confidentiality regulations had
9958 been violated.The inquiry stemmed from a Reuters report on Sept. 17 disclosing that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested an increase in the discount rate amid mounting evidence the pace of economic expansion is likely to remain brisk in the second half of
9958 1996.The story, written by New York-based reporter Isabelle Clary, quoted an unnamed senior Fed official. It caused bond prices to fall sharply and long-term interest rates to jump.The disclosure came ahead of the scheduled Sept. 24 meeting of the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to consider interest rate policy.Senate Banking
9958 Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, wrote to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan asking for an accounting of the incident."As I know you are aware, the premature disclosure of such sensitive interest rate information can add to fluctuations in financial markets, moving rates when no immediate change was intended,"
9958 D'Amato said in a copy of the letter dated Sept. 23 and released to the media."I know that you agree that these types of disclosures cannot be tolerated if we want to maintain the Federal Reserve's ability to effectively implement monetary policy," D'Amato said.Fed spokesman Joseph Coyne declined comment on
9958 the reported probe, which was disclosed Monday by the Washington Post and the New York Times. "We have nothing to say," he said. Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg also declined comment.A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Washington said, "We anticipate that if the investigation produces any evidence of
9958 criminal wrongdoing the U.S. Attorney's Office will become involved."Another official said Justice Department prosecutors would await any evidence from the FBI and the inquiry before considering further what laws might have been violated. "It is very much up in the air," the official said. "The question is what law has
9958 been broken. They don't know."A Reuters spokesman said the company had not been contacted by the FBI.</

9961 The government's budget deficit widened in August to $41.83 billion, a 23.6 percent increase from the $33.85 billion shortfall posted a year earlier in August 1995, the Treasury Department has said.Last month's deficit also was far higher than July's shortfall of $27.1 billion.One reason cited by the Treasury on Monday

9968 Lifting millions of rural people around the world out of poverty is a key to ensuring a secure food supply and protecting the environment, officials of the World Bank said on Monday."We are concerned that there is total inadequate interest in rural poverty around the world," Andrew Steer, director of
9968 the bank's Environment Department, said at a briefing before the bank's annual conference on the environment this week.The conference in Washington will focus on ways to improve living conditions in rural areas, which contain about 75 percent of the world's poor, and how that can help improve conditions in urban
9968 areas, restore the environment and fight poverty."It is not that the rural poor should be helped before the urban poor. The problems of both must be addressed, but the rural poor must not be forgotten in the global rush to modernisation," Ismail Serageldin, the bank's vice president for Environmentally Sustainable
9968 Development, said in a statement."A thriving rural economy will generate benefits far beyond the boundaries of any local area," he said."From the beginning of the industrial age, down to the amazing advances of the East Asian countries of the 1980s, a strong rural economy has been a necessary pre-condition for
9968 strong national economic growth."More than 800 million people go hungry every day and more than 500 million children do not get enough food to fully develop physically and mentally, and most of those live in rural areas, the bank said."There is a sort of seduction going on as world food
9968 prices have tended to be fairly low, that therefore things are under control with regard to food," Steer said."Even when food supplies are fairly ample" the desperately poor in food-producing areas go hungry, he said.Effective rural development is the best means to fight hunger, increase food production and protect the
9968 environment, the bank said.Food supplies must double by 2025 to meet population growth, meaning far more will have to be produced from the same or a smaller share of land, the bank said. That raises a potential for more hunger and environmental devastation."If agriculture is not intensified, in an environmentaly
9968 appropriate fashion, then the sheer expansion of the population and its requirement will lead to the destruction of the world's forests from slash-and-burn farming of poor, small holders who barely feed their families," Serageldin said.</

9972 The United States and Russia on Monday approved the first phase of a new agreement on anti- missile systems and called for negotiations on a second and final phase to start next month.U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said after talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov the two sides
9972 had reached a milestone in their attempt to work out which systems will be permitted under a 24-year-old arms treaty.The issue has bedevilled U.S.-Russian arms talks since the "Star Wars" days of the 1980s, with Moscow suspicious that the United States was trying to develop an anti-missile shield that would
9972 make the whole Russian strategic arsenal useless.The Clinton administration has been resisting pressure from Republican opponents to develop a nationwide missile defence system in defiance of the 1972 U.S.-Soviet Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) treaty, which forbids one.The arms agreement was announced after three and a half hours of talks which apparently
9972 registered little progress on NATO expansion, Iraq or Bosnia. Christopher and Primakov are attending the current United Nations General Assembly session.U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin last year asked negotiators to work out which systems were strategic, and hence limited by the ABM treaty, and which were
9972 smaller-scale "theater" systems which are not limited.Experts from the United States, Russia and the Soviet successor states of Kazakhstan, Belarus and Ukraine worked out draft accords in June on lower-speed systems."What we did today was to confirm that the United States and Russia accept those documents ... and are prepared
9972 now to move ahead as quickly as possible to complete the final agreement," Under Secretary of State Lynn Davis said.A joint statement said deputy foreign ministers would sign the part one agreement at the end of October. The United States and Russia meanwhile proposed that part two negotiations should start
9972 on Oct. 7.The phase one agreement specifies that all theatre missile defence systems with interceptor speeds up to three km (1.8 miles) per second are permitted under the ABM treaty, unless they are tested against targets with speeds over five km (3.1 miles) per second or ranges greater than 3,500
9972 km (2,175 miles), Davis told reporters.She said the Patriot system, used against Iraqi Scud missiles in the Gulf War, its successor system and other lower-speed systems the United States has under development had all been determined to be compliant with the ABM treaty.Christopher told a joint news conference with Primakov:
9972 "This important progress assures that we can effectively defend against theatre ballistic missiles, while ensuring the integrity of the ABM treaty."Primakov said that the successful conclusion of the second phase -- on higher speed systems -- "undoubtedly can move ahead the process of ratification" of the START-2 U.S.-Russian strategic missile
9972 treaty by the Russian parliament.Russian deputies have dragged their heels over START, which will radically reduce strategic arsenals and has been ratified by the U.S. Congress, partly out of concerns over possible U.S. violations of the ABM treaty.There was no sign of progress at the Christopher-Primakov talks on the thorny
9972 issue of NATO expansion. Primakov said there were still "different approaches" to the question.NATO wants to name at a summit next year the first former Warsaw Pact countries to be admitted to the Western alliance. But Russia, despite some recent signs of flexibility, still objects to NATO's borders being moved
9972 up to its own.State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns indicated that the two countries continued to disagree over Iraq. Moscow sharply criticised U.S. missile strikes on Iraq this month after Baghdad's forces entered Western-protected northern Iraq.Primakov "did reiterate the Russian position against unilateral actions," Burns said.Christopher said he had asked Primakov
9972 to convey his and Clinton's concern for the health of Yeltsin, who has admitted he needs heart surgery. But Burns said U.S. officials learned nothing new about the Russian president's condition.</

9974 Listen to the music of Duke Ellington and invariably you hear someone else, a little known composer and arranger who worked with Ellington for three decades but who only recently has begun to win recognition as his equal.The man was Billy Strayhorn, composer of such enduring classics such as "Lush
9974 Life," "Chelsea Bridge," and "Take the A Train," signature tune of the Ellington orchestra. Perhaps even more significantly, he wrote in close collaboration with Ellington, swapping ideas, creating arrangements, fleshing out harmonies and lyrics on tunes like "Satin Doll," which was only a riff before Strayhorn brought it to life.Few
9974 people outside the close-knit world of jazz musicians knew of Strayhorn's crucial role in the Ellington organisation. While Ellington gave him credit -- and they considered each other best friends -- it was never at his own expense. Ellington's name after all sold the concert tickets.Strayhorn remained in Ellington's shadow
9974 his entire life, dying of cancer in 1967 at age 51, a genius without a public following. Now that may be changing. With recent critically acclaimed biography "Lush Life" (Farrar, Straus and Giroux) by David Hajdu, and several recordings focusing on Strayhorn's work, the shadow is finally lifting."He was a
9974 genuinely heroic figure because he defied so many of the rules -- the things our culture values so strongly like the pursuit of fame, fortune and ego gratification," Hajdu told Reuters. He suggests that another reason for Strayhorn's relative anonymity was that he was gay -- and openly so in
9974 an intolerant era. He could afford to be out of the closet in the 1950s within the security of the Ellington fold, but had he been on his own as a gay, black bandleader he would have been the target of prejudice.As a result, only his close friends and the
9974 musicians who played his works really knew of his artistic accomplishments -- ones which are now being viewed as on a par with Ellington and other great composers of 20th century American music."There wasn't anybody who didn't want to talk to me about Strayhorn," said Hajdu, who worked on the
9974 book for a dozen years and interviewed scores of people. "As soon as I raised his name in the jazz world everybody had something to say. It was like a dam waiting to break open. People wanted to talk about him but no one had ever been asked before."Lena Horne,
9974 who called Strayhorn the only man she ever loved, invited Hajdu to her house for an interview. He said dozens of others who have since died filled in the blanks of Strayhorn's extraordinary story.Along with the book, an artistic portrait of Strayhorn is emerging from previously unknown compositions stored in
9974 the Ellington archive at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington. Walter van de Leur, a Dutch musicologist who discovered the works, found that many had never been performed and few outside of Ellington's small circle even knew they existed. Van de Leur said Strayhorn on average composed at least a piece
9974 a week for the 30 years he worked with the Duke.Eight of the newly discovered works, which seem out of character with the Ellington Orchestra, appear on a recent CD from Kokopelli called "Portrait of a Silk Thread," played by the Dutch Jazz Orchestra. Nonesuch this year also issued a
9974 recording of Strayhorn material played by pianist Fred Hersch, "Passion Flower."Dovetailing with the Hajdu book, Verve compiled a disk of Strayhorn works by the likes of Ella Fitzgerald, Ben Webster, Joe Henderson, Sarah Vaughan and Oscar Peterson, among others. And Blue Note is reissuing the only solo work ever recorded
9974 by Strayhorn, out of print for decades.On these recordings, you hear the personality of the composer unfold. Strayhorn's ballads hint at sadness and longing but the melodies are infectious. The tunes swing hard at times but always come across with an airy lightness.He personified the big band era but added
9974 an element that was more complex, probing and introspective. He brought in elements of western classical music and was not afraid to go beyond swing, to early forms of modal jazz in the 1940s that would not be explored for several years.His best compositions, like "Lush Life" or "Something to
9974 Live For," express an after-hours melancholy. He called this time, when the martinis from the night before are still flowing, "halfway to dawn" and it was his favourite -- a time of vulnerability and honesty."Who is Billy Strayhorn? At first it was a mystery to me but listening to his
9974 music I couldn't help being struck by the depth and beauty and majesty of it," Hajdu said. "How could no one know him?"</

9975 Treasure Ventures Inc., said his salvage crew in the Bahamas recently uncovered artifacts including a bottle and pottery shards that indicate the presence of a Spanish ship.But it is too soon to tell if the wreck is that of the Nuestra Senora de la Concepcion, which went down in 1563
9975 and has become Treasure Ventures' Holy Grail. "If we find the Concepcion, it will be the largest treasure find in modern times," Burgess said in an interview from a bar -- the only telephone available on Ragged Island, about 60 miles (96 km) off the northern coast of Cuba.According to
9975 manifests found in Spanish archives, the Concepcion was carrying at least 25 tonnes of gold and silver, coins, chests of precious stones and jewelry to the king of Spain and personal items that belonged to the widow of Spanish explorer Hernando Cortes. 9975 booty from the Concepcion could top $1 billion.But that is a big "if."Treasure Ventures, which began sifting through eight shipwrecks this summer, has yet to find any treasure. Most of the wrecks they found appear to be from the late 1700s and early 1800s and have yielded a couple of
9975 cannon, a piece of gold jewelry, shards of pottery and spoons. Bad weather has hampered efforts to dive at the most promising site, said Burgess, the grandson of a Yukon gold prospector.The real target of the quest is the Concepcion. The hunt began in 1993 when Treasure Ventures sent three
9975 researchers to Spain to search archives. Dr. Eugene Lyon, director of the Centre for Historic Research at Florida's Flagler College, said he directed the firm to a researcher in Spain. 9975 to have yielded some $400 million in treasure.The Spanish archive search yielded clues to where the Concepcion was believed to have sunk. 9975 from the Bahamian government. This spring, divers began the search for the Concepcion.Treasure Ventures has raised about $850,000 from investors thus far to fund the expedition, which has its own home page on the Internet. But it has only enough money in its coffers to finance about one more season
9975 of searching, Burgess said.Treasure Ventures board member Michael Coopet, a Minnesota tax lawyer, is leading the search for a corporate sponsor. 9975 got seduced by the whole project. I fell in love with it," he said. "It's a very romantic story."The search for treasure at the bottom of the sea is largely the work of professional salvagers. It can be at the same time exciting, expensive and painstaking.For example, Terrawest Industries Inc.,
9975 a publicly traded company based in Vancouver, British Columbia, began searching in Cuban waters in July 1995 in a five-year joint venture with Canpac Divers Inc. of Vancouver and the Cuban government.Terrawest has found some wrecks but no treasure yet, said Don Myers, a spokesman for the company.At the moment,
9975 Treasure Ventures is in the same boat. "We just have to continue to look, searching, using our hunches," Coopet said. "And come hell or high water, we're going to find the Concepcion."</

9994 media services on October 9, says that the process will be a lengthy one in consultation with all concerned and that at the end of the day a world solution could be needed.He told Reuters in a recent interview the aim of the paper would be to find out exactly
9994 how the authors of pornography on the Internet could be identified and secondly how the pornography could then be interrupted.New media services were left out of the scope of revisions to the television without frontiers directive, but Oreja said that that did not mean they should be excluded from regulation

9994 of these messages," he said.The call for a European-wide solution to pornography and paedophilia on the internet is expected to be a central theme of EU justice ministers in Dublin on Thursday and Friday when they discuss ways of fighting the child sex trade.EU culture ministers could also discuss it
9994 at their own informal meeting in the Irish town of Galway on Wednesday.The discovery of four murdered girls in Belgium and a child murder, prostitution and pornography ring has focussed the world's attention on the child sex trade and fuelled calls for a clamp down on the internet, which at
9994 the moment is little policed and where anonymity is assured.Oreja said among the options raised in the discussion paper were the possibility of encrypting access so that only those who pay could see the programmes, or including a special computer chip -- commonly known as a V-chip -- to screen
9994 against pornographic content.Other options were a code of professional ethics in the sector or an international convention.Oreja, aware that Internet servers can simply move to a neighbouring country to get round any restrictions agreed at European level, said problems with satellite television had shown that national and European regulations were
9994 not enough."We know that national regulation is not enough, that European regulation is not enough...We may need to have a world regulation of these matters, but let's go step by step. We do not have a European regulation ," he said.The idea of a professional code of ethics in which
9994 the media would regulate itself is acknowledgment that European regulation of the internet could face opposition on freedom of information grounds."I think everything can not be said. I think that violence can have its limits, I think that pornography can have its limits. I am in favour of that, but
9994 it can be that the sector itself prepares a code of ethics," he said.He said such a code could help get round wide differences between EU member countries, who have widely differing laws on what can be considered pornography and eroticism.</

10008 Sweden put forward a detailed proposal on Tuesday on how the EU should step up its efforts to fight unemployment amid continued scepticism against the idea among heavyweights Britain, Germany and France.Denmark, Belgium and Austria have previously presented their own proposals on a special employment chapter in the treaty of
10008 the 15-nation European Union."With an employment chapter we know that the fight against unemployment will always top the EU's agenda," said Gunnar Lund, Sweden's chief negotiator at the inter-governmental conference (IGC) which is reforming the EU and its institutions.All member states agree that lowering an unemployment rate of some 11
10008 percent, more than twice the rate in the United States, is a key priority. But there are different views on what role the EU should play.Lund said a "large majority" were now in favour of an employment chapter in the treaty, which would legally bind the EU to consider job
10008 creation."There are still countries which are not delighted with the idea," Lund told reporters during the second day of the two-day meeting.But he said there seemed now to be a clearly more open attitude from France and Germany.A background paper from the Irish EU presidency confirmed that most countries were
10008 in favour of introducing "suitably formulated new provisions" on employment in the treaty.However, it added: "Others are opposed to this."Lund said the issue would be discussed by EU foreign ministers when they meet next week in Luxembourg.He stressed that the proposal in no way would interfere with plans to create
10008 a single currency in 1999, which some have feared, or automatically lead to more spending.Employment policies would remain mainly a national responsibility, he added.According to the Swedish proposal, EU countries would commit themselves to a policy which promotes "a high and sustainable level of employment and low unemployment."Each country would
10008 adopt multi-annual employment programmes and the EU would monitor the developments in each member state.In the case when a country's employment policies were not in line with EU objectives, EU ministers may "make the necessary recommendations to the member state concerned."To promote coordination of national policies, a special employment committee
10008 with representatives from each memger states would be set up to review the employment situation.</

10010 The European Commission said on Tuesday it would ask a group of experts to try to resolve a longstanding impasse over legislation that would allow firms to set up as "European" companies rather than national ones.The question has stymied European Union governments, which have been discussing the idea of a
10010 European Company Statute for more than 20 years.The main conflict has involved provisions on worker participation in company decisions, with Germany promoting its own system of "co-determination" between employees and managers and Britain arguing there should be no mandatory rules.Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn told reporters after a meeting of
10010 EU social affairs ministers that he would ask five "high-level" labour policy experts to tackle the problem.He also confirmed that he planned to ask trade unions and employers to negotiate rules to require national companies to set up procedures to inform and consult their workers.That accord could then be turned
10010 into EU law.The initiative -- which would be taken under the Social Protocol, which exempts Britain -- would complement the EU's "works council directive", which already requires multinational companies to set up such systems.The social affairs ministers generally supported the idea of setting up a committee to examine the European
10010 Company Statute, although Britain questioned whether it would achieve anything, EU officials said.The Union is coming under increasing pressure from industry to close what is seen as a big gap in its effort to create a single market -- the inability of companies with operations in different member states to
10010 form a single legal entity under EU law.But Germany has insisted on requiring European companies to set up procedures equivalent to its own system of employee representation on company boards. It rejected a recent Commission proposal to draw up EU-wide legislation on worker consultation that would apply to the new
10010 European companies, saying that fell short of worker "participation".Flynn said he would appoint the experts -- including representatives of the European Trade Union Confederation and the Union of Industrial and Employers' Confederations of Europe -- by the end of the year and ask them to report back in three months.He
10010 said their effort could also unblock legislation that would create legal frameworks for a European association, European cooperative society and European mutual society, all of which are also blocked by the worker-participation dispute.</

10023 a directive.A programme would allow the assembly more say in drawing up the legislation but the final text would be less specifically binding on the member states than a directive.Rapporteur Karl-Heinz Florenz believes one solution would be for the European Commission to formulate a coherent overall policy for EU water
10023 resources setting out the major objectives and the actions needed to achieve them.In a report expected to be adopted by the environmental committee, the German Christian Democrat suggests that EU ministers and the parliament should adopt this overall policy in the form of an action programme which includes explicit implementing
10023 measures.The Commission should then come up with a proposal for a water resources framework directive which converts this overall strategy into a legally-binding directive, the draft report says.Among the recommendations the committee is expected to make are a call for the EU not to dilute its policies on water protection,
10023 which recent Commission reports show is deteriorating.In particular, Euro-MPs are likely to criticise the Commission's communication on EU water policy - COM(96)59 - for disregarding EU treaty references to the need to respect the precautionary principle.This means "such substantive requirements as emission standards and quality objectives are largely abandoned," according
10023 to Florenz's report.The environment committee is due on Wednesday to adopt reports on two "daughter directives" on water policy. One concerns the quality of drinking water -- COM(94)612 -- the other Europe's bathing waters -- COM(94)36.</

10033 sharp cut in prices to prevent a big increase in production as farmers rush to use spare production capacity.A reduction in prices would help the EU withstand increased competition from cheap imports as it further opens its borders under the next world trade agreement.The EU would also avoid having to
10033 impose milk production quotas or pay compensation to farmers from former communist countries in eastern Europe when they join the EU.EU officials said that member states reacted as follows to the three options discussed in the report:1. 10033 beyond 2000. They argued that the quota system ensured market stability, adequate income for producers, secure supplies for consumers and an EU presence on world markets.2. Quota/Prices: Belgium, Netherlands and Finland backed this comromise approach which would allow some price fluctuation in line with international markets and increased imports due
10033 under the new world trade agreement.3. Gradual ending of quotas combined with compensation paid directly to farmers: Only Britain, Sweden and Denmark backed this free market approach.France, which criticised the report for being biased towards the free market option, said it was premature to discuss dairy policy reform.Italy said that
10033 any change in quotas must include an increase in its allocation which only covers 60 percent of its needs.The European Commission reminded member states that any changes would have to be compatible with the rules of the World Trade Organisation.It added that economic efficiency, export capability and social factors --
10033 such as steps to aid young farmers or producers in mountain regions -- must also be taken into account.The Commission is due to present dairy reform proposals early next year and it will be the subject of the next informal Farm Council in Zeeland in May 1997 under the Dutch

10039 as he opened the treaty for signature.The foreign ministers of China, France, Russia and Britain, representing the other four known nuclear powers, signed immediately after Clinton. 10039 requires 44 nations with a nuclear potential to ratify it through their national legislatures before it goes into force. 10039 scholars believe that any state that signs the treaty is obligated to abide by it. At minimum the document is expected to create an international norm that would make testing a near moral impossibility.</

10061 The Social Affairs Council formally adopted on Tueday the posted workers directive, which guarantees employees who are sent by their companies to work in another EU state the same pay and working conditions as those hired locally.The Council, after several years of debate, adopted the legislation -- which aims to
10061 ensure that cross-border workers are not exploited and do not undercut local standards -- as an "A" (nondiscussion) point.National governments have three years to turn it into law.Agreement had proved difficult because of a conflict between countries including Germany, France and the Benelux states who wanted to protect their social
10061 standards and others such as Britain, Ireland, Portugal and Spain who wanted maximum flexibility for their workers.The Council reached a provisional accord on the legislation, COM(93)225, in March after the text was watered down to allow governments to exempt some short-term workers from the rules.It adopted a formal common position
10061 in June, which was endorsed last week without amendment by the European Parliament.The legislation allows governments to wait for one month to apply minimum pay regulations to cross-border employees -- or allow trade unions and employers to negotiate such a delay.They can also exempt "non-significant" amounts of work -- to
10061 be defined by them -- from rules on minimum wages and paid holidays and wait up to eight days to apply those rules to assembly and installation work.In the latter case, the work would have to be performed as part of a service contract tied to the purchase of equipment
10061 and the exemption could not be applied to construction work.In addition to pay and holidays, the rules apply to maximum work periods and minimum rest periods, supply of workers by temporary employment agencies, health and safety standards and protection of pregnant women and young people.Britain, which argued that the text
10061 was too restrictive and included so many exemptions it would only confuse employers, voted against the legislation.Portugal, a big exporter of construction labour, abstained, complaining that the text included stricter rules for that sector than for others.</

10081 Europe's plans for currency union may steal the limelight at international finance talks in Washington this weekend amid questions about what it will mean for world economic growth and the dollar.Europe's finance ministers hold talks with the Group of Seven (G7) rich nations this weekend confident their plans for economic
10081 and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 are firmly on track.That makes all the more pressing questions on whether Europe's combined drive to squeeze budget deficits, in the face of persistent mass unemployment, will continue to dampen economic growth, making it the weak link in the world economy.And, crucially for the
10081 Americans, whether pressure for a policy change builds up to the extent that the fledgling monetary union goes for a weaker exchange rate against the dollar to lift growth and get people back to work."I am sure the temptation is very real. The core (richer nothern European states) look at
10081 the devaluers with a certain amount of jealousy," Banque Internationale de Placement economist Marie Owens-Thomsen said.French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters the last time G7 ministers met at a summit in France in June that he had been surprised how much EMU had dominated the talks.After talks this weekend
10081 in Dublin, where EU ministers set out the nuts and bolts of how EMU will work, that focus is likely to intensify both at the G7 and in the corridors of an International Monetary Fund and World Bank meeting next week.France in particular would like to see a stronger dollar
10081 to make Europe's economies more competitive in world markets, although it is unclear how much support it enjoys from Germany, its main partner in driving monetary union forward.In an interview with the daily La Tribune Desfosses published on Monday, Arthuis said EMU would mean calls for a stronger dollar would
10081 be listened to more. "It is indeed one of the reasons for a single currency," he said.Europe will have two crucial ways of influencing the dollar-euro rate -- in fixing it at the launch of EMU in 1999 and in managing a potentially big surplus of dollar reserves when central
10081 banks merge into the future European Central Bank.The euro is to be exchanged on a one-for-one basis for the ecu -- potentially a weaker currency since it is based on all countries in the European Union, including those whose economies might not be judged healthy enough for early membership of
10081 EMU.Most argue, however, that the one-for-one commitment will mean that the ecu will rise to reflect the stronger economies of core northern European countries likely to join EMU first."The key question is what is the political will in Europe to push up the dollar. At the end of the day,
10081 the ecu movements will be reflecting the political statements," ABN Amro economist Philippe Brossard said.That factor will also determine whether an expected surplus of central bank dollar reserves is used agressively to push the dollar up through intervention on foreign exchange markets.But for central bankers, seen ruling EMU via the
10081 powerful European Central Bank, there seems little risk of a devaluation which could threaten the primary goal of fighting inflation.For such anti-inflation hawks, the currency stability created by the euro, the liquity of the vast bond market growing around it, and the euro's potential role as a reserve currency, will
10081 lead to lower interest rates which will in themselves give a much-needed lift to growth.They also insist that Europe needs reform to the labour market rather than a devaluation to create jobs."Unemployment is a structural problem in Europe," Owens-Thomsen said, adding there was no evidence that devaluation would boost jobs.
10081 "The problem in Europe lies elsewhere."Brossard also argued that despite French calls for a ministerial council to oversee EMU, which so far have received only a lukewarm response, there was little chance of a united political front to promote devaluation."Clearly there is not a European will equivalent to the U.S.
10081 will to depreciate the dollar against the yen. There is not a government in Europe to deal with the exchange rate," he said.</

10099 Dutch Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma told a transport conference she advocated road pricing as a way of improving traffic flows and said the Netherlands was on course for partial road pricing by 2001."In 2000/2001 the Dutch government will, and I stress will, introduce road pricing on parts of the network.
10099 Other countries are setting up similar systems," she told the European Market for Infrastructural Projects conference on Tuesday.Jorritsma said she was not in favour of large-scale construction of new roads as this was not a realistic option for such a small and densely populated country as the Netherlands.Targeted construction aimed
10099 at opening up bottlenecks and filling in missing links would help eliminate traffic congestion in and around the major Dutch urban areas, she said.Jorritsma said investment was being made to increase the efficiency of infrastructure use, including the designation of special peak period road lanes, speed limits linked to time
10099 periods and situation-specific traffic information boards.Fixed costs paid by vehicle owners should be reduced and variable costs increased to tackle congestion, the minister told delegates. "The principle is 'he who drives pays'," she said.Jorritsma told the conference the anticipated growth in traffic volumes which would accompany economic growth in the
10099 coming years would place a greater demand than ever on transport infrastructure in the Netherlands.The Netherlands was faced with the problem of having to absorb the growth in traffic in a sustainable way, while at the same time giving priority to port and urban centre access."In practice this means we
10099 will have to invest more in infrastructure with the view to achieving more efficient use of existing transport networks," she said, adding this particularly applied to the use of roads for short-distance goods transport.Individuals needed to be able to make a conscious choice of whether or not they used the
10099 private car. "To enable them to make such a choice, we need to invest in better, more efficient public transport," Jorritsma said.Government had a clear role to play in making more efficient use of transport infrastructure, which also meant using more than one mode of transport in long distance goods
10099 transport."Most of the funding for these investments will have to come from national budgets. 10106 also involves trafficking in drugs, women, cars and nuclear materials and money laundering.But EU officials hope that the EU will be now so shaken that national governments will now put aside their reservations.Bruton said Ireland would urge the ministers to extend the mandate of the EU's embryonic police agency Europol,

10106 vital work analysing data provided by various police forces.Gradin said she would also urge the increased practice in member states of trying at home the many Europeans who go overseas as "sex tourists" to indulge in sex with children.Belgium has said it will push for a Europe-wide solution to combat

10107 shape to meet the conditions for entry to monetary union.The budgetary conditions have proved the most challenging of a series of economic criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty which must be met by would-be EMU participants.But Kohl made clear that the answer to the problems countries were facing in

10139 Telematics, the combination of telecommunications technology with information systems, is one tool European countries can use to help defeat traffic congestion as transport demand surges ahead of network expansion in the early part of the next century.Klaus Rehder, substitute member of the European Parliament's committee on transport and tourism told
10139 delegates to a transport conference on Tuesday that telematics was being examined as a way of improving safety, traffic flows and reducing emissions.The three-day European Market for Infrastructural Projects conference is discussing European telecoms and transport issues."We are sure that telematics advances must be taken into consideration in decisions on
10139 trans-European networks and stress that possibilities for bringing about a shift in traffic by means of telematics must be explored as well," Rehder said.Telematics allows road users to avoid congestion, pointing out alternative routes, while freight companies can keep closer tabs on their trucks with positioning equipment.The technology could have
10139 an important role to play soon as EU Commission forecasts see a doubling in transport demand by the year 2010 and only modest expansion of existing networks, said Rehder. "Other forecasts see even faster growth than that."Rehder told delegates the Commission was proposing to develop a European rail traffic management
10139 which involved neighbouring countries and proposed telematic applications for 2,000 km of the busiest European highways and 10 cities."A modest 10 percent decrease in road traffic congestion would bring cost savings of 10 billion ECUs a year," he said.The European Parliament was calling on the Commission to encourage private investment
10139 into telematics and even though the sector might be shy, the parliament was proposing to consider ways of using telematics in controlling police, fire and other emergency services vehicles.But large-scale telematics could not be introduced overnight. "Data networks need to be expanded and powerful low-cost computers must be developed and
10139 linked in networks," Rehder said, pointing out that only a limited number of transmission frequencies were currently available.Apart from health and safety issues related to electro magnetic radiation and driver distraction, attention should be drawn to data protection, Rehder said."There must be no possibility that personal data or movement patterns
10139 might be recorded outside users' control in a form that could be stored," he told the conference."I am sure when all these proposals and questions have been treated, telematics can contribute to a more intelligent use of infrastructure. New and additional efforts in telematics are worthwhile and will point the
10139 way ahead for the future," he said. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000</

10144 Sweden -- now running at just 0.6 percent -- had been held firmly in check."The prospect of inflation during 1997, as well as in the first half of 1998, being in line with the two percent inflation target is good," the bank said.In fact, inflation had been lower than envisaged
10144 in the bank's last report, which was published in June."This is primarily because the transitory effects of falling interest rates and import prices have been greater than expected," the Riksbank said, adding that economic developments had otherwise been in line with its previous assessments.With the threat of inflation firmly banished,
10144 the central bank said way was clear for further cuts in its key interest rate, the repo rate.This was underlined just half an hour after the publication of the inflation report as the bank trimmed the repo rate, which is its main monetary policy tool, by a further 10 basis
10144 points to 5.05 percent in what was the 20th such move this year.The repo rate has fallen by almost four percentage points from 8.91 percent in January, whilst the crown has steadily appreciated against the mark and the rate of inflation has continually fallen.The main cloud on the Swedish economic
10144 horizon has been growth, or lack of it, but the Riksbank said it was slightly more optimistic in this respect too."The economic slowdown towards the end of 1995 was brief, and there has been an upturn during 1996," the bank said."A total growth rate of three to four percent for
10144 1996 and 1997 combined is still considered most probably, although today the emphasis is in the upper half of this interval."What could upset the inflationary apple cart is wage-driven price rises. 10144 percentage points higher than in the first quarter.Deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten told Reuters Financial Television that although wages were the greatest threat to the Riksbank's inflation scenario, he did not believe the effects would be dramatic."I am not too worried for the next year or two primarily because we
10144 don't think that demand wil be strong enough to leave room for prices to go up," Heikensten said."But in a longer perspective the wages increases we have had here during 1996 are clearly too high."Analysts said that although the Riksbank would be keeping a close check on consumer demand, any
10144 wage-led rise in inflation would be modest."CPI inflation proper would be via a pickup in consumer demand, but our best guess is that this will remain sluggish so I'm looking for moderate upturn," analyst Katharina Hoyland of JP Morgan told Reuters.With almost four hundred basis points of repo rate cuts

10165 The United States, Russia and Norway will sign a milestone agreement on Thursday for dealing jointly with nuclear and other waste stored or dumped in the Arctic by the former Communist superpower's military.The Arctic Military and Environmental Cooperation (AMEC) pact will be signed by U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, Russian
10165 Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and Norwegian counterpart Joergen Kosmo at the end of an informal NATO meeting in the Norwegian west coast city of Bergen.Rodionov will attend a special session at the meeting, which opens on Wednesday. The 16 NATO defence ministers will also discuss what follow-on force to keep
10165 in Bosnia after the current mission's mandate ends in late December.NATO member Norway has pushed for the AMEC agreement in an effort to put more international focus on radioactive waste piling up on its doorstep -- Russia's Kola peninsula, home to giant nuclear submarine bases. The Scandinavian country shares a
10165 200 km (125 miles) Arctic frontier with Russia."We have been working on this agreement for a year and a half," Kosmo said. "It is another step in the continuing and emerging cooperation between the three countries in cleaning up the Arctic military environment."The Kola bases form an environmental rather than
10165 a military threat to Norway now that the Cold War is over. Cleaning up radioactive pollution on the peninsula has become a major issue in Norwegian foreign policy.The agreement also deals with the dumping of whole nuclear reactors in the sea during the Communist era.Although no final plans have been
10165 made, the signing is expected to be followed in the near future by a meeting with senior Russian military officials in Murmansk, the main city on the peninsula.The Norwegian defence ministry was tightlipped about the practical implications of the pact, but U.S. officials said in Washington last week the agreement
10165 would address radioactive waste handling and oil pollution."The principal purpose of the AMEC agreement is to change the environmental conditions in the Russian Arctic region," a U.S. official said.Six projects, four of which are about radioactive waste, will be formally endorsed by the ministers in Bergen.The projects include the joint
10165 development of prototype containers for interim storage of spent nuclear fuel and work on technology for treatment of liquid as well as solid radioactive waste.A plant for treating low-level liquid radioactive waste is already being built in Murmansk under a joint effort initiatied earlier by Norway, Russia and the United
10165 States.Norwegian experts say storage sites on the Kola peninsula for spent fuel and other nuclear waste from vessels scrapped under disarmament agreements are inadequate and radiation could leak into the Barents Sea.Russia has more than 80 operational nuclear submarines and two nuclear-powered cruisers stationed at bases on the Kola. 10192 Sweden put forward a detailed proposal on Tuesday on how the EU should step up efforts to fight unemployment amid continued scepticism over the idea among heavyweights Britain, Germany and France.Denmark, Belgium and Austria have previously presented their own proposals on a special employment chapter in the treaty of the
10192 15-nation European Union."With an employment chapter, we know that the fight against unemployment will always top the EU's agenda," said Gunnar Lund, Sweden's chief negotiator at the inter-governmental conference (IGC) which is reforming the EU and its institutions.All member states agree that lowering an unemployment rate of some 11 percent,
10192 more than twice that in the United States, is a key priority. But there are different views on what role the EU should play.Lund said a "large majority" were now in favour of an employment chapter in the treaty, which would legally bind the EU to consider job creation."There are
10192 still countries which are not deligthed with the idea," he told reporters on the second day of the two-day talks.But he said there seemed now to be a clearly more open attitude from France and Germany.A background paper from the Irish EU presidency confirmed that most countries were in favour
10192 of introducing "suitably formulated new provisions" on employment in the treaty.However, it added: "Others are opposed to this."According to the Swedish proposal, EU countries would commit themselves to a policy which promotes "a high and sustainable level of employment and low unemployment."Each country would adopt multi-year employment programmes and the
10192 EU would monitor the developments in each member state.In the case when a country's employment policies were not in line with EU objectives, EU ministers may "make the necessary recommendations to the member state concerned."Lund said the issue would be discussed by EU foreign ministers when they meet next week
10192 in Luxembourg.He stressed that the proposal in no way would interfere with plans to create a single currency in 1999 as feared by some, or automatically lead to more spending.Employment policies would remain mainly a national responsibility, he added.To promote coordination of national policies, a special employment committee with representatives
10192 from each member state would be set up to review the employment situation.</

10201 Proposals to bail out countries pushed by almost unpayable debts into deepening poverty are so rigid that very few stand much hope of help before the turn of the century, the Commonwealth believes.In a confidential report, obtained by Reuters on Tuesday that will top the agenda at this week's meeting
10201 of Commonwealth finance ministers in Bermuda, the group argues that the international community has imposed too many rules."These restrictions reduce to only 11 the number of countries likely to receive multilateral debt relief, and delay relief so that only three will receive comprehensive treatment," it said.Several of the 53 members
10201 of the Commonwealth, which groups members of the former British Empire, are saddled with large debts to multilateral financial institutions such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank.Historically, poorer countries have been forced to borrow from these institutions, whose industrial nation shareholders only recently agreed to even consider
10201 writing off some of the debt.By contrast, major developing countries such as in Latin America were able to borrow from commercial banks with whom they have rescheduled defaulted debt payments on far easier terms.Britain has been pressing for greater help, including selling some of the IMF's $40 billion in gold
10201 reserves, to release funds for heavily-indebted poor countries.The issue will be one of the main topics at next week's annual IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington when industrial countries will come under further pressure to do more to help the poor."In theory up to 20 countries are eligible (for debt relief).
10201 But, in reality they are focusing on only two or three," one Commonwealth official said."The proposals currently being developed need considerable strengthening if they are to have a decisive impact on the multilateral debt problems of heavily indebted poor countries" the report said, adding it welcomed steps taken so far.The
10201 report, which Commonwealth sources said had input from the British Treasury, said the criteria and timeframe for countries to join in any relief scheme were too restrictive.For example, a country has to have a proven three-year economic track record before individual creditor countries will help and another three after that
10201 before the multilateral financial agencies step in.The question of the IMF selling some of its gold has yet to be resolved after two years of debate, with countries such as Germany fiercely opposed to selling what they see as the IMF's family jewels.Last week, the IMF's board put off any
10201 decision on the sale of gold until consensus could be reached.Financing the relief is also open to doubt.The report said that the IMF and World Bank estimate the cost of the initiative would be $5.6 billion, of which they will provide only $2 billion.It urged the criteria be changed so
10201 that as many countries as possible get relief by 2000 and that it is funded fairly among all the creditors and not shouldered by budget-conscious industrial countries.</

10203 European Union employees who are sent by their companies to work in another EU state must be offered the same pay and working conditions as those hired locally, under legislation adopted on Tuesday.EU social affairs ministers, after several years of debate, formally adopted the "posted workers directive", which aims to
10203 ensure that cross-border workers are not exploited and do not undercut local standards.National governments have three years to turn it into law.Agreement had proved difficult because of a conflict between countries including Germany, France and the Benelux states which wanted to protect their social standards and others such as Britain,
10203 Ireland, Portugal and Spain who wanted maximum flexibility for their workers.The ministers reached a provisional accord in March, which was endorsed last week by the European Parliament, after the draft was watered down to allow governments to exempt some short-term workers from the rules.Governments can wait for one month, for
10203 example, to apply minimum pay regulations to cross-border employees -- or allow trade unions and employers to negotiate such a delay.They can also exempt "non-significant" amounts of work -- to be defined by them -- from rules on minimum wages and paid holidays and wait up to eight days to
10203 apply those rules to assembly and installation work.In the latter case, the work would have to be performed as part of a service contract tied to the purchase of equipment and the exemption could not be applied to construction work.In addition to pay and holidays, the rules apply to maximum
10203 work periods and minimum rest periods, supply of workers by temporary employment agencies, health and safety standards and protection of pregnant women and young people.Britain, which argued that the text was too restrictive and included so many exemptions it would only confuse employers, voted against the legislation.Portugal, a big exporter
10203 of construction labour, abstained, complaining that the text included stricter rules for that sector than for others.</
