11097 Dial Corp Wednesday announced a restructuring that will eliminate 250 positions and result in pretax savings of $40 million. The following is a copy of the company's news release.--------------- PRESS RELEASE ---------------------PHOENIX--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 25, (Reuter)The Dial Corporation (NYSE: DL), the consumer products company that was created in an Aug. 15
11097 spin-off, announced today that its board of directors has approved a plan to streamline its management and administrative organization, eliminate approximately 250 positions and sell or discontinue a number of underperforming brands and related assets.The result will be an annual pretax savings of $40 million.Malcolm Jozoff, Dial's chairman, president and
11097 chief executive officer, said that approximately one-half of the $40 million annual pretax savings will be targeted to improve short-term profitability (earnings per share), while the balance will be invested to enhance Dial's long-term profitability through investments in brand equity and technology efficiencies."These actions are essential to improve Dial's profitability
11097 and earnings," Jozoff said.The company expects to take a one-time write-off of about $50 million in the third quarter of 1996 to cover all costs associated with the streamlining."We are determined to structure The Dial Corporation for success," Jozoff said. "We are realists. If a company our size doesn't take
11097 the difficult steps necessary to achieve profitable growth, some bigger company just might come along and show us how to do it. We know what we have to do, and we are doing it."Other companies have faced similar problems and have taken similar actions. Each and every one of our
11097 competitors has already streamlined staff, shed nonproductive assets and reduced costs. For Dial, these actions are essential."Further, Jozoff said that it has become clear that the company's 1996 earnings are likely to be about 15 percent lower than the consensus of security analysts' forecasts, which were formulated prior to the
11097 spin-off. He noted that slowness in new-product acceptance and selected detergent and personal care programs has impacted results."The streamlining will let us work on these problems quickly as a way to rebuild Dial's profitability and strength," Jozoff said.Following are key elements of the streamlining:Centralize management and reduce overhead: Dial is
11097 centralizing its management functions to eliminate redundancy, increase flexibility and provide better focus and clearer lines of accountability. For example, Dial will generate greater buying clout with suppliers by combining its six purchasing locations into one and will reach a critical mass in research and development by combining laboratories and
11097 functions. Overall, Dial expects to reduce its overhead expenses by 20 percent.As a step in the new corporate strategy, Dial announced today that Scott McHenry has joined the company as senior vice president, marketing and sales. McHenry was formerly a partner at McKinsey &amp; Company, where he co-headed the North
11097 American consumer packaged goods practice.Trim the workforce: Approximately 250 positions will be eliminated, with more than 80 percent of the reductions coming from management and administration. The workforce reduction will drop Dial's total number of employees to 2,800, down 33 percent from 4,200 in 1990. Affected employees are being notified
11097 today."We deeply regret the need to reduce our workforce," Jozoff said. "But it is absolutely essential if the company is to achieve its financial goals. We aren't adjusting our secretary-to-manager ratio by eliminating secretaries. We're adjusting it by eliminating managers."Cull underperforming brands: Dial will trim its SKUs (stock-keeping units) by
11097 about 50 percent. These underperforming SKUs represent less than 10 percent of Dial's total sales volume. Most will be discontinued, but some may be sold."This will free resources to build other products faster," Jozoff said.He noted that one-third of Dial's total product line had been introduced in just the past
11097 five years, a rate that could not be supported adequately by the company's limited resources."It's time to retrench and refocus on our key brands," he said. "I'm talking about Dial soaps, Purex detergents, Armour Star food products, Renuzit air fresheners and others that are major competitors. We are going to
11097 be disciplined in our approach to new product development and the targeting of acquisitions."Move the corporate headquarters: Dial plans to vacate its present headquarters space in a Phoenix office tower, a facility that it shares with its former parent company. Jozoff noted that the current headquarters location is too large
11097 and too costly for the streamlined company. The company is considering several metropolitan areas, including Phoenix, and expects to reach a decision by year end.In 1995, Dial (then the consumer products division of what is now Viad Corp.) announced the closing of six of its U.S. manufacturing plants and the
11097 elimination of nearly 700 jobs, principally at the production facilities. Management and corporate staff positions were virtually untouched during the cutback."Last year's restructuring was the first step," Jozoff said. "It reset the asset base and plant enrollment. Now, we are taking the next critical steps to reduce overhead, cull unproductive
11097 SKUs and finish the write-off of fixed assets. Once done, we'll have the ability to improve earnings per share, set the right prices for our detergents and bar soaps, increase consumer advertising and invest in selected new products. We are completing the streamlining job by reducing management overhead to a
11097 level that's appropriate for our new, smaller, more cost-conscious company."The Dial Corporation -- which has one of the strongest consumer franchises in the industry -- manufactures and markets personal care, household and laundry products and shelf-stable food. Its products have been in the American marketplace for more than 100 years
11097 and are found in nine out of every 10 U.S. homes. -0-</

11112 Argentina should stick to the currency board system that has allowed it to achieve among the lowest inflation rates in the world, IMF chief economist Michael Mussa said Wednesday."I think that, at this stage, to stay the course is the right prescription for Argentine economic policy," Mussa said at a
11112 news conference on the International Monetary Fund's World Economic Outlook report. A debate is growing in Argentina about the future of the currency board established by law in 1991 to end the peso's prolonged tumble against the dollar.The system, which forces the Argentine central bank to back every peso in
11112 circulation with U.S. dollars, gold or bonds, restored confidence in the local currency and helped defeat a bout of hyperinflation.However, pressured by a struggling recovery from last year's recession and record levels of unemployment, even some former staunch supporters of the currency board are starting to argue that it has
11112 outlived its purpose."This is an issue that needs to be evaluated on the basis of the medium term, rather than this month or this year," Mussa said in answer to a question on whether Argentina should keep or scrap its currency board.The IMF's chief economist pointed out that under that
11112 exchange system, which effectively pegged the peso to the dollar, Argentina achieved its best economic performance in over six decades.Before the 1995 Mexican peso crisis whipped its economy, Argentina GDP growth averaged about eight percent and it had brought inflation from over 5,000 percent to single digits. Mussa added that
11112 Argentina's economy contracted by only half as much as Mexico's did last year, and that Argentine inflation fell while Mexican consumer prices rocketed."So if we are doing comparisons, there is no doubt that the Argentine economy survived the shock a great deal better," he said.In its most recent report, the
11112 IMF forecast that Argentina's GDP would grow by about 2.5 percent this year after last year's 4.4 percent drop. Mexico's is due to rebound 3.5 percent this year after a 6.9 percent contraction in 1995.The IMF also sees Argentine inflation falling to 0.3 percent this year from 3.2 percent in
11112 1995, while Mexico's will likely end at around 34 percent, almost unchanged from last year's 35 percent."We now see clear evidence that the Argentine economy is recovering, and its inflation is essentially the lowest in the world," Mussa said."It will take some time, of course, for real wages and some

11118 The IMF said Wednesday it saw signs that European economic growth was starting to pick up but warned that the upswing could be hampered by the drive to meet tough budget goals set out in the Maastricht Treaty.In its semi-annual World Economic Outlook, the International Monetary Fund forecast that growth
11118 throughout the European Union would increase to 2.5 percent next year from 1.6 percent in 1996.But, it added, "The recovery in Europe may be weaker than projected because it may be restrained ... by the short-term contractionary effects of fiscal consolidation efforts being implemented in most EU countries partly to
11118 satisfy the Maastricht criteria by 1997."Uncertainties about "policy implementation" and concerns about high unemployment may also hamper the recovery, it added.Under the Maastricht Treaty, governments that wish to be founding members of European Monetary Union in 1999 must reduce their 1997 budget deficits to the equivalent of three percent of
11118 gross domestic product, although there is some flexibility built into that target. The IMF said it expects both Germany and France to meet the three percent target, although it made clear that depended on economic growth picking up as expected."The three percent deficit goal (for France) seems within reach provided
11118 activity strengthens during the period ahead," it said.Flemming Larsen, Deputy Director at the IMF's Research Department, was also encouraged by the progress that Italy has made in reining its its bloated budget."We are quite optimistic about Italy's medium-term outlook and scope for eventually meeting the (Maastricht) convergence criteria," Larsen told
11118 reporters.But he added that it was difficult to predict precisely when that would occur, because of lack of full information on Italy's budget.The IMF was gloomy about the outlook for European unemployment, forecasting only a small fall next year and warning that joblessness could even rise if labor markets are
11118 not comprehensively reformed.It expects average unemployment in the European Union of 11 percent next year, compared with 11.4 percent this year. "The real risk in Europe is that in the absence of comprehensive labor market reforms, unemployment rates could continue their steady upward march," the IMF said. "This underscores the
11118 urgency of tackling the problem more forcefully."It accused European governments of "excessive timidity" in labor market policies and recommended a whole set of possible reforms.They included: reduced unemployment benefits with tighter eligibility criteria and of shorter duration; lower payroll taxes, particularly for low-wage workers; minimum wage cuts; and changes in
11118 the way governments handle collective bargaining agreements.</

11129 Developing countries are reaping the benefits of structural reform and powerful macroeconomic fundamentals to boost economic growth, according to the International Monetary Fund.In its World Economic Outlook, the IMF projected that the developing nations would post average 6.3 percent growth output in 1996, up from 5.9 percent last year, as
11129 Mexico and Argentina recover, growth in Africa strengthens and the expansion in a number of Asian economies moderates.Activity in the emerging markets was expected to remain buoyant on the the basis of strong domestic fundamentals and continued strong capital inflows, particularly of foreign direct investment, the IMF said.Still, many countries
11129 struggle with macroeconomic imbalances and structural impediments that keep their living standards well below potential.The IMF called on emerging countries to reform their public sectors, remove price distortions, liberalize foreign trade and payments, open up foreign direct investment and strengthen the financial systems' capacity to mobilize domestic savings and allocate
11129 financial resources. Such reforms, essential elements of a comprehensive growth strategy, would need to be supported by prudent macroeconomic policies aimed at containing fiscal deficits, controlling inflation and maintaining external viability.To reduce the risks of banking crisis, "the emerging markets need to enhance the soundness of their financial sectors through
11129 strong prudential standards and supervision" the IMF said.While inflation is well under control in most emerging markets, the IMF said the combination of widening deficits on current account and rapid growth testified to excess demand pressures in Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.China would need to intensify its state enterprise reform, further
11129 liberalize trade, remove its few remaining restrictions on current account payments to strengthen the role of market forces in resource allocation, the IMF said.In India, the key to sustained performance would be ambitious fiscal consolidation that would relieve pressures on prices and the balance of payments, free resources for productive
11129 investment and provide a more conducive environment for needed structural reforms, the IMF said. Brazil would need fiscal consolidation and structural reforms, especially trade liberalization to safeguard progress on the inflation front and permit stronger sustained growth.Sustained adjustment efforts in Mexico should help to further strengthen market confidence and permit
11129 growth to become firmly established, the IMF said.</

11131 The global economy has shaken off weakness in western Europe and is expected to achieve healthy growth through next year, the International Monetary Fund said Wednesday.The IMF, in its semi-annual report card on the economy, gave good grades to the emerging market countries, saying they are reaping the benefits from
11131 an often painful return to fundamentals undertaken in recent years."The global economic expansion is expected to continue at a satisfactory pace in 1996-97 and over the medium term," the IMF report said.In a briefing on the report, IMF chief economist Michael Mussa told reporters that "We expect a moderate strengthening
11131 and continued good performance on the inflation front."The report estimated that the global economy would grow by 3.8 percent this year and 4.1 percent in 1997 after growing 3.5 percent in 1995.Industrial countries were expected to grow 2.3 percent this year and 2.5 percent in 1997 after growing 2.1 percent
11131 last year. Developing countries also showed vigorous activity, growing 6.3 percent this year from 5.9 percent in 1995. Growth will slow slightly next year to 6.2 percent.The report said the industrial countries showed uneven results with the United States chalking up robust growth and low unemployment with Germany and France
11131 lagging behind.However, it said that the outlook for Europe was improved as exchange rates came back into line, setting the stage for increased activity."Together with a correction of earlier exchange rate misalignments, this has improved prospects for a resumption of stronger growth in the latter part of 1996," the report
11131 said.It said entrenched inflation that has stalked policymakers for years is finally on the run but cautioned officials to guard the exit in case prices pressures return with the strengthening economy."Inflation rates in industrial countries, as well as in a number of developing countries have declined to their lowest levels
11131 in decades," the report said.It added that "monetary authorities will, of course course, need to remain vigilant to incipient price pressures as growth continues or strengthens. As an example, it said the U.S. economy was growing flat out with low unemployment and would benefit from a tightening of monetary policy
11131 so that inflation doesn't break loose.The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee met Tuesday, however, and decided to leave rates unchanged for now. Still, the IMF projects short term rates will raise about one-half percentage point next year.As it has in the past, the IMF scolded Europe for not taking
11131 the tough actions needed to reform its poorly functioning labor markets."For many countries, particularly in Europe, fiscal imbalances are related to shortcomings in the function of labor markets, which has resulted in a dramatic upward trend in unemployment over the past 25 years," the report said.It said that although the
11131 Japanese economy has responded remarkably well to stimulative efforts by the authorities with growth estimated to be 3.5 percent this year after edging up only 0.9 percent in 1995, it is probably too soon to move interest rates higher."But," it added, "official interest rates will obviously need to be adjusted
11131 upward as the recovery gets further underway." As a result, it estimated that growth in Japan would moderate to 2.7 percent in 1997.Turning to Germany, which is estimated to grow 1.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent in 1997 after being up 1.9 percent in 1995, the IMF said the
11131 country had acted properly in easing monetary policy over the past year to help secure the recovery."However," it added," it is still too early to conclude that the recent round of interest rate reductions has fully run its course."The report also made clear that the so-called transition economies of eastern
11131 Europe and the former Soviet Union that had often dominated the focus of IMF policymakers in recent years may have turned the corner."The rewards for comprehensive reform and stabilization efforts are very striking among the transition countries, where the results of economic transformation are increasingly visible," the report said.It estimated
11131 they would grow by 0.4 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1997 after five years of decline. The report also gave high marks to Mexico for coming out of the crisis that required a Herculean effort by the international community and the IMF, saying sustained efforts at economic reform
11131 should strengthen market confidence and permit growth to be firmly established."Particulary noteworthy was the the recovery in Latin America where Mexico has truly made substantial progress this year recovering from the recession of last year," said Mussa.</

11139 rates, were caught out by the U.S. central bank's decision to leave rates alone on Tuesday.Analysts said the U.S. move was a calculated gamble that the American economy will slow before inflation starts to rise. But it initially disappointed foreign exchanges where higher rates would have made dollar-based assets more
11139 attractive to investors.Stocks in London and Paris put on a strong performance despite an unsteady opening on Wall Street, but the star was Frankfurt which continued a bull-run to finish floor trade at a new peak.The U.S. rates move triggered a wave of buying for German stocks, pushing the DAX
11139 index up to end at 2,658.97, eclipsing the previous best close of 2,646.10 set on September 20.And trading on the computerised IBIS index finished close to its new record trading high of 2,665.65 set earlier in the day.Frankfurt traders who had sold shares in anticipation of an increase in U.S.
11139 interest rates went back into the market to buy at the decision to leave the rates unchanged."The climate is right," one trader said, referring to the U.S. interest rate news.But the volumes traded were low and traders were worried that the deals were not big enough for the market to
11139 feel secure with its new highs, particularly as most investors still believe a U.S. rate rise is possible soon.In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks ended up 0.6 percent, recovering from three day's of losses and taking heart from gains in U.S. Treasury bonds after the rate decision."There has been obvious
11139 relief that the Fed did nothing and we have seen a few buyers again this morning," said one trader.In the previous three sessions the FTSE 100 index dropped some 64 points from its near-record high of 3,974.3 on September 19.Some traders saw the market's strength continuing. 11139 a golden scenario, being good value and backed by the strongest economic growth in Europe," said Robin Griffiths, chart specialist at HSBC James Capel.But the U.S. decision to leave interest rates unchanged disappointed some investors, who feared U.S. rates will have to be raised even more later, traders said.Paris shares

11140 Just as seasonal demand for precious metals is picking up, prices have tumbled.Gold is weak. Silver is at an 18-month low. Platinum and palladium are cheaper than at any time in three years. And the retreat may continue amid fiercely bearish sentiment even as demand strengthens, analysts said."If there is
11140 a view in the market, it is usually strong enough to override the seasonal factor," bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland said on Wednesday."It seems since the end of August the (investment) funds have had a view, and they're pessimistic," he added.Typically, the middle of September is
11140 a signal for an increase in gold demand from Asia as well as from U.S. and European jewellery fabricators.But any seasonal boost has been overshadowed so far by a big speculative play led by U.S. funds last week. It sent silver plunging below its key $5 an ounce level, and
11140 its weakness has spilled over into the other precious metals.Gold, already stuck in a protracted downtrend, reacted to silver's sell-off by easing to fresh two-month lows just above the technically significant $380 an ounce level.Bullion closed at $382.65 an ounce on Wednesday, compared to around $415 at the start of
11140 the year.Technical analysts who study charts of historical prices to calculate future trends, said gold's staying power above $380 held the key to the rest of the precious metals."We've got a divergence between gold and silver at the moment, where silver seems to be breaking down and gold isn't," said
11140 Cliff Green of Trend Analysis."It's all eyes on gold -- if it remains above $380, then maybe there's upside potential for silver." If not, however, the complex is liable to crumble further.Silver had dropped to 18-month lows last week and was still vulnerable to losses to as low as $4.50
11140 an ounce, Green said.On Wednesday it was off lows but still vulnerable, closing at $4.92 an ounce. Silver, an industrial metal, is more volatile than gold and therefore an obvious target for speculators."It's very easy to move the silver market around and I guess people got tired of waiting for
11140 see prices move up to $6," said Kevin Crisp, an analyst at JP Morgan.Platinum and palladium have also come under pressure from silver after being undermined over the summer by steady supplies from producer Russia and slack industrial demand.Platinum has hovered around 2-1/2 year lows in recent days and its
11140 stablemate palladium dipped to three-year lows.Analysts said demand for gold bullion will rise as jewellers establish inventories for Christmas and Chinese New Year."Demand is looking reasonably good at this point," said Crisp of J.P. Morgan. "The sentiment is uniformly bearish for the metals, but that could mean there are some
11140 surprises in store."But so far, the demand trickling in has done little more than put support under the market rather than lead prices up. "The physical demand is taking up the surplus and slowing the decline. It's not enough to tip the balance," a dealer said.That's because professional investors have
11140 turned up their noses at the precious metals.Gold's traditionally role as a "safe haven" in times of political and economic crisis has been called into question as investors turn to more profitable stocks and bonds.A proposal by the International Monetary Fund to sell some gold reserves has also cast a
11140 pall on gold, though analysts say the market would easily absorb the amount in question."Funds are fickle, they don't care if it's gold or green cheese. They bought it in January, they're selling it now. The flucutations and flows are background noise," UBS's Smith said.</
11141 British researchers said on Wednesday they had found more evidence about how the female hormone oestrogen affects mood.George Fink and Barbara Sumner of Britain's Medical Research Council's Brain Metabolism Unit in Edinburgh said oestrogen helped the brain use more serotonin, a chemical important to mood and sleep.In a letter to
11141 the science journal Nature, they said oestrogen created more receptors in nerve cells for serotonin. The receptors are where a chemical "docks" into a cell."An acute surge of oestrogen in the female rat induces a significant increase of (serotonin) receptors in the higher centres of the forebrain, suggesting that this
11141 may be a key mechanism in the psychotropic effect of oestrogen," they wrote.They noted that previous research had shown clear links between oestrogen and mood, but said scientists were not sure how this happened."The role of oestrogen in affective disorders (depression and mania) is suggested by the fact that menopausal
11141 and postnatal depression are associated with a massive drop in plasma (blood) oestrogen concentrations, and oestrogen has been reported to be effective in treatment of depression in women."They said their findings provided "compelling evidence that the acute effects of oestrogen on mood and mental state are mediated at least in
11141 part by an increase in density of (serotonin) receptors".Serotonin is a neurotransmitter, a hormone that helps carry messages between nerve cells. Several new antidepressant drugs, such as Prozac, work by interacting with the serotonin transporter, while some hallucinogens interfere with it.</

11144 Britain has cautiously welcomed a new test for the human form of mad cow disease, saying it would only help confirm that patients who already had symptoms of the disease were infected.U.S. researchers earlier said they had found a way to detect Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease in living patients, whereas previously it
11144 could only be diagnosed by brain autopsies."We only have evidence that the test is positive when the patient already has symptoms," Professor John Pattison, chairman of the government's Spongiform Disease Advisory Committee, told BBC television on Wednesday.The British government said in March it had identified a new strain of CJD
11144 in 12 victims and said they probably caught it from eating beef infected with Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease).The announcement prompted the European Union to ban all exports of British beef and beef products.News of the U.S. test, which works by detecting a protein released into the
11144 spinal fluid by CJD, triggered speculation that dormant forms of the disease could be detected in people who had shown no symptoms.But Pattison rejected the idea and said mass screenings of the population would not work either because other brain illnesses could also give a positive reading."It looks as if
11144 this is a protein excreted into the spinal fluid when there is a considerable amount of brain damage...if you don't select the patients very carefully in terms of their symptoms, you do get positives in other conditions," he said.Pattison said it would be some time before the test could be
11144 adapted to detect BSE in live cattle."The information we have on cattle is very slight indeed. Only nine samples have been tested and only six were positive, so much more work needs to be done on that," he said."I think the emphasis on the moment is that it's only cattle
11144 who've already got symptoms who would be positive. We haven't yet got any evidence about whether or not it's positive in the pre-clinical phase of the disease."</

11148 An Asian lotus flower that can create its own heat probably creates a cozy, warm space for pollinating insects, Australian researchers said on Wednesday.Roger Seymour and Paul Schultze-Motel, zoologists at the University of Adelaide, said the sacred lotus had an almost unique ability to produce and regulate heat.It can regulate
11148 its own temperature in much in the same way that birds and mammals do, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature."In air temperatures varying between 10 and 30 degrees C (50 and 86 degrees F), the flowers remain between 30 and 35 degrees C (86 and 95
11148 degrees F) throughout a two to four day period," they said, saying the flowers seemed to use starch to produce the heat.Only two other plants, one a philodendron, have been shown to have the same ability. Others flowers produce heat but do not control it in such a precise way.Scientists
11148 think heat could help the flowers to spread their scent more effectively or may protect them from cold.Seymour and Schultze-Motel said the lotus could be rewarding the insects that pollinate it. Insects cannot generate body heat like animals can but need to be warm to fly."The environment in the floral
11148 chamber would maintain a high body temperature for the insect and promote not only feeding, digestion and reproductive behaviour, but also suitable body temperatures for flight," the zoologists said.</
11149 Two "dramatic" bursts of gamma rays from a suspected black hole some 400 million light years away have mystified and intrigued astronomers.A team of U.S., Irish and British astronomers and physicists said their observations gave stronger support to the idea that the object was a black hole and not, as
11149 other physicists have said, a compact cluster of stars.Writing in the science journal Nature, they said the bursts were much stronger than any flare-up of gamma rays ever seen.John Patrick Finley of Purdue University in Indiana said the gamma-ray flare probably came from matter being sucked into the black hole."Something
11149 is probably falling into this central black hole and we are seeing the energy it is losing," he said in a telephone interview.Black holes, believed to be collapsed stars that generate tremendous amounts of gravity, intrigue astonomers because they know so little about them. Their force is so strong that
11149 nothing can escape from them, not even light.Scientists can see energy coming from the matter that circles around the black hole as it is pulled in.This particular black hole, Markarian 421, is 400 million light years away in the northern sky. Finley and colleagues saw the two bursts in May
11149 while they were watching Markarian 421 from the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in Arizona.They had already seen visible light and x-rays coming from Markarian 421, but nothing like the gamma bursts."We know that there is an enormous amount of energetic material shooting out in these beams," Finley said. "They were
11149 incredibly intense in both cases. But also, the second one was incredibly short. That's actually more mystifying."Bursts of energy can go on for days, but the second burst lasted only half an hour. This made Finley, an astrophysicist, suspect that Markarian is indeed a black hole."People have speculated it could
11149 also be a massive, very compact cluster of stars," he said. But the short burst indicated that it was no bigger than our solar system -- with a mass millions of times that of our own sun.Finley said the observations would not have been possible a few years ago. New
11149 cameras and imaging techniques now allow physicists to "see" gamma rays as they hit Earth's atmosphere."The gamma rays that come from the object are coming straight towards us," he said. "It makes basically a big flash of light in the atmosphere."Most astronomers complain the atmosphere interferes with light or radio
11149 waves coming from distant stars and galaxies.But Finley said: "We are the only branch of astronomy which benefits from the fact that we have an atmosphere. Literally, the atmosphere is part of our detector."</

11159 British retailers on Wednesday launched a campaign to help stores combat robbery and violence, which cost the industry at least 1.5 billion pounds ($2.35 billion) last year.The crime prevention effort, backed by the government, aims to train shop owners and their staff to try and prevent retail theft and cope
11159 with robbery and violence.Last year, there were more than 15,000 robberies at retail outlets, up 17 percent on the year before, with losses more than doubling to 29 million pounds from 12 million, according to statistics from the British Retail Consortium.There were 11,540 violent incidents reported and 1,154 staff injured
11159 as a result.Jerry Walton, managing director of Whitbread Plc's off-licence chain Thresher and chairman of Retail Action Group, said the statistics did not tell the whole story. "The real victims are the innocent people involved in the offences who are threatened with violence, shot, stabbed or clubbed."He said off-licences and
11159 small chemist shops were particularly vulnerable. Thresher recorded 1,600 serious incidents in its 1,600 stores last year, although not one per shop, Walton told a news conference.He said big retailing firms had the capacity to train staff and support those affected by crime but staff in small shops were much
11159 more isolated."Independent retailers work long hours, frequently in difficult trading areas and suffer particular problems because they also live over or near the shop," he said.Home Affairs minister Timothy Kirkhope, giving his support to the training effort, said the risk to small retailers of being a victim of an attack
11159 was five times higher per employee.The training package, which includes two training videos -- Stop Violence and Counter Violence -- is sponsored by the BRC, leading retailers and National Lottery company Camelot LOTT.CN. The films show how to deter thieves and how to diffuse potentially violent situations.David Boot of retail
11159 consultancy Compass Vision, which produced the videos, said the increase in part time work meant staff were less experienced in dealing with aggression, or "store rage" as it has been dubbed in the newspapers. ($1=.6392 Pound)</

11169 A top British geneticist said on Wednesday that he and colleagues had taken a first step towards gene therapy by using genes to treat cystic fibrosis patients.Dr Chris Higgins, chair of clinical biochemistry at Oxford University, said the tests showed the technique was safe.The hereditary disease, usually appearing in infancy
11169 or childhood, impairs breathing and digestion.Eight volunteers with cystic fibrosis were given one dose of normal genes to counteract the genetic mutation that causes cystic fibrosis. Six of them were cured, temporarily, of the debilitating symptoms of the disease."It worked," Higgins said.Higgins said the technique used was not strictly gene
11169 therapy. "What we are really doing is gene transfer, not gene therapy. But we believe it can also have clinical benefit."True gene therapy would involve permanently altering a patient's genes, not just the genes in a cell that will eventually die. No one has done it yet.Higgins' group delivered normal
11169 DNA to existing cells. To make a more permanent change, stem cells, which give birth to other cells, would have to be changed.A step further would involve germ cells -- which would permanently alter a person's DNA and allow them to pass on the changes to their children."Not only is
11169 germ-line therapy not possible, but in many countries, like this one, it is not legal either," Higgins told a conference organised by Britain's Royal Society -- the country's academy of sciences -- on the moral, legal and ethical questions of gene therapy.Higgins, who said he was preparing to publish his
11169 findings, said the important part was that the therapy was safe. "It did no harm, no damage whatsoever," he said.But it only worked for three weeks, which did not surprise Higgins. He said the experiment delivered therapeutic genes into the nose, where cells are renewed frequently.Higgins' team is now analysing
11169 the results of a trial involving multiple doses, which could have long-term effects.One in 20 people of European descent carries the cystic fibrosis gene. CF is one of the most commonly inherited genetic diseases and it is a favourite target for gene therapy.The CF gene, identified and cloned in 1989,
11169 affects an iron channel -- an opening in the cell membrane that lets chloride, essential to cell function, in and out of the cell. That is why cystic fibrosis affects so many different organs, causing a buildup of mucus in the lungs and interrupting digestion.Most efforts towards gene therapy use
11169 viruses. Viruses work by injecting their own genetic material, either RNA or DNA, into a victim cell. They can be manipulated to deliver the correct gene instead, and are extremely efficient.But viruses can also be dangerous, and the body often develops an immune response that counteracts any good.So Higgins' team
11169 is working with liposomes, fatty molecules that can bind to the cell membrane. They can be manipulated to incorporate whatever DNA the scientists want to deliver to cells, although they are less efficient than viruses.The volunteers were given a nasal drip of the genetically modified liposomes. The target was the
11169 epithelial cells that line the nose. Tests were then done to see whether the cells of the volunteers were working normally. They were."We can deliver the DNA, it functions, it makes the protein, the protein works," Higgins said. But he estimated it would be 10 years before true gene therapy
11169 was possible."We are going to have to get a lot of smart science done, a lot of investment. There are going to be no quick fixes."</

The moves were needed "in order to maintain and improve the competitiveness of the industry".An invitation for the financial industry to
11171 put forward its views on regulation followed the release on Monday of the second report of the Deregulation Task Force.This urged cutting existing compliance costs and suggested the government should press financial services regulators to contribute to a net reduction of 100 million pounds ($156.4 million) over two years across
11171 the industry.Knight said the government accepted most of the task force's recommendations, adding that some were already underway. She said the regulators should aim to give the industry the right service at the right price, adding there would be cost savings for the industry if it helped to simplify the
11171 rules.She told a news briefing that suggestions by the opposition Labour Party for all regulators to be brought more closely under the umbrella of the Securities and Investment Board (SIB) were flawed."That would be both expensive and disruptive," she said.The aim of the changes was to "get the existing system
11171 working better."This view was backed by the minister for deregulation Roger Freeman, who said: "It's not about the structure of regulation but how it works and how it is enforced.""The next initiative is to promote a more cost-effective regulatory system which SIB is pushing forward. 11171 a lively debate on the Personal Investment Authority's (PIA) evolution project to ensure a simpler system for the retail financial services market," Knight said.The deregulation task force also called for the introduction of a civil penalty regime "for areas of malpractice such as market abuse, to tackle a wider range
11171 of cases quicker than the current criminal procedures permit".In addition it said a "serious examination of the continued use and selection of juries in criminal fraud trials" was needed. 11185 Britain's top employers group the Confederation of British Industry on Wednesday called for a British budget offering only minimal tax cuts but its plea may fall on deaf ears with an election looming, analysts said.The CBI on Wednesday, urged the government to trim its real spending target by two billion
11185 pounds ($3.1 billion) at November's budget and opt for tax cuts of only about one billion pounds in order to ensure public deficits head lower.But economists said tax cuts to the tune of at least three billion pounds were more likely although Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke would probably
11185 not break the bank."What we want is a budget which delivers a sound fiscal position," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of Barclays Bank Plc and the CBI's economic affairs committee. "The Chancellor should have prudence as a watchword."The Conservative government must call an election by May 1997 and trails the opposition
11185 Labour Party badly in the polls. As a result, Clarke is under pressure to cut taxes, cut interest rates and generally do anything he can to improve Tory fortunes.The CBI said the key economic point for Clarke was that Britain's public deficit, or public sector borrowing requirement, had consistently overshot
11185 targets in recent years.CBI director-general Adair Turner said the public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) was the one negative part of a generally positive economic backdrop and needed to be addressed.But Kevin Gardiner, UK economist at Morgan Stanley, said Clarke could cut income taxes by about three billion pounds on November
11185 26 and still produce a lower forecast for the PSBR if he got his sums right.Three billion pounds could take 1.5 or even two percentage points off the basic rate of income tax, now at 24 percent.Gardiner said the Treasury's projection for a public sector borrowing requirement of 23 billion
11185 pounds in 1997/98 was probably overcautious as the economy seems set to grow quite robustly for the rest of this year and next.If Clarke and his Treasury ministers could find some extra cuts in the budgets of government departments, and Gardiner thought they could, tax cuts can be justified.Here again,
11185 the CBI begged to differ. Turner said the spending cuts demanded by his organisation should come out of the government's contingency reserve -- a fund for emergency spending -- not departmental budgets."Further reductions (in departments' spending)...will not be easy," he said, adding that the CBI did not wish to see
11185 spending cut on education and training or capital infrastructure.Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets, agreed with the CBI that a neutral or even tight budget was needed, given the size of Britain's public sector deficit.But he said reasonably substantial tax cuts could still be afforded. "We think we will
11185 see tax cuts of several billion pounds, but given the state of public finances they will have to be offset by planned spending cuts."Loynes said that if push came to shove, and Clarke had to choose between tax or interest rate cuts for maximum political effect, then he would probably
11185 opt for the fiscal side."The tax cuts would have the highest impact, particularly in headline terms," Loynes said. "Interest rates are already at very low levels."Gardiner agreed. "More people pay tax than have mortgages, so income tax cuts would seem to be the political favourite."The CBI said any tax cuts
11185 should be aimed at reducing the burden it the lower end of the income scale. It also argued for measures to assist small and medium-sized enterprises to be prioritised. ($1=.6392 Pound) REUTER</

11195 By Neil Winton, Science and Technology CorrespondentBritish business has overblown expectations for electronic commerce generated over the Internet, a survey showed Wednesday.According to KPMG Management Consulting, Britain"s top companies expect to generate sales of about 170 billion pounds a year over the Internet in five years.But unless companies invest seriously,
11195 and soon, these hopes are unlikely to materialise."This estimate (of 170 billion pounds in British sales) is made despite very low levels of investment in the technology and the fact that more than 80 percent of the companies questioned cannot currently attribute any sales whatsoever to the Net," KPMG said.The
11195 survey reveals very low investment plans in Internet technology, and miniscule current sales generated through the worldwide computer network."Things would have to change pretty drastically for this to be achieved," KPMG partner Paul Baker told a news conference. "We are wondering how they are going to do it."The survey, of
11195 100 British companies with sales exceeding 200 million pounds a year, showed they expected 17 percent, or almost one in five of their sales, to come directly via the Internet in five years time.This compares with between two and three percent now."However, the survey also shows that companies' current and
11195 planned levels of investment in the Internet are very low and out of all proportion with their expectations," KPMG said in a statement accompanying the survey.The companies involved in the survey were from the finance, manufacturing, distribution and retail sectors."This gap between sky-high expectations and reality means that companies need
11195 to gain more knowledge of the Internet, more investment, and a serious look at how companies can benefit from this," KPMG consultant Jonathan Barling-Twigg said.The world of electronic commerce generates more hype than fact.Studies forecasting a world of future consumers lounging at home with their personal computers ordering pizzas, holidays,
11195 shopping, insurance or doing their banking, tend to have steeply pointing graphs.At one end, sales tend to be close to zero. The projection over five years or more often extrapolates sales into the billions.At a recent conference in Paris, IDG, the U.S. information technology consultancy and publisher, reckoned that by
11195 2000, 27 million European households would own personal computers, up from two million in 1995.Hewlett-Packard Co executive vice-president Rick Belluzzo talked about "pervasive computing", where information technology would become a utility like electricity. Devices would be as ubiquitous as toasters and electric shavers.This vision may be well on the way
11195 to becoming true in the U.S., where 39 percent of homes have personal computers, compared with 25 percent in Britain and Europe's 20 percent.But in Britain urgent action is required to kickstart the infomation age into life.</

11204 A British pathologist said on Wednesday that Central African coffee production could be crippled if an epidemic which has already shaved output in some affected areas by more than 50 percent is not contained."Wilt is a major disease in Central Africa at the moment. If steps are not taken to
11204 stop or contain it, the whole of coffee production in Central Africa is under threat," Julie Flood, tropical plant pathologist at the International Mycological Institute, said.Flood said wilt, or tracheomycosis, which strips coffee trees of their leaves and attacks the base through fungal spores, is most critical in northeastern Zaire
11204 but has now spread to neighbouring Uganda, Africa's largest grower."We need to act quickly...What is required in the short-term is a fire fighting excercise to eradicate the disease to uproot and burn diseased trees," Flood told Reuters in an interview during a break in a meeting of the International Coffee
11204 Organization (ICO).Flood said Zaire has suffered production losses of as much as 56 percent in affected areas since 1986.While Zaire's coffee production is only a fraction of Uganda's, with average annual exports of some 4.0 million 60-kg bags, some 20 percent of its population or some 8 million could lose
11204 their livelihood."This disease is a reality. Twenty percent of Zaire's population live off coffee," Noel Munaga, President of Zaire's Coffee Board said on Wednesday."If the disease continues to spread, some eight million people are condemned to unemployment," he added.Flood said that eradicating the disease in the long-term needs effective breeding
11204 programmes for resistant strains."That is the only practical and sustainable way of controling wilt disease," she said.If not contained, the disease, which can be transmitted through winds or rain splash carrying the inffected spores, could even spread to leading coffee producers in South and Central America."It could in theory (spread)
11204 but only if there was a transfer of material from Central Africa to Southern America...But I think the threat is more reasonably within Africa," she added.Further research is also needed to define the cause of this new wilt epidemic after the disease was successfully eradicated in Zaire in the 1950s
11204 through resistant breeding."We have to find out whether this epidemic has been caused by the pathogen mutating to a more aggressive strain, in which case this is very, very serious," she said.</

11205 banks will get involved in buying volatility and perhaps gamma trading, especially in the light of problems with Russia and the U.S. elections," White said.Gamma measures is the rate of change between delta and an underlying market while delta measures the rate of change between options prices and the underlying
11205 market.White said implied volatility of November options on December Bund futures was around 4.40 percent compared with 4.66 percent at Tuesday's close.On the slightly less popular December options, implied volatility was down to 4.62 percent from Tuesday's 4.97 percent, he added.Analysts said investors were back hedging their overall bond positions
11205 with markets likely to remain nervous over inflation and monetary policy until the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on November 13.Mark Robinson, options broker at HSBC Futures, said volatilities had come down only slightly since Tuesday, mainly because they had not really spiked up before the FOMC meeting."If
11205 they had moved up more you would have seen more unwinding, but given they only ticked up then there was no reason to see them come down more," Robinson said.Robinson said volatility might drift slightly lower in the next week or two.But if more strong U.S. economic data appeared, starting
11205 with September U.S. non-farm payrolls due on October 4, sentiment concerning the need for an interest rate rise would start to build again before the FOMC November meeting."If they had raised rates on Tuesday, the act would have been done and you might have had more volatility over the next
11205 day or so while the market readjusted," Robinson said."But this (the FOMC stance) leaves it all open and the next (rate) move is still up," he said.Robinson said such a situation "will always keep volatility ready to squeeze higher" against the general bond market trend toward lower volatility in the
11205 past few months.White said short sterling futures had one of the busiest days of the year due to bearish trades. 11221 Canadian miner Falconbridge Ltd. said on Wednesday that President and Chief Executive Officer Frank Pickard died of natural causes in Chile.Pickard, 63, died during a visit to the Falconbridge's joint-venture Collahuasi copper site in northern Chile, the Toronto-based company said in a statement.A company spokeswoman said the board of directors
11221 would meet soon to discuss Pickard's replacement.Earlier this year, Pickard led a C$4.1 billion ($3 billion) takeover bid for junior miner Diamond Fields Resources Inc. and its prized Voisey's Bay nickel deposit in Labrador in northeastern Canada.But Falconbridge was defeated by a richer C$4.3 billion offer ($3.2 billion) from rival
11221 mining giant Inco Ltd.Pickard is the second Canadian mining chief executive to die in recent months.Lawrie Reinertson, former president and chief executive officer of Rio Algom Ltd., died of a heart attack in July.Falconbridge is the western world's third-largest nickel producer and is owned 43.6 percent by Toronto-based Noranda Inc.</
11222 The Canadian government, stung by a near loss in a referendum on Quebec separation last year, has decided to ask the Supreme Court to rule on the legality of any future unilateral declaration of independence, Liberal politicians said on Wednesday."I am very happy we have decided to go to the
11222 Supreme Court," Member of Parliament Sheila Finestone, a Quebecer who used to be in the federal cabinet, told reporters after a Liberal caucus meeting in Parliament.The decision, which immediately drew the wrath of French-speaking Quebec separatists, was designed to lay the rules of the game out more clearly well ahead
11222 of the heat of any future referendum campaign. The Liberal government has consistently declared that the rule of law must be respected in any struggle for sovereignty."The minister of justice (Allan Rock) has taken a decision which I personally support," said Member of Parliament Nick Discepola, also from Quebec. "Nobody
11222 is above the law."Rock told Parliament he would announce his intentions in the coming days.Michel Gauthier, leader of Parliament's official opposition, the separatist Bloc Quebecois, argued that since the Constitution does not speak about the rules of separation, the Supreme Court has nothing to say. "It's our problem, our future,"
11222 he told the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. "It's not a problem that concerns the judges of the Supreme Court."Hammering Prime Minister Jean Chretien later in Parliament, Gauthier said in any case Quebec does not recognize the Canadian constitution.Separatists came within one percentage point of winning a referendum last Oct. 30. Chretien,
11222 himself from Quebec, came under scathing criticism after the close call for appearing to have taken few measures to guard against a split.It was not yet clear what questions the government would ask the court to decide or what would prevent separatists from proceeding with independence regardless of the ruling.However,
11222 Discepola asked: "If they don't do it legally, with the respect of the constitution, how can they lay claim to international recognition as a country afterwards?"Ottawa's appeal to the Supreme Court would be separate from Quebec lawyer Guy Bertrand's court battle against separation. The former separatist was mulling whether to
11222 continue with his demand before a Quebec Superior Court judge for an injunction against any future sovereignty referendums that would lead to a unilateral declaration of independence.In a move that sparked outrage in Quebec City, the federal government backed Bertrand's case in court, arguing that the Canadian constitution and the
11222 courts should have a role to play in any Quebec secession process. Quebec government lawyers argued that Quebec voters alone can decide their political future through a democratic vote in a referendum.Under Quebec law the separatist Quebec government cannot hold another sovereignty referendum until after the next Quebec election. That
11222 is to be called at the provincial premier's discretion and could be up to three years away.</
11223 A former Thai bank official arrested on fraud charges in Canada will face extradition proceedings starting Oct. 30, a Canadian court ruled on Wednesday.Rakesh Saxena, a former treasury advisor to the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce, was arrested near Vancouver in July by Canadian and Thai police.Saxena, 45, an Indian
11223 national and resident of Thailand, is accused of colluding with a group of other bank executives in embezzling $63.3 million. He has denied the charges.Justice Jon Sigurdson set the date for Saxena's extradition proceeding at a brief British Columbia Supreme Court hearing on Wednesday in Vancouver.Saxena, who was an independent
11223 treasury adviser to the bank, was granted bail following his arrest on condition that he post C$1.25 million (US$909,000) in bond and surrender his passport.At least four bank employees, including its president, have appeared before the courts in Thailand and were released on bail. The Thai government took control of
11223 the bank in May after it faced a public run on deposits.The country's central bank has said that the Bangkok Bank of Commerce has more than $3 billion of bad, risky and non-performing loans.</

11225 The Canadian province of British Columbia said on Wednesday it intends to sue tobacco companies in a bid to recover health-care costs for smoking-related illnesses.Legal experts believed the lawsuit, similar to 15 already launched by U.S. states, would be the first of its kind by a governmental body outside the
11225 United States.British Columbia Health Minister Joy MacPhail said the lawsuit was part of an intensified campaign by the province to fight smoking."I have asked the lawyers in my ministry ... to pursue all options around taking the tobacco companies to court for the health-care costs imposed upon our system as
11225 a result of tobacco use," MacPhail said in remarks distributed by her ministry."We will be pursuing all our legal options to the full limit."British Columbia, like other Canadian provinces, provides universal health care. Fred Bass of the British Columbia Doctors Stop Smoking Project told the Canadian Press news agency that
11225 smoking costs the provincial health-care system an estimated C$420 million to C$560 million (US$311 million to US$415 million a year.A ministry spokesman said no date has been set for the lawsuit to be filed, although the province had decided in principle to proceed with the case. "Clearly the intention is
11225 to sue," he said.The ministry did not release the names of the companies to be targeted by the lawsuit.Richard Daynard, chairman of the Tobacco Products Liability Project at Northeastern Law School in Boston, said he believes that British Columbia would be the first governmental agency outside the United States to
11225 sue the tobacco industry to recoup health-care costs of smokers."This should send shivers down the spine of tobacco industry executives who think the only threat is in the United States," Daynard said.So far 15 states have sued cigarette companies seeking reimbursement of Medicaid costs and last week Illinois said it
11225 planned to become the 16th state. San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Jose and 10 other counties in California have also sued the industry and Erie County, New York, which includes the city of Buffalo, also plans to sue.</
11226 A decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday to leave U.S. interest rates at current levels has renewed speculation that the Bank of Canada will soon lower short-term rates here, analysts said on Wednesday.But market watchers remain divided over whether Canada's central bank will take the opportunity to cut
11226 interest rates for the eighth time this year."The market is very much split on what the Bank will or won't do following the Fed's inaction," said Anita Lauria, an economist with Salomon Brothers. The Canadian money market has rallied sharply since the Fed decision, partly pricing in a Bank of
11226 Canada ease.Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill last traded at 3.73 percent, compared with 3.88 percent just before the announcenment. The three-month cash bill traded at 3.87 percent, compared with 3.95 percent.The Bank of Canada was seen being on hold ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on concern the Fed
11226 would hike rates 25 basis points. Now that the FOMC will not be meeting again until early November, many think Canada's central bank has a window of opportunity to cut rates further. Those expecting the central bank to ease monetary policy said Canada's output gap of about 3.0 percent and
11226 inflation rate of just 1.4 percent provide the Bank of Canada with both the incentive and leeway to cut rates further."I think it's very likely. There's a lot of excess capacity in the Canadian economy," said Barry Davenport, senior vice-president of treasury with Bank of Montreal. "If they see there's
11226 a window open which will enable them to provide a rate cut I think they'll take that opportunity."Another incentive for the central bank to lower rates is spending cuts by Canadian governments, analysts said. These spending cuts, aimed at reducing government deficits, will result in "fiscal drag" on the economy
11226 over the next several years which can be partially offset by lower interest rates.Market watchers sceptical that the central bank will cut rates counter that there are several major factors which more than offset the reasons for a rate cut.The reason cited most often is the easing already done by
11226 the Bank of Canada. Since May, 1995 the central bank has cut rates by 400 basis points. This year alone it has cut seven times, six of those independent of any Fed easings. "The bank doesn't necessarily have to ease anymore. Let's face it. They've done a lot of easing
11226 that's coming through the system," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.Gregory and other analysts noted that recent economic indicators, including employment growth, suggest past easings by bank are already begun to stimulate the economy."We're seeing some evidence that the economy is getting back on its feet
11226 to some extent. That might suggest an on hold stance particularly in light of the significant easing that the Bank has done," said Salomon's Lauria. Lauria said Salomon's position is that the Bank of Canada signalled after its most recent rate cut on August 22 that it has eased enough
11226 to boost growth. In the press release announcing the ease, the Bank said "the cumulative monetary ease now in place is substantial and can be expected to have a positive impact on the economy over the next year or so."Investors are now focusing on the value of the Canadian dollar
11226 for signals as to whether the Bank of Canada will cut further, analysts said. If the dollar, which gained following the Fed decision, appreciated further it would tighten overall monetary conditions in Canada, making exports less attractive. Analysts said this could prompt the Bank of Canada to cut rates in
11226 order to rebalance monetary conditions.The Bank of Montreal's Davenport said the central bank could cut if the Canadian dollar continues to trade near current levels at C$1.3663 and an appreciation to C$1.3635 would definitely trigger a cut.Gregory said the currency would have to appreciate much more sharply than that to
11226 trigger a cut.He said unless the currency "catches fire" and trades to the C$1.35 level the Bank will not cut rates to offset currency appreciation.-- Jeffrey Hodgson (416) 941-8105, e-mail: jeffrey.hodgson@reuters.com</
11227 Officials at the Toronto, Vancouver and Alberta Stock Exchanges say the sizzling hot junior mining sector faces closer scrutiny after a series of wild stock market rides."There's no question there's increased surveillance," Neil Winchester, manager of surveillance for the Toronto Stock Exchange, said in an interview."We're keeping a close eye
11227 on companies that are in play. We're certainly watching them a lot more closely that we would have." Regulators are trying to chill the junior mining sector after events set off by a pair of exploration companies traded on the Alberta Stock Exchange last spring.Shares in Timbuktu Gold Corp have
11227 been halted since April after its stock price shot up to about 30 from just pennies on drill results from Mali.An investigation suggested the company's ore samples were probably tampered with and that the company's then president Oliver Reese had past regulatory problems with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
11227 In May, Cartaway Resources Corp plunged to 2 from 21 after shareholders found drill results disappointing.Although the junior mining sector cooled down over the summer, it has heated up again this autumn and surveillance officials said they were taking extra precautions to ensure that announcements from junior companies were straightforward."I
11227 guess naturally every exchange is afraid of what has happened in the past with Cartaway and Timbuktu situations," said Toronto's Winchester. "That could very easily happen here. I'm not saying we're exempt from something like that." The Toronto exchange has been using geologists to double-check news releases about material changes
11227 before they are made public, said Winchester.Officials are also keeping an eye out for exaggerated news that may come from companies involved in Indonesia, Canada's Labrador and parts of South America that try to ride on the coattails of recent huge discoveries, he said.Last week, the exchange halted two junior
11227 companies -- Atlanta Gold Corp and Goldstake Explorations Inc -- to take a closer look at results from Indonesia properties. The Alberta exchange has introduced changes to restrict the involvement of brokerages in public offerings of junior mining companies. Brokerages can own only five percent of the shares under the
11227 new rules.Vancouver officials are being more vigilant in their monitoring of directors and officers of junior companies to ensure they do not overpromote their stocks, said Angela Huxham, in charge of surveillance at the exchange."We've got to be like that, because with junior companies there are problems in the market,"
11227 she said. "We will look at who got shares, how much they're spending on investor relations, review all the financial statements, all new appointments of directors;, anyone new, we check them out," she said. "We're very pro-active because we've got to be. It's a long haul."She said the exchange had
11227 kept Borneo Gold Corp halted since last week, asking for clarification of assay results from Indonesia.But the problems of exaggerated drill results and unscrupulous promoters are no worse now than they have been in the past, said Frank Giustra, president of Yorkton Securities. "I think the problem is there have
11227 been so many great successes - Bre-X, Diamond Fields, Arequipa," he said."This market is sitting on the edge of its seat hoping to find the next big one. People get overly excited and they jump the gun."Investors buy on the slightest rumor, hoping to catch the upside of a climbing
11227 junior company. They do not take the time to study the company's prospects, Giustra said.-- Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104</

11230 A controversial bill to ban the gasoline additive MMT will is scheduled for debate in Canada's House of Commons on Wednesday afternoon, parliament said on Wednesday.The bill, which aims to ban the import and interprovincial trade of MMT, faces a final debate before a vote by the House of Commons,
11230 the Canadian parliament's lower chamber. The debate will be preceded by a speech by Environment Minister Sergio Marchi, who reintroduced the bill last spring after it was set aside at the end of parliament's session in February. If it passes the House of Commons vote, the bill will go to
11230 the Senate for final approval before becoming law.MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, is a fuel octane enhancer. It has been used as a replacement for lead in gasoline in Canada since 1977.Two weeks ago, Richmond, Va.-based Ethyl Corp, threatened Ottawa with a US$201 million lawsuit under the North American Free Trade
11230 Agreement in a bid to stop the bill. Ethyl Corp is the parent of Ethyl Canada, the sole manufacturer of MMT in the country.But Marchi said he would continue to press the bill in parliament despite the lawsuit.The use of MMT in the United States has been permitted since late
11230 1995 after a U.S. Court of Appeals overruled Environmental Protection Agency objections to the additive.-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745</

11231 week. A second-phase shutdown for in-line testing of the work ended on Tuesday.Gas for September delivery at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.19/1.195 per gigajoule range, down from C$1.26 last week. October gas was talked at C$1.17 per GJ, about the same as last week.One
11231 Calgary-based trader said prices were expected to fall further on Thursday after players worked to get their accounts in order following the compressor work.The trader said storage injections were also expected to resume in the second half of the week. Withdrawals at Alberta facilities were said to total 434 million
11231 cubic feet per day.Meanwhile, British Columbia gas was trading stronger. Gas for export at Sumas, Washington was discussed at US$1.10/1.12 per million British thermal units, up a dime from last week. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624</

11235 Cominco Ltd will likely be the first of a string of Canadian base metal producers expected to post lower earnings in the third quarter, analysts said on Wednesday.Vancouver-based Cominco said earlier today it expects third quarter earnings to be down from the previous quarter because of lower metal prices, reduced
11235 thoughput and grade at its Highland Valley copper mine and scheduled shutdowns at the Sullivan mine and Trail smelter."I expect the same thing for all of them (base metal producers)," said industry analyst Tony Hayes at Credifinance. Since metal prices have been poor this quarter, "...there's very little they can
11235 do about it," said Hayes."If you don't have the price, you can't have the revenue."The third quarter has historically produced lower earnings in the mining sector because Canadian companies often schedule shutdowns during the warm summer months, said analyst Bruce Reid of Yorkton Securities.But this year, the period will hold
11235 a double whammy for most companies because of low metal prices."It's really copper that is the problem," Reid said. "A lot of companies are going to get slaughtered." Falconbridge Ltd and Inco Ltd will likely suffer because of their exposure to copper and flat nickel prices, Reid said.But the two
11235 nickel giants will not be hurt as much as Rio Algom Ltd or Noranda Inc because of their relatively greater dependence on copper, he said.Quarterly earnings will expose the stamina of base metal producers, said analyst Manford Mallory of Research Capital Corp.Only low-cost producers will be able to report credible
11235 profits, Mallory said. In times of good metals prices, most producers report solid earnings, he explained.But this quarter, "I think there will be more of a differential in the results."-- Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104</

11243 three have pleaded not guilty to charges of genocide and crimes against humanity.Rutuganda, accused of having been a top member of Rwanda's notorious Interahamwe militia which played a leading role in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, did not appear in court on Wednesday.He has been held at a civilian hospital

11246 The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda on Wednesay agreed to postpone until next March the start of trial against a Rwandan Hutu accused of genocide and crimes against humanity, ruling that he was too sick to stand trial next month.But the three-judge tribunal turned down a defence request to provisionally
11246 free the defendant, Georges Rutaganda, saying a sufficient case had not been made for his release."The tribunal decides that the date of the beginning of the trial of Georges Anderson Rutaganda is postponed to March 6, 1997," said the presiding judge.He added that the tribunal "decides that a sufficient case...has
11246 not been made out on both a legal and practical basis for the immediate provisional release of Georges Rutaganda."The tribunal noted that since being transferred to its headquarters in Arusha, Tanzania, Rutaganda had been seriously ill but was given medical care and transferred to a civilian hospital.Rutaganda did not appear
11246 in court during Wednesday's session at the request of his Belgian defence lawyer Luc de Temmerman.The tribunal was convening for the first time since May to consider De Temmerman's request that Rutaganda be set free on medical grounds.The tribunal was created by the United Nations after the genocide in Rwanda
11246 between April and June 1994, when up to one million minority Tutsis and pro-opposition Hutus were killed.The killings broke out in the tiny country after the assassination of Hutu president Juvenal Habyarimana on April 6, 1994. 11246 for Habyarimana's death -- and Hutus opposed to his military rule.The tribunal has a mandate to try only the top planners and perpetrators of the genocide.The tribunal, which has yet to begin trials, has indicted 21 people and is holding three in custody. They face a maximum penalty of life
11246 imprisonment if found guilty.The tribunal is supposed to begin its first trial on Thursday against Jean Paul Akayesu, 43, also accused of genocide. Akayesu's lawyers have sought an adjournment on procedural and other grounds. That request will be heard on Thursday.</

11289 The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, sitting for the first time since May, considered a request on Wednesday that a Rwandan Hutu charged with genocide be released on medical grounds.Tribunal officials told Reuters that Belgian defence lawyer Luc de Temmerman was meeting judges and prosecutors in this northern Tanzanian town
11289 to argue in camera that his client Georges Rutaganda was too ill to stand trial.The tribunal was created by the United Nations after the genocide in Rwanda between April and June 1994, when up to one million minority Tutsis and pro-opposition Hutus were killed.Its mandate is to try the top
11289 planners and perpetrators of the genocide, not the tens of thousands of ordinary killers.The tribunal, which has yet to begin trials, has indicted only 21 people and has only three in its custody. They face a maximum penalty of life imprisonment if found guilty.De Temmerman wants Rutaganda released so he
11289 can be treated for his undisclosed ailment."The judges and prosecutors are meeting to decide whether he should be released or not," tribunal spokeswoman Beatrice Lacoste told Reuters. She said he was "very ill" and the court would announce its decision later on Wednesday.The tribunal is supposed to open its first
11289 trial on Thursday with Jean Paul Akayesu, aged 43 and also accused of genocide. But Akayesu's lawyers have sought an adjournment on procedural and other grounds. That application will be heard on Thursday.Rutaganda, a former agricultural engineer and businessman, is accused of being the second vice-president of the national committee
11289 of the Interahamwe, a militia group which played a leading role in the 1994 genocide.He was charged in late May with eight counts of genocide, crimes against humanity (extermination), crimes against humanity (murder) and violations of Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions. Rutaganda, like two others held at Arusha, pleaded
11289 not guilty.Rutaganda is accused of arming Hutu extremists in April 1994 and ordering the murder of Tutsi civilians with machetes, guns, grenades and by drowning. The prosecution alleges some victims were forced to dig their own graves.Rutaganda is also charged with distributing weapons to Interhamwe militia and stationing militiamen near
11289 his office in Kigali to catch ethnic minority Tutsis.He is charged with participating in an attack on a technical school where thousands of unarmed Tutsi men, women and children were sheltering and taking part in a second attack on survivors.The six-page indictment says in June 1994 Rutaganda ordered people to
11289 bury the bodies of victims to conceal his crimes.The killings broke out in the tiny country after the assassination of Hutu president Juvenal Habyarimana on April 6, 1994. Angry followers including the army, militia and Hutu civilians hunted down Tutsis -- blamed for Habyarimana's death -- and Hutus opposed to
11289 his military rule.In Rwanda, where the death penalty exists for the most guilty, there are 80,000 detainees waiting to be charged, tried or released.The tribunal says 10 indictees are in custody -- three in Arusha, two in Belgium, one in Switzerland and four in Cameroon.
