11311 The prisoners in pink shorts stooped over enamel bowls of steaming food, splitting potatoes and sifting through meat stew with their fingers until the soldiers were satisfied.The guards at Rwanda's Gikondo prison were checking for weapons and other banned items at the thrice-weekly meal delivery by the families of some
11311 of the 5,000 inmates.They are among 80,000 detainees, overwhelmingly from the Hutu majority, waiting to be charged, tried or released for their alleged role in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.The wheels of justice, to punish those who butchered up to one million people in a period of three months, have
11311 ground slowly. Rwanda's post-genocide government blames the delay on the murder or flight into exile of hundreds of judicial personnel and on the destruction of courts and files.But early in September and with no fanfare the government adopted its Genocide Law, the crucial text for deciding levels of guilt and
11311 punishment in trials for years to come."We are making the last arrangements to start trials," said Gerard Gahima, the acting minister of justice.The new law divides defendants into four categories but states that only those in category one are "liable to the death penalty". Execution will be by firing squad,
11311 Gahima told Reuters in an interview.The law covers the period from October 1, 1990, to December 31, 1994. But the vast bulk of those who stand accused are blamed for their actions between April and June, 1994, when minority Tutsis and opposition supporters from the Hutu majority were targetted for
11311 extermination.Category one is headed by those who planned, instigated and supervised the genocide or crimes against humanity. It includes prominent people, such as priests, who perpetrated or fostered genocide right down to village level. It covers killers who acted with "zeal and excessive malice" and people who may not have
11311 killed but who "committed acts of sexual torture".Ordinary killers, the tens of thousands in the genocide's infantry, are in category two and liable to life imprisonment."You cannot punish everyone the same way or you would end up putting hundreds of thousands of people to death," Gahima said.The transitional parliament broadened
11311 the scope of category one from the government's first draft.The law contains a Confession and Guilty Plea procedure allowing reduced prison terms for those who confess honestly before trial. But even if they confess, people convicted in category one will not benefit from reduced penalties.Category three is for serious assaults
11311 against the person and category four covers offences against property.Gikondo's inmates want to know more about the Genocide Law. They have a sketchy knowledge of its provisions, gleaned from reports on Radio Rwanda."How does it fit in with the Penal Code?" Sylvestre Miseso, 28, secretary-general of the Gikondo prisoners' association,
11311 wanted to know from a visiting Reuters correspondent.He said he was arrested in August 1995, 14 months after the end of the genocide, on the denunciation of someone who claimed he was manning a roadblock at Ruhengeri in April 1994. Tutsis and moderate Hutus were picked out at these roadblocks
11311 and usually put to death with machetes and clubs."I wasn't there, I was working in Kigali at the time. But I'm ready to be judged," said Miseso. He has a 'dossier', a legal file, and is accused of genocide. But he and other inmates thought as many as 50 percent
11311 of their number had no dossier and had not been charged.An older man said he had been detained without charge since July, 1994. "None of us 94s have dossiers," he complained.The group pressing around Miseso in Gikondo's central yard agreed about one thing. They had no intention of accepting the
11311 Confession and Guilty Plea offer."How can you confess to a crime you didn't commit? And nobody wants to ask for forgiveness without knowing what he's supposed to have done," Miseso said to general consent.The paradox is that none of the genocide's big fish is in custody in Rwanda. They fled
11311 abroad in good time and now live in refugee camps in Zaire or Tanzania or in more comfortable exile in capitals around the world.Those in the West, and in some African countries, are in little fear of extradition to Rwanda because courts oppose the existence of the death sentence.The main
11311 threat to category one suspects abroad is that they will be extradited to the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR), the U.N. body created to try leaders of the genocide in Arusha, Tanzania.But the ICTR, after nearly two years in existence and with a 1996 budget of $36 million, has
11311 so far managed to take only three suspects into its own custody. Unlike the 80,000 detainees in Rwanda, the trio's diet includes croissants for breakfast.If they are hard-up, Arusha's suspects will have top defence lawyers paid for by the ICTR. If they are found guilty, life imprisonment in humane conditions
11311 will be the maximum penalty.</

11333 65-year-old leader has been under observation since September 13.The surgery, which Yeltsin himself said was necessary if he were to continue to lead an active political life, looks certain to go ahead, although doctors have voiced caution and media speculation has been rife about possible complications.The liberal newspaper Sevodnya said
11333 on Wednesday that, whatever the council of doctors decided, "the operation was necessary for political considerations".The doctors, led by chief surgeon Renat Akchurin, were scheduled to meet Yeltsin (0900 GMT) to decide whether or not to go ahead with the surgery, when and how it should be performed.But Akchurin, a
11333 former pupil of the veteran DeBakey, on Tuesday ruled out cancellation of the bypass surgery.Sevodnya said that if the doctors cast doubt on the operation going ahead or if it were postponed for a significant period, Russia could be plunged into more uncertainty that Yeltsin's opponents were sure to exploit.The
11333 communist opposition have already seized on the health issue, accusing Yeltsin's camp of deceiving the electorate in the July 3 vote, which gave the president another four years in office, and suggesting that he should retire if unfit.Akchurin gave them further ammunition in a frank television interview at the weekend
11333 in which he said Yeltsin may have had a third heart attack between the first and second rounds of voting.At the time, Yeltsin disappeared from public view but his aides insisted that he was merely exhausted and had a cold.Yeltsin's heart problems became clear only on September 5 when he
11333 said he had opted for surgery rather than lead a passive life which had never been his style."Even if an operation is not necessary on patient Yeltsin, President Yeltsin will have to be operated on," Sevodnya said. "Otherwise, he can expect to face a major scandal.""It is not clear how
11333 he could remain president after he refuses surgical intervention on the functioning of his heart."Nevertheless, doctors have expressed concern about possible complications ranging from pneumonia to kidney failure.Akchurin, who would lead the team performing the surgery, hinted at the weekend that the doctors may decide to put the operation off
11333 for up to eight weeks, hoping the president will be strong enough by then to withstand the operation.On Tuesday Yeltsin appeared to have trouble speaking in a brief heavily-edited television clip released by the Kremlin.Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday Yeltsin's resignation now was out of the question and
11333 condemned the opposition call. 11333 for this.The president's absence from the political scene has fuelled speculation about a power struggle between Chernomyrdin and presidential administration chief Anatoly Chubais on the one hand and security supremo Alexander Lebed on the other.</

11336 late June or early July. 11336 I would say the chance (of success) is about 80 percent, but we hope that in six weeks the percentage would be close to 100," he said.The doctors' comments must have come as some relief to Kremlin aides hoping to keep Yeltsin in power for as long as possible.But Yeltsin

11348 Boris Yeltsin needs time for his heart to recover from a bout of blood supply problems before a bypass operation to relieve his clogged arteries. Doctors also need to look into an unexplained blood problem.But the Russian president's medical team, confirming their decision to operate in six to eight weeks,
11348 gave an optimistic assessment of his health on Wednesday. His liver, kidneys and brain were working normally, they said.Michael DeBakey, the Houston-based pioneer of heart bypass surgery who has been asked by U.S. President Bill Clinton to make Yeltsin his "first priority", said he was encouraged by an improvement in
11348 the heart action but wanted an explanation for possible intestinal bleeding before operating."The timing for the operation is dependent to a great extent on what the medical team observes over the next six weeks in terms of correcting some of the problems that exist and in terms of preparing him
11348 for the operation," he told a news conference.Other specialists said the delay was curious.Hans Borst, a leading German cardiologist attending a conference in Moscow, said it was highly unusual for patients to wait more than a week, given the risk of new heart attacks.But DeBakey said: "It's important to understand
11348 what may seem to be a delay in the operation not in terms of a delay but preparation for the operation."Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon who will operate, told the news conference the wait would raise the chances of success to close to 100 percent from 80 percent at the
11348 moment."The encouraging aspect is the fact that his cardiac function, muscle function, has improved during the past month," DeBakey said. "That's a very good sign indicating that there is continuous improvement to take place and secondly that the operation will be even more successful."Bypass surgery grafts veins, usually from the
11348 leg, to route blood around clogged arteries and into the heart. Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year as a result of poor blood supply.Akchurin said at the weekend that Yeltsin probably had a third attack in late June or early July, when he suddenly dropped out of sight near
11348 the end of his reelection campaign.DeBakey said there was evidence of a "decrease in the function of the cardiac muscle", which is usually due to weak blood flow.But he said: "The encouraging thing about this is the fact that in the envelope between about a month ago when he may
11348 have had the damage to his myocardium (heart muscle) there has been a significant improvement in muscular function.""This gives us good justification for prolonging this period of rehabilitation programme...to improve his condition and get him in better shape for the operation. So this is one of the basic reasons we're
11348 doing it as well as in a sense to correct these other little problems."These were not specific heart problems and included a loss of haemoglobin, the red blood pigment that carries oxygen round the body, perhaps by intestinal bleeding. Contradicting recent rumours, DeBakey said Yeltsin had no liver or kidney
11348 trouble."He has kidney function, his liver functions are perfectly normal," he said. Blood vessels away from the heart were also in good condition, raising the chance of restoring circulation."But there was during the past month a loss of haemoglobin haematically (in blood) and we don't know exactly what caused that.
11348 The most likely thing is loss through the gastro-intestinal tract," he said.This was not uncommon and was being treated by blood transfusions, he said.</

11353 and identification until 1997.U.N. spokesman Alexander Ivanko in Sarajevo said there was evidence Pilica, one of four mass grave sites under investigation, had been disturbed.A tribunal spokesman in The Hague told Reuters a site at Lazete had also been tampered with."From what I understand a number of bodies and/or parts
11353 of bodies may have been removed before the tribunal team arrived in the area," Ivanko said of the Pilica site."All we can say is that the site has been tampered with in what seems to be in a pretty sloppy way."The tribunal began exhumations in July and has been active
11353 at four grave sites -- Cerska, Nova Kasaba, Lazete and Pilica.All of the graves were believed to contain the remains of victims killed after Serb forces overran the Moslem enclave of Srebrenica in eastern Bosnia in the summer of 1995.Thousands of Moslems, mostly men and boys, are missing and presumed
11353 dead in the aftermath of the Serb onslaught. Surviving eyewitnesses have identified about a dozen mass grave locations associated with the fall of Srebrenica.U.N. sources said investigators had recovered between 400 and 500 bodies from the four sites investigated to date.They could not be more precise about the number because
11353 the remains were badly decomposed in many cases and parts of several skeletons might have been mixed together during recovery.Former Bosnian Serb President Radovan Karadzic and his army commander, General Ratko Mladic, were indicted by the U.N. tribunal for war crimes at Srebrenica. 11353 in Bosnia to help implement the provisions of the Dayton peace agreement have refused to provide fixed security at suspected mass grave sites despite widespread fears that valuable evidence might be destroyed.Instead, NATO has relied on roving patrols and aerial surveillance to deter and detect tampering, with uncertain success.Ivanko explained
11353 that, despite the end of exhumation operations for 1996, forensic experts would continue working out of the morgue in Kalesija, east of Tuzla.U.N. scientists at the morgue examine recovered human remains to try to determine time and cause of death as part of the continuing criminal investigation into Bosnian war
11353 crimes.Tribunal investigators on Tuesday handed over to Bosnian government authorities the skeletons, clothing and anthropological information on 33 bodies exhumed from Nova Kasaba in July.U.N. sources said that only two of the bodies carried documentation which might lead to their final identification.</

11355 The decision by cardiologists on Wednesday to delay operating on Boris Yeltsin's sick heart amounted to a prescription for weeks more political uncertainty, despite putting the Kremlin's worst fears to rest.The good news for the Russian president was that the doctors concluded he should be fit enough to survive heart
11355 surgery and that delaying the operation would give him an almost 100 percent chance of survival and the prospect of resuming normal work.The bad news was that the bypass operation will not go ahead for at least six to eight weeks and the usual period of recuperation after such surgery
11355 is six weeks to two months.The impact of Yeltsin's absence for at least three more months will be limited by the fact that he has already been little more than a figurehead leader for most of the summer, Russian political experts said.But they said there was also a danger that
11355 rivalries in the Kremlin would intensify and upset the delicate balance in the team which is governing on behalf of the 65-year-old president."In one sense this delay is not a sensation because Yeltsin has not controlled anything for a long time and to an extent the Russian regime is already
11355 operating without him," political analyst Lilia Shevtsova told Reuters."But we now have a situation of political gridlock. There will be a lot of uncertainly for a long time and decisions will be put off. What we face is unpredictability and stagnation."The main power rivals are widely depicted as Prime Minister
11355 Viktor Chernomyrdin, Yeltsin's stolid pro-reform prime minister for almost four years, and security tsar Alexander Lebed, an ambitious but politically inexperienced reserve general.Another potential presidential hopeful is Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov, and Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais is widely seen as keen to accumalate power despite being an unlikely presidential challenger.Yeltsin
11355 looks set to delay implementing a decree to transfer his duties temporarily to Chernomyrdin until he has surgery, meaning he will continue to be in charge despite his illness."If powers were transferred to Chernomyrdin temporarily, everything would be clear-cut and the powers of Lebed and Chubais would be watered down,"
11355 said Lyudmila Telen, deputy editor of the Moscow News newspaper."Without the decree, these two will continue to try to have an influence in the economy and political matters."Shevtsova said such rivalries and a lack of clarity over the division of power could lead to increased confusion in policy-making and a
11355 lack of coordination in decision-making.Worse still, she said, decisions on important issues could be slowed down or put off entirely, increasing the risk of a crisis blowing up over problems such as a backlog of unpaid wages to millions of workers."Tension could increase and problems could grow in areas such
11355 as the far east and central Russia. The big question is whether all these problems are concentrated at the same time," she said.Yeltsin's old enemy, former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, said in a radio interview that the president should resign to stop Russia becoming a "hostage of unclear, troubled times".Gorbachev
11355 drew a parallel with the latter years of Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev's rule in which his ability to govern was badly affected by illness in a period known as "the era of stagnation".But the doctors on Wednesday played down the likelihood of that happening in Yeltsin's case, saying patients usually
11355 live for more than 10 years after the operation he is due to have.Kremlin aides will welcome this and be relieved not to have heard the worst possible news for them -- that Yeltsin's overall health was so poor the operation would have to be cancelled.Presidential aides appear keen to
11355 keep Yeltsin in office as long as possible, whether he is working normally or more "passively", to avoid an early presidential election which Lebed or the opposition communists might be capable of winning.Many political analysts say Lebed is little liked in the Kremlin and that his rivals fear he would
11355 benefit from an early election after coming third behind Yeltsin in this year's poll. A communist success would be an even harder pill to swallow.</

11387 Doctors decided on Wednesday to operate on President Boris Yeltsin's heart but said it would take up to eight weeks to prepare him in order to increase his chances of surviving and recovering full strength.Following is a chronology of Yeltsin's health problems, both real and rumoured.October 1991 - Yeltsin is
11387 ordered to take two weeks' rest after aides said he had suffered minor heart problems.February 1992 - Yeltsin tells French television: "I have never had any heart trouble. Every day I have a cold shower -- I am in very good shape."July 1995 - Yeltsin goes into hospital with an
11387 ischaemic heart condition -- a blood supply problem. He spends two weeks in hospital followed by two weeks in a sanatorium.October 26, 1995 - Yeltsin is taken to hospital and doctors say it is again an ischaemic heart condition. He moves to the sanatorium a month later and leaves on
11387 New Year's Eve.June 28, 1996 - Yeltsin misses a meeting with farmers between the two rounds of the Russian presidential election. Aides say he has a sore throat.July 3 - Yeltsin fails to turn up to vote at his regular Moscow polling station as scheduled and votes instead at the
11387 Barvikha residence which also houses a medical centre.August 2 - A Yeltsin aide says the president is suffering from "colossal weariness" after his election campaign and needs two months of peace and quiet.August 9 - In his first public appearance since June 26, Yeltsin takes his oath of office. 11387 appears for just 16 minutes, moves awkwardly and speaks for only 45 seconds.August 19 - Yeltsin's spokesman denies a report in U.S. magazine Time, which said that Yeltsin would go to a Swiss clinic for a heart bypass operation after suffering further heart problems in the second half of July.August
11387 23 - The Kremlin press office denies a press report that Yeltsin will have treatment at a special clinic.Sept 5 - Yeltsin, in a shock announcement breaking with secretive Kremlin tradition, says he has agreed to have heart surgery, later announced to be a heart bypass operation, probably to take
11387 place at the end of the month in Moscow.Sept 12 - NTV commercial television says foreign doctors will participate in Yeltsin's surgery.Sept 13 - Yeltsin goes into Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital for a weekend of pre-surgery tests but he stays there to prepare for operation.Sept 16-17 - The Kremlin twice

11387 and serious". He extends the president's pre-surgery hospital stay for a third time. Dr Renat Akchurin, who is expected to lead the operation on Yeltsin, tells a U.S. television channel that the president had an unreported heart attack in late June or early July, between the two rounds of the
11387 presidential election.Sept 25, 1996 - Top doctors meet Yeltsin and rule that the surgery will go ahead but he needs between six and eight weeks of preparation in hospital to increase his chances of surviving the operation and return to normal life.</

11389 Serbian sugar refineries could process about 2.5 million tonnes of sugar beet and produce around 270,000 tonnes of sugar this season, an industry expert said on Wednesday."We can produce up to 280,000 tonnes of sugar this season and cover domestic needs," Milan Petrovic, director of one of the top Serbian
11389 sugar refineries in Crvenka, said.According to other expert estimates, Serbia's sugar needs run between 350,000 and 400,000 tonnes a year."The average expected sugar content in this season's sugar beet crop was around 15.5 percent against 14 percent in the previous season," Petrovic told Reuters.The government plans to raise the area
11389 under sugar beet by 30,000 hectares in 1997, taking it to 110,000 hectares, said Vlajko Stojiljkovic, head of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.The state's aim was to boost sugar production to 700,000 tonnes in 1997, equivalent to the refineries' capacity.Petrovic said this figure was unrealistic, but even if the increased
11389 crop managed to produce a surplus over domestic consumption, he insisted there would be no exports until the state met producers' demands."As long as the government does not provide export subsidies, we cannot sell abroad, because we'll have to export at lower prices," he said.The refinery director added that the
11389 main bottlenecks lay with inefficient agriculture, difficulties with weeding and inadequate infrastructure.Sugar refineries were seeking new price parities from the government, intervention by the Commodity Reserve Agency and protection from substantially cheaper imports.According to Petrovic, the production cost for locally refined sugar was 4.68 dinars (1.47 German marks) per kg
11389 -- well above the retail price of 3.95 dinars. One kg of imported Cuban sugar does not exceed 1.4 marks, he said.Producers are demanding protection from cheaper imports, which totalled about 100,000 tonnes of raw sugar and 40,000 tonnes of white sugar during January-August. The most efficient protection would be
11389 introducing import quotas, he said.Under the Yugoslav system, refineries are responsible for organising farmers to grow enough sugar beet for their needs. Refineries are prohibited from buying beet on the open market.Farmers are reluctant to grow sugar beet because cash payments cover only one third of the crop's value. The
11389 balance is paid in fuel and fertilisers.The government pays farmers a maximum of 0.27 dinars per kg of sugar beet.--Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254</

11392 Yugoslav firms see lack of credits and working capital as the main obstacles to speedier revival of production, the Belgrade Economics Institute said in its latest August Market Barometer report."Lack of credits has been the dominant obstacle for a long period now, which reflects the firmness of monetary policy and
11392 access to money flows," Goran Pitic, economist with the institute, told a news conference on Tuesday.The institute's report is based on a poll of 300 Yugoslav industry and energy firms.Lack of access to credits was listed as the main problem by 37.5 percent, shortage of raw materials by 24.6 percent,
11392 and low demand by 20.6 percent of the firms.Internal debts were still very high, but firms said they expected the situation to improve slightly in coming months.According to the Institute for Market Research, internal debts reached 3.98 billion dinars at the end of July when M1 money supply stood at
11392 4.34 billion dinars.Despite industrial growth of 2.1 percent in August over July, most firms described the economic climate as bad.After climbing to 6.6 percent in July, inflation slowed to 2.3 percent in August, and was 99.2 percent year-on-year."As many as 68.6 percent believe prices will go up in the last
11392 quarter, while only 0.7 percent said they expected them to drop," Pitic said.Use of capacities improved slightly to 55.2 percent over July's 53 percent, but stocks of raw materials and finished goods were very low."The overall position of firms was described as bad by 31.8 percent, while 14.2 percent said
11392 it was good. This means that they see business risk as very high," Pitic said.Despite dwindling optimism, 35.5 percent still saw the situation -- particularly domestic demand -- as improving by the year end, but were less hopeful that exports would pick up."Since one of the main tasks of economic
11392 policy is to strengthen hard currency reserves, it is worrying that as many as 41 percent of the firms said they are not planning exports in the next three months," Pitic said.Although exports maintained an upward trend, the trade deficit in the January-August period grew to over one billion dollars,
11392 with exports worth $1.1 billion and imports $2.265 billion.Only 27.2 percent of the firms believe there will be investments from local sources, while less than 10 percent said they expected funds from abroad -- despite the prospect of an end to lingering international sanctions. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381

11400 A multinational consortium with an ambitious project to build a pipeline to export Kazakh crude oil to world markets is trying to move faster but is unlikely to meet key deadlines, energy sources said on Wednesday.The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) has revised upward the amount of oil it initially plans
11400 to move once the first phase of the $1.2 billion link is built.But it will not meet a key restructuring deadline on September 30 that would have kickstarted the project."We're now looking at a higher system, a higher capacity, and the risk allocation has changed," said Ed Smith, general director
11400 of Caspian Pipeline Consortium Ltd and a project executive at the Oman Oil Company, a CPC shareholder."There are a multitude of issues that need to be worked out that make it a challenge to finish restructuring September 30."CPC groups original shareholders Kazakhstan, Oman and Russia, which have a combined 50
11400 percent stake, with Chevron Corp, LUKoil, Mobil Corp, Rosneft, Oman Oil Company, British Gas Plc, Agip SpA of Italy, Munaigaz and Oryx Energy Co.Another Western executive at CPC said the consortium was working to restructure ownership so that U.S. companies directly or indirectly have at least a 30 percent stake
11400 to take advantage of a U.S.-Russian tax treaty reducing tax burdens. Currently the U.S. firms have just under 30 percent.CPC's project to send the oil through an as yet unbuilt pipeline around the Caspian Sea, across Russia and to the Black Sea, is a cauldron of complex financing and geo-political
11400 issues."If you look at the entire pipeline, it does force us to reconsider the entire contracting strategy," said the second CPC source, referring to calls by Chevron and Mobil to build the pipeline in one go instead of in stages."It's probably appropriate to look at rebidding the job."The U.S.-Italian Willbros/Saipem
11400 joint venture won a contract in August 1995 to build the first phase of the pipeline, from the southern Russian town of Kropotkin to a new sea terminal north of Novorossiisk on the Black Sea.Chevron and Mobil, with no way to export oil from their giant Tengizchevroil (TCO) project in
11400 Kazakhstan, are eager for the pipeline to be built, since problems in securing an export route have kept them from increasing output as planned.CPC recently raised the amount of crude it hopes to transport in the initial stage to 28 million tonnes a year by the end of 1997 from
11400 15 million tonnes.The original, total final capacity of about 70 million tonnes a year has not changed."The roughest edge is the taxation and liability issue," said one source in CPC, referring to profits, local and value-added taxes. 11456 Romania's average monthly inflation over the first eight months of 1996 quickened to 3.0 percent, double the year-ago rate, National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed on Wednesday.Data showed monthly inflation in the food sector, which takes the bulk of consumer spending, was 2.7 percent in January-August, up from 1.3 percent
11456 last year.Non-food sector inflation was 3.3 percent, up from 1.5 percent, and services sector inflation 3.5 percent, up from 2.4.The CNS said price rises in the non-food sector were higher than because of rises in the price of clothing, footwear, furniture and refrigerators and freezers.The marked rise in average monthly
11456 inflation in the services sector was a result of higher train fares and tariffs for community services, including water supply, sewerage and sanitation services, and public transport.Monthly inflation was 3.8 percent in August, when year-on-year inflation was 44.2 percent.The CNS said August inflation was above the monthly January-August average because
11456 of the delayed impact of energy and fuel price rises in July.Under pressure from World Bank to bring energy prices closer to international norms, Romania jacked up electricity and thermal power prices by 58 percent and fuel by some 30 percent early in July.The rises pushed July inflation to 7.5
11456 percent -- the biggest monthly increase in two years -- and, according to official estimates, are expected to hoist 12-month inflation this year to around 30 percent from a previously forecast 20 percent. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264</

11466 The figures look good on Russia's long-suffering economy before next week's meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, but political doubts and concern on the budget have cast a shadow over the achievements.Helped by a $10 billion three-year IMF loan, subject to tough monthly monitoring, Russia has slashed
11466 inflation and is seeing the first signs of economic growth."On the surface, and in reality, things are going pretty well in the economic sphere," said a senior Western economist.Russia's team at the annual meetings will be led by new economic chief Vladimir Potanin, 35, a former commercial banker who has
11466 little experience of politics.But he has a heady message for Washington.Consumer prices fell 0.2 percent in August after a 17.8 percent rise in January 1995. The government is forecasting a rate for the year of 22 percent, compared with 131 percent in 1995, although the actual rate may be lower
11466 than that.Industrial output, half what it was when economic reform began in 1992, has started to pick up. Economists expect gross domestic product to grow next year.The rouble is relatively stable and progress has been made in rescheduling Russia's debts to the London and Paris Clubs of commercial bank and
11466 government creditors. A debut Eurobond is in preparation.But there have been hitches along the way.The IMF delayed payment of its July tranche of the loan because of concern over the budget deficit, swollen by high yields paid on Treasury bills and tax exemptions handed out during the presidential election campaign.The
11466 money was eventually paid, new budget targets were agreed and the IMF said reform was back on track."The programme has been renegotiated and approved so there is no special need to get anything else from the IMF/World Bank meeting," said Jochen Wermuth, head of the Economic Expert Group at the
11466 Finance Ministry.Russia's new government has declared war on tax dodgers, but revenues will still be "the number one issue" in Washington, the economist said.The Russian economy is mired in a non-payments crisis which means workers and pensioners are not paid for months and firms run up vast debts to suppliers
11466 and to the tax authorities.Analysts said the IMF would be keen for assurances that revenues will be sufficient to keep the budget deficit and inflation down and to cover necessary social spending."It is a matter of political will. The highest authorities have got to make it clear to everybody about
11466 tax collection," the economist said.However, Russia is undergoing a period of deep political uncertainty. President Boris Yeltsin, who wields enormous power, is preparing for heart surgery. This has unnerved markets and Russian stocks and bonds have fallen sharply.Analysts say investors feared a period of drift in the economy, rather than
11466 any full-scale reversal of reform.Wermuth said concern was misplaced. "Business is going on as usual," he said.Apart from Yeltsin's health, foreign investors often cite the state of the banking system as an obstacle to putting their money into Russia.Central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin, who will be in Washington, has said
11466 there is no systemic crisis.Kremlin aide Mikhail Delyagin said Russia had entered a new low-inflation era which demanded understanding from the IMF."I hope they understand that reform is continuing and has entered a new phase and that they understand the difficulties Russia has met in this new phase," he said.</

11489 The fanfare over Ukraine's first post-Soviet constitution has died away, but one question vital to a free market economy remains unanswered -- can land be privately owned?Diplomats and analysts studying the document, produced during an all-night session of parliament in late June, say no."The constitution guarantees everything under the sun
11489 but as far as Western-style land ownership, which is one of the foundations of a market economy, is concerned, it doesn't do it," said a Western diplomat.Without such guarantees investors cannot know whether they will own the land on which their factories are built, those wishing to farm privately are
11489 wary of striking off on their own, and people wishing to build homes on property they own outright are forced to wait until the law of the land is clarified."This constitution is a step in the right direction but in order to accomplish the privatisation of agricultural land more specific
11489 reforms need to be legislated in the new civil and land codes," said Chuck Costanza, a project manager with the International Finance Corporation (IFC).Private land ownership has long been a goal of President Leonid Kuchma's economic reform programme, started in late 1994. But parliament, dominated by communists and their allies,
11489 has maintained that land must remain in public hands.There are no plans to let foreigners buy land either, and Western investors complain that their local joint ventures with Ukrainian companies are also unable to buy land.The IFC, the World Bank's private investment arm, has been running several land privatisation projects
11489 but, ultimately, the land has remained in state hands.Some 35,000 private farmers who have been given government land face a six-year moratorium on its sale.Article 14 of the constitution states: "The land is the main source of national wealth, which is under the special protection of the state."It continues: "The
11489 property right on land is guaranteed. This right shall be acquired and executed by legal entities and state only according to the law."Experts said the statement is not clear because it does not specify land ownership; private, collective or state-owned."The language was watered down, so the constitution doesn't forbid it,
11489 and it doesn't guarantee it," said a Western diplomat.Kuchma, determined to push ahead with land reform and privatisation in the agriculture sector, has at times issued decrees ordering collective farms be divided -- only to add to the confusion of those trying to carry out his orders."Do you give more
11489 weight to the land code or to the decree, which gives you more freedom?" an analyst said.Contradictory legislation in all walks of life, inherited from the days of the former Soviet Union, is a constant headache to foreign funding bodies and investors.Ukraine has attracted only about $1.5 billion in foreign
11489 investment since independence five years ago, but government officials predicted it would grow to $2 billion by the end of the year.The recently-reconvened parliament is unlikely to clarify the land issue through the civil and land codes, according to one Western diplomat."You can rest assured that the people who had
11489 it watered down in the constitution will try to have it watered down in these laws as well," he said.A new land code has been rejected twice by parliament, said Alexy Onyshenko, an IFC consultant and a professor for the Institute of Economic Studies with the National Academy of Sciences."This
11489 is a very complex political question," he said. "As far as I can see the right to own land now exists but there are many people against it, who fear selling Ukrainian land."He said many bureaucrats, who carry a great deal of weight in post-Soviet society, stand in the way
11489 of land reform."Nothing will happen without a fight," Onyshenko said.</
11490 Foreign direct investment (FDI) in the five countries of the Central European Free Trade Area (CEFTA) more than doubled in 1995 to $8.890 billion, the United Nations said on Wednesday.The World Investment Report by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) said Hungary and the Czech Republic led
11490 CEFTA in their rate of FDI growth, while Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia posted relatively solid gains.Mainly due to privatisations, inflows into Hungary and the Czech Republic tripled to $3.5 billion and $2.5 billion respectively.The European Union comprises most of the direct investment in the region holding three quarters of FDI
11490 stock in Hungary and two thirds in the Czech Republic, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia, it said."(The EU) is the most important trading partner for all (central/eastern European) countries, reflecting intra-firm trade flows...and the importance of the region as a production base for exports to the European Union," it said.Some 60
11490 percent of the Czech Republic's inflows in 1995 were related to the privatisation of its telecommunications monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. and oil refineries, and Hungary's rise also was due largely to its telecommunications sell-off."Inflows into the Czech Republic and Hungary are, however, much more volatile because much is related to
11490 privatisation," the report said.Non-privatisation-related FDI inflows in the so-called Visegrad countries were higher in Poland than in Hungary and the Czech Republic, UNCTAD said, "reflecting the better growth performance of the former.""Among the Visegrad countries, Poland was the first to make the turnaround in economic growth after the initial transition
11490 shock," it said.The report showed small but steady FDI growth in CEFTA aspirants, with 1995 inflows increasing to $135 million from $106 million in Bulgaria and to $373 million from $340 million in 1994 in Romania.FDI INFLOWS IN 1995 (in millions of dollars): inflows stock FDI inflows per capita 1995

11499 The world economy may be more integrated, but many of the poorest countries are still under the threat of being left out of the new wealth being created, Commonwealth Secretary General Emeka Anyaoku said on Tuesday.His comments, at the opening of the group's meeting of finance ministers, echo concerns from
11499 member countries that more has to be done to help poor developing nations shake off the almost intolerable burden of debt and give their economies a more hopeful future. "Many developing countries, including several least developed and small states, have yet to benefit from integration and face the risk of
11499 being marginalised in an increasingly competitive world," Anyaoku said.He pointed to a recent "shocking" report that said the wealth of the world's 358 richest people equalled the combined income of 45 percent of the world's population."I believe that this (globalisation) is the key challenge which the international community needs to
11499 address in the coming years...global cooperation is imperative," he said. Debt is the dominant topic at this meeting of some 53 Commonwealth countries.Many members of the old British Empire are poor and heavily in debt and range from tiny island states such as Nauru, which relies on the export of
11499 bird droppings for fertiliser for its livlihood to Asian giant India, as well as wealthy nations such as Canada and Britain.Anyaoku said there needed to be early resolution of the debt issue, continued adequate amounts of aid, an open international trading environment and measures to deal with the surge in
11499 capital flows in and out of developing countries. A report by the Commonwealth said proposals to bail out countries pushed by debt into deepening poverty are so rigid that very few stand much hope of help before the turn of the century.Britain has been pressing for greater help, including selling
11499 some of the International Monetary Fund's $40 billion in gold reserves, to release funds for the heavily indebted poor countries.The issue will be one of the main topics at next week's annual IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington when industrial countries will come under further pressure to do more to help
11499 the poor.In his speech, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, urged fellow Commonwealth finance ministers to to press for a resolution of the problem of debt relief at the Washington talks."A succesful conclusion is urgently needed," he said.</

11539 negotiated the contracts for most of Argentina's unionized workers, would not back down.Two opinion polls published on Wednesday indicated that betweeen 54 and 69 percent of Argentines support the strike. But only 30 percent in one survey said they would walk out.The reforms include loosening restrictions on working hours and
11539 holidays, allowing for wages to vary depending on economic conditions and for overtime to be payable in days off in lieu of cash, and creating unemployment insurance schemes funded by employers. They also allow companies to negotiate contracts directly with their workers in place of separate industries striking collective wage
11539 deals with trade unions.Authorities argue the reforms are needed to lower employer costs and give firms flexibility to change working conditions to suit the economic climate, making them more competitive. The government predicts that employers, with lower costs, will hire workers again and help slash the jobless rate to single
11539 digit levels by the end of the decade."Many of the collective agreements negotiated by the CGT make fast and efficient responses to (economic) change difficult, costly, slow or impossible," reads a draft for the government's labour bill released late on Tuesday.The ruling Peronist Party's majority in Congress has shown only
11539 lukewarm support at best for the reforms, with Jorge Matzkin, leader in the lower house, telling Reuters recently he had no evidence previous reforms created jobs.But Labour Minister Armando Caro Figueroa reiterated a government threat to impose the reforms by decree by the end of the year if Congress refuses
11539 to approve them.Congress is also debating several austerity measures, including an increase in fuel taxes, to narrow a widening budget deficit.</

11559 Recent good rains have dispelled clowds of gloom from northern and central Argentine crop lands and regenerated prospects for wheat and maize, traders said Wednesday."I think we'll see 14 million-odd tonnes of wheat. I wouldn't have any fear predicting that," a trader told Reuters. He said that rains in zones
11559 until now hardest hit by drought, in Cordoba province, will permit some farmers to dig up their shrivelled wheat and sow soybeans, maize or sunflower."They were scared to make the switch without rain, and risk ending up with two ruined crops," he said, "In other areas which were less badly
11559 hit the rain will let them stay with wheat, even though yields may be down 30 percent or 35 percent." Traders said farmers were beginning maize sowing with enthusiasm in northern areas, and moisture levels have improved markedly everywhere except for a small area of southeastern Cordoba."My maize number is
11559 12.5 million, 13 million tonnes. But it's still early, anything could happen," the first trader said. "But the main thing is that it looks like the weather situation is getting back to normal," he said. He explained that he had heard a forecast for good rains up to November, a
11559 dry December, and then above average rain for the next few months.Another trader agreed that the rains have greatly improved crop prospects: "We've avoided a disaster in wheat. Now to say we might get a crop of 14.5 million tonnes or 14.2 million tonnes is realistic again. Given normal rain
11559 from here on, the harvest is saved." Maize, sunflower and soybean sowing prospects have also been improved, he said. "The soybean crop could easily be of similar size to last season. Although with more wheat planted there'll be a greater proportion of second crop beans, which yield less."But he said
11559 that 10-12 percent less sunflower should be sown than last year, and that the dry spell has already foiled plans to sow sunflower in some 40,000 hectares in the north. Argentine farmers produced some 9.2 million tonnes of wheat in 1995/96, along with 10.5 million tonnes of maize, 12.7 million
11559 tonnes of soybeans, and 5.6 million tonnes of sunflower seed, according to the Agricultural Secretariat.The Secretariat said last week that wheat sowing has risen 35 percent from drought-blighted 1995/96. It expected maize sowing to rise by 5.7 percent, soybean sowing to fall by three percent, and sunflower sowing to dip
11559 12.7 percent.-- Buenos Aires Newsroom +541 318-0655</

11562 Despite a severe domestic recession, Venezuelan textiles and fibreglass manufacturer Sudamtex expects first half net profits for fiscal 1997 to rise five percent in real terms on the year before, company President Kenneth Johnson told Reuters."Total sales will probably be between flat and up three percent with exports compensating for
11562 lower local sales. But net income should be up some five percent on better margins," he said. The first half of the company's fiscal year is from July to December. Venezuela's second largest private sector exporter reported year-end sales of 64 billion bolivars ($136 million) in June and net profits
11562 of eight billion bolivars ($17 million), all expressed in constant June 30 bolivars.The improved margins largely derive from $100 million in production upgrades and plant investment, which only came fully on stream last year."We're probably now the most modern textile company in the whole of Latin America," said Johnson, who
11562 undertook the expansion with an eye towards taking advantage of greater regional integration. With operations in both Uruguay and Venezuela -- as well as in Belgium and the UK where Sudamtex supplies retailing chain Marks &amp; Spencer -- "We're really pushing for greater trade integration, especially Venezuela joining Mercosur."Exports as
11562 a percentage of total sales have steadily risen, reaching 60 percent in 1996 from 57 percent in 1995. In addition, Korean industrial giant Samsung is expected to sign soon for an investment that will double Sudamtex's Uruguay operations. Samsung will pay for the expansion and take all the additional production
11562 for the first five years."The deal should be put to bed in the next 30 days," he said.But while textiles have traditionally represented the 50- year-old company's core business, "You can't ignore that the most significant change in Venezuela over the past year has been the oil opening," Johnson said.
11562 The company -- which has only turned a loss once, in 1981 -- has recently created a petroleum division designed to piggy-back on the sector's opening to foreign investment by providing fibreglass storage tanks and high-pressure tubing.Fiscal 1997 sales of the energy equipment are expected to reach $17 million, rising
11562 to $50 million in three years, so that "over time textiles will contribute less and less to total sales".The debt taken on to fuel recent investments "is manageable, given our cash flow," Johnson said. Total group bank debt currently stands at some $100 million, but interest coverage, at 2.2 percent
11562 "is very strong," he added, and total exposure is only "around $10 million.""We think next year will be a truly strong one with up to 5 percent growth," Johnson said.-- Caracas newsroom, 582 834405</

11566 Mexican trade development bank Banco Nacional de Comercio Exterior (Bancomext) may return to the international bond markets next year to raise about $2 billion, the bank's assistant director general of finances said.The bond issues would be part of its overall financing program, including lines of credit and commercial paper, that
11566 could total as much as $10 billion over the course of 1997, Julio Mendez Rubio told Reuters in an interview. "It depends a lot on what demand is. If demand for the financing is concentrated more in the long term, then we would be calculating that it (bond issuance) will
11566 be about $2 billion," he said.The lion's share of next year's financings will be in short-term loans and commercial paper. Some of that will be rolled over as the paper comes due during the year, bumping up the overall year total, he said.The bank's lending programs, which determine the amount
11566 it must borrow, are still under discussion with other sectors and departments of the government. Bancomext is Mexico's second-largest development bank after Nacional Financiera (Nafin), and promotes and finances foreign trade. Exports have been one of the hottest sectors of the Mexican economy since the 1994 devaluation of the peso
11566 and the ensuing economic crash.With its trade-linked advantage, Bancomext was able to lead Mexican borrowers back to the global markets after the crash. In June 1995, the development bank placed a $300 million floating-rate note, up from the initial $200 million on offer, a placement which is credited with paving
11566 the way for Mexico to start floating more issues. Mendez said one of his overriding considerations in deciding where to borrow is where to get the cheapest funds."One thing that exporters have to take into account is the cost of financing, and we have to try to supply that financing
11566 at the cheapest rate possible...," he said. "We have to be aggressive in terms of pricing for the outside funds that we arrange in order to lend them here to exporters."The strategy is to go where the funds are the cheapest, whether that be in the German market, or in
11566 Japan, or in the Yankee market...," he added. For example, over the last year the development bank has placed issues in yen and German marks.In May, it placed a 10-year bond for $250 million in the United States and Europe to help finance a dam project, marking one of the
11566 first 10-year bonds to be placed by Mexico.One of its main sources of short-term funds is from lines of credit, or trade lines, with a large number of international banks, he said. The bank also has a European global commercial paper program, its Euro medium-term notes program, worth about $2.5
11566 billion. That complements its investment-grade commercial paper program in the United States, worth $300 million, and lines of credit with various export banks.Mendez said Bancomext's access to markets has rebounded to where it was before the crash, even if spreads on longer-term paper are still slightly above pre-crash levels."In terms
11566 of access to the markets, I think that we are practically equal," he said."In terms of cost, we are a little above what we paid before the crisis for long-term (financing), but for the short-term, we are below the costs that we paid before the crisis. With each placement, we
11566 have fortunately been able to reduce the cost of our funding," Mendez said.In September, Bancomext officials said that they expected to grant about $9.0 billion in credits for 1996.-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559E-mail at robert.kozak@reuters.com</

11577 Britain on Wednesday told the world's major creditors not to wait for each other to provide vital debt relief for poor countries.Help is vital if developing countries are to attract private investors but they must be prepared to open up their economies and not throw money away on military spending,
11577 Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told Commonwealth finance ministers."We now stand on the threshold of an agreement to the heavily indebted poor country initiative," he said."We need to agree that the main creditors -- the World Bank, the IMF and the Paris Club of bilateral creditors -- should coordinate
11577 their decisions. They must not wait for each other to make the first move."Clarke said he would press the issue at next week's annual meeting of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF).Proposals at the moment would force a country to wait too long for help and Clarke urged
11577 that rules be less bureaucratic."We must be reasonable, especially when we are dealing with countries that are dependent on the world market for one or two agricultural products," he added.The measure for debt sustainability should be at the lower end of the World Bank range -- 20 percent for the
11577 annual debt service to export ratio and 200 percent for the debt stock to export ratio.Private capital flows are crucial for developing countries but Clarke warned them against the temptation to put up barriers against such inflows on the pretext that they would disrupt their economies."I am not suggesting that
11577 countries should be forced to liberalise immediately....but I believe it is important that we signal the direction in which we want to go," he said.Clarke welcomed proposals by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) that developed countries end all tariffs on products from the poorest countries.A number of the small Commonwealth
11577 countries, such as banana exporters in the Caribbean, are worried that the WTO would put an end to their preferential treatment by major industrial countries."The developed world must avoid giving aid to poorer countries with one hand, and closing the door on their exports with the other," Clarke said.</

11636 Hundreds of children from poor Colombian families crossed the country by mule, bus and foot this month in search of a smile and the promise of a new life.They and their families -- drawn by radio and TV advertisements beamed into shantytowns and impoverished rural zones -- went in search

11636 were treated."In the space of just five days, hundreds of children will have been given new lives after being hidden in shame. In this day and age and at a time when the United States and Colombian governments are fighting, this is an opportunity to show that problems can be

11636 anything but fluids since his jaw fused shut when he was five.In a painstaking three-hour operation, Magee cut open his teenage patient's scalp, took muscle tissue from his temple region and used it to make a new jaw. The hole in Zamora's temple was then filled with a special plastic.Magee's
11636 colleagues also went to work in three other hospitals in the provincial cities of Cali, Manizales and Duitama. 11636 butt of cruel jokes by his peers because of his cleft lip, put on a brave face as he looked forward to the day he can grin like the rest of the children in the schoolyard. He, like some of the other patients, will need a follow-up operation but this

11641 letter of intent to set one up with Mexico's Grupo Financiero Inverlat just three weeks later.On the plus side, Santander's Argentine pension subsidiary Origenes AFJP in September bought out its rival Activa-Anticipar in a deal that will make it the giant of that industry. That suggests it has the clout
11641 to make the business work in Mexico, Santander officials said.THE ENVY OF ITS PEERSWith all the foreign experience available to its competitors, one Mexican banking giant already has a foothold that makes it the envy of the nascent industry.Bancomer, owner of Mexico's second largest bank, currently holds some 35 percent
11641 of accounts in the government-run Retirement Savings System (SAR), and it hopes many workers will be more ready to keep their funds in the bank than shift them elsewhere.But it has not rested on its laurels. Receiving a $47 million payment to link up with U.S. insurer Aetna and Chile's
11641 AFP Santa Maria, it has already surveyed potential clients on what they want from a pension fund.It can also count on what officials say was $100 million invested in SAR-related computer systems over the last four years to set up what is expected to be one of the most sophisticated
11641 systems in the industry.SOME 17 RUNNERS SEEN IN THE LINE-UPAccording to industry expert Ernesto O'Farrill of consulting firm Bursametrica, some 17 Afores will seek approval to start business on January 1.He estimates Bancomer's fund will achieve a 13 percent market share next year, while a partnership of Mexico's largest bank
11641 Banamex and Dutch insurer Aegon should garner 10 percent."It's very healthy that at the start of the race you see strong Afores. In a market like this which is starting from scratch, the natural tendency is to start with a large number," he told Reuters. "Then they will need to
11641 be more competitive and that will shrink the numbers over time."He said he did not expect to see companies recouping their initial outlay for as long as seven years, but said the amount of workers eligible for pensions schemes in Mexico was bound to make it profitable. On the regulations
11641 front, there were several hurdles to overcome, however.O'Farrill raised doubts about the smooth running of complex data banks at the central bank and the Social Security Institute set up to coordinate the pension contributions. He worried that account information could get lost, possibly undermining the credibility of the system.BOWING TO
11641 POLITICAL PRESSUREAnalysts have also accused the government of bowing to political pressures in limiting Afore investments in the first year to mostly inflation-indexed, low-risk instruments."It's a total controversy," O'Farrill said. "You're going to hurt the whole system...there will be little competitiveness and you won't be able to see which are
11641 the best Afores."In an interview, Daniel Lederman, vice-president of planning at the pension regulatory commission Consar said the investment restrictions were aimed at avoiding heavy losses. "It was a difficult change from a political point of view and we have to be careful there are (positive) returns."Once Zedillo approves the
11641 regulations, he said, potential Afores will have some 20 days to apply for approval at Consar. Then they will face rigorous checks to ensure they are up to the task of running the accounts and are well capitalised.The process "should be ready in January," he said. "Until we see when
11641 the regulations are published, we can't be sure."</

11645 An Australian man with prostate cancer has become the first person to die under the world's first law permitting voluntary euthanasia, a doctor in the outback region of the Northern Territory said on Thursday.The man was killed with a lethal injection.Dr Philip Nitschke administered the injection at the patient's home
11645 in the Northern Territory capital of Darwin."A patient has taken advantage of the law and gone ahead and determined to have his life ended last weekend," Nitschke told Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) radio.Nitschke said the patient died on Sunday after medical specialists had signed the necessary paperwork under contoversial assisted-suicide
11645 legislation which took effect in the Northern Territory in July."On the day elected by the patient he simply indicated to me that he wished to go ahead and I was able to carry out that particular wish of the patient, and things went ahead very smoothly, very well," he said.Describing
11645 the death of the man, Nitschke said it was a "very poignant moment"."There was also a feeling, of course, that this was the first time ever that a person has been able to legally end their life."And there was that sense of history as well," Nitschke said.The patient had terminal
11645 cancer and had been ill for a number of years, the doctor said.The world's first voluntary euthanasia law was narrowly passed by the Northern Territory legislature but has been bitterly opposed by Australia's leading medical association, right-to-life groups and the Vatican.Australian Prime Minister John Howard has endorsed moves in the
11645 national parliament to overturn the legislation but will allow a conscience vote by politicians."It is a matter of principle," Howard said earlier this month. "It goes to the essence of what we see life to be and the sanctity of it and the importance of it and the quality of
11645 it."The territory law allows doctors to help terminally-ill patients kill themselves with a lethal injection or pills.But until last weekend the law had not been used as doctors were unsure of their legal position in the face of forthcoming High Court and parliamentary challenges.Euthanasia is illegal in elsewhere in Australia
11645 but doctors say it is unofficially practised.</

11650 Australian Prime Minister John Howard, who has angered Beijing by agreeing to see the Dalai Lama, said on Wednesday he would not bow to Chinese trade threats over his meeting with the exiled Tibetan leader."I hope they don't carry through with that threat, but I don't bow to threats," Howard
11650 told Channel Nine television on the eve of the meeting."No self-respecting prime minister of this country would ever bow to that kind of threat," he added.A Chinese foreign ministry spokesman on Tuesday threatened possible trade retaliation after news that Howard would receive the Dalai Lama in his Sydney office on
11650 Thursday."The Australian government receiving the Dalai Lama is interference in China's internal affairs," said Shen Guofang.China views the Dalai Lama as a politically inspired troublemaker in his bid for Tibetan autonomy.But earlier on Wednesday, Beijing indicated that a diplomatic spat with Germany over Tibet had ended by inviting Germany's president
11650 for a visit and renewing an invitation to German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.Kinkel had been due to visit China in July, but Beijing withdrew its invitation after German parliamentarians passed a resolution accusing China of trying to eradicate Tibet's cultural identity.China invaded Tibet in 1950 and claims ancient sovereignty over
11650 the remote Himalayan region.The Dalai Lama, a Buddhist god-king at home, fled in 1959 after an abortive rebellion against Chinese rule.Howard told Channel Nine that he thought the latest row should never have happened: "I think they've created a problem out of nothing. It was never on for the prime
11650 minister of Australia not to meet the Dalai Lama."I'm going to meet him. He's a religious leader of some consequence," he said."What I'm saying is that there's no reason why my extending the normal courtesy of meeting him should affect the relationship between Australia and China. I've made that clear
11650 to the Chinese," Howard said.Howard's political aides, including Defence Minister Ian McLachlan, defended the prime minister's decision to meet the Dalai Lama."We're a democracy and we can do what we think is right. If we want to meet the Dalai Lama, well that's the way it is," McLachlan told reporters.
11650 "If we never offended any country, ever, we would not do anything."Meanwhile, Howard came under increased pressure to push Beijing to begin talks on Tibet's future.The Australia Tibet Council urged him to back the Dalai Lama's campaign for autonomy for his Himalayan homeland.Neither the prime minister's office nor officials with
11650 the Dalai Lama could say what would be discussed at Thursday's meeting, although Howard aides were keen to portray it as a private meeting with a religious leader.The meeting will be at Howard's Sydney office, where he conducts most of his business when parliament in Canberra is not in session.</
11651 International tourism growth in New Zealand is likely to settle at seven to eight percent per annum through to the end of the decade, somewhat below the record growth of the early 1990s, Standard and Poor's said in a report on the sector.S&amp;P said the growth outlook was moderate and
11651 largely dependent on risk factors outside the control of New Zealand operators, such as world and domestic economic conditions, relative costs, exchange rates and air access. But the defence of the America's Cup yachting trophy and the Sydney Olympic Games, both in 2000, will generate a strong spurt in international
11651 tourism at the turn of the decade, it said.Tourism contributed about 10 percent of Gross Domestic Product in fiscal 1996 and earned about NZ$4.8 billion or 19 percent of export earnings. It provides some 200,000 fulltime equivalent jobs.S&amp;P said the industry was highly fragmented between many firms of all sizes,
11651 and seasonality of demand was a negative factor. Margins and profits were highly volatile and variable. It maintained its industry ranking for the sector at C. S&amp;P said it expected the accommodation sector to come under significant pressure in the next two years due to increased room supply and slowing
11651 growth rates. Some 1,500 extra rooms have come on the market since mid-1995, with 820 more to open by mid-1997."By making such a large incremental addition to capacity within the industry in a period of relative weak growth, operators are placing themselves under pressure to cut rates to maintain economical
11651 occupancy levels. However, lowering room rates creates expectations that are very difficult to readjust," the report said. New Zealand's main listed companies in the tourism sector are Air New Zealand Ltd, CDL Hotels NZ Ltd, the Helicopter Line, Shotover Jet Ltd and Sky City Ltd.S&amp;P said the ownership of the
11651 country's three main airports was likely to gravitate towards private investors, depending on the government's willingness to sell down its stakes. It holds 51.6 percent of Auckland, 25 percent of Christchurch and 66 percent of Wellington airports.-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746</

11654 Electricity Corporation of New Zealand said on Thursday it had secured NZ$1.4 billion in revenue over the next five years from its long-term contracts.General Manager of Marketing Peter Larsen said ECNZ's memorandum of understanding with the government required the corporation to offer set percentages of its firm capacity by tender
11654 through long-term contracts."On June 26, 1996, ECNZ invited 43 registered tenderers to tender for 32,796 gigawatt hours of electricity price contracts. This quantity was offered over five years in five separate tender rounds," he said. The fifth and final tender round closed on September 17."We regard the tender as an
11654 overwhelming success. Some 94 percent of the total volume on offer was allocated to bidders," Larsen said. Similar to an auction, market supply and demand determined the price paid for the electricity hedge contracts.He said the average clearing prices for all years were higher than the set reserve prices.Larsen said
11654 that when New Zealand's competitive wholesale electricity market began from October 1, it was likely that spot prices would vary. "Spot prices are set every half hour and it is difficult to predict what the average level of the spot price will be, particularly in the first year of operation,"
11654 he said."Successful participation in the tender has guaranteed buyers the price they will pay for their electricity in the future, which reduces their exposure to spot price fluctuation, allowing better business planning."Larsen added: "We now look forward to full participation in New Zealand's first fully competitive wholesale electricity market when
11654 it begins next month."-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746</
11655 The Australian government's index of skilled job vacancies fell 0.7 percent in September, the Employment Department said on Thursday. 11655 electonics group. 11663 An earthquake measuring 6.2 on the Richter scale was felt across wide areas of New Zealand's North and South Islands late on Wednesday but there were no reports of damage.In the capital, Wellington, the quake shook windowpanes and rattled houses. It appeared to come in two waves, lasting up to
11663 a minute in total.Seismologist Ken Gledhill of the Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences told Reuters it measured 6.2 on Richter and was centred about 40 km (25 miles) north of the North Island town of Wanganui.Gledhill said the quake occurred at great depth -- about 250 km (155 miles)
11663 below the earth's surface -- and therefore would have caused little damage, although it was widely felt.Radio New Zealand said it shook towns from Taranaki on the west coast of the North Island to Christchurch on the east coast of the South. While some people said they felt two distinct
11663 earthquakes, Gledhill said these were actually two waves of the same tremor.New Zealand is part of a band of earthquake activity around the Pacific Rim and on average experiences one quake a year measuring higher than 6.0 on Richter.</
11664 The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), facing criticism about the wisdom of its US$2.4 billion takeover of Magma Copper, expressed confidence on Wednesday that it could rope in runaway production costs.The assurance helped lift BHP's share price above the A$16.00 level, ending a week of harsh comment by brokers
11664 and investors that one of Australia's best known and biggest companies had paid a top-of-the-cycle price for the U.S.-based mining and smelting operation.BHP shares gained 28 cents to end local trade at A$16.20, tracking a recovery in most mining stocks as overnight base metal prices improved.The company's embattled managing director,
11664 John Prescott, told reporters that while production costs had soared since BHP bought Arizona-based Magma in January, this problem would be tackled as a priority.After being told last week that Magma lost money in the 1996/97 first quarter (June/August), disgruntled shareholders were told on Tuesday at the BHP annual meeting
11664 that Magma's production costs had jumped to about 85 U.S. cents a pound to match the current spot price, meaning the operation was only a break-even proposition.This production cost compared with 68 U.S. cents when the takeover was completed."There's some one-offs in there that we need to address and there's
11664 no doubt that we can improve on the 85 cents," Prescott said."It's not as if there's some fundamental weakness in the Magma business. The basis is there for a strong performance for BHP," he said.BHP last Friday reported a below-forecast first quarter net profit of A$287 million in the three
11664 months to August 31, compared with A$372 million a year ago, due largely to a slump in profits from its copper division.While every effort would be made to fix problems at Magma, Prescott could not say when it would return to profits."Hopefully what we've seen is an aberration rather than
11664 a continuing thing," he said, adding he did not know what copper prices would do."They are at a very low level. I don't think they're going to go up a lot in the near term.""A turnaround is certainly achievable," said Peter O'Connor, an analyst for Macquarie Equities Ltd, of the
11664 Magma outlook.By world standards, analysts say an average production cost of 68 cents is high, while 85 cents is deeply troubling, particularly given the mid-year collapse of the international copper market in the wake of the Sumitomo Corp trading scandal.The benchmark copper sales price is now only about 86 cents,
11664 down from around US$1.15 at the start of the year.BHP's other major copper mines, the Escondida mine in Chile and Ok Tedi in Papua New Guinea produce copper for 40 U.S. cents or less per pound, casting a shadow over Magma.Elaine Prior, an analyst for McIntosh Securities, said costs at
11664 these mines are lower because the ore bodies are richer and there is more associated gold in them than at Magma.(A$ = 78.66 U.S. cents)-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

11682 An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale rocked Lijiang county in southwestern China's Yunnan province early on Wednesday, just months after a huge quake devastated the area, local officials said.The tremor, which hit the county at around 3.25 a.m. (1925 GMT), toppled walls and sent roof tiles tumbling in
11682 the mountain villages around scenic Lijiang town, an official of the county's anti-earthquake headquarters said.Local officials contacted by telephone said 17 people in villages near the county centre had been injured, but none seriously."We have sent people to investigate...we don't think there will be many casualties because this is a
11682 mountain area and the population is sparse," she said.Lijiang county has been struggling to rebuild its economy and tourist industry since an earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale hit the area on February 3, killing at least 304 people and injuring more than 16,000.The Xinhua news agency said Wednesday's
11682 earthquake had hit the same area as the February catastrophe.It was followed by a landslide that hit an area 100 km (60 miles) from the county centre at dawn, the official agency said but gave no details.Lijiang town's traditional architecture and Naxi ethnic minority population have long made it one
11682 of Yunnan province's top tourist attractions, but the picturesque area has been plagued by tremors in recent months.The February quake damaged more than 1.17 million homes, completely destroyed 340,000, left 160,000 people without shelter and caused huge economic damage, local officials said.Chinese experts say the country is currently going through
11682 a period of intense seismological activity that will last until the end of the century.A total of 50 earthquakes measuring more than 5.0 on the Richter scale hit China in 1995, an increase of 18.5 percent from the year before, official figures show.Tremors in China have killed more than 550,000
11682 people since 1900, accounting for 53 percent of the world's total deaths from earthquakes, Xinhua said in June.</

11694 an interview.Offices in eastern Europe will follow.Caspian, started by former Barings chief executive Christopher Heath in late 1995, now has research offices in Mexico, Argentina and Brazil.It has also opened offices in Hong Kong, Bombay, New Delhi, Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok.Offices in Taipei, Manila and Jakarta are also being considered,
11694 Clayton said.He said unlike the larger research houses which cover both developed and developing markets, Caspian will focus on the emerging markets of Latin America, Asia and eastern Europe."We are 100 percent committed to emerging markets. We are not interested in developed markets in the West like the U.S., U.K.
11694 markets," Clayton said. "We are focusing on high growth markets."Recent industry consolidation which saw big investment banks gobbling up smaller competitors cut the number of so-called boutique houses, and provided Caspian with its window of opportunity, he said."The niche is being created as a result of all previous niche players
11694 in emerging markets being acquired by the larger investment banks," Clayton said.He pointed to the acquisition of British houses Barings, Smith New Court and Kleinwort Benson by Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, Merrill Lynch of the U.S. and Germany's Dresdner Bank AG, respectively, as some examples."Those companies became part of bigger
11694 groups which are part of developed markets," he said.Caspian Holdings earlier this month announced it has raised $85 million via a rights issue to existing shareholders to expand the company's capital to $100 million.The new money, which included cash from investors in Korea, Thailand, Singapore, India and Mexico, would enable
11694 Caspian to expand into corporate finance and asset management, Caspian chief executive Heath said. 11694 Hong Kong, its regional sales and dealing centre.Its Kuala Lumpur office is the only Asian office so far with a full headcount of seven research analysts. The other offices are being built-up gradually, Clayton said.</

11709 a member, would meet on Thursday to discuss the national oil reserve policy."The five percent reserve (for imported products) is reasonable. 11709 to be required to double their stockpiles to 10 percent from January 1997. 11736 US$350."On the macroeconomic front, the government has undertaken policies which are broadly sound and good. 11736 percent in January and February."On the inflation rate, it's very good news," he said. Inflation jumped to 19 percent at end-1995 from 6.7 percent in 1994. The government hopes the rate will fall to 12 percent this year.The Laotian kip depreciated in value after inflation soared, dipping to 930 against
11736 the U.S. dollar in the second half of 1995 from 720 in the first half of the year.Wade said the government had also maintained high economic growth, and the IMF was confident that earlier predictions of a 7.5 percent growth in the gross domestic product (GDP) would continue through 1996,
11736 up from 7.1 percent in 1995."We see that growth continues to be high at 7.5 percent. 11736 economy nearly collapsed after experimenting with socialist policies in the mid-1980s. Then the cash-strapped government introduced new reforms aimed at moving towards a market economy.The government has since liberalised exchange rate policies, strictly controlled by the central bank in the past, by allowing commercial banks to set their own independent
11736 rates.The authorities have also increased revenues for the national budget and encouraged higher cash crop production to raise incomes.
