11740 could be derailed by strong opposition from Finance Ministry officials."It's still up in the air whether the reforms can be carried out as planned," Takagi said.Analysts said the coalition was unlikely to adopt its plan as a government plan ahead of the election -- which would be a way to
11740 guarantee its implemention under any government."Most probably the Liberal Democrats want to make the new body a voter-attractive portion of their plan for administrative reform, one of the biggest issues in the upcoming election campaign," the Asahi Shimbun newspaper said in an editorial.The coalition's reform plan calls for streamlining of
11740 the ministry's functions by merging its banking and securities bureaux into one. 11763 to rise to 10.2 million tonnes this year from 9.2 million tonnes in 1995. However, this may be scaled back.Kang Won Industries Co Ltd and Korea Iron and Steel Co Ltd were also expected to cut production by 20 percent, traders said. Inchon Iron and Steel Co Ltd said it
11763 preferred raising exports to cutting production."We are making every effort to enhance exports instead of cutting our output," said an Inchon Iron official."The slowdown in the domestic construction sector has helped manufacturers pile up huge stocks. Most local producers may suffer from carrying cost of record high inventories."According to a
11763 survey by KISA in July, South Korea's exports were seen climbing to more than 300,000 tonnes this year from 105,000 tonnes in 1995. The Hanbo official said export prices of deformed bar fell to $270 per tonne (FOB) in early September, compared with $300 in the first six months of
11763 this year.South Korea exports its products to Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia and also to Iran, he said.Hanbo's annual reinforcing bar production will reach about two million tonnes this year, he added.Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co Ltd has not yet decided on a course of action, a spokesman
11763 said."We have not decided yet whether to cut our production," he said."But we are well aware of the current market situation and think a cut in production may be needed to keep a balance in the domestic supply and demand.""Local steel makers will have a meeting on this matter by
11763 the end of September," the Dong Kuk spokesman said.Another option for reinforcing bar makers would be to boost exports, traders said."We are trying more than ever to export our products. We have already completed 55,000 tonnes of export deals for the fourth quarter shipment," the Hanbo official said.</

11776 tactics, they said.The NLD evolved from nationwide demonstrations in 1988 which ended with thousands killed or imprisoned when troops fired on protesters who had flocked to the streets calling for change.It was set up nine days after the military staged a coup and set up SLORC."We were founded in order
11776 to work for democracy in Burma," Suu Kyi said recently. "We were founded to prevent dictatorship from coming back."The NLD started out with a fair amount of freedom, as leaders like Suu Kyi travelled across the country in late 1988 and 1989 to talk about democracy and urge opposition to
11776 military rule.But the party's growth had since been stunted by intimidation, diplomats say."It's a desperate situation," said one diplomat when asked about the NLD's progress since 1988."There has been a systematic undermining and reduction of effectiveness of the NLD by the SLORC. NLD membership has dropped and SLORC has limited
11776 the NLD's ability to manoeuvre."A key sign that SLORC never really meant to accept opposition was seen after 1990 general elections, organised by SLORC, which the NLD won by a landslide. It was never allowed to assume power.Suu Kyi, daughter of Burma's revered independence leader, Aung San, had been put
11776 under house arrest eight months before the poll was held. After the elections, SLORC arrested many elected NLD members or frightened others into exile.Many have since been released, but the long years of imprisonment, which often included torture for political prisoners, took its toll and reduced the ranks of vocal
11776 democracy supporters, diplomats said.Suu Kyi, who was released in July 1995 after six years of house arrest, complained recently that SLORC was not allowing the NLD to function as a legally registered organisation.Party officials were regularly intimidated and the party was unable to hold formal meetings, she said.Nobel Peace Laureate
11776 Suu Kyi has been silenced from making any major attacks against the government by a new law which forbids anyone from disrupting the country's peace and stability.Diplomats said many NLD supporters were too scared to attend Suu Kyi's weekly speeches at the front gates of her house."There's just an atmosphere
11776 of repression, fear and intimidation now. SLORC's efforts have worked," one said.SLORC launched a sweeping crackdown on democracy activists in May, arresting more than 260 elected NLD members ahead of a contorversial party gathering at Suu Kyi's house.The majority were released after about 10 days, but many were forced to
11776 sign declarations agreeing to resign from the party and politics, opposition sources said.Since May, nearly 70 people have been arrested or charged by SLORC, including nine youths recently detained for distributing pamphlets outside Suu Kyi's house on the weekends.Last weekend Suu Kyi urged continued support for the NLD."When the people
11776 voted for the NLD they did so with the meaning of 'we support the NLD'. Voting for us means promising to support our work," she said."Our work has not changed. Therefore it is necessary for you to keep on supporting us as you did when you voted for us."</

11787 The latest U.S.-Iraq tensions highlight the need for Asian oil consumers to be less dependent on Middle East crude, a Japanese exploration company official said on Wednesday."It is essential to increase the self-sufficiency of oil and gas for the sake of energy security in our region." saidAkira Sakurai, Vice President
11787 of Japan National Oil Corporation (JNOC)."We should strive to promote and accelerate the exploration and development activities," he told a regional offshore oil conference.Sakurai said consuming countries needed to understand the seriousness of being over-dependent on Middle East oil due to that region's political volatility.He said projections by Japan's Institute
11787 of Energy Economics put Asia's oil demand at 17.6 million barrrels per day (bpd) in 2000, rising to 20.7 million bpd by 2005.He said China would be a bigger oil consumer than Japan by 2010, while countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), would use almost the same
11787 amount as Japan. ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and VietnamMost Asian countries would become increasingly dependent on imported oil over the next 15 years, he said. Japan now imports nearly 80 percent of its oil from the Middle East.By 2010, more than 70 percent of Asia's
11787 oil requirements would come from the Middle East if current trends continued, Sakurai said.He said the use of advanced technology would speed up oil and gas exploration in Asia. Such investments should be done by private companies, while governement should provide "reasonably attractive terms and conditions", he added.JNOC is active
11787 in oil exploration and production projects in China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Burma, Pakistan and Papua New Guinea.</
11788 Increased use of automobiles is expected to boost China's demand for gasoline and gas oil to 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2010, 3.1 times what the country consumed in 1994, a study showed on Wednesday.From 1994 to 2010, China's gasoline and gas oil demand is expected to grow
11788 by about 1.4 million bpd, which is about the equivalent of Japan's consumption in 1994, the Institute of Energy Economics (IEE), a private think-tank, said."China is expected to become a major consumer of oil products such as gasoline and gas oil, as the country becomes more reliant on cars and
11788 trucks," Yasuhiro Tanaka, an economist with the IEE, told reporters."Existing means of transportation, such as trains and ships, are not expected to have the capacity to accommodate the country's growing economy," Tanaka said.The number of automobiles in China is forecast to grow from 10.4 million in 1995 to 18 million
11788 in 2000 and 40 million in 2010, Tanaka said.The figures show China will have about 30 automobiles per 1,000 people in 2010, which is about the same as the current situation in the Philippines and Indonesia, he said."China will still be at the earliest stage of motorisation in 2010," Tanaka
11788 said.In 2010, China's gasoline demand for automobiles is forecast to be 2.7 times that of 1994, while demand for gas oil is expected to be 4.8 times higher compared to 1994, he said.Tanaka attributed the sharp jump in gas oil to an increase in the number of trucks using diesel
11788 fuel rather than gasoline.China's crude oil imports are expected to increase sharply after 2000, intensifying competition with Japan for Middle Eastern crudes, Tanaka said.</

11792 A slew of samurai bond issues by borrowers with low credit ratings are making Japanese authorities think they may need some way of resolving problems in the event of a default, market sources said on Wednesday.Japan's Ministry of Finance abolished samurai bond eligibility standards in January, opening the door for
11792 foreign issuers which have low credit ratings but want to issue such bonds, and this has spurred the recent issuing boom."Personally, I feel that there is a need to come up with some kind of measurement to cope, particularly in times of actual default," an official at the ministry said."I
11792 see it as a problem, that we do not have any resolution scheme for when trouble actually occurs," he said.Samurais are yen-denominated bonds issued in Japan by a non-Japanese borrower.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) issued a report last Wednesday warning emerging-market borrowers and retail investors in Germany and Japan of
11792 the risks posed by the mushrooming issuance of yen- and mark-denominated bonds.The IMF said the sharp increase in such issues has been led by countries in Latin America, although some eastern European nations have also been active borrowers."Basically, we feel the same way as what the IMF mentioned in that
11792 report," the MOF official said.The ministry official said concerns about repayment problems have burgeoned particularly after Bulgaria's Mineralbank failed to redeem five billion yen worth of samurai bonds to Japanese creditors when they matured in June.MOF avoided direct comment on the Mineralbank problem because its bonds were privately placed, but
11792 it has been monitoring the situation carefully.Underwriting sources estimate the volume of samurai bond issues from January up to now total a record high of about 2.9 trillion yen. Of that, about 20 percent are of sub-investment grade, which means a credit rating of below triple B (BBB).They said borrowers'
11792 eagerness to issue bonds waned a bit particularly after the Bulgarian problem, but their appetite has grown again.Mexico and the National Bank of Romania, both of which are of sub-investment grade, have recently launched samurai bonds, following a major wave of issues by Brazil and Turkey shortly after MOF's deregulation."Depending
11792 on the syndicators, Mexican bonds have mixed sales status. But in general, they are well-received by investors," one syndicate source said. "Romanian bonds have been actively absorbed due to their high coupon."Underwriting sources said more sovereign issues with low credit ratings are likely to be launched by Argentina, Turkey, Poland
11792 and Hungary in the foreseeable future."From our point of view, we don't want new regulations," said Masaru Hamazaki, deputy manager at Yamaichi Research Institute."But more important, securities firms need to acquire knowledge with which to inform the investors," he said. "It's our role to analyse in depth to provide investors
11792 with full information about issuers."Another MOF official said there was no need to create new rules, adding: "The ministry had deregulated the eligibility rules only recently... It's unlikely the government will set up rules again.""We believe investors will make decisions on their own good judgement. It is not our duty
11792 to interfere with that," he said.</

11801 or drink to drug them, stab or strangle them to death and then steal all their money and valuables, said a detailed police report on his crimes."The devil tempted me. I was short of money, living in one room with eight children, my wife and my mother," Othman told a
11801 news conference organised by the Cairo police."I'm very sad for the victims. Every time I killed one I would feel very sorry and I would cry over the body," he added.The police report said Othman killed first in 1989, when he took Abdelfattah Fahmi el-Sayyed on a trip to the
11801 northeastern province of Ismailia, poisoned him with the insecticide and stole 300 pounds (then about $130) from him."I was so relieved that I was not found out that I swore I wouldn't do it again," Othman told the news conference. "But in 1994 I needed money so I went back
11801 to killing."He killed four people in the first six months of that year, including a young female cousin from the southern town of Sohag and a young male relative, for no apparent reason.The police report said he took those two on an outing to Salhia, a thinly populated fruit-growing area
11801 northeast of Cairo, killed them and set fire to their bodies.Othman also killed in anger, stabbing one man dead in the southern town of Minya during an argument and poisoning to death a Cairo drug dealer with whom he had quarreled.His last victim, and the one whose death was traced
11801 to him, was Sayyeda Mohamed Mahmoud, a 47-year-old fruit merchant from the Cairo suburb of Rod el-Farag, where Othman also lived.He took her to Abu Sweir in the northeastern province of Sharkia, also on a fruit-buying trip, drugged her, tried to rape her, and strangled with his hands and her
11801 scarf when she resisted, the police report said.He smashed her face with a stick, knocking out three teeth, stripped her of her gold jewellery and stole 6,000 pounds ($1,760) which she was carrying, it added.He then pressed her thumbprint onto one of her cheques, which he later tried to cash
11801 at her bank. Illiterates use thumbprints instead of signatures.The police said they caught Othman because the woman was reported missing and someone had seen her in his company. Police searched his room and found stolen goods.</

11803 In his first 100 days in office, rightwing Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu has turned the Middle East clock back years, Arab leaders say.He has infuriated most of his Arab neighbours, driven Palestinians to despair and helped bring the word "war" back into the political vocabulary of the region.Gone is the
11803 goodwill which former prime minister Shimon Peres and his predecessor, assassinated leader Yitzhak Rabin, built up through three years of diplomatic footwork.Gone is the vision of a common Middle East market where, after more than 40 years of Arab-Israeli conflict, barriers to trade and travel might come tumbling down.An Israeli
11803 decision on Tuesday to open an archaeological tunnel in Jerusalem near Islam's third holiest shrine was, in Arab eyes, Netanyahu's latest provocation.The move sparked the bloodiest day of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers in the West Bank since the Jewish state handed over parts of the area to the
11803 PLO in 1994, leaving at least three Palestinians dead and 300 wounded.Netanyahu said in France he would telephone Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to try to ease tensions but did not think the violence warranted cutting short his European tour."This is the big crisis between the Israelis and the Palestinians, and
11803 the Arabs, and the Moslems and the Christians," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in the self-ruled Gaza Strip.The Gulf state of Qatar has postponed plans to open a trade office in Tel Aviv, in one of the first overt steps away from normalising relations with the Jewish state.When a
11803 Middle East economic conference meets in Cairo in November, it is likely to be a subdued affair, quite unlike the peace jamboree the Egyptian hosts had hoped to organise."Back to square one" is the phrase on the lips of many an Arab minister and in the columns of Arabic newspapers."To
11803 come in 1996 with the same ideas as in the 30s, the 40s, the 50s and the 60s, that's dangerous... We cannot go along with it," said Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.In Arab eyes, the reason for the present sour and hostile mood in Arab-Israeli relations is simple -- Netanyahu
11803 has questioned the land-for-peace principle which has been at the heart of Middle East peace diplomacy since the 1970s, when Israel gave the Sinai peninsula back to Egypt.The Madrid peace conference in 1991, at which Netanyahu's Likud party represented Israel, took place on the same understanding. In contacts with Syria,
11803 the previous Israeli government had agreed in principle to give back all the Golan Heights, Israeli and Egyptian officials say.On top of that, the Arabs say, Netanyahu has failed to put into effect measures clearly agreed between Israel and the autonomous Palestinian Authority, such as redeploying its troops in the
11803 West Bank town of Hebron.Mubarak, now firmly aligned with Syria in diplomatic confrontation with the Jewish state, has bluntly accused Netanyahu of reneging on commitments he made at their first meeting in July.All parties have been anxious to play down the risk of a shooting war but Syria has raised
11803 eyebrows in Israel by redeploying its forces in Lebanon and Israelis asked questions about this month's big military manoeuvres by Egypt.But short of war, an implausible course since they believe Israel has nuclear weapons, the Arabs have no easy options for persuading the new Israeli government to change its tune.The
11803 United States, which twisted Israel's arm to bring it to the Madrid conference, is out of the picture because of the presidential elections in November.Conventional wisdom is that U.S. presidential candidates dare not take on the influential pro-Israeli lobby.Egypt has tried a war of words, hurling epithets such as arrogant,
11803 impudent and stupid at Israel's new rulers. Some Arabs have played on Netanyahu's name, the first two syllables of which mean putrid in Arabic."I do not have a magic recipe," Moussa said in an interview this week. "But a start to serious action would be for the Arabs to stand
11803 together...and reject this approach of Netanyahu's."In June, Egypt organised the first Arab summit in five years, to coordinate the Arab response to the election of Netanyahu.It ended with a warning to Israel that Arab states would have to reconsider the gestures they have made towards Israel if Israel tries to
11803 change the ground rules for the peace talks.Arab foreign ministers met in Cairo again this month and recommended a course of action in a secret report to Mubarak.For the past 10 days Mubarak has been contacting other Arab leaders, either by telephone or by written message, but diplomats say they
11803 do not expect any dramatic decision.</

11832 U.S. researchers have found a way to detect mad cow disease with a simple test that could avoid the mass slaughter of thousands of British cattle suspected of having the disorder.The findings, to be published on Thursday in The New England Journal of Medicine, are based on the discovery of
11832 a protein in cattle, humans and other animals suffering from a class of fatal brain disorders that resemble mad cow disease. The protein is absent in other unrelated forms of dementia.Currently, the disease can only be diagnosed in brain autopsies, meaning that entire herds are often destroyed. The new test
11832 can be done on live animals."The best veterinarians have been wrong nearly one-third of the time (diagnosing mad cow disease)," California Institute of Technology (CalTech) biologist Michael Harrington said, explaining the need for an accurate diagnosis."There is no other test you can perform on a living animal. You have to
11832 slaughter it first."Harrington, with other CalTech scientists and a team of researchers at the National Institute of Health in Bethesda, Maryland, wrote the report on the new diagnosis.The protein combination linked to mad cow disease was discovered 14 years ago in humans with related nervous system disorders. But Harrington's team
11832 was the first to find an antibody that detected the presence of that protein."It was like a key that fit in a lock," he said. "We were able to develop a simple quick test that can be done in less than a day in any competent biochemistry lab anywhere in
11832 the world."Researchers conceded the test might need to be refined before it is used on volumes of cattle. Initial research was performed not on cattle but on humans suffering from a strain of the disease known as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, or Kuru, which is the most common way it is manifest
11832 in people.Kuru has been found to be most prevalent among tribes with cannibalistic practices. But researchers said it was marked by the same protein combination found in mad cow disease, so the diagnosis should work just as effectively in cattle.The ability to distinguish mad cow disease in cattle from other
11832 behaviour disorders is a breakthrough since only the mad cow class of dementia is believed to be transmitted through the food chain, posing the threat of illness or death to people who eat contaminated beef.Ten cases of mad cow disease, formally Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy, were reported in humans in the
11832 United Kingdom this year. The outbreak set off an international panic in which some health officials advised the precautionary slaughter of thousands of animals.Mad cow disease is believed to be transmitted to cattle that are fed the meat of sheep suffering from a related ailment known as scrapie for the
11832 way afflicted animals fall against walls and scrape the wool off their bodies. Cattle suffering from mad cow disease stagger, lose their balance and become uncooperative in herds.More than 160,000 cases of mad cow disease have been discovered in cattle in the United Kingdom since an outbreak that started in
11832 the mid-1980s. Feeding practices have since been changed to prevent transmission of Scrapie from sheep and scientists believe it is now on its way to being eradicated.Researchers fear many humans who ate infected beef 10 years ago may still be at risk since the disease has an incubation period of
11833 A study of more than 10,000 children has found smoking only five cigarettes a day can affect youngsters' lungs and that teenage girls are particularly vulnerable.The smoking rate among teenage girls has been rising dramatically, to the point where they have become the major source of new smokers in the
11833 United States.Researchers led by Dr. Diane Gold of Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston assessed smoking's differing effects on boys and girls by regularly examining 12,253 white children in six states. They measured each youngster's smoking habits and tested their lung capacity and ability to force air through their lungs.The
11833 data show that "smoking as few as five cigarettes per day can reduce lung function growth of both boys and girls during adolescence," Gold said. "Furthermore, we find that girls in the teen years may be particularly vulnerable to these cigarette effects."Reporting in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine, the
11833 researchers found that girls who did not smoke tended to develop the strongest lung capacity at the age of 17 or 18. But among girls in that age group who smoked, lung capacity actually declined."Rates of wheezing increased according to the amount smoked and were higher for girls than for
11833 boys at each level of smoking," the researchers found.The findings do not mean boys who smoke are immune to such problems. Smoking slowed development of the lungs in both sexes but "the defiicits may be greater in girls," the researchers said.Girls may be more likely to wheeze because they tend
11833 to be smaller than boys, so the airways leading to their lungs tend to be narrower, the researchers speculated.In previous research, Gold and her colleagues discovered smoking among teenagers increased the risk of chest illnesses, chronic cough, wheezing and bronchitis.The children involved in the study came from St. Louis; Topeka,
11833 Kansas; Portage, Wisconsin; Watertown, Massachusetts; Kingston and Harriman, Tennessee; and Steubenville and Mingo Junction, Ohio.</

11843 Bending a little-known financial instrument into a tool for his re-election campaign, President Bill Clinton on Wednesday outlined plans to issue Treasury bonds that are protected against inflation.Appearing at a campaign rally outside Pittsburgh, Clinton promoted the bonds, which guarantee an interest rate above the rate of inflation, as a
11843 new and safe way for people to save for college, retirement or buying a home."Inflation protection bonds can be a solid rock upon which families build their futures and their dreams," Clinton told a boisterous audience at the Robert Morris College. "Not a penny of value will ever be lost
11843 to anyone who buys them because of inflation."The bonds, which will first be issued in January, will have a maturity of 10 years and be designed to pay investors an interest rate above the consumer price index, one of the most common measures of inflation.Regular Treasury bonds offer no such
11843 guarantee, so as inflation rises the fixed interest they pay loses its value.The Treasury Department has long studied issuing such securities, which are used by Britain and Canada, and announced on May 16 that it intended to do so as an experiment. It said then that they would be sold
11843 in amounts as low as $1,000, putting them within reach of average Americans.The White House said on Wednesday that by January 1998 the Treasury would also start issuing inflation-protected savings bonds in amounts as low as $50, which would make them available to small savers.It also said the administration would
11843 propose legislation to eliminate the minimum-age requirement of 24 years for purchasers of education savings bonds and to widen those educational institutions that qualify for them.How the complicated world of U.S. Treasury bond issues entered the hurlyburly of a U.S. presidential election was a case study in the powers of
11843 incumbency.Knowing that the bonds were under study, Clinton was using them to enliven a campaign trip and stress saving for education, home ownership and retirement -- themes he has repeatedly evoked during this election year.National opinion polls show Clinton holding a double digit lead against his Republican opponent, Bob Dole.
11843 A Reuters poll published on Wednesday showed him with a 16 percentage point lead in Pennsylvania, beating Dole 47.7-31.7.The Dole campaign quickly criticised the bond plan, deriding it as a "new Clinton mini-proposal.""You'd need a microscope and a pair of tweezers to find Bill Clinton's vision for a second term,"
11843 Dole spokeswoman Christina Martin said in a statement. "Clinton is trying to hide behind an ever-increasing heap of mini-proposals that would expand the size and scope of government one inch at a time."While the bonds could certainly be used for all the purposes Clinton outlined, economists typically offered two, quite
11843 different, justifications for their use.The first was that the bonds, when traded, would give policymakers a much clearer read than ordinary bonds on the market's inflation expectations -- a key determinant of inflation.The second was that if the government was successful in keeping inflation low, over the longer term the
11843 bonds were expected to lower the Treasury's cost of financing the U.S. government's debt.Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the strongest argument against the plan was that it would lower resistance against inflation, but the administration decided the fear was groundless and Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan was "supportive" of the
11843 plan.Greenspan handed Clinton an election-season gift on Tuesday by not raising interest rates, suggesting the Federal Reserve believed inflation would stay tame despite the current strong growth.</

11850 Starting this fall, four big companies are creating Internet malls in perhaps the biggest test yet of whether cyberspace can become profitable.Putting the department store on the computer screen may ultimately replace or drastically change the suburban mall, some say, based on the high number of households with personal computers.Among
11850 themselves, the Internet mall operators will undoubtedly draw lots of blood because of their large financial commitment and ambitious goals.International Business Machines Corp. says that its "World Avenue" will become the "world's leading Internet mall," primarily because of the company's advanced technology, spokesman said in an interview.Time Warner Inc. believes
11850 that its "Dream Shop" will show superiority coming from its pioneering efforts on cable television and its extensive marketing know-how, according to its spokesman.The other two principal contenders are the Microsoft Corp. and America Online Inc., both capable of delivering effective shopping systems.AT&amp;T reportedly is mulling over its involvement in
11850 Internet shopping. As results begin to show, a host of smaller companies are expected to enter the competition."Dream Shop" includes such famous names as Burdine's department stores of Florida, Williams-Sonoma, Eddie Bauer, Spiegel and Sharper Image."World Avenue" has the Express division of The Limited, Hudson Bay Co. of Canada and
11850 Robert Waxman Cameras of Denver. IBM will soon announce 15 to 20 more retailers on its site, while Time Warner already has 14 and expects more soon."I can foresee 30 percent of American households eventually buying their clothing and home needs over the Internet," predicts Rod Parker, vice president for
11850 interactive merchandising at Time Warner.Ambitious claims for Internet shopping can be expected from the companies involved, of course. But a highly qualified, independent observer is perhaps even more optimistic for the Internet players, although pessimistic for traditional retailers."Internet retailing will play an important role in the future so that 10
11850 to 15 years from now, the American retail centre of gravity will swing from stores to screens," said New York's Walter K. 11850 on the Internet," Levy said. 11850 as in several search engines such as Yahoo.The general theme was on "shopping conveniently and safely," said Tim Breuer, spokesman for IBM's Distribution Industry activities. "The ads brought the consumer our 'World Avenue' but also rotated around the stores already operating in it," he said.The customer clicks on the store
11850 he or she prefers, and is then presented with various merchandise.The shopper can load up computer "shopping baskets" and click on "pay" by credit card number. Merchandise is then delivered to the customer's home.Any results yet? "We've gotten some but can't say what they are at this point," Breuer said.
11850 "We are tracking them carefully. But we are convinced that the Internet is the right medium for 'World Avenue' and is a very effective electronic commerce medium."Stressing that IBM's technology "sets us apart," he said that several technical features in "World Avenue" provide important benefits to consumers and retailers.One is
11850 "Accessorization," in which a particular store will be able to suggest complementary merchandise to a viewer who has already made a selection. Another is assembling information about each customer's shopping and buying habits so the retailer can have an Internet customer database.Time Warner's "Dream Shop" has similar features.Parker thinks that
11850 Internet shopping is much superior to TV shopping because "the upscale customer and others really want shopping on demand while TV is so linear, meaning that the TV customer has to sit there and wait for the merchandise to come to her. The interactive shopping allows the customer to take
11850 the initiative," said Parker.Levy said the success of the Internet as a selling medium "depends on how many people in the country become as used to the personal computer as they are with the gas or electric range, the telephone and the television set.""Once that number reaches a threshold point,
11850 there's no question that shopping on the Internet will thoroughly change American retailing."</

11852 Liberal arts undergraduate students often have no idea of where their interest in history, literature or psychology will lead them, but sooner or later, running their own business is likely to be an option."All too often, it hits as the only option available to someone," said Sandy Weinberg, chairman of
11852 the department of entrepreneurship at Muhlenberg College, in Allentown, Pa."If we look at current entrepreneurs, I don't think you'd find anyone who majored in entrepreneurship. It would be people who had an interest in a particular field and are applying it to make a living."Weinberg says students need to ask,
11852 "'How can I apply what I'm learning to make a living as an entrepreneur?' That's the kind of question we need to ask, and what we can help with."The school's programme, one of the few such undergraduate departments in the nation, aims to combine liberal arts studies with teaching skills
11852 needed to run a small business."The largest group of students in the programme are majoring in traditional liberal arts areas -- they really have no idea what their traditional liberal arts study may lead to," said Weinberg. "The programme aims to combine entrepreneurship with liberal arts studies."Some of the students
11852 come from family businesses and plan to return to them after graduating. Others think they will start a business sooner or later."Those people need to understand the traps and opportunities that enterpreneurship presents," said Weinberg.About 1,700 students attend Muhlenberg, a liberal arts college in northeastern Pennsylvania established in the 1840s.
11852 The entrepreneurship programme is now in its fourth year, with a total of about 30 students.Of the program's first six graduates, who entered as sophomores, all were double majors -- one in english, one in biology, and the other four in marketing and finance. About half of them are now
11852 working in their own businesses, and half are in other people's businesses."We suggest that if you want to start a business, it should be your second career move," said Weinberg. "You should make your first mistakes using someone else's money."The college encourages students to have a double major, focusing on
11852 a traditional liberal arts area as well as entrepreneurship."I'm not sure a student ought to spend the kind of money Muhlenberg costs -- $17,000 -- and get just a single major. We encourage a double major," said Weinberg."I can't imagine a parent paying that kind of money if the student
11852 is going to end up opening a T-shirt store. If all you want to do is start a small business, you may be better off taking that tuition money and investing it in that small business," he said."But if you're studying to be a biologist or a physician and decide
11852 to apply this somewhere else, you should understand how a business pays off. This is not an end in itself, but a process."Students in Muhlenberg's entrepreneurial programme take the school's basic business curriculum of five courses in general accounting, marketing, management, finance and macro-economics. They are also required to complete
11852 another 20 courses in liberal arts, human behaviour, foreign language, physical education and other areas.The entrepreneurship courses include small business management; internship in a small business; consulting through the college's small business institute; and what Weinberg calls "Capstone Strategies" -- studying other startup efforts that have succeeded or failed.In the
11852 small business management course, "We take them from developing a business plan to starting a company, getting financing and as far as developing an exit strategy," Weinberg said.As part of the internship programme, students work in a startup company for several hours a week. For example, one student is working
11852 with a local publishing company doing a marketing survey; another is doing marketing for a small restaurant that wants to expand.In the college's Small Business Institute, students are assigned to a small company to work on solving a specific problem.To offer students more hands-on experience, the school also has set
11852 up several on-campus ventures. One of them, an electronic publishing company, publishes books, student poetry, laboratory manuals and even a history board game on computer disks.A student-run late-night convenience store and snack bar serves the local community, and a medical services venture modelled on a health maintenance organisation supplies prescription
11852 and non-prescription pharmaceuticals to supplement the college-run student health services.Questions or comments on the Newbiz column can be addressed to DANIEL.GREBLER@REUTERS.COM@INTERNET</

"On the plus side we have banks, food stocks and household products -- those whose earnings tend to do well if the
11854 economy slows. On the negative side, autos and retailers."Citicorp edged up 1/8 to 89-7/8, Sara Lee added 7/8 to 34-3/4, General Motors lost 7/8 to 47-1/2 and Sears Roebuck fell 1/4 to 45-1/2.Wall Street again punished companies that warned that their earnings would disappoint.Apple South slumped 7-7/8 to 13 and
11854 Checkpoint tumbled nine to 27-3/8 after both said their earnings would fall short of expectations."There is a deep concern that earnings are going to slow and you need to pick the stocks of companies that will continue to post good earnings," Johnson said.Among other stocks, Loral Space rose 2-1/2 to
11854 15-3/4 after agreeing to buy AT&amp;T's SkyNet Satellite Services for $712.5 million. The deal would create one of the world's largest satellite-based businesses. AT&amp;T rose 1/4 to 51-3/4 after Tuesday's 5-5/8-point drubbing on its downbeat earnings forecast.Apria Healthcare lost 3-3/8 to 17-3/8. The company said its third-quarter income would fall
11854 short of Wall Street expectations.TCSI Corp., a maker of communications software for telephone companies, lost 5-1/4 to 15-1/2 on market talk that the company would not meet third-quarter earnings expectations. Company officials were not available for comment.Biotechs rallied from a summer slump after some positive industry news. Protein Design jumped
11854 9-7/8 to 26 after the company and Roche Holding said their Zenepax drug was successful for preventing kidney transplant rejection in a late-stage trial.Several initial public offerings drew buying interest. Snyder Communications, which provides outsourced marketing services, surged 3-5/8 to 20-5/8.American Residential Services, a provider of heating, ventilation and air
11854 conditioning systems service, rose three to 18 and Coffee People lost 3/4 to 8-1/4.Among stronger technology stocks, International Business Machines rose 2-3/8 to 126-1/2, Micron rose 1-1/8 to 32-1/2, Cisco Systems was up 2-11/16 to 63-3/16 and Intel added 3/4 to 97-1/4.The Standard &amp; Poor's composite index of 500 stocks
11854 rose 0.22 of a point to 685.83. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.49 to 565.89.The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.07 to 365.30. The average share was up 1 cent.The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues --

11855 Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole brushed aside his low standing in polls on Wednesday and confidently predicted victory over President Bill Clinton based on his economic plan.Dole flew to Amana, Iowa, for a farm rally at a huge farm equipment show, the Farm Progress Show, which draws 100,000 people daily
11855 and expressed a confidence he will be elected even though he lags by double digits in polls.Dole, from neighbouring Kansas and introduced as "the hero of the heartland," promoted his economic programme based on tax cuts and asked the rally crowd to compare his plan to Clinton's, a focus he
11855 believes will get voters to switch to him once they know his programme."Take a look at President Clinton's record of high taxes, high spending and a slow growth economy and compare it to our plan," he said."Our plan is simply this: you keep more of your freedom, and more money
11855 in your pocket or more money in your paycheck ... and get the economy moving," Dole said."We've had the slowest growth we've had in a century," Dole said, repeating a claim Clinton disputes by noting the long period of economic expansion.Dole wound up a two-day campaign trip to Detroit, Shelby,
11855 Ohio, St. Louis and Iowa before heading back to Washington and then on to Florida for preparations for presidential debates.In St. Louis he said he would win the election because he had better ideas.And his running mate Jack Kemp went further on a morning television interview, saying overcoming a double-digit
11855 lead by Clinton would be "a piece of cake."Dole was in a fighting mood before about 2,000 students jammed into an auditorium at St. Louis University.This was supposed to be the date of the first debate between Dole and Clinton at nearby Washington University, but both camps changed the date
11855 of the first of two debates to Oct. 6 in Hartford, Connecticut, and excluded Reform Party candidate Ross Perot from taking part.The paths of Dole and Perot -- who blames Dole and a bipartisan debate commission for shutting him out of the debates -- crossed in this city.Perot planned to
11855 come to St. Louis University on Wednesday night when he is expected to continue his campaign to get into the debates. Perot also has filed a federal lawsuit in his bid to be a debater.Dole urged the students here to tune into the debate a week from Sunday so "you'll
11855 hear from Bob Dole, the next president of the United States."A few pro-Perot hecklers were in the college audience, but Dole told his cheering student fans "don't be distracted by the noises here, it's all going to be over and we're going to win, we're going to win because we
11855 have the ideas because we have the agenda."Dole pushed his economic package, centred on a 15 percent income tax cut, a capital gains tax cut and a $500 per child tax credit, at the rally in St. Louis.This Mississippi River city was in an ecstatic mood since its St. Louis
11855 Cardinals baseball team clinched the National League Central Division on Tuesday, the first time the team had won a playoff spot since 1987."And there's good reason to celebrate today," Dole said, noting the win by the Cardinals.He then joked "if I wanted to titillate the press I would have said
11855 the St. Louis Browns" -- referring to the city's long departed baseball team in a joke about his comment in California last week when he congratulated a pitcher for the long-gone "Brooklyn Dodgers" for a no-hitter instead of the Los Angeles Dodgers.</
11856 Mexico's foreign minister expressed concern on Wednesday over a "new mood" of hostility to foreign migrants in the United States but said he was relieved a draft immigration bill had been watered down.Congressional negotiators on Tuesday approved details of a bill that deletes a Republican-backed provision allowing states to bar
11856 the children of illegal immigrants from public schools. Both houses of Congress now have to vote on the bill.Speaking before talks with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, Mexico's secretary of foreign affairs, Jose Angel Gurria, said he was "relieved that it's not going to have the chapter on education."But
11856 he told reporters he was "worried more generally about the context in which all this legislation is being proposed.""That is something, by the way, which we feel will stay. It's not a question of, you know, disappearing after the November (U.S. presidential) election," he said."I think there is a new
11856 mood, and it's not good. We don't like what we see in terms of the attitudes of some members of the Congress and some regions in the United States, where the phenomenon of migration has given rise to attitudes which seem to be very hostile to migrants."Gurria said that while
11856 Mexico did not want to encourage illegality, "we're worried about the impact on human rights, labour rights." The country also feared that attitudes toward illegal migrants could spill over into attitudes toward legal migrants, he said.State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said later that Gurria's remarks had struck a chord with
11856 Christopher."Frankly, I can tell you that Secretary Christopher ... was in substantial agreement that the United States needed to remain an outward-focused country, a country that is open to foreigners, open certainly to immigration," he told reporters.Both Gurria and Christopher played down differences over the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which punishes
11856 foreign companies that use property in Cuba that was seized by the Communist government in Havana from people who are now U.S. citizens. One Mexican and one Canadian firm have so far been targeted.Gurria said the issue had "got everybody worried" but he had been working with Christopher and his
11856 aides "in terms of how we can deal with the situation."Christopher said Washington wanted to implement the law in a way that would hurt Cuba and minimise the impact on U.S. allies. The Clinton administration, clearly unenthusiastic about the law, has suspended a provision allowing Americans to sue foreign firms
11856 "trafficking" in their former property.Gurria and Christopher hailed their countries' cooperation in the fight against the drug trade. Recent years have seen rising quantities of illicit drugs shipped through Mexico to the United States from producer countries in South America.Burns said that as part of U.S. anti-drug aid to Latin
11856 America, the United States would supply Mexico with 20 helicopters for use along the two countries' common border and hoped to be able to provide 53 more later.Out of $100 million promised on Tuesday by President Bill Clinton to help Latin American countries fight drug trafficking, $37 million will go
11857 Prices on the New York Stock Exchange closed higher in heavy trading Wednesday.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 3.33 to 5877.36.The NYSE composite rose 0.07 to 365.30.The average price per share rose $0.01.Gainers beat losers 1298 to 1033.Volume was 451,698,160, compared with 457,893,720 Tuesday.</

11862 Service Corp. International, North America's largest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries, said Wednesday it was committed to buying Loewen Group Inc. despite having been rebuffed by its smaller rival.Houston-based Service Corp., which last week offered to buy Loewen in a friendly stock transaction valued at $2.8 billion, said it
11862 will hold a board meeting on Oct. 1 to consider its next move.Industry analysts said they expected Service Corp. to launch a hostile takeover bid, perhaps as early as next week.After meeting for about seven hours to discuss the offer, Loewen's board of directors late Tuesday unanimously rejected it, saying
11862 the unsolicited $43-a-share bid was inadequate and that it intended to remain an independent company."We are disappointed that the Loewen board of directors rejected our proposals without ever returning our calls or seeking more information from us. The actions of the Loewen board simply deprive its stockholders of the oppportunity
11862 to receive prompt value for their shares," Service Corp. Chairman Robert Waltrip said in a statement.Service Corp. disclosed its offer last week and indicated it would be willing to raise the bid if Loewen granted it access to its financial records. The offer also calls for Service Corp. to assume
11862 about $1.3 billion of Loewen debt."I think (a hostile bid) looks fairly assured," said Kara Cheseby at the brokerage Legg Mason Wood Walker.Service Corp. could not be reached for comment."I think (Service Corp.) ought to withdraw their offer and that will really anger the Loewen shareholders," said Todd Richter of
11862 Dean Witter. However, he acknowledged that Service Corp. is unlikely to walk away from the proposed transaction.Instead, he speculated Service Corp. may try to lure Loewen shareholders by offering a higher price in a hostile offer.Meanwhile, Loewen defended its decision and said it would not even be swayed by an
11862 offer as high as $52 a share. Analysts have speculated that Service Corp. could afford to pay as much as $50 a share without diluting its own earnings."I can't see any intellectual reason or rationale how the two could come together," Chief Executive Officer Raymond Loewen said in a telephone
11862 conference call. "I do not see any rational reason how they could ever acquire our company."He also said Loewen's growth prospects were superior to Service Corp.'s, adding that this year's sales would exceed $900 million and would increase by about $300 million annually.Analysts have said that Service might have a
11862 difficult time winning Loewen in a hostile bid because Raymond Loewen holds about 15 percent of the company's common shares and insiders hold about another 3 percent.Service Corp. noted that its offer represented a 48.9 percent premium over the price Loewen stock was trading at 30 days before its offer."In
11862 addition, since Loewen stockholders would be receiving stock, they would continue to participate in Loewen's business as well as share in the upside of our business," said Service Corp. President William Heiligbrodt.The belief that Service Corp. will pursue Loewen on a hostile basis comes mainly from its aggressive track record.Service
11862 Corp. successfully wooed funeral firm Great Southern Group Plc of Britian two years ago despite an initial rejection. Service eventually paid $174.1 million for the British company after hiking its offer twice for Great Southern, which was holding talks with Loewen and another potential buyer.Just a few weeks later it
11862 bought Plantsbrook Plc, also of Britain, for $290 million. The two acquisitions gave Service Corp. a 15 percent stake in the British funeral home market.Shares of Loewen rose about 34 cents to $41.34 on Nasdaq. Service Corp. stock lost 50 cents to $29.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.</

11872 Sales of existing homes eased in August for a third month in a row, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday, though not enough to suggest a sharp decline in the housing market.The real estate lobby group said sales of existing, or used, homes fell 0.5 percent in August to
11872 a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.13 million. That followed a revised decline of 0.2 percent to 4.15 million in July and a sharper 2.8 percent drop in June sales.Resales of used homes exceeded four million a year for six consecutive months through August, a sizzling pace that industry analysts
11872 said underlined the durability of the housing sector."These numbers are reflecting a very healthy housing market right now," said economist David Lereah of the Mortgage Bankers Association. "According to these numbers, there is no sign of a slowdown."The real estate agents' group revised upward its estimate of July sales to
11872 an annual rate of 4.15 million instead of the 4.14 million it reported a month ago.A boom in homebuilding and sales helped power the robust 4.8 percent annual rate of expansion in the national economy during the second quarter -- the most vigorous growth in two years.Sales of existing homes
11872 peaked in May at a record rate of 4.28 million a year."The nation's housing market is easing in for a soft landing," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors. After the surge in sales earlier in the year, he said, "it's only natural that the market
11872 will correct itself."Economist David Seiders of the National Association of Home Builders said a slowing in housing activity -- both building and sales -- might be welcomed at this point.Policy-making members of the Federal Reserve decided on Tuesday against raising interest rates, apparently believing the overall economy was cooling on
11872 its own enough to keep inflation in check."Things are still at a very good level for housing activity but it's pretty clear the pace will be down for the third quarter," Seiders said. "That's probably the way that the Fed saw the housing sector," he added.The moderate waning in sales
11872 of used homes last month occurred despite somewhat cheaper long-term mortgage rates.The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said the average rate for a 30-year mortgage loan in August was 8 percent, down from July's 8.25 percent average and June's 8.32 percent.During August, sales of existing homes fell
11872 9.5 percent in the Northeast to 570,000 a year, while in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing market, they were down 1.9 percent to a rate of 1.53 million.But in the Midwest, August sales edged up 0.9 percent to a rate of 1.07 million a year and in the
11872 West they increased strongly, by 5.6 percent to 950,000 a year.The average price for an existing home resold in August was $149,900, up slightly from $149,600 in July.</

11876 The Senate Wednesday approved a four-year International Natural Rubber Agreement designed to control the price and supply of the commodity, which is essential to a host of major American industries.The Senate approved the agreement by voice vote. The House does not debate treaties.The United States has entered into two previous
11876 rubber pacts, in 1979 and 1987. But the Clinton administration has said this is the last such treaty the United States intends to agree to, saying it is time to move toward a free market.Supporters of the agreement said it was needed to prevent wide price swings and protect domestic
11876 industries. The United States is the world's largest user of natural rubber, but produces none of its own."Virtually all Americans, whether they're aware of it or not, depend on rubber products every day of the week. Any American who drives a car or rides a bus or takes a taxi
11876 to work relies on rubber products," said Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms."Many Americans may not be aware that we are completely dependent on foreign countries for our supply of natural rubber," the North Carolian Republican said.Opponents charged that the International Natural Rubber Organisation, established under the agreements, was
11876 basically a cartel that artificially set prices and hurt American consumers."Big labour, big business, importers all favour the treaty. People who are concerned about the taxpayers of this country and consumers of this country will want to vote against this treaty," said Colorado Republican Sen. Hank Brown.In a letter to
11876 Congress earlier this summer, President Clinton said U.S. participation in one final pact was needed to give business and labour time to prepare for a free market in rubber.He also said the agreement would strengthen U.S. relations with Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand, which together account for about 80 percent of
11876 the world production of natural rubber.The agreement stabilises prices through use of a buffer stock of not more than 550,000 tons. The buffer stock is used to keep rubber prices, which in the past have fluctuated wildly, within a set price band.Both producing and consuming national contribute funds to the
11876 buffer stock, according to their share of world rubber exports and imports.The pact contains language barring members of the rubber organisation from acting to manipulate rubber prices or restrict supplies outside the agreement.</
11877 The White House released documents Wednesday that it said proved President Clinton's insistence that the collection of confidential FBI reports on Republicans was simply a bureaucratic blunder.But a Senate investigator said other documents continued to raise questions about the improper White House acquisition of hundreds of FBI files on former
11877 Republican officials, although nefarious purposes had not been proven.White House officials said the documents showed White House security aide Anthony Marceca was working from inaccurate lists produced by the Secret Service when he obtained the FBI secret background files.A White House associate counsel, Mark Fabiani, released a thick stack of
11877 papers that he said constituted the faulty Secret Service lists Marceca was using. He said the White House would have released them sooner but they had been in the custody of Kenneth Starr, the independent counsel investigating cases involving Clinton and his wife, Hillary."These newly revealed Secret Service lists support
11877 what the White House has said all along about the FBI files matter: The files were mistakenly sought as the result of a bureaucratic blunder," Fabiani said.Republicans have suggested that in collecting the files on Republicans, the White House was compiling an "enemies list" and committed an extreme violation of
11877 privacy.At a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on the so-called "filegate" affair Wednesday, Chairman Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican, called the White House release of documents "irrelevant" because Marceca knew at the time that officials of prior administrations were included in the file requests, as shown by other documents.Hatch said a
11877 log in which Marceca's office recorded the receipt of FBI files contained unexplained gaps and the committee had discovered pages had been deliberately removed.He cited a memo from Marceca's former boss at the personnel security office, Craig Livingstone, to former White House associate counsel William Kennedy, saying: "Once the initial
11877 rush subsides we will begin to request copies of files from the FBI on carryovers. This will be our first glance at the background information of their employees."Livingstone testified to the committee that the memo merely dealt with White House employees who were being retained by the Clinton administration. He
11877 said he had no recollection of removing pages from the log or asking anyone else to do so and he believed a six-month gap in the log was due merely to the fact that it had not been kept up to date.The House Government Reform and Oversight Committee adopted an
11877 interim report on the FBI files case Tuesday and called for FBI General Counsel Howard Shapiro to resign. It accused the White House of trying to politicize the bureau.In prepared testimony to the Judiciary Committee, Shapiro said he regretted that contacts he had with the White House in the file
11877 affair had raised questions about the FBI's independence and in hindsight would do things differently.The records released by the White House had been part of two boxes of documents the White House turned over to the FBI in June and the FBI turned them over to Starr's office.When Starr was
11877 asked to return them, the White House was told they would be sent back when disclosure "would not hinder or impede our investigation." Deputy independent counsel John Bates returned the lists Tuesday, saying in a letter that "we believe that time has been reached."Fabiani said the release of the lists
11877 undermined the Republicans' argument by proving the Secret Service produced them in June 1993 -- months after Clinton took office. This would mean the Secret Service was mistakenly giving the White House names of people who no longer worked there, he said.</
11878 Scientists are developing vaccines that could save the lives of millions of children a year, but the price may prove a huge barrier to poor nations, world health officials said on Wednesday.A report by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and UNICEF surveyed progress in reaching children around the world with
11878 vaccines now available and prospects for new or improved vaccines that could save up to 8 million more children a year within 10 or 15 years."The 21st century is the century of the vaccine," said Dr. Ciro de Quadros, a top WHO adviser on immunisation. But he added, "The vaccine
11878 of the future will be more expensive than the vaccine of today."Many of the newer vaccines use genetic or molecular biology technology that is much more expensive than the older vaccines that cost a few cents a dose. Vaccine development also occurs mainly in the private sector in industrialised countries
11878 and these vaccines may not work as well against the slightly different strains of diseases in poorer countries, where the market is not as profitable for drug companies.Scientists and health officials at a WHO briefing in Washington also pointed out that vaccines were a potent weapon against diseases and infections
11878 that were becoming dangerously resistant to antibiotics.WHO and UNICEF noted huge successes in the past two decades. Since 1974, the percentage of children vaccinated against polio, measles, tetanus, diphtheria, whooping cough and tuberculosis has risen from 5 percent to 80 percent of the 130 million children born each year.That drive
11878 against those six childhood killers, carried out under the Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI), saves an estimated two million more lives a year. But of the 12 million children under age 5 who die each year, 2 million die from diseases that could be prevented by vaccines. In some African
11878 nations, vaccination rates are still only about 50 percent.Vaccines against hepatitis B and yellow fever have been added to the EPI list but are not yet widely available in developing nations. For instance, of 33 countries identified as at risk for yellow fever, vaccine coverage was only 9 percent in
11878 1994. In some places, it was all but nonexistent.In recent years there has been a shift so that all but the poorest countries have become self-sufficient in paying for EPI vaccines, which cost only a few pennies each. But the next generation of vaccines, against diseases like rotavirus, shigella, dengue
11878 and meningitis, may cost dollars instead.WHO and UNICEF outlined four major goals to get around what they called a "herculean" funding task.They are not asking for free vaccines for poor countries but they do want more "tiered pricing" so that manufacturers charge less to poorer nations. They also want governments
11878 and donors to commit to spend more on vaccines and they want aid targeted better to countries in most need.They also said more public health and advocacy was required so that governments and donor countries, which may not balk at expensive drugs and hospital expenses, recognise the value of vaccines."In
11878 the long run, treatment to save the lives of children not immunised against vaccine-preventable diseases and the legacy of disabled children will cost a lot more -- both in money and needless suffering for children and their families," the agencies concluded.</

11883 with the opening planned for the summer of 1988.The project involves renovating the St. Moritz Hotel to its former Art Deco splendor and building 700 new rooms in a 17-story tower. The architects promise to blend classic Florida architecture with the new Miami beach spirit.The Loews Miami Beach Hotel is
11883 located in the heart of the Art Deco district, once a rundown area which in recent years has undergone a rennaissance into a district of trendy restaurants, nightclubs and shops.But the lack of business-standard accommodations was harming the Miami Convention Centre, prompting the Miami Beach City Commission to seek partners
11883 for a new luxury hotel. Loews beat five other bidders to secure the project."Loews hotels is very opportunistic but also conservative when it comes to expansion," said Chief Executive Officer Jonathan Tisch, who was in Miami for Thursday's ground-breaking ceremony."But given the uniqueness of the site, the growth of Miami
11883 Beach and the city's involvement it was something we couldn't pass up," he said.The city will provide $29 million, Loews $40 million and $66 million more will come in a loan from a consortium of banks headed by Bankers Trust, Tisch said. The Miami Beach Redevelopment Agency is providing $50
11883 million in incentives.Tisch said he expected 70 percent of the trade to be from group business and 30 percent from individual travelers, and hopes hotel will turn a profit as soon as possible."The early response from groups has been terrific." 11883 to date.Tisch himself is no stranger to Miami or its hotels. His father built the Americana, now the Sheraton Bal Harbour, 40 years ago."I have fond memories of that place. I learned to swim in the pool at the Americana in the early 1960s. I met President Kennedy there in
11883 1962."Loews Hotels is part of Loews Corp., which is controlled by the Tisch family. 11883 Inc. They are the 750-room Portofino Hotel, slated to open in 1999, and the 1,200 room Royal Bali Hotel, set to open in 2000, Tisch said.</

11892 A computer specialist for a U.S. Navy intelligence agency has been arrested on espionage charges for passing secret and top-secret documents to a South Korean Embassy official, the FBI said on Wednesday.It said Robert Kim, 56, an 18-year government employee who worked at a U.S. Navy intelligence office in Suitland,
11892 Maryland, was arrested without incident Tuesday night at a diplomatic reception at Fort Myer, Virginia.Kim was charged with passing classified information to a South Korean agent, a naval attache at the embassy in Washington identified as Capt. Dong-Il Baek.Baek's office declined to comment, but a Justice Department source said the
11892 naval officer, who arrived in 1994 for a three-year tour, would soon leave the United States for Seoul.At a five-minute court hearing in Alexandria, Virginia, prosecutor Robert Chestnut said Kim should be held in jail without bail "because of his close relationship with Korea, there is a serious risk of
11892 flight."Jim Clark, a court-appointed defence lawyer, replied that Kim's wife and son live in the area and denying him bond "unfairly prejudges Mr. Kim." A federal magistrate set a new hearing for Monday on whether Kim should be held without bond.Kim, of Sterling, Virginia, was born in Seoul and became
11892 a U.S. citizen in 1974. He was charged with passing the classified information from May through September.FBI agent Gloria Harbold said in a 21-page affidavit that Kim regularly searched the Navy intelligence computer system for secret and top-secret documents."Kim copies and stores these documents in his work computer, removes classification
11892 markings and prints them on his office printer and transmits them to Baek," she said.Harbold said investigators obtained evidence against Kim from electronic and video surveillance, and searches at work and his mail.She said the FBI on May 5 seached his work computer, finding a file containing a letter dated
11892 Jan. 24, 1996, in which Kim offered his services to Baek. Kim said he hoped Baek had digested "the materials I have sent you" and warns him to "please be careful."Harbold said Kim had stored in his computer a number of "K" files containing U.S. government documents on North and
11892 South Korea and other Asian-Pacific countries.On May 10, electronic surveillance revealed Kim telephoned Baek and Baek confirmed he received "it" -- an apparent reference to a package of several classified documents. Baek added, "You don't know much much I treasure this."Harbold said the FBI on several occasions in August and
11892 September even intercepted envelopes Kim had mailed to Baek, opened them to find various classified documents, and then allowed all but a few of the documents to be received.The FBI said its surveillance revealed Kim playing golf at a course in Fort Meade, Maryland, with Baek and two high-ranking South
11892 Korean naval officials."I know that Kim has used his vehicle and briefcase to transport classified documents from his office to his home and to the home of Captain Baek. Kim has also used manila envelopes and stamps that Baek provided him with return address labels," Harbold said.A Justice Department official
11892 said the case was much less signficant than the scandal involving former Central Intelligence Agency agent Aldrich Ames, who was sentenced to life in prison for spying for Moscow for $2.5 million.Kim was charged under an espionage law that carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison, the official
11892 said.Clinton administration officials said they were disturbed by the incident but it was unlikely to affect U.S.-Korea ties."Relations between the United States and the Republic of Korea are strong and of the nature that they can endure any alleged wrongdoing by an individual," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.Secretary
11892 of State Warren Christopher said he was very disturbed by Kim's arrest and said Washington had been in touch with South Korean officials over the case.</

11894 the candidates answer questions from undecided voters."What they're trying to do is renegotiate several points. 11894 signed it. 11894 would take notes. I can't imagine President Clinton would want to take advantage of his war wounds," he said.In the 1992 town hall meeting between Clinton, President George Bush and Ross Perot, the three candidates sat on bar stools took no notes.As for changing the time of the debate, Dole
11894 officials said that was in everybody's best interests to ensure as large a television audience as possible.Warfield said campaign experts were still reviewing the draft agreement before signing it because it contained new elements not agreed to in the negotiations.The two sides agreed on Saturday to hold two presidential and

11896 How many of us have enjoyed a vacation, only to find its restful effects diminished within days, or even hours, of returning to work?A resort vacation can delightful in the short run, but after the photos are developed and the sun tan fades, there's often little to remember.But combine a
11896 resort setting with programmes designed to enrich the body, soul or intellect, and you may end up getting something of long-lasting value at a price no greater than your budget can afford."Vacations like this are not necessarily cheap, but they will last all your life," said Ellen Lederman, author of
11896 the new book, "Vacations That Can Change Your Life" (Sourcebooks, November 1996, $16.95)."Work only goes so far. It doesn't give a lot of personal satisfaction," said Lederman, a counsellor and occupational therapist in Alpharetta, Ga., an Atlanta suburb.Often in a bucolic or a resort-like setting, many run by not-for-profit organisations,
11896 vacationers can participate in typical activites such as sports, swimming or hiking while learning life-long skills, such as a language, meditation or conflict resolution.Lederman breaks adventure, workshop or retreat vacations into five very flexible categories: holistic, spiritual, health and healing, self-imporovement and learning.Holistic vacations integrate mind, body and spirit. Vacationers
11896 can take classes in such things as dream interpretation, eating disorders and assertiveness training in resort-like settings."This is different from a spa in that it is a lot less passive," she said. "Here, (a vacationer) is actively engaged in change ... You don't say 'do for me' as you would
11896 at a spa."Here, you're learning ways to change your life, and change in the future."Examples of this type of vacation are Eselen Institute, Big Sur, Calif. (408-667-3000) and another well known example is Disney Institute in Orlando, Fla. (800-496-6337).A spiritual vacation would be a religious retreat, with accommodations ranging from
11896 the simple at a monestary or ashram, to the more lavish at a resort."It gives you a chance to regroup -- go into a beautiful setting and get yourself together," Lederman said.On a healing and health-promoting vacation, "weight reduction goes beyone fat farms -- it's not just a quick fix,"
11896 she said.Several run by the Seventh Day Adventist Church offer vegetarian diets and exercise but are "more supportive than a spa." One such area is the Wildwood Lifestyle Centre, Wildwood, Ga. (800-634-9355).Self-improvement vacations offer the opportunity to build or improve relationships. Most vacations provide the time to focus on the
11896 individual, such as classes in assertiveness training, goal setting or stress reduction.The Option Institute and Fellowship, in Sheffield, Mass., (413-229-2100) was founded by a father of an autistic boy. Here, people go for a week to better their communications skills and, hopefully, become more able to cope with the ups
11896 and downs of life.Learning vacations combine the relaxation of a traditional vacation with the opportunity to learn a new skill, such as a foreign language, filmmaking, dramatic arts or writing.At Camp Winnarainbow in Berkeley, Calif. (510-525-4304), the study of circus skills and performing arts helps build self-confidence, Lederman said.The Rowe
11896 Camp and Conference Centre in Rowe, Mass., (413-339-4954), run by the Unitarian Universalist Church, is a holistic summer camp for adults and children, where among other activities, visitors can take classes in how to laugh.Lederman said that on average a value-added vacation will cost about $100 a day, including accommodations,
11896 classes and meals.However, since many of the resorts are run by not-for-profit organisations, prospective visitors should ask if scholarships are available. Also, some may offer work/study programmes, where a reduction in fees might be given in exchange for gardening, meal preparation or office duties.When selecting a vacation of this type,
11896 Lederman suggests that visitors do a bit of research and read brochures to get a feel for what is offered and to whom the centre is geared."This book is just the first step in determining what kind of vacation to take," she said.To order "Vacations That Can Change Your Life,"
11896 call Sourcebooks at 1-800-43-BRIGHT (274448).- - - -You can write to Judith Schoolman at Reuters, 199 Water Street, 10th floor, New York, N.Y. 10038. E-mail JUDITH.SCHOOLMAN(at)REUTERS.COM.</
11897 The United States said on Wednesday it was considering evacuating thousands more Kurds from northern Iraq because it believed they were at risk.State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said the Kurds being considered for airlift worked for private voluntary organisations that helped maintain the U.S.-led safe haven in northern Iraq.The
11897 programme of assisting and protecting Kurds in the region collapsed after troops of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein several weeks ago entered the north to help one Kurdish faction defeat its rival in armed conflict."No decision has been made on this (but) it is our inclination to do this if we
11897 can," Davies said.The United States recently evacuated to the Pacific island of Guam via Turkey 2,100 Kurds and their families who were working directly for U.S. government in northern Iraq.Davies said the new evacuation under discussion would involve "thousands" more Kurds. "We do believe there are credible threats to this
11897 second group of people," he said, refusing to go into details.Davies also said he could not discuss logistics for the evacuation because those plans are still under discussion.He said the United States did not evacuate these Kurds with the first wave last week because its "first loyalty" was to its
11897 direct employees who were considered at greatest risk of attack by Saddam's forces. Also, the U.S. employees were all in one place and clearly identified, he said.</
