11899 Frequent flyer miles, created to keep you hooked on an airline, seem worthless unless you accumulate enough to get a free air ticket.But for jet-setting business travelers, yet another trip on a packed airplane is hardly a bonus after months of wearying travel.Airlines' answer -- free miles for such unlikely
11899 deals as your mortgage payment, home purchases and cash advances on your credit card. And rewards that money cannot buy.Like a chance to be Circus Ringmaster of The Greatest Show on Earth in the city of your choice. Or Honorary Coach of the Harlem Globetrotters. How about a private skating
11899 lesson by Nancy Kerrigan? Or hammering nails with former President Jimmy Carter to build a home for a needy family?All these awards are yours for an estimated 100,000 to 300,000 Northwest Airlines miles at the carrier's DreamPerks Auction at Sotheby's on Friday. If you lack the miles to bid, you
11899 can buy them for 5 cents a mile, making the 35 fantasy awards worth $5,000 to $15,000 each. Most of the packages include first class flights and luxury lodgings for two.Northwest, which has 15 million mileage holders, will donate proceeds mainly to Habitat for Humanity International to build homes for
11899 the needy worldwide."Frequent flyer miles have become a kind of de facto currency," said David Redden, senior vice president and director of Sotheby's New York. "You need creativity to spend the miles. This is a mechanism for dealing with that dilemma."Airlines are wracking their brains to reward you for flying
11899 with them because, despite the cost, it's better than losing a customer to a competitor.American Airlines now allows members to earn one mile for every dollar of interest paid on a new mortgage with one of five lenders. Consumers can also earn 15,000 miles for every $100,000 of the purchase
11899 or sale price of a home when using a participating real estate broker.For example, the sale of a $150,000 home would earn 22,500 miles -- more than enough for a coach flight within the continental United States (20,000 miles).Even payments for such mundane services as lawn mowing, carpet cleaning or
11899 housekeeping will now earn miles, not to mention telephone and credit card bills.Awards are now easier to earn because some require fewer than the 15,000 miles needed for free air tickets or upgrades. American Airline now offers one-night stays at major hotel chains for as few as 10,000 miles and
11899 a two-day weekday or three-day weekend car rental for 12,000 miles.In other words, frequent flyer mile programmes are here to stay. And, in case you didn't know, miles on Continental, USAir and Delta Air Lines do not expire. So it pays to treat them as currency you can shop with,
11899 accumulate sweat-free and even use for retirement. And compare programmes."Consumers always screw up and assume all programmes are created equal," said Randy Peterson, editor and publisher ofo Inside Flyer magazine (800-209-2870) in Colorado Springs, Colo."Do you want a free ticket to Hawaii? If so, choose an airline that goes there.
11899 USAir does not."If do not fly a lot, get on a programme with miles that don't expire, because it could take you four or five years to earn a free trip. Stick with an airline instead of scattering your miles among rivals.This is especially important for frequent flyers because most
11899 airlines offer special perks like free upgrades, bonus miles and advance boarding to consumers who fly 25,000 miles or more a year on the carrier.Accumulate miles faster on land by charging purchases on an affiliated credit, and using a long distance phone carrier that offers free miles. For example, American
11899 Express card holders earn miles that can be used on Delta, Continental, USAir, Aeromexico, Swissair, Sabena and Southwest Airlines.MCI Communications Corp. lets you earn free travel on American, Continental, Northwest or Southwest Airlines."Get the most value from your miles instead of just using them" anyhow, said Peterson, who also publishes
11899 "The Official Frequent Flyer Guidebook" which compares programmes.For example, don't waste 25,000 miles to redeem a roundtrip ticket from New York to Pittsburgh, worth about $150, when you could fly as far as the West Coast. For another 5,000 to 10,000 miles, you could go to Europe."Remember that programmes these
11899 days are complex, with wide variety of partners," said Peterson. "The fastest way to a free award is by understanding the partners. In most instances, you're not paying more. You just have to be a wise consumer like in any other investment."</

11905 WASHINGTON - The Federal Reserve has issued new rules designed to make car leases easier to understand, but you don't have to go into the fine print to understand this basic fact of auto leasing: It's rarely a sound financial move.To oversimplify, auto leasing usually makes sense in only two
11905 situations. It works for business owners who can sometimes take bigger deductions if they lease the company car than buy it. And it works for people who are hell bent on driving newer and more expensive cars than they can actually afford to buy.Why? When you lease a car for
11905 two or three years, you spend less on a monthly basis than you would buying a car, but at the end of the lease, you own no car.Business people can use that arrangement to deduct their lease costs from their taxable income and save cash to use for other business
11905 expenses. Conspicuous consumers like leases because they can make costly new cars more affordable on a monthly basis.For the rest of the world, there are two cheaper way to get wheels. You can buy an affordable car and keep it for at least one year after it is paid off.
11905 Or you can look for a good used car among the thousands of formerly leased vehicles now glutting the market.Despite those alternatives, leasing has taken off in America. About one of every three new cars driving off the lots are leased, says the Fed.So the new rules, which don't go
11905 into effect for a full year, will be helpful to many. Many companies say they will try to abide by the tougher disclosure requirements before they have to.Before the rules go into effect, car leasers can protect themselves by bringing their business to dealers who agree to abide by the
11905 tougher disclosure rules ahead of schedule. And they can learn a little about their leases, so they understand exactly what they are paying.The new rules will force dealers to use a new disclosure form, which will soon be available to consumers from the Federal Reserve.Even without the form, these are
11905 the questions you need answered before you can decide if a lease is worthwhile:-- What is the gross capitalised cost? This is the actual price of the car that's built into the lease. Leasing experts suggest that you first cut your best deal on a car without telling the sales
11905 person whether you want to lease or buy. Then negotiate the lease separately.-- What is the residual value, and how fair is it? That's the amount that the car is going to be worth on the day you return it. To make sure that your dealer is not artificially lowering
11905 the residual value, double check it against the Kelley Blue Book Residual Value Guide, available at your local library, bank, dealer, or direct if you dial (800)258-3266.-- What's the hidden interest cost? In dealer parlance, this is the "lease rate." Even after the Fed rules go into effect, this will
11905 not have to be disclosed in percentages, but only in dollar amounts.Here's how you find it: Subtract the residual value from the capitalised costs, and that will get you the depreciation built into the lease. Then subtract the depreciation from the total payments you will be asked to make on
11905 the lease. The dollar amount left is the total interest you'll pay. That dollar amount will be printed plainly on the Fed's disclosure form; you'll be able to shop one lease against another by comparing that figure.-- To figure out your interest rate, add the car price and the residual
11905 value. Divide by 2, and then multiply by the number of years in the lease. Then divide the total interest in dollars you are paying by that figure. That's a complicated formula, but one you can take from lease to lease or dealer to dealer to see if you're getting
11905 a good deal.-- If you'd rather some one else do the number crunching for you, and you are seriously interested in leasing, consider investing $129.95 in a software programme called Expert Lease Pro. This is a lease-vs.-buy calculator that is stuffed with current car data, including retail pricing for all
11905 new vehicles, the latest incentives, and lease guide residual value. It can compare leases to see which one is best, or make a lease-vs.-buy calculation for the car you've already picked out. It's available from Chart Software at (800)418-8450.----You can Email Linda Stern at 72160.1546(at)compuserve.com or write to her in
11905 care of Reuters, Suite 410, 1333 H St., NW, Washington, DC 20005. She regrets that she cannot answer each letter individually, but will cover your questions in upcoming columns.</

11907 Last October, an Intel-led consortium pledged to develop technology that would let people watch TV programmes and related Web pages on their PCs.A little less than a year later, they're beginning to deliver on that promise.Computers and add-on cards with the so-called Intercast technology are trickling into stores. NBC, CNN
11907 and QVC are "intercasting" selected TV shows. MTV parent Viacom, and Boston's WGBH are preparing programming. Other broadcasters are expected to announce plans in coming weeks.But as with the TV shows premiering this fall, it's too soon to tell whether Intercast will be must-see TV.Other add-on TV receiver cards for
11907 PCs never became as popular as supporters hoped, stymied in part by high prices.In the year since Intel announced Intercast, industry attention has shifted away from putting TV inside a PC toward putting a PC -- specifically the Internet -- inside a TV.Dozens of companies are now working on various
11907 schemes for incorporating access to the World Wide Web and other parts of the Internet into the family TV set.Still, Intercast merits watching -- in more ways than one -- because to date, it's one of the most advanced attempts to marry TV and the Net.The technology is relatively straightforward.Broadcasters
11907 use a portion of the TV signal called the vertical blanking interval to send pages written in HTML -- the Web's programming language -- along with regular video transmissions.Consumers with Intercast-equipped computers pick up the signals either through the air waves, or where it's available, their local cable company.When Intercast
11907 software is turned on, people see a TV picture in the upper left corner of the computer screen and related information on a Web-like page across the bottom half. For example: in a televised football game, the quarterback's career statistics or favourite pass plays could appear on the Web page
11907 while the TV screen showed him throwing a pass.The upper right side of the screen is reserved for controls and a list of other Intercast files stored on the computer's hard drive. (See Intel's demos of how Intercast works at http://www.intel.com/iaweb/intercast/index.htm.)Intercast software includes a custom browser that reads the transmitted
11907 HTML material, but it's not a full-fledged Web browser, a minus for broadcasters who want to tie online ordering, live chat or other interactive features into their Intercast programming.For now, consumers need a separate Internet connection to get onto the Web while they're intercasting.Sources said, however, that the problem could
11907 be resolved by December, when Intel plans to upgrade the technology to work with popular Web browsers from Netscape and Microsoft.Lorie Wigle, Intel home marketing manager, declined to discuss upgrades.Plug-in circuit boards that add Intercast technology to an existing Pentium PC started shipping in July, but didn't really take off
11907 until earlier this month, when retailer CompUSA discounted the boards to $100.Since then, sales have quadrupled to about 10,000 a month, and should jump to 25,000 a month during the holiday shopping season, said Ken Plotkin, marketing vice president at Hauppage Computer Works, the Hauppage, N.Y., company making the boards.So
11907 far, Compaq and AST Research are the only two computer makers including Intercast technology in new multimedia home PCs. Sony, Diamond Multimedia and ATI have expressed support for the technology, and Intel is negotiating with other PC makers and manufacturers of add-in graphics cards, Intel's Wigle said.Eventually, the technology could
11907 become standard on high-end home PCs, she said."We joke that the chicken has finally met the egg," Wigle said.For today, what can people watch?On NBC, they can tune into one NFL football game a week, or solve murders along with Tim Bayliss, Frank Pembelton and the other Baltimore police detectives
11907 on "Homicide: Life on the Streets."NBC will add Intercast programming to "Dateline" in October, and plans to announce additional content next spring, including programming for affiliate cable networks CNBC and MSNBC. NBC's arrangement with the Intercast Industry Group consortium precludes other national networks from offering the interactive programming until July
11907 1997.On cable, CNN is offering 24-hour Intercast content with its continuous news coverage. QVC also began offering 24-hour Intercast content a month ago to augment its TV home shopping channel."We do think it's a killer app," said Stuart Spiegel, head of QVC's interactive endeavours. "Once it becomes a standard, we're
11907 talking about something that has real power."(Michelle V. Rafter writes about cyberspace and technology from Los Angeles. Reach her at mvrafter(at)deltanet.com. Opinions expressed in this column are her own).</

11913 WesterFed Financial Corp. said Wednesday it agreed to acquire intrastate rival Security Bancorp for about $45 million, forming the largest publicly traded banking company in Montana.The news sent Security's stock soaring $7 to $27.50 on the Nasdaq market in midday trading. 11913 Nasdaq.WesterFed, which is based in Missoula, is the holding company for Western Federal Savings Bank of Montana and Security Bancorp, based in Billings, is the holding company for Security Bank FSB.The combined company will have total assets approaching $1 billion, total deposits of $640 million and 35 offices in 20
11913 communities throughout Montana.Under the terms of the agreement, Security Bancorp shareholders may opt to receive either $30 in cash for each of their shares, swap their stock for WesterFed shares or may choose to receive cash and stock as long as the stock portion is 40 to 45 percent of
11913 the deal.The exchange ratio will depend on the average closing price of WesterFed stock for the 20 trading days beginning 30 trading days prior to the closing of the deal.Based on WesterFed's stock price of $15.75 on Wednesday, and excluding stock options, the merger would have a value of about
11913 $45.4 million, WesterFed said.WesterFed said the deal was expected to add to earnings in the first full fiscal year of combined operations, assuming only modest cost reductions.</

11920 A computer specialist with access to top secret U.S. naval intelligence was arrested at a diplomatic reception at Fort Myer, Virginia, on Tuesday on charges of spying for South Korea, the FBI said on Wednesday.Robert Kim, 56, a 19-year government employee who worked at the U.S. Navy intelligence offices in
11920 Suitland, Maryland, was to be arraigned in U.S. District Court in Alexandria, Virginia on Wednesday, FBI spokeswoman Susan Lloyd said.He was to be charged with passing classified information to a South Korean agent, a Korean naval attache identified as Capt. 11920 was born in Korea and became a U.S. citizen in 1974.Lloyd said he was not an intelligence officer but had access through his computer to top secret information. She did not say what secrets he dealt with.Justice Department officials said the arrest came after "a number of months of investigation."
11920 Lloyd said agents searched Kim's house, car and office at about the same time as his arrest, which came during a reception at Fort Myer in Arlington, Virginia, near the Pentagon. He lives in a quiet residential suburb about 20 miles (32 km) west of Washington.Officials said prosecutors would give
11920 a U.S. magistrate details of the case against Kim at his arraignment at the same courthouse where CIA agent Aldrich Ames was sentenced to life in prison for spying for the Soviet Union for $2.5 million.Kim was to be charged under an espionage statute that carries a maximum penalty of
11920 10 years in prison, according to a Justice Department official.Clinton administration officials said they were disturbed by the incident but it was unlikely to affect U.S.-Korea ties."Relations between the United States and the Republic of Korea are strong and of the nature that they can endure any alleged wrongdoing by
11920 an individual," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters travelling with President Bill Clinton on a campaign trip to Pennsylvania.Secretary of State Warren Christopher said he was very disturbed by Kim's arrest and said Washington had been in touch with South Korean officials over the case."I've been very disturbed by
11920 the reports that I have received of that arrest and the incident itself," he told reporters before talks in New York with Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria. 11920 understand why my comments will be very limited."Christopher met on Tuesday afternoon with South Korean Foreign Minister Gong Ro-mung but State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the matter had not been raised. Christopher said "the arrest wasn't made until last night," implying it came after his meeting with Gong.Over the
11920 years there have been a number of espionage cases involving the passing of classified information to nations friendly to the United States.Among the most prominent, U.S. Navy intelligence analyst Jonathan Pollard, who worked at the same facility as Kim, pleaded guilty in 1986 to spying for Israel in a case
11920 that strained relations between the two nations.Pollard, an American Jew, claimed he was acting out of concern for Israel's security because the United States had not been sharing all of its top-secret information. But prosecutors said he was motivated by money.Clinton this year denied a pardon request for Pollard, who
11920 is serving a life sentence. He cited the serious nature of Pollard's crime.Other cases involving U.S. allies included a former State Department communications officer who in 1993 admitted spying for Greece, a former U.S. serviceman arrested in 1993 for passing secrets to the Philippines and a former U.S. Army analyst
11920 who pleaded guilty in 1988 to spying for South Africa.</

11933 Mesa Air Group has signed an agreement with the Federal Aviation Administration to pay a $500,000 fine for maintenance problems and to further improve flight safety, the FAA said Wednesday.It said $250,000 of the fine would be waived if the new safety steps were implemented according to the approved plan.The
11933 fine and stipulated further safety steps were announced by Mesa last week.Mesa, with more than 150 planes, is a major operator of commuter services under such names as United Express, USAir Express and America West Express, as well as Mesa Airlines.The FAA cited violations by Mesa that included allowing engines
11933 to be started without a fire guard on hand, allowing passengers to walk near an aircraft with its engines running, improperly repairing fuel leaks and improperly installing screws on a propeller blade.The FAA also said Mesa was using outdated flight manuals.It said Mesa disputed some of the agency's findings.FAA officials
11933 said an inspection of Mesa began last year and another was continuing now to assure it complied with the new safety standards that commuters must meet by next March to bring their safety level up to that of the big carriers.The officials said that if Mesa failed to meet the
11933 deadlines it would be fined $5,000 for each missed deadline.In a statement, the FAA said both it and Mesa also realised that because of the carrier's future expansion plans, operational changes were needed to cope with the additional planes and routes.The FAA conceded after the crash of ValuJet flight 592
11933 near Miami May 11, killing all 110 on board, that closer scrutiny had to be given to young, fast-growing airlines.After an inspection, ValuJet was grounded. The agency cited maintenance problems in handling its fast-growing fleet.FAA officials said that all of Mesa's shortcomings were corrected by the time FAA officials began
11933 their inspections or by the time the inspections were completed.Thomas Stuckey, flight standards manager in the FAA's Dallas-Fort Worth office, said when inspectors went in they found some unsafe conditions in aircraft not in service as well as failures to comply with FAA approved company manual.He said the $500,000 fine
11933 was leveled because of these violations, but "the carrier today is in compliance."He said the new standards Mesa must meet included hiring a full time director of training and more training instructors, using more flight simulators and starting an internal audit and evaluation programme.</

11935 A team of Italian doctors has identified a drug that can provide modest protection to the pancreas during surgery, according to a report in the New England Journal of Medicine.Damage to the pancreas, which aids in digestion, is one of the most common complications of ERCP surgery, designed to examine
11935 the tubes sending fluids to the intestine from the pancreas and liver.A team led by Dr. Giorgio Cavallini of the University of Verona found that giving the drug gabexate to 208 volunteers before surgery made them less likely to experience complications related to the pancreas, the Journal said in its
11935 Thursday edition.While eight percent of 210 patients who received a placebo suffered an inflammation of the pancreas, the problem only surfaced in two percent of the gabexate recipients.The results mean "gabexate reduced pancreatic damage related to ERCP," the Cavallini team said in the Journal.It was unclear, however, how widely the
11935 drug would be accepted. ERCP is usually performed as outpatient surgery, but gabexate has to be given intravenously over a 12-hour period.That requirement, plus its cost of about $260 per treatment, meant "the additional overall costs of gabexate therapy would be substantial," Dr. Kees Huibregtse of the Academic Medical Centre
11935 in Amsterdam said in an editorial in the Journal.Gabexate is sold under the brand name Foy by Lepetit in Lainate, Italy, which helped pay for the study.</

11937 The Environmental Protection Agency Wednesday proposed forcing a number of industries to disclose how they use toxic chemicals, expanding a community-right-to-know programme on industrial toxins.The plan would apply to industries currently forced to report on the toxic chemicals they release into the environment in a programme called the Toxic Release
11937 Inventory."The expansion we are considering would give the public the right to know not just which chemicals come out of local industrial facilities, but which chemicals go into their neighbourhoods and how they are used," EPA Administrator Carol Browner said in a statement."Putting information about local pollution into the hands
11937 of the public is the single most effective, common-sense tool available for protecting public health and the environment," Browner said.Currently 20 categories of industries covering some 23,000 facilities must make Toxic Release Inventory reports on their chemical emissions, and the Clinton administration has proposed expanding the categories and adding another
11937 6,400 facilities.Reporting on how industries use toxic chemicals "would expand public information available on toxic chemicals that enter local industrial facilities; the amounts of chemicals transformed into products and waste; and toxic chemicals that leave the facility," the EPA statement said.President Clinton last month said the administration intended to expand
11937 chemical emissions reporting, a programme disliked by many of the regulated industries and which a number of Republicans in Congress sought to curb.A spokeswoman for the National Association of Manufacturers said the industry group was studying the plan."In general NAM opposes expansion of the TRI to include chemcial uses," she

11939 Hasbro Inc. said Wednesday it will close its Amsterdam, N.Y. manufacturing facility, which employs 400 people, at the end of November.Production of Playskool toys that took place there will be moved to a facility in Texas, Hasbro said.Hasbro said it was developing severance packages for all its employees and will
11939 establish a centre to retrain and prepare laid-off Hasbro workers for re-employment.The company was not immediately available to say if a charge would be involved with the plant closing."After much deliberation and a careful analysis of our manufacturing capacity, we reached this difficult but necessary decision," Jerry Ligon, president of
11939 Hasbro's manufacturing service group, said in a statement.Ligon said competition in the toy business required the Pawtucket, R.I.-based company to adjust its production load at its North American plants.Hasbro acquired the plant from Coleco Industries Inc. in 1988. 11941 The U.S. General Accounting Office (GAO) is concerned that U.S. futures exchanges may not meet federal regulatory standards established last year for tracking trades.In a report to Congress released today, the GAO reviewed actions taken by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to improve audit trail systems at futures exchanges."We are
11941 concerned that the momentum toward achieving compliance could be lost," the report stated. In August, the CFTC said two of the world's largest futures exchanges -- the Chicago Board of Trade and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange -- had audit trail systems that failed to meet standards originally set in the
11941 Futures Trading Practices Act of 1992.Those standards demand 90 percent accuracy in monitoring trades. The exchanges have a deadline of January 1, 1997, to meet the standards.The GAO said Wednesday the CBOT and CME "do not yet meet the heightened standards," and the implementation of electronic trading terminals to help
11941 do so is uncertain." A bill to reform the Commodity Exchange Act introduced this month by Senators Richard Lugar, an Indiana Republican, and Patrick Leahy, a Vermont Democrat, would clarify audit trail requirements imposed by earlier legislation.The bill would clarify the intent of Congress that the audit trail statute requires
11941 a minimum performance standard but does not mandate the use of any particular technology. The Lugar-Leahy bill is considered unlikely to pass this year but is expected to be revived next year.The GAO report recommended that Congress be kept up to date on progress by the exchanges towards audit trail
11941 targets as well as other requirements in the act, and on any steps taken by the CFTC to ensure this is done. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com</

11943 A record annual income of $1.8 billion, led by healthy U.S. equity earnings of 26.15 percent, has prompted managers to consider investing a larger amount of the $17.6 billion Alaska Permanent Fund in corporate stocks, officials said Wednesday.The earnings total was released at the start of the fund's two-day annual
11943 meeting of the fund, a state-owned endowment established 20 years ago and augmented each year with regular contributions from the state's oil earnings.In fiscal year 1996, the fund realized a 13.43 percent return on investments, led by the equity earnings, officials said.Forty-nine percent of the fund was invested in U.S.
11943 and international equities.Forty-three percent was invested in fixed-income securities, which had an average annual return of 4.18 percent. The remainder was invested in real estate, which had a 7.98 percent return.Under state law, the fund is allowed to invest up to 50 percent of its assets in equities.That reflects an
11943 incremental increase authorized earlier this year by the Alaska state Legislature, which passed a bill removing foreign fixed-income assets from the overall equity calculation.At next year's legislative session, fund officials may ask the legislature for authority to invest more of the assets in equities, said executive director Byron Mallott."We're going
11943 to continue to look at our statuatory allocation to see if we need to look for more investment in equities, because that's where the strength of the market is," Mallott said.It is likely that fund managers would seek permission from the legislature next year to increase equity investment to 60
11943 percent, he said."It would likely be in that range," he said, noting that comparable pension funds have an average 56 percent of their assets invested in equities.The Alaska Permanent Fund was established by an amendement to the state constitution passed the year before the trans-Alaska oil pipeline began operations.Conceived by
11943 former Gov. Jay Hammond, it was intended to grow through investement and perpetual deposits of about 20 percent of annual oil royalty income.Fiscal year 1996, which ended June 30, was the first in which permanent fund earnings exceeded total state oil revenues.That was due to the bullish stock market, Mallott
11943 said, and is not likely to be repeated for about five years. The state earned about $1.5 billion in the fiscal year from oil royalties, taxes and fees, according to Permanent Fund records.In time, dwindling North Slope oil production will make the eclipse permanent, Mallott said."Our surpassing oil revenue coming
11943 into the general fund is not likely to come again until after the turn of the century. At that point it will continue," he said.This year's milestone is "a hint of what the Permanent Fund will be in Alaska's fiscal future," Mallott said.For the past 15 years, the fund has
11943 paid an annual dividend to almost every year-round Alaska residents. Any Alaskan adult or child who has been in the state for two years and who spends most of the year in the state is eligible for the dividend.This year's dividend, to be announced Wednesday night, is expected to be
11943 over $1,100, a record. Last year's dividend was $990.30.--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650</
11944 The Senate was expected to sustain President Bill Clinton's veto of the so-called "partial birth" abortion bill on Thursday, amid signs abortion rights supporters are increasingly edgy about the emotional issue.Both Democrats and Republicans said on Wednesday they expected the Senate to uphold Clinton's veto, although a handful of lawmakers
11944 who initially voted against the bill may change position on the contentious election-year issue.The House of Representatives narrowly voted to override the veto last week. The bill passed the Senate 54-44 in December, well short of the two-thirds majority needed for a veto override.Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott called the
11944 vote an uphill battle, but added "it could get to be a lot closer than people thought" as lawmakers switched sides."Partial birth" abortion, technically called dilation and evacuation, is sometimes used in later-term abortions. Under the technique a foetus is partially delivered feet first until just the head remains in
11944 the birth canal. The brains are then suctioned out and the skull collapsed.The legislation -- the first time Congress has moved to ban a specific abortion technique -- represents a turning point in the abortion debate from generalities to a graphic focus on the details of specific techniques.The emotional debate;
11944 intense opposition by the Catholic Church, which sent millions of postcards to Congress; and recent news articles showing it may be used more often than originally claimed, seem to be having an impact.Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, who voted against the original bill, said he had promised fellow Democrats he
11944 would try to work out a compromise measure after Thursday's vote.Daschle said he had no objection to banning the procedure for elective abortions where there was no health problem, but wanted to ensure it would be available when medically needed."We have no reservations about prohibiting the practice for purposes of
11944 just mere convenience, but we do believe that there are very vital, very important health issues that have to be addressed," said Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat."I have made a commitment ... to see if we can't work out language that would be suitable on all sides, and come back
11944 and pass this bill 100-0 next year," he said.Abortion opponents call the health exception a loophole to let the abortions continue and quote a coalition of physicians who contend there is no medical reason for the procedure.Further, they point to recent newspaper articles indicating the technique may be used more
11944 frequently than previously believed and in second-trimester abortions where there is no health problem with the woman or foetus."We aren't coming back next year and working out (any) compromise," said Andrea Sheldon, director of government affairs for the Traditional Values Coalition.Abortion rights groups initially estimated the technique was used about
11944 500 times a year, mainly in cases of severe foetal abnormalities."Many senators who voted against the ban in December are becoming uncomfortable as they see their rationale unravel," said Douglas Johnson of the National Right to Life Committee.When Clinton vetoed the bill in April, he said he had concerns about
11944 the procedure but could not sign it because it did not include constitutional protections for a woman's health.The National Abortion and Reproductive Rights Action League challenged news reports saying the total was higher."We're getting all caught up in the numbers ... and we're allowing the other side to distract us,"
11944 said NARAL president Kate Michelman who called the bill "an unprecedented intrusion into medical practice" that would endanger women's health.According to the Alan Guttmacher Institute, nearly 90 perecent of the 1.5 million U.S. abortions each year take place in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy.</

11947 A key Democratic senator charged Wednesday that Republicans were poised to give in to the National Rifle Association and let child-abusers keep their guns, reversing a one-sided Senate vote on gun control.Gun control is one of several issues being negotiated between Republicans and Democrats as part of an omnibus spending
11947 bill they intend to pass to keep the government funded after the Oct. 1 start of the new fiscal year.Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, said the Senate-passed bill to ban gun ownership by child- and spouse-abusers was being substantially weakened in negotiations with the House at the urging
11947 of Republicans opposed to gun control."It will jeopardise the lives of thousands of battered women and children around the nation," he said on the Senate floor. "I know the NRA has a lot of power around here. But isn't there some point at which we draw the line?"The House has
11947 not approved the gun control bill that cleared the Senate by 97-2 on Sept. 12 as an amendment to the Treasury Department's 1997 funding. The entire bill was pulled before a final vote because of disagreements over other issues.Lawmakers reported they were near agreement on all spending issues, including the
11947 approximately $6.5 billion President Clinton wanted for schools, illegal drug control and anti-terrorist measures. But policy issues still divide them."Money is not an issue," Senate Appropriations Committee chairman Mark Hatfield, R-Oregon, told reporters after a meeting with House Speaker Newt Gingrich, R-Georgia.Lautenberg said he would use "all the tools at
11947 my disposal" to fight changes in the gun ban. These tools could include the threat to hold up passage of the spending bill. Congress must vote by Oct. 1 to fund government agencies for 1997 or risk another unpopular government closure.The proposed new gun control language would also allow spousal
11947 abusers to keep their guns if they were convicted by a judge in what is known as a bench trial rather than in a trial by jury.And spousal abusers would be given an added civil right. At the time they were charged with abuse, they would have to be warned
11947 of the possible loss of a right to own guns. If the warning were not delivered, they could keep their guns even if convicted.Accused criminals must be warned of their rights to keep silent and to have an attorney.In more than 30 states, battering a spouse or child is considered
11947 a misdemeanor, a crime punishable by no more than a year in jail. In those same states, phyiscal attack on a neighbour or a neighbour's child is a felony, a crime punishable by more than a year in jail.Sen. Paul Wellstone, D-Minnesota, noted recently that the vast majority of the
11947 2 million cases of spousal abuse each year involve the battering of wives or former wives and in 150,000 cases a gun was present.The House earlier this year killed the gun-control measure when passed by the Senate as part of an anti-stalking bill.</

11950 Ohio hospital.She toured a birthing centre at Lakewood Hospital in a Cleveland suburb and spoke as part of a panel there on medical care for new mothers and babies.Mrs. Clinton praised Congress for the bipartisan effort that led to passage Tuesday of legislation assuring at least a two-day hospital stay

11951 Mental impairment is not a "normal" part of ageing and many cases of dementia can be treated, according to U.S. health guidelines released on Wednesday.Even when the problem cannot be cured, such as Alzheimer's disease, early diagnosis is still advisable."Early recognition of Alzheimer's disease or identification of other types of
11951 dementias can prevent costly and inappropriate treatment and give patients and family members time to address the complex financial, legal and medical conditions these conditions present," said Paul Costa of the National Institute on Ageing, and the co-chair of the panel that drew up the guidelines.The clinical practice guidelines are
11951 the last in a series drawn up by the Agency for Health Care Policy and Research, part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.About one in five apparent cases of dementia are treatable, due to such disorders as depression or drug interaction, which is a particular problem among
11951 older people taking several medications for chronic conditions.Yet many people, including some health care professionals, regard such symptoms as a difficulty absorbing new information, problems in handling complex tasks or trouble with spatial orientation as sad but normal parts of ageing.But according to the guidelines, they are instead signals that
11951 a doctor should be consulted. If Alzheimer's is suspected, the elderly person should be followed carefully.</

11953 NEW YORK, Sept 25 - Standard &amp; Poor's Corp today said it has assigned its triple-B' rating to Paragould, Ark.'s $15 million hospital revenue bonds series 1996, issued for Arkansas Methodist Hospital.The rating reflects a strong financial profile characterized by consistently excellent earnings, healthy cash flow, and growing liquidity. Factors
11953 precluding a higher rating include aggressive capital plans, concentrated medical staff, and a restrictive payor mix.Strict cost controls, revenue enhancements, light managed care, and volume growth produce strong earnings. Admissions at the 129-bed hospital increased 6.4% over the past three years to 4,117 patients in fiscal 1996. Outpatient visits also
11953 grew 6% over the same period. Operating and excess margins averaged 8% and 10%, respectively, from fiscal 1992-1996. The strong earnings and manageable pro forma debt burden produced maximum debt service coverage above 2.40 times over the past three years. Because of the excellent profits, aggressive accounts receivable collection, and
11953 moderate capital expenses, cash and investments increased to $15.4 million, or 265 days' operating expenses in fiscal 1996, from $6.2 million or 129 days' three year earlier.However, the hospital is embarking on a substantial $20 million modernization and expansion project, mostly to accommodate ambulatory services. The project's major components include
11953 outpatient surgery, medical office, women's unit, and physical therapy additions, along with emergency room, surgery, and imaging department renovations. A $5 million equity contribution will finance the 17-physician medical office building. Nonetheless, post-issuance cash compares favorably to debt and remains healthy at $10.4 million, or 183 days operating expenses. A
11953 healthy $24.8 million equity position comfortably supports the new debt, evidenced by 38% pro forma debt to capitalization.Successful physician recruitment and service additions increased primary service area inpatient market share to 50% in fiscal 1996, from historical 46% levels. Direct competition in the hospital's northeastern Arkansas service area is limited,
11953 but out-migration to Jonesboro, 22 miles south, remains high. Management anticipates that the master facilities plan will continue boosting its physician recruitment success and reduce its reliance on the top-10 revenue producing doctors, which currently generate 62% of total revenue. Moreover, while the medical staff has grown to 28 active
11953 admitters, the hospital remains vulnerable because of its small size. Although Medicare accounts for a high 55.6% of revenue, the hospital's favorable cost structure allows it to generate a profit under the program.OUTLOOK: Stable.The outlook anticipates project completion on time and within budget. It also expects consistent profitability and cash
11953 flow generation, not necessarily at historical levels, Standard &amp; Poor's said.</

11957 Most people know the feeling of driving along a highway and watching a small winged insect make violent and messy contact with the windscreen.But few view the results as lovingly as Mark Hostetler, a University of Florida researcher and devoted student of splattered bug remains.Hostetler has just published "That Gunk
11957 on Your Car," a book that opens up the world of insects to those outside the scientific community through the goo left by vehicular impact."It's a good way to introduce people to science and insects without being humdrum and boring," Hostetler said on Wednesday.The book includes illustrations to help match
11957 up pre- and post-splat bugs, facts about insects and suggestions for do-it-yourself experiments.Hostetler said he collected many of his pictures by haunting local bus stations, where he documented the entomological results of long-distance trips."The buses have these big, flat windscreens, so when the insects hit, they would sometimes stick there
11957 and I could collect the bug too," he said.He also collected specimens by attaching a small net to the roof of his car as he drove 12,000 miles (19,000 km) around the country. When he ran into a cloud of bugs, "I would pull over to the side of the
11957 road and compare the insect in the net with the splat," he said."That Gunk on Your Car" costs $10 and is about the same size as the field guides birdwatchers use to identify their winged quarry."(The size is) just right for your glove compartment, so when you have an unfortunate
11957 encounter with an insect along the highway, you can identify it right away," Hostetler said.Besides distributing the book to Gainesville-area bookstores, Hostetler is offering it through the Internet at http://nersp.nerdc.ufl.edu/arm/people/hos.html.</

11959 a tougher version of the school ban, drafted by California Republican Elton Gallegly, when it was debating the immigration bill last March. 11959 be adopted in the Senate and is still threatened with a veto.The earlier version would have allowed states to remove current illegal alien students from public schools. 11962 The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved a bill aimed at stemming a tide of illegal immigration over Democratic protests against provisions they said unfairly targeted legal aliens.The vote was 305-123, with 76 Democrats joining the Republican majority in favour of the Republican-drafted bill.The measure now goes to the Senate
11962 where Democratic Leader Tom Daschle has been hinting at a possible filibuster.Versions of the bill were approved overwhelmingly by the House and Senate earlier this year. But final congressional action was held up for months by a dispute over a provision allowing states to deny illegal immigrant children a public
11962 school education.President Bill Clinton said the provision would lead him to veto the bill. Republican presidential Bob Dole had supported it. 11962 was leaving his options open on whether he would sign the bill, a spokeswoman said, saying the president was talking to members of Congress about strengthening work-place enforcement of laws against hiring illegal aliens.During the House debate, Democrats voiced anger at being left out of the drafting of the compromise
11962 measure, which they said was done in "back rooms" in concert with the Dole campaign.They also complained the measure would require Americans who wanted to bring a close family member to the United States to meet financial standards that would be beyond low-income people.Proponents of the bill said it would
11962 insure that sponsors of immigrants were held to their commitment to make sure their relatives were not a drain on taxpayers.Critics also denounced provisions tightening up on admission of people arriving in the country without documents in search of asylum, saying it gave too much latitude to immigration inspectors.Democrats charged
11962 that the bill removed safeguards for Americans such as Hispanics against discrimination by employers fearful of hiring aliens, and did not do enough to crack down on employers hiring illegals.They criticised provisions they said would make legal immigrants liable for deportation if they used certain welfare programmes for more than
11962 a year, including tax-financed health care for AIDS victims.They also complained that the building of new fences against illegal migration near San Diego was being exempted from some environmental laws.The bill would:- double the size of the border patrol, adding 5,000 new agents and 1,500 support personnel over five years
11962 and adding other investigators to trace people who overstay their visas;- authorise the building of new fences along the Mexican border near San Diego;- beef up penalties for alien smuggling and document fraud and speed removal of illegal aliens;- set up pilot projects for employers to verify their workers' immigration
11962 status and stengthen barriers against illegal aliens getting welfare benefits.</

11973 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe International Monetary Fund on Wednesday painted a bleak picture of Europe as a region plagued by sky-high unemployment and boxed in by its drive to launch a single currency in 1999.While European Union nations are generally expected to enjoy faster economic growth in 1997, many
11973 remain saddled with deep-seated problems that will require tough action to solve, the IMF said in its semi-annual World Economic Outlook.Those problems include labour markets that do not seem to work well and government budget deficits that remain too high and hinder long-term growth."The real risk in Europe is that
11973 ... unemployment rates could continue their steady upward march," the IMF said. "This underscores the urgency of tackling the problem more forcefully."In the short-run, the Fund sees better times ahead for Europe. Growth throughout the European Union is expected to average 2.5 percent next year, up from 1.6 percent in
11973 1996.Unemployment is projected to slip to an average of 11 percent in 1997, from 11.4 percent this year.The IMF though warned that its economic projections could prove too optimistic, especially if Europe's headlong drive to cut budget deficits under the Maastricht Treaty acts as more of a drag on growth
11973 than expected.The Maastricht treaty sets out tough budget guidelines that European Union countries must meet in 1997 for entry into European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999."The recovery in Europe may be weaker than projected because it may be restrained ... by the short-term contractionary effects of fiscal consolidation efforts being
11973 implemented in most EU countries partly to satisfy the Maastricht criteria by 1997," the IMF said.Paradoxically, if growth is held back by the drive to slash budget deficits, that will make satisfying the Maastricht criteria that much more difficult.Slower growth tends to bloat budget deficits by pushing up government spending
11973 on uenmployment and other benefits and depressing tax revenues from economic activity.The IMF said it expected Germany and France -- perhaps the two countries most important to a successful launch of EMU -- to satisfy the Maastricht criteria. But it made clear that depended on economic growth picking up as
11973 expected.If growth does not strengthen, the IMF signalled it would prefer European nations to temporarily allow their budget deficits to rise in line with the weakness of their economies rather than to cut them to meet the tough Maastricht criteria."It is important to avoid aggravating a difficult situation through unduly
11973 procyclical (tight) fiscal policies," the Fund said.Whatever the short-term problems posed by Maastricht, the IMf made clear that in the medium term European countries need to put their public finances in order. But that will require reining in spending in such politically explosive areas as pensions and unemployment benefits.It linked
11973 Europe's high budget deficits to its excessive unemployment. Europe's high unemployment bloats deficits by pushing up spending and robbing governments of tax revenues.The IMF said comprehensive labour market reforms would be needed to really drive down unemployment. Faster economic growth would help, but there was a limit on how much
11973 it could do."As much as eight to nine percentage points of the EU's current unemployment rate of over 11 percent is widely considered to be structural in the sense that it is unlikely that it could be absorbed through cyclical recovery alone, without significant inflationary risks," the Fund said.It accused
11973 European governments of "excessive timidity" in tackling the problem and recommended a whole set of reforms.They included: reduced unemployment benefits with tighter eligibility criteria and of shorter duration; lower payroll taxes, particularly for low-wage workers; minimum wage cuts; and changes in the way governments handle collective bargaining agreements.</

11977 being discussed, said he expected the agency to tap the debt markets during the week of October 7.While it was possible the agency will opt to sell the debt towards the end of the week of September 30, he said he doubted that would happen.PaineWebber Inc will lead the underwriting
11977 team that will sell the bonds through negotiation, aided by Merrill Lynch &amp; Co and Bear Stearns Inc.The new debt will be sold in two parts, with the first comprised of around $400 million of senior lien issues, which the agency expects to be rated AAA.As much as $223 million
11977 of subordinate lien issues also will be sold. 11977 sold debt backed by funds appropriated by the New York State legislature, but this will be the first time it has returned to the capital markets with its own issues.The Urban Development Corp expects to save money with the refunding, on a present value basis, which includes extending the maturity
11977 of the debt by 11 years to 2026."It completely restructures the New York State Urban Development Corp (issues) and it's the first debt issuance since 1974 for the Urban Development Corp on its own," Branca said.No estimate of how much the agency stands to save was immediately available, partly because
11977 this calculation depends on market conditions when the issues are sold.And as key part of the restructuring, the state will no longer have a moral obligation to repay the debt if the risk of a default should develop. "We're looking to remove the moral obligation of the State of New

11984 to cover the costs associated with the changes.The move is the latest in a series of restructurings at Dial, which recently spun off its travel services unit into a separate company called Viad Corp.In a statement, Dial also said it expects 1996 earnings will be about 15 percent lower than
11984 most analysts had expected, due to slowness in new-product acceptance, as well as selected detergent and personal care programmes.Jozoff said the changes, which were expected to reduce overhead costs by 20 percent, were the "crucial second step" in the firm's attempts to "keep our costs in line with the competition
11984 in a very price sensitive consumer marketplace."The first step in that process came in August when Dial spun off Viad. 11984 cutback.Of the 250 additional job cuts, about 80 percent are to come from management and administration, leaving Dial with about 2,800 employees, a 33 percent drop from 4,200 in 1990. 11990 With U.N. members now lining up to sign the landmark nuclear test ban treaty, the United States aims to keep pressure on key holdout India to reverse it's adamant refusal to join.Some U.S. officials insist this is a realistic goal despite New Delhi's seemingly intractable opposition to the pact. But
11990 more pessimistic experts worry that too heavy-handed a U.S. approach could backfire in ominous ways."We're only beginning to develop a longer-term plan (for India)," one administration official told Reuters. 11990 they are paying."Assistant Secretary of State for Political-Military Affairs Thomas McNamara, meanwhile, told defence writers:"I don't know how its going to change, I don't know when it's going to change and in fact I cannot even be certain whether it's going to change. But I think there will be a
11990 number of internal and international pressures that will build on India to change its position."Under the terms of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which the United States and the other four nuclear powers signed on Tuesday in New York, the international community has two years to persuade India to come
11990 on board.India's signature is vital. The pact -- outlawing all atomic weapons tests -- cannot take effect with its monitoring provisions without ratification by the five nuclear powers, which also include Britain, France, China and Russia, and the three nuclear threshold states -- India, Pakistan and Israel -- deemed to
11990 be capable of building nuclear weapons quickly.New Delhi has declared unyielding opposition to the treaty, saying it undermines Indian sovereignty and preserves an elite nuclear "haves" club by not setting a date for disarmament.India took the unusual step of facing down the world by blocking the Conference on Disarmament in
11990 Geneva, which negotiated the treaty, from sending it to the United Nations for signing. But supporters still took the pact to New York.While India won in the obscure Geneva process, its isolation at the U.N., where only Bhutan and Libya joined New Delhi in opposing the treaty, prompted new soul-searching
11990 at home on whether the decision really served Indian interests.This suggests India may be more receptive to pro-treaty arguments. Washington has told India it will not be sanctioned but officials say there are "consequences."India is seeking a rotating seat on the U.N. Security Council later this year but almost certainly
11990 will not get it, in part because of its position on the test-ban pact, officials said. Japan is more likely to be given the seat.Also, U.S. officials say while India and the United States have recently improved ties, there could be even more economic and other cooperation if India signed
11990 the nuclear accord.President Bill Clinton addressed one of India's main concerns in a U.N. speech on Tuesday by reasserting his aim to negotiate with Russia deeper cuts in their nuclear arsenals.There is no date set for such talks and one is unlikely until the START 2 arms reduction treaty, languishing
11990 in Moscow, is ratified by the Russian parliament.George Perkovich, an arms expert and director of the non-profit W. Alton Jones Foundation in Charlottesville, Virgina, agrees a new intense debate is raging in India over the treaty but told Reuters "it is extremely unlikely India is going to sign" this treaty.The
11990 debate pits Indians who now want to pursue a nuclear programme with vigour, including testing, versus those who say the test ban treaty loss isolated India and testing should not go forward.The two sides reflect a fundamental strategic choice."Does India concentrate on becoming a major international power through its economic
11990 power (which means you don't test nuclear weapons or deploy missiles because there is an economic cost to that) or does it become a major power the way other major powers did -- through military capability," Perkovich said.Most Indian prime ministers have viewed economic progress as the best route. But
11990 Perkovich said provocations by China or Pakistan or excessive U.S. pressure on India could force New Delhi to launch an atomic test or deploy the Prithvi missile.U.S. officials do not expect India to test but are worried about possible new missile deployments. "Right now the goal is to make sure
11990 India doesn't exacerbate the situation," one official said. The next step is to defuse tensions with Pakistan and finally to "go down a different path that's going to make it easier for India to sign the treaty," he said.</

12010 House and Senate negotiators reached agreement on a bill to help fund national parks through corporate sponsorships and to let national parks raise their entrance fees, lawmakers said Wednesday.The bill, whose final passage remained uncertain in the congressional session's waning few days, also would create five parks, set up a
12010 trust to manage the San Francisco Presidio -- a former military installation being turned into a park -- and establish several new memorials.Alaska Republican Sen. Frank Murkowski, one of the sponsors, told a news conference contentious measures were stripped from the bill in an effort to get it passed in
12010 the session's final days."In a presidential year, obtaining the votes to override a veto would have been impossible," Murkowski said. "We made a necessary compromise to save other important measures."A spokesman for Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said he was still weighing whether to accept the bill
12010 and environmental sources said there were rumblings other senators may move to block it. This late in the session, any opposition likely would kill the bill.Among measures dropped from the bill was one pushed by Murkowski to extend an exclusive contract held by the Ketchikan Pulp Co for access to
12010 timber in Alaska's Tongass National Forest. The bill would transfer eight remaining years of the pulp mill's exclusive contract to timber from the Tongass temperate rainforest to Ketchikan's sawmills, which environmentalists also opposed.Also dropped was a Republican-backed plan to reform grazing fees on federal land, which the White House rejected,
12010 and a measure that would have freed up large tracts of Utah wilderness for development.California Democratic Sens. Barbara Boxer and Dianne Feinstein said the bill had important benefits for their state and had bipartisan support. But environmentalists opposed corporate sponsorship for parks, saying it would cheapen the national treasures."We have
12010 grave reservations about anything that would commercialize the parks," said Chuck Clussen of the Natural Resources Defence Council.Critics also said the bill would discourage the federal government from funding parks, letting corporations pick up the slack, and would make the Interior secretary regulator of corporations that are raising funds for
12010 his deparment's parks.But backers argued it was essential to get money to refurbish the parks and said the bill had safeguards to prevent businesses from commercializing parks.</

12014 The IMF said on Wednesday it saw the possibility of significantly faster economic growth in former Communist bloc countries, but voiced doubts they would be able to duplicate East Asia's economic success."These countries have important strengths, particularly in terms of human capital," the International Monetary Fund said in its semi-annual
12014 World Economic Outlook."There are several factors that could significantly raise growth rates, including the scope for expansion of the service sector and the potential to catch up to the best available technology," it added.But the former Communist bloc nations, which include Eastern Europe, former Soviet republics and Russia, also have
12014 some economic weaknesses, the IMF said.They include rapidly-aging -- and slowly growing -- populations and weak banking systems."In many respects ... the longer-term foundations for growth do not look as favorable as they do in many of the dynamic emerging market countries in the developing world," the IMF said.In the
12014 short run, the IMF sees faster economic growth in what it calls the transition economies. Growth in those economies is projected to pick up to four percent next year, from 0.4 percent this year. In Central and Eastern Europe in particular, the IMF sees growth strengthening to 4.2 percent in
12014 1997 from 1.6 percent in 1996.The Fund also forecast a turn-around in Russia in 1997."Conditions appear to be in place for activity to pick up next year," it said."Containment of fiscal imbalances, especially through greater efforts to collect tax revenues, and further deepening of the reform process are essential if
12014 the expected recovery is to become firmly established," the IMF added.</

The
12022 county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year. The legislation also abolishes the state Housing Bond Credit Committee, whose responsibilities will be assigned to California Housing Finance Agency and Local Agency Indebtedness Fund Loan Program.The housing bond committee was established by the state Legislature to supervise the California Housing
12022 Finance Agency's revenue bond proposals."I am a strong supporter of streamlining government, which means eliminating unnecessary government programs and improving those that work," Fong said.</

12035 After skyrocketing earlier this year, prices for a slice of airwaves that will carry a new generation of cellular phone service have veered back toward earth at the latest, and largest, government auction.Bids at the Federal Communications Commission's latest sale of new wireless phone permits were running at nearly a
12035 tenth the value of the average bid at a high-flying sale ended in May."The prices are extraordinarily low by any standard," said Jonathan Foxman of BIA Consulting Inc. in Chantilly, Va.The auction passed the $1 billion mark on Monday, after 27 rounds of bidding by companies wanting to offer personal
12035 communications service, or PCS as the new service is called.But bidding lags the $10.2 billion the government raised at its "C-Block" auction that ended in May, which was reserved for smaller companies.That sale passed $3 billion after 13 rounds. Analysts said prices then were unrealistically high. The FCC raised $7.7
12035 billion at its first PCS auction in 1995.PCS technology is expected to turn the wireless phone into a mass-market product, allowing consumers to use different communications services -- such as phone, paging, fax and Internet access -- through a single hand-held device.Units of Sprint Corp. and AT&amp;T Corp. lead the
12035 latest bidding.Analysts cited an oversupply of companies wanting to break into the PCS market and the smaller airwave parcels the FCC is auctioning as among the factors behind the slower bidding.They also cited the slow speed some major winners from the C-Block auction -- including NextWave Telecom Inc. and General
12035 Wireless Inc. -- face in raising money to proceed with plans."The sources of finance are limited," said Mark Lowenstein of Yankee Group Inc., a Boston consulting firm.As of Wednesday midday, the FCC had raised $1.09 billion after nearly a month of bidding. The sale involves 145 bidders vying for 1,479
12035 PCS licenses in markets across the nation. It is the largest number of licenses offered simultaneously.Current bids are "much more rational in terms of what people can make in these markets," said economist David Roddy of Deloitte &amp; Touche Consulting Group.Based on 1995 population sizes covered by the licenses, companies
12035 at the C-Block sale on average paid $37.97 a person. Today, bidders currently are offering the equivalent of about $4 a person for a similar airwave parcel, said BIA's Foxman.While the latest auction is not expected to meet the rich prices paid earlier, Foxman still held out the prospect that
12035 bidding could pick up."It's early in the process and prices may well go up substantially. But I don't expect it will reach the prices in the C-Block," he said.Analysts said the cheaper prices reflect several factors:-- The airwave chunks being sold in the current auction, at 10 MHz a piece,
12035 are a third smaller and so less attractive than the 30 MHz slices sold in the two previous PCS auctions.-- The PCS market is becoming overcrowded with new players and a price war looms. That leaves little room for relative newcomers to turn a profit.-- Some winners in the C-Block
12035 auction are not having an easy time raising the money to fund their ventures, after plunking down bids ranging into the billions of dollars.San Diego-based Nextwave -- which placed winning bids of $4.2 billion -- filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June to offer $300 million worth of
12035 stock and $400 million in bonds. The offerings have yet to proceed."The high-yield debt market has been extremely chilly to the C-Block players," said Steve Zecola, a top executive at US 1 Communications Corp., who earlier led a company that dropped out of the C-Block auction after prices in his
12035 opinion became too expensive.A NextWave spokeswoman declined to comment, citing SEC rules about discussing a securities filing.Corey Linquist of Dallas-based General Wireless, which has filed with the SEC to offer $165 million in stock and $220 million in bonds, said, "We're happy where we're at."</

12053 Long derided as the "snail mail" alternative to zippier electronic mail, the U.S. Postal Service is plotting its own foray into cyberspace.Although still in various stages of testing and development, Post Office projects include a digital postal meter that can be filled online, a service to verify the autheticity of
12053 e-mail and an archive for digital data.The postal service has a long history of nurturing new communications technologies, Paul Raines, programme manager for electronic commerce services, noted."The Postal Service has always been there as a sort of enabler of technology," Raines said, noting the services' early support of railroads, telegraphs
12053 and airplanes.The postal service contracted for air delivery of mail in the early days of powered flight while the rest of the government hesitated. Eventually, the service built a network of beacons, towers and airfields to speed service.Much of the Post Office's thrust on the Internet is to create an
12053 infrastructure of standards and universally accepted practices. The technology, in many cases, is decades old.For example, in the 1970s, researchers developed a system called public key encryption for ensuring the security and authenticity of e-mail or other electronic documents.Everyone using the system gets two software "keys," one kept secret and
12053 one made publicly available.A user runs any document through a special programme that codes the document with the private software key. The document can be decoded only with the companion public key. Anyone who receives the document can be sure of its source with the public key.The process can also
12053 work in reverse. To send a secret message, the message is encoded with the intended recipient's public key. It can then only be decoded with the private key.But for the system to work, some entity must disseminate the public keys and insure that keys are registered in the names of
12053 their true owners. The Post Office may be perfectly suited for such a job.The first service, time-stamping and authenticating e-mail, is basically a simple variation on public key encryption. Each message is encoded using the Post Office's own private key and can be verified against the service's public key."That can
12053 be important for a legal document if you want to prove that it existed at a certain date and time or if you were submitting your taxes to the IRS electronically and you want to prove that you had it in by April 15," Raines said.Next year, the service will
12053 begin trials for a wider ranging encryption key programme, registering pairs of keys for individuals and businesses to avoid duplication and then making public keys accessible.The Post office also plans to expand existing service on its Web site (http://www.usps.gov), called MoversNet, with encryption. The service offers advice for movers, tips
12053 for packing, discounts on van rentals and other information.Eventually, using encryption, people will be able to register a change of address over the Internet for mail forwarding.Not everyone supports the Post Office's new drive in electronic commerce, with opposition particularly among companies that offer competing services.A leading bank lobbying group,
12053 the American Bankers Association, blasted the Post office's plans in a letter to the service earlier this month."The USPS should stick to its primary mission of delivering mail," the banking group wrote.Services under consideration, which banks might also provide, are "inappropriate diversions from USPS' charter mission," the bankers added.</

12060 The International Monetary Fund warned Europe on Wednesday against persisting with its headlong drive to reduce budget deficits under the Maastricht Treaty if economic growth fails to pick up as expected."It is important to avoid aggravating a difficult situation through unduly procyclical (tight) fiscal policies," the IMF said in its
12060 semi-annual World Economic Outlook.The Fund does expect European Union economic growth to pick up next year, to 2.5 percent, from 1.6 percent in 1996.If that occurs, a number of nations, including France, should be able to cut their 1997 budget deficits in line with criteria set out in Maastricht and
12060 thus qualify for membership in European Monetary Union at its launch in 1999, it said.But problems will crop up if growth remains weak -- a risk that the IMF made clear could not be ruled out.In that case, the Fund signalled that it would prefer European nations to temporarily allow
12060 their budget deficits to increase in line with the weakness of their economies rather than to cut them to meet the tough Maastricht criteria. "If recent economic weakness were to be prolonged, it may ... be necessary to allow fiscal policy to provide automatic stabilizers for activity, but only in
12060 those countries that are making convincing and adequate progress in reducing structural imbalances," the IMF said.According to a chart in the World Economic Outlook, France and Germany, among others, would seem to qualify as countries making such progress.The IMF made clear that in the medium term European countries need to
12060 put their public finances in order -- Maastricht or not."Progressive elimination of fiscal imbalances is necessary for an improvement in growth performance over the medium term," the IMF said.And it linked Europe's high budget deficits to its excessive unemployment rates."As much as eight to nine percentage points of the EU's
12060 current unemployment rate of over 11 percent is widely considered to be structural in the sense that it is unlikely that it could be absorbed through cyclical recovery alone, without significant inflationary risks," the Fund said.It backed widespread labor market reforms to tackle that.</

12063 The Federal Reserve's decision this week to keep interest rates steady shows it is willing to err on the side of growth as it seeks to determine if new forces in the economy are holding inflation down."Clearly, there are structural changes in the economy that have made it more unclear
12063 as to how to conduct monetary policy," said Ryan Krueger of Krueger Washington Research."There is a sense that we may be in a new era where inflation is lower and where you can have wage increases without necessarily seeing higher inflation," he added. Following a meeting Tuesday of the central
12063 bank's Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed chose not to raise rates.The decision stunned many economists who believe recent robust growth and a 5.1 percent unemployment rate were a recipe for higher inflation. It also stirred talk that, with the presidential election just six weeks away, a desire to stay
12063 out of the political fray may have kept the Fed on hold."Since it was a close call I think the election may have been a factor in the decision," said Lawrence Chimerine, managing director at the Economic Strategy Institute. More important, though, was the desire by many at the Fed
12063 to test whether its old rules on inflation still apply, he said.Analysts widely believe Tuesday's meeting was one of the more contentious ones in recent history, particularly in light of the disclosure that eight of the 12 regional Fed banks had submitted requests for discount rate increases.Former Fed Vice Chairman
12063 Preston Martin said discussion of theories about growth and inflation probably dominated the debate with Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan emerging as the pivotal figure in tilting a majority of the FOMC toward steady policy. Given Greenspan's abilities as a consensus-builder, Martin said that, in the end, "I'll bet you there
12063 were only two or three dissenting votes."A key subject of debate among economists inside and outside the Fed concerns the relationship between unemployment and inflation.Until recently, many experts viewed a 6 percent jobless rate as the so-called "non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment" (NAIRU) -- the lowest level of unemployment that
12063 can be sustained without causing wage pressures and, ultimately, higher inflation.After the jobless rate has stayed below 6 percent for more than two years without a noticeable price pickup, many experts believe the NAIRU has fallen but they differ on how low it is.Still, with the unemployment rate now at
12063 a seven-year low of 5.1 percent and amid signs that wages are beginning to head higher, economists believe the Fed is testing the limits of noninflationary growth by not raising rates. "They are taking a small risk at this point," said economist Daniel Bachman of the WEFA Group. "Looking at
12063 the labor market right now there is a little bit of a reason to believe that the Fed might be behind the curve (on fighting inflation)."Still, Bachman said he thinks the Fed made the right call in not raising rates, particularly because he is predicting that the economy is set
12063 to slow after booming at a 4.8 percent rate in the second quarter."There were some very good arguments on the side of the people on the FOMC who didn't see evidence that inflation was going to pick up," said chief economist James Annable of First Chicago NBD."I think (the lack
12063 of a rate rise) is a rather healthy sign that the Federal Reserve is looking closely to see how this economy is working and if its old rules have changed."</

12065 of the liver, according to media reports.Homicide investigators hoped Toole did not take the secret of the boy's death to his grave -- that he had made a deathbed confession or that his death would bring new witnesses to light, police said Wednesday.Toole was long the prime suspect in the
12065 brutal slaying of Walsh, abducted from a department store in Hollywood, Florida July 27, 1981. The boy's head was found two weeks later in a canal in Vero Beach, 120 miles to the north.Toole, 49, confessed to scores of murders and was serving five life sentences for several arson murders
12065 unrelated to the Walsh case. No relative claimed his body and he was buried at Union Correctional Insitution in Raiford, Florida.He confessed to killing Adam Walsh in late 1984 but later recanted. Although he was never charged with the crime, he remained a prime suspect because of blood found on
12065 the floor of his car and on a machete he once told police he used to cut off the boy's head.A DNA link was never established and evidence in the case, including the car, disappeared. But police said Wednesday that Toole remained until his death their strongest suspect."We're hoping this
12065 may be a turn in the investigation," said Hollywood Police spokeswoman Stephanie Norris."There may be people that for one of many reasons didn't want to come forward while he was alive," she said. "Perhaps they didn't want to see Ottis go to the electric chair. Perhaps they were afraid. That
12065 fear is no longer there."Norris said investigators would try to interview anyone who had contact with Toole during his final days, including medical personnel and clergy, to determine if he made any "dying declaration" on the killing. 12065 but were not told of his illness.Adam's father, John Walsh, who gained fame following the death of his son as the host of the anti-crime television show "America's Most Wanted," told Miami Fox affiliate WSVN: "This is just another setback, just another heartbreak. 12065 family? No closure. No closure."</

12081 or 60 cents a share, from $71 million, or 52 cents a share, a year ago.However, Lehman said its net revenues, which represent total revenues less interest expenses, slipped 4 percent to $722 million from $750 million last year.
