12087 The White House released documents Wednesday that it said proved President Clinton's insistence that the collection of confidential FBI reports on Republicans was simply a bureaucratic blunder.Officials said the documents showed White House security official Anthony Marceca was working from inaccurate lists produced by the Secret Service when he obtained
12087 from the FBI secret background investigations on hundreds of Republicans from the administrations of Ronald Reagan and George Bush.A White House associate counsel, Mark Fabiani, released a thick stack of papers that he said constituted the faulty Secret Service lists Marceca was using. He said the White House would have
12087 released them sooner but they had been in the custody of Kenneth Starr, the independent counsel investigating cases involving Clinton and his wife, Hillary."These newly revealed Secret Service lists support what the White House has said all along about the FBI files matter: The files were mistakenly sought as the
12087 result of a bureaucratic blunder," Fabiani said.Republicans have charged that in collecting the files on Republicans, the White House was compiling an "enemies list" and committed an extreme violation of privacy.The House Government Reform and Oversight Committee adopted an interim report on the FBI files case Tuesday and called for
12087 a top FBI official to resign. It accused the White House of trying to politicize the bureau.Republicans reject Clinton's explanation that aides sought files on the wrong people in the course of approving people for regular access to the White House because the Secret Service provided lists with people who
12087 no longer worked there.Sen. Orrin Hatch of Utah, chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, said he was not convinced the White House was innocent. He said the committee had evidence that Marceca, knowing the lists were inaccurate, requested from the FBI background reports on Republicans he knew no longer worked
12087 at the White House."Perhaps this will shed some light," he told CNN, referring to the newly released documents. Hatch's committee was holding a hearing to investigate the files case further, with testimony from witnesses including the White House's former personnel security chief, Craig Livingstone.The lists were in two boxes of
12087 documents the White House turned over to the FBI in June when it was disclosed that Marceca, who worked for Livingstone, had collected the files.Fabiani said the White House had sought their return to prove its point that the lists were faulty but the FBI had turned them over to
12087 Starr's investigators.When Starr was asked to return them, the White House was told they would be sent back "at such time when disclosure of the documents would not hinder or impede our investigation." Deputy independent counsel John Bates returned the lists Tuesday, saying in a letter that "we believe that
12087 time has been reached."Fabiani said the release of the lists undermined the Republicans' argument by proving the Secret Service produced them in June 1993 -- months after Clinton took office. This would mean the Secret Service was mistakenly giving the White House names of people who no longer worked there,
12087 he said."Republicans said it was an enemies list, but we said it was an older list used to do searches for FBI files," he said.</
12088 Most U.S. corporations do not believe proposals by the Securities and Exchange Commission to enhance disclosure of derivatives holdings would improve investors' understanding of the risks involved, according to a new survey of companies.About 50 percent of 319 public and private companies surveyed said investor understanding would improve "not at
12088 all" if the companies reported current values of derivatives, off-balance-sheet financial instruments whose value changes in conjunction with other instruments, commodities or price indexes, the survey by the Treasury Management Association found.Another 30 percent said the reporting would help "to a small extent," while fewer than 20 percent said it
12088 would help "to a moderate extent" or more.The association, a group representing more than 8,000 treasury officials, conducted the survey over the summer and released preliminary results at a conference of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association here on Wednesday. Many firms also said in the survey that the SEC's
12088 proposed disclosure scheme did not accurately describe most of their financial risk management activities.About 17 percent said the descriptions were "not at all" accurate, and another 35 percent said they were accurate "to a small extent."About 33 percent said the requirements would describe their activities accurately "to a moderate extent,"
12088 and 14 percent said "to a great extent or more."The SEC offered firms three possible methods for reporting on derivatives activities: transactions listed in tabular form, an analysis of positions' sensitivity to various market moves, and use of quantitative figures such as "value at risk."Surveyed firms said all three choices
12088 would be costly. About 54 percent said tabular presentation would involve a moderate or great added expense, while about 46 percent said it would be a minor or small incremental expense.Some 79 percent said sensitivity analysis would involve a moderate or great expense, and 89 percent said "value at risk"
12088 would be a moderate or great expense. Larger firms in the survey said they already make some derivatives disclosures. For firms with at least $1 billion in revenues, 83 percent report notes on derivatives use, though not all firms disclosed the notional amount of derivatives used or stated whether the
12088 instruments were held for trading or other purposes.--Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312 REUTER</

12104 If Democrats win control of the House of Representatives in November it will be with the help of victorious candidates who believe President Bill Clinton's declaration that the era of big government is over.Republicans charge that, if Democrats win, "liberals" are poised to grab control of powerful House committees and
12104 move full speed ahead to raise taxes and boost government spending.But even some Democrats said the power of liberal committee chairmen would be diluted by a new wave of moderate Democratic members of Congress.Analysts say the Democrats have a decent shot at making the net gains necessary to regain a
12104 majority in the 435-seat House, where Republicans have a 235-198 edge with one seat vacant and one independent who votes with the Democrats.Control of the House means the party in power can set the legislative agenda and use the committee structure to put its favourite issues in the spotlight.Republicans dismiss
12104 Democratic chances of reversing the 1994 outcome, which brought Republicans to power in the House for the first time in 40 years. But with many races in doubt, Republicans are sounding an alarm about what Democrats would do if they do take over."Their true agenda is a liberal agenda, marked
12104 by greater government control, more spending and higher taxes," declared Republican National Committee Chairman Haley Barbour.He pointed to members such as Wisconsin Democrat David Obey, first in line to chair the powerful Appropriations Committee, which controls most spending. Obey wants government to expand its reach rather than contract.But the new
12104 breed of Democratic candidates include many fiscal conservatives for whom balancing the federal budget is an article of faith.Some voted for a welfare reform plan Clinton signed into law over the objections of liberals such as Democratic Representative Anthony Beilenson of California, who complained it would hurt the poor. Beilenson
12104 is retiring and the Democrat running to replace him, Brad Sherman, feels differently."I probably would have cast a vote in favour," says Sherman, despite his belief the welfare measure needed some changes.Even in the inner cities things are changing. 12104 Indianapolis, opposed the welfare bill but ran a tough welfare system herself in that Midwest city.Carson, who was on welfare as a child, cut 85,000 people from the rolls, instituted "workfare" requiring people to earn their benefits and slashed $9.3 million.And in the Washington state primary this month, moderate Democrats
12104 beat liberals in three districts to face conservative first-term Republicans. During a visit last week, Clinton said Washington has "a bigger opportunity than any other state to say 'we need change in Congress.'"These new Democrats, running for open seats or challenging Republicans, are modelling themselves on Clinton, who once proposed
12104 a major expansion of government power in health care but now says he is not a liberal."We will have an infusion of moderate Democrats who want to win re-election as well as election," said Democratic Representative Howard Berman of California.</
12105 With the global financial system in a period of unprecedented change, the role of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank seem both enhanced, yet somehow diminished.Only a handful of countries still shun membership in the two lending institutions, so they are able to carry their message and their assistance
12105 far and wide as never before.At the same time, the multi-trillion dollar private markets are holding such sway these days -- effortlessly moving money across borders into emerging economies -- that they make the power of the IMF and Bank appear less relevant."The world of foreign financial involvement in developing
12105 economies and emerging markets is being driven today by private capital, by private investors, by private lenders," said Charles Dallara, managing director of the Institute of International Finance."I think there is a very different set of rules for the IMF and World Bank today. They no longer are the dominant
12105 supplier of finance -- in fact on a net basis in the aggregate they provide very little in finance for these countries," Dallara adds. It is against this backdrop that the two institutions begin their annual meetings this week, as they attempt to deal with issues ranging from a controversial
12105 new debt relief initiative to ways to head off global economic crisis.Much of the discussion reflects the disturbing ability of the tightly-woven international financial system to quickly spread problems from one country to others around the world.This was most recently seen during what IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus has called
12105 the first economic crisis of the 21st century, the unraveling of Mexico that required a Herculean international rescue effort to repair its economy.That experience helped spawned several initiatives, including a new IMF bulletin board on the Internet on which users can be directed to country data in a number of
12105 emerging markets on a more timely basis.This seemed key since the 1994-1995 Mexican peso crisis caught many investors off guard and spread quickly to some of its surrounding neighbors and even countries in Eastern Europe. Critics said the crisis might have been avoided if data on the Mexican economy was
12105 more readily available. "The new IMF standards will improve the availability, the quality and the international comparability of information that is vital both for the formulation of sound economic policies and for the smooth functioning of global financial markets," U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said last week.At the same time,
12105 officials are putting the final touches on a $54 billion war chest that can be used to help countries overwhelmed by economic crises similar to the Mexican debacle.The pool of funds will be discussed during the annual meeting although final approval is unlikely at that time. It would double the
12105 amount in the General Arrangements to Borrow established by the Group of 10 industrial countries.This doubling is to be accomplished by establishing a facility called the New Arrangements to Borrow with a number of countries, including Austria, Australia, Denmark, Finland, South Korea, Luxembourg, Malasia, Norway, Singapore, Spain and Thailand considering
12105 pledging funds to help in a crisis.Policymakers will also discuss a new plan to assist poor countries hit by overwhelming debt, including outstanding loans to the IMF and World Bank. The plan could include the sale of some IMF gold but this has yet to be worked out. But the
12105 debt relief plan has its critics. Officials attending this week's meeting of Commonwealth Finance Ministers in Bermuda take the view that the plan is so restrictive it will help few countries who really need it."These restrictions reduce to only 11 the number of countries likely to receive multilateral debt relief,
12105 and delay relief so that only three will receive comprehensive treatment," a confidential report at the meeting said.Policymakers will also review proposals to increase the IMF's quota to help replenish the agency's coffers, hard hit by huge loans to Mexico and Russia in recent years. IMF Managing director Michel Camdessus
12105 is seeking a doubling to $440 billion.Lastly, there will be discussion of a plan to allocate the IMF's own money, the Special Drawing Right, to newer members of the IMF that have been short-changed compared to older members. It is estimated this would amount to about 26 billion SDRS, or

12107 Federal safety regulators are investigating seat belt problems in 1997 F150 pickup trucks from Ford Motor Co., as well as fuel leakage reports on an undetermined number of 1996 Chrysler Corp. minivans.The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said Wednesday it has received 29 reports that seat belts were loose
12107 or improperly attached on the pickups. Causes included a missing bolt, missing nut and an unthreaded bolt hole.Ford told NHTSA it has not changed its seatbelt installation procedure, but has added another inspection at the assembly plant. More than 95 percent of the 171,641 trucks included in the probe were
12107 built on or before May 1, 1996.The agency said it opened an investigation into all models of 1996 Chrysler minivans after receiving nine complaints from owners about fuel tank leaks. NHTSA said preliminary information indicates the leak occurs where the fuel pump joins the fuel tank.Chrysler spokeswoman Michele Tinson said
12107 the company and agency are trying to determine how many minivans may be affected. She said Chrysler is cooperating with the investigation.Separately, NHTSA said it opened a preliminary investigation into 500,000 1988-90 Ford Aerostar minivans because of reports of cracked fuel tanks.Regulators have received 26 complaints from owners about "serious
12107 incidents of fuel leakage" from cracks or split seams on the top of fuel tanks.Ford changed to a 21-gallon tank from a 17-gallon tank in October 1988. NHTSA said it has received complaints from owners with both sized tanks.NHTSA is also looking into 250,000 1994-96 F250 four-wheel-drive pickup trucks from
12107 Ford. It has received seven owner complaints about the front suspension separating from the frame of the truck.Reports have included sheared bolts, missing nuts on bolts and loose fasteners with elongated holes, which NHTSA said could result in a loss of control.Ford spokeswoman Francine Romine-MacBride said the automaker is aware
12107 of the investigations and is cooperating with NHTSA.NHTSA disclosed the probes in its monthly defect investigation report. The cases involved in the new investigations did not result in any accidents or injuries.</

12109 U.S. broiler production could rise at least five percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.In a monthly outlook, the USDA said that placements of broiler chicks has begun to increase significantly compared to last year and are up one to four percent since mid-August. These
12109 birds will be slaughtered in early fall.Wholesale broiler prices are expected to remain strong, despite the higher produciton, supported by strong export demand, USDA said. 12109 by a wide margin.Broiler shipments of 101 million pounds to China have more than doubled in the first seven months of 1996 from last year.Exports of other chicken products were up three-fold in July from a year earlier, reflecting growth to Canada, Hong Kong and Japan.September turkey production is expected
12109 to increase about six percent, but USDA said negative returns during 1996 are epxected to slow production increases during 1997. Turkey exports to Russia have soared over the past 18 months, USDA said. Russia is now the second largest export market for U.S. turkey, behind only Mexico.Exports to Russia in
12109 July were 22 million pounds, more than double the previous year and 53 percent of all turkey exports that month. Exports to Russia so far in 1996 have reached 74 million pounds.USDA said if exports to Russian continue at the current stron pace, it is possible Russia will surpass Mexico
12109 as the largest customer of U.S. turkeys.</

12117 By Alan Elsner, Political CorrespondentPresident Bill Clinton leads Republican Bob Dole by 15.4 percentage points in a Reuters poll of voter sentiment across the neighbouring battleground states of Pennsylvania and New Jersey.The poll of 997 likely voters, conducted Sept 22-24 by John Zogby Group International, gave Clinton an aggregate of
12117 47.6 percent in the two states. Dole had 32.2 percent and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot had 6.5 percent. Some 12.8 percent of respondents were undecided. The poll carried a margin of error of plus or minus 3.2 percentage points.Clinton's lead was slightly greater in Pennsylvania, where he led Dole
12117 by 16 percentage points. In New Jersey, Dole was 14.6 points behind. The margin of error for the Pennsylvania sub-group was plus or minus four percentage points. For New Jersey, it was plus or minus five points.The poll was yet another sign that Clinton remains comfortably positioned to triumph in
12117 the Nov. 5 election. Both states have popular Republican governors and swung heavily Republican in the 1994 congressional elections.Both candidates have campaigned heavily in both states. Clinton was in New Jersey Tuesday and Pennsylvania Wednesday.Pollster John Zogby noted that in this poll, as in all previous Reuters polls, Dole's support
12117 remained mired well below 40 percent."Dole appears hopelessly locked in the 30's nationally and state by state. At some point Dole will have to move up into the 40s if he is to make this a race," said Zogby.With 270 Electoral College votes needed to win the presidency in the
12117 indirect U.S. system, Pennsylvania is the fifth biggest state with 23 votes. New Jersey has 15 votes.A Reuters poll last week found Clinton with similar leads in the Midwestern states of Michigan, Ohio and Illinois, which have a combined 61 Electoral College votes.The poll came at the end of a
12117 week when Dole repeatedly blamed Clinton in speeches and paid advertisements for an increase in the use of illegal drugs by young people.But a large majority of voters said they disagreed that Clinton was responsible. In both states, only 20 percent said they agreed with Dole's argument, while 70 percent
12117 disagreed.Dole's other top issue, his promise of a 15 percent income tax cut, was modelled on the strategy that helped New Jersey Gov. Christine Todd Whitman score a come-from-behind victory over Democrat Jim Florio to win the governorship in 1993.But in follow-up interviews voters, including many Republicans and Dole supporters,
12117 continued to express deep scepticism that Dole could deliver."I don't agree with Dole's tax cut. Somewhere down the road, we'll all have to pay for it," said Gary Clemons, a casket maker in Mount Wolf, Pennsylvania, who nevertheless said he would support the Republican nominee.Others are not so charitable. The
12117 poll showed that only 62 percent of Republicans are backing Dole while 76 percent of Democrats support Clinton.Several voters also criticised Dole for opposing Perot's inclusion in the upcoming presidential debates."Perot should be in the debates. It was misguided of Dole to oppose him. He's listening to his advisers who
12117 have him convinced he's an old man who knows nothing about politics, which is ludicrous," said Diane McClarty, a homemaker from Montclair, New Jersey who backed Perot in 1992 but supports Dole this time.The poll showed a continued wide gender gap. Clinton led by only eight points among men but
12117 by 23 points among women."Republican policies have become very mean-spirited. Women care more about education, children and the underprivileged and these issues are the heart of this election," said Deborah Hill-Haney, a chemist from Metuchen, New Jersey.In congressional races. Democrats had small leads in both states -- five points in
12117 Pennsylvania and less than one point in New Jersey.Clinton carried New Jersey by just over two percentage points in 1992 and Pennsylvania by nine points. 12122 U.S. municipal bond prices were up 3/8 of a point as plentiful customer lists drew strong interest from bidders, traders said."It's been a good day today," one trader said, adding that while "the bid wanted wires have not been light," bidding was aggressive and broad-based."I don't think there is any
12122 concession in our market right now," he said. "With the (Federal Reserve) on hold for now and the fact that the calendar is so light..you kind of have to take your shots right now on the secondary side, you know, on the bid wanteds." While he hadn't added them up,
12122 the trader said he saw 10 to 11 lists in circulation from funds and other accounts."It's kind of interesting, they are all selling kind of the same area, '05 to '09 and then '10 to '16," the trader said. "We had one little list of 25-(year) and 30-year paper but
12122 in terms of par value it paled in comparison to this other stuff."A second trader reported seeing about 22 bid lists out."I haven't added up the par amount, but (there was) a lot of selling today," he said.Traders attributed municipals' strength to Federal Reserve policy makers' decision to stand pat
12122 on interest rates."Definitely the market has a better tone since the Fed didn't act," one trader said. He added, however, "I thought that we had room to improve even if they did raise 25 basis point because I think we were a little overdone."In the government market, the benchmark 30-year
12122 bond was up 19/32 at 07-20/32 to yield 6.94 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 11/32 at 113-31/32. The December T-bond contract was up 19/32 at 109-7/32. The MOB spread was 152 ticks.--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655</
12123 The American Automobile Association (AAA) and an oil industry group are locking horns over premium gasoline following claims by AAA that drivers are wasting $1.7 billion a year buying the higher-octane fuel."Many drivers are falling for the 'octane myth' in gasoline ads and are giving $1.7 billion to the nation's
12123 oil industry needlessly," the Washington-based AAA said in a prepared statement issued Tuesday. "That's dead wrong, they're giving short shrift to the facts," countered Thomas Hogarty, senior research manager for the American Petroleum Institute, who defended premium for promoting low-knock combustion."Contrary to popular opinion, premium gas does not provide more
12123 power, doesn't improve performance, burn more clearly, reduce engine wear or improve mileage," AAA spokesman Dave Van Sickle insisted. The AAA said consumers should realize "only exotic cars, some sport utility vehicles and vehicles with high-performance engines really need premium," which costs consumers about 15 cents a gallon more than
12123 regular grade fuel.The nationwide auto club contended fewer than 10 percent of cars on U.S. roads needed premium although it constitutes nearly 20 percent of total gas sold.Its renewed attack against premium echoes the Federal Trade Commission's own clarion call against premium last week. The federal agency, seeking to warn
12123 consumers against paying extra, sued Exxon Corp on Sept. 17 for making allegedly overblown advertising claims that premium enabled engines to run cleaner and with better mileage.Exxon was the fourth major U.S. oil company called to task by the FTC, but the first not to settle before a suit was
12123 filed.Hogarty conceded in a telephone interview there was little evidence premium reduced engine wear or improved mileage."I won't argue with those points," he said. But Hogarty said a recent study by the Coordinating Research Council, an oil industry group based in Atlanta, Georgia, showed 19 percent of U.S. vehicles needed
12123 premium to assure smooth combustion and prevent knocking and ping noises associated with lower-octane fuels."Light trucks, vans and utility vehicles are less likely to get by on regular," he said, because of built-in vehicle "knock sensors" that limit acceleration ability if fuel quality is below the premium standard of 92-
12123 to 93-grade octane.Regular octane level, a measure of resistance to knocking, is rated at 87-grade. What's more, Hogarty said vast numbers of old vehicles that once used anti-knock leaded fuel, now outlawed, can't operate properly on regular unleaded gasoline."They (AAA) are giving short shrift to a lot of old cars
12123 and trucks," he said, adding that many of the vintage vehicles are operated in the western United States.-- New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632</

12125 A ruling by a U.S. District Court judge in Chicago on whether or not to dismiss or delay a lawsuit challenging Illinois' removal of a state subsidy for a bond-financed waste-to-energy incinerator has been delayed.The ruling scheduled for Wednesday by Judge Brian Duff was postponed until Oct. 23, according to
12125 attorneys representing the parties in the lawsuit.Attorneys representing Illinois officials sued by the developer of an incinerator in the Chicago suburb of Robbins had asked the judge to dismiss the case on the grounds the 11th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution precludes lawsuits dealing with public funds.In this case, public
12125 funds involved a subsidy Illinois had been guarenteeing to incinerator developers that allowed them to sell the electricity they generated to utilities at a higher rate.If the lawsuit was not dismissed, the state asked the judge to defer the case until a similar lawsuit filed by other incinerator developers in
12125 Cook County Circuit Court was decided.A decision on whether that case will be dismissed is expected within days. Following oral arguments earlier this month on the state's motion to dismiss the case, Judge Edwin Berman said he would rule by Monday.At stake in both lawsuits is the viability of nearly
12125 $500 million of tax-exempt, unrated bonds that were sold for three incinerator projects in Robbins, Ford Heights and Fulton and which were largely dependent on the state subsidy.CGE Ford Heights, the developer of the Ford Heights incinerator, has already filed for bankruptcy as its litigation against the state continues. That
12125 lawsuit has been joined by developer CGE Fulton and bondholders.The Illinois Development Finance Authority sold $79.6 million of bonds for the Ford Heights project in 1994, while Fulton sold $84.6 million of bonds last December. The Fulton sale occured just before the Illinois General Assembly voted to yank the incinerator
12125 subsidy that had been in effect since 1987. The measure was signed into law in March by Gov. Jim Edgar.Meanwhile, Foster Wheeler Corp. announced last week a tender offer for nearly $320 million of bonds sold by Robbins in 1994 for the incinerator had been initiated. Under the tender, which
12125 ends Oct. 15, the bonds would be restructured with a lower interest rate and additional credit support, as well as other changes.The Robbins incinerator was developed by Illinois subsidiaries of Foster Wheeler.--Karen Pierog, 312-408-8647</

12134 "We believe we can realize $40 billion in cash receipts at the farm level by 2002."The goal, part of a vision statement issued Wednesday, was based on demand and production estimates and on government and environmental policy trends, said Everett Nordine, co-chairman of the task force that wrote the statement."The
12134 $40 billion level can be reached in several ways," Nordine said. "We can increase demand. We can also add value to our product in current markets by using new technology and developing new uses for corn."U.S. corn growers produce about 70 percent of the world export market share, NCGA said.--Chicago
12135 Tropical Storm Isidore swiftly gained strength in the mid-Atlantic on Wednesday and could become a hurricane within 24 hours, the National Hurricane Center said.Isidore graduated to tropical storm status early on Wednesday, becoming the ninth tropical storm of the Atlantic hurricane season. By 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), its maximum
12135 sustained winds had risen to 65 mph (105 kph), nearing the threshold of 74 mph (120 kph) at which a tropical storm becomes a hurricane."It really got its act together during the night," said Brian Jarvinen, a forecaster at the hurricane center. "We may have a hurricane by tomorrow because
12135 this system is sitting right on a tongue of warm water and the upper level features are ripe for development."At its current speed and position, Isidore would not approach the Caribbean for four to five days, he said.At 11 a.m. EDT, it was located at latitude 10.8 north and longitude
12135 31.0 west, about 550 miles (885 km) west-southwest of Africa's Cape Verde islands. It was upgraded from a tropical depression to a tropical storm six hours earlier.The storm was moving west-northwest at 21 mph (34 kph) but was expected to slow down, forecasters said.</

"We are not going to return the unit to service until
12139 we know what happened."Staff at the burn unit of the Columbia-Augusta Regional Medical Centre in Augusta, Georgia, confirmed they had admitted four of the workers, all men. "They are all in critical condition," a nurse told Reuters, saying they had second- and third-degree burns.The remaining workers, two men and a
12139 woman, were in less serious condition at hospitals in Seneca and Greenville, South Carolina.The pipe burst late Tuesday at one of three nuclear power generators in Duke Power Co.'s Oconee facility in Seneca, in the northwest corner of the state. The plant was returning to service after a leaking valve
12139 forced it to shut down Monday.The accident was not in the nuclear part of the plant and no radioactivity was released, the company said.The last serious injury to a worker at Oconee occurred in the 1970s. He too was scalded when a steam pipe burst.The Oconee generators each have a
12139 generating capacity of 846 megawatts. Duke Power Co. is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.</

12144 between U.S. firms and three Chinese agencies. Kantor said the contracts were a result of a June agreement on intellectual property rights. The meeting of the U.S.-China Joint Commission on Commerce and Trade also was to discuss establishment of a title verification office in Beijing and additional copyright and trademark
12144 training."I do not anticipate any dramatic breakthroughs outside of our ability to continue this process," Kantor told reporters."Remember, we're building a normal and, hopefully, productive trade relationship which will be reciprocal in nature with China." While the commission was to focus on 10 business sectors, Kantor said at a private
12144 session with Wu, "each of us will raise a number of issues that will cover the waterfront of trade" between the nations. 12144 rules that virtually cut off U.S. wheat sales. Wu might want to discuss textile exports, he said."I would assume we would discuss this and exchange our views," Kantor said of the textile trade.China is the fifth largest U.S. trade partner and sells far more than it buys. The U.S. trade
12144 deficit with China was $33.8 billion in 1995 and totaled $18.5 billion at the end of this July.</

12149 to cut the deficit to a reasonable size and I think we will do it."The Bank of Israel would respond to tighter fiscal policy by easing interest rates, Meridor said. He declined comment whether the Bank of Israel acted agressively enough in trimming its key lending rate for October by
12149 0.3 percentage points to an annualized 15.5 percent. "What we need to do is cut the budget and lower interest rates," Meridor said. 12154 The U.S. House late Monday approved a House-Senate compromise bill that includes billions of dollars in funding for federal housing and environmental programs of interest to the municipal bond market.By a vote of 388-25, the House agreed to provide $64.4 billion in funds for the Department of Housing and Urban
12154 Development, Environmental Protection Agency, Veterans Administration and independent agencies.Earlier in the day, the Senate "deemed" the bill passed upon approved by the House, which means the measure now goes to President Clinton for signature.The measure includes $3.6 billion for expiring Section 8 housing contracts, below the $4.5 billion cleared recently
12154 by the House and $3.8 billion provided by the Senate.Housing lobbyists, however, said the $3.6 billion apparently is enough to provide HUD the money it needs for renewals of contracts due to expire under the Section 8 rent subsidy program.The bill cleared last night also provides $4.6 billion for Community
12154 Development Block Grants and $1.4 billion for the HOME investment partnerships program, unchanged from totals approved by the House and Senate earlier.The bill provides $625 million for Clean Water State Revolving Funds and $1.250 billion for Safe Drinking Water State Revolving Funds.The overall funding measure is three percent higher than
12154 Congress appropriated for HUD and the other agencies in the current 1996 fiscal year, but 3.5 percent less than President Clinton requested.--Vicky Stamas, 202-898-8314</

12158 Bob Dole calls them "Listening to America" meetings, where he takes questions from "real people," but most seem to feature adoring Republican fans dishing out flattery.The Republican presidential nominee uses a town meeting format more often now in an effort to energise a campaign mired in weak poll ratings with
12158 only six weeks left to catch President Clinton before the Nov. 5 election.The encounters are so arranged that Dole is usually surrounded by people who ask about favourite subjects, such as his proposal to cut income tax rates by 15 percent.That was the case in this north-central Ohio farm community
12158 where several hundred people gathered at a vocational school on Tuesday and peppered him with fluffy questions.Typical was his first interrogator, who described herself as an educator, said "this is indeed an honour" and asked about one of Dole's favourite political targets, the liberal-oriented teachers' unions.Dole batted that one out
12158 of the park, taking a swipe at the National Education Association -- the nation's biggest teachers' union and an old nemesis, which he claims gives 99 percent of its contributions to Democrat Clinton. He portrayed himself as a champion of teachers, as opposed to their unions, and said his education
12158 plans were "teacher friendly."The next man asked him to explain his tax cut, a chore Dole relished as he replied at great length "This is not a Wall Street tax. This is a Main Street tax," he said.Another woman wanted to know how he would pay for school vouchers, a
12158 Republican-favoured scheme that would help parents send their children to private schools of their choice. Dole devoured that one as well, saying he would free up some of the funds by abolishing the federal Department of Education.And so it went, one "soft-ball" query after another sailing in from a uniformly
12158 friendly crowd.-----Dole's new efforts to take the offensive against Clinton include regular efforts to paint him as "an old-style, dyed-in-the-wool, big-spending liberal" -- as he put it at one rally in Detroit on Tuesday.Yet, the Kansas conservative also regularly lists some of the most liberal of liberals as his "friends."That
12158 includes Sen. Edward Kennedy, the Massachusetts Democrat widely regarded as the dean of Washington liberals and proud of it. Dole, who retired as Senate majority leader last spring after 35 years in Congress, regularly cites Kennedy in his speeches as an example of a liberal Democratic taxer.But he also calls
12158 Kennedy his "friend," an honorific also bestowed on such well-known traditional liberals as New York Sen. Pat Moynihan, the late Democratic Sen. Phil Hart of Michigan and the late Vice President Hubert Humphrey, an enduring symbol of American liberalism.Dole, known as a collegial compromiser in the clubby Senate and ill
12158 at ease with the personal-attack politics he must now practice, insists on making the point that Clinton and the rest are his opponents but not his enemies.-----Wherever he goes, Dole attracts his own crowd of Republican "paparazzi" -- men, women and youngsters who strive to snap photos of him as
12158 if he was a visiting movie star.And he is a willing participant in these picture-taking sessions with crowds pressing the ropes at his appearances.He even sometimes offers one of those cardboard throwaway cameras to those who lack their own, as he did in Shelby, where dozens of fans waited to
12158 shake his hand and get a photo."We'll just take the picture and give you the camera," he told an elderly couple. "We've got plenty of those."</

12160 South Carolina's unemployment rate declined slightly to 5.9 percent in August from 6 percent in July, the state Employment Security Commission said Wednesday.The state added 5,600 jobs during the month, putting total nonfarm employment at 1.68 million.Government posted the largest gain, 2,200 jobs, as schools and colleges began preparing for
12160 the fall term. Trade increased by 1,600 jobs and services gained 1,100. Transporation and public utilities added 500 jobs while finance, insurance and real estate gained 300. Construction lost 100 jobs and was the only major sector to report a decrease."We expect little change in the economy over the next
12160 few months," said commission Executive Director Robert David. "State and local schools will pick up jobs as restaffing continues but tourist-related losses in trade and services will likely keep the jobless rate at round 6 percent."Beaufort County had the state's lowest unemployment rate for August, 3 percent, while Marlboro County
12160 had the highest, 16.3 percent.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</

12172 Massachusetts Treasurer Joe Malone will urge legislators to adopt a bill requiring the state's two pension funds to divest their tobacco holdings, a spokesman said Wednesday.The state's public employee pension funds, with $16.1 billion in assets, had $188 million in holdings of tobacco stocks as of June 30, Malone's spokesman
12172 Eric Fehrnstrom said. The two largest tobacco holdings were in Philip Morris Co and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. Malone had been neutral on the issue allowing his fund managers to hold and buy tobacco stocks to achieve the funds' goals of "investing for the benefit of the retirees," said the
12172 treasurer's spokesman Eric Fehrnstrom.But Fehrnstrom said Malone, a Republican who has made little secret that he wants to run for governor, changed his mind when a study by Boston Capital found that based on five- and 10-year results the state would lose little in the way of returns if it
12172 chose to divest the holdings. Democrat Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, who also is being touted as a gubernatorial candidate, is one of 14 state attorneys general suing the tobacco companies seeking to recover health care costs.The Massachusetts Legislature enacted a law before its final session in July requiring tobacco companies
12172 to list the ingredients of each brand. The industry, lead by Philip Morris, subsequently filed suit against the state seeking the block the measure. The Democrat-controlled Legislature also overrode incumbent Republican Gov. William Weld's veto of a bill to impose a 25-cents-a-pack tax on cigarettes to cover healthcare costs for
12172 the state's 160,000 uninsured children.Fehrnstrom said Malone's change of heart came about after he tried unsuccessfully to influence the tobacco companies at spring shareholders meetings and wrote urging them to restrict "their most objectionable practices...They never even responded to our letters."Malone is urging the Legislature, which is meeting informally between
12172 now and January, to pass a bill that would require the pension funds to divest tobacco holdings."The measure would not set any new precedents," Ferhnstrom said."We've had legislation that has limited investment in South Africa and in Northern Ireland."</

12178 The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday painted an optimistic picture of inflation developments in countries around the world but stressed the need for continued vigilance against price pressures."Inflation rates in industrial countries, as well as in a number of developing countries, have declined to their lowest levels in decades," the
12178 Fund said in its semi-annual "World Economic Outlook."The report said that in a number of industrial countries, inflation rates are "close to, or approaching, reasonable price stability."However, the IMF cautioned, "Monetary authorities will, of course, need to remain vigilant to incipient price pressures as growth continues or strengthens.""With appropriately designed
12178 monetary and fiscal policies, it should be possible to keep inflation low and to reduce it further over time, while minimizing undesirable short-term fluctuations in output," the IMF said. On the subject of working toward price stability while minimizing adverse consequences for economic output, the IMF report made reference to
12178 a monetary policy approach called "opportunistic disinflation," which was outlined in a recent study by two Federal Reserve Board economists. The approach takes advantage of recessions to achieve gains against inflation."The U.S. Federal Reserve in particular has emphasized the importance of preventing inflation from rising significantly during economic expansions while
12178 taking advantage of economic slowdowns to bring inflation down," the IMF said.Looking at the reasons for the favorable inflation developments, the Fund gave credit to central banks and governments for their determination to bring prices under control."Despite initial hesitation and policy mistakes, governments and central banks have applied the hard-learned
12178 lessons from the high inflation decades of the 1970s and 1980s with increasing success," the Fund said.The IMF also said increased openness to trade has also played a role in tempering inflation. While emphasizing the importance of working toward price stability, the report suggested that a zero inflation rate may
12178 not be an optimal target for central banks.It pointed out that perceived upward baises in the inflation gauges of many countries could mean that they might run the risk of deflation if they were to target zero inflation.The report also highlighted the difficulty of engineering negative real short-term interest rates,
12178 if needed in times of recession, when inflation is zero.On the other hand, the Fund pointed to benefits for growth from low inflation, saying, "The evidence is strongly indicative of a negative relationship between inflation and long-term growth, even at moderates rates of inflation of 10 to 30 percent.""High rates
12178 of inflation are clearly harmful to growth," the Fund said.</

12221 a massive investigation into a suspected corruption network of up to 50 managers, including airport staff and 20 contractors.Experts say corruption has always played a quiet role in German business, but the stakes have risen dramatically, especially in the battle for major public service contracts.While a fur coat or expensive
12221 dinner might have bought success in a public bid in the 1970s, prosecutors say some government officials are now demanding cash payments of thousands or even millions of marks (dollars) just for information.Reliable figures are hard to find, but prosecutors estimate the annual cost of corruption in the public building
12221 sector alone at 5 billion to 10 billion marks ($3.3 billion to $6.6 billion) -- a figure which gives the cash-strapped government an added incentive for a clampdown.In the state of Hesse, which includes the business capital of Frankfurt, systematic bribery costs the state finances between 120 million marks ($79
12221 million) and 170 million marks ($113 million) a year."Compared with France or Italy, for example, the situation is fairly limited. But that doesn't change the fact that the level of corruption here -- for our society and with our legal system -- is dramatic and emotionally unacceptable," said Frankfurt senior
12221 public prosecutor Wolfgang Schaupensteiner.Schaupensteiner heads a nine-year-old specialist corruption task force -- Germany's first ever -- and says he is deluged with work. His division has probed 1,700 corruption cases to date and brought around 340 to court."We have over 300 cases pending," he said in an interview. "Every time
12221 one of our investigators clears up one case, it leads to dozens more, like an avalanche. 12221 bribery," he said.The Frankfurt airport case alone, where losses on overpriced contracts and payments for non-existent deliveries are estimated at tens of millions of marks (dollars), is so much broader than it seemed at first that investigations will drag on at least until 1998, Schaupensteiner said.The scandals, continually highlighted in
12221 the media, have exploded Germany's belief that its public servants and business executives were above the kind of wheeling and dealing more associated with their more chaotic Mediterranean neighbours."Controls must be sharpened if the state is not to suffer lasting damage ... But the roots are in society's moral code
12221 ... If it is viewed as chic to bribe here and cheat a bit there, a corruption-free society remains a dream," the Berliner Morgenpost newspaper said in a recent editorial.The German cabinet in June approved a draft corruption law making price-fixing deals between firms bidding for contracts a criminal offence
12221 punishable with up to five years' prison.The proposals also raise the penalty for bribery in business to five years from one year and impose a maximum 10 years for giving or accepting bribes in the public service sector. Prosecutors welcome what they say is overdue action from Bonn but say
12221 the government should take a tougher line.Prosecutors and other justice officials have also called for reduced sentences for individuals who inform on a corruption ring, an almost unheard of occurrence at present because of the danger of prosecution."Principles like free competition are also at stake here, not just state funds.
12221 We have to stop corporate crime and corruption from gaining a stronger foothold here," said Schaupensteiner.</

12236 Hot Bird," she told an industry conference. But she added:"We can't go ahead because the law is the law...We cannot create. We are at the maximum."Renting a transponder on the Hot Bird 2 satellite, which becomes operational in early December, costs 7.5 billion lire ($5 million) a year for a
12236 12-year contract.One transponder could offer six to eight channels.The new satellite will enable broadcasters to offer dozens of new channels via sophisticated digital technology. Analysts believe the Italian satellite market, a relative infant compared with other European countries, is ripe for growth.Under the draft legislation, which Mediaset has hotly contested,
12236 the group would be required to transfer one of its three terrestrial stations to satellite because of provisions setting a ceiling of 30 percent in any one TV market.The government estimates that Mediaset has 36 percent of the terrestrial television market.Wade said that transferring an advertising-supported free station to satellite
12236 would not be economically viable.Mediaset would run into problems with programme rights -- it only has terrestrial rights for its movies -- and would face stiff competition from Italian pay-TV specialist, Telepiu."I don't know...whether we could keep it (the channel)," Wade said. "It would be a condemned channel."Media analysts said
12236 investors were undeterred by the regulatory uncertainty. 12236 organiser.Analysts judge cable technology too expensive to take off in Italy as it has done in the United States or Britain, but reckon satellite has good prospects and investors will take the risk."Italians watch a lot of television and they don't spend a lot of money on pay-TV," said Brian
12236 Sturgess, global media strategist at ING Barings in London.He said the Italian market looked somewhat like Britain's before Rupert Murdoch launched his BSkyB satellite group. 12237 reactors operating in eight of the EU's 15 member states, generating one third of the bloc's electricity and making it the world's leading producer.However, "to maintain the useful role of nuclear energy in the future" some common EU principles have to be followed, the Commission said.The Commission adopted at its
12237 weekly meeting a draft "Illustrative Nuclear Programme", assessing the different features of EU nuclear energy and identifying its challenges.The Commission said the use of nuclear energy had a favourable impact on the security of supply, qualified jobs, fuel imports and reductions of carbon dioxide emissions.Nuclear energy helped to reduce fossil
12237 fuel consumption and the subsequent reduced demand on the international oil market had made a contribution towards "moderating" oil prices."On the other hand, there are questions related to the concerns on safety, transport, management of waste, decommissioning and non-prolifiration," the Commission said.Further technological development and increased international cooperation was needed,
12237 it said.The Commission programme did not state production targets, giving priority to the free functioning of the market.Among the suggested principles, the Commission said each member state had the right to decide whether to develop the peaceful use of nuclear energy.In addition, member states need "to ensure a high degree
12237 of nuclear safety, respect non-proliferation requirements as provided for in relevant international agreements as well as high level of human health production."The Association of the European Nuclear Industry Forums (FORATOM) welcomed the programme, saying the EU must rely on non-fossil fuel electricity generation if it is to meet its international
12237 commitments to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases."The realistic economic solution is more reliance on nuclear energy," FORATOM said in a statement.However, it said the industry acknowledged the challenges it faced. 12240 the victors in the war."We are pleased that a large number of member states are in favour of a permanent seat for Germany on the Security Council," Kinkel said. "This, the principal guardian of world peace, still bears the countenance of the year 1945 but it now needs a new

12240 Council.Kinkel said the United Nations, in a financial crisis that threatens it with bankruptcy, would have to find still more savings. 12248 A lovingly restored DC-3 Dakota which crashed into the sea off the Dutch coast on Wednesday first took to the skies more than half a century ago.Eleven thousand of the planes were built between 1935 and 1948 and around 1,000 of them are believed to be still flying with air
12248 forces, commercially or for fun.The plane involved in Wednesday's crash was operated by a band of aviation enthusiasts known as the Dutch Dakota Association (DDA) which bought it in 1983 for 300,000 guilders ($160,000) and restored it to its former glory.As well as air show displays, it was used for
12248 pleasure flights for DDA members and sponsors, regularly carrying up to 32 passengers and six crew.Made by the Douglas Aircraft Corporation, Dakotas were traditionally equipped with two 1,200-horsepower Pratt and Whitney propeller engines which gave them a cruising speed of about 200 km per hour (125 mph).The Dakota dominated the
12248 skies in the 1930s and 1940s, ferrying supplies during the Normandy landings in France in 1944 and the Berlin airlift of 1948. The ubiquitous plane was the mainstay of passenger fleets but it was far from luxurious.Compared to modern aircraft it was noisy, slow, and unpressurised -- passengers had to
12248 wear breathing apparatus to fly over mountains. Journeys of any distance would take days rather than hours, although this was quicker than the sea journey of weeks.The Dakota became the workhorse for cargo and passengers in every corner of the globe.Its name, experts say, derives from a shortening of the
12248 plane's original title the Douglas Aircraft Corporation Transport Aircraft (DACoTA). This was soon corrupted to Dakota, after the U.S. state, by pilots of Britain's Royal Air Force.The Dutch national airline KLM has fond memories of the earlier DC-2 version of the Dakota -- it won the historic London to Melbourne
12248 race in 1934 with one.The usual Dakota interior has eight closely spaced bench seats on each side, next to square windows. They can be folded against the windows to allow room for cargo.British entrepreneur Richard Branson, head of Virgin Atlantic Airways, has used them for pleasure flights in Florida.In 1993
12248 six Dakotas from Britain's Marine Pollution Control Unit were used to spray dispersant on an oil slick from a stricken tanker in the Shetland Islands.</

12314 The sorry saga of the French state bank Credit Lyonnais reads like the script of a movie that could well have been made by the Hollywood studios which it owned in its heyday.News that the government is coming to its financial rescue for the third year in a row is
12314 undoubtedly a relief -- but also humbling for a bank nationalised by President Charles de Gaulle to underpin French economic recovery after World War Two.In the space of five years, the bank has fallen with a thud from the dizzy heights of 1980s and turned in losses in the tens
12314 of billions of francs. Politicians and technocrats fought over who to blame and, to crown it, the Paris headquarters burnt down.Things went badly awry in the 1990s when many of the huge investments, acquisitions and loans that made it the biggest bank outside Japan turned sour.The bill was a staggering
12314 loss of 21 billion francs ($4.1 billion) between 1992 and 1994, the forced exit of the former chairman Jean-Yves Haberer and the start of several, highly costly and complicated government attempts to put the bank back on its feet.Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has also asked for an inquiry to establish
12314 who precisely was to blame and whether company law should be revised to enlarge on legal liability for company accounts.Some also see the inquiry as a clever political manoeuvre to pursue Haberer, who was appointed in 1988 under late Socialist President Francois Mitterrand, at a time when the current centre-right
12314 ruling coalition is mired in a series of probes into political party funding and housing scandals.One of the debacles that pushed Credit Lyonnais to the brink of ruin was a $1.0 billion loan to Italian businessmen Giancarlo Paretti and Florio Fiorini to buy the Metro Goldwyn Mayer film studios.The bank
12314 inherited the studios after they went bankrupt and now been sold off under a divestment programme which is part of a government rescue package put into action last year.That package was the second in two years but a third rescue is now under preparation because the complex financing of the
12314 1995 rescue plan that was supposed to help the bank is actually draining money away from it.This year alone the bank is expected to lose three billion francs on a shortfall between the interest payments it gets from a separate holding company which is selling off its assets and the
12314 interest rates it is paying on the money it lent to the holding company to carry out the sell-off programme.An emergency government aid of 3.9 billion francs passed the hurdle of European Commission approval on Wednesday and is designed to alleviate the pain while the French finance ministry works on
12314 what will undoubtedly by a far more costly cure.The EU authorities put an estimate of 45 billion francs on the cost of the 1995 rescue alone and details of the third plan have yet to emerge.If the film-makers are interested, there are plenty of other spicy bits for a movie.The
12314 bank's 19th century headquarters, whose architect drew inspiration from the Louvre museum, was gutted in May.And another of its most celebrated clients is himself in the movies. 12322 Germany's stock market is not as well prepared for global competition as its bond market and banks should help by selling shareholdings, a top Bundesbank official said on Wednesday.Risk aversion is not the only cause of German reluctance to invest in shares, Johann Wilhelm Gaddum, deputy president of Germany's central
12322 bank, said in the text of a speech due to be delivered at a stock market conference in Bonn.An inadequate supply of attractive shares was the main cause, and banks were partly to blame because they were withholding shares from the market."Despite historic price highs on the stock exchange and
12322 successful share launches by various companies the mood appears to be depressed because all measures taken so far do not appear to have given the German stock market the big breakthrough."Banks have been accused of wielding too much power through their large stakes in industrial companies. Forthcoming stock market legislation
12322 is widely expected to avoid rigorous measures like slapping a limit on banks' shareholdings.Gaddum said that even though lawmakers, market organisers and major players had done much to prepare the share market for global competition, it still lacked breadth and depth.The stock market could become more attractive if there were
12322 more joint stock companies and if existing share stakes were more widely distributed, he said."It would be desirable if banks took suitable companies public more often than they have done in the past...," Gaddum said. "This would partly deflate the recurring debate about banking power and would also contribute to
12322 strengthening and reviving the German stock market."The lack of shares explained why trade concentrated on relatively few liquid stocks and why the share prices of medium-sized businesses often made large price swings.A successful stock market launch of state telephone company Deutsche Telekom in November, Germany's biggest ever flotation, would help
12322 boost share ownership, Gaddum said.But he had praise for the German system of universal banks, saying the tradition of close ties between banks and industrial companies had proved an important stabilising factor in Germany's corporate scene.In addition, banks sometimes had good reason for buying and holding on to industrial share
12322 stakes, Gaddum said.He also called on the government to remove differences in taxation which put partnerships and single-person companies at an advantage over incorporated firms and thereby hampered the formation of joint stock companies.The bond market, meanwhile, was in shape for the challenge posed by European Monetary Union in 1999,
12322 when German markets would lose their main attraction the mark, Gaddum said.Following the government's decision to issue limited volumes of short-term paper each quarter as well 30-year debt each year if possible, the market would have an adequate supply of paper across the maturity spectrum.That would enable it to compete
12322 for investors' capital after monetary union when the absence of separate currencies will focus investors' interest on a nation's creditworthiness and debt management, Gaddum said.He also said it was in Germany's interest to convert existing government debt into Euros from the start of the planned 1999 launch of the single
12322 currency.Such a move would secure sufficient market liquidity for bonds and prevent a split in the market which would lead to a loss of liquidity and competitiveness, Gaddum said.Germany has yet to decide when to transform its existing bonds into Euros.</

12325 The European Union must not scrap the cumulative limit for pesticides in water when it revises the 1980 drinking water directive, the European Parliament's environment committee will say next month.A European Commission proposal to revise the directive -- COM(94)612 -- retains the existing limit of 0.1 microgrammes of pesticide per
12325 litre for individual pesticides but scraps the 0.5 microgrammes per litre cumulative total.But the parliament's environment committee is set on October 30 to approve a report which insists the cumulative ceiling must be reinstated.The draft report, prepared by British Socialist Ken Collins, insists the EU must not relax its pressure
12325 on the member states to clean up their water supplies, especially in the light of their dismal record of compliance with the existing directive.Collins cites European Environmental Agency figures showing that pesticide limits in drinking water have been exceeded on 75 percent of the EU's arable land, and that nitrates
12325 have increased in more than 66 percent of the EU's rivers and most of its lakes.One of the Commission's main proposals for improving drinking water quality is an 80 percent cut in the permitted lead content, mostly from replacing lead pipes and fittings.The Commission estimates this could cost the member
12325 states more than 50 billion Ecus. Collins suggests money should be made available from the Structural Funds for certain regions to help them foot the bill.But they should have 10 years to bring their water up to scratch, Collins says, not 15 as proposed by the Commission.Unlike the Commission, Collins
12325 does not believe governments should be able to force householders to replace lead pipes on their property.Instead, he thinks they should report to the Commission "on the incidence of lead piping in households and come forward within five years with a plan to replace the lead piping in these homes".The

12334 Germany is keen to resolve the financial problems of the world's poorest nations, but remains adamant that sales of International Monetary Fund gold are not the right way to fund debt relief, Bonn said on Wednesday.German Finance minister Theo Waigel said in a statement released ahead of the meeting, "The
12334 federal government continues to reject a sale of IMF gold." A senior official told a briefing in Bonn in advance of international meetings to be held in Washington later this week that Germany remained convinced that there were favourable alternatives to halp provide debt relief to the poor."We do not
12334 need to activate the IMF's gold resources to resolve the problems of a very limited number of countries," the official said.Germany and a small number of other countries have joined forces to block a plan to sell a small amount of IMF gold to fund additional aid to a group
12334 of up to 20 very poor nations.Their action, motivated by concern that such sales could set a bad precedent, has caused some irritation to other leading industrial countries, particularly the United States.The U.S., along with other supporters of the gold sale plan, sees the proposal as a tidy way of
12334 providing relief to poor countries without tapping domestic budgets.But the Bonn source said that the whole discussion about gold sales -- which he said had been proposed to stop a relatively small funding gap of about 1.1 billion dollars -- had been blown out of proportion."This whole argument is really
12334 about a completely different issue," the official said. "It has become a sort of status symbol whether the sales take place or not. But the decisive thing is to agree an initiative to help the poorest countries."Germany is proposing direct debt forgiveness for poor countries from their creditors as a
12334 means to make sure the nations concerned do not collapse under their debt burdens.The senior source said that Germany was prepared to raise the level of debt forgiveness offered to such weak nations to 80 percent, compared with the current maximum of 67 percent, providing a decision was made on
12334 a case-by-case basis and the other conditions attached to the deal were appropriate."Germany is prepared to agree that the debt forgiveness level of 67 percent could be raised to 80 percent in the cases of individual countries and if all other conditions are in place," the source said.He made clear
12334 that Bonn would not agree to the 90 percent forgiveness level sought by the IMF and said that even this level was unacceptable to some countries in the Group of Seven rich nations, which will meet in Washington next week."Only 80 percent, not more," he said, adding "There is no
12334 consensus for 80 percent in the G7. At least one country has great problems with going above that."But despite the diametrically opposed views on the gold sale plans, the source said he did not expect open conflict to break out in this month's Washington talks.Referring to a row which broke
12334 out two years ago at a meeting in Madrid -- when rich and poor nations hit deadlock on a plan to issue more of the IMF's own currency, the Special Drawing Right -- the official said, "I assume one will want to avoid a situation like 1994."Instead, the various committees
12334 were likely to confine their comments to welcoming the IMF's recently-announced decision to step up aid for the world's poorest nations.The statement from IMF managing director Michel Camdessus this week pledged more aid for poor nations but neatly side-stepped the issue of how this would be offered.</

12337 European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy on Wednesday sought to downplay a debate over which monetary strategy should be adopted for the single European currency, saying the systems could be combined.Lamfalussy said the systems most widely discussed -- monetary targeting favoured by the Bundesbank and directly targeting inflation favoured by
12337 the Bank of England -- were more similar than different and that both seek price stability.The German central bank has been pushing for the future European Central Bank to adopt a monetary strategy, which reviews money supply to monitor inflation, while the British central bank has pushed for its inflation
12337 system to be adopted."It should be pointed out that similarities between the behaviour of central banks which pursue these two strategies seem to be greater than the differences, in general, and that the combination of these strategies might not be impossible," Lamfalussy said in the text of a speech.An advance
12337 text of the speech by Lamfalussy to a banking group in Duesseldorf was made available under embargo.Lamfalussy said central banks applying inflation targeting include monetary aggregates among their indicators while the Bundesbank, which applies monetary targeting, does not react to movements in monetary aggregrates "in a mechanical way."The choice of
12337 which system to use is left open in the Maastricht Treaty, which provides the guidelines to implement currency union in January 1999. The decision must be finalised shortly before the start of the currency union.Lamfalussy said research shows the monetary targeting system could be feasible because money demand at the
12337 level of the European Union is fairly stable and M3 money supply, a general measure of funds in circulation, is controllable.He also said directly targeting inflation "could be particularly useful" if money demand was unstable due to financial innovations in the run-up to currency union or after the new currency,
12337 to be called the Euro, is introduced.Lamfalussy said convergence among central banks in the use of monetary policy instruments was "well under way," noting the use of open market operations and security repurchase funds.In addition, Lamfalussy said "a certain convergence" was evident in required reserves and standing facilities and that
12337 there was "broad consensus on the main lines of the operational framework of the future single monetary policy".--John Gilardi, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525</

12347 four-day-old offensive against the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE)."According to estimates made by ground troops, over 75 terrorists were killed on Tuesday and more than 100 wounded," he told a news conference.The Defence Ministry said more than 330 rebels were either killed or wounded on Sunday and Monday
12347 in fighting near the town of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.The army lost 58 soldiers and had 115 wounded near Kilinochchi since Sunday when they launched the offensive after more than a month's lull in the conflict.The LTTE, seeking an independent homeland
12347 for minority Tamils, on Wednesday killed 15 more soldiers in an attack in the army-controlled northern Jaffna Peninsula, north of Kilinochchi, a ministry statement said."In Jaffna, terrorists activated a claymore mine against a vehicle carrying security forces personnel. 12347 said.Defence analysts said the rebels could launch more attacks in army-controlled areas to divert attention from fighting near their stronghold.Military officials earlier said security forces had renewed air and artillery strikes near Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo, in a bid to break through guerrilla resistance.Munasinghe said two
12347 columns of troops were advancing from the road junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, in a pincer-shape offensive.One column of troops was now five km (three miles) southeast of Paranthan while on the other flank, troops had advanced seven km (four miles) southwest of the
12347 town, he said.Several army divisions were taking part in the assault, and the rebels were resisting mainly with mortars, he said.Analysts said government troops were trying a pincer move to outflank the rebels, who were well dug in at Kilinochchi.The Voice of Tigers radio, mouthpiece of the LTTE, reported heavy

12350 attacking Kabul from the east, south and southwest, the sources said.The Islamic rebels made a lightning thrust up the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway after capturing the strategic town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, overnight.No independent account of the fighting was immediately available.The latest Taleban advances followed a series
12350 of spectacular gains in eastern Afghanistan this month and put the survival of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government in doubt.Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, who rejoined the government in May under a peace deal with Rabbani, has since lost virtually all the territory previously controlled by his Hezb-i-Islami faction, including Sarobi.The government,
12350 hemmed in by the latest Taleban advances, turned to opposition militia commander General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls Kabul's last supply route to the north.An Islamabad-based official of Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli faction said Interior Minister Yunus Qanuni was holding talks with Dostum in Uzbekistan's capital Tashkent on Wednesday.He said Dostum had

12350 been taken over completely," one source said. 12350 of supporting the Taleban. 12353 The Afghan Taleban militia captured the strategic government-held town of Sarobi east of Kabul overnight and thrust north towards a government airbase.Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami faction, which had controlled Sarobi, confirmed that the Taleban had seized the town, 70 km (44 miles) east of the Afghan capital."Sarobi has fallen
12353 and Hezb-i-Islami fighters blew up an ammunition dump and some vehicles as they retreated," said a Hezb-i-Islami source in the Pakistani city of Peshawar.The Taleban seized Sarobi at about midnight (1900 GMT Tuesday) in a two-pronged assault after resistance died away, Taleban sources in Pakistan said.They said the militia had
12353 also taken the nearby Naghlu Dam and hydro-electric plant that began supplying power to parts of Kabul only 10 days ago after a break of two and a half years.The capture of the town was the latest in a series of spectacular Taleban gains in eastern Afghanistan this month and
12353 a big setback to President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government.It was another blow to Hekmatyar, who has now lost virtually all the territory previously controlled by Hezb-i-Islami.Taleban sources said the Islamic rebels were now advancing northwards from Naghlu up the Tagab Valley that leads to the main government airbase at Bagram, 50
12353 km (31 miles) north of Kabul, backed by hundreds of fresh troops from Jalalabad."Sarobi has been taken over completely," a Taleban source in the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar said. "Now, inshallah (God willing), we will reach Kabul."Retreating government forces left behind many dead fighters and large quantities of weapons,
12353 the Taleban source said.The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Taleban sources as saying the government had lost hundreds of dead in and around Sarobi, while 105 had been captured. At least 14 Taleban fighters had been killed and 25 wounded.Taleban sources said their forces had advanced on Sarobi northwards
12353 from Hisarak district in the adjoining Nangarhar province, and westwards along the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway.Resistance had subsided by sunset on Tuesday while mopping up operations were completed by midnight, Taleban sources said.Kabul radio, monitored in Islamabad, said government forces had killed 100 rebels and destroyed many military vehicles in Tuesday's
12353 battle for Sarobi, but did not report Taleban gains.On Tuesday, the government-run radio said rockets fired by the Taleban killed three civilians and wounded nine in Kabul.Taleban sources said a government jet dropped cluster bombs near Jalalabad airport on Tuesday, but caused no damage.The Islamic rebels have tightened their grip
12353 on eastern provinces this month as part of a drive to seize Kabul, oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.A Taleban transport plane landed at Bagram on Tuesday, but there were conflicting accounts of the incident.Kabul radio said the Russian-made Antonov-32 plane carrying 33 Taleban and seven
12353 Pakistani military men had been hijacked by a "brave mujahid (struggler)" on a flight between the Taleban-held cities of Herat and Kandahar.Taleban sources confirmed that the plane had landed in Bagram, but said the pilot had defected. They denied any Pakistanis had been on board the aircraft.Pakistan also denied the
12353 report. "This is absolutely untrue. There are no Pakistani military personnel engaged in fighting anywhere in Afghanistan," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.The Afghan government has often accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban. Islamabad denies the charge.</

12365 The Afghan Taleban militia battled to the eastern edge of Kabul on Wednesday and a top United Nations official said they could be on the verge of seizing the city.The Afghan government called for a special meeting of the U.N. Security Council, accusing Pakistan of backing the Taleban.Taleban sources said
12365 the rebels had captured Pul-i-Charki village on the outskirts of the city, as well as the military academy, threatening the survival of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government.Government sources in Kabul confirmed the Taleban were at the gates of the city and that the strategic town of Sarobi, east of the capital,
12365 had fallen. But they said the rebel advance on Kabul had been repulsed.The Taleban said fighting had moved on to the customs house area, only five km (three miles) from the city.U.N. Under-Secretary General Marrack Goulding, in touch with U.N. officials in the Afghan capital, said he hoped the Security
12365 Council would endorse an appeal for a ceasefire and negotiations on Wednesday." "We are getting indications ... that Kabul may be on the point of falling," he told reporters in New York.He said there had been signs that government troops were defecting or refusing to fight in the face of
12365 the Taleban attacks, both in Kabul and other cities.Rebel sources said government jets were bombing the Taleban, who were attacking Kabul from the east, south and southwest.U.N. staff in Kabul said there were chaotic scenes in the city with tanks and military vehicles on the move as the Taleban forces
12365 advanced. They had no word on casualties.The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) prepared to send two planes to Kabul on Thursday to evacuate foreigners wanting to leave, an ICRC official in Pakistan said.Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar called on troops loyal to Rabbani to stop fighting because their
12365 leader was "preparing to flee", Omar's spokesman Wakil Ahmed said from Taleban headquarters in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar. Omar offered an amnesty to anyone who joined the Taleban.The Taleban, who emerged from the obscurity of religious schools in Pakistan two years ago, have been fighting to oust Rabbani
12365 and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.The Afghan government has often accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban. Islamabad denies the charge.Omar said the Taleban had no ethnic or regional prejudices and only wanted to enforce Islamic sharia (law).The Islamic rebels thrust rapidly up the main highway to the capital
12365 through the precipitous Kabul gorge after seizing the key town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, in the night.U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl urged factions battling for Kabul to stop fighting and avert civilian casualties."My message is: spare the lives of the innocent civilians who have already suffered
12365 enough from years of useless bloodshed," said Holl in a statement issued in Islamabad.He appealed to all factions to observe an immediate ceasefire and start talks on a lasting settlement.Holl urged "those countries with influence in Afghanistan to persuade the warring parties to abandon the course of war and cooperate
12365 with the United Nations" in the search for peace.But the Taleban appeared determined to keep up their military momentum and seize the prize of Kabul, following their spectacular gains in eastern Afghanistan this month.The demand for an extraordinary session of the Security Council was made in a statement issued by
12365 the Afghan Foreign Ministry, official Kabul Radio, monitored in Islamabad, said. The government, hemmed in by the Taleban, turned to opposition militia commander General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls Kabul's last supply route to the north.An Islamabad-based official of Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli faction said Interior Minister Yunus Qanuni was holding talks
12365 with Dostum in Uzbekistan's capital Tashkent on Wednesday. Dostum is in Tahkent for medical treatment.Dostum is a foe of Rabbani, but is despised by the Taleban for his communist past. Last month he reopened the Salang highway linking Kabul to the north under an informal truce.</
