12367 The Indian government on Wednesday announced the first round of public asset sales for the year 1996-97 (April/March) as a step to bring its fiscal deficit to a targeted five percent of gross domestic product.India said it will sell a seven percent stake in its external telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar
12367 Nigam Ltd and five percent in its crude oil refining company Indian Oil Corporation.The joint sale is expected to earn India around 15 billion rupees. The government is keen to raise at least 50 billion rupees before the current financial year ends in March 1997.A government spokesman announced the plan
12367 to sell partial stakes in the two firms following a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.Currently the government has an 82 percent stake in VSNL, the state-run agency which controls overseas telecommunications services in India.The government has a 95 percent stake in IOC.The spokesman said the shares could
12367 be sold in both domestic and overseas markets.The spokesman said the exact prices of the two firms will be decided in consultations with merchant bankers to be appointed by the firms.Analysts in India expect VSNL's share to be priced at around 1,350 rupees while IOC is expected to be offered
12367 at 750 rupees. The exat date for sale for shares is yet to be decided.The government expects to raise another 35 billion rupees in two more tranches of sale of shares. These divestments will be done on the basis of recommendations made by a special panel appointed recently.The panel is
12367 expected to examine about 240 state companies involved in various sectors including oil, telecommunication, steel, engineering and chemicals before before it recommends sale offers.The government had targeted the sale of state shares as an important way to raise money for various items of expenditure as part of its economic reforms
12367 initiated in 1991.However, depressed market conditions triggered mainly by poor money supply have often been an obstacle for smooth sale of shares in the past offers.India could raise only around 3.6 billion rupees by sale of state shares in 1995-96 (April/March) against a projected 70 billion. India ended 1995-96 with
12367 an estimated fiscal deficit of 5.9 percent of is GDP.--Arindam Nag, New Delhi newsroom +91-11-301 2024</

12370 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday announced relaxations in the norms for investments in unlisted Indian firms by expatriate Indians and overseas corporate bodies. The relaxations in the norms announced by the RBI are:*Further liberalisation in the present scheme for 100 percent investments in loss-making units by expatriate
12370 Indians.*General permission would be granted for interest-free non-repatriable loans from expatriate relatives for personal purposes and for business activities. Interest-free repatriable loans up to $250,000 would be cleared by the RBI automatically. Other cases would continue to be cleared by the RBI on a case by case basis.*RBI will permit
12370 the transfer of funds from one non-resident (external) (NRE) account to the NRE account of another person.*Expatriate Indians/overseas corporate bodies shall be permitted to establish schools and colleges on the same terms and conditions as a resident individual/corporate body.*The existing 40 percent scheme will be abolished and investment by expatriate
12370 Indians/overseas corporate bodies will be allowed in unlisted companies up to 51 percent on a repatriation basis.*Participation by expatriate Indians in venture capital activity will be permitted on the same terms and conditions as foreign investment in this area.*Housing finance companies will be permitted to grant loans to expatriate Indians
12370 for acquisition/improvement to the existing houses on the same terms and conditions as applicable to residents.The RBI said detailed instructions would be issued shortly.-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000</

12381 An unusually dangerous strain of tropical dengue fever has killed 19 people in the Indian capital since the middle of last month, a doctor said on Wednesday.Dr D.C. 12392 India must speed up the deregulation of its economy and use the proceeds from sales of stakes in public firms to retire its massive debt burden, Lehman Brothers vice-chairman Howard Clark said on Wednesday."Lehman's experience with privatisation and disinvestment in other emerging economies has convinced me that disinvesment is a
12392 powerful prescription for improving the economy and creating a positive environment for private sector business," Clark said.Clark, leading a delegation of U.S. businessmen to India to meet officials of the Federal government that took power in June, said the relatively slow pace of disinvestment was preventing increased foreign investment flows.The
12392 United States, which invested an estimated $192.4 million in India in 1995/96 (April/March) according to India's central bank, is the largest foreign investor in India.Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda recently set the country a target of attracting $10 billion of foreign direct investment each year. The bulk of this
12392 is needed to shore up the crumbling infrastructure sector, crucial to the success of a reform programme started in 1991."Debt service absorbs over 40 percent of every dollar," Clark said. "This makes it hard for India to fund the education, social services and infrastructure needed to facilitate rapid development."Many of
12392 India's state-owned enterprises are inefficient and overstaffed, and a drain on state finances, Clark said. Even enterprises in the black yield only a fraction of the potential return on investment, compared with private sector firms in the same sectors."The solution is clear. The government must sell off these companies and
12392 use the proceeds to retire debt," Clark said.India plans to raise 50 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) through the sale of partial stakes in state-owned units.Another member of the delegation, Tommy Thompson, vice-president of Texas-based Coastal Power Co, said it would be easy for India to generate its entire $10
12392 billion foreign direct investment target from American firms alone."American companies are ready and willing and eager to bring these investments into India and meet the target," he said.But delegation members said the country would have to allay some of the foreign investors' fears."India must make it clear that foreign investment
12392 is welcome without restrictions and limitations," said Richard Johannessen, president of Ingersoll-Rand Asia Pacific."It must have a meaningful intellectual property rights law to attract more foreign investment."U.S. firms seeking to invest in India's infrastructure sector want to put their money in housing rather than ports, roads, power or telecommunications sectors
12392 where the Indian government would prefer direct investment, delegates said.David Wolf, president of the Fremont Group, said he believed U.S. firms would invest $1 billion in India annually if the laws were changed to allow them to venture into the housing sector."There is a tremendous shortage of good quality housing,"
12392 Wolf said. "The firms could bring in low-cost modern techniques to build homes that are energy-efficient and material-efficient. Lots of ancillary companies could be set up here."-- New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024</

12403 Indian coffee exporters are cancelling forward contracts amid fears that the government might impose export controls due to a shortfall in domestic stocks, traders said on Wednesday.They said exporters were keen to cancel contracts as prices in the domestic market were expected to rise above global prices and feared that
12403 the government would clamp down on exports to ensure a steady supply in the local market in the winter months."All export contracts between September and December have been cancelled. These stocks will be made available in the domestic market," said Ashwin Shah, a leading exporter.Traders did not give details about
12403 the quantity of coffee on forward contracts being cancelled. But they said that while some exporters had already cancelled contracts, many more were in the process of doing so.India exports about 180,000 tonnes of coffeea year.Forward contracts -- agreements entered into by an exporter to export at a specified date
12403 and at a certain price -- generally contain provisions for cancellation.But if exporters cancel a forward contract, they have to pay a damage cost or penalty, Coffee Board officials said. It is not legally binding. Legal provisions are only for the payment of penalty.Coffee Board chairman Philipose Matthai said that
12403 in the event of a shortage, the government had several options including capping exports, allowing imports, and purchase of coffee by the board from growers for further sales.Shah said exporters would be able to make up the loss suffered on forward contracts since domestic rates were higher than world prices.Traders
12403 said the domestic price of coffee was about 120 rupees per kg, compared to 80 rupees in the global market.Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said last week that the government would not tolerate a speculative price rise in the doemstic market following the abolition of a quota system.He said the government
12403 would encourage imports if necessary.The government announced on September 14 that coffee growers would no longer be required to pool their output for auction by the state-run Coffee Board in domestic and export markets.It abolished a quota system that obligated growers to sell 30 percent of their output to the
12403 pool.Dealers said coffee powder prices in the retail market rose five to ten rupees per kg following the government decision.They predicted a further increase of about 15 rupees per kg by the year-end due to the stock shortfall.Dealers said prices had risen due to an anticipated shortage of coffee in
12403 the remaining three months of 1996.Growers said unseasonal rains had reduced India's projected coffee output in 1995/96 (October-September) to about 160,000 tonnes, against the Coffee Board's target of 235,000 tonnes.Coffee Board member H.B. 12424 a pattern of gradual downward adjustments, the SBP cut its rate sharply on September 10 to 36.9700/37.1549 to the dollar from 35.6200/35.7981 fixed on August 29."The devaluation should have been enough to reduce the differential between the official and unofficial dollar rates, but the market doesn't seem to agree," a
12424 Western economist said.The devaluation sparked rumours -- officially denied -- that the government might freeze foreign currency deposits to help boost its depleting foreign reserves, which stood at $2.34 billion in August against $2.82 billion in August 1995.Individuals, not trusting central bank denials, have since pulled about $200 million from
12424 forex bank accounts, bankers say."The historically sharp rise in the premium on forward dollar buying indicates that the market is not only short of dollars but has lost confidence in the rupee," Arshad said.Dealers said the erosion of the rupee, which has lost 5.31 percent of its dollar value since
12424 July 1 and 7.95 percent since January 1, had weakened the confidence of importers who are heavily buying forward dollars to hedge their positions.A foreign banker, who asked not to be named, said the market was anticipating a further loss of up to four percent in the rupee's value against

12430 Mother Teresa was released from hospital on Wednesday and taken back to her religious order after being given a clean bill of health, a doctor treating the revered Roman Catholic missionary said.Eyes closed and hands folded, the 86-year-old nun, who was taken to hospital last week after falling from a
12430 chair, was carried on a stretcher into the Missionaries of Charity order where nuns greeted her with applause, witnesses said."God bless you," Mother Teresa said to Sister Frederica, the order's second-ranking nun, as she was carried from an ambulance into the Missionaries of Charity headquarters, her home in the eastern
12430 Indian city of Calcutta.To the sound of the chapel bell, about 30 nuns surrounded Mother Teresa and sang and danced in joy before she was taken to the order's prayer room, witnesses said.Later Mother Teresa, wearing her traditional white and blue-trimmed sari, was carried to her room where she was
12430 examined by a doctor, they said.A doctor said Mother Teresa was carried on a stretcher because of longstanding back pain and not because of any lingering effects from the fall onto her head that she suffered on September 16."There is no cause for concern," said Dr A.K. Bardhan of Woodlands
12430 Nursing Home where she had undergone treatment.He said a brain scan earlier on Wednesday at nearby Belview Nursing Home showed a blood clot detected last week had disappeared."The blood clot detected in the first scan has been completely dissolved after 10 days of medication," he told reporters.Sister Priscilla, a senior
12430 nun, said Mother Teresa was resting in bed. "We are very happy. We are grateful to God that she is back," she said.The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner has spent two stints in hospital in the past month.She spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and
12430 early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.Less than two weeks after she returned to her religious order, Mother Teresa fell off a chair and hit her head.Doctors discovered a spot on her brain last week, but Bardhan said it had since dissolved.</

12432 Sri Lankan forces renewed air and artillery strikes on the rebel Tamil Tigers' northern stronghold on Wednesday in a bid to break through guerrilla resistance, military officials said.The rebel Voice of Tigers radio, mouthpiece of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), reported heavy fighting in the guerrillas' Kilinochchi base
12432 and said many civilians had been killed.But a military spokesman said the strikes were focused on identified enemy positions."We have been pounding the enemy to wipe out their resistance," he said.Defence analysts said the pre-dawn air and artillery attacks could mean the army was on the advance again after consolidating
12432 their positions in newly captured areas.The military spokesman said troops had repulsed several rebel counter-attacks on army defences overnight."Terrorists fired mortars at our forward defences last night. There were also several confrontations along our defences but we have no details of casualties yet," he said.Thousands of troops, backed by tanks,
12432 artillery and air support, have been advancing on Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo, in their first offensive in more than a month. The operation was launched on Sunday.The spokesman said the army was consolidating at Morasamoddai, a road junction just northeast of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point
12432 to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.Defence analysts said government troops were trying to outflank the rebels, who were well dug in at Kilinochchi.At least 37 soldiers were killed and 79 wounded in the first two days of the offensive, the defence ministry said.On Monday, 35 guerrillas were killed
12432 and 100 wounded after some 200 rebels were killed or wounded on Sunday, the ministry said.No casualty update was given on Tuesday.Diplomats said heavy army casualties indicated the LTTE were putting up strong resistance. The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's
12432 north and east.Military officials said they had stepped up surveillance in the Jaffna lagoon between the army-held Jaffna peninsula and the mainland, just north of Kilinochchi, to deter rebel attempts to land reinforcements by boat."Ground troops have seen LTTE boats hugging the coast," said a military officer. "They may be
12432 trying to bring up reinforcements as Kilinochchi is important for them. It is the last major town in their hands with a hospital and other infrastructure."The army has said it wants to reopen the highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through a large swathe of rebel-held territory separating Jaffna
12432 and the mainland.The military has been targeting Kilinochchi since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.</

12448 before intermediaries stop the fighting.Nov 4: Taleban capture provincial capital of Kandahar after rescuing a 30-truck convoy from local commanders. 12448 Mullah Naqib. 12448 capital of Wardak province, southwest of Kabul, from Hezb-i-Islami, then in opposition.Feb 13: Taleban capture Pul-i-Alam, capital of Logar province, from Hezb-i-Islami.Feb 14: Taleban reach gates of Kabul, capturing Hekmatyar's Charasyab base, 25 km (15 miles) south of capital.March 10: Taleban seize Karte Seh area of Kabul from Shi'ite Moslem
12448 Hezb-i-Wahdat group and its leader Abdul Ali Mazari.March 11: Government forces oust Taleban from Karte Seh.March 13: Hezb-i-Wahdat leader Abdul Ali Mazari is killed in captivity. 12448 near Iranian border.Sept 5: Taleban capture western city of Herat from government forces which had held it since 1992. They ban girls from going to school and women from working in offices.Oct 11: Taleban advance to gates of Kabul for second time, capturing Charasyab and later Rishkor and Khairabad hills.Oct
12448 14: Taleban accuse Iran of letting border be used for incursion into western Afghanistan by pro-government forces.1996:April 3: About 1,000 Moslem clergymen choose Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar as Amir-ul-Momineen (commander of the faithful), denouncing Rabbani as unfit to lead Islamic nation.June 1: Government confirms loss of Chaghcharan, capital of

12452 Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said on Wednesday its forces had captured the strategic government-held town of Sarobi east of the capital Kabul and were thrusting north towards a key government airbase.Taleban forces seized Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, at about midnight (1900 GMT Tuesday) in a two-pronged assault
12452 after resistance died away, Taleban sources in Pakistan said.There was no immediate independent confirmation that Sarobi had fallen in what would be the latest in a series of spectacular Taleban gains in eastern Afghanistan this month.It would be a major setback to the Kabul government led by President Burhanuddin Rabbani
12452 and to Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, whose Hezb-i-Islami faction had held Sarobi.Taleban sources said the Islamic rebels were now advancing northwards up the Tagab Valley that leads to the main government airbase at Bagram, 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul."Sarobi has been taken over completely," a Taleban source in
12452 the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar said. "Now, inshallah (God willing), we will reach Kabul."Retreating government forces left behind many dead fighters and large quantities of weapons, the source said.A Pakistan-based Afghan news service, Afghan Islamic Press, said about 50 government fighters were killed. There was no word on Taleban
12452 casualties.Taleban sources said their forces had advanced on Sarobi northwards from Hisarak district in the adjoining Nangarhar province, and westwards along the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway.Resistance had subsided by sunset on Tuesday while mopping up operations were completed by midnight, Taleban sources said.On Tuesday, official Kabul Radio said rockets fired by
12452 the Taleban killed three civilians and wounded nine in the capital.The radio, monitored in Islamabad, said the rockets had hit residential areas near Kabul university.Taleban sources in the eastern city of Jalalabad said a government jet had dropped cluster bombs near the city's airport, but had caused no damage or
12452 casualties.The Islamic rebel force has tightened its grip on eastern provinces this month as part of a drive to seize Kabul, oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.Kabul radio said government forces had killed 100 rebels and destroyed many military vehicles in Tuesday's battle for Sarobi.A Taleban
12452 transport plane landed at Bagram on Tuesday, but there were conflicting accounts of the incident.Kabul radio said the Russian-made Antonov-32 plane carrying 33 Taleban and seven Pakistani military men had been hijacked by a "brave mujahid (struggler)" on a flight between the Taleban-held cities of Herat and Kandahar.Taleban sources confirmed
12452 that the plane had landed in Bagram, but said the pilot had defected. They denied any Pakistanis had been on board the aircraft.Pakistan also denied the report. "This is absolutely untrue. There are no Pakistani military personnel engaged in fighting anywhere in Afghanistan," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.The Afghan government
12452 has often accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban. Islamabad denies the charge.</
12453 Thirteen-year-old Beauty had to entertain five clients each day during her two months in a Dhaka brothel before she was rescued by a women lawyers' group."They came of all ages, had different taste and demands. I had to satisfy them, to the best of my ability, to escape torture," the
12453 girl said, two days after she was housed in a shelter run by the Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association (BNWLA).The girl is part of a horrific chain of abuse and murder affecting Bangladeshi women."It's hard to believe...but it's the truth. It's the cruel reality we face," said Salma Ali, executive
12453 director of the association.The home, which can accommodate at most 30 girls even if they share beds and sleep on the floor, has been the last hope for some girls.They have little prospect of being restored to their parents, having a family or living freely."My mother has refused to take
12453 me back because her second husband would not accept me," said 10-year-old Tiya.Pinky, 14, was rescued by police and handed over to BNWLA."I managed to escape just by sheer luck. A deal was made between the man who stole me from my family and a prospective buyer for 100,000 taka
12453 ($2,500)," she said."I overheard their conversation. I was to be smuggled to India. I was preparing for a life in brothel or even worse but the BNWLA rescued me," she said.Also in the BNWLA home was Rahima, who was married in 1993. "I had almost three years of married life
12453 but suddenly my husband started to change."One day he cut off one of my hands, one leg and a ear. That was not enough for him. He tied me up and left me on a train line where someone found and brought me to this home."BNWLA trained Rahima to teach
12453 knitting to other girls at the shelter."This is an unending story of unfolding tragedies," said Salma Ali, a senior lawyer. The girls at the shelter said they loved Ali very much. "She is just mother-like, caring, highly disciplined and a good administrator," Rahima told Reuters.Ali's work continues outside the shelter.Juthi,
12453 17, does not live in the home but visits Ali almost every week, along with her sister Moyna.Juthi was rescued with BNWLA's help while she was being smuggled into India. The BNWLA is helping Moyna in her search for her son, who was picked up by a family friend one
12453 day but never seen again."We deal with a variety of cases -- trafficking, torture, rape, prostitution," Ali said.She said she was investigating reports of smuggled women and children not only being sexually abused but also killed for their body parts."If only part of the reports we have are true I
12453 can say humanity is in danger at a time when everybody talks about human rights," she said.A draft report prepared by BNWLA member Mominul Islam said confessions made by some traffickers arrested by police revealed that "corneas, kidneys and blood extracted from children" were sold at a high price, especially
12453 in India.It said Bangladeshis smuggled to India were also killed and their skeletons sold."India is the world's biggest skeleton exporter. But Indian people are mostly Hindus who are cremated; the Moslems are very sensitive and their bodies cannot be used for skeleton exports."Then the likelihood is that most of the
12453 skeletons come from people smuggled in from other countries. The traffickers are possibly the main source for supplying kidneys, blood, corneas in the Indian hospitals and clinics," the report said.A 1995 Bangladeshi law providing for the death sentence as the maximum penalty for torture, rape, trafficking and killing of women
12453 and children has also been largely ineffective, lawyers said.BNWLA said some 200,000 Bangladeshi women were smuggled to Pakistan alone over the last 10 years.Most victims come from poor families and are lured by traffickers on fake promises of jobs, marriage and good life, Ali said."Trying to save the victims and
12453 curb the growing flesh trade has been an uphill task. But we will not to give up."</

12458 The American Automobile Association and an oil industry group locked horns Wednesday, a day after the AAA said drivers wasted $1.7 billion a year buying higher-octane gasoline."Many drivers are falling for the 'octane myth' in gasoline ads and are giving $1.7 billion to the nation's oil industry needlessly," the Washington-based
12458 motorists' group said in a statement on Tuesday.The AAA said consumers should realise "only exotic cars, some sport utility vehicles and vehicles with high-performance engines really need premium," which costs consumers about 15 cents a gallon more than regular grade fuel.The nationwide auto club contended fewer than 10 percent of
12458 cars on U.S. roads needed premium although it constituted nearly 20 percent of total gas sold.The renewed attack against premium echoed a similar call by the Federal Trade Commission last week. The federal agency, seeking to warn consumers against paying extra, sued Exxon Corp. on Sept. 17 for making allegedly
12458 overblown advertising claims that premium enabled engines to run cleaner and with better mileage.Exxon, the fourth major U.S. oil company called to task by the FTC, became the first not to settle before a suit was filed."Contrary to popular opinion, premium gas does not provide more power, doesn't improve performance,
12458 burn more clearly, reduce engine wear or improve mileage," AAA spokesman Dave Van Sickle said Wednesday.An oil industry group disputed some of AAA's claims."That's dead wrong, they're giving short shrift to the facts," said Thomas Hogarty, senior research manager for the American Petroleum Institute, who defended premium for promoting low-knock
12458 combustion.Hogarty conceded in a telephone interview there was little evidence premium reduced engine wear or improved mileage."I won't argue with those points," he said.But Hogarty said a recent study by the Coordinating Research Council, an oil industry group based in Atlanta, showed 19 percent of U.S. vehicles needed premium to
12458 assure smooth combustion and prevent knocking and ping noises associated with lower-octane fuels."Light trucks, vans and utility vehicles are less likely to get by on regular," he said, because of built-in vehicle "knock sensors" that limit acceleration ability if fuel quality is below the premium standard of 92- to 93-grade
12458 octane.Regular gasoline's octane level, a measure of resistance to knocking, is rated at 87-grade.Hogarty also said vast numbers of old vehicles that once used anti-knock leaded fuel, now outlawed, cannot operate properly on regular unleaded gasoline."They (AAA) are giving short shrift to a lot of old cars and trucks," he
12458 said, adding that many of the vintage vehicles are operated in the western United States.</
12459 The global economy has shaken off weakness in Western Europe and is expected to achieve healthy growth through next year, the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday.The IMF, in its semiannual report card on the economy, gave good grades to the emerging market countries, saying they are reaping the benefits
12459 from an often-painful return to fundamentals undertaken in recent years."The global economic expansion is expected to continue at a satisfactory pace in 1996-97 and over the medium term," the IMF report said.In a briefing on the report, IMF chief economist Michael Mussa told reporters, "We expect a moderate strengthening and
12459 continued good performance on the inflaiton front."The report by the international lending agency estimated the global economy would grow by 3.8 percent this year and 4.1 percent in 1997 after growing 3.5 percent in 1995.Industrial countries were expected to grow 2.3 percent this year and 2.5 percent in 1997 after
12459 growing 2.1 percent last year.Developing countries also showed vigorous activity, growing 6.3 percent this year from 5.9 percent in 1995. Growth will slow slightly next year to 6.2 percent.The report said the industrial countries showed uneven results. The the United States chalked up robust growth and low unemployment but Germany
12459 and France lagged behind.However, it said the outlook for Europe was improved as exchange rates came back into line, setting the stage for increased activity."Together with a correction of earlier exchange rate misalignments, this has improved prospects for a resumption of stronger growth in the latter part of 1996," the
12459 report said.It said the entrenched inflation that has stalked policy makers for years is finally on the run, but cautioned officials to guard the exit in case price pressures return with the strengthening economy."Inflation rates in industrial countries, as well as in a number of developing countries have declined to
12459 their lowest levels in decades," the report said. "Monetary authorities will, of course course, need to remain vigilant" regarding price pressures as growth continues or strengthens.As an example, it said the U.S. economy was growing flat out with low unemployment and would benefit from a tightening of monetary policy so
12459 inflation doesn't break loose.However, the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee decided to leave rates unchanged for now in its meeting Tuesday. Still the IMF projects short-term rates will rise about one-half of a percentage point next year.As it has in the past, the IMF scolded Europe for not taking the
12459 tough actions needed to reform its poorly functioning labour markets."For many countries, particularly in Europe, fiscal imbalances are related to shortcomings in the function of labour markets, which has resulted in a dramatic upward trend in unemployment over the past 25 years," the report said.It said that, although the Japanese
12459 economy has responded remarkably well to stimulative efforts by the authorities with growth estimated at 3.5 percent this year after edging up only 0.9 percent in 1995, it is probably too soon to move interest rates higher."But official interest rates will obviously need to be adjusted upward as the recovery
12459 gets further under way,"As a result, it estimated growth in Japan would moderate to 2.7 percent in 1997.Turning to Germany, which is estimated to grow 1.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent in 1997 after being up 1.9 percent in 1995, the IMF said the country had acted properly in
12459 easing monetary policy over the past year to help secure recovery.The report also made clear that the so-called transition economies of Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, which have often been the main focus of IMF policy makers in recent years, may have turned the corner. It estimated they
12459 would grow by 0.4 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1997 after five years of decline."The rewards for comprehensive reform and stabilisation efforts are very striking among the transition countries, where the results of economic transformation are increasingly visible," the report said.</

12461 or 60 cents a share, from $71 million, or 52 cents a share, a year ago.However, Lehman said its net revenues, which represent total revenues less interest expenses, slipped 4 percent to $722 million from $750 million last year. 12461 volatile markets and delayed underwritings were among the key reasons the company failed to extend its streak of quarterly revenue growth."Volatile conditions in the debt and equity markets, as well as seasonal softness in several businesses, interrupted the five consecutive quarters of higher revenues we had posted," Chairman Richard Fuld
12461 said in a statement.Lehman also cited the effects of interest rate movements on customer trading volumes and decisions by issuers to delay scheduled underwritings for the decline.For the nine months, Lehman said its net income soared by 66 percent to $289 million, or $2.28 a share, from $174 million, or
12461 $1.27 a share, the year earlier. 12461 revenues fell to $77 million from $116 million while interest and dividend revenues rose to $2.96 billion from $2.83 billion.However, interest expenses for the quarter rose to $2.86 billion from $2.70 billion, more than offsetting the increase in interest and dividend related revenues.Other revenues fell to $4 million from $11
12461 million.Below the revenue line, the picture was somewhat better, with Lehman's return on common equity rising to 9.0 percent from 8.5 percent a year ago. 12461 the second quarter's 20.2 percent level but up from 14.5 percent a year ago."While quarterly revenue was off for a number of market-related and seasonal reasons, it is important to note that our discipline around expenses remained strong," Fuld said.Total non-interest expenses for the quarter fell to $606 million from

12469 Switzerland sees no reason to renegotiate a 1946 deal on reparation payments for buying Nazi gold, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.The spokesman was replying to demands by a senior U.S. senator, Alfonse D'Amato, who asked the U.S. administration on Tuesday to reopen the pact between Switzerland and the
12469 World War Two Allied powers."This treaty has been negotiated, signed and honoured and 50 years have elapsed. This treaty is valid and for the time being we have nothing more to comment on it," foreign ministry spokesman Jean-Philippe Tissieres told Reuters.Tissieres also said there was no reason to comment because
12469 D'Amato's demand was made in a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher rather than in any official form to the Berne government.D'Amato based his call on newly declassified U.S. government documents that he said showed Swiss banks, companies and the government had accepted far more Nazi assets and
12469 treasures than Swiss negotiators admitted to during the 1945-46 talks."We must obtain the truth after fifty years of deception and manipulation by the Swiss," D'Amato wrote.Tissieres said discovering the truth about Switzerland's role as neutral banker to both Nazi Germany and its victims, including the fate of Nazi and Jewish
12469 assets after the war, was the point of a government historical commission announced last week."It is precisely the will of the government to shed all light on this period of history," he said.The government commission, expected to start up by next April, will work parallel to an international commission set
12469 up by Swiss banks and world Jewish groups in May with a narrower mandate to find lost accounts left by Holocaust victims.Members of parliament also rejected the idea of reopening the 1946 Washington Agreement that settled Allied claims against Switzerland for Nazi assets, including stolen gold, sold or banked in
12469 the neutral Alpine country during the war.Under the accord, the Swiss paid 250 million Swiss franc (about $60 million at the time) in return for buying gold stolen by Nazi forces and another $121 million dollars for Nazi assets frozen in Switzerland shortly before the war's end."This is a treaty
12469 under international law...I can think of no example for an international treaty being renegotiated 50 years after the fact," said Lilli Nabholz, head of the law commission of the National Council, or lower chamber.Nabholz, who drafted a recent bill setting up a historical commission on Switzerland's financial role in World
12469 War Two, said any reopening of reparation talks would affect all Allied powers and virtually every European state.It would also raise questions about how much of the Swiss payment for Nazi gold was actually distributed by the U.S., Britain and France to victims of the Holocaust, she said. The fourth
12469 wartime ally, the Soviet Union, was excluded."This is not a matter just between the United States and Switzerland. The treaty was signed by the victorious Allied powers in the names of all allied states," she said.</

12520 Congress and the White House grappled Tuesday with the final details of a major spending bill needed to avoid a government shutdown, as Senate leaders warned next week's deadline may force them into a weekend session.Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, and Republican Senate Whip Don Nickles
12520 of Oklahoma, said they might have to provide temporary government funds for a few days next week while negotiations continue.Unlike last year, when budget disputes pushed the government into two partial closures, all sides said this week they were determined to avoid a closure just before the Nov. 5 election.
12520 The government's new fiscal year starts next Tuesday and without passage of the multibillion-dollar bill many agencies would be forced to close."I am not going to prolong this artificially just to keep us here," Daschle told reporters. At the same time, Democrats will insist Republicans give details of the spending
12520 bill and amendments before they agree to allow a vote."I'm ruling out Democrats stopping a continuing resolution from passing simply to make a political point. I am not ruling out holding our ground," he said at a news conference at the end of Tuesday's session.Later he added that negotiations on
12520 adding immigration reform and other issues to the bill could prolong the debate and force Congress to pass interim funding.From the other side, Nickles said Republicans also had reservations about Democratic policies added to the bill and might want to hold out for a short-term funding.Republican leaders, faced with polls
12520 that show Democrats stand a chance of reclaiming control of at least the House, are anxious to send their lawmakers home to campaign. But Daschle noted that several Democratic senators faced close races as well and his party wanted to free them to campaign.Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi,
12520 who sets the Senate schedule, said he had given lawmakers notice they should be prepared to work through the weekend, or to return Monday for final passage of the bill.The largest item in the spending bill is the Defense Department's $245 billion. The rest will go to fund many federal
12520 agencies whose regular appropriations have not cleared Congress.The negotiations so far have given President Clinton most of the $6.5 billion he wanted in extra domestic spending and for anti-terrorism programs. Still to be decided are several policy issues, including an abortion-related issue concerning curbs on U.S. contributions to international agencies
12520 that use private funding for abortion services.The House expected to begin debate on the spending bill, often called a continuing resolution, by Thursday or Friday, said Republican Leader Dick Armey of Texas.But "this is the last train out of the station," Armey said, and members were eager to attach their
12520 special projects to the bill.Lawmakers have said they will try to attach legislation to ban gun ownership by people convicted of domestic violence, give banks some regulatory relief and give health plan physicians a clear right to discuss all available treatments wth patients.Armey said he did not expect the government
12520 would be allowed to close, but that there could be disagreements before final resolution of all outstanding issues.</

12522 The New York Power Authority (NYPA) outlined a rate plan for use of its transmission lines that would accomodate the opening of the nation's power grid to competing wholesale electricity suppliers."We believe in open access and we believe all transmission owners must participate actively to bring its full benefits to
12522 consumers," said NYPA chief executive officer C.D. Rappleyea in a statement.Current and new NYPA transmission customers served by a single line would see no increase in transmission rates, the utility said. The proposal also included a "rolled-in" rate for customers who receive power over more than one NYPA transmission line,
12522 it said.The new rolled-in rate would affect relatively few customers and increase their overall electricity bills by less than one percent, NYPA said.NYPA's trustees on Tuesday gave preliminary approval to an initial rolled-in rate of $2.23 a kilowatt-month (kw-month) for firm service on multiple segments of the utility's transmission network,
12522 replacing the current rate of $2.19, it said. The new rate reflects the overall costs of NYPA's integrated transmission system, as required by Federal Energy Regulatory Commission methodology, the utility said.NYPA said its trustees also proposed keeping its current firm rates for single transmission lines. These include charges of $1.60
12522 per kw-month for service on a line from Massena to Marcy, near Utica; $1.60 for service from Marcy to East Fishkill in Dutchess County; and $1.30 for lines carrying electricity from the St Lawrence-Franklin D Roosevelt and Niagara hydroelectric projects. The rate for non-firm, or interruptible, transmission would be pegged
12522 to the new firm rolled-in rate and would not exceed charges for an equivalent amount of firm service.Following additional customer meetings and a public forum Nov 14 in New York City, the trustees would take final action on the proposed open access tariffs, NYPA said.The utility said it expected to
12522 file these transmission tariffs with FERC by the end of 1996.NYPA noted it continued to discuss with the seven investor-owned utility members of the New York Power Pool on a single statewide transmission tariff that could supplant its own proposed tariff.Earlier this year, FERC directed the nation's electric utilities to
12522 open their transmission lines to competing electricity suppliers to promote competition, boost efficiency and reduce costs for consumers.NYPA, a state-owned power agency, supplies a fourth of the New York's electricity.-- New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622</

12529 The Clinton administration is not ready to release a widely anticipated proposal to relax export restrictions on computer encoding technology, a Commerce Department official said on Wednesday.Undersecretary of Commerce William Reinsch, at a hearing of the House Judiciary Committee, said the proposal had not yet been formalized."Our work is not
12529 yet done," Reinsch said in prepared testimony. "We are continuing to consult with industry and international partners to refine our proposal." The Judiciary Committee was holding a hearing on Resolution 3011, a bill that would dramatically relax encryption export limits.Vice President Al Gore outlined the administration's ideas for relaxing limits
12529 on encryption exports in July, saying export controls should be liberalized only if encryption programs include so-called key escrow components.The computer industry and many members of Congress oppose the key escrow and argue that foreign competitors will sell encryption programs without escrow features.Reinsch said the key escrow approach is needed
12529 to help law enforcement and intelligence agencies deal with encryption."This approach balances economic needs with law enforcement concerns and is one that many of our major trading partners, most notably the United Kingdom, are also adopting," Reinsch said in his testimony.He said the United States is working in the Organization
12529 for Economic Cooperation and Development to craft a global policy for encryption.</

12558 Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc said volatile market conditions and delayed underwritings were among the key reasons the company failed to extend a more than year-long streak of quarterly revenue growth.Lehman's third quarter net revenues, which represents total revenues less interest expenses, amounted to $722 million, short of both the $750
12558 million in net revenues it posted a year ago and the second quarter's $833 million. "Volatile conditions in the debt and equity markets, as well as seasonal softness in several businesses, interrupted the five consecutive quarters of higher revenues we had posted," Lehman Chairman and Chief Executive Richard Fuld said
12558 in a statement.Lehman also cited the effects of interest rate movements on customer trading volumes and decisions by issuers to delay scheduled underwritings for the decline.For the quarter, revenues from principal transactions rose to $303 million from $245 million a year ago but investment banking revenues fell to $237 million
12558 from $251 million. Commissions revenues fell to $77 million from $116 million while interest and dividend revenues rose to $2.96 billion from $2.83 billion.However, interest expenses for the quarter rose to $2.86 billion from $2.70 billion, more than offsetting the increase in interest and dividend related revenues.Other revenues fell to
12558 $4 million from $11 million.Below the revenue line, the picture was somewhat better, with Lehman's return on common equity rising to 9.0 percent from 8.5 percent a year ago. Still, that was well short of the 13.4 percent figure posted in the second quarter. Lehman's pre-tax margin for the quarter
12558 was 16.0 percent, down from the second quarter's 20.2 percent level but up from 14.5 percent a year ago."While quarterly revenue was off for a number of market related and seasonal reasons, it is important to note that our discipline around expenses remained strong," Fuld said.Total non-interest expenses for the
12558 quarter fell to $606 million from $641 million a year ago, a key reason the company was able to improve quarterly net earnings to $77 million or $0.60 per share from $71 million or $0.52 per share last year.-- New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1610</

12612 Europe's plans for currency union may steal the limelight at international finance talks in Washington this weekend amid questions about what it will mean for world economic growth and the dollar.Europe's finance ministers hold talks with the Group of Seven (G7) rich nations this weekend confident their plans for economic
12612 and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 are firmly on track.That makes all the more pressing questions on whether Europe's combined drive to squeeze budget deficits, in the face of persistent mass unemployment, will continue to dampen economic growth, making it the weak link in the world economy.And, crucially for the
12612 Americans, whether pressure for a policy change builds up to the extent that the fledgling monetary union goes for a weaker exchange rate against the dollar to lift growth and get people back to work."I am sure the temptation is very real. The core (richer nothern European states) look at
12612 the devaluers with a certain amount of jealousy," Banque Internationale de Placement economist Marie Owens-Thomsen said.French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters the last time G7 ministers met at a summit in France in June that he had been surprised how much EMU had dominated the talks.After talks this weekend
12612 in Dublin, where EU ministers set out the nuts and bolts of how EMU will work, that focus is likely to intensify both at the G7 and in the corridors of an International Monetary Fund and World Bank meeting next week.France in particular would like to see a stronger dollar
12612 to make Europe's economies more competitive in world markets, although it is unclear how much support it enjoys from Germany, its main partner in driving monetary union forward.In an interview with the daily La Tribune Desfosses published on Monday, Arthuis said EMU would mean calls for a stronger dollar would
12612 be listened to more. "It is indeed one of the reasons for a single currency," he said.Europe will have two crucial ways of influencing the dollar-euro rate -- in fixing it at the launch of EMU in 1999 and in managing a potentially big surplus of dollar reserves when central
12612 banks merge into the future European Central Bank.The euro is to be exchanged on a one-for-one basis for the ecu -- potentially a weaker currency since it is based on all countries in the European Union, including those whose economies might not be judged healthy enough for early membership of
12612 EMU.Most argue, however, that the one-for-one commitment will mean that the ecu will rise to reflect the stronger economies of core northern European countries likely to join EMU first."The key question is what is the political will in Europe to push up the dollar. At the end of the day,
12612 the ecu movements will be reflecting the political statements," ABN Amro economist Philippe Brossard said.That factor will also determine whether an expected surplus of central bank dollar reserves is used agressively to push the dollar up through intervention on foreign exchange markets.But for central bankers, seen ruling EMU via the
12612 powerful European Central Bank, there seems little risk of a devaluation which could threaten the primary goal of fighting inflation.For such anti-inflation hawks, the currency stability created by the euro, the liquity of the vast bond market growing around it, and the euro's potential role as a reserve currency, will
12612 lead to lower interest rates which will in themselves give a much-needed lift to growth.They also insist that Europe needs reform to the labour market rather than a devaluation to create jobs."Unemployment is a structural problem in Europe," Owens-Thomsen said, adding there was no evidence that devaluation would boost jobs.
12612 "The problem in Europe lies elsewhere."Brossard also argued that despite French calls for a ministerial council to oversee EMU, which so far have received only a lukewarm response, there was little chance of a united political front to promote devaluation."Clearly there is not a European will equivalent to the U.S.
12612 will to depreciate the dollar against the yen. There is not a government in Europe to deal with the exchange rate," he said.</

12623 Luminaries from London's financial community gather on Wednesday on the long-deserted stock exchange floor to mark the ten-year anniversary of the "Big Bang" reforms which killed off floor trading in London.Yet a decade after the radical reforms swept away years of share trading tradition in Europe's busiest stock market, major
12623 questions remain about the exchange's future direction -- making Big Bang seem an unfinished revolution to many in the market.For next year the London Stock Exchange (LSE) plans a new share trading network where trades are automatically matched by computer, supplementing the current system where market makers set prices on
12623 screen but agree trades by phone.But details of the new "order-driven" system are still being defined and it was accepted reluctantly by leading brokerages."It well be another big cultural shock if we go to an order driven system," said one senior trader, "it will be as big a change as
12623 Big Bang."Under the deregulating British government of Margaret Thatcher, the Big Bang reforms abolished fixed commissions on share trades and ended the division between jobbers who traded stock and brokers who placed the orders.Small on paper, the reforms of October 27 1986 changed the face of the London stock market.They
12623 led to a wave of mergers to create the big integrated investment banks that dominate the London stock market today.Meantime the introduction of the Seaq electronic share trading screen quickly killed off the old stock exchange trading floor, adding to the dramatic process that shaped careers and is etched into
12623 the memories of market players."What upset me and people of my era was that we were going to have to leave our stage and go sit behind screens," said Brian Winterflood, managing director of broking house Winterflood Securities."Getting up to go to that stock exchange in those days was like
12623 getting up to go to the theater for me. It was a wonderful place," said Winterflood, who joined the LSE in 1953. "Leaving the floor was a tragedy for me. But one adopts and adapts."Robin Packer, a managing director of brokerage UBS, said he and many of his colleagues on
12623 the LSE floor feared electronic trading threatened their livelihood."There was this feeling that under the new system, there wouldn't be a role for us," Packer said. "There were a lot who fell to the wayside. But a lot of people got into sales trading, and that's a very important function
12623 in today's markets."When reforms were first introduced a decade ago, the feeling among traders, jobbers and brokers was that firms were not given enough time to implement changes, said Packer."We had been given very little time to organize a new system. There was also the feeling that they were breaking
12623 up a system that was hugely efficient. "But at the end of the day, (the new system) was more efficient and international."Indeed, the LSE fended off competiton from European bourses and remains Europe's busiest stock exchange. An unprecedented 646.3 billion pounds of UK and Irish stocks changed hands in 1995,
12623 a rise of 6.6 percent.The LSE, criticised for dragging its feet in carrying out its current reforms, is this week expected to approve a more precise definition of the new order-driven market -- paving the way for the introduction of the service next summer.The continuing revolution seems inevitable but some
12623 old hands believe something valuable has been lost in the past ten years of upheaval."The system had to change because it wasn't moving ahead fast enough to be in the international game," said Winterflood. "It was a place where my word was my bond. Now that's gone."-- London Newsroom +44

12625 notes and commercial paper in the Eurobond market."This transaction is a significant step in removing low-margin assets from the balance sheet," said NatWest chief executive Derek Wanless.Banking analysts agreed the overall significance of the move -- known technically as securitisation -- was marginal since Natwest is already rich in cash,
12625 although they welcomed its efforts to maximise shareholder value."It's a sound strategic move getting assets off the balance sheet but the capital significance...is reasonably small in terms of the group," ABN AMRO Hoare Govett banking analyst Steven Thorn said.Thorn said that NatWest, after lagging other banks in aggressively removing low-margin
12625 loans from its books, is now starting to match them.The move rekindled speculation over what NatWest was planning to do with the extra funds since it already has more than adequate capital ratios and these would be further raised.The bank is known to want to boost its capacity to sell
12625 retail financial products in Britain, possibly through the purchase of a life insurance company or building society, but Wanless said recently it had not found any acquisitions which met its criteria.In the absence of acquisitions, NatWest in July announced a 450 million pound share repurchase programme which, it said, was
12625 in line with its policy of returning value to shareholders.Corporate loans have carried notoriously low margings in recent years with some banks withdrawing to a large extent from this type of business.But banks have often thought it important to bite the bullet and accept low returns if they wish to

12640 News that Britain's National Westminster Bank plans to turn $5.0 billion worth of high-quality, low-margin corporate loans into securities sparked a flurry of speculation and hopes for an asset-backed revival. Details of NatWest's jumbo loan securitisation deal were sketchy on Wednesday but players expected much of the paper to surface
12640 at the end of October and to be triple-A rated."It is most likely it will be rated triple-A, although this is not essential," said a director specialising in the asset-backed market at a British bank."A top-notch rating would make sense to shift this volume of paper," he said. "But there
12640 is always a cost-effectiveness trade off. A lower rating means less credit enhancement costs."Officials at National Westminster Bank would not comment further on the issue.Roadshows for the deal are expected to start October 7.NatWest said earlier it planned to securitise about $5.0 billion of its corporate syndicated loans to release
12640 around 200 million stg of capital to boost the bank's balance sheet."The success of the deal will depend entirely on the pricing as long as the structure is not very complex," said a Eurobond syndicate head at a U.S. bank."Most securitised deals are rated triple-A, so the pricing becomes much
12640 more of a consideration than, for example, the name of the borrower," he said.Although this is the first securitisation by an issuer of corporate loans, pricing should be helped by comparison with a number of outstanding AAA deals, the official said.NatWest said it will repackage loans -- made to British,
12640 European and U.S. companies -- and issue sterling and dollar-denominated asset-backed FRNs and commercial paper (CP) in the Eurobond and U.S. private placement markets.Some speculated as much as half could be raised via CP.The planned transaction is being seen as another leap forward for the European asset-backed market which has
12640 already seen significant process in recent months.Since the European asset-backed market started in earnest in the mid-1980s, around $60 billion has been issued.In the U.S. -- the Euro asset-backed market's older and much bigger cousin -- $100 billion of asset-backed securities were launched in 1995 alone.Market growth is driven by
12640 yield-hungry investors looking for high quality assets that gave a return over Libor.Landmark deals in Europe include the use of securitisation for acquisition finance (Birmingham Midshires Building Society), corporate restructuring (GPA), privatisations (Bullet trains) and infrastructure finance (Road Management Consolidated).The U.S. asset-backed market, ahead of Europe in size and in
12640 terms of financial innovation, has yet to use the securitisation of large corporate loans."In particular, attention in the U.S. has focused on securitising marginal new assets, with less emphasis on old, traditional assets like loans," the syndicate source said.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748</

12650 George Staple, director of Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO), said on Wednesday that the court ruling in the Maxwell case last week had weakened the system of trying people accused of major financial fraud."The position now is that in the most complex fraud cases the indictment will be split up
12650 to produce a series of manageable trials...but it is very unlikely that a second trial will ever take place," Staple told a London conference on combating financial crime."The full criminality is unlikely ever to come before a court, nor will the defendants. The system is thereby emasculated," Staple added.Staple said
12650 the judge's ruling in the Maxwell case, which threw out a second trial against Kevin Maxwell, son of media tycoon Robert Maxwell who died in 1991, had made it clear that it would be "unusual" for a second trial to take place.Kevin and his brother Ian were acquitted in January
12650 after an eight-month trial and Judge John Buckley said last Thursday that a second trial against Kevin would "serve no further public interest". He later recorded not guilty verdicts.Staple said while the Maxwell ruling did not "necessarily mean that after an acquittal severed counts cannot be tried in a subsequent
12650 trial", it meant later trials were unlikely.He said indictments had already been reduced to a "bare minimum" after directions in the Blue Arrow case.The SFO decided to "sever" the counts in the Maxwell trials to make the case more jury-friendly. This policy was encouraged by the appeal court which had
12650 quashed the guilty verdicts in the notorious Blue Arrow case.Staple said this had been at the forefront of the way the SFO planned its investigations and prosecutions. It has not "overloaded indictments" but has tried to "reflect in the charges sufficient criminality to enable juries, on the evidence, to convict
12650 with confidence".But there would inevitably be cases with several principal defendants "which are so complex that it is impossible to reduce them to a point where the whole indictment against all the defendants can be tried in a single trial".The Maxwell case was an example of this and had therefore
12650 been split up into several trials which, Staple said, were thought "to be fair and manageable before a separate jury".But as a consequence, the first and subsequent trials would only go ahead on part of the available evidence and not all the defendants would be before the court in each
12650 case."The jury will never see the full weight of the case against all." he said.Staple said it was not a question of whether juries can understand the cases and "still less is it a question of the decisions of juries not being accepted by the authorities...they are accepted".He said the
12650 main question was whether it was reasonable to ask an ordinary jury to sit through the entire lengthy case and at the end of this process deliver a verdict."I said last week that the judgement in the Maxwell case had serious implications for the prosecution of the largest and most
12650 complex criminal cases. A solution to this problem is now urgently required," Staple concluded.</

12671 Rhodium prices, which have been battered by U.S. speculator selling over the last week, could remain under pressure until the market hits $200 an ounce.Rhodium is now around $245, close to a January 1996 low and a mid-1980s nadir of around $230 -- a major retracement from dizzy heights of
12671 $7,000 reached in 1990 as booming demand from autocatalyst makers burnt off global supplies.Traders said estimates of the recent selling varied considerably, from as much as 1.25 tonnes (72,000 ounces) down to a more conservative 5,000 ounces."There were few buyers around to soak up the selling which saw the the
12671 market nosedive last week," a trader said.The market is destined for $200 before any stability emerges," another trader said.Others agreed, saying the speculative source, a buyer around two years ago, decided to liquidate in an illiquid market.The amount of rhodium held is quite considerable, as 72,000 ounces is nearly equivalent
12671 to annual Russian supply.The buying mostly took place in 1994 when prices ranged roughly between $560 and $930 and was largely a speculative venture, regardless of market fundamentals or global demand. "I think the long just got fed up with the whole scenario and decided to sell, though in such
12671 a thin market they found few willing buyers," a trader commented. "Noone is taking a position at the moment as they adopt a wait-and-see attitude," another added.Some traders suggested that producers may enter the market soon to prop up teetering values, a move that may encourge short-covering."I believe the bottom
12671 of the market is towards $200 where buying is expected to come into play," a trader said. Global stock levels are at high levels, and the autocatalyst industry will continue to be supplied by long term contracts from the two major producers, South Africa and Russia.According to platinum group refiner
12671 Johnson Matthey Plc the inventory overhang will continue to weigh on prices in 1996.Johnson Matthey said demand in 1995 jumped to 459,000 ounces from 386,000 in 1994, but supply failed to keep pace, rising 10,000 ounces to 436,000. This created a 23,000 ounce deficit. In Europe on Wednesday rhodium, which
12671 is also used in the glass and computer industries, ranged between $230 and $260 an ounce on the free-market.Meanwhile, Johnson Matthey's daily European price was quoted at $280 an ounce.--London Newsroom +44 71 510 8075</

12673 LONDON, Sept 25 (LPC) - National Westminster Bank's plan to securitise $5 billion of corporate loans is part of a broad movement by banks to move marginally profitable assets off balance sheets while retaining strategic relationships with borrowers, bankers say.Margins on bank loans to large corporate clients are at cyclical
12673 lows - with the average AA rated borrower in the UK paying just 13.66 bps over LIBOR - yet banks like NatWest are forced to participate in the sector in order to pave the way for other, more profitable business with borrowers.To keep the relationship but sell the debt NatWest
12673 will have to create an instrument that is attractive to investors while reassuring large corporate borrowers that a securitisation is in their best interests too, observers say."How will company treasurers feel about this?" one banker asked. Other banks in London have been working towards increasing the secondary market for corporate
12673 loans for much the same reasons. Secondary sales of loans involve selling large chunks of existing loan, usually to sophisticated investors or other banks. Banks are keen to develop these markets because, though some like NatWest can dull the pain of lending at low rates by earning fees for arranging
12673 loans and for administrative duties, loans to high-quality borrowers on thin margins are not seen as an ideal use of capital.But these efforts to foment a secondary market for corporate debt have faced resistance from corporations that are loath to allow their debt to pass outside a small group of
12673 relationship banks. That's because secondary sales of debt often carry with them the right to vote on amendments to a loan or participate in negotiations if the borrower goes into default.NatWest may be able to get around this hurdle by retaining the voting rights itself and selling to investors a
12673 stream of interest and repayment of principal in exchange for assuming credit risk. If so, the relationship between the bank and the borrower will be much as before except that the ultimate funding will come from investors.However, if voting rights are retained by banks an issue for investors is how
12673 they would be represented if a loan went bad. NatWest will use high-quality, investment grade loans, thus reducing the likelihood of default, bankers said.NatWest declined to comment, citing US Securities and Exchange Commission regulations.Theoretically, securitisation should offer benefits to borrowers if it becomes widespread, bankers say. "It should drive interest
12673 rates in the syndicated loan market down because it will add to liquidity," said the head of syndication at a major bank.This, of course, would only add to banks' motivation to securitise.James Saft 44-0171-542-4048</

12675 of tens or even hundreds of thousands of pounds are not uncommon in the City of London.Hughes said closing the loophole by insisting bonuses are paid in cash could bring in 350 million pounds a year, which the party proposed should be earmarked to ease the pressure on the creaking
12675 NHS.It could be used to employ more than 10,000 extra NHS nurses and to cut waiting times for hospital operations. Later David Laws, a parliamentary researcher for the Liberals, said the Treasury had now closed the gold bars tax loophole.But he said this has merely prompted the firms to find

12682 Russian President Boris Yeltsin would have been in deeper trouble if he had developed his heart trouble 25 years ago.Stone Age healers were doing crude brain surgery 10,000 years ago, likewise the ancient Egyptians, but heart surgery is a modern, hi-tech operation.It could not be seriously attempted until after World
12682 War Two, when drugs and technology made the heart-lung machine possible. This takes over for patients' circulation during heart surgery -- keeping them alive while the heart is cut into, manipulated or, in the case of a transplant, removed.The heart bypass surgery Yeltsin is apparently about to undergo was still
12682 highly experimental in the late 1960s and has only recently become more routine than an appendectomy.In the case of the Kremlin leader, the problem seems to be whether he is well enough for an operation."To do heart surgery, you need to use a heart-lung machine and to do that you
12682 need to be able to anticoagulate the blood," said John Pepper of London's Royal Brompton Hospital, one of Britain's top heart surgeons.Until the anticoagulant drug heparin was synthesised from a liver chemical, there was no way to keep a patient's blood artificially circulating."All sorts of peculiar surgery was being done,"
12682 Pepper said. Sometimes patients were packed in ice to slow their metabolisms and reduce the need for oxygen. This gave surgeons about eight minutes to do their work before they had to re-start the heart."It was perfectly feasible but you could not do many things," pioneer British heart surgeon Donald
12682 Ross said.It was not really until the 1950s that doctors seriously attempted heart surgery, beginning on children and babies with congenital heart problems.Surgeons started repairing damaged heart valves in the early 1960s but were not able to address the problem of clogged arteries until the late 1960s.Coronary artery disease is
12682 one of the biggest killers of the Western world. Fats in the blood oxidise and clog up the arteries. Yeltsin is the most prominent recent victim, but it affects millions.Had Yeltsin developed his heart problems before the late 1960s, he would have simply suffered with chest pain and heart attacks
12682 until he died."He would have been up a creek," Pepper said. "There wouldn't have been anything to offer him."In 1967 doctors at the Cleveland Clinic in Cleveland, Ohio performed the first heart bypass, using a vein to literally pass by a clogged artery to restore blood flow from the heart.British
12682 doctors duplicated the operation in 1968, and advances were made very quickly. Nonetheless, it was dangerous."The patient had to be pretty tough," said Pepper. "The mortality was horrific and you were offered people who were desperate. The methods of investigation were very crude and a lot of things were not
12682 understood."But the results were often dramatic. When in December 1967 South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first heart transplant, heart surgeons became the heroes of the age.Pepper said there was still a long way to go. "In the history of surgery, this has been the most investigated and studied
12682 operation ever," he said.By the 1980s it was clear that an artery was better for the operation than a vein, and techniques were refined further. The death rate from the operation fell to two percent.Now, coronary bypass surgery is one of the most frequently performed operations. "In the U.S. a
12682 coronary operation is more common than an appendectomy," Pepper said. "I do 250 to 300 a year."Doctors are experimenting with more advanced technuques, the latest being minimally invasive surgery, done with an endoscope -- a tiny camera attached to a cable that allows surgeons to operate without cracking open the
12682 chest.Some of the techniques even allow surgery without the use of the heart-lung machine.</

12699 U.S. stocks in London were steady to slightly lower on Wednesday as the market digested the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged and mulled over the weakness of the Dow and the dollar."It's surprisingly quiet at the moment...I think the market has really gone into "wait and see'
12699 mode. Most had expected the Fed to make a move on rates," one dealer said.Traders said the Fed's inaction had pulled the prospect of third-quarter earnings back into focus, with worries fuelled by a shock profit warning from telecoms group AT&amp;T Corp and the impact of the weaker dollar. AT&amp;T's
12699 weakness weighed on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which closed 20.71 points lower at 5,874.03. Traders said the Dow was likely to open slightly lower on Wednesday.Dealers said AT&amp;T, which dropped $5-3/4 to $51-1/2 overnight, was trading $1/4 higher in London at $51-3/4."The one thing that hit Wall Street was
12699 the question mark over third-quarter earnings, particularly at AT&amp;T," Sonja Shechter, European equity strategist at Daiwa Europe Ltd, said.Shechter said the market could enter a holding pattern amid debate about earnings. The Fed inaction also meant uncertainty about a still-expected tightening would overshadow the market. "People will get even more
12699 jittery about economic data," Shechter said.Among other movers in London, Texas Instruments was down $1/8 at $57-1/4. The stock gained heavily overnight and was upgraded to buy from hold by Montgomery Securities.--London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367</
12700 Heavy rains over Europe's beet areas may hamper harvesting and increase the threat of frost damage, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.Rains had been two to four times what was normal for September, and more were forecast, Licht said in its daily report."Additional rains are expected which will make harvesting
12700 extremely difficult," the report said."Moreover, the later the harvest, the greater the danger of an early frost, which could lead to noticeable losses."While the very heavy rains in Europe's eastern half had finally ended, September rainfall for the area to date was still 150 to 350 percent of normal levels,
12700 Licht said."The rains not only affected sugar content, but also hampered harvesting operations," it said.But while the former Soviet Union had suffered heavy rains in the week ending September 24, light rains had been seen in the southern half of Europe.Northern areas, including most of Britain, Germany and Poland, had
12700 been mostly dry.--Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064</
12701 International debt markets face weeks of anxiety over inflation as they wait to see whether the U.S. Federal Reserve was prudent to leave interest rates steady after a crucial policy meeting, analysts said on Wednesday.In such an uncertain environment, investors should avoid U.S. Treasuries and look for gains in Canada
12701 and Europe, they said."Most people had expected some sort of movement from the Fed and there is a concern that they are now starting to get behind the curve," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London."The markets are vulnerable to any strong U.S. data and signs that
12701 inflation is picking up," he said.Many analysts were busy reworking their bond strategies on Wednesday after Federal Reserve surprised some by keeping interest rates unchanged after its policy meeting on Tuesday.The federal funds rate was kept at 5.25 percent and the discount rate at 5.00 percent. There was no word
12701 of explanation from the central bank.While bond prices initially greeted the decision by rising with relief, analysts expected relief to soon turn to angst as markets faced up to the reality of a bubbling U.S. economy and substantial wage inflation.Lurking in the background was the idea that the Fed had
12701 overlooked inflation pressures in order not rock the economic policy boat before presidential elections on November 5."There are two issues the market fears," said Adam Chester, international bond strategtist at Yamaichi International Europe in London. "Firstly, that the Fed might be politically inspired and secondly that the Fed...might have too
12701 rosy a picture of growth in the second half," he said.Chester said the economy was unlikely to slow as much as the Fed expected."All the signs are that the fourth quarter is going to be very strong indeed going into the Christmas sales season." Inflation, buoyed by wage and oil
12701 price rises, would see a sharp rise over the balance of the year, he said.Signs of a vibrant economy included second quarter growth of 4.8 percent, a jobless rate of 5.1 percent in August and a three-year rise in average earnings, analysts said.Nevertheless, inflation remains subdued at 2.9 percent in
12701 August.IBJ's Edmonds said debt markets will remain on inflation guard until the next Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC) on November 13.In the meantime major statistics, including September payrolls next Friday, will cause hand-wringing, he said.If the data show growth remains robust, the Fed will have to consider a significant
12701 rate rise in November, said Edmonds. This could mean a 50 basis point rise."There's always a risk that when a central bank delays, when they do move they have to be more aggressive," he said.With uncertainty in the U.S. market set to linger, Michael O'Hanlon, chief international economist at PaineWebber
12701 in London, said Canadian markets looked a better bet."The lack of a Fed move means there is a great possibility the Bank of Canada can cut rates which will help the short and long end of the market," he said.O'Hanlon also favoured core European markets but said investors should extend
12701 along the yield curve."People whould extend duration in core Europe because the Bundesbank will continue to frustrate with the pace of its easing and the repo rate is likely to remain at 3.0 percent for a little while longer," he said.High yielding markets, especially Italy, will continue to do well
12701 as long as the dollar does not suffer too much from the Fed's inaction, he said.-- International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176</

12703 PowerGen Plc, Britian's second biggest generator, said on Wednesday it was closing the last of its power stations to burn Orimulsion, dubbed the world's filthiest fuel.PowerGen said it would try to redeploy the 41 staff employed at the 500 megawatt Ince plant in northwest England plant, or seek voluntary redundancies.The
12703 closure of Ince marks the end of PowerGen's current dealings with Orimulsion, a cheap fuel from Venezuela that has triggered attacks from environmentalists and legal action from a car firm that alleged fallout damaged paintwork on new cars."The Ince closure will follow the ending of the five-year Orimulsion contract for
12703 Ince which will not be renewed," PowerGen said in a statement.The company said the power station, near Chester, would stop generating electricity at the end of next March.To make up for the loss of power, PowerGen will start up a generating unit at Fiddler's Ferry power station in Warrington, also
12703 in northwest England.The unit was placed in reserve in March 1994 and should return to commercial operating in December.PoweGen closed its Richborough power plant in Kent, south east England in March. Richborough was the only other of its three originally oil-fired power stations that had been adapted to burn Orimulsion.</
