12707 Divisions over Europe within Britain's Conservative party yawned as wide as ever on Wednesday despite attempts by Prime Minister John Major to lay down the law on his wait-and-see policy towards a single currency.Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine warned so-called Eurosceptics and pro-Europeans that their squabbling could cost the party
12707 victory at the next election, due by next May."What they're doing is creating an impression of disunity, the only consequence of which can be to put into power a Labour government," Heseltine told BBC radio. Labour leads the ruling party in opinion polls by about 20 points.He was speaking soon
12707 after John Redwood, a leading Euro-sceptic opposed to closer European ties, challenged Major's ruling that the government would keep its options open on whether to join the European Union's planned single currency.Redwood, who quit the cabinet in a failed bid to oust Major from the Conservative party leadership in July
12707 1995, said events this week had shown that the wait-and-see approach was dangerous.Major tried to defuse a row sparked when finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Sunday it would be "pathetic" if Britain were to rule out initial participation in the single currency, due to be launched in 1999, only
12707 to join later.Clarke, the cabinet's leading pro-European, was accused by junior foreign minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor, a Euro-sceptic, of going beyond the government's agreed line.But Major told reporters late on Tuesday that Clarke had been misrepresented in the press and that the turmoil, in effect, was all one big misunderstanding.In
12707 clear defiance of Major, Redwood returned to the attack on Wednesday. He insisted that Clarke had stepped out of line by expressing a clear preference for economic and monetary union (EMU) and said it was worrying that he had done so."We have seen this week how dangerous it can be
12707 if you leave all the options open. That can be very tempting for one minister to go further on the airways than he should have done and lead to public dissension," Redwood said.He said he still hoped the government would explicitly reject EMU in advance of the election."Whilst it's still
12707 possible to say today that they don't have to make up their mind, by the time we get to the general election we'll be very close indeed to them having to make up their mind, and I think the public will expect more guidance on how they'll do so," he
12707 said.But another former cabinet minister, pro-European David Hunt, immediately contradicted Redwood, telling BBC radio it would be "foolish" for Britain to close its options on EMU now.He was backed by Heseltine, who said it would be an abdication of Britain's national interest if it denied itself a chance to influence
12707 negotiations over the single currency by ruling out participation now.Major, whose six years as prime minister have been dogged by divisions over Europe, will be hoping that the latest row dies down before the Conservatives' showcase annual conference starts on October 8.But Paddy Ashdown, whose centrist Liberal Democrats are holding
12707 their own conference this week, said the extraordinary feuding showed the Conservatives were in "total and utter internal chaos" and no longer fit to govern."The sooner they leave and call a general election so the country can have a decent, strong government again, the better for them and the better
12707 for all of us," he said.</

12709 The dollar was frail in Europe on Wednesday, smarting from the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates unchanged and bracing for further losses.The policy-making Federal Open Market Committee signalled no rate change after Tuesday's meeting, catching out a market which had priced in a 25 basis-point rise in
12709 the federal funds target rate, at which banks charge each other for overnight money."The Fed's taking a risk and the dollar's vulnerable to any sort of strong data or any pick-up in inflation," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ in London.The dollar was quoted at 1.5066 marks by 0912
12709 GMT, some way below late Tuesday's European level of 1.5127 although off a New York low of 1.5000.The U.S. currency was far more resilient against the yen, turning around an overnight dive to 108.95 yen to trade at 109.95, up from the previous European close of 109.78.The Fed's inaction had
12709 many market watchers speculating it could be "behind the curve" on inflation, and concerned that a reluctance to hike interest rates ahead of the U.S. election on November 5 had influenced its decision. That threw the focus onto the FOMC's next meeting on November 13.Some also said Tuesday's meeting had
12709 lasted longer than usual, suggesting that there was a split over whether or not to change policy and so increasing the risk of a November rate hike if there was no further confirmation of economic slowdown.Dealers said the dollar looked fragile after its inability to recoup overnight losses against the
12709 mark."It's struggling a bit. A lot of people came in and believed it was the thing to do to buy the dollar for a rebound, but it doesn't look that healthy," said Peter Heath, senior dealer at Merita Bank. He saw the upside blocked at around 1.5075, with a re-test
12709 of overnight lows possible.Bids should protect the downside below 1.50 marks for now, however, Heath said. "I think the range has moved from 1.5120-70 to 1.5020-70," he added.Some feared dollar/mark could probe even lower. Chase Investment Bank saw 1.4975 as the first target, with potential for a test of lows
12709 seen this summer -- when the dollar plunged as far as 1.4635 -- if that level was broken."We see the (Fed) decision as fairly unambiguously dollar negative," Chase said in its daily market brief.All eyes will now be on U.S. data for confirmation that the economy is indeed decelerating, analysts
12709 said.U.S. existing home sales for August were due to appear later on Wednesday, although the market was more interested in Thursday's durable goods figures and Friday's GDP.The really big one is the October 4 release of this month's U.S. non-farm payrolls, an indicator which has wreaked havoc on the markets
12709 in the past, analysts noted."I think the economy will slow down but I believe the risks are asymmetric," said IBJ's Edmonds. "If anything we're going to see inflation pick up, given the tightness in the labour market."Analysts warned that the dollar remained at risk if data indeed showed the U.S.
12709 economy losing momentum."As incoming data provides further evidence that the economy is decelerating, starting with durable goods tomorrow, the market will need to reconsider whether the Fed will still tighten this year," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell."Such a reassessment could yet exert greater pressure on
12709 the dollar," he added.All the same, analysts said the dollar should claw some near-term support ahead of the the meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers in Washington at the weekend.</

12716 Change in leadership of the world's major political and economic powers was, in the past, a potentially catastrophic event for financial markets.Now, as Russian President Boris Yeltsin battles with serious heart problems and U.S. President Bill Clinton fights for re-election, markets are playing it much cooler.But analysts warned political risk
12716 is not dead, and could yet rear up again in the most unlikely places -- the apparently rock steady core of Europe. "The key thing is whether the disappearance of Clinton and Yeltsin would change the world," said Stephen Bell, chief economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London."And the truth
12716 is -- not very much."In the 1980s, the lingering cold war and worldwide economic recession provided a volatile mix for the markets.But with the Soviet empire now fragmented and capitalist economic orthodoxy taking root across the world, financial markets have become increasingly inured to political shocks.Analysts noted two 1990 crises
12716 -- the coup which briefly ousted then Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev (Corrects from Russian President Boris Yeltsin) and the Gulf War. In both cases, major market reactions were later judged to be overreactions and reversed.Now, U.S. bombing of Iraq or calls for Yeltsin to resign give only a faint boost
12716 to the dollar or gold, usually safe-haven investments in times of perceived crisis."Political risk is relevant, but the old days when you'd see five or even 10 big figures movement on dollar/mark. Those days are over," said Bell.Analysts say two main factors have reduced markets' sensitivity to political turmoil. "Since
12716 the fall of the Soviet Union, markets have been crying wolf about Russia, so the impact of every twist and turn in Russian politics is getting smaller," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko in London."(Russia) is a very small part of western trade, the economy is not going
12716 to collapse to the extent that you would see thousands of refugees flood over the borders. So, all those previous scare stories are being put into a proper perspective."Convergence in major industrialised nations toward low inflation, sustained growth and some unemployment has also meant few fundamental economic moves from government
12716 changes. "In Britain, for example, people now say the differences between the two main political parties are very small. So, the risk we would see a dramatic change in economic policy with a change in government are greatly reduced," said Nikko's Thomson."Its much the same in the U.S. The policies
12716 (of the two main presidential candidates) are so similar that it's really more a a debate about personalities."With bodies such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank seeking to impose a core policy of fiscal austerity and export-led growth on the world's developing nations, that critical mass will
12716 increase, analysts said. But the drive to an all-embracing orthodoxy may turn out to be a double-edged sword.While this conformity spreads to all corners of the globe, political risk may reappear in major industrialised nations, particularly in Europe."If you want to identify political risk in the next two to three
12716 years, it lies not in Russia, but in western Europe," said Thomson.The only economic game being played in Europe is the push towards closer integration and a single currency. Any threat to that, would leave a dangerous vacuum, economists said. "An awful lot in Europe hangs on this EMU (European
12716 Monetary Union) project. And there is no "plan B" in countries like France Italy, Spain, Belgium, even Germany...it is the dominant political issue for them," said DMG's Bell.If EMU, set to start in 1999, goes ahead, all well and good.But if it dissolves before starting, or collapses soon afterwards, the
12716 bricks and mortar of the most prominent, if not the only, support for economic policy in Europe would crumble."If EMU went, it would remove a consensus amongst European parties that reflects a great deal of political influence on economic policies," said Bell. Furthermore, the drive to cut budget deficits and
12716 inflation to squeeze European economies into the shape required for a single currency has pushed countries such as Germany and France to the brink of, or even into, recession.Unemployment has soared and popular support for a single currency has understandably waned.Most of all, analysts warned against complacency, saying it would
12716 be dangerous for investors to treat the reduction of poltical risk asscociated with the old-style superpowers as a sign it has disappeared all together. DMG's Bell said that with "market-friendly politicians in place across the world," political risk was not being taken as seriously as it it should."That will change,"
12716 he said. "Unemployment is Europe's biggest problem, political mistrust of the centre is the United States' biggest problem and Japan has dramatic social change."At the moment all this is being suppressed. But people will get fed up. I see 1997 as quite a difficult year for the poltical world."-- Kate

12722 their handling of the slaughter of cattle vulnerable to Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease."Ministers decreed that the hugely profitable cattle cull should be left in the hands of a cosy little carve-up by the cartel of big abattoir and renderers groups," he said. The government had now
12722 admitted the price paid to abattoirs to slaughter cattle -- 87.50 stg per animal -- was four times what its advisers thought economic, and payments had been cut."It is estimated that five companies have made many millions of excess profits as a result of this favouritism," Tyler told delegates. "Who
12722 is making a killing now?""Meanwhile smaller abattoirs have been driven out of business, the cull of over-30-month (old) cattle has been managed with inconceivable incompetence, the backlog of cows waiting on the farms is growing and specialist beef producers are on the brink of bankruptcy." 12722 than the European Union for the crisis, saying cattle should have been culled years earlier to contain the disease, and that farm minister Douglas Hogg had shown "all the diplomatic finesse of a bull in a china shop".The conference went on to debate an emergency motion urging the government to
12722 break the impasse over the export ban on British beef by submitting detailed proposals on how to proceed with a selective cull of cattle under 30 months to Brussels as soon as possible.-- London Newsroom *44 171 542 7950</

12724 Commonwealth ministers gather in New York this weekend to decide whether to impose sanctions on Nigeria but officials say deepening splits among member states could torpedo the meeting."This is turning out to be a real mess," said one senior Commonwealth diplomat who asked not to be named.The eight-nation Commonwealth Ministerial
12724 Action Group (CMAG) agreed a set of sanctions against Nigeria in May to propel the military government toward democracy.But in June CMAG said the measures -- including a ban on sporting links and arms sales -- would be frozen until the New York meeting to give Nigeria a chance for
12724 further talks.The Commonwealth, a grouping of Britain and its former colonies and protectorates, suspended oil-rich Nigeria last November after the execution of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other minority-rights activists.CMAG members such as Canada are losing patience with the government of General Sani Abacha and say that only a hard
12724 line approach will bear results, but others take a softer approach.Relations among CMAG states were further eroded when the group called off a planned fact-finding mission to Nigeria last month after Abuja refused to let ministers meet human rights campaigners and opposition groups.Nigeria says it wants to discuss its suspension
12724 from the Commonwealth before expanding the dialogue to other topics.Some CMAG members such as Zimbabwe want the fact-finding mission to go ahead to keep the lines of communication open with Abuja but Canada and New Zealand say this would be pointless without guarantees of access to opposition members."None of us
12724 can see any great good news coming out of the New York meeting, whatever angle you look at it from," said a British official.Abacha last year set out a plan to restore civilian rule by October 1998, which CMAG says is too long.Some Commonwealth officials expressed irritation with Canadian Foreign
12724 Minister Lloyd Axworthy, saying he was needlessly antagonising the Nigerians."Axworthy seems to have lost the script on this one. He does not understand that the Nigerians are a very proud people and you have to try to flatter them by making them feel important," said one official who asked not
12724 to be identified.Axworthy, irritated by what he saw as Commonwealth inertia on Nigeria, announced after the June CMAG meeting that Canada would unilaterally apply the agreed sanctions.But most Commonwealth officials agree the measures are little more than an irritant and say only an embargo on oil sales -- which most
12724 observers said would be virtually impossible to impose -- could damage the Nigerian government.Diplomats said Washington was backing away from the idea of imposing its own sanctions on the grounds that such measures should be coordinated with the European Union, but this approach has not found favour everywhere."To be effective,
12724 the American approach should be backed by specific sanction threats," the New York Times said last week, calling for a ban on all U.S. investment. The United States buys 40 percent of its oil from Nigeria."Effective American diplomacy with Nigeria requires the threat and use of sanctions. General Abacha has
12724 proved to be the kind of man who listens to nothing else."CMAG comprises Malaysia, Zimbabwe, Jamaica, Ghana, Britain, New Zealand, South Africa and Canada.</

12750 Shares in National Westminster Bank rose on Wednesday after it said that it planned to securitise about five billion dollars of its corporate loans to release capital to the banking group, analysts said.By 0750 GMT the shares had added 5p to 666-1/2p.Overnight news that the U.S. Federal Reserve had decided
12750 to leave interest rates unchanged also helped lift banking stocks across the board as prices rebounded from Tuesday's bout of profit-taking ahead of the rate decision.Barclays shares rose 4-1/2p to 937p, Royal Bank of Scotland 12p to 483-1/2p and LLoyds 5p to 376-1/2p. The initial significance of the NatWest move
12750 was small, analysts said. NatWest already has a high Tier 1 capital adequacy ratio and will raise it by about 200 million stg by freeing capital via the removal of loans from the balance sheet.It also means that the reduction in future capital needed to support and expand the loan
12750 book will increase free cash flow by about 10 million stg a year on an ongoing basis, analysts said."It's a sound strategic move getting assets off the balance sheet but the capital significance initially and ongoing is reasonably small in terms of the group," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett banking
12750 analyst Steven Thorn. "The real interest is that it shows Natwest, after many years of lagging Barclays' strategy of very aggressively removing low margin loans from its balance sheet, are taking a very firm step in the same direction," he said.The move signalled that NatWest management were now committed to
12750 policies focused on shareholder value and as such was very good news, added Thorn.The transaction means NatWest will transform corporate loans into stg and dollar-denominated floating rate notes and commercial paper, issued into the Eurobond market as well as the U.S. 144A private placement market. NatWest said the securitisation would
12750 improve its Tier 1 ratio by about 0.2 percent. The ratio stood at 7.6 in July when the bank reported its first-half results.NatWest will start presentations to investors in London, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Bahrain, Dublin, Frankfurt and Luxembourg in early October to sell the securities.But NatWest's move is unlikely to
12750 spark a wave of securitisation in the industry with Barclays, in particular, already having done much to remove low margin lending from its balance sheet. The process itself is not innovative, though the size is, which, said Thorn, showed the commitment of Natwest to improving the return on the balance
12750 sheet and adding to shareholder value."Almost whatever they do with the money -- unless they make a very low return acquisition -- will increase shareholder value," said Thorn."This is just another piece in the jigsaw to suggest NatWest has turned the corner and that the large discount of the shares
12750 to the rest of the sector is unsustainable in the medium term."-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8712</

12754 High crude oil prices are expected to fuel strong third-quarter earnings in the Canadian oil and gas sector, although oil price hedging will temper the fortunes of several firms, analysts said.Average results for the sector, which has been a stock market bright light for several months, should exceed those posted
12754 in the third quarter of 1995 and the second quarter of this year, said Martin Molyneaux, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp. "Third quarter overall should look good operationally and very good financially," Molyneaux said. "Both commodities are headed in the right direction and volumes are up."West Texas Intermediate oil prices,
12754 driven by uncertainty surrounding the return of Iraqi oil to world markets amid Iraqi-U.S. conflict, have so far averaged US$22.16 a barrel in the third quarter.That is up from US$17.77 a barrel in the July-September period of 1995. Alberta spot natural gas prices, while showing much smaller gains than those
12754 in eastern North America, are also headed for a better quarter. Gas at Empress, Alberta has averaged C$1.27 per gigajoule this quarter, up from C$1.06 in the same period last year.But many Canadian producers are expected to realize higher gas rices because of longer term supply contracts and an ability
12754 to export gas into the more lucrative eastern Canadian and U.S. markets. Analysts at several investment houses, including FirstEnergy and CIBC Woody Gundy, said they expected busy drillers Renaissance Energy Ltd and Canadian Natural Resources Ltd to be among the producers showing the strongest results this quarter.Wood Gundy's Peter Linder
12754 said Renaissance, Canadian Natural and Crestar Energy Inc were expected to enjoy the full effects of high crude prices and strong growth in oil output.Canadian Natural's takeover of Sceptre Resources Ltd was made official during the quarter. Molyneaux said he also expected international producer Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd and heavy
12754 oil firm Elan Energy Inc to be among the profit leaders in the sector.Overall, production growth should be much stronger than in the second quarter, when an unusually long winter and spring breakup put a lid on drilling programs in western Canada, analysts said.Results from several companies, however, were expected
12754 to be overshadowed by hedging programs put in place before the crude oil price surge earlier this year. Companies that sold forward much of their crude production at prices that looked like premiums at the time of the deals, began to see potential fortunes erode in the second quarter, said
12754 ScotiaMcleod analyst Henry Cohen."It will be a big problem in the third quarter again," Cohen said.Companies projected to suffer from oil price hedging exposure include PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, Wascana Energy Inc, Petro-Canada and Alberta Energy Co Ltd.Integrated oil companies, including Petro-Canada, Shell Canada Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd, were expected
12754 to post weaker results in the quarter due to high feedstock costs for their refineries, and gasoline price wars, especially in Quebec and the Atlantic provinces, Molyneaux said.He said the exception would be Suncor Inc, which alone among the four major integrated firms, produces more oil than it processes.-- Reuters

12775 The United States is backing off a subsidy battle with the European Union over wheat exports but may not do so for long if world prices continue to suffer, grain traders said on Wednesday.Competition is growing fierce between exporters now that bumper crops in much of the world have cut
12775 wheat prices by as much as half from records set just five months ago, said traders at an industry gathering in southern Turkey."Things are going to be pretty rough in the next few months, especially when crops start arriving in Australia and Argentina (in December)," a senior grain executive predicted.The
12775 U.S. and Europe, two major exporters who traditionally use subsidies to shore up grain exports, suspended the aid last year as supplies tightened after a series of poor harvests that sent world grain stocks to 20-year lows.But pressure is growing on Washington to revert to export subsidies after the EU
12775 restored its own programme last week to shield its farmers from the new fall in world prices.The U.S. grain industry has already applied for help with exports of wheat flour, traders said.Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Tuesday he had not ruled out restoring Washington's so-called Export Enhancement Programme (EEP)
12775 but it was too early to do so yet.EU farm director-general Guy Legras also sounded conciliatory in comments made on Wednesday."Subsidies are destined to bring European prices in line with world prices and allow normal exports without any intention to cut prices or to be aggressive," he said. Benchmark wheat
12775 prices paid by importers have dropped to around $160 per tonne after almost $300 last year, traders said.Without subsidies, European wheat is worth closer to $180 per tonne while unsubsidised Argentine wheat is being promised ahead of harvest for as little as $140."People are buying hand-to-mouth at the moment. They
12775 are all waiting to see if prices keep going down," another trader said.If export subsidies are used in the coming year, it will be a long-awaited first test of the Uruguay Round global trade pact on agriculture which came into force last year, restricting aid.The pact commits the U.S. and
12775 Europe to reducing subsidised exports by 21 percent over six years to 2001. But it gathered dust for 12 months when subsidies unexpectedly disappeared.Analysts and even some of the agreement's negotiators believe it may still lack teeth, because last year's unused quotas of some 20 million tonnes of subsidised sales
12775 by each side can technically be added to this year's allocations.That would notionally set a ceiling far higher than either side's ability to export and leave room for a grain trade war. They must, however, reach the final targets on time in 2001.But while traders expect aggressive competition, few believe
12775 either Brussels or Washington is ready to return to a full-scale subsidy feud that ate up billions of dollars during the 1980s.A U.S. official told the conference in Turkey that Washington had been in touch with the European Commission in Brussels to try to steer it away from using subsidies.The
12775 EU appears to have ignored the advice, but modest initial aid worth less than $2 million suggests a soft-pedal approach, traders said."I don't think the Americans want to use EEP this year but it depends on what happens in the market. They won't stand back and see their market share
12775 fall to pieces," one trader said.</

12817 When Benjamin Netanyahu clasped the hand of his former enemy Yasser Arafat, Arabs hoped the ice that had shrouded Middle East peace talks since the Israeli election had been broken.Now, after 100 days of Netanyahu as Israel's prime minister, the chill in Israeli-Arab relations runs deeper.Netanyahu, who heads a coalition
12817 of conservatives, Jewish settlers and rabbis, has however thwarted critics who said he would freeze the peace process.He soon realised, political analysts and diplomats say, that to stand still meant displeasing his guardian ally the United States, which for five years has been nudging Arab and Jew towards a settlement
12817 on the basis of land-for-peace.So, after much hestitation, Netanyahu agreed to meet Palestinian President Arafat and resume talks on implementing the 1993 Oslo agreement on self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza signed by the ousted Labour government.The Clinton administration, which had openly backed Labour in the election, sighed with
12817 relief. In briefings, U.S. diplomats papered over the cracks in their own and Netanyahu's foreign policy, stressing that the new government was committed to Oslo but needed time to find its feet.Israeli officials expect the grace period with Washington to last until after the U.S. presidential elections in November as
12817 neither candidate wishes to be seen as tough on Israel.For the Arabs and Netanyahu's opponents within Israel, the new prime minister's honeymoon period is long past. They accuse his Likud-led government of substituting movement for action."Until now I don't know whether he is a man of talk or action," said
12817 political commentator Hanan Crystal. "The meeting with Arafat was a show. Until we see how he handles Hebron we will not know whether he has made the transition from a good political campaigner to statesman."Other analysts and Western diplomats agree Hebron will be the acid test for Likud's commitment to
12817 Oslo. Netanyahu has delayed redeploying Israeli troops in the West Bank town as agreed by Labour, citing security concerns, a mantra of the right-wing. Hebron is a microcosm of some of the most explosive issues still to be negotiated -- the future of Jewish settlements on Arab land and control
12817 of places holy to both Jews and Moslems.Honouring commitments like Hebron could cost Netanyahu right-wing support in his coalition. He could even lose cabinet ministers like Benny Begin, son of Menachem Begin, and staunch settlement supporter Ariel Sharon, analysts say.But Labour is still the single biggest party in parliament and
12817 would back Netanyahu on Oslo implementation.Analysts believe Netanyahu has little choice but to work with Arafat and the United States on the peace process, albeit without an explicit commitment to trade captured Arab land for peace. The question is how fast and how far."When we came in to office we
12817 were told that we would halt everything, nothing will move and so on," Netanyahu said when asked by reporters about Arab charges that his first 100 days had been "a disaster"."We said no, we come with a different agenda of how to achieve peace and we intend to negotiate. First,
12817 I said we will create informal contacts with the Palestinian Authority. We did. Secondly we'll create formal contacts on the ministerial level. We did. Thirdly we'll arrive at a package, a way, of addressing the outstanding issues. We did. And fourth we'll begin to negotiate on the key issues, all
12817 of them, including Hebron, and we're doing that."It's not a snail's pace advance," he said.Netanyahu's list does not impress Arabs who see him as stalling on Oslo while expanding Jewish settlement on Palestinian land and tightening Israel's grip on Arab East Jerusalem."This is a fictitious peace process of meetings without
12817 substance and action, while on the ground they carry out actions that totally negate the peace process," Palestinian cabinet minister Hanan Ashrawi said.Critics say Netanyahu's biggest achievement in the past 100 days has been to unite the Arabs. 12823 Plans to set up a sugar refinery at the heart of one of the world's biggest sugar-consuming regions have been expanded, with forecast annual capacity possibly doubled to 360,000 tonnes."We are now looking at 300,000-360,000 tonnes (a year)," sugar trader Ali Redha Darwish told Reuters on Wednesday.He and seven other
12823 prominent Omani businessmen are planning to set up the $70 million National Sugar Refinery (NSR) at Muscat's Mina Qaboos harbour by October 1998 to cash in on the Gulf's huge appetite for sugar.At about 30 kg per head, annual sugar consumption in the Arabian Peninsula is among the highest in
12823 the world.Much of the sugar is imported from Europe. "The biggest losers (from the new refinery) will be Europe," Darwish said.He and his partners will be competing in the region with the new Al Khaleej refinery in Dubai, which aims at 720,000 tonnes annual output, and a refinery in Jeddah,
12823 which plans to produce 500,000 tonnes a year from early 1997.But Darwish thinks there is room for all of them."The Saudi refinery will cater to about 90 percent of the Saudi market. If they reach their target, the Dubai refinery will be covering about 50 percent of the Gulf without
12823 Saudi."Demand for white sugar imports in the Gulf and Iran and Iraq, but excluding Saudi Arabia, is about 1.7 million tonnes."Even if the Dubai refinery comes to full production, there is plenty of room for both of us. We will have 1.1 million tonnes capacity between the two of us
12823 and demand of about 1.7 million tonnes."Neighbour Yemen was "the ace up our sleeve", Darwish said.The impoverished state imports about 600,000 tonnes a year mainly from South Africa, Thailand, Brazil and Europe, Darwish said, adding, "We have the advantage of proximity."Besides the huge regional market for sugar, Darwish said recently
12823 high white sugar premiums, lower freight costs for raw, versus refined, imports and cheap energy costs in oil and gas rich Oman were important incentives.But government approval to flatten a granite hill and build the plant within the port had not yet been secured and a final feasibility study was
12823 due soon.Once it gets the go-ahead, the firm would float 40 percent of its shares and list on the Muscat stock exchange, he said.</
12824 The United Nations will press on with resettling Iraqi Gulf War refugees who are increasingly frustrated with the desert camp in Saudi Arabia where they have spent five years, a U.N. official said on Wednesday."The resettlement programme will continue in 1997, which will be the seventh year at the camp
12824 for the remaining refugees, because there is no other solution," said Abdul Mawla al-Solh, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) representative in Saudi Arabia."Frustration (among refugees) is very high," he said in a telephone interview.Solh said 617 Iraqi refugees left for the United States on Monday and another 511
12824 are due to leave on Wednesday night and Thursday, leaving around 10,000 refugees at the Rafha desert camp.A U.S.-led coalition based in Saudi Arabia ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of Kuwait in February 1991. By mid-1991 about 32,000 Iraqi refugees remained in Saudi Arabia out of up to 70,000 refugees and
12824 prisoners of war.The camp was set up as a transit location until refugees, including soldiers who surrended, were resettled or repatriated.Solh said from June 1991 to the end of this September the UNHCR will have resettled 19,372 refugees, while 3,005 had over the last five years accepted to return to
12824 Iraq.He said delegations from Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Canada and Australia were due in the next two months to interview remaining refugees and decide who to resettle in their countries.Solh said Saudi Arabia, which has spent about 2.5 billion riyals ($666 million) for camp expenses including housing and services, has made
12824 it clear the refugees could stay until they are repatriated.An UNHCR official had said in July the refugees were losing hope of ever leaving, felt betrayed by the West and were growing increasingly fed up with the isolation at the camp, known as the "Refugee Hilton of the Gulf War".The
12824 camp is air conditioned and has schools and hospitals, but is ringed by barbed wire and the refugees are not allowed to leave.Three years ago 13 people were killed in a riot over the barring of new arrivals, but U.N. officials say since then there has been no trouble.</
12825 In his first 100 days in office, rightwing Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu has turned the Middle East clock back years, Arab leaders say.He has infuriated most of his Arab neighbours, driven Palestinians to despair and helped bring the word "war" back into the political vocabulary of the region.Gone is the
12825 goodwill which former prime minister Shimon Peres and his predecessor, assassinated leader Yitzhak Rabin, built up through three years of diplomatic footwork.Gone is the vision of a common Middle East market where, after more than 40 years of Arab-Israeli conflict, barriers to trade and travel might come tumbling down.Arab governments
12825 will not hurry to roll out red carpets for Israel's new leaders or open missions in the Jewish state.The Gulf state of Qatar has postponed plans to open a trade office in Tel Aviv, in one of the first overt steps away from normalising relations with the Jewish state.When a
12825 Middle East economic conference meets in Cairo in November, it is likely to be a subdued affair, quite unlike the peace jamboree the Egyptian hosts had hoped to organise."Back to square one" is the phrase on the lips of many an Arab minister and in the columns of Arabic newspapers."To
12825 come in 1996 with the same ideas as in the 30s, the 40s, the 50s and the 60s, that's dangerous... We cannot go along with it," said Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.In Arab eyes, the reason for the present sour and hostile mood in Arab-Israeli relations is simple -- Netanyahu
12825 has questioned the land-for-peace principle which has been at the heart of Middle East peace diplomacy since the 1970s, when Israel gave the Sinai peninsula back to Egypt.The Madrid peace conference in 1991, at which Netanyahu's Likud party represented Israel, took place on the same understanding. In contacts with Syria,
12825 the previous Israeli government had agreed in principle to give back all the Golan Heights, Israeli and Egyptian officials say.On top of that, the Arabs say, Netanyahu has failed to put into effect measures clearly agreed between Israel and the autonomous Palestinian Authority, such as redeploying its troops in the
12825 West Bank town of Hebron.Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, now firmly aligned with Syria in diplomatic confrontation with the Jewish state, has bluntly accused Netanyahu of reneging on commitments he made at their first meeting in July.All parties have been anxious to play down the risk of a shooting war but
12825 Syria has raised eyebrows in Israel by redeploying its forces in Lebanon and Israelis asked questions about this month's big military manoeuvres by Egypt.But short of war, an implausible course since they believe Israel has nuclear weapons, the Arabs have no easy options for persuading the new Israeli government to
12825 change its tune.The United States, which twisted Israel's arm to bring it to the Madrid conference, is out of the picture because of the presidential elections in November.Conventional wisdom is that U.S. presidential candidates dare not take on the influential pro-Israeli lobby.Egypt has tried a war of words, hurling epithets
12825 such as arrogant, impudent and stupid at Israel's new rulers. Some Arabs have played on Netanyahu's name, the first two syllables of which mean putrid in Arabic."I do not have a magic recipe," Moussa said in an interview this week. "But a start to serious action would be for the
12825 Arabs to stand together...and reject this approach of Netanyahu's."In June, Egypt organised the first Arab summit in five years, to coordinate the Arab response to the election of Netanyahu.It ended with a warning to Israel that Arab states would have to reconsider the gestures they have made towards Israel if
12825 Israel tries to change the ground rules for the peace talks.Arab foreign ministers met in Cairo again this month and recommended a course of action in a secret report to Mubarak.For the past 10 days Mubarak has been contacting other Arab leaders, either by telephone or by written message, but
12825 diplomats say they do not expect any dramatic decision.</

12830 Sales of existing homes fell modestly in August, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday, a third straight monthly decline as the housing market showed signs of leveling off.The real estate lobby group said sales of existing, or used, homes fell 0.5 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted annual
12830 rate of 4.13 million. That followed a revised decline of 0.2 percent to 4.15 million in July and a sharper 2.8 percent drop in June sales.The falloff in August existing-home sales was not quite as sharp as forecast by Wall Street economists, who had forecast a drop in the sales
12830 rate to 4.09 million a year.The real estate group revised up its estimate of July sales to an annual rate of 4.15 million instead of the 4.14 million it reported a month ago.Despite three months of weakening business, sales of existing homes in August still were 2 percent higher than
12830 a year earlier in August 1995, when they were selling at a rate of 4.05 million a year.Nonetheless, the falloff in sales last month occurred despite cheaper long-term mortgage rates that seemed to indicate some steam was going out of a robust housing market.The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or
12830 Freddie Mac, said the average rate for a 30-year mortgage loan in August was 8 percent, down from July's 8.25 percent average and June's 8.32 percent."The nation's housing market is easing in for a soft landing," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors. He added that
12830 after surging earlier this year, "it's only natural that the market will correct itself."Sales of existing homes peaked in May at a record annual rate of 4.28 million.A waning housing market would fit with Federal Reserve policy-makers' evident belief that the overall economy os slowing. On Tuesday, the Fed decided
12830 against raising interest rates in the apparent hope that the economy was likely to cool off on its own and so keep inflation in check.During August, sales of existing homes fell 9.5 percent in the Northeast to 570,000 a year while in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing market,
12830 they were down 1.9 percent to a rate of 1.53 million.But in the Midwest, August sales edged up 0.9 percent to a rate of 1.07 million a year and in the West they increased strongly by 5.6 percent to 950,000 a year.The average price for an existing home resold in
12830 August was $149,900, up slightly from $149,600 in July.</

12855 Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, was convicted on Tuesday on all but one count of illegally giving gifts and favors to then Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.The agricultural firm was also convicted of taking part in a scheme to funnel illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry
12855 and of two charges of wire fraud.The convictions -- the first to come out of the government's two-year investigation of the former Clinton cabinet member -- could have serious implications for pending cases in the probe and do not bode well for Espy and others still under investigation, legal experts
12855 said."Today's verdict reflects that juries are tired of what they regard as corruption in big business and government and it will give steam to the prosecutor's efforts to proceed further against other people in this matter," University of Georgetown law professor Paul Rothstein said."This gives our investigation some impetus," Independent
12855 Counsel Donald Smaltz, who is heading the widespread probe, told reporters after the verdict was announced. "Each case will be judged on its own merit ... but this should send a strong signal," he said.Sun-Diamond said it was considering an immediate appeal of the conviction. "Sun-Diamond has consistently maintained that
12855 its conduct and relationship with the former Secretary of Agriculture has been lawful and proper," it said.Espy lawyer Reid Weingarten said his client was not feeling any more pressure as a result of the verdict."I know that Mike Espy never provided any favors for Sun-Diamond ... I have complete confidence
12855 that at the end of the day, Mike Espy will be completely exonerated," he said.Sun-Diamond, whose affiliates include Sun Maid raisins, Sunsweet prunes and Diamond Walnut, had been charged with violating nine criminal counts involving illegal gratuities and illegal campaign contributions to Espy and his brother in 1993 and 1994
12855 while Espy headed the huge agriculture agency.He resigned as a cabinet secretary in 1994 amid accusations that he had taken illegal gifts and favors from companies his agency was charged to regulate.After deliberating for 9-1/2 hours over two days a jury found Sun-Diamond not guilty of only one of the
12855 counts, which alleged that the cooperative had paid transportation costs for Espy's girlfriend to accompany him to a conference in Greece.The government said the company, acting through its Washington lobbyist Richard Douglas, a close personal friend of Espy, used the enticements of expensive gifts and favors to Espy and his
12855 girlfriend and campaign contributions to Henry Espy to try to sway Espy on important issues.Sun-Diamond attorney Richard Hibey said the company was innocent of any wrongdoing and that the gifts, which included lavish meals, a luggage set and a weekend outing to the U.S. Tennis Open tournament in 1993, reflected
12855 the close friendship between Douglas and Espy, and nothing more.Legal sources said the verdict was an important victory for prosectors, who had been accused of over-reaching their authority and of investigating relatively insignificant discretions."This is a very substantial victory for the independent counsel," said former U.S. prosecutor Joseph di Genova.
12855 "This obviously gives validation to his efforts.So far the investigation has yielded five sets of criminal indictments and charges against more than a dozen individuals and concerns including the Washington lobbyist for Tyson Foods, the huge Arkansas-based chicken processor whose chairman has long had close ties with President Bill Clinton,
12855 a former governor of Arkansas.Tyson Foods has been a focus of the Espy investigation since the start after it was learned the firm gave Espy and his girlfriend tickets to Super Bowl playoffs in 1993 and a scholarship potentially worth almost $10,000 to the girlfriend.</

12858 A federal judge on Tuesday entered formal judgment on the $5 billion fine slapped on Exxon Corp by a jury two years ago as punishment for the disastrous 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.U.S. District Court Judge H. Russel Holland approved the punitive fine -- the largest assessed by a jury
12858 against a corporation -- along with compensation to commercial fishermen, accrued interest and a $5,000 punitive fine against former Exxon supertanker captain Joseph Hazelwood.The entry of judgment ended years of litigation at the District Court level, one plaintiff attorney said."This is the principle goal to which we have been striving
12858 for the last 7 1/2 years," said Dave Oesting, a lead attorney for the thousands of fishermen, Alaska Natives, property owners and others who sued the oil giant over the 11 million gallon (41.6 million litres) spill in Prince William Sound."We finally achieved closure at the trial court level of
12858 all aspects of this litigation," Oesting said.The formal entry of judgment allows Exxon to appeal the trial verdict to a higher court. The company said it will enter a notice of appeal within 30 days."During the past two years, Exxon has raised a number of legal issues concerning the trial.
12858 Exxon's arguments on these issues have not been accepted by the Federal District Court, but we believe they establish a strong record for appeal," Exxon Chairman Lee Raymond said in a company statement.Recent appellate and U.S. Supreme Court decisions had made Exxon optimistic about the outcome of an appeal, Raymond
12858 said."The puntive damages in this case are unwarranted and fail every legal or logical test of reasonableness. We believe that this judgment should be set aside or substantially reduced by the appellate court," he said.The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals is expected to hear the case in 1997, Exxon said.The
12858 entry of judgment also starts the accrual of interest on the $5 billion punitive award, Oesting said. The interest rate set by the court is 5.9 percent, he said.Holland's order approved $19.5 million in compensation -- the result of the $287 million that the jury ordered in payment to approximately
12858 10,000 commercial salmon and herring fishermen, minus credits for previous payments made by Exxon.The order also assessed the pre-judgment interest at $37.9 million, billed to both Exxon and Hazelwood. That interest accrued on the $287 million compensatory award, Oesting said.The totals result from a summer-long, three-phase trial conducted in Holland's
12859 Members of the jury pool for the O.J. Simpson civil trial split mostly along racial lines Tuesday, with whites saying he was probably guilty of murder and blacks convinced of his innocence.Reflecting America's racial divide over Simpson's acquittal last October on criminal charges, prospective jurors expressed strong opinions about whether
12859 the former football star was responsible for the 1994 killings of his former wife and a friend of hers.A white man who described all paid expert witnesses in the first trial as "whores" and a white woman who insisted she would have a hard time setting aside her belief in
12859 Simpson's guilt were among those accepted as potential jurors in the case.But the one panellist who received an unqualified stamp of approval from both sides was a black woman who professed near-total ignorance of the most highly publicised murder case in U.S. history.As jury selection became increasingly bogged down in
12859 lengthy questioning, Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki pressed attorneys to keep the process moving.Twelve regular jurors and eight alternates are needed to sit in judgment in the wrongful-death civil case brought against Simpson by the families of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman. Jury selection entered its fourth day Tuesday and was
12859 expected to last at least two to three weeks more.Simpson looked on attentively, scribbling notes and occasionally whispering to his attorneys. During breaks, he wandered into the spectators' gallery and bantered with reporters about football and golf, but steered clear of discussing the case."You got 12 lawyers working for a
12859 defendant who is flat broke. That's a phenomenal thing," he said jokingly in an aside to his bodyguard.Simpson, whose personal fortune was once estimated at $10 million, spent millions on his criminal defence, and the legal fees are now mounting for his civil trial. He could be forced to pay
12859 heavy damages if he loses the case.When the questioning got under way Tuesday, the racial divide between white and black jurors soon became clear.A black man in his 30s said he believed police had tampered with blood evidence in the case -- a major thrust of Simpson's defence in his
12859 criminal trial.A white man in his 40s and a white woman in her 50s both said they thought Simpson was "definitely guilty" of the murders. They were removed from the panel.A white man in his 60s said "professional witnesses" like forensics expert Henry Lee, who testified for the the defence
12859 in Simpson's criminal trial, were "whores" who will "say what they've been paid to say." He was allowed to stay on the panel over the defence team's strong objections.But it was Juror 39 who had courtroom observers scratching their heads when she said she knew almost nothing about Simpson's criminal
12859 trial, which was broadcast live on national television. "I'm not really sure of what went on," she said. "I didn't have time. I work and I have two kids."Stan Goldman, a Loyola University law professor, said attorneys in the case should be wary of such statements. "You never know when
12859 someone wants to get on the trial because they have a hidden agenda," he said.Out of the 15 people questioned Tuesday, seven -- three whites, two blacks and two Asian-Americans -- were allowed to remain in the jury pool. Those who survive the latest phase, designed to weed out panelsts
12859 prejudiced by publicity, will move on to the the next, in which they will be questioned about race, domestic violence and other issues.</
12860 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentThe U.S. Federal Reserve held off from increasing interest rates on Tuesday in what analysts described as a calculated gamble that the economy will slow before inflation starts to rise."Instead of raising rates, they've crossed their fingers," said Robert Brusca, chief economist for Wall Street broker
12860 Nikko Securities Inc.President Clinton hailed the central bank's decision, saying it showed that the economy was on track."I just think it shows we've got a strong economy with no inflation. I'm glad about that," Clinton told reporters during a campaign visit to New Jersey.The decision was good news for Clinton,
12860 who has been counting on a trouble-free economy in the run-up to the Nov. 5 election to help him win a second, four-year term.Wall Street's reaction was mixed. After surging in the immediate wake of the Fed announcement, share prices fell back on profit-taking following their recent record run. The
12860 Dow Jones industrial average closed 20.71 points lower at 5,874.Bond prices gained, with the pace-setting 30-year Treasury issue jumping nearly a half point, pushing the yield down to 6.98 percent from 7.02 percent Monday.Many analysts still expect the Fed to raise interest rates sometime in the coming months, possibly at
12860 its next policy meeting on Nov. 13 -- eight days after the election."If it hadn't been for the election, they probably would have raised rates," said David Wyss, of Massachusetts-based consultants DRI/McGraw Hill.As is its wont, the secretive Fed did not formally announce its decision to hold rates steady, but
12860 instead merely said that it had ended its meeting after 4-1/2 hours of talks."The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended at 1:40 p.m. (1740 GMT)," central bank spokesman Joseph Coyne said. "There is no further announcement."The bland statement hid what analysts believed was one of the more contentious meetings of
12860 the policy-making committee.Anti-inflation hawks at the Fed, particularly at its regional banks, have made no secret of their desire for higher rates to cool off the economy and head off inflation.Tuesday's decision left the federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight money at 5-1/4 percent and the
12860 discount rate the Fed charges banks for loans at five percent.The central bank has not changed either rate since Jan. 31, when it cut them both by a quarter percentage point.Fed policymakers were faced with conflicting evidence on the state of the economy when they met on Tuesday.By opting not
12860 to raise rates now, the Fed is hoping that economic growth will slow down enough on its own to head off the risk of higher inflation, analysts said.In the words of Fed Governor Janet Yellen, the economy is operating in an "inflationary danger zone." But so far there is no
12860 clear sign of higher inflation.At 5.1 percent, the unemployment rate is at its lowest point in more than seven years and at a level that in the past has often led to stepped-up wage demands and higher inflation.Wages, in fact, have already begun to pick up. But so far companies
12860 have been unable to pass through those higher labour costs to consumers in the form of price increases.Much will depend on the future course of the economy.In the second quarter, the economy grew at a 4.8 percent clip -- its fastest pace in two years and about twice the rate
12860 most analysts reckon is sustainable on a long-term basis without fanning inflation.Growth has slowed since then, as consumer spending, which accounts for about two-thirds of the economy, has slackened.But with consumer confidence at about a six-year high, labour markets tight and wages rising, some analysts -- and Fed anti-inflation hawks
12860 -- question whether the slowdown that is on its way will be enough to keep price pressures in check.The central bank was under considerable political pressure not to raise rates Tuesday, six weeks ahead of the election.Seventy eight lawmakers -- all but two of them Democrats -- wrote to Fed
12860 Chairman Alan Greenspan on Monday contending that a rate rise now would hurt, not help the economy.And Clinton administration officials have argued that inflation remained quiescent, strongly implying that they saw no need for the independent central bank to raise rates.</

12865 U.S. Representative Joseph Kennedy II (D-Mass) Tuesday unveiled a plan to increase home heating oil inventories to avert possible abrupt price hikes during the cold winter months.During a press conference at a Boston heating oil depot, Kennedy called on the Clinton Administration to sell off Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude
12865 oil and buy home heating oil to be released into the market in case of price spikes this winter."The stage may be set for a significant increase in retail prices for home heating oil and diesel fuel over the next several months," Kennedy said.The plan comes at a time of
12865 extremely low heating oil stock levels. Weekly reports by the Energy Information Administration and American Petroleum Institute show refiners' distillate inventories hovering 15 percent below five-year averages for this time of year.In the key East Coast region, distillate inventories are running 30 percent below year-ago levels.Kennedy said the low inventory
12865 leaves cold-weather states vulnerable to price hikes as high as 20 cents per gallon in case of severe cold."This could mean the average family having to pay $200 more this winter to keep warm. The impact would be felt by all consumers, but the burden would fall particularly hard on
12865 low income households and senior citizens, Kennedy said.Kennedy joined 21 senators and 19 representatives in sending a letter last Wednesday to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, asking whether the government could sell SPR crude to stem steep price jumps.--Patrick Connole, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1828</

12875 Miami expects a budget shortfall for fiscal 1997, but the size of the deficit will not be made public until city officials outline proposed remedies at a budget meeting on Thursday.Mayor Joe Carollo has said the shortfall is at least $25 million, or about 10 percent of the $250 million
12875 operating budget. Acting City Merrett Stierheim did not return Reuter calls over several days, but has already apprised rating analysts of the problem."What he told me specifically is they were identifying the size of the shortfall, there was a shortfall," said John Incorvaia, a vice president at Moody's Investors Service.
12875 "They're trying to identify the magnitude of the problem and they want to present that along with the remedies at the Thursday meeting."Incorvaia said Stierheim assured him the city would be able to make debt service payments on all of its bonds."They are not affected and they are fully budgeted
12875 for," he quoted Stierheim as saying.Moody's cut Miami's general obligation bond rating from A1 to single-A in 1992. Incorvaia said it was too early to tell whether the budget problem would have any credit impact."We're talking about a budget imbalance going into fiscal 1997, which they are on the front
12875 end of and they can make some response to it," he said.The city begins fiscal 1997 on Oct 1.An official at Standard &amp; Poor's Corp, which also rates Miami's GO debt single-A, said it was aware of the shortfall although the analyst involved was not available for comment Wednesday.City Manager
12875 Cesar resgined on Sept 12 after he was charged by federal prosecutors with bribery conspiracy in connection with city contracts. He had been scheduled to submit his budget to city commissioners that same day, and said at the time that the proposed budget was balanced.Incorvaia said he asked Stierheim whether
12875 the problems were on the revenue or expenditure side and "He suggested it was going to be a little of both."Last year the city was forced to eliminate 428 positions thorugh layoffs and early retirements in order to balance its budget.The city is near the state's 10-mill limit on property
12875 taxes for operating costs, and any effort to raise taxes or fees would be politically difficult in light of the corruption charges.City Commissioner Miller Dawkins was also charged in the bribery case, and prosecutors said former City Finance Director Manohar Surana had agreed to plead guilty on related charges.Surana resigned
12875 in August, shortly before federal prosecutors revealed he had worn a hidden wire to record conversations implicating Odio, Dawkins and a well-known lobbyist.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</

12880 U.S. homeowners who plan to stay in their homes at least five years are likely to refinance their mortgages when rates fall one to two percentage points, according to a survey of homeowners.The study, released by Mortgage Bankers Association of America (MBA), examined mortgage refinancing among 1,500 U.S. homeowners who
12880 originated or refinanced a home mortgage between January 1991 and March 1996.The survey was sponsored by MBA, Citicorp, First Union Corp, First Chicago NBD Corp and Norwest Corp.About 80 percent of respondents who planned to keep their homes for five years or more would refinance if mortgage rates fell one
12880 to two percentage points, the study found.More than half of survey respondents refinanced their original mortgages to take advantage of competitive rates and lower fees, MBA said.R.S. Carmichael &amp; Co Inc, a management consulting firm, conducted the study.--N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660</

12884 Widepsread rain was forecast for the U.S. central Plains and Midwest for the balance of the week, which should delay winter wheat planting in the Plains and corn harvest in the Midwest, meteorologists said.Rain and cold should also extend south across northern Texas, which may be detrimental to the sorghum
12884 and cotton."There is a tremendous rainfall event coming up for the corn belt," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather, who forecasts widespread amounts of 1/2 to two inches through Friday with three to four inches likely in localized areas. Similar rain amounts were forecast from now into the weekend
12884 from Nebraska to Texas. Across north Texas, the rain followed by low temperatures from the upper 30s (degrees Fahrenheit) to low 40s may be harmful to cotton."The cotton area down around Lubbock also will be turning colder...which is not very favorable," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.Low temperatures in
12884 the mid 30s were forecast for the western Midwest Friday and Saturday. The weather could produce scattered frost, but meteorologists doubt there will be widespread frost damage to corn and soybeans then. Cloudy skies with this week's rain system should prevent temperatures from dipping into low 30s across the Midwest,
12884 they said.Another cold system is likely next week.Weather Services' Burgio said a cold air mass should form in Canada early next week that could move south into the United States.Burgio said it is too early to forecast low temperatures but that the cold system bears watching.--Chicago newsdesk 312-408-8720--</

12918 A worldwide network to share information on air safety should be set up to swap and disseminate the wealth of data that already exists to make flying safer, a top industry official urged here Tuesday."We're going to have to find ways to close the door, leave the badges behind and
12918 share information about what causes aviation accidents," Edmond Soliday, vice president of corporate safety and security for UAL Corp's United Airlines told the Americas Conference on Aviation.If accident rates don't improve worldwide, the Boeing Co has projected that by the year 2015 with increased air traffic there will be a
12918 fatal air accident every eight to ten days, officials at the conference noted."We must find new ways to share information that are faster, more accurate, more comprehensive, more organized and more secure," Soliday said.One barrier to such cooperation is that many entities do not trust one another to share information,
12918 he said. Carriers do not trust their competitors or unions and nobody trusts the government, he said.Another speaker at the meeting of airline industry and public officials from throughout North and South America, Barry Bermingham, deputy assistant administrator for the Federal Aviation Administration, told of potentially dangerous quirks at some
12918 airports that "all the pilots knew about" and compensate for, but are not discussed. Eventually some of these problems have caused accidents, Bermingham said.Soliday urged the creation of some type of flight safety round table which would have no ties to any organization, manufacturer, airline or government. "The key ingredient
12918 to our success is trust," Soliday said.The Federal Aviation Administration is pushing a similar proposal it calls a Global Analysis and Information Network or GAIN."GAIN would make (safety information) available online to aviation safety researchers everywhere," said David Hinson, FAA administrator."GAIN has a lot of positive things going for it,"
12918 Soliday told Reuters, but "it rests on the expectation that people will freely give information. I think you have got to build trust before you build systems. You have got to bring people together first."Under Soliday's round table plan, information would be shared orally and "all information would remain the
12918 property of the participants. No raw data would be given up."But besides the roundtable idea, Soliday urged aviation participants to trust each other more and swap information informally."We (United) have shared our emergency response manual with at least 60 carriers," he said.</

12923 NEW YORK, Sept 24 - Standard &amp; Poor's lowered its ratings of the ITT Hartford group of companies (Hartford) as shown in the list below. The ratings outlook for ITT Hartford Group Inc. is stable.The rating action is based primarily on increased concern with the overall strength of Hartford's consolidated
12923 capital. Partially offsetting this is a superior business position within the markets that Hartford operates.While Standard &amp; Poor's expects capitalization to continue to improve from previous levels, it is now the company's view that such levels are no longer supportive of a double-A'-plus rating. This view incorporates the rapid growth
12923 in life revenue and assets, as well as risk-based capital measures and a destacked operating leverage tolerance (excluding affiliates) for Hartford Fire of 3 to 1, which Standard &amp; Poor's does not consider as acceptable for the prior rating.While capital needs should diminish, especially as the life subsidiary is able
12923 to self-finance its growth, Standard &amp; Poor's believes capital adequacy ratios will only gradually return to more supportive levels.Hartford Fire has enjoyed consistently strong operating results; however, returns on revenue have only slightly exceeded those of the industry over the last five years.Results during the first half of 1996 were
12923 impacted adversely by unusually high catastrophe losses experienced during the first quarter of the year.Operating performance of the life operations has been strong, with an average pretax return on assets of .70% over the past five years. Life earnings are supported by a low expense structure and well priced products.Hartford
12923 maintains a superior business position with a well-defined commercial lines book and AARP-endorsed personal lines products. Furthermore, Standard &amp; Poor's views Hartford Life as one of the leading annuity writers in the United States, with success in both fixed and variable markets.While premium growth in the domestic property-casualty businesses has
12923 been flat, consistent with the industry, growth in life premiums and deposits have been strong, increasing from $6 billion in 1991 to $16 billion in 1995. This strong growth continued through the first six months of 1996, with Hartford leading the market in variable annuity sales.EXPECTATIONSThis rating action assumes continued
12923 significant capital raising initiatives on the part of Hartford over the next year.These initiatives, in combination with continued improvement in operating earnings, excluding any unusual charges, should allow the group to improve its overall capital position. The spin-off from ITT has enabled the group to access external capital and gradually
12923 grow funds internally, as dividend requirements have been greatly reduced, Standard &amp; Poor's said. 12925 A federal judge on Tuesday entered formal judgment on the $5 billion fine slapped on Exxon Corp by a jury two years ago as punishment for the disastrous 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.U.S. District Court Judge H. Russel Holland approved the punitive fine -- the largest assessed by a jury
12925 against a corporation -- along with compensation to commercial fishermen, accrued interest and a $5,000 punitive fine against former Exxon supertanker captain Joseph Hazelwood.The entry of judgment ended years of litigation at the District Court level, one plaintiff attorney said."This is the principle goal to which we have been striving
12925 for the last 7 1/2 years," said Dave Oesting, a lead attorney for the thousands of fishermen, Alaska Natives, property owners and others who sued the oil giant over the 11 million gallon (41.6 million litres) spill in Prince William Sound."We finally achieved closure at the trial court level of
12925 all aspects of this litigation," Oesting said.The formal entry of judgment allows Exxon to appeal the trial verdict to a higher court. The company said it will enter a notice of appeal within 30 days."During the past two years, Exxon has raised a number of legal issues concerning the trial.
12925 Exxon's arguments on these issues have not been accepted by the Federal District Court, but we believe they establish a strong record for appeal," Exxon Chairman Lee Raymond said in a company statement.Recent appellate and U.S. Supreme Court decisions had made Exxon optimistic about the outcome of an appeal, Raymond
12925 said."The puntive damages in this case are unwarranted and fail every legal or logical test of reasonableness. We believe that this judgment should be set aside or substantially reduced by the appellate court," he said.The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals is expected to hear the case in 1997, Exxon said.The
12925 entry of judgment also starts the accrual of interest on the $5 billion punitive award, Oesting said. The interest rate set by the court is 5.9 percent, he said.Holland's order approved $19.5 million in compensation -- the result of the $287 million that the jury ordered in payment to approximately
12925 10,000 commercial salmon and herring fishermen, minus credits for previous payments made by Exxon.The order also assessed the pre-judgment interest at $37.9 million, billed to both Exxon and Hazelwood. That interest accrued on the $287 million compensatory award, Oesting said.The totals result from a summer-long, three-phase trial conducted in Holland's
12926 The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted on Tuesday to oppose a ballot initiative that would limit the ability of local governments to impose fees, assessments and taxes.The Board voted 3-2 to oppose Proposition 218, which will appear on the November 5 ballot.The proposition would require that a majority
12926 of local voters in an election approve any increase in general taxes. It would also limit local government's use of fees and assessments. Los Angeles County Chief Administrative Officer David Janssen warned the supervisors last week that the proposition would substantially reduce local government revenues, eliminate assessments and fee exemptions
12926 for all levels of government and increase governmental operating costs.He said the measure would effectively eliminate the library assessment and put the fire protection district assessment at risk."Proposition 218 threatens the reliability of any tax, assessment, fee, or charge based on revenue source, as the electorate is granted initiative authority
12926 to reduce or repeal any such tax, assessment, fee or charge," Janssen said.In a separate development, proponents and opponents of Proposition 218 testified in Sacramento, Calif., before a joint state Senate panel about the impacts of the proposal.</

12931 U.S. wheat export sales have been running at a breakneck pace in the early 1996/97 marketing year, but analysts said Tuesday that won't last much longer."For the months of June, July and August, the main competitors that we have -- the EU and Canada -- were completely out of the
12931 market," said Charlie Sernatinger, vice president of Chicago grain sales for Man International. "They felt that their end-of-season stocks were below pipeline levels." Joe Christopher, a wheat analyst at LFG in Kansas City, said a good percentage of the U.S. export book to date was built in late spring, when
12931 prices were "astronomical and going higher all the time.""A lot of people -- knowing there weren't any other available stocks in the world -- came here and booked out ahead a little and got some coverage," Christopher said."We also ran the (May/July) inverse to a record high and forced a
12931 lot of people to cancel April/May commitments and move them into June, and so we had a big June/July book," Christopher said. But analysts said U.S. dominance of export sales has already started to shift as competitors such as Europe, Australia and Argentina head toward near-record wheat harvests."Only in the
12931 month of September have the Europeans begun to become sellers and they're only selling for November forward," Sernatinger said. "The Canadians started shipping aggressively this month."Christopher predicted that U.S. wheat export business will "drop off considerably" in coming months as European and Canadian exports resume. Bill Tierney, Kansas State University
12931 extension economist, said current U.S. wheat export commitments as a percentage of total projected exports represents "one of the largest sales as a percentage of annual as of this date."Tierney said that as of last Thursday, 1996/97 U.S. wheat export commitments of 566 million bushels constituted 64 percent of his
12931 projection for total 1996/97 wheat exports of 885 million bushels.That compares to a 20-year average of 52 percent for the same mid-September period. Tierney based his projected total 1996/97 U.S. wheat export figure on USDA's September wheat export estimate of 925 million bushels, except that he subtracted 40 million bushels
12931 for wheat products such as flour."The USDA does not provide a separate projection for product and grain, so I had to guesstimate product since export commitment figures...are for grain only," he said.Tierney said he calculated export commitments of 566 million bushels by adding export inspections to date plus undelivered sales
12931 as reported in last Thursday's USDA export inspection report. Turning to wheat by class, Tierney said hard red winter wheat export commitments as of Thursday were 188 million bushels -- about 77 percent of his projection of total HRW wheat exports of 245 million bushels.His calculated ratio of 77 percent
12931 compares to an average HRW wheat ratio of 51 percent over the last 20 years.Tierney's ratio for soft red winter wheat export commitments versus total projected SRW wheat exports was also 77 percent, compared to the 20-year average of 66 percent.The ratio for dark northern spring wheat was 58 percent,
12931 compared to the average of 49 percent. Evidence of current tightness in winter wheat supplies can be seen in the most recent data on Kansas City Board of Trade deliverable wheat stocks.The KCBT said Tuesday that as of September 20, there were 6.564 million bushels of deliverable wheat stocks in
12931 the Kansas City area, a little more than half of the 11.743 million bushels in deliverable position a year ago.--Greg Frost, 816 561-8671</

12940 Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton said she will draft a special welfare reform bill for the District of Columbia, saying the law recently passed by Congress to reform welfare nationwide would compound the District's financial problems.Norton, the District's non-voting representative in Congress, wrote to Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala
12940 asking the Clinton administration for help in drafting the bill. Norton said the new welfare law, which was signed by President Clinton last month, was "based on a federal-state model that is wholly inapplicable to the District.""The difference is that other cities have states that will act as safety nets,
12940 while the District lacks any state," Norton said.The new law requires that next year every state and the District put 25 percent of it welfare recipients to work or lose up to 5 percent of its federal welfare funds. Last week, the Clinton administration withdrew its approval of a waiver
12940 that would have softened some effects of the bill on the District. Norton argued that the new law leaves the city in a "virtually impossible position -- enforce an unenforceable bill ... or face increasing annual losses of federal funds, guaranteed to compound the District's insolvency."A spokeswoman for Shalala said
12940 the department had received the letter. "All I can really tell you is we plan to provide the District as well as all 50 states the assistance they need to implement the new law," Shalala's spokeswoman, Melissa Skolfield, said.</
