12951 U.S. Treasury securities prices ended higher on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve decided not to lift interest rates.The decision mildly surprised the market where many had thought recent wage gains and a low unemployment rate were forerunners of inflation that would persuade Fed officials to raise rates at Tuesday's much
12951 anticipated policy meeting.In the half hour before the Fed released its statement, prices climbed about a third of a point from levels that had been nearly unchanged on the day. On news the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left rates untouched, the market doubled that gain then receded. The bellwether
12951 30-year bond rose 3/4 point, then cut its gain to end at 97-1/32, up 14/32, to yield 6.99 percent."The kneejerk reaction was the simple one in which the market rallied to news that rates are going to be held steady for a time but then prices backed down from their
12951 peaks on the thought that the Fed is doing experiments with inflation and that it's not as vigilant on inflation as perhaps it should be," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. Short-term bill rates, which are most responsive to near-term Fed policy adjustments, fell sharply as
12951 prospects for higher official interest rates receded at least until the Fed's next policy meeting in November, analysts said.Three- and six-month Treasury bill rates fell 20 basis points and 14 basis points, respectively, closing at 4.97 percent and 5.15 percent."This puts us right back to square zero with people handicapping
12951 what November's meeting will result in," said economist Neal Soss, senior advisor to CS First Boston Corp. "You'll be dealing with a 5-1/4 percent Federal funds rate until November at the earliest," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.Samuel Kahan, president of
12951 A.S.K. Financial Research Ltd., said the Fed had relied on "the basic assumption that the economic numbers are suffiently mixed that a case can be made for the economy's moderation in the future."Kahan said that "if one believes the retail sales reports, it looks like third-quarter GDP (gross domestic product)
12951 will come in around two- or 2.5 percent or so." Second-half GDP growth of two percent or less would probably assuage most inflation concerns in the market.Kahan said the second element of the Fed's decision to hold rates steady is that so far, inflation has not accelerated."There may be fear
12951 of inflation, but the most telling feature is that the core CPI (Consumer Price Index) and the other general price indicators have remained virtually unchanged despite the fact that the unemployment rate has been below the six-percent mark for two years and is now almost a full percentage point below
12951 that at 5.1 percent," Kahan said. Elliott Platt, managing director, economic research at Donaldson, Lufkin &amp; Jenrette, said the big risk to the market now is the arrival of stronger-than-anticipated economic data.Platt, himself, expects upcoming reports on durable goods orders, new home sales and September payroll growth to be subdued.Anything
12951 contrary to that would set the market back, he said."That's the big risk," Platt said. "Let's say the September payrolls report is strong and the next CPI is up 0.3 percent. The market could have a horrible case of indigestion which would have been mitigated by some sort of pre-emptive
12951 rate hike by the Fed. But the Fed apparently thinks it's a risk worth taking."At the close, the year bill rate was down 12 basis points to 5.40 percent. The two-year note was up 6/32 to 99-31/32, yielding 6.14 percent, the five-year note up 12/32 at 99-31/32, yielding 6.51 percent
12951 and the 10-year note up 15/32 at 101-24/32 to yield 6.75 percent. -- 212-859-1679</

12966 interest."If I find negative things happening, I will revoke the compact," Glickman said. "If it was used to raise milk prices to consumers, particularly poor consumers, or prejudice the free flow of milk between regions, I will revoke the compact." The Compact, an item of dispute for six years that
12966 finally made it into the 1996 federal farm policy law, empowers a six-state commission to raise the price of fluid milk bound for retail stores by up to 25 percent.The states involved are Massachusetts, Maine, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Vermont and Rhode Island.Proponents said it would help northeast dairy farmers stay
12966 in business and assure adequate local milk supplies. But opponents including consumer groups said it will raise milk prices, inspire other regional "milk plans" to protect farm incomes, and prevent the free market from setting prices. 12966 of the deal."Secretary Glickman's decision to authorize the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact is a direct attack on Wisconsin dairy farmers," Thompson said in a statement widely circulated by his office in this leading dairy producing state.But Glickman rejected that assertion."Dairy policy is more complicated than nuclear physics," Glickman said. "The
12966 compact will have no impact specifically on Wisconsin. It's just not that big of a factor in the marketplace."Glickman added that the legislatures and governors of each of the six Northeast states had approved the deal and consumer surveys had shown 92 to 95 percent approval of it."I didn't have
12966 much choice but to approve it," he said.(Emily Kaiser 312 408 8720)</

12969 Using an arcane financial instrument for his re-election campaign, President Bill Clinton on Wednesday will outline plans to issue Treasury bonds that are protected against inflation.Clinton is to announce the plan during a campaign appearance at Robert Morris College in Pittsburgh. The Treasury Department plans to begin offering the new
12969 securities in January.The president is promoting the new bond in terms of helping Americans pay for the cost of education, but officials stressed they might also help families save for retirement or first homes.They will be offered in denominations as low as $1,000, putting them within the reach of average
12969 Americans. The bonds will offer protection against inflation by having an interest rate that is pegged to the rate of inflation, as opposed to regular Treasury bonds, whose fixed interest loses value when the cost of other things goes up."The goal is to provide an investment which has an insurance
12969 policy against inflation," a senior administration official said. "We think this is going to be attractive to a lot of people."This type of bonds has never been offered in the United States but has been used in Canada and Britain. Officials expect individuals as well as pension funds to purchase
12969 them as a safe part of a whole portfolio.The officials said Clinton will also announce plans to broaden the savings bond programme to add some inflation protection to regular savings bonds, which can be purchased for as little as $50.How the complicated world of U.S. Treasury bond issues has entered
12969 the hurlyburly of a U.S. presidential election is a case study in the powers of incumbency.Knowing that the bonds were under study, Clinton is using them to enliven a campaign trip and stress saving for education, home ownership and retirement -- themes he has repeatedly evoked during this election year.Treasury
12969 Secretary Robert Rubin announced on May 16 that the Treasury planned to issue the inflation-indexed bonds as a multi-year experiment and was studying precisely what form they might take. The securities are designed to strengthen national savings by offering people an investment that guarantees a return that exceeds inflation. The
12969 Treasury also expects them to cut its financing costs.</

12986 NATO countries moved closer on Wednesday towards a commitment to keep thousands of troops in Bosnia next year after the mandate of the current peace mission runs out on December 20.NATO diplomats said the Atlantic alliance's 16 defence ministers, meeting informally in this Norwegian port city, accepted that some sort
12986 of force would probably be necessary to stop the country slipping back into war."Nobody said we did not need a Bosnia force...it is an option which can no longer be kept in the background," one NATO official said. "There was an overwhelming consensus that although we have achieved a lot,
12986 we have not achieved enough to say that peace has been achieved," he added.Alliance diplomats said the ministers wanted the military to begin a study of the tasks that any force would be required to undertake and the risks it would face, but said it was premature to discuss its
12986 size or mandate."We must decide on force aims before we can even discuss its size," a senior alliance diplomat told Reuters.NATO sources said that, although U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry did not explicitly say U.S. troops would be in the force, there was broad agreement that it would include the
12986 same countries as the current Implementation Force (IFOR).The U.S. now has 15,000 troops serving in the 52,000-strong IFOR force, which was sent in last December to police the Dayton peace accords. Britain and France, the other main contributors, would not remain without a U.S. ground presence.The issue is sensitive in
12986 the United States ahead of the November 5 presidential election there. President Bill Clinton originally said the troops would be home by the end of the year.NATO officials said the military would be instructed at the next meeting of the alliance's policy-making North Atlantic Council to start work on four
12986 options for 1997.These would involve:-- total withdrawal of existing force in line with the current political instructions.-- a deterrence force limited to preventing an outbreak of fresh fighting.-- a deterrence force with a wider mandate to provide a general security framework in which emerging civilian structures could begin to function.--
12986 a force fulfilling deterrence and giving much wider support to civilian reconstruction efforts, including freedom of movement for refugees and returnees."There was a general consensus that the force has to have the freedom to do its job," the official said, adding that ministers all insisted on the need to have
12986 continued Russian involvement in the follow-on force.He also said that the allies all agreed any new force must conform with the requirments of Dayton, be equipped with a U.N. mandate, have the full consent of all parties and have the means to protect itself.The defence ministers, leaving some of the
12986 more delicate issues to be resolved by foreign ministers, said any new force could only be despatched as part of a wider political framework setting out the international community's medium-term aims.They also stressed it must have a clear timetable for handover to civilian authorities and avoid any "open-ended commitment to
12986 maintain a force" in the Balkan country.NATO sources said NATO's Supreme Allied Commander in Europe (SACEUR), General George Joulwan, had briefed the ministers on the need to move from an implementation to stabilisation force, but wanted "clear political instructions". "Joulwan kept stressing the need for clarity," one diplomat said.Other diplomats
12986 said there was a general acceptance that the coming year could produce more problems than this year with the return of refugees and the emergence of legitimate institutions complicating NATO's work.The ministers also agreed the current force would not begin a withdrawal until after municipal elections, now set for late
12986 November. Officials said the alliance was committed to providing the same sort of security blanket it gave to countrywide polls on September 14, but emphasised any postponement would not delay the start of the current withdrawal plans.</

12991 EFTA COURTINFORMATION NOTE PREPARED BY EFTA COURTDOCUMENT DATE: SEPTEMBER 25, 1996EFTA Court gives two rulings on important issues of European labour lawOn 25 September, 1996, the EFTA Court rendered two advisory opinions on the Interpretation of Council Directive 77/287/EEC of 14 February, 1977, on the approximation of the laws of
12991 the Member States relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses. The Court held that (1) depending on the circumstances the replacement of a service provider may constitute a transfer in the sense of the directive and (2) an
12991 obligation of the transferor to pay premiums to a supplementary pension scheme concerning old-age, invalidity and survivor's benefits it not transferred.The Gulating Court of Appeals and the City Court of Stavanger in Norway had requested advisory opinions in cases pending before them.The case before the Gulating Court of Appeals concerns
12991 a claim by Mr Eilert Eidesund that his present employer, Stavanger Catering A/S, should pay certain pension insurance premiums, which his former employer had paid into an insurance scheme, apparently on the basis of a local collective agreement with the employer. A similar action was brought by Mr Torgeir Langeland
12991 against Norske Fabricom A/S. Mr Eidesund had been employed by a company providing catering and cleaning services, Mr Langeland by a company providing plumbing services, on oil-drilling platforms in the North Sea. In the case Eidesund, after termination of the service contract a new company, Stavanger Catering A/S, obtained a
12991 contract to provide the same services. In the case Langeland, the undertaking was purchased by a new service provider, Norske Fabricom A/S.The Court of Justice of the European Communities has been occupied with the concept of transfer in Article 1 of the directive in numerous cases. But none of these
12991 cases deal directly with the situation where an alleged transfer consists of a succession of two independent service providers. The EFTA Court noted that the supply of services or goods to one among several customers would normally not qualify as a distinct part of the supplier's business within the meaning
12991 of the directive. The same holds true of the loss of one customer to a competing company.The EFTA Court held that Article 1 (1) of the Directive is to be interpreted so as to mean that, where catering services for an undertaking have by contract been entrusted to a company,
12991 the termination of that contract and the conclusion of a new contract for the same services with another company does not exclude the directive from being applicable. In order to determine that there is a transfer of undertaking in the meaning of the directive, an economic entity with its own
12991 identity must be transferred and this identity must be retained. In order to ascertain whether these conditions are fulfilled in a case such as the one at hand, it is necessary to determine whether or not tangible assets, such as buildings and moveable property, or intangible assets, such as patents
12991 or know-how, are transferred, the value and the nature of the assets, whether or not a majority of the employees, or employees with a special expertise or experience, are taken over, whether customers are transferred, the degree of similarity between the activities carried an before and after the transfer, and
12991 the period, if any, for which the activities were suspended.The EFTA Court further ruled that according to Article 3 (3) of the directive, the employer's obligation to pay premiums to supplementary pension schemes for an employee is not transferred to the new employer. The accrual of pension benefits and the
12991 payment of pension premiums are inseparable. It would be without any economic sense to require premium payments to be made when no further benefits are to accrue. From this must follow that the transferor's obligation to pay premiums towards old-age, invalidity and survivors' benefits, is excluded from the transfer.Further information
12991 is available from Meinhard Novak, Legal Secretary at the EFTA Court (Phone 352 42108 323 - Fax 352 434389). It should be noted that no comment on the cases can be made by the Court.</

12996 by his new government's 42 ministers and deputy ministers.Simitis, 60, won Sunday's national election and has formed a cabinet which mixes experienced ministers with a new generation of reformers who helped to put him in power.A reserved technocrat who studied economics in Germany and Britain, Simitis steered the socialists safely
12996 into a new era when he succeeded party founder and legend Andreas Papandreou as prime minister in January.The ceremony marked the formal start of the post-Papandreou era, with a new generation socialist leader and his hand-picked cabinet setting a firm pro-Western course and turning their back on Papandreou's unpredictable, anti-Western
12996 ways.Political commentators had predicted the socialists would be torn apart after the departure of Papandreou, who forged the powerful party from various leftist factions after a military junta fell in 1974.Papandreou, revered by the left, was elected Greece's first socialist prime minister in 1981. 12996 1993 but resigned in poor health in January. He died in June.Simitis has called on Greeks to work hard, make sacrifices and meet European Union economic targets. 13001 Elderly cancer patients are being denied radiotherapy because of a misconception that older people cannot tolerate the treatment, according to a new study presented by cancer experts on Wednesday.Speaking at an international conference on cancer in Vienna, Pierre Scalliet, Professor of Radiotherapy at Belgium's Cliniques Universitaires St-Luc, said the study
13001 showed patients should be evaluated on their state of health, not their age."A heavy drinker and smoker aged 40 will be much less healthy than many 80-year-olds. Age by itself is not a basis for selecting treatment," he told Reuters.The study involving some 13,000 cancer patients in Europe aged between
13001 40 and 80 provided the first data showing no major difference in the way old and young people responded to radiotherapy, he said.Patients with thoracic, pelvic and head and neck cancer were monitored in 20 trials by the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC).Survival was comparable in
13001 each age group, and only older patients who received thoracic radiation suffered greater toxicity, or side-effects, than younger patients."But this was temporary and not significant -- certainly no reason to differentiate between age groups," Scalliet said.He said the number of cancer patients would rise dramatically in the next 10 years
13001 as more people in Europe reached old age, and doctors needed to be prepared to cope with the change."Cancer is a time-bomb as far as infrastructure and medical training is concerned," he said, noting the number of cancer patients was likely to increase by around ten percent by 2007."We need
13001 to be able to plan ahead or we won't be able to cope with the increase. There are enough doctors but not enough specific training in the treatment of elderly patients," he added.Cancer experts on Monday told delegates at the four-day European Society of Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology conference that
13001 about half of all cancer patients survive and that 40 percent of those have received radiotherapy.But despite the evidence, doctors in Europe generally remained cautious about recommending radiotherapy and were unaware of its benefits, they said."Radiation is a well established treatment already responsible for saving five million Europeans alive today,"
13001 said Jens Overgaard, Professor of Oncology at Denmark's Aarhus University.</

13022 Organisation and former Eastern bloc countries -- and also has observer status within the Western European Union (WEU), the future defence arm of the EU.Vranitzky said, however, that these links -- along with Austria's participation in peacekeeping forces in Cyprus and Bosnia -- did not affect neutrality.The EU is debating
13022 closer defence links as part of the inter-governmental conference (IGC), the EU's reworking of its treaties,Negotiators have been considering amending the treaties to involve the EU, using the WEU, in peacekeeping and humanitarian missions.Finland and Sweden, which along with Ireland make up the bloc's other neutrals, have promoted this idea.
13022 Vranitzky was non-commital about the plan.Austria, perched on the former Cold War border between the feuding Eastern and Western blocs, has been neutral since 1955, when it drew up its post-World War Two constitution.The Soviet Union, which occupied Austria after the war with allies Britain, France and the United States,
13022 demanded Austria enshrine neutrality as a central pillar of its national charter before it agreed to withdraw its troops.</

13030 Bundesbank Deputy President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Wednesday that it was in Germany's interest to convert existing government debt into Euros from the start of the planned 1999 launch of the single currency.Such a move would secure sufficient market liquidity for bonds and prevent a split in the market
13030 which would lead to a loss of liquidity and competitiveness, Gaddum said in a speech.Germany has yet to decide when to transform its existing bonds into Euros.Gaddum also said he was optimistic the government would one day be able to announce its bond issue plans for a full year, thereby
13030 meeting international standards. At present it announces issue calendars each quarter."Beyond the regular quarterly issue calendar there is really only the question when and perhaps if the government will issue (10-year or 30-year) bonds," Gaddum said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery at a stock market conference."But
13030 here too we are confident that refined fiscal planning will one day permit a complete annual calendar, which has become the international standard in recent years."Gaddum also said preparation for the introduction of stripping -- separate trading of principal and interest for certain bonds -- was well under way and
13030 that he was confident it would be launched next year as announced."That will enable institutional investors in particular to cover the whole of the yield curve," Gaddum said.Germany this year started issuing short-term government debt to boost market liquidity and help develop the bond market ahead of the Euro's launch
13030 when it will lose its main attraction, the mark.The government also pledged to issue 30-year debt each year provided market conditions allowed it."If the federal government carries out its intention to serve the 30-year segment of the market once a year, we believe that as regards instruments and issue procedures
13030 we will be able to meet all challenges arising from the disappearance of the mark," Gaddum said.--David Crossland, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525</

13031 too much power through their large stakes in industrial companies, but coming stock market legislation is widely expected to avoid rigorous measures like slapping a limit on banks' shareholdings.Gaddum said that even though lawmakers, market organisers and major players had done much to prepare the share market for global competition,
13031 it still lacked breadth and depth.The market could become more attractive if there were more joint stock companies and if existing share stakes were more widely distributed, he said."It would be desirable if banks took suitable companies public more often than they have done in the past...," Gaddum said. 13031 would partly deflate the recurring debate about banking power and would also contribute to strengthening and reviving the German stock market."The speech was due to be delivered at a stock market conference in Bonn."Not only are there not enough listed shareholding companies," Gaddum said. 13031 companies is in the firm hands of family shareholders, banks, insurers and other companies."This part of capital is fundamentally unavailable for stock market trade."The resulting lack of shares explained why trade concentrated on relatively few liquid stocks and why the share prices of small and medium-sized businesses were often subject
13031 to large price swings, Gaddum said.But he had praise for the German system of universal banks, saying the tradition of close ties between banks and industrial companies had proved an important stabilising factor in Germany's corporate scene.In addition, banks sometimes had good reason for buying and holding on to industrial

13052 use the legislation as a way to force more flexibile working conditions into Germany.The new policy, which was part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's austerity plan to boost weak employment and whip Germany's finances in shape for European currency union, will likely lead to more labour unrest during the fall, union
13052 leaders said.IG Metall said it was planning protests against the new law, including a nationwide metal workers union protest day on October 10. 13052 on Tuesday had called on employers and unions to avoid escalating the fight over sick pay and said the two should resolve their differences in negotiations.At the centre of the debate is the issue of whether the government's sick pay laws are meant to apply to existing contracts or only

13053 that was bang in line with expectations," Gwyn Hacche, senior economist at HSBC James Capel in London, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a rise in gross domestic product (GDP) of 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter, 1.9 to 2.0 percent year-on-year.The quarterly figures actually came in somewhat lower
13053 at 0.5 percent, but this was partly due to revisions of the first quarter data, Hacche said.The National Statistics Institute (INE) said first quarter growth had been revised to a rise of 0.6 percent quarter-on-quarter, 2.0 percent year-on-year, compared with the previous figures of 0.8 percent and 1.9 percent respectively.Spanish
13053 analysts said the figures mean the government is likely to achieve its 1996 growth target of 2.3 percent, a forecast it relies on to reduce the 1997 budget deficit to the level required to join a single European currency.The data also leave the Bank of Spain free to focus on
13053 the 1997 budget due to be presented on Monday and which is expected to be followed by a rate cut the day after."(Recovery) in the third and fourth quarters will help us reach a growth rate of 2.3 or 2.25 percent for 1996 and a number around 2.5 percent in
13053 1997," Alfredo Urrutia, capital markets economist at Societe Generale in Madrid, told RFTV."The scenario for rates remains the same," said Carmen Hernansaez, economist at FG in Madrid. "The Bank of Spain is more focused on politics and the upcoming budget."Some analysts doubted, however, that Spain could meet its growth and
13053 budget deficit targets."I personally doubt that the government can reach 2.3 percent this year and I think there is a risk that for next year, the figure may fall below 2.5 percent," said Hacche.He forecast Spain's budget deficit would fall below four percent of GDP next year but fail to
13053 satisfy the Maastricht target of a 3.0 percent ratio needed to join the first wave of monetary union (EMU) in 1999. He thought the government might also miss its inflation target of 2.6 percent in 1997.Others, like Alfredo Urrutia, said Spain could narrowly miss the three percent budget deficit target
13053 in 1997 but would join a single currency in a second membership phase."I think Spain will come pretty close to the mark (on next year's budget deficit target). It has a chance to make it not on Day One, but on Day Two", he said.Analysts said the recovery in private
13053 consumption remained the main motor for growth in the second half of the year. 13053 annual growth target, and the rise in exports with a strong revision of first quarter figures."The INE said exports rose 9.1 percent in the second quarter and revised the first quarter figure up to 8.7 percent from 5.3 percent previously.</

13056 linked the baptism of Frankish king Clovis to France's 1,500-year history as a nation.He had avoided doing so at an outdoor mass for 200,000 worshippers in the cathedral city of Reims on Sunday, winning praise from French commentators for skirting a clash over the country's religious and secular traditions.Addressing pilgrims
13056 from his native Poland, the Pope said:"When in 1980 I visit the Church of France for the first time I asked the following question: "France, what have you done with your baptism after 15 centuries?'. This visit, this pilgrimage, has been a magnificent response."He said at the end of his
13056 remarks: "Dear pilgrims, give thanks with me for this beautiful, marvellous response to the baptism of a nation which is very close to us (in Poland) and which shows great sympathy for us."Clovis was a central figure in French history before the 1789 Revolution abolished the monarchy. Born in what
13056 is now Belgium, he was baptised in Reims around 496.He ruled from eastern France to the Netherlands and Germany and extended his kingdom in battles against tribes such as the Visigoths to cover most of modern France.French secularists had accused the Pope of violating a 1905 law separating church and
13056 state by holding the mass in Reims to mark the anniversary of the Clovis baptism, which the extreme-right National Front portrays as France's "birthday".Protest marches against the visit in Paris and other cities, however, were low key.The Pope upset France's other religious groups on his first visit in 1980 when
13056 he spoke of France's 1,500-year history as a nation. "France, eldest daughter of the Church, what have you done with the promises of your baptism?" he asked then.He did not refer to France as "eldest daughter of the Church" neither during his latest visit nor at Wednesday's audience.</

13107 A leading human rights group on Wednesday accused Sweden, long known for its open door immigration policy, of treating asylum seekers unfairly in recent years.Human Rights Watch alleged that under its tough, new approach on immigration Sweden has rejected asylum seekers without giving their cases a fair hearing."In recent years
13107 Sweden has sent asylum seekers back to some of the world's worst trouble spots after concluding that their asylum claims were "manifestly unfounded'," a report by the U.S.-based group said.It added that Sweden had set up a number of increasingly restrictive policies in reponse to a sharp rise in the
13107 number of asylum seekers in the 1990s.Sweden had no limits to how long a person could be held in custody while decisions were made about their application, and, although not detained in bad conditions, they were treated like criminals, it said.Some were held for more than a year," it added."Sweden
13107 detains some asylum seekers in remand prisons where they are fully integrated with common criminals and subject to a criminal detention regime," the report said.Sweden's open-door immigration policy made it a haven for immigrants from the 1960s onwards and now nearly one in eight of the 8.8 million people living
13107 in Sweden are immigrants or have at least one immigrant parent.But, with the break-up of the former Soviet Union and the conflict in the former Yugoslavia, the number of asylum seekers rose dramatically. Immigration peaked at 78,987 cases in 1994.Sweden began toughening up its rules, limiting the number of immigrants,
13107 and the number fell to 32,486 in 1995."To escape poverty in hope of a better life is only human, but we cannot remove the injustices in the world by giving asylum to everyone who leaves their country to seek a better future," Immigration Minister Pierre Schori said recently.New legislation put
13107 before parliament this month aims to clarify who will be accepted into Sweden and streamline the application process."A major reform of this policy is planned for this fall, with the government promising to pursue an even stricter asylum regime," the report said.Rising unemployment, the recession and a growing resentment towards
13107 immigrants coincided with an influx of applicants and allowed restrictive policies to evolve, the report said.Despite this many Swedes remain opposed to the changes.</

13146 The European Court of Human Rights dismissed on Wednesday a British gypsy's claim that the South Cambridgeshire District Council had violated her human rights by refusing to let her and her family live in three caravans on land she owned near the village of Willingham.The council said Jane Buckley's caravans
13146 were an eyesore in a rural area, and suggested that she and her children live on an official site instead. But she refused, saying the official site was crime-ridden and not a fit place for a single mother with young children to live.The European court ruled that Britain's planning permission
13146 and criminal justice laws did not violate gypsies' rights to follow their traditional lifestyle and that the reasons and means invoked in Buckley's case had not been excessive."It did not appear that the applicant had at any time been penalised or subjected to any detrimental treatment for attempting to follow
13146 a traditional gypsy lifestyle. In fact, it appeared that the relevant national policy had been aimed at enabling gypsies to cater for their own needs," the court said.</
13147 European Union justice ministers will discuss tougher drugs laws in Dublin on Thursday, close to a spot where angry citizens took the law into their own hands and beat to death a suspected drug pusher with baseball bats.Over a two-day informal meeting in Dublin Castle, they will debate how to
13147 satisfy a general outcry across the 15-nation bloc against the spread of drugs and try to persuade parents, citizen groups and social workers that vigilante justice is unnecessary.The brutal murder in Dublin last May of AIDS sufferer, heroin addict and minor criminal Josey Dwyer illustrated the depth of the problem.A
13147 further reminder came in June when contract killers, thought to have been hired by a drugs baron, shot dead the country's premier investigative journalist for knowing too much.Ireland's Justice Minister Nora Owen, whose country is current EU president, said she was pushing for uniform sentencing at the top end of
13147 the scale for drugs traffickers and increased cooperation across borders."I am confident that...as a result of some initiatives I have taken as President of the Council and from proposals being put forward by other countries, that we will make progress in trafficking laws whether it is drugs, children or women,"
13147 Owen told reporters at a briefing ahead of Thursday's meeting.Owen said Ireland already had tough legislation in place, allowing for life sentencing of drugs traffickers."I want each minister to commit themselves in their own countries to bring in such legislation, if they have not already got it in place. Basically
13147 their laws should contain in them a sentence (for drugs traffickers) that reflects the most serious sentence that they give for crimes," she said.She said such legislation did not conflict with allowing people to smoke cannabis in cafes in countries like the Netherlands. "That is not trafficking," Owen said.She said
13147 other ministers had asked for "a great deal of discussion" of man-made drugs being manufactured in European and neighbouring countries such as Poland and Hungary."Fast and furious we are now becoming producers of drugs ourselves. Man-made drugs are becoming more and more of a problem as they are seen as
13147 almost respectable, just like popping a tablet," she said.The advancement of drug profiling can help track down where a drug was made, she said. The European Drugs Unit, based in the Hague, has identified chemical imprints on drugs which reveal their origin."By doing a chemical analysis on these drugs and
13147 profiling the chemicals that go into them, one can say these originated in Holland or Poland or wherever," Owen said."This may identify regular routes for traffickers and may also lead to blacklisting or controlling of some of the substances which are now being used to make these man-made drugs."</

13152 By Nicholas Doughty, Diplomatic CorrespondentThe growing gulf between the world's rich and poor has taken centre stage at the annual U.N. General Assembly, with warnings of dire consequences if more is not done to close the "poverty gap".More than one billion people, or one-fifth of the world's population, live in
13152 poverty -- most of them in Africa and parts of Asia. Wealthy countries have been cutting development aid, despite widespread concerns that unchecked poverty will bring more conflict, social unrest and mass migration.Government leaders and foreign ministers gathered in New York for the annual U.N. General Assembly this week have
13152 highlighted the problem and called for urgent action, although with few signs of agreement on how to tackle the problems.Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia said the much-vaunted trend toward globalization in trade and other areas, following the end of the Cold War, had brought problems as well as benefits.He
13152 said globalization had bred "a world which generates prosperity and a healthy competition ... but a world which also swells the ranks of the destitute and the outcast".Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said it was time to act after a series of major U.N. conferences on development issues in the
13152 last few years, which have produced public pledges to cut poverty but brought few results so far."The road map is clear; we do not need to study it any further," he told the 185-nation assembly on Tuesday.Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and other delegates from developing countries complained bitterly that
13152 their concerns were being ignored and that the gap between rich and poor countries was widening.Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura appealed for major aid and debt relief for Africa, which has been ravaged by war and famine."The situation in Africa ... today seems like a corpse where vultures come
13152 to feed," he said.Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind devoted large parts of their speeches to the need for a "new global partnerhsip" between developed and developing nations.Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, speaking on behalf of the 15-nation European Union, recalled a U.N. pledge on
13152 its 50th anniversary last year to be of "greater service to ... those who are suffering and deeply deprived"."Despite decades of efforts and resources, the poverty gap has widened not narrowed ... The time is long overdue to mount a new global offensive against poverty, a major cause of instability
13152 and conflict," Spring said.Britain's Rifkind said the world's wealthy now enjoyed unprecedented benefits -- travel, consumer goods, entertainment and new technology including the Internet."But these fruits are denied the vast majority of the planet's population. The number of people who live in absolute poverty is still growing. Their misery is
13152 a challenge to all our consciences," he said.Rifkind said greater trade opportunities for developing nations, more private investment, less protectionism and more debt relief would help alleviate the problems.But Denmark, one of the world's biggest aid donors, said the poorest nations would get little or no private investment and had
13152 little potential to benefit from trade.Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen castigated wealthy nations for cutting development aid, saying the fall in official development assistance was "deplorable".In 1995, such assistance averaged just 0.27 percent of Gross National Product (GNP), the lowest level since the United Nations first set a target
13152 of more than twice that level in 1970. Only four countries in the world, Denmark among them, had exceeded that U.N. target last year, Petersen said.</

13181 Verplaetse told L'Echo newspaper.Verplaetse said that using the bank's reserves could shave more than 200 billion Belgian francs from the debt, saving Belgium some debt service charges, but added the government would lose interest it currently receives on the reserves.The Belgian national bank has built up 236 billion francs in
13181 reserves from gold sales over recent years. Under a draft law adopted by the government last Friday this "unavailable surplus on capital gains on gold (sales)" could be used to cut the debt.Verplaetse told L'Echo that a "small part" of the 236 billion was not available because it belongs to
13181 Luxembourg under the terms of the two countries' 74-year-old currency union.The government law also specifies July 1, 1996, as a deadline for valuing the reserve.Verplaetse told L'Echo he believed the reserves should only be used as part of a wider plan to reduce the debt."I expect therefore that that government
13181 also takes steps to reduce the debt through other measures...Notably through privatisations. 13194 "a piece of cake."Dole was in a fighting mood before about 2,000 students jammed into an auditorium at St. Louis University on what was supposed to be the date of the first debate between Dole and Clinton at nearby Washington University. But they changed the date and place to Oct.
13194 6 in Hartford, Connecticut.The paths of Dole and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, who blames Dole and a bipartisan debate commission for shutting him out of the debates, were to cross in this city. Perot planned to come to St. Louis University on Wednesday and continue his campaign to be
13194 included in the debates.A few pro-Perot hecklers were in the audience but Dole told cheering fans "don't be distracted by the noises here, it's all going to be over and we're going to win, we're going to win because we have the ideas, because we have the agenda."Dole pushed his
13194 economic package, centred on a 15 percent across-the-board income tax rate cut, a capital gains tax cut and a $500 per child tax credit.This Mississippi River city was in an ecstatic mood since its St. Louis Cardinals baseball team clinched the National League Central Division on Tuesday, the first time

13195 from an official announcement, sources told the Variety newspaper that Continental and Comcast will each make FNC available to about 300,000 subscribers on Oct. 7, the date the network makes its debut.In exchange for the vote of confidence in FNC, Fox will pay Comcast and Continental about $10 per subscriber,
13195 the highest launch-budget fee in the history of cable. Six weeks ago, Fox TV also agreed to shell out $50 million to buy 33 percent of the Golf Channel, funnelling needed cash to the network, two of whose owners are Continental and Comcast.Separately, a unit of Fox moved a step
13195 closer to acquiring New World Communications Group Inc., which operates TV stations in a dozen cities and distributes programming for network and cable operators.New World said it reached a definitive agreement to merge with a unit of Fox Television in a stock swap that would value New World at more
13195 than $2.5 billion. The parties announced a tentative agreement on July 17.The deal between New World and Fox is expected to allow News Corp., Murdoch's holding company, to secure a stronger place in world broadcasting by making it the biggest owner of TV stations in the United States.Brian Roberts, president
13195 of Comcast Corp., said his deal for FNC envisions a rollout that will expand the 300,000 figure to about a million of Comcast's 3.5 million subscriber base over the next three years.Continental executives were unavailable for comment, but other sources said the cable company's agreement will inflate the launch total
13195 to about 1.5 million subscribers by fall 1999. Continental's total is currently about 4.2 million subscribers.Roberts says that despite the huge launch fee, he is limiting Comcast's commitment to less than a third of its subscriber base until the network proves its value.Comcast's subscriber commitment to MSNBC, the new all-news
13195 network jointly owned by NBC and Microsoft Corp., will end up at about 2 million, he said, because of "retransmission consent" deals. Many of Comcast's systems agreed to buy MSNBC in exchange for being allowed to carry a local NBC-owned TV station for no extra payment.The bottom line is that
13195 MSNBC is way ahead of FNC in the battle to become the top cable-news competitor of CNN. MSNBC had 24 million subscribers at its July launch, while FNC will have, at best, 12 million on Oct. 7 -- 10 million of which come from cable systems owned by John Malone's
13195 Tele-Communications Inc.Long-range commitments from cable operators will propel MSNBC to 50 million subscribers by the end of the decade.</

13198 Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told a news conference that the new plan was unlikely to go through without "real and substantive" divestments by the company, which was once the world's largest bank outside Japan.Credit Lyonnais is already benefiting from a rescue plan worth up to 45 billion francs ($8.8
13198 billion), which was cleared by the Commission, the European Union's executive body, in July 1995.Speaking in an unusually conciliatory tone, Van Miert said the plan had failed to live up to expectations due to the sluggish French financial markets and the bank's poor image in France."(Credit Lyonnais') rivals said at
13198 the time that the Commission had not been tough enough and that it (the 1995 rescue plan) would turn the bank into a 'super champion,'" Van Miert said. "We see today that that was not the case."He declined to say how much the French authorities might have to pay for
13198 another bailout, but said it would be a "considerable figure."EU rules on rescue aid for ailing businesses allow for subsidies to be paid if they are limited to putting a company back on its feet without harming competition.French bank Societe Generale has challenged the commission's backing of the 1995 rescue
13198 plan before the European Court in Luxembourg.Asked whether the commission would call for the early sale of Credit Lyonnais in return for further help, Van Miert said it was no use pushing for a state sale of the bank before it was financially attractive again.The French government has committed itself
13198 to privatising Lyonnais by the year 2000.The emergency aid package set Wednesday included cancellation of an obligation to grant below-market rate loans to a state-backed entity to which the bank had transferred about 130 billion francs ($25.5 billion) of shaky assets.The bank had said that it would loose 3 billion
13198 francs ($588 million) in funding the loan this year.Van Miert said that provided the French government formally notified the Commission quickly of planned changes at the bank, the executive body could make a final decision on the new plan by year-end.</

13202 rate of 4.13 million. That followed a revised decline of 0.2 percent to 4.15 million in July and a sharper 2.8 percent drop in June sales. The falloff in August existing-home sales was not quite as sharp as forecast by Wall Street economists, who had forecast a drop in the
13202 sales rate to 4.09 million a year.The real estate group revised up its estimate of July sales to an annual rate of 4.15 million instead of the 4.14 million it reported a month ago.Despite three months of weakening business, sales of existing homes in August still were 2 percent higher
13202 than a year earlier in August 1995, when they were selling at a rate of 4.05 million a year.Nonetheless, the falloff in sales last month occurred despite cheaper long-term mortgage rates that seemed to indicate some steam was going out of a robust housing market.The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp.,
13202 or Freddie Mac, said the average rate for a 30-year mortgage loan in August was 8 percent, down from July's 8.25 percent average and June's 8.32 percent."The nation's housing market is easing in for a soft landing," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors. 13202 that after surging earlier this year, "it's only natural that the market will correct itself."Sales of existing homes peaked in May at a record annual rate of 4.28 million.A waning housing market would fit with Federal Reserve policy-makers' evident belief that the overall economy os slowing. 13202 decided against raising interest rates in the apparent hope that the economy was likely to cool off on its own and so keep inflation in check.During August, sales of existing homes fell 9.5 percent in the Northeast to 570,000 a year while in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing
13202 market, they were down 1.9 percent to a rate of 1.53 million.But in the Midwest, August sales edged up 0.9 percent to a rate of 1.07 million a year and in the West they increased strongly by 5.6 percent to 950,000 a year.The average price for an existing home resold
13202 in August was $149,900, up slightly from $149,600 in July.</

13204 of local municipality officials at which he unveiled the key points of the draft 1997 budget.The draft is expected to be finalised by the government at its cabinet meeting on Thursday.Medgyessy said that the country will continue budget cuts, including reduced funding in real terms for state agencies and local
13204 authorities, but will ease company tax burdens in an effort to reach two to three percent economic growth next year, compared to a two percent target in 1996.Hungary also hopes to reduce its current account deficit to $1.5 billion in 1997, from this year's planned $2 billion, although Medgyessy acknowledged
13204 this forecast could be optimistic as greater economic growth may boost imports.Medgyessy said Hungarians understood that the painful economic programme launched in March 1995 was necessary, but the measures, including social spending cuts, only solved immediate problems and created merely the basis of growth.The stabilisation programme, which aimed at reining
13204 in the country's soaring budget and current account deficits, caused real wages to slump by ten percent last year and by a projected two percent this year.Former Finance Minister Lajos Bokros, whom Medgyessy replaced in March, was often criticised for strangling the economy with high taxes and budget cuts.Medgyessy said
13204 Hungary will further reduce budget spending with the budget only redistributing 49.5 percent of the GDP next year, compared with 62 percent in 1994.Subsidies to agencies financed from the state budget will increase by 15 percent next year, while local authority funding will rise by 13 percent, compared with projected
13204 18 percent inflation, he said.Planned changes in the the tax and the social security system and amortization rules will favour enterprises and plug the social security's soaring deficit, which could reach 60 billion forints ($382 million) this year, compared with the 17.8 billion target, he added.Medgyessy said one of the
13204 key points of the reforms are planned changes in the system of social security contributions, including a widening of the range of revenues upon which social security contribution is paid and a new minimum social security contribution.Medgyessy added Hungary will cut social security contributions in 1997 by substantially less than
13204 the previously planned 2.5 percentage points."I would not like to get into a situation again when, with a 60-billion social security deficit in our back, we are searching for solutions," Medgyessy said.He said he also planned to launch other regulation changes to crack down on tax evasion. 13206 The United States is backing off a subsidy battle with the European Union over wheat exports but may not do so for long if world prices continue to suffer, grain traders said on Wednesday.Competition is growing fierce between exporters now that bumper crops in much of the world have cut
13206 wheat prices by as much as half from records set just five months ago, said traders at an industry gathering in southern Turkey."Things are going to be pretty rough in the next few months, especially when crops start arriving in Australia and Argentina (in December)," a senior grain executive predicted.The
13206 U.S. and Europe, two major exporters who traditionally use subsidies to shore up grain exports, suspended the aid last year as supplies tightened after a series of poor harvests that sent world grain stocks to 20-year lows.But pressure is growing on Washington to revert to export subsidies after the EU
13206 restored its own programme last week to shield its farmers from the new fall in world prices.The U.S. grain industry has already applied for help with exports of wheat flour, traders said.Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Tuesday he had not ruled out restoring Washington's so-called Export Enhancement Programme (EEP)
13206 but it was too early to do so yet.EU farm director-general Guy Legras also sounded conciliatory in comments made on Wednesday."Subsidies are destined to bring European prices in line with world prices and allow normal exports without any intention to cut prices or to be aggressive," he said. Benchmark wheat
13206 prices paid by importers have dropped to around $160 per tonne after almost $300 last year, traders said.Without subsidies, European wheat is worth closer to $180 per tonne while unsubsidised Argentine wheat is being promised ahead of harvest for as little as $140."People are buying hand-to-mouth at the moment. They
13206 are all waiting to see if prices keep going down," another trader said.If export subsidies are used in the coming year, it will be a long-awaited first test of the Uruguay Round global trade pact on agriculture which came into force last year, restricting aid.The pact commits the U.S. and
13206 Europe to reducing subsidised exports by 21 percent over six years to 2001. But it gathered dust for 12 months when subsidies unexpectedly disappeared.Analysts and even some of the agreement's negotiators believe it may still lack teeth, because last year's unused quotas of some 20 million tonnes of subsidised sales
13206 by each side can technically be added to this year's allocations.That would notionally set a ceiling far higher than either side's ability to export and leave room for a grain trade war. They must, however, reach the final targets on time in 2001.But while traders expect aggressive competition, few believe
13206 either Brussels or Washington is ready to return to a full-scale subsidy feud that ate up billions of dollars during the 1980s.A U.S. official told the conference in Turkey that Washington had been in touch with the European Commission in Brussels to try to steer it away from using subsidies.The
13206 EU appears to have ignored the advice, but modest initial aid worth less than $2 million suggests a soft-pedal approach, traders said."I don't think the Americans want to use EEP this year but it depends on what happens in the market. They won't stand back and see their market share
13206 fall to pieces," one trader said.</

13210 saw a growth of about 20-25 percent as suficient to get the Nairobi bourse "very vibrant".Mbaru also foresaw the trading of government treasury bills and government bonds on the bourse as well as fully privatising the power sector.Mbaru said that public education about share trading was still very poor in
13210 Kenya and investors often bought shares and held onto them for a long time. 13210 in a pathetic situation. There are power shortages, vehicles are destroyed by too many potholes, telephone lines sometimes do not work and sometimes there isn't a steady supply of clean water. 13210 equities market. 13214 that was bang in line with expectations," Gwyn Hacche, senior economist at HSBC James Capel in London, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a rise in gross domestic product (GDP) of 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter, 1.9 to 2.0 percent year-on-year.The quarterly figures actually came in somewhat lower

13214 analysts said the figures mean the government is likely to achieve its 1996 growth target of 2.3 percent, a forecast it relies on to reduce the 1997 budget deficit to the level required to join a single European currency.The data also leave the Bank of Spain free to focus on
13214 the 1997 budget due to be presented on Monday and which is expected to be followed by a rate cut the day after."(Recovery) in the third and fourth quarters will help us reach a growth rate of 2.3 or 2.25 percent for 1996 and a number around 2.5 percent in
13214 1997," Alfredo Urrutia, capital markets economist at Societe Generale in Madrid, told RFTV."The scenario for rates remains the same," said Carmen Hernansaez, economist at FG in Madrid. 13214 budget deficit targets."I personally doubt that the government can reach 2.3 percent this year and I think there is a risk that for next year, the figure may fall below 2.5 percent," said Hacche.He forecast Spain's budget deficit would fall below four percent of GDP next year but fail to
13214 satisfy the Maastricht target of a 3.0 percent ratio needed to join the first wave of monetary union (EMU) in 1999. 13214 consumption remained the main motor for growth in the second half of the year. 13235 Financial markets used to panic at a hint of political risk but in today's post cold war orthodoxy they play it much cooler. Perhaps too cool. Analysts warn that political risk is not dead, and could yet rear up again in the most unlikely places -- including the apparently rock
13235 steady core of Europe."The key thing is whether the disappearance of Clinton and Yeltsin would change the world," said Stephen Bell, chief economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London."And the truth is -- not very much."In the 1980s, the lingering Cold War and worldwide economic recession (and frothy booms) provided
13235 a volatile mix for the markets.But with the Soviet empire now fragmented and capitalist economic orthodoxy taking root across the world, financial markets have become increasingly inured to political shocks.Analysts noted two early 1990s crises -- the coup which temporarily ousted then Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev and the Gulf War.
13235 In both cases, major market reactions were later judged to be overdone and were quickly reversed.Now, U.S. bombing of Iraq or calls from top Russian politicians for Yeltsin to resign give only a faint boost to the dollar or gold -- usually safe-havens in times of crisis."Political risk is relevant,
13235 but the old days when you'd see five or even 10 big figures movement on dollar/mark -- those days are over," said Bell.Analysts say two main factors have reduced markets' sensitivity to political turmoil."Since the fall of the Soviet Union, markets have been crying wolf about Russia, so the impact
13235 of every twist and turn in Russian politics is getting smaller," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko in London.The second drive has come from major industrialised nations, growth in an economic consensus favouring low inflation, healthy growth and tolerance of a certain level of unemployment means even changes
13235 in government produce few economic moves."In Britain, for example, people now say the differences between the two main poltical parties are very small -- so the risk we would see a dramatic change in economic policy with a change in government are greatly reduced," said Nikko's Thomson."Its much in he
13235 same in the U.S.."With bodies such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank seeking to impose a core policy of fiscal austerity and export-led growth on the world's developing nations, that critical mass will increase, analysts said.But this push for an all-embracing orthodoxy may turn out to be
13235 a double-edged sword. While the conformity spreads across the globe, political risk may reappear in Europe, analysts said."If you want to identify political risk in the next two to hree years, it lies not in Russia, but in western Europe," said Thomson.The only economic game being played in Europe is
13235 the push towards closer integration and a single currency. Any threat to that, would leave a dangerous vacuum, economists said. "An awful lot in Europe hangs on EMU. And there is no "plan B" in countries like France, Italy, Spain, Belgium, even Germany ... its the dominant political issue for
13235 them," said DMG's Bell. If European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) -- scheduled to start in 1999 -- does go ahead, all well and good.But if it dissolves before starting, or collapses soon afterwards, the bricks and mortar of the most prominent, if not the only, support for economic policy
13235 in Europe would crumble."If EMU went, it would remove a consensus amongst European parties that reflects a great deal of political influence on economic policies," said Bell.Most of all, analysts warned against complacency, saying it would be dangerous for investors to treat the reduction of poltical risk asscociated with the
13235 old-style superpowers as a sign it has disappeared altogether.DMG's Bell said that with "market-friendly politicians in place across the world," political risk was not being taken as seriously as it it should."That will change," he said. "Unemployment is Europe's biggest problem, political mistrust of the centre is the United States'
13235 biggest problem, and Japan has dramatic social change.""At the moment all this is being suppressed. But people will get fed up. I see 1997 as quite a difficult year for the political world."</

13238 into a new era when he succeeded party founder and legend Andreas Papandreou as prime minister in January.The ceremony marked the formal start of the post-Papandreou era, with a new generation socialist leader and his hand-picked cabinet setting a firm pro-Western course and turning their back on Papandreou's unpredictable, anti-Western
13238 ways.Political commentators had predicted the socialists would be torn apart after the departure of Papandreou, who forged the powerful party from various leftist factions after a military junta fell in 1974.Papandreou, revered by the left, was elected Greece's first socialist prime minister in 1981. 13238 1993 but resigned in poor health in January. He died in June.Simitis has called on Greeks to work hard, make sacrifices and meet European Union economic targets. 13252 Kate KellandEuropean debt futures breathed a sigh of relief on Wednesday as the prospect of higher interest rates in the U.S. was pushed down the line, analysts said.While German Bund futures led the way with a 23 basis point jump higher at the open, French and Italian debt futures powered
13252 through to set new contract highs. "There is a bit of relief out there," said Jonathan York, a futures broker at Cater Allen on London's LIFFE floor."There is a good atmosphere and things are looking quite nice for now," he said. Analysts said the respite for U.S. debt -- which
13252 gained on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve decided to keep U.S. monetary policy on hold -- may be shortlived, but they said European bonds may be able to bask a little longer."The fact that they haven't raised rates in the U.S. is slightly inflationary at the long-end, said Norman Beauchamp,
13252 head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London. "Once the initial euphoria has gone, the U.S. (market) will come down."After a strong opening, German Bund futures held their ground in early trade. They were trading 22 basis points higher at 98.39 by 0719 GMT. French December notionnel futures set a
13252 new contract high at 124.40, crashing through the previous 124.26 record with the first trade of the day, while Italy's December BTP contract replaced Tuesday's record high with another at 119.90.British gilts had a slightly more moderate start as domestic political concerns kept a cap on their gains. December gilt
13252 futures were 7/32 higher at 107-22 by 0733 GMT.Players said positive sentiment was evident on the LIFFE trading floor, since many had said before the key U.S. policy-setting meeting on Tuesday that any move on interest rates would be a very close call. The latest poll of views, conducted by
13252 Reuters on Tuesday, showed that a slim majority of economists -- 31 of 55 surveyed -- had expected the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to raise the 5.25 percent federal funds rate.U.S. December T-bond futures gained almost one full point to a high at 109-00 on the news, but later
13252 recoiled to close 17/32 higher at 108-20. By 0746 GMT on Wednesday the futures contract was quoted 4/32 down at 108-16 in automated trade."If you take away Fed tightening for now and it gives a slightly softer tone to the dollar, European bonds can certainly do well in the short
13252 term," said economist Andrew Bevan. "Really this is another nail in the coffin for talk of higher interest rates in Japan and even of Bundesbank policy starting to turn," said Bevan, Goldman Sach's senior bond economist in London.But analysts said the outlook for European debt further out and towards the
13252 end of this year was less chirpy."The U.S. market will come to the conclusion that the Fed is behind the curve," said Bevan. "And when that happens it is going to be difficult for European bonds too."-- Kate Kelland, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682</

13256 Foreign direct investment (FDI) amongst developed countries has risen sharply since a trough in 1993 to make up two thirds of all inflows and 85 percent of total outflows in 1995, the United Nations said on Wednesday.Data in the latest World Investment Report from the United Nations Conference on Trade
13256 and Development (UNCTAD) showed growth of FDI inflows to developed countries was greatest for the United States, Britain, France and Australia. The United States, Britain and Germany also invested the most abroad.FDI inflows to the United States surged by more than 21 percent over the 1994 level, reaching $60 billion
13256 in 1995.This was more than all inflows to developing countries in 1992 and was twice the size of inflows to Britain in 1995."Increases in inflows in 1995 were recorded in equity capital flows and reinvested earnings," the report said. "Reflecting a strong recovery of M&amp;A (merger and acquisition) activity by
13256 Western European transnational corporations, equity flows to the U.S. grew by 15 percent to $39.5 billion".Pharmaceuticals and biotechnology were the favoured sectors, with reinvested earnings almost tripling from 1994 to $13.3 billion in 1995.Germany was the largest investor in the United States with $11 billion, followed by Britain with $10
13256 billion. Japan's transnational corporations (TNCs) invested $4.0 billion.The United States also invested far more abroad than any other country in 1995, with outflows of $100 billion. This was $58 billion more than the next highest investor, Britain.Most of U.S. FDI abroad -- about 60 percent in 1994-95 -- was financed
13256 by reinvested earnings, with intra-company loans declining by 42 percent to some $4.7 billion. This is partly explained by the interest rate differential between the United States and other countries, the UNCTAD report said.Britain was the most favoured destination for U.S. FDI, but it was also attractive to firms from
13256 Western Europe and Japan, especially through mergers and aquisitions."Relatively low costs and corporate taxes in comparison with other European Union members have played a role in attracting FDI into the United Kingdom," UNCTAD said.Outflows from Britain in 1995 also reached a record $38 billion, headed mainly for the United States
13256 and European Union.Germany saw FDI inflows rise sharply in 1995 after negative inflow in 1994 because of the strong mark and high corporate taxes. The new investment was mainly in real estate and holding companies, anticipating further mark strength, UNCTAD said.The report also noted that although the United States does
13256 more trade with Asia than Western Europe, there are more FDI flows from the U.S. to western Europe."This is likely to be the case for some time, but the rates of increase in FDI flows from the United States towards Asia are now greater than those inflows towards Western Europe,
13256 with annual rates respectively 6.6 percent and 4.3 percent." It suggests "the Asia century has not yet begun for the U.S.".On Japan, UNCTAD said its FDI policies had evolved from strategies to offset restrictions in key markets in the 1980s to a focus on strengthening global competitiveness now.It noted that
13256 Japanese trading companies have around 5,500 foreign affiliates worldwide but only 85 of them are in Africa and 60 in central and eastern Europe, mainly because of weak historical and trade links with these regions and little official development assistance.</

13269 not hindering one or another," he said.Senior Palestinian officials warned Israel on Saturday its expansion of Jewish settlements was leading Jews and Arabs towards "confrontation and disaster".The television said Netanyahu made the promise on Sunday after the ultra-Orthodox Agudat Israel party threatened to leave his government unless more homes were

13269 previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May, gave them limited self-rule in parts of the territories.Final status peace talks are to deal with these issues but have yet to resume under Netanyahu.The Israeli prime minister reiterated his opposition to a Palestinian state but said he was determined to pursue talks

13274 significant step in removing low-margin assets from the balance sheet," said NatWest chief executive Derek Wanless.The move immediately raised the question of what NatWest was planning to do with the extra capital since it already has more than adequate capital ratios and these would be further raised.The bank is known
13274 to want to boost its capacity to sell retail financial products in the UK, possibly through the purchase of a building society but has said in the past that it has not found any acquisitions which meet its criteria. In the absence of acquisitions, NatWest in July announced a 450
13274 million pounds share repurchase programme which, it said, was in line with its policy of returning value to shareholders.Corporate loans have carried notoriously low margings in recent years with some banks withdrawing to a large extent from this type of business. ($1=.6420 Pound)</
13275 The dollar was frail in morning Europe, smarting from the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates unchanged and bracing for further losses.The policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) signalled no policy change after Tuesday's meeting, catching out a market which had priced in a 25 basis-point rise in
13275 the federal funds target rate."The Fed's taking a risk and the dollar's vulnerable to any sort of strong data or any pick-up in inflation," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ in London. The dollar was quoted at 1.5062/68 marks by 0731 GMT, some way below late Tuesday's European level
13275 of 1.5125/30 although off a New York low of 1.5000.Dollar/yen was more resilient, turning around an overnight dive to 108.95 to trade at 109.72/77, barely changed from its previous close in Europe.The Fed's inaction had many market watchers speculating it could be "behind the curve" on inflation, and concerned that
13275 a reluctance to hike interest rates ahead of the U.S. elections had influenced its decision. That threw the focus onto the FOMC's next meeting on November 13. Some also said Tuesday's meeting had lasted longer than usual, suggesting that there was a split over whether or not to change policy
13275 and so increasing the risk of a November rate hike if there was no further confirmation of economic slowdown.Dealers said the dollar looked fragile after its inability to recoup its overnight losses against the mark."It's struggling a bit. A lot of people came in and believed it was the thing
13275 to do to buy the dollar for a rebound, but it doesn't look that healthy," said Peter Heath, senior dealer at Merita Bank here. He saw the upside blocked at around 1.5075, with a re-test of overnight lows possible. Bids should protect the downside below 1.50 marks for now, however,
13275 Heath said. "I think the range has moved from 1.5120-70 to 1.5020-70," he added.Some feared dollar/mark could probe even lower. Chase Investment Bank saw 1.4975 as the first target, with potential for a test of lows seen this summer -- when the dollar plunged as far as 1.4635 -- if
13275 that level was broken."We see the (Fed) decision as fairly unambiguously dollar negative," Chase said in its daily market brief.All eyes will now be on U.S. data releases for confirmation that the economy is indeed decelerating, analysts said. Today sees the release of U.S. existing home sales for August at
13275 1400 GMT, although the market is more interested in Thursday's durable goods figures and Friday's GDP.The really big one is the October 4 release of this month's U.S. non-farm payrolls, an indicator which has wreaked havoc on the markets in the past."I think the economy will slow down but I
13275 believe the risks are asymmetric," said IBJ's Edmonds. "If anything we're going to see inflation pick up given the tightness in the labour market."Analysts warned that the dollar remained at risk if data indeed showed the U.S. economy losing momentum. "As incoming data provides further evidence that the economy is
13275 decelerating, starting with durable goods tomorrow, the market will need to reconsider whether the Fed will still tighten this year," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell here."Such a reassessment could yet exert greater pressure on the dollar," he added.All the same, analysts said the U.S. unit
13275 should claw some near-term support from the meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers in Washington at the weekend.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8968</

13288 With just 2.5 million people in a land roughly a quarter the size of Austria, Wales would be one of the smallest members of the European Union.But size and population notwithstanding, Dafydd Wigley and his Welsh nationalist party Plaid Cymru are pushing for an independent Wales early in the next
13288 millennium.Fed up with 17 years of unbroken Conservative government in London and with an election due in less than eight months, nationalism in the principality is growing and Plaid Cymru says the time is ripe for radical change."We're fighting to give the people of Wales a real choice," said Wigley,
13288 the party's president, in a rousing speech to its annual conference in the resort of Llandudno.But before Wales can take a seat at the U.N. General Assembly or have a direct voice in Brussels it must cut the ties that have bound it to England since the act of union
13288 in 1536.If the opposition Labour Party wins the election, and judging by their 20-point lead in opinion polls it is likely to do so, it has promised a referendum on an elected non-legislative assembly for Wales.Wigley, one of Plaid Cymru's four members of parliament, brands anything less than a full
13288 law-making body, similar to that already promised by Labour to Scotland, an insult."We're being offered a toothless assembly," he told the party faithful in a bilingual speech in Welsh and English."It would be a constitutional outrage to deny the people of Wales their choice of a referendum and to restrict
13288 that choice to a simple yes/no vote."Wales' second party is pressing for a multi-optional referendum with four choices -- no change, an elected assembly, a law-making parliament and self-government within Europe."If all we are getting is a non-legislative assembly, an assembly with none of the sort of power that the
13288 individual states have in the United States, the question is whether that body is worth having at all," Wigley told Reuters.Wigley thinks not and he is not alone. A recent BBC research poll showed that 53 percent of the Welsh people are in favour of a parliament with primary legislative
13288 powers.Labour's offer falls short of its objective "because we want full self-government within Europe. We see that as a sensible, meaningful step forward," Wigley added.The ruling Conservatives see any power-sharing with Wales and Scotland as the first steps down the road to an eventual break-up of the United Kingdom. They
13288 say a series of reforms since 1979 has brought government nearer to the Welsh people."What Labour proposes amounts to nothing less than an attempt to foist an entirely new constitutional order on our people based on fashionable left-wing prejudices in defiance of the wisdom of the ages," party chairman Brian
13288 Mawhinney said in February of Labour's plans for an assembly.Plaid Cymru is confident of increasing its share of Wales' 40 seats in parliament from four to six in the next election and hopes to capture 16 percent or 200,000 votes.It realises it has an uphill battle in breaking Labour's stronghold
13288 in an ancient country known for its rich heritage, that has produced the likes of poet Dylan Thomas and theatrical giant Richard Burton, as well as its history of trade unionisn and socialism.Fiercely non-conformist, the miners and ironworkers in the industrial south and farmers in the picture-postcard valleys of the
13288 north vetoed a similar referendum in 1979.That effort failed because the time was wrong, said Wigley, and circumstances are different now."Nationalism is much stronger now than 1979. After 17 years of Tory (Conservative) government and having four Secretaries of State for Wales that weren't even Welsh members of parliament that
13288 shows the checks and balances in the system don't work."We've got a mountain to climb to pass Labour but I believe Labour is shooting themselves in the foot on two scores: one with the constitutional score, and the second is that their agenda is moving to the right."They are moving
13288 away from their traditional tenets and those were beliefs held very dearly by a lot of people in Wales."Under leader Tony Blair, Labour has ditched many of its traditional socialist beliefs and moved to the political centre ground.With a recent revival firmly establishing Welsh as an official language alongside English,
13288 and a Welsh language televison station beaming programmes to its half-million speakers, Plaid Cymru argues that its vision for a new Wales is not improbable.First, a law-making parliament of 100 members elected under a proportional representation system. Not less than five years later a referendum on full self-government making Wales
13288 an independent country.Wigley has already questioned Chinmay Gharekhan, a senior adviser to U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, about a place for Wales in the General Assembley."He indicated that the U.N. has a place for every self-governing country however large or small," Wigley said.</
