13698 A federal judge on Tuesday entered formal judgment on the $5 billion fine slapped on Exxon Corp by a jury two years ago as punishment for the disasterous 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.U.S. District Court Judge H. Russel Holland approved the punitive fine -- the largest assessed by a jury
13698 against a corporation -- along with compensation to commercial fishermen, accrued interest and a $5,000 punitive fine against former Exxon supertanker captain Joseph Hazelwood.The entry of judgment ended years of litigation at the District Court level, one plaintiff attorney said."This is the principle goal to which we have been striving
13698 for the last 7 1/2 years," said Dave Oesting, a lead attorney for the thousands of fishermen, Alaska Natives, property owners and others who sued the oil giant over the 11 million gallon (41.6 million litres) spill."We finally achieved closure at the trial court level of all aspects of this
13698 litigation," Oesting said.The formal entry of judgment allows Exxon to appeal the trial verdict to a higher court. The company has said it intends to seek a reversal from the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals.Holland's order approved $19.5 million in compensation -- the result of the $287 million that the
13698 jury ordered in payment to approximately 10,000 commercial salmon and herring fishermen, minus credits for previous payments made by Exxon.The order also assessed the pre-judgment interest at $37.9 million, billed to both Exxon and Hazelwood.The totals result from a summer-long, three-phase trial conducted in Holland's court in 1994.In most civil
13698 trials, formal judgment is entered shortly after juries issue their verdicts. But judgment in the Exxon Valdez case was delayed because of the complicated nature of the litigation. It involved two civil trials in federal and state courts and several separate settlements for various plaintiff groups.The oil disaster occurred March
13698 24, 1989, when the Exxon Valdez supertanker grounded on a reef in Prince William Sound. The tanker, under Hazelwood's command, spewed 11 million gallons (41.6 million litres) of oil into the icy waters, spreading over more 1,200 shoreline miles (1,900 km) and affecting national parks and a national forest.It killed
13698 thousands of marine mammals and hundred of thousands of seabirds, government scientists said.Exxon spent over $2 billion to clean up the spill. In 1991, the company agreed to pay $1.025 billion over 10 years to settle federal and state government civil and criminal complaints over environmental damages.</

13706 Accounting standards that dictate the information companies must provide to investors are falling out of step with the modern economy, the U.S. General Accounting Office said in a report released Tuesday.Changes in the economy "are significantly challenging the relevance of historical cost-based financial statements and the traditional audit of those
13706 statements," the research arm of Congress said.In the new economy, investors receive information more rapidly than in the past using online services, while companies fund their operations with complex financial instruments that can dramatically fluctuate in value, the GAO reported.Under existing rules, companies often report the initial or historic cost
13706 of their assets instead of current values."For the accounting profession to successfully move to a more modern era of auditing and provide expanded assurance services, it must more vigorously continue to address the major unresolved issues," the GAO said.The Financial Accounting Standards Board, a private body that sets accounting standards
13706 for public companies, has proposed new rules for complex instruments like derivatives. But companies have complained that the rules are burdensome and likely to confuse rather than edify investors.The GAO called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to take the lead in forging a consensus among all parties to modernise
13706 accounting standards."The SEC, given its responsibilities under federal securities laws, is in a pivotal position to assume a leadership role," the GAO said.The accounting profession could also do more to reveal fraudulent activity and prevent unexpected losses, the GAO found.Auditors should review the effectiveness of companies' internal controls, the checks
13706 and balances put in place to prevent fraudulent or unauthorised transactions, the GAO said."Effective internal controls are the first line of defence for safeguarding assets and preventing fraudulent financial reporting -- a lesson well learned from the savings and loan crisis," the GAO said.The GAO praised a recent SEC initiative
13706 to increase public participation in the accounting standards setting process. At the SEC's behest, the parent body of the FASB will include more public representatives.The GAO report, titled "The Accounting Profession, Major Issues: Progress and Concerns," was prompted by a request from Congressman John Dingell, ranking minority member of the

13713 Before you invest in any mutual fund, the fund sponsor should send you a prospectus -- a document that includes considerable information about the fund's official investment policy.Should you read it? Probably -- but don't expect it to tell you everything you need to know about the fund.For starters, the
13713 prospectus will tell you about the fund's fees. The fund's expense ratio shows its annual expenses as a percentage of its assets -- for example, a fund with a 1 percent expense ratio spends $1 of every $100 on expenses.How much is too much? That depends partly on the fund
13713 category. For example, an emerging markets fund may have sizable research expenses, so you might reasonably expect to pay as much as 1.7 percent of your investment in annual fund expenses. Indeed, a fund that is spending more on research in that area might even do a better job.By contrast,
13713 an investment grade bond fund shouldn't cost nearly as much to manage. The difference in returns between two funds with comparable credit quality and average maturities isn't likely to be great.So why not go with a cheap fund? Example: Vanguard Fixed-Income Short-Term Corporate (800-662-7447; $3,000 minimum investment; 6.4 percent recent
13713 yield; no-load) invests in short-term investment-grade bonds. The fund may also invest in U.S. government securities, commercial paper, or bank obligations.Another inexpensive choice from Vanguard: Vanguard Fixed-Income GNMA (800-662-7447; $3,000 minimum; 7.4 percent recent yield; no-load) invests in Government National Mortgage Association certificates. The fund attempts to maintain an intermediate-term
13713 average weighted maturity.A fund's risks also should be spelled out in the document.Since lawyers write prospectuses, you can be sure that the description of risks will be extremely detailed. That means you can review all of the worst possible things that can happen when you invest in the fund.If you're
13713 still comfortable holding its shares, that's a sign that you'll be able to stay with the fund through short-term fluctuations that might shake out less-informed investors.The prospectus will also tell you about a fund's past performance. You can compare those numbers with the performance results of similar funds, which you'll
13713 find in those funds' prospectuses, or in outside references such as Morningstar Mutual Funds, available in many libraries.Another reason to read fund prospectuses is to get an idea of the different types of funds that exist.For example, if you order prospectuses for five different bond funds, you will see some
13713 important differences. One fund might invest up to 10 percent in overseas bonds, while another shuns such holdings altogether. Or a fund might invest in long-term securities whose values fluctuate with interest rates, while its competitor sticks to short-term bonds.Differences in credit quality also are common even within the same
13713 category: One investment grade bond fund might invest only in AAA-rated securities, while another can buy a modest slug of high-yield, low-quality bonds.Equity fund prospectuses will sometimes spell out stylistic differences between funds. You might learn that one manager prefers to buy shares of firms whose profits are rising sharply,
13713 while another focuses on slow-growth, asset-rich companies.Once you've read a few prospectuses, you'll get a sense of what to expect -- and what not to expect. For example, the prospectus may not tell you much about the fund's current investments or the manager's general investment philosophy. Reading the most recent
13713 annual report might help -- and the best fund managers typically pride themselves on clearly explaining their strategy to shareholders.Beyond that, Morningstar can help with a review of the fund's historical performance, recent strategy and current outlook. If you're willing to part with a few dollars to get still better
13713 information on a smaller universe of funds, consider the No-Load Fund Analyst (510-254-9017; $225 for 12 monthly issues and annual guidebook).(EDITORS: Clint Willis is a freelance writer who covers financial issues for Reuters. Any opinions in the column are solely those of Mr. Willis.)</

13721 Swiss National Bank governors Thursday cut the discount rate by half a percentage point to 1.0 percent, matching a record low and weakening the strong Swiss franc.A central bank statement said the move, effective Friday, was in line with the recent decline in Swiss money market rates.An SNB spokesman said
13721 the bank decided to cut the discount rate as a means of underscoring the recent decline in money market rates."The (rate cut) move is more a reassurance to the market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," SNB spokesman Werner Abegg said.Market analysts said the move
13721 confirmed a trend already evident in the money market, and underscored the SNB's intentions to keep money rates low.The central bank noted in its statement that it had been supplying the money market with additional liquidity since the beginning of August "in order to prevent monetary strain" and as a
13721 result, some money market rates fell below the discount rate."By lowering the discount rate, the Swiss National Bank underlines its expectation that the interest rate decline will continue for some time," it added.The discount rate was last cut to 1 percent in February 1978, a record low where it stayed
13721 until a return to 2.0 percent in November 1979. The most recent rate change was a drop of 50 basis points last Dec. 14.The Swiss franc, whose strength has been blamed in part for a sluggish economy by making exports expensive, fell against the dollar and German mark immediately after
13721 the SNB announcement.The dollar rose to 1.2505/2515 Swiss francs about an hour after the SNB announcement from 1.2425 before the news.</
13722 Orders for costly manufactured goods tumbled at the sharpest rate in 16 months during August, the Commerce Department said on Thursday, as demand weakened for nearly every category of product.New orders for durable goods dropped 3.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $167 billion -- the biggest monthly decline since a
13722 3.4 percent plunge in April l995 -- after a revised 1.4 percent rise in July.Economists said the report reinforced the view that the economy is slowing and seemed to support the Federal Reserve's decision this week to keep interest rates unchanged."It clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum, and
13722 that growth in the third quarter is going to come in only a fraction of what it was in the second quarter, and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day," said Irwin Kellner, chief economist at Chase Regional Bank."One might wonder
13722 if (Federal Reserve Board Chairman) Alan Greenspan had the number before we did." said Vincent Malanga of Lasalle Economics in New York.Investors responded positively to the news, pushing the inflation-sensitive 30-year Treasury bond up 16/32, or $5.00 per $1,000 face value, and pulling its yield down to 6.89 percent from
13722 6.93 percent Wednesday.The August decline was much steeper than anticipated by Wall Street economists, who had forecast only a slight 0.1 percent fall from July.Previously, the department said July durables orders had risen by 1.7 percent, but it revised that downward.Virtually the only type of manufactured good that registered an
13722 orders increase last month was the volatile category of defence goods, which rose 9 percent to $5.2 billion after a 40.9 percent fall in July.Excluding defence, durables orders were down 3.5 percent in August, the largest decrease since a 3.6 percent fall more than two years ago, in July 1993,

13734 A staggering increase in the international reserves of major Latin American states means they are now positioned to shed the stigma of default by eliminating their high yielding Brady bonds, analysts said on Thursday.Since the end of 1989 international reserve holdings, excluding gold, of Latin America's six biggest Brady countries
13734 have more than quintupled -- from $21 billion in 1989 to $111 billion at present."International liquidity (excluding gold) of $111 billion is not far short of Latin America's total Brady issue of $122 billion and exceeds the market value of the Brady issue," said Paul Luke, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's head
13734 of emerging market research."This comfortable liquidity position, itself in part a reflection of the ability of Latin America to attract external finance...means that these countries are well placed to buy back their high-yielding external obligations," he said.With some additional financing these countries could probably eliminate their Brady bonds altogether, while
13734 the impetus to retire them should make them an attractive investment in the meantime, he added.Richard Gray, emerging markets analyst at Bankamerica, agreed but with reservations."The high level of reserves does facilitate this process, but I would watch the quality of reserves," he said.He pointed to the high component of
13734 "hot money" within Brazil's reserve basket, adding it would be dangerous to commit such short-term money to buying back long-term instruments.The biggest reserves' jump has took place in Brazil, where 1989's $17.5 billion is now brushing $60 million. Argentina recorded the biggest proportional increase with reserves up twelve-fold over the
13734 same period, while Peru has seen a tenfold rise.Ecuador, Mexico and Venezuela have all seen their reserves double or triple."The scale of the increase is quite staggering in comparison with other countries," Luke said.Earlier this year Mexico set a precedent in attempting to retire some of its collateralised Brady bonds
13734 -- restructured commercial debt issued to replace defaulted commercial loans of the 1980s. It has also used the proceeds from recent long-dated global bond issues to buy back $1.2 billion of its own Brady debt at face value.Since then the Philippines has exchanged some of its Bradys for a fresh
13734 20-year bond, while Brazil has passed legislation allowing it to replace its Bradys with global bonds.Peru, in the process of a Brady bond restructuring, said earlier this month it too planned to buy back some of its commercial debt. 13754 $39.08.A cocktail of factors is fuelling the rally, including strong fourth-quarter demand for crudes like Tapis, which are rich in middle distillate products, like gas oil and jet fuel, when refined."Prices are getting very strong and a lot is related to middle distillate demand. 13754 other problems so that traders are scrambling for crude," one oil trader said.The middle distillates demand is exacerbated by U.S. data that show distillate stocks in the energy hungry United States are running almost 19 million barrels below last year's levels and are only building slowly. 13754 for Asian crude and products.Traditionally, distillate stocks grow strongly as the fourth quarter winter season approaches and demand for heating grows.But despite the seasonal factor, other ingredients are adding to the cocktail, crude traders said.Reduced output from Indonesia's 90,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) light sweet Belida field -- as a floating storage
13754 vessel is moored -- is reducing available supplies.Ongoing production problems at Australia's 115,000 barrels per day (bpd) light-sweet Cossack field, which at times has cut output to just 50,000 bpd, is another ingredient.Rising refinery demand from South Korea is a further factor. 13754 to 2.44 million bpd in 1996 from 1.82 million in 1995.As part of South Korea's expansion, Yukong Ltd, the country's largest oil refiner, is bringing a 200,000 bpd distillate unit to commercial production in early October.In Indonesia, a 70,000 bpd basic refining unit is due to come on stream in
13754 November for a new petrochemical plant. The unit can only take very light crude oil in order to produce light distillates, like naphtha.In addition, the strength of the Brent futures market, which is just below post Gulf War highs, is making West African crude oil too expensive to bring to
13754 Asia.West African crudes often compete against Asia's light sweet grades and are priced against the North Sea Brent market.The cocktail has transferred into higher prices for a range of light sweet crude oils, apart from just Tapis.An oil major sold 500,000 barrels of mid October lifting Australian North West Shelf
13754 condensate at a premium of 60 cents above its Arun price benchmark. The condensate normally trades at a 30 or 40 cents premium.A European major sold 600,000 barrels of late October lifting Australian Kutubu crude oil to China at a market premium of 18 cents pre barrel. Kutubu traded only
13754 last week at a discount of 30 cents.A major sold 250,000 barrels of early November lifting Skua crude, which normally trades at parity to Tapis crude, at a premium of $1.05 to a trader.</

13770 Athletic shoe maker Reebok International Ltd. Thursday invited arch-rival Nike to team up and stamp out child labour at their factories around the world, particularly in Pakistan."This isn't about business principles. This is about making the world a little better," said Reebok Chairman Paul Fireman after an Executive Forum of
13770 the Greater Boston Chamber of Commerce meeting."This isn't a challenge. This is an invitation," he stressed.Fireman wrote to Phil Knight, his counterpart at Nike, after reading Knight's letter to his shareholders that spoke of an increased commitment to the human rights of workers making Nike products."I have a radical idea,"
13770 Fireman wrote. "Suppose you and I worked together on this issue... Through your position as leader of the most powerful brand, through our combined market share strength, and through Reebok's own experience in human rights, I think the partnership would be awesome."Both firms came under fire after press reports found
13770 their Pakistani subcontractors that make soccer balls used child labour.A company review "found that 20 to 25 percent of the stitchers are between the ages of nine and 13," said Fireman, whose firm sponsors its own human rights award and various Amnesty International projects.The Pakistani families count on the children's
13770 income, he said, and "are not looking for intervention with their way of life."So Reebok, which fired one contractor for using underage labour, "is building a new facility which will be the home for all Reebok ball production, including stitching. We'll support education and vocational training for the children in
13770 the area," Fireman said.Nike spokesman Keith Peters said Knight was aware of Fireman's letter and "it will take some time to consider it. Obviously, we've been considering a variety of things for weeks now. This is a new wrinkle and it deserves consideration."Knight, in a Sept. 16 letter to shareholders
13770 dealing specifically with criticism of Nike's labour practices in developing countries, wrote, "For the past 18 months, we have hired Ernst &amp; Young to conduct unannounced audits to ensure adherence to our Code of Conduct."Within the next year, we will invite a group other than Ernst &amp; Young to review
13770 the factories making Nike shoes. We know these are the best shoe factories in the world, and we will encourage this independent group to make its findings public," Knight wrote.Peters said Nike will open five of its own facilities in Pakistan, the first one in Sialkot within the next eight
13770 weeks.Soccer, while still a fledgling sport in the United States, provides a multibillion dollar market worldwide for makers of apparel and sport equipment."I hope this proposal will help end the exploitation of children's labour," said Representative Joseph Kennedy, D-Mass., one of the harshest critics. "These two industry giants working with
13770 other labour and human rights organisations along with soccer ball industry could finally put an end to these practices."</
13771 Chrysler Corp. has impressed Detroit and Wall Street with its remarkable turnaround over the last five years, but is worried that American consumers have not taken enough notice.To help snuff out lingering perceptions of vehicle quality problems and portray itself as a designer of innovative cars and trucks, Detroit's No.
13771 3 automaker said this week it is launching two all-new advertising campaigns, including its first new corporate image campaign since ex-chairman Lee Iacocca's last television spots in 1992.The automaker also is trying to put a new luster into its premium Chrysler brand, which still suffers from an image as a
13771 seller of gussied-up "K-cars," even though its entire product line has been replaced since 1992."The perception of Chrysler lags reality," said Chrysler-Plymouth/Jeep-Eagle Division General Manager Martin Levine, who introduced the campaigns here this week to Chrysler-Plymouth dealers. "We need to change the way people feel about the Chrysler brand and
13771 the way they think about Chrysler products."Analysts expect Chrysler to earn record profits in 1996, a far cry from the early 1990s, when its car and truck lines were severely outdated and recession left it short on cash for new products. But the lean years forced Chrysler to slash costs
13771 and develop better vehicles more quickly, allowing it to push its share of the U.S. car and truck market up to 16 percent.The new campaigns will help lay the groundwork for $23 billion that Chrysler plans to spend to develop new products over the next five years, company executives said.The
13771 Chrysler brand campaign makes an emotional appeal with television commercials featuring children asking philosophical questions like, "Just because something hasn't been done before, does that mean it can't be done?"With the tag line, "What's new in your world?", the ads aim to portraying Chrysler as new, young and innovative.Longtime automotive
13771 consultant Christopher Cedergren said it may take a long time for Chrysler to make consumers forget about the vinyl tops on its now-extinct Imperial and Fifth Avenue models, but added that the division is headed in the right direction."Five or six years ago, anything with a Chrysler badge on it
13771 was fuddy-duddy," Cedergren said. "It was a fleet brand."Cars like the sleek Sebring convertible, however, give the company an opportunity to attract new buyers, he said.Still, Chrysler won't give up price promotion in the new campaign -- ads for the slow-selling LHS luxury sedan will emphasise a aggressive, $359-a-month lease
13771 payment.Chrysler officials would not disclose spending on the new brand campaign, but the trade publication Advertising Age estimates it at about $147 million this year, about the same as the division spent in 1995.John McDonald, Chrysler's new vice president of marketing, said the company and its dealers will spend a
13771 combined $2 billion on all advertising this year.Advertising Age estimated that Chrysler is putting about $40 million behind its new corporate image campaign.Chrysler's last corporate ad campaign in 1992 featured commercials with the soon-to-retire Iacocca presiding over the demolition of the automaker's ancient Jefferson Avenue assembly plant and watching its
13771 boxy old sedans "morph" into the sleek LH cars.In the old campaign, Iacocca, who last year feuded with Chrysler's board over his involvement in billionaire investor Kirk Kerkorian's failed takeover bid, took much of the credit for Chrysler's rebound, saying, "When it's your last time at bat, it sure is
13771 nice to hit a home run."The new print campaign features anecdotes of Chrysler designers and engineers taking risks and getting inspiration from hot-rod model car kits, and uses the tag line, "Great Cars. Great Trucks. Chrysler Corporation.""The last one was trying to communicate we were a changing company," said Chrysler
13771 spokeswoman Terri Houtman. "This one is communicating the fact that we are a truly different company."</
13772 The Transportation Department Thursday gave ValuJet Inc. a green light to resume flying, ending a three-month grounding for safety reasons after a crash in May that killed 110 people.ValuJet has said it would be ready to fly as soon as possible after Transportation Department certification, but with fewer planes and
13772 to fewer cities.Before its grounding it was one of the fastest-growing low-cost airlines in the country, flying 51 aircraft to numerous southern and southeastern cities.At first, it will be allowed to fly only 15 planes, and it will need Federal Aviation Administration approval to increase its fleet, the department said.The
13772 low-cost carrier was grounded on June 17 following an ongoing safety inspection of its operations that was intensfied after its Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades near Miami on May 11.A cause has not yet been determined, but investigators think that oxygen generators being carried in its hold may
13772 have ignited, causing a fire that led to the crash.In the FAA's grounding order, ValuJet was cited for a series of maintenance and operations problems, and its return to flying was conditioned on correcting them.Industry analysts said ValuJet will face stiff new competition from Delta Air Lines Inc. and Southwest
13772 Airlines Co. when it returns to the skies.Before it was grounded, ValuJet's low costs had attracted many customers and become a nightmare for full-service carriers such as Delta, which like ValuJet is based in Atlanta.Delta's new low-cost carrier, Delta Express, is to start service next week with 25 Boeing Co.
13772 737-200 aircraft flying daily nonstop service from 10 northern cities to Orlando and four other destinations in Florida.Florida, always competitive and a prime market for ValuJet in the past, has become even more cutthroat with new low-cost service from Southwest Airlines.ValuJet said it would resume scheduled flights on Monday between
13772 Atlanta and four cities with $19 one-way introductory fares on all nonstop flights.On Aug. 29, after ValuJet made changes ordered by the FAA, the agency approved it to resume flying and the Transportation Department gave tentative approval. But the department also asked for comment on ValuJet's financial status and whether
13772 the management was fit to run a safe airline.There were few questions about its finances. But department officials said they had received numerous comments on the airline's safety, including one from the Association of Flight Attedants that alleged ValuJet falsified training records.Officials said, however, the allegations were checked out and
13772 found to be without merit.One official said the department took time with the comments because it wanted to "walk the extra mile" and "to be certain that we looked at carefully and considered anything that had a bearing on Val? fitness."Asked if ValuJet was safe to fly, John Coleman, director
13772 of the department's office of aviation analysis, said, "ValuJet has met all the FAA's requirments and they have met all our requirements and we have certificated them to fly."The FAA had said that for ValuJet to fly again it must retrain its pilots, instructors and maintenance personnel and reduce the
13772 number of outside contractors it uses to be better able to supervise their work.The department in its approval had to judge if ValuJet's management was capable of running a safe airline, and it concluded that "the company will operate in compliance with safety regulations."FAA officials have said the agency allowed
13772 the airline to grow too quickly and should have put it under increased safety scrutiny far earlier.It has started a programme to monitor the safety of start-up and fast-growing airlines.</

13774 PepsiCo Inc., said Thursday it planned to restructure its international operations and take special charges that will cause its third quarter earnings to fall short of year-earlier results.The company will refocus on its core businesses of Pepsi-Cola beverage products, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and Kentucky Fried Chicken restaurants and Frito-Lay
13774 snacks, said Roger Enrico, PepsiCo's chief executive officer. "Now is the time to re-evaluate all other businesses in our portfolio, as well as to streamline our operations, especially international beverages," Enrico said.Pepsi said its international operations will be restructured to trim operating expenses by $100 million a year and shift
13774 its focus to "those markets in which we are already strong." The company also will write down the value of investments in operations in Argentina and Brazil.Those aspects of the restructuring will result in a special charges totalling about $525 million, or 31 cents a share, in the third and
13774 fourth quarters."Clearly we've had problems in our international beverage business," Enrico said. "But I believe we're moving to fix them quickly and get ourselves on a sound strategic footing.</

13776 Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Thursday that China was failing to take "serious" action to join the World Trade Organisation, despite Beijing's expressed desires to be a part of the global trading forum.Barshefsky told a Seattle business group that Chinese officials were "just treading water" on the
13776 issue of joining the WTO and that there has been no real movement in Beijing's position for a couple of years.She made her remarks to the Seattle group as China's Trade Minister Wu Yi was in Washington, D.C., discussing a number of trade issues with Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor and
13776 other U.S. officials.The two sides are expected to cover a wide range of trade issues including a long-running dispute over U.S. wheat exports to China.China has refused to accept U.S. wheat that contains TCK smut, a fungus, on the grounds that the wheat might infect domestic crops. But U.S. officials
13776 say there is no danger because the wheat is milled and consumed far from China's wheat region.Kantor said he did not expect a resolution of the dispute during this week's meetings.Chinese textile exports to the United States and copyright protection and a recent agreement aimed at curbing piracy in China
13776 are also expected to be part of the discussions."They have not shown a serious intent in getting into the WTO," Barshefsky told the business group. Beijing, which wants to guarantee markets for its rapidly growing export economy, has expressed a strong desire to join the global trading system and Washington,
13776 eyeing the huge potential of the Chinese market, has said it wants China in the WTO.But Washington wants Beijing to undertake a number of economic reforms that would open its markets to more foreign goods as a condition to joining the WTO.China has said it wants to be part of
13776 the trading system under the more lenient rules given developing countries. But U.S. officials say China's economy is just too big to give it developing country benefits.Barshefsky said that China's lack of action reflects domestic political wrangling over economic reforms and a concern that some state-owned enterprises may not be
13776 able to compete with foreign products.The issue is important for Washington, because the U.S. trade deficit with China has grown rapidly in recent years and is now second only to the U.S. deficit with Japan, which was $60 billion last year.The U.S. deficit with China hit $34 billion in 1995
13776 and reached nearly $20 billion during the first seven months of 1996.U.S. officials have said the deficit reflects a lack of U.S. access to China's growing markets.</
13777 Nine more winners in a recent high-flying government auction of new wireless phone licenses defaulted on payments, regulators said Thursday, a further sign that some winners are struggling to raise money.One of the companies -- Carolina PCS 1 L.P. of Shelby, N.C. -- was the ninth highest of the 89
13777 original winners in the Federal Communications Commission's sale of permits to offer a new generation of cellular phones.It won nine licenses worth $92.7 million. The auction, which ended in May, was reserved for smaller companies.The FCC said eight smaller winners -- the high bidders on a total of 22 licenses
13777 worth $38.1 million -- also defaulted on the second of two payments to the agency, each equal to 5 percent of a company's total bid. Payments were due Tuesday.In May, two other companies defaulted on the initial 5 percent downpayment and the FCC re-auctioned the licenses.The "C-Block" auction of personal
13777 communications services (PCS) licenses raised an eye-popping $10.2 billion. The price tag spurred analysts to warn that some winners would fail to raise the financing needed to proceed.Rumours that as many as half of the winners would default on their FCC payments have yet to materialise.PCS backers promise to turn
13777 the wireless phone into a mass-market product, allowing consumers to access different communications services -- such as phone, paging, fax and Internet access -- through one hand-held device.The other eight companies which defaulted were: Longstreet Communication International, Holmdel, N.J.; MFRI Inc., Stroudsburg, Pa.; Mountain Solutions Ltd., Lakewood, Colo.; National Telecom
13777 PCS Inc., Stamford, Conn.; RFW Inc., New York, N.Y.; Roberts-Roberts &amp; Associates, St. Louis; Southern Wireless, Hilton Head, S.C.; and Wireless Telecommunications Co., Scottsbluff, Neb.Three companies -- who ultimately did make the payments but were late -- asked the FCC to waive the payment rules. Up to now, the FCC
13777 has taken a hard stance on such requests.The nine companies follow two other winning bidders who defaulted on the initial 5 percent FCC payment. One of the companies was the No. 4 bidder in the auction, BDPCS Inc. of Portola Valley, Calif. The FCC denied the two waiver requests.An FCC
13777 spokeswoman said the agency would act on the latest requests "as soon as possible."The defaults are more evidence some winners are finding it tough to scrape up financing amid scepticism among potential lenders over the profitability of PCS. Analysts say there are too many companies wanting to get into the
13777 business.Two of the top winners in the C-Block auction -- No. 1 NextWave Telecom Inc. and No. 3 General Wireless Inc. -- have faced hurdles on Wall Street in raising funds, analysts said.</

13779 The dollar climbed against major currencies Thursday after a surprisingly large cut in Swiss interest rates hurt the Swiss franc and the German mark, traders and analysts said.Lower rates in Switzerland make the dollar more attractive by enhancing the relative value of dollar-denominated assets.The Swiss National Bank, Switzerland's central bank,
13779 cut its discount rate to an 18-year low at 1.0 percent from 1.5 percent in a bid to spur its sluggish economy. Investors promptly sold Swiss francs and German marks for dollars."People understood Switzerland had to do something to get its economy going. I don't think they were quite ready
13779 to see such a large reduction in rates," said Lisa Finstrom, currency analyst at Smith Barney.The dollar late Thursday rose to 1.2530 Swiss francs from 1.2415 late on Wednesday and to 1.5230 German marks from 1.5170. Against the Japanese yen, the dollar rose to 110.63 from 110.47. The British pound
13779 stood unchanged at $1.5613. The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3675 from C$1.3663.The dollar's rally against the Swiss franc also hurt the mark, with investors also expecting lower German interest rates in coming months."People that had been flocking to the Swiss franc got hurt a bit and the higher dollar puts
13779 pressure on the mark," said Gabriel Grippo, chief currency dealer at Credit Agricole.The Italian lira saw solid buying for a second straight day, bolstered by official Italian predictions that Italy would slash its budget deficit in 1997 and qualify for a proposed single European currency.The lira remained near its strongest
13779 level in two years, reached Wednesday, below 1000 to the mark. The selling of marks for lira also bolstered the dollar against the mark, dealers said."There was more talk about Italy doing well. That should continue to put pressure on the mark and put legs under the dollar," Grippo said.Much
13779 of the dollar's rally occurred in Asian and European trading. As markets closed in Europe, many investors sold off dollars to take profits, thus limiting further gains.But an afternoon report that a top Japanese economic official called the United States the best place for Japanese investment helped the dollar edge
13779 to a session high against the yen.Meanwhile, influential economist Fred Bergsten, director of the Institute for International Economics, told reporters in Washington that Japanese officials were seeking to weaken the yen to lower the cost of Japanese exports."The dollar has to play some catch-up against the yen," said Grippo. "I
13779 think tomorrow we should take out 111 (yen) and test 111.50."The dollar's 1996 high is 111.19 yen reached on July 8.Investors appear to have already forgotten their disappointment at Federal Reserve officials' decision not to raise interest rates at a policy-making meeting on Tuesday.A report of a surprising drop of
13779 3.1 percent in durable goods orders in August eased many investors' fears that the economy might overheat, feeding inflation. That encouraged a sharp rally in Treasury bond prices and boosted the dollar, dealers said."There was a little nervousness about how prudent that Fed decision will prove to be, but now
13779 there's a perception that our long-term interest rates aren't looking so fearful," Smith Barney's Finstrom said.</

13782 ADT Ltd., the largest electronic security company in North America and Britain, is breaking into the vehicle protection business.The Boca Raton, Fla.-based company next month will begin selling Carcop, an electronic vehicle tracking system that is designed to help motorists with everything from lost keys to carjackings."We're looking at something
13782 big here," said Steve Ruzika, president of ADT's electronic security services division.Ruzika discussed the Carcop system at a two-day conference about mergers and acquisitions in the security industry. It was sponsored by several organisations, including Lehman Brothers.ADT will launch Carcop in Miami and Atlanta on Oct. 1, with a national
13782 roll-out set for next year. It will cost $500 to $900 with additional monthly monitoring fees of less than $20.Ruzika expressed confidence about the expected sales for the new system, saying that internal projections of 100,000 units to be installed next year are "reasonably conservative."Once a Carcop unit is installed,
13782 the ADT monitoring centre can track a vehicle's movements, remotely unlock doors, roll down windows or disable the car. Motorists can also use a personal code to trigger an alarm system once they are inside the vehicle. ADT's control centre will be notified if the vehicle's door is opened while
13782 the system is engaged.Ruzika declined to disclose the company's financial projections for Carcop, but indicated labour costs for the new system will not be significant because vehicles installed with the Carcop system will be monitored at ADT's existing control centres. Distributors will install the units."This company has the resources and
13782 the distribution channel and the relationships to make a dent in this market," said Andrew Jeffrey, an analyst at Robertson Stephens &amp; Co.ADT previously has discussed the Carcop system with industry analysts, but the company apparently has not promoted it heavily outside Wall Street.Ruzika said ADT is working with insurance
13782 companies so that motorists who buy the Carcop system will receive a discount on their premiums.He said ADT faced little competition on the Carcop system. Several other companies provide a similar service, "but in a smaller way", he said.</

13785 Orders for costly manufactured goods plunged in August while new applications for jobless pay surged last week, the government reported on Thursday, in fresh signs of a slowing economy.The Commerce Department said new orders for durable goods fell a surprisingly steep 3.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $167 billion last
13785 month.It was the biggest monthly drop in demand for expensive and long-lasting products like new cars, computers and appliances since a 3.4 percent plunge in April l995 and followed a downward revised 1.4 percent rise in July.Separately, the Labour Department said the number of people filing their first claims for
13785 jobless pay jumped by 11,000 last week to 340,000. 13785 as confirmation that the Federal Reserve correctly assessed the economy as slowing on its own when it decided not to raise interest rates this week."It clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum, and that growth in the third quarter is going to come in only a fraction of what
13785 it was in the second quarter, and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day," said Irwin Keller, chief economist at Chase Regional Bank in New York.The news bolstered a downward trend in interest rates as the inflation-sensitive 30-year Treasury bond jumped
13785 17/32, or $5.31 per $1,000 face value, and its yield fell to 6.89 percent from 6.93 percent on Wednesday.Previously, the department said July durables orders had risen by 1.7 percent, but it revised that gain downward.The only type of manufactured goods for which orders increased last month was defence goods,
13785 which rose 9 percent to $5.2 billion after a 40.9 percent fall in July.Excluding defence, durables orders were down even more sharply, by 3.5 percent in August, the largest decrease since a 3.6 percent fall more than two years ago, in July 1993. The decline followed a 3.5 percent rise
13785 in July.The national economy expanded at a 4.8 percent annual rate during the second quarter, its strongest growth in two years, which contributed to fears that pressure on wages were rising.But Federal Reserve policy-makers who met Tuesday evidently foresaw the economy slowing enough in the second half to thwart inflationary
13785 risks when they decided to keep interest rates steady.Robert Dederick, economic consultant to Northern Trust Co. in Chicago, said the weakening durable goods orders "certainly makes the Fed decision look reasonable." 13785 July and August.The biggest single drop in durables orders during August was for transportation goods, which fell 7.9 percent to $37.9 billion, a third straight monthly decrease after drops of 1.6 percent in July and 1.3 percent in June.Weaker demand for new commercial aircraft and parts accounted for more than
13785 half the falloff in transportation goods. 13795 franc, he said.The new single European currency is to come into effect under monetary union due to start on January 1, 1999.The African ministers gave an upbeat message at their regular half-yearly meeting about their countries' economic prospects after the devaluation three years ago of the CFA franc against the
13795 French franc."The message is one of confidence," Arthuis told reporters.Thirteen of the African countries devalued their common currency by 50 percent in 1994 and the 14th, the Comoros Islands in the Indian Ocean, devalued by 33 percent.France precipitated the devaluation by making its aid contingent on the countries winning the
13795 International Monetary Fund's backing.The IMF demanded that they must break a 46-year-old fixed parity with the franc because it made their manufacturing costs higher than their neighbours and was paralysing economic growth.Since devaluation, growth has returned and exports have climbed. 13795 Minister Niamien N'Goran said.He said inflation in West Africa had been brought down to between minus one percent and plus nine percent, depending on the country. It had been running at an average 40 percent in the Franc zone only three years ago.The ministers said growth in the zone should
13795 be at least 4.6 percent in 1996 after shrinking on average by 0.8 percent a year from 1990 to 1993. But the ministers said more needed to be done to encourage private investment.The ministers also urged more progress on debt relief. But N'Goran said he was optimistic the Paris Club
13795 of creditor nations would agree to offer better debt relief conditions than the Naples terms currently available -- under which two-thirds of the debt of low-income countries can be written off.N'Goran said the countries were pressing for the terms to be amended to allow up to 80 percent of the
13795 debt to be written off. Debt costs were "preventing essential investment in basic areas like health and education," he said.Arthuis said France supported easier debt relief on a case by case basis and was optimistic an accord would soon be reached.</

13806 compromise in wage talks and unaccustomed alliances with employers that have since soured.And the tension does not help ahead of the start of wage negotiations for 1997 contracts, slated to begin in December.German workers for years have enjoyed six weeks of full pay for sick leave, which comes in addition
13806 to the usual allotment of six weeks holiday.The new law calls for sick time to be paid at 80 percent of normal salary, prompting protests which recall a 16-week strike in 1957 when employers sought to cut benefits.Employer groups said they were seeking dialogue with unions over the issue, noting
13806 that German law forbids strikes over political issues.Union actions will likely be tied to disputes over changing current contracts. 13806 strong mark and high labour costs are driving jobs abroad and keeping unemployment at home near post-war highs, which raises public spending and weighs on the deficit that needs to be cut for entry into currency union."If anything, if there was no currency union, the mark would be even more

13808 European Union decision makers are at odds with ordinary citizens over the worth, role and future of the 15-nation bloc, a survey revealed on Thursday.A poll by Eurobarometer showed 94 percent of "decision makers" in the European Union thought EU membership a good thing, compared to just 48 percent of
13808 ordinary people.Decision makers were said by Eurobarometer to be elected politicians, senior civil servants, business or labour group leaders, media chiefs and leading academic or cultural figures.The survey questioned nearly 4,000 decision makers across the EU and the results were compared with a similar poll of ordinary people released last
13808 month.Some 63 percent of decision makers thought the EU did not play a big enough role in world affairs while 29 percent felt it had the right amount of influence.Ninety percent of decision makers thought their country had benefitted from EU membership compared to just 45 percent of ordinary people.Decision
13808 makers were more closely allied to popular opinion on the priorities facing the EU over the next decade with maintaining peace, fighting unemployment and combatting terrorism and drugs ranking high in both groups.But support for a single European currency varied significantly with 85 percent of decision makers either "for" or
13808 "somewhat for" the idea, compared to 54 percent of the public.Opinion varied considerably among member states on the worth of a single currency. Only 30 percent of decision makers from Britain -- which has an opt out of the scheme -- were "very much for" participation, although a further 30
13808 percent were "somewhat for".In contrast, some 93 percent of Luxembourg's decision makers were in favour of a single currency.The survey also revealed strong support by decision makers for a more important role for the European Parliament in the EU's decision making, although there was no comparison for ordinary citizens.Some 83
13808 percent felt the European Commission -- the EU's executive -- should resign without the majority support of the parliament, while 65 percent backed the idea of a European government responsible to parliament.</

13811 Swiss money market rates.An SNB spokesman said the bank decided to cut the discount rate as a means of underscoring the recent decline in money market rates."The (rate cut) move is more a reassurance to the market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," SNB spokesman
13811 Werner Abegg said.Market analysts said the move confirmed a trend already evident in the money market, and underscored the SNB's intentions to keep money rates low.Money market traders had earlier said no cut was expected today, but added it could not be ruled out near-term.The SNB pointed out in its
13811 statement that it had been supplying the money market with additional liquidity since the beginning of August "in order to prevent monetary strain" and as a result, some money market rates fell below the discount rate."By lowering the discount rate, the Swiss National Bank underlines its expectation that the interest
13811 rate decline will continue for some time," it added.The discount rate was last cut to one percent in February 1978, a record low where it stayed until a return to 2.0 percent in November 1979. The most recent rate change was a drop of 50 basis points last December 14.The
13811 Swiss franc, whose strength has been blamed in part for a sluggish economy by making exports expensive, fell against the dollar and German mark immediately after the SNB announcement.The dollar rose to 1.2505/2515 Swiss francs about an hour after the SNB announcement from 1.2425 before the news.CS Trading Research director
13811 Gerard Piasko said he expected both the dollar and mark to consolidate at higher levels against the Swisss franc in the short-term and seek further gains.Piasko forecast a near-term mark/Swiss level around 82.35 and dollar above the 1.2500 mark.Manfred Gutmann, senior economist at UBS, said the cut was not unexpected
13811 because short-term market rates had declined and the discount rate should be lower than those."This is a signal that they will continue their relatively strong supply of money...The signal is they want the Swiss franc exchange rate lower," Gutmann said.Guttman said he expected no significant boost to the real economy,
13811 which has posted six quarters of declining gross domestic product (GDP).He said UBS was sticking to a forecast that the franc would weaken slightly over the next three to six months, with short-term market rates below two percent, bonds at around four percent, and GDP growing 0.8 percent in 1997

13822 "I get the impression that companies are consciously downsizing."The imposition of a minimum tax on companies in India's 1996/97 budget in July -- which removed the tax shelter previously available on large capital investments -- had dampened investment enthusiasm, he said."Last year was a good year for credit," said Prabodh
13822 Agarwal, banking analyst at securities firm James Capel B&amp;K."This year it has been slow to pick up. It should pick up now, but the growth may not be high because of the industrial slowdown."Agarwal said cuts in prime lending rates were not likely to lead to a substantial increase in

13824 Robust demand has boosted the rice trade in India and Vietnam with a slew of contracts and shipments headed for Africa, Latin America and the Middle East, traders said on Thursday.Indian rice exporters have started signing contracts in anticipation of a bumper rice harvest beginning in early October, the traders
13824 said."A good harvest is expected and contracts are signed to export from the new crop," said Prem Garg, a leading foodgrains exporter in New Delhi.Indian traders said the contracts for October shipments started at around US$15-$30 a tonne less than current shipments.Indian five percent long grain non-Basmati rice for October
13824 shipment was quoted at $285-$290 a tonne FOB, 10 percent at $275, 15 percent at $250 and 25 percent at $235, they said."The export demand is mainly for the five percent and 10 percent broken varieties. In the lower grades our prices are much higher than Vietnam prices," Garg said."Our
13824 only hope is to export higher grades like five percent, 10 percent, 15 percent," said Mulraj Tanna, a leading exporter from Bombay. "In lower varieties, we are outpriced."Traders said Vietnamese exporters were benefitting from relatively low prices and from the Indian crop not yet coming into the market.Vietnam's official media
13824 said this week rice exports in the first nine months of 1996 were estimated at 2.15 million tonnes. For the whole of 1995, exports were 2.025 million tonnes.They said that since the start of September, the Philippines, Sri Lanka and Senegal had between them ordered more than 50,000 tonnes of
13824 low quality rice from Vietnam.Traders said they expected shipments to total around 300,000 tonnes this month and the Ministry of Agriculture has asked for the export quota this year to be raised to 2.3-2.5 million tonnes from two million in 1995."It's not really a big problem," said one trader. "If
13824 exporters want to sell more, they'll get the quota.""Prices for all grades are starting to firm up," said one trader. "Sales have really been pretty strong this month."Five-percent broken grade was quoted at $280-$283 a tonne and 10-percent at $265-$270, both little changed from last week.The situation was not as
13824 rosy in Thailand, where the market remained quiet as exporters slowed down buying and awaited an easing of prices, trade sources said.While benchmark 100 percent white B rice prices dipped slightly, prices of premium grade fragrant rice rose sharply.The benchmark 100 percent white B was quoted at around US$335-$340 per
13824 tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $338-$340 last week.Fragrant rice was quoted at around $600 a tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $585 last week and an average of $528 in August as supplies were tight amid depleting stocks due to brisk demand in recent months.Traders said exporters slowed down buying of
13824 100 percent white B grade in a bid to force prices down. Demand also eased as foreign buyers were sidelined by high prices.But the prices barely dropped because only small supplies entered the market as millers slowed down activity to support the market."The prices of Thai rice are too high
13824 compared with those of Vietnam and India. It doesn't give much incentive to buy at the moment," said one trader.</

13832 Canadian Justice Minister Allan Rock on Thursday said he would ask the country's Supreme Court to rule on the legality of any future unilateral declaration of independence by French-speaking Quebec.Following a razor-thin victory for federalists in last October's referendum on Quebec separation, the Liberal government's action was seen as a
13832 bid to set clear rules on who gets the final word in any future vote on independence.Quebec reacted dismissively to Ottawa's latest move."There is only one court that can decide the political future of Quebec. It is, of course, in Quebec, by the people of Quebec," the province's premier Lucien
13832 Bouchard told reporters in Quebec City.Bouchard's separatist goverment has argued that Quebec people alone have the right to chose whether to keep their province in Canada, but Rock on Thursday said this view contradicted both Canada's constitution and international law."In our view, that position is contrary to Canadian law, is
13832 unsupported by international law and is deeply threatening to the orderly governance of our land," Rock told parliament.He said the government would seek a Supreme Court ruling on whether a unilateral declaration of independence by the Quebec government is legal under Canada's constitution and international law and whether domestic or
13832 international law would take precedence in Canada if there is a conflict."The government of Canada does not argue against the legitimacy of a consultative referendum," Rock said. "But however important that consultation may be, the result of a referendum does not, in and of itself, effect legal change."The Liberal government's
13832 failure to take more decisive measures against a possible split attracted severe criticism after separatists came within one percentage point of winning the October referendum.Bouchard discarded Ottawa's decision and said a Supreme Court ruling would have no impact on future referendums on Quebec sovereignty."It is certain that it will not
13832 affect in any way the future of Quebec and the determination of this government to hold a referendum," he told Quebec City reporters in French.Asked whether Ottawa's action would affect his "referendum calendar," Bouchard replied: "Not at all," adding that he would continue focusing on Quebec's economic woes.Rock's announcement was
13832 also met with outrage by the separatist Bloc Quebecois, which holds official opposition status in Canada's Parliament."Now that it is afraid of losing, the federal goverment is trying to throw doubt on the entire Quebec referendum process, and to impose its own referendum rules," Bloc Quebecois deputy Pierrette Venne said
13832 in response to Rock's announcement.Ottawa's appeal to the Supreme Court would be separate from Quebec lawyer Guy Bertrand's court battle against separation. The former separatist was mulling whether to continue with his demand before a Quebec Superior Court judge for an injunction against any future sovereignty referendums that would lead
13832 to a unilateral declaration of independence.In a move that sparked outrage in Quebec City, the federal government backed Bertrand's case in court, arguing that the Canadian constitution and the courts should have a role to play in any Quebec secession process. Quebec's lawyers argued that Quebec voters alone can decide
13832 their political future through a democratic vote in a referendum.Under Quebec law, the separatist government cannot hold another sovereignty referendum until after the next Quebec election. That is to be called at the provincial premier's discretion and could be up to three years away.</

13836 AMR Corp chief executive Robert Crandall said Thursday that the airline company's earnings were expected to be weaker in the second half of the year than they were in the first half.He said profits at AMR, parent of American Airlines, had improved strongly year over year in the first half.
13836 "I expect that level of improvement to drop dramatically as the year goes on...Certainly earnings will not be as good in the rest of the year as they have been in the first part of the year," he said, referring to the third and fourth quarters. He spoke to reporters
13836 after a speech to a business group in Vancouver. "I think earnings in the fourth quarter will be a good deal weaker than they have been year-over-year to date," Crandall said. He cited a sharp rise in fuel prices and the reimposition of a 10 percent U.S. federal excise tax.Crandall
13836 said AMR expects to close the initial public offering on its SABRE Group Holdings Inc unit in mid-October. AMR announced plans to spin off about 16 percent of the reservation and information system earlier this month.Crandall said AMR hopes the offering will be priced at the high end of its
13836 estimated range of $20 to $23 a share. The deal is valued at about $434 million. AMR has set no new target date for the finalization of its delayed alliance with British Airways Plc, Crandall said.The two companies originally aimed to complete the link by next April, but the implementation
13836 has been delayed by slow progress in talks between the United States and the United Kingdom on liberalizing air travel.Crandall said the two airlines would remain patient as long as that process still has "positive momentum." If it received a "negative signal" from either government, then AMR would "go off
13836 and do something else," he said. He did not elaborate on what those other options might be but said the alliance with British Airways was the most logical. In his talk to the Vancouver Board of Trade, Crandall said he thought the alliance would cause trans-Atlantic fares to decrease.Crandall said
13836 he expects airline fares overall to decline in real terms by about one to two percent a year for the foreseeable future, a trend that he said has been in place for 20 years. Crandall said American hopes to strengthen its link with Canadian Airlines Corp and its Vancouver hub
13836 to boost its traffic, especially to Asia.-- Reuters Vancouver Bureau (604) 664-7314</

13846 The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday filed charges against three former executives of California Micro Devices Corp., alleging fraud and insider trading for the one-time high-flying technology company.The SEC complaint alleges former President Surendra Gupta committed fraud by helping inflate California Micro's revenues in its fiscal year ended June
13846 30, 1994.Two other former plant managers, Bhasker Rao and Ramana Penumarty, were also charged with fraud and insider trading, according to the complaint."We absolutely deny the allegation and intend to fight it vigorously," William Goodman, a San Francisco-based attorney and counsel for Gupta, said.Rao and Penumarty could not be reached,
13846 and California Micro Devices Chief Financial Officer John Trewin declined to comment on the matter.Based in the heart of Silicon Valley in Milpitas, Calif., California Micro makes advanced electronics based on thin film technology that are used in communications and computing equipment.The charges, filed in U.S. District Court for the
13846 Northern District of California, stem from accounting irregularities that surfaced in the fall of 1994 and led to the restatement of 1994 earnings and the resignations of the three executives, Chairman Chan Desaigoudar and Treasurer Steven Hencke.The SEC claimed the three executives directed employees to falisify documents to show products
13846 had been shipped when in fact they had not. In some cases, the products had not even been manufactured, according to the complaint.In addition, the SEC alleged Rao and Penumarty sold stock in the company while they knew about the irregularities.By selling the stock based on non-public information, Rao and
13846 Penumarty avoided losses of roughly $70,000 and $58,000, respectively, the SEC claimed.By August 1994, California Micro Devices's stock traded as high as $22 a share based on strong projected earnings growth.On Aug. 4 of that year, the company reported a fiscal 1994 net profit of $5 million, or 62 cents
13846 a share. But the stock plunged to $13.125 as investor concern arose over charges in its report.By October, when the company finally disclosed it would have to restate its earnings due to what it described as "possible revenue recognition and accounting issues," the stock was down to $5.25. Eventually it
13846 bottomed at $3.875.In February 1995, after the resignation of its top executives, California Micro Devices finally restated 1994 earnings to reflect a net loss of $15.2 million, or $1.88 a share. Revenues were restated to $30.1 million, down from the previous $45.3 million.On Thursday, California Micro's stock was at $6.69

13862 Let's face it, most lead scrap merchants only think of TV as something to watch after a hard day following prices on the LME.But a viable new source of lead scrap could be staring them in the face as they settle down in front of the tube."TV glass is the
13862 area of recycling where opportunities exist to a greater extent," George Gange, general sales manager of Hammond Lead Products, Ind. told delegates at the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries meeting. Lead is used in glass for TV tubes to protect viewers from the rays emitted by the cathode. A 19

13863 The G24 group of developing countries is willing to support a proposal that would break a two-year deadlock with industrialized nations over the issue of SDRs, the IMF's currency, according to a draft report.The draft was prepared for delegates of the G24 countries from Africa, Asia, and Latin America, who
13863 will meet here Friday and Saturday, as part of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank."In a spirit of solidarity, (delegates) were prepared to support a one-time move to equalize the ratio of cumulative allocations (of SDRs) to present quotas," said a copy of the
13863 draft obtained by Reuters.The Special Drawing Rights, an artificial currency issued by the IMF, allows member countries to beef up their currency reserves and effectively boost their borrowing power.The G24, which groups countries as diverse as India, Saudi Arabia and Brazil, had blocked since a meeting in Madrid two years
13863 ago a plan supported by the rich nations to allot about 16 billion SDRs (worth nearly $23 billion) to the IMF's newest members, so-called "transition" countries like Russia. Arguing that the IMF's articles only allowed for general allocations of SDRs, they supported an alternative proposal made by IMF managing director
13863 Michel Camdessus to issue 36 billion SDRs for a broad-based distribution.Leading members of the Group of Seven industrialized countries, however, objected to such a large issue, charging that it could trigger inflation.Camdessus told a news conference Thursday that a breakthrough had been achieved recently, as the IMF's executive board, where
13863 all members are represented, supported yet another plan drafted by his staff.The new plan entails amending the IMF's articles to allow for a special "equity" allocation to bring all countries up to the same ratio of SDRs to their membership quotas.Camdessus said members have not yet reached an agreement on
13863 the size of the issue but ventured that it could be around 26 billion SDRs. The G24 draft report said it supported the IMF chief's suggestion "for a benchmark ratio of 33 percent of quotas as a minimum figure for providing a modest contribution to meeting world liquidity needs".The amendment
13863 of the IMF articles would still have to be approved by member countries' governments.-- Peter Bate, IMF Newsroom (202) 898-8325</

13868 Zinc premiums have climbed higher in the United States to cover the cost of importing more metal, but premiums are set to fall closer to their traditional levels, according to Ed Schmidt of Big River Zinc."I would like to see the premium stay at six cents, but I don't think
13868 it will stay there," Schmidt told delegates of the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries round table here.Big River was recently taken over by Korea Zinc, one of the world's biggest producers. Physical zinc in the United States is priced by adding a premium to London Metal Exchange cash zinc price.
13868 The present premium is about 6.0 to 6.5 cents per pound.Schmidt said premiums of six cents and above were "short- term" and will fall to the average rate of 4.5 cents.Schmidt argued that the cost of importing "opportunistic" metal - zinc from countries which normally don't export large volumes to
13868 the U.S. - was about 6 cents per pound, which is why premiums rose because metal was tight at present.But in some cases, premiums for importing metal could be much lower if inland freight costs are reduced. This year the U.S. is forecast to import 539,000 tonnes from Canada, 104,000
13868 tonnes from Mexico, and 137,000 tonnes in total from Australia, Finland, Norway, Peru and Spain.Brasil, seen as an opportunistic supplier, was expected to export 39,000 tonnes to the U.S. this year, with 10,000 tonnes from other countries.Total U.S. imports in 1996 will be 835,000 tonnes with U.S. consumption forecast to
13868 reach 1.235 million tonnes, Schmidt said. Some 25,000 tonnes will be sold from the U.S. government stockpile. U.S. production is about 380,000 tonnes. U.S. zinc production has remained flat for several years while demand continues to grow as new galvanizing lines are being built, consuming an extra 5,000 to 10,000
13868 tonnes a year per line.A good indication of current premiums were the U.S. Mint which buys special high grade metal for making penny coins, and the government stockpile, which sells prime western and high grade metal. The difference in the price is usually about 2.5 cents per pound, Schmidt said.But
13868 trader Morton Schwarz of Trademet told delegates, "It's highly unlikely we will see a reversing in the upward bias in premiums this year." Schwarz cautioned that people in the zinc market have been lulled into a false sense of security because of weak zinc prices on LME. "The price doldrums
13868 are about to change and the cold zinc winds are about to be ignited," he said.Russian metal availability has fallen and is now sold at only a $5 to $10 per tonne discount to LME cash, compared to a $10 per tonne premium paid for Western special high grade."Chinese demand
13868 for zinc is also understated," Schwarz said.Refined zinc stocks are falling, and although most expected a zinc concentrates surplus over the next 12 months, the magnitidue of it will be much less, at just 40,000 to 100,000 tonnes. Schwarz said this was manageable and will leave treatment charges for concentrates
13868 in 1997 largely unchanged at $190 to $195 per tonne basis LME price of $1,000 per tonne.-- Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-859-1646</

13886 Future financial crises in emerging markets should be resolved with a market-based approach rather than by resorting to massive international bailouts, a financiers group said.In a report to be published Friday, the International Institute of Finance also advocated that emerging economies act swiftly to adjust fiscal and monetary policies at
13886 the onset of a financial crisis.But it saw a key role for markets, noting that falling equity prices tend to attract bargain hunters and encourage other investors to ride out the storm. "Markets can't depend on official bailouts," said Charles Dallara, the group's managing director, at a briefing which coincided
13886 with the start of events associated with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank."Investors won't learn the lessons they need to learn," said Dallara whose group's membership includes commercial banks, securities firms, fund managers and insurance companies.The Mexican peso crisis of 1994/95, which prompted large-scale official
13886 assistance, has prompted both the public and private sectors to develop a range of proposals for new ways to address future financial crises should they arise.The IIF said its proposed strategy takes into account the greater role that equity plays in emerging capital markets. The share of long-term bank claims
13886 in total debt is much lower than in the 1980s, the group also noted.As a result, attempts to control outflows by rescheduling debt are likely to prove more difficult than in the past.The private sector is expected to invest some $225 billion in emerging market economies this year, according to
13886 the group's chief economist, William Cline, who led the group that produced the report. The report calls for crises to be dealt with on a case-by-case basis, rather than through predetermined arrangements supervised by official international organizations. It also rejected any approach that would create new international bankruptcy mechanisms.But the
13886 group did call for preemptive measures to help avert potential crises. "Structural weaknesses must be addressed with persistence or they will resurface during periods of stress," the report said.Shoring up domestic banking systems should be a top priority for emerging economies and multilateral agencies, the report said. It noted the
13886 potential for a weak banking system to "transform a temporary external shock into a sustained recession."</

13895 Hedging is a necessary way of controlling financial risk in the energy industry, particularly for smallfry companies, executives told an energy conference Thursday."A number of observers have concluded that their firms should not hedge, however this conclusion may be incorrect," Philip Verleger, an economist with Charles River Associates Inc, said
13895 at the annual Herold's Pacesetters Energy Conference here."Risk management is a tool that may have value to corporate managers and may add to shareholder value. The key is to use the tool correctly," the Washington-based economist said. Verleger and other executives in the commodity derivatives industry stressed that a number
13895 of hedging debacles of the past few years have scared off potential participants in the marketplace.The misbegotten hedges included substantial losses in 1994 at the U.S. unit of Metallgesellschaft AG and massive copper trading losses disclosed earlier this year at Sumitomo Corp.Verleger and others acknowledged there was a periously deep
13895 potential downside in cases of ill-conceived derivatives risk management. "When it's not done correctly anything can happen," said Peter Dupre, director of derivatives marketing at Phibro Inc, a subsidiary of Salomon IncBut when done correctly hedging can be a lifesaver, particularly for small, more financially vulnerable companies, Dupre and others
13895 said.Verleger noted Triton Energy's use of a hedge to pay for an investment in Colombia as one noteworthy example of sound risk management. "Triton's swap stands as one of the most innovative and attractive examples of the use of hedging in energy markets," Verleger said."In this transaction, Triton swapped over
13895 10 million barrels of oil with an investment bank, receiving a cash payment," he said, noting the money was used to pay for Triton's share of the pipeline built to move Cusiana crude from Colombia to the Gulf of Mexico.By hedging, or locking in prices for its oil, Verleger said
13895 Triton averted the risk of having to give up all or part of its stake in the mammoth Cusiana field had oil prices collapsed. Executives said that while huge companies have the wherewithal to choose whether or not to hedge, for many small companies it is vital insurance.Verleger said Triton's
13895 hedging play in Colombia met with approval from shareholders because the company was thought to be too small to finance its investment in the pipeline without hedging, Verleger said."When one looks to hedge, one should have a very clear sense of what kind of (financial) exposure you have," said Charles
13895 Adams, vice president of Morgan Stanley in New York."Risk management markets are alive and well," he said. -- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 212 859-1620</

13897 The World Bank said Thursday it was working to reinforce the growing role of the private sector in development, saying commercial activity was central to reducing global poverty.The bank said it had recently launched a business partnership center designed to help meet the needs of the private sector in dealing
13897 with the developing world.This is in addition to a decision to make coordination of private sector activities between the various Bank agencies a a senior management responsibility."Countries throughout the world are working to enhance the role of the private sector in their national development because it is central to reducing
13897 poverty," the Bank said in its annual report.It said during the 1996 fiscal year, which ended June 30, the bank was working in every region in the world to improve the business environment by encouraging countries to identify and overcome constraints to competitiveness.The bank assists countries in privatizing their industries
13897 and in so-called enterprise reform by providing advice and analysis, making loans for technical assistance, and in providing loan guarantees in some cases.But World Bank President James Wolfensohn made clear that many developing countries were not enjoying huge inflows of private investment."Despite the explosive growth in the world economy, many
13897 countries are being left behind," he said.He also emphasized that government-to-government aid has been falling dramatically as the large industrial countries tighten their belts to reduce budget deficits.The private sector is making up some of the difference but it has been highly selective with 75 percent of all private investment
13897 going to just 12 countries. Those 12 are China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Peru, Hungary, Poland, Egypt and Nigeria.For its part, the bank has making increased efforts to make certain its development projects go according to plan and that funding installments are not held up by poor planning.In
13897 the past, the bank has been criticized for measuring its success by the amount of money it commits each year rather than how successful the projects do after going on line.In a briefing for reporters to discuss the annual report, World Bank Managing Director Gautam Kaji said that the bank
13897 is doing much better in disbursing funds as projects progress."I expect a continued robust performance on disbursements," Kaji told reporters.But the flow of funds into emerging economies has made the bank rethink its role, he said, stepping aside from some projects it might have undertaken in the past in favor
13897 of private industry.The World Bank currently provided loan guarantees in some of the more developed countries and was trying to find ways to provide the same service in very poorest nations."We are looking at ways in which ... we can provide some element of comfort to the private sector in
13897 a couple of these countries," Kaji said.</
