13901 The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) gave final approval on Thursday to a California plan to reduce ozone pollution in seven areas with unhealthy levels of the smog ingredient.The California state implementation plan, or SIP, would help the state meet federal health standards in those areas, some of which suffer
13901 from the nation's highest ozone levels."Today we are approving this plan, which sets out a blueprint for the state to bring healthy air to all Californians," Felicia Marcus, regional administrator for U.S. EPA's western region said in a statement. The plan, first submitted in 1994, received preliminary approval early this
13901 year pending public review and comment.Under the U.S. Clean Air Act, states with unhealthful air are required to submit plans showing how health standards for smog will be met by the deadlines set forth in the law.Ground-level ozone damages lung tissue and makes the lungs sensitive to other irritants."EPA's goal
13901 has always been to work with the state to develop its own clean air plan that makes economic and environmental sense for the people of California," Marcus said. The plan sets deadlines for cleaner air based on each of the seven area's current levels of pollution.The South Coast region, including
13901 Los Angeles, must attain the plans standards by 2010, the Southeast Desert by 2007, Ventura and Sacramento by 2005, San Joaquin and San Diego by 1999, and Santa Barbara by 1996.The EPA recently proposed a tightening of national emission standards for heavy-duty trucks and buses, set new standards for lawn
13901 mowers and marine vessels and together with California, agreed with manufacturers to set standards for diesel engines in construction and farm equipment. The South Coast Air Quality Management District, an air regulator for greater Los Angeles, recently released a draft 1997 air quality plan, but it remains incomplete and has
13901 not been submitted to the EPA. It was not included in today's approved plans, the EPA said.</

13940 newsletter. "We had that period in July when the market was down and there were a lot of long faces on Wall Street."About $17.93 billion in net new cash flowed into stock mutual funds in August versus $5.76 billion, according to final data compiled by the Investment Company Institute. New
13940 sales into stock funds, excluding such categories as investor redemptions, edged off slightly to $33.6 billion in August from $35 billion in July. 13940 to the ICI, a major fund industry trade group.Combined assets of all funds increased to $3.224 trillion from a revised $3.139 trillion in July. 13940 July, with $1.7 million in August versus an outflow of $1 billion in July.Money market funds had inflows of $12.58 billion in August versus $22.35 billion in July.Charles Biderman, president of Trim Tabs Financial Services, said investors took a fancy to more conservative stock funds in August. 13989 the alleged injuries."The fact is that Dow Chemical is not now and never has been in any silicone business, including the breast implant business and should not be in this litigation," John Scriven, general counsel for Dow Chemical, said in a statement.Plaintiff attorney Joe Dunn from the Laguna Niguel, Calif.,

13989 14,000 breast implant cases pending against it. 13989 cases to be heard by state court juries. Dow Chemical is also facing about 150 cases in the Texas state court system.The company is also appealing a Nevada jury verdict from October 1995 that ordered the company to pay $14.1 million in damages to a woman who had Dow Corning
13989 implants. That verdict was the first case in which Dow Chemical went to trial as a sole defendant in a breast implant case.Dow Corning was originally named as a co-defendant in that case. But its May 1995 decision to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy court protection froze the thousands of lawsuits

14015 estate investment trust led by investor Sam Zell, on Wednesday filed suit against Chateau and various board members, and ROC Communities Inc over a pending merger between Chateau and ROC. 14015 offer of $26 a share.After receiving the unsolicited offers, Chateau went back to ROC and revised a merger the two agreed on in July.In a U.S. District Court in Maryland, MHC filed suit seeking a temporary restraining order to prevent Chateau from repurchasing 1.45 million shares as approved by its
14015 board and to keep ROC from purchasing 350,000 shares. 14015 telephone interview, Kellogg said he expects a decision today on the request, the only point argued today."We weren't doing it anyway," Kellogg said, referring to the approved repurchase plan. 14015 block MHC's tender offer. The suit alleges the proposed merger disenfranchises Chateau shareholders by reducing the voting requirement and manipulating the vote. 14015 is more like $10 million for Chateau shareholders and $20 million for ROC shareholders."The only way that will figure in to all the shareholders would be if all the properties were sold," he said, adding Chateau has not sold property in at least than 10 years. "We're in the business

14022 Bellcore said Thursday it issued an alert to its clients about a potentially serious problem that could impact the security of the "smart cards" used by many domestic and international phone companies and banking institutions.The company said a smart card can be manipulated into making a computational error which can
14022 then render it vulnerable to techniques used by cryptographers to extract secrets stored in the card, including the secret key used to authenticate the legitimacy of that card.Bellcore, the research arm of the seven regional Bell companies, said it also notified them that Bellcore is available to analyze the various
14022 devices and computers that are used by all electronic cash systems to determine the extent of a potential threat to any particular system.</

14024 The Federal Aviation Administration on Thursday said it rated Indonesia as "conditional" in its ability to assure the safety of its air carriers operating in the United States.The FAA said the term "conditional" indicates that its inspectors found areas in Indonesia's civil aviation authority that did not meet international aviation
14024 safety standards.Countries whose air carriers fly to the United States must adhere to the safety guidelines of the U.N.'s International Civil Aviation Organization's aviation safety standards. The FAA assessment determines whether a country has a civil aviation authority in place and the extent to which that authority ensures that operational
14024 and safety procedures are maintained by its air carriers while operating in the U.S.The FAA, with the cooperation of the host country, only assesses countries whose airlines have operating rights to or from the United States, or have requested such rights.When a country is assessed as "conditional," the FAA negotiates
14024 with the country's civil aviation authority to implement corrective measures. During the negotiations, the FAA permits limited operations by the country's air carriers to the U.S. under heightened FAA operations inspections and surveillance.</

14085 Alan Blinder, former vice chairman of the Federal Reserve, Thursday said the central bank acted appropriately this week when it opted not to raise interest rates."I think it was an extremely close call, and they did the right thing," Blinder told reporters after speaking at a Business Week symposium.Blinder said
14085 the "preponderance of evidence" supported the idea that it would be best to wait.He pointed out that data such as recent retail sales reports suggest that the economy is set to slow down in the closing months of this year, meaning that it might not be necessary for the Fed
14085 to tighten credit in order to rein in growth.Blinder also discussed the long-term trends in the economy, saying he disagreed with those who say the economy is capable of growing at more than two to 2.5 percent without generating inflation. Blinder noted that the economy has grown at only slightly
14085 more than two percent for the past few years, as both the unemployment rate and inflation have held steady.If the true potential growth rate of the economy was a lot faster, unemployment would have fallen further by now, Blinder said.He identified 5.6 percent as the likely level for the non-accelerating
14085 inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU).Blinder said 5.6 percent "seems to be an excellent estimate of the area in which inflation neither accelerates nor decelerates." Although the jobless rate fell to 5.1 percent in August, Blinder said that if the economy slows the rate would likely move higher toward the range
14085 of 5.4 to 5.8 percent, which he said was a healthy area.Blinder, asked whether Tuesday's decision by the Fed to keep rates steady was a sign officials were pursuing a policy of "opportunistic disinflation," which he has advocated, said he thought it was."More than anything else it was an expression
14085 of patience," he said of the decision. "If the Fed was hell-bent on getting to zero inflation as fast as possible it surely would have been raising interest rates the last few meetings."He added, "The fact that (the Fed) has been patient ... is a very strong sign that the
14085 center of the Fed -- indeed a majority at the Fed -- believe in more opportunistic patience to bring the inflation down."Under the opportunistic approach, policymakers do not actively attempt to push inflation down when it is already at low levels. Instead, they take advantage of naturally occuring economic downturns
14085 to lock in further gains against inflation. But if inflation seems set to pick up, policymakers following opportunisitic disinflation would strenously fight it.</

14095 of this year, Dataquest said.Microsoft Corp continues to dominate the market, but a Dataquest analyst said that if the second quarter's slowdown in shipments continues there could be serious ramifications for Microsoft and the entire software market. "Microsoft relies extensively on suite revenue and profitability to drive its overall business,
14095 so any sort of a slowdown will concern Microsoft," said Dan Lavin, an analyst with Dataquest's Personal Computing Software program."This market is still astonishingly healthy and profitable, but these early warning signs warrant careful attention," he added.Suites refer to a set of distinct software applications designed to work in tandem.
14095 They typically include word processing, spreadsheet and database programs. Leading examples include Microsoft's Office, International Business Machines Corp's Lotus SmartSuite and Corel Corp's WordPerfect and Office Professional suites.Based on preliminary estimates, Dataquest said that Microsoft's share of the suite market, measured in terms of revenue for the second quarter of
14095 1996, slipped slightly to 84.5 percent from 87.4 percent in the year-ago second quarter.IBM's Lotus share of the most recent second quarter's suite market was roughly steady year-to-year at 7.8 percent. Corel gained a few points to hold 7.7 percent in the quarter. Corel had a very strong second quarter
14095 as revenue reached $68.6 million in the second quarter of this year.Lavin said Corel's success is due to the huge initial shipment of the new WordPerfect suite, although he warned that these products did not sell through to customers at the same rate that the company shipped the product to
14095 its distributors.Corel acquired WordPerfect from Novell Inc in January 1996.Dataquest said Lotus is succeeding in its goal of increasing SmartSuite unit shipments market share in 1996, with its share rising to 26.3 percent in the second quarter of this year, up from 12.4 percent in the same quarter last year.A
14095 key reason behind the gain is that SmartSuite is now bundled with every new IBM Aptiva consumer PC that ships.As a result, Microsoft's second quarter market share in terms of shipments was 66.3 percent, down from 80.0 percent in the second quarter of 1995.Corel's unit shipments held steady year-over-year at
14095 around 7.5 percent, Dataquest found.Because of rounding, the market share figures do not add up to 100 percent exactly.-- Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1736</

14099 International Business Machines Corp unveiled Thursday a line of personal computers that breaks ground in turning PCs into networked home appliances that fit conveniently in any room of the house.IBM said it has redesigned its new Aptiva "S Series" so a user has easy access to key features -- the
14099 keyboard, floppy drive, compact disc player, and monitor -- while the PC's main box can be stowed away under a desk, or perhaps a closet. "The Aptiva split system creates a better fit between consumers and their home computers by directly addressing their distinct usage, space and styling requirements," said
14099 Jose Garcia, general manager of IBM's consumer desktop unit.Even as these "split system" machines mark a significant departure from the clunky, all-in-one, beige boxes that dominate corporate offices, the new home PC line nonetheless borrows an insight from corporate personal computer systems. By separating the central processing unit from the
14099 essential user controls, IBM said it is paving the way for creating home computer networks similar in key respects to the local area networks that now dominate office PC systems.The new Aptivas reflect IBM's vision of extending home computers by locating "access stations" in rooms throughout the house that serve
14099 a variety of specialized functions, in effect turning the home into a computer local area network. These smaller computing units would be linked to a powerful server, or central processing machine, that could deliver entertainment or video games to the living room or housekeeping and business tools to the study.A
14099 home's lighting, heating, telephone and Internet communications, security and even lawn sprinkler systems could be managed in this way, according to IBM officials.Eventually such systems could act as a bridge from the home to cable, phone and utility companies. "It's as close to a grand slam as IBM has ever
14099 hit in the consumer market," said PC industry analyst Richard Zwetchkenbaum of International Data Corp, a Framingham, Mass.-based market research firm.But Emily Green, a Forrester Research analyst, said that while the machines offer several promising new features, their premium pricing -- complete systems start at around $3,000 -- are likely
14099 to keep them out of reach of first-time PC buyers.She noted that the entry of Sony Corp and several other Japanese consumer electronic giants into the U.S. home PC market is behind the drive by IBM and other established PC makers to make the latest home PCs more consumer-oriented."Sony has
14099 everyone else scared that Sony might be able to make a leap from last year's round of gray boxes to something new," Green said. "Everyone is trying to show they can think out of the box -- literally out of the gray box."IBM ranked behind Packard Bell Corp and Compaq
14099 Computer Corp, the number one and two suppliers of PCs to the U.S. consumer market, according to statistics compiled by market research firm Dataquest for the second quarter of 1996.-- New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1736</

14111 Argentina's economy is basically strong but its government must complete decisive reforms, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said Thursday."Argentina is truly on its way to entering the new century on a very, very solid basis," Camdessus said at a news conference held ahead of next week's joint meeting
14111 of the IMF and the World Bank. However, Camdessus said Argentina had yet to complete its structural reforms and grapple with pervasive corruption."Argentina is already playing in the world's first class league of strong economies (but) you can't stay there or prosper there if you don't get rid of the
14111 corruption factor and if you don't generally improve governance," he said.Camdessus pointed out that corruption was a problem all over the world, adding that Argentine authorities were committed to fight it.He added that governments that undertake structural reforms also have to be ready to face up to vested interests, such
14111 as trade unions that oppose measures to introduce flexibility in job markets.Argentina's trade unions started Thursday a 36-hour nationwide strike against the economic programs of President Carlos Menem, who has derided the protest as a lame excuse for a long weekend.Camdessus argued that one of the keys to solving Argentina's
14111 record unemployment rate, which under Menem has grown to 17 percent of the workforce, was to "reduce the privileges of those who have jobs for the benefits of those who do not have jobs". According to the IMF chief, the reforms Argentina launched in 1991 produced its best economic results
14111 in over 60 years."Argentina has made great progress towards the in-depth modernization of its economic structure, it got rid of inflation and it has availed itself with a currency which is as good as the dollar," he added.Argentina's peso is linked to the dollar by a 1991 law that established
14111 a currency board, under which its central bank must back the local currency with U.S. dollars, gold or government bonds.-- IMF newsroom (202) 898-8351</
14112 U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday called the world economic outlook encouraging although he said that growth in Europe and Japan still looks "quite moderate."In a wide-ranging briefing ahead of international meetings starting later this week, Rubin also reiterated his support for a strong dollar and his belief that
14112 the IMF will ultimately need to sell some gold to aid the world's poor.Rubin was upbeat on the outlook for the U.S. economy, calling it "very healthy" and saying he sees no sign of inflation reigniting. Growth looks set to remain solid. Rubin said that many U.S. industries are competitive
14112 globally now and he reiterated his opposition to using the dollar as a tool to better America's trade position.Currencies follow fundamentals, and U.S. fundamentals look "very good," he said."Prospects have improved in Japan and Europe, but growth in those regions still looks quite moderate," Rubin added.He said that it was
14112 "critically important" that Japan continue to pursue policies aimed at promoting domestic demand-led growth. "As you get into a period now where there will be somewhat of a change in (Japanese) fiscal conditions if nothing is done, obviously one needs to be watchful," Rubin said.With an election looming in Japan,
14112 Tokyo looks set to pass up a chance to issue a supplementary fall budget that some analysts argue is needed to keep its recovery on track."We are of course always interested in growth in Europe, too," Rubin said. "We look forward to a discussion by our European colleagues about their
14112 progress toward EMU (European Monetary Union) and the implications of these developments for the world economy." Rubin stressed the importance of European economic growth for the world and the U.S. economy and said he would be interested in hearing his European counterparts' views about the best policy mix to attain
14112 healthy growth.On Saturday, Rubin will meet finance ministers and central bankers from the rest of the Group of Seven -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan. That gathering will take place on the fringes of the semi-annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. Rubin said that
14112 he believed that the IMF would need to sell some of its gold to finance continuation of its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) and its participation in a multilateral debt relief plan.ESAF, which lends money to the world's poorest nations at virtually no interest charge, has enough resources to last
14112 until the year 1999 or 2000, he noted. "Once you get past that, you're going to need gold sales," Rubin said."In terms of how much they will be, I just don't know," he said. "The IMF at that time will sit down with its members to determine how many countries
14112 are involved in this, how much is needed, then you make a judgment on how much gold needs to be sold."Once the IMF decides to sell gold, the United States would be prepared to consult with Congress about the possibility of a U.S. bilateral contribution to the Fund's efforts to
14112 aid the world's poor, he said.Rubin said the U.S. also backs expanding the scope of debt relief provided by Paris Club creditors to poor countries to up to 80 percent from the current 67 percent limit.</

14124 since the Fed meeting.The December euro contract shows moderating expectations of tightening, for example. 14124 June contract gained the same to yield 6.05 percent.Spreads on two-year LIBOR swaps tightened by one to two basis points after the Fed meeting, but have since widened. On Thursday, spreads were quoted at 17 basis points bid, 19 to 20 basis points offered. Spreads were just a few basis

14128 capital equipment for the semiconductor industry, said difficult conditions in the industry prompted its actions. 14128 about eight to 12 percent in fiscal 1997 compared to fiscal 1996 due to a decline in capital spending by semiconductor device manufacturers.The company said fiscal 1996 pro forma net income is expected to be between $27.5 million and $29 million, or $1.20 to $1.25 per share, compared with $20.5
14128 million or $1.09 per share in the prior year. 14128 stock offerings completed in February and June 1995.FSI said its cost control measures will include mandatory furlough days, a reduction in executive compensation, a salary freeze for the entire employee base plus the workforce cuts. 14128 and engineering facility in Chaska, Minn. until mid-1997 instead of moving in December 1996."The semiconductor industry is experiencing a slowdown, which FSI and many independent industry analysts expect to last through the middle of calendar 1997," said chairman Joel Elftmann in a statement."The current employment level is beyond what we
14128 can sustain during this period," Elftmann added. 14128 "This backlog, along with recently announced orders and anticipated orders, provides us with a strong base to begin fiscal 1997," said Elftmann. "However, customers can cancel or delay orders. 14129 International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Thursday said he had a majority backing for modest sales of the Fund's gold if needed to help finance debt relief for poor countries.Speaking to a news conference, Camdessus said there was the "necessary support" to optimize resources in order fully to
14129 fund the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, a fund that offers financial aid to poor countries.Camdessus said he was unsure of the timing of any decision to sell up to five million ounces IMF gold or even if it would be necessary. He made clear the Fund would consider gold sales
14129 only if member countries could not come up with enough funding to replenish the ESAF and get the new program to assist poor countries under way.Turning to Europe, Camdessus expressed confidence that the deadline for the launch of a single European currency would be reached."I am confident that on Friday,
14129 the first of (January) 1999, we will have the new Euro system started," he said.He also said it was feasible for European countries to meet the budget goals set out in the Maastricht Treaty."We are of the view here that the Maastricht timetable is feasible," he said. "The success that
14129 the European countries have had in reducing inflation, in most cases already to very low levels, is indeed extraorinarily encouraging."He said given the expectations for economic growth, "Most European countries should be able to satisfy the Maastricht Treaty requirements for general government deficits."Under the Treaty, governments that wish to be
14129 founding members of European Monetary Union in 1999 must reduce their 1997 budget deficits to the equivalent of three percent of GDP, although there is some flexibility in the target.</
14130 The Colombian economy will expand by 3.5 percent in 1996, but build up to 5.0 percent growth next year as domestic demand accelerates, Colombia's Finance Minister Jos Antonio Ocampo said Thursday.The minister said that domestic demand, which was dampened by high domestic interest rates this year, will lead the economic
14130 upswing into next year. Oil and traditional exports will also boost the recovery, he said."The government projection is that we will grow at 3.5 percent in 1996," Ocampo said, adding that a private consulting firm pegged this year's growth at 3.1 percent. The government projects growth of 5.0 percent in
14130 1997 and 6.0 percent in 1998, compared with private forecasts of 4.0 percent and 5.0 percent for the two years, the minister said."There is a general consensus the current slowdown will give way to a recovery over the next two years," Ocampo said. "The major driving force in the recovery
14130 will be the recovery of domestic demand."The rebound in neighboring Venezuela should also help the Colombian economy, Ocampo said. Ocampo, speaking to investors at the Americas Society here, said the strength of the Colombian peso in recent months was due to increased foreign direct investment that brought an increased supply
14130 of dollars into the country.He also linked the peso's strength to the calming of Colombian markets after the easing of the political crisis surrounding President Ernesto Samper.For much of the year, Samper has been dogged by allegations that he knowingly accepted campaign contributions in 1994 from drug traffickers. The president,
14130 who was exonerated by a Congressional investigation, has steadfastly maintained his innocence and rebuffed numerous calls for his resignation.Ocampo said that, as the political climate stabilized, market fears of a major peso devaluation dissipated.He said that the Colombian government stopped bolstering its currency in mid-July, after seeing its mounting strength."We
14130 stopped selling dollars in mid-July," Ocampo said. "We have not sold a single dollar." The minister also said the government planned to expand the central government's foreign borrowing to $1.8 billion in 1997 from $1.4 billion this year.He explained the government's decision earlier this week to postpone a planned mark-denominated
14130 bond launch was because of insufficient time to finish the deal.Ocampo reassured investors on the upcoming rotation of members of the Monetary Board. The terms of two members of the board will expire in February 1997, and the president will appoint their replacements."I don't think there should be any major
14130 change in monetary stance as a result of the rotation in February 1997," he said.-- George Lerner, 212 859-1671</

14151 The uncertainty surrounding rugby union's European Cup increased on Thursday when it emerged that the final has been postponed to an undetermined date.The expanded competition, featuring clubs and provinces from England, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, France and Italy, had been scheduled to reach a climax on January 4 with the semifinals
14151 being played in mid-November.Now, to suit television who wanted more high-profile matches, a quarter-final round has been added with the semifinals switched to the first Saturday in January. A decision on where and when the final is played will be delayed until after the semifinals.Organisers are still hunting for a
14151 host broadcaster in Britain after ITV's withdrawal this week. Rugby sources said ITV were still prepared to screen the matches to publicise the tournament but would not be paying for them.Welsh Rugby Union chairman Vernon Pugh said negotiations were still continuing with other broadcasters and the chief sponsors, but reiterated
14151 the 20-team tournament, as well as the European Conference, would start as planned on October 12.Pugh admitted there had been concern from France over recent developments and suggested some representatives of leading English clubs, who have been reluctant to commit themselves to the tournament, should stop rocking the boat."We have
14151 had a process of destabalisation that has been in place for more than 12 months," said Pugh."The French were concerned about any prospect of the tournament being devalued, but I was able to assure them they would be getting a feed of the matches in Britain."They see the European Cup
14151 as being very significant. I would have thought clubs like Leicester and Bath would want to prove they're the best in Europe."Lions coach Ian McGeechan and French counterpart Jean-Claude Skrela are among those who think the tournament will be of immense value if the clubs treat it seriously."It's very important
14151 for clubs in the northern hemisphere to recreate the quality of rugby being played in the southern hemisphere," said Skrela."The European Cup offers a level of intensity between club and international rugby which should allow our players to make the step up more easily."</

14157 Coach Ian McGeechan wants the British Isles to play home test series as part of northern hemisphere rugby's blueprint for the new professional era.McGeechan, who will be in charge when the Lions depart in May for a 13-match tour of South Africa, believes there would be huge interest on all
14157 sides if major touring sides were given the chance to play the Lions on a regular basis."I think we underestimate how big the Lions are in South Africa. They see it as the biggest tour, full stop," McGeechan said on Wednesday after the official unveiling of the Lions' kit, which
14157 will include a sponsor's name for the first time."I think we should be having test series at home. If South Africa or New Zealand were here, playing against all the home unions followed by a three-test Lions tour, the interest would be incredible."The Lions concept faced an uncertain future last
14157 year when the game turned professional, but McGeechan feels the partnership between the four home unions should be seen as a positive example in the ongoing row between English clubs and the Rugby Football Union (RFU)."The Lions are going to become very important over the next few years, because they
14157 provide both tradition and modernity," he said, looking ahead to a daunting Lions programme which includes three tests on consecutive weekends in Cape Town, Durban and Johannesburg."Going to South Africa or New Zealand is the biggest challenge any player will face. This is the first professional tour and playing back-to-back
14157 tests on three consecutive Saturdays means we've only got 4-5 weeks to pull everything together."But we've just got to accept it and I think there are a lot of talented players who will emerge."Ray Williams, chairman of the Four Home Unions committee, confirmed the tour was "very definitely on" following
14157 discussions with South African Rugby Football Union supremo Louis Luyt last week.The first Lions tour to the Republic was in 1910. The British Isles only series victory in eight attempts came under Willie John McBride in 1974.</

14172 England, took over as coach of Shimizu earlier this year.He said afterwards: "I was nervous throughout the match, in which we gave all we had."Shimizu are currently placing 12th in the 16-team J.League table. 14174 The United States is banking on a high-performance European import to break Spain's stranglehold on the Fed Cup when the two nations meet in the finals this weekend.Co-world number one Monica Seles has been tabbed by U.S. captain Billie Jean King to spearhead her adopted country's campaign to claim the
14174 trophy the United States last held in 1990 -- not coincidentally the last year Spain missed the finals.There has been one superpower in Fed Cup competition this decade -- Spain -- featuring the most successful 1-2 punch the women's international team championship has seen since its inception in 1963."There are
14174 two good reasons why Spain has won everything the last few years," said King, "and that is Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Conchita Martinez -- the number two and three players in the world. They are the reason that Spain has been so dominating."Since the pair teamed for Federation Cup in
14174 the late 1980s they have been world beaters.The battling Barcelona baseliners have carried Spain to four Fed Cup titles in the last five years, including the last three. The finals begin with two singles on Saturday, followed by reverse singles and doubles on Sunday.This weekend's tie on the indoor carpet
14174 at the Atlantic City Convention Centre will mark Spain's sixth consecutive appearance in the finals and eighth in nine years -- all based on the play of Sanchez and Martinez, who usually join forces to play doubles as well as contesting the singles.For the third year in a row Spain
14174 and the United States meet at the last stage, with one significant difference this time around -- Seles."I wanted to be in the Olympics and Fed Cup for many years," said the Yugoslav-born Seles, who became a U.S. citizen in 1994 but has felt like an all-American girl since she
14174 laid eyes on her first Florida shopping mall at age 12.Seles, now 22, made her Fed Cup debut in July in the semifinals in Japan, where she easily won both her singles, crunching Kimiko Date with the loss of just two games.Seles faltered in the quarter-finals at the Olympics, but
14174 Fed Cup teammates Lindsay Davenport (singles) and Mary Joe Fernandez (doubles) walked away with gold.And Davenport's golden moment came at the expense of none other than Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.Linda Wild completes the American quartet, giving King a number of singles and doubles options. Davenport and Fernandez won the French Open
14174 doubles title this year and Davenport combined with Wild in the 5-0 semifinal win over Japan.Sanchez brings an impressive 35-11 Fed Cup singles record into the tie, while Martinez boasts a formidable 36-6 singles mark, 4-0 this year.It was former Wimbledon champion Martinez who proved the saviour in Spain's 3-2
14174 semifinal win over France, taking both her singles matches when Sanchez faltered, then teaming with Sanchez for the clinching doubles win.The last time the United States beat Spain in a final was back in 1989 when another rather impressive European import -- Martina Navratilova -- teamed with Chris Evert to
14174 beat a much younger, and no doubt awestruck, Sanchez and Martinez.The Spanish duo may not be in awe of Seles, but neither has figured a way to beat her either.Seles is 12-1 against Sanchez, including a victory last Sunday in a final in Tokyo. She raised her record to 9-0
14174 versus Martinez with a straight sets semifinal win at the U.S. Open earlier this month.Still, the Spaniards carry a wealth of Fed Cup finals experience into the weekend."She has the pressure," Sanchez said of Seles, who has never played a final in the team format. "(We'll) just go out and
14174 see what happens, sometimes statistics are not true."The Spaniards won't have the home court advantage as they did last year in Valencia. But as always, Sanchez is prepared to battle until the last ball bounces twice."We made the court as slow as can be last year because the Americans didn't
14174 like it," she recalled."This surface is much faster but as a pro you have to know how to play on any surface, and keep fighting."</

14179 The National Hockey League's Board of Governors, meeting in New York Wednesday, approved a series of rules changes for this season, one of which eliminates the "tag-up" play.The rules now -- as they did before officials began permitting the tag-up play to reduce stoppages in play -- will require that
14179 all offensive players be clear of the attacking zone before a puck is shot into the zone.A player in the attacking zone when a teammate dumps the puck in can no longer tag up in the neutral zone and return to the attacking zone without being called offsides.Another rules change
14179 appears aimed at the Florida Panther fans who pelted the ice with plastic rats last season and during last spring's Stanley Cup playoffs.According to the new rule, "any concerted or widespread conduct by the fans which results in the littering of the ice with any type of object will not
14179 be tolerated. A two-minute delay of game penalty may be assessed against the home team."The new rule will not apply to fans who toss hats onto the ice in the traditional celebration of a home-team hat trick.The NHL also adjusted its high-sticking rule, raising the standard from waist to shoulder
14179 height and exempting players who make contact with an opponent on a normal backswing or follow-through of a shot.However, an injury caused accidentally or carelessly by carrying a stick above the shoulder will result in a double minor penalty. Trying to injure an opponent by high-sticking, successfully or not, will
14179 result in a match penalty.Previously, accidental high-sticking injury brought a double minor penalty and careless injury a major and game misconduct.A minor penalty is still levied for striking an opponent above his shoulder.In other changes, a player who receives a major elbowing or charging penalty that results in an injury
14179 to an opponent's head or face will also be assessed a game misconduct.Players who attempt to head-butt, butt-end or spear an opponent will receive double-minor penalties, while game misconduct penalties will be assessed to players who succeed in head-butting, butt-ending or spearing.Also, the board approved the Panthers' request for a
14179 public offering of shares in the club. The offering is limited to 49 percent, with H. Wayne Huizenga and his family retaining a controlling interest. The plan still requires the approval of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.</

14191 there is no progress we will have to act," he said, adding that the Commission had received complaints.But UEFA spokesman Salvatore Cuccu said that UEFA and the EU were in close contact with each other regarding TV rights and but said Van Miert's warning should be regarded as part of
14191 the on-going debate."UEFA are working closely with the EU and a solution will be found in the next two years."Developments in digital technology and satellite television over the past few years have revolutionised the way soccer is now broadcast around the continent, and new rules are being established to take
14191 account of the huge new developments.Commission sources said the complaints had been filed by television channels which broadcast UEFA matches but do not have exclusivity rights. 14194 South Africa's largest trade union federation on Thursday accused white-led parties of negotiating in bad faith and threatened union action to defend the constitutional tilt towards worker rights.Neil Coleman, the Congress of South African Trade Unions' lobbyist at parliament, told reporters that National Party and Democratic Party proposals to amend
14194 a rejected labour relations clause of the draft constitution sought to undermine hard-won union rights."They're trying to reintroduce something that they know is unacceptable and it really is extremely provocative," he said."The message (from Cosatu) is to call on members to keep a close watch on the process and to
14194 remain ready to react to a call by the leadership of the federation to defend the positions won during the constitutional negotiations," he said.Coleman declined to say whether the federation would resort to strike action to defend a constitutional right to strike that is not linked to an employer's right
14194 to lock out strikers.The NP and DP have proposed amendments to a draft constitution partly rejected by the Constitutional Court which could reopen a bitter autumn debate about lock-out rights.Constitution writers declined to include a lock-out provision in their blueprint for post-apartheid rule, but declared the Labour Relations Act which
14194 guarantees a limited lock-out right immune to constitutional challenge.The Constitutional Court ruled that all law should be subject to constitutional challenge.The NP and DP endorsed a proposal to entrench an employer's right to collective bargaining, but added a reference to the "collective...exercise of economic power" by employers as a balance
14194 against the entrenched right to strike."It would entrench not only the lock out, but other action. The experts say it is a camouflaged way of introducing the lock out, which has been decisively rejected by the Constitutional Court," Coleman said."The court recognised that there is an inequality of power between
14194 the parties and that therefore the right to strike was not equal to the right to lock out."A sub-committee looking at w a new labour relations clause.Parties agreed to meet privately on Friday to explore ways to resolve the conflict, which should be settled by October 11.</

14196 The former chief of a covert South African police hit squad said on Thursday an apartheid spy had been involved in the 1986 assassination of Swedish prime minister Olof Palme.Eugene de Kock made the allegation while testifying in mitigation of sentence before the judge who convicted him last month of
14196 six murders and a series of other crimes.President Nelson Mandela's ruling African National Congress (ANC) reacted to the disclosure on Thursday night saying that -- if true -- it owed it to Sweden to ensure the perpetrators faced justice.De Kock, a colonel in the apartheid-era police, told the judge he
14196 had volunteered information to the prosecution."Like the assassination of Swedish prime minister Olof Palme," he said."It was one of Craig Williamson's 'Operation Long Reach' projects. I wanted it to be investigated before it was covered up," he said.Williamson was one of the white minority government's most effective spies during the
14196 1970s and 1980s and has admitted to carrying out bombings and other actions against anti-apartheid activists.He could not be reached immediately for comment on de Kock's statement. Operation Long Reach was a secret programme by the apartheid government to harass or silence its opponents abroad.The ANC, calling Palme a friend
14196 and staunch supporter of its anti-apartheid struggle, said it had requested the Attorney- General's office to keep a close watch on de Kock's trial to ensure that if international terrorism had been committed, legal action would be instituted."The people of South Africa owe it to Olof Palme and the people
14196 of Sweden, and democrats the world over, to ensure that the perpetrators of this evil deed face the full might of the law," the ANC said in its statement.The former black liberation movement also called on ex-president F.W. de Klerk's white-led National Party (NP) to make public any knowledge it
14196 might have on Palme's death."The National Party government must come clean on their knowledge or otherwise of this matter."The ANC has always believed that the murder of anti- apartheid activists at home and abroad was not the work of maverick elements within the former security forces, but a cold and
14196 calculated state action against democrats the world over," the party said.De Kock has previously said during the trial that he and Williamson collaborated in blowing up the ANC's offices in London while the ANC was still waging its liberation struggle.He gave no indication what motive Williamson would have had for
14196 involvement in Palme's murder but the Swedish leader had close ties to the ANC, which took power in South Africa's first all-race election in 1994.Palme's assassination by a gunman in a Stockholm street has never been solved although a broad range of theories have been put forward. The murder weapon
14196 has never been found.De Kock has applied to the country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission for amnesty for his crimes. The commission, set up to heal the wounds of apartheid, has powers to grant amnesty to perpetrators of human rights abuses who confess to their deeds.</

14198 The British government said on Thursday it was considering funding a new land resettlement programme in Zimbabwe after years of withholding aid over the use of a controversial land acquisition policy.Mark Lowcock, the head of a five-member British land appraisal mission to Zimbabwe, told a news conference London was talking
14198 to President Robert Mugabe's government about a resettlement scheme aimed at reducing rural poverty in the southern African state."We envisage a programme, including land acquisition, which the British government could help fund on the basis of the willing-seller principle," said Lowcock, who is deputy head of the Overseas Development Agency's
14198 office in Harare.He said it was still too early to say what the outcome would be, "but on the basis of our work so far, we are confident it should be possible to design a further programme which will justify funding by the British government and other interested donors."Britain --
14198 Zimbabwe's former colonial master -- helped settle thousands of black peasants after Zimbabwe's 1980 independence, but it withheld some money in the late 1980s when Mugabe adopted a controversial policy of forcibly acquiring farms from minority whites who occupy most of the country's fertile land.Mugabe, who swept to power in
14198 1980 after a seven-year guerrilla war during on a promise to give blacks a bigger share of the land, has forcibly bought some farms under that policy, but he has avoided the wholesale seizures many economists feared would derail Zimbabwe's mainstay agriculture sector.Over the past two years, Mugabe has been
14198 threatening to nationalise the white-owned farms without paying any compensation if Britain does not provide some money.At least a quarter of Zimbabwe's 10.5 million people has applied to be resettled.Lowcock, whose two-week land appraisal mission to Zimbabwe is due to end on October 4, said he did not know how
14198 much Britain was prepared to spend on a new resettlement scheme, but he said it would not be restricted to the Z$56 million (U.S.$5.42 million) left from the old allocation of Z$323 million (U.S.$31.2 million)."The principle objective of the (new resettlement) programme would be reduction of rural poverty. The programme
14198 would need to have an acceptable economic rate of return, be cost effective and be sustainable," he said.The scale and pace of implementation, Lowcock said, would need to reflect the implementation capacity and other constraints faced by relevant government and other institutions in Zimbabwe.$1=10.33</

14207 be restarted at the beginning of December, he said.Bulgaria's overstretched energy industry has been forced to ration electricity supplies since 1978 until 1973, relying on all the six reactors in Kozloduy's 3,760-megawatt plant and on its coal-fired thermal plants to meet the power needs.Bulgaria imports 80 percent of its energy
14207 resources and currently suffers an acute economic crisis.Earlier this week the central bank put nine ailing banks under special supervision and raised the interest rate to a record high of 300 percent in a bid to stabilise the country's wrecked financial system.Another problem for the Kozloduy plant is its fresh

14221 the granting academic titles.It also gives the ministry a say in the process of creating or closing existing university faculties.The law has come under fierce criticism by oposition deputies, as well as the country's academic representatives, who say it violates the principle of academic freedom and has an anti-democratic spirit."The
14221 proposed paragraph (on the ministry's decisive powers)... is a ruthless interference into the autonomy of universities and academic rights and freedoms of their authorities and individuals," Slovak university chiefs said in an open letter addressed to the government and parliament.Minister of Education, Eva Slavkovska, rejected the criticism, however, saying the
14221 ministry had no intention to cast doubts on professional decisions of the academic bodies."However, the ministry must have an opportunity to decide in a case if the university breaches the law or general regulations," she told parliament prior to the vote.In July, Madelaine Albright, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations,
14221 conveyed U.S.concerns of some legislative moves by the Slovak government, including the education law amendment.Immediately after the vote, opposition deputies said they had collected the neccesary minimum of 30 signatures, to demand an extra-ordinary session of parliament, with the only item on the agenda to be a non-confidence vote on
14221 Slavkovska.But Slavkovska, a member of the junior governing coalition partner, the ultra-right Slovak National Party, has the support of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democractic Slovakia (HZDS) and is expected to survive any non-confidence vote.</

14224 Romanian and U.S. medical experts have joined hands to track down a type of mosquito believed to be the carrier of a virus which killed 40 people in Balkan country's worst viral meningitis epidemic in a decade."Some 70 local specialists and visiting epidemiologists from the U.S. Center of Disease Control
14224 will capture mosquitos and send them to France's Pasteur Institute to see whether they are infected with the virus which caused the (meningitis) epidemic," Adrian Strainu-Cercel, a senior health ministry official, told a news conference on Thursday.As many as 453 patients, including some 50 children, were hospitalised across Romania after
14224 the epidemic erupted at the end of July. Of the 40 death toll, most were elderly people.Lab tests conducted at the Paris-based Pasteur Institute confirmed that the patients were suffering from the West Nile virus."We isolated the virus, now we must identify the carrier, which mosquito species is responsible for
14224 spreading the disease," Strainu-Cercel said.Lack of hygiene is behind meningitis spread. The viral disease, which usually lasts a week, causes high fever, headaches and vomiting and affects the gastro-intestinal tract.There is no specific drug treatment for the virus, which can degenerate into a fatal inflammation of the brain, known as
14224 meningoencephalitis.In 1986 Romania suffered an epidemic of the more dangerous bacterial meningitis which killed some 15,000 people in central Africa this year.</

14235 Nicu Ceausescu, the hard-drinking, womanising youngest son of Romania's late Stalinist dictator, died in a Vienna hospital on Thursday, where he was being treated for serious liver disease.Nicu, 45, was flown to Austria a week ago for specialised surgery in an attempt to save his life, after Romanian doctors admitted
14235 they lacked the necessary medical and surgical equipment to deal with his condition.His elder brother Valentin, said he was shocked by the news and could not immediately comment.Nicu was known as a womaniser who squandered vast sums of public money at the gambling tables of Las Vegas and other casino
14235 towns. His flamboyant reputation symbolised what many saw as the moral bankruptcy of his father's dictatorship.Nicu was rushed to the Bucharest university hospital on September 14 with internal bleeding, caused by what doctors said was a varicose oesophagus and acute liver cirrhosis.Nicu's critical health condition, coupled with a shortage of
14235 modern medical equipment, prevented Romanian doctors from performing vital surgery to prepare him for a liver transplant.He was flown to Vienna General Hospital last week where doctors were expected to bring his bleeding under control. He was believed to be on waiting list for the transplant when he died."Mr Ceausescu
14235 died at 6 a.m. (local time, 0400 GMT) this morning," a hospital spokeswoman said.His girlfriend of several years, Dana Radu, had accompanied him to the Vienna hospital.Nicu was the youngest of three children of late communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife, Elena.A violent revolution in December 1989 ousted the
14235 Ceausescus after a ruthless 24-year rule. They were shot by firing squad on Christmas Day.The communist nomenclatura, including the Ceausescu children, enjoyed luxurious lifestyles while the mass of the population lived in dire poverty with food rationing, power blackouts and lack of heating.Meat, dairy products and other staples had become
14235 scarce as Ceausecu tried to pay back foreign debt.Nicu, a physicist, was head of the Communist Party's youth wing and was posted to Sibiu in the early 1980s, where local people remember him for trying to resist his father's severe economic belt-tightening policies.Valentin, a nuclear physicist, and his sister Zoe,
14235 a mathematician, have kept a low profile since they were released from detention in 1990.Groomed to be his father's successor, Nicu was Communist Party boss in the central county of Sibiu when the 1989 revolution broke out.He was sentenced to 20 years in jail for mass murder after ordering the
14235 repression of protests in his Sibiu fiefdom during the 1989 revolt.He had always denied the mass-murder charge and accused the post-communist authorities of making him a scapegoat. That charge was later dropped and only a five-year sentence for illegal gun possession was upheld.By the time of his release on health
14235 grounds in November 1992, he had served half of the jail term -- enough for parole based on good behaviour.Romanian prosecutors earlier this year closed the file on a criminal probe launched against the Ceausescu children in the wake of the anti-communist revolution.They were cleared of charges of undermining the
14235 national economy -- charges on which their parents were killed -- by using their privileged position to exploit assets of the now defunct Communist Party.A foreign travel ban on the children was also lifted.Many Romanians now harbour ambivalent feelings about the Ceausescu era and their fall.Living standards are lower and
14235 many people believe the true story of the 1989 revolution -- which many see as a coup d'etat by former communists who have held power ever since -- has yet to be told. REUTER</

14242 World wheat prices will come under pressure in 1997 from this year's bumper crops but low stock levels will continue and add to price volatilities, the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Thursday.A monthly report by the IGC, an authoritative monitor of supply and demand in the grains trade, reported
14242 higher crop estimates for the European Union (EU), Argentina and Australia.It raised its forecast for this year's total wheat harvest by 8.0 million tonnes from a previous estimate to 571 million.But the bumper crops expected from Australia and Argentina, which rank among the world's top five wheat exporters, would weigh
14242 on prices early next year, the IGC said."The southern hemisphere harvests as they become available will have a strong influence on prices," said Bill de Maria, IGC assistant executive director. "There is the possibility of price pressure later in the season." Argentina's output was seen rising 5.8 million tonnes to
14242 14.5 million tonnes but its wheat would mostly arrive after January."They haven't got extensive storage facilities so the pressure for them will be to sell into the export market," de Maria told Reuters.Australia, which is re-emerging as a big potential seller to China, was seen harvesting 19 million tonnes of
14242 wheat, two million more than in 1995, after increasing the area sown to wheat, the IGC said.The present production trends reverse a price "spike" when drought in several key areas resulted in a drop in world grain stocks to the lowest since the 1970s.But low stocks are likely to continue
14242 for some years yet and increase price volatility on world markets, the IGC said.Although world stocks were forecast to rise by 10.0 million tonnes to 104 million by the end of this crop year, they would still be the lowest since 1980 except for last year."What's happened is that farmers
14242 saw better prices so they went for production in a big way," de Maria said, adding that even a small shift in total supplies could affect price trends.In its report, the London-based IGC said a "significant rebuilding" of global wheat stocks was expected."Even though the growth in total availabilities of
14242 wheat in relation to global consumption is relatively small, it has already been sufficient to have had a pronounced influence on the course of international prices for wheat," the IGC said."Perhaps the main lesson is that with lower levels of stocks, price volatility increases and current production prospects assume greater
14242 importance in assessments of world supply and demand for wheat."-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

14252 Several British doctors stepped into a growing debate over abortion on Friday, declaring that women who want to terminate their pregnancies should not fear that the foetus is suffering.In a clear message to anti-abortion groups which have presented videotape of foetuses twitching and apparently grimacing in the womb, the doctors
14252 said unborn babies could not feel pain.Several papers in the British Medical Journal addressed the issue and their consensus was that foetuses' nervous systems were not advanced enough to experience pain, at least not before about 17 weeks."Can a foetus feel pain? Given the definitions of feeling and pain the
14252 answer must be no," wrote Adrian Lloyd-Thomas of London's Great Ormond Street Hospital for children and Maria Fitzgerald of University College London.Babies showed reflexes to what could be painful stimuli, they said, but did not have enough brain development to register this consciously."Scientific evidence suggests women considering abortion can be
14252 assured that foetuses do not experience pain in the way that people who oppose abortion claim," said Dr Stuart Derbyshire of the University of Manchester.Vivette Glover and Nicholas Fisk of Queen Charlotte's and Chelsea Hospital in London said no one really knew if or when a foetus became conscious, so
14252 it would be better to err on the side of caution."The question of pain or suffering during termination of pregnancy is especially difficult," they wrote."Terminations are usually carried out before 20 weeks, when it is particularly uncertain whether the foetus feels anything at all. It may feel something, however, especially
14252 towards mid-gestation."Doctors used to say that new born babies could not feel pain, but studies have since shown that they do.But the doctors, all paediatricians, obstetricians or neurologists, writing in the British Medical Journal said foetuses were different from newborns.The abortion debate has come to the fore in Britain since
14252 recent reports of a woman who had one healthy twin aborted but kept another.A second woman who took fertility drugs announced she would try to carry eight foetuses to term.Doctors say the second woman should have some of the foetuses aborted to prevent them all dying. Anti-abortion groups have been
14252 very vocal in their opposition, demanding a re-think of Britain's abortion laws."These articles are a useful balance to what has been, until now, a hysterical and ill-informed discussion," said Ann Furedi of the Birth Control Trust charity."Doctors are not sadists. They perform abortions to relieve the suffering of women, not
14252 because they wish to inflict suffering on foetuses."</

14256 Governments and aid agencies have a moral and ethical duty to provide better health care to victims of war as combatants increasingly target civilians, an international team of doctors said on Friday.The conflict in ex-Yugoslavia especially illustrated how the elderly and women and children were taking the brunt of violence
14256 instead of soldiers, they wrote in the Lancet medical journal."More than in any other conflicts, the Bosnian tragedy has highlighted how wars are being focused on civilians, and are being designed to break the fabric of society by eroding health and the capacity of people to function normally," Dr Srecko
14256 Simic of Sarajevo's Kosevo Hospital and Dr Manuel Carballo of Geneva's International Centre for Migration and Health said."The denial of food, water, heat, shelter and physical and mental wellbeing to the people of Sarajevo and the other towns that were besieged for three and a half years has reminded us
14256 of mediaeval strategies in which the health and human rights of people were of little meaning."They said humanitarian agencies needed to focus on health care."The notion that healthcare services must inevitably suffer along with other services must be challenged and replaced by one that emphasises the ethical obligation of the
14256 international community to ensure continuity and even improvement of services in war," they wrote."At no time is the investment in women, mothers and children more important than in conflict and post-conflict periods."The long-term effects of the war would not be assessed for decades, they said. But simple things could ease
14256 the suffering -- and help prevent birth defects, psychological damage and other problems."For pregnant women, special food supplements should be fortified," they suggested.Health professionals should all lobby hard to keep health care in the 20th century. Otherwise, they said, "we will all be party to taking health back in time."</
14257 The old adage that an apple a day keeps the doctor away is true, doctors reported on Friday -- people who eat fresh fruit every day have fewer heart attacks.A Europe-wide study of diet and health also found that meat-eaters are more likely to be obese.The study, published in the
14257 British Medical Journal, added to a growing weight of evidence that people's bodies need a steady input of fresh fruit and vegetables.Britain's Imperial Cancer Research Fund (ICRF) and Medical Research Council are doing a study of 11,000 "health-conscious" people recruited through health-food stores, clinics and vegetarian societies.Interim results published on
14257 Friday show that, over a 17-year period, there were 32 percent fewer stroke deaths among people who ate fresh fruit every day compared to those who did not. They found a 24 percent drop in heart attack deaths and a 21 percent deacrease in deaths of all kinds."This study shows
14257 that if you do eat fresh fruit daily, the chances of dying from a heart attack or stroke are significantly reduced," said one of the report's authors, Dr Tim Key."It's a simple message which supports the old saying "an apple a day...'"Key added that there was also evidence fresh fruit
14257 protects against cancer and the study would be looking at this.In the second half of the study, 21,000 people classified as meat-eaters, fish-eaters, vegetarians or vegans were monitored for obesity, defined as being 20 percent over ideal weight."Within the group of meat-eaters 9.2 percent of women and 6.4 percent of
14257 men were clinically obese," the ICRF said in a statement. Among those who did not eat meat, including fish-eaters, 2.7 percent of men and 4.8 percent of the women were obese. Non meat-eaters were also slimmer, with vegans the slimmest. The longer the time since someone had eaten meat, the
14257 slimmer he or she was."These data suggest that a meat-free diet is associated with a low prevalence of obesity," Key's group wrote.</
14258 Britain, the country hardest hit by mad cow disease and a frightening new human equivalent, has been "uncomfortably" slow in developing tests for the disease, the Lancet medical journal said on Friday.Both U.S. and German researchers had reported live tests for BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy or mad cow disease) and
14258 Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) while Britain had come up with nothing, it said in an editorial.Dr Michael Harrington of the California Institute of Technology in suburban Pasadena said on Thursday he had developed a test that homes in on two proteins produced by the body in reponse to BSE or CJD
14258 infection.Inga Zerr and colleagues of Georg-August-Universitaet in Gottingen reported in the Lancet on Friday that they, too had developed a test using the cerebrospinal fluid of suspected CJD victims. They said the test was 80 percent accurate.Both BSE and CJD -- brain-wasting and fatal illnesses -- can currently only be
14258 positively diagnosed by brain autopsy. A "live" test would allow a living victim to be diagnosed."The news is potentially excellent. The course of the BSE epidemic may now be tracked in live animals, rendering a policy of indiscriminate slaughter barbaric," the journal, one of the most respected international journals of
14258 medicine, said."But further, and decidedly uncomfortable, questions arise," it went on. "Why were laboratory tests for spongiform encephalopathies developed in the USA and in Germany, countries that have worldwide average incidences of CJD, now new variant CJD, and no BSE?" it asked."Why did it take a report of 10 cases
14258 of new variant CJD to force the U.K. Ministry of Agriculture Fisheries and food to pay serious attention to BSE research, doubling its research investment for 1996/97 to 10.4 million pounds ($16 million) from 5.4 million pounds the previous year?"British government policies had led to the sacrifice of thousands of
14258 healthy cattle, it said. "They have also threatened the belief that UK scientists can respond adequately to a new infectious risk."British BSE experts immediately cast doubts on the usefulness of the tests."We only have evidence that the test is positive when the patient already has symptoms," John Pattison, chairman of
14258 the government's Spongiform Encephalopathy Advisory Committee, told BBC television on Wednesday.The British government said in March it had identified a new strain of CJD and said victims probably caught it from eating BSE-infected beef. Twelve people, 11 in Britain and one on France, have succumbed to the new variant.The announcement
14258 prompted the European Union to ban all exports of British beef and beef products. Britain embarked on a campaign to slaughter older animals thought most at risk of BSE.Pattison noted also that Harrington had only tested his new assay on nine cows, and did not have enough information to tell
14258 whether the test could be used to screen herds for the disease. ($1=.6416 Pound)</

14273 A record 23.7 million foreign tourists visited Britain in 1995 but the figures disguised the fact that the country's hotel industry has problems and needs shaking up, senior industry officials said on Thursday.The British Tourist Authority (BTA) said the visitors -- an increase of 13 percent on 1994 -- spent
14273 11.9 billion pounds ($18.5 billion), up 20 percent from the previous year."We have consolidated our recovery in global market share which we started to build two years ago, when Britain hit a record low of 4.4 percent. Today the figure is five percent," BTA chairman Anthony Sell told a news
14273 conference.Sell said the authority now was selling Britain as an fashionable country enjoying a major cultural renaissance."We've managed to recreate the image of Britain as an exciting, stylish and contemporary destination," he said, adding that preliminary figures for the first half of 1996 showed visitor numbers up 12 percent and
14273 spending up six percent."We are seeing growth three times the world average. Most of our competitors are seeing slower rates of growth and some are experiencing significant losses," Sell said.The figures conceal continuing problems in the hotel sector but BTA chairman David Quarmby said these were being tackled.A study carried
14273 out last year for the Department of National Heritage showed significant numbers of foreign visitors were unhappy with the quality and cost of their hotel rooms, especially in London."We are aware that research shows some visitors were not wholly satisfied with the quality of accommodation. We are working with the
14273 London Tourist Board and the hotel industry to address questions of quality," Quarmby said in an interview.He said 10,000 more hotel rooms would be needed in London by the turn of the century and he called for an increase in budget hotels of the kind found in France, where a
14273 family room costs around 35 pounds ($55).Tourists are also confused by five separate hotel classification schemes operating in Britain. Quarmby said talks were being held to merge the five into a single body, although he admitted progress had not been easy.</

14276 these falls were more than offset by rises in the number of people claiming a range of other benefits including family credit, sickness benefit, one parent benefit and invalidity benefit.The number receiving sickness and invalidity benefit rose by 157,000 to 2.4 million in the year to April 1995, the latest

14286 The 18 member airlines of the Cargo Multinational EDI Association (Cargo MEDIA) have agreed dates in 1997 for the implementation for key airfreight electronic data interchange(EDI) items, the association said in a statement.These include the implementation of an EDI based reservations facility, a neutral air waybill and four priority status
14286 messages, it addedCargo Media chairman, Robert Cutler from Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said the outcome "was a significant achievement by the group and confirms the commitment of its members in meeting their customer requirements in a quality and timely manner."The agreement came during Cargo Media's board meeting in Paris in
14286 mid-September. The airlines also agreed to consider setting up in each of their home markets, an EDI implementation group to promote and develop such messaging, the statement said.The first group has been set up in the UK and will be chaired by British Airways Plc, while a similar group will
14286 be formed in the U.S. and be chaired by Northwest Airlines.In detail the following measures(Schedule One) will start on January 1,1997.*Use of an EDI reservations facility, enabling customers to make bookings electronically with member airlines.*Introduction of the four priority status messages on which the group has been working. These are*consignments
14286 departed on a given flight(DEP)*consignments delivered to consignee (DLV)*consignments transferred to another airline or transportcompany (TFD).Most members will also introduce the discrepancy(DIS) message for missing cargo(MSCA), found cargo(FDCA) and offloaded cargo (OFLD) by the same date, it added .The remaining members will implement these no later than 30th June 1997.All
14286 member airlines confirmed that they would use the IATA Edition 14 Version 6 of the air waybill message (FWB) as a minimum with effect from January 1, 1997. They also agreed to support the introduction of the neutral air waybill in all markets.The statement said the Paris meeting also reviewed
14286 other messages (Schedule Two) and confirmed their implementation from end-1997. These are*consignment received from shipper or forwarder (RCS),*consignment received from flight(RCF)*consignment received from another airline(RCT)*consignment booked or rebooked (BKD)*consignment cleared customs(CCD) as well as the discrepancy messages for consignment short shipped (SPPD) and consignment overloaded (OVLD).A bar code labelling implementation
14286 programme will be prepared for the group by March 1997, for consideration by each member with a view to the introduction of bar code technology at all member-served airports at home and overseas, it added.To ensure consistency in the application of bar code label procedure in the industry, representatives of
14286 all member airlines will meet in the near future for a seminar on the subject, the statement said.Cargo MEDIA was formed in 1995 to promote EDI amongst in the airfreight industry and it says its members now handle 75 percent of the world's scheduled international air cargo.Apart from the airlines
14286 mentioned above, Cargo MEDIA members are Aer Lingus, Air Canada, Air France, Alitalia , American Airlines, Austrian Airlines, Japan Airlines, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Korean Airlines, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Qantas SAS, Singapore Airlines, Swissair and United Airlines. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017</

14295 justified," said ASDA coprporate counsel Nick Cooper. 14295 products at set minimum prices.ASDA said Bayer had objected to ASDA's refusal to increase the 30-tablet pack price on Alka Seltzer and had obtained a court injunction against the supermarket chain."We are disappointed with the ruling," Cooper added. 14295 a classic example." Britain's Office of Fair Trading has been investigating RPM in healthcare products and is expected to decide shortly whether to refer the issue to the restrictive practices court.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.</

14299 London-based analyst.But traders and ACPC delegates said a wave of leftist guerrilla attacks and highway blockades across the country was unlikely to derail Colombia's commitment to ACPC efforts to stabilise supply and put a floor under coffee prices.Colombia is the world's second-largest producer after Brazil with exports representing about 18
14299 percent of total world supply.Colombia's coffee exporters have already felt the effects of the rebel violence, announcing this week that some coffee shipments would have to be delayed."The guerrillas are definitely seeking to upset the apple cart," added the analyst.Offensives over the past few months by Colombia's largest rebel forces,
14299 the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and the National Liberation Army (ELN), have split the country and brought chaos to overland transport."There are grave concerns about guerrillas because they're not bothered what grade of coffee we're hauling, they just set it on fire. 14299 panic," said a Colombian private exporter.Some coffee traders this week hinted domestic problems might deflect Colombia's attention at the two day meeting of ACPC, that represents 80 percent of world production.But ACPC sources saw this as unrealistic."Colombia's commitment is unquestionable," said one."The Federation (Colombia's coffee federation) is fully committed to
14299 the ACPC. I would ignore any talk of flailing commitment," said a source, familiar with Colombian policy.At its meeting on Friday and Saturday, the ACPC will contemplate the effectiveness of its 1995/96 and 1996/97 export plans and review the market situation.The ACPC last met in May when it agreed a
14299 new plan to limit green coffee exports from its 14 members to 53.5 million 60-kg bags in the year to June 1997 against 45.8 million in 1995/96.ACPC Secretary-General Roberio Oliviera Silva said preliminary figures showed ACPC exports in the 1995/96 period reached 47 million 60-kilo bags against the target of
14299 45.8 million."I am very happy with that figure. It shows we are able to coordinate our efforts in terms of putting a floor under supply," Oliviera told Reuters.Since the ACPC's last meeting in May, second-month robusta coffee futures have slid from $1,970 a tonne to their lowest level in over
14299 two years at $1,475 a tonne.When asked if the ACPC was concerned about recent price falls, Oliviera said: "We are always concerned about the price evolution, especially when prices fall. We will analyse the market situation. It is on the agenda."</

14310 British Telecommunications (BT) said on Thursday that a 1.1 billion pound ($1.7 billion) investment in France had secured its position as a pan-European telecom player and dismissed criticism that it was a gamble.The company is taking a 25 percent stake in a new, four billion pound French telecom group, CEGETEL,
14310 which it hopes will become the main rival to state-owned France Telecom when the French market is opened up to competition in 1998.BT, which already has operations in 30 countries and employs about 130,000 staff world-wide, is also investing the share capital of BT France, worth about 100 million francs
14310 ($19.4 million), in the venture with France's Compagnie Generale des Eaux.Analysts welcomed the news that secures BT's presence in France with one of the best partners available -- and knocks out its major rival in Europe, U.S. telecom giant AT&amp;T."Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE), is the only major company in
14310 France that has made serious noises about wanting to compete with France Telecom," said a London-based telecoms analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.The deal, which BT said would be marginally earnings dilutive in the short term but was expected to have "significant long-term benefits", comes on top of BT's alliances in
14310 Spain, Italy, Germany, France, Holland and Scandinavia."It now gives us enough reach that we can call ourselves pan-European," said Sir Peter Bonfield, BT's chief executive. "We can gain economies of scale across Europe with billing systems and technology."Bonfield dismissed criticism that BT was paying over the odds in a desperate
14310 attempt to gain access to the French telecom market, estimated to be worth about 14.8 billion pounds."It's not short-term desperation, it's long-term planning," he told a news conference, adding that talks between the two companies had been "short and mostly sweet"."It is a lot of money but I think it
14310 is a fair price," he said. BT said it would be disappointed if it did not gain access to 15-20 percent of the French telecoms market.BT is hoping that CEGETEL, which has not yet traded and currently has only mobile telephone interests, will next year win a fixed licence to
14310 operate a full range of telephony services in France from 1998.BT now says it is well-placed to become the second operator in major European countries ahead of market liberalisation in 1998. But Bonfield said it was too soon for BT to switch its focus away from this continent and towards
14310 key Asian markets.As there is no magic January 1, 1998 date for competition in Asian telephone markets, Bonfield said BT -- which already has a joint venture in Japan, the world's second-largest telecom market -- would be seeking alliances there "country by country".BT and CGE, which is taking a 50
14310 percent stake in CEGETEL, are teaming up with American's SBC Communications Inc, formerly South Western Bell, which is taking a 15 percent stake, and Germany's Mannesmann, which is taking 10 percent.CEGETEL's principle asset is its 76.8 percent stake in loss-making SFR, France's number two mobile telephone group. SFR says it
14310 has won about 40 percent of the mobile telecom market, with over 700,000 subscribers.The company, which posted a pretax loss of 769 million francs in 1995, is not expected to move into profit before 1998 and has been criticised for not investing soon enough in GSM (global system for mobile
14310 communications) technology.Britain's mobile telephone operator Vodafone Group has a 20 percent stake in SFR. Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' is selling its indirect holding in the French company as part of the deal.BT's shares were trading at a steady 364.5p, up two pence.
