14313 IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had assigned Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, an individual rating of B/C and a legal rating of 2. IBCA said in a statement that its rating reflected the prospective deterioration in Thailand's economic environment, which could be expected to
14313 some degree to impact negatively Bangkok Bank's balance sheet."The bank's good performance record would warrant a higher ranking, were it not for the uncertainty created by Thailand's impending economic slowdown," the statement said.IBCA said the individual rating was an evaluation of the bank's financial strength based on the premise that
14313 it was entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners. The highest Individual rating awarded by IBCA is A. Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if it ran into trouble. IBCA
14313 said Bangkok Bank had developed a strong franchise throughout the South-East Asian region and maintained in excess of 20 percent loan and deposit market shares in its home market.In common with other Thai banks, Bangkok Bank had benefited from a favourable operating environment in recent years, experiencing buoyant growth in
14313 revenues and loan assets and a low level of loan losses. Non performing loans accounted for less than four percent of loans at March 1996. Notwithstanding its dominant market position, Bangkok Bank's performance ratios were not as impressive as some of its rivals, in part because the bank provided more
14313 than it needs to in good years in order to smooth its profitability in subsequent years."Therefore, the level of provisioning does not truly reflect the quality of the loan book but should ensure that profitability is not severely affected by the expected slowdown in the Thai economy," the statement added.--

14322 High world prices for grains and potatoes and European Union (EU) aid payments combined to make 1995/96 the most profitable year ever for British farmers, according to chartered accountants Deloitte &amp; Touche.But this combination is unlikely to be repeated and the firm said farmers must plan for leaner times and
14322 expect much more volatile markets as trade barriers are reduced.The survey of farm incomes is based on the actual returns from the 83,000 hectares farmed by Deloitte &amp; Touche's Agriculture's clients in lowland England.Average land use was 62 percent combinable crops, eight percent root crops, 14 percent for forage/dairy with
14322 nine percent in set-aside.The survey shows average net income in the year to end-June 1996 rose 29 percent to 363 stg a hectare, said Deloitte partner Vincent Hedley Lewis.But there was a wide gap between the most and least profitable farmers with the top 25 percent seeing net income rising
14322 20 percent to 717 stg a hectare whilst for the bottom quartile it climbed 82 stg to just 104 stg a hectare.Most of the improvements came from a sharp improvement in combinable crops and were due to factors beyond farmers' control like weather, world trade, exchange rates and to a
14322 lesser extent EU policy.Deloitte said the best farmers made the most efficient use of inputs.The top 25 percent had the highest wheat yeilds of 8.28 tonne per hectare and thanks to tight cost controls including spending less than the average on sprays, had the lowest production costs per tonne of
14322 79 stg.The lowest quartile of Deloitte's clients achieved a wheat yield of 7.78 tonnes a hectare at a cost of 99 stg a tonne.Farm size, soil types and the amount spent on variable costs were not significant factors in differentiating between farmers' profitability.--Douglas Learmond, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7773</

14323 Dealers said the next major hurdle for the dollar was now at 1.5250 marks where profit-taking set in earlier in the session.The dollar got a helping hand from a half point cut in the Swiss discount rate to 1.0 percent. The move was in line with the recent decline in
14323 money market rates, the SNB said."The Swiss rate cut had quite a psychological impact on the dollar as it highlighted the dire economic situation in Europe," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.The Swiss franc tumbled after the cut to a low of 1.2565 per dollar and
14323 82.35 centimes from around 81.87 and 1.2425 just before the move. It settled at 82.28/31 and 1.2524/34 later. 14323 1.54/1.55 mark area, provided U.S. yields did not drop more sharply."If that happened the dollar's yield premium would be diminishing which would put a question mark over its ability to rally much further in the longer term," said Norfield.A surprisingly large drop in U.S. durable goods orders for August confirmed
14323 the view of some analysts that the Federal Reserve was right not to raise rates at this stage. Others wondered whether the U.S. central bank will need to raise rates later this year. But since durable goods data are often subject to major revisions the dollar took the data in
14323 its stride and stayed afloat above 1.52 marks."The data suggest the economy is slowing and that it might be less likely that the Fed will raise rates if this continues," said Stretch at NatWest. "But durable goods are a notoriously volatile number, so I wouldn't get too hung about it."Orders

14327 Alistair Darling, the opposition Labour Party's shadow chief secretary at the UK Treasury, re-affirmed the Party's commitment to give tax incentives for long-term savings and to streamline insurance regulations.Darling told delegates at an insurance industry conference in Newcastle that a Labour government "would ensure appropriate fiscal incentives to encourage long
14327 term savings, such as life insurance."He declined to make any solid promises on tax, but said he recognised the imbalance in tax treatment between life insurance on one hand and personal equity plans (PEPs) and tax exempt savings deposits (TESSAs) on the other, and reiterated his party's opinion that it
14327 is right to use tax benefits for such a goal.He added that Labour wants to simplify regulation of the insurance and financial sectors under the Securities and Investments Board, which would oversee the work of certain other self-regulating authorities.The proposal follows a series of problems in parts of the UK
14327 financial sector in recent years involving the mis-selling of pensions in the UK and difficulties at Lloyd's of London insurance market."The current system is confusing and does not lead to public confidence," Darling told delegates at the Chartered Insurance Institute conference in Newcastle."We don't want to put the job into
14327 the hands of civil servants or politicians - we aim to have a blend of public and professional interest. We want to promote a new professionalism - that is where the future of this industry lies."Darling added that although it might be difficult to bring in regulatory and tax changes
14327 at the same time, he hoped both could be done reasonably close to each other.His appearance at the conference was the latest in a series of measures aimed at winning confidence from the financial sector that a Labour government would not be bad for business.Asked by one insurer about his
14327 views on European monetary union, Darling said: "We have no difficulty with the idea of a single currency, but whether or not this country joins must depend on whether there is a sustainable economic convergence. We have to be absolutely sure that the structures set up are going to work."--

14345 Canada's exports of canola and canola oil are not likely to rise in response to European concerns about a new variety of genetically altered U.S. soybeans, Canola Council of Canada vice president Tony Zatylny said."We do not benefit from this flap, although we are watching very carefully to see what
14345 this means for our canola exports in the long term," Zatylny told Reuters, noting that a percentage of Canadian canola is produced from transgenic seed. EuroCommerce, a trade group that represents food retailers and wholesalers in 20 European countries, said on Thursday that it wanted gene-altered soybeans to be identified
14345 in foodstuffs.U.S. farmers are just starting this year's soybean harvest, which included the first batches of a genetically altered soybean strain developed by U.S. chemical company Monsanto to withstand its herbicide, Roundup.The American Soybean Association estimates that only 30-50 million bushels of "Roundup Ready" genetically altered soybeans will be produced
14345 this year, or at most about two percent of the estimated 2.3 billion bushel U.S. crop. A report from Germany's farm price office ZMP on Thursday said rapeseed oil was replacing soyoil in some European buying now because of doubts about consumer acceptance and trade rules.Europe was still a relatively
14345 small market for Canadian canola, which mainly goes to Japan, the U.S. and Mexico. From 1989 to 1995 Canada exported about 380,000 tonnes of canola to Europe annually, against 1.7 million tonnes to Japan, he said.Zatylny said five herbicide-tolerant transgenic varieties of canola were registered in Canada, representing three to
14345 four percent of nine million acres of canola planted this year. Canada already has a system in place to identify genetically altered canola, he said.Canadian canola exports to Japan were identity-preserved and marked transgenic and non-transgenic, Zatylny said."However, it appears that we will soon have clearance to export transgenic canola
14345 to Japan, probably next year," Zatylny said.But he said the genetics question has to be cleared up in Europe, which does not have all the rules in place for accepting genetically altered crops."Now the question is, if they (EU) approve genetically altered soybeans, will that approval extend to canola?" he
14345 said.(Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720)</
14346 The president of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Thursday the Canadian exploration company it will begin its search for a heavyweight mining partner in the first half of October."In the first couple of weeks, we should be more definite in determining what we're going to offer," David Walsh, Bre-X's president
14346 and chief executive told Reuters.Bre-X wants a major mining partner to help it develop the spectacular Busang gold deposit, he said. The Calgary-based company will wait until it has received work contracts from the Indonesian government before the bidding, Walsh said. The Indonesian contract of work is expected in the
14346 next couple of weeks, he said and the company plans to release to release more drilling results and reserve estimates when it announces the contract, Ward told Reuters by telephone.The winning bidder will not necessarily depend on price. "Price isn't everything. You can get a little bit less if you
14346 have a better operator," said Ward.Bre-X has not yet decided how the partnership will be arranged. It will consider a merger, acquisition, joint venture or sale of a majority interest in the gold deposit, Ward said. "We may just zero in on one company that may fit the bill, that
14346 we can live and work with," he said, adding that the bidding process will be kept "low-key"."We don't want to get into an auction thing, that's not what we want to do," he said.Only a few major mining companies have the operating experience and deep pockets to be able to
14346 consider operating the rich deposit, said Ward.Bre-X has already been in contact with these companies, but Ward declined to name them. Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc said this week it was interested but would wait to see Bre-X's terms before deciding whether to put in an offer.Bre-X has said previously it
14346 wanted to sell a 25 percent piece of Busang. But now, under the guidance of its financial advisers, the company is considering a wide range of options, Walsh disclosed."As we get into the number crunching, we want to have total flexibility with a partner," he said. "We don't want to
14346 be tied to anything that's been said before."Drilling at the Busang deposit has outlined at least 46 million ounces of gold so far, but experts believe the deposit will be much larger, becoming one of the richest gold deposits in the world.-- Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104</

14348 The Canadian Wheat Board reduced its September Pool Return Outlooks (PROs) for wheat and feed barley prices for the 1996/97 (August/July) crop year by $15 and $7 per tonne on promising output, the CWB said.The PROs are a monthly Board estimate of world prices but not connected to CWB initial
14348 payments to farmers, which were announced July 29 and took effect August 1, 1996.Benchmark No1 Canada Western Red Spring Wheat PROs dropped to the $217-$237 range from the $232-$252 range in August.No1 Canada Western Feed Barley fell to $150-$170 from the $157-$177 range in July. Special select Canada Western Two-Row
14348 Malting Barley prices rose to the $225-$245 range from July's $230-$250.Durum wheat slipped to $205-$235 from $210-$240. Six-row malt barley slipped to $185-$205 from $191-$211.The CWB said wheat prices dropped on improved wheat output prospects in several major exporting and importing regions. Global wheat production is projected to increase by
14348 eight percent over last year. With most of this increase expected to occur in the five major exporting regions, the market anticipates more intense competition, driving prices down substantially from this spring. Despite projections for relatively tight world stocks at the end of 1996-97, the European Union (EU) has resumed
14348 the use of export subsidies on wheat sales to markets previously buying commercially.Barley prices fell this month because of increased projections for EU barley production. Production was projected to be up 16 percent from a year ago.Favorable crop quality prospects caused two-row and six-row barley prices to drop. Rains aided
14348 Australia's two-row crop and EU's malting barley was better than expected. The U.S., a major customer for Canadian six-row barley, has completed its harvest with better than expected quality which may reduce demand for Canadian supplies. 14350 Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard said on Thursday the Canadian government's request for a Supreme Court ruling on Quebec separation will not affect his government's sovereignty referendum plans."It is certain that it will not affect in any way the future of Quebec and the determination of this government to hold a
14350 referendum," Bouchard told reporters in French at the provincial legislature. Bouchard was reacting to the Canadian government's announcement on Wednesday that it would ask the country's Supreme Court to rule on the legality of any future unilateral declaration of independence by Quebec.Asked whether the federal government's action would affect his
14350 "referendum calendar," Bouchard replied: "Not at all."He said Quebec will continue to focus on putting its fiscal house in order and tackling its economic problems, including its high unemployement rate. Bouchard has said previously that he would hold another referendum on Quebec sovereignty only after the next provincial election, which
14350 can be called at his government's discretion, but could be up to three years away.Bouchard said Quebec will not appear before the Supreme Court to defend against the federal government's action on the sovereignty issue."This is not for a tribunal (court) to decide those questions," Bouchard said in English. Those
14350 questions are about the sovereignty of a will democratically expressed by a people."-- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434</
14351 Canada's Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy has bitterly attacked "appeasers" within the Commonwealth for trying to weaken sanctions against Nigeria's military regime.Axworthy, stung by criticism of Canada's aggressive approach to sanctions, warned the Commonwealth in a newspaper interview published on Thursday that it risked allowing Nigeria to "get away with" executing
14351 author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other political dissidents last November."There are officials working on this in the Commonwealth who have lost all sight of what it's all about," Axworthy told the Toronto Globe and Mail in an interview from the United Nations."It's a sad commentary on the attitude of some
14351 people inside the Commonwealth that they're talking about flattering the Nigerians, who only a few months ago were executing political dissidents and are still engaged in the most active kind of repression," he said.The Canadian foreign minister was reacting to a Reuters report from London on Wednesday in which some
14351 Commonwealth officials expressed irritation with Axworthy, saying he was needlessly antagonizing Nigeria."Axworthy seems to have lost the script on this one," said one unnamed Commonwealth official. "He does not understand that the Nigerians are a very proud people and you have to try to flatter them by making them feel
14351 important."Axworthy hit back, saying the comment "sounds like a ploy by some of the appeasers inside the Commonwealth secretariat to try to soften even further the stand on Nigeria, which is already, I think, sadly diluted."The Commonwealth's London-based secretariat has more than 300 employees and administers the affairs of the
14351 53-nation Commonwealth, which groups Britain and its former colonies and protectorates.Nigeria's military regime, led by Gen. Sani Abacha, in addition to executing the nine minority-rights activists, has jailed hundreds of other dissidents and repeatedly delayed its own target dates to hold national elections.The country, which became independent in 1960, was
14351 suspended from the Commonwealth after the executions last year. Commonwealth ministers also agreed on a package of sanctions that included a ban on sports links and arms sales, but not on oil imports, which are Nigeria's main source of export earnings.Axworthy said he feared a Commonwealth ministers meeting set for
14351 this Saturday in New York would produce little progress on sanctions."We'll have our discussion this weekend, but it seems to me they're simply setting up the scenario for another delay ...," he told the Globe and Mail. "Time is getting awfully short."</

14355 Analysts say North American newsprint commodity prices are likely to head lower over the next few months and reach bottom in early 1997.Newsprint is currently being sold to core customers in the eastern United States at $500 to $570 a metric ton, a precipitous slide from the price cycle peak
14355 of $740 a tonne in March.Analysts expect the price to decline further in the coming months, possibly eroding to $500 a tonne and below. "We will see $550-540 (a tonne) for October and then I will expect $500 before the end of the year and $450 bottom sometime early next
14355 year," said Richard Kelertas, of Bunting Warburg Inc.Kelertas is one of the most bearish analysts on the outlook for newsprint prices, but others agree that the North American newsprint industry, including the big Canadian producers such as Abitibi-Price Inc, Stone-Consolidated Corp and Avenor Inc, are in for a rough ride
14355 in the months ahead. The main problem is that the industry is burdened by producer and consumer inventory surpluses that are heading toward historic highs.Preliminary figures for August show that North American producer and consumer newsprint inventories (excluding Canadian consumers) were at roughly 2 million tonnes, well above the 1.6
14355 million tonne norm expected for this period. Most analysts are now negative on the newsprint sector and expect to stay that way until sometime in 1997.The Toronto Stock Exchange's paper and forest products index is down 22 percent from its 1995 peak and analysts say it could slip another three
14355 to five percent. Newsprint makers' stock prices could slip below their 52-week lows."Things may bottom and stay at the bottom for some time," said independent analyst John Duncanson. Newspapers struggling to maintain circulation and advertising revenues have been cutting back on their newsprint usage. Conservation measures, such as printing smaller
14355 and fewer newspaper pages, competition from electronic media and mergers and acquisitions in the publishing industry have also crimped newsprint consumption.Newsprint makers have also been hurt by their own zeal in ramping up prices aggressively in 1994 and 1995. The price hikes hurt newspaper publisher profits just as the industry
14355 was coping with tough circulation and advertising markets. Ironically, some of those hardest hit, Abitibi-Price and Stone-Consolidated, have been North American leaders in taking downtime at their newsprint mills in an effort to redress inventory surplusses.Since January, Stone-Consolidated has taken a total of 128,000 tonnes of downtime at its Canadian
14355 mills, including three weeks slated for its Kenora, Ontario mill in October, which is traditionally the industry's biggest shipment month. Saucier estimates that to bring producer and consumer inventories back into line, the operating rate for all of the North America industry must decline to 90 percent. If U.S. newsprint
14355 makers do not lower their operating rate convincingly, Canadian producers would have to drop their rate to 84 percent, an unrealistically low rate, he said.Jim Rowland, publisher of the newsletter Canadian Paper Analyst, said the lack of industry discipline means newprint commodity prices could decline to the cash-cost level of
14355 the sector's highest-cost producers. "A lot of smaller and mid-size producers have been running flat out," Rowland said.Still, there are some hopeful signs on the horizon. While newsprint prices may slip further, consumption levels may have already hit bottom, said Saucier."I think we have hit bottom in terms of consumption,
14355 but the price declines show how powerful an inventory correction can be," he said. But it may take several months to work through the inventory surplusses That situation will be exacerbated by an estimated 3-4 million tonnes of new newsprint production capacity coming on stream globally from mill start-ups and
14355 machine accelerations between 1995 and 1998, mainly in Asia.Canadian newsprint producers already have been diverting newsprint from traditional Asian markets to Europe, where prices are higher than their North American counterparts but are also falling."When you've got tonnage that you want to move, you tend to spot price it, or
14355 offer deals, and that brings prices down," Kelertas said.U.S. newsprint producers have not done their part to curtail production in the face of declining shipments, said Richard Saucier, analyst at ScotiaMcLeod Inc."Since the beginning of the year, the newsprint industry's operating rate in the United States has been 97 percent,
14355 while it has been 91 percent in Canada," Saucier said.-- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434</

14358 six murders and a series of other crimes.De Kock, a colonel in the apartheid-era police, told the judge he had volunteered information to the prosecution."Like the assassination of Swedish prime minister Olof Palme," he said."It was one of Craig Williamson's 'Operation Long Reach' projects. I wanted it to be investigated
14358 before it was covered up," he said.Williamson was one of the white minority government's most effective spies during the 1970s and 1980s and has admitted to carrying out bombings and other actions against anti-apartheid activists.He could not be reached immediately for comment on de Kock's statement. Operation Long Reach was
14358 a secret programme by the apartheid government to harass or silence its opponents abroad.President Nelson Mandela's ruling African National Congress (ANC) reacted to the disclosures saying that -- if true -- it owed it to Sweden to ensure the perpetrators faced justice.Calling Palme a friend and staunch supporter of its
14358 anti- apartheid struggle, the ANC requested the senior state prosecutor to keep a close watch on de Kock's trial to ensure that if international terrorism had indeed been committed, action would be instituted."The people of South Africa owe it to Olof Palme and the people of Sweden, and democrats the
14358 world over, to ensure that the perpetrators of this evil deed face the full might of the law," the ANC said in its statement.The former black liberation movement also called on ex-president F.W. de Klerk's white-led National Party (NP) to make public any knowledge it might have of Palme's death."The
14358 National Party government must come clean on their knowledge or otherwise of this matter."The ANC has always believed that the murder of anti- apartheid activists at home and abroad was not the work of maverick elements within the former security forces, but a cold and calculated state action against democrats
14358 the world over," the party said.De Kock has previously said during the trial that he and Williamson collaborated in blowing up the ANC's offices in London while the ANC was still waging its liberation struggle.He gave no indication what motive Williamson would have had for involvement in Palme's murder but
14358 the Swedish leader had close ties to the ANC, which took power in South Africa's first all-race election in 1994.Palme's assassination by a gunman in a Stockholm street has never been solved although a broad range of theories have been put forward. The murder weapon has never been found.De Kock
14358 has applied to the country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission for amnesty for his crimes.The commission, set up to heal the wounds of apartheid, has powers to grant amnesty to perpetrators of human rights abuses who confess to their deeds.</

14370 producers, staff and Ivorian nationals.The government said that the sell-off formed part of the liberalisation of the West African nation's cotton sector.Ivory Coast set up the company in 1974 with France's Compagnie Francaise de Developpement des Textiles (CFDT). 14370 marketing Ivory Coast's cotton crop. 14370 supporting producers. 14374 Oil producer Congo, striving to inject new life into its listless economy, is part way through an ambitious programme to boost domestic electricity generation and it has already started to feel the benefit.But with work having begun on a huge project at Sounda in Kouilou region in the west, officials
14374 say it is hoping one day to become an exporter of power to neighbours on the world's poorest continent.Officials at the state power company Societe Nationale d'Electricite (SNE) say that electricity imports from Zaire dropped from 45 percent of needs in 1995 to two percent in 1996.This follows the rehabilitation
14374 in May of the Djoue River hydro-electric plant with the help of South African funding and expertise, they add.Congo, despite its oil exports, slipped into economic decline in the 1980s but the government of President Pascal Lissouba is working to cut its budget deficit under the guidance of the World
14374 Bank and the International Monetary Fund.Officials say that Congo has run up a debt estimated at nine billion CFA francs with neighbouring Zaire for electricity imports from its giant Inga dam.Self-sufficiency in power generation is a goal several other pre-emerging African economies -- notably Ivory Coast and Ghana -- have
14374 set themselves.Congo, like Zaire, has considerable hydro-electric potential on the rivers that criss-cross its territory. A tiny part of its generating capacity is thermal.Djoue, outside the capital Brazzaville, is the oldest hydro-electric plant in Central Africa. The 15-megawatt plant was knocked out of action by a flood in 1991.South African
14374 company Rotek provided the expertise to get it working again while the South African Investek Bank Limited provided the funding in the form of a 4.5 billion CFA loan.Officials say the annual saving of bringing Djoue back on stream will be an estimated 800 million CFA francs.The government launched a
14374 two-year programme in 1995 to cut Congo's dependence on Zairean electricity, to extend electricity to more homes and above all to ensure that the national economy enjoys what it dubbed high quality and adequate energy supply.Congo's main plant -- 74 MW -- is on the Bouenza River.The Djoue scheme was
14374 just one of several designed to boost Congo's electricity production capacity from 162 megawatts to 412 megawatts using plants powered by the nation's rivers.The programme requires investment of 206 billion CFA francs 79 percent of which the government hopes to fund from the private sector, 18.5 percent from its own
14374 resources and 2.5 percent from the state power company. It has high hopes of encouraging further South African investment.The largest project, launched on June 15 by Lissouba, envisages construction of a 1,000 megawatt dam at Sounda in the Kouilou region. 14404 Ivory Coast has postponed an announcement on the opening of its 1996/97 coffee marketing campaign because of world price fluctuations, industry sources say.Ivorian Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan told an industry review on Wednesday that the date would most likely be set for late 1996 or early 1997.The Ivory Coast
14404 has in recent years announced the date and price for its coffee marketing campaign in September, at the same time that it sets the date and price for its cocoa marketing campaign."They have probably postponed for a technical reason. They don't know what price to set," one analyst said."But there's
14404 plenty of coffee out there and some traitants might be offering low prices. Some farmers will have to sell before a price is set."Farmers need money in early October to pay school fees.Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze told Wednesday's review producer country losses had not been stemmed even though world
14404 stocks were at their lowest in seven years.World prices have fallen since the Ivory Coast set the 1995/96 producer price of 700 CFA per kilo of bagged coffee and trade sources expect a cut in the rate when it is set for 1996/97.Robusta coffee futures slid to more than two-year
14404 lows of $1,471 a tonne on September 20 1996 after touching near 10-year highs of $4,140 a tonne in September 1994, following frosts and drought in Brazil, the world's largest producer.Slides in robusta futures reflect higher retail prices, which have bitten into world consumption, and a recovery in global production
14404 led by Brazil, analysts say.Gauze said the future of the cocoa sector in Ivory Coast, the world's largest producer, was looking good."It could be the same for coffee. 14404 instruments for regulating next year's coffee campaign," he added.Traders and Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) delegates in London said they were not expecting any fireworks at the ACPC meeting on Friday and Saturday as the group's mandate is to contemplate the effectiveness of last year's and this year's export
14404 plans.Analysts in Abidjan say the government is making heavy losses. "For every tonne sold there is a margin of loss for the government. Under the bareme (the price scale covering the whole marketing chain), total costs are higher than the world price," one said.Effective government price support in September was
14404 about 100 CFA franc a kilo but had been as high as 200 CFA, he added."The IMF and the World Bank will not accept this and the farm prices will go down to perhaps to 400 or 500 CFA a kilo," he added.An IMF "illustrative calculation" suggests the farm-gate price
14404 could be pared to 480 CFA a kilo.Traders and exporters expect a cut of anywhere between 50 and 250 CFA a kilo but expect little change in cocoa prices as next year's crop is already forecast down and disincentives to production appear unnecessary.Ivory Coast aims to produce 350,000 tonnes of
14404 coffee a year by 2002. Forecasters put the 1995/96 total at 170,000 tonnes against 194,000 in 1994/95 but the 1996/97 crop is expected to exceed 200,000 due to good farm maintenance.Cumulative exports in the first 11 months of the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season were 137,150 tonnes against 108,184 tonnes in the
14404 same period of 1994/95.Some traders and exporters said they expected a coffee price to be set in mid-November.Ivory Coast opened this year's 1995/96 coffee marketing season on October 7 with an official recommended producer price of 700 CFA a kilo for bagged coffee.The minimum farm-gate indicator price included a five
14404 CFA payment towards the coffee sack and exporters had largely paid that price, Gauze said. 14405 South Africa unveiled a long-awaited telecommunications bill on Thursday, setting the regulatory framework for restructuring the industry, including partial privatisation of state-owned utility Telkom.Minister of Posts and Telecommunications Jay Naidoo said the legislation would be considered by parliament when it reconvened on October 7 and should be passed into law
14405 by the year-end.It sets ground rules for a liberalised telecoms market to be monitored by two independent watchdogs, the South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and the Universal Service Agency.These bodies will ensure fair competition and equitable countrywide coverage, as well as regulating prices via a formula linked to consumer price
14405 inflation.Naidoo reiterated the aim was to conclude a deal by next March or April for a strategic equity partner to take a stake of up to 30 percent in Telkom, in a move seen as spearheading the government's privatisation drive.Eight potential partners have been identified, but the list may be
14405 narrowed in coming weeks."We expect that due diligence will begin some time in October and we will be in a position to ask for proposals from possible partners by November," Naidoo said."These will then be evaluated and by early February we should have final proposals from shortlisted candidates."The potential partners
14405 are France Telecom, Deutsche Telkom, British Telecommunications Plc, Stet Spa, a Dutch and Swedish consortium of KPN and Telia, Bell Atlantic Corp, South Western Bell Corp and Telekom Malaysia Bhd.One key issue affecting any bid will be the period of exclusivity granted to Telkom's fixed voice telephony business.Naidoo argues protection
14405 from direct competition is needed to help build universal service and rebalance tariffs.This period is not spelled out in the bill and will be laid down when Telkom receives a licence next year.The government wants five to seven (corrects from three to five) years exclusivity, but this is subject to
14405 discussion within the World Trade Organisation (WTO).The WTO has set a deadline of February 27, 1997, for submissions for liberalising telecoms markets."We don't think we will have any difficulties at the WTO negotiations. There are countries going for much longer periods of exclusivity than we are," Naidoo said.The South African
14405 government has undertaken to double the number of domestic telephones over the next five years from four million serving mainly white areas at present to eight million, with a much greater penetration in traditionally black areas.To do this it requires an injection of cash and skills, plus a period of
14405 transition from monopoly to free market, Naidoo said.Nonetheless, the government was committed to opening up the market and the new bill would put South Africa on a par with telecommunications regimes in Argentina, Canada and Britain.The Telkom deal is South Africa's first major privatisation project and seen as a litmus
14405 test of the government's commitment to sell off state assets.Other states enterprises in line for full or partial privatisation include South African Airways, the airports company, sections of the rail and road transport network, state-owned leisure facilities and, possibly, electricity generator Eskom.</

14416 The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda ruled on Thursday that witnesses in the future trial of a Hutu accused of genocide and crimes against humanity in 1994 must not be publicly identified.As procedural issues delayed the start of the first trial, South African judge Navanethem Pillay accepted a prosecution request
14416 that names and addresses of witnesses should not be disclosed to the public or the media on security grounds.She banned sketching or photographing of witnesses inside or outside the tribunal building and said witnesses would use pseudonyms. 14416 them prepare their cases.Prosecutor Yakob Haile Mariam asked the court to rule that witnesses should not be publicly identified in the case against Georges Rutaganda, whose trial has been put back to next March."Several hundred survivors of genocide have been killed and maimed. 14416 and relatives of the accused will seek revenge on them and their families," Yakob told the three-judge tribunal."The house of one of our witnesses was burned. She was told that she would be killed if she came to Tanzania to testify against Mr Rutaganda," Yakob added.Rutaganda, 38, is one of
14416 three Rwandan Hutus awaiting trial at tribunal headquarters in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha. 14416 in Rwanda, did not appear in court on Wednesday.He has been held at a civilian hospital in Arusha since September 5. 14416 to go elsewhere for treatment.On Thursday, De Temmerman said it was ludicrous for the prosecution to ask for witness protection."I am the last to want to threaten anyone. So today to claim that people are being attacked in their homes because they are going to testify is ludicrous," he told

14416 prosecution request for secrecy of witnesses in the trial of another defendant, Jean Paul Akayesu, who was mayor of Rwanda's Taba commune during the genocide.The trial of Akayesu -- the first by the tribunal -- was scheduled to start on Thursday. 14416 by the United Nations in November 1994 after the massacre in Rwanda that year of up to a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates.Mass slaughter began shortly after the assassination of Hutu President Juvenal Habyarimana on April 6, 1994. 14416 Rwanda.The tribunal's mandate is to try solely top genocide planners and perpetrators. Of the 21 people indicted so far, only three are in custody in Arusha. They face a maximum of life imprisonment if found guilty.</

14440 Tiny Gambia, one of Africa's smallest states, holds a presidential election on Thursday with 1994 coup leader Colonel Yahya Jammeh seeking legitimacy through the ballot box.Born of British and French colonial rivalry in the 19th century and surrounded by Francophone Senegal, the West African tourist haven and groundnut producer won
14440 independence from Britain in 1965.Jammeh, 31, toppled the mainly Moslem nation's civilian independence president Sir Dawda Jawara in a bloodless coup in July 1994 accusing him of corruption.Jammeh has strengthened ties with Libya and Taiwan as links with Gambia's traditional Western partners have cooled.Critics have denounced arbitrary arrests, clampdowns on
14440 the press and frequent changes to cabinet posts but Jammeh bowed to international pressure by modifying his initial plan to delay elections until 1998.Parliamentary elections are planned for December 11.Following are key facts about Gambia:POPULATION - 1.1 million (1994 World Bank estimate). Ethnic groups: Mandinka, Fula, Wolof, Jola, Serahuli, and
14440 a small Creole, or Aku, community.LANGUAGE: English (official).RELIGION: Moslem (85 per cent), Christian and animist.CAPITAL: Banjul (population: 60,000).AREA - 11,300 sq km (4,360 sq miles). Finger-shaped Gambia is 50 km wide by 350 km long, named after the river that flows through it and is surrounded by Senegal except for
14440 a short Atlantic coastline.ARMED FORCES - 800 members of the army plus a 70-member marine unit with four inshore patrol boats. (Source: International Institute for Strategic Studies, The Military Balance 1995-96).ECONOMY - Gross National Product: $363 million (1994). Per capita GNP $330 (1994) External debt (1994): $419 million. (Source: World
14440 Bank)Currency: dalasi ($1=9.8 dalasi)Exports: groundnuts, cotton, rice, fish. Tourism from Western Europe is also a major source of foreign exchange.Gambia's economy is based on growing and processing of groundnuts, and on tourism, which was hard hit by the 1994 coup. A 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc regional currency used
14440 in neighbouring Senegal damaged a valuable re-export trade. Many foreign donors suspended or reduced development aid after the coup, though Libya and Taiwan have increased cooperation. Foreign exchange reserves have dropped, but the dalasi has maintained its value.HISTORY - A British protectorate since 1888, Gambia gained independence in 1965 as
14440 a constitutional monarchy. Jawara, a Scottish-trained veterinary surgeon, was named prime minister in 1962 after his People's Progressive Party won elections. In April 1970, Gambia became a republic with Jawara as president. Jawara survived a coup attempt by leftists in 1981 thanks to the intervention of Senegalese troops. The abortive
14440 coup, in which hundreds of people died, prompted Jawara to sign a loose confederation treaty with Senegal. The pact collapsed in August 1989, mainly because of Gambia's reluctance to speed up trade and customs union for fear of losing its identity. In July 1994, a group of young army lieutenants
14440 led by Jammeh seized power and Jawara went into exile. The Armed Forces Provisional Ruling Council suspended the constitution and banned political parties. In November 1994, Jammeh survived an attempted counter-coup from within the army in which several people were killed. In January 1995, he sacked his vice-chairman and interior
14440 minister, accusing them of planning to kill him and seize power. Jammeh initially said he planned to stay in power until the end of 1998 but reduced the transition to two years after a storm of international protest. Before the coup, Gambia had several opposition parties, including the National Convention
14440 Party led by former vice-president Sherif Mustapha Dibba, and the Gambia People's Party, led by another former vice-president, Assan Musa Camara. Jammeh, who left the army to contest the poll, barred all politicians who had served with Jawara from standing for election.</

14450 The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.SOVECON ESTIMATES RUSSIAN 1996 SUNFLOWER SEED OUTPUT AT ABOUT 3.5 MILLION TONNES AFTER 4.2 MILLION IN 1995MOSCOW, Sept 26 - Despite some
14450 decline in domestic prices, sunflower seed remains one of Russia's most profitable crops, and sunflower seed exports are a major source of hard currency earnings for Russian farmers.In 1996, a delayed spring followed by very hot weather seriously affected sunflower seed sowing in the North Caucasus, particularly in Rostov oblast.As
14450 a result, Russia's 1996 total area sown to sunflowers declined to 3.9 million hectares, after 4.1 million in 1995, due mainly to a decline in plantings in the North Caucasus.Plantings increased in other sunflower-producing areas, except West Siberia (Table 1).In 1996, the sunflower seed harvest started later than last year.By
14450 September 18, about four percent of planted area had been harvested, 146,300 ha. At the same time last year 438,500 ha had been harvested.Forecasts at this stage are quite tentative, but lower sunflower seed yields at the beginning of the harvest in the North Caucasus (Table 2) indicate a very
14450 likely decline in yields in this region against year-ago levels.As a result, SovEcon forecasts sunflower seed output in the region at 1.7-1.8 million tonnes, versus 2.4 million tonnes in 1995.In Povolzhsk, sunflower seed yields are expected to be close to last year's level. Output is forecast at 0.75-0.8 million tonnes,
14450 versus 0.8 million tonnes in 1995.Assuming normal harvest progress, Central-Chernozem sunflower seed production is anticipated to be about 0.65-0.7 million tonnes, versus 0.73 million tonnes in 1995.As a result, SovEcon provisionally forecasts 1996 sunflower seed output in Russia at about 3.5-3.6 million tonnes, after 4.2 million in 1995, or some
14450 15 percent lower.However, 1996 output will be the second largest in the 1990s, and Russia is likely to continue its sunflower seed exports in 1996-1997, especially in light of sunflower seed crop failure in Ukraine. 14462 As the mighty Trans-Siberian express lurches out of Moscow for Beijing, a smiling attendant dishes out the spittoons.A hairy blanket, creased sheet and lumpy pillow complete the Chinese Railways travel kit for passengers who will spend the next six days and 7,865 km (4,915 miles) on the fabled train.The dimpled
14462 tin basin is a rude reminder that the trek to China across Siberia and Mongolia is not for the faint-hearted. In the day of neatly-packaged and sanitised luxury travel, it remains among the world's last great adventures.From the hubbub of Moscow's Yaroslavskii Station through the empty stillness of the Mongolian
14462 plains, the journey on train T4 is long, hard, crude -- and endlessly interesting.Running on tracks begun in the last decade of last century, the train follows lines etched across Siberia in blood and tears by millions of political exiles from the Tsars to the Soviet communists. Slave labour laid
14462 many of the rails.It shakes, rattles and rolls across five time zones, through vast forests and treeless grasslands, past brightly-painted log cabins and dull grey concrete cities, over mountains and rivers from the Russian steppes to the Great Wall of China.Several trains follow the routes along the length of the
14462 world's biggest country. The green, snaking T4 is one of the busiest -- a moving marketplace of Chinese traders, Russian travellers and foreign tourists.The T4 leaves Yaroslavskii station in scenes of mild chaos at 7.50 p.m. very Tuesday. Female station attendants harass luggage-laden passengers with cries of "minutes, minutes" half
14462 an hour before departure.Second, or Hard Class, sleeper accommodation is literal -- a bunk like a board, a pillow which could double as a sandbag and a bathroom used by dozens of others and never cleaned.On the other hand, the no-smoking signs throughout the train are entirely theoretical. Led by
14462 the chain-smoking staff and a large woman who grimly presided over the restaurant car, passengers filled most of the train with an acrid fug.As an appetite repressant, smoking probably was encouraged by the awfulness of the restaurant. Most items on the eight-page menu were unavailable -- even the beef stroganoff
14462 was more off than on. The rest was reminiscent of the chow which movies show being slopped up on wagon trains in America's Wild West.Prewarned travellers in the wagons of Russia's Wild East train tucked into rations carried from home. Tinned caviar, amazingly cheap in Moscow, makes a tasty mid-Siberian
14462 snack.Many passengers simply filled up, for breakfast, lunch and dinner, with the cheap vodka that was in ample supply.Life aboard quickly settles into an easy routine of sleeping and window-gazing. Each morning the carriages awake to a dawn chorus of expectoration as travellers clear their head passages into the spittoons.The
14462 train whistles through Perm, once closed to foreigners; Yekaterinburg, where the last Tsar and his family were murdered; Omsk, where Dostoyevsky did four years hard labour from 1849; Krasnoyarsk, Irkutsk, Novosibirsk. Under royalty and communism much of the area was forbidden.At 2,078 km (1,300 miles), it passes a four metre
14462 (12-ft) high pillar marking the beginning of Siberia -- the place where multitudes of exiles said their last farewells.Many of these once-fearful places have become profit centres for Chinese traders who hang out of the train windows at stations day and night, swapping piles of clothing for fistfuls of roubles.
14462 As we turn towards Mongolia, the traders disembark with their remaining wares and head back again.There are as yet few visible signs of capitalist development in Siberia. Peasant families, bent double in the fields, still gather potatoes by hand as the birch trees blaze gold in a watery autumn sun.
14462 Many timbered villages, without roads of any kind, can have changed little in centuries.The train pulls slowly through smoggy smokestack cities past crumbling factories, festering buildings and rusty rolling stock which give an overwhelming sense of widespread dilapidation.The scene is strikingly different along the line in booming China, where modernistic
14462 smoked-glass offices are rising in several bustling cities.In Mongolia, the virginal Gobi desert has been marked for intensive strip mining.For now, the empty vastness sees only the occasional yurt, or tent, of a nomadic family, herds of wild horses and a few camels. From airliners leaving vapour trails high above,
14462 our train must look like a caterpillar on a great big cabbage leaf.After crossing the Great Wall, the train ends its journey of 139 hours 45 minutes precisely on time at 3.35 p.m. on Monday.As it nears Beijing, attendants vacuum the carpets for the first time and many weary travellers,
14462 as in hotels around the world, cast around their rooms for an appropriate souvenir of an unforgettable trip.But there are no bathroom sachets, no slippers or robes to be had. And the attendants have secured the spittoons.</

14479 current practice.Budget expenditures will be curbed by increasing subsidies to state agencies by only 15 percent and to local municipalities by 13 percent in 1997, compared with the 18 percent inflation target, Medgyessy said.Hungary will begin the reform of social security contributions in 1997 so as to break the social

14496 a surge in blue chips on Thursday pushed the bourse up for the first time in eight sessions, giving rise to optimism among traders that the market would now show signs of recovery.The PX50 index closed on Thursday at 548.9, up 2.5 points."The decline was really not based on fundamental
14496 changes, but events related to Agrobanka and speculation about Kocarnik and Tosovsky," Daniel Gladis of Atlantik Financni Trhy told Reuters.Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka added: "I expect the market should stabilise by the end of the week, and investor interest could increase by next week."On September 17, the Czech National
14496 Bank placed Agrobanka under forced administration after it suffered liquidity problems due to Kreditni's failure and the investigation of people in the case who are also connected to Agrobanka.But Gladis said the move is another badly-needed step in reforming the banking sector -- the CNB has now placed 12 banks
14496 under some form of supervision over the past two years, shutting many -- and should speed up overall market reforms."I think that people will realise that what happened is actually a positive sign for the market because it is forcing a cleanup," he added.The Czech capital market has long been
14496 cast by investors as being murky, where little regulation and poor enforcement of laws allow most trading to be done off-market with only a trickle of information being made public.They point to Agrobanka's problems, which are considered to stem from its dealings with Motoinvest, an investment group shrouded in secrecy
14496 that stormed onto the market last year with a series of takeover battles against big institutions.One official from Motoinvest was indicted on criminal fraud charges for a debt swap scheme which police said led, in part, to Kreditni's failure with losses of nearly 12 billion czech crowns ($445.1 million).Agrobanka is
14496 the largest wholly-private Czech bank with basic capital of some four billion crowns at the end of last year. Motoinvest has denied any responsibility for any of the problems at Kreditni or Agrobanka, where people associated with the group hold board seats.Adding to the market's woes have been some unfavourable
14496 economic figures in the last week, such as a slight slowdown in GDP growth to 4.0 percent in the second quarter from 4.6 in the first quarter, and January-August trade figures showing an all-time record deficit of 100.9 billion crowns."The Czech Republic has usually had good macro-economic numbers, but some
14496 of the more recent figures are not so rosy," said Jay King of Wood and Company."With these weaknesses and the bourse's good run before that, there has been a nice chance to take profits. I'm not sure if we will see the investors return so quickly to boost the market."($1=26.96

14503 it. The government should cut interest rates to avoid economic collapse.The government, following recipes from the International Monetary Fund, has deliberately kept monetary policy tight.Glazyev said Russia's proposed budget for 1997, which aims to keep inflation firmly under control, would deepen the economic malaise and stoke up social tensions."For 1997
14503 they have proposed to us zero growth in production that preserves the depression and accelerates the chaos which in turn leads to a shrinking of the national wealth," he said.Russia's gross domestic product (GDP) and industrial production both contracted by five percent in the first half of 1996 compared with
14503 the same period a year earlier.However, consumer prices fell 0.2 percent in August and the government, helped by a $10 billion three-year IMF loan, hopes to bring the annual figure down to 22 percent this year, from 131 percent in 1995."Low inflation is good but that cannot be our sole
14503 aim if we want to see economic growth," Glazyev said, noting that high interest rates had exacerbated the government's debts.He also called for fiscal reforms to stimulate investment and for the creation of development banks to channel funds into industry as in Japan and some other countries.Glazyev said government decisions
14503 diverged from the aims of the president."The government (of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin) should work towards the goals of the president. 14503 armed forces, which need twice as much money as the state budget can afford," he said.Earlier on Thursday Lebed, an ambitious general who came a strong third in this summer's presidential poll, repeated a warning that the cash-strapped army was close to mutiny.Lebed, secretary of the Security Council which groups
14503 senior ministers, appears to be jostling with Chernomyrdin and other officials for position in the political vacuum that has emerged in Moscow as doctors prepare Yeltsin for heart surgery.Lebed recently called for an overhaul of the 1997 budget, saying more money should be made available to the armed forces, agriculture,
14503 heavy industry and other sectors.He proposed raising the extra revenues by hiking prices of natural resources, ending preferential import duties for foreign firms and charging higher rents for the use of state property.Lebed, a controversial figure, is mistrusted by many in the Kremlin, especially after his apparent success in engineering

14511 more Western funds to close the plant -- site of the world's biggest nuclear accident in 1986."Is a new explosion brewing under the sarcophagus?" screamed the headline in the daily Vseukrainsky Vedomosti."How long can we soldier on like this?" said Demokratychna Ukraina. "'Something is happening under the sarcophagus'. That is
14511 the clearest scientific explanation we have been given."Russia's top liberal daily Izvestia was far blunter."Nuclear blackmail for their own ends?" read the daily's headline. "Kiev is again using Chernobyl to intimidate the world but specialists see no real danger."Ukraine's nuclear authorities launched another attempt to ease the tension unleashed by
14511 Environment Minister Yuri Kostenko's statement this week that a limited nuclear chain reaction had occurred inside the "tomb".The State Nuclear authority, Derzhkomatom, issued a statement denying "any suggestion that the containment structure is on the brink of an accident".Its chairman Viktor Chebrov said a commission investigating the higher readings had
14511 found no proof of a chain reaction. But he stressed a new structure had to be built.Kostenko said on Tuesday that water seeping through 1,000 square metres of cracks had increased neutron activity and caused the limited nuclear chain reaction.He said no one knew for certain just what was occurring
14511 inside the structure, an engineering feat erected in the chaotic aftermath of the 1986 fire and explosion.But other officials, supported by Ukraine's most respected academics, backpedalled within 24 hours. Statements were read on evening newscasts saying the high readings were not unusual.President Leonid Kuchma's top security official, an expert in
14511 nuclear rocket technology, said Kostenko was not qualified to make such judgments. Kostenko himself retreated by saying any new reaction would be limited in scale.Russian nuclear experts also said they saw no danger from the increases. A senior official of Russia's Nuclear Energy Ministry told Interfax news agency that measuring
14511 equipment inside the "tomb" was too old to give reliable readings.Western experts said the levels were far below anything which could provoke a new explosion.Residents questioned on Kiev streets all appeared resigned to the risks of living within 140 km (90 miles) of the station."It does worry me. But this
14511 has been going on for so long that we're used to it," said office worker Galina Isakova, 59."But what are we supposed to believe with all these statements and denials?"Wealthy Group of Seven countries have pledged more than $3 billion to help Ukraine meet its pledge to close Chernobyl's two
14511 working reactors by the year 2000.But Kostenko, Ukraine's top negotiator on Chernobyl, and other ministers say the money is not being released quickly enough and say the date may be postponed unless the West proves more forthcoming.They also accuse the West of concentrating too much on upgrading Ukraine's inefficient energy
14511 sector and forgetting the dangers posed by the "sarcophagus".</

14533 President Boris Yeltsin's absence as he prepares for heart surgery has provoked more jostling for position within the Kremlin and encouraged speculation that other top politicians are preparing for presidential bids.The following are brief portraits of the leaders who are likely to be involved in a struggle for power following
14533 the decision by doctors on Wednesday to delay Yeltsin's planned heart operation for at least six more weeks.VIKTOR CHERNOMYRDIN, 58. Prime Minister. Stolid, pro-reform leader who will take over Yeltsin's duties temporarily when the Kremlin leader undergoes surgery. Would assume power for three months until a new election if Yeltsin
14533 were incapacitated but has avoided making comments which would make him appear too ambitious. Has been loyal to Yeltsin since he was named prime minister in December 1992 and represents stability for Western economists. Has powerful backers in the natural gas industry which he used to head, and in business
14533 circles, but his grey image limits his potential to win votes.ALEXANDER LEBED, 46. National security adviser and secretary of president's Security Council. Outspoken former paratroop general and Afghan war veteran who was appointed by Yeltsin last June in a vote-winning move after Lebed finished third in presidential election. Has proved
14533 independent, unpredictable and outspoken, and won a reputation as a loose cannon by making controversial statements on wide-ranging issues. Main achievement since taking office has been to sign a peace deal in Chechnya but most leaders in Moscow have criticised it. Does not hide presidential ambitions but has little political
14533 experience and few allies in the Kremlin, financial circles or other influential groups in Moscow. His views on the economy and reform remain hazy.YURI LUZHKOV, 60. Moscow Mayor. Won landslide re-election last June which reinforced Muscovites' view of him as a man who gets things done and confirmed his popular
14533 appeal. His appeal outside Moscow may be limited but a number of recent trips outside the capital suggest he is trying to widen his appeal and lay the ground for a presidential bid. Backed by big business and financial groups in Moscow, his support would be valuable for any other
14533 candidate if he did not run for president and he could become a major powerbroker. Denies he would challenge Yeltsin, with whom he has good relations.GENNADY ZYUGANOV, 52. Communist Party leader. Was second to Yeltsin in presidential election last July but says he could win if the president stepped down
14533 now. He says Russians' patience is wearing thin with the hardships endured under reforms and that frustration with unpaid wages favours him. Has recently forged wider alliance with other leftist and nationalist groups to strengthen the left's bid for power. His presidential ambitions are hampered by limited access to mass
14533 media, lack of charisma and few financial resources. Business circles and the West are largely distrustful of his advocacy of a mixed economy of state and private ownership.ANATOLY CHUBAIS, 41. Head of presidential administration. Unlikely presidential challenger, at least for some years, but widely seen as anxious to consolidate his
14533 position. His post as Yeltsin's chief-of-staff gives him huge influence and makes him a potential kingmaker. A former privatisation chief, he is a supporter of rapid reforms who is liked by the West but many workers blame him for the hardships they have endured under reforms. Won high position as
14533 reward for helping mastermind Yeltsin's re-election. Widely seen as ally of Chernomyrdin rather than Lebed, he is a fierce critic of Zyuganov and has a bumpy relationship with Luzhkov.</

14555 the measure was intended to muzzle the few independent news organisations that had managed to avoid takeovers by interests fronting for Tudjman's HDZ party.Tudjman took offence at Feral's way of criticising his proposal that the remains of members of Croatia's World War Two Nazi puppet regime should be reburied at

14555 to sustain the guilt of the accused, as neither the articles nor photo montages could be interpreted as slanderous.He said the montage was obviously absurd, and was included in the satirical supplement of the issue, while the articles merely passed judgment on aspects of political activity.State prosecutor Visnja Loncar had

14567 But he made clear his alliance with Yeltsin was conditional."I've come to serve the state, not you. That's what I told Yeltsin," Lebed told Nezavisimaya Gazeta in an interview.It took him less than two weeks in office to announce an end to the 21-month Chechnya war, which had caused tens
14567 of thousands of casualties and inflicted humiliating defeats on Russian troops.But Lebed admitted to Nezavisimaya that public approval of his peace deal with separatist leaders was far from unanimous.Some top politicians have said the deal, which legalised the separatist leadership, agreed terms for a troop withdrawal and postponed for five
14567 years the key issue of whether Chechnya may become independent, could divide Russia.Many people, including the military, viewed it as a further humilitation to the Russian nation.Both the Chechnya deal and Lebed's open distaste for professional politicians appeal to many Russians.But Lebed, who makes no secret of his presidential ambitions,
14567 has made little progress on other key election promises, notably fighting crime and corruption.He complains that President Boris Yeltsin's illness has isolated him in the Kremlin and prevented him from carrying out many of his plans."An alliance has been formed, but unfortunately the president has health problems," he told Izvestia

14567 with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais.Lebed's press office said in a statement that Izvestia had not agreed the final text of interview with him. 14573 Nicu Ceausescu, who died on Thursday in a Vienna hospital, was a hard-drinking womaniser whose playboy reputation once symbolised the moral bankruptcy of his father's Romanian communist dictatorship.The 45-year-old youngest son of Nicolae Ceausescu, executed in Romania's December 1989 revolution, had been suffering from serious liver disease.He was flown to
14573 Austria a week ago for specialised surgery after Romanian doctors acknowledged they lacked medical and surgical equipment to deal with his condition.He had been rushed to the Bucharest university hospital on September 14 with internal bleeding, caused by what doctors said was a varicose oesophagus and acute liver cirrhosis.He was
14573 believed to be on the waiting list for a liver transplant when he died.Under his father's rule, Nicu enjoyed a playboy lifestyle and squandered vast sums of public money at the gambling tables of Las Vegas and other casino towns.Nicu was the youngest of the three children of the late
14573 dictator and his wife Elena. He was his father's political heir apparent and was communist party boss in the central Romanian town of Sibiu until Nicolae Ceausescu's downfall.In his palatial villa he indulged a ferocious appetite for excess: women, drink and wild parties were the norm. A reluctant member of
14573 his entourage was Olympic gymnast Nadia Comaneci.A violent revolution in 1989 ousted the Ceausescus after a ruthless 24-year rule. Nicolae and Elena were shot by firing squad on Christmas Day.Nicu, a physicist, was head of the Communist Party's youth wing and was posted to Sibiu in the early 1980s, where
14573 local people remember him for trying to resist his father's severe economic belt-tightening policies.Shortly before his parents' execution, he was arrested and charged with ordering troops to fire on demonstrators in Sibiu during the uprising and with illegal possession of firearms.Nicu denied the charge, saying he had already left town
14573 when troops opened fire killing 91 people and wounding 208.He was jailed for 20 years in September 1990 after being convicted for "instigating aggravated murder" and illegally possessing a firearm.By the time of his release on health grounds in November 1992, he had served half of the jail term --
14573 enough for parole based on good behaviour.Romanian prosecutors earlier this year closed the file on a criminal probe launched against the Ceausescu children in the wake of the anti-communist revolution.They were cleared of charges of undermining the national economy -- charges on which their parents were killed -- by using
14573 their privileged position to exploit assets of the now defunct Communist Party.A foreign travel ban on the children was also lifted.Many Romanians now harbour ambivalent feelings about the Ceausescu era and their fall.Living standards are lower and many people believe the true story of the 1989 revolution -- which many
14573 see as a coup d'etat by former communists who have held power ever since -- has yet to be told.Nicu is survived by his brother Valentin, a nuclear physicist, and his sister Zoe, a mathematician. Both have kept a low profile since they were released from detention in 1990.</

14607 its preference for longer-term liquidity sterilisation," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters."We further realise that the yield of 9.3 percent on our liquidity bills was not sufficient," he added.The NBS held a bill auction of an unspecified tranche of three month liquidity bills on Wednesday, but failed to attract
14607 bids as dealers complained the central bank's yield expectations were much lower than the market's.Most banks, according to dealers, submitted bids at around 10 percent.It was the sixteenth time this year there were no bids at an NBS bill auction, or all had been rejected. 14615 Argentine unions began a 36-hour general strike on Thursday accusing President Carlos Menem of betraying workers and the Peronist labour movement and robbing the country of job security.Tens of thousands thronged Buenos Aires' Plaza de Mayo to hear the head of the main CGT union federation, Rodolfo Daer, warn the
14615 Peronist government that "it cannot rule with its back to the people and the people will not forgive betrayal."The CGT had been an ally of Menem since he came to power in 1989, but called a "Strike And A Half" in protest at 17.1 percent unemployment, labour reforms in favour
14615 of employers and recent tax hikes and worker benefit reductions.The stoppage that began at noon (1500 GMT) is the second in two months. Menem complained this week that the labour unrest would cost the economy $2.7 billion -- or one percent of gross national product. Flights were disrupted and financial
14615 markets had what one trader called a "wasted day" of slow business. Public transport chaos was expected on Friday.Menem angered unions and opposition parties by calling it a "tourist strike" -- an excuse for a long weekend.But Daer, once a Menem confidant, snapped back in a speech to a crowd
14615 he estimated at 100,000 people: "We are here to say that they are the tourists and we are the working men."It looked like the strongest challenge yet to Menem's free-market economic reforms, which have been hailed for reducing inflation to zero from 5,000 percent since he took power but which
14615 have also doubled unemployment.Menem and Economy Minister Roque Fernandez stood defiantly by their reforms. Menem wrote in La Nacion newspaper "Strikes don't stop laws" and Fernandez told reporters: "No way are we thinking of changing the economic plan."Flushed with success after Congress finally approved his tax austerity package -- fuel
14615 and income tax hikes designed to plug a growing budget deficit -- late on Wednesday, Fernandez said: "No way are we thinking of changing the economic plan."Underscoring his determination to chase fiscal solvency rather than job-creation, Fernandez announced the sell-off of the state mortgage bank Banco Hipotecario, valued at $3-3.5
14615 billion, and added that public transport fares may go up.Menem vowed to push ahead with labour reforms to lower employers' costs and make them more likely to take on staff. He wants wages dependent on economic conditions, looser rules on working hours and holidays, collective pay deals scrapped and redundancy
14615 payments replaced by unemployment insurance."They want to destabilise unemployment but we will not let them," said Daer.Opposition Radical Party leader Rodolfo Terragno said the strike showed "Menem's margin to continue with policies that have produced monstrous unemployment, recession and social discontent is narrowing."In the historic Plaza, the sun, drums, peanut
14615 vendors, blue-and-white flags and portraits of Peronist Party founders Juan and Evita Peron gave the protest a festive air; but the message for Menem was anything but friendly.As the crowds struck up the "Peronist March", the head of a CGT delegation from Concordia in Entre Rios province moaned that his
14615 city "was one of the most prosperous in the country before this corrupt government came. Now it has one of the highest levels of unemployment in Argentina."</

14617 Europe's second Ariane-5 rocket, due to be launched in mid-April 1997 at the earliest, will put two "dummy" satellites into orbit to try to demonstrate its reliability, space officials said on Thursday.The first Ariane-5 rocket exploded less than 40 seconds after lift-off in June, destroying four uninsured scientific satellites worth
14617 $500 million and delivering a devastating setback to development of Western Europe's new-generation rocket.Specialists in Kourou said the "dummy" satellites would cost less than $3 million."The objective of Ariane flight 502 is to demonstrate the rocket's capacity to launch double satellite payloads into Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)," said Jean-Marie Luton,
14617 director of the European Space Agency (ESA)."We will launch two instrument platforms that represent satellite masses," Luton told a news conference in Paris broadcast to the ESA launch centre in French Guiana.Luton said the explosion on the maiden Ariane-5 flight represented a financial loss of $350 million and set back
14617 the Ariane-5 programme by at least a year. Arianespace had planned to start using Ariane-5 for its customers in 1997."We are considering restructuring the programme's financing by a redistribution of Ariane-5's budget, more funding from member states and a contribution from the programme's industrial partners," Luton said.The second and final
14617 Ariane-5 test flight was initially scheduled for this month but was pushed back to April 1997 and a third test flight has been ordered.An inquiry board investigating the explosion concluded in July that the failure was caused by software design errors in a guidance system.The Paris-based Arianespace company that launches
14617 the Ariane rocket series said it would order more flight proven Ariane-4 rockets. The company had initially planned to phase out the Ariane-4 and use only Ariane-5s by the year 2000."This transition period has now become delicate. We have taken the decision to order more Ariane-4 rockets," Arianespace president Charles
14617 Bigot said."I cannot now give you an exact number but I would estimate it to be about five or six to meet the demands of our clients scheduled for launch in 1999," he added.Arianespace has on order 22 more Ariane-4 rockets and 14 Ariane-5 rockets to service a customer backload
14617 of 42 heavy satellites to launch worth an estimated $4.1 billion.</

14655 Brady told reporters at the outset of a two-day trip to eye business prospects. Brady, who retired from the U.S. Treasury in 1993, oversaw the restructuring of billions of dollars in developing world debt into U.S.-backed Brady bonds.He founded Darby Overseas Investments Ltd in 1994 to invest in promising mid-sized
14655 Latin American firms. Darby has $180 million in funds invested in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.But so far Darby has avoided Brazil, one of the largest holders of restructured foreign debt with some $54 billion in Brady bonds. "Investment opportunities in other countries came up earlier and (Brazil's economic
14655 stabilization plan) was put in later than all of the major Latin American countries," Brady said.He added, however, that Brazil has made great strides on the inflation front over the past two years, which has provided a stable backdrop for steady economic growth.Under the Brazilian government's stabilization program known as
14655 the Real Plan, monthly inflation rates have fallen from 50 percent to below one percent since the plan's inception in July 1994. "We are looking to make investments with entrepreneurs and firms that are in the middle range, both privately held and publicly traded companies," Brady said, adding he was
14655 optimistic about increasing Darby's $180 million in funds under management.Brady, who is Darby's chairman and chief executive officer, said he would visit Rio de Janeiro on Friday, where he would continue to hold private talks with Brazilian firms.Brady spent 34 years as an investment banker before becoming U.S. Treasury Secretary
14655 in 1988 under former President Ronald Reagan.</

14689 land and suspended for two years new licenses for the logging of mahogany and virola trees.The measures came after official data showed 5,750 square miles (14,900 square km) of Brazil's Amazon forest were cleared in 1994, up from 4,298 square miles (11,130 square km) in 1991.Eduardo Martins, president of the
14689 government's Brazilian Environment Institute (Ibama), acknowledged that illegal burning was continuing but said hopes that the government could stop destruction immediately were unrealistic."Without a doubt, a lot of the burnings (Greenpeace) is detecting are in violation of the decrees, but even if we had an effective monitoring system, it would
14689 be very difficult to get to them before they happen," Martins said.Ibama is currently concentrating on preventing illegal logging, which it considers to be the principal threat to the Amazon basin, and will only begin detecting forest burning next year when new satellite data is due for release.Kishimani of Greenpeace
14689 said urgent action was needed and called on the government to stop immediately all loans from state banks to cattle farmers in the Amazon region. 14689 the sector, it will be giving a signal to the farmers that they can keep on destroying the forests," he said.</

14749 They come in their hundreds of thousands, wearing Stetsons, whooping and blasting the music of Kenny Rogers from their pick-up trucks.Every year, Brazil's growing ranks of "caubois" converge in dusty traffic jams on this otherwise sleepy town in Sao Paulo state's fertile sugarcane and orange belt for 10 days of
14749 raucous rodeo competition and Wild West fun.Barretos is the highlight of Brazil's 1,200 annual rodeos and the place to be seen for the suddenly fashionable world of "country" culture. 14749 European-oriented city of Sao Paulo, smart-set teenagers step expertly in U.S. Deep South-style line dances and sing country hits in word-perfect English. 14749 peasant woman."We all grew up watching Bonanza. 14749 began bringing their herds from deep in the interior to the town's refrigerated abattoir. 14749 1.1 million visitors to the purpose-built Cowboy Park, making it the second largest rodeo event in the world, after Calgary in Canada, organisers said.For 10 hot days and nights in August, farmers in designer jeans and boots mixed with drunks, clutching the black Virgin Mary that is the patron saint
14749 of farmworkers. 14749 sponsors, cowboys from Brazil and beyond were thrown one after another from evil-looking bulls or snorting, bucking broncos."They had to virtually carry me out of the ring," said Art Watson from California, on his first painful trip to Brazil as a professional bullrider. 14749 breed than those on the North American circuit, and more wily at getting a man in the dirt, he concluded.Local cowboy Genival Pereira Queiroz knows only too well the tricks of the local bulls, which are crossbreeds of strong European cattle and the quickfooted, humpbacked nilori breed from India. 14749 takes medication daily to avoid the blackouts that a hoof to the head in 1993 still give him."It's that combination of power and agility that gets the gringos," he said.On semi-finals night, the packed stands were a sea of white Stetson cowboy hats, bobbing in time with short, loud blasts
14749 of rock 'n roll anthems. The crowd went wild when rodeo commentator Asa Branca, known as White Wing, landed in a cloud of red dust in a helicopter.The only moment of calm came with a half-time tribute to three recent departures to the great rodeo in the sky. Giant, beef-fed
14749 men, their hats clasped to their chests, shed silent tears for one of the deceased, a much-loved millionaire killed this year when his car struck a horse.In the invitation-only box of a major Brazilian beer company, sponsors and media executives, arm-in-arm with models in frilly tops and knee-high boots, marvelled
