14765 Following are economists' initial reactions to New Zealand June quarter GDP data released on Friday.Real seasonally-adjusted production-based GDP rose 0.3 percent in the quarter and 2.1 percent seasonally-adjusted from the year ago quarter, versus consensus forecasts of 0.4 percent and 1.8 percent respectively.PAUL STEWART, ANZ CHIEF ECONOMIST "I think the
14765 production-based series is pretty much in line with expectations, so further evidence that the economy is slowing but still a reasonable rate of growth -- the economy is not collapsing."I think (we) still place greater reliance on the production-based figure, but the expenditure-based one was a bit weaker."No significant impact
14765 (on currency and rates). I think the GDP data is fairly historical anyway and not significantly out of line with expectation, so no implications for monetary policy." ROGER KERR, BANCORP EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR"It's pretty much in line with what we expected, but I think some of the sector groups are perhaps
14765 a bit weaker than we expected."Manufacturing and construction, two big parts of the economy, they're into negative for the first time for some time."I think this result would be in line with the Reserve Bank's expectations and the scenario that they've been painting. "I think it does confirm to some
14765 extent the slowdown in the economy -- it's not across the board by any stretch, but I think it does fit their (the RBNZ's) scenario and I don't think it brings forward or pushes out when monetary policy may be able to be eased."BEVAN GRAHAM, WESTPAC CHIEF ECONOMISTGraham said the
14765 surprise was the upward revision to 0.7 percent from 0.4 percent for March quarter production-based GDP, which made the slowdown between March and June stronger than expected.Otherwise the figures were in line with expectations."The growth path is coming down," Graham said. He said the data were not market-moving as they
14765 were largely historical and did not take account of tax cuts which took effect on July 1."What the Reserve Bank is concerned about is where we're at now and where we're going. The June quarter is very historical."</

14767 New Zealand's real seasonally adjusted Gross Domestic Product grew 0.3 percent in the June quarter, marginally below economists' forecasts of 0.4 percent, Statistics New Zealand data released on Friday showed.The growth rate was the smallest for 16 quarters, since September 1992 when it fell 0.7 percent.The actual annual growth in
14767 the June year was 2.6 percent against forecasts of 2.3 percent and against 3.1 percent growth in the March year.The expenditure-based measure showed no change in the June quarter. Acting Government Statistician Ian Ewing said the economy continued to slow following the relatively strong growth pattern during 1994 and early
14767 1995.The annual growth rate has fallen from a peak of 6.6 percent in the 1994 June year and 4.8 percent in the June 1995 year.During the June year, employment increased 3.7 percent but this was partially offset by a fall in average hours worked of 0.8 percent. Houshold and government
14767 spending showed small increases in the June quarter as did business investment. However, these rises were more than offset by a large rundown in stocks resulting in total internal demand falling by 0.4 percent.This is the first quarterly decrease in stocks for five years, Ewing said.There was recovery in exports
14767 of 3.0 percent following two quarterly falls, largely as a result of strong growth in dairy exports. Manufactured exports were also up.Imports rose 1.6 percent, down on the 4.1 percent rise last quarter but still up 6.8 percent for the June year. The rise in business investment in the June
14767 quarter was primarily the result of an increase in investment in plant, machinery and equipment which rose 5.0 percent after a 3.8 percent decrease in the previous quarter.For the June year, business investment remained at high levels, up 8.5 percent, although this was down on the very strong annual increases
14767 of 17.7 percent and 16.6 percent recorded in the previous two years.Business activity, which excludes general government and owner-occupied housing, grew by only 0.3 percent this quarter. This was largely the result of continuing growth in service industries which are up 0.8 percent this quarter and 4.8 percent for the
14767 June year.Growth in the communications industry over the past eight years continued, and was especially strong in telecommunications.This rise in activity however, was moderated by little or no growth in other industries. Primary industry production was flat at 0.1 percent and other goods-producing industries were down 0.5 percent with manufacturing
14767 down 0.5 percent, electricity, gas and water down 0.7 percent and construction down 0.5 percent.The level of manufacturing activity fell 0.5 percent this quarter and flattened down to 0.7 percent for the June year.-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746</

14781 After a meal and a relaxing drink with his doctor on a warm Sunday afternoon, death came quietly to cancer sufferer Bob Dent in the world's first legal assisted suicide.Dent's quiet death with family and friends in his home in this sleepy tropical town has ignited debate about whether "mercy
14781 killings" should be legal in some cases, or whether the dying should endure their agony until death comes naturally.The government that runs this rugged and remote outback territory represents less than one percent of Australia's 18 million people, but its introduction of the world's first law legalising assisted suicide has
14781 far-reaching impact in Australia and overseas, say supporters and critics alike."This (death) clearly makes this a national debate," said government politician Kevin Andrews, sponsor of a private bill that would see the national parliament use its constitutional powers to over-ride the territory law."I don't think any longer can anyone say
14781 that this is something which simply affects the Northern Territory."Dent himself fuelled the debate with an emotional plea from beyond the grave for Australia's parliament to reject Andrews and let the dying ease their pain and die with dignity.In an open letter released on Thursday but written on the eve
14781 of his death by computer-delivered lethal injection, Dent said painkilling drugs given for his terminal prostate cancer made him suicidal."Drugs given to enhance the pain-relieving effects of the morphine have caused me to feel suicidal to the point that I would have blown my head off if I had had
14781 a gun," he wrote."The church and state should be kept separate. What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain."If you disagree with voluntary euthanasia, then don't use it, but
14781 please don't deny the right to me to use it," wrote Dent, who in his final moments on Sunday told his doctor euthanasia was "an act of love".While community and political leaders strongly condemn the law, a range of separate opinion polls show strong public support -- between seven and
14781 eight out of every 10 Australians.Opponents, including political, aboriginal, medical, religious and other community leaders, say killing can never be legalised, warning abuse would follow and the weak would suffer.Supporters, such as Dent's doctor and spearhead of the pro-euthansia campaign, Philip Nitschke, counter that people should be able to choose
14781 death for themselves when the pain gets too much, if they are still mentally sound.Both sides agree the debate won't go away.Andrews' challenge, backed by conservative Prime Minister John Howard, Labour opposition chief Kim Beazley and others, is due for parliamentary debate later this month.A coalition of medical, religious and
14781 aboriginal groups is asking the country's peak court, the High Court, to declare the law unconstitutional.Andrews, warning of the danger of abuse, said the debate was not about the individual's right to choose. "Once you have this legislation...it will be uncontrolled and subject to widespread abuse," he told reporters.Church groups
14781 see the law as nothing more than legalised murder or suicide and moral decay. "I was, and still am, deeply ashamed that Australia should be the only country in the world to legalise the killing of an innocent person," Roman Catholic archbishop of Sydney Edward Clancy told reporters.A politician from
14781 Howard's Liberal Party, Victorian state government leader Jeff Kennett, said euthanasia was beautiful."For people to be able to die with grace and dignity at their choosing, as opposed to suffering, is just beautiful."Life is about choice; death should be about choice and politicians ought to butt out," he said in
14781 a radio invterview.The fate of Andrews' political challenge is uncertain.While the government holds a strong majority, both sides of politics have agreed to free their members from party orders and allow them to vote according to their conscience.One issue on which both sides agree is that Bob Dent's death on
14781 that warm Sunday afternoon won't be the last.Nitschke, having convinced the necessary specialist and psychiatrist to support him once, believes he can do so again.He has five more patients on his books seeking to die.</

14783 New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark held out an olive branch to the left-wing Alliance on Thursday, saying she hoped the two parties could talk business after next month's election.Clark sounded a conciliatory note towards Alliance leader Jim Anderton in a televised debate between party leaders."I know that Labour can
14783 lead the next government. I am prepared to reach out to other political parties which share a number of common objectives," Clark said."Jim Anderton and I have agreed on a lot in the past. There are things in economic policy we don't agree with...We know where the differences are. After
14783 the election, Jim, I would like to be talking to you and your people..."Labour and the Alliance share common ground in wanting to repeal the union-busting Employment Contracts Act and in some areas of health, education and housing policy.The Alliance, however, is more interventionist and protectionist, campaigning to reverse the
14783 sale of state-owned Forestry Corp to a Fletcher Forest-led consortium including China's Citic. It wants to reshape the Reserve Bank Act to make the central bank target growth and employment as well as price stability.Labour and the Alliance, along with economic nationalist New Zealand First, are drawing around 50 percent
14783 support in opinion polls. If they can work together, they could oust the conservative National Party government.National has about 38 percent and its re-election chances depend mainly on the free-market ACT and morals-based Christian Coalition, neither of which is certain of winning seats.The left remains split, however, by Labour's refusal

14784 An Australian cancer patient who said he lived on a "roller-coaster of pain" has committed the world's first legally-assisted suicide, sparking a fiery national debate on the issue of mercy killing.Bob Dent, a 66-year-old former carpenter from this northern outback city, died from a computer-delivered lethal injection last Sunday after
14784 persuading doctors he had nothing to live for.He shared a last meal and drink with doctor Philip Nitschke and told him that what he was doing was an "act of love"."If I were to keep a pet animal in the same condition I am in, I would be prosecuted," Dent
14784 wrote in an open letter to Australian members of parliament on the eve of his death."For months I have been on a roller-coaster of pain made worse by the unwanted side effects of the drugs."Australian church leaders, who want the Northern Territory voluntary euthanasia law quashed, were outraged.Sydney's Roman Catholic
14784 archbishop Edward Clancy said he was "deeply ashamed that Australia should be the only country in the world to legalise the killing of an innocent person."Respect, reverence for human life is a cornerstone of our civilisation," Clancy said. "When that goes, our society begins to unravel."Dent's death marked the first
14784 time that the Northern Territory's euthanasia law had been successfully used since it came into operation on July 1.It saw battlelines drawn up on Thursday for a fresh fight over mercy killing. Government backbencher Kevin Andrews, who has launched a private action in federal parliament to have the state's law
14784 quashed, said euthanasia was now a national issue.It also polarised opinion in Australia, with one state politician describing it as "beautiful" and church leaders expressing their shame.Victoria state premier Jeff Kennett, a supporter of voluntary euthanasia, said moves to have the law quashed were immoral."For people to be able to
14784 die with grace and dignity at their choosing as opposed to suffering is just beautiful," Kennett told reporters."Life is about choice; death should be about choice and politicians ought to butt out."Nitschke told reporters up to five more people from around Australia had sought to use the legislation and that
14784 another death could occur within weeks."There is little doubt that the events surrounding this first use of the act will make it that much easier for the next terminally ill person," Nitschke said.The doctor, dubbed Australia's "Doctor Death" after American euthanasia campaigner Jack Kevorkian, said the atmosphere in Dent's Darwin
14784 home had at first been tense.But he said Dent had reassured him as he died, telling him that what he was doing was "an act of love"."The patient was expressing a sense of gratitude. He was as happy as someone could be under the circumstances," he said.Dent wrote that he
14784 he had been an active, outgoing person and that "being unable to live a normal life causes much mental and psychological pain, which can never be relieved by medication".The deputy prime minister in Australia's conservative government, Tim Fischer, repeated warnings the territory law was a move towards "a culture of
14784 death".Prime Minister John Howard, Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley, other prominent community leaders and Australia's indigenous Aborigines have all condemned the law.Previous political and legal challenges against the law in the Northern Territory have failed, although a coalition of doctors, church and Aboriginal leaders have petitioned the Australian High Court
14784 to declare the law unconstitutional.Dent in his letter urged parliament to allow people to choose to die when Andrews' bill is voted on later this year."The church and state should be kept separate," he wrote. "What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe,
14784 to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain."If you disagree with voluntary euthanasia, then don't use it, but please don't deny the right to me to use it."</

14789 A Hong Kong activist leapt to his death in a roiling East China Sea on Thursday after Japanese patrol boats thwarted his protest ship's bid to land on a disputed archipelago to claim it back for China.David Chan, 45, and four other protesters had jumped into the storm-whipped sea, vowing
14789 to defy even Japan's claim to waters surrounding the uninhabited cluster of islands.Chan's death was the first in a wave of protests to sweep Hong Kong, Taiwan, Macau and China since July, when Japanese ultranationalists built a lighthouse and raised Japan's flag on the islands northeast of Taiwan to assert
14789 Tokyo's sovereignty.The tragedy aboard the rusty tanker Kien Hwa 2, witnessed by reporters aboard the nearby fishing boat Hanghai, brought expressions of regret in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei -- and calls for cooler heads.But it also heightened tension between Japan, which has claimed the islands since 1895 as
14789 the Senkakus, and China, which calls them the Diaoyus and has claimed them for centuries.China, keen to marshal patriotism stirred by the sovereignty row without offending Japanese investors, reiterated its call for Tokyo to restrain right-wing activists whose actions have whipped up Chinese nationalism against Japan.Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang
14789 said China had an "unshakeable" will to safeguard its territory and urged Japan to act to prevent a further deterioration of the dispute.Japan, which has sought to cool Chinese anger, issued a statement citing the "utmost efforts" of Japanese medics to save Chan and regretting his death "from the heart"."We
14789 strongly hope this type of incident is never repeated," Japanese Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said.Early on Friday, the Kien Hwa and its sombre passengers put into port in Taiwan's Keelung for the grim task of returning Chan's body to Hong Kong.The ship complied with Taiwan's request not to fly
14789 rival China's red flag as it came into port at Keelung, nor was it used to wrap Chan's body as it was put ashore."I couldn't grasp what was going through my mind," Hong Kong reporter Jackson Liao recalled as he stepped from the Kien Hwa. "I saw this man die
14789 right by my feet.""Down with Japanese imperialism!" some 200 sympathetic Taiwan protesters chanted at Keelung. "Protect the Diaoyus!"Fearing a nationalist backlash, Japan's Hong Kong diplomatic mission sought police protection for all Japanese organisations in the British territory, including private firms.The ship had set out from Hong Kong on Sunday, with
14789 protest leader Chan vowing to plant China's flag on the islands and pull down Japan's flag and the offending lighthouse.Some 17 Japanese coastal patrol boats and several aircraft circled the tanker as it neared the islands, allowing it no closer than two nautical miles offshore early on Thursday.It was after
14789 the ship's pilot opposed a proposed landing by rubber raft that Chan and four others donned life vests, tied themselves to ropes and dived into the sea.Chan, a non-swimmer, lost consciousness as he was dragged beside the ship for 15 minutes, often below the heavy waves.Protesters initially seemed not to
14789 sense the seriousness of Chan's plight. Though alive when pulled aboard, he could not be revived by crew or Japanese medics put aboard by helicopter.A Japanese doctor declared Chan dead.Another protester was seriously injured and flown to Okinawa in southern Japan. Three were plucked from the sea unhurt.Grief swept those
14789 aboard the Kien Hwa 2. "When it happened everybody felt very saddened," activist Ma Ding said in Taiwan.Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule in mid-1997 and many Hong Kong people see the dispute as a test of China's strength and integrity.</

14801 arch-rival Taiwan and the British colony of Hong Kong, where protests against Japan's control of the potentially resource-rich islands have become common events.Activist Chan drowned after he leapt into the sea near the islands from the Hong Kong vessel Kien Hwa 2. 14819 by the trading scandal at the company's fund management subsidiary, Jardine Fleming Investment Management."No," Strutt said, when asked if there was a connection."The shareholders have been discussing for quite some time the structure of how they would involve themselves in the group going forward," he said.Regulators in London and Hong
14819 Kong hit Jardine Fleming with heavy penalties last month after revealing that a Hong Kong-based fund manager was allocating trades late, allowing for a change in price. Some trades involved his personal account.Jardine Fleming was fined 700,000 sterling. It voluntarily paid US$19.3 million to disadvantaged clients.Robert Thomas also retired from
14819 the board on Thursday, cutting all remaining ties after resigning last month as chief executive of Jardine Fleming Investment Management and Jardine Fleming Asset Management, the company's London-based fund management company.London's investment watchdog, the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, withdrew Thomas' registration and revoked Jardine Fleming Asset Management's authorisation.Many observers in
14819 Hong Kong were unconvinced by the company's denials of a connection between the resignations, the drastic management shake-up, and the trading scandal."Given what happened, this is no surprise," said Gary Greenberg, deputy managing director at Peregrine Asset Management in Hong Kong."Jardine Fleming's asset management division grew very quickly over the
14819 last decade and their compliance culture did not change at the same pace," he said.Said another fund manager: "People in the industry knew how they operated on the fund management side of the business for many, many years. Everyone knew about it. It was common knowledge."Strutt rejected all allegations that
14819 his company operated in a "cowboy" style."When these sorts of remarks come up you can usually trace them to competitors," Strutt said. "We have been known for our active style of fund management...but I don't think it's fair to say this is a cowboy operation. I don't think that's a
14819 sensible or mature judgment."Regulators said last month that they were convinced Jardine Fleming would operate within a "culture of compliance."But Greenberg said the shake-up is a talisman of change in Hong Kong's freewheeling commercial culture."There is a lot of offshore money now in Hong Kong. It's no longer secret money.
14819 A lot of this is institutional money and institutional money is not quite as forgiving of a fund manager," Greenberg said.</
14820 The captain of a protest ship said on Thursday he felt partly to blame for the drowning of one of his passengers, who dived into the East China Sea to protest Japan's claim to disputed chain of islandsProtestor David Chan, leader of 18 activists aboard the protest ship Kien Hwa
14820 2, died on Thursday after leaping into the sea to defy a blockade of the islands by Japanese patrol boats."I did not have the time to think for a moment that I should let him (Chan) do this or not, but I agreed to him," Ngai Lup-chee, captain of the
14820 tanker, said on government radio."He (Chan) was not a good swimmer and the rope and lifejacket were not tied in a quite correct and traditional way. Under the circumstances, many things had gone wrong. And as the commander of the ship I feel some responsibility," Ngai said.Chan and four other
14820 protesters who jumped with him, tied themselves to the ship and were dragged along side the vessel for several minutes.One of the other four was seriously hurt and later flown to a hospital in the Japanese prefecture of Okinawa.The other three were plucked from the sea unharmed.Ngai, who twice refused
14820 to let the group land on the islands due to rough seas, said he regretted his decision."I felt I should have agreed to their second request as I had turned down their first request to land on the island," he said.Chan's drowning was the first death in almost two months
14820 of protests that have swept through Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau since Japanese activists built a lighthouse and raised Japanese flags on the islands.Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.Tokyo's claim to what it
14820 calls the Senkaku Islands dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries, referring to them as the Diaoyus.</

14823 good for these firms," said Eric Liu of National Securities.Expected price rises for integrated circuit chips should also boost computer companies' performance, brokers said.Analysts and dealers in Singapore, however, were cautious over the sudden popularity of semiconductor stocks."We have yet to see indications from suppliers that there is indeed a
14823 turnaround," an analyst at Singapore brokerage said."It could be a blip," a senior institutional dealer said. 14823 years to absorb."Bullishness in the chip sector in Tokyo even towed semiconductor equipment firm shares higher. 14823 far the shares had not been rising in line with those of U.S. chip makers."MPI is a bit downstream from wafer fabrication, so they are not so affected by the prices," said analyst Bernard Tan of Merrill Lynch Singapore Private Ltd.</

14824 campaigns by ethnic Chinese in Taiwan, Hong Kong and China trying to force Japan to give up the islands which Tokyo calls the Senkaku group and China calls the Diaoyus.The long-simmering dispute erupted in July when Japanese rightwingers built a lighthouse on one of the islands."The ship will probably come
14824 for docking in the early morning hours on Friday," an official at the northern Keelung port said."If they want to dock in order to replenish supplies, repair and rest, I see no problems," another official at the northern Keelung port said by telephone. 14824 China five-star flag at the front."A Hong Kong television reporter aboard the Kien Hwa 2 said earlier on Thursday that the ship's captain wanted to sail to Keelung rather than return to Hong Kong following the protest.Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since the two separated after a
14824 civil war in 1949, but it typically allows private Chinese vessels to dock for humanitarian assistance.Taiwan's state-run Central News Agency quoted unnamed navigation officials as saying Taipei would allow Kien Hwa 2 to dock on humanitarian grounds even if it flies China's flag. 14824 insisted the flag must not fly at the bow."International guidelines do not have any restrictions on what flag a boat may fly or carry. But according to commonly accepted norms and courtesy the only flag that flies at the front should be the flag of the host country," he said.Chan's
14824 group sailed out of Hong Kong last Sunday intending to rip down the lighthouse and Japanese flags and to plant a People's Republic of China red communist flag, claiming the islands as Chinese sovereign territory. 14870 deficit, which ran at 8.1 percent of GDP last year, remains high.Central bank balance of payments data for July suggests a net outflow of foreign funds. 14878 Japan's Health Ministry said on Thursday it could not identify the exact source of a food poisoning epidemic that swept across the nation this summer, but still suspects radish sprouts as a possible cause.The ministry said in its final report on the crisis that it was unable to specify the
14878 source and route by which the deadly O-157 bacteria spread, creating one of the biggest health scandals since World War Two.But the report said there was reason to believe that contaminated radish sprouts, a salad vegetable similar to cress, were the cause of the poisoning from the O-157 E. coli
14878 bacillus, which killed 11 people and made more than 9,500 ill.The western Japan city of Sakai was hit hardest by the epidemic, with more than 6,500 people, mainly schoolchildren, affected. Experts believe the bacteria was in school lunches.But investigators failed to track down the original source of the bacillus and
14878 schools in Sakai stopped supplying school lunches when classes resumed this autumn."The government cannot call the epidemic over until all elementary schools resume their lunch programme," chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.A farmer identified by investigators as producing suspected radish sprouts said his company planned to file
14878 a damage suit against the central government."None of the tests showed our products carried the bacteria. I just can't accept it (the conclusion)," the farmer told reporters.Parents of children affected by the poisoning in Sakai said earlier this month they would sue the city for damages.Sakai Mayor Hideo Hataya said
14878 on Wednesday he would return part of his salary for the next six months to take responsibility for the outbreak in schools.Kajiyama said that as of September 20, eight people in Sakai were still in hospital, of whom one was said to be in serious condition.</

14886 Singapore's futures exchange said on Thursday it plans to extend the pit trading session for Euroyen futures and options from next month, but dealers said the move was unlikely to stir added interest in the contracts.The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said in a circular to its members that trading
14886 time for the Japanese interest rate futures and options contracts would be extended by an hour to 1205 GMT with effect from October 15. The move was to avoid widening the gap between the close of pit trading on SIMEX and the opening of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) floor
14886 as Chicago returns from daylight savings to normal trading hours, the exchange said.SIMEX and CME established a mutual offset system for the trading of Euroyen futures on March 6, shortly before a similar arrangement was launched between Tokyo and London's futures exchanges.Under the SIMEX/CME link-up, first established for Eurodollar, or
14886 U.S. interest rate futures in 1984, traders can take positions on one exchange and offset them on the other. "We'll now have to sit in the office for 13 hours a day and I doubt even Singaporean clients will trade (the Euroyen) during that extra hour," said a dealer with
14886 a European institution.Dealers said the extended hours were unlikely to be lifted once Chicago returned to daylight savings time next year and that they, viewed the move more as an attempt by SIMEX to raise its stake in the competition between exchanges."The Euroyen is already almost covered round the clock.
14886 Why do they want to eat into the London hours," said a dealer with another European house. He said the contract could already be traded on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) during the interval between SIMEX and CME.The Euroyen contract tended to be thinly traded outside
14886 Asian hours, due to the absence of market-moving news and the fact that the Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange, which sees the highest Euroyen volume, is closed then, he said.But a dealer with a U.S. institution said the extended hours could lead to added turnover in Euroyen futures as the
14886 only after-hours option currently available to traders was the screen-based Automated Trading System (ATS). "I think it's good in the sense that the ATS system has not really taken off because the bids and offers are kind of far apart and they hardly move all night," he said.The SIMEX circular,
14886 made available to Reuters, said trading of Euroyen futures on the automated system would also start one hour later at 1235 GMT from October 15.-- Singapore newsroom +65 870-3080</

14893 The price of Asia's benchmark Tapis crude oil reached its highest level since the Gulf War on Thursday, boosted by strong demand for light, low sulphur crude.Malaysia's Tapis was offered by a producer at $24.00/$24.10 per barrel -- the highest level since the 1990/1991 Gulf War when price assessments reached
14893 $39.08.A cocktail of factors is fuelling the rally, including strong fourth-quarter demand for crudes like Tapis, which are rich in middle distillate products, like gas oil and jet fuel, when refined."Prices are getting very strong and a lot is related to middle distillate demand. But there have been lots of
14893 other problems so that traders are scrambling for crude," one oil trader said.The middle distillates demand is exacerbated by U.S. data that show distillate stocks in the energy hungry United States are running almost 19 million barrels below last year's levels and are only building slowly. That could create demand
14893 for Asian crude and products.Traditionally, distillate stocks grow strongly as the fourth quarter winter season approaches and demand for heating grows.But despite the seasonal factor, other ingredients are adding to the cocktail, crude traders said.Reduced output from Indonesia's 90,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) light sweet Belida field -- as a floating storage
14893 vessel is moored -- is reducing available supplies.Ongoing production problems at Australia's 115,000 barrels per day (bpd) light-sweet Cossack field, which at times has cut output to just 50,000 bpd, is another ingredient.Rising refinery demand from South Korea is a further factor. The country's refining capacity is expected to grow
14893 to 2.44 million bpd in 1996 from 1.82 million in 1995.As part of South Korea's expansion, Yukong Ltd, the country's largest oil refiner, is bringing a 200,000 bpd distillate unit to commercial production in early October.In Indonesia, a 70,000 bpd basic refining unit is due to come on stream in
14893 November for a new petrochemical plant. The unit can only take very light crude oil in order to produce light distillates, like naphtha.In addition, the strength of the Brent futures market, which is just below post Gulf War highs, is making West African crude oil too expensive to bring to
14893 Asia.West African crudes often compete against Asia's light sweet grades and are priced against the North Sea Brent market.The cocktail has transferred into higher prices for a range of light sweet crude oils, apart from just Tapis.An oil major sold 500,000 barrels of mid October lifting Australian North West Shelf
14893 condensate at a premium of 60 cents above its Arun price benchmark. The condensate normally trades at a 30 or 40 cents premium.A European major sold 600,000 barrels of late October lifting Australian Kutubu crude oil to China at a market premium of 18 cents pre barrel. Kutubu traded only
14893 last week at a discount of 30 cents.A major sold 250,000 barrels of early November lifting Skua crude, which normally trades at parity to Tapis crude, at a premium of $1.05 to a trader.</

14899 Japan was plunged into a diplomatic quagmire on Thursday over a chain of disputed island in the East China Sea after an activist from a Hong Kong ship jumped overboard to his death in waters near the islands.Despite the first death in connection with a simmering sovereignty dispute over the
14899 small uninhabited islands, Japan has no alternative to its current stance of claiming ownership of the islands and waiting for the protests to calm down, political analysts said.Group leader David Chan died soon after jumping into rough seas from a chartered Hong Kong vessel to protest against Japan's claim to
14899 the islands, called the Senkakus in Japan and the Diaoyus in Chinese."There is no effective diplomatic step Japan could take to quell the emotion-filled protests," said Nozomu Akizuki of Tokai University near Tokyo.The long-dormant dispute over the islands erupted in July after Japanese right-wingers erected a makeshift lighthouse on one
14899 of them, sparking anti-Japanese protests in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau.Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda tried to calm the affair when he told his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen at the United Nations in New York on Wednesday that Tokyo would not let Japanese right-wingers take further action on the
14899 islands.Apart from Japan's wartime aggression, anti-Japanese sentiment among Chinese and people of Chinese descent stems from a long history of troubled Sino-Japanese relations, Akizuki said.He said Chinese people were obsessed with their traditional view that their culture was far superior to that of Japan."But Japan, the wartime aggressor in China,
14899 is now more advanced on the economic front. That's not what China wants," he said.Akio Watanabe of Aoyama Gakuin University in Tokyo said there was no prospect of the dispute being settled in the near future.He said the only possible solution could be that the countries concerned would jointly control
14899 and develop the islands for their mutual benefit.The territorial dispute had escalated to boiling point because of a lack of diplomatic skills on the part of Japan, political analyst Minoru Morita said."The Senkaku problem has pushed Japan into a diplomatic crisis," he said.He warned that the dispute could spread further
14899 to affect Japanese companies operating in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong."Japan must seriously consider the possibility of Japanese companies being kicked out of the countries concerned," he said.Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for
14899 centuries.The Taiwan government also claims ownership of the islands, saying they are under the jurisdiction of the northeastern Taiwanese county of Ilan.Japan was given control of the islands in 1972 by the United States, which had administered the islands along with Okinawa since the end of World War Two. But
14899 the U.S. government at the time said any outstanding territorial issue should be settled among the countries concerned.</

14902 Japan imported 25.16 million kilolitres (kl) of crude oil in August, up 19 percent from the same period a year earlier and up 39.4 percent from July, the trade ministry said on Thursday.A Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) official told reporters there was no specific reason for the
14902 sharp rise in August imports."Fluctuations in imports are mostly due to crude oil shipment schedules," the MITI official said.The sharp increase in August imports offsets the drop in July imports, he said. Japan, which relies heavily on the Middle East for its crude oil, imported 19.61 million kl from that
14902 area, which accounted for 77.9 percent of total August imports, MITI said.The United Arab Emirates, which produces crude grades such as Dubai and Murban, was the top source of crude oil for the 36th straight month, MITI said. Imports from the UAE accounted for 6.6 million kilolitres, or 30.3 percent
14902 of total imports.Saudi Arabia was the second largest supplier to Japan with imports reaching 5.04 million kl, followed by Iranian crude imports of 2.1 million kl.In August, the first ever Alaskan crude imports of 206,354 kl reached Japan, MITI said.Japanese refiners processed 21.68 million kl of crude in August, up
14902 4.7 percent from the same period a year earlier, marking a year-on-year rise for the fourth consecutive month.Refinery operating rates were at 83.1 percent, up from 80.1 percent a year earlier. Utilisation rates generally rise towards the end of the year as refiners build kerosene stocks for the winter months.The
14902 amount of crude used for direct burning by electricity utilities fell 2.6 percent to 1.76 million kl from a year earlier, but rose 14.1 percent from July, MITI said.</

14904 each side of a disc, enough to record 133 minutes of film and sound.Toshiba said worldwide demand for DVD-related hardware is expected to reach 120 million units in calendar 2000. 14956 Matching up new genetic research with long-term epidemiological studies, scientists have gathered strong evidence that a recently-discovered genetic defect can protect some people against the AIDS virus.Scientists have long sought to understand why some people exposed to the HIV virus do not become infected. They are eager to identify any
14956 natural defences against AIDS, in the hope that they can gain further insight into the disease and develop new therapies or vaccines to treat or prevent it.In research appearing on Friday in the journal Science, a team at the National Cancer Institute (NCI) took the recent findings about the CKR5
14956 gene and linked it to data on AIDS gathered in six major epidemiological studies nationwide."We entered into a collaboration with a number of epidemiologist who have been tracking HIV exposed and infected patients for the last 15 years," lead researcher Stephen O'Brien of the NCI said in an interview.The HIV
14956 virus infects a cell in a multi-step process. It must grab onto the cell, and then it must penetrate it. The CKR5 defect, discovered just months ago, interrupts that penetration process in white blood cells known as macrophages.Looking at health history data on 1955 people, scientists confirmed that not one
14956 of the 17 people who had two copies of the defective CKR5 gene, one inherited from each parent, had developed AIDS despite exposure to the HIV virus.The findings provide only a piece of the puzzle, however, O'Brien cautioned. There were 622 people in the studies who were not HIV infected
14956 despite high risk of exposure, or repeated exposure. But only 17 had this dual genetic defect."We explained three percent of the cases. We still have to find out about the other 97," he said.The researchers also found that a single copy of the gene defect did not provide immunity. Of
14956 the 282 people who had one altered copy of the gene, about two-thirds were HIV-infected.But homosexual males with one defective CKR5 gene who were HIV infected tended to live two or three years longer before developing AIDS symptoms than those without a defect.But for reasons not yet understood, haemophiliacs with
14956 the same single copy defect were less likely to progress slowly.The genetic defect was much more common among U.S. whites than among U.S. blacks, the scientists found. Based on the research done so far, it has not been seen in African blacks.</

14959 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentTreasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday urged rich creditor countries to do more to help debt-ridden poor nations get back on their feet.Speaking to reporters ahead of the semi-annual IMF/World Bank meeting here, Rubin said Washington backs expanding the scope of debt relief provided by the
14959 "Paris Club" of creditors to as much as 80 percent from the 67 percent ceiling now."The Paris Club reduction should be up to 80 percent," he said.Representatives of the creditors' club, which includes the United States, are meeting this week in Paris to discuss how they can participate in a
14959 multi-billion dollar initiative to provide expanded debt relief to the world's poor.The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have already pledged to do their part and have called on the Paris Club to expand the size of its debt relief to cover 90 percent of outstanding loans.World Bank President
14959 James Wolfensohn warned last week that some debt-ridden poor nations would not be able to put their economies back on track if the Paris Club opts to provide only 80 percent debt relief.Oxfam International, a private environmental and development group, singled out the Paris Club as the biggest obstacle now
14959 to the multi-billion debt relief initiative.It warned on Thursday that failure to act could cost the lives of 21 million children in Africa.It remains unclear though just how much the Paris Club will be willing to do. Although major creditors such as the United States seem to be lining up
14959 behind providing 80 percent debt relief, the stance of others is still uncertain.In a Sept. 12 letter to the Fund, Paris Club head Christian Noyer said creditor nations would determine how much to expand their debt relief on a case-by-case basis, "taking account of the largest possible contributions of the
14959 World Bank and the IMF."The IMF last week promised to find the financing necessary for it to take part in the debt relief initiative, but stopped short of spelling out where the money would come from.Rubin told reporters on Thursday that the United States still believed that the Fund will
14959 have to sell off some of its nearly 104 million ounces of gold to do that.But Germany and a few other industrial nations oppose gold sales and instead want the IMF to use bilateral contributions from member nations to aid the world's poor.Rubin told reporters on Thursday that the United
14959 States would be willing to consult with Congress about possibly making such a contribution, but only if the IMF first agreed to sell some of its gold.He suggested though that a decision on gold sales may not need to be made for some years, as the IMF currently has enough
14959 money in its kitty to last until around the year 2000.</

14975 Before you invest in any mutual fund, the fund sponsor should send you a prospectus -- a document that includes considerable information about the fund's official investment policy.Should you read it? Probably -- but don't expect it to tell you everything you need to know about the fund.For starters, the
14975 prospectus will tell you about the fund's fees. The fund's expense ratio shows its annual expenses as a percentage of its assets -- for example, a fund with a 1 percent expense ratio spends $1 of every $100 on expenses.How much is too much? That depends partly on the fund
14975 category. For example, an emerging markets fund may have sizable research expenses, so you might reasonably expect to pay as much as 1.7 percent of your investment in annual fund expenses. Indeed, a fund that is spending more on research in that area might even do a better job.By contrast,
14975 an investment grade bond fund shouldn't cost nearly as much to manage. The difference in returns between two funds with comparable credit quality and average maturities isn't likely to be great.So why not go with a cheap fund? Example: Vanguard Fixed-Income Short-Term Corporate (800-662-7447; $3,000 minimum investment; 6.4 percent recent
14975 yield; no-load) invests in short-term investment-grade bonds. The fund may also invest in U.S. government securities, commercial paper, or bank obligations.Another inexpensive choice from Vanguard: Vanguard Fixed-Income GNMA (800-662-7447; $3,000 minimum; 7.4 percent recent yield; no-load) invests in Government National Mortgage Association certificates. The fund attempts to maintain an intermediate-term
14975 average weighted maturity.A fund's risks also should be spelled out in the document.Since lawyers write prospectuses, you can be sure that the description of risks will be extremely detailed. That means you can review all of the worst possible things that can happen when you invest in the fund.If you're
14975 still comfortable holding its shares, that's a sign that you'll be able to stay with the fund through short-term fluctuations that might shake out less-informed investors.The prospectus will also tell you about a fund's past performance. You can compare those numbers with the performance results of similar funds, which you'll
14975 find in those funds' prospectuses, or in outside references such as Morningstar Mutual Funds, available in many libraries.Another reason to read fund prospectuses is to get an idea of the different types of funds that exist.For example, if you order prospectuses for five different bond funds, you will see some
14975 important differences. One fund might invest up to 10 percent in overseas bonds, while another shuns such holdings altogether. Or a fund might invest in long-term securities whose values fluctuate with interest rates, while its competitor sticks to short-term bonds.Differences in credit quality also are common even within the same
14975 category: One investment grade bond fund might invest only in AAA-rated securities, while another can buy a modest slug of high-yield, low-quality bonds.Equity fund prospectuses will sometimes spell out stylistic differences between funds. You might learn that one manager prefers to buy shares of firms whose profits are rising sharply,
14975 while another focuses on slow-growth, asset-rich companies.Once you've read a few prospectuses, you'll get a sense of what to expect -- and what not to expect. For example, the prospectus may not tell you much about the fund's current investments or the manager's general investment philosophy. Reading the most recent
14975 annual report might help -- and the best fund managers typically pride themselves on clearly explaining their strategy to shareholders.Beyond that, Morningstar can help with a review of the fund's historical performance, recent strategy and current outlook. If you're willing to part with a few dollars to get still better
14975 information on a smaller universe of funds, consider the No-Load Fund Analyst (510-254-9017; $225 for 12 monthly issues and annual guidebook).(EDITORS: Clint Willis is a freelance writer who covers financial issues for Reuters. Any opinions in the column are solely those of Mr. Willis.)</

14979 After 188 days in orbit on a Russian space station, NASA endurance champion Shannon Lucid returned to Earth on Thursday and celebrated with a box of M&amp;M candies sent by President Bill Clinton.The $2 billion shuttle Atlantis slipped through the Florida morning sky and touched down at Kennedy Space Centre
14979 at 8:13 a.m. EDT (1213 GMT).National Aeronautics and Space Administration chief Daniel Goldin welcomed Lucid back to Earth with a large box of M&amp;Ms from Clinton. "I've never seen a box of M&amp;Ms with the presidental seal on top of it," he told reporters.During the flight, Lucid expressed her craving
14979 for the candy and had packets of M&amp;Ms delivered to Mir aboard unmanned cargo craft.Clinton later made a telephone call to congratulate Lucid on the successful end of the mission."You've been a terrific inspiration for young women around the country and all around the world," he said. "You've given us
14979 all a great deal to be proud of and a lot of thrills. We're glad you're home safe and sound."The president also checked to make sure she had received her M&amp;Ms.Lucid replied, "That was so nice and so thoughtful of you. Really, really appreciate that."She rode home in a reclining
14979 seat designed to cushion her from the effects of gravity. After six months in weightlessness, the 53-year-old biochemist was expected to feel weak and woozy, NASA doctors said."Welcome home, Shannon, from your record-setting mission," spacecraft communicator Bill Gregory radioed from mission control in Houston as the shuttle came to a
14979 halt on the three-mile-long (4.8-km-long) runway.The touchdown marked the end of a 75-million-mile (121-million-km) voyage for Lucid, who spent six months performing scientific research aboard Russia's Mir space station."There is an acute recovery during the first few days where she gets her land legs back, so to speak," said Dr.
14979 Roger Billica, chief of medical operations at Johnson Space Centre in Houston. "That's followed by a two-to-three-week period of a very active rehabilitation programme."Within an hour of landing, Lucid and her five crewmates left Atlantis and boarded a special transport vehicle."She came out of the shuttle on her own power,
14979 but I think a couple of people just were holding onto her just to make sure she wouldn't fall," NASA Administrator Goldin said.Dr Gaylen Johnson, the surgeon who monitored Lucid's health from Earth throughout her flight, earlier boarded the shuttle on the runway to gauge the astronaut's condition.A team of
14979 physicians, physical therapists, trainers, dieticians and psychologists are standing by to assist Lucid over the next few weeks if necessary. Her six-month stay in space was the longest by an American and a record for a woman."The docs say that she is in really good health, that there are no
14979 surprises and they expect her rehabilitation to go normal," said Frank Culbertson, who heads NASA's shuttle-Mir programme.The Atlantis astronauts were expected to stay in Florida overnight and return to their homes in Houston on Friday. Lucid may be allowed home on Friday night, accompanied by a doctor.The veteran spacewoman, who
14979 joined NASA in 1978, was the first of six astronauts who will staff the remote Russian space outpost into 1998. 14979 and Alexander Kaleri. The shuttle will return to Mir in January for another change of crew.</

14992 Semiconductor industry firms Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Varian Associates Inc. announced plans Thursday to trim their payrolls due to slower demand for computer chips.Advanced Micro, which makes computer chips, said it planned to cut up to 200 jobs and take a $6 million charge and semiconductor equipment firm Varian
14992 said it was cutting 115 workers."In light of weak demand, the company has carefully reviewed operations in order to achieve and maintain appropriate staffing levels," Advanced Micro said in a statement."Issues that were identified as a result of those reviews included overlapping or redundant activities and skill sets that do
14992 not match current or future requirements. These concerns are being addressed by the workforce reduction."Advanced Micro reported a $35 million loss in the second quarter ended June 30 vs. a profit of $80.7 million in the year-ago quarter, reflecting a significant decline in revenues from its once-lucrative flash memory chips.Sunnyvale,
14992 Calif.-based Advanced Micro employs 12,500 people worldwide.Varian said its cuts, which reduce overall employment by less than 2 percent, affect semiconductor equipment factories in Gloucester, Mass. and Palo Alto, Calif."The semiconductor industry continues to suffer from overcapacity and price discounting, and that inevitably means lower demand for new chip-making equipment,"
14992 said Executive Vice President Richard Aurelio. "While we know the cycle will turn up again, right now it's impossible to predict when."As a result, these moves are needed to keep our costs in balance with the slowdown in orders during the interim."He said about 85 of the positions affected are
14992 at the Gloucester plant, which had a similar reduction in mid-August. The remainder are at the Palo Alto unit.Semiconductor sales have slowed considerably this year, reflecting a glut in the market and sharply lower prices for memory chips. In recent weeks, however, prices have started to rebound.Spot prices for 16
14992 megabit DRAM chips, the most popular configuration, have risen to $10 from $8 in early August. The increase benefits all producers, including Micron Technology Inc. and Texas Instruments Inc., he said.Advanced Micro's stock fell 87.5 cents to $15.125, and Palo Alto, Calif.-based Varian was down 62.5 cents at $47.50 on
14992 the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.</
14993 President Bill Clinton on Thursday urged Israelis and Palestinians to end the bloodshed in the Arab territories and not take "unnecessarily provocative actions" that exacerbate tensions.With a rising death toll from two days of clashes between Palestinians and Israelis in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, Clinton and his top
14993 officials engaged in frantic diplomatic efforts to try to salvage the Middle East peace process.Clinton stopped short of calling Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in east Jerusalem a provocation but made clear Washington felt it was an irritant to the peace process.Addressing both Israelis and
14993 Palestinians, he said: "Our message to them is this: It is in everyone's interest to resolve their differences peacefully, to work together on security and to avoid any actions that could make progress on the peace between Israelis and Palestinians more difficult."Asked if Israel should seal up the tunnel, he
14993 said: "What I think is they need to end the violence and they need to discuss these matters between them and they need to ask themselves, all of them do, what can we do to avoid unnecessarily provocative actions."White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters "the parties should take no
14993 steps that raise new issues" and he said the tunnel "is clearly a new issue."Arab anger at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's failure to extend self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza boiled over on Wednesday when his right-wing government opened an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places.Israeli troops killed
14993 33 Palestinians and PLO police shot dead 10 Israelis in gun battles and stone-throwing clashes on Thursday, the bloodiest day in the West Bank and Gaza since Yasser Arafat set up his self-rule Palestinian government.The fierce fighting shook U.S. hopes of keeping alive Arab-Israeli peace talks, stalled since Netanyahu came
14993 to power 100 days ago.Secretary of State Warren Christopher, in New York at the U.N. 14993 Dennis Ross has been on the phone almost continously to Arafat, other Palestinians and Netanyahu adviser Dore Gold."We have to reach some agreement with the other parties about how we proceed from here. If they come up with the idea that perhaps a trip out there is worthwhile then obviously
14993 the secretary is going to consider it," State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said.Clinton said he would speak to Christopher later in the day to discuss whether it would be helpful to send a U.S. delegation to the region. "We are prepared to do anything we can that will be
14993 of assistance," he said.Burns said the United States "is not going to point the finger of blame at either side" because it would not be helpful. But he said: "We do have private views and we are asserting those views."Other U.S. officials, asked if Washington had asked Israel to close
14993 the tunnel, declined to comment.Burns said Christopher did not know in advance about the opening of the tunnel but could not say if U.S. diplomats in the region knew about it. He declined to get into the merits of the dispute but said: "The fact is the tunnel was opened
14993 and the fact is there's been terrible violence since then."He called King Hussein of Jordan's proposal to close the tunnel and have experts study the matter "a good faith effort" but said there was no U.S. view one way or the other on it.Christopher was to meet the foreign ministers
14993 of Egypt, Israel, Saudi Arabia and the Gulf Cooperation Council states on Friday in New York.</

14995 By Gail Appleson, Law CorrespondentA young money manager touted as the next Warren Buffett was charged with fraud Thursday in the 1995 public offering of a reinsurance company he founded and for lying to Chemical Bank to obtain $24 million in loans.The charges accuse 31-year-old Christopher Bagdasarian along with a
14995 former partner at Deloitte &amp; Touche, LLP of providing false information in last year's offering of Omaha, Neb.-based Normandy America Inc.In an unusual move, the initial public offering was pulled from the Nasdaq market on Aug. 16, 1995, after one day of trading. Lead underwriter Salomon Brothers had said at
14995 the time that the IPO was withdrawn due to market conditions.Bagdasarian, the founder, chairman and chief executive officer of Normandy America was frequently compared in the financial press last year to Warren Buffett because of his flashy investment track record.Bagdasarian, who lives in Montecito, Calif., had stated in his Securities
14995 and Exchange Commission filing prior to last year's IPO that he had been managing money for 10 years, providing his investors with an annualized return of 29 percent. He said that he began with $37 million in 1984 and ended up managing more than $700 million.This would have meant the
14995 defendant was 19 when he had $37 million.Bagdasarian was named in an eight-count criminal complaint filed by the Manhattan U.S. attorney's office and during a court hearing waived his right to an indictment by a federal grand jury.His lawyer Michael Armstrong would not comment on whether Bagdasarian would later plead
14995 guilty to the charges, as sometimes happens when a defendant is charged in a complaint rather than by indictment.If convicted, he faces up to 165 years in prison and a $5.75 million fine.Samuel White, 35, of La Canada, Calif., a certified public accountant and former partner in Deloitte &amp; Touche's
14995 Los Angeles office was named in an eight-count indictment. White, who provided accounting and tax advise to Bagdasarian, faces the same penalties.Both men are accused of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, bank fraud and perjury. They were also sued by the SEC on related civil charges.Bagdasarian claimed his investment success
14995 as investment manager and president of California-based Criterion Holdings, Inc. He said he made investments on behalf of himself and others through Criterion and its broker-dealer subsidiary.Prosecutors allege that the scheme began in February 1992, when Bagdasarian first approached Chemical seeking an $8 million standby letter of credit that he
14995 needed for his planned purchase of a Gulfstream IV aircraft.In connection with his request, he represented himself as a highly successful investment manager and owned a portfolio of "blue-chip" securities valued at more than $130 million.He was able to get about $24.55 million in loans and other credits from Chemical
14995 Bank from 1992 through 1994 by allegedly lying about the value of his securities and cash holdings. White allegedly assisted in the scheme by wrongfully verifying that Deloitte had confirmed Bagdasarian's holdings.The men vastly overstated the value of Bagdasarian's portfolio claiming that it reached more than $521 million, prosecutors alleged.In
14995 the second part of the scheme, Bagdasarian approached Salomon seeking its assistance in raising capital for Normandy America. Salomon, along with Alex Brown &amp; Co. and Schroder Wertheim &amp; Co. agreed to underwrite the $196.4 million initial public offering and a $20.6 million private placement.The complaint alleges that in August
14995 1994 he falsely represented to Salomon that he had achieved multi-year returns of about 30 percent per year on about $700 million in assets under his management. Bagdasarian and White allegedly represented that the securities were held in about 30 entities located outside the United States.They resisted Salomon's request for
14995 details by claiming the structure of the offshore entities were created by and was proprietary to Deloitte.Prosecutors also allege that when Salomon tried to interview people whose assets were invested with Bagdasarian, the defendant recruited a Normandy employee to impersonate an investor who claimed that he had achieved 20 percent

15000 flooded the system. 15011 The dollar held its overnight gains in U.S. trade, closing nearly flat after holding off profit-takers, dealers and analysts said.The greenback saw steady bid interest after a surprising Swiss interest rate cut and signs of Italian economic vigor.Switzerland cut its discount rate to an 18-year low at 1.0 percent from
15011 1.5 and investors fled Swiss francs and marks."People understood Switzerland had to do something to get its economy going. I don't think they were quite ready to see such a large reduction in rates," said Lisa Finstrom, currency analyst at Smith Barney. The dollar edged higher to close at 1.2542/47
15011 Swiss francs from 1.2525/35 at the open, but up sharply from 1.2410/20 at Wednesday's close.The dollar was also barely higher at 110.62/72 yen from 110.60/65 and 1.5234/39 marks from 1.5227/30 at the open, but held most of a rise from 1.5165/75 marks at Wednesday's close.The dollar/Swiss rally also hurt the
15011 mark, with investors also expecting lower German interest rates in coming months."People that had been flocking to the Swiss francs got hurt a bit and the higher dollar puts pressure on the mark," said Gabriel Grippo, chief currency dealer at Credit Agricole. The lira saw solid buying for a second
15011 straight day, boosted by official Italian predictions that Italy would slash its budget deficit to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, qualifying for a proposed single European currency.The lira remained near its strongest level in two years, reached Wednesday, below 1000 to the mark. Mark/lira sales also bolstered
15011 the dollar against the mark, dealers said."There was more talk about Italy doing well. That should continue to put pressure on the mark and put legs under the dollar," Grippo said. Much of the dollar's rally occurred in Asian and European trading. As markets closed in Europe, many investors sold
15011 off dollars to take profits, limiting further dollar gains.But an afternoon report that Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara called the United States the best place for Japanese investment helped the dollar edge to a new session high against the yen, dealers said.Meanwhile, influential economist Fred Bergsten, director of
15011 the Institute for International Economics, told reporters in Washington that Japanese officials were seeking to weaken the yen to lower the cost of Japanese exports. "The dollar has to play some catch-up against the yen," said Grippo. "I think tomorrow we should take out 111 (yen) and test 111.50."The dollar's
15011 1996 high is 111.19 yen reached on July 8.Investors appear to have already forgotten their disappointment at Federal Reserve officials' decision not to raise interest rates at a policy making meeting Tuesday.A report of a surprising 3.1-percent drop in durable goods orders in August eased investor fear that the U.S.
15011 economy may overheat and see higher inflation. That stoked a sharp rally in Treasury bond prices and lifted the dollar, dealers said. "There was a little nervousness about how prudent that Fed decision will prove to be, but now there's a perception that our long-term interest rates aren't looking so
15011 fearful," Finstrom said.In other trade, sterling inched higher to $1.5612/17 from $1.5608/18 at the open. The dollar slipped to Canadian $1.3676/81 from C$1.3678/83. The Australian dollar hardly moved, closing at $0.7925/30 from $0.7924/29.--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664</
15012 Living a campaigning politician's fondest dream, President Bill Clinton championed motherhood on Thursday by signing a law that guarantees women a 48-hour hospital stay after childbirth."Parents may rush to the hospital but they shouldn't be rushed out of it unless it's the right thing to do for the parent and
15012 the child. This law is common sense and now it is the law of the land," Clinton said at a Rose Garden ceremony.The "Newborns' and Mothers' Protection Act" was tied to a $64.4 billion government money bill that also improves health benefits for mental patients and children with spina bifida
15012 born to Vietnam veterans.It grew out of public complaints about health care plans that forced new mothers to leave the hospital as soon as 10 hours after a normal delivery. The new law requires health insurers to let women stay in the hospital for 48 hours after a normal delivery
15012 and 96 hours after a Caesarean.The so-called 48-hour rule, which could reinforce the "gender gap" advantage that Clinton enjoys over Republican challenger Bob Dole, was approved by a Republican-controlled Congress that was increasingly putting its own interests above those of the party's trouble-plagued presidential candidate.The gender gap referred to election
15012 polls that showed women voters prefer Clinton to Dole by as much as 29 percentage points."By ensuring 48-hour hospital stays for mothers and newborns, battling discrimination against mental illness, caring for children of veterans who suffer from a terrible disease, we affirm that we will do everything we can to
15012 strengthen our families," Clinton said.The health care reforms were attached to a bill providing money for federal housing programmes, veterans' health care, environmental protection and space research.The new maternity and mental health rules take effect on Jan. 1, 1998 while the spina bifida provision will start Oct. 1, 1997. The
15012 expansion of mental health coverage was expected to benefit 75 million Americans with group health insurance and those covered by government-funded Medicaid.While health plans will not be required to cover mental illness, those that do will no longer be permitted to set lower maximum payment amounts for mental health treatment.An
15012 estimated 3,000 children of Vietnam veterans, many of whom are now adults, stand to share in about $44 million worth of disability benefits, job training support and health care provided by veterans' hospitals.The benefit was provided after studies showed a link between children born with spina bifida, a crippling neurological
15012 birth defect, and exposure to Agent Orange while the father served in Vietnam."The children of our soldiers should not have to suffer for the sacrifice of their parents," Clinton said.Several mothers with infants attended the Rose Garden bill-signing ceremony, which also featured remarks by Vice President Al Gore, his wife
15012 Tipper and Hillary Rodham Clinton.With less than six weeks left before the election, Clinton holds a double-digit overall lead over Dole in most of the polls, and nearly every domestic issue on which presidential elections usually turn has been breaking his way.Clinton's soaring political fortunes got a further boost with
15012 the release of annual census data on household income."In one year median household income was up $898 after inflation. That's the biggest increase in a decade. Over the last two years, the typical American family has seen its income rise $1,600 over inflation," Clinton said.The figures gave the Democratic president
15012 powerful new ammunition with which to counter a key thrust of Dole's campaign, which is that Americans would be better off economically by putting him in the White House.</

15014 A U.S. Commerce Department official on Thursday said the Federal Reserve Board did not receive the August report on durable goods orders ahead of its release today at 8:30 a.m. (1230 GMT)"There is no evidence that any premature release of data occurred surrounding the durable goods release Sept. 26, 1996,"
15014 said Jane Callen, a Commerce official who conducts briefings where economic indicators are released.She said the department adheres strictly to a directive that prohibits the early release of the data to anyone other than the President through the Council of Economic Advisers. Executive branch officials who receive the data are
15014 prohibited from releasing the data or commenting on it ahead of the scheduled release time.The Commerce Department's report of a 3.1 percent drop in August durable goods orders hinted at greater-than-expected weakness in the manufacturing sector.That fuelled some talk that perhaps some members of the Federal Reserve policy-setting Open Market
15014 Committee had the data at the time of their most recent meeting on Sept. 24.At that meeting, the Fed surprised many economists by refraining from raising interest rates. A number of economists felt a rate rise was necessary to cool down the economy.</

15021 After 188 days in orbit on a Russian space station, NASA's endurance champion Shannon Lucid rode back to Earth on Thursday aboard the U.S. shuttle Atlantis.The $2 billion reusable spaceship slipped through the Florida morning sky and touched down at Kennedy Space Centre at 8:13 a.m. EDT (1213 GMT)."Welcome home,
15021 Shannon, from your record-setting mission," spacecraft communicator Bill Gregory radioed from mission control in Houston as the shuttle came to a halt on the three-mile-long (4.8-km-long) runway.The touchdown marked the end of a 75-million-mile (121 million km) voyage for Lucid, who spent six months performing scientific research aboard Russia's Mir
15021 space station.Lucid rode home in a reclining seat designed to cushion her from the effects of gravity. After six months in weightlessness, the 53-year-old biochemist was expected to feel weak and woozy, National Aeronautics and Space Administration doctors said."There is an acute recovery during the first few days where she
15021 gets her land legs back, so to speak," said Dr. Roger Billica, chief of medical operations at Johnson Space Centre in Houston. "That's followed by a two-to-three-week period of a very active rehabilitation programme."Within an hour of landing Lucid and her five crewmates left Atlantis and boarded a special transport
15021 vehicle. "She came out of the shuttle on her own power but I think a couple of people just were holding onto her just to make sure she wouldn't fall," NASA Administrator Daniel Goldin said.Dr. Gaylen Johnson, the surgeon who monitored Lucid's health from Earth throughout her flight, had earlier
15021 boarded the shuttle on the runway to gauge the astronaut's condition.A team of physicians, physical therapists, trainers, dieticians and psychologists are standing by to assist Lucid over the next few weeks if necessary. Her six-month stay in space was the longest by an American and a record for a woman."The
15021 docs say that she is in really good health, that there are no surprises and they expect her rehabilitation to go normal," said Frank Culbertson, who heads NASA's shuttle-Mir programme.Goldin welcome Lucid back to Earth with a large box of M&amp;Ms from President Bill Clinton. "I've never (before) seen a
15021 box of M&amp;Ms with the presidental seal on top of it," he said.During the flight, Lucid expressed her craving for the candy and had packets of M&amp;Ms delivered to Mir aboard unmanned cargo craft.The Atlantis astronauts were expected to stay in Florida overnight and return to their homes in Houston
15021 on Friday. Lucid may be allowed home on Friday night, accompanied by a doctor.The veteran spacewoman, who joined NASA in 1978, was the first of six astronauts who will staff the remote Russian space outpost into 1998. Her place on Mir was taken by astronaut John Blaha, a 54-year-old Vietnam
15021 veteran.Atlantis left him at the station for a four-month tour of duty with Russian cosmonauts Valeri Korzun and Alexander Kaleri. The shuttle will return to Mir in January for another change of crew.</

15025 longitude 36.2 west. 15031 (The following is an opinion column by Allan J. Lichtman, a political historian with the American University in Washington DC. This views expressed are those of the author and do not reflect Reuters)By Allan J. LichtmanPresident Clinton and House Speaker Newt Gingrich may soon find themselves saying with the Duke
15031 of Wellington that "nothing except a battle lost can be half so melancholy as a battle won."Both look like winning re-election in November, but both may face rocky times thereafter when scandals and legal problems, delayed by the campaign, come home to haunt them.Shortly after the election, the Supreme Court
15031 will decide whether Paula Jones' sexual harassment suit can be heard while Clinton serves as president.Meanwhile, Special Prosecutor Kenneth Starr is relentlessly investigating the Clintons' involvement in Whitewater, the firing of White House travel office employees and the receipt of confidential FBI files on former White House employees.Starr may be
15031 competent and fair-minded, but he's a partisan Republican who will dig for incriminating evidence against the Clintons and make the most of what he finds.How many government officials in this era of borderline business deals and complicated regulations would survive a dedicated prosecutor with $50 million to plumb the depths
15031 of their public and private lives?The investigation against Gingrich is less intense but may be even more dangerous. The Georgia lawmaker will face grave charges that he violated tax laws in financing his college course on "Renewing American Civilisation."My prediction is that Gingrich will not last another year as speaker
15031 even if the Republicans retain control of the House in November.Charges against Gingrich have been pending for two years in the bipartisan House ethics committee. Last December, the Committee appointed James Cole as outside counsel to investigate the allegations.Cole recently filed a report summarizing the evidence in the Gingrich case,
15031 but House Republicans blocked its release. Allegedly, the report contains information highly damaging to the speaker.The Cole report will probably stay buried until after Election Day. But charges against the speaker will be heard next year.Gingrich may be hoist on his own petard. In 1989, when the House probed ethics
15031 charges against Speaker James Wright, Gingrich pushed the investigation to a speedy conclusion and insisted that a speaker must be above even the appearance of wrongdoing.Beyond his legal problems, Clinton faces an extraordinary historical challenge. Every two-term Democratic president of the last 100 years has faced a grim second-term slump.The
15031 Great Depression of the 1890s ravaged America during Grover Cleveland's second term.Woodrow Wilson won victories in World War I but botched the peace.Franklin Roosevelt launched ill-fated schemes to pack the Supreme Court and purge conservatives from the Democratic Party.Harry Truman lost China to the Communists, fell short of victory in
15031 Korea and failed enact his Fair Deal proposals.Lyndon Johnson fell victim to his disastrous escalation in Vietnam.Roosevelt ran for a third term in 1940 and won, but Republicans succeeded each of the other four two-term Democrats. Not since Martin Van Buren succeeded Andrew Jackson in 1840 has a two-term Democratic
15031 president turned the White House over to a successor of his own party.Clinton's political skill may help him break the two-term Democratic jinx. But history also teaches that scandals usually erupt during a president's second term.Examples include Watergate, Iran/Contra, and the Truman-era corruption that became known as the "mess in
15031 Washington."Clinton and Gingrich, arguably the two most powerful politicians in the United States, appear to be in for the political battles of their lives -- battles that have nothing to do with the upcoming election.</

15041 pork product values have advanced the past couple of days, and instances some products posted sharp gains, and this is keeping packer demand for cash hogs strong. Cash hog prices rose $0.50 to $2.00 per cwt Thursday and expectations are for cash markets to trade steady to higher Friday, they
15041 said.Some strength was also attributed to expectations that the report will show lighter than year ago hog numbers and the prospect for increasing hog numbers next year. 15041 report point to all hogs as of September 1 at 96.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 97.5 percent. Kept for breeding estimates averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94 to 99 percent and kept for market estimates averaged 96.5 and ranged 95 to
15041 98 percent of last year.But farrowing intention estimates for September/November and December/February averaged near 100 percent and the high end of expectations ranged from 102 to 105 percent.
