15045 The Clinton administration promised House lawmakers Thursday that it would make no new commitments to curb U.S. carbon emissions before it knows what impact new obligations might have on the economy."We will not agree to any specific targets until we've completed the analysis," Assistant Secretary of State Eileen Claussen said
15045 at a packed House energy and power panel hearing on international negotiations to combat global warming.The administration expects to complete its analysis by the end of this year or early next year, said Under Secretary of Commerce Everett Ehrlich.Scientists widely believe man-made carbon emissions have a significant impact on the
15045 earth's climate and should be cut in order to prevent a range of crises, including massive floods, hurricanes, and the spread of tropical diseases.Lawmakers, nervous that new environmental measures will hammer U.S. industry, were taken aback when the Clinton administration in July said it would work toward an agreement which
15045 included legally binding targets for cutting emissions.While the administration said emissions should be pared, Claussen agreed with House members that a December 1997 deadline was "ambitious" for reaching a decision that would require industrialized countries to take major steps to meet strict targets and timetables.The date for an agreement was
15045 set by international negotiators seeking to combat global warming beyond 2000.House members repeated pleas that Washington should not agree to impose tighter requirements on U.S. industry than on competitors in developing countries.Any agreement imposing different requirements on industrialized and developing countries "would be very poorly received up here," warned Rep.
15045 John Dingell of Michigan, the top Democrat on the House Commerce Committee.But Claussen said only that the administration would not agree to any measures that forced the United States to cap its emissions at the same level per person as developing countries, where emissions per person are a fraction of
15045 the current U.S. level."Any future commitment must be predicated on ensuring that the U.S. ecnomy remains robust and internationally competitive," the administration said in a statement.</

15047 U.S. and European Union trade chiefs were set to meet Thursday in an effort to resolve a dispute over information technology and move forward on the effort to get an international agreement.Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who last week accused Europe of backing away from an agreement to eliminate
15047 tariffs on a wide range of electronic products, told reporters that she would discuss the technology accord with European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan late Thursday.She said she was encouraged by a letter this week from Brittan on the issue, but that Europe lacked unity on the matter which made
15047 it difficult to reach agreement."I am encouraged, but I don't think we're there yet," Barshefsky told reporters following a speech to a business group. "Clearly Europe has to come to a rapid decision on this issue. We will not be able to move forward on this initiative ... without Europe
15047 because we will not let Europe free ride on our tariff reductions."The Information Technology Agreement (ITA) would eliminate tariffs on a wide range of information products including computer chips, software and telecommunications equipment. Barshefsky and Brittan were in Seattle to attend a meeting of Quadrilateral (Quad) trade ministers which also
15047 includes Canada's Arthur Eggleton and Japan's Shunpei Tsukahara.Barshefsky has said that Quad leadership on a technology deal is needed to win a global agreement at the first meeting of World Trade Organisation ministers to be held in Singapore in December.Barshefsky declined to discuss the content of the letter, but EU
15047 sources in Brussels said that Europe was backing down from an ultimatum that insisted on European inclusion in a U.S.-Japan semiconductor alliance in order to press for a wider ITA agreement.The letter was said to suggest that work on the ITA could begin if the "discriminatory aspects" of a U.S.-Japan
15047 chip alliance, renewed this summer, were not applied until after the ITA is finalised.But Barshefsky said the semiconductor issue can be easily resolved and that Europe appears to be backing away from the ITA because it does not have full agreement among its members. Brittan has denied that Europe is
15047 backing away from the ITA.U.S. government and industry officials have said that some EU member states are seeking other trade concessions as a price for ending duties on information technology even though European electronic companies are willing to see tariffs dropped."There is no question that Europe is holding back on
15047 the ITA, using as an excuse the issue of semiconductors, which we think is readily resolveable, or using as an excuse the need to link ITA with other unrelated issues," Barshefsky said."It is clear there is at this point, no unanimity among the (EU) member states to move forward as
15047 aggressively as we, Canada, Japan and others are ready to move," she added.</

15048 poorest nation in the western hemisphere."A stable Caribbean is good for a stable Florida," said Gov. Lawton Chiles, flanked at a news conference by a delegation from Haiti's legislature. "It is in our best interest to promote a strong economy and democracy in Haiti."Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide,
15048 was overthrown in a bloody military coup just eight months after his 1991 inauguration and was restored to power three years later after a multinational military intervention.Florida, the closest U.S. state to Haiti, has been hit in recent years by Haiti's political and economic unrest as thousands of refugees streamed
15048 to U.S. shores."Of all the states, Florida has the most important ties to Haiti, not just refugees and immigration but also significant business interests," said Terry McCoy of the University of Florida's Centre for Latin American Studies. "It's not just Florida giving to Haiti. Florida is benefitting too."Organisers said the
15048 Florida/Haiti Initiative, using more than $250,000 in federal and state funds, is a largely volunteer effort to match U.S. groups and individuals to Haitian organisations."A strong democracy in Haiti is the best way we can protect Florida against any other massive immigration exodus," Chiles said. 15048 that."During their three-day visit, Haitian delegates will meet with business leaders, educators, health care providers and government officials to study how U.S.institutions operate.Garry Guiteau, first secretary of the Haitian Chamber of Deputies, said such exchanges are critical to the Caribbean nation, which is the region's newest democracy."The world in which
15048 we live today is very interconnected," Guiteau said through an interpreter. "Everyone has to help his neighbour. And today, more than ever, Haiti needs your help."</
15049 The United States expects to admit about 78,000 refugees in the next 12 months, most of them from Bosnia and the former Soviet Union, a senior State Department official said on Thursday.The number is about 6,000 more than in the current U.S. fiscal year that ends on Monday, but 22,000
15049 less than the previous year, Under Secretary of State Timothy Wirth told a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing. He said the figures reflected changing world conditions.Wirth said the United States had set a ceiling of 18,000 refugees from Bosnia from all ethnic groups in the next 12 months, 3,000 more than
15049 this year when only Bosnian Moslems with relatives in the United States were eligible for resettlement without U.N. referral.He said other refugee ceilings for 1997 were 30,000 from the former Soviet Union, 10,000 from Indochina, 7,000 from Africa, 4,000 from Cuba and the rest of Latin America and 4,000 from
15049 the Near East and South Asia. The other slots will be held in reserve for use as needed.Wirth said only about 100,000 of two million Bosnians who had been displaced by the war had returned to their homes. "We are committed to make the Dayton accords (which call for resettlement)
15049 work," he said.Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum told reporters at the State Department that refugees were one of the main issues discussed on Thursday by Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Bosnian leaders at a meeting in Washington."Freedom of movement and refugee return is something which has been discussed
15049 a number of times, and which everyone agrees has not been moving as fast as it should and, again, we will be giving strong support to that," Kornblum said.Wirth said 1997 would probably be the last year of large scale refugee processing in Southeast Asia, which began in 1975 after
15049 North Vietnam defeated South Vietnam.More than 1.2 million Indochinese have been admitted to the United States under a programme to help those who were U.S. allies or who were children of American soldiers.The United States admits refugees if they can show that they are likely to face persecution if they
15049 are forced to return to their home countries. The refugee programme is separate from aliens who are admitted as immigrants.Senator Alan Simpson, Republican of Wyoming, urged the administration to limit refugee admissions to those who truly needed to be resettled on a case by case basis. He said the current
15049 programme was sometimes used to make political statements.</

15051 Dow Chemical Co. said Thursday the California Court of Appeal here upheld a lower court ruling that dismisses the company from liability in 1,800 silicone breast implant lawsuits.Dow Chemical, of Midland, Mich., said the decision means that Dow has been dismissed from about 5,000 of the approximately 14,000 cases pending
15051 against it.Dow Chemical and Dow Corning Corp., a joint venture with Corning Inc., have been sued by thousands of women with silicone breast implants who allege the implants have caused medical problems such as connective tissue diseases.Dow Chemical argues that because it did not develop or manufacture breast implants, it
15051 should not be held responsible for their alleged injuries based on its half ownership of Dow Corning. Dow has acknowledged that it conducted industrial worker safety testing of some silicone compounds in the 1940s and 1950s under contract to Dow Corning.Dow Corning, at one time the world's largest maker of
15051 silicone breast implants, froze the thousands of lawsuits it is facing when it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in May 1995. It denies the claims, saying there is no medical evidence to support the allegations.In the California case, Dow Chemical and Corning originally were granted a summary judgment dismissing

15055 Doctors were given more leeway to try experimental emergency treatments on critically ill or injured patients who cannot give their informed consent under new rules announced by U.S. health officials Thursday.The Food and Drug Administration issued final rules to make it easier for people to get experimental drugs and medical
15055 devices in life-threatening emergencies. The National Institutes of Health released a companion document on emergency consent waivers."These rules address a difficult ethical situation and they apply fair, common sense tests for allowing the use of experimental treatments in life-threatening emergencies," said Secretary of Health and Human Services Donna Shalala.Such treatment
15055 would only be allowed under strictly defined conditions, when alternatives were unproven or unsatisfactory and where the research followed established rules for clinical trials.The medical and scientific community have been struggling to determine how to conduct such badly needed research without violating patients' rights to informed consent.Earlier drafts of the
15055 rules were debated and discussed extensively. The final rule will be published in the Federal Register on Oct. 2, and become effective 30 days later.</

15060 The House Thursday passed a $4.6 billion package put together by House and Senate negotiators to fund water and flood control projects such as dredging, dams and levees.The legislation for four years of projects was a compromise between the $5.1 billion House bill and a $3.6 billion Senate bill.With Congress
15060 hoping to adjourn this weekend or early next week, the Senate was expected to vote soon on the measure, and send it on to President Clinton who was expected to sign it.The bill would decrease the federal cost share of flood control projects to 65 percent from 75 percent, raising
15060 the local share and and requiring that local governments implement flood plain management plans before they become eligible for flood control projects.The bill also provided for federal and local cost-sharing to dispose of dredged material from navigation projects, giving the federal government more role in what can be a serious
15060 environmental problem.In another measure pushed by the White House, the bill authorises the administration's plan to restore the Everglades and the south Florida ecosystem.Backers called it the "greenist" water projects bill ever, with a quarter of its spending directed at restoring or improving the environment in areas including the Chesapeake
15060 Bay and the Great Lakes.Several environmental and conservation groups had opposed the bill, but largely dropped their opposition as spending was cut and changes were made during the House-Senate conference."That $3.8 billion is much lower than it was a week ago," said Scott Faber of American Rivers conservation group. That
15060 is the federal share of the bill's $4.6 total, with the remainder coming from state and local governments.Faber said two water projects remained in the bill that environmental groups opposed, but he doubted it would be enough to stop Clinton from signing it.Those measures were waiving the local cost-share of
15060 a $119 million flood control project along the Yazoo River in Mississippi, and authorising a $138 million dam on the Russell Fork of the Big Sandy River in Virginia, Faber said.Dropped from the bill was a controversial plan to release water from Upper Missouri River reservoirs to lengthen the river's
15060 navigational season, regardless of the reservoirs' water levels.</

15072 A Minnesota accounting firm has offered to calculate what municipal bond issuers may owe IRS under the Service's recent "yield burning" notice for a fee of $1,000 per issue, a letter obtained by Reuters says.Barthe &amp; Wahrman (Corrects), based in Bloomington, said in the Sept. 19 three-page letter addressed to
15072 issuers nationwide that it is offering an "independent service" to help municipal financial managers grapple with the problem."The IRS places the responsibility on you for determining whether yield burning has occurred," the firm's letter says. Municipalities would have to agree to pay Treasury the difference between the price they paid
15072 and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest on that figure, IRS said.Amy Dunbar, director of governmental affairs for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, said her group recently notified about 100 bond lawyers about the Barthe &amp; Wahrman letter via E-Mail.David Walton, a partner
15072 with Jones Hall Hill &amp; White in San Francisco and a former IRS attorney, called Barthe &amp; Wahrman "opportunists.""IRS is studying the issue. This (letter) assumes that people are going to buckle under and just send IRS a check. I think there are some serious questions on the appropriateness of
15072 the IRS standard," including use of the spot price, Walton said.Walton said the National League of Cities and other groups "need to be very vocal to IRS about putting the burden of all this enforcement on the cities.""Why should cities have to pay money to these accountants to figure out
15072 something that the IRS, if they have a concern, should be looking at" during audits of municipalities, Walton said.Barthe &amp; Wahrman said it recently examined a refunding bond issue of less than $10 million and calculated "a yield burn in excess of $100,000. Failure to comply with the Revenue Ruling
15072 could also result in the loss of the bond issue's tax exempt status," the firm added.--Vicky Stamas, 202-898-8314</

15086 A copper and bronze trail of bells, tweezers and other artifacts could transform how archaeologists look at the political and cultural powerhouses of pre-Colombian Mexico, researchers said on Thursday.Research appearing in Friday's edition of the journal Science links metal artifacts from sites as far away as Belize and the Yucatan
15086 with mines and ore deposits in western Mexico, long thought to be an ancient backwater."Western Mexico had not been considered a major player in Mesoamerican events," said Dorothy Hosler, an archaeologist and expert in ancient technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology."But these findings show that these people were interacting
15086 in an intensive and significant way with other political entities," said Hosler, who with her Florida International University co-author Andrew Macfarlane used lead isotope analysis to analyse the metal alloys in the artifacts and link them to the West Mexican mines.The archaeologists believe that their findings establish that the peoples
15086 of western Mexico, including one group known as Tarascans, were deeply involved in the complex network of trade and commerce across Mexico from around 1200 to 1521 A.D.By exporting objects that had sacred or political significance, they affected the religious and ritual behaviours of the region, not just the economy,
15086 said Hosler.She would like to turn her attention to finding the worksites or processing centres to learn more about the artisans, culture and trade.Because of their grand pyramids and architectural monuments, as well as their well-documented contacts with the Spanish conquest, the Aztecs and the Maya have been the most
15086 studied.But the Tarascans, who lived in the highlands of Michoacan "are really considered an empire. They defeated the Aztecs in various skirmishes," she said.They controlled some mining sites in Michoacan while sites in nearby Jalisco were "presumably under the control of smaller political entities," she said.Metallurgy was developed in South
15086 America and made its way to Mesoamerica, partly via a coastal maritime route, in around 600 to 700 A.D., she said. It advanced over the next 500 years or so in what is now western Mexico.Characteristic artifacts included bells, used in healing rituals, shamanistic ceremonies and to communicate with the
15086 supernatural and tweezers, particularly oversized tweezers worn as adornments by priests and other members of the elite and probably used to remove facial hair."Tweezers have a fascinating history. They were very elaborate and they became some sort of a symbol of political and social power," added Hosler, who was funded
15086 in part by mining and smelting companies in Mexico, Peru and the United States with an interest in uncovering their history.Hosler believes that her findings will encourage other archaeologists and anthropologists to take another look at the region, and to start looking for further evidence of trade routes."I think what
15086 will happen is people may start looking for these kind of analogies in other materials, like obsidian, which shows up all over Mesoamerica," she said.One question she asks is: If the westerners exported metal products, what did they import in exchange?</

15088 The Census Bureau reported Thursday that 1.6 million Americans climbed out of poverty last year and that household income was rising, news that had President Clinton and his re-election campaign crowing.The Census Bureau said that in 1995, there were 36.4 million poor people living in the United States, 1.6 million
15088 fewer than recorded in 1994. It was the second straight year of decline in the poverty level.The bureau also said that between 1994 and 1995, for the first time in six years, households in the United States experienced an annual increase in median income after adjusting for inflation.The Census report
15088 said the average household's median income rose by $888 after inflation to $34,076 in 1995. However, it noted that household income has not recovered to its 1989 pre-recession peak of $35,421 in 1995 dollars.Clinton ballyhooed the new statistics at every opportunity, talking about them at a Rose Garden bill-signing ceremony
15088 then again during a visit to Capitol Hill."It is clear that we are moving on the right track," Clinton said. "Today it is clear that more and more of our people are sharing in that prosperity."Clinton said the drop in the poverty rate was the largest one-year decline in 27
15088 years. Aides said he was referring to 1968, when the poverty level went down 2.3 million from 27.7 million in 1967.The campaign of Republican candidate Bob Dole, who has accused Clinton of pursuing policies leading to shrinking paychecks, was not convinced."These cold economic statistics may please Bill Clinton, but they
15088 do nothing to comfort a homemaker trying to buy groceries or a wage earner worried about the next paycheck," said Dole campaign spokesman Nelson Warfield.Charging that "economic anxiety is real in America today," Warfield said the Census data shows that median household income is still below the level it reached
15088 in 1989.He said earnings of full-time workers, men and women, declined so that the improvement in household income is due primarily to more members of a household working.The Census Bureau, a part of the Commerce Department, said its annual study of incomes found that incomes of white and black households
15088 rose, although Hispanic households suffered a drop and Asian and Pacific families saw no change.The Centre on Budget and Policy Priorities, a Washington think tank, said in an analysis of the Census report that the improvements in poverty and income in 1995 were substantial.But it said that while income grew
15088 for lower- and middle-income households, only the wealthiest fifth of the U.S. population has seen its average income return to pre-recession levels."The average income of each of the bottom four-fifths of the population remains below 1989 levels," the analysis said.</

15096 While many economists have been predicting interest rates will rise later this year, a few actually expect rates to remain steady or fall over the next 12 months."You can expect that minority view to become a majority view in the weeks and months ahead," said Alan Levenson, money market economist
15096 at UBS Securities Inc."This is a very different type of economic cycle," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London."Inflation is subdued and set to remain subdued, and economic growth is likely to slow to a steadier pace over the next six to 12 months. Against that background,
15096 there is no need for the Fed to tighten."That view stands in marked contrast to those that had the market predicting a 0.25 percentage point increase in short term rates earlier this week, as the Federal Reserve debated the state of the economy and the need for a change in
15096 interest rates.Low unemployment, rising wages and increasing retail sales all pointed to an accelerating economy, factors that would be expected to favour an increase in interest rates to prevent inflation, said Robert Forrestal, former Atlanta Fed president and now a partner at law firm Smith Gambrell and Russell.The Federal Reserve
15096 decided on Tuesday to hold short-term rates steady."We think the Federal Reserve is basically on vacation for at least until the middle of winter," said Vincent Malanga, an economist at LaSalle Economics in New York.Economists note that long-term rates in the bond market already have risen to about 6.90 percent
15096 from 6.03 percent in January, when the Fed last changed short-term rates, cutting them by a quarter point in a bid to spur economic growth.The Fed controls two key short-term rates but long-term bond rates fluctuate according to market forces.In addition, bank loan growth has slowed, consumer debt has swollen
15096 to record post-war levels and the stock market's early-year rally has sputtered, all of which point to slower consumer spending in the medium to long term."Consumers in the first half of the year were spending money faster than it was coming in," said Bruce Steinberg, economist at Merrill Lynch and
15096 Co. Inc. "Job growth was strong, but they managed to spend a lot faster than even the income that was generated by that job growth," he said.Consumers fuel about two-thirds of economic activity with their purchases of goods and services.Fed policy-makers were faced with conflicting evidence on the state of
15096 the economy when they met on Tuesday. By opting not to raise rates, the Fed was betting that economic growth will slow enough on its own to head off the risk of higher inflation down the road, analysts said."Greenspan started the second half of the year with a firm view
15096 that the economy was going to slow down early enough and fast enough to to head off any inflationary pressures before they really began building," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc."Now in September, with the August data and particularly the retail sales and the trade
15096 numbers, he's got some modest amount of hope that his forecast will come true," he added.Reports out Thursday also pointed to a slowing economy. Orders for costly manufactured goods tumbled in August while new applications for jobless pay surged last week, the government reported.Meanwhile, recent increases in wages will not
15096 necessarily feed a pickup in inflation, analysts said, noting companies faced with stiff global competition are hesitant to raise prices, even if labour costs are rising."The labour market is tight and wage rates are rising, but it hasn't produced any inflation yet," said Charles Lieberman, chief economist at Chase Securities
15096 Inc.If the forecasts for slower economic growth materialise, analysts said everyone from bond investors to mortgage holders could gain."More often on adjusted rates, like mortage rates on equity loans and things like that ... you would see those rates going down," Levenson said.He said he expects the Fed to cut
15096 rates in 1997."The first instalment, the first (quarter-point) cut in the funds rate, will come in the first quarter," he said.The federal funds rate, which banks charge each other for overnight loans, is 5.25 percent, and the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks for loans, is 5 percent. The
15096 Fed has held the rates steady since cutting each by a quarter point on Jan. 31.</

15108 other officials.Ortiz, testifying in the trial of alleged cartel leader Juan Garcia Abrego, said the cartel began using INS buses to ship drugs in 1986 and kept it up until 1990 when one of the INS staffers working with the drug dealers was caught.The drugs were stashed on buses used
15108 to transport illegal immigrants captured in southern Texas to Houston, 300 miles to the northeast, for flights back to their homelands, he said.The beauty of the scheme, he testified, was that the INS buses were never checked at U.S. government checkpoints inside Texas where agents searched all vehicles for drugs."They
15108 just waved (them) on," said Ortiz, who was arrested in 1993 and sentenced to 70 months in prison after agreeing to cooperate with U.S. prosecutors.He said Mexican police and other officials were easy targets for cartel bribery. 15108 but freed after payoffs, he said."They (Mexican officials) had Mr. Medrano but they let him go. They (the cartel) would pay his way out before they took him to jail," he said.Medrano finally went to jail in 1993. He died in prison of liver problems on Aug. 20, the Mexican
15108 government said.Under cross-examination by defence attorney Tony Canales, Ortiz told of paying $45,000 to a Mexico City police commander in a McDonald's restaurant in the Mexican capital."You have no faith in the police in Mexico?" Canales asked."I don't have none, sir. The police over there are bribed, corrupt -- you
15108 can buy them," Ortiz said.Garcia Abrego, a former cookie factory worker from Texas, was captured in Monterrey, Mexico in January and flown to Houston for trial. 15108 of the Gulf Cartel, which once shipped up to one-third of the cocaine consumed in the United States. His lawyers say he was not.Ortiz said he never met Garcia Abrego but was told he was the boss. The cartel hierarchy was secretive and reclusive but maintained strict discipline through the
15108 use of violence, sometimes ordering the murder of cartel members who broke the rules, he said.One of the cartel's top hit men went by the Spanish nickname of "El Amable" ("The Gent"), Ortiz said.</

15111 to see such a large reduction in rates," said Lisa Finstrom, currency analyst at Smith Barney.The dollar late Thursday rose to 1.2530 Swiss francs from 1.2415 late on Wednesday and to 1.5230 German marks from 1.5170. 15111 stood unchanged at $1.5613. 15111 level in two years, reached Wednesday, below 1000 to the mark. The selling of marks for lira also bolstered the dollar against the mark, dealers said."There was more talk about Italy doing well. That should continue to put pressure on the mark and put legs under the dollar," Grippo said.Much
15111 of the dollar's rally occurred in Asian and European trading. 15111 to a session high against the yen.Meanwhile, influential economist Fred Bergsten, director of the Institute for International Economics, told reporters in Washington that Japanese officials were seeking to weaken the yen to lower the cost of Japanese exports."The dollar has to play some catch-up against the yen," said Grippo. 15122 Federal health experts said Thursday there were unusual outbreaks of influenza in Alaska and Washington state this summer, which might signal an early beginning to the flu season.The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said summer outbreaks such as those that occurred in the two states in June and
15122 July "are not common.""It can be a potential warning that the season is going to come earlier, but it's not an exact science," said the CDC's Dr. Keiji Fukuda.The CDC said the same three flu strains that prevailed last year were expected this winter and this year's vaccine should protect
15122 most people from the disease. "In this year's vaccine formulation ... there appears to be a good match," Fukuda said.Flu vaccination is recommended for people aged 65 or older and residents of nursing homes or other chronic care facilities. It is also urged for adults and children with chronic pulmonary
15122 or cardiovascular disorders, including children with asthma.Health officials said people who have suffered chronic metabolic diseases, renal dysfunction, haemoglobinopathies or immunosuppression in the past year should also get a shot. 15122 should be vaccinated as well, the CDC said.</

15129 U.S. rail freight volume as measured in intermodal traffic stood at 169,093 trailers and containers in the week ended September 21, the highest level in 51 weeks, a railroad group said Thursday in a statement.The Association of American Railroads said the last time intermodal traffic was higher was when it
15129 totalled 171,285 trailers and containers in the week ended September 30, 1995.AAR also said that intermodal traffic in the September 21 week was up 3.7 percent from 163,044 trailers and containers in the year-ago week. AAR said total carloads, which do not include intermodal, were 357,286, down one percent from
15129 360,768 in the same 1995 week.Ton-miles also fell 0.4 percent to 26.5 billion in the week from 26.6 billion last year. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile."The continued softness in grain loadings was the major story again this week," AAR chief economist Harvey Levine said. Grain
15129 was down 32.1 percent to 18,931 carloads from 27,896 in the year-ago week. AAR said other big declines were in food and kindred products, which fell 10.5 percent to 8,366 carloads from 9,346 last year, and coke, which fell 10.7 percent to 5,426 carloads from 6,073.Primary forest products also fell
15129 8.1 percent to 7,704 carloads from 8,385 last year, while grain mill products totalled 8,866, down 6.5 percent from 9,483 in the year-ago week, AAR said.Lumber and wood products fell 0.5 percent to 5,496 carloads from 5,526 last year, AAR said.The biggest increases were in petroleum products, which rose nine
15129 percent to 5,877 carloads from 5,394 in the year-ago week, and metals and metal products, which rose 6.3 percent to 13,496 carloads from 12,701.Coal loadings also increased five percent to 141,181 from 134,477 last year. Motor vehicles and equipment carloads were 22,129, also up five percent from 21,076 last year,
15129 AAR said.In the first 38 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose two percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 0.7 percent, but carloads fell 0.9 percent, AAR said.</

15143 The Pentagon said on Thursday it did not tell U.S. troops in the 1991 Gulf War that an anti-nerve gas drug they took was experimental because it did not want Iraq to learn of U.S. defences."I believe there was a conscious decision made at the time not to tell the
15143 troops," a spokesman, Captain Michael Doubleday said. The drug was pyridostogmine
15143 bromide and investigators are studying whether its use in combination with insecticides or other chemicals U.S. troops were exposed to might be a cause for illnesses veterans have suffered since the war."In retrospect had circumstances been otherwise we probably would have proceded differently," Doubleday said.But he said the Defence Department
15143 believed then and believes now that the drug is safe and would have been an effective defence if Iraq had launched nerve gas against coalition forces.He said a large study found that fewer than one-tenth of one percent of the troops suffered side effects such as nausea and cramps that
15143 would have caused them to be taken off the drug.</

15145 Francisco-based company said that analysis was continuing.Meanwhile, a provision in recently passed healthcare legislation would allow payment to patients expected to die within two years to be tax exempt. Chodes said he expects this to help expand use of viatical settlements to people other than AIDS patients. He noted that
15145 cancer accounts for a far greater percentage of deaths in the United States than HIV infection."There isn't any particular reason why a cancer patient wouldn't be as good if not better candidate for" a viatical settlement, he said.Viaticus estimates that, on an industry-wide basis, about $800 million in policies will
15145 be purchased through viatical settlement in 1996. That will jump to over $1 billion by 1998, it said. "With this tax bill, that rate is going to rapidly increase," he said, adding that Viaticus, which buys close to a third of the $500 million in policies it considers, will grow
15145 with that business."We'll be a significant percentage of that number and the largest participant, we believe," Chodes said.Viaticus pays 60 to 85 percent of the face value of a policy to a terminally ill person, maintains the premium on the policy, then collects the full value when the person dies.
15145 When Viaticus does not buy a policy, it is usually because the policyholder chooses to sell to another company or to not take a settlement at all, a spokesman said.While 50 percent of Viaticus' business currently comes from AIDS patients, Chodes expects that to drop to 25 percent next year.The
15145 company is growing its business through education campaigns with social workers, estate planners and others involved with finances of terminally ill patients. Viaticus is also marketing viatical settlement as an employee benefit to corporate benefits managers.--Reuters Chicago newsdesk, 312-408-8787</

15148 the ADT monitoring center can track a vehicle's movements, remotely unlock doors, roll down windows or disable the car. 15148 the system is engaged.Ruzika declined to disclose the company's financial projections for CARCOP, but indicated labor costs for the new system will not be significant because vehicles installed with the CARCOP system will be monitored at ADT's existing control centers. 15149 Prosecutors in the Oklahoma City bombing case want only one trial for the two defendants, saying Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols were alleged to be co-conspirators and should be tried together, court records showed on Thursday."The deadly results of this conspiracy, as well as all the crime scene and forensic
15149 evidence, are admissible against both defendants," prosecutors wrote in a filing with the court on Wednesday that was made public Thursday.McVeigh and Nichols, charged in the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that claimed the lives of 168 people and injured hundreds more, both want
15149 separate trials.Defence teams argued the strategy for the two defendants will be "antagonistic" and that defendants risk "spillover guilt" if put on trial together.Next week U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch will hold a key pre-trial hearing on the defence motion for severance.Prosecutors are anxious to try both defendants together,
15149 saying one trial would present a fuller picture of the bombing and spare what they called unnecessary suffering by the victims' and relatives of those killed.The date for the Denver trial was not set, but was expected either late this year or early next.Prosecutors said a single trial allows the
15149 case to be presented to jurors in its entirety. "While McVeigh actually delivered the bomb to the Murrah Building ... Nichols is charged both as a principal and as an aider and abetter of McVeigh," lawyers for the government said.McVeigh's team was also concerned about statements Nichols made when he
15149 was questioned two days after the bombing, but prosecutors said the statements added little to what they called a "powerful case" against McVeigh.Prosecutors also argued that case law did not establish a defendant's right to a separate trial because an "antagonistic" defence might result in each defendant pointing a finger
15149 of guilt at the other.The Department of Justice lawyers also said that a defendant may be protected from any "spillover" prejudice by a proper instruction to jurors.Statements by McVeigh about the conspiracy to commit the bombing should apply to Nichols because prosecutors will show that Nichols never withdrew from the
15149 conspiracy, government lawyers said.Prosecutors also dismissed as unnecessary Nichols' lawyers' request that two juries be impaneled if one trial is held, but they said such a move would be preferable to holding two separate trials.</

15153 following a speech to a business group. She said she will discuss the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) late Thursday with European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan. 15153 not be able to move forward on this initiative ... without Europe because we will not let Europe free-ride on our tariff reductions."Brittan and Barshefsky are in Seattle for a quadrilateral trade ministers meeting Friday and Saturday that will also include Canada's Arthur Eggleton and Japan's Shunpei Tsukahara. 15159 Swimming against Wall Street's tighter credit tide, a growing minority of economists expects U.S. interest rates to remain steady or actually drop over the next 12 months."You can expect that minority view to become a majority view in the weeks and months ahead," said Alan Levenson, money market economist at
15159 UBS Securities Inc.Alan Greenspan's virtues. The sentiment, bolstered by the Federal Reserve's decision to keep monetary policy unchanged earlier this week, stems from the notion that the economy is cooling without the help of further central bank action."We think the Federal Reserve is basically on vacation for at least until
15159 the middle of winter," said Vincent Malanga, an economist at LaSalle Economics in New York.Several aspects of the current economic cycle, mainly in the consumer and banking sectors, support the view that the economy may slow without Fed intervention. Financial conditions remain mostly on the restrictive side. Long-term interest rates,
15159 for example, have risen already to 6.88 percent from 6.03 percent in January, when the Fed last cut interest rates.Thus, analysts said that a slowdown in bank loan growth, tighter lending standards and a more gradual pace of wealth creation in the equity market are all tightening financial conditions.Also, consumer
15159 debt has swollen to post-war record levels, a phenomena that has cast a shadow on forecasts about the behavior of spending in the medium to long term. "Consumers in the first half of the year were spending money faster than it was coming in," said Bruce Steinberg, economist and manager
15159 of macroanalysis at Merrill Lynch and Co Inc. "Job growth was strong, but they managed to spend a lot faster than even the income that was generated by that job growth," he added.If higher debt is any indication of caution for future spending, analysts said consumers should think twice before
15159 reaching into their pockets in the months ahead.The consumer sector accounts for around two-thirds of the nation's Gross Domestic Product. Analysts said though that taking such an approach on the economy requires some confidence and a lot of patience. But being as it is, patience appears to be one of
15159 Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's virtues."Greenspan started the second half of the year with a firm view that the economy was going to slow down early enough and fast enough to head off any inflationary pressures before they really began building," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy
15159 Securities Inc. "Now in September, with the August data and particularly the retail sales and the trade numbers, he's got some modest amount of hope that his forecast will come true," he added.The lack of hard evidence that slight increases in wages seen recently will inevitably trigger inflation is another
15159 reason prompting the Fed to remain on hold, analysts said."The labor market is tight and wage rates are rising, but it hasn't produced any inflation yet," said Charles Lieberman, chief economist at Chase Securities Inc. If the forecasts for slower economic growth materialize, analysts said that just about everyone, from
15159 bond investors to mortgage holders, could gain."More often on adjusted rates, like mortage rates on equity loans and things like that ... you would see those rates going down," Levenson said.The UBS economist, an aggressive defender of lower rates, said he expects the Federal Reserve to cut the federal funds
15159 rate -- currently at 5.25 percent -- by 75 basis points over the balance of 1997."The first installment, the first 25-basis-point cut in the funds rate, will come in the first quarter," he said.The federal funds rate is the overnight rate banks charge each other for overnight loans.-- 212-859-1676</

15179 had sought more prison time plus fines, contending that the punishment they received was too light and that Koon had profited from his notoriety "to the tune of close to $10 million.""We're satisfied," Koon's attorney, Ira Salzman, said outside court. 15179 effort to impose further punishment.Koon, Powell and two other officers were acquitted of the beatings in state court in April 1992, touching off three days of rioting in Los Angeles that left 54 people dead and more than $1 billion in damage.Koon and Powell were later convicted in a federal
15179 trial, while former officers Timothy Wind and Theodore Briseno were found not guilty.Under federal sentencing rules, Koon and Powell faced a potential sentence of 70 to 87 months, but Davies departed from the guidelines and imposed 30-month prison terms.Black community leaders denounced the sentence as far too lenient for the
15179 defendants' roles in the videotaped attack, which was shown repeatedly on national television and sparked outrage against police brutality.Davies at the time cited several factors in justifying his "downward departures" from the sentencing guidelines, including his view that King had resisted arrest and was partly responsible for his own beating.Davies
15179 also said the officers were susceptible to abuse by others inmates in prison, that they had been subjected to state and federal prosecutions and that they had lost their jobs and livelihood.Acting on a request from prosecutors, a federal appeals court ruled that Davies should not have departed from the
15179 guidelines and, by implication, that the two should have drawn longer sentences. But the Supreme Court disagreed, ruling that most of the reasons Davies used to impose shorter prison terms were legally sound.In a final effort to change the judge's mind, Middleton said Thursday that the men should at least
15179 be fined. He contended that Koon had earned millions of dollars from sales of his book and contributions to a legal fund used to pay for his defence in three trials.King, who won $3.8 million in damages from the city of Los Angeles and has continued having regular run-ins with
15179 the police, was not in court Thursday. But Koon and Powell sat behind their attorneys, showing no emotion when the judge announced his decision.</

15192 the hazardous components and reduces and stabilizes the radionuclides.Hanford is one of several storage sites for radioactive nuclear waste produced during the arms race between the United States and the former Soviet Union. Highly radioactive waste has been stored in large underground tanks since 1944.Molten Metal said about 56 million
15192 gallons of waste are stored in 177 tanks. These caustic wastes are in the form of liquids, slurries, saltcakes, and sludges.The Tank Waste Remediation System Program was established in 1991 to manage treatment and disposal of these wastes in a safe, cost-effective, and environmentally sound manner.Molten Metal noted complete cleanup
15192 of the Hanford Tanks could require 30 years and cost as much as $30 billion.In addition to Hanford, similar wastes are stored at four other sites in the U.S. -- the Savannah River site in South Carolina; the Idaho National Engineering Laboratory; a site in West Valley, N.Y,; and a
15192 site in Oak Ridge, Tenn. Many other similar sites exist around the world.-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710</

15195 the plans in 1995, up from 80 percent in 1994.One sign that people are looking more long-term in their 401(K) investments is the fact that 59 percent of the account balances of those surveyed were in equity funds, compared with 45 percent in 1990, Wray said."It's really clear that the

15211 Orders for costly manufactured goods plunged in August while new applications for jobless pay surged last week, the government reported on Thursday, in fresh signs of a slowing economy.The Commerce Department said new orders for durable goods fell a surprisingly steep 3.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $167 billion last
15211 month.It was the biggest monthly drop in demand for expensive and long-lasting products like new cars, computers and appliances since a 3.4 percent plunge in April l995 and followed a downward revised 1.4 percent rise in July.Separately, the Labour Department said the number of people filing their first claims for
15211 jobless pay jumped by 11,000 last week to 340,000. The surge was unexpected since analysts had predicted that tight labour markets meant hiring was so brisk that fewer people needed unemployment benefits.The reports were seen as a sign the industrial sector was having difficulty holding onto recent gains, as well
15211 as confirmation that the Federal Reserve correctly assessed the economy as slowing on its own when it decided not to raise interest rates this week."It clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum, and that growth in the third quarter is going to come in only a fraction of what
15211 it was in the second quarter, and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day," said Irwin Keller, chief economist at Chase Regional Bank in New York.The news bolstered a downward trend in interest rates as the inflation-sensitive 30-year Treasury bond jumped
15211 17/32, or $5.31 per $1,000 face value, and its yield fell to 6.89 percent from 6.93 percent on Wednesday.Previously, the department said July durables orders had risen by 1.7 percent, but it revised that gain downward.The only type of manufactured goods for which orders increased last month was defence goods,
15211 which rose 9 percent to $5.2 billion after a 40.9 percent fall in July.Excluding defence, durables orders were down even more sharply, by 3.5 percent in August, the largest decrease since a 3.6 percent fall more than two years ago, in July 1993. The decline followed a 3.5 percent rise
15211 in July.The national economy expanded at a 4.8 percent annual rate during the second quarter, its strongest growth in two years, which contributed to fears that pressure on wages were rising.But Federal Reserve policy-makers who met Tuesday evidently foresaw the economy slowing enough in the second half to thwart inflationary
15211 risks when they decided to keep interest rates steady.Robert Dederick, economic consultant to Northern Trust Co. in Chicago, said the weakening durable goods orders "certainly makes the Fed decision look reasonable." He stressed there was no indication of a precipitous fall in manufacturing.Weak foreign economies are providing a soft market
15211 for U.S.-made goods and consumers have curbed their retail buying, but both could bounce back, Dederick said."We're moving higher on a trend basis but at a moderate pace as export demand is restrained and there's a reluctance to build inventories voluntarily," he added, noting that retail sales virtually stalled in
15211 July and August.The biggest single drop in durables orders during August was for transportation goods, which fell 7.9 percent to $37.9 billion, a third straight monthly decrease after drops of 1.6 percent in July and 1.3 percent in June.Weaker demand for new commercial aircraft and parts accounted for more than
15211 half the falloff in transportation goods. 15211 for electronic equipment fell 5.6 percent to $26.5 billion last month after gaining 4.9 percent in July.Non-defence capital goods orders, an indicator of businesses' investment in new equipment, plummeted 10.1 percent in August after a 7.2 percent rise in July.Shipments of durable goods, which measure current demand in manufacturing industries,
15211 rose 0.3 percent in August to $168.2 billion after a 0.5 percent increase in July.</

15214 abortion, technically called intact dilation and evacuation, is sometimes used in second and third trimester abortions. 15214 to ban a specific abortion technique. 15214 the bill if elected. 15214 told by their doctors the procedure was their safest option.They charged the bill would endanger women and was a first step toward making all abortions illegal."How could we ever know more than a physican?" said California Democrat Barbara Boxer, who spoke next to a large photograph of a woman who
15214 underwent the procedure."For anyone who thinks this is not in the political arena, why zid it take five months (from the veto) to bring this override here, in the last week of the session?" she said.The bill has a narrow exception allowing the procedure to save a woman's life. In
15214 vetoing the bill, Clinton said he had concerns about the procedure but could not sign it because it did not include constitutional protections for health.Opponents displayed large black-and-white drawings depicting the procedure, which they compared to infanticide."Sometimes party loyalty does demand too much and this is one of these times,"
15214 said Lott, calling on Democrats to break with the president. 15231 More than a dozen research teams are seeking pieces of a meteorite to look for evidence that primitive, single-cell organisms existed billions of years ago on Mars, a NASA scientist said.A space agency advisory panel will begin on Friday to consider about 15 requests for slices of the Martian meteorite
15231 as scientists around the world seek to shed more light on one of the great mysteries of our universe -- the possible existence of life on Mars."We are getting requests to do a variety of studies that are aimed at confirming, or perhaps denying, the results that have already been
15231 published," Marilyn Lindstrom, a curator with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, said in a recent interview.A consortium of NASA and university scientists announced in August it had discovered microfossil remains in a meteorite known as ALH84001. Blasted away from the surface of Mars by the impact of an asteroid
15231 about 16 million years ago, the meteorite carried to Earth evidence of organic, carbon-based molecules -- the building blocks of life on Earth.Researchers have proposed several strategies for testing the findings of the NASA consortium, including studies of the cell walls of microfossils found in the meteorite, of the age
15231 of carbonates in the rock and of different types of organic compounds like amino acids that would confirm the existence of life.NASA and the National Science Foundation are considering jointly funding some of the research into the Martian meteorite, and Lindstrom said she expects she will eventually field about 50
15231 requests for pieces of the rock. Details of the research proposals to be considered in the weekend meeting were not released.Even before the NASA consortium published its theory in Science magazine, some 30 slices and 100 chips of the meteorite were in the hands of researchers. NASA has a dozen
15231 confirmed Martian meteorites in its collection, but the one found in the Allen Fields of Antarctica in 1984 was considered the best prospect for yielding clues to life on the Red Planet."This is the one that's very old, the one with the best likelihood of life," said Lindstrom, curator of
15231 the space agency's Martian asteroid collection, housed at the Johnson Space Centre in Houston.In the ALH84001 meteorite, which weighs about 4 pounds 3 ounces (1.9 kg), carbonates are present in less than 1 percent of the rock, and possible organic matter is found in less than 10 percent of the
15231 orange carbonate deposits, she said.While researchers study slivers carved from the meteorite for evidence of life on Mars, a separate piece of the rock is being put to more Earthly uses. A large chunk was promised to the Smithsonian Institution for a public display, and is periodically brought to Capitol
15231 Hill for private exhibits in Congress, which sets NASA's research budget.</

15246 Federal prosecutors have subpoenaed documents in connection with insolvent Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co's (EMLICO) move last year to Bermuda, a person familiar with the situation said.The U.S. attorney's office in Boston last week delivered a subpoena to an EMLICO reinsurer demanding information about EMLICO's redomestication, the source said.The U.S.
15246 attorney's office in Boston declined to comment. The subpoena specifically seeks copies of a 1994 memo prepared by the London law firm Clifford Chance &amp; Co and documents prepared by Chadbourne &amp; Parke, outside counsel for EMLICO, General Electric Co's liability insurer, the source said.The Clifford Chance memo was reported
15246 in the trade press to discuss the advantages of a move to Bermuda and the Chadbourne &amp; Parke documents include a flow chart showing what would happen if EMLICO liquidated in Massachusetts, the source said. Kemper Insurance Co unit Kemper Reinsurance Co, which was served with the subpoena, last week
15246 filed a motion with the Massachusetts Appeals Court for permission to comply with the subpoena. Those documents had been placed under a seal earlier in the year.When asked about the subpoena, a General Electric spokesman said the company does not comment on investigations.Meanwhile, EMLICO's reinsurers have asked the Massachusetts division
15246 of insurance to reconsider its decision in July not to reopen proceedings that allowed EMLICO to relocate. The insurance division said it was reviewing public comment on the issue, but had not yet decided whether or not to reconsider its earlier decision.EMLICO's reinsurers, including Kemper Reinsurance, General Re Corp, Allstate
15246 Corp and Lloyd's of London, contend that EMLICO deliberately misled Massachusetts insurance regulators about its solvency, allowing it to move to Bermuda to take advantage of the island's creditor-friendly regulations. 15246 to pay under Massachusetts law.But General Electric, EMLICO's sole creditor, has contended those allegations were made by reinsurers in an attempt to avoid their contractual responsibilities.EMLICO won permission to relocate to Bermuda after a short hearing in June 1995. By October, EMLICO had filed for insolvency with about a $500
15246 million surplus shortfall. 15246 have had against the insolvency funds.In another related action, Kemper Reinsurance is scheduled to go before a Bermuda judge for a two week hearing, beginning on October 8, to seek permission to have the court reconsider Bermuda's approval of EMLICO's redomestication.The redomestication was approved by Bermuda's minister of finance and
15246 registrar of companies. Kemper has asked that the court reconsider those approvals, but the request came after a deadline for such actions had passed.A Bermuda judge in late July ruled that EMLICO could proceed with its liquidation.-- 212-859-1716</

15250 International Business Machines Corp. unveiled Thursday a new line of personal computers that breaks new ground in turning PCs into networked home appliances that fit conveniently in any room of a house.IBM said it has redesigned its new Aptiva "S Series" so a user has easy access to key features
15250 -- the keyboard, floppy drive, compact disc player and monitor -- while the PC's main box can be stowed away under a desk, or perhaps a closet.The PC systems take a number of their architectural cues from the tradition of slick, modular consumer electronics.The new Aptiva machines are charcoal gray
15250 and have modular components that owe much of their inspiration to home stereo or television/videocasette player systems.IBM said the "S Series" will come in four basic models running either Pentium 166 or 200 megahertz chips and have up to 3.2 gigabytes of storage capacity, the latest CD-ROM drives, modems and
15250 a variety of multimedia features.The basic Aptiva models range in price from $2,499 to $3,099, excluding monitors, which run another $499 to $799, the prices of a 15-inch or 17-inch screen, respectively. The line is available immediately from retailers."It's as close to a grand slam as IBM has ever hit
15250 in the consumer market," said PC industry analyst Richard Zwetchkenbaum of International Data Corp., a Framingham, Mass.-based market research firm.Emily Green, a Forrester Research analyst, said that while the machines offer several promising new features, their premium pricing -- complete systems start at around $3,000 -- are likely to keep
15250 them out of reach of first-time PC buyers.She noted that the entry of Sony Corp. and several other Japanese consumer electronic giants into the U.S. home PC market is behind the drive by IBM and other established PC makers to make the latest home PCs more consumer-oriented.Jose Garcia, general manager
15250 of IBM's consumer desktop unit, said, "The Aptiva split system creates a better fit between consumers and their home computers by directly addressing their distinct usage, space and styling requirements."But while these "split system" machines mark a significant departure from the clunky, all-in-one, beige boxes that dominate corporate offices, IBM's
15250 new home PC line borrows an insight from corporate personal computer systems.By separating the central processing unit from the essential user controls, IBM said it was paving the way for creating home computer networks similar in key respects to the local area networks that now dominate office PC systems.The new
15250 Aptivas reflect IBM's vision of extending home computers by locating "access stations" in rooms throughout the house that serve a variety of specialised functions, in effect turning the home into a computer local area network.These smaller computing units would be linked to a powerful server, or central processing machine, that
15250 could deliver entertainment or video games to the living room or housekeeping and business tools to the study.A home's lighting, heating, telephone and Internet communications, security and even lawn sprinkler systems could be managed in this way, according to IBM officials.Eventually such systems could act as a bridge from the
15250 home to cable, phone and utility companies.Besides the stand-alone media console that houses the CD-ROM and floppy disk drives and power controls, the new Aptivas offer several other innovative features.Its RingCentral software turns the PC into a telephone, answering machine, fax and e-mail system, allowing a user to call home
15250 and ask the PC to read back electronic mail messages, using unique IBM voice translation technology.The software also includes a caller identification feature that allows the user to record specific messages for different callers. A call placed from the phone number of one's mother would trigger a message for her
15250 only, for example.IBM stock was up 87.5 cents at $127.375 in early trading Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange.</

15255 With an eye on new markets, Medtronic Inc is developing a low-cost pacemaker exclusively for sale in China, India and other developing Asian nations.The simple, inexpensive Champion model is set for release in February or March next year, said Steve Harrison, a marketing manager on the project, in an interview
15255 Wednesday.The Champion will sell for less than the current average Chinese pacemaker price of about $1,200, he said.The units will be made at a $10-million factory and office complex Medtronic is constructing in Shanghai. The complex will be the first wholly foreign-owned pacemaker plant in China and represents a modest,
15255 but potentially lucrative wager on Asian growth, analysts said."Emerging markets like China, India and similar countries in that part of the world have sizable populations that represent important new growth opportunities for companies like Medtronic," said Cowen &amp; Co analyst Michael Mullen."Most companies in the medical technology industry have been
15255 looking for ways to legitimize moves into these markets because the big issue is how you get paid," Mullen said. Only a fifth of China's population has healthcare coverage of any sort. But since the Chinese population is 1.2 billion, that small fraction represents a huge market, Mullen said."There is
15255 a sizable middle and upper class that exists now in China and is growing rapidly, and also in India and these other countries," he said.Although common in the Western world and Japan for treating slow or irregular heartbeats, pacemakers remain a rarity in developing countries, Medtronic said.In the United States,
15255 where a pacemaker costs about $6,000, about 550 people per million have a pacemaker implant. In Hong Kong, the rate is 200 per million, Harrison said.In China, with a population of 1.2 billion, there are only three to four pacemaker implants per million. Implant rates in India and other Asian
15255 nations are also low.The total Chinese pacemaker market today is about 4,500 units per year and Minneapolis-based Medtronic has about 30 percent of it, Harrison said.Competition from St. Jude Medical Inc and others is intense, he said, and some local competitors are emerging. But he added that Medtronic is not
15255 aware of any rival developing a market-specific product like the Champion.Medtronic holds 51 percent of the $2.4-billion global pacemaker market. Its shares were up 7/8 to 62-5/8.</
15256 Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc and Roche Holding Ltd's Hoffmann-La Roche Inc on Thursday said they initiated human clinical trials of an anti-cancer MMP inhibitor designated AG3340.The companies said in phase I clinical studies to be conducted at Inveresk Research in Edinburgh, Scotland, the safety and pharmacokinetic parameters of single and multiple
15256 oral doses of AG3340 will be evaluated in healthy volunteers in order to determine an optimal dose and schedule for administration of the drug in subsequent efficacy studies. AG3340 is a small, synthetic molecule designed to selectively inactivate certain members of a family of enzymes known as matrix metalloproteases (MMPs).In
15256 preclinical studies, AG3340 demonstrated significant anti-tumor and anti-metastatic activity against several murine and human tumors growing in laboratory animals, the companies said . In these studies, AG3340 proved active when administered either orally or intraperitoneally. A full panel of preclinical toxicology studies showed AG3340 to be well tolerated and acceptable
15256 for human clinical testing.Under terms of the collaboration, Roche will bear 80 percent of the development costs of AG3340 and will lead commercialization of the drug outside of North America subject to payment of royalties to Agouron. Roche and Agouron will co-promote AG3340 in North America and will share equally
15256 in profits derived from North American sales of the drug.</

15277 64 percent in New Jersey.It was the same story in a Reuters poll of Illinois, Michigan and Ohio taken last week. 15277 a small but critical segment of Republican voters.In two dozen follow-up interviews with voters, the magnitude of Dole's problem became clear. 15277 said Mary Espinosa, a teacher's aide for handicapped children in Rahway, New Jersey, who voted for then-President George Bush in 1992 and for Republican Gov. 15303 Medical insurer Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield, responding to mounting competition in the healthcare industry, said on Thursday that it would seek approval from New York state regulators to convert itself into a for-profit organisation.The proposal -- which also calls for creation of a charitable foundation to fill the
15303 company's traditional role of providing health care for uninsured and poor people -- must be approved by a state court, the state Department of Insurance and the state Attorney General's Office.Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield, one of the biggest insurers of last resort in the United States, said its
15303 board had approved the proposal and would hold public hearings on the matter."Given current market conditions, we believe we have no choice but to take this step," Dr. Michael Stocker, the company's president and chief executive, said in a statement."This plan serves our mission to provide charitable services and ensures
15303 our growth in this new competitive marketplace."If approved, the proposed conversion would give the company entry to public capital markets and allow it to compete against for-profit healthcare insurers and managed-care organisations, the company said."Health plans need large amounts of capital to acquire the latest technology and form partnerships with
15303 top-flight doctors and hospitals," Empire said in announcing its proposal.About a half dozen Blue Cross firms in other states have already converted either partly or completely into for-profit companies.The 60-year-old New York company said its proposal "avoids many of the pitfalls experienced by other Blue Cross and Blue Shield plans."
15303 Among them were disputes over control of the new companies and compensation for top executives.Under its plan, Empire would transfer its assets, liabilities and business to its existing for-profit subsidiaries.The organisation would then convert to a nonprofit foundation or create a new foundation that would own 100 percent of the
15303 stock of the for-profit subsidiary.The foundation would sell some of the for-profit subsidiary's stock to the public, Empire said.Over five years, the foundation would sell at least 95 percent of the for-profit subsidiary's equity and use the cash for charitable purposes.Empire said the nonprofit foundation would have its own directors
15303 and operate under a new name."The independent for-profit company would carry on business under the Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield name and conduct a second public offering of stock at some point in the future to raise funds in the capital market," Empire said.No managers or directors would benefit
15303 financially from the transactions, it added.Empire said final details of the proposal have yet to be fixed, pending public hearings and consultations with state regulators. Some terms of the plan must also be approved by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Empire said.</

15305 the parent and the child," Clinton said of the measure, which grew from complaints about health care plans that forced new mothers to leave the hospital as soon as 10 hours after a normal delivery. The "Newborns' and Mothers' Protection Act" was tied to a $64.4 billion government money bill
15305 that also improves health benefits for mental patients and children with spina bifida born to Vietnam veterans.It was approved by a Republican-controlled Congress that is increasingly putting its own interests above those of the party's trouble-plagued presidential candidate Bob Dole. 15306 Proler International Corp. said Thursday it has begun litigation against Hugo Neu Corp., its joint venture partner in the scrap metals business, for trying to block the company's proposed merger with Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc.Separately, Hugo Neu said it obtained a temporary restraining order in New York State Supreme Court
15306 on Tuesday prohibiting Proler from disclosing confidential business information to Schnitzer.Houston-based Proler, which recycles scrap metals and industrial wastes to produce commercial products, agreed earlier this month to be acquired by Schnitzer for $7.50 a share, or about $35 million.At the time, Proler said it had rejected an offer from
15306 Hugo Neu to buy its interests in the companies' three scrap metals joint ventures.Proler said it initiated litigation in Harris County, Texas, after learning of Hugo Neu's temporary restraining order, which it said appears to undermine its merger agreement with Schnitzer.Proler is seeking compensatory and punitive damages for any resulting
15306 losses that may be incurred by the company and its stockholders.Hugo Neu said it considers Schnitzer a competitor of its scrap metal business with Proler and that a hearing has been scheduled for Oct. 2 to look at its request for an injunction.Proler's stock fell 12.5 cents to $7.25 on
