15307 By Nicholas Doughty, Diplomatic CorrespondentThe European Union and Islamic nations criticised Israel on Thursday over the erupting Israeli-Palestinian crisis, telling the Jewish state it must prove its commitment to Middle East peace.Their comments, on the margins of the annual U.N. General Assembly in New York, came as U.N. Secretary-General Boutros
15307 Boutros-Ghali appealed for calm and the Security Council met to discuss what could be done to stop the killing.Israeli troops killed 39 Palestinians and Palestinian forces shot to death 11 Israelis in running battles on Thursday, the bloodiest day in the West Bank and Gaza since Yasser Arafat set up
15307 his self-rule government.Israel declared a state of emergency.Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who speaks for the 15-nation European Union as his country currently holds the EU presidency, said he had conveyed to Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy "our deepest concern in relation to the lack of momentum in the peace
15307 process.""We emphasised very strongly and affirmatively the concern of the European Union that it was necessary for Israel to show ... a renewed commitment to the process. ... Signals need to be given by the Israeli government," he said.British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said the deterioration in Middle East peace
15307 efforts was "very worrying," and German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said he had appealed to both sides for calm.Spring said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should maintain contacts with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to show the world that Israel would honour peace agreements reached by the previous Labour government."It is
15307 necessary for Israel to give a signal, to take action that will demonstrate ... that Israel remains committed to peace," Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said."The disturbing fact ... is that in the Arab countries in the region the credibility of the Israeli government is being questioned and its commitment
15307 to peace, and that I think is dangerous and should not be allowed to continue."Arab anger at Netanyahu's failure to extend self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza boiled over after his Likud government opened a tunnel near the al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock mosques."Matters like that should be
15307 avoided in a situation which is particularly tense and fragile. ... Great care should be taken in terms of any action that could cause incidents and loss of life," Ireland's Spring said.Boutros-Ghali took a similar line in urging restraint.In a statement, the U.N. secretary-general called on both sides to end
15307 the violence and to "resume in earnest negotiations that will lead to full implementation of the agreements already reached."Islamic nations also met to discuss the crisis and issued a statement afterwards criticising Israel, calling on it to honour previous agreements and calling the opening of the tunnel "an illegal act.""The
15307 hesitations of the Israeli government ... are paralysing (peace) efforts," Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), told the meeting. "To question the agreements undertaken ... would be a dangerous precedent."Farouk Kaddoumi, foreign affairs spokesman for the Palestinians, told the OIC meeting that Israel
15307 had abandoned the principle of "land for peace" in negotiations."The situation is deteriorating," he said."This is an inevitable outcome of the policy pursued by Israel."</
15308 Sket GmbH, the former East Germany's biggest heavy machinery group, said Thursday it would undergo massive restructuring and shed nearly a third of its work force.Managing director Werner Kirchgaesser told reporters that it was necessary to spin off Sket's steel rolling mills, cable and wire plants and oil divisions into
15308 separate companies.Kirchgaesser, formerly head of Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, was speaking after a meeting of the money-losing machinery maker's supervisory board.Breaking up the company into independent parts would lead to the loss of 600 jobs from a work force of 1,850.Management said the restructuring plan could bring the company back into profitability
15308 by the end of 1998. It expects a loss of around 190 million marks ($125 million) this year.The supervisory board will make a final decision about the restructuring on Oct. 14.</
15309 Foreign ministers of major powers said on Thursday that U.N. sanctions against rump Yugoslavia would shortly be lifted, following elections earlier this month in Bosnia.They were speaking after the United States, key European allies and Russia met to discuss how to shore up peace in Bosnia following the vote to
15309 elect joint institutions to run the multi-ethnic state foreseen in last year's Dayton peace accord.A statement on the meeting said the ministers in the so- called Contact Group "looked forward to early certification of the Sept. 14 Bosnian elections and to the lifting of sanctions by the U.N. Security Council
15309 soon thereafter.""I think there was agreement right round the table that the conditions laid down in Dayton have been broadly satisfied and that it's appropriate for the sanctions to be lifted pretty soon," British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said."I think it's days we're talking about, not weeks," Rifkind told reporters.
15309 U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum said he expected Security Council action to begin next week.The United Nations imposed the sanctions in 1992 because of Serbia's role in fomenting the Bosnian war. They were suspended after the Dayton agreement but have yet to be finally lifted.Ministers of Contact Group
15309 nations -- the United States, Russia, Britain, France and Germany -- met at the U.S. Mission to the United Nations, on the margins of the U.N. General Assembly in New York.Later, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher met successively with Bosnia's Moslem President Alija Izetbegovic, Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic
15309 and Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic.The Security Council cannot lift the sanctions until the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which supervised the elections, has certified that they met the standards laid down by Dayton.But Robert Frowick, head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, told the meeting he
15309 expected to do this within 48 hours.The statement called on Bosnia's Moslem, Serb and Croat factions to redouble efforts to create a unified, multi-ethnic Bosnia, to set up the joint presidency elected Sept. 14 and to hold the first presidency meeting in Sarajevo next week.Bosnia peace coordinator Carl Bildt said
15309 he wanted to see the U.N. specify that it was ready to re-impose sanctions if necessary, an idea also supported by the United States.This could be done "against anyone that would undertake actions that would threaten the unity of Bosnia-Herzegovina or in other ways seriously jeopardise the implementation of the
15309 peace agreement", Bildt told reporters.Bosnia's Serbs and Croats are widely suspected of wanting to merge the parts of Bosnia that they control with Serbia and Croatia respectively at some point in the future, although Dayton forbids them to do so.The United States plans to retain its own "outer wall" of
15309 sanctions to debar rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro -- from access to international financial institutions or from taking former Yugoslavia's U.N. seat.Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, representing the European Union, said there had been no discussion by the Contact Group of an international peacekeeping force to replace the NATO-led
15309 IFOR, whose mandate expires in December.But he said: "I think there is a general view emerging from all of our discussions in New York this week that there will have to be a new post-IFOR mandate. The shape of that or the actual scale of it has not been discussed
15309 in any detail yet."Izetbegovic told reporters some kind of force would have to remain. "We believe that the extension of the IFOR presence is necessary for at least two more years," he said.U.N. diplomats said two meetings -- one in November and one in December -- were planned to work
15309 out the basis for a continuing international involvement in Bosnia.The first, expected to be held Nov. 14 in Paris, would involve the Group of Seven top industrial nations, Russia and an Islamic representative. The second would be held in London with exact dates and participation still to be decided.</
15310 The Vatican voiced horror on Thursday at the world's first legally-assisted suicide, saying no law or human suffering could justify euthanasia."One remains stupified and horrified by this shocking case of euthanasia that was requested and granted," said Father Gino Concetti, a Vatican moral theologian close to Pope John Paul.He was
15310 reacting to the case of an elderly cancer patient who became the first person to take his life under a unique voluntary euthanasia law in Australia's Northern Territory.The man, Bob Dent, died by a computer-delivered lethal injection in Darwin on Sunday after persuading doctors that his case was hopeless and
15310 he knew what he was doing."No law of the state can justify euthanasia. This would mean the end of human civilisation based on love and justice," Concetti told Reuters.Concetti said those opposed to euthanasia had to react strongly to the Australian death. Concetti had expected to publish an editorial condemning
15310 the case in the Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano on Thursday but it will appear in the paper at a later date."We must rail against the culture of death because life, even that which is in a terminal state because of an atrocious and incurable illness, is inviolable and sacred," Concetti
15310 said.The Roman Catholic Church teaches that life begins at the moment of conception and ends at the moment of natural death.The Church bans active euthanasia but does allow families to refuse or interrupt the use of life-supporting equipment in cases where patients are terminally ill.In his 1995 encyclical Evangelium Vitae
15310 (The Gospel of Life), the Pope branded abortion and euthanasia as evils no man could justify and urged all Christians to oppose them.Saying life had to be respected "at all costs", Concetti asserted that the Church's position against euthanasia was not insensitive to the suffering of the terminally ill."Nonetheless, it
15310 is unacceptable that a person decides to take his own life or procure one's own death," Concetti said.Darwin doctor Philip Nitschke told Reuters he had helped Dent administer a lethal injection on Sunday. It was the first time that the Northern Territory's euthanasia law had been successfully used since it
15310 came into operation on July 1.Dent, in an emotional open letter written on the eve of his death, said that he had been living on a "roller-coaster of pain" and would have killed himself with a gun if he had one.Concetti rejected assertions by proponents of euthanasia that a life
15310 reduced to pain was essentially worthless."Pain can be relieved by the appropriate drugs and...in Christian teaching it can even be the means for the redemption of the individual and for others," Concetti said.Dent, in his last letter on the topic that has bitterly divided Australians and people around the world,
15310 said the Church should not be allowed to influence laws on euthanasia."The Church and state should be kept separate," Dent wrote. "What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain."--

15311 calming gestures, in particular returning the tunnel under the Holy City to its initial state," a foreign ministry statement said.Paris called for an immediate summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to resume peace negotiations and enable a full implementation of self-rule accords already signed.It
15311 also asked the European Union to provide immediate special financial and humanitarian aid to help the Palestinian Authority cope with the crisis.Earlier on Thursday, French President Jacques Chirac telephoned Arafat to express support and appeal for calm.In a 20-minute phone call, Chirac "assured (Arafat) of his solidarity and support after
15311 the grave incidents in the Palestinian territories", the president's office said.In an earlier statement, the Foreign Ministry accused Israel of triggering the violence, in which at least 44 Palestinians and 11 Israelis were killed, by opening the archeological tunnel close to al-Aqsa Mosque, one of Islam's holiest shrine.It called the
15311 violence a worrying throwback to the 1987-93 Intifada, or uprising, against Israeli occupation.A delegation of Arab ambassadors, including Palestinian envoy Leila Shahid, met the head of the French Foreign Ministry to thank France for its stance and ask it to continue.</
15312 World governments voiced alarm at an explosion of Israeli-Palestinian violence on Thursday and most, well beyond the Arab world, blamed hardline Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu for provoking a second Intifada.The United States, Russia, France and Britain all appealed for calm and urged Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to return
15312 quickly to peace negotiations.Arab states hailed what they called "the Intifada of the Palestinian people" and said a tunnel Israel had opened in Arab East Jerusalem was part of a plot to destroy a Moslem shrine.After at least 55 people were killed in riots and gun battles in the occupied
15312 West Bank and Gaza, U.S. President Bill Clinton said he has asked both Israel and the Palestinians to "end this violence" and resume peace talks.Without openly apportioning blame for the worst bloodshed since the 1993 Israel-PLO peace accords, Clinton urged both sides "to avoid unnecessarily provocative actions", an apparent veiled
15312 reference to the Israeli tunnel under Jerusalem.The United States is Israel's closest ally and the dominant power in the Middle East. A further blow-up could weigh on Clinton's campaign for re-election in November.European and Arab nations pinned the blame squarely on the Jewish state's hawkish 100-day-old government.By late Thursday, 44
15312 Arabs and 11 Israelis had been killed in two days of widespread mayhem. Israel declared a state of emergency in the West Bank and Gaza Strip and sent in tanks and helicopters to quell the unrest.Television images of the bloodshed recalled the worst days of the 1987-93 Intifada (uprising), in
15312 which Palestinians rose up against Israeli occupation.At the United Nations, where the Security Council was due to discuss the crisis, the European Union and Islamic nations criticised Israel and urged it to prove its commitment to the crumbling Middle East peace process.The Paris-based U.N. cultural agency UNESCO accused Israel of
15312 violating international principles by excavating in occupied land and, echoing Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, urged it to close the tunnel.Russia, co-sponsor with Washington of the Middle East peace process, said: "The fact that the Israeli authorities, in a unilateral fashion, opened a tunnel next to a Moslem holy site provoked
15312 a spontaneous protest by the Palestinian population."France said the violent reaction was predictable. President Jacques Chirac, who urged Netanyahu in Paris on Wednesday to avoid provocations and return to land-for-peace negotiations launched by his Labour predecessors, telephoned Arafat to express his "solidarity and support" for the Palestinians.Britain, Italy and Germany
15312 also faulted Israel. The violence wrecked Netanyahu's quest for European support, and forced him to cut short a three-country tour of Britain, France and Germany and rush home to handle the crisis.Diplomats said there was concern in Western capitals that Arafat might not be able to control the explosion of
15312 Palestinian anger after months of perceived procrastination and humiliation by Israel and that it might trigger wider violence, possibly drawing in Lebanon and Syria."Many governments think Netanyahu is getting what he deserves for reducing the peace process to a crawl, going back on the agreement to withdraw from Hebron and
15312 resuming Israeli settlement in the West Bank. But the implications are frightening," said one European Middle East-watcher.Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal, whose country brokered the 1993 Israel-PLO peace accords, told Reuters: "The broad unrest is a signal of the deep frustration among many sectors of the Palestinian community as
15312 a result of the lack of progress in the peace process."The tunnel and many other items are not large themselves but add together to heighten frustrations and lead to the sort of broad unrest we are seeing now."</

15313 the seriousness of sniping at Juppe within the centre-right coalition, and of the damage it is causing in public opinion.An IPSOS opinion poll published on Thursday showed Chirac's approval rating at a record low since his election. Just 36 percent of voters said they supported the president's action, a fall
15313 of five points in a month. 15313 comments won applause and followed a blistering attack on the prime minister by back-bencher Etienne Garnier on Wednesday, "disapproval" by veteran Gaullist Pierre Mazeaud and criticism by former interior minister Charles Pasqua.Juppe has called a parliamentary confidence vote next Wednesday in an effort to unite his fractious centre-right coalition but
15313 this has done nothing to stop the sniping.Party officials said Garnier faced possible disciplinary action for calling Juppe an "irreparable prime minister...whose dogmatism and clumsiness are leading the country towards insurmountable problems and unacceptable inequality."Balladur, defeated for the presidency by Chirac last year, said in his speech: "We will not
15313 respond to citizens' concerns by multiplying and refining our legal arsenal, nor by changing the election law at the risk of depriving the Fifth Republic of any stable majority."Juppe split his coalition by proposing a "dose" of proportional representation in the parliamentary voting system and a new anti-racism law to
15313 make it easier to prosecute extreme-right anti-immigration crusader Jean-Marie Le Pen.The Union for French Democracy (UDF), junior partner in the coalition, criticised both ideas at its parliamentary conference earlier this week.Balladur, who had shunned Gaullist meetings since his presidential defeat in May 1995, said he supported Juppe's government when it
15313 took unpopular decisions to cut public spending and bring down the budget deficit."But that is not enough. We must do more," he said. "This is all necessary but not sufficient to return quickly to growth and employment, we must go further and complete this with action on the fiscal, wage
15313 and monetary fronts."Pericard hinted that Garnier could be de-selected by the party for his attack on Juppe. He told reporters that Garnier had "crossed the red line" and talked like an opponent.</

15315 Cegetel company, which will compete against state-owned France Telecom from 1998.The French market will open up to private operators from January 1998 under a European Union (EU) directive that ends France Telecom's domestic monopoly.Messier told a news conference this was "the first day of competition in the French telecommunications market".CGE
15315 will hold 50 percent of Cegetel, BT 25 percent, U.S. telecoms firm SBC 15 percent and Germany's Mannesman AG 10 percent.But Messier said the final stakes could change by five percent either way when final contracts were signed late 1996.The company will have seven billion francs capital to meet its
15315 investment needs over the next three years."Cegetel will enable us to introduce real competition and choice to the French telecommunications market across a wide range of services," BT chairman Ian Vallance said."We look forward to competing head-to-head with France Telecom across the full spectrum of telecommunications services, including of course
15315 the residential telephone market. The opportunity is too good ... to miss."CGE already runs the SFR French mobile telephone network through the French Cofira consortium and has made Cegetel its vehicle to seize a share in the lucrative long-distance call and corporate network sectors.A number of crucial corporate moves lie
15315 behind the creation of Cegetel, which Messier will chair.CGE will transfer its SFR unit to Cegetel.French telecommunications and engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom is selling its 25 percent stake in Cofira to BT for an undisclosed amount.BT is paying 1.1 billion pounds ($1.71 billion) in cash for 25 percent in Cegetel
15315 and transferring its BT France subsidiary to Cegetel. Vallance declined to put a value on the French subsidiary.SBC is investing 1.5 billion francs to raise its share in the Transcell holding company, which holds SBC's 15 percent stake in Cegetel, to 30 percent from 22 percent.Messier declined to give details
15315 of how Mannesman was acquiring its 10 percent in Cegetel. In Germany, a Mannesman spokesman said it could raise that stake to 15 percent.The Cegetel deal effectively sidelines a relationship CGE has with U.S. telecoms giant AT&amp;T and the European Unisource consortium. "We had to make a choice for the
15315 partner for Cegetel," Messier said.Through its link-up with BT, the French company will gain access to the Concert joint venture the British company created with MCI of the U.S., giving Cegetel a global stretch.Messier said Cegetel aims to capture 40 percent of the domestic mobile telephone market by 2003, a
15315 market which is expected to grow almost tenfold. It wants 10 percent of the long-distance market and 10 percent of all local calls. ($1=.6416 Pound) ($1=5.145 French Franc)</

15316 Exhibition Centre, which has a capacity of over 4,000 people, in the presence of high-level guests including representatives of overseas governments and international organisations."This will be a very important occasion, both as a symbol but also representing the joint will of the British and Chinese governments with regard to smooth

15327 market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," SNB spokesman Werner Abegg added.Many traders were taken by surprise by the timing of the move, although they said the trend was clear given low money market rates, a relatively strong franc and a weak domestic economy that
15327 has contracted six quarters in a row.The franc fell against the dollar and German mark on the news. The dollar was trading around 1.2521 francs by late afternoon, up from 1.2425 before the news. The mark was up around 82.27 Swiss centimes per mark from about 81.90.Analysts suggested the SNB

15327 plays no role at all any more," said Rainer Marian at CS Economic Research in Zurich.He said foreign exchange speculators could now safely assume that 82.5 Swiss centimes per mark no longer had to be the perceived upper limit for the German currency, as in the past.Ian Amstad, international economist
15327 at Bankers Trust in London, said the SNB sought to make the franc less attractive to investors wary about the stability of Europe's single currency, to arrive in 1999 as part of economic and monetary union (EMU)."The Swiss are worried about the impact of a fudged EMU on the Swiss

15327 do little in any event to hold back the tide if it came."In the case of massive speculative flows, the only thing they could do is peg the franc" to the single currency, he said, even though SNB officials say this would be the absolute last resort.The discount rate, which

15331 The Vatican voiced horror on Thursday at the world's first legally-assisted suicide, saying no law or human suffering could justify euthanasia."One remains stupified and horrified by this shocking case of euthanasia that was requested and granted," said Father Gino Concetti, a Vatican moral theologian close to Pope John Paul.He was
15331 reacting to the case of an elderly cancer patient who became the first person to take his life under a unique voluntary euthanasia law in Australia's Northern Territory.The man, Bob Dent, died by a computer-delivered lethal injection in Darwin on Sunday after persuading doctors that his case was hopeless and
15331 he knew what he was doing."No law of the state can justify euthanasia. 15331 the case in the Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano on Thursday but it will appear in the paper at a later date."We must rail against the culture of death because life, even that which is in a terminal state because of an atrocious and incurable illness, is inviolable and sacred," Concetti
15331 said.The Roman Catholic Church teaches that life begins at the moment of conception and ends at the moment of natural death.The Church bans active euthanasia but does allow families to refuse or interrupt the use of life-supporting equipment in cases where patients are terminally ill.In his 1995 encyclical Evangelium Vitae
15331 (The Gospel of Life), the Pope branded abortion and euthanasia as evils no man could justify and urged all Christians to oppose them.Saying life had to be respected "at all costs", Concetti asserted that the Church's position against euthanasia was not insensitive to the suffering of the terminally ill."Nonetheless, it
15331 is unacceptable that a person decides to take his own life or procure one's own death," Concetti said.Darwin doctor Philip Nitschke told Reuters he had helped Dent administer a lethal injection on Sunday. It was the first time that the Northern Territory's euthanasia law had been successfully used since it
15331 came into operation on July 1.Dent, in an emotional open letter written on the eve of his death, said that he had been living on a "roller-coaster of pain" and would have killed himself with a gun if he had one.Concetti rejected assertions by proponents of euthanasia that a life
15331 reduced to pain was essentially worthless."Pain can be relieved by the appropriate drugs and...in Christian teaching it can even be the means for the redemption of the individual and for others," Concetti said.Dent, in his last letter on the topic that has bitterly divided Australians and people around the world,
15331 said the Church should not be allowed to influence laws on euthanasia."The Church and state should be kept separate," Dent wrote. "What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain."</

15333 NATO countries said on Thursday they would press ahead with expansion plans next year and grant full membership to former communist enemies in eastern and central Europe despite Russian objections."At a summit next year several countries will be invited to start accession talks," U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry told reporters
15333 after a two-day informal meeting of the 16-nation alliance's defence ministers in Bergen, Norway.Perry declined to be drawn on which countries may be invited to join the alliance, but emphasised the process would go ahead whatever Moscow's concerns."If I thought that those actions (expansion) were threatening Russia I would have
15333 a very different view, but I don't believe that for a minute," Perry said.Since the end of the Cold War, ex-Communist countries have been seeking to join NATO to guarantee their future security against Russia. Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are the most likely candidates, but could be joined
15333 by Slovenia.NATO hopes to buy off Russia by offering it a new all- embracing security pact in the form of a treaty or charter which it says it will negotiate in parallel with its first enlargement since the late 1970s.Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, who met the ministers for a
15333 separate "16+1" session after the main session, repeated Moscow's view that it considered there was "no strategic necessity" to enlarge the alliance."Our country does not want the NATO expansion at present... we in our country are concerned," he told a press conference.But Rodionov notably steered clear of the fiery rhethoric
15333 that accompanied a virulent anti-enlargement campaign by Moscow last year and said his country was ready to work with NATO on the planning of a possible new peace force for Bosnia."We are ready to cooperate," he told reporters.Maintaining Russian public opinion was firmly opposed to any alliance expansion, Rodionov hinted
15333 Moscow's position could change as growing cooperation with NATO changed public perception of its Cold War foe."We may support this idea when our public is convinced that NATO has indeed passed through a genuine transformation in accordance with the new conditions of the political situation."Rodionov also said the dispute over
15333 enlargement should not stand in the way of cooperation in other areas, such as Bosnia."That (Bosnia) is another matter, one thing is not in contradiction with another," he said in reply to a question.NATO is hoping it can entice Russia to take part actively in the alliance's Partnership for Peace
15333 (PFP) programme designed to try and fill a security vacuum in central and eastern Europe created by the collapse of communism.The alliance wants to upgrade PFP and offer it as an alternative to countries left out of next year's expansion, but which still want an insurance policy against a rebirth
15333 of an expansionist Russia."What we are doing with NATO and what we are doing with Partnership for Peace is creating a security circle for all of Europe... our goal is not to threaten Russia, but to bring Russia into that security circle," Perry said.NATO diplomats say the aim is to
15333 try to dovetail approval of both enlargement and a new pact for Russia at next year's heads of government summit which would also endorse reform of the alliance's command structures.</

15335 Economic reform pursued by Colombia over the past six years have boosted the politically- troubled Latin American country's integration into the world economy, the World Trade Organisation said on Thursday.In a report on Colombian trade policies, WTO analysts said the so-called "Apertura" trade liberalisation programme launched in 1990 had brought
15335 down tariffs and non-tariff barriers to imports and led to openings for foreign service providers.This nationally-initiated process had been given further impetus by wider commitments to opening up its previously highly-protected markets for goods and services taken on in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round world trade negotiations."The opening of the economy
15335 has created new investment oportunities, which should also be encouraged by improved macroeconomic stability, solid growth and ongoing fiscal reforms," the WTO analysts said.The agreements reached in the Round, held under the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), were finalised in a world treaty signed in Morocco in
15335 1994, clearing the way for the launch of the WTO to replace the GATT in 1995.Colombia, one of the major economies in Latin America, said in its own report to the WTO that since the organisation had started operations it had recognised the advantages it could offer to an emerging
15335 economy."We have perceived the benefits which may derive from a rule-based system and more precise disciplines, as well as from a strengthened dispute-settlement mechanism which can guarantee the effective functioning of the multi-lateral trading system," the Bogota government said.The rules of the WTO which prevent countries blocking rulings by neutral
15335 panels in trade disputes are widely seen by developing countries as giving them firmer ground than under the GATT to challenge the big trading powers.While very few small economies took complaints to the GATT, developing countries are involved in many of the over 50 disputes already brought to the WTO,
15335 encouraged by the very first panel ruling which found in favour of Venezuela against the United States.Many feel the big powers -- including the United States, Colombia's main trading partner, and the European Union -- have been slow to open up markets to their products while they have adapted national
15335 policies to the new overall trade rules.An echo of this came in the Colombian report.While Colombia was confident the benefits of the new world trading system would be shared, it said, this could be achieved "if the supply of exports from the developing countries such as Colombia is treated in
15335 the same way as products and services from developed countries."The WTO analysts noted that Colombia -- linked in the Andean Pact with Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela -- was looking for new agreements with Latin American partners which would bring an expansion of regional trade growth.But the country was also
15335 looking for trade opportunities beyond the region and was actively engaged in negotiations to establish a free trade area for the Americas.</

15349 France assured the 14 members of the African Franc zone on Wednesday that their French-backed currency would keep its value when the French franc is replaced in 1999 by the planned new European currency known as the Euro."There will be no devaluation" of the CFA franc currency when European monetary
15349 union comes into effect, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said after hosting a one-day meeting attended by his counterparts from France's former African colonies. All that would change when the new European currency is introduced is that the CFA franc's parity would be fixed "against the Euro instead of the franc,"
15349 he said.The new single European currency is to come into effect under monetary union due to start on January 1, 1999.The ministers from the 14 African countries gave an upbeat message at their regular half-yearly meeting about their countries' economic prospects in the wake of the devaluation three years ago
15349 of the CFA franc against the French franc."The message is one of confidence," Arthuis told reporters. France's 13 former African colonies devalued their common currency by 50 percent in 1994. The 14th country in the zone, the Comoros Islands in the Indian Ocean, devalued by 33 percent.France precipitated the drastic
15349 devaluation by making its aid contingent on the countries winning the International Monetary Fund's backing. The IMF demanded they break a 46-year-old fixed parity with the franc because it made their manufacturing costs higher than their neighbours and was paralysing economic growth. Since devaluation, growth has returned and exports have
15349 risen. "We have mastered inflation...we have mastered spending," Cote d'Ivoire finance minister Niamien N'Goran said.He said inflation in west Africa had been wrestled down to between minus one percent to plus nine percent, depending on the country. It had been running at an average 40 percent in the Franc zone
15349 only three years ago.The ministers said growth in the zone should be at least 4.6 percent in 1996 after shrinking on average by 0.8 percent a year from 1990 to 1993. But the ministers said more needed to be done to encourage private investment.The ministers also urged more progress on
15349 debt relief. But N'Goran was optimistic the Paris Club of creditor nations would agree to offer better debt relief conditions than the Naples terms currently available -- under which two-thirds of the debt of low-income countries can be written off.N'Goran said the countries were pressing for the terms to be
15349 amended to allow up to 80 percent of the debt to be written off. Debt costs were "preventing essential investment in basic areas like health and education," he said.Arthuis said France supported easier debt relief on a "case by case basis" and was optimistic accord would soon be reached.</

15370 superiority and its medical experiments on human subjects during the World War Two era, German deputies had blocked the convention earlier this year, saying controls on research on human embryos and mentally deficient individuals were insufficient.As approved by the parliamentary assembly, the code would ban discrimination based on an individual's
15370 genetic makeup and would forbid choosing the sex of one's baby.It would allow organ and tissue transplants only with the donor's consent and solely for therapeutic purposes.Research on human subjects could be conducted only with the subject's consent and if an experiment promised a greater benefit than its risks, as
15370 determined by outsiders.Studies on individuals with a diminished capacity to provide their informed consent, such as minors or the mentally ill, would be subject to even stricter limitations under the code.The code also would impose restrictions on test-tube babies and research on human embryos.</

15377 leader has."I am convinced the 1997 deficit will be cut to 3.0, even 2.9 percent," said Generale Bank chief economist Peter Praet, adding that he was sure Dehaene would keep his budget on track."That is why markets are so positive about Belgium."Belgian 10 year bonds yielded 6.22 percent on Thursday,
15377 a historically low 15 basis points over equivalent German bonds.But like most of his colleagues, Praet has doubts about the quality of the budget package.As in all previous budgets of the past decade, the 1997 one is expected to be full of minor spending cuts and tax hikes, complemented by
15377 one-shot measures and some accounting tricks.A serious reform of Belgium's generous welfare system -- the root of all budget evil -- is not expected this year."Belgium is not made for revolutions, and the budget will be typically Belgian: a series of little cuts," said Credit Communal economist Jacques De Pover.Analysts
15377 estimate the government will need to take between 100 and 110 billion francs ($3.51 billion) worth of austerity measures.About 30 billion is seen coming from social security, partly from an increase in women's retirement age to 65 from 60.A hike of indirect taxes is seen providing another 30 billion francs.
15377 Labour income in Belgium is already taxed to the hilt, but Belgium's indirect taxes only add up to 12.4 percent of GDP in 1995, compared to 13.6 percent for its three big neigbour states and 13.4 percent for the EU, a BBL study said."There is room for a hike," said

15387 the nuclear waste. 15387 nuclear fuel properly."That is the main problem," he said. 15387 inspection," he said. "The civilian radiation authorities in Norway, Russia and the United States are being kept out. We fear information will be kept away from the public."</

15395 The European Court of Justice told a Swedish court on Thursday that it may not require a national from another member state to lodge a security if none is required from a Swedish national.When a British company sought relief in a Swedish court for payment on goods delivered against Swedish
15395 companies, the defendants asked the court to require the company to place in escrow funds necessary to cover judicial costs.Although a 1980 Swedish law requires such security, the Swedish District Court found that the 1988 Lugano Convention superceded the earlier law and that none was needed.The Swedish defendants appealed to
15395 the Supreme Court, which asked the European court to review Community law.The court said that national rules on civil procedure fell within the scope of non-discrimination policies under article 6 of the EC Treaty, and that a provision such as the 1980 Swedish law was manifestly discriminatory.The court said Sweden
15395 could not require a security to cover judicial costs from citizens of other member states unless it also required one for Swedish nationals.***EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Swedish)"Equal treatment - Discrimination on the grounds of nationality - Security for the costs of judicial
15395 proceedings"In Case C-43/95Reference from the Hogsta Domstolen, Stockholm, for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court betweenData Delecta AktiebolagRonny ForsbergandMSL Dynamics Ltdon the interpretation of article 6 of the EC Treaty---THE COURT hereby rulesThe first paragraph of article 6 of the EC Treaty precludes a member state
15395 from requiring a legal person established in another member state which has brought, before one of its courts, an action against one of its nationals or a company established in the member state in question to lodge security for the costs of proceedings, where no such requirement can be imposed
15395 on legal persons from that state, in a situation in which the action is connected with the exercise of fundamental freedoms guaranteed by Community law.</

15397 The World Health Organisation said on Thursday it was launching a new drive to fight an explosion of cholera in West Africa, where the disease has spread rapidly in the past three years.The United Nations agency said it was jointly funding the programme -- to be implemented in partnership with
15397 national health ministries -- together with a special grant from the Swiss government."The incidence of cholera has risen dramatically throughout West Africa in recent years," a statement from the WHO's Geneva headquarters said.Of the 16 countries in the new project, only six had reported the disease in 1993 but this
15397 year there had been cases in 13 of them.The annual number of cases in the region had exploded from a total of only 7,000 in 1993 to 42,500 in the first nine months of this year, and fatalities had seen a nine-fold increase -- from 369 in 1993 to more
15397 than 2,900 so far this year.The West African region now accounted for two-thirds of all cholera cases on the continent and more than 70 per cent of all deaths there from the disease.The 16 countries involved in the project are Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Chad, Ivory Coast, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea,
15397 Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo.The WHO said a main aim of the drive would be to improve the region's capacity for a rapid response to cholera outbreaks and for treatment of individual cases. The average fatality rate for all 16 countries was currently running at
15397 six per cent."The project will also seek to improve the capacity of participating countries to develop and implement a common policy for epidemic preparedness and control," the WHO declared."It will stress food safety, health education for better hygiene in the home and the workplace, provision and use of safe water,
15397 and access to sanitation facilities."An earlier anti-cholera project launched by the WHO in six countries of Southern Africa in 1993 has reduced the average annual case total from more than 57,000 to fewer than 1,500, the agency said.</

15430 The European Court of Justice dismissed on Thursday a bid by the French Republic to annul the Commission's classification as state aid of funds from a French National Employment Fund (FNE) to Kimberly Clark Sopalin.In 1993, Kimberly Clark, under a company reconstruction plan, dismissed employees under a social plan governed
15430 by French law. Twenty-five percent, FF 27.25 million, of that plan was funded by France.The Commission declared France's contribution to Kimberly Clark's social plan as illegal state aid under EC Treaty article 92, saying it was intended to facilitate the development of certain economic activities.The Commission attatched importance to the
15430 reduction of capacity at Kimberly Clark, that the laid-off workers were the main beneficiaries and the limited amount of aid granted.France claimed the Commission errred in law as the mechanism put into place by the FNE constitutes a general measure for the benefit of employees intended to combat unemployment.But the
15430 court found the treaty does not distinguish between measures of state intervention based on their causes or aims, but defines them in relation to their effects."The social character of the FNE assistance is not therefore sufficient to exclude it outright from being catergorized as aid," the court said.The court found
15430 that under the system FNE operates, contributions to certain undertakings may place them in a more favourable situation than their competitors, classifying such contributions as state aid.***EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT(Court transltion into English. Original language of the case: Italian)"Cadmium
15433 discharges - Interpretation of Council directives 76/464/EEC and 83/513/EEC - Direct effect - Possibility for a directive to be relied on an against an individual"In Case C-168/95Reference from the Pretura Circondariale di Vicenza (Italy) for a preliminary ruling in the criminal proceedings before that court againstLuciano Arcaraon the interpretation of

15433 1)---THE COURT hereby rules1. Article 3 of Council directive 76/464/EEC of 4 May 1976 on pollution caused by certain dangerous substances discharged into the aquatic environment of the Community is to be interpreted as making any discharge of cadmium, irrespective of the date on which the plant from which it
15433 comes commenced operation, subject to the issue of a prior authorization.2. 15433 may not be relied upon before the national court.</

15458 The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Community customs provisions do not preclude member states from reclassifying facts at the time of violation, when setting penalties.The French government initated proceedings in 1990 against an importer who falsely declared the origin of steel beams and plates as Yugoslavia, and not
15458 the former German Democratic Republic, in 1985.At the time France initiated its prosecution, the former East Germany had united with West Germany. The court noted that as soon as Germany was unified, all Community provisions applied to the former eastern state as well."However, it must be stressed that the extension
15458 of the Community customs territory ... constitutes a new material fact which does not have the effect of releasing member states from obligation to ... guarantee Community law ... such an extension does not preclude national courts from penalizing breaches of Community legislation on conditions ...which make the penalty effective,
15458 proportionate and dissuasive, " the court said.The court's decision will permit the French court to look at the facts under national law at the time of the customs' breach.***EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)"Customs declaration - Country of origin - German unification -
15458 Penalties"In Case C-341/94Reference by the Cour d'Appel, Paris, for a preliminary ruling in the criminal proceedings before that court againstAndre AllainandSteel Trading France SARL, as a party liable at civil lawon the consequences to be drawn, following the unification of the Federal Republic of Germany and the German Democratic Republic
15458 and the rest of the Community's customs territory with regard to the possible reclassification of facts for the purpose of imposing penalties---THE COURT hereby rulesThe Community customs provisions, applicable following the unification of the Federal Republic of Germany and the German Democratic Republic, do not preclude a reclassificatin of facts
15458 under national law with a view to penalizing breaches of the Community legislation applicable at the material time.</

15463 Easdaq promises to give start-up firms access to a wider range of capital than their national stock markets can provide.Share prices will be quoted in the currency chosen by the listed company. 15464 Plans to update a 21-year old EU law on bathing water will make it cheaper for governments to monitor water quality but might not make swimming safer, a European Parliament official said on Thursday."The directive has been improved. Safety for the swimmer will be at least at the same level
15464 while the cost (of implementing the directive) has been reduced," an assistant to Dutch Christian Democrat Doeke Eisma told Reuters.Parliament's environment committee is currently examining a draft report by Eisma on a European Commission proposal to update a 1975 directive on bathing water quality -- COM(94)36.Despite the member states' parlous
15464 record of compliance with the 1975 directive, Eisma's report suggests they can be trusted properly to monitor and clean up their bathing waters.Of the 18,000 beaches in the European Union covered by the Commission's 1995 bathing water report, more than 3,000 either failed to meet EU minimum requirements on clean
15464 water or were not monitored closely enough to determine whether they complied.Part of the problem was the list of pollutants the member states were expected to monitor was so long that in some cases they simply did not bother, according to Eisma's assistant, Gerbenjay Gerbrandy.The Commission has made their lives
15464 cheaper and easier by dropping from the list a series of substances which it deems do not affect bathers' health directly although they do damage the environment.These include heavy metals, cyanide, pesticides, amonia, nitrates and phosphates.The omissions were acceptable, Gerbrandy said, because these substances should be covered by the EU's
15464 planned framework directive on water policy.He said it was important to find a compromise between bathers' safety and the cost to the water industry of keeping lakes, rivers and coastal waters clean."Science provides us with information which shows for a certain standard of water quality the number of people who
15464 will fall sick. We then have to look at the cost to the water industry of preventing that sickness," he said.Another problem with getting the member states to respect the existing directive is that it gives them too much leeway for deciding which areas they have to monitor and clean
15464 up, says Eisma's report.The directive defines a bathing area as one where there are "a considerable number of bathers" and its definition of the bathing season is equally vague.Eisma's report suggests using the phrase "many bathers" would be an improvement.Gerbrandy said referring to precise figures, such as the number of
15464 bathers per square metre, was not a solution since that could exempt governments from monitoring large but uncrowded beaches.The member states had to be trusted to be conscientious on this point, he said.Eisma believes they cannot however be trusted to inform the Commission of abnormally high but short-lived levels of
15464 pollution.His report calls for the deletion of a clause which allows the member states to exclude short-lived peaks of pollution from their water quality analyses if the pollution subsides within two days and if they inform Brussels.The report also recommends introducing harmonised methods for testing water quality, in the form
15464 of a code of conduct.</

15475 An Indian court on Thursday rejected a request by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for legal protection against arrest in a criminal conspiracy case, court officials said.The Delhi High court denied Rao's request for anticipatory bail in the $100,000 case, they said. Anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest."The
15475 application for anticipatory bail is dismissed," judge S.K. Mahajan said. "The application is not maintainable."Rao's lawyer had asked on Wednesday for anticipatory bail before a hearing next Monday in the cheating case.Rao abruptly resigned as president of the Congress party on Saturday after a judge ordered him to appear in
15475 court as a co-accused at Monday's hearing.Indian expatriate businessman Lakhubhai Pathak alleges that Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in an unsuccessful attempt to win a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured
15475 him at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done."Rao has said he is innocent and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.The two other accused, Chandraswami and his personal aide, are currently in judicial custody in Tihar jail,
15475 Asia's biggest prison, in the Indian capital. 15475 as head of Congress, he had already been under pressure to quit after leading India's oldest party to its worst defeat in general elections that ended in May. 15475 of parliament, Rao has no immunity in the case.Rao's counsel argued on Thursday that his client was bound to be arrested next week because he would be charged with a criminal offence."Mr Rao has to be arrested on September 30 when he appears before the trial court, and he has
15475 to apply for bail," Rao's lawyer, Kapil Sibal, said.Arguing against Rao's request for anticipatory bail, the counsel for the Central Bureau of Investigation said the former prime minister was not going to be arrested before September 30, and thus had no reason to ask for anticipatory bail.Judge Mahajan said no
15475 arrest warrant had been issued and, if Rao was detained on Monday, he could immediately ask for ordinary bail.Court officials said Rao was expected to lodge an appeal of the High Court's decision with the Supreme Court either on Thursday or Friday.The Times of India newspaper said the government was
15475 drawing up a plan for giving Rao medical assistance if he is sent to jail. Rao has a history of heart trouble.</

15477 fresh troops on all frontlines, Defence Ministry sources said.The Taleban attacks came from Butkhak, about 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Kabul, and Koh-i-Koruk, about 20 km to the southwest, they said.More than 150 rebel fighters were killed in a four-hour battle for a customs house in eastern Kabul starting
15477 at midnight, the sources said.They said the customs house was now no-man's land, but government forces held the nearby Pul-i-Charkhi jail, which Taleban sources in neighbouring Pakistan said had been captured by the militia. 15477 northwest Pakistani town of Peshawar earlier said the militia forces had penetrated eastern Kabul overnight and were only about five km (three miles) from the presidential palace.The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) also quoted other Taleban sources as saying the militia had broken through government lines in the south and
15477 southwest of Kabul.There was no independent confirmation of these reports.Hospital sources in Kabul said at least three civilians were killed and 21 wounded by overnight Taleban rocketing on Kabul.The Defence Ministry sources denied a Taleban claim that the militia forces had advanced up the Tagab valley close to the main

15477 government report on Wednesday night that its forces had repulsed the militia from the east of the capital.The source, speaking anonymously, said Taleban forces entered the city from Pul-i-Charkhi village, which they said they had captured on Wednesday in a swift advance after seizing the strategic eastern town of Sarobi.Official
15477 Kabul Radio said on Wednesday night the Taleban had cut off electricity to Kabul only 10 days after it was restored to part of the city from an eastern power house after two years.The 15-nation U.N. Security Council made an appeal for a ceasefire and peace talks after a meeting
15477 in New York."The members of the council call upon the parties to stop fighting immediately, to agree to a ceasefire and to enter into serious negotiations to find a political solution to this conflict," the current council president, Alfredo Lopes Cabral of Guinea-Bissau, told reporters.The council, which has made similar

15488 MINISTER RAO SEEKS ANTICIPATORY BAILFormer prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao moved the Delhi High Court seeking anticipatory bail fearing arrest in the Lakhubhai Pathak cheating case. The former prime minister is appearing before Additional District and Sessions Judge on September 30 in the case. Following Rao's application, the Delhi High
15488 Court issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation to show cause as to why Rao's plea for anticipatory bail should not be admitted.----The PioneerBULLETS IMPLANTED IN POLICEMEN'S BODIES AS PROOF OF VIOLENCEMuzaffarnagar district administration has been held responsible for police attrocities committed on Uttarakhand agitators in October 1994. The
15488 Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has established that the district administration manufactured evidence to cover up police atrocities on the agitators. In 1994 thousands of agitators demanding separate statehood for the Uttarakhand region in Uttar Pradesh were assulted by the police and women raped. CBI found unfired bullets were surgically
15488 implanted under the skin of five constables as evidence that Uttarakhand demonstrators had used firearms against the police.----Financial ExpressFDI IN UNLISTED COMPANIES RAISED TO 51 PCTThe Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the foreign direct investment (FDI) limit in unlisted companies to 51 percent on a repatriable basis. This
15488 is aimed at attracting greater FDI from non-resident Indians (NRIs). RBI's existing scheme allowing NRIs to invest up to 40 percent thus stands abolished. The central bank has put norms for NRI participation in venture capital companies at par with foreign investors.----BPL TO RAISE $200 MLN FROM AMERICAN MARKETBPL group's
15488 BPL Cellular Holding Ltd is raising $200 million through an issue of American Depository Receipts. The issue, to be listed on NASDAQ, will have a greenshoe option of 15 percent. The issue will be offered via an SEC registered initial public offering. The company is awaiting the final approval of
15488 the government.----BIDS FOR OIL EXPLORATION IN SEVEN BLOCKS CLEAREDThe Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) has accorded clearance to several bids for oil and gas exploration and some under offers for development of small-sized fields. CCEA has cleared seven blocks as per the recommendation of the Empowered Committee of Secretaries.
15488 A total of 33 bids for 18 blocks were received for the 34 blocks offered. Of these, U.S. companies Occidental International Exploration and Production Company were awarded two onshore blocks AA ON 4 and AA ON 6 in the Assam Arakan region. The Assam Company Limited and US based Medallion
15488 Company togather bagged AA ON 7 while Reliance-Enron combine got BB-OS/8.----CENTRAL BANK TO EASE FOREIGN CURRENCY DEPOSIT NORMSThe Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will soon allow select non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) to raise deposits in foreign currency. These deposits would be similar to the foreign currency non-resident deposits allowed to
15488 banks. Sources said the NBFCs would bear the exchange risk on these deposits.---- The Economic TimesBANK WITH 10.5 BLN RUPEE CAPITAL PLANNEDA group of Gulf-based non-resident Indians (NRIs) has proposed to set up a private bank with a capital base of 10.5 billion rupees. The new bank, to be called
15488 Trade and Commerce Bank, would be registered in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. Sources said the NRIs would be putting up 38 percent, or four billion rupees, of the total equity and the investment would be made on a repatriable basis.----BHARAT PETROLEUM FIGHTS SHY OF MAIDEN ISSUEBharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL) plans
15488 to defer its 4.5 billion rupee public issue because of poor market conditions. The issue was to hit the market this October. BPCL had filed a price band of 270 to 320 rupees with the bourse regulator. The public sector major, however, is yet to formally put its applications with
15488 the Registrar of Companies.----Business StandardFOREIGN BANKS RUSH FOR GILTSForeign banks have turned speculators in the securities market as secondary debt market trading touched 2.18 billion rupee mark on the National Stock Exchange. With most of the nationalised banks turning sellers, the foreign banks have stepped into the debt market to
15488 make a quick buck. This has pepped up activity in the debt market. Treasury heads with foreign banks said they were not lending their money to the corporate sector but were, instead, deploying the funds in the short term securities.----INDIA FIGHTS BID TO TRAMMEL RIGHT TO REGULATE INVESTMENTIndia plans to
15488 oppose the multilateral agreement on investment (MAI) being pushed by the OECD countries. It further plans to insist on retaining government rights to regulate foreign direct investment inflows. India would place its views at the coming MAI meet at Delhi to thrash out a common viewpoint for developing countries on
15488 emerging trade issues. Nineteen developing countries have been invited for the meet, of which 10 have confirmed participation, including Pakistan and Bangladesh.----TATA'S SMALL CAR TO MATERIALISE IN 1998Tata Engineering &amp; Locomotive Co Ltd (TELCO) plans to launch its small passenger car in 1998. Company sources said the car would be
15488 a utility vehicle in the 800-1000cc range. While pricing has not been worked out, it would be competing with the Maruti 800 and the Zen, the sources added. The company plans to set up a 150,000 per year capacity car unit. The plant will be part of the comprehensive facility
15488 being set up by TELCO. This will have flexible lines capable of manufacturing the small car, the Sumo and other models.----The ObserverITC CLASSIC TO SEEK NOD FOR GDRITC Classic Finance Ltd, a subsidiary of ITC Ltd, is seeking shareholders' approval for raising $45 million loan from the International Finance Corporation
15488 (IFC). The loan from IFC is for on-lending to export oriented eligible companies for equipment finance, foreign capital expenditure and infrastructural project finance. The company is also planning to raise $25 million through an issue of Global Depository Receipts at a later date.----Business Line63 FDI PROPOSALS CLEAREDThe Industry Ministry has
15488 cleared 63 foreign direct investment proposals amounting to 54.1 billion rupees. The proposals have total export projection up to 19 billion rupees over five to seven years. The proposals relate to software, engineering, electronics, power cotton and synthetic yarn, floriculture, financial services, medical services and pharmaceuticals. The major companies whose
15488 proposals with 100 percent foreign equity have been approved include G.M. Iocomotive Group ($5 millions) for support services to the Railways, Micon AS Denmark (100 million rupees) for the construction of a wind turbine power plant. E.M. Warburg, Pincus and Co. Inc. New York, has agreed to pump in 371
15488 million rupees to market and distribute telecom hardware for cellular and paging services. Viba Siat S.R.I. of Italy with an investment of seven million rupees plans to carry on activities in the field of machinery for manufacture of synthetic fibre.----</

15490 Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia appeared poised to capture Kabul on Friday as defenders loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani were reported pulling out of the besieged capital.Taleban sources in neighbouring Pakistan said the militia had seized the main government airbase at Bagram, 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul after
15490 taking parts of the capital, including its disused Khwaja Rawash airport.There was no immediate independent confirmation of these reports, but witnesses in Kabul said government forces appeared to be abandoning the capital they had vowed to fight to their death to defend.The Taleban sources said the militia had also taken
15490 Kabul's Soviet-built Microrayon housing complex in the east and the diplomatic Wazir Akbar Khan district in central Kabul.The sources, quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), said troops loyal to President Rabbani were fleeing northwards, but his militia forces were resisting Taleban fighters near the presidential palace in central
15490 Kabul.There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report, which also said the Taleban had taken Kohe Asmai hill, known as Television Hill, in the middle of Kabul.While the airport in Kabul was made unusable by factional fighting, the Soviet-built Bagram, shared by jet fighters and civilian airliners, was the
15490 only base left giving the government an air link with the outside world.On Thursday night much of the city resembled a ghost town with streets virtually deserted except for small groups of government soldiers trudging through the streets.There were only sporadic exchanges of machine-gun and small arms fire heard from
15490 the edges of the city. The security ministry building had been abandoned and at least six tanks and several trucks full of troops had been seen leaving the city.Some civilians had fled the city on the road north earlier in the day in dozens of trucks and buses, but with
15490 a curfew in force most Kabul citizens stayed in their homes.In the Wasir Akbar Khan diplomatic quarter, small groups of residents came onto the streets to burn posters of President Rabbani and his military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.There was no information about the whereabouts of Rabbani, Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
15490 and military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.The Taleban, which emerged from obscurity two years ago and now controls most of Afghanistan, seeks to oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order. Its leader Mullah Mohammad Omar said recently it had no ethnic or regional prejudices and only wanted to enforce Islamic
15490 sharia (law).Earlier on Thursday, the official government spokesman, Amrullah, told reporters it would fight to the death to defend the capital. "We are establishing defences in every street of Kabul," he said as the two sides fought in the outskirts.Amrullah accused Pakistan of sending military technicians to help the Taleban
15490 and said other countries, which he refused to name, were also aiding the rebels.Pakistan denied the accusations. "We have had and will continue to observe total neutrality while we must maintain a close watch on the events as they develop," a Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman said in Islamabad.An official of
15490 the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Jan-Luc Paladini, said there had been hundreds of dead and wounded on both sides in the past two days.The ICRC on Thursday stopped all flights from Bagram to the Pakistani city of Peshawar after evacuating 50 people, including 16 ICRC delegates, leaving
15490 only staff needed for emergencies."The ICRC is staying in Kabul. We are not leaving," he said.</
15491 Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the capital Kabul on Friday with forces of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city, witnesses said.The Taleban movement burst onto the Afghan scene two years ago after it was formed by Islamic religious students led by Mullah
15491 Muhammad Omar. They launched a campaign against local Mujahideen guerrilla commanders who had preyed on traders at checkposts in the southern province of Kandahar.Here is a chronology of the rise of the Islamic militia:1994:Oct 11: Taleban clash with local commander at Spinboldak on the Pakistan-Afghan border. Ten people are killed
15491 and 20 wounded before intermediaries stop the fighting.Nov 4: Taleban capture provincial capital of Kandahar after rescuing a 30-truck convoy from local commanders. The convoy had been sent by Pakistan to open a trade route to Central Asia.Taleban take Kandahar airport and a base held by a commander of Gulbuddin
15491 Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party, Mullah Naqib. More than 50 people are killed in four days of fighting.Nov 29: Afghan government issues statement through its embassy in Islamabad, calling Taleban "an Islamic and humane effort".1995:January: Taleban capture southeastern province of Ghazni.Feb 10: Taleban capture most of eastern province of Logar and town
15491 of Maidan Shahr, capital of Wardak province, southwest of Kabul, from Hezb-i-Islami, then in opposition.Feb 13: Taleban capture Pul-i-Alam, capital of Logar province, from Hezb-i-Islami.Feb 14: Taleban reach gates of Kabul, capturing Hekmatyar's Charasyab base, 25 km (15 miles) south of capital.March 10: Taleban seize Karte Seh area of Kabul
15491 from Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-i-Wahdat group and its leader Abdul Ali Mazari.March 11: Government forces oust Taleban from Karte Seh.March 13: Hezb-i-Wahdat leader Abdul Ali Mazari is killed in captivity. Taleban say he died in shootout after trying to seize gun in helicopter flying him from Charasyab to Kandahar.March 19: Troops
15491 loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani oust Taleban from Charasyab in militia's first major defeat.Aug 3: Taleban jets force chartered Russian Ilyushin-76 cargo plane carrying ammunition for Kabul to land in Kandahar with seven Russian crew, who are held hostage.Sept 3: Taleban capture big government air base at Shindand in western
15491 province of Farah near Iranian border.Sept 5: Taleban capture western city of Herat from government forces which had held it since 1992. They ban girls from going to school and women from working in offices.Oct 11: Taleban advance to gates of Kabul for second time, capturing Charasyab and later Rishkor
15491 and Khairabad hills.Oct 14: Taleban accuse Iran of letting border be used for incursion into western Afghanistan by pro-government forces.1996:April 3: About 1,000 Moslem clergymen choose Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar as Amir-ul-Momineen (commander of the faithful), denouncing Rabbani as unfit to lead Islamic nation.June 1: Government confirms loss of
15491 Chaghcharan, capital of the central province of Ghor, to Taleban.June 26: Taleban launch deadly rocket attack on Kabul, killing at least 54 people and wounding 118, as Hekmatyar resumes post of prime minister under peace deal with Rabbani.Aug 16: Seven Russian airmen held hostage in Kandahar for over a year
15491 escape to Abu Dhabi in their own Ilyushin-76 plane.Sept 5: Taleban launch offensive in eastern Afghanistan.Sept 11: Taleban capture eastern city of Jalalabad and surrounding Nangarhar province adjoining Pakistan border.Sept 13: Taleban capture eastern province of Laghman and its capital Mehtar Lam.Sept 22: Taleban say they capture Kunar, the last
15491 eastern province held by pro-government forces.Sept 25: Taleban say they capture strategic town of Sarobi, 70 km (31 miles) east of Kabul, and thrust north towards Bagram military airbase, 50 km (31 miles) north of the capital.Sept 26: Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the capital Kabul with forces
15491 of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city, witnesses said.</
15492 Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia captured the government's main airbase at Bagram, north of the capital Kabul, on Thursday night, Taleban sources in Pakistan said. The sources, quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) service, said troops loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani were fleeing northwards.The militia forces also captured
15492 Kabul's diplomatic Wazir Akbar Khan district at night and were battling government troops near the presidential palace in the centre of the capital.Earlier, Taleban sources in Pakistan said the militia had captured Kabul's disused Khwaja Rawash airport and the Soviet-built Microrayon housing district.</
15493 Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the beleaguered capital Kabul on Thursday with forces of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city.Kabul resembled a ghost town soon after night fell, with government checkpoints abandoned and small groups of soldiers trudging through otherwise deserted streets
15493 away from front lines on the city's eastern side.Some civilians fled the city on the road north earlier in the day in dozens of trucks and buses. But with a curfew in force, most Kabul citizens sat tight in their homes.In the Wasir Akbar Khan diplomatic quarter, small groups of
15493 residents came onto the streets to burn posters of President Burhanuddin Rabbani and his military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.The Taleban has taken control of most of Afghanistan since it launched a drive to oust Rabbani and plans to enforce a strict Islamic order in Afghanistan.There was no evidence its fighters
15493 were advancing into the city but there seemed little to stop them. They had earlier penetrated to within five km (three miles) of the presidential palace.I drove shortly before nightfall through desolate streets virtually devoid of traffic. The security ministry building had been abandoned and stood empty.Eyewitnesses reported seeing six
15493 government tanks and a number of trucks laden with Rabbani's soldiers heading north out of the city on one of the few roads still open.With Kabul in darkness and no electricity, there were few signs of fighting, with only sporadic exchanges of machine-gun and small arms fire heard from the
15493 edges of the city.There was no indication whether Rabbani and Masood were still in the city which their forces had held doggedly for months against a siege by Taleban with artillery and rockets lodged in the mountains that surround Kabul.The city itself had been calm earlier on Thursday with shops
15493 and markets open.The 15-nation U.N. Security Council appealed for a ceasefire and peace talks after a meeting in New York on Wednesday.The Taleban's gains appeared to come fast. Earlier in the day the beleaguered government's spokesman Amrullah had told reporters it would establish defences "in every street"."We are defending the
15493 country's pride against Pakistani puppets. Pakistan wants to control our country," he said.Pakistan denied the accusations.But an Afghan aid worker said: "The Taleban are coming, one hundred percent."It was not clear if the Taleban had seized control of a new road to the government's main airbase at Bagram, north of
15493 Kabul. The old road to Bagram was earlier still in government hands.An official of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Jan-Luc Paladini, said there had been hundreds of dead and wounded on both sides in the past two days.The ICRC on Thursday stopped all flights from Bagram to
15493 the Pakistani city of Peshawar after evacuating 50 people, including 16 ICRC delegates, leaving only staff needed for emergencies.Before night fell, government troops had feverishly dug new positions in the prestigious Mickroryan housing district in eastern Kabul while tanks made defensive manoeuvres.But Taleban sources in Pakistan later said the militia
15493 had entered Mickroray area and were battling government forces there. There was no independent confirmation of this report.</

15497 Hundreds of thousands of Hindu devotees bid a noisy farewell to the elephant god Ganesha on Thursday by immersing his idols in the sea.Beating drums and dancing along the crowded roads of India's commercial capital Bombay, devotees made their way to scores of beaches for the climax of a 10-day
15497 festival.The immersions celebrate the birth of Ganesha, the son of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction and his consort Parvati."Ganapati bappa moriya (long live Lord Ganesha)", chanted the devotees amid ear- shattering blasts from fire-crackers.Ganesha came in all shapes and sizes, from tiny idols carried on the heads of
15497 devotees to giants weighing a few tonnes that required trucks to haul them.There was Ganesha dancing on the hood of a snake, another sitting on a lotus and another as a manifestation of Lord Vishnu, the allusions drawn from Hindu mythological lore.Saffron flags atop the trucks carrying the idols fluttered
15497 in the evening sea breeze, spreading a mild fragrance from the marigold flowers showered by devotees.At the main immersion site, Chowpatty Beach in south Bombay, police set up scores of lifeguard towers."It's all quiet," said a fire brigade official. "We are only worried that some devotees might come drunk and
15497 wander into the sea," the official said.Two speed boats cruised along at a distance as the devotees waded into the sea with the idols. Helicopters hovered overhead.The state of Maharashtra, of which Bombay is the capital, declared a holiday and most private businesses closed early to help them avoid traffic
15497 jams during the processions.The authorities banned the sale of liquor and ordered the closure of all bars across the state for the day.Chowpatty Beach resembled a carnival with shops, food stalls, and children's rides.As darkness descended on the city, the floodlights at Chowpatty gave the atmosphere a mythological aura."Pudcha varshi
15497 lowkar ya (come early next year)," the devotees chanted as they bid their god a fond farewell.--Bombay Newsroom +91-22-265-9000</

15529 Thursday.Bhatia said HLL had passed on to customers the benefits it received from excise relief on its products.India's two federal governments had in the past three years lowered excise duties on consumer products, including soaps and personal products, under a liberalised economic programme.HLL, a subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever
15529 Plc, is a market leader in some brands of soaps, detergents and personal products. 15529 percent growth in 1996, he said.Bhatia said a surge in demand for consumer products in rural India in the wake of widespread monsoon rains could further help Hindustan Lever's performance in the current year.India is a predominently agricultural country, where a satisfactory monsoon normally leads to a good harvest of

15529 to live with them," she said. 15529 future.HLL is expected to emerge as India's largest food and consumer products firm with the planned merger of Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd, another Unilever subsidiary in India, by December.</

15536 ended in May.An Indian expatriate businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, alleges Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in a failed attempt to secure a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured him at a meeting
15536 in a New York hotel that his "work would be done".Rao has said he is innocent and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.The two other accused, Chandraswami and his personal assistant, are currently in judicial custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison located

15538 late last year."Up till then, banks were taking one day at a time cushioned by fat profit margins," said Mangala Boyagoda Treasury Manager of Union Bank of Colombo."But high rates forced banks to adopt scientific treasury management and take steps to hedge positive and negative gaps," he said.A flurry of
15538 new savings schemes have been launched by banks so far this year while a growing number of companies rushed to cut exposure to short-term debt through debentures, floating rate notes and certificates of deposit and securitisations.The average call money rate in the last quarter of 1995 skyrocketed to 30.9 percent,
15538 against an overall 1995 average of about 20, after the government's defence spending exceeded budget by 10 billion rupees ($178.6 million) following an end to a truce in its war with separatist Tamil rebels.The problem was compounded by two development banks which resorted to short-term funds due to delays in
15538 sourcing longer term credit lines, dealers said."Necessity was the mother of invention. 15538 management has pushed down money market rates, despite the government's continued heavy defence expenditure which is expected to again overshoot budget by 10 billion rupees this year, dealers said."The average money rate from January to August 1996 was 13.8 percent. 15538 savings scheme.
