15884 One hundred days into the new Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu, hopes for Arab-Israeli peace have been replaced by the old fears of Middle East war and the bloody suppression of Palestinian protests.As the Palestinian death toll mounted on Thursday in clashes triggered by the Israeli prime minister's decision to
15884 open a tunnel in Jerusalem adjacent to Islam's third holiest site, the question shifted from the health of the peace process to whether it still exists.Foreign governments appealed for a resumption of the peace talks begun five years ago but the violence racking the Palestinian lands occupied by Israel in
15884 1967 looked eerily reminiscent of the intifada -- the Palestinian uprising against Israeli rule that began in 1987 and did not officially end for nearly six years."Whoever is in a position of leadership...should calm passions and not inflame them. He should return to the negotiating table and not preach violence,"
15884 Netanyahu said in France on Wednesday night as the toll grew.The problem is what Netanyahu puts on the negotiating table is markedly less than what Arabs and Israelis were discussing under the Labour-led government that the Likud party leader defeated last May.Palestinians see the opening of a second entrace to
15884 a tunnel in the Moslem quarter of Jerusalem's Old City during the night, as symbolic of his approach to negotiations. The previous government had bowed to Arab objections about a tunnel built to show the foundations of the wall around the Temple Mount -- the site 2,000 years ago of
15884 the Jewish temple but home for the past 1,300 years to the al-Aqsa mosque.The tunnel, seen by the Arab world as a further tightening of Israel's grip over the city occupied in the 1967 Middle East war, was the fuse that ignited a power keg of other Palestinian grievances accumulated
15884 under Netanyahu.Palestinians, abandoning their quixotic quest for regaining all of pre-Israel Palestine, joined the U.S.-driven peace talks in Madrid in 1991. Their gains under Israel's Labour government were modest, but they were driven on by the hope that the process would end in full independence with East Jerusalem as their
15884 capital.Even before he took office in June, Netanyahu made clear that would never happen under him. Rather than begin "final status" talks to address those issues, he has failed to implement even agreements signed by the previous Israeli government. Jewish settlement of occupied Arab land has accelerated.Instead of the economic
15884 gains they expected, Palestinians have seen unemployment and poverty soar as investment failed to materialise and Netanyahu kept severe restrictions on them reaching jobs inside Israel.Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, risking the support of his own people by cracking down on Palestinian opponents of peace with Israel, was ignored by Netanyahu
15884 until early this month. When the current violence erupted, Netanyahu first called Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, not Arafat.Hopes for broader Arab-Israeli peace look no healthier. Even countries that moved closer to Israel in the five years of peace talks have grown increasingly critical of Netanyahu's policies, above all his rejection
15884 of the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace that was the basis for the negotiations.Arab governments, even in Jordan which signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994 and has since become the Jewish state's closest Arab friend, know Netanyahu's 100 days in office is likely to have
15884 reinforced existing popular suspicions about Israeli goals in the peace process.Israel-Syrian talks made little headway under the previous Israeli government, but the sporadic negotiations have now been replaced by warnings that the alternative to peace is another war. Both Syria and Lebanon have moved forces closer to Israeli troops occupying
15884 Syria's Golan Heights and a "security zone" inside Lebanon.Netanyahu has rejected Syria's key demand for peace, withdrawing the previous government's offer to return at least part of the Golan Heights, which was captured along with the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip in 1967.As prospects for Middle East
15884 peace disintegrate, U.S. President Bill Clinton is under pressure to act despite his reluctance to alienate Netanyahu in the final weeks of a U.S. presidential election where he wants the Jewish vote.That pressure is also reminiscent of an earlier time. The United States, after years of relative inactivity, was pushed
15884 back into seeking Middle East peace in the late 1980s by the bloody televised images of the intifada.</

15895 Kuwaiti women run businesses, head diplomatic missions and help to steer the country's oil industry but when Kuwaitis go to the polls on October 7, they won't take part.Women are barred from running for parliament or even voting.Activists for women's rights have renewed their 30-year campaign for what some --
15895 including Moslem traditionalists -- see as a right guaranteed by Kuwait's constitution and Islam.They have called on women to stay home from work on Sunday in a demand for political rights."Why don't you, citizen sister, express your objection to discrimination practised against you? Join us in the work strike day,"
15895 the activists said in a statement.Campaigners have had to fight on two fronts -- to lobby men for the right to vote while persuading women to back their struggle."A woman should stay home and raise children," said one angry bedouin of demands by Kuwaiti women for political rights.Denying women the
15895 right to vote is among the few things that unite Kuwaiti politicians -- for now at least. Many liberals are concerned that if women were allowed to vote, Islamists would increase their strength in parliament.They say Moslem traditionalists are better organised and women would vote for candidates picked by the
15895 man in the house."Women in Britain, for instance, were not given the right to vote until decades of democracy had passed," said liberal parliament member Abdul-Mohsen al-Mudej, a former oil minister.Western powers which helped liberate Kuwait in 1991 of an Iraqi occupation have praised democratic reforms introduced in Kuwait while
15895 urging the country to give women the right to vote."It is unfinished business," said a senior Western diplomat.During the Iraqi occupation the Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah said in exile he would consider allowing women to vote, adding that the issue required time.The debate was revived in 1992 when Kuwait's
15895 parliament was restored but both the assembly and the government appeared reluctant to introduce the reform.Women activists have held sporadic protests in Kuwait to demand political rights. In March about 40 woman lawyers, scientists and academics demonstrated outside parliament.Mona al-Ghareeb, a woman consultant at parliament and a university teacher who
15895 plans to join the strike on Sunday, told Reuters: "Political awarness among men was less in the past, now they are better. This is also true for women."Women now accept that they will not take part in the vote for the parliament which will take Kuwait into the next century
15895 but they are trying to woo candidates to support their cause in the new assembly.Few believe a post-election cabinet would include a woman, unprecedented in Gulf Arab states."Women's campaign to change their social and political situation will not pay if change was anticipated from the powers of darkness (hardline deputies),"
15895 wrote liberal columnist Naji al-Zaid."They have only one way: urge the Emir," he wrote in al-Qabas newspaper.</
15896 Turkey, facing energy shortages, is planning to open local tenders to have 44 more hydraulic power plants built in addition to 11 for which it invited tenders on Tuesday, an energy official said on Thursday."We will build those plants on the build-operate-transfer (BOT) model," said Mehmet Koyuncu, power affairs director
15896 at the energy ministry."Tenders have already been put out for the first 11 of them and those for the remaining 44 will be tendered later," he told Reuters, but did not say when.He said the plants would be small-size production units which local contractors can build in four years on
15896 average.Energy Minister Recai Kutan said Turkey's power demand would have risen by 12 percent this year, up from earlier estimates of eight percent, due to increasing number of industrial factories.Turkey has a power generation capacity of 105 billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) and is expected to produce 93.1 billion kWh against a
15896 demand of 97.5 billion.It began importing electricity from Iran to make up for shortfall in supply and talks on imports from Georgia and Bulgaria are underway.The BOT model, devised in the 1980s to finance big infrastructure projects through foreign-led consortia, hit bureaucratic snags after the constitutional court ruled that their
15896 finances should be inspected by the Council of State, which has delayed several big projects for years.The government earlier this year introduced another model, called build-operate (BO), only for thermal power plants to encourage industrial plants to build their own power plants.Officials said the 11 initial power plants would have
15896 a total established capacity of 2,688 MegaWatts (MW) and produce 9.29 billion kWh a year when completed.Koyuncu did not say how much the remaining 44 plants were planned to produce.Kutan said the government would break the ground for a 1,400-MW, 9.5-billion kWh gas-fired power plant near the industrial city of
15896 Bursa in the next two weeks.He said the plant, to be built by a consortium led by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, would cost about $550 million and be completed in two-and-a-half years.-- Ankara Newsroom +90 312 4462940</

15908 NASA's space endurance champion Shannon Lucid was homeward bound on Thursday as the shuttle Atlantis fired its braking rockets for a landing in Florida.Atlantis was scheduled to touchdown in Florida at 8:13 a.m. EDT (1213 GMT), bringing to an end the 75.2 million mile (121 million km) journey of NASA's
15908 space endurance champion.Flying backwards off the west coast of Australia, Atlantis skipper Bill Readdy fired the shuttle's braking rockets at 7:06 a.m. EDT (1106 GMT) to begin the hour-long descent through the atmosphere."Looked great to us up here too, and especially Shannon," radioed Readdy as mission control confirmed a sucessful
15908 burn."I bet she can taste those M&amp;Ms already," said spacecraft communicator Bill Gregory from mission control, referring to Lucid's favourite candy.The final leg of Lucid's journey would take her across the Pacific Ocean, reaching the coast of North America above British Columbia, Canada, close to Vancouver.The shuttle will enter U.S.
15908 airspace over North Dakota, gliding across the country, crossing the east coast of Georgia, before flying down the Florida shoreline and turning to land at Kennedy Space Centre.On its 10-day mission, Atlantis collected Lucid from the Russian space station Mir where she had spent six months in orbit, longer than
15908 any other woman and a record for an American astronaut.The 53-year-old mother of three was to ride home in a reclining seat to cushion her body against the tug of gravity. After six months in weightlessness, the space agency's doctors expect her to feel weak and woozy.Flight controllers required near
15908 pristine weather conditions for the landing because of the failure of one of three auxiliary power units shortly after Atlantis reached orbit on Sept. 16.The shuttle can land safely with just two of these devices but the loss of a second could place it in danger. Light winds and mostly
15908 clear skies were needed for Atlantis to land.The shuttle will be met on the runway by a team of doctors, nurses and paramedics in case Lucid should require medical attention after her 188-day stay in space.Atlantis spent five days linked to Russia's orbiting outpost. The shuttle crew transferred more than
15908 6,000 lbs of supplies to and from the station and left behind Lucid's replacement, John Blaha.Blaha, a 54-year-old former Vietnam veteran, is due to spend four months aboard Mir. Atlantis will return in January to retrieve him.</
15909 Police in riot gear on Wednesday broke up an unruly demonstration at a suburban university campus against a visit by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke for a debate on affirmative action.Several people were arrested at California State University at Northridge after about 200 protesters opposing Duke clashed with
15909 a smaller group of his supporters, police said.Dozens of police officers, some on horseback, used batons and "flash-bang" percussion devices to disperse the crowd after fighting erupted outside the student union building where Duke and Los Angeles civil rights activist Joe Hicks held a public debate.A few demonstrators pelted police
15909 with rocks, and several people were injured. "Go home, KKK," some protesters chanted. "Death to fascists," one woman yelled.Duke, an avowed white supremacist who has served in the Louisiana legislature and made unsuccessful bids for the U.S. Senate, was in Los Angeles to speak out against affirmative action -- programmes
15909 that give preference to women, blacks and other minorities in hiring, education and business.But the visit by Duke, who was invited and paid an appearance fee by the university's student government, angered many students and minority activists opposed to giving him a forum to express his views.Some of the harhest
15909 criticism of Duke's appearance came from supporters of Proposition 209, the Nov. 5 California ballot initiative that calls for outlawing affirmative action programmes by state and local government agencies. Backers of the measure say Duke was invited as a ploy to discredit the initiative through association with his extremist views.Inside
15909 the college auditorium, the debate was briefly interrupted when a man charged the stage shouting "racist" at Duke. Police grabbed the protester and removed him.Speaking to an audience of more than 500, Duke claimed affirmative action "discriminates against white people in jobs, promotions, scholarships, college admissions and loan programmes."But Hicks
15909 responded with ridicule. "It's the cry of every unqualified white guy who ever gets aced out of a job because they don't want to admit that out there are some minority folks and some women who've got better qualifications," he said.</
15910 U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen on Wednesday hailed a significant improvement in Sino-U.S. relations after a long period of tension over trade, Taiwan and human rights.Christopher, noting it was his third meeting with Qian in the last five months, said their frequent encounters
15910 "seem to me to have paid off in the marked improvement in our ties in recent months."Qian, appearing with Christopher at a brief news conference before the meeting on the fringes of a U.N. General Assembly session, agreed that there had been "positive progress" and that the atmosphere had "improved
15910 significantly."Only six months ago, the two nuclear powers were at loggerheads over Taiwan, Chinese sales of nuclear technology to Pakistan and piracy by Chinese companies of U.S. compact disks and computer software.But Qian noted that since then, a dispute over export of ring magnets -- used in making nuclear weapons
15910 -- to Pakistan had been resolved, intellectual property rights agreements had been reached and Washington had renewed China's most-favored nation trade status.U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord cautioned after the meeting that despite the upbeat tone, some problems between the two countries were far from bring resolved."We are not
15910 naive or complacent. We know there's difficult issues out there," he told reporters, mentioning specifically non-proliferation and human rights.As well as long-standing U.S. concerns over Chinese sales of missiles and nuclear power technology to Iran, recent U.S. press reports have said China is thought to have supplied Pakistan with technology
15910 to make M-11 ballistic missiles."They have made some progress, but there are remaining problems," Lord said. "There are continuing concerns about their dealings with Iran and Pakistan, and these refer to both nuclear areas and missile areas and even some conventional areas."On human rights, Lord said Christopher raised with Qian
15910 the release of people imprisoned for expressing their views, access to prisons and prisoners and the situation in Tibet, which the United States recognizes as part of China.The Christopher-Qian meeting came one day before U.S. and Chinese trade officials meet in Washington to follow up a June agreement aimed at
15910 resolving a long dispute on intellectual property rights.Christopher told journalists it was "critically important that China implement these new agreements."Qian said remaining problems included Taiwan, although tensions which reached a peak last March during presidential elections on the island -- considered a renegade province by Beijing -- have abated.Lord said
15910 Qian raised U.S. arms sales to Taiwan, with which Washington has only unofficial relations.Lord said Qian sounded a conciliatory note over the British colony of Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule next July, in particular over the appointment of a new chief executive to succeed the present governor-general."He thought
15910 that the appointment, which he didn't in any way foreshadow ... would be reassuring to the people of Hong Kong and to the outside world," Lord said.Earlier, Qian dodged a question over Beijing's approach to the election of a U.N. secretary-general at the end of this year. Washington says it
15910 will not allow the current incumbent, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, to serve a second term.The Chinese minister said Beijing was satisfied with Boutros-Ghali, but was waiting to hear the views of the Organization of African Unity.If Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian, cannot be re-elected, first priority in finding a successor is expected to be
15910 given to another candidate from the African continent.</

15911 put on hold as a result."'Frasier' is currently on hiatus and will resume production in October," the statement said.There was no immediate word on how long Grammer would stay at the Betty Ford Centre near Palm Springs, California, which has provided treatment to numerous Hollywood celebrities trying to overcome alcoholism
15911 and drug addiction.Grammer, who plays a psychologist turned radio talk show host on the Emmy Award-winning show, was booked on suspicion of drunken driving after crashing his sports car outside his suburban Los Angles home last weekend.The 40-year old actor was hospitalized for a head injury sustained in the crash.
15911 He agreed to a blood-alcohol test but results have not yet been released, officials said. Prosecutors will decide later whether to charge him formally with drunken driving.Grammer has a history of substance abuse and has been convicted of drunken driving and cocaine possession."The producers and cast of 'Frasier', as well
15911 as Kelsey's friends and colleagues ... support his decision and wish him a speedy recovery," the show's statement said.</
15912 The United States on Wednesday mounted a frantic diplomatic effort to defuse a bloody Israel-Palestinian confrontation and urged both sides not to raise new issues that could scuttle fragile peace talks.U.S. officials were reported to be in constant touch -- making several phone calls an hour -- with the region
15912 into Wednesday night.Secretary of State Warren Christopher telephoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Paris and other senior U.S. officials spoke to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat as well as senior Israeli and Egyptian leaders.State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Christopher and Netanyahu "agreed that specific steps had to be taken
15912 to calm the situation. The prime minister told the secretary that he did have some ideas that he was going to put into play."Burns said he believed Netanyahu intended to leave Paris as soon as he could after official appointments on Thursday morning and return to Israel, cutting short a
15912 European trip.Later Christopher expressed "deep concern" over the bloody clashes in the West Bank and called on the two sides to return to the negotiating table.Christopher, in New York for the U.N. General Assembly, said he urged Netanyahu to calm the situation and officials said U.S. Middle East Coordinator Dennis
15912 Ross passed the same message to Arafat."We've been following the situation last night and today with deep concern," Christopher told reporters before a meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen."We have urged the parties to defuse the situation, to restore calm in the area -- that's what needs to be
15912 done now. They should return to the negotiating table and make progress on the significant issues before them," he added.White House spokesman Mike McCurry, with President Bill Clinton on a campaign trip in Philadelphia, said: "A return to violence and bloodshed is certainly not the way to deepen and nurture
15912 the peace process that has brought so much hope to both Arab and Jew."U.S. officials spoke after Israeli soldiers were reported to have shot to death at least seven Palestinians, wounded 300 others and fought running gun battles with Arafat's police in the town of Ramallah, north of Bethlehem.They were
15912 the bloodiest clashes in the West Bank since Palestinian rule began two years ago.The fighting began after Netanyahu opened a second entrance to a tunnel in Jerusalem near the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third-holiest shrine.Netanyahu said he merely implemented a previous Labour government decision because the
15912 new tunnel made an important archaeological site more accessible to tourists.The underground tunnel, with sensitivities for the whole Moslem world, provided a perfect vehicle to mobilise popular sentiment against Netanyahu's delay in implementing self-rule.Palestinians say Israel is trying to turn Jerusalem into a wholly Jewish city, letting Jews build there
15912 but not Arabs.Burns, in New York with Christopher, said: "The United States firmly believes that neither Israel nor the Palestinians should create other issues that can make the situation more difficult."U.S. officials tried not to get involved in the specifics of the tunnel dispute.But Burns said the clashes partly concerned
15912 "Jerusalem issues, religious issues, historical issues. The final status talks that have been agreed upon are the venue for those issues to be discussed, and our very strong view is that these issues will not be resolved on the street by either side."Jerusalem's future is a key issue to be
15912 decided in final status peace talks agreed to by Israel and the Palestinians as part of their 1993 Oslo peace accords which provided for Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza.</

15914 CHICAGO, Sept 25, Reuter - The number of hogs on U.S. farms is seen holding below year-ago levels for the rest of the year, but supplies may well increase in 1997, livestock market analysts said.The trend is expected to be confirmed by Friday's quarterly U.S. Agriculture Department Hogs and Pigs
15914 Report."The report will tell us that we have fewer hogs for the next six months but after that we should start to move toward at least as many or more hogs than we had the previous year," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp. USDA's data will be
15914 released Friday at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.Analysts' estimates for all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms as of September 1 averaged 96.2 percent of a year ago and ranged from 95.0 to 97.5 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94.0 to 99.0 and
15914 hogs kept for marketing averaged 96.5 percent of a year ago in a range of 95.0 to 98.0 pct.Analysts said breeding herd data will be the most scrutinized part of the report. Producers have appeared to be stabilizing the breeding herd recently by sending fewer sows to slaughter. Dan Vaught,
15914 analyst for AG Edwards, said that producers received higher prices for hogs since the last USDA quarterly report, which likely is sparking expansion plans."Expanding the breeding herd during the summer is not very hard because the breeding herd is always the largest at the end of June. They only need
15914 to retain some gilts and cull fewer sows to increase production," Vaught said.Cash prices have consistently been over $55 per hundredweight (cwt) and over $60 for a couple of months -- good incentive to expand, Vaught added. Farrowing intentions were also seen expanding which resulted in some estimates for third
15914 quarter farrowings to exceed 100 percent. This will influence hog supplies in the second quarter of 1997.Levitt noted that it was too late for producers to do anything about hog supplies in the final quarter this year and first quarter next year. However, they could increase production by the second
15914 quarter of 1997 which could boost hog supplies to or above the previous year's first quarter. Fourth quarter farrowings were also seen larger which will influence hog supplies next summer. September-November farrowing intentions estimates averaged 98.7 percent of a year ago in a range of 96.0 to 102.0 percent and
15914 December-February intentions projections averaged 99.9 percent in a range of 94.0 to 105.0 percent.Most analysts also expected the USDA to again make adjustments to previous reports based on slaughter rates not matching previous projections."The USDA may have to go back and do some revisions on the June report again because
15914 the slaughter numbers haven't matched up well, particularly with the weight breakdown from the last report," Vaught said."In June, hog slaughter was way down -- eight to ten percent at times -- and the weight breakdown basically implied a two- to three-percent reduction. Lately slaughter rates have been more than
15914 two to three percent below last year when the hog report implied some three to five percent below last year," Vaught added.--312-408-8720</

15926 U.S. municipal bond prices rose about 1/4 point Thursday morning after the August durable goods report dropped much more than expected, traders said.The U.S. Commerce Department said durable goods orders fell 3.1 percent last month. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast the figure would show only a 0.1 percent decline.Analysts
15926 said the figure might lend credence to the idea that the economy is slowing on its own, supporting the Federal Reserve's decision Tuesday not to raise interest rates.The Treasury market also registered its approval of the weak data. The long bond jumped more than 1/2 point following the number, moving
15926 the yield to 6.89 percent.Among actively traded municipal bonds, yields on Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were down five basis points to 5.83 percent.Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were down six basis points to 5.70 percent.But some market participants said they were leery
15926 of rallying off of one number. "We're peeking through the 6.90 level, which seems to be very uncomfortable every time we get there," said Richard Visconti, head of muni trading at W.R. Lazard &amp; Co.Visconti said the market will need to see a chain of several more market-friendly numbers if
15926 it hopes to maintain these levels.Debt futures also rose off the durable goods number. The December municipal contract was up 18/32 to 114-16/32, and the December T-bond was up the same amount to 109-25/32. That left the MOB spread unchanged from Wednesday's close at 151 ticks. 15943 Tropical Storm Isidore turned into a minimal-strength hurricane in the open Atlantic early on Thursday after its winds rose to 75 mph (120 kmh), the National Hurricane Center said.At 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT), Isidore was located about 725 miles (1160 km) west-southwest of the Cape Verde Islands in the
15943 eastern Atlantic, at latitude 11.8 north and longitude 34.7 west.The storm was moving west-northwest at 15 mph (24 kmh) and was expected to strengthen, forecasters at the hurricane center said. It remained several days from land.Hurricane force winds extended outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the center.Isidore is
15943 the seventh hurricane to form this season in the Atlantic.</

15944 from the fees earned by Grigsby's firm, Grigsby Brandford &amp; Co, which was was senior manager for the recyling plant bond issue. 15945 Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported August durable goods fell 3.1 percent.U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.1-percent decline in orders.VINCENT MALANGA, LASALLE ECONOMICS, NEW YORK: "One might wonder if (Federal Reserve Board Chairman) Alan Greenspan had the number before we did."
15945 Malanga was referring to the central bank's decision earlier this week to keep short-term interest rates unchanged despite some signs of strength. Speaking on Reuters Financial Television, Malanga added that the data were healthy for the economy and were consistent with current quarter growth of around 2.0 percent.DAN SETO, SENIOR
15945 ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "Transportation was especially soft this month ... ex-transportation, the estimate was down 1.6 percent, but you also did see softness in other areas. As far as the (Treasury) market is concerned, this can be taken as one sign that the economy may be
15945 moderating, but we discourage people from reading too much into one month's ... orders." JOHN CANAVAN, TREASURY MARKET ANALYST, STONE &amp; MCCARTHY RESEARCH ASSOCIATES INC: "All in all, it looked pretty weak, even the details. It didn't look strong and the (Treasury) market has obviously reacted that way. Coming on
15945 the heels of the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged, it really just continues to add to the very positive tone in the market at the moment. I know that aircraft orders were down and we were looking for that to be the case after very strong aircraft orders last
15945 month."Those who want it to lend credence (to the Fed decision) will see it that way, but we have to see a lot more data." IRWIN KELLNER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CHASE REGIONAL BANK:"Durable goods are a volatile figure. But it clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum, and that growth
15945 in the third quarter is going to come in only a fraction of what it was in the second quarter, and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day."It looks pretty widespread. Commercial aircraft, motor vehicles and parts were down, and this
15945 drop of 3.0 percent was clearly many times what was expected," he added. Kellner continued: "If you take transportation, it was down 1.5 percent. So, it is pretty clear this was a weak figure even allowing for the volatility. That, in combination with lack of inflation in most parts of
15945 the economy, suggests that the Fed did the right thing."MICHAEL STRAUSS, EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT AND CHIEF ECONOMIST, YAMAICHI INTERNATIONAL (AMERICA) INC: "It reverses the upside surprise we had in the month of July. After being about 2.0 (percentage points) stronger than expected, it's now about 2.0 (percentage) points weaker." Strauss
15945 went on: "The biggest areas of weakness are the auto and aircraft components. The aircraft component is not going to be an area that's sustainable."The durables have been so erratic for a while that it's hard to get too excited about one month. The pattern for durables has been very
15945 strong this year."(In August) over the past eight years, the numbers have ranged from down 5.0 or 6.0 percent to up about 13.0 percent. August is a highly volatile month for the seires, (and) the series itself is highly volatile." TIM MCGEE, CHIEF ECONOMIST, TOKAI BANK LTD: "It shows that
15945 the signs of strength we were seeing in orders were a mirage. It confirms (Greenspan's) view that the economy is slowing down. So, it would therefore be a mistake to raise rates now because if the economy is slowing down, he may need to lower them some time next year."MICHAEL
15945 ENGLUND, CHIEF ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL: "Non- defense capital goods numbers are quite weak. Non-defense was down, too. So the concentration of the orders weakeness in the non-defense capital goods sector should help the bond market." Englund added: "For the economy in general, it suggests further evidence that we may be
15945 seeing some slowing in economic activity through the end of the year ... The fact that we see fairly widespread declines in the orders and the shipments data and the concentration of weakness in the non-defense capital goods is a good sign for bonds."CARY LEAHEY, SENIOR FINANCIAL MARKET ECONOMIST, LEHMAN
15945 GOVERNMENT SECURITIES: "If you take out transportation, it's still down only 1.6 percent, but you've shifted the trend ... way back so the market's treating it very favorably.""This suggests you could get a number on (Gross Domestic Product) below or well below 2.0 percent, maybe close to 1.5 percent. So
15945 that, combined with the (rise in jobless) claims is all very favorable for the front end of the curve."-- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660</

15954 After 188 days in orbit, NASA's space endurance champion Shannon Lucid returned to earth on Thursday aboard shuttle Atlantis.The $2 billion reusable spaceship touched down at Florida's Kennedy Space Center at 8:13 a.m. EDT (1213 GMT), bringing to an end Lucid's record-breaking, six-month mission to Russia's space station Mir. On
15954 its 10-day flight, Atlantis collected Lucid from the Russian space station Mir where she had spent six months in orbit, longer than any other American and a record for a woman of any nationality.The 53-year-old mother of three rode home aboard Atlantis in a reclining seat to cushion her body
15954 against the tug of gravity. After six months in weightlessness, the space agency's doctors expected her to feel weak and woozy.Blaha, a 54-year-old former Vietnam veteran, replaced her aboard Mir where he is due to spend four months.</
15955 The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) could issue a final ruling on ValuJet Inc's resumption of flight service by the end of this week, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Thursday.The newspaper quoted an aide to U.S. Rep. Mac Collins of Georgia as saying that this week was "looking good" for
15955 a final ruling from the government.ValuJet officials were not available for comment on the report. ValuJet was forced to suspend operations in June amid a swarm of alleged safety violations discovered in the aftermath of the May 11 crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades, which left 110 people
15955 dead.The DOT tentatively appoved ValuJet's restart on August 29, the same day the Federal Aviation Administration returned the airline's operating certificate. The department then allowed 11 days for objections and company responses and has spent the last two weeks in review. The Association of Flight Attendants, some relatives of Flight
15955 592 victims and at least one stockholder have lodged objections, arguing that the airline should not be allowed to fly except with new top management.The newspaper said DOT officials rejected that demand in their tentative approval but were obligated to consider any additional issues raised.Earlier this week, ValuJet executives told

15965 annual payout to state residents from the 20-year-old fund, built with oil revenues and investment income.Distribution of dividend checks is scheduled to start early next month. More than half the of recipients are expected to receive their payments in direct deposits to their bank accounts, fund officials said.The total dividend
15965 payout will be $613.3 million, according to Permanent Fund financial reports.Until this year, the highest dividend payout was the first, totaling $1,000 for each recipient. 15965 in assets, according to the annual report issued Wednesday.Almost all year-round Alaskans, including children, are eligible to receive fund dividends. 15965 annual disposable income for the state's "least fortunate families."Annual spending of dividend proceeds creates 8,000 jobs in the state, Condon said."For many of us, the dividend enriches our lives in many ways," he said.</

15971 The global economy has shaken off weakness in Western Europe and is expected to achieve healthy growth through next year, the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday.The IMF, in its semiannual report card on the economy, gave good grades to the emerging market countries, saying they are reaping the benefits
15971 from an often-painful return to fundamentals undertaken in recent years."The global economic expansion is expected to continue at a satisfactory pace in 1996-97 and over the medium term," the IMF report said.In a briefing on the report, IMF chief economist Michael Mussa told reporters, "We expect a moderate strengthening and
15971 continued good performance on the inflaiton front."The report by the international lending agency estimated the global economy would grow by 3.8 percent this year and 4.1 percent in 1997 after growing 3.5 percent in 1995.Industrial countries were expected to grow 2.3 percent this year and 2.5 percent in 1997 after
15971 growing 2.1 percent last year.Developing countries also showed vigorous activity, growing 6.3 percent this year from 5.9 percent in 1995. Growth will slow slightly next year to 6.2 percent.The report said the industrial countries showed uneven results. The the United States chalked up robust growth and low unemployment but Germany
15971 and France lagged behind.However, it said the outlook for Europe was improved as exchange rates came back into line, setting the stage for increased activity."Together with a correction of earlier exchange rate misalignments, this has improved prospects for a resumption of stronger growth in the latter part of 1996," the
15971 report said.It said the entrenched inflation that has stalked policy makers for years is finally on the run, but cautioned officials to guard the exit in case price pressures return with the strengthening economy."Inflation rates in industrial countries, as well as in a number of developing countries have declined to
15971 their lowest levels in decades," the report said. "Monetary authorities will, of course course, need to remain vigilant" regarding price pressures as growth continues or strengthens.As an example, it said the U.S. economy was growing flat out with low unemployment and would benefit from a tightening of monetary policy so
15971 inflation doesn't break loose.However, the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee decided to leave rates unchanged for now in its meeting Tuesday. Still the IMF projects short-term rates will rise about one-half of a percentage point next year.As it has in the past, the IMF scolded Europe for not taking the
15971 tough actions needed to reform its poorly functioning labour markets."For many countries, particularly in Europe, fiscal imbalances are related to shortcomings in the function of labour markets, which has resulted in a dramatic upward trend in unemployment over the past 25 years," the report said.It said that, although the Japanese
15971 economy has responded remarkably well to stimulative efforts by the authorities with growth estimated at 3.5 percent this year after edging up only 0.9 percent in 1995, it is probably too soon to move interest rates higher."But official interest rates will obviously need to be adjusted upward as the recovery
15971 gets further under way,"As a result, it estimated growth in Japan would moderate to 2.7 percent in 1997.Turning to Germany, which is estimated to grow 1.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent in 1997 after being up 1.9 percent in 1995, the IMF said the country had acted properly in
15971 easing monetary policy over the past year to help secure recovery.The report also made clear that the so-called transition economies of Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, which have often been the main focus of IMF policy makers in recent years, may have turned the corner. It estimated they
15971 would grow by 0.4 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1997 after five years of decline."The rewards for comprehensive reform and stabilisation efforts are very striking among the transition countries, where the results of economic transformation are increasingly visible," the report said.</

15975 With U.N. members now lining up to sign the landmark nuclear test ban treaty, the United States aims to keep pressure on key holdout India to reverse it's adamant refusal to join.Some U.S. officials insist this is a realistic goal despite New Delhi's seemingly intractable opposition to the pact. But
15975 more pessimistic experts worry that too heavy-handed a U.S. approach could backfire in ominous ways."We're only beginning to develop a longer-term plan (for India)," one administration official told Reuters. "But we can't let the pressure off. It has to be clear that there's a price in terms of self-isolation that
15975 they are paying."Assistant Secretary of State for Political-Military Affairs Thomas McNamara, meanwhile, told defence writers:"I don't know how its going to change, I don't know when it's going to change and in fact I cannot even be certain whether it's going to change. But I think there will be a
15975 number of internal and international pressures that will build on India to change its position."Under the terms of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which the United States and the other four nuclear powers signed on Tuesday in New York, the international community has two years to persuade India to come
15975 on board.India's signature is vital. The pact -- outlawing all atomic weapons tests -- cannot take effect with its monitoring provisions without ratification by the five nuclear powers, which also include Britain, France, China and Russia, and the three nuclear threshold states -- India, Pakistan and Israel -- deemed to
15975 be capable of building nuclear weapons quickly.New Delhi has declared unyielding opposition to the treaty, saying it undermines Indian sovereignty and preserves an elite nuclear "haves" club by not setting a date for disarmament.India took the unusual step of facing down the world by blocking the Conference on Disarmament in
15975 Geneva, which negotiated the treaty, from sending it to the United Nations for signing. But supporters still took the pact to New York.While India won in the obscure Geneva process, its isolation at the U.N., where only Bhutan and Libya joined New Delhi in opposing the treaty, prompted new soul-searching
15975 at home on whether the decision really served Indian interests.This suggests India may be more receptive to pro-treaty arguments. Washington has told India it will not be sanctioned but officials say there are "consequences."India is seeking a rotating seat on the U.N. Security Council later this year but almost certainly
15975 will not get it, in part because of its position on the test-ban pact, officials said. Japan is more likely to be given the seat.Also, U.S. officials say while India and the United States have recently improved ties, there could be even more economic and other cooperation if India signed
15975 the nuclear accord.President Bill Clinton addressed one of India's main concerns in a U.N. speech on Tuesday by reasserting his aim to negotiate with Russia deeper cuts in their nuclear arsenals.There is no date set for such talks and one is unlikely until the START 2 arms reduction treaty, languishing
15975 in Moscow, is ratified by the Russian parliament.George Perkovich, an arms expert and director of the non-profit W. Alton Jones Foundation in Charlottesville, Virgina, agrees a new intense debate is raging in India over the treaty but told Reuters "it is extremely unlikely India is going to sign" this treaty.The
15975 debate pits Indians who now want to pursue a nuclear programme with vigour, including testing, versus those who say the test ban treaty loss isolated India and testing should not go forward.The two sides reflect a fundamental strategic choice."Does India concentrate on becoming a major international power through its economic
15975 power (which means you don't test nuclear weapons or deploy missiles because there is an economic cost to that) or does it become a major power the way other major powers did -- through military capability," Perkovich said.Most Indian prime ministers have viewed economic progress as the best route. But
15975 Perkovich said provocations by China or Pakistan or excessive U.S. pressure on India could force New Delhi to launch an atomic test or deploy the Prithvi missile.U.S. officials do not expect India to test but are worried about possible new missile deployments. "Right now the goal is to make sure
15975 India doesn't exacerbate the situation," one official said. The next step is to defuse tensions with Pakistan and finally to "go down a different path that's going to make it easier for India to sign the treaty," he said.</

15987 the rocket's capacity to launch double satellite payloads into Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)," Jean-Marie Luton, director of the European Space Agency (ESA), told a news conference."We will launch two instrument platforms that represent satellite masses," Luton told a news conference in Paris broadcast to the ESA launch centre in French
15987 Guiana.In a major setback for the European space programme, the first Ariane-5 exploded less than 40 seconds after lift-off on June 4. It was carrying an uninsured payload of four scientific satellites with a value of $500 million.Specialists in Kourou said that the "dummy" satellites would cost less than $3
15987 million.An inquiry board investigating the explosion concluded in July that the failure was caused by software design errors in the rocket's inertial reference guidance system.The explosion was a major setback for Western Europe's effort to maintain its position as leader in launching commercial satellites, and to launch eventually a manned
15987 mission aboard Ariane-5 for Europe's participation in the international space station Alpha.The Paris-based Arianespace company that launches the Ariane rocket series said it would make an additional order for more flight proven Ariane-4 rockets.The company had plannned to phase out gradually use of Ariane-4 and use exclusively Ariane-5 by the
15987 year 2000."This transition period has now become delicate. We have taken the decision to order more Ariane-4 rockets," Arianespace president Charles Bigot said."I cannot now give you an exact number but I would estimate it to be about five or six to meet the demands of our clients scheduled for
15987 launch in 1999," he added.Arianespace has on order 22 more Ariane-4 rockets and 14 Ariane-5 rockets to service a customer backload of 42 heavy satellites to launch worth an estimated $4.1 billion.It was scheduled to begin using Ariane-5 for its customers in early 1997 but that will now be delayed
15987 for at least a year.</

15993 the Chamber is getting mixed up in this."He said that he hoped to finish his three-year term as head of the Chamber in the spring.But Veyrat, whose restaurant in Veyrier-du-Lac is threatened with closure because of huge debts, said Blanc and Ducasse aggravated the dispute by pointing to the debts

15993 criticised as too innovative included a vegetable ravioli that omitted pasta and use of verbena sauce with a poularde fatted chicken."A traditional recipe in France is poularde with tarragon. Verbena doesn't taste much different, does it?" he said.</
15994 European Union justice ministers, reacting to a Belgian child-murder and sex scandal, on Thursday agreed to extend the scope of the EU's police agency Europol so it could help fight the sex trade in children and women.Irish Justice Minister Nora Owen said the ministers, meeting for a two-day session in
15994 Dublin, reached political agreement on the plan to extend the mandate of the Europol Drugs Unit to cover this kind of crime."We intend to fight against the work of criminals in the trafficking of people in the same way as we fight against drugs trafficking," Chief of the Hague-based agency
15994 Juergen Storbeck told reporters after the agreement was made.The agreement, which includes a move to exchange police officers throughout the EU and set up centres to fight the sex trade will be formalised at another meeting of EU ministers.EU members, traditionally reluctant to increase the EU's crime-fighting role, were stung
15994 into action after the discovery of the bodies of four murdered girls in Belgium highlighted the world trade in child sex and pornography."I'm very impressed. In the 20 years I've been in the business I've never seen such speed of agreement," Storbeck said.Storbeck said the agency, which already helps fight
15994 drugs trafficking and money laundering, could help speed up exchanges of information between different police bureaux in the 15-nation EU and carry out strategic analysis.With Europol's help information on missing children and people suspected of abducting them could be exchanged between criminal, customs and border police in less than an
15994 hour.The agency could help coordinate parallel investigations in different member states, he said.Over the next few weeks Europol officers would meet to try and identify problems in international cooperation and develop new methods of fighting the crime."This will lead to a common action plan to be given to ministers for
15994 possible agreement this year or the beginning of next year," he said.But Storbeck urged ministers to ratify the Europol convention urgently so the agency could pool and analyse information via its central computer.He stressed the agency, which employs 115 officials, could not instigate and carry out investigations on its own,
15994 but could only back up work done by national police agencies."We are only a support unit and if they request support we give that support," he said, adding it was not yet clear exactly how many new staff Europol might need to carry out its new role.</

15996 U.S. Secretary of Defence William Perry, shrugging off Russia's virulent opposition, said on Thursday that NATO's expansion to take in former communist enemies would go ahead next year."At a summit next year several countries will be invited to start accession talks," he told reporters after a two-day informal meeting of
15996 the alliance's 16 defence ministers.Perry declined to be drawn on which countries may be invited to join the alliance, but emphasised the process would go ahead despite Russian objections which he maintained were unfounded."If I thought that those actions (expansion) were threatening Russia I would have a very different view,
15996 but I don't believe that for a minute," Perry said.Since the end of the Cold War, ex-Communist countries have been seeking to join NATO to guarantee their future security against Russia. Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are the most likely candidates, but could be joined by Slovenia.NATO hopes to
15996 buy off Russia by offering it a new all- embracing security pact which it says it will negotiate in parallel with its first enlargement since the late 1970s.Perry said he would bring up that issue in talks later on Thursday with his Russian counterpart Igor Rodionov which he said would
15996 also centre on how to build on Russia's landmark cooperation in the alliance-led peace mission in Bosnia.NATO is also hoping it can entice Russia to take part actively in the alliance's Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme designed to try and fill a security vacuum in central and eastern Europe created
15996 by the collapse of communism.The alliance wants to upgrade PFP and offer it as an alternative to countries left out of next year's expansion, but which still want an insurance policy against a rebirth of an expansionist Russia."What we are doing with NATO and what we are doing with Partnership
15996 for Peace is creating a security circle for all of Europe... our goal is not to threaten Russia, but to bring Russia into that security circle," Perry said.NATO diplomats say the aim is to try to dovetail approval of both enlargement and a new pact for Russia at next year's
15996 heads of government summit which would also endorse reform of the alliance's command structures.But if that was not possible, Perry made clear that enlargement would go ahead anyway."There is a very important principle here, we are open to new nations that are qualified and want to join. We believe that
15996 is a very important principle," Perry said.Germany's Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said there was a consensus on the need to move ahead with expansion, but said it could be done without alienating Moscow. "The time is ripe for a decision to be made at next year's summit," he told reporters,
15996 but he said that left plenty of time to reach a "new strategic partnership between a new NATO and a new Russia."Alliance Secretary-General Javier Solana earlier said the two-day meeting had also made considerable progress towards establishing a "leaner, more efficient NATO" capable of undertaking Bosnia-style crisis-management tasks.France has indicated
15996 it will play a full part in any new NATO.Perry, citing Washington's naval and air commitment in the Mediterranean, ruled out handing the command post in southern Europe for rotation by European allies as requested by Paris.Solana said the alliance would also discuss in detail with Rodionov, Russia's participation in
15996 any follow-on force the alliance may send to Bosnia next year to continue policing the Dayton peace accords.Russia has already indicated it would be prepared to serve in that force, but the alliance is set to offer Moscow permanent liaison officers at several command levels to build on contacts created
15996 last year in organising the current force.</

15997 liver cirrhosis and viral inflammation of the liver," Vienna General Hospital said in a statement.A womaniser and gambler who squandered vast sums at gaming tables across the world, Nicu was being groomed as his father's successor before a violent revolution toppled the Stalinist dictator in December 1989.Nicolae Ceausescu and his
15997 wife, Elena, were shot by firing squad on Christmas Day, ending their ruthless 24-year rule.Doctors in Vienna performed surgery last Friday to staunch bleeding from veins detached from his oesophagus. 15997 not been in need of a liver transplant as the organ had been functioning adequately. 16004 Economic reform pursued by Colombia over the past six years have boosted the politically- troubled Latin American country's integration into the world economy, the World Trade Organisation said on Thursday.In a report on Colombian trade policies, WTO analysts said the so-called "Apertura" trade liberalisation programme launched in 1990 had brought
16004 down tariffs and non-tariff barriers to imports and led to openings for foreign service providers.This nationally-initiated process had been given further impetus by wider commitments to opening up its previously highly-protected markets for goods and services taken on in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round world trade negotiations."The opening of the economy
16004 has created new investment oportunities, which should also be encouraged by improved macroeconomic stability, solid growth and ongoing fiscal reforms," the WTO analysts said.The agreements reached in the Round, held under the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), were finalised in a world treaty signed in Morocco in
16004 1994, clearing the way for the launch of the WTO to replace the GATT in 1995.Colombia, one of the major economies in Latin America, said in its own report to the WTO that since the organisation had started operations it had recognised the advantages it could offer to an emerging
16004 economy."We have perceived the benefits which may derive from a rule-based system and more precise disciplines, as well as from a strengthened dispute-settlement mechanism which can guarantee the effective functioning of the multi-lateral trading system," the Bogota government said.The rules of the WTO which prevent countries blocking rulings by neutral
16004 panels in trade disputes are widely seen by developing countries as giving them firmer ground than under the GATT to challenge the big trading powers.While very few small economies took complaints to the GATT, developing countries are involved in many of the over 50 disputes already brought to the WTO,
16004 encouraged by the very first panel ruling which found in favour of Venezuela against the United States.Many feel the big powers -- including the United States, Colombia's main trading partner, and the European Union -- have been slow to open up markets to their products while they have adapted national
16004 policies to the new overall trade rules.An echo of this came in the Colombian report.While Colombia was confident the benefits of the new world trading system would be shared, it said, this could be achieved "if the supply of exports from the developing countries such as Colombia is treated in
16004 the same way as products and services from developed countries."The WTO analysts noted that Colombia -- linked in the Andean Pact with Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela -- was looking for new agreements with Latin American partners which would bring an expansion of regional trade growth.But the country was also
16004 looking for trade opportunities beyond the region and was actively engaged in negotiations to establish a free trade area for the Americas.</

16033 Struggling European barge operators have welcomed steady rises in freight rates this year, but the improvements will not be enough to stave off major structural change in the industry, operators and analysts say.Backwardation, when current prices are higher than those in the future, has forced oil companies to draw down
16033 stocks and transport products at greater speed and with shorter notice.While oil tanking companies have suffered from the resulting lower stocks, barge operators have profited from the greater flexibility demanded by suppliers.The bustle of trading during the recent Iraq crisis combined with low Rhine water levels to push freight rates
16033 to their highest levels since last December and well above peaks in February and March.The prices were so high, at one point, that some product was moving to Switzerland from the Netherlands by train, operators said. In the past, barge operators say, freight rates have only risen sharply in winter
16033 when cold weather and a rush on products such as heating oil coincide.Even outside the busy periods, prices this year have risen, resulting in a higher minimum freight price."Compared with last year, the lower end of freight rates has increased," said Dutch oil consultant Pieter Kulsen who monitors Rhine shipping
16033 rates.However, the barge industry is still plagued by overcapacity, with about 1,600 barges plying between the Dutch and Belgian refineries and berths along the Rhine."The minimum prices are higher, but there are too many barges on the Rhine and throughout Germany. Prices today are just break-even. This is the fourth
16033 or fifth (consecutive) bad year," said Dick Heijstek of Otex, one of the largest barge charterers.The problems originated at the beginning of the 1990s when healthy rates led to new entrants and fresh barge construction. Fierce bargaining by oil companies product suppliers forced the many barge operators to reduce their
16033 rates."For many of the players, the rates at the moment are just enough to cover the interest on their debts," said a charterer at market giants Van Ommeren.The problems forced the European Union to extend its barge scrapping scheme for a further year in a Council directive issued this summer.The
16033 "old-for-new" scheme, as it is known, states that for every tonne of new shipping constructed, one and a half tonnes of old shipping must be scrapped.The European Union hopes the barge fleet will decline by five percent each year and thereby fall by a total of around 15 percent by
16033 the end of 1999. To encourage the move, the European Union injected 20 million Ecus for one year."The policy was endorsed in June of this year and should go some way to solving the problem of oversupply," said EU transport commission spokeswoman Sarah Lambert.Charterers agree capacity must be cut, but
16033 are sceptical of long-term success as the EU withdraws its involvement in the push towards complete market liberalisation by January 2000."(A capacity reduction of) 10 to 15 percent should be enough.... but when the prices increase, we risk returning to the problem (of overcapacity) again," said Heijstek.-- Amsterdam Newsroom, +31

16046 ordinary people.Decision makers were said by Eurobarometer to be elected politicians, senior civil servants, business or labour group leaders, media chiefs and leading academic or cultural figures.The survey questioned nearly 4,000 decision makers across the EU and the results were compared with a similar poll of ordinary people released last
16046 month.Some 63 percent of decision makers thought the EU did not play a big enough role in world affairs while 29 percent felt it had the right amount of influence.Ninety percent of decision makers thought their country had benefitted from EU membership compared to just 45 percent of ordinary people.Decision
16046 makers were more closely allied to popular opinion on the priorities facing the EU over the next decade with maintaining peace, fighting unemployment and combatting terrorism and drugs ranking high in both groups.But support for a single European currency varied significantly with 85 percent of decision makers either "for" or
16046 "somewhat for" the idea, compared to 54 percent of the public.Opinion varied greatly among member states on the worth of a single currency. Only 30 percent of decision makers from Britain -- which has an opt out of the scheme -- were "very much for" participation, although another 30 percent
16046 were "somewhat for".In contrast, some 93 percent of Luxembourg's decision makers were in favour of a single currency.The survey also revealed strong support by decision makers for a more important role for the European Parliament in the EU's decision making, although there was no comparison for ordinary citizens.Some 83 percent

16052 in late December. 16052 November 5 U.S. presidential election.Perry said the Clinton administration would consult Congress over the decision and several missions would be considered for a new force, including simply preventing war or a more expanded "stabilisation" of the current shaky peace in Bosnia.Stabilisation could focus on duties such as guaranteeing freedom of
16052 movement for civilians in Bosnia, Perry said. 16052 not to turn soldiers into a Bosnia police force, refused to take an immediate position on what a new military force should do."I do not want at this time to express a personal view, or certainly for that matter a United States view, on which of those missions is preferred,"
16052 he said."I want to see what the findings are from the military authorities, what the recommendations are from the Council (the North Atlantic Council of NATO). At that time, I will be prepared to make a recommendation to the President. But I am not at this time."But Perry stressed that

16056 European Union decision makers are at odds with ordinary citizens over the worth, role and future of the 15-nation bloc, a survey revealed on Thursday.A poll by Eurobarometer showed 94 percent of "decision makers" in the European Union thought EU membership a good thing, compared to just 48 percent of
16056 ordinary people.Decision makers were said by Eurobarometer to be elected politicians, senior civil servants, business or labour group leaders, media chiefs and leading academic or cultural figures. The survey questioned nearly 4,000 decision makers across the EU and the results were compared with a similar poll of ordinary people released
16056 last month.Some 63 percent of decision makers thought the EU did not play a big enough role in world affairs while 29 percent felt it had the right amount of influence.Ninety percent of decision makers thought their country had benefitted from EU membership compared to just 45 percent of ordinary
16056 people. Decision makers were more closely allied to popular opinion on the priorities facing the EU over the next decade with maintaining peace, fighting unemployment and combatting terrorism and drugs ranking high in both groups.But support for a single European currency varied significantly with 85 percent of decision makers either
16056 "for" or "somewhat for" the idea, compared to 54 percent of the public.Opinion varied considerably among member states on the worth of a single currency. Only 30 percent of decision makers from Britain -- which has an opt out of the scheme -- were "very much for" participation, although a
16056 further 30 percent were "somewhat for".In contrast, some 93 percent of Luxembourg's decision makers were in favour of a single currency.The survey also revealed strong support by decision makers for a more important role for the European Parliament in the EU's decision making, although there was no comparison for ordinary
16056 citizens.Some 83 percent felt the European Commission -- the EU's executive -- should resign without the majority support of the parliament, while 65 percent backed the idea of a European government responsible to parliament.</

16060 The European Court of Justice decided on Thursday lawyers benefitting from VAT exemptions in one member state are not entitled to a refund of VAT paid in another member state, according to Community VAT rules.A Belgian lawyer, Etienne Debouche, leased a car in the Netherlands. The car was used exclusively
16060 for professional activity in Belgium and Debouche asked the Dutch authorities for a refund of the VAT he paid.The Eighth VAT directive explicitly states that to qualify for a refund an individual must produce a certificate stating he is subject to VAT in his member state. Debouche produced a statement
16060 from Belgium that he was not subject to VAT in Belgium.The court noted the Eighth directive is not meant to circumvent VAT rules under the Sixth VAT directive, but only to eliminate discrepancies between member states' rules.The court said, "the Eighth directive must not lead to the treatment of taxable
16060 persons differing according to the member state in the territroy of which they are established."The court noted that if Debouche were to receive the refund, he would receive better treatment than Dutch lawyers.***EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT(Court translation into English. 16060 the member states relating to turnover taxes - Arrangements for the refund of value added tax to taxable persons not established in the territory of the country) is to be interpreted as meaning that the fact that a lawyer benefits, pursuant to article 28(3)(b) of the Sixth Council directive (No
16060 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment) and Annex F thereto, from an exemption in the member state in which he is established does not entitle him

16072 by mid-1997 a plan for harmonising the EU's approach to using radio frequencies and authorising the satellite communications systems that operate in the EU.The EU would act only if CEPT did not make satisfactory progress.Most member states objected to the original text because it would have authorised the Commission to
16072 draw up criteria for licensing operators and to play a major role in selecting the operators.The Commission argued that the EU needed to develop a united front, warning that the EU could be bound by decisions made elsewhere, especially the United States -- which has already licensed several personal communications
16072 systems that are poised to set up global operations by the end of the decade.They include Globalstar, led by U.S. companies Qualcomm Inc and Loral Corp; Iridium, led by the U.S.'s Motorola Inc; and Odyssey, with Canada's Teleglobe Inc and the U.S.'s TRW Inc.But EU governments argued that enough coordination
16072 already took place through organisations such as the CEPT and International Telecommunications Union and that no special EU effort was needed since the number of satellite networks would be small.The compromise text leaves the final decision to authorise satellite personal communications networks up to national governments. But it asks them
16072 to coordinate their procedures if the number of operators must be limited because of a shortage of frequencies.</

16091 prostate cancer patient in his mid-60s, became the world's first legally-assisted suicide when he was given a lethal injection under controversial mercy killing legislation introduced in July in Australia's Northern Territory.The Dutch Justice Ministry said the landmark death was unlikely to speed up government deliberations over whether to legalise euthanasia
16091 in the Netherlands, where some 1,500 cases of mercy killing are reported annually."We have our own legal proceedings and what happens abroad will not affect the decision-making here," a Justice Ministry spokesman said.Although technically illegal, euthanasia is tolerated under Dutch law if certain guidelines are followed.Doctors are virtually assured of
16091 freedom from prosecution if the patient was of sound mind, in unbearable physical or mental pain and had repeatedly asked for death.Before ending a patient's life, a doctor has to consult a second, independent physician. The whole process must be documented and reported under special disclosure procedures introduced in 1993.Public
16091 acceptance of euthanasia is widespread, with a poll earlier this year showing that 84 percent of Dutch people supported the practice to relieve unbearable and irremediable suffering.However death-on-demand campaigners say existing procedures do not give doctors sufficient legal protection, arguing successive administrations have interpreted the guidelines differently.As a result, they
16091 argue, patients in need are being refused the right to die by doctors fearful of prosecution.The current three-party coalition will review the need for new euthanasia legislation based on the outcome of an inquiry into existing reporting procedures.The report of the inquiry, due to have been presented in October, has
16091 been delayed until November, virtually ruling out the prospect of new legislation during the current cabinet term, the Justice Ministry spokesman said."The current administration has one and a half years to run, I think one can assume that there will be no new euthanasia law within that time," he said.If
16091 current euthanasia practice is legalised in the Netherlands, Dutch legislation will reach far beyond Australia's, where right-to-die laws extend only to the terminally ill.Dutch jurisprudence on the issue so far indicates doctors will legitimately be able to end the life of people who are not terminally ill or even physically
16091 infirm.In 1994 the Dutch Supreme Court upheld the right of a psychiatrist to end the life of a physically healthy woman who lost the will to live after she divorced and her sons died, ruling that unbearable mental suffering also constituted sufficient grounds for euthanasia.The scope of Dutch mercy-killing laws

16097 of bill should have been drawn up 25 years ago. 16097 it to the National Consultative Human Rights Committee, which will give its opinion later on Thursday.The bill would make anyone making a racist statement in public liable to one year in prison and a 300,000 franc ($60,000) fine. Sanctions would increase to two years in jail and a 500,000 franc
16097 ($100,000) fine if the remark were judged an incitement to discrimination, hate or violence.The bill also widens the scope of existing legislation to include statements aimed at "an ethnic group, a nation, a race or a religion" and lengthens the statute of limitations, currently at three months, to one year.Meanwhile,

16101 Following is the full text of the Alcatel Alsthom first half results' statement."On September 25, 1996, Serge Tchuruk, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, presented the first half 1996 results and reported the progress on Alcatel Alsthom's recovery plan to the Board of Directors.""During the first half, the Group registered income
16101 from operations of 0.5 billion francs compared with 1.4 billion francs in the first half of 1995 and a net loss of 0.4 billion compared with a loss of 1.2 billion in the corresponding period of 1995.""The Board of Directors noted that the results were in line with the action
16101 program and reflected the recent trends amd the still limited effects of the current recovery plan. The Board also noted that the effects of the plan, already noticable for the second half, enabled the Group to aim at a return to break-even for the whole year and to foresee a
16101 significant reduction in debt, taking into account the divestments already completed as of today."RESULTS AT JUNE 30, 1996"At the same time, the Telecom sector's activities have been repositioned towards high growth market segments thanks to a competitive product portfolio particularly adopted to the most recent market trends.""Activities during the first
16101 half were characterised by numerous commercial successes which, despite the market fall in undersea cables, resulted in a global increase of 3.8 percent in orders, which reached 81.5 billion francs. The growth was particularly strong in the Telecom sector.""Sales during the first half, which mainly reflected delivery of orders received
16101 in 1995, amounted to 74.3 billion francs, a decrease of 3.4 percent over the same period in 1995, on a comparable basis.""Income from operations amounted to 0.5 billion francs compared to 1.4 billion during the first half of 1995.""This decrease comes from the Telecoms sector for 0.6 billion and the
16101 Cables sector for 0.3 billion.""The Telecom sector's income from operations (-1.1 billion), declined compared to the first half (1995 - 0.5 billion). However, it shows an improvement over the second half 1995 (-2.8 billion or -1.3 billion excluding exceptional items) and should return to a postive level for the second
16101 half.""Income from operations in the Cables sector amounted to 0.9 billion francs. The decrease compared to the first half 1995 is due to the strong deterioration in the undersea cable activities."GEC Alsthom maintained its income from operations at 0.6 billion francs at the same level as in the first half
16101 of 1995, within the context of a power generation market still characterised by intense competition. Orders increased during the first half and major achievements were recorded in the rail transportation activities, notable in North America.""Income from operations in the "Systems" activities, while negative, did improve. The loss recorded in income
16101 from operations is entirely due to the integration of Alcatel Siete where restructuring is satisfactorily progressing.""Saft registered income from operations at approximately the same level as that of the first half 1995. The activities continue to grow, particularly in the high potential technological markets.""The increase of 0.8 billion in net
16101 income, is mainly due to a reduction in income tax and an increase in net income of equity affiliates.""During the first half and income tax credit of 0.1 billion was registered compared with a charge of 1.3 billion during the first half 1995. This difference is partly due to a
16101 decrease in income from consolidated companies, but mainly reflects an improved management of the Group's worldwide tax position, and the effects of recognizing tax consolidation in th year in which it occured, in compliance with international accounting standards.""In addition, net income of equity affiliates, which include notably the results of
16101 Havas, Framatome, Shanghia Bell, and Cofira (after exceptional items), increased from 0.1 billion in the first half 1995 to 0.8 billion in the first half 1996." PROGRESS OF THE RECOVERY PLAN"The plan announced a few months ago is progressing according to expectations.""Half of the 10 billion asset disposal program has
16101 been achieved. It should be completed in the coming months, which will result in a substantial reduction of the debt to equity ratio. This refocusing is complemented by the simplification of the Group's legal structure wherein the number of legal entities has already been reduced by more than 300, representing
16101 a third of the previous count.""The objective of achieving global savings of 7.0 billion francs per year by 1998 is maintained.""Restructuring measures, mainly concerning the Telecoms and Cable sectors, have become indispensable due to the radical changes occuring in the Group's economic environment. Since mid-1995, close to 20,000 job reduction,
16101 principally in Europe, have been announced or realized in these two sectors. The subsequent plans seeks all possible solutions to reclassify affected employees."Simultaniously, the Group has began a program to significantly reduce (by 10 billion francs) its gross operating assets as well as its administrative expenses which could allow annual
16101 savings of over 2.0 billion francs."TELECOM ACTIVITIES"The Group's Telecommunications activities sector has undergone significant changes during the last months, which deserve a special mention.""The first half 1996 was characterised by a clear resumption in orders (+21 percent) and of sales (+5 percent) despite a decrease in switching, which is due
16101 to a drop in prices, the shrinkage of some major markets, in particular France, and the significant decrease in exports to China, where local production has considerably increased.""To respond, the Group has reinforced its software and service offerings in switching for it to remain one of the major key elements
16101 of Alcatel's portfolio.""Conversely, the product portfolio is undergoing significant transformation, favoring sector with high growth potential: transmission, access systems, data netwroks, mobile infrastructure. Orders and sales will progress by more than 40 percent in 1996 in the field of transmission. This development is especially accelerating in the U.S. where sales
16101 have doubled over the last four years, passing the one billion dollar treshold this year.""Similarly, in access systems, where the market is expanding strongly (+ 20 percent per year) Alcatel will also register a growth in its orders and sales of over 40 percent in 1996.""The strategy of alliances and
16101 partnerships is being pursued, through cooperations with Sharp in the mobile handset activities, and with the signing of an agreement with Motorola regarding mobile communications infrastructure (CDMA and DECT standards) and for the cross supply of equipment"."All of these actions together should allow the Telecom business to regain a significant
16101 growth rate in the coming years (+5 to +10 percent per year)."-- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452</
