16116 Plans to set up a permanent international criminal court have been held up by haggling over just how independent it should be, experts and academics said.As the ad-hoc tribunals dealing with grave breaches of human rights in former Yugoslavia and Rwanda press ahead with their work, efforts to create a
16116 permanent successor to them are still bogged down with preliminaries."The major powers...are not ready to move at this stage towards the establishment of such a court. They all feel that it is premature and that it needs more time to mature politically," said Professor Cherif Bassiouni of DePaul University in
16116 Chicago.Bassiouni is vice-chairman of a U.N. committee set up to draft a statute for a permanent court to try individuals suspected of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.This preparatory committee has held two three-week sessions this year but Bassiouni said it had made little headway on core issues because
16116 some countries were bent on delaying the project.One big problem has been the relationship between the court and the powerful U.N. Security Council where Britain, China, France, Russia and the U.S. have permanent seats and a veto."The United States, the United Kingdom and France would like to have a court,
16116 but they would like to see it under the control of the Security Council," said Bassiouni."Then you have a core group of about 50 countries, mostly Europeans...who want a truly independent court."Bassiouni, speaking in a personal capacity, said the battle centred on whether the Security Council or an independent prosecutor
16116 would play the key role in launching prosecutions.He said he favoured complete independence of the proposed court from the Security Council, arguing that this would bring it into line with universally accepted principles of government."Everybody now recognises that the judiciary...should be independent of the political branch of government," he said.Professor
16116 Adam Roberts of Oxford University said U.N. members would remain wary of setting up a permanent criminal court until they could examine the small print."For example will Russia support an international criminal court if it might issue warrants against Russian officers involved in Chechnya? All states have skeletons in the
16116 cupboard that will make them nervous," he said.Roberts, editor of "Documents on the Laws of War", said the debate over who controls the process of prosecution made it unlikely that a permanent court would be set up soon: "I'm not particularly optimistic. I think it will take time."He said it
16116 was more likely that the ad-hoc tribunal in The Hague would undergo gradual expansion of its responsibilities to include crises occurring in other regions of the world.Bassiouni believes that a permanent court will eventually be established, though initially at least it might not be as independent and powerful as he
16116 would have hoped."I think it will probably be watered down, that's my fear... but it can be amended subsequently and we can enhance it."Bassiouni said the limited success of the Yugoslav and Rwanda tribunals in getting suspects into the dock had not reduced public support for international criminal prosecutions."People see
16116 that as a political impediment. They don't see it as an inherent weakness. I think that world public opinion is able to separate the wheat from the chaff," he said.Roberts said the two ad-hoc tribunals had inevitably run into problems as they were borne out of the Security Council's reluctance
16116 to take decisive action in Bosnia and Rwanda."They were something of a substitute for action...It's a classic problem of political theory that law without power is rather weak law and that's what we see with these tribunals."The U.N. General Assembly is due to review the project for a permanent criminal
16116 court in late October.Bassiouni hopes it will ask the preparatory committee to finish its work by April 1, 1998 so a diplomatic conference can be called to finalise the text of a treaty setting up the court.Nick Howen, head of legal affairs for London-based human rights group Amnesty International, urged
16116 U.N. members to press ahead and set up the court."The future of this court really hangs in the balance now. The 185 member states of the United Nations...have the power to make this court a reality," he said.</

16135 The Telecommunications Council has a good chance on Friday of reaching a political agreement on a regime for authorising and licensing telecoms operators in the post-liberalisation era, diplomats said.Ministers are expected to endorse a draft directive, COM(95)545, that would require governments to set up open and nondiscriminatory procedures for authorising
16135 companies to offer telecoms services or infrastructure once state monopolies are abolished.Most member states have accepted a compromise on the main conflicts -- when to require individual licenses as opposed to "general authorisations" -- and when governments can limit the number of those licenses, diplomats said.The new text would allow
16135 member states to require individual licenses for all companies offering voice telephone services or public networks.That goes beyond the Commission's proposal, which envisaged individual licenses only in certain cases, for example to allocate radio frequencies or numbers, grant access to land or impose public service obligations.It wanted governments to rely
16135 mostly on "general authorisation" schemes allowing all companies that comply with certain rules to set up business.But countries including France, Greece, Italy, Portugal and Spain fought to expand the use of individual licenses."Not all the liberal countries are happy (with the compromise), but we think they will come around," one
16135 diplomat said.The new text, however, rejected a bid by some countries to allow governments to limit the number of operators in a given sector because their markets are small.The ministers look set to agree only to allow limits if needed to ensure the efficient use of radio frequencies or --
16135 on a temporary basis -- because of a shortage of telephone numbers.That responds to a request from Spain, which said it needed more time to reorganise its numbering system, diplomats said.</

16160 The European Commission's decision on Wednesday to allow 3.9 billion French francs ($766 million) in urgent aid to Credit Lyonnais has highlighted its role in monitoring government bail outs in the European Union.The Commission often comes under pressure from national governments seeking to protect pet industries and companies and, like
16160 authorities elsewhere, is sometimes faced with the prospects of dealing with a company that is "too big to fail".Credit Lyonnais, some Commission officials have said, is clearly a case of the latter. The rules, however, permit the Commission to refuse any further aid to the company, even if this means
16160 it goes under.The Commission has, for example, been accused of letting Germany's largest shipbuilder, Bremer Vulkan, go bankrupt by insisting that it paid back subsidies.But other struggling companies -- notably airlines -- have had huge salvage plans approved on the controversial condition that they do not ask for more.The Commission's
16160 discretion comes courtesy of the EU treaty, which lays out the following rules:- State aid that distorts competition by favouring certain industries or goods in trade between EU states is illegal throughout the 15-nation bloc because it is incompatible with the EU's single market.- Some types of aid are specifically
16160 exempted from this, notably aid to make good damage caused by a natural disaster or "exceptional occurrences".The latter phrasing is particularly open to interpretation. Some have argued that even a fall in currency values can be considered exceptional.- Other types of aid are can be exempted at the Commission's discretion.These
16160 include aid to promote development in abnormally poor regions, aid to remedy a serious disruption in a country's economy, and aid to help development of sectors or areas if the aid is not viewed as hurting the common interest.Again, the latter allows for considerable interpretation.When it comes to rescue plans,
16160 such as Credit Lyonnais's, the Commission often authorises the aid providing certain conditions are met.These can include capacity cuts and divestments. Although it never formally demands that a company is privatised, it has encouraged this on a number of occasions, most notably with French computer firm Bull.</

16167 The British Takeover Panel, which polices mergers and acquisitions, has launched a fierce campaign against plans to impose EU-wide rules on takeover bids, saying they are unnecessary and dangerous.In an interview with Reuters this week the panel's director-general Alistair Defriez stressed the fear that a European Commission draft directive on
16167 the issue would provide for "tactical litigation" by disgruntled parties.Defriez advocated, instead, lighter, non-binding, rules such as a recommendation."We are worried that parties may be using the oportunity that will be created by the directive to pursue their disputes in takeover bids outside the takeover panel" Defriez said.He said there
16167 was a real danger this would become a defensive tactic to obtain an injunction and delay a bid. Defriez was afraid not only of the British courts -- which have so far discouraged such tactical moves -- but also the European court in Luxembourg which would almost certainly be called
16167 to give a final ruling.The Commission proposed in February a much watered down version of a 10-year attempt to impose common rules on takeover bids. The new draft sets general principles such as equal treatment of all shareholders and the obligation for the board of the target company to abstain
16167 from any action that is not in the interest of the company's owners.Defriez said such principles were already safeguarded in the British non-statutory system and in most other EU states.Britain is one of the EU's most active countries in the field of mergers and acquisitions. According to Commission figures, British
16167 companies are among the most targeted and certainly the most agressive when it comes to bidding for foreign firms.In what was seen as an attempt to accomodate the British system, the Commission said in the draft directive that national governments were free to implement the directive other than by legislative
16167 means.But Defriez thought governments would transpose it into national laws if adopted to avoid legal interpretation challenges."It would be ironic indeed if the directive which is modelled on the takeover code in the UK were introduced and seriously damaged that system," Defriez said.The European Parliament legal affairs committee is expected
16167 to draft a report on the proposed directive in October to allow for the house to give its first reading at its December session. It is only then that EU ministers are expected to discuss the plan.</

16181 continuation of the recent moderate income policy was seen very important," TT director-general Johannes Koroma said."Particularly important was that corporate taxation will not in any way be tightened, including energy and environment taxes, and that the government would clearly announce that it scarps its planned depreciation reform," he addded.But although

16187 price level by October 1," Jaroslav Havlicek, president of Swedish pulp producer Rottneros told Reuters. 16187 cleared up before a price increase could be accepted."A lot depends on what happens to the Norscan stock (of market pulp in the Nordic countries) in September," he said.Another factor affecting pulp prices would be fine paper prices, industry sources said. 16187 effect in Europe during the autumn.If these were to be rejected by the market, it will probably be more difficult for mills to accept an increase in pulp prices.Lars Lofgren, head of marketing for cut sheets at Swedish SCA's Wifsta mill, said that price increases for uncoated sheet had been
16187 implemented on some markets."We have introduced price increase in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. 16191 The number of jobs in the service sector increased by 58,000 year-on-year to 1,387,000 in August, Statistics Finland (SF) said in a statement on Thursday.However, compared to July this year, there was a decrease of 20,00 jobs in the sector, it said.In secondary production, the number of jobs rose by
16191 7,000 to 587,000 and in primary production -- farming and forestry -- the number of jobs fell to 156,000 from 173,000, it said.In all, SF estimated that 2,135,000 were employed, up from 2,089,000 in August 1995 but down from 2,228,000 in July 1996.The estimated number of unemployed was 403,000, down
16191 from 421,000 in July but about unchanged compared to the 404,000 in August last year.The unemployment rate thus fell 0.3 percentage points year-on-year to 15.9 percent but was unchanged compared to July this year, it said.SF's unemployment survey covers 10,000 Finns and SF said its margin of error in August
16191 was +/- 0.8 percetage points in the unmployment rate.-- Helsinki newsroom +358-0-6805 0245</
16192 The International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private finance wing of the World Bank, said its future work in developing countries will focus on mobilising domestic savings and promoting new fund vehicles.As part of a report on investment funds in emerging markets released this week, the Washington-based IFC said it would
16192 help promote pension funds, mutual funds and local pools for venture capital funds as a way of encouraging domestic savings."The IFC will also work closely with the World Bank to support pension reforms," the report said.It will identify technical partners and invest in private pension fund managers in order to
16192 help set high standards for pension fund management.Private equity funds and venture capital funds, particularly in new sectors and new countries would help add depth and liquidity to markets, drawing in new domestic and foreign investors, the IFC said.For "pre-emerging" markets, which have not yet benefited from foreign portfolio investment,
16192 the IFC will help set up portfolio funds to attract capital. The IFC said Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Cambodia were immediate targets.More sophisticated investors who want access to emerging markets returns but a lower risk profile have been attracted by index funds, and the IFC said it would continue
16192 to roll out index funds in more regions."As well as promoting specific funds, this work will involve adding new markets to its Emerging Markets Database," the report said. "Indeed, several countries are asking IFC to include them in the coverage, as this ensures automatic foreign portfolio investment from index funds."The
16192 IFC noted that as bond markets in developing countries deepen, there would be opportunities to promote funds investing in private corporate debt.But it said its efforts would "depend to a significant extent on liberalisation efforts by governments (including those not directly related to funds, such as privatisation and private participation
16192 in infrastructure) and investor perceptions."-- Caroline Allen, London newsroom +44 171 542 6414</
16193 U.K. biotech specialist Celltech Group Plc said on Thursday that it had been granted a key patent covering certain forms of artificially-created human antibodies by the U.S. patent office.Human antibodies, which are naturally-occurring proteins, are being copied for use in combatting a range of diseases, including heart disease, rheumatoid arthritis
16193 and cancer.In a statement Celltech said the patent, which lasts until 2014, will "substantially extend" the protection of products which it is developing using antibodies, and should lead to royalties from other companies using Celltech technology.Antibodies are being used to create a defense mechanism within the body against infections caused
16193 by organisms like bacteria and viruses.Early antibodies derived from animals failed to work effectively because they caused a major immune response when injected into humans.Scientists believe the ability to engineer artificial human antibodies in the laboratory, which are well tolerated by patients, has opened the way for a whole new
16193 class of drugs.Celltech is working on antibody-based treatments for psoriasis, cancer, rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn's disease.</

16194 After overcoming resistance at 815p, the shares could then reach 850p, technical analysts said.+ Turnover in the shares has increased following the breakout and the completion of a continuation head-and-shoulders pattern confirm the positive stance on the stock. Recent chart breakout on high volume by shares in life insurer Legal
16194 &amp; General suggest the stock price may run up towards 850p, after negotiating initial resistance at 815p, technical analysts said."The stock has made a clean break on the price-relative chart and from 740p on the absolute price chart," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.By 0750 GMT, the
16194 shares were down 1/2 to 793-1/2p. They embarked on a long-term bull trend in 1995, from a low of 415p in January that year, and over the past nine months they have shuffled sideways between 665p and 740p, noted Glydon. Turnover in the shares had declined over the summer months
16194 but picked up smartly as the shares broke-out. This implies the extent of investor interest in the shares and a likelihood that more buyers will be attracted to the shares fuelling further price rises.Breakout from 740p may have completed a particular chart pattern which is rarely seen, said Glydon.This is
16194 a continuation head-and-shoulders pattern, in which the share price first traces out three distinct troughs following an uptrend. The pattern is completed by an upward break from a line connecting the two peaks within the pattern so that the original upward trend can continue.Legal &amp; General's price-relative chart -- of
16194 the share price divided by the All-Share index -- is now at a 12-month high, implying further outperformance for the shares against the general market, said Glydon."The shares are still in a long-term uptrend," he added.-- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7954</
16195 Gerry Adams, leader of the Sinn Fein political wing of the IRA, cancelled a controversial private visit to Britain's parliament on Thursday and accused the opposition Labour Party of a "McCarthy-style witch hunt".Adams had hoped to launch his autobiograhy in the historic building on the banks of the Thames River,
16195 just three days after British police foiled what they said was an imminent bomb attack by Irish Republican Army guerrillas.Parliamentary officials cancelled the launch at the weekend but left-wing Labour member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn defied critics and said he would host a private meeting with Adams instead.Adams said he
16195 called off the meeting because the controversy surrounding the visit put Corbyn and another Labour MP, Tony Benn, who was also due to attend in an untenable position."I came here as a guest. I have no wish to create difficulties, especially for Jeremy or Tony, or those others who have
16195 taken a progressive position on Ireland," he said in a statement."The internal Labour Party dispute -- which is in effect a McCarthy-style witch-hunt -- has been a major distraction from the real issues."Labour party officials had threatened to throw Corbyn out of the party if he went ahead with the
16195 meeting. Benn, a former cabinet minister, could have faced similar disciplinary action."We utterly condemn his proposed action. If he persists it will be a matter for disciplinary action," Donald Dewar, Labour's chief parliamentary business manager, said on Wednesday."It is particularly reprehensible in the light of recent events involving the IRA,"
16195 Dewar added.Adams played down the political furore surrounding the visit and said the venue was trivial. It involved an internal dispute with the Labour Party and masked the more urgent problem facing the British and Irish governments -- the breakdown of the peace process in Northern Ireland."There are bigger issues,
16195 and the biggest issue is how to work out a peace settlement in Ireland," he told reporters."I think all of us have to fulfil our responsibilities... for a real peace process."On Monday police shot dead an IRA suspect in London and seized 10 tonnes of explosives in raids that dealt
16195 a severe blow to IRA guerrillas who are battling to oust Britain from Northern Ireland. Five other men were detained in the raids.Adams was elected MP for West Belfast in the 1980s but never took his seat in the House of Commons. He said he regarded Britain as an occupying
16195 power in the province and has refused to take an oath of allegiance to the British monarch.He has visited parliament several times in the past few years since as a former legislator he cannot be barred.</

16197 - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring CompanyDAILY TELEGRAPH-- BLACK YEAR FOR PDFM AS 'VALUE STYLE' FLOPSPDFM, the fund management giant, has announced that it has had one of the worst years in equities since 1992. The underperformance is thought to have been because PDFM had taken a seven
16197 billion stg bet that the markets of London and New York would crash. However it has now emerged that PDFM's problems have been compounded by backing the wrong investments. The investment strategy has been called 'value style' and has many proponents in America, but PDFM is one of few adherents
16197 in Britain.-- CLARKE MAY TARGET PROFIT-RELATED PAYFears that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke may tax reliefs for profit-related pay schemes in his November Budget have been fuelled by figures from the Inland Revenue which forecast that the cost to the Exchequer of the schemes will jump from one billion stg last year
16197 to 1.5 billion stg in the current tax year. The number of people whose salaries are directly linked to their employer's profits has more than doubled to 3.5 million in the past three years.-- CBI BACKS CALLS FOR BUDGET RESTRAINTThe Confederation of British Industry has reinforced the opinion of business
16197 organisations on Budget representations by calling for a tighter grip on public spending and limited tax cuts. The central part of a CBI package formally presented to Chancellor Kenneth Clarke two weeks ago is of spending cuts of 5.3 billion stg and tax reductions at one billion stg. The CBI's
16197 call for restraint is in line with representations from the Institute of Directors and other business organisations which want Mr Clarke to resist pressure for a pre-election giveaway.THE TIMES-- BT AND NEWS INTERNATIONAL TO LAUNCH INTERNET SERVICEBritish Telecom and News International are set to launch their own Internet service in
16197 January called Springboard. It's content is designed for mass-market appeal and will range from News International's titles, which include The Times, to information about television programmes. 16197 Rupert Gavin said that the start-up costs would be sizeable, but they could be less than ten million stg.-- NATWEST TO SHED 3.2 BILLION STG IN LOANSThe UK's biggest bank, NatWest, is to shed 3.2 billion stg worth of company loans from its lending book and sell them on a
16197 new type of security to other banks, building societies, pension funds and other international investors. The move will pave the way for rival banks and City institutions to follow suit and could create a new market of tradeable corporate loan notes or securities worth up to 32 billion stg. The
16197 move will involve loans to 300 of NatWest's larger and more creditworthy company customers.-- BRITAIN TO TOP EURO ECONOMY LEAGUE'According to the International Monetary Fund, Britain is to have the most successful economy in Europe for the fourth year running in 1997. 16197 growth rate, see a further significant decline in unemployment and show no sign of any serious inflationary problems. 16197 would be no compulsory redundancies. 16201 UK regulatory body IMRO said it has terminated the registration of Geoffrey de Sibert, the former chief executive of InterCapital Asset Management.A statement from the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation said de Sibert has agreed to a settlement of disciplinary proceedings brought against him by IMRO."Mr de Sibert did not exercise
16201 the integrity required of a registered Individual, from about April 1994 to March 1995, when he knowingly and deliberately overvalued warrants held by one of the funds managed by InterCapital," IMRO said.The regulator said de Sibert "knew or should have known" his actions would cause the fund to be overvalued
16201 by between 2.25 million stg and 9.7 million stg, or up to 25 percent of the fund's correct valuation.Investors joining the fund would be unfairly disadvantaged and those leaving unfairly advantaged. The fund would be unable to pay to all investors the perceived value of their holding.IMRO said the breach
16201 meant the fund appeared to perform better than it had, and de Sibert had "deliberately failed to obtain the consent of the directors and auditors of the fund for his methods of valuing the warrants".De Sibert was Chief Executive of InterCapital from February 1992 to March 1995. InterCapital was placed
16201 into a voluntary creditor's liquidation on April 4, 1995 and no longer conducts investment business.De Sibert will pay IMRO's costs of 5,000 stg.-- Caroline Allen, London newsroom +44 171 5423 6414</

16212 Standard &amp; Poor's said on Thursday it raised its long-term foreign currency rating on the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to BB minus, and has revised the outlook on the rating to stable from positive. In addition, S&amp;P said it affirmed its BBB minus long-term and A3 short-term ratings on Jordan's
16212 dinar-denominated debt."The outlook on the local currency rating remains stable," it said in a statement.S&amp;P said it had also assigned its BB minus rating to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan's Brady bonds, totaling US$745 million, including US$494 million in par bonds due 2023, US$157 million in discount bonds due 2023,
16212 and US$94 million in past due interest bonds due 2023. "The upgrade is based on progress in strengthening public finances, underpinned by a strong commitment to fiscal restraint, which is reducing Jordan's vulnerability to adverse external economic and political developments," S&amp;P said."Adherence to an ambitious IMF-sponsored economic adjustment programme, renewed
16212 earlier this year until 1998, should ensure that Jordan's still-weak external payments and foreign exchange positions continue to improve.""A low external debt service burden, projected at 14 to-15 percent of exports over the next two to three years, also supports the upgrade," S&amp;P said. S&amp;P said deepening fiscal reforms were
16212 expected to keep budget out turns in small surplus for the fifth and sixth consecutive years in 1996 and 1997."This, in turn, should sustain the downward trend in the public debt burden," said S&amp;P."Supported by ongoing microeconomic reforms and an increasingly stable regional environment, robust export growth is expected to
16212 contain current account deficits to under three percent of GDP annually during 1996/1997," the agency said. "Coupled with likely additional debt relief from official creditors next year, modest external imbalances gradually should raise Jordan's low foreign exchange reserves," S&amp;P said.S&amp;P said the investment-grade local currency rating reflected the low stock
16212 of dinar debt (about 17 percent of GDP this year), the interest payments on which absorb only one percent of government revenues."The central bank's demonstrated ability to contain inflation to single digits, even during periods of acute political and financial stress, also underpins the higher dinar rating," said S&amp;P. S&amp;P
16212 said Jordan's ratings were constrained by the following.-- A favorably structured, but heavy, gross government debt burden, which, at 122 percent of GDP in 1996, is the highest among similarly rated sovereigns, and limits fiscal and external payments flexibility.-- The low level of foreign exchange reserves, the most liquid portion
16212 of which is equivalent to under two months of imports and remain vulnerable to balance of payments pressures-- A dependence on remittances, tourism receipts, and intra-regional trade, which are sensitive to potential setbacks in the peace process. "The outlook balances the commitment to disciplined fiscal and monetary policies, with still-limited
16212 financial flexibility, and the challenge of advancing fiscal reforms as high unemployment persists," said S&amp;P.It said recent disturbances which followed increases in bread prices posed little near-term threat to the government and to domestic stability owing to King Hussein's popularity and strong political position. "However uncertainties surrounding the resolution of
16212 the Israeli-Palestinian conflict pose risks to Jordan's balance of payments, and its internal and external security over the long term," S&amp;P said.--International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041</

16218 of 750 million stg in August.GLENN DAVIES, CREDIT LYONNAIS (RFTV)"The whole-world figure for July looks somewhat worse than expected...a little bit worrying." 16218 smaller than people were looking for." STEPHEN HANNAH, IBJ INTERNATIONAL"We were rather surprised by the weakness of imports by the UK from Europe. Our suspicion is that UK activity is picking up quite sharply at the moment and we would expect to see some strong pickup in imports from our
16218 European partners over the next few months. The overall trend is very flat. The global balance is averaging about one to 1-1/4 billion per month, so we're not moving out of the trend. It doesn't really help the Chancellor with his case for lower interest rates. I think we're still
16218 looking at the opposite scenario." JEREMY HAWKINS, BANK OF AMERICA"UK trade data mixed, with the July global shortfall larger than expected but the August non-EU deficit surprisingly small. Global picture shows a widening in the shortfall with the EU in July, but with exports down and imports up, almost certainly says more about the relative performance of UK domestic demand vs EU demand than anything to
16218 do with stg being over-valued." -- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774</

16254 Irish Republican leader Gerry Adams has cancelled a controversial private visit on Thursday to Britain's parliament, an opposition legislator who invited him said.The visit by the leader of Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) political wing, would have come just three days after British police foiled what they said
16254 was an imminent IRA bomb attack.Police shot dead an IRA suspect in London on Monday and seized 10 tonnes of explosives in raids that dealt a severe blow to IRA guerrillas who are battling to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.Opposition Labour Party member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn, who was roundly
16254 criticised by his own party for issuing the invitation to Adams, said the Sinn Fein leader had cancelled his visit to the House of Commons (lower house) but gave no reason, the Press Association news agency reported.The agency quoted a spokesman for Corbyn as saying it was Adams who had
16254 pulled out and that that the invitation had not been withdrawn in the face of threats from the Labour leadership to throw Corbyn out of the party.Adams had hoped to launch his autobiography in the House of Commons building on Thursday, but the launch was cancelled by parliamentary officials over
16254 the weekend so Corbyn issued his private invitation instead.Adams was elected MP for West Belfast in the 1980s but never took his seat in the House of Commons. He said he regarded Britain as an occupying power in the province and has refused to take an oath of allegiance to
16254 the British monarch.He has visited parliament several times in the past few years since as a former legislator he cannot be barred.</
16255 His "demon" eyes stare from posters across Britain, courtesy of John Major's Conservatives.The ruling party, battling to hold on to power after 17 years in office, are portraying Labour leader Tony Blair as a bogeyman, eager to endanger the country's economic recovery.Ironically, the Conservatives' slogan "New Labour, New Danger" has
16255 struck more of a chord with left-wing Labour supporters than with wavering voters.With Blair up to 20 points ahead in opinion polls, few are prepared to rock the Labour boat openly before the election due before May 1997.But the whisperings of discontent at Blair's discarding of Labour's socialist dogma surface
16255 almost daily in the press, hurting the party more than any external attack."A major western political party has fallen into the hands of someone with a background not from that party," said Labour party activist Tony Coello after reports that Blair was now considering easing party links with the unions."A
16255 lot of people are disappointed."Blair, a high-powered lawyer with little in common with the party's working-class roots, has ditched old-style socialism for a platform designed to appeal to business and the middle class.Old ideas such as universal welfare and the redistribution of wealth through tax are near-heresy in New Labour,
16255 replaced with work programmes for the unemployed and praise for entrepreneurs.Many traditional Labour voters are bemused by the speed of change. "Whether the leadership has got it right...I just don't know," said Malcolm Speake, a Labour councillor in the central English city of Birmingham, once the heart of Britain's industrial
16255 powerhouse but now struggling to come to terms with structural change.Most of the open dissent has come from within the team who will form Blair's government, known as the shadow cabinet.Under party rules, the top posts go to people voted for by Labour members of parliament, a system which burdens
16255 Blair with people selected for their skill at winning support from internal party factions rather than aptitude for government.In time, Blair has indicated he will ditch this system, too.But for now, saddled with people unhappy with his low tax platform -- like veteran Clare Short, who represents a swathe of
16255 inner-city Birmingham -- he has simply shuffled them into low key jobs. Short, for example, is now in charge of overseas aid.Add in a press traditionally pro-Conservative and the hothouse atmosphere of parliament where MPs and journalists rub shoulders and trade gossip detached from the real world, and you have
16255 fertile ground for stories of dissent.Blair is seeking to outflank the parliamentary party by balloting members on Labour's draft manifesto for the election.Blair has dubbed it the "contract with the people" -- in a brazen copy of the Republican party's "Contract with America" campaign which swept them to control of
16255 Congress.But members will have to accept or reject the draft as it stands, with no chance of changing it. Faced with this choice, some members will give their backing -- with bad grace."No matter how people grit their teeth, there will be a healthy vote of endorsement to the leadership,"
16255 Coello said. "People are biting their lip, they don't want to be blamed for defeat."Political analysts say this attitude could return to haunt Blair after the election.A report last month by researchers at Hull University suggested that Blair could face regular defeat in parliament from his own left-wingers if he
16255 has less than a 60-seat majority in the 651-strong House of Commons.Advisers to Blair dismiss such studies, arguing that older, traditional Labour MPs are stepping down and the new intake is likely to be very pro-Blair. Activists also dismiss the dissent, pointing to a huge surge in new members since
16255 Blair took over."The press are trying to build up dissension," said Cecily Gale, another activist in the Edgbaston area of Birmingham."It's been a real culture change and the influx of new members is extremely high," she told Reuters. "People realise we can't go back to the 1970s...Instead, people are looking
16255 ahead at what's going to happen at the end of the 1990s and in 2000."Blair retains an unshaken confidence that he has taken the right road, one he believes most members will follow him down.In a tantalising glimpse of his post-election plans, Blair has hinted that he is determined not
16255 to be halted by internal dissent, even if this means ditching the left and forging some kind of alliance with the minority Liberal Democratss.Blair used an interview in the Observer newspaper this month to minimise the distance between Labour and the Liberals.In a clear threat that he could seek backing
16255 from the Liberals if left-wing rebels in his own party make governing difficult, Blair said: "New Labour has the chance to build a genuine radical movement of the centre and centre-left for the future."Left-wingers would be left isolated or forced out. A natural home would be the breakaway Socialist Labour
16255 Party set up by firebrand miners' leader Arthur Scargill after he quit Labour in protest at what he called Blair's betrayal of state ownership.Blair's aides were quietly delighted at Scargill's departure, seeing it as reinforcing the party leader's message that he had distanced himself from old policies linked inextricably in
16255 voters' minds to the industrial strife of the 1970s.For any traditionalists who still believe Blair will eventually be forced to trim his reforming zeal by pressure from within the party, Blair delivered an uncompromising message."In the brutal game of tactics, we shall continue to do what is necessary to win,
16255 because without winning, radical politics will never happen at all," he told the Observer.</
16256 Northern Ireland's peace process is faltering. But, tourism aside, its economy is thriving."The basic story is really quiet good with strong growth prospects," Graham Gudgin, director of the Northern Ireland Economic Research Centre told Reuters.He was speaking on the eve of resumed peace talks in Belfast after a summer of
16256 violent unrest and sectarian tension which blackened the province's image as a tourist destination but has failed to blemish its overall economic performance.Gudgin said the main victim of political unrest was tourism but this represented only a minute part of overall Gross Domestic Product (GDP), contributing about two percent per
16256 annum to a 12 billion pound ($18.79 billion) annual take.Other sectors of the economy, especially local manufacturing, had proved resilient to the 25-year "Troubles" and were now performing exceptionally well, he said.The region has been the fastest growing in Britain for some time. "It has been a much more successful
16256 economy in growth terms then most people realise," said Gudgin.The economy, which had grown steadily during the past decade, blossomed when twin guerrilla ceasefires in late 1994 gave a 17-month respite to 25 years of bloodshed.Tourism was one of the main beneficiaries of the ceasefires and the Northern Ireland Tourist
16256 Board (NITB) said visitors to the province reached record levels.The number of holiday visitors in 1995 showed a 67 percent increase over the previous year and the total visitor spend reached 214 million pounds, an increase of 17 percent on 1994, official figures show.But a ceasefire by the Irish Republican
16256 Army, which wants a united Ireland, collapsed in early 1996 with an IRA bomb in London.Tension in Northern Ireland soared when Protestant demonstrations forced police to reverse a ban on a July 12 march through a Roman Catholic area of the town of Portadown from a church at Drumcree, igniting
16256 Catholic anger instead."The events of the summer of 1996 did more damage to tourism than the whole of the troubles. It just shows what a sensitive and volatile business tourism is. Some (smaller) tourist venues were empty in August for the first time ever," Gudgin said.Other areas of the economy
16256 are not so sensitive to the province's political turmoil. "Ninety eight percent of the economy, outside tourism, is really not very much affected either by ceasefires or lack of them," Gudgin said.A Confederation of British Industry (CBI) regional trends survey, published in August, showed manufacturers' confidence in Northern Ireland the
16256 most buoyant of all British regions."Our latest survey on the manufacturing industry found Northern Ireland the most optimistic region in the UK and that was reflected in the higher growth they had seen in their orders and output than the rest of the UK," Sudhir Junankar, CBI associate director for
16256 economics, told Reuters.Northern Ireland manufacturing exports grew by 21 percent to 2.6 billion pounds in the year ending in March 1995 and by 48 percent over the most recently measured four year period, compared to a growth rate of 30 percent for the British manufacturing industry as a whole, official
16256 figures show."The economy itself is doing well, particularly manufacturing and within that indigenous manufacturing has done well in comparison to most other parts of the UK," Gudgin said.Its manufacturing export includes clothes, electrical goods and computer parts as well as traditional industries in the ship-building and aerospace sector."The externally (foreign)
16256 owned sector, some of which have been here for 30 years, is about 50 percent of the total but it is the locally owned sector which is growing fastest and is the main success story and does much better than the equivalent in the (Irish) Republic or mainland Britain," said
16256 Gudgin.Belfast-based management consultants BDO Stoy Hayward said a recent confidence survey on the Northern Ireland hotel industry confirmed the "severe" negative impact current political uncertainty had on tourism."We have been conducting surveys for over two years now and recorded growing confidence over that period as a result of opportunities that
16256 peace had brought," said Shaun Kelly, Stoy Hayward's partner in charge of tourism services."We conducted a survey in March after the Canary Wharf (London) bomb and had seen some decline in confidence but this survey has showed a more marked decline," Kelly added. ($1=.6385 Stg)</

16264 An elderly Australian man dying of prostate cancer has become the world's first person to take his own life under a controversial voluntary euthanasia law, the doctor who assisted in his suicide said on Thursday.News of the death surprised and outraged civil and religious leaders and renewed debate over a
16264 "mercy killing" law that many Australians, including Prime Minister John Howard, want to see quashed.Dr Philip Nitschke told Reuters his patient died on Sunday from a lethal injection in Darwin, the capital of the remote Northern Territory, which residents fear could become the world's "Death Capital".Nitschke said his computerised euthanasia
16264 system -- which asks a series of questions before administering the lethal drugs -- had been used in the death. But he would not say whether he or his patient, a man in his mid-60s who did not want to be named, pressed the buttons to administer the drugs."We made
16264 use of the computer software and the questions were answered and the machine delivered the medication," he told Reuters from Darwin. "The patient was expressing a sense of gratitude. He was as happy as someone could be under the circumstances."Nitschke has been dubbed "Australia's Doctor Death" after Jack Kevorkian, the
16264 American doctor who has attended 40 suicides in his campaign to legalise euthanasia.Nitschke said he felt sad but relieved at helping the man die. "You couldn't not be affected by it," he said. "It's a very difficult business ... and it's not the sort of thing you would want to
16264 make a habit of -- it certainly took its toll."I came out with a sense that I had done something good. There was also a bit of a sense of history."Sydney's Roman Catholic archbishop, Edward Clancy, said the death was "a shameful day for Australia"."At least this deplorable act may
16264 serve to bring the stark reality of euthanasia fully home to the consciousness of all Australians and further instances of this ugly evil may yet be prevented," he said in a statement.Nitschke's patient wrote a letter the day before he died pleading with Australia's national parliament not to overturn the
16264 territory law, beset by controversy and a series of challenges since it came into operation on July 1."The church and state should be kept separate," the man wrote. "What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to
16264 their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain until some doctor in his omniscience decides that I have had enough and that he increases the morphine until I die."If you disagree with voluntary euthanasia, then don't use it, but please don't deny the right to me to use it if I
16264 want to."A member of Howard's conservative government has launched a private action in parliament, with Howard's backing, which would see the national parliament use its constitutional powers to quash the territory law.The challenge is the latest in a series of legal and political challenges that had delayed use of the
16264 law because doctors were unsure of their legal position.Challenges in the territory parliament and the territory's Supreme Court have failed.The law faces a separate threat in Australia's highest court, the High Court, where an anti-euthanasia coalition of doctors, church and Aboriginal leaders is seeking to have it declared unconstitutional.Nitschke said
16264 that the man's death would help future assisted suicides. "The next one will be easier, it always gets easier," he said.</

16268 fallen out of favour.Next to south Africa, Australian producers are some of the biggest forward sellers in the world, relying on the sales to to fund new mine development and exploration programmes. 16268 in Japanese yen or U.S. dollars has become highly unattractive, bullion dealers say.This could change if Australian interest rates are lowered sometime this year, which would likely apply some downward pressure on the Australian dollar, some analysts think.The weaker the Australian dollar is against other currencies the more attractive it

16285 Darwin doctor Philip Nitschke said he felt sad but relieved as the Nembutal was injected into the elderly man lying at home in his bed in the sleepy tropical city of Darwin on a sunny Sunday afternoon.Nitschke, dubbed "Doctor Death" by his critics, had just helped terminal cancer patient Bob
16285 Dent administer a lethal injection to become the first man to die under the world's first voluntary euthanasia law."You couldn't not be affected by it," Nitschke, who has devoted himself to the controversial pro-euthanasia campaign, told Reuters by telephone from Darwin."It's a very difficult business."It couldn't be an average day
16285 and it's not the sort of thing you would want to make a habit of -- it certainly took its toll."Nitschke said he had been worried on Sunday. The atmosphere in Dent's house had at first been tense.But Dent, 66, who had suffered five long years of agonising pain from
16285 prostate cancer, told his doctor the assisted suicide was an act of love."I came out of that with a sense that I had done something good," Nitschke said."It was a very difficult time for me, but I was left with the overwhelming feeling that I had done the right thing,

16285 one patient, 66-year-old taxi driver Max Bell, die in agony because he had been unable to find the two doctors and psychiatrist needed to approve a voluntary euthanasia bid.Nitschke said Dent's death brought him the certainty that he could now help five other patients who have come to him asking

16290 The following is an excerpt from an open letter, dated September 21, sent to Australian parliamentarians by Bob Dent, the man who has become the first person to use the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law.Dent was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 1991."By mid-1995, I was having difficulty urinating as the
16290 cancer in the prostate gland had closed off the urethra."I had to have a catheter inserted in order to empty my bladder. I continued with daily self-catheterisation until the passage closed right over."An indwelling catheter and leg bag was the next step."In August 1995, a trans-urethral resection of the prostate
16290 (TURP) was done by a Perth urologist, to chip away the cancer and reopen the urethra, so that I did not have to use the catheter and leg bag to collect the urine."By May 1996, the urethra had once again become blocked and I again had to make use of
16290 a catheter and leg bag -- an embarrassing and uncomfortable situation, especially in Darwin's climate."In June 1996, I had another TURP and this operation worked reasonably well, but the rest of my body was deteriorating quickly."I have lost 25 kg in weight. My latest blood tests, taken on September 2,
16290 1996, indicated an acceleration of the cancer with the prostatic specific antigen rising to 1298 (normal is 0 to 4). The red cell picture was suggestive of infiltration of the bone marrow by the cancer."This was confirmed by chest X-rays..."Two specialists ... have both said nothing further can be done..."Already
16290 my urine flow is diminishing. Further TURPs are not advisable, even if my weakened body could tolerate a general anaesthetic. I have no wish for further experimentation by the Palliative Care people in their efforts to control my pain. My current program involves taking 30 tablets a day!"For months I
16290 have been on a roller coaster of pain made worse by the unwanted side effects of the drugs."Morphine causes constipation, laxatives taken work erratically, often resulting in loss of bowel control in the middle of the night. I have to have a rubber sheet on my bed, like a child
16290 who is not yet toilet trained."Other drugs given to enhance the pain-relieving effects of the morphine have caused me to feel suicidal to the point that I would have blown my head off if I had had a gun."I can do little for myself, and require 24-hour nursing care. My
16290 haemoglobin has fallen to 8.3 (normal is 13.5 to 18.5). My red cells are decreased in number and deformed because of the cancer in the bone marrow."This anaemia causes shortness of breath and fainting because of the cells' inability to carry the required oxygen."An attempt was made to alleviate the
16290 symptoms of the anaemia, by giving me two units of a healthy person's blood."The procedure took all day, was uncomfortable, and did no good whatsoever. There is now a constant fear of a fall which could cause terrible injury to my fragile bones. I cannot even get a hug in
16290 case my ribs crack."My own pain is made worse by watching my wife suffering as she cares for me; bathing and drying me, caring after my 'accidents' in the middle of the night, and watching my body fade away. If I were to keep a pet animal in the same
16290 condition I am in, I would be prosecuted."I have always been an active, outgoing person, and being unable to live a normal life causes much mental psychological pain, which can never be relieved by medication."I read with increasing horror newspaper stories of (member of parliament) Kevin Andrew's attempt to overturn
16290 the most compassionate piece of legislation in the world. (Actually, my wife had to read the newspaper stories to me as I can no longer focus my eyes)."The church and state must remain separate."What right has anyone, because of their own religious faith (to which I don't subscribe), to demand
16290 that I behave according to their rules until some omniscient doctor decides that I must have had enough and goes ahead and increases my morphine until I die?"If you disagree with voluntary euthanasia, then don't use it, but don't deny me the right to use it if and when I
16290 want to go."I am immensely grateful that I have the opportunity to use the 'Rights of the Terminally III Act' to ask my doctor Philip Nitschke to assist me to relieve this interminable suffering and to end my life in a dignified and compassionate manner."</

16294 to the point that I would have blown my head off if I had had a gun."I have always been an active, outgoing person, and being unable to live a normal life causes much mental and psychological pain, which can never be relieved by medication."Nitschke told reporters the atmosphere at
16294 Dent's Darwin home, where the euthanasia was carried out, had at first been tense and disquieting.But Dent had reassured him and told him it was an act of love. "The patient was expressing a sense of gratitude. He was as happy as someone could be under the circumstances," Nitschke said.The

16294 it came into operation, the law has been hit by a series of political and legal challenges which had until this month deterred doctors from approving patients' deaths.Government backbencher Kevin Andrews, backed by Howard, has launched a private action in parliament that would see the national parliament use its constitutional
16294 powers to quash the territory law.But Dent, in his letter, urged parliament to allow people to choose to die when the bill is voted on later this year."The church and state should be kept separate," he wrote. "What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I
16294 don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain."If you disagree with voluntary euthanasia, then don't use it, but please don't deny the right to me to use it."Andrews told reporters he was protecting the community and warned the law could be abused."It's
16294 not just an issue that affects one individual, or even that individual and his or her families, it's a matter which effects the entire community.... the way in which we see things such as death and care and what hope we give people," he said.Andrews' challenge is the latest in
16294 a series of legal and political attacks on the territory law.Challenges in the territory parliament and the territory's Supreme Court have failed.The law faces a separate threat in Australia's highest court, the High Court, where an anti-euthanasia coalition of doctors, church and Aboriginal leaders is seeking to have it declared

16313 Australian economists are generally forecasting another cut in official interest rates by the end of the year but are less sure on the outlook for the Australian dollar, the International Banks and Securities Association of Australia (IBSA) said.In its latest quarterly survey of member bank economists released Thursday, IBSA found
16313 only two out of 11 were not looking for another easing in monetary policy."Continued patchy economic growth and the favourable outlook for inflation should allow the Reserve Bank to cut rates," said Ric Simes, chief economist at Rothschild Australia. Official rates are presently at 7.00 percent, having been cut by
16313 0.50 point on July 31.The economists expected headline inflation to fall below the underlying rate over the next few quarters to around 2.00 percent on average."A very sharp drop in headline inflation occurs from this quarter's figures as previous taxation rises drop out, the benefits of the A$ appreciation accrue,
16313 and recent mortgage rate reductions are reflected in the figures," said Ivan Colhoun, an associate director at Bain. "We expect headline inflation around 1.5 percent in each of the December and March quarters." The headline consumer price index stood at 3.1 percent in the June quarter.Economists were divided on where
16313 the Australian dollar was heading with forecasts ranging from as low as 72 U.S. cents to as high as 83 cents by the end of the March quarter."The A$ has got ahead of the commodity price story," said Chris Caton, chief economist sat Bankers Trust Australia who sees the dollar
16313 at 77 cents in the next two quarters."The currency is now 18 percent above its mid-1995 trough but the RBA index of commodity prices has risen by less than 10 percent," he said. Yasushi Usuda, an economist at Tokai Finance Australia, saw the dollar declining to 75 cents by the
16313 March quarter partly due to fear of another interest rate cut here.The Australian dollar was around US$0.7910 at midday on Thursday.However, Citbank Australia's senior economist Stephen Koukoulas was more optimistic, predicting a rise to 83 cents by the March quarter on relative gains in the current account deficit and favourable
16313 fundamentals. The yield on 10-year Commonwealth bonds was generally expected to remain around its current 7.84 percent. Caton at Bankers Trust said the yield differential against 10-year U.S. Treasuries had already priced in a lot of good news."The differential was 240 basis points in April; it is now less than
16313 half of that," he said.The yield gap at midday Thursday was 109 basis points.-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

16319 Electricity prices in New Zealand will undoubtedly be volatile in the new wholesale market which begins next week, Electricity Corporation of New Zealand said on Thursday.The country's largest generator of electricity also declared the tendering of its long-term electricity contracts an overwhelming success. "I think the fact that there is
16319 a new regime that comes into effect from the first of October, and a likelihood that there will be more volatility in the price of electricity, has probably encouraged buyers to participate strongly," ECNZ general manager of marketing Peter Larsen said in an interview.About 94 percent of the volume on
16319 offer was allocated to bidders, securing around NZ$1.4 billion in revenue over a five year period for the state-owned generator.Eighty percent of ECNZ's total generation is now allocated in contracts for the next 12 months, leaving only 20 percent exposed to the new spot market, down from 38 percent previously.
16319 Under a memorandum of understanding with the government, ECNZ, which dominates the generation industry with a 67 percent market share, is obligated to offer set percentages of its firm capacity by tender though long-term contracts."In effect, we have to have contracts that go out at least five years in the
16319 market at any one point in time, so we will continue to offer contracts on an on-going basis until such time as our market share reduces to 45 percent," Larsen said.But the contracts are also a boon for ECNZ. "We have the opportunity to write contracts with our customers more
16319 than 12 months in advance. We have never had long-term contracts out of the market before. I think the final outcome for ECNZ is greater revenue certainty," Larsen said.The new market will bring many changes, among them the scrapping of a price cap on electricity.Previously, the effective cost of producing
16319 the most expensive unit of electricity -- through diesel-fired generation -- placed a cap on price of about 16 cents per unit. "It is true that the cap has been removed, which was artificially established under the previous regime," said Larsen."There will be strong competition in terms of offering capacity
16319 into the (market) pool, and people's offering behaviour will depend on their ability to generate and the contract cover that they have," he said."The resulting spot price will fluctuate without a doubt. Whether it fluctuates beyond the previously set artificial cap will depend on the forces of supply and demand
16319 at that time." ECNZ's contract tender clearing prices for the next 12 months were about 1.0 to 1.5 percent higher than current prices and increased about six percent over a five-year period.Larsen said he was absolutely confident that true competition would emerge between ECNZ and the other state-owned generator, Contact
16319 Energy, which would act to keep prices down."The wholesale market will see competition between generators in terms of offering their capacity into the pool and the benefit for consumers should be a price for electricity that buyers and sellers agree upon," Larsen said.-- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4714 272</

16334 By Matthew Goodson, economist at Garlick &amp; CoWELLINGTON, Sept 26 - Over the course of May and June, New Zealand financial markets talked themselves into an absolute spin on the subject of political risk.Since then, a gradual erosion of NZ First's poll support has seen the focus turn very much
16334 back to core economic information, most of which has been favourable in terms of pointing to a future monetary easing. Thus the attitude of the market towards politics has gone full circle, with the overall view now being one of utter complacency. In what follows, we argue that the numbers
16334 for a right-leaning coalition are by no means certain and that the risks of alternative political outcomes have not been priced into NZ financial assets.Financial markets have taken considerable solace from the recent rise of the Christian Coalition and ACT past five percent in most polls and the strong likelihood
16334 that United will take Ohariu. However, it is not clear that a right-leaning coalition will be the result. Many of the Christian and ACT voters would otherwise vote National and there will be a very low "wasted list vote" percentage on parties who fail to make the five percent threshold.Thus
16334 a coalition may need up to 49 percent of the list vote to actually have a majority in Parliament. If there is an electorate seat overhang, then the requirement would move past 50 percent.In contrast to the doubt surrounding the right-leaning coalition numbers, a grouping of Labour, NZ First and
16334 the Alliance clearly adds up. Previously, this was dismissed as extremely unlikely given the Alliance's refusal to participate in any formal coalition structures but the recent commitment by Jim Anderton to take part in a "Clayton's coalition" has brought the left-leaning bloc right back into the picture. Similarly, the fact
16334 that Labour is slowly consolidating itself above NZ First means that such a coalition is a real possibility.Although the precise coalition make-up is as clear as mud, one near certainty post-election is that NZ First will be in the driver's seat. Unless the right-leaning parties sneak the thinnest of majorities,
16334 whichever way NZ First swings will prove absolutely critical. Given the public debate between Tau Henare and Winston Peters over this very issue, we could be in for a very messy coalition negotiating process.Thus the fact that NZ First has moved back from 30 percent to around 18 percent really
16334 means nothing because in the final analysis, they are likely to hold the balance of power.Although a lack of cross-party agreement may prevent major policy changes, one can only imagine the uncertainty that will prevail as financial markets hang on Winston Peters' every word. It has become something of a
16334 party mantra that MMP will result in no major policy changes. At a surface glance, academic studies support this conclusion, which revolves on the key tenet that insufficient cross-party agreement is possible to make any such changes.However, to rest on this conclusion is to totally misrepresent the argument. A left-leaning
16334 coalition could still have a considerable impact on economic policy, it's just that this impact would be larger still if FPP prevailed. Thus while MMP will prevent the complete overthrow of the existing policy framework in the event of a left-leaning coalition, the precise outcome of the election will still
16334 matter an awful lot.To be a devil's advocate, let's sketch a scene of the sorts of policy prognostications that markets will likely have to grapple with in the weeks following the election.Look out for kites to be flown on subjects such as considerable fiscal policy concessions, amendments to the Employment
16334 Contracts Act in favour of collective bargaining, a capital gains tax, a higher top income tax rate, a higher company tax rate, a move away from light-handed regulation of utilities, a wider inflation target and a further tightening of immigration criteria.While no single one of these possible policies constitutes an
16334 abandonment of the existing framework, they collectively add up to something that financial markets would be rather less than enthused with.Such policies would be by no means abnormal in the context of the rest of the OECD but this begs the question of why overseas investors are so heavily weighted
16334 in NZ compared to other countries. The short term impact on these investors' perceptions of a messy coalition negotiation process and the disappearance of the multi-year free lunch on the NZ dollar (in the event of a wider inflation target) need only be imagined.Unless the right-leaning parties gain an electoral
16334 majority, the remainder of 1996 will not be a happy time for financial markets.Lest our views be put in the Dr Doom category, it is vital to note that our negativity is basically short term in nature. Academic research into the determinants of economic growth (and hence earnings growth) shows
16334 that the degree of investment in physical and human capital is far more important than politics.Politics only matters when it reaches the stage of civil war. Moreover, the inflationary implications of MMP will be relatively small given that central bank independence will likely remain. A wider inflation target would release
16334 a veritable flood of funds out of cash and bank deposits in favour of bonds and equities, while a concomitant fall in the exchange rate would lend a major boost to earnings growth. However, these factors may not make themselves apparent for quite some time after the election.Finally, we are
16334 not saying that any of these changes will necessarily happen or that a left-wing coalition will triumph. We simply don't know. What we are arguing is that market participants will begin to talk about such changes and that the risk of their occurrence is not currently priced into financial markets.Investors
16334 should not put their heads in the sand and pray that a left-leaning coalition will not occur on the basis that it is too awful to contemplate. It could easily happen and prudent investors should begin accounting for the possibility now.(Note - The opinions expressed in this article represent the
16334 views of the author only. They should not be seen as reflecting the views of Reuters).</

16337 procedure to become the first Australian to end his life under the law.Here is a brief outline of the steps involved:-- patients who are over 18, terminally ill and in unbearable pain or suffering must first contact a doctor resident in the Northern Territory and ask for approval for voluntary
16337 euthanasia. 16337 The specialist must also be a resident of Nothern Territory, but the psychiatrist can come from elsewhere in Australia;-- a seven day cooling-off period follows;-- after the waiting period, patients must reconfirm their request, and wait at least another 48 hours;-- if the territory authorities grant final approval, the assisted
16337 suicide can take place in the territory at any time the patients choose;-- the law lists a range of drugs which can be taken orally or by injection. If patients cannot administer the drugs themselves, the doctor is allowed to do so;-- drugs are administered in two stages. First, a
16337 barbiturate sends the patient to sleep within seconds. Then, a muscle-relaxant kills the patient by asphyxiation within minutes;-- the favoured method at this stage appears to be a computerised system developed by Dr Nitschke that takes the patient through a series of questions before a fatal injection. The final question
16337 says: "If you press 'Yes', you will cause a lethal injection to be given within 30 seconds, and you will die. Do you wish to proceed?";-- the coroner is advised and the death certificate records the patient died by euthanasia, listing the drugs used;-- the coroner can order an investigation

16385 What if Japan held an election and nobody came?Politicians jockeying for position ahead of a looming general election could find their toughest battles are not with each other, but against an apathy which has frayed many voters' attachment to any party at all.Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, in a widely expected
16385 move, told his ruling coalition partners on Thursday that he would dissolve parliament's Lower House on Friday.Polls must be held within 40 days of a dissolution and coalition officials have said October 20 is the likely date.The election will be the first poll for the Lower House -- the more
16385 powerful of Japan's two chambers of parliament -- since the conservative Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) temporarily lost a nearly four-decade grip on power in July 1993. Hashimoto is now LDP president.It is also the first test of a new electoral system which combines 300 single-member districts with 200 districts where
16385 members are selected by proportional representation.Critics charged that the old multi-member district system stifled policy debate, favoured rural voters, fostered corruption and blocked emergence of true two-party democracy.Wooing the masses of voters -- nearly half by many estimates -- who do not support any particular party and who may decline
16385 to cast their ballots at all will be a major challenge, though admittedly less so for politicians backed by well-oiled machines and ample funds, analysts said."Apathy does serve the interests of a lot of people, although they can't say that out loud," one analyst said.The main rivals in the election
16385 are the LDP, the conservative opposition Shinshinto, and the Democratic Party, a new group led by would-be reformers which must rely mostly on rebels from the LDP's current partners, the tiny New Party Sakigake and the Social Democrats, for members.Many pundits say the LDP is likely to win a plurality
16385 but will have to seek junior partners to form yet another coalition government. Surprises, however, could be in store."The most important factor is that more than 50 percent of the electorate are in no sympathy with any particular party," said Takashi Inoguchi, a political scientist at the United Nations University
16385 in Tokyo. "It's very, very volatile."Many voters were disillusioned by machinations which followed the unravelling of an unwieldy coalition which ousted the LDP in August 1993.That coalition delivered its promised electoral reform -- no mean feat -- but the LDP's return to power in 1994 in a ruling bloc that
16385 included its long-time rivals, the Socialists, left many dubious about prospects for meaningful change."In spite of all the turmoil in 1993, the LDP is back in power, and there is discontent with the reform parties, which failed to deliver a new kind of politics," said John Neuffer, a political analyst
16385 at Mitsui Marine Research Institute.Aware of a vague popular sentiment that old ways must be altered, politicians of every ilk are proclaiming dedication to "reform", co-opting rivals' slogans and blurring policy gaps.Topping the list of changes everyone says they want is "administrative reform", a broad concept encompassing varying prescriptions for
16385 smaller government, more political control over policy, and fewer of the regulations critics say suffocate Japan's private sector.One of the few areas where voters will have a clear choice is over an increase in the nation's three percent consumption tax, which is due to rise to five percent from April.The
16385 LDP is defending the unpopular tax increase as vital given Japan's huge budget deficit and its rapidly aging population, while Shinshinto is calling for a freeze until real administrative reform and government cost-cutting takes place."That's an issue, but it's not exactly a vision for the nation," Neuffer said.</

16402 David Chan held aloft China's red national flag, the one he intended to plant on a disputed East China Sea islet, and led his band of supporters in a rendition of the Chinese national anthem.Minutes later he stepped aboard a rusty tanker and set sail for the islands over which
16402 he was determined to assert China's sovereignty. "We will not retreat," Chan told Reuters, just before he began his voyage to the islands last Sunday.That act of defiance led to Chan's death on Thursday and made him the first casualty in a growing chorus of protests by Chinese communities in
16402 Hong Kong, Taiwan, China and Macau.Chan laid careful plans for the voyage in the Kien Hwa 2 to the cluster of tiny islands which Japan calls the Senkaku group and which China claims as the Diaoyu isles.The leader of the somewhat motley array of 18 activists planned to play a
16402 game of maritime cat-and-mouse with a fleet of Japanese coastguard vessels and to storm the islands and tear down a makeshift lighthouse built by Japanese rightwingers."We will use every tactic and every strategy...to dodge the Japanese patrol boats and get on to those islands to raise the Chinese flag and
16402 restore our sovereignty," he said.The 45-year-old media consultant and father of two was a seasoned street activist, donning a colourful headband and brandishing placards during recent demonstrations accusing the Japanese of invading the islands.But even Chan knew that trying to out-manoeuvre the Japanese coastguard on two Zodiac inflatable dinghies badly
16402 in need of repair was a dangerous, even reckless mission.If Chan was prepared to be a martyr, he gave no indication. "We know this could be dangerous, but this is Chinese territory, and we have every right to land there," he said confidently at the start of the voyage."We are
16402 civilians, we have no weapons, no explosives, and our ship is only a cargo ship, it's not armed. We will not retreat," Chan said.Within 24 hours of reaching the waters around the disputed islands northeast of Taiwan, the Kien Hwa 2 was hemmed in by up to 20 Japanese coast
16402 guard vessels.Earlier in the day, stormy seas had forced the protest ship to abandon efforts to land.Chan made a last gesture of defiance.Shackled to his ship by a length of rope that the men had evidently thought would keep them safe in rough seas, Chan and four other activists leapt
16402 into the sea.Efforts to rescue Chan were hampered when he lost consciousness as he was dragged in the wake of the vessel.In a supreme irony, a Japanese medical team boarded the Kien Hwa 2 to try to revive Chan, whose body had been hauled on deck nearly an hour after
16402 he jumped overboard."A doctor from Japan who boarded the Hong Kong ship confirmed that Chan Yuk Cheung David was dead," a spokesman for Japan's Maritime Safety Agency said.</

16406 China's central bank is considering phasing out the quotas for credit and loans which are a key part of the government's control mechanism for the economy, bankers and analysts said on Thursday.The quotas are one of the pillars of the centrally-planned economy, under which the Beijing leadership controls nationwide money
16406 supply by setting loan limits for major banks."We are considering such a move (to abolish the quotas) but no timetable has been set," said a central bank official reached by telephone from Beijing. Other officials declined to comment.Local media reports have said the People's Bank of China would like to
16406 start phasing out the loan quota system from early next year.The quotas limit loans by the four major state banks, the Construction Bank, Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank (ICBC) and the Agricultural Bank, to control nationwide money supply.Banking analysts said the issue had become more significant with
16406 the sharp fall in the market share of the Big Four in the past few years.The four are estimated to handle about 50 percent of all loans in China, compared with more than 80 percent in the late 1980s, with the remainder covered by smaller state banks which are not
16406 subject to quota restrictions."The abolition of the quota system is a must to turn the major state banks into real commercial banks in line with international practice," said a Beijing-based ICBC banker."We believe changes will happen before too long because China's financial reforms are now in full swing," he added.
16406 "It is becoming more and more difficult for the central bank to control money supply through the quota system."The official Economic Information News on Wednesday quoted unnamed officials as saying the central bank would start cancelling quotas for the state banks from as early as next year to accelerate their
16406 transformation into commercial banks.The paper said the central bank has already started ending the quotas on an experimental basis for some banks, such as those in Shanghai, and allowing them to lend purely on the basis of their reserves and debt-to-equity ratio.Most of Shanghai branches of the major state banks
16406 declined to comment, but a spokeswoman for the Shanghai branch of the Bank of China said it had not used the new system.Since the start of this year, Beijing has started to use other methods to adjust money supply including the establishment of a local currency interbank market early this
16406 year and the launch of central bank open market operations in April.But these methods are still officially in a test phase and their scale is limited by the central authorities.Analysts said they believed it will be years before the interbank market and open market operations alone will be an effective
16406 means of controlling money supply.</
