16466 Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told his partners in Japan's ruling coalition on Thursday that he will dissolve parliament's Lower House on Friday, paving the way for elections widely expected to be held on October 20.Shoichi Ide, president of Sakigake, one of the three coalition parties, disclosed the prime minister's comment
16466 to reporters after a meeting of coalition leaders."The prime minister told us that there was no other time when parliament could be dissolved than the opening of its special session on Friday," Ide told reporters.He did not provide a date for the general election, but government officials have said openly
16466 that an October 20 vote is expected. October 20 is a Sunday, the day Japanese elections are traditionally held, and the polls must be called within 40 days of a dissolution of parliament.Polls are not mandated until July 1997, but Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) -- the biggest partner in
16466 the coalition -- favours going before voters as early as possible before April, when a rise in an unpopular national sales tax will take effect. The consumption tax is to be raised to five percent from three percent.The smaller coalition parties had wanted more time, as they are locked in
16466 a bitter row over how to regroup for the polls, which will be held under a revised electoral system expected to benefit larger parties.Although the LDP is expected to get the most votes, no single party is likely to capture a majority in the 500-seat Lower House.This means the LDP
16466 could be forced to form a another coalition with one or more of its political rivals.The main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) is projected to finish second with around 200 Lower House seats.Except for the planned rise in the sales tax, there are few major policy issues facing the country.Japan's
16466 economy is recovering from a slump that followed the bursting of an asset "bubble" -- the end of an era of soaring real estate and stock prices -- in the early 1990s. But analysts and government experts agree it remains fragile and could be seriously set back by a rise
16466 in the sales tax.Hashimoto is Japan's fourth prime minister since the last general election in 1993, when the pro-business LDP lost its grip on power for the first time in 38 years.The polls will be the first under a system designed to make campaigning less costly and reduce graft. In
16466 place of a multi-seat system, 300 seats will be decided on a first-past-the-post basis and the other 200 by proportional representation.Members of the less-powerful Upper House are elected on a fixed schedule unrelated to the terms of the Lower House.</

16486 for that," he added.Under rules set out by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), banks operating globally must have a capital adequacy ratio -- the ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-related assets -- of more than eight percent.But bankers say that to compete aggressively in the international banking
16486 industry, banks need a capital adequacy ratio much higher than the required eight percent.Yamamoto said Fuji Bank, which has assets totalling about 51 trillion yen ($463 billion), aims to raise its preliminary international capital adequacy ratio to 10 percent and stabilise it there by the business year ending March 1999.Fuji's
16486 capital/asset ratio was 8.36 percent as of March 31.In June, Fuji changed a corporate rule to make it possible for it to issue preferred stocks. But Yamamoto said this was only to open up more options for supporting Fuji's BIS ratio and added that the bank was not considering any
16486 new share issues at the moment."We haven't decided when to increase our capital. We are going to pick the right time by watching the market carefully," he said.Meanwhile, Fuji was not considering trimming its assets to help its capital ratio, Yamamoto said.He said Fuji was likely to sell a large
16486 number of shares it owns under cross-shareholding schemes, in which companies hold stakes in each other to strengthen ties. 16486 its assets to support its capital-to-asset ratio, Yamamoto said.Asked about the bank's earnings for the half-year ending September 30, Yamamoto said: "Our forecast figures haven't changed from the ones we have announced before. 16486 net profit of 40 billion yen ($363 million)."Fuji believes it can achieve its parent net profit forecast of 70 billion yen ($636 million) in 1996/97 while continuing to dispose of problem loans aggressively, he said.He said Fuji had brought its problem loans down to a manageable level. 16495 Japan's claim to small disputed islands in the East China Sea dates back to January 1895 when the government formally declared the Senkaku Islands, called the Diaoyus in Chinese, part of Okinawa Prefecture.The territory lies in the East China Sea, west of Japan's Okinawa island, northeast of Taiwan and east
16495 of China's southeastern Fujian coast.It is now uninhabited but until the 1940s could boast a dried fish factory on one of its larger islands.With the signing of the San Francisco Peace Treaty in 1951, Japan was deprived of all of its territories seized since 1895, including Taiwan, Korea, and southern
16495 Sakhalin.The U.S. trusteeship of the Ryukyu Islands, the current Okinawa Prefecture, was permitted indefinitely, and the Senkaku Islands, registered as part of Okinawa, were also under the jurisdiction of U.S. forces until Okinawa's return in 1972.During the U.S. occupation of Okinawa, the islands were used for military drills by U.S.
16495 forces.In 1971, Taiwan and China both officially claimed the islands as theirs, but neither China nor Japan brought up the issue in 1972 when the two nations issued the landmark China-Japan joint communique.Japan ceased diplomatic relations with Taiwan following the communique, recognising only the communist government.When Japan signed a peace
16495 treaty with China in 1978, Deng Xiaoping, the then vice-premier of China, said the territorial issue between the two countries "will be shelved until the next generation comes up with a solution".But the Japanese government claimed there was no pending territorial issue regarding the Senkaku Islands.In the same year, a
16495 first makeshift lighthouse was set up by a Japanese ultra-rightist group on the largest of the islands, called Uozuri-jima in Japanese.The first major flare-up on the issue of sovereignty, which had been dormant for many years, came in 1988 when the same rightist group Nihon Seinen Sha (Japan Youth Federation)
16495 rebuilt the lighthouse and sought official recognition.Taiwan had been particularly strong in voicing its protest, which made Japan back down and leave the application for official recognition of the lighthouse pending "out of diplomatic considerations", according to a Maritime Safety Agency spokesman.Japan lodged a formal protest in 1992 when China
16495 claimed the disputed islands by enacting the Law of the People's Republic of China on its Territorial Waters and Their Contiguous Areas.In the law, China claimed the South China Sea and much of East China Sea, which includes the Senkaku Islands, as "contiguous areas".The United Nations Convention on the Law
16495 of the Sea -- adopted by the General Assembly in November 1994 to nudge countries with rival territorial claims to settle them -- only sparked renewed rivalry.In July, the rightist group built its third lighthouse in the smaller of the islands, owned by a family in Saitama Prefecture north of
16495 Tokyo.The Japanese government has continuously maintained that it was not involved in, nor would it endorse, any private activity taking place on privately owned property.</

16580 A management buyout of a Malaysian government property firm has spawned overnight a huge conglomerate -- making millionaires of the managers -- in the latest chapter of Malaysia's ambitious privatisation programme.On August 22, 14 senior managers of Perbadanan Nasional (Pernas) took control of the privatised company, which in its heyday
16580 was used as a vehicle to take over British concerns in the post-colonial era.The new entity, Pernas International Holdings Bhd (PIHB), has emerged as Malaysia's biggest hotel operator with 11 now in the stable and two more on the drawing board.PIHB suddenly became a dominant force in the palm oil
16580 sector with 195,000 acres (79,000 hectares) under cultivation and plans to expand to 300,000 acres (121,400 hectares) in five years.It also wound up with a controlling stake in Malayawata Steel and two other listed firms, along with construction and engineering companies."For a little less than 500 million ringgit ($200 million),
16580 the 14 individuals have gained control of a robust and healthy conglomerate with net assets of more than three billion ringgit...," the Business Times daily said in a commentary.The privatisation was a two-step process. Pernas' assets were injected into PIHB for 1.15 billion ringgit. The managers then took a controlling
16580 32 percent stake in the enlarged PIHB for 495 million ringgit.The money will be loaned to them by a local bank "on very favourable terms", Shahriman Tunku Sulaiman, Pernas chairman for the past 20 years, told analysts and journalists.BIGGEST MANAGEMENT BUYOUT IN MALAYSIAN HISTORYThe deal was striking, not only because
16580 it was the biggest management buyout in Malaysian history, but also because there was so little fuss over the demise of Pernas.Pernas was set up in 1969, after racial riots between Malays and Chinese, to build wealth among "Bumiputras" (native sons) in an economy long dominated by ethnic Chinese.Pernas was
16580 in charge of seizing control of the country's major economic assets, such as then plantation-based Sime Darby Bhd, which was itself privatised years later.Its importance waned when Permodalan Nasional Bhd became the force for creating Bumiputra wealth through unit trusts. Sime and other firms were sold to PNB at bargain
16580 prices.The end of Pernas reflects a major shift in government thinking, starting from about five years ago, analysts say.SHIFT IN GOVERNMENT POLICYThe Malay-dominated government is no longer so concerned with creating a large pool of Bumiputra entrepreneurs.Privatisation contracts have usually gone to a small group of politically well-connected Malays who,
16580 the government believes, have the wherewithal to handle big projects.Last year's privatisation of Hicom Holdings Bhd, a conglomerate which manufactures the Malaysian-made Proton car, and the sale of Malaysian Airline System Bhd the year before, followed a familiar pattern.Hicom was sold to Yahaya Ahmad, who heads the automotive firm Diversified
16580 Resources Bhd.Tajudin Ramli took a controlling 32 percent stake in Malaysian Airlines for 1.79 billion ringgit in the largest privatisation deal to date, after negotiating the biggest personal loan ever granted in Malaysia.Tajudin is among a group of bumiputra tycoons known as "Daim's boys", executives who used to work in
16580 companies owned by former finance minister Daim Zainuddin.Daim, himself a self-made billionaire and author of the government's privatisation programme, is believed to have helped Yahaya secure a 1.7 billion ringgit offshore loan to finance the Hicom deal.Jomo Sundaram, an economics professor at the University of Malaya who has written extensively
16580 about Malaysia's privatisation programme, said the Pernas case broke a pattern."At least in this case, it was a management buyout. The company was turned over to a group that one presumes has a demonstrated competency and track record."That has not always been the case in the past," he added.Jomo was
16580 critical of the privatisation programme for selling off state assets at bargain-basement prices.OBJECTIVES OF PRIVATISATIONThe objectives of privatisation in cutting government spending, generating revenue and deepening the capital markets, have been subordinated to the "Malay wealth-enhancing objective, particularly to the politically well-connected".Malaysia's privatisation policy drew criticism at last year's party
16580 convention of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) for benefiting the few. Some analysts say it may come up again at this year's convention in October.Mahathir told the convention last year the government wanted "talented, responsible and serious entrepreneurs" for projects. It was better than the old
16580 way of handing out shares, land or licences to bumiputras "without taking into account their performance, background or capabilities".Hicom and MAS were sold to Tajudin and Yahaya because they could raise the money and the government believed those who owned stakes in companies managed them better, Mahathir said.But critics say
16580 Mahathir's privatisation policy smacks of cronyism and poses certain risks for foreign investors."The problem is, such local businessmen tend to ride on the coat tails of prominent political figures whose rise and fall add to uncertainty about the business environment," said a report by Political &amp; Economic Risk Consultancy on
16580 Malaysia."Foreign investors looking for long-term business partners, therefore, face the possibility of exposing themselves to substantial political risk."It is an open secret, for instance, that there is no love lost between deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim -- Mahathir's heir apparent -- and Daim, his predecessor at the
16580 finance ministry and UMNO's current treasurer.Another of "Daim's boys" stands to gain in the next project up on the privatisation block -- state-run railway KTM Bhd.A three-party consortium led by Renong Bhd, along with Bolton Properties Bhd and Diversified Resources has been, in principle, awarded the railway privatisation.One the companies
16580 is headed by Daim proteges -- Renong executive chairman Halim Saad. Like Tajudin and other bumiputra tycoons, Halim worked for Daim in the state property firm Peremba Bhd in the 1980s.Malaysia's 1996-2000 Five-Year Plan, unveiled in May, identified 23 other major projects slated for privatisation.OTHER PROJECTS SALTED FOR PRIVATISATIONThey include
16580 debt-laden Perwaja Steel, which was recently awarded to small Bumiputra-owned steel firm Maju Holdings.Other privatisation projects include the nation's second largest bank, Bank Bumiputra Malaysia; Bank Simpanan Nasional, several highways, ports, hospitals and government agencies.Privatisation has played a key role in bringing in new technology and attracting foreign funds since
16580 most of the projects involved a foreign tie-up, a stock exchange listing or, as in the case of Pernas, a new share issue, analysts said."One of the aims of privatisation in Malaysia has been to deepen the capital markets and to use the capital markets to raise money for infrastructure

16593 The Bank of Lebanon has changed its intervention mechanism on the Beirut foreign exchange market by shifting from a single mid-price quotation to a bid-offer system, foreign exchange dealers said on Thursday.The Bank has since Tuesday set a difference of three Lebanese pounds between the prices at which it intervenes
16593 to buy and sell dollars, the dealers said.This replaces a single mid-price at which it either bought or sold dollars in the past, depending on the market.Dealers said the change would stimulate interbank trading, making the market less dependent on the central bank and more on supply and demand."This gives
16593 us dealers the opportunity to quote between each other. I believe it's very good," Wadih Sabbagh, chief foreign exchange dealer at Byblos Bank, told Reuters.The central bank offered on Thursday to buy dollars at 1,557 pounds and to sell at 1,560. The dollar closed at 1,558.75.Sabbagh said the Forex Club-Liban
16593 had asked central bank governor Riad Salameh nine months ago to set buying and selling prices to allow a spread for foreign exchange dealers to quote, and the World Bank had recommended the change."We expected this earlier, but now they have responded," Sabbagh said.The central bank's practice of setting a
16593 single price for the past few years had idled Beirut dealers by making the market dependent on the Bank of Lebanon for buying and selling dollars, he said.Another Beirut dealer who asked not to be identified said the Bank of Lebanon had set the band very narrow to maintain stability
16593 while giving leeway for commercial banks to make a market within those boundaries."It's not very significant because they are setting the boundaries in a very narrow band," the dealer said, "but in the longer term I think it's a step in the right direction because it will make the market
16593 more affected by supply and demand rather than just by the central bank."Dealers said the central bank was taking advantage of a surge of confidence in the pound on the Beirut market during the past four weeks."I think it's a very clear sign of confidence in the pound," the dealer
16593 said.He said investors were selling dollars to buy pounds, but if tension developed in the system the central bank would narrow the band."But I think with time, if we remain in a stable scenario, the band will tend to widen....Bit by bit we are moving more towards supply and demand
16593 in the interbank market."-- Andrew Tarnowski - Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 353078</

16622 Kuwait, political odd-man-out among Gulf Arab states, draws the uneasy gaze of its neighbours next month by electing a body they would prefer to do without -- a parliament.Only men may vote in the second assembly polls since the 1991 Gulf War, but in such a politically conservative region it
16622 is remarkable any country holds elections at all, Kuwaitis say.The sharp-tongued chamber is no rubber stamp. It has taken painful bites out of government prestige throughout its 33 years of existence and in particular since the 1991 Gulf War, with tough probes into alleged corruption.Some call parliament Kuwait's best-kept political
16622 secret.The nearest it came to international prominence recently was when it was asked by Kuwait's government to approve the deployment this month of 3,500 U.S. troops in the latest security flare-up with former occupier Baghdad.But while its international profile may be low, the assembly is the focus of bad-tempered domestic
16622 politics and notorious throughout the Gulf for the venom of its verbal exchanges.Gathering weekly in a splendid chamber, MPs engage in a political blood-letting that horrifies neighbouring states reliant solely on ruling families or virtual one-party systems.Walkouts, finger-pointing and shouting matches provide drama in moments when Kuwait's uneasy compromise between
16622 hereditary rule and popular participation temporarily breaks down.But despite parliament's confrontations with the government and its dogged pursuit of more power, its existence has helped boost the country's overall political stability, diplomats say.Six years after the turmoil of Iraq's 1990-91 occupation Kuwait is probably the most stable country in the
16622 Gulf because parliament provides a forum for people's views, diplomats say."Look at the unrest happening in Bahrain and elsewhere in the Gulf. Here in Kuwait we have this important safety valve," says Islamist opposition lawmaker Adnan Abdul-Samad.The government headed by the ruling Sabah family is expected to work hard in
16622 the limited franchise, October 7 polls to wrest control of the chamber from opposition deputies whose war on corruption has earned them powerful enemies as well as fans.Parliament's Islamists, liberals and independents have made their presence felt wherever Kuwaiti officials do business -- from Europe, to Asia and the United
16622 States -- by trying to monitor closely flows of public funds.Much of their work is a reaction to Kuwait as it was run in parliament's absence in the late 1980s when, MPs allege, Kuwaiti officials presided over an orgy of kickbacks, influence-peddling and mismanagement that cost Kuwait billions of dollars.MPs
16622 attribute the alleged graft to the absence of assembly oversight. Kuwaiti leaders dissolved parliament in 1986 during the Iran-Iraq war amid political and security tensions.Kuwait was shaken by pro-democracy protests in early 1990 that police quelled with tear gas and opposition arrests.The state revived parliament with elections in 1992, mindful
16622 that its human rights record was in the international spotlight after the 1991 Gulf War ended a seven-month Iraqi occupation.MPs' targets have been high profile. Parliament was a key force behind the 1994 indictment of former oil minister Sheikh Ali Khalifa al-Sabah, by common consent the most gifted minister of
16622 his generation and once a major personality in world oil, on charges of earning illegal profits.Sheikh Ali denies all charges. The trial continues.Whatever the outcome of the polls, the prime minister is by tradition a Sabah member. But parliament's political complexion is important because Kuwaiti stability has traditionally depended on
16622 cooperation between the chamber and the government.The opposition seeks more parliamentary control over the state machinery and more elected MPs serving in the cabinet - aims they are determined to pursue in the next assembly term.MPs say some of the men they have pursued in their graft probe -- many
16622 of them in voluntary exile -- retain links to authority and seek to bring about a more docile parliament.</

16637 French economic growth prospects look good for the third quarter of 1996 due to strong household spending but could retreat in the following three months with an end to car-buying incentives, economists said on Thursday.The economic outlook for the third quarter was bolstered by strong household spending data released by
16637 national statistics institute INSEE on Thursday, with spending rising 3.0 percent in August after a dip of 0.6 percent in July.INSEE highlighted that the August spending surge was largely due to an 18.1 percent rise in car sales, which have in turn been further boosted by a new-cars-for-old subsidy scheme
16637 coming to an end on September 30."We already knew car sales had been very strong in August so the surprise is not in car sales. There's a possible surprise in sense that durables, white and brown products that is, have performed very well," said Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley
16637 investment bank."Over the full year, consumption will be much higher than anyone had expected, including the government," he said."That said, car sales in September will be even higher than in August. But the price will be a fourth quarter which will turn out negative in terms of consumption. 1997 will
16637 start with a negative."Philippe Brossard, economist at ABN Amro, said he expected 1.0 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) in the third quarter, due to strong spending but also a rise in the number of working days in the INSEE data compared to the second quarter.Chaney said he was
16637 "now confident of 1.1 percent GDP growth in the third quarter" and he was revising his expectations for third quarter household spending for the period to 1.2 percent from a previous forecast of 0.7 percent.David Naude, economist at JP Morgan investment bank also said he was expecting "renewed weakness" in

16721 To many it is a song by Abba. To Londoners it is a railway station.But to millions with a feeling for history it was the scene of the battle that broke France's military dominance of Europe -- although not all could say just where it is.Given that there are some
16721 75 Waterloos scattered around the globe, that is hardly surprising .Researchers have identified 35 Waterloos in the United States, three in Canada, 15 in Britain, eight in Australia, five in Jamaica and others in the Caribbean, Sierra Leone, Germany, Ireland and even one in France -- although the name is
16721 understandably not terribly popular in that country.But the original Waterloo is in Belgium, 20 km (12 miles) south of the capital Brussels, and it is celebrating this month its 200th anniversary as a self-governing commune."Ours is the real Waterloo...but many of the others have outgrown the parent," said Yves Vander
16721 Cruysen, the town's alderman for culture and tourism.Indeed, it was only the occupation of the area by the French Revolutionary forces in 1796 that finally allowed Waterloo to break free of its domination by neighbouring Braine-l'Alleud -- although it took 30 years more of wrangling to set the borders.Many of
16721 the other Waterloos around the world were actually founded by soldiers who took part in the epic battle in June 1815, when an allied army led by Britain's Duke of Wellington and helped by a Prussian force led by Marshal Bluecher trounced the French army led by Napoleon Bonaparte.An estimated
16721 40,000 soldiers -- one-in-five of those who fought in the battle -- were killed. But the battle put the town on the map."Waterloo is known throughout the world for the battle. But we wanted to show everyone there is much more to the place than that," Vander Cruysen said.Nowadays Waterloo,
16721 a solely French-speaking commune in this bilingual country, is a somewhat calmer place with a highly cosmopolitan character.As part of its bicentennial celebrations, Waterloo has invited the civic heads from all of its namesakes to join in the party. Most have had to decline but 10 will be there at
16721 the end of September to wave the flag.The celebrations kick off on Thursday September 26 when the 10 will meet their Belgian counterpart and open an exhibition on the history of Waterloo from its rural start, through the battle and on to its present international status.But the high points will
16721 be on Friday, Saturday and Sunday with a bicentennial banquet, an international fair and a vintage and veteran car rally respectively.For 1,796 francs ($58) -- symbolic of the year in which Waterloo won its freedom -- diners will be able to feast on local cheeses, fresh and smoked salmon, roast
16721 scampi with shallots and tomatoes, roast lamb with maize crepes, cake, coffee and a selection of wines and -- of course -- water.But of the set-piece events, the most eclectic is likely to be the international fair, including samples of many of the different cultures represented among Waterloo's 28,000 inhabitants.Vander
16721 Cruysen said that with 96 different nationalities listed among Waterloo's inhabitants, it could justifiably claim to be about the most cosmopolitan commune in Belgium.Americans, English, Koreans, Finns, French, Greeks, Indians, Irish, Japanese, Norwegians and Swedes are just some of the nationalities to be found in the town -- making it
16721 easy to understand why it is as normal to hear English as French on the streets.</
16722 Central bank governors used to call their finance ministers after a Group of Seven (G7) summit to hear what happened.Now, finance ministers call central bank governors after the monthly meeting at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) in Basle for an update.While this may not always be the case, it
16722 is clear central banks have taken over the lead from governments as the main agents in the global financial markets, leading economists say.The expansion of the membership of BIS with nine emerging economic powers underscores the key role of central banks and ultimately foreshadows changes to the core of BIS,
16722 the Group of 10 (G10) leading industrial nations, economists say."BIS is becoming more important as a forum for central banks because central banks are becoming more important," said Christopher Huhne, managing director of sovereign ratings at European rating agency IBCA.Earlier this month, the board of BIS, made up of G10
16722 central bank governors, invited nine new central banks from Russia, China, India, Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Saudi Arabia, Brazil and Mexico to join the 32-member organisation."The expansion will give BIS more visibility, clout and legitimacy in a wide number of countries," said Peter Kenen, professor of economics at Princeton
16722 University.MOVE SYMBOLISES NEW ECONOMIC WORLD ORDERWhile the move largely formalises the growing involvement of emerging countries in BIS in recent years, it symbolises the new economic world order and BIS's push to play a key role."If BIS had stuck with its previous membership, it would have had a declining influence,"
16722 said Morris Goldstein, senior fellow at the Institute for International Economics.The BIS expansion comes only days before final agreement is expected on boosting emergency credit lines the International Monetary Fund (IMF) can draw on in times of severe crisis.New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB) should complement the $25 billion of existing
16722 credit lines in the General Arrangements to Borrow (GAB) and involve many emerging countries, including new BIS members South Korea, Hong Kong and Singapore.BIS serves as an example of how international organisations must adapt to changing times if they want to remain relevant."This will be the form for international financial
16722 institutions of the 21st century," said Avinash Persaud, head of currency research at J.P.Morgan.The BIS, the IMF and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) are all adapting to the shift in economic power away from Western Europe.But rather than jostle for power, OECD chief economist Kumiharu Shigehara said
16722 all three institutions have roles to play and are now carving out their specific niches.UNIQUE CHARACTER OF BISBIS, the world's oldest international financial institution, has a unique standing among international organisations because it is owned and governed by central banks."BIS is the international organisation for central banks. It is the
16722 only organisation that is run by and for central banks, where finance ministries don't get to look in," said Huhne.Although BIS was founded in 1930 to deal with the German reparations after World War One, its key function was always to serve as a forum for cooperation among central banks.Cooperation
16722 not only takes the form of monthly meetings of central bank governors -- particularly G10 -- but BIS also serves as a hub for discussions among central bankers or supervisors about monetary policy and financial stability.G10 actually comprises 11 countries. The G7 -- the U.S., Japan, Germany, Canada, Britain, France
16722 and Italy -- as well as the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden and Switzerland.Frequent face-to-face meetings by governors and central bank staff is highly valued by central bankers as creating a level of personal trust that serves them well in times of crises."I cannot underestimate the importance of trust and personal relations.
16722 That is really what banking is all about, the word of someone," said Kenen.Including emerging economies into this exclusive club should strengthen early warning systems and help bankers or supervisors react in a timely fashion to potential trouble spots."The new members will take an active role as a way to
16722 improve banking and market statistics," Shigehara said.Over the years -- notably in the British sterling crises of the 1960s -- the BIS participated in ad hoc assistance to defend speculative attacs on currencies and it was also active in arranging a $10 billion line of credit to Mexico in 1995.The
16722 growing prominence of independent central banks has thrust the BIS further into the spotlight.In a world of integrated capital markets, movements in exchange rates play a larger role in policy transmission, necessitating a growing need for communication and cooperation among monetary authorities, economists say.A further implication of the globalisation of
16722 international financial markets is the need to integrate the rapidly growing emerging markets in work toward fostering systemic stability."You can't have a discussion about international financial markets and crisis management, particularly after Mexico, without emerging economies. Otherwise you get a distorted view of the world," said Goldstein.While the expansion of
16722 BIS reflects the economic might of emerging nations, the impetus to reach out came from the creation of the European Monetary Instititute (EMI) in 1994, the forerunner to a European Central Bank.Plans to set up an Asian-style BIS probably added impetus to the expansion to avoid competing institutions.Since the 1960s
16722 BIS has been associated mainly with European issues and provided a host of services, including a secretariat for the committee of EEC central bank governors and became the agent for the European Monetary Cooperation Fund in 1973.But this work has shifted to EMI in Frankfurt and is likely to encourage
16722 Europe's G10 members to speak with a single voice."My suspicion is that European central banks would still have individual seats on the BIS board, but clearly speak with one voice in a very enchanced degree," said Norman Williams, European economist at Barclays de Zoete Wedd (BZW).The decline in the relative
16722 wealth and influence of G10 economies and the growing importance of financial systems in emerging countries is likely to put pressure on smaller G10 countries to give up their seat around the table."We won't have a situation where the G10 dictates what the standards are," Goldstein said. "That just won't

16729 Dade County Finance Director Ed Marquez said Friday he had been subpoenaed to testify before a federal grand jury investigating corruption in the county's bond deals.Marquez said County Manager Armando Vidal and bond administrator Lidia Monzon had also been subpoenaed to appear before the grand jury in Miami on Tuesday.The
16729 subpoenas came one day after federal prosecutors subpoeaned records from numerous Dade County bond deals involving San Francisco-based municipal bond firm Grigsby Brandford &amp; Co, Marquez said.The Miami Herald reported Thursday that FBI videotapes show Calvin Grigsby, the former president of the firm, allegedly offering Dade County Commissioner James Burke
16729 a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering a $183 million Dade County bond deal to the firm.The conversation allegedly took place last month in a San Francisco hotel where Burke, Grigsby and Miami municipal bond firm owner Howard Gary discussed the kickbacks, the newspaper said.The first subpoena also requested records
16729 related to the method the county uses to select bond underwriters, and records for several past and upcoming bond deals involving Grigsby Brandford."The inkling I got is they're going to cover the same stuff they're asking for on the other subpoenas," Marquez said of his pending grand jury appearance.Marquez said
16729 federal investigators gave no indication how long the grand jury investigation would last.Vidal and Monzon were not immediately available for comment late Friday.Burke, who was chairman of the finance committee that oversees county bond issues, said the Securities and Exchange Commission had also subpoenaed documents from the finance department."I've encouraged
16729 them (department staff) to send more than they subpoenaed because I want to get the full story of what happened," said Burke in an interview.Burke has denied wrongdoing and told Reuters there was no bribe. Gary, Grigsby, the FBI and federal prosecutors have all declined to comment.No charges have been
16729 filed in connection with the Dade County bond allegations.Burke, who is black, said he believes investigators were probing "primarily the minority transactions and black firms" because he has been an advocate for including minority-owned firms in bond deals."I've said from the rostrum that things are not going to be fair
16729 until you have inclusion of black firms, particularly at the senior level," Burke said.Also subpoenaed were records documenting how Grigsby Brandford was chosen as senior manager for the issue.Regarding allegations in press reports that he steered to Grigsby Brandford a $183 million revenue bond refunding for a recyling plant, Burke
16729 said the firm was selected as senior manager by the plant owner in response to an unsolicited proposal from Grigsby Brandford.Other Dade County finance officials have said the underwriter was selected by recycling plant officials, and not by the county.The other deal linked to the allegations, a tentative $165 million
16729 revenue bond issue for a new basketball arena, was awarded to Grigsby Brandford because they were next in line among the county's standing pool of bond underwriters, Burke said."It was part of our regular rotation," he said.</
16730 Robert Holland said Friday that he was resigning as president and chief executive of Ben &amp; Jerry's Homemade Inc. to allow a marketing specialist to take the helm of the ice cream maker as it seeks to expand overseas."The reasons I'm making way for a new CEO is that I
16730 have good instincts, but not world-class experience in the consumer goods business," Holland said in a telephone interview after announcing he was leaving the Vermont-based company known for its quirky product names and corporate largesse.Holland and company co-founder Ben Cohen both said the 56-year-old Holland's departure, on Oct. 31, will
16730 come at a time when many of the goals he faced upon taking over less than two years ago have been met.Still, the company's stock lost $1, or almost 8 percent, after the news was announced. The shares later recovered a bit to trade at $12.75, down 50 cents, in
16730 afternoon trading on Nasdaq.Ben &amp; Jerry's said this month it expected third-quarter earnings to be "materially" below last year's, but Holland said things were improving as the company battles archrival Haagen-Daz for sales in the market for premium ice cream, which is about 2 percent of all ice-cream sales."Our earnings
16730 are back on track to where they were before the third quarter," Holland said. "We're away from the precipice. Our earnings are solid."Holland replaced the firm's famous founders early in 1995, when the company -- originally known for its counter-culture corporate culture -- moved from a "founder-led" system to a
16730 more professional management structure.As health-conscious Americans began swearing off fattening foods, Holland was brought in to introduce the company's products, like "Cherry Garcia" and "Chunky Monkey" ice cream, to sweet-toothed consumers overseas.The no-nonsense, button-downed executive -- the antithesis of the bearded, tie-dyed founders of the company, whose scruffy visages appear
16730 on every pint -- did manage to restore order to Ben &amp; Jerry's operations and finances.Holland said the ice cream maker's expansion into Europe was on target, although "not as fast as I would like," and Ben &amp; Jerry's would enter the Japanese market with an eye on the entire
16730 Pacific Rim.However, with premium ice cream in countries like Britain selling at twice the price of lower-priced brands, Holland said, a highly experienced marketing executive with international skills was needed to run the company."We've got a pretty sophisticated challenge," he said from the company's new headquarters in Burlington, Vt.He said
16730 a key challenge to boosting sales was to get more consumers to make a taste test. Many people who buy a first pint are repeat buyers, but that getting that first trial is difficult.Holland, a former chief executive of a plastics firm and consultant to Fortune 500 companies, took over
16730 at Ben &amp; Jerry's in February 1995 with great fanfare after Cohen stepped up to the role of chairman.He was hired after the company launched an unorthodox search campaign through newspaper advertisements in which it invited candidates to write essays explaining why they were suited for the job.After receiving more
16730 than 22,500 responses to its "Yo, I'm Your CEO" write-in campaign, Ben &amp; Jerry's hired Holland, although there were reports that he was actually found through an executive search firm."Bob arrived just when we needed him to help straighten out our operations, get our new plant up and running, start
16730 our international business and launch our new sorbet line. We are very grateful for his contribution," said Cohen, who with Jerry Greenfield turned a correspondence course in ice cream-making into a $150 million company.Holland said that in addition to its overseas expansion, the company had also upgraded its manufacturing operations
16730 and improved employee morale, once said to be on the decline, under a new human resources director."Ben &amp; Jerry's has great products, great people and a promising future," Holland said in a statement.The company, however, does not have a successor for Holland, who will remain as a director through June
16730 1997.Bruce Bowman, senior director of operations, was given the additional title of chief operating officer on an interim basis and will oversee day-to-day management of the company until a successor to Holland is found.The company said a subcommittee of the board would begin a search for a new CEO immediately.</

16733 The Belgian government on Friday reached agreement on a 1997 budget designed to pave the way for it to meet the economic targets for European economic and monetary union (EMU) without damaging consumer confidence.A government source told Reuters on Friday that an 80 billion franc ($2.55 billion) austerity package will
16733 cut Belgium's state deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 from an estimated 3.0 percent in 1996."There is a full agreement on the budget. We will reach the 2.9 percent target without hurting the average consumer too much," the source said.Under the Maastricht Treaty, would-be members
16733 of a European single currency must meet a deficit target of 3.0 percent of GDP in 1997. Other criteria cover debt and inflation.Cabinet aides will hammer out the final details of the package over the weekend, after which it will go to a full cabinet session of the centre-left government
16733 on Monday.Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will present the full text of the 1997 budget to the Belgian parliament on Tuesday afternoon."The three percent norm is reached, that is what financial markets want. And with the exception of beer drinkers, this budget is not going to hurt anyone," said BBL
16733 analyst Peter Vanden Houte.Dehaene appears to have shied away from raising already record-high income tax and radical reform of the country's social security system.On the taxation side, the 1997 budget hits hard at unhealthy habits -- such as smoking, drinking and driving a car.On the spending side, Dehaene has made
16733 a first stab a reforming Belgium's pension system. With a rapidly ageing population, this is a time bomb for the country's already troubled state finances.Taxes, mainly indirect, will rise by 30 billion francs. Taxes on petrol will be raised by one franc per litre in October and another franc in
16733 January. Taxes on beer will rise by one franc per 25-centilitre bottle, on spirits by 12 francs per 75-centilitre bottle, the source said.The council of ministers on Friday approved higher excise duties by executive decree. Most will take effect as of October.The investment world will also have to contribute an
16733 estimated five billion francs.Retail investors will have to pay a 0.3 percent tax on physical delivery of securities by banks and brokerages."A small price for anonymity," one analyst said. For tax reasons, many Belgians avoid holding registered securities and prefer holding bearer stocks and bonds in their safes.Banks will have
16733 to pay a 0.06 percent tax on the amount outstanding in savings books accounts, tax-free savings accounts which are Belgium's most popular savings schemes.The source also said that 50 billion francs of spending cuts had been decided in the social security sector.The most visible measure is a gradual increase of
16733 women's retirement age to 65 years from 60 over a 13-year period, although this will have little impact on the 1997 budget.The government also decided on a two percent tax on all early retirement pensions.Most other measures in the social security sector are highly technical. They include a reduction of
16733 family allowances for teenagers, a reduction in unemployment benefits for older people and some targeted measures in the health sector. ($1=31.33 Belgian Franc)</

16737 European Union ministers on Friday agreed a key part of their plan to liberalise EU telecommunications markets with a regime for licensing companies once state monopolies are ended.They also agreed to coordinate the regulation of satellite systems that will begin to offer mobile phone and data-transmission services by the end
16737 of the decade.But telecoms ministers watered down the European Commission proposals for both initiatives, which must be approved by the European Parliament before final adoption.The telecoms licensing plan requires governments to use open and objective procedures and establishes a "one-stop shopping" system for companies wanting to operate in more than
16737 one EU state.A final sticking point was over when operators must apply for individual licences and when to allow them to fall under a "general authorisation" scheme requiring no prior approval.The European Commission wanted to restrict the use of individual licences to cases where governments needed to allocate radio frequencies
16737 or numbers, grant access to land or impose public service obligations.But the ministers decided EU states should be allowed to require individual licences as well for all providers of voice telephone services or public telecommunications networks, EU officials said.They also agreed that governments should be able to limit the number
16737 of operators in a given sector only if needed to ensure the efficient use of radio frequencies or, on a temporary basis, because of a shortage of telephone numbers.That responded to a request from Spain, which said it needed more time to reorganise its numbering system as required under previous
16737 EU legislation.The text said governments must, in principle, decide applications for individual licences within six weeks, although that could be extended up to eight months in cases of competitive bidding.On satellite personal communications services, the ministers agreed a watered-down plan that would give primary responsibility to the inter-governmental European Conference
16737 for Postal and Telecommunications Administrations (CEPT).The European Commission had hoped to set up a single EU system for selecting and authorising satellite systems that will begin to offer mobile phone and data communications services by the end of the decade.However, EU member states in earlier discussions resisted the plan because
16737 it would have allowed the Commission to draw up criteria for licensing operators and to play a major role in selecting them.EU officials said the ministers agreed to ask CEPT to take a series of actions by mid-1997, including harmonising the use of frequency bands and the procedures for authorising
16737 the new systems.The legislation also asks the Commission and CEPT to set up a "one-, stop-shopping" system to make it easier for operators to get licensed in more than one EU state at the same time.The ultimate decision on whether to allow a communications system to operate a satellite uplink
16737 rests with individual EU states.EU states would be required to implement the telecommunications licensing regime by December 31, 1997, just in time for the January 1, 1998 EU deadline for liberalising all telecoms sectors in most member countries.The satellite plan will take force 20 days after it is published in

16738 in 1995, then rebound to 1.0 percent in 1997."The economy bottomed out in the first quarter and we expect it to improve next year, but the upswing will be very modest because of the government's savings programme and pressure from weak domestic demand," WIFO deputy head Ewalt Walterskirchen told a
16738 news conference.Buoyant exports would contribute to the upturn next year, WIFO's report said, noting that exporters were benefiting from relatively stable foreign currency markets and strong demand from central and eastern Europe. 16738 weakened after a promising first half. 16738 WIFO said.The institute traced the drop to the effects of government savings and a higher tax burden from the beginning of 1997. 16738 was likely to remain in the doldrums in the short term, Walterskirchen said. The problem was structural and the industry would have to take sharper measures to become more competitive."Austria has rested on its laurels for too long as far as tourism is concerned. We must now look to other
16738 areas to compensate for the downturn in this sector."The industry has seen revenues fall from 70 billion schillings ($6.54 billion) at their peak to around 20 billion schillings last year.Inflation would remain at a modest 1.7 percent this year and next, compared with 2.2 percent in 1995, WIFO predicted."For a
16738 hard-currency country it (the inflation rate) is not as good as should be expected," the head of the Institute for Advanced Studies, Bernhard Felderer, said.Overall sluggish economic growth meant there would be no turnaround in the employment market, with the number of jobless rising to 7.1 percent this year from

16746 Two British tobacco companies facing a new threat of legal action against the health effects of smoking cigarettes are set to maintain their longstanding robust defence of their record, industry experts said on Friday.Forty cancer sufferers plan to sue Imperial Tobacco, about to be demerged from Hanson Plc, and American
16746 Brands Inc unit Gallaher, in a group action.Their lawyers said the case would be based on the alleged failure of the firms -- which produce such brands as Benson and Hedges, Players, Embassy and Silk Cut -- to reduce the levels of tar in their cigarettes after doctors in the
16746 late 1950s began saying tar could lead to the onset of cancer.Share analysts said the thrust of the case was not new, and was of a type the industry had successfully defended itself against in the past, but saw the lawyer's approach as new.Despite being denied legal aid, the plaintiffs
16746 are to press on with their case because the lawyers representing them are prepared to work on a so-called "no-win, no-fee" basis."This is a step change in the litigation risk for firms," said Juliane Jessup, tobacco analyst at UBS in London.She added that the availability of the approach, little used
16746 in British courts up to now, was set to be a boost for potential plaintiffs who have in the past faced prohibitive legal costs.A flurry of new lawsuits would, inevitably, also mean higher defence costs for companies, she added. "If there are more cases it will be more expensive for
16746 the industry to defend."However, analysts also doubted that the change of tack by plaintiffs would lead to anything other than a continued robust defence from the tobacco companies in Britain."It's fatal for these companies to settle out of court," said analyst Mark Duffy at SBC Warburg.He added that if the
16746 cancer victims' cases come to court as a group action, as planned, historical experience from lawsuits in the United States and Britain suggested they would have a lower chance of success than taking action individually."If it is a group action, that seems a difficult way to go about it if
16746 you're a plaintiff," he said.In particular, he pointed out, tobacco companies' lawyers had often managed to expose variances in plaintiffs' injuries and circumstances that undermined the "commonality" of claims.Along with other analysts, Duffy nevertheless saw no reason for cigarette companies to be complacent and simply rest on their past record
16746 in beating back such lawsuits.Several analysts said that investors should be aware of the potential costs that could come from cases known as "failure to warn" in which plaintiffs claim that tobacco firms' knew of health risks in the past but did not provide warnings.Experience to date suggests that such
16746 cases need more than injured parties and anecdotal evidence to make them stick, and that evidence in the form of so-called "smoking gun" testimony from disgruntled employees, or in documents, may be key.The main conclusions share analysts draw from the latest UK move, therefore, are that the use of the
16746 British legal system is catching up, perhaps equal to where the U.S. was 20 years ago, and that British firms should be steeled for more cases."This has to be factored into the Imperial Tobacco valuation," SBC's Duffy said, refering to the market's likely approach to the Hanson unit, due to
16746 start trading next Tuesday."Maybe the share's yield premium should be 50 percent rather than the 40 percent (initially considered right)," he added.This would still be below the extra risk factor, compared to the wider share market, seen in companies heavily-exposed to the U.S. legal scene, he added.Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc,
16746 for example, is heavily involved in the U.S. cigarette market and its shares yield a premium of about 70 percent over the market.</

16779 World Bank President James Wolfensohn said on Friday the international community was near agreement on a debt relief plan for poor countries and expected the first cases to be dealt with by yearend."My guess is that between now and the end of the year we will have our first cases,"
16779 Wolfensohn said."I think we're very close to reaching a positive and productive agreement that will allow us to proceed immediately on specific cases," he said.Wolfensohn conceded that details remain to be worked out, noting that the Paris Club of creditor nations had yet to announce the specifics of their part
16779 of the debt relief plan.The International Monetary Fund and World Bank have called for the Paris Club to forgive some 90 percent of loans but Wolfensohn said it would be less than that, though he was uncertain by how much."I don't know if it's 80 percent but it certainly not
16779 going to be 90 percent," he said.Oxfam International, a private development group, lashed out at the apparent decision to reduce the forgiveness to less that 90 percent."Without a clear commitment from the Paris Club to reduce 90 percent of debt, the viability of the entire initiative could be undermined," the
16779 group said in a statement.Diplomatic sources said there appears to be consensus emerging in the Paris Club to offer debt relief of up to 80 percent on a case-by-case basis.It currently provides relief of up to 67 percent under so-called Naples terms.Wolfensohn met with reporters ahead of the annual meetings
16779 of the Bank and International Monetary Fund at which the debt plan is a key agenda item.The aim is to provide debt relief not just from creditor nations but also from the IMF and World Bank, whose loans to poor countries have themselves become a problem.The Paris Club has long
16779 said it is willing to improve debt relief to very poor countries provided the IMF and World Bank themselves do their own share in helping them.The plan has generated considerable controversy because the IMF had recommended the sale of a small portion of its gold hoard to help fund its
16779 programme as well as finance its existing Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility.But IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus made clear on Thursday that while the programme was a "done deal," the gold sales would only be considered if funding by donor countries, the World Bank and the Fund itself fell short.In his
16779 remarks, Wolfensohn said the Bank had already committed some $500 million to the effort and he was prepared to recommend that a total $2 billion be pledged in the years ahead.Leaders of the Group of Seven rich nations agreed at a summit in Lyon, France, last June that debt relief
16779 should be improved for the world's poorest nations, with the Paris Club, IMF and World Bank all playing a role.G7 finance ministers from the United States, Germany, France, Britain, Italy, Canada and Japan were expected to discuss the debt plan when they meet on Saturday.</

16780 debtors starting in 1990 to replace defaulted commercial bank borrowings.The IMF might use the meeting to release a second $115 million tranche of standby loan to Bulgaria, which the Fund postponed until the government fulfilled pledges to close loss-making state firms, said Luis R. 16781 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentThe United States is expected to chide Europe and Japan about the need to nurture their fledgling economic recoveries at a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations on Saturday.But the criticism is likely to be muted because the outlook for the world
16781 economy as a whole looks bright."Obviously it will be important to keep the momentum of growth in place in both Europe and Japan," U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said. "We'll be looking forward to a frank discussion on these issues."Faster growth in Europe and Japan would be good for
16781 the United States because it would boost demand for American exports, helping sustain its 5-1/2-year-old economic upswing.For its part, the United States is likely to be faced with questions at the G7 meeting about its willingness to take tough action to balance its government budget and hold inflation in check.The
16781 International Monetary Fund (IMF) this week said the United States needs to raise interest rates to prevent the economy from overheating and head off inflation.Saturday's meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- is shaping up
16781 to be a low-key gathering free of the rancour evident in the past.With the United States and Japan both faced with upcoming elections and Europe preoccupied with its efforts to launch a single currency in 1999, there is little incentive for any of the policymakers to engage in a public
16781 war of words.Currency markets, often the bugaboo of G7 meetings, have remained calm. The dollar has been buoyant, but so far the United States does not seem concerned that will hurt its exporters by robbing them of competitiveness on world markets,"The key currencies are now in ... a solid, well-justified
16781 constellation and we don't forsee major changes in the near future," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said.On the one issue that may have sparked heated debate at the G7 meeting -- a controversial proposal to sell IMF gold -- the group has agreed to disagree and put off
16781 a decision.A German source, who declined to be named, said he did not expect open conflict on the issue here in Washington.The United States and Britain back gold sales to help the world's poor. Germany and Italy are opposed.The G7 gathering, which is taking place on the fringes of the
16781 semi-annual IMF/World Bank meeting, comes as the outlook for the world economy is turning brighter.The IMF has forecast that world growth will pick up to 4.1 percent next year from 3.8 percent in 1996.U.S. Treasury Seceratry Robert Rubin has called the global outlook "encouraging" but has also made clear that
16781 Washington will be monitoring developments in Europe and Japan closely.Rubin in the past has raised questions about Europe's head-long drive to slash budget deficits under its plan to launch European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.At the last meeting of G7 economic policymakers in April, European nations argued that a stronger
16781 dolar was needed to help put their economies back on track, while the United States advocated European interest rate cuts as the solution.Both have occurred, taking the sting out of the short-term economic debate, but leaving open the question of the long-term impact of EMU on the world economy."It (the
16781 dollar) is not an issue. We will not be making it an issue," the German source said.Japanese officials too have signalled that they do not intend to push for a stronger dolar at the G7 meeting."The current dollar/yen rate correctly reflects economic fundamentals and I think it is in a
16781 comfortable range for both Japan and the United States," a Japanese official said.Rubin though said that it was "critically important" that Japan continue to pursue policies aimed at promoting domestic demand-led growth.</

16787 The U.S. economy expanded at a slightly less robust rate in the second quarter than previously thought, the Commerce Department said on Friday, though it still surged ahead at the fastest rate in two years.The nation's gross domestic product, or GDP, grew at a 4.7 percent annual rate instead of
16787 4.8 percent in the three months from April through June, the government said in a final revision of second-quarter activity.The pace of expansion already has begun to slow since mid-year, with most analysts forecasting growth in a range of about 2 percent to 2.5 percent in the final six months
16787 of the year. The last time the U.S. economy grew more vigorously was in the second quarter of 1994, when it boomed ahead at a 4.9 percent annual rate.The main reason for slightly revising down the second-quarter GDP figure was that federal government spending was not quite as strong as
16787 estimated earlier. The Commerce Department said federal spending climbed at a $10.5 billion annual rate instead of $11.9 billion estimated a month ago.GDP measures the value of all goods and services produced by workers and capital within U.S. borders.Second-quarter GDP grew at more than twice the rate registered in the
16787 first three months of the year, when the economy expanded at a 2 percent annual rate.Most of the final second-quarter revisions were small and the Commerce Department said they did not significantly change its earlier presentation of national economic activity."Growth was markedly higher in the second quarter than the first,
16787 and the step-up was mainly accounted for by an upturn in non-farm business inventory investment and by a pickup in state and local governemnt spending," the department said.The first estimate of third-quarter GDP will not be available for another month. But there already are signs of slowing as consumer spending
16787 softens at home and lackluster overseas economies limit foreign sales of U.S.-made goods.Sales at retail stores barely edged up in July and August. The latest available figures show the U.S. trade balance deteriorated sharply in July as exports weakened.During the second quarter, businesses increased their inventories by a revised $7.1
16787 billion instead of $7.2 billion estimated a month ago. That followed a $3 billion decrease in stocks of unsold goods during the first quarter and bolstered growth by keeping production up.Consumer spending expanded by 3.4 percent at a $38.5 billion annual rate in the second quarter, the same as estimated
16787 a month ago, after growing by 3.5 percent in the first quarter.There were small upward revisions in second-quarter investment in producers' durable equipment and in net exports. Spending on residential investment shot up by 16.3 percent at a $10.4 billion annual rate in the second quarter, more than twice the
16787 7.4 percent first-quarter increase.There was no sign of inflation threat. Two inflation measures in the GDP report were left unrevised as the implicit price deflator advanced at a 1.8 percent annual rate, compared with 2.2 percent in the first quarter.A separate fixed-weights measure of price changes rose 2.2 percent compared
16787 with 2.3 percent in the first quarter.Despite the strong second-quarter economic expansion, corporate profits weakened, falling 0.2 percent from the first quarter to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $408.1 billion.Department officials said it was the first time in a year that quarterly profits dipped, since they fell 2 percent
16787 in the second quarter of 1995.</

16797 cut Belgium's state deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 from an estimated 3.0 percent in 1996."There is a full agreement on the budget. We will reach the 2.9 percent target without hurting the average consumer too much," the source said.Under the Maastricht Treaty, would-be members
16797 of a European single currency must meet a deficit target of 3.0 percent of GDP in 1997. Other criteria cover debt and inflation.Cabinet aides will hammer out the final details of the package over the weekend, after which it will go to a full cabinet session of the centre-left government
16797 on Monday.Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will present the full text of the 1997 budget to the Belgian parliament on Tuesday afternoon.Dehaene appears to have shied away from raising already record-high income tax and radical reform of the country's social security system.On the taxation side, the 1997 budget hits hard
16797 at unhealthy habits -- such as smoking, drinking and driving a car.On the spending side, Dehaene has made a first stab a reforming Belgium's pension system. With a rapidly ageing population, this is a time bomb for the country's already troubled state finances.Taxes, mainly indirect, will rise by 30 billion
16797 francs. Taxes on petrol will be raised by one franc per litre in October and another franc in January. Taxes on beer will rise by one franc per 25-centilitre bottle, on spirits by 12 francs per 75-centilitre bottle, the source said.The full council of ministers on Friday approved higher excise
16797 duties by executive decree. Most will take effect as of October.The investment world will also have to contribute more. Retail investors will have to pay a 0.3 percent tax on physical delivery of securities by banks and brokerages."A small price for anonymity," one analyst said. For tax reasons, many Belgians
16797 avoid holding registered securities and prefer holding bearer stocks and bonds in their safes.Banks will have to pay a 0.06 percent tax on the amount outstanding in savings books accounts, tax-free regulated savings accounts which are Belgium's most popular savings schemes.It was not immediately clear how turnover wwould be defined,
16797 but Belgian media estimated the total cost to the Belgian banking sector at five billion francs.The source also said that 50 billion francs of spending cuts had been decided in the social security sector.The most visible measure will be a gradual increase of women's retirement age to 65 years from
16797 60 over a 13-year period, although this will have little impact on the 1997 budget.The government also decided on a two percent tax on all early retirement pensions.Most other measures in the social security sector are highly technical. They include a reduction of family allowances for teenagers, a reduction in
16797 unemployment benefits for older people and some targeted measures in the health sector. ($1=31.33 Belgian Franc)</

16800 Sweden has become an increasingly stable country," Backstrom told Reuters this past weekend in Dublin.ERM membership could underscore Sweden's increased economic stability and also further demonstrate its determination to continue with a policy aimed at low inflation and sound public finances, he said.But he said it was important to have

16807 Recognising the power that speculators have to create currency turmoil, European Union authorities are looking at how to minimise the risks in the run-up to the launch of a common currency.Past currency upheavals, such as in September 1992 when Britain and Italy were forced out of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism,
16807 have focused attention on how to smooth the transition towards economic and monetary union (EMU).At issue is the critical period between early 1998, when the EU will decide which countries qualify for EMU, and January 1, 1999 when the common euro currency is launched. Then the currencies of EMU members
16807 will become "irrevocably" fixed.Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of Europe's future central bank -- the European Monetary Institute -- has tried to defuse market speculation about conversion rates by arguing they should fixed by averaging past rates between EMU currencies. The length of the averaging process -- six months, a year, or
16807 two years -- would still have to be decided.It is an idea which is gaining ground among EU officials.As one EU monetary official put it: "If they know in advance what the calculation will be, it's more likely that speculation would be constructive...converging rather than diverging."The averaging technique could be
16807 announced to financial markets when EMU members are chosen.While the Maastricht Treaty that governs the single currency process allows rates to be fixed only on January 1, 1999 -- announcing the method would dispel market uncertainty.The issue was informally discussed by some of those attending a meeting of EU finance
16807 ministers in Dublin last weekend.Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt told reporters that Lamfalussy had proposed announcing an averaging approach at the same time as a decision is taken on EMU participants.While the matter is not currently under discussion by either the European Commission or the EU's Monetary Committee, some officials
16807 predict it will win support."Our own thinking is that there is not substantial opposition," said one official, adding that the only ones who might object are countries which might want to engage in a "last-minute devaluation" ahead of the start of EMU.While the plan could go a long way towards
16807 reducing speculative activity on the foreign exchange markets, some say an announcement could signal that central banks of EMU nations were less than prepared to defend a given set of parity rates.Christopher Taylor, an economist at the National Institute of Economic Research in London, said there were basically two options
16807 for dealing with the key period before the single currency is launched."The issue is between a pre-announcement of the fixed set of rates and some sort of formula," Taylor said.A third option, the one laid out in the treaty, would be to accept market rates on January 1, 1999. Few,
16807 however, seem prepared to go that route.Under the first approach, EMU members would announce the central parity rates between currencies they were ready to defend, creating a sort of de facto monetary union.Assuming a close degree of convergence, the parity rates might be very near to those which currently exist.This
16807 would be a bold step, and some say it would put the German Bundesbank in a very uncomfortable spot. Essentially, the central bank would have to be prepared to engage in unlimited intervention.An alternative would be Lamfalussy's plan, which Taylor says lets governments off the hook a bit but might
16807 also signal to markets that something could go wrong."The question is still what if there is some unforeseen event," he added. "I think it boils down to whether there would be some exogenous occurence."A sharp rise in U.S. interest rates, a war, or some other form of external shock would
16807 put EU monetary authorities on the defensive. An averaging technique could make management of a crisis a bit easier, say analysts.</

16810 French unemployment leapt to a record in August, with the biggest monthly increase in more than three years pushing the jobless rate to 12.6 percent at a time when government economic policy is under increasing fire.The number of people out of work in France jumped 39,500 in August to 3,085,100
16810 and the jobless rate based on International Labour Organisation (ILO) criteria, which exclude jobseekers who did any work, hit a record 12.6 percent, up from 12.5 percent."It's an extraordinary number, quite a shock," said Philippe Brossard, an economist with ABN Amro investment bank in Paris.The leap in jobless numbers will
16810 turn up the heat on Prime Minister Alain Juppe, whose policy of austerity and spending cuts is coming under increasing criticism from the ranks of his own centre-right ruling coalition as well as trade unions."This is going to raise the gloom and unhappiness in the parliament. We're heading for a
16810 tough political weekend," said Brossard.Juppe has called a parliamentary confidence vote for next Wednesday in an effort to unite his fractious coalition. Sniping from within his own RPR party prompted President Jacques Chirac to intervene in Juppe's defence on Thursday.Juppe has been counting on an upturn in the economy in
16810 the second half of this year and had got a fillip from news earlier this week that household spending was gathering pace.But the latest jobless figures will do nothing to help his efforts to talk up public morale as Juppe and Chirac fight to dispel gloom and crank up consumer
16810 spending and business investment.Brossard and several other specialists said the latest news reinforced the view that there would have to be further interest rate cutting by the Bank of France to help the economy.Economists said it was still hard to measure the social and political fall-out."Clearly it's important because it
16810 comes amid tensions in the government, but as long as Chirac supports Juppe we should not have too much of a political fight," said David Naude, an economist with JP Morgan bank.Despite already simmering labour union tension, Naude said the surge in unemployment could actually have the effect of cowing
16810 people rather than sparking unrest."When people see jobless numbers rising they may be less willing to demand pay rises or strike," he said. "It's not clear-cut."Valerie Plagnol, an economist at Credit Commercial de France said: "It does increase the potential for social tensions when there is little hope for unemployment
16810 and these are only August numbers. There were plans to cut more jobs in a number of sectors in September.""It also means that pickup in household consumption in third quarter won't be supportive for the fourth quarter (economic growth). The momentum beyond third quarter cannot be assured at all," she
16810 said.French unemployment had fallen by 20,000 in July but that drop had been written off by economists as an aberration due to seasonal factors."The figures are the reflection of an economy that remains weak. I would expect unemployment to keep edging up to reach around 12.7, 12.8 percent by the
16810 end of the year," Jean-Louis Mourier, economist at Louis Dreyfus Finance said in the wake of the August data.</
16811 Germany's upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, voted on Friday to move to Berlin by the end of the century when the government and lower house also move to the capital of unified Germany.Thirteen of Germany's 16 regional states represented in the Bundesrat backed the proposal to move to Berlin
16811 later this decade reversing their decision five years ago to stay in Bonn. Bundesrat members have complained that the upper house would lose influence if it were to stay behind in Bonn, while the 672-member lower house moved to the seat of government in Berlin of Berlin, 600 km (375
16811 miles) to the east.Many argue it would also be a waste of money if officials had to shuttle between the two legislative chambers hundreds of miles (km) apart.Even Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has supported efforts to keep some federal ministries in Bonn, had called the Bundesrat's 1991 decision to stay
16811 behind after the rest of the government moves to Berlin absurd.The government plans to move from Bonn, a quiet Rhineside town of 300,000 that was West Germany's provisional capital between 1949 and 1990, to the 3.4 million city in 1999.</

16819 Badminton tests a new scoring system next week which could herald the biggest change in the sport since it began in 1893.Instead of playing best-of-three games, first to 15 points per game, the Dutch Open will experiment with best-of-five games, first to nine points.Supporters of five games say it makes
16819 for better television, allows more time for commerical breaks and is more exciting because there are more decisive points.It has the extra advantage of unifying men's and women's singles. At present, women play best-of-three to 11 points. More experiments will be made, starting in Norway in November, but to become
16819 universally adopted the change would need an 80 percent majority among International Badminton Federation (IBF) members.Resistance may be strongest among the Asians who have generally dominated the sport over the last few years and might see less need to change a system which seems to suit their "slow-burn" approach.IBF council
16819 member Martijn van Dooremalen said on Friday it could take a number of years to make the change. "But if we want the sport to grow and become more successful, we need to experiment," he added.</

16868 The South African petrochemicals industry is seriously weighing up a Taiwanese proposal for a $3.4 billion aromatics plant in the Eastern Cape, despite serious doubts about its viability.The industry had promised to react to the proposal by the end of September, but several key players including Polifin Ltd could not
16868 attend meetings scheduled for this week.The meetings are now scheduled for the second week of October and plans by Taiwan to issue a press release about the project next week might have to be delayed.The plant, which would be a joint venture project between the two countries to produce polyester
16868 fibre for the textile industry, was proposed on a recent visit to South Africa by a Taiwanese delegation led by Deputy Premier Hsu Li-Teh."There is hesitancy on the practicalities of the project, but it is clear that we need to show some support because the government wants this," an industry
16868 source said.The government has identified the Coega Industrial Development Zone off Algoa Bay in the Eastern Cape for the plant, which is expected to create up to 80,000 jobs in spin-off developments.The Eastern Cape is an African National Congress (ANC) stronghold with high levels of poverty and unemployment and the
16868 ANC is understood to be keen to stimulate development in the region.Hsu's promises of substantial investment in South Africa have been met with some cynicism in the industry as being a ploy to win South Africa's support in the diplomatic wrangle over the "two China's" issue.Industry sources said a major
16868 concern about the project was that it was aimed at boosting job creation in the Eastern Cape by producing polyester for a new labour intensive textile complex."South Africa should only consider building such a plant if it can compete with the rest of the world in textiles," an industry source
16868 said."That assumes that the garments made will be exported and that labour rates in the textile industry will compete with other parts of the world."Unless the government was prepared to implement its highly contested "flexible" wage policy to get around union norms of minimum wages, which are above those in
16868 the Far East, the plant would not be a world player in exports.The competitiveness of the plant would also be affected by the fact that the feedstock to produce the aromatics would be imported crude or naphtha.This raised the question of whether South Africa should instead consider a plant just
16868 to meet local needs, analysts said. A recent edition of local newspaper Engineering News said if the petrochemical complex went ahead it was likely to receive some tax benefits, including three years accelerated depreciation on assets, coupled with a two-year tax holiday.-- Cape Town newsroom +27 21 25-2238</
