16876 A new system aimed at overhauling South Africa's shambolic customs and excise controls has been designed and could be phased in over the next three years, according to its backers.South Africa loses billions of rand each year in revenue through corruption and fraud at its ports, a problem which has
16876 been compounded by understaffing and poor technology.The Technological Information Management System, developed by private firm IPES and now being assessed by officials, would initially link databases at the Department of Trade and Industry, port authority Portnet and Customs and Excise.It would introduce information such as transaction statistics, a bar code
16876 system providing container information as well as a tracking system using terrestrial radio and satellite tracking.A scanning mechanism and a software package aimed at providing real time data on the movement of imports and exports is also planned.An initial phase, which would focus on customs law enforcement at four transport
16876 hubs -- Durban, Cape Town, City Deep in Johannesburg and Beit Bridge on the border of South Africa and Zimbabwe -- would take four months to implement.Leon Vermaak, the designer of the system, said the development of the system stemmed from the need to eradicate South Africa's reputation of being
16876 a smuggler's dream."South Africa has become a smuggler's den and could easily gain the reputation of being the smuggler's capital of the world because of the near collapse of customs control," Vermaak said.It also took cognisance of Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's recent statement that no industrial policy could have integrity
16876 until the country had efficient customs control.Vermaak said lax customs controls cost South Africa some five billion rand a year in lost Value Added Tax receipts as well as providing a fillip for a burgeoning grey import market -- estimated to be a 12 billion rand a year industry.Ben van
16876 Rensburg, senior economist at the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob), put the total loss of tax revenue at something between 12 and 20 billion rand a year."A linked database system will start to solve this specific problem because it will give you those linkages between importation, customs and excise,
16876 VAT, and income tax," Van Rensburg said.An advantage of the system would be that it would improve the reliability of South African trade data -- lambasted by economists recently as unreliable."Our import and export numbers have become almost the laughing stock of the financial world. We know that those numbers
16876 are not to be trusted," van Rensburg said."We think that putting a proper, trustworthy database in place and which we know good data is coming in and out is a starting point of solving the problem," he added.Vermaak said the system has already been presented to most of the stakeholders
16876 and the private sector who had approved the concept in principle.High level talks are currently underway to discuss the financing of the project which is expected to result in a decision being made on whether government or the private sector will fund the scheme.-- Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003</
16877 By Edward Osborn, consultant to Edey, Rogers (Pty) LtdThe favourite lament of bankers and central bankers is the low savings rate. The Victorian virtue of thrift is no longer with us.The lamentation over low savings invariably arises in the context of investment, which to every one is obviously a good
16877 thing. There is an implicit suggestion that investment turns on the level of savings; the more savings the greater the volume of investment.This, unfortunately, reflects that bankers are not economically literate, for the two are independent of each other, being carried out by different agents and with different motivations. Broadly,
16877 however, it is the level of investment activity that determines the rate of savings.This is clear for a closed economy, for the greater the investment the higher the level of economic activity, disposable incomes and likely level of savings. The absence of savings, however, can be a drag on investment
16877 through its financing in that interest rates will be that much higher and investments sensitive to interest rates will be curbed. In the national accounts savings and investment are always equal, as they say, ex post.In South Africa savings are now down to 16.7 percent of GDP, but this reflects
16877 the low level of investment activity, or fixed capital formation.Savings are dominated by the corporate sector. In 1995, for example, total corporate savings in the form of depreciation provisions and company after-depreciation savings amounted to 94.2 billion rand, whereas the total net national savings amounted to 81 billion rand. The
16877 savings of the private household sector amounted to six billion rand, but there was a dissavings by the government sector of 19.2 billion rand.Given this structure of savings the banker prescription for the improvement of the economy will be the reduction of government dissavings, or the budget deficit, and the
16877 encouragement of private household savings.The budget deficit embraces both government dissavings, general government capital formation, capital transfers and loans. However, the major part is dissavings. The reduction of these dissavings through increased taxes would simply be a shift from the other sectors reducing their savings. Hence the usual course to
16877 follow would be through reduced government expenditures, actually non-interest expenditures.If this can be done through the elimination of waste and inefficiency, well and good, but if it is to be achieved through sharp reductions in the size of the bureaucracy care has to be taken for the measures can be
16877 deflationary, resulting in a drop in GDP and indeed in savings.The intended sharp drop in the budget deficit to four percent next year is probably more hubris than practical but if it were to be achieved through draconian cut-backs the effects could be serious indeed, coming on top of the
16877 general tendency of recent years of downsizing of establishments.Which brings us to the matter of the personal sector savings. These have been in decline in recent years and this has been the subject of much head shaking and consternation. The prescription is more voluntary savings and less consumption expenditure. This
16877 needs a little more teasing out.First, the sector's savings are derived in the national accouts as the residual or difference between estimated disposable income after payment of direct taxes and estimated private consumption expenditure. Clearly, savings as a residual are a net aggregate. Gross institutional savings in the form of
16877 pension contributions and life policy premiums of about 50 billion rand are reduced to a net savings figure for the sector of six billion rand.Significantly consumption expenditure has been rising as a proportion of disposable income over the last three years of the economic upturn, from 94.6 percent in 1993
16877 to 97.6 percent in 1995. Consumption expenditure has thus been rising relatively and this has been financed in a number of ways.Unfortunately no official efforts have been made as yet to show the make up of the financing of consumption expenditure. But the financing would be in terms of the
16877 normal categories of disposable income, customer credit, credit card finance, hire purchase financing and other forms of bank loans and advances, and should embrace also the redistribution of income through crime and the diversion of income through boycotting.Crime in the form of burglaries, car thefts and other theft that results
16877 in expenditure on the replacement of goods through the agency of short-term insurers will be an addition to private consumption expenditure and an effective reduction in savings. In effect such crime-based consumption is a redistribution of income through the mechanism of the insurance industry.The stratum of consumption in respect of
16877 goods in replacement of stolen goods and property is considerable and would be contained in the total claims on the short-term insurers for motor and miscellaneous business, which were 5.6 billion rand in 1995. The Nedcor Project on Crime, Violence and Investment quite rightly gives emphasis to the cost of
16877 crime in South Africa.The other side of the coin, however, is the dependence of the South African economy on crime in terms of sustaining consumption expenditure and the production that is its counterpart.For example, according to the Nedcor study there were 97,950 car thefts in 1995, that is nearly 47
16877 percent of total sales in the year. Obviously not all these car thefts resulted in new car replacements, but a significant proportion would be.Boycotting of rents and local government rates and other charges has also bolstered purchasing power, impacting on total consumption expenditure and the financial balances of other sectors,
16877 in particular worsening the deficit position of the government sector. Boycotting represents a diversion of the disposal of income to the disadvantage of government, in particular, but to the advantage of the sectors producing consumer goods, say.Finally one has to take note of the apparent paradox that investment decisions are
16877 more likely to be influenced by growing consumption rather than by growing savings. The Nedcor project has demonstrated quite clearly that the major motivations for fixed investment lie with economic growth and market opportunities. Both of these are strongly dictated by market opportunities. Both of these are strongly dictated by
16877 the level of private consumption expenditure, rather than the attenuation of consumption in favour of savings.Regrettably crime and boycotting have made a positive contribution towards sustaining economic growth in South Africa and, indeed, there is a fair degree of dependence of the economy on anti-social behaviour. Not that it is
16877 to be encouraged. It just happens to be a fact of life. / / / / / / /(The opinions expressed in this article represent those of the author only. They should not be seen to represent the views of Reuters.)</

16880 right reasons.The year-on-year growth in net foreign assets slowed to 10.5 billion crowns from August 1995 to August 1996 to total 59.1 billion crowns, after 12-month growth of 13.7 billion crowns in July.Meanwhile growth in net domestic assets rose 50.9 billion crowns to 317.2 billion crowns in August, after a
16880 50.8 billion crown 12-month increase in July."M2 slowed down, but for a bad reason. The net foreign asset contribution to the money supply declined," a western banker who requested anonymity, told Reuters.In mid-July, the NBS approved a series of measures aimed at stemming money supply growth, including raising banks' minimum
16880 reserve levels and a key lending rate, and widening the band in which it fixes the crown to scare off speculative hot money.The move was aimed at curbing a short-term lending activity by local banks, which is at the heart of M2 growth.Local banks have been repatriating their assets from
16880 abroad to have funds to extend the loans to "lucrative Slovak clients", increasingly also in foreign exchange."The aggregate growth moderated only slightly and, as a one-month phenomena, one should wait at least for another month to assess the decline's roots," said Martin Barto, an ING Barings analyst.But the NBS, despite
16880 having said it expected the first reliable results of the measures in October or by the end of the year, took further steps on Thursday to push banks to buy its three-month liquidity bills, its main tightening tool.The NBS raised its bill repurchase rate by 50 basis points to 8.70
16880 percent, and also cut its reverse repo rate by 20 basis points to 7.20 percent on Thursday."The NBS cautiousness is justified, loosening of a monetary policy is fine in a country where restructuring is guaranteed, but this is not the case in Slovakia," Juraj Rencko, an independent economist, told Reuters."Contrary

16897 more 90 percent of the level they were at before the fall of communism in 1989.In the period after 1989, the country's armaments firms failed in overcoming the conversion shock, as also the workforce in the whole sector was reduced to some 18,000 people, from 80,000 in the mid-80s.But ZTS
16897 Deputy Director for strategy Pavel Motl told Reuters that railway transport equipment and construction machines, and not arms will be the focus of production."We plan to boost our production to some nine billion crowns in 2000, from the current 1.6 billion, with the armaments production accounting for a maximum of
16897 20-30 percent of the overall output," he said."For example, we are close to signing a contract with German engineering company Krauss-Maffei on cooperation in a railway programme," he added.Motl said ZTS on Thursday also signed a framework agreement with an unspecified Russian firm, which is, as well as the Slovak
16897 firm, seeking to change production away from non-military purposes. 16897 we need the state to help in making easier loan conditions with banks," he said.Dubnica is a member of the new state-run holding company, DMD Holding a.s., with launched its activities in January to coordinate the production and exports of some 26 country's arms producers.Motl said that each firm in
16897 DMD had offered its own recovery and development programme, which the government should review as a whole by November."We (Dubnica) drafted 15 programmes, each consisting of several projects, but so far mostly without contracts," he said. 16897 trouble with the labour unions, after it became public that it intends to sack over one-third of its 5,600 strong workforce, resulting in strike-threats and demonstrations outside the government offices."The company will not make massive lay offs, at least until our programmes are reviewed by the government," Motl said.</

16902 New Russian and Chinese data on the 1956 Hungarian Uprising unveiled at a conference in Budapest on Friday shows how close Soviet leader Nikita Kruschev was to recognising Hungary's revolutionary government of the time.Documents recently released by Russian president Boris Yeltsin show that two days before the final Soviet invasion
16902 to overthrow the government of Imre Nagy, Kruschev was still exploring ways of recognising Nagy's leadership and pulling all Red Army troops out of Hungary.The evidence appears as Hungarians prepare to mark the 40th anniversary next month of the uprising against Stalinism which was suppressed by the Soviet tanks after
16902 12 days. Around 25,000 people are estimated to have died in the fighting, which many scholars see as signalling the deathknell of communism.Vitaly Afiani, deputy director of the former archives of the Soviet Communist Party central committee, said the documents consist mainly of notes taken by Vladimir Malin, head of
16902 the chancellery of the Soviet Communist Party central committee, of unminuted Soviet politburo meetings.The sessions were held between the outbreak of the uprising on October 23 and the Soviet invasion beginning on November 2."The Malin notes show (politburo) sessions were held continuously on the Hungarian question in an agitated way,"
16902 Afiani told Reuters. "The majority of the presidium were in favour of the Nagy government and even discussed the possibility of the withdrawal of troops."According to Afiani, Kruschev saw Nagy, a reform Communist, as someone who would work within the Communist system. He was also influenced by the Suez crisis
16902 following Egyptian president Gamal Abdul Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal.Britain and France were preparing to invade Egypt to take the canal back and Kruschev did not want the Soviet Union to be accused of similar "imperialistic" behaviour.However, Afiani's evidence shows how the picture had dramatically changed by the morning
16902 of October 31st following the British and French invasion of Egypt and crucial consultations the night before with the Chinese delegation, which included current Chinese leader Den Xiao Ping."Kruschev opened the morning session by saying the presidium had to fundamentally revise the condition it took the day before," Afiani said.
16902 "He expressed the view that if troops pull out of Hungary that would 'cheer up the imperialists', the British, French and the Americans."Jian Chen, who left communist China in the 1980s to become a leading Cold War scholar in the United States, on Friday presented new evidence from Deng's interpreter
16902 in Moscow and the then Chinese leader Mao Zedong's political secretary."We already knew China pushed the Soviet Union to take a harsh attitude," Chen told Reuters. "Now we see the contrast with their attitude to Poland, where they warned against Moscow's intervention."Kruschev had allowed Poland to replace its Stalinist government
16902 with a reform communist leadership but was now considering invading the country to end reforms, a move which China opposed.However, Chen said reports of communist party members being lynched in Budapest and the general tone of international reporting as communicated to Peking by the Chinese Embassy in Budapest led Mao
16902 to conclude the Hungarians were anti-communist rather than just anti-Soviet as the Poles were."On the evening of October 30th Deng and Chinese party vice chairman Liu Shaoqi, told Kruschev 'You have to do something, you cannot give up Hungary.'"The pressure on Kruschev was increased by reports of the invasion of
16902 Egypt, which Kruschev probably then thought would fall to the West, with Hungary possibly following, Afiani said.In fact the United States intervened soon afterwards to force the British and French to withdraw their forces.</

16909 Playboy, liberal? Romanians are undecided on how to remember Nicu Ceausescu, the youngest son of the late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu who died in a Vienna hospital from acute liver disease on Thursday.Nicu had been groomed to succeed his father, but that ended with the December 1989 uprising in which
16909 Ceausescu and his wife Elena were shot by a firing squad.The playboy lifestyle of "the princeling" as he was dubbed during the communist era had contrasted with the poverty and food shortages that were the lot of most Romanians and epitomised the corruption of his father's rule."We'll be better off
16909 when Nicu takes over, because he'll gamble Romania at roulette tables in Las Vegas and the Americans will win us over," ran a popular communist-era joke.But some remembered a less known, kinder side to the heir apparent. Leading commentator Ion Cristoiu said Nicu had been seen as a liberal by
16909 people of his own generation in contrast to his father's hardline supporters."His stand often put him on a collision course with the old guard around his father," he told Reuters.Vienna hospital doctors said Nicu, 45, died "from bleeding of the oesophagus as a result of liver cirrhosis and viral inflammation
16909 of the liver".Romanian private broadcasters flashed the news. State media kept their cover to a minimum."I don't have any feelings at all. I can't have feelings for people like the Ceausescus," said pensioner Jana Ioanid, echoing loathing deeply rooted among many Romanians, who still smart at the memory of Ceausescu's
16909 ruthless 24-year rule.But despite his past reputation as a womaniser and gambler who squandered vast sums at gaming tables across the world, many first reactions in Romania were sympathetic."This is sad news, although it was expected given his grave illness. May God rest his soul, which was unjustly tormented," said
16909 pensioner Elisabeta Antim from Sibiu, Nicu's Transylvanian fiefdom where local people remember him for trying to oppose his father's severe economic belt-tightening.Nicu's elder brother Valentin and his sister Zoe were affected by the news of his death in Vienna, where Nicu had been flown by friends last week after Romanian
16909 doctors said they lacked medical and surgical equipment to treat his condition."He didn't have a last wish...He had his friends...We hadn't seen each other often lately," Valentin said.An Austrian magazine said friends of Nicu's had paid for his treatment in Vienna, reporting that $37,000 had been deposited with the Austrian
16909 embassy in Bucharest.Nicu was arrested shortly before his parents' execution and charged with ordering troops to fire on protesters in Sibiu during the 1989 uprising. He always protested his innocence."He served out his sentence for illegal gun possession, and he (died) cleared of all other charges," said Valentin, who lobbied
16909 to have Nicu freed from jail in November 1992.Friends will fly Nicu's body back home later this week. Relatives are making arrangements for his funeral in Bucharest, sources close to his family said. REUTER</

16925 Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove said General Motors Corp's Canadian subsidiary insisted he meet with the chief executive officer of a secret buyer for two of its parts plants in Canada.The leader of Canada's largest private sector union said he told the CEO of "Newco" that he could
16925 buy four GM parts plants including a fabrication plant in Oshawa, Ontario and a trim plant in Windsor, but that the union would insist the employees are covered by its master labor agreement with GM."I told him you can buy if you want, you buy us, but you also buy
16925 the CAW-GM master collective agreement," he said. Hargrove said the union would insist on making a deal similar to its agreement with American Axle, which bought GM's axle plant in St. Catharines, Ontario three years ago. Although it is considered a separate company by GM, American Axle's workers are covered
16925 by the union's agreement with GM.Sources close to the talks hinted that "Newco" may be a U.S. Wall Street investment firm named Joseph, Littlejohn &amp; Levy, a private investment partnership."I can't tell you who it is, but I can say it is a U.S. investment firm and the executive is
16925 an American," the source said. Reuters reported on September 6 that General Motors refused to confirm reports in the Oakland Press in Pontiac, Michigan that Joseph, Littlejohn and Levy was negotiating to buy four parts plants from GM.GM has said it intends to sell interior components plants in Livonia and
16925 Flint, Michigan as a package deal that includes the Oshawa and Windsor plants in Canada.The CAW began negotiating with General Motors of Canada Ltd for a new collective labor agreement on Monday, one day after ratifying a groundbreaking deal with Chrysler Corp's Canadian subsidiary. The union had said it intends
16925 to reverse GM's outsourcing decisions along the lines of its deal with Chrysler, which set down a moratorium on plant closures and sales and committed the company to refrain from reducing jobs through outsourcing."They will accept the Chrysler pattern," Hargrove said.Traditionally the Canadian Auto Workers union sets an established pattern
16925 at the first car company it negotiates with and then applies that deal to the other two subsidiaries of big North American auto companies.Spokesmen for General Motors were unavailable for comment.-- Paul Casciato (416) 941-8100, or e-mail: paul.casciato@reuters.com</

16931 A wide-ranging aviation bill stepping up airport security against terrorist attacks was blocked in the U.S. Senate on Friday, effectively stalling any action on the bill until next year.Wisconsin Democratic Sen. Russell Feingold objected to taking up the bill, complaining it contained a special interest provision designed to prevent Federal
16931 Express employees from forming a union.Feingold's move effectively blocked action on the bill, which passed the House of Representatives earlier Friday. Because Congress was expected to adjourn in the next few days, the bill was likely to be shelved for the year."The provision makes a significant change in federal law
16931 to give Federal Express an edge in its current attempt to stop some of its employees from forming a union ... that's the issue, let's just get that out of here," Feingold said.Among the anti-terorrism provisions were requirements that airlines do background checks on employees screening passengers, baggage and cargo
16931 and that the Federal Aviation Administration certify security firms doing the screening.The bill also established rules for record-setting flights stemming from the crash of a plane this year in which 7-year-old Jessica Dubroff was killed while trying to become the youngest pilot to fly across the country.The rules would bar
16931 anyone without a valid pilot's certificate and medical certificate from handling the controls of a plane while trying to set a record.Also in the measure were reforms of the way airlines deal with families of crash victims. They were taken from a separate bill drafted after complaints by families of
16931 victims of the July 17 TWA 800 crash off Long Island, New York.The provision regarding Federal Express would allow reclassifying employees under the Railway Labor Act rather than the National Labor Relations Act. The change, which would require employees to organize nationally rather than being allowed to organize locally, would
16931 make it more difficult for them to strike.</
16932 Emergency crews scrambled to clean up an estimated 600 barrels of oil that leaked from a Liberian-registered tanker that struck a drawbridge on Friday, officials said.The 560-foot (170-meter) Julie N was entering Portland Harbor with a cargo of approximately 210,000 barrels of No. 2 distillate fuel when it struck a
16932 granite abutment on a bridge across the harbor, officials said.The cause of the accident was not immediately known. Seas were calm and winds light but the 85-foot-wide ship (25-meter) was trying to make it through the bridge's 95-foot (28-meter) opening, officials said"The difficulty of the approach to the Portland bridge
16932 is well known," Coast Guard Commander Burton Russell told reporters. The ship had a harbor pilot on board at the time of the accident, he said.The accident punched holes in two of the ship's tanks, spilling both distillate fuel from the load and bunker oil used by the ship into
16932 the water. The total spill was estimated at 600 barrels but the exact amount was not known.The Coast Guard said both leaks had stopped. The heavier oil was contained around the now docked ship, but lighter distillate could seen and smelled around the harbor. The lighter fuel was expected to
16932 evaporate in the next few days.Officials said the size of the spill was reduced both because of the quick response of emergency crews and the captain's decision to dock at a nearby oil terminal which had pollution control booms to trap the bunker oil.The Coast Guard closed Portland harbor and
16932 ordered the autoferry Scotia Prince, which runs daily between Portland and Yarmouth, Nova Scotia to divert to Bar Harbor. Lobster fishing in the harbor area was banned.The accident left Portland with both an environmental and transportation problem. The 80-year-old drawbridge is a major commuter route and is now stuck in
16932 the open position because of broken electrical cables and bent metal.Gov. Angus King said the bridge would be repaired even though a larger replacement drawbridge is being built and scheduled to open next summer.The Julie N is owned by New York-based Maritime Overseas Corp, a unit of Overseas Shipholding Group
16932 Inc, a company official said. It was chartered by Global Petroleum Corp. and scheduled to discharge its load at Sprague Oil in Portland.</
16933 Microsoft Corp. Friday said its sales growth and profit margins may decline in fiscal 1997 after big gains in the prior year that were driven largely by the launch of the Windows 95 operating system.In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Microsoft focused on a likely slowdown in
16933 revenue growth in the first two quarters of the fiscal year that began July 1, and it noted that the operating expenses were expected to increase in the current year."Because of the fixed nature of a signficant portion of such expenses, coupled with the possibility of slower revenue growth, operating
16933 margins in 1997 may decrease from those in 1996," it said.But industry analysts said the statement merely refelcted the company's traditional conservatism in its public comments about its financial outlook."We're accustomed to these kind of comments in the company's annual report to shareholders," said Rick Sherlund at Goldman Sachs &amp;
16933 Co.He and other analysts said they expected the company's profit margins to rise this year, although Microsoft is not expected to repeat its high revenue growth rate.Microsoft executives previously had told industry analysts and reporters they expected revenue growth this year to be lower than the 46 percent reported for
16933 the year that ended June 30 and which included the new Windows system."This was an unusually high growth rate -- the highest since '92," chief financial officer Mike Brown told Reuters in July. "I don't expect as much next year."Analyst Scott McAdams of Ragen MacKenzie estimated Microsoft's revenue would grow
16933 22 percent this year to $10.59 billion, compared with last year's $8.67 billion.He estimated Microsoft's operating profit margin would rise to 37.4 percent of revenues from 35.5 percent last year and 34.3 percent in fiscal 1995. He estimated Microsoft would generate net income of $2.74 billion or $4.15 a share
16933 this year, up from $2.19 billion or $3.43 a share.Microsoft stock, which rose $2.375 to $134.375 in Nasdaq trading Friday, fell $1.25 in the after-hours market on the cautionary statement, traders said.In a letter published in the company's annual report to shareholders Friday, Microsoft Chairman officer Bill Gates emphasized he
16933 and other company executives were optimistic about the company's prospects."In our dialogue with the financial community, we go out of our way to point out the challenges of maintaining or increasing our profitability," Gates said. "Despite this, we feel the prospects for our business over the next decade are very
16933 strong."A proxy statement sent to shareholders disclosed that Gates was paid $563,000 in salary and bonus last year, a raise of about $147,000 over fiscal 1995. His 24 percent stake in the company was valued at nearly $19 billion.</
16934 Republicans Friday charged Democrats with deliberately raising the threat of another government closure to win political points even as negotiators said they were making progress on the 1997 budget.The Republican National Committee aired radio ads in Washington and selected Democratic districts. In it they accused Democrats of blocking a budget
16934 agreement in hopes the public would blame Republicans for the gridlock as they did last winter when the government closed twice."That means the government could shut down. Again," it said.While federal commuters were listening to the radio spot, lawmakers of both parties and White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta
16934 were expressing optimism on the outcome of their marathon talks through a more than 2,000 page spending bill.House Appropriations Committee chairman Bob Livingston, R-Louisiana, told reporters "We are making steady progress," and his Senate counterpart, Mark Hatfield of Oregon, said only 25 issues of 140 in dispute remained.Thursday's bargaining session
16934 broke off at 4 a.m. EDT and resumed a few hours later to continue all Friday with the intention of wrapping up the deal in a special Saturday session."We're getting there slowly, bit by bit, step by step," Panetta said at the lunch break.This massive bill, or a separate version
16934 to give the government a few days' funds, must pass before Tuesday's start of the 1997 fiscal year. Without approval to spend money after Oct. 1, many agencies would be forced to close.A major snag developed when negotiations on the reform of immigration laws apparently stalled over administration efforts to
16934 gain concessions from Republicans, making it likely it will be voted on separately Monday.Republican Sen. Alan Simpson of Wyoming accused the White House of negotiating in bad faith. "I am sick of it," he said on the Senate floor.Both sides have identified many policy issues on which there are deep
16934 disagreements. In addition to immigration reform, Democrats are insisting on an amendment to protect physicians' communications with patients and a ban on gun ownership by convicted spouse abusers. They also object to a Republican plan which they said would deny some elderly and disabled supplemental Social Security benefits.These and the
16934 politically volatile issue of U.S. aid to international family planning agencies that use non-U.S. funds for abortion services will probably be left for negotiations at the highest levels in Congress and the White House.Republicans, eager to conclude this year's session, agreed to give President Clinton an additional $6.5 billion for
16934 education, anti-drug efforts and to fight terrorism. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott conceded some of his members felt they had given Clinton too much.The money for these programs would be raised by selling cellular communications airwaves to telecommunications companies, raising thrift deposit insurance reserves and selling oil from the strategic
16934 petroleum reserve.Called an omnibus spending bill, the budget agreement would pay for some of the government's most costly activities -- defense, education, labor, environmental protection, national parks, the White House, the Treasury, foreign aid, law enforcement and a host of others.Hatfield said up to $1 billion in Pentagon money could
16934 be shifted to fight terrorism. About $300 million to $400 million of that would directly involve military programs.</

16954 Atlantic Richfield unit ARCO Alaska Inc. and Andarko Petroleum Corp. have struck an agreement to combine their exploration efforts in part of southcentral Alaska's Cook Inlet, officials said.The two-year alliance will cover 127,000 onshore and offshore acres of ARCO's upper Cook Inlet leasehold, the companies said.An ARCO Alaska spokesman said
16954 Friday that Anadarko's seismic technology could prove fruitful in the Cook Inlet area, Alaska's oldest oil-producing region. "Oil exploration really is about the application of new ideas, sometimes to old areas," ARCO Alaska spokesman Ronnie Chappell said. "New ideas and a fresh perspective can be very valuable."The agreement does not
16954 include the Sunfish prospect, which was discovered by ARCO and partner Phillips Petroleum, or the Beluga River gas field.The alliance was unveiled Thursday. Financial terms were not revealed. Under the agreement, Houston-based Anadarko will manage an Anchorage-based exploration team made up of geoscientists from both companies, officials said.Anadarko will serve
16954 as operator and earn a 50 percent share of ARCO's working interest in Cook Inlet leases by conducting new exploration work, officials said.That work will include seismic surveys, completion of geological and geophysical studies and drilling of exploration wells, the companies said. Chappell said ARCO will benefit from its expanded
16954 partnership with Anadarko, which has joined with Arco in exploring the North Slope's Colville River Delta area."We've been acting with them on the North Slope and we felt like it was a really good fit," he said.Anadarko has had impressive exploration successes elsewhere, Chappell said.An Anadarko official said that company
16954 will also benefit from the Cook Inlet partnership, which was effective September 1. "This agreement joins two companies with complementary strengths," John Seitz, Anadarko's senior vice president for exploration, said in a news release issued Thursday."ARCO has long experience in Alaska, tremendous knowledge of the area and the largest land
16954 position in Cook Inlet. Anadarko will bring a new look and a fresh, creative perspective to evaluatoin of that resource base," Seitz said.</

16960 The Securities and Exchange Commission will need more funding, should Congress require it to step up oversight of investment advisers, a function it currently can not cope with because of "woefully inadequate" funds, SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt said on Friday.Levitt made his agency's position clear in a letter to Rep.
16960 Thomas Bliley, the Virginia Republican who chairs the House Commerce Committee and who is pushing for enactment of a securities bill within the current congressional term.Levitt said,"our resources are woefully inadequate to protect the millions of American investors who depend on the services of investment advisers." He noted that the
16960 SEC now examines smaller investment firms at an average of once every 44 years, "which is tantamount to no examination at all."Levitt sent the letter even as House and Senate negotiators were still at loggerheads over the bill's provisions governing the investment advisory industry.Senate proponents led by Texas Republican Phil
16960 Gramm want the SEC to shoulder greater responsibility in licensing and regulating investment advisory firms with more than $25 million in assets. Negotiators in the House, including ranking Democrats in the Commerce Committee, initially wanted to allow state regulators to oversee the nation's 150,000 investment advisers, but later said they
16960 would be willing to go along with Gramm provided the SEC got additional funding. The House negotiators also asked that the advisers be required to comply with additional disclosure and other rules.Legislative aides said Gramm is unwilling to grant the SEC additional funding, a position he has espoused in the
16960 past. No breakthrough had been reached on the issue as of early Friday evening, the aides added.</

16962 NeoPath Inc Friday said a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel made a recommendation not to approve the conmpany's submission for the use of the AutoPap System as a Primary Screener of Pap smear slides pending the completion of additional premarket studies.The following is a copy of the company's statement.-----------------
16962 FULL TEXT --------------------REDMOND, Wash.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 27, 1996--NeoPath, Inc. (NASDAQ:NPTH) announced today that a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Hematology and Pathology Devices Advisory Panel made a recommendation not to approve at this time the supplement to the company's premarket approval (PMA) submission for the use of the AutoPap(R) System
16962 as a Primary Screener of Pap smear slides pending the completion of additional premarket studies.The Advisory Panel's recommendation will be considered by the FDA in completing its review of the company's supplement application.The Advisory Panel asked NeoPath to present additional, on-site data that use of the AutoPap System as a
16962 Primary Screener of microscopic images from Pap smear slides is superior to the current standard of review, i.e., by a cytotechnologist followed by quality control review."FDA approval of the company's AutoPap 300 QC System a year ago was an important defining event for NeoPath, and we look forward to continuing
16962 to build a base of customers on this product," said Alan C. Nelson, Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of NeoPath Inc."We intend to work vigilantly to answer all of the Panel's questions and resubmit this matter to the FDA's Division of Clinical Laboratory Devices. Moreover, we will continue to
16962 provide our existing customers with the high level of service to which they have become accustomed, and will move forward with our marketing of the AutoPap 300 QC System. We are very confident that we will be able to meet the Panel's requests for further data on the Primary Screener
16962 indication," Nelson said.The AutoPap System utilizes proprietary image-processing computers to identify those pap smears with the highest potential for abnormality. The image-interpretation technology of the AutoPap System consists of integrated high-speed microscopes, specialized image interpretation software and field-of-view computers. This technology allows for rapid acquisition, analysis and classification of information
16962 contained within complex, highly variable images such as those that occur in the cellular material of a Pap smear. Based on those images, the system automatically analyzes and extracts important features of cellular material and classifies specimens.NeoPath's PMA supplement was accepted for filing on June 6, 1996. The original PMA
16962 application for the AutoPap System to be used for quality control rescreening was submitted to the FDA on Feb. 24, 1995, and approved on Sept. 29, 1995. The U.S. Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) approved use of the device as a replacement for traditional methods of quality control rescreening in
16962 March of 1996.NeoPath, Inc.'s core expertise is in the research, development, and commercialization of technologies to automate the interpretation of medical images. The company, which is based in Redmond, has approximately 175 employees. -0-Forward-looking statements in this release are made pursuant to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities
16962 Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These forward-looking statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties, including without limitation, product and manufacturing regulatory approvals; the company's limited manufacturing, marketing, customer service and support capabilities; the company's sole or limited source of supply of certain components; the status of competing products; and
16962 other risks and uncertainties detailed in the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.</

16970 said in a statement. 16972 to build trucks at the facility with only 1,500 hourly UAW employees, down from about 2,000 currently.The surplus employees will be put into a pool of idled GM workers who continue to earn nearly full pay, but GM spokesman Thomas Beamon said the company expects many of them to retire
16972 or be transferred to other plants.All workers at the plant will be placed on temporary layoff for a few months in the early part of 1997.The announcement marks the first time GM has identified the specific trucks it intends to build at the plant, which is undergoing a $260 million
16972 conversion project.Analysts said the plant ultimately will be capable of building 150,000 to 175,000 trucks a year, but shortages of components will hold the facility's production below that.However, GM faces stiff competition in the large sport/utility market, particularly from Ford Motor Co.'s new Expedition vehicle, said Michael Robinet, an automotive
16972 analyst with CSM Forecasting in Farmington Hills, Mich."I think initially the plant will be busy, but the long-term prospects could be called into question," Robinet said. "There's a looming overcapacity sitation towards the end of the decade."All the pickup trucks built at Arlington, will be extended-cab models with an optional
16972 third door. GM now builds extended-cab, three-door pickups only in Oshawa, Ontario.The plant also will become the sole source for a new police version of the Chevrolet Tahoe. The less-luxurious two-wheel-drive vehicle will be equipped with a 5.7-liter V-8 engine, a heavy-duty suspension and other special equipment.The project is part
16972 of a long-term plan that GM has to boost truck production to more than 50 percent of its total North American capacity. For the first six months of 1996, trucks made up about 45 percent of GM's output.</

17011 New York State Electric &amp; Gas Corp said on Friday that its transition to competition proposal calls for a five year rate freeze while allowing most customers to increase electricity use at half the present price.The proposal, which seeks to move toward competition at a slower rate than proposed by
17011 state regulators, calls for functional separation of generation from other operations.The utility said the rate freeze, proposed to start August 1, 1997, depends on NYSEG being allowed to raise prices 2.8 percent this year and 2.7 percent in 1997. In late August, the New York Public Service Commission postponed a
17011 decision on a rate structure proposed by NYSEG to implement this year's 2.8 percent increase.This action was cited by several utility sources as one of the reasons the Energy Association of New York filed suit last week challenging the industry restructuring proposal resulting from the commission's Competitive Opportunities Proceeding.As part
17011 of that proceeding, the commission put forward its proposals in May, requesting proposals from individual utilities by October 1. NYSEG was the first to respond, filing its proposal, which it calls NYSEPlan, Friday. "We strongly support competition and NYSEGPlan is designed to treat customers and shareholders fairly during the transition
17011 to competition," said executive vice president Jack H. Roskoz. "It would provide customers with stable prices and safe, reliable service. Shareholders would continue to have a reasonable opportunity to fully recover prudent investments."Retail competition would be phased in under NYSEGPlan, beginning August 1, 1998, the utility said."After one year of
17011 retail competition in areas yet to be selected, we would work with customers and other parties...to assess its success. 17011 1997, the utility said. That's eight months later than the commission proposed."In today's energy marketplace most electric utilities own generating stations and use the power from those stations to serve their customers. 17011 would then compete in an unregulated market," Roskoz said.-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.</

17016 Latin American regulators should closely monitor telltale domestic interest rates that can serve as early warning signs to help prevent financial crises, Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) experts advised on Friday.At a conference on the fringes of the IMF-World Bank annual meeting, IADB economists also recommended policies to strengthen banks in
17016 a region known for colossal financial catastrophes. The cleanup of last year's Mexico's banking crisis has already cost that country the equivalent of six percentage points of GDP. Venezuela's 1994 collapse consumed a full 15 percentage points of its GDP.IADB principal advisor Liliana Rojas-Suarez and bank consultant Steven Weisbrod suggested
17016 that Latin American regulators keep close tabs on their interbank markets.Pointing to their research on Argentina and Mexico, the economists said regulators could have divined which banks would get into trouble as early as two years before the 1995 peso crisis. "Many of the banks that paid the highest rates
17016 in the interbank markets in 1993 and 1994 were the ones that had to be rescued last year," said Rojas-Suarez.She also argued that that risk-weighted capital-to-assets banking standards were not as effective in Latin America as in industrialized countries.In many Latin American countries, where wealth is highly concentrated, banks are
17016 often the financial arms of large business groups. Loose accounting standards allow bank owners to shuffle assets between their holdings to produce picture-perfect balance sheets for regulators. Domestic interbank markets usually had the knack of telling who was headed for trouble, Rojas-Suarez said.Ecuador's Central Bank general manager, Augusto de la
17016 Torre, acknowledged that the quality of bank capital in the region could be fictitious.He recounted the case of an Ecuadorean bank that transfered deposits through a web of offshore corporations, only to repatriate the funds as genuine capital increases."We know that good capital only grows through sweat and tears, so
17016 quick capital expansion usually puts banks on the list of suspects," he said. The IADB's chief economist, Ricardo Hausmann, said Latin American countries should actively promote foreign investment in their banking industry, just as they do in other sectors of their economies."Latin America is integrated to international financial markets but
17016 its links are shallow. There's where the dangers lie," he said.Hausmann pointed out that the opening of capital accounts in Latin America have not translated into cheaper, better or more varied financial products for consumers.With the exception of Panama, which has a highly developed domestic banking sector besides its well-known
17016 offshore financial services industry, in most Latin American countries bank debt represents a relatively low percentage of GDP.According to Hausmann, opening up Latin American financial markets to foreign banks and encouraging domestic banks to turn international will promote stability in two ways.On one hand, foreign banks will have access to
17016 their parents' stock of capital and international liquidity if they get in trouble. On the other, regionally diversified banks will be more likely to weather country-specific shocks.</

17029 United States Enrichment Corp said on Friday that its fourth quarter, ended June 30 declined due primarily to changes in the timing of customer fuel requirements.The company, which provides fuel enrichment services to electric utilities operating nuclear power plants, reported revenue of $421.0 million for the quarter, down from $446.0
17029 million a year earlier. Net income declined to $82.4 million from $135.6 million a year earlier. USEC is a government corporation in the process of privatizing. As a government corporation, it is exempt from federal, state and local income taxes.During 1996, the company said, it changed to a June 30
17029 fiscal year end from September 30 to more closely align with its natural business cycle. Results for fiscal 1995 have been restated to reflect the change in year end.For fiscal 1996, USEC reported revenue of $1.41 billion compared with record revenue of $1.61 billion for the restated year ended June
17029 30, 1995. Net income amounted to $304.1 million compared with record net income of $447.5 million a year earlier. The lower revenue for the fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year 1996 was attributable primarily to changes in the timing of customer fuel requirements, the company said.Customer requirements are determined by
17029 refueling schedules that generally range from 12 to 24 months and are affected by, among other things, the seasonal nature of electricity demand and production, it said.The timing of customer reactor fuel reloads tends to be fairly predictable over the long run, but may impact quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year comparisons.The decline
17029 in fourth quarter and year earnings resulted from lower revenue, increased spending on the Atomic Vapor Laser Isotope Separation process and higher unit production costs at the gaseous diffusion plants, USEC said.It said the higher unit production costs were the result of lower production levels at the plants. Production levels
17029 declined at the gaseous diffusion plants as a result of increased maintenance activities, changes in regulatory requirements, and increased purchases of low enriched uranium from Russia. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.</

17059 The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 11 to one at its August 20 meeting to keep short-term interest rates unchanged, and maintained its policy bias toward tightening, according to meeting minutes released on Friday.Citing concerns about inflationary pressures, Minneapolis Fed president Gary Stern dissented in favor of an immediate
17059 tightening. Stern also dissented at the July gathering. The FOMC has since met again on Tuesday of this week and elected to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at 5.25 percent, its level since January 31."Mr. Stern dissented because he believed that policy should become modestly more restrictive," the minutes
17059 said, adding Stern was concerned that "in the absence of a substantial and sustained improvement in productivity, the prevailing pattern of demand might engender an increase in inflationary pressures."The minutes showed a "differing view" from most at the FOMC giving "more weight to the risks of rising inflation." The "differing
17059 view" also found "a prompt policy action was needed to contain inflation and set the stage for further progress toward price stability."While deciding to keep rates unchanged, U.S. policy makers reiterated their commitment to the preemptive monetary policy introduced in February 1994, the minutes showed:"The prudent course at this point
17059 was to await further developments that would permit them to assess the possible need for some tightening with a higher degree of confidence... At the same time, it was emphasized the Committee remained committed to a policy that would resist a rise in inflation. "Such a policy would entail moving
17059 in anticipation of greater price pressures and before they showed through to actual inflation."The minutes further showed the FOMC adopted a tightening bias -- a "directive (that) would imply any tightening should be implemented promptly if developments were perceived as pointing to rising inflation."One concern expressed by FOMC members regarding
17059 the possible implications of an immediate rate hike was that "policy tightening at this point might generate an excessive reaction in financial markets." Concern about financial markets' eventual reaction to a tightening was raised "both because it was not generally expected and because it would represent a change in policy
17059 direction that might well lead to expectations of further policy tightening," the minutes said."Such a development could have serious adverse consequences for economic activity if the expansion was in fact already slowing to a more sustainable and less inflationary pace," the minutes added.The minutes also showed the jury was still
17059 out at the FOMC regarding growth and inflation expectations. The FOMC noted "increases in prices remained remarkably subdued for an extended period in relation to measures of resource utilization, notably the rate of unemployment."The U.S. unemployment stood at 5.4 percent in July -- the latest rate reported at the time
17059 of the FOMC meeting.Among the reasons cited at the meeting as possible factors accounting for the subdued inflation performance were "highly competitive markets... comparatively small increases in labor compensation... (that) appeared to reflect worker concerns about job security... as well as substantially reduced increases in benefit costs." While FOMC members
17059 "cited a variety of indications that economic growth was slowing from a very rapid pace," they also acknowledged "the extent of the slowing remained uncertain and it was unclear at this juncture whether the expansion would slow sufficiently to contain pressures on the labor and other producer resources."Also, the minutes
17059 said "the (Fed Board) staff forecast prepared for this meeting suggested the expansion would slow to a rate around, or perhaps a little above, the economy's estimated growth potential." The minutes did not spell out what the U.S. growth potential rate is.-- 212-859-1666</
17060 The financial woes faced by Latin America's banks are not unique to the region and should not be treated as such by regulators, said Andrew Crockett, general manager at the Bank for International Settlements."Latin America has not been alone in facing financial difficulties and fragility and the sources of the
17060 problems are not unique," said Crockett, speaking to an audience of bankers and regulators at the Inter-American Development Bank here.He cited an IMF study which found that 131 of 181 member countries had suffered significant banking crises in the past. He also noted that macroeconomic volatility or fluctuating interest rates
17060 -- a major source of concern for Latin America's banking system -- were at the root of banking problems in the Spanish and Nordic banking systems as well as the Savings and Loan crisis in the U.S."That means that the rules and practices that have to be adopted in Latin
17060 America ... have to be consistent with those being adopted in other countries facing similar problems," Crockett added."We need to have an overall comprehensive umbrella of banking standards, practices and understandings that is applicable in any area of the world, depending upon the particular circumstances of the individual countries," Crockett
17060 said.He said such an "umbrella" did not preclude national differentiation where internationally agreed upon standards were insufficient.He added however, that it would be "very unfortunate" to design rules that were "generically different in different areas of the world."</

17068 had been on the generous side and because company officials said the acquisition would dilute earnings per share by 50 percent or more in 1997. The dilution on cash flow in 1997 would be about 20 percent, they said. But few in the market had any argument with the strategic
17068 move further towards broadcasting."Belo has an extremely attractive newspaper in Dallas, which is better than average, but broadcasting is still considered to be an industry of superior growth and superior returns," said Kara Cheseby of Legg Mason Wood Walker.Belo is not the first publisher to chart such a route. 17068 Co, the owner of the Chicago Tribune, earlier this year bought Renaissance Communications Corp for $1.13 billion and both Gannett Co Inc and the New York Times Co have also moved steadily into broadcasting. 17068 acquisitions in both radio and television and many media groups have been anxious to act quickly or else get left behind.Building up an attractive portfolio of stations allows owners far greater negotiating power in terms of network affiliation and programming.Newspapers, even those with firm market pentration such as the Dallas
17068 Morning News and the Providence Journal-Bulletin, have meanwhile continued to see advertizing siphoned off by other media. 17078 The House Friday passed a bill to protect the nation's declining fisheries, clearing the legislation for President Clinton's signature.The House voted 384 to 30 for the measure, which the White House has said it generally supported as well. But in debate some Democrats complained they were forced to accept the
17078 Senate's somewhat weaker version of the bill intended to clamp down on wasteful fishing practices and protect fish habitat.With the congressional session drawing to a close, other congressmen said the bill was such a drastic improvement from the current law that they felt they could not wait another year or
17078 two to pass a stronger bill. The House approved the Senate bill to avoid the time-consuming process of working out differences between the two versions.While conservation groups generally preferred the House bill, they endorsed the final bill reforming the 20-year-old Magnuson Fisheries Act. The act was written to make U.S.
17078 fisheries off-limits to foreign fishing operations but it spurred a rush for domestic exploitation of fishing resources.With over-fishing and the wasteful practice of netting large amounts of non-commercial aquatic life, then dumping it overboard dead or dying, many fisheries are on the brink of collapse. In the North Pacific alone,
17078 as much as 750 million pounds of fish is dumped overboard annually and Gulf shrimpers dump nearly that much.The Commerce Department has said restoring fisheries would have a $25 billion economic impact and create 300,000 jobs.While the House passed its original version of the bill a year ago, the measure
17078 stalled in the Senate in a dispute between Alaska and Washington state lawmakers over access to North Pacific fisheries.After the Senate unanimously passed its bill this month, Alaska Republican Sen. Ted Stevens warned that if the new rules did not work to curb wasteful practices of factory fishing trawlers in
17078 the North Pacific, he would push a bill to ban the trawlers. Trawlers operate mostly out of Washington.</

17081 that the department may ask Nationwide to provide refunds to approximately 47,000 policyholders who have already seen their rates rise. 17081 and found Nationwide's estimates to be about 20 percent higher than actual costs.The company had losses of $193 million from hurricanes Hugo, Andrew, Erin and Opal, the state contends. 17081 computer-generated data, McLaughlin said. 17090 General agreement was reached Friday on banking measures to deal with remnants of the savings and loan crisis, with final action hinged upon a spending bill being crafted in Congress.The Administration and Congressional Republicans worked out a compromise overnight on measures intended to ease regulatory burdens on banks which had
17090 been holding up the rest of the banking legislation.The banking provisions are now expected to be added into a catch-all appropriations bill which is still being worked out. The cornerstone of the banking legislation is a provision to beef up the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF), which insures deposits at
17090 thrifts.That fund has been undercapitalized because much of the premiums paid by thrifts are diverted to make the $793 million annual interest payments on Financing Corp. (FICO) bonds.Those bonds were issued in the late 1980s to help with the clean-up of hundreds of failed savings and loans.The legislation would require
17090 thrifts to pay a one-time charge totaling $4.7 billion to boost the SAIF to its required level, and then banks would share the FICO interest payments.</

17102 trade ministers from Japan, Canada, the European Union and the United States. 17102 want to help to make sure that what happens in Singapore is going to be forward looking and that it will be a successful conference," Canadian Trade Minister Arthur Eggleton told reporters ahead of a morning session. U.S. trade officials have said there would be little chance of the ITA
17102 being agreed to at the December WTO meeting if Quad members were unable to agree among themselves.The ITA would eliminate tariffs by 2000 on a wide range of electronic products, including computers, chips, software, fax machines, modems and other telecommunications equipment. 17102 idea of eliminating tariffs on those products is not negotiable.European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan has said the main stumbling block is the U.S./Japan semiconductor alliance. 17103 record-setting western Gulf lease sale this week, spending a total $62 million to place winning bids on 123 blocks.The lease sale drew a record 929 bids and $356.1 million in high bids, with interest in deepwater tracts fueled by lower royalty rates designed to boost domestic oil production.In a consortium
17103 with Texaco Inc and Amoco Corp, Shell Offshore won rights to the deepest tract in the lease round, a section of the Alaminos Canyon lying in more than 10,000 feet of water 156 miles from Port Isabel, Texas. That prospect lies well out of the reach of modern drilling technology,
17103 and probably will not be explored before the turn of the century unless there are revolutionary advances in drilling technology, he said.Shell Offshore in April spudded the deepest well so far in the Gulf, drilling its first Baha well in 7,620 feet of water in Alaminos Canyon, which lies 150

17104 Sustainable economic growth and tame inflation in the United States, combined with Japan's desire for a weaker yen and the mark's recent slump against other European currencies, could keep the dollar rallying even if the Federal Reserve does not tighten credit this year."As long as growth moderates towards (the) 2.0

17104 on Tuesday by leaving short-term rates unchanged. 17104 level which is the level that Mr. Sakakibara has mentioned in the past as being a level he thinks would be acceptable," said Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics.Earlier this month, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the international finance bureau at Japan's Ministry of Finance's (MOF), said Japan has
17104 no specific target for the dollar/yen exchange rate but any level justified by fundamentals is good. 17104 30 international edition of Business Week magazine, Sakakibara said, "As long as this Japanese capital outflow continues, we are going to be looking at a strengthening dollar." 17104 the dollar rally could peter out and the mark firm slightly if the trend towards convergence trades in Europe should slow. "Right now I think that the dollar's rally (against the mark) is based more on these convergence trades in Europe," Widness said, adding "those will calm down and I
17104 wouldn't be surprised if the market starts to have second doubts on how much of a lock there is on European Monetary Union by 1998."Widness said "these rallies" of other currencies against the mark "will peter out" by the end of the year and the mark "will look a little
17104 firmer" against the dollar and other currencies, he said.Recent ballooning of the U.S. international trade deficit also clouds any upbeat dollar scenario. 17105 The September U.S. employment report might persuade investors to bet on neutral Federal Reserve monetary policy for the next couple of months, economists said on Friday.Although the economy created more than 200,000 new jobs each month from May through August, 26 economists in a Reuters survey projected, on average, that
17105 166,000 new jobs were added in September. At the same time, the unemployment rate rose slightly to 5.2 percent in September from 5.1 percent the month before, the experts forecast."The bond market is trying to figure out whether the Fed can wait longer after staying on hold at its last
17105 (policy) meeting," said Peter Kretzmer, an economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc. "A report like this would tend to argue, yes."After central bank policymakers ended this week's meeting without raising interest rates, inflation doves quickly touted post-meeting data as evidence of the Fed's credibility: durable goods orders fell 3.1 percent
17105 last month and weekly jobless claims breeched the 330,000-level for the first time in several weeks.But both of those reports fluctuate widely.The central bank's next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is set for November 13, and many economists believe next Friday's jobs data will set the stage for another
17105 interest rate non-event."If we get a sanguine employment report, combined with (a weak September) retail sales report, then I think the Fed would stay on hold," said Kretzmer. Economists calling for lower payrolls said a boomlet of teaching jobs boosted payrolls last month, while earlier start dates for the school
17105 year skewed the report's seasonal adjustments."There are a couple of factors that inflated August, but the same factors are going to deflate the September number a little," said Michael Strauss, executive vice president and chief economist at Yamaichi International (America) Inc.Last month non-farm payrolls grew by 250,000 and the unemployment
17105 rate dipped to 5.1 percent. "People are saying 30 (or) 40 thousand will have to come off that number" to account for the teacher bloat, said Astrid Adolfson, senior economist at MCM MoneyWatch Inc.A drop of greater magnitude might hint at weakening of the labor market's underlying trend, some economists
17105 said. But most of the experts said the labor sector remains tight.Strauss, for instance, forecast a payrolls number of 175,000, and he said anything over 125,000 would suggest job creation "above long-term (sustainable) employment growth.""There is a good chance the (Treasury) market is going to try to view the number
17105 in a favorable light," said Strauss. "(But) there might be some disappointment if it's not significantly weaker than what we're talking about."Besides payrolls and the unemployment rate, the economists in the Reuters survey projected average hourly earnings rose 0.2 percent to $11.89. And they forecast the average workweek expanded one-tenth
17105 of an hour to 34.5 hours.Such small increases should not cause much concern for bond investors or others who fear wage inflation, said NationsBanc's Kretzmer. While hourly earnings have risen steadily in recent months, real earnings have grown by less than 1.0 percent in the past year, he said."I really
17105 don't think that's too out of line," said Kretzmer.-- 212-859-1868</

17121 Nearly 17,000 people had $4.8 million restored to their 401(k) retirement plans after employers made use of a "grace" period to replace funds they failed to deposit properly, the government said Friday.The Labor Department released data showing that 170 small to mid-sized businesses voluntarily returned employee contributions and made good
17121 on lost earnings after they were given six months to do so without penalty. The amnesty program, which expired earlier this month, was part of a broader Clinton administration effort to police for fraudulent activity in 401(k) plans. So far, the crackdown has resulted in investigations that have led to
17121 the return of another $10 million in employee funds."We don't have any evidence the problem is widespread but ... there are going to be a few rotten apples," Labor Secretary Robert Reich said in an interview. "We at the Labor Department have to continue to act aggressively." As a result
17121 of the grace period, contributions were repaid to plans affecting 16,800 participants. Amounts ranged from $43 to more than $200,000, the department said.The employers, which included technology companies, law firms, physicians and credit unions among others, admitted to being delinquent for reasons ranging from computer errors to diverting funds to
17121 pay bills.Amnesty was not an option for those employers "who had engaged in the most egregious conduct," the department said. Companies were disqualified, for example, if they were already the subject of a criminal investigation or if they failed to make deposits that exceeded the total amount of employee contributions
17121 for all of 1995.Some 23.4 million people participated in more than 170,000 401k plans with total combined assets of $613 billion in 1993, the latest year for which data are available.The 401k retirement plan is named for the part of the U.S. tax code that allows workers to deduct a
17121 portion of income before it is taxed, invest it and pay no taxes on the money until it is withdrawn at retirement.Reich cautioned employees to check their 401(k) statements against their paystubs on a regular basis to ensure that their contributions have been posted accurately."There is no substitute for diligence
17121 on the part of employees," Reich said.The department launched its 401(k) enforcement program in 1995 after it received an increase in the number of complaints about the plans.It issued a new rule last month that requires employers to deposit money withheld from workers' checks for 401(k) plans within 15 days

17133 risk of massive losses from a major catastrophe like an earthquake or hurricane.Insurers have grown increasingly reluctant to write insurance in catastrophe-prone areas following huge losses on the U.S. East Coast from Hurricane Andrew in 1992 and on the earthquake in Northridge, Calif., in 1994.The system would let an insurer
17133 reduce its exposure to catastrophes by allowing it to pay another company to accept some of its risk or by allowing it to give away one set of risks in return for accepting a separate bundle of risks. Everest Reinsurance Holdings Inc in August said it had agreed to become
17133 the first subscriber to Catex, saying it believed the system had the potential to develop into a new source of business.An Everest Re spokeswoman on Friday said the company did not know whether the exchange was ready to begin operating on Tuesday.In addition, she said she did not know whether

17133 the scope of its system to allow subscribers to trade risks for cash, rather than just swapping risk for risk, making the transactions much more like traditional reinsurance.At that time, Catex said it expected to begin operations with a 60-90 day trial period in which subscribers could conduct experimental mock

17175 a person can buy a 1996 Cutlass Supreme for $19,900 and receive an X-90 on a free one-year lease.Suzuki has long been a small player in the domestic vehicle market, reaching a sales peak in 1987 with 83,334 units. In 1988, the company was battered by news and consumer group
17175 reports that its Samuri minisport-utility was prone to tip over. 17175 American buyers, who mostly associate the company with the rollover controversy.One year later, the X-90 is far below even its modest sales targets."The X-90 has probably been their most disappointing product next to the Samuri," said Steve Kosowski, product and market analyst for AutoPacific Inc., a consulting firm in Santa
17175 Ana, Calif.What went wrong?Analysts say the concept was flawed. 17175 runabout, the X-90 has also been criticized for limited power, excessive road noise and mediocre handling.Also unfortunate is the fact that competition is stiffer in the mini sport/utility segment.The RAV4 from Toyota Motor Corp. has proven to be a hit with price-conscious buyers looking for a practical car-based vehicle. 17175 this year Honda Motor Co. Ltd. will enter the field with its CR-V.Suzuki officials are sticking behind their product, however, arguing that it will take time for the X-90 to create sufficient awareness and generate a following. 17175 that, said Anne Bryan, a spokeswoman for American Suzuki."The X-90 is a very unique car and people either love it or hate it," she said. 17175 the profile of the X-90. 17207 General Motors Corp said Friday its Arlington, Texas, plant will produce Chevrolet and GMC C/K full-size pickup trucks and Tahoe and Yukon full-size sport/utility vehicles, starting in the third quarter of 1997.The announcement is GM's first official confirmation of its product plans for the Arlington plant. Previously, the automaker had
17207 said it would convert the plant from car to truck manufacturing but had not identified specific products. The plant now builds GM's full-size Chevrolet Caprice, Buick Roadmaster and Cadillac Fleetwood cars, which will be phased out by the end of 1996.GM said the pickup trucks built at Arlington will all
17207 be extended-cab models with the optional third door, providing a second source for the popular vehicles. Currently, GM builds extended-cab, three-door pickups in Oshawa, Ontario.The plant also will become the sole source for a new police version of the Chevrolet Tahoe. The less-luxurious two-wheel-drive vehicle will be equipped with a
17207 5.7-liter V-8 engine, a heavy-duty suspension and other special equipment. GM said the conversion of the plant to truck production will be completed in the second quarter of 1997.Contractors have already refurbished and added over 100,000 square feet to the body shop, installed robots in the paint shop, and added
17207 an automated storage and retrieval system for painted truck bodies. Renovation of the general assembly area will begin after the end of 1996.The project is part of a long-term plan that GM has to boost truck production to more than 50 percent of its total North American capacity. For the
17207 first six months of 1996, trucks made up about 45 percent of GM's output. The automaker is investing about $260 million in the Arlington conversion project. GM has not disclosed the plant's future capacity, but last year, it built about 127,000 cars, a figure analysts say is well below the
17207 facility's capability.GM spokesman Jeff Kuhlman said the 1998-model-year C/K pickups and four-door Tahoe and Yukon trucks scheduled for Arlington will be carry-over vehicles from the current product lines. The automaker is scheduled to introduce redesigned full-size pickup trucks for the 1999 model year.The Tahoe police package production will start in
17207 the summer of 1997, GM said. "Conversion of the Arlington plant is the latest in a number of steps we've taken over the past several years to increase our production capacity for full-size trucks," said Michael Grimaldi, GM vice president and vehicle line executive for full-size trucks. "It allows us
17207 to build more of the products customers are demanding."At a press conference Friday at the Texas State Fair, Grimaldi predicted that the worldwide truck market would grow to 20 million units from 15 million in the next several years.Truck sales in North America alone are expected to increase to 50
17207 percent from 43 percent of the current market over the same time frame, he said.</
17208 Global Outdoors Inc said the Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed that its financial statements be revised to defer certain revenue for lifetime memberships.It said the proposed revision would "substantially reduce the revenues and profits of the company." 17208 Club. 17208 has proposed that Global's financial statements be revised to defer revenue for lifetime memberships and amortize it on a straight line basis over the estimated period which the member is expected to use the land and facilities.Global said it has consulted with its accountants regarding the SEC proposal.It said it
17208 expects to file a response to the SEC in the near future, but that it is uncertain what the ultimate determination will be.</

17247 and Far East benchmark Dubai crude."The Brent-Dubai spread is extremely wide, so there is no encouragement to take barrels to the Far East," said a trader."There's certainly no spot interest."Brent was about $2.25 a barrel more expensive than Dubai on the forward paper markets on Friday. The Brent/Dubai spread in
17247 September has averaged about 70 cents a barrel more than in August.The spread ballooned earlier this month as Middle East tension combined with growing concern about low northern hemisphere heating oil stocks to push benchmark Brent crude futures to a new post-Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel."While the spread
17247 is not favourable at the moment, buyers like the South Koreans do need sweet crudes," said a trader."But when it gets to this kind of level and it doesn't make sense economically...they usually turn to Australian grades," he added.Growing refinery capacity in the region and tighter emission standards for refined
17247 products has sparked fresh Asian demand this year for low sulphur West African barrels.Exports peaked at a record one million barrels in February before petering out almost entirely in May and June. They recovered strongly in July to reach 800,000 bpd.Apart from the Indian Oil Corp's regular purchase of three
17247 very large crude carriers (VLCCs) of Nigerian Qua Iboe, October exports have been limited to two VLCCs to Taiwan's CPC.Despite the lack of an arbitrage window to the Far East and difficult economics for transatlantic sales, premiums have recovered as European and U.S. refiners scrambled for sweet, middle distillate-rich barrels
17247 like Forcados and Bonny Medium, traders said."There's certainly very little Nigerian crude left in October, maybe the odd Brass River, Escravos and a Qua Iboe," said a trader.European and U.S. refiners are running at full tilt in an attempt to rebuild heating oil stocks before winter sets in. 17247 also gearing up for a switch to low sulphur diesel on October 1.-- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930</
