17249 The world's biggest gold miners, with an eye to expansion, are enthusiastically staking out projects in gold-rich countries recently considered too politically risky for investment.In sharp contrast, South Africa, still the world's top producer, is struggling to stem a decline in output and the mature industry there holds little interest
17249 for expansion."There's no question South Africa's market share is going to decline. Exploration going into South Africa is negligible," Tom Dale, managing director of Gengold Ltd, told a gold conference of top mining houses on Thursday.South Africa used to consistently produce about 600 tons of gold annually, but would do
17249 well now to stabilise at around 500 tons per year, Dale added.Budgets for exploration topped $100 million per year for some of the houses attending the conference, sponsored by RBC Dominion Securities Inc."Africa is a veritable treasure house as yet not fully tapped. In the next century, Africa outside of
17249 South Africa will emerge as the major gold-producing continent," said Sam Jonah of Ghana-based Ashanti Goldfields Corp.The political situation in Ghana has improved greatly in recent years and is attracting big mining houses, Jonah noted.Barrick Gold Corp., which spent the first 10 of its 12-year life as a North American
17249 miner, has set out to double in size over the next decade, said chairman Peter Munk.Munk waxed enthusiastic about South America for its rich gold deposits and recently warmed investment climate. Barrick has interests in Peru, Argentina and Chile."In Chile, the raised fist of Che Guevara is a romantic fantasty
17249 of teenagers which becomes less attractive when you grow up. This counter revolution has spread and we're going to find a totally different climate there," Munk said. Barrick completed a C$1 billion ($ ) takeover of theexploration company Arequipa Resources Ltd last month, solidifying its position as the world's third
17249 biggest gold producer and giving it ownership of Arequipa Pierina gold deposit in Peru.Countries within the former Soviet Union were also slowly sparking cautious interest.U.S.-based Newmont Mining Corp. chairman Ron Cambre said the company was pleased with its first project in Uzbekistan and was considering a second with similar reserves
17249 of around seven million ounces in the Angren mining district."We have an aggressive programme in the international arena," Cambre said. "Uzbekistan has excellent leadership. It's a different culture but we're getting better at dealing with it."Gengold's Dale noted that South African companies were focusing on getting leaner and increasing productivity.
17249 "We may look dead, but we're still kicking," he said."There's a revolution going on in the South African mining industry," he added, noting it concentrated on paring overhead costs and top-heavy corporate structure, improving productivity and boosting cooperation through mineral rights swaps."Successful mining houses will be those who implement change,"
17249 he said."And if you don't improve capacity utilization, then production will continue on a sharp downward curve."</

17267 Wellington lack a vital power source, and ability to slip into overdrive and give back what is being received.The agenda for Wellington over the rest of this season is quite clear. 17267 20 or 21 points, probably just a couple away from qualifying for the National Provincial Championship (NPC) semifinals.The remaining two matches, away against Counties and Otago, represent two difficult assignments. Wellington were beaten 29-3 by Counties in Pukekohe two years ago, and their record at Carisbrook is little better. Both
17267 those teams are in desperate need of points themselves. To have to win both these matches to qualify is a very big task. So when Tiatia this week talked about the need for the Wellington forwards to become mentally tougher in a hurry, he was only talking reality if the
17267 side is to qualify."We're slowly getting there as a team," Tiatia said. "I'm not too worried about the backs. They're doing great. If we give them the ball on a plate they put it over the line."So the onus goes on to all eight of us forwards, as well as
17267 those in the reserves, to get mentally tougher and do the hard work." Waikato, in the opinion of many, will not have the collective mind on the job on Sunday because of the upcoming clash of the giants against Auckland five days later.That would be a very foolish thought if
17267 Wellington coach Frank Walker and his players allow it. The Waikato outfit are a professional one fully aware of the need for championship points against Wellington.Waikato have 18 points at present. If they miss out altogether against Wellington and loses the shield to Auckland, they could end up not qualifying
17267 at all for the semis. So Tiatia and his fellow players have to shut any thought of Waikato "not being on the job" out of their minds. They have to do it all themselves. And that means further forward improvement and a tougher attitude in the set pieces, where Wellington
17267 are struggling to win their own ball."If we can't win our ball from set pieces, we're never going to win a game. So we're definitely going to target Waikato as a must-win," Taitia said. Now that the big loose forward is really back into his game after a succession of
17267 injuries last year and this, he can think about his future, about whether he's better at No 7 or No 8, and whether he thinks about chasing an international jersey for the All Blacks or Samoa.Hurricanes coach Frank Oliver went against the general feeling on Tiatia by playing him at
17267 No 7 for much of the Super 12, and now Wellington's Frank Walker has gone the same way. "I'm enjoying No 7 but I still need more games there to learn the mechanics and get my base fitness up a bit. But I do really enjoy No 8 -- I'd
17267 be lying if I said I didn't," Tiatia said."However, some coaches have said I might go a little bit further as an openside flanker, so I have to weigh up both positions pretty quickly."Tiatia, of course, has always yearned for an All Black jersey, even though his father Iete Tiatia
17267 is a backbone of local Samoan rugby. But he's having trouble convincing "the right people". 17267 keen about me coming across to help Samoa, but I've told him I'll give it another year. If the All Black jersey doesn't happen, then I guess it wasn't meant to be," Tiatia said."I've just got to give it everything in the remaining games of the season, and I'll go

17277 The Loewen Group Inc. said Friday that Florida's attorney general has launched an antitrust investigation of Service Corp. International's proposed $2.8 billion takeover of Loewen.Loewen, North America's second biggest funeral home and cemetery operator, said it received a civil subpoena for documents in connection with the probe.Houston-based Service is the
17277 biggest operator in the industry and the two companies are archrivals. Loewen this week rejected the $43-a-share stock bid by Service, which is widely expected to launch a higher hostile bid next week after its board meets on Tuesday."We welcome the scrutiny of the Florida attorney general's office and other
17277 state regulators as well, since SCI clearly intends to eliminate its most formidable competitor in the North American marketplace," said Chief Executive Ray Loewen.Service had no immediate comment.Loewen's announcement of the investigation appeared aimed at bolstering its fight against Service by raising worries about potential barriers to the deal in
17277 the minds of investors. Ray Loewen has rejected a takeover, saying he could see no business rationale for a deal with Service.After the news, Loewen stock was off 62.5 cents at $40.50 on Nasdaq while Service gained 37.5 cents to $30.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.Loewen said the Florida
17277 subpoena suggests "a wide ranging investigation into the potential impact of the proposed acquisition on pricing, Medicare/Medicaid issues and market concentration for cemeteries and funeral homes" in Florida.A Loewen spokesman said the company knew of no other states with investigations underway. A combined Service and Loewen would have a 23.4
17277 percent share of funeral homes in Florida, according to the New York Times. The newspaper said there were 13 other states where their combined share would be higher than 10 percent.Loewen has said it believes antitrust concerns would be a major obstacle to the takeover, but many industry analysts have
17277 discounted that theory, saying antitrust hurdles could be overcome.Both Service and Loewen have been aggressively buying independent funeral homes and cemeteries across the United States as the highly fragmented industry consolidates.Analysts and institutional investors said they expected Service Corp. to raise its bid for Loewen to $45 to $48 a
17277 share next week. "I think that is very realistic," Dean Witter analyst Todd Richter said of a bid in that range."Up to the high 40s it's a good deal" for Service Corp., he said.Analysts said a higher bid would intensify pressure on Loewen to negotiate a deal but expected Loewen
17277 to continue to resist. Ray Loewen, who has a reputation as a tough fighter and holds 15 percent of the company's stock, has said even $52 would not make him feel under pressure to sell.</

17284 Clearnet Communications Inc said on Friday that it will launch on Monday its new wireless business communications service under the trade name MiKE.MiKE is a digital wireless communications service for business that integrates mobile phone, dispatch or group and private call radio, alphanumeric paging and messaging services into a single
17284 handset.Through a Motorola Inc handset, subscribers will be able to communicate via cellular phone and two-way radio, and receive text messages, including those via the Internet, and pager messages, company officials told reporters. The network will initially be operational in the corridor between Quebec City and Windsor, Ontario, but the
17284 company said it planned eventually to roll out the service nationally."We want to be anywhere with MiKE that business takes place," said Wade Oosterman, vice president of sales and marketing.Clearnet's cellular telephone tariff would match those of Canada's two largest cellular phone service providers, BCE Mobile Communications Inc unit Bell
17284 Mobility and Rogers Cantel Communications Inc, he said. Clearnet officials declined to discuss the potential or expected subscriber base and revenues for MiKE. Oosterman said the company has raised C$1.1 billion of financing to fund the expansion of the MiKE network and a personal communications services (PCS) network that it
17284 plans to launch nationally in Canada in mid-1997.But MiKE will offer local calling areas that are on average 15 to 20 percent larger and calls will be billed by the second instead of by the minute.The great advantage for subscribers will be the flexibility offered by providing all four communications
17284 services in one handset, and the quality of a digital network, Oosterman said.A similar combination phone service was launched on September 16 in certain areas of the United States by Nextel Communications Inc, a 20 percent shareholder in Clearnet. The Nextel system also uses Motorola technology. -- Reuters Montreal bureau

17288 in Dakar.With 45 of 47 constituencies or 81 percent of the vote counted, Jammeh's tally was 199,650 votes or 55 percent of the total. 17288 was assured.Two marginal civilian candidates -- hotel manager Amath Bah of the National Reconciliation Party and Sidia Jatta of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism -- polled 20,977 and 10,571 votes respectively.Electoral commission chairman Gabriel Roberts was expected to make a formal declaration of results later.It was
17288 not immediately clear if there had been any direct threat to Darboe, who was reported by state television to have cast his vote in Banjul on Thursday, polling day.Some of his aides were arrested during campaign violence and many said they were beaten up by soldiers after a clash with
17288 Jammeh supporters a few days before voting.Jammeh's win is bound to alarm democracy campaigners in West Africa faced with a new political challenge: coupmakers exploiting the advantage of incumbency to legitimise their rule through the ballot box.Such elections left political tension in their wake in Niger and Chad.Jammeh, 31, seized
17288 power in a 1994 coup, toppling elected president Sir Dawda Jawara who had ruled the tiny country of one million people from independence from Britain in 1965.Jammeh resigned from the army last month to contest the elections that he brought forward from 1998 following Western pressure. 17288 and some put a temporary ban on their nationals travelling to the tourist haven.Jammeh turned to Libya, Cuba and Taiwan who gave aid for new projects in health, education and infrastructure that he has openly cited to woo voters.Jammeh and military associates formed the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction
17288 that nominated him. 17289 Darboe's 58,356 but commentators said the race was still open as results had not been announced for two of Darboe's strongholds.The Senegalese sources said that Darboe, 48-year-old vice-president of the Gambia Bar Association, was at the embassy with his two wives and three children.Gambia, born of 19th century Anglo-French colonial
17289 rivalry, won independence from Britain in 1965 and is surrounded by Francophone Senegal apart from a stretch of Atlantic coastline.Jawara survived a coup attempt by leftists in 1981 thanks to the intervention of Senegalese troops. The abortive coup, in which hundreds of people died, prompted Jawara to sign a loose
17289 confederation treaty with Senegal.The pact collapsed in 1989 with Gambia reluctant to speed up trade and customs union for fear of losing its identity.</
17290 Matthew TostevinA Nigerian motor-show opened on Friday amidst gloom over the state of vehicle sales in the depressed economy."There are not as many exhibitors as there were a few years ago, the economy is so wobbly," Yewande Ayo, organiser of Automania, told Reuters.At one time Africa's most populous nation had
17290 six vehicle assembly plants. Now it has only one -- run by Peugeot Automobiles Nigeria."Business is very dull. Very, very dull. We're here at the show in one more effort to try and improve things," said Sola Ajidagba of CFAO Motors, distributors for Mitsubishi, Land Rover, Daewoo and Iveco."All sectors
17290 have been hit although commercial vehicles are marginally better than the rest, we are having to look at new strategies to increase sales."Ajidagba said CFAO had cut profit margins and introduced hire-purchase terms over 24 months, as well as increasing spending on publicity."In the past we waited for customers to
17290 come to the sales rooms, now we have to get out to them," he said.Since Volkswagen and Fiat closed their assembly plants Peugeot is the only company to produce as much as 35 percent of the components of its vehicles inside Nigeria itself.Production at the plant in the northern city
17290 of Kaduna has risen to around 30 vehicles per day in 1996 from 15 to 20 in 1995.But this is far below the 150 per day in 1991 and 260 per day in the early 1980s, when Nigeria still rode high on the oil boom.The economic decline was accelerated by
17290 a wave of strikes and riots which followed the annulment of presidential elections in 1993 by a previous military government.A four-fold fuel price hike in 1994, shortage of foreign exchange and lack of confidence in the economy saw inflation running above 80 percent a year.While relative macroeconomic stability has returned,
17290 there is still no sign of increased demand."Before business in Nigeria was fantastic, now the market is shrinking, so competition is increasing, prices are coming down and so are margins," said Frederic Larrouilh of French group SOEXIMEX, which imports spare parts.Nigeria is a centre for the whole of West and
17290 Central Africa as a source of motor spares, but surrounding economies are performing little better than Nigeria's own, and in many cases worse."We are forced to diversify and are looking at other import businesses, Nigeria is a huge potential market," Larrouilh said.Facing difficulties in sourcing foreign exchange he said SOEXIMEX
17290 had begun exporting cocoa to pay for imports.Notably absent from the show were Nigeria's biggest car importers -- those bringing second hand cars, often in doubtful working order, from Europe.Official statistics show over 85,000 used cars were imported in 1995, compared to 15,000 new cars. Unofficially, used car imports are
17290 likely to be higher."From those that I know I can tell you the used car importers are also suffering," said Ajidagba.</

17292 murder of Hutu President Juvenal Habyarimana.It was the second postponement ordered by the tribunal in three days. 17292 the judge after the court refused to rule on a defence motion for Akayesu's temporary release.The court also decided on Friday that witnesses in Akayesu's trial should not be identified to the public or media for their protection.On Thursday, Scheers had threatened to resign unless the tribunal granted a postponement.
17292 He had also sought the temporary release of Akayesu.Akayesu was the local government leader in Rwanda's Taba commune in the three-month genocide and is charged with failing to stop killings, inciting the public to slaughter, hunting down minority Tutsis and ordering killings.The tribunal has been dogged by delays, poor communications
17292 from its base in the northern Tanzanian farming town of Arusha, and the vast problem of finding who was responsible for the genocide.It has indicted only 21 suspects and has only three in detention, charged with crimes against humanity and genocide.</

17349 A new system aimed at overhauling South Africa's chaotic customs and excise controls has been designed and could be phased in over the next three years, according to its backers.South Africa loses billions of rand each year in revenue through corruption and fraud at its ports, a problem that has
17349 been compounded by understaffing and poor technology.The Technological Information Management System, developed by private firm IPES and now being assessed by officials, would initially link databases at the Department of Trade and Industry, port authority Portnet and Customs and Excise.It would introduce information such as transaction statistics, a bar code
17349 system providing container information and a tracking system using terrestrial radio and satellite tracking.A scanning mechanism and a software package aimed at providing real time data on the movement of imports and exports is also planned.An initial phase, which would focus on customs law enforcement at four transport hubs --
17349 Durban, Cape Town, City Deep in Johannesburg and Beit Bridge on the border of South Africa and Zimbabwe -- would take four months to implement.Leon Vermaak, the designer of the system, said the development of the system stemmed from the need to eradicate South Africa's reputation of being a smuggler's
17349 dream."South Africa has become a smuggler's den and could easily gain the reputation of being the smuggler's capital of the world because of the near collapse of customs control," Vermaak said.It also took cognisance of Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's recent statement that no industrial policy could have integrity until the
17349 country had efficient customs control.Vermaak said lax customs controls cost South Africa some five billion rand a year in lost Value Added Tax receipts as well as providing a fillip for a burgeoning grey import market, estimated to be a 12 billion rand a year industry.Ben van Rensburg, senior economist
17349 at the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob), put the total loss of tax revenue at something between 12 and 20 billion rand a year."A linked database system will start to solve this specific problem because it will give you those linkages between importation, customs and excise, VAT and income
17349 tax," Van Rensburg said.An advantage of the system would include improving the reliability of South African trade data, which economists have recently lambasted as unreliable."Our import and export numbers have become almost the laughing stock of the financial world. We know that those numbers are not to be trusted," van
17349 Rensburg said."We think that putting a proper, trustworthy database in place and which we know good data is coming in and out is a starting point of solving the problem," he added.Vermaak said the system has already been presented to most of the stakeholders and the private sector who had
17349 approved the concept in principle.High level talks are currently underway to discuss the financing of the project, which is expected to result in a decision being made on whether government or the private sector will fund the scheme.-- Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003</

17358 Templeton Asset Management SA, a subsidiary of the U.S.-based fund manager, said on Friday it was seeking a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) ruling on whether certain South African asset swaps might contravene U.S. law.Managing director John Phillips said the company, which has $800 million under management, had not engaged
17358 in any swaps pending clarification from the U.S. watchdog.Templeton is concerned that so-called "quid pro quo" swaps might be illegal under U.S. law since companies could end up earning two fees, creating a potential clash with their fiduciary duties.The group petitioned the SEC for an exemptive order giving a green
17358 light to South African asset swaps three months ago and hopes to receive a ruling soon, Phillips told Reuters."There is a possible conflict of interests on which we are asking the SEC to rule," he said.The legal uncertainty arises because of the 1940 U.S. Investment Company Act, which prohibits an
17358 investment company from receiving any additional fees in addition to management fees as a result of a trasaction.Such double fees can arise with South African asset swaps if the same investment company that carried out the swap is then hired to manage the foreign credit issued to the local company
17358 by the Reserve Bank, he said.However, not all South African swaps work on this quid pro quo basis.In some cases, two parties simply swap assets directly -- for example, certain South African shares in exchange for international shares. In other cases, a third party may be appointed as manager, thereby
17358 avoiding any potential conflict.The Reserve Bank introduced the concept of asset swaps in July 1995, whereby local institutions could trade assets held domestically for those of a foreign partner. The swaps can include both equities and bonds.A total of nearly 15 billion rand in asset swaps have been authorised since
17358 last July.Reserve Bank officials were not immediately available to comment.-- Ben Hirschler, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003</

17375 In rolling hills roamed by lions, South Africa has discovered the citadel of an aloof king and queen that experts say will help rewrite both the distant and near past.The unearthing of southern Africa's first royal remains, along with gold jewellery, West African-style ornaments and even Chinese pottery, has been
17375 hailed as the most exciting find for years.Archaeologists say Thulamela has given up clues that will help piece together the largely unknown history of the area and its people. The hilltop site, deep in the Kruger National Park bush, was used from 1200 to 1640, then suddenly abandoned.Its links with
17375 Great Zimbabwe, a mysterious ancient city across the present-day border that housed 14,000 people despite arid land, are clear.Politicians say Thulamela has also given the lie to the apartheid version of history which held that South Africa's interior was empty when the whites arrived at the Cape in 1652 --
17375 and that the blacks who came later were savages."We always knew these were lies but we never had the evidence. Now we have that evidence," Environment Minister Pallo Jordan told some 850 people celebrating Thulamela's official opening on Tuesday, the Heritage Day holiday.Gold braid, beads and bracelets testify to the
17375 king and queen's immense wealth. The Chinese pottery and gongs, believed to be West African, also showed their people traded extensively.Archaeologist Sydney Miller has spent the last three years scouring the country's remote northeastern corner for "lost cities", told of in the oral history of tribes banished from their land
17375 in 1969 to make way for wild animals.Thulamela, or "the place of giving birth", is surrounded by fat 1,000-year-old baobab trees and overlooks a long-distance elephant trail that locals also used as a trade route."It is playing an important part in the reconstruction of the history of South Africa," Miller
17375 said.He climbed its steep hill about 1,000 times to dig under the scorching sun -- protected by armed rangers against lions, leopards and elephants -- before his team's effort paid off.The first gold beads were unearthed a few months ago.Beneath two tall grey syringa trees, right on the crest of
17375 the hill with views into neighbouring Mozambique, Miller and his team then found the king, who was around 45 to 60 when he died.They nicknamed him Ingwe (Leopard), after two of the wild cats appeared nearby as the discovery was made.His body had been dismembered and neatly laid to rest,
17375 possibly following a custom in which the leader's bodily fluids would be collected for his successor to drink.Ingwe's queen, curled in a foetal position denoting respect, was buried separately but still within the high stone walls.The royal couple are being examined by scientists and will then be reburied where they
17375 lay for up to 400 years.Ethnologists believe they followed the ideology of sacred leadership, meaning the aloof royals would rarely have appeared to the 1,500 or so common folk who lived in thatched huts below.They appear to be the last rulers of Thulamela before its people -- believed to be
17375 the trader-farmer ancestors of the region's Venda tribe -- moved on to a new home.Experts think that Thulamela itself and several other sites nearby were founded after an exodus of people from Great Zimbabwe as it lost control of its far-flung kingdom.Life at Thulamela seems to have been peaceful, unlike
17375 nearby Makahane whose cruel king, legend has it, made women work naked in the fields and killed any man who objected.He hung warriors over a cliff by their ankles and dropped them if they failed to catch a vulture or eagle chick."It is not clear what happened to the people
17375 of Thulamela after the late 17th Century. Further studies will hopefully shed more light," said a small new exhibition near the site.The two-metre (six-foot) high walls of the royal compound have just been reconstructed from the stones that lay for centuries just where they had fallen, knocked down by tree

17420 audit by Ernst &amp; Young according to U.S. GAAP shows.Net income in the first half of 1995 to Russian standards on a cash basis was only 66.6 billion roubles.But the net profit in the U.S. GAAP statement included hefty gains on holding net monetary liabilities, essentially gains made when payments
17420 were delayed and hyperinflation reduced the real value of the liabilities."If you are able to delay the payment of any liability in fixed terms in a hyperinflationary economy you have reduced those costs and made a gain," said Chuck Buckner, audit partner at Ernst &amp; Young.Chernogorneft gains from this kind
17420 of payment delay were 456 billion roubles in 1995 and 1.1 trillion roubles, adjusted for inflation, in 1994, on sales of 2.5 trillion roubles and 2.2 trillion roubles, respectively.As a result Chernogorneft's net income and income before tax were much bigger than its operating profit.Chernogorneft's financial advisor SovLink said the
17420 new statement showed the company was stronger than Russian accounting suggested."Even if you discount the holding sum, you will find its earnings are a lot stronger than under Russian financials," said Michael Boboshko, a Sovlink analyst.But other analysts said the new statement indicated oil companies could face increasing financial problems
17420 from taxes without the inflationary buffer."They were trying to collect as soon as possible and pay as late as possible," said CentreInvest Securities research chief James Fenkner. 17420 other non-profits taxes were 841 billion roubles in 1995 and 964 billion roubles in 1994. 17420 these figures," he said, adding that taking out the inflation gains gave roughly the same picture as the Russian-standard books. 17420 percent of sales."This is a good healthy company. But taxes are at the level where hardly anybody can operate. 17421 Russian spies past and present emerged from the shadows on Friday to pay their last respects to the man who stole U.S. plans for the atom bomb and arranged to have Stalin's rival Leon Trotsky killed with an ice pick.The Cold War fought by Pavel Sudoplatov -- who died on
17421 Tuesday aged 89 -- is long over. But colleagues who turned up at a modest funeral ceremony in a Moscow suburb found it hard to shake off the habits of a lifetime.One pensioner who worked with Sudoplatov gave his name in a covert whisper and one of the younger spies
17421 -- identifiable by matching macs, leather jackets and wary looks -- made one up when pressed to identify himself. 17421 severe, multi-faceted, unseen front has left us," former foreign intelligence agent Yuri Oleshnikov told around 100, mainly elderly mourners."Thanks to his titanic and collosal work...the Soviet Union became a nuclear state in a very short time," he told the group gathered around Sudoplatov's flower-strewn open coffin.Sudoplatov saw both sides of
17421 the brutal world of the Soviet secret services. 17421 15-year jail term as the work of evil careerists."He loved people, he loved his department, he was noble and cultured and loved his work," said one elderly man. Asked his name, he covered his hand with his mouth. "Colonel Viktor Glazunov. He and I worked a lot together," he muttered
17421 quietly.Glazunov said Sudoplatov was a charming and firm but fair man who never raised his voice. He was also a great one for secrecy. "He always told us not to greet each other if there was someone else there who we did not know. We just walked past".A former World
17421 War Two partisan from Belarus said that for a long time she knew Sudoplatov only as "Comrade Andrei".Sudoplatov's autobiography, just published in Russian, caused a storm when it came out in English two years ago.Many scientists and historians disputed his claim that Robert Oppenheimer -- the "father" of the U.S.
17421 atomic bomb -- and his fellow scientists had leaked nuclear secrets to Moscow, allowing the Soviet Union to develop nuclear weapons.Russia's spy chiefs, breaking their traditional silence, said there had been no direct handover of data from the scientists. 17421 not agents but sources of information.In 1953, after 32 years in the Soviet secret services, Sudoplatov was taken from his office on the seventh floor of the KGB headquarters and locked up in the basement as prisoner number eight. He was not officially rehabilitated until 1992.The cover of his autobiography
17421 refers to him as "the Soviet Union's main diversionary and terrorist" but Sudoplatov said the interview, with the Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily, that he did not consider himself a terrorist.Foreign intelligence spokeswoman Tatyana Samolis said you could not blame Sudoplatov without asking whether you yourself would have had the courage and
17421 will to oppose the Soviet system."He was a man of his times, when any task set from above was zealously fulfilled and it was not done to think about...the value of human life at all," she told Itar-Tass news agency.Alexander Minkin, a leading investigative journalist working for the popular Moskovsky
17421 Komsomolets daily, said he had got to know Sudoplatov over the past three years and had seen documents relating to the theft of the atom bomb technology."I think the medals he won for his work during the war -- although not for killing Trotsky or the Ukrainian nationalists -- should
17421 be returned to his family," he said."I feel ashamed that today's authorities are not showing their respects here," he said, adding that the current intelligence agents were not a patch on Sudoplatov. "Maybe they are ashamed too."</

17455 Imre Nagy's government, Khrushchev was still exploring ways of recognising Nagy's leadership.The evidence appears as Hungarians prepare to mark the 40th anniversary next month of the uprising against Stalinism which was suppressed by Soviet tanks after 12 days.Around 25,000 people are estimated to have died in the fighting, a peak
17455 of Cold War hostility.Vitaly Afiani, deputy director of the archives of the Soviet Communist Party central committee, said the documents consisted mainly of notes of unminuted meetings of the former Soviet Union's ruling Politburo. They were taken by Vladimir Malin, head of the chancellery of the central committee.The sessions were
17455 held between the outbreak of the uprising on October 23 and the Soviet invasion beginning on November 2."The Malin notes show (Politburo) sessions were held continuously on the Hungarian question in an agitated way," Afiani told Reuters. "The majority of the presidium was in favour of the Nagy government and
17455 even discussed the possibility of the withdrawal of troops."According to Afiani, Khrushchev saw Nagy, a reform communist, as someone who would work within the Communist system. He was also influenced by the Suez crisis following Egyptian president Gamal Abdul Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal.Britain and France were preparing to
17455 invade Egypt to take the canal back and Khrushchev did not want the Soviet Union to be accused of similar "imperialistic" behaviour.However, Afiani's evidence shows how the picture had dramatically changed by the morning of October 31 following the British and French invasion and crucial consultations the night before with
17455 the Chinese delegation, which included current Chinese leader Deng Xiao Ping."Khrushchev opened the morning session by saying the presidium had to fundamentally revise the condition it took the day before," Afiani said. "He expressed the view that if troops pulled out of Hungary that would 'cheer up the imperialists', the
17455 British, French and the Americans."Jian Chen, who left communist China in the 1980s to become a leading Cold War scholar in the United States, on Friday presented new evidence from Deng's interpreter in Moscow and the then Chinese leader Mao Zedong's political secretary."We already knew China pushed the Soviet Union
17455 to take a harsh attitude," Chen told Reuters. "Now we see the contrast with their attitude to Poland, where they warned against Moscow's intervention."Khrushchev had allowed Poland to replace its Stalinist government with a reform communist leadership but was now considering invading the country to end reforms, a move which
17455 China opposed.However, Chen said reports of communist party members being lynched in Budapest and the general tone of international reporting as communicated to Peking by the Chinese Embassy in Budapest led Mao to conclude the Hungarians were anti-communist rather than just anti-Soviet as the Poles were."On the evening of October
17455 30 Deng and Chinese party vice chairman Liu Shaoqi, told Khrushchev 'You have to do something, you cannot give up Hungary.'"The pressure on Khrushchev was increased by reports of the invasion of Egypt, which Kruschev probably then thought would fall to the West, with Hungary possibly following, Afiani said.In fact
17455 the United States intervened soon afterwards to force the British and French to withdraw.</

17488 Romania took one more step towards a free market system on Friday when a long-awaited over-the-counter (OTC) trading system went on stream to handle shares from the ex-communist country's mass selloff scheme."This is a historic moment, the crowning of the mass privatisation programme which opens a new page in the
17488 practice of market economy," Romanian President Ion Iliescu said, pressing a computer key at a ceremony to launch the system.The RASDAQ system, modelled on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange and developed under a $21 million capital market project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development, will undergo 30 days of
17488 testing. Actual trading will start by end-October."During this testing period orders will be collected and stocks to enter trading on this market will be taken from a pre-selected batch of around 150 companies," said Septimiu Stoica, president of the RASDAQ SRL administration board.The RASDAQ is expected to eventually trade shares
17488 in some 5,000 medium-sized companies, most of them privatised under the mass selloff, through 74 dealers and brokers and some 300 work stations across the country.Under an ambitious scheme launched in October 1995, 17 million Romanians were invited to swap coupons for around 600 million shares in some 4,000 state
17488 companies. The process ended in March with a subscription percentage of around 90 percent.The OTC market, which missed two previous deadlines due to poor infrastructure and problems in creating a share registry, is expected to break the hold the state still has on industry and to attract much-needed foreign investment.Stock
17488 brokers say the OTC system is a needed addition to the capital market as the young Bucharest bourse lost stamina over the last few months and only trades 13 stocks.The OTC is also hailed by Romania's 12 investment funds which say the OTC market gives fund managers the investment tools
17488 they need to develop."This (the OTC system) is a clear signal that economic reform is progressing at an accelerated pace," Finance Minister Florin Georgescu told Reuters Television at Monday's ceremony. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264</

17526 Russian utilities may become a growth area of the country's economy, but crippling power strikes in the Far East show the stark limits of their success.Strikes by power workers demanding back pay have spread through the Far East from the eastern port of Vladivostok to the volcanic Kamchatka peninsula and
17526 up to Siberia's frosty Yakutia region. Workers further west may join the action soon."If we don't get emergency help from the federal government...then winter is going to freeze the region," one strike leader said earlier this month.But the power sector is still favoured by foreign investors. Stock prices, led by
17526 Moscow utility Mosenergo, rose more than threefold ahead of the June presidential election."The electricity sector in Russia...is obviously headed for strong revenue growth and earnings growth on top of that," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell research chief Jim Nail. He expected utility revenues to soar 75 percent in three to five
17526 years.The question is why investors are looking so favourably at a sector with huge debts and a legacy of crippling government restrictions -- including orders banning firms from cutting off key suppliers in industry and the military."It is a vicious circle -- utilities are owed billions and billions of dollars
17526 by their customers and they owe billions and billions of dollars back to their suppliers, the government, and their employees," said Nail.Vladimir Konovalov, chief economist at the World Bank in Moscow, said low domestic prices were partly to blame for the crisis."Local energy regulators have tried to keep prices down
17526 for consumers and have shot themselves in the foot," he said.Power stations are an obvious example of an acute cash flow problem hitting Russian industry, where firms often barter for supplies and pay workers in kind.United City Bank energy analyst Natalya Ivanova estimated Russian firms pay only 15-20 percent of
17526 their power bills in cash.She said one Siberian timber plant pays for power in a barter scheme which involved 20 companies, beginning with timber shipments to a paper maker and ending with deliveries of cars and trucks to the timber plant's electricity supplier.Firms without cash pay workers in with the
17526 goods they make -- with refrigerators at a refrigerator factory, for example.But power plants have nothing to barter."A power plant cannot pay wages with its own products, unlike companies which produce consumer goods," said Ivanova.A 1995 presidential decree -- now expired -- made it illegal for utilities to cut off
17526 supplies to important consumers, such as municipalities and the defence sector.But with workers across Russia owed 36 trillion roubles ($6.7 billion) in back wages at the end of August some firms fear strikes will spread before the economy can right itself."We will have a very big problem in Russia," said
17526 Oleg Deripaska, chief executive of Russia's third largest aluminium smelter, Sayansk Aluminium. "Strikes will happen more often."Perched on Siberia's rolling steppe in the middle of the vast country, Deripaska said Sayansk had advanced $1 million in mid-September to the local hydroelectric utility, which other customers had not paid, to end
17526 a week-long strike."A lot of workers saw they got results -- they made a show and they got money," said a worried Deripaska. Workers at the power station then sent a note of solidarity to strikers in the Far East.Ivanova said conditions could be ripe for strikes at 10 of
17526 Russia's 89 regional utilities, including Samarenergo, located some 900 km (560 miles) southeast of Moscow.But economists said Russian industry was unlikely to face a country-wide strike, in part because the authorities are ready to allow local power firms more independence and give utilities the possibility of generating profit.Morgan Grenfell's Nail
17526 said utilities would probably shed jobs and increase rates for some household consumers, who pay 10 percent of the average cost of electricity in western Europe.These measures should improve the wage picture for workers, but would make life even more difficult for ordinary Russians."The payment problem is temporary," Nail said.
17526 "The power companies will muddle by." He said Mosenergo's collection rate rose to 78 percent recently from about 55 percent last year.The World Bank's Konovalov said the government was unlikely to cave in to industry and local government subsidy demands."In the old days you could force a subsidy from Moscow
17526 to get out of such a predicament, but Moscow doesn't have the money any more," he said.</
17527 The often-praised Czech economy may be starting to show cracks from the pressure of an economic slowdown, a rising trade deficit and problems in the capital market that continue to drive investors away.Over the years, economists have hailed Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his policies which have produced one of
17527 the lowest inflation rates in the region, good GDP growth and an unemployment rate of about three percent.Many of those same analysts are now saying that while the economy is not yet in serious trouble, it is showing signs of wear and tear brought about by inefficiencies and shortfalls in
17527 its restructuring."For all the Thatcherite rhetoric, the Klaus government has not exposed the economy to unfettered market forces," Merrill Lynch said in a September investor report."Compared to other Central European nations, the Czech Republic has proved dilatory in restructuring enterprises in order to improve efficiency," the report added.Two years ago,
17527 Klaus boated that while some ex-communist neighbours were trying to avoid drastic economic surgery, the Czech Republic was already out of the operating theatre and in the fitness centre, building up muscle.Since 1992 the economy has moved from recession to 4.8 percent consumption-driven real growth in 1995, as inflation fell
17527 from double digits to below nine percent.Unemployment remains around three percent, and official statistics say nearly 70 percent of the economy is made by companies in, at least nominally, private hands.Czechs, for the most part, are fully employed, buying truckloads of western goods, and living in incredibly cheap state-controlled housing.ANALYSTS
17527 WARNINGSBut analysts, following the Klaus analogy, say there are signs the patient may have fooled the doctor into thinking its wounds had healed.Last week the Czech Statistical Bureau released figures showing gross domestic product growth slowed in the second quarter, sending some disappointed analysts scrambling to revise their full year
17527 forecasts downward.Real economic growth for the second quarter slowed to 4.0 percent year-on-year from 4.6 percent in the first quarter."The preliminary GDP growth (of 4.0 percent) as reported for the second quarter by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) last week was significantly lower than we expected," said Martin Kupka of
17527 Patria Finance.This week Patria revised its full year GDP forecast downward by one percentage point to 4.5 percent, while the CSU forecast remains at 5.1 percent.GOVERNMENT SHOULD DO MORE TO BOOST EXPORTSAnalysts say responsibility for the downturn could be be attributed partly to the sluggish performance of many of the
17527 Czech Republic's major trading partners in the European Union and some said the government should do more to boost exports.Despite signs the climb in imports is levelling out, the rapidly-growing trade deficit continues to spook many analysts and is at the heart of a troubling current account deficit.The first half
17527 current account deficit widened to $1.7 billion from $722.5 million in first half of 1995. In rapidly increasing numbers, Czechs are buying foreign goods for their factories and also their garages and living rooms.The trade deficit ballooned to a record 100.9 billion Czech crowns ($3.74 billion) for the January-August period,
17527 up from 59.5 billion for the same period last year.Klaus, who has said until now that the trade deficit merely reflected the cost of a necessary modernisation of Czech industry, has called a meeting of ministers and officials on October 8 to tackle the problem.Meanwhile, the capital account surplus --
17527 which had previously covered a huge inflow of imports during the Czech economic transformation -- plummeted in the first half to $800.8 million from $3.1 billion for the period last year.Josef Poeschl, a Czech specialist at the Vienna Institute for Comparative Economic Studies (WIIW), says a huge jump in the
17527 current account deficit beyond 1995's four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) could seriously damage confidence."The government has two alternatives: to accept a devaluation which I do not think would be a catastrophe. The other choice concerns the trade deficit, where they could slow imports by implementing an import surcharge,"
17527 he said."If the current account deficit gets to be around six or seven percent of GDP, it can be dangerous."Merrill Lynch said: "Exports need to be stimulated if the foundations for stable and sustained growth are to be established, and if the currency is to be preserved at current levels
17527 over the longer term."STABLE CROWN CORNERSTONE OF ECONOMIC REFORMA stable crown has been one of the cornerstones of Klaus's economic reforms.This has made the crown a target for speculators who have found the combination of stability and real interest rate differentials against western currencies of around seven percent irresistable, pushing
17527 it to record highs.That stability may be in jeopardy, with analysts pointing to a recent banking crisis that has exposed problems in capital market regulation, and weakened the crown by some three percent against the dollar in less than a week.In August, the Czech National Bank rescinded Kreditni Banka's licence
17527 after it ran up losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns following a series of non-performing loans and debt swaps.Later it put Agrobanka, the fifth largest Czech bank, under forced administration, saying it had become illiquid partly due to its ties to Kreditni and investment group Motoinvest.Investors have long complained
17527 about transparency problems in the Czech markets, with many choosing the smaller Polish and Hungarian markets where legislation is more developed."Clearly there are problems in the Czech banking system," said Jan Vanous, director of economic analysis firm PlanEcon."It's a problem of what I would call morally unsuitable investors from Czech
17527 financial institutions that should never have been allowed to either set up a bank, or become a major shareholder in one," he said, without naming names.Vanous said the current system, set up in large part by Klaus as finance minister in the former Czechoslovakia, has created a circle of ownership
17527 that is stalling badly-needed restructuring at many firms and is hindering economic output."We have a set-up where the state controls the banks, the banks control the investment companies, and investment companies control the enterprises -- It's one cosy set up."What we need is to achieve some clear separation from the
17527 state, particularly the financial sector, and then put pressure on the banks to make money instead of being instruments of state policy. This would do a lot to help repair the economy." ($1=26.96 Czech Crown)</

17530 One question is going to dominate Brazilian politics in the coming months -- will President Fernando Henrique Cardoso emulate his Argentine and Peruvian counterparts and win a chance for a second term?Cardoso's dream of being the first Brazilian president ever to be re-elected was Brasilia's worst kept secret until he
17530 confirmed recently that he wants to be Brazil's first reelected president. "I am in favour of re-election as an idea and if the constitution were to be rewritten I think I should have the right to stand," he said in a newspaper interview.With high personal approval ratings and the "Real
17530 Plan," which stopped raging inflation, still popular, he would be hard to beat in 1998. But he is barred from re-election by the constitution, which restricts holders of executive office -- presidents, governors and mayors -- to one term.Hardly a day goes by without a soap opera actress, an Olympic
17530 athlete or a visiting head of state emerging from the presidential office to tell reporters how wonderful four more Cardoso years would be. Government ministers and markets are also arguing ever more fervently that Brazil needs the continuity of another Cardoso term to build on newfound economic stability begun in
17530 July 1994 with the Real Plan.The plan, dreamed up by Cardoso when he was finance minister in the government of President Itamar Franco, introduced a new currency, the real, which was tied loosely to the dollar, and did away with automatic, monthly wage and price increases that for years had
17530 fuelled inflation. As a result, inflation has fallen to below 0.5 percent a month, down from an annualized 5,000 percent in June 1994.Cardoso, if he remains in office until 2002, would seek to deepen his government reforms, which have been modest so far, dismantle Brazil's restrictive labour laws, improve its
17530 crumbling roads, ports and railways, and press ahead with regional and global trade agreements, analysts say."There can be no economic stability without political stability," said parliamentary deputy Jose Mendonca Filho, whose bill to rewrite the constitution and allow re-election has been gathering dust in Congress for a year and a
17530 half.Committee-level debate is expected to begin in mid-October and government whips are rolling up their sleeves for what is likely to prove the Cardoso administration's biggest challenge to date in the volatile Chamber of Deputies."There's nothing on the agenda other than re-election. 17530 for now," said Dora Kramer, the doyenne of Brasilia's political columnists.Rewriting the constitution is no easy task. 17538 a six-year term in 1994.Arriagada will be replaced by Juan Villarzu, the president of state copper company Codelco and a leader of Frei's Christian Democratic party.There was no official word on Arriagada's future but officials have said privately he was tipped to be the next ambassador to the United States.
17538 Arriagada, Frei's top political adviser, had taken criticism for a series of missteps since Frei took office, including the defeat in Congress of constitutional reforms aimed at curbing the military's power. 17538 Budget Chief Jose Pablo Arellano, who only an hour before the reshuffle had held a news conference to announce the government's 1997 budget. Arellano is a well-known economist. 17538 sought a younger image for his government.Agriculture Minister Emiliano Ortega was replaced by chief trade negotiator Carlos Mladinic and Transport and Communications Minister Narciso Irureta was replaced by his number two, Transport Secretary Claudio Hohmann.Planning Minister Luis Maira was replaced by economist Roberto Pizarro. 17563 The most telling sign that retailer Organizacion Soriana SA's traditional grip on northern Mexico may be slipping is an ultra-modern, gigantic supermarket being built here by H.E.B. Grocery Co.The sleek, art deco-style superstore, due to open early next year, is the first foray into Mexico by the Texas-based chain, which
17563 plans eventually to open five stores in the Monterrey area. H.E.B. follows other retailers, local and foreign, who are setting up shop in northern Mexico, where an export boom has created just about the only healthy market of consumers in a country still licking its wounds from the 1994 peso
17563 crash.Mexico's Cifra, the country's biggest retail company, plans to open up a handful superstores within a year as part of its joint venture with U.S.-based Wal-Mart.And France's Carrefour also is eyeing northern Mexico for places to set up its successful superstores, analysts say. The moves have caused some industry watchers
17563 to wonder whether Soriana will be able to maintain what have been the highest profit margins of any Mexican retailer -- margins that have doubled Soriana's stock price since the start of the year."We know the competition is coming and we are ready for it," Soriana's chief financial officer Javier
17563 Lozano said on Friday during a retail conference here.Until now, the Monterrey-based chain has dominated this area's lonely retail landscape, setting up dozens of single- format hypermarkets. It targets low and middle-income consumers with mostly food items and few high-priced imports. Soriana was one of the few Mexican retailers to
17563 emerge from the devaluation largely unscathed. A mostly cash-only expansion philosophy left the company with little debt, free to grow while other retailers were scaling back.The retailer has opened three new stores this year and plans on two more, bringing its total to 61 outlets. It wants to open seven
17563 new stores next year, and possibly more the year after depending on cash flow, Lozano said.Despite expansion, the company has managed to reduce its total debt further, from 185 million pesos at the start of the year to a current 72 million pesos. Lozano admitted competition is likely to squeeze
17563 the company's margins. And he said he expects little help from the Mexican economy in helping create a bigger pie for all competitors."The recovery for the individual consumer will not happen in the short-run, even in the medium-run. Consumers suffered a serious setback and the recovery will be gradual," Lozano
17563 said.But the company does have several things in its favor, such as its regional focus that allows it to have economies of scale and low distribution costs. Soriana is positioned to take advantage of a weak economy. Northern Mexicans will no longer drive a few hours to the U.S. border
17563 for shopping or buy imports here for at least a few years, two trends that were booming before the devaluation."We offer products that are geared to the (middle and low) economic level -- functional products that aren't necessarily the latest trend but are cheaper than what they can buy in
17563 the United States," Lozano said.The company expects the Mexican consumer to remain wary of credit offered by department stores even after the effects of the devaluation wear off, he said. Industry trends also favor superstores like Soriana and H.E.B. versus traditional outdoor markets or Mom-and-Pop stores."Growth in our stores sales
17563 should more than offset the fall in margins," he said.During September, Soriana has seen overall sales to grow by about 13 percent and same-store sales to rise some 9 percent compared to the same month of 1995, according to Lozano.-- Mexico City newsroom 525 7289565</

17612 Brazil's economy will grow by a modest 2.2 percent in 1997 because of constraints imposed by the country's distorted macroeconomic policy, Salomon Brothers said."A mix of tight monetary policy, a relatively overvalued exchange rate and a lax fiscal stance will keep Brazil's output below potential in 1997, with growth registering
17612 2.2 percent," Lawrence Goodman, head of Salomon's Latin American economic research, said in a report. The Salomon forecast is sharply lower than government projections for 4.0 percent to 5.0 percent growth in gross domestic product next year.Brazil's economy is expected to grow by between 2.5 percent and 3.0 percent this
17612 year.In the report, co-authored by Salomon's Brazil economist Michael Hart, Salomon says Brazil's internal debt will grow next year due to a public sector borrowing requirement in excess of 6.0 percent of gross domestic product.The country is also expected to experience its fourth current account deficit in 1997, it said.The
17612 report forecasts a current account deficit of 3.4 percent of GDP in 1997, up from a projected 1996 shortfall of 2.9 percent of GDP. It adds that the deficit will constrain GDP targets and limit the prospect for futher appreciation of the real currency as a policy tool.The report also
17612 noted that continued fiscal deficits and a measured depreciation of the exchange rate will lead to high real lending rates.-- John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 232-4411</

17614 Facing a heavy debt repayment schedule over the next couple of years, Mexico will be juggling a number of pressing demands for its cash, experts say.With obligations to the U.S. Treasury, the International Monetary Fund and other organizations, and market debt coming due, Mexico will have to refinance or renegotiate
17614 a large amount of debt in the next few years. On top of that are efforts by the federal government to buy back Brady bonds, an effort that some economists say could continue. "They (the federal government) have debt falling due. They have obligations to pay back. They would like
17614 to pay back money to the U.S. government and the IMF as quickly as possible to get rid of that liability," said ING Barings economist Arturo Porzecanski."I really think that their priority will be to repay the U.S. Treasury and the IMF in an anticipated manner," he said.Santander Investment estimates
17614 that public sector and central bank debt amortizations in 1997 will total $9.88 billion, and $13.65 billion in 1998, before rising to $15.27 billion in 1999, then falling to $10.69 billion in 2000. Much of that debt, however, is owed to the IMF or other multilateral organizations, which the Mexican
17614 government believes it can pay back from international reserves, from financing in international debt markets or by trying to negotiate an extension of what it owes to the IMF."We are not overly concerned. A large portion of that debt is non-market," said Santander Investment economist Hector Chavez. "The refinancing strategy
17614 to date has been adequate, but obviously with 1997 coming and additional payments the government has to think about using favourable international conditions to meet its obligations," Chavez said.Santander estimates that Mexico's market debt service from 1997 to 2000 will be $15.0 billion, while non-market, such as to the IMF,
17614 the U.S. Treasury, and other organizations, will be about $35.0 billion.Mexico's recent debt placements have been for the most part warmly received in markets. It bought back a nominal $1.24 billion worth of discount Brady bonds, replacing them with proceeds from a $1.0 billion 20-year issue earlier this month. That
17614 followed an earlier placement in May of a $1.75 billion 30-year bond in another Brady bond swap.But it has also been using money from debt placement to repay the U.S. and the IMF money they lent during the peso crisis in 1995. In July, Mexico placed $6.0 billion of floating-rate
17614 bank notes and used collateral freed in the 30-year bond swap and some other operations to pay back $7.0 billion owed to the U.S. Treasury.The Mexican government also paid back the IMF $1.0 billion with proceeds from the placement of a $920 million Samurai bond issue in June. As well
17614 as paying back more of what it owes to the IMF, Mexico could also try to buy back more of its outstanding Brady bonds, aiming to tighten the spread on its debt and lessen the high servicing costs of the repayments it will have to make over the next two
17614 years, economists said.The discount Brady bonds, besides tieing up collateral, may also soon have to pay a premium depending on the price of oil, for their so-called value recovery rights."For the collateral that is tied up, the spread is too wide and so they are going to buy them back
17614 as much as possible and get the spread down," said Lehman Brothers senior economist Darryl McLeod."It (buying the Bradies back) lowers the cost of borrowing for the money that they are going to need to borrow to pay back to the IMF, and to the Treasury," added McLeod.Sentiment on Mexico
17614 has improved since the economic crash.Standard &amp; Poor's, for example, recently raised the outlook on Mexico to stable from negative.-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559</

17631 Clarke, will be agreed in Washington."I am not expecting that we will get down to details of...how much gold will be sold and when," Clarke said.The ministers said they realised it was important for developing countries to get their own economic house in order as well as seeking help outside.But

17645 The capture of Kabul on Friday by Afghanistan's Taleban militia crowns a series of stunning successes that has transformed a band of Islamic student vigilantes into overwhelming victors.About two years after it was formed as a movement of theology students in the southern province of Kandahar, the Taleban has now
17645 proclaimed itself the new rulers of the war-shattered country.As the warriors took over a ruined capital, they hanged a former president and his brother and proclaimed the complete enforcement of Islam on the country.The Taleban, which in Pashtu language means "seekers", or "students", burst on to the Afghan scene in
17645 October 1994 after it was founded by Mullah Muhammad Omar, a one-eyed former guerrilla fighter wounded several times in battles in the guerrilla war against Soviet occupation in the 1980s.Little is known of Omar, who, according to news reports, returned to religious studies after 1989 when the Soviet forces left
17645 Afghanistan. He is in his 30s.Riding a wave of revulsion against local warlords and general weariness over the country's civil war, he and other religious students formed the Taleban and battled Mujahideen guerrilla commanders who had preyed on traders at checkposts in the southern province of Kandahar.Their ranks grew rapidly.
17645 Despite military setbacks in 1995, they proved more united and better disciplined than the faction-ridden government and rival guerrilla groups.Few believed in 1994 that the group had the muscle to challenge the main mujahideen factions hardened by years of guerrilla war against Soviet occupation.Many of its recruits were said to
17645 be Afghan refugees attending Islamic Madrassahs, or schools, in Pakistan's border provinces of North West Frontier and Baluchistan, a factor that apparently led to suspicions that Pakistan backed the movement.The suspicions increased in November 1994 when Taleban rescued a 30-truck trade caravan which Pakistan had sent to open a trade
17645 route to Central Asia but was blocked by a guerrilla group. 17645 Herat, capital of the province of the same name bordering Iran.This also raised fears in Shi'ite Moslem Iran of the rise of the Sunni Moslem Taleban in view of the traditional rivalry between Islam's two main sects.Pakistan has repeatedly denied it is pro-Taleban, saying it has no favourites among the
17645 Afghan factions.The Taleban has remained a secretive organisation, revealing little of its structure or political ambitions. According to news reports out of Afghanistan, its fundamentalism has not always proven popular.Banning television sets, closing girls' schools and forcing women to cover their faces, the movement has not always gone down well
17645 in areas under its control.But for the most part, Taleban administration apparently has been relatively efficient, free of the corruption and interference common under other factions, and allowing modest commerce to be revived.How Afghanistan as a whole would thrive under Taleban rule is less certain.Within hours of taking over Kabul,
17645 the militia hanged former president Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai from a concrete traffic-control post at the gates of the presidential palace.The movement also announced that an interim, six-man ruling council would now run the country.A declaration issued by Omar and quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP)
17645 news service named his deputy, Mullah Mohammad Rabbani (no relation of the Afghan president) to head the council.According to Jane's Defence Weekly last year, the movement's central leadership, or shura, is composed of eight members, of whom Omar, Mohammad Rabbani, Borjan and Mohammad Abbas are the key players.Mohammad Rabbani was
17645 named governor of the newly captured Nangarhar earlier this month.Little is known of the others, except most appear to share the background of being born in Kandahar, fighting the Soviet occupation and returning to their religious studies after the Soviet withdrawal in 1989.</

17654 and political problems...," he said."And it is generally believed that a multi-party coalition government could lead to conflicts and political problems," he added."I therefore see it appropriate to dissolve the house so as to return the important mandate of political determination to the people at this turning point," he added.Banharn
17654 vowed to be an honest caretaker prime minister and said he would supervise a new election fairly.The premier had agreed to quit last Saturday in return for support from his allies at a no-confidence vote against him in parliament. Banharn later won the vote with their support, but he was
17654 embarrassed and effectively lost hold of his job.Coalition leaders had been meeting frequently since last Saturday to try to find a replacement for Banharn.Banharn avoided their meetings and kept them in suspense. 17661 Taxi drivers in the Chinese city Qingdao went on strike to protest against a new government levy, the latest in a series of rare cases of industrial action, drivers and officials said on Friday.Cab operators in Qingdao city, in northern China's Shandong province, kerbed their cars on Tuesday and Wednesday
17661 to show their anger at a 10,000 ($1,200) yuan levy recently announced by the city government, they said."We went on strike for two days," said one driver. "Everyone is angry at the fee... it's too much."The unofficial action was led by staff at some of Qingdao's largest taxi companies and
17661 was backed by almost all the city's cab operators, said the driver, who did not want to be identified.The stoppage followed similar action by dissatisfied drivers in cities across northern China, including the port city of Tianjin and the Shandong provincial capital of Jinan, he said.Industrial action is rare in
17661 China, where all labour unions are controlled by the ruling Communist Party and breaches of worker discipline are quickly quelled.Controls on industrial action did not apply to taxis, which although officially registered with cab companies, could just simply leave the road to make their point, the driver said."It isn't like
17661 a factory going on strike... we just stay at home. There's nothing they can do," he said.City officials dismissed the action as poorly organised, weakly suported and unlikely to change municipal policy."I don't think there is any chance of this rule being changed," said one official. "This is not a
17661 real action, it's just some people stopping driving."It's not a strike. A strike is illegal," said the official who declined to be identified.A surplus of taxis in Qingdao, a former German-run concession blessed with golden beaches and a temperate climate, forced the city to auction new licences for would-be drivers
17661 for around 100,000 yuan, he said.With new drivers paying such a hefty fee, the levy on existing drivers was very reasonable, he said. The levy is believed to be a one-off payment although it possibly could be once every several years.Some drivers continued to operate during the stoppage, sometimes sticking
17661 to suburban roads out of fear of attack from striking colleagues in the city centre, but residents said the strike appeared remarkably solid."You couldn't see a taxi anywhere," said a shop attendant at the city airport. "It seemed 100 percent."The action appeared inspired at least partly by the success of
17661 their colleagues in Jinan city, where thousands of taxi drivers earlier this month ended a three-day work stoppage after the municipal government met protesters and agreed to lower fees.While some Qingdao drivers joked about holding public demonstrations to back their protest against the new levy, one driver said such talk
17661 could never turn to action."Nobody dares demonstrate. People get detained when they demonstrate," he said.</

17672 was worthwhile, but if he died in Japanese waters it is sad, and shame on the Chinese government," said activist Wong Wai-ming.Chan, 45, died when he jumped into the sea from a rusty protest ship on Thursday in a last act of defiance over Japan's rule of what it calls
17672 the Senkaku Islands. Both China and Taiwan also claim the islands, which they call the Diaoyus.At stake is a cluster of uninhabited rocky outcrops. They have kindled fiery passions among the Chinese since Japanese extremists built a lighthouse and planted flags there in July.Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the
17672 islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.Tokyo's claim dates to 1895 when it defeated China and seized Taiwan and other islands. China has claimed the disputed islets for centuries. The British colony of Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule next year.Also Friday,
17672 the distressed skipper of the protest tanker Kien Hwa 2 apologised to Chan's family at the airport."I had promised before setting sail for the Diaoyu Islands that I would bring them back safely. I failed. I brought one less person back," said a weeping Ngai Lup-chee.The tragedy shocked Hong Kong's
17672 majority Chinese community and complicated a dilemma facing Beijing and Tokyo, who are anxious not to let the dispute wreck relations.The two Asian powers seemed helpless to tackle the anti-Japan mood. "Do you have any suggestions? We're racking our brains," Japanese government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters in Tokyo.China's mission
17672 in Hong Kong said activists in the territory and in nearby Macau should show restraint."The Chinese government sympathises with activities that are being conducted in Hong Kong to protect the Diaoyus...but it hopes these activities in Hong Kong and Macau can be conducted in a rational manner," he told Reuters."The
17672 Chinese government advocates settling this conflict peacefully through diplomatic channels," he said.Nozomu Akizuki, a professor at Tokai University near Tokyo, said there was no solution at present. "A rash action would merely add fuel to the flames. The best thing to do is to remain silent," he said.Activists in Taiwan,
17672 considered a renegade province by Beijing, said a protest flotilla of more than 20 boats would sail to the disputed islands on October 6.Hong Kong groups plan a candlelight vigil to mourn Chan on Sunday.On a visit to Australia, Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan urged protesters not to jeopardise
17672 relations with Tokyo."I understand the depth of feeling but I hope that views will be expressed in a calm manner without affecting the relationship between ourselves and Japan," she said.At least six organisations have sprouted in Hong Kong in recent weeks in a wave of nationalistic fervour.Small protest groups gathered
17672 outside Japan's consulate shouting "down with Japanese militarism" and handed in petitions to consular staff on Friday urging Japan to quit the islands.</
17673 China's contracted foreign funds totalled $53.52 billion in January-July, an increase of 35.2 percent compared with the same period last year, the China Information said on Friday.Direct foreign investment reached $48.52 billion during the first seven months, up 31.7 percent over the year-ago period, the newspaper quoted figures from the
17673 State Statistical Bureau as showing.Actual foreign funds used rose four percent in the period to $26.81 billion, the newspaper said.Foreign loans totalled $4.78 billion, a rise of 100 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.Contracted funds for solely foreign-invested projects jumped 55.1 percent to $18.44 billion while funds for
17673 joint ventures rose 35.2 percent year-on-year, it said.Investment in cooperative projects slipped by 8.6 percent, it said without giving further details.The report attributed the rises in part to Beijing's efforts to attract more investment to primary and secondary industries.Contracted foreign funds in those industries in the first six months of
17673 the year had accounted for 77.7 percent of total foreign investment in the period, up by 15.7 percentage points compared with the same period in 1995, it said.Overseas investors had poured more funds into more remote and backward western and central areas, with investment in those areas growing at more
17673 than 50 percent in the first half, it said.</
17674 Thailand's outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa will dissolve parlaiment and call a snap election on November 17, Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej said on Friday.The surprise decision, conveyed by Samak, a close ally of the premier, angered some coalition partners who had expected Banharn to name a successor and leave the
17674 coalition intact.Samak told reporters that Banharn, who leads a six-party coalition government that controls 209 of the 391 seats in parliament, would make an announcement later.Samak said Banharn had decided to dissolve the house because there was no full agreement among members of his coalition on the choice of a
17674 replacement.Banharn last Saturday was forced by his allies to declare he would quit within seven days, and had kept the nation and his coalition allies in the dark over his replacement for six days."There was a deadlock on the choice (of a new prime minister)," Samak said after coalition leaders
17674 met with Banharn.The announcement shocked supporters of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, leader of the New Aspiration Party, the second largest party in the coalition. Chavalit had been seen as front-runner for the premiership.But Chavalit failed to get the nomination after losing support from key members of Banharn's core Chart Thai
17674 party, which has 91 seats, coalition sources said.There was no immediate comment from Chavalit."It (the decision) surprised me because he had promised that he would not dissolve the house," said Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan, who is also in charge of economic affairs in the administration.Another coalition leader, Chalerm Yoobumroong, who
17674 heads the small Muon Chon party, said Banharn made the decision without consulting coalition partners."He solely made the decision, so he has to explain to the people why he did not keep his word," he said.A royal proclamation on holding a fresh election was expected later, government sources said.</

17676 (NLD) party to coincide with discussions of a sanctions bill against Burma in the U.S. Congress."The United States Embassy coordinated with the NLD for more than one month to organise this meeting so it coincided with discussions of the Cohen ammendment in Congress," a senior Burmese official told Reuters.A U.S.
17676 government official dismissed the accusation as "ridiculous," and said the United States had no control over the actions of Suu Kyi or her party.Suu Kyi, who was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995, had called a party congress for Friday through Sunday to celebrate the NLD's
17676 eighth anniversary. The group was formed in August 1988 following months of unprecedented protests against military rule that left thousands dead or imprisoned.The U.S. Congress, due to adjourn on Friday, has yet to vote on the 1997 Foreign Operations Appropriations bill, which includes the Cohen amendment on Burma.The amendment urges
17676 Burma's military government to improve its human rights record and says the United States will not offer Burma assistance except for humanitarian or anti-narcotics aid. It is supported by the Clinton administration and welcomed by Nobel Peace laureate Suu Kyi.The measure also allows the president to prohibit U.S. investment in
17676 Burma if Suu Kyi is rearrested or exiled, or if there is large-scale repression of the opposition.U.S. officials expect the bill to be approved by both the House and the Senate and to be signed into law by Clinton.On Friday, Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) detained
17676 many NLD members planning to attend the congress, the Burmese official said without giving numbers.Security police also set up roadblocks and checkpoints to block off University Avenue in front of Suu Kyi's home, where the congress was to be held. No one was allowed to go near the house although
17676 the official said Suu Kyi was not being detained.The official said the SLORC blocked the street and detained the NLD members because the party did not receive permission to hold the meeting, and because the NLD was working with Western governments like the United States to destabilise Burma.Burmese officials said
17676 U.S. charge d'affairs Marilyn Meyers had met government officials earlier in the week to urge them not to prevent the NLD from holding the meeting.A U.S. Embassy spokesman confirmed that Meyers had met officials from the Foreign Ministry, but did not say what they discussed.The NLD won a landslide victory
17676 in the 1990 general election but was never allowed to take power because the SLORC refused to recognise the results of the poll.</
