17680 Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen said on Friday the breakaway Khmer Rouge faction would have to drop its plan to govern its own separate state or face possible arrest.Khmer Rouge dissident leader Ieng Sary would be in violation of the constitution if he tried to create a state-within-a-state around his former
17680 bases along the Thai border, Hun Sen told graduating students at Phnom Penh University."The separatists cannot be a third force and cannot be self-governing," he said. "If any place continues making a state-within-a-state and does not merge forces, we will use force to suppress this and we will arrest and
17680 try them."We give them a choice. They can face both the government and the Khmer Rouge hardliners or they can agree to merge forces immediately, receiving salaries for their soldiers and letting the government enter their areas."Ieng Sary, foreign minister for the Khmer Rouge during its brutal 1975-79 regime, and
17680 commanders of Khmer Rouge divisions broke with the mainstream of the guerrilla faction last month.They have asked that their Pailin stronghold remain under their control as the centre of a new province in the northwest.Hun Sen said the breakaway troops must merge their forces with the Cambodian military immediately and
17680 unconditionally."Today the decision of the royal government (is being delivered via northwest) Battambang province to all commanders of the Khmer Rouge separatists to merge forces and territory as soon as possible, without delay and without conditions," he said.First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh took a more conciliatory tone toward the
17680 dissident rebels on Friday, indicating that their two most senior commanders, Sok Peap and Ei Chien, could be given senior, regional-level military posts.Ieng Sary's commanders had asked for top central command posts in the army and military."I think that we will appoint at least Sok Peap, Ei Chien as the
17680 deputy commanders of the military region... It is very necessary, otherwise we cannot move forward," said the prince.King Norodom Sihanouk on September 14 granted an amnesty to Ieng Sary, who was sentenced to death in absentia with Pol Pot for their role in the genocide of more than one million
17680 people during the late 1970s. Merger began a few days later.Hun Sen said Ieng Sary had accepted the authority of the constitution and the law by asking for a royal amnesty, so he had no right to make decisions about appointments or territory.The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-brokered peace accord
17680 with their rivals in 1991 but later reneged on the pact and have been fighting the coalition government that emerged from general elections in 1991.</

17683 The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) on Friday released a list of 50 approved stocks permitted to be sold short.Short selling of securities will be allowed starting on Monday. Under the practice, an investor sells securities he does not own in the hope of replacing them at lower prices.The number
17683 of stocks approved is higher than the 20-30 stocks that the exchange earlier indicated would be on the list. Because of strict criteria, market regulators had indicated that only the strongest capitalised, most liquid stocks would be short-sale candidates.The criteria for approval included an average daily market capitalisation of over
17683 2 billion ringgit for the past three months, at least 100 million shares in public float, at least 2,000 registered shareholders, five years uninterrupted after-tax profit record and average monthly share volume trade of more than two million shares for the past 12 calendar months.Just about all the top 20
17683 biggest capitalised companies in Malaysia made the list, with the notable exceptions of Malaysia International Shipping Corp Bhd (MISC), Rothmans of Pall Mall (Malaysia) Bhd, which is the subsidiary of the U.K. tobacco concern; container shipping concern PDZ Holdings Bhd and car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd.Otherwise, the list encompasses
17683 the biggest names in Malaysia's stock market including national airline Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS), as well as giant telephone utility Telekom Malaysia Bhd and state-controlled electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd.Banks and financial services firms formed the biggest contingent on the list, with 13 representatives.KLSE officials were not available for
17683 queries about the list make-up. The exchange said in a statement that the list was "as agreed by the Securities Commission."Under the KLSE's rules, only stockbrokers which have in-place exchange-approved written guidelines on 'know your customer practices' will be permitted to engage in regulated shortselling.The guidelines include apprising customers of
17683 the risks involved, and making sure the clients can meet their financial commitments.-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603 201 4813)</

17699 growing economic strength.The speakers, including senior diplomats, academics and businessmen, were attending a symposium to mark the 10th anniversary of the centre.Paul Wolfowitz, a former U.S. assistant secretary of state, said China's growing strength made some people think of the bipolar superpower confrontation that existed between the United States and
17699 the former Soviet Union and of a possible return of the Cold War."It would be a terrible tragedy for both countries and the world if that happened," he said.Li Shenzhi, president of the Chinese Association for American Studies, said that the concept of the need to "contain China" was increasingly
17699 common in American thinking, and that this was not helpful to the development of Sino-US relations."All elements of the relationship are negotiable except the Taiwan issue," Li said, referring to China's policy that Taiwan is a renegade province that must be reunited with the mailand. 17699 retreat on that issue."Steve Levine, professor of history at Duke University, said skilful political leadership was needed by both sides of the relationship, which has been dogged by a range of differences including Taiwan, human rights and protection of intellectual property.He said the United States suffered on occasion from what
17699 he called "the arrogance of power," and that China's increasing strength and confidence could be leading it down the same path."There are the early warning signs of the arrogance of power (with the Chinese), for instance in their handling of Taiwan and the South China Sea issue," he said.China claims
17699 a vast area of the South China Sea, despite opposing claims from other countries in the area.Former U.S. ambassador to China Arthur Hummel said one of the fundamental reasons for the strains in Sino-American relations was that China's political reforms had lagged far behind economic development."Evidence of strains caused by

17699 at all, it is very simple. It is at a total standstill," the official said.Asked how the Chinese system should be changed, he said: "I would not dare to answer that. I do not have that much freedom, there is a problem with human rights as you know."But the official

17708 Online Internet guide Yahoo! Inc is looking to Asia for opportunities to expand, and could set up a presence outside Japan within six to 12 months, said chief Jerry Yang on Friday."One of the main reasons I'm here is to understand a little better what opportunities are here...what kind of
17708 activities (Asia's) having on the Internet and who's getting on the Internet and what kind of content is being developed," Yang, a co-founder of Yahoo!, told Reuters in an interview.He said international expansion was key to the U.S.-based company's growth. Yahoo! has joint ventures in Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany,
17708 France and Canada to provide sites tailored for users in those countries.Australia would probably be the next place for Yahoo to enter, but Asia was a high priority, he said."We might want to do something targeted towards the English speaking/reading population, something like a mirror site, basically duplicating what we
17708 have in the States here in a local server, so people can have better access, faster access -- an Asian server," he said.This could happen within six to 12 months. Later Yahoo! would look to providing information in Asian languages, he said."We would try to do what we've done in
17708 other regions, which is to collect information that's specific to this area but also allow them to access the global database," he said.Yahoo also has to figure out how to sell advertising -- which would be its prime revenue generator -- in Asia."Right now the opportunities we believe are really
17708 in the advertising area. The Internet media is very much like other media, such as television and radio," which rely on advertising.An estimated one percent of total U.S. advertising spending, or about US$2.0 billion, would be allocated to the Internet by 2000, he said. Yahoo! had 230 advertisers in June."The
17708 Asian advertising market is a developing market...and we're catching it at the right place," he said. "We can probably get an even higher percentage as...(advertising) budgets increase over time."Yang said Yahoo! identifed itself not as a technology or software firm, but as a media company, which people are gradually viewing
17708 as an information service."From a media standpoint, we are very much differentiated...not just a search and directory, a lot of news, a lot of stock quotes.""Stock quotes alone are now doing more than one million page queries a day," he said.Yahoo! has 1.5 million to 2 million users per day,
17708 and about 300 million pages viewed per month.He said the company's strengths included developing regional content. In the U.S., Yahoo! has launched sites for metropolitan areas like San Francisco and Los Angeles. Yahoo! is also aggressively developing personalised information services."If people always think of Yahoo! when they need to find
17708 information - that's our goal," said Yang.He said in the longer term, the Internet could sustain two to three prominent players who use the same approach of being content providers through branding and advertising."I think we will be among the two or three," he said.</

17715 Boeing Co. said it has developed a cure for cargo smoke detection systems in new Boeing 777 airliners which have been giving false alarms.The manufacturer said in a statement received here that the "fix" will be certified by America's Federal Aviation Administration(FAA) in mid-October and a service bulletin issued to
17715 airlines before a retrofit programme is begun.More than a dozen passengers were injured in June when more than 300 had to make an emergency evacuation from a Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd 777 which had just landed in Hong Kong. The false fire alarm is thought to have been caused by
17715 its belly cargo which included live frogs -- a popular Chinese food.An Emirates 777 had a similar false alarm involving a cargo of mangoes. Both airlines imposed a ban on live or perishable cargo in their aircraft until a solution was found.Boeing said until the problem was solved it had
17715 issued recommendations about cargoes with a high moisture content to other 777 operators.Cargo smoke detection systems which use photoelectric sensors to 'look' for light reflected off air particles have a history of problems with dust and moisture which have caused false alarms in the past, it said.Boeing said it was
17715 difficult during flight testing to replicate the exact environment the aircraft encounters in service -- such as dealing with live frogs and perishables with a high moisture content.In-service problems which often took 12 to 16 months to fix had in this case been cured in 4-1/2 months, it added.--Air Cargo

17785 A prisoner was killed and 18 people injured Friday when a riot broke out at a California maximum security prison and guards opened fire to quell it, officials said.About 100 Hispanic and black prisoners, some armed with home-made knives, started fighting in the exercise yard at California State Prison Sacramento,
17785 said Christine May, a spokeswoman for the California Department of Corrections.The riot at the prison near Folsom, 20 miles east of Sacramento, was quickly brought under control when security guards opened fire on the warring prisoners.After being briefed by Jim Gomez, director of the state Department of Corrections, California Gov.
17785 Pete Wilson said the riot was "evidently a fight between two gangs within the prison.""The gangs are racially organised and this was a fight between the African-American gang and the Latino gang," he told reporters.May said the prisoner who died was shot in the buttocks but it was not yet
17785 known if the bullet caused his death.Marilyn Broddrick, a spokeswoman for the prison, said 14 prisoners were also injured. Eight suffered stab wounds and six suffered gunshot wounds, she said.Most of the wounded were taken by ambulance to the University of California at Davis Medical Centre in Sacramento.Four prison staff
17785 members were also injured and two of them were taken to outside hospitals, Broddrick said.The condition of the injured was not immediately available.Ambulances raced to and from the prison and local television showed bandaged prisoners being unloaded from ambulances at the hospital.Broddrick said prison guards used pepper spray, batons and
17785 fired rubber baton rounds -- larger than rubber bullets -- before opening fire with live rounds when the prisoners continued to fight.About 17 shots were fired, May said.Broddrick said the prison would be locked down -- meaning prisoners would be confined to their cells -- at least through the weekend
17785 while prison officials investigated what caused the clash. May said the prison is overcrowded as are all California prisons. It holds 3,200 prisoners but is
17785 designed for 1,700, she said.</

17788 next Friday when a hearing on whether to set bail would be held.Ntakirutimana has been charged by the U.N. 17788 attack April 16, 1994, in which hundreds of men, women and children were killed.FBI spokesman Mike Appleby said it was likely Ntakirutimana's extradition would be sought, which would require presentation of the evidence against him.Prosecutors told reporters evidence included statements from a Dutch policeman and a prosecutor with the tribunal.Ntakirutimana

17788 about six months. 17788 with unspecified problems of the oesophagus and could die in jail. 17797 be made by the Paris Club of creditor nations to the debt initiative, officials said.G7 finance ministers -- from the United States, Canada, Japan, Germany, France, Italy and Britain -- are hoping to sketch out some of the details of the Paris Club contribution after their meeting here on Saturday.The
17797 IMF appears to have sidestepped for now a row over whether it should sell a small portion of its gold reserves to finance its share of the initiative by agreeing it has enough money for the time being to contribute.As regards the World Bank, Wolfensohn said it was willing to
17797 put some $2 billion forward for the next few years to contribute to the debt programme, reaffirming a commitment made at a G7 summit in Lyon, France in June.But details of the Paris Club's plans to improve debt relief have yet to be announced.The IMF and World Bank had initially
17797 called for the Paris Club to forgive some 90 percent of loans, compared to 67 percent currently available for the world's poorest nations, under so-called Naples terms of debt relief.In reality, Naples terms offer a write-off of much less than that since usually only a part of the debt owed
17797 is covered by any Paris Club agreement ahead of a cut-off date often fixed in the early 1980s.Countries remain obliged to pay debt servicing on loans taken out after that to maintain their creditworthiness.Wolfensohn said the Paris Club improved debt relief would be less than 90 percent, but he was
17797 uncertain by how much."I don't know if it's 80 percent but it certainly not going to be 90 percent," he said.Diplomatic sources said there appeared to be a consensus emerging to offer debt relief of up to 80 percent on a case-by-case basis. Paris Club officials had no comment on
17797 the likely scale of its proposed debt relief.Private development agency Oxfam International slammed the Paris Club for dragging its heels on debt relief."Without a clear commitment from the Paris Club to reduce 90 percent of debt, the viability of the entire initiative could be undermined," the group said in a
17797 statement.According to some estimates, about four or five countries would not be able to put their economies back on even keel and achieve so-called debt sustainability if the Paris Club only extends 80 percent debt relief.</

17800 President Bill Clinton took his confident re-election campaign riding into Texas Friday, looking to take away from Republican Bob Dole a vote-rich state that has not gone to a Democratic presidential candidate in 20 years.At rallies under overcast skies in Fort Worth and Longview, Clinton said his economic policies were
17800 paying dividends for the American people and boasted that he has reduced the size of government far more than his Republican predecessors."If you look at the results of what I said we would do and what we have done and how much better off Texas is today than it was
17800 four years ago, if the people want to give me a fair shot and look to the future, yes I think we can carry Texas, because it's right for the American people," Clinton said.In Fort Worth's Sundance Square, named for a 19th-century outlaw called the Sundance Kid, Clinton's appearance was
17800 preceded by theme songs to old Western movies and even remarks from former House Speaker Jim Wright, a Texan who resigned under an ethical cloud in 1989. Wright attacked the Republican Congress as obstructionist and mean-spirited.Clinton took on a folksy manner, expressing pride in the cowboy hat a supporter gave
17800 him, and telling the crowd it was OK if Dole supporters showed up: "Don't boo 'em. They're welcome here." And he had fun when the microphone briefly went dead. "Turn this thing on," he said to cheers.He was to address a third rally later in the day in Houston and
17800 spend the evening there raising $1 million for the Democratic Party.A Democratic presidential candidate has not carried Texas since Jimmy Carter in 1976. The state's 32 electoral votes are the third-largest prize, behind California's 54 and New York's 33, in the race for 270 electoral votes and victory.Texas is the
17800 adopted home state of former President George Bush, the Republican whom Clinton defeated in 1992, and Bush's son is governor. Clinton lost Texas to Bush in 1992 with Texas billionaire and third-party candidate Ross Perot in third place.A University of Texas poll Sept. 19 put Clinton and Dole in a
17800 dead heat in the state, each with 41 percent support. But Republicans dismiss it.Clinton, his Southern accent deepening, told the rallies that Republicans talked a great deal about reducing the size of government but never did when they held the White House."They hated it so much, but they couldn't bear
17800 to be outside of it. It kind of tickled me. But they never did anything about it," he said in Longview. He said the federal government under him has been reduced to as small as it was when John Kennedy was president.Doug Sosnik, White House director of political affairs, sounded
17800 a confident note, saying he did not see how Dole could get to 270 electoral votes without Texas."I think it would be hard for him. I'm not sure how easy it's going to be for him to hit 270. We are having a hard time figuring out what map, which
17800 states he's going after to get to 270. If he doesn't win Texas, I think it will be much harder," Sosnik told reporters.Appearing with Clinton at the rallies was the Democratic candidate for the Senate, Victor Morales, a high school teacher who came out of nowhere to win the Democratic
17800 primary by driving a pickup truck around the state in his campaign.He seeks to unseat incumbent Republican Sen. Phil Gramm but he is far behind in the polls and most analysts give him little chance of derailing the high-spending Gramm campaign.White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton considered "inappropriate" remarks
17800 Morales made recently about Republican Representative Henry Bonilla but welcomed Morales' statement of regret.Morales had called the Hispanic-American Bonilla "a wannabe white.""Where I grew up we called them coconuts, white on the inside, brown on the outside," Morales said.Clinton was on the first day of a two-day campaign swing. He
17800 is to travel to Rhode Island and Massachusetts on Saturday.</

17805 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentThe United States is expected to chide Europe and Japan about the need to nurture their fledgling economic recoveries at a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) leading industrial nations on Saturday.But the criticism is likely to be muted because the outlook for the
17805 world economy as a whole looks bright."Obviously it will be important to keep the momentum of growth in place in both Europe and Japan," U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said. "We'll be looking forward to a frank discussion on these issues."Faster growth in Europe and Japan would be good
17805 for the United States because it would boost demand for American exports, helping sustain its 5-1/2-year-old economic upswing.For its part, the United States is likely to be faced with questions at the G7 meeting about its willingness to take tough action to balance its government budget and hold inflation in
17805 check.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) this week said the United States needs to raise interest rates to prevent the economy from overheating and head off inflation.Saturday's meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- is shaping
17805 up to be a low-key gathering free of the rancour evident in the past.With the United States and Japan both faced with upcoming elections and Europe preoccupied with its efforts to launch a single currency in 1999, there is little incentive for any of the policymakers to engage in a
17805 public war of words.Currency markets, often the bugaboo of G7 meetings, have remained calm. The dollar has been buoyant, but so far the United States does not seem concerned that will hurt its exporters by robbing them of competitiveness on world markets,"The key currencies are now in ... a solid,
17805 well-justified constellation and we don't forsee major changes in the near future," IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said.On the one issue that may have sparked heated debate at the G7 meeting -- a controversial proposal to sell IMF gold -- the group has agreed to disagree and put off a
17805 decision.The United States and Britain back gold sales to finance debt relief for poor nations. Germany and Italy are opposed, saying the money should come from bilateral contributions.The IMF has enough money on hand now to participate in the joint debt initiative with the World Bank and the Paris Club
17805 of creditor nations. The G7, which forms the backbone of the Paris Club, is expected to sketch out on Saturday what creditor nations are prepared to do to help.The G7 gathering, which is taking place on the fringes of the annual IMF/World Bank meeting, comes as the outlook for the
17805 world economy is turning brighter.The IMF has forecast that world growth will pick up to 4.1 percent next year from 3.8 percent in 1996.U.S. Treasury Seceratry Robert Rubin has called the global outlook "encouraging" but has also made clear that Washington will be monitoring developments in Europe and Japan closely.Rubin
17805 in the past has raised questions about Europe's head-long drive to slash budget deficits under its plan to launch European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.At the last meeting of G7 economic policymakers in April, European nations argued that a stronger dolar was needed to help put their economies back on
17805 track, while the United States advocated European interest rate cuts as the solution.Both have occurred, taking the sting out of the short-term economic debate, but leaving open the question of the long-term impact of EMU on the world economy."It (the dollar) is not an issue. We will not be making
17805 it an issue," the German source said.Japanese officials too have signalled that they do not intend to push for a stronger dolar at the G7 meeting."The current dollar/yen rate correctly reflects economic fundamentals and I think it is in a comfortable range for both Japan and the United States," a
17805 Japanese official said.Rubin though said that it was "critically important" that Japan continue to pursue policies aimed at promoting domestic demand-led growth.</

17809 Robert Holland said Friday that he was resigning as president and chief executive of Ben &amp; Jerry's Homemade Inc. to allow a marketing specialist to take the helm of the ice cream maker as it seeks to expand overseas."The reasons I'm making way for a new CEO is that I
17809 have good instincts, but not world-class experience in the consumer goods business," Holland said in a telephone interview after announcing he was leaving the Vermont-based company known for its quirky product names and corporate largesse.Holland and company co-founder Ben Cohen both said the 56-year-old Holland's departure, on Oct. 31, will
17809 come at a time when many of the goals he faced upon taking over less than two years ago have been met.Still, the company's stock lost $1, or almost 8 percent, after the news was announced. The shares later recovered a bit to trade at $12.75, down 50 cents, in
17809 afternoon trading on Nasdaq.Ben &amp; Jerry's said this month it expected third-quarter earnings to be "materially" below last year's, but Holland said things were improving as the company battles archrival Haagen-Daz for sales in the market for premium ice cream, which is about 2 percent of all ice-cream sales."Our earnings
17809 are back on track to where they were before the third quarter," Holland said. "We're away from the precipice. Our earnings are solid."Holland replaced the firm's famous founders early in 1995, when the company -- originally known for its counter-culture corporate culture -- moved from a "founder-led" system to a
17809 more professional management structure.As health-conscious Americans began swearing off fattening foods, Holland was brought in to introduce the company's products, like "Cherry Garcia" and "Chunky Monkey" ice cream, to sweet-toothed consumers overseas.The no-nonsense, button-downed executive -- the antithesis of the bearded, tie-dyed founders of the company, whose scruffy visages appear
17809 on every pint -- did manage to restore order to Ben &amp; Jerry's operations and finances.Holland said the ice cream maker's expansion into Europe was on target, although "not as fast as I would like," and Ben &amp; Jerry's would enter the Japanese market with an eye on the entire
17809 Pacific Rim.However, with premium ice cream in countries like Britain selling at twice the price of lower-priced brands, Holland said, a highly experienced marketing executive with international skills was needed to run the company."We've got a pretty sophisticated challenge," he said from the company's new headquarters in Burlington, Vt.He said
17809 a key challenge to boosting sales was to get more consumers to make a taste test. Many people who buy a first pint are repeat buyers, but that getting that first trial is difficult.Holland, a former chief executive of a plastics firm and consultant to Fortune 500 companies, took over
17809 at Ben &amp; Jerry's in February 1995 with great fanfare after Cohen stepped up to the role of chairman.He was hired after the company launched an unorthodox search campaign through newspaper advertisements in which it invited candidates to write essays explaining why they were suited for the job.After receiving more
17809 than 22,500 responses to its "Yo, I'm Your CEO" write-in campaign, Ben &amp; Jerry's hired Holland, although there were reports that he was actually found through an executive search firm."Bob arrived just when we needed him to help straighten out our operations, get our new plant up and running, start
17809 our international business and launch our new sorbet line. We are very grateful for his contribution," said Cohen, who with Jerry Greenfield turned a correspondence course in ice cream-making into a $150 million company.Holland said that in addition to its overseas expansion, the company had also upgraded its manufacturing operations
17809 and improved employee morale, once said to be on the decline, under a new human resources director."Ben &amp; Jerry's has great products, great people and a promising future," Holland said in a statement.The company, however, does not have a successor for Holland, who will remain as a director through June
17809 1997.Bruce Bowman, senior director of operations, was given the additional title of chief operating officer on an interim basis and will oversee day-to-day management of the company until a successor to Holland is found.The company said a subcommittee of the board would begin a search for a new CEO immediately.</

17811 Several years into a 10-year fight with cancer, 39-year-old Lawrence Imbordino was told his condition was terminal.The illness has been tough on the jazz musician's family as well. Though he had medical insurance, Imbordino was faced with thousands of dollars of out-of-pocket medical costs that almost forced him to sell
17811 his house in a hurry.But last year, he opted to sell his life insurance policy for less than its face value so he would have money to meet his bills and do something special for his wife and children."I did a little of both," Imbordino said of his decision to
17811 use his $30,000 settlement to take his family to Disney World and to pay some bills. "I took care of myself and my bill collectors."The settlement helped us get our head above water, a little bit," he said.Imbordino may represent a trend in the so-called viatical settlement industry, which started
17811 by paying off settlements for AIDS patients in the early part of the decade.With greater acceptance of the settlements and news of promising treatments for AIDS, some in the industry expect cancer patients to overtake AIDS patients as the primary recipients of viatical settlements.One company planning on that transition is
17811 Viaticus Inc., a unit of CNA Financial Corp., and a major player in the industry."Certainly, Viaticus would expect that cancer would become the leading condition that we help by the end of next year," Viaticus President Gary Chodes said in a recent interview. "Other companies probably aren't going to make
17811 the transition in the same way."Within AIDS, that market is becoming more mature and with some of the treatment protocols that come out, it makes some of the people with AIDS not eligible for viatical settlement," Chodes said.Dignity Partners Inc. said in July that it was temporarily ceasing to process
17811 new applications from individuals diagnosed with AIDS and the virus that causes it while it further analyses research results on AIDS treatments presented at the International AIDS conference this summer. Last week, the San Francisco-based company said that analysis was continuing.A provision in recently passed healthcare legislation would allow payments
17811 to patients expected to die within two years to be tax exempt.Chodes said he expected this to help expand use of viatical settlements for people other than AIDS patients. He noted that cancer accounts for a far greater percentage of deaths in the United States than AIDS."There isn't any particular
17811 reason why a cancer patient wouldn't be as good if not better candidate" for a settlement, he said.Viaticus estimated that about $800 million in policies will be purchased by the industry in viatical settlements this year, with the figure jumping to over $1 billion by 1998."That rate is going to
17811 rapidly increase," he said, adding that Viaticus, which buys nearly a third of the $500 million in policies it considers, will grow with that business.While 50 percent of Viaticus' business currently comes from AIDS patients, Chodes expects that to drop to 25 percent next year.Viaticus pays up to 85 percent
17811 of the face value of a policy to a terminally ill person, maintains the premium on the policy, and then collects the full value when the person dies. Its decision whether to accept a policy and how much to pay is based on premium cost, life expectancy and terms of
17811 the policy.While receiving the settlement was helpful, it was also stressful, Imbordino said."To be approved for it also says that everybody agrees that 'Yeah, you're in pretty big trouble, pal,'" he said.Imbordino said he received about 75 percent of the value of his policy, which helped postpone a decision to
17811 sell his house for more than a year.The house is now on the market and he has sold one of the family's two cars, but the settlement gave him some time to plan."This would have happened maybe much more catastrophically if we weren't able to get the benefit from Viaticus,"

17818 Ben &amp; Jerry's Homemade Inc., the iconoclastic ice cream maker known for its quirky product names and corporate largess, said Friday that Robert Holland was resigning as president and chief executive after less than two years in the job.The company's stock lost $1, or almost 8 percent, immediately after the
17818 news was announced, but the shares recovered to trade at $12.625, down 62.5 cents, in midday trading on the Nasdaq market.Ben &amp; Jerry's said earlier this month that it expected its third-quarter earnings to be "materially' below last year's.Holland replaced the firm's famous founders early in 1995, when the company
17818 -- originally known for its counter-culture corporate culture -- moved from a "founder-led" system to a more professional management structure.As health-conscious Americans began swearing off fattening foods, Holland was brought in to introduce the company's products, like "Cherry Garcia" and "Chunky Monkey" ice cream, to sweet-toothed consumers overseas."Bob arrived just
17818 when we needed him to help straighten out our operations, get our new plant up and running, start our international business and launch our new sorbet line. We are very grateful for his contribution," co-founder and Chairman Ben Cohen said in a brief statement announcing Holland's sudden departure, effective Oct.
17818 31.Holland was hired after the company launched an unorthodox executive search campaign through newspaper advertisements in which it invited would-be candidates to write essays explaining why they were suited for the job. After receiving more than 22,500 responses to its "Yo, I'm Your CEO" write-in campaign, Ben &amp; Jerry's announced
17818 that it had hired Holland, although there were reports that he was actually found through an executive search firm.The no-nonsense, button-downed executive -- the antithesis of the bearded, tie-dyed founders of the company, whose scruffy visages appear on every pint -- did manage to restore order to Ben &amp; Jerry's
17818 operations and finances. But he may have lost a struggle over the company's direction.Holland argued that Ben &amp; Jerry's must expand more aggressively. Cohen, who with Jerry Greenfield turned a correspondence course in ice cream-making into a $150 million company, favoured slower growth that would not harm the socially-conscious company's
17818 relations with its employees or the tiny Vermont communities where it operates.Ben &amp; Jerry's pledges 7.5 percent of its pretax profits to social causes -- from antinuclear campaigns to gay rights. It also uses its purchasing power to back its values, buying milk and cream from Vermont family farms, even
17818 though it costs more.The company also gives three free pints of ice cream a day to each of its 700 employees, most of whom wear jeans or shorts to work."Ben &amp; Jerry's has great products, great people and a promising future," Holland said in a statement."However, at this juncture a
17818 change appears appropriate. When you couple the marketplace challenges with the predictably tough demands associated with succeeding founders, the need for accelerated succession is clear."The company, however, does not have a successor for Holland, who had vowed to make the unorthodox manufacturer and retailer more profitable by tighter management of
17818 areas such as raw materials, distribution, inventories and waste.The announcement said a subcommittee of the board would begin a serach for a new CEO.The company said Holland, a former chief executive of a plastics firm and consultant to Fortune 500 companies, will remain as a director through June 1997.Bruce Bowman,
17818 senior director of operations, was given the additional title of chief operating officer on an interim basis and would oversee day-to-day management of the company, it said.</

17820 to break cleanly above 94.28 August high to confirm confidence that there will be no credit tightening this year. U.S. Treasury bond futures, which have made handsome gains this week, will likely see choppy trading in the coming days as the market prepares for next Friday's September U.S. jobs data,
17820 analysts said."Next week is a big week of economic releases, and this market is in a number-to-number mode," said Charles Ovis, manager of global trading at EVEREN Securities."It creates an extremely volatile trading environment that is difficult to trade short-term, but the overall technical make-up in the market is fairly
17820 strong," he added. "We'll go into next Friday's unemployment number probably towards the top of this range, and if we get anything below the forecast (in non-farm payrolls) we'll have a shot to break the 6-3/4 (percent in the long bond yield)," he noted.According to a recent Reuters survey, economists
17820 on average expect a gain of 192,000 in non-farm payrolls against August's 250,000 gain.Ovis saw 109-00 in December T-bond futures, which was an important peak prior to last Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting, as a key support level in maintaining the market's bullish momentum. Michael Zentz, director of fixed
17820 income at Pegasus Econometrics Group, said the 109-area also represented a 62 percent retracement of the August-September decline.To extend gains and test new highs, the bond market, besides resolving overbought conditions in momentum indicators, needed to see the shorter end of the curve show confidence in further pricing out any
17820 future Fed rate hikes, Zentz said.He said he wanted the December eurodollar futures to climb well above 94.28 August high. "If I were to see them trade eight pips above that -- a clean breakout -- I would have to suspect that the market is comfortable pricing out that other
17820 25 basis points and the short end won't be a drag to the long end," he said."On a breakout, maybe I'll have to abandon the swing trading mode I've been in all summer and start to wonder if we're not trending," he added.Fundamentally, Ovis at EVEREN said a slower second
17820 half economic growth forecast by the Fed could be starting to materialize and that there was a healthy inflow of foreign capital into the bond market.-- Chicago Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com</

17822 Some assorted notes for business travelers:Moving UpYes, it really is getting harder to win an upgrade to first or business class, even with a bank-full of frequent flier points.The explosion of mileage awards (banks are even handing them out now as a prize to lure home equity loan customers) has
17822 flooded the system. Meanwhile, the number of first and business class seats available hasn't increased in the past few years.Frequent Flyer Magazine reports in its October issue that some travelers go through hoops to assure themselves of an upgrade -- like calling to request one at midnight on those carriers
17822 that take requests a day or two ahead of the flight.For those who do manage an upgrade, or whose company policy permits that level of travel, the same issue of the magazine gives an extensive rundown of business class service by carrier, listing such things as type of aircraft, seat
17822 arrangements and whether fax or laptop dataports are available on the plane.Bonus PointsOn the hotel front, Hyatt is offering 500 bonus points to members of its Gold Passport frequent guest programme who book and complete reservations through its Internet site.A spokeswoman said the promotion is designed to familarize travelers with
17822 using the Net to book a room.The Hyatt site is http://www.hyatt.com and can be used to reserve space at 103 of the group's hotels and resorts in North America.Busy SkiesIt's up and away as far as crowded air traffic is concerned.According to the Federal Aviation Administration and the Air Transport
17822 Association there will be 562 million airline passengers on board U.S. carriers this year, but that figure will swell to 673 million by the end of the century.By the year 2007 the passenger level will hit 856 million.A Personal PillowAir travelers who'd rather not use the pillows that live in
17822 the overhead bins have an alternative -- a personal pillow whose manufacturer says is a perfect size for briefcase or carry-on bag.The "Pillow-To-Go" costs $19.95 and is antibacterial and hypo-allergenic, according to Talatech Inc. It stores rolled-up, fastened with a Velcro strip, and deploys to a 15-inch square that is
17822 13 inches thick.The pillow is made of a latex foam with thousands of tiny air channels that keep it cooler in summer and warmer in winter, the manufacturer says.The company reports "tons" of orders since the pillow went on the market earlier this year. It can be ordered by calling
17822 1-800-TALATECH.No. 1 MistakeThe most common mistake travelers make is the most obvious -- getting the time or date of the flight wrong.That information comes from Uniglobe Travel International Inc., which says it studied thousands of calls to a 24-hour help line it operates.About a third of the calls were for
17822 reservation changes, and a large number of those were because of missed flights, the company said.Top HotelsThe Four Seasons Hotel in Chicago has been named the top city hotel in the United States in a reader poll conducted by Andrew Harper's Hideaway Reports. It traded places with the Hotel Bel-Air
17822 in Los Angeles, which finished first last year.Third place went to the Four Seasons in New York, fourth to the St. Regis in New York and fifth to the Ritz-Carlton in San Francisco.The rest of the top 10 in order: The Peninsula, Beverly Hills; Ritz-Carlton, Boston; Mansion on Turtle Creek,
17822 Dallas; Ritz-Carlton, Chicago and Mandarin Oriental, San Francisco.-----Business travelers: Question, complaint or pet peeve? Send them to Away on Business, c/o Reuters, Room 1170, 311 S. Wacker Dr., Chicago 60606. Or via Internet E-mail Mike.Conlon(at)Reuters.com using the "at" sign on computer keyboards. We cannot promise personal replies but will try
17822 to address letters as space permits.</

17830 President Bill Clinton on Friday welcomed astronaut Shannon Lucid back to Earth after a record 188 days in space, marvelling at her "amazing achievement.""There's so many things to say about the incredible skill and stamina and dedication it takes to be in space for six months ... It's a monument
17830 to the human spirit," said Clinton, in Texas on a re-election campaign trip.Dressed in a blue flight uniform, the 53-year-old Lucid, who returned on Thursday, looked a little unsteady on her feet as she walked to the podium for the official greeting outside the NASA hangar at Ellington Air Force
17830 Base.Lucid was with the crew of the shuttle Atlantis that picked her up from the Russian space station Mir where she set records for the longest time in space by a woman and an American.Atlantis landed at Kennedy Space Centre in Florida on Thursday morning. Despite spending six months in
17830 a weightless environment, Lucid managed to walk off the shuttle thanks to a grueling exercise regimen aboard Mir.She was originally scheduled to return to Earth in August but her stay was extended for six weeks when the shuttle was grounded for mechanical problems and two hurricanes."I think we all feel
17830 at least that we've gotten to know Dr. Lucid, watching her grin and bear it as the mission was extended, hearing her eagerness to see her family, her yearning for what she called 'the wind in the sun,'" Clinton said."Perhaps more than she knows, she has also set a remarkable
17830 example for a new generation of young Americans and especially young girls all across this country who look up at her and see new possibilities for themselves," he said.Clinton said Lucid's mission "continues to cement the close and growing bonds" between the U.S. and Russian space programmes.</
17831 Ford Motor Co.'s U.S. hourly workers are expected to swiftly ratify a rich new United Auto Workers contract this weekend as the union continues talks with both General Motors Corp. and Chrysler Corp."The decision still hasn't been made as to where we're going to concentrate our bargaining next," UAW spokesman
17831 Bobbie Barbee said Friday.UAW President Stephen Yokich met with top negotiators at both companies earlier this week to help move the talks forward, Barbee said.Bargaining in subcommittees at both GM and Chrysler was expected to continue over the weekend, company and union officials said."All issues are being discussed," said a
17831 person familiar with GM's negotiations.Industry observers had expected the UAW, which reached an agreement with Ford on September 17, to bargain next with Chrysler because the Canadian Auto Workers union is now threatening to strike GM's Canadian operations.But Yokich has consistently delayed decisions on bargaining targets throughout the 1996 negotiations
17831 to gain leverage over the automakers.Analysts say Chrysler can easily afford the provisions of the Ford contract, which require the company to maintain jobs for about 95 percent of its current 105,000-member hourly UAW workforce during the pact's three-year term. But the pact is expected to cause problems for GM,
17831 which needs to shrink its workforce to cut costs to competitive levels.UAW officials expect Ford workers to approve the pact by an overwhelming margin. The deal provides $13,900 in economic gains for the average worker over the life of the pact, plus substantial increases in pension benefits, and $1,000 per
17831 child per year in college tuition assistance."It's viewed very favorably in our plant," Carl Dowell, president of Local 862 in Louisville, Ky., said of the agreement.Final results of the voting are expected to be announced on Monday.Meanwhile, the leader of the Canadian Auto Workers said Friday that he told the
17831 top executive of a prospective buyer of two of GM's Canadian parts plants that the union would insist that he honor terms of the next GM contract.CAW President Buzz Hargrove declined to identify the buyer, but UAW officials have identified it as Joseph, Littlejohn &amp; Levy, a New York-based investment
17831 firm."I told him, 'You can buy if you want. You buy us, but you also buy the CAW-GM master collective agreement,'" Hargrove told reporters.Joseph, Littlejohn &amp; Levy also is negotiating to buy two of GM's U.S. parts plants, said Whitey Hale, president of UAW Local 326 at one of the
17831 facilities in Flint, Mich. The other plants are located in Livonia, Mich., and Windsor and Oshawa, Ontario.Hale said he wants the UAW to take a tougher stance against the sale of the facilities, which make door hinges, window mechanisms, door panels and other interior trim parts."I think if our UAW
17831 leadership were more militant, they could save those plants. They should take a lesson from Hargrove," he said.</

17833 The United States on Friday was reconsidering whether it would evacuate thousands more Kurds from Iraq as it earlier indicated it was planning to do.Two days ago, State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies told a news briefing "no decision has been made on this (evacuation but) it is our inclination
17833 to do this if we can."But on Friday, Davies seemed much less certain of U.S. plans, telling reporters: "We're still looking at options ... for ensuring the safety of employees of NGOs (non-governmental organizations) of interest to the United States."This is a complex situation. It's a very fluid situation. And
17833 all I would add is that it's going to take some time to work through this," Davies said.Another U.S. official who spoke on condition of anonymity told Reuters: "We were all ready to go but now there's all this second-guessing" about the operation. He indicated a debate was underway among
17833 administration officials.The Kurds under discussion worked for private voluntary organizations that helped maintain the U.S.-led safe haven in northern Iraq.The program of assisting and protecting Kurds in the region collapsed after troops of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein several weeks ago entered the north to help a Kurdish faction defeat its
17833 rival in armed conflict.The United States recently evacuated to the Pacific island of Guam via Turkey 2,100 Kurds and their families who were working directly for the U.S. government in northern Iraq.On Wednesday, Davies said Washington was inclined to evacuate Kurds and others working for the humanitarian groups -- estimated
17833 at upwards of 4,000 -- because they were at risk.But on Friday, he even hedged on that point, saying "some of these individuals may be at risk."The operation is complicated because "there are more people than we brought out earlier. They're spread out all over the place. And they belong
17833 to many different organizations," he said."We're looking at how we can minimize the risk to these people, up to and including bringing them out of the country."Turkey initially objected to U.S. plans for the earlier evacuation because of concerns some of the individuals might have been members of the Kurdistan
17833 Workers Party (PKK), which has long been engaged in a separatist war with Ankara.The 2,100 people in the earlier evacuation crossed into Turkey and were flown on commercial airliners to Guam. Davies said Turkey was not an impediment to another evacuation.The second-guessing on the evacuation could reflect what one official
17833 called a "redefinition" of the U.S. role in northern Iraq since Saddam extended his control in the area.Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau told Congress this week the Clinton administration was not bound to keep Saddam from restoring control over the ethnic "safe haven" in northern Iraq set up after
17833 the 1991 Gulf War."We have no commitment to protect them against their own bad judgment if one party invites Saddam Hussein in" to help it against the other, he said.Davies said Pelletreau was misinterpreted and cited the no-fly zone over the north as evidence of U.S. leadership in carrying out
17833 a U.N. resolution "to protect the Kurds to the extent possible from (Saddam's) depredations."But Davies stressed that "we were never at a stage where ... we gave some kind of an ironclad security guarantee to the Kurds of northern Iraq."</

17835 The income gap between California's highest and lowest wage earners has widened since early in the 1980s, according to a report Friday.The California Franchise Tax Board said in the report that the highest income Californians, the top one percent, experienced an overall income increase of 42.3 percent from 1980 to
17835 the 1994 tax year.The lowest 20 percent of the state's wage earners experienced a decrease of over 15 percent in the same period, the tax board said in its report.The report contained data from 1980 through the 1994 tax year on adjusted gross income, which accounts for inflation and for
17835 tax law changes.The Franchise Tax Board also found that some 68 percent of all taxpayers in the state make $40,000 or less annually. Only 1.3 percent of taxpayers make $200,000 or more per year."These figures describe more than income distribution," said Johan Klehs, Franchise Tax Board member and Board of
17835 Equalization chair. "It tells a disturbing story of the daily struggle of hard working wage earners who must labor even harder in order to make their financial ends meet.""The information is important because the public and policy makers need to be aware of this factual analysis as we determine possible
17835 courses of action to bridge the income level gap," Klehs said.</

17839 The U.S. Defence Department said Friday it did not deliberately withhold information from U.S. troops in the 1991 Gulf War on an anti-nerve gas drug to keep Iraq from learning about U.S. defences.Almost completely reversing comments made at a Pentagon briefing on Thursday, it said the troops were not told
17839 the drug was being used on an investigational basis and might have side effects but said that information was not deliberately withheld from them."There was no effort to withhold information from the troops," it said. "Information had been prepared to distribute to them, however it did not arrive before hostilities
17839 were initiated."Researchers are now studying whether the drug, pyridostigmine bromide (PB), in combination with insecticides or other chemicals in the Gulf War, might be one cause for illnesses thousands of veterans have suffered since."In retrospect, it was a mistake not to thoroughly inform the troops that PB was an investigational
17839 new drug or to brief them on the possible side effects," the statement said.A Pentagon spokesman, Capt. Michael Doubleday, had said at a news briefing on Thursday, "I believe there was a conscious decision made at the time not to tell the troops."He said the reason was to keep information
17839 away from Iraq on U.S. preparations "to defend against certain kinds of chemical weapons."The Food and Drug Administration gave the Defence Department a waiver allowing it to distribute the drug to troops without their consent. But it gave the waiver on condition they be told it was being used in
17839 combat for the first time on an investigational basis and that they be told of possible side effects.It said a small number of troops suffered side effects including nausea, cramps and headaches.</

17842 The Senate on Friday unanimously passed a $4.6 billion bill for water projects and flood control projects, sending it to the White House.The House Thursday approved the bill for four year's worth of projects, which was a compromise between the House's $5.1 billion measure and the Senate's $3.6 billion version.Several
17842 environmental and conservation groups that had opposed the bill lifted their objections when some projects were dropped and more environmental requirements were put in.The bill would decrease the federal cost share of flood control projects to 65 percent from 75 percent, raising the local share and requiring that local governments
17842 implement flood plain management plans before they become eligible for flood control projects.The bill also provided for federal and local cost-sharing to dispose of dredged material from navigation projects, giving the federal government more role in what can be a serious environmental problem.In another measure pushed by the White House,
17842 the bill authorises the administration's plan to restore the Everglades and the south Florida ecosystem.</
17843 Federal Reserve policy-makers voted 11-1 at their Aug. 20 meeting to keep short-term interest rates unchanged, according to minutes released Friday.However, the Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) remained ready to tighten credit if necessary to prevent inflation, the minutes showed.Citing concerns about inflationary pressures and dissenting from
17843 the majority, Minneapolis Fed president Gary Stern voted for of an immediate increase in short-term interest rates. Stern also dissented at the July gathering.The FOMC has since met again on Tuesday and elected to keep short-term rates -- specifically, the federal funds rate, which banks charge each other for overnight
17843 loans -- unchanged at 5.25 percent, its level since Jan. 31."Mr. Stern dissented because he believed that policy should become modestly more restrictive," the minutes said. Stern was concerned that "in the absence of a substantial and sustained improvement in productivity, the prevailing pattern of demand might engender an increase
17843 in inflationary pressures," it added.One concern expressed by FOMC members regarding the possible implications of an immediate rate hike was that "policy tightening at this point might generate an excessive reaction in financial markets."The minutes also showed the jury was still out at the FOMC regarding growth and inflation expectations.The
17843 FOMC noted "increases in prices remained remarkably subdued for an extended period in relation to measures of resource utilization, notably the rate of unemployment."The unemployment rate stood at 5.4 percent in July -- the latest rate reported at the time of the FOMC meeting.Among the reasons cited at the meeting
17843 as possible factors accounting for the subdued inflation performance were "highly competitive markets... comparatively small increases in labour compensation ... (that) appeared to reflect worker concerns about job security... as well as substantially reduced increases in benefit costs."While deciding to keep rates unchanged, the policy-makers reiterated their commitment to the
17843 pre-emptive monetary policy introduced in February 1994, the minutes showed."The prudent course at this point was to await further developments that would permit them to assess the possible need for some tightening with a higher degree of confidence... At the same time, it was emphasised the committee remained committed to
17843 a policy that would resist a rise in inflation," they said.</

17852 Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman announced Friday that the Agriculture Department will give $14.5 million to 18 states to help protect vulnerable farmland from urban sprawl.The money from the agency's new Farmland Protection Program will be leveraged with state and local funds so that approximately $55 million will be provided to
17852 buy development rights from farmers to keep productive farmland in use."We don't think we can sit back and take our farmland for granted," Glickman told reporters. "As our cities sprawl into neighboring rural areas, our farms are in danger of becoming subdivisions or shopping malls."The government intiative -- the first
17852 ever of its kind -- will protect at least 50,000 acres of productive farmland on 103 farms in 18 states, Glickman said.The Farmland Protection Program was established in the 1996 Farm Bill with total funding of $35 million over six years.Under the program, the Agriculture Department works with state and
17852 local projects to help acquire conservation easements or other interests in valuable agricultural land to limit nonagricultural uses of that land.To participate in the program, states, tribes or local governments must submit proposals to the federal government to help provide matching funds to protect the land. The department received requests
17852 to protect 176,000 acres of framland in the first go-around. The agency then selected 50,000 acres of the best land in the most danger.Proposals were selected from: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin."We
17852 believe population growth will be exceedingly strong in the next decade ... We're trying to get ready to feed a hungry world," said Agriculture Secretary Glickman.</
17853 U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman stepped up a verbal battle over the world wheat market on Friday, issuing a new warning to the European Union that he will fight subsidies with subsidies.He said the U.S. administration was watching closely to see if EU wheat pricing becomes aggressive and threatened to
17853 restart U.S. subsidies if it does."If, in fact, we see a serious and appreciable interest by the Europeans to weave their subsidized tentacles throughout the world, then we will take action," he said.World grain markets have been largely free of export subsidies for more than a year, because high prices
17853 and dwindling supplies made them unnecessary.But the European Union restarted wheat subsidies last week, with officials there saying they were necessary to bridge a temporary gap between world and EU prices.Glickman said at a news briefing that although there was no contingency plan on paper yet, his officials were already
17853 talking to other U.S. agencies about using the Export Enhancement Program (EEP) of subsidies.The program is funded at $100 million for fiscal 1997, which starts next week, half the level for 1996, and Glickman said he would ask Congress for more funds if necessary."If the subsidies are enhanced overseas, and
17853 if we think that the threat is great to United States grain production, we'll ask Congress for additional money," he said.Despite the strong talk, U.S. analysts said subsidies were unlikely in the short term, pointing to a government report due on Monday that is expected to say wheat stocks on
17853 Sept. 1 were at their lowest levels in two decades.The European Commission's director general for agriculture, Guy Legras, sought on Wednesday to calm U.S. fears, saying the EU was planning no measures to boost wheat exports and wanted no confrontation with the United States.But Pat Roberts, who chairs the powerful
17853 Agriculture Committee in the House of Representatives and who is from a major wheat-growing district in Kansas, said on Wednesday Glickman should think hard about using the EEP."The pressure is building within the wheat industry towards reactivation of EEP," Carl Schwensen of the National Association of Wheat Growers said.Schwensen said
17853 he would also like to see Glickman take a stand against Australia's and Canada's pricing policies.A group representing wheat growers in North Dakota wrote to Glickman on Thursday asking him to renew the subsidies.A report on Thursday by the International Grains Council (IGC) gave a gloomy outlook for wheat prices,
17853 which would make a subsidy war more likely.</
17854 Midwest flour mills will face more difficulty trying to source hard red winter wheat in coming weeks if U.S. farmers continue to hold off from selling their crop, grain industry sources said Friday."To say that mills are scurrying at the moment is certainly not right, but the lack of farmer
17854 selling has made it a tougher job for mills to do their purchasing," said one mill buyer in eastern Kansas who asked not to be named.Analysts said they did not expect the pace of farmer sales to increase sharply any time soon. Tom Neher, a grain merchant for Benson-Quinn Commodities
17854 in Kansas City, attributed the lack of farmer selling to three key factors: relatively low current prices; farmers' desire to defer income for tax purposes; and more pressing farm tasks."They already sold some at harvest to cover costs...and they're planning to hold on to the rest of it until they
17854 get a better price than what they have now," Neher said. "The other thing is the tax part of it, wanting to defer income."Producers have also been trying to harvest fall crops and plant next year's wheat crop. That means marketing grain has been a distant third priority, Neher said.

17855 Colombian officials said a series of pilot errors led to the crash of an American Airlines jet in a mountainous area of Colombia last December, according to a final report released in Washington on Friday.Aeronautica Civil, the Colombian civilian aviation authority, confirmed that one of the flight's pilots entered an
17855 incorrect computer code that caused the AMR Corp's American Airlines plane to turn away from its destination toward the city of Bogota.The Boeing 757 was bound for Cali in southern Colombia when pilots lost track of its position. It slammed into a mountain, killing all but four of the 167
17855 passengers and crew aboard.Probable causes of the crash were pegged to the lack of "situational awareness" of the flight crew regarding the plane's proximity to terrain and the crew's failure to discontinue the approach.The report found that the pilot inadvertently entered the wrong computer command, changing the flight's course without
17855 verifying whether it was the correct choice and without first obtaining the approval of the other pilot, contrary to American's procedures.The crew's failure to revert to basic radio navigation when the computer-assisted navigation became confusing was also cited as one of the probable causes of the crash.Contributing factors to the
17855 cause of the accident included the crew's ongoing efforts to speed their approach and landing to avoid potential delays, the report said.The crew also failed to release the "speed brakes" of the Boeing 757 when it was using an escape manoeuvre to try to avoid the mountain, the report said.Colombian
17855 officials recommended that the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration develop and impose standards related to the use of automation in flight navigation.The report called on the FAA to require airlines to provide pilots with the training and tools to recognise when computers became an obstacle to navigating a flight and when
17855 to revert to basic radio navigation.It also recommended the FAA require new planes to automatically release speed brakes in situations "demanding maximum thrust and climb capability."</

17859 higher now that the pig crop has been confirmed at low levels. "There was a lot of concern, with the high hog prices in the summer and the recent declines in the corn market, that we were going to see a return to rather substantial expansion in the U.S. hog

17863 California Gov. Pete Wilson signed controversial legislation on Friday to create a $10.5 billion publicly-run agency to sell earthquake insurance to homeowners.Wilson, a Republican, said the legislation should help to end California's insurance availability crisis for homeowners seeking earthquake coverage."Earthquakes will always be a fact of life in California, but
17863 homeowners no longer must risk a devastating, unrecoverable loss because they couldn't get insurance," Wilson said. The legislation signed Friday will implement the so-called California Earthquake Authority. The proposal was approved by the Legislature in August after months of heated debate.California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said the authority should begin
17863 to sell policies by December 1."Gov. Wilson's signature on legislation creating the California Earthquake Authority means that California's economic recovery will proceed on course -- uninterrupted by the evaporation of homeowners' insurance and the paralyzing effect that would have on the state's real estate market," Quackenbush said in a statement.
17863 As a public entity, the authority will be tax-exempt, enabling it to build up enough reserves to cover major earthquake disasters.The authority will be capable of funding $10.5 billion through a combination of sources, including insurer contributions, policyholder premiums, capital markets, and reinsurance.Quackenbush maintains that the authority would, in its
17863 first year of operation, have enough resources to pay all claims from an earthquake more than twice as destructive as the devastating 1994 Northridge quake. Wilson said mammoth natural disasters like the Northridge quake create a magnitude of loss that can plunge an insurance company into insolvency.Such disasters, coupled with
17863 California's requirement that homeowner policyholders be offered earthquake insurance, have severely restricted the availability of these policies.The California Department of Insurance estimated that about 99 percent of California insurers had restricted or stopped selling homeowner and earthquake insurance, making it difficult for homebuyers to obtain mortgages."The CEA (California Earthquake Authority)
17863 will provide much-needed relief for the insurance availablility shortage," Wilson said.</

17878 Nearly 17,000 people had $4.8 million restored to their 401(k) retirement plans after employers made use of a grace period to replace funds they had failed to deposit properly, the government said Friday.The Labour Department released data showing that 170 small to mid-sized businesses voluntarily returned employee contributions and made
17878 good on lost earnings after they were given six months to do so without penalty.The amnesty programme, which expired earlier this month, was part of a broader Clinton administration effort to end fraudulent activity in 401(k) plans. So far, the crackdown has resulted in investigations that have led to the
17878 return of another $10 million in employee funds."We don't have any evidence the problem is widespread but ... there are going to be a few rotten apples," Labour Secretary Robert Reich said in an interview. "We at the Labour Department have to continue to act aggressively."As a result of the
17878 grace period, contributions were repaid to plans affecting 16,800 participants. Amounts ranged from $43 to more than $200,000, the department said.The employers, which included technology companies, law firms, physicians and credit unions among others, admitted to being delinquent for reasons ranging from computer errors to diverting funds to pay bills.Amnesty
17878 was not an option for those employers "who had engaged in the most egregious conduct," the department said.Companies were disqualified, for example, if they were already the subject of a criminal investigation or if they failed to make deposits that exceeded the total amount of employee contributions for all of
17878 1995.Some 23.4 million people participated in more than 170,000 401(k) plans with total combined assets of $613 billion in 1993, the latest year for which data are available.The retirement plan is named for the part of the U.S. tax code that allows workers to deduct a portion of income before
17878 it is taxed, invest it and pay no taxes on the money until it is withdrawn at retirement.Reich cautioned employees to check their 401(k) statements against their paystubs on a regular basis to ensure that their contributions have been posted accurately."There is no substitute for diligence on the part of
17878 employees," Reich said.The department launched its 401(k) enforcement programme in 1995 after it received an increased number of complaints about the plans.It issued a new rule last month that requires employers to deposit money withheld from workers' checks for 401(k) plans within 15 days instead of 90 days.</

17888 Massachusetts on Friday said that it was starting its drive to improve its seaports with a $110,000 grant for the port of Salem as part of a program that eventually includes selling around $300 million of bonds.In addition to the engineering study for Salem, the list of near-term projects includes
17888 more than $500,000 for Gloucester, Salem, Fall River and New Bedford, said Richard Armstrong, the executive director of the Seaport Council. The council is an advisory group.The start of the program was announced on Friday by Lieutenant Governor Paul Cellucci, who held a news conference in Salem.The state hopes to
17888 start an electronic fish auction three or four months from now, which it expects will help raise prices by making it easier for potential purchasers around the world to bid for the catch.The Seaport Bond Bill, which was approved this summer, includes $100 million for coastal facilities, like docks and
17888 warehouses, approximately $100 million for dredging, and another $100 million to improve rail links.At present, Massachusetts cannot handle double-stacked containers, a limitation it plans to correct.However, the program will be funded on a pay-as-you-go basis, Armstrong said. "You basically put off selling the bonds until you really need the cash
17888 in the harbor," he explained, adding that the first sorts of projects being undertaken, like feasibility studies, are much less costly than some of the ones that will begin later on, like dredging harbors.--Joan Gralla, 212-859-1654</
17889 A collector of presidential memorabilia paid $4,125 for a postcard illustrated with a racially charged picture that President Bill Clinton sent 30 years ago to his grandmother.The postcard, dated in 1966, made clear the future president did not pick out the card and there were no racist comments in his
17889 writing. Herman Darvick of Rockville Centre, New York, who auctioned off the postcard, said on Friday it was the picture that made the postcard distinctive.The picture of a smiling black boy polishing a 195-pound (88 kg) watermelon was accompanied by an inscription that identified Clinton's hometown of Hope, Arkansas, as
17889 "Home of the World's Largest Watermelon."In the postcard the 19-year-old Georgetown University student wrote to his grandmother in an Arkansas nursing home, "Dear Mammaw, Thought I would send you one of your cards just to prove I'm using them!"The picture of the child with the watermelon evoked a racist image
17889 projected at the time of black people in the South as being poor and uneducated.But the auctioneer said in defence of Clinton, "He didn't pick them out, it's not that detrimental, it won't lose him the black vote or anything. It's something that he sent out in 1966 that he
17889 wouldn't send out in 1996."Clinton, who also wrote "My tests are over and I'm just starting the second term," signed it "Bill" and scribbled above his return address "Wm. J. Clinton".Darvick sold the postcard Thursday night to a Los Angeles collector who asked not to be identified. He previously sold
17889 a love letter written to a girlfriend by Clinton when he was a student at Oxford University in England.</

17894 The dollar ended slightly higher against major currencies as investors continued to sell German marks amid improving prospects for a planned single European currency.Funds flocked to the British pound, which would remain outside the proposed European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the exodus from the mark helped bolster the
17894 dollar."Everybody is getting out of marks because it looks like EMU is going to go through. The dollar will benefit from mark weakness," said Francois Akl, chief currency dealer at Gulf International Bank in New York.The dollar late Friday rose to 1.5244 marks from 1.5236 late Thursday and to 110.90
17894 Japanese yen from 110.67.The British pound rose to $1.5637 from $1.5614. The dollar climbed to 1.2565 Swiss francs from 1.2544, but fell to Canadian $1.3632 from C$1.3678.The mark typically enjoys broad investment flows because of Germany's traditional status as the strongest economy in Europe and a fiercely anti-inflation central bank.But
17894 EMU would eliminate the mark and the perceived safety of investing in the German currency.Meanwhile, Italy formally unveiled its 1997 budget, which Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi asserted would meet strict financial conditions for the lira to join EMU, drawing more funds away from the mark."As EMU becomes reality, you
17894 don't need the mark as a safe haven anymore," said Hillel Waxman, first vice president for foreign exchange and securities at Bank Leumi Trust Co. of New York.For the second straight session, the dollar's gains were confined to overseas trading hours, with European investors seen unloading marks.The dollar dipped briefly
17894 against the yen during Tokyo trading on a news report that Bank of Japan officials were concerned that Japanese long-term interest rates were too low.Japanese officials declined to comment and the dollar soon rebounded amid a general view that Japan's economy was too weak to withstand higher interest rates."The Japanese
17894 economy is still very weak and they have no reason to raise rates," Akl said.Dealers reported strong dollar buying from Japanese investors as the Japanese fiscal year midpoint nears. That trend should end when the second half begins October 1.The dollar now stands just below its 1996 high of 111.19
17894 yen, a key technical level which should complicate future dollar gains, dealers said.Looking ahead, a Saturday meeting in Washington of the finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations could offer clues about official views on recent currency market trends.The group, known as the G7, is expected to focus
17894 on efforts to stimulate economic growth in Europe, with any statement on currencies likely to show general complacency, dealers said."I think everyone will come in very happy with where the dollar is," said Waxman. "From a currency standpoint, the world is looking fine."</

17904 form a representative interim government that can begin the process of reconciliation nationwide," he said.The Taleban militia appealed on Friday for international recognition of its government after its forces captured the capital Kabul.Two years after their formation, the one-time band of Islamic student vigilantes took over a ruined capital, hanged
17904 former president Najibullah and his brother and proclaimed the complete enforcement of Islam in the war-wracked country.Despite the fact that the group had taken power by force, and hanged Najibullah, Davies said Washington had not ruled out recognising the new regime and establishing diplomatic relations."I just think it's really too
17904 early to pronounce ourselves on questions like diplomatic relations yet," he said.Also, asked about the Taleban's intentions to impose Islamic law, Davies said: "At this stage, we're not reading anything into that."He added that since the Taleban "appear to hold a majority of the cards at this stage, our call
17904 on them is to use their new position of authority to move to establish democratic institutions and to move to a process of national reconciliation.""The extrajudicial action taken against Najibullah and his associates was a regrettable development," the spokesman said.The United States has not had an embassy in Kabul since
17904 the Soviets left in the late 1980s. But there have been some low-level contacts with the Taleban, Davies said.The spokesman said that Americans in Kabul who wanted to leave the capital as the Taleban approached have been evacuated but some Americans who made the choice to stay remain there.</
