18115 Taleban commanders said on Friday they had hanged former Afghan president Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai after the capture of Kabul.The bodies of the two men were hanging from a concrete traffic-control post at the gates of the presidential palace as a crowd of more than a thousand people
18115 crowded around to watch.I saw Najibullah's body, battered and bloody, hanging with a steel wire noose around the neck."We killed him because he was the murderer of our people," Noor Hakmal, a Taleban commander who entered the city from Charasyab, south of Kabul overnight, told Reuters.Hakmal said the Taleban was
18115 searching the city for President Burhanuddin Rabbani, Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and military chief Ahmad Shah Masood but there was no word on their whereabouts.The burly Najibullah had lived in the United Nations office in Kabul since April 1992 when he was ousted by mujahideen guerrilla forces after 14 years
18115 of civil war.Ahmadzai was a former security chief under Najibullah's Soviet-backed government.Earlier Taleban leaders said they had taken control of Kabul and met with no resistance from government forces.They vowed to enforce an Islamic system in the country. 18115 agency in Pakistan, delared Afghanistan a "completely Islamic state" where a "complete Islamic system will be enforced".Celebratory bursts of machine-gun fire and occasional explosions echoed across the city at dawn but the Afghan capital was relatively calm as Taleban fighters set up checkpoints to search vehicles, the witnesses said.All key
18115 government installations appeared to be in Taleban hands including the Presidential Palace and the Ministries of Defence, Security and Foreign Affairs.No government forces were visible on the city's streets.Troops had been seen leaving Kabul some hours before, on the only government-controlled road out of Kabul.Witnesses said a convoy of four-wheeled
18115 drive vehicles and cars left the city during the night and government forces blew up several ammunition dumps before they retreated.Taleban commandsers said they had also captured Bagram airbase, 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul, as well as the disused Kabul airport near the city.Witnesses said tanks, artillery and
18115 trucks loaded with soldiers headed north, apparently towards Jabal us-Sharaj, the headquarters of military chief Masood at the entrance to the Panjshir valley.Kabul itself was quiet on Friday. 18115 in the eastern suburbs laden with belongings after fleeing earlier fighting.</

18121 The Taleban Islamic militia entered Kabul in tanks and on foot overnight on Friday, meeting little resistance from forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani, witnesses said.There was no fighting in Kabul.Celebratory bursts of machine-gun fire and occasional explosions echoed across the city at dawn but the Afghan capital was relatively
18121 calm as Taleban fighters set up checkpoints to search vehicles, the eyewitnesses said.All key government installations appeared to be in Taleban hands including the Presidential Palace and the Ministries of Defence, Security and Foreign Affairs.No government forces were visible on the city's streets.Civilians were walking in the streets in the
18121 morning past Taleban fighters who were controlling crossroads.Taleban forces entered the city from the east at about 1 a.m. local time (2130 GMT).They stopped in one street in the diplomatic Wazir Akbar Kahan Li neighbourhood and set up a loudspeaker and recited from the Koran for 15 minutes.The fate of
18121 Rabbani, his military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, and Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar was not immediately known.A few hours before the taleban arrived, govt troops began pulling out.Witnesses said tanks, artillery and trucks loaded with soldiers headed north out of the city apparently towards Jabal us-Sharaj, Masood's headquarters at the entrance
18121 to the Panjshir valley, where he and his best fighters come from.Overnight on Thursday Taleban sources in Pakistan had said the Islamic militia appeared poised to capture the capital after seizing the main government airbase north of Kabul and parts of the city, including its abandoned Khwaja Rawash airport.Deputy foreign
18121 minister Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai told Reuters Television at the United Nations late on Thursday that government troops were leaving Kabul to avoid a "bloodbath" with the rebels, and the country's besieged president was considering handing over power.The minister said Masood had gone north of the city, taking with him jet
18121 fighters and other military hardware.</
18122 Afghan government troops were leaving Kabul to avoid a "bloodbath" with Islamic rebels, and the country's besieged president was considering handing over power, deputy foreign minister Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai said.Taleban Islamic militia appeared poised to capture the capital having seized the main government airbase north of Kabul and parts of
18122 the city, including its abandoned Khwaja Rawash airport, Taleban sources in neighbouring Pakistan said.The minister said that the country's military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, had gone north of the city, taking with him jet fighters and other military hardware.The president, Burhanuddin Rabbani, was on the outskirts of the capital and
18122 would decide on Friday about a "transfer of power", he said in an interview with Reuters Television at the United Nations late on Thursday."Masood has decided to retreat to territory north of the city because he didn't want Kabul city to turn into a bloodbath," the minister said."The president is
18122 in the outskirts to the north and by tomorrow will announce his decision whether to leave the capital," he said adding that the president would take the advice of other members of his high council.He said he thought "there will be a transfer of power, to whom we do not
18122 know," adding that he would be consulting with members of his high council.He said he hoped that Afghanistan's former King, Zahir Shah, ousted in 1973 and now in Rome, would return to the country as even the Taleban would accept him in a leadership role.A spokeswoman for U.N. 18122 militia had also taken Kabul's Soviet-built Microrayon housing complex in the east and the diplomatic Wazir Akbar Khan district in central Kabul.The sources, quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), said troops loyal to President Rabbani were fleeing northwards, but his militia forces were resisting Taleban fighters near the
18122 presidential palace in central Kabul.There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report, which also said the Taleban had taken Kohe Asmai hill, known as Television Hill, in the middle of Kabul.While the airport in Kabul was made unusable by factional fighting, the Soviet-built Bagram, shared by jet fighters and
18122 civilian airliners, was the only base left giving the government an air link with the outside world.Some civilians had fled the city on the road north earlier in the day in dozens of trucks and buses, but with a curfew in force most Kabul citizens stayed in their homes.The Taleban,

18126 says that it is not against the Koran, you have to kill him and hang his body for three days until people say this is the body of the drinker who did not obey the Koran and Allah's order," he said."We call upon the international community to recognise us as
18126 the government of the Islamic state of Afghanistan," Taleban spokesman Wakil Ahmad told Reuters by telephone from the southern Afghan town of Kandahar.Neighbouring Pakistan appeared to signal the first recognition of the new regime by announcing it would dispatch officials for talks in Kabul.Life appeared normal in the shattered capital,
18126 which government forces abandoned hours before the Taleban entered around 1 a.m. on Friday (2130 GMT on Thursday).The bodies of Najibullah, who led a Soviet-backed government until he was ejected in April 1992, and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai were strung up in the centre of the city, watched by curious
18126 crowds.The Taleban described ousted Rabbani, prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and Masood as "national criminals" for not accepting a Taleban amnesty in return for a surrender.The men fled Kabul before the Taleban marched in."We call upon the international community to recognise us as the government of the Islamic state of Afghanistan,"
18126 Taleban spokesman Wakil Ahmad said.Witnesses said Kabul's streets were bustling with pedestrians, cyclists and cars and shops and markets were open despite an Islamic holiday. Militia tanks had pulled back to sidestreets although fighters were still visible at key points.People laden with belongings were seen returning to their homes in
18126 the eastern suburbs after fleeing earlier fighting.All key government installations appeared to be in Taleban hands, including the Presidential Palace and the Ministries of Defence, Security and Foreign Affairs.The country's currency, the afghani, surged to 11,000 to the U.S. dollar from the 18,500 level it was trading at before Kabul
18126 fell. "We think the afghani will strengthen when the market reopens tomorrow," money changer Javaid told Reuters.India stepped up security at the homes of former Afghan leaders living in New Delhi, police said. 18126 Babrak Karmal.The International Committee of the Red Cross said in Geneva the Taleban had agreed it could continue humanitarian relief operations, including approval for a 35-truck relief convoy.In Tehran, Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani called on the Afghan factions to stop fighting and set up a joint administration. 18126 called for reconciliation in Afghanistan and said Najibullah's execution was "regrettable."The Taleban announced just hours after the takeover that an interim six-man ruling council would run the country.A declaration by Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar quoted by AIP, named his deputy, Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, no relation of the ousted

18132 The Over The Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI) must allow all companies to list on its bourse, a committee said on Friday.At present, only companies with a paid-up capital of less than 50 million rupees are allowed to list on the OTCEI.The committee was appointed in April by market regulator
18132 Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to suggest ways to revamp the working of OTCEI."Investors in all companies which have a post-issue equity of less than 100 million rupees should have the benefit of market making and sponsorship," the committee said."If these (recommendations) are done, then OTCEI should pick
18132 up fairly fast," committee chairman S.A Dave told reporters.The measure was among a number of recommendations made by the committee to revitalise the OTCEI.OTCEI, India's first exchange to introduce electronic trade and market making, was started in 1990 to assist promoters of small companies and help retail investors.The OTCEI's network
18132 of dealers and members is spread over 42 cities in India.The exchange failed to take off as the lack of adequate funding from financial institutions and settlement problems affected operations. It has been dogged by inadequate trading volumes and poor interest shown by small promoters and dealers."A small corpus of
18132 about 500 million to one billion rupees by promoter institutions for investment in fundamentally strong OTCEI listed stocks would certainly provide a considerable boost to the OTCEI market," the committee said.The OTCEI was promoted by state-run institutions like the Unit Trust of India, the Life Insurance Corp, Industrial Development Bank

18155 Taleban Islamic militia have taken over Kabul and declared that Afghanistan will be run as an Islamic state.The following are some of the key facts about the country.Population: About 17 million, of whom more than 2.4 million are nomadic tribesmen. An estimated five million Afghans lived as refugees in Pakistan
18155 and Iran during the Soviet occupation in the 1980s. Islam is the main religion. Most are Sunni Moslems but there is a minority of at least one million Shi'ite Moslems.Area: 245,665 square miles (636,270 sq km). Landlocked Afghanistan borders the Central Asia republics to the north, Iran to the west
18155 and Pakistan to the south and east. Its north-east tip touches China.Refugees: About five million Afghans fled the country during the Soviet occupation. Most returned to their homes after mujahideen guerrillas took power in April 1992.Capital: Kabul has been the capital of Afghanistan since 1776. It has a population of
18155 800,000 to one million. Since April 1992, when the mujahideen captured Kabul, more than 40,000 people have beek killed and one million people have fled the city in bitter factional fighting.Currency: The Afghani had fallen to 9,781 to one U.S. dollar on Thursday from 7,500 to the dollar in January.Economy:
18155 Afghanistan has not had a formal economy since April 1992. The infrastructure of many major cities has been destroyed in the past 4-1/2 years of factional fighting. There are severe shortages of water, food, housing and other basic necessities.Trade: Under international law, Pakistan gave landlocked Afghanistan permission to import goods
18155 duty-free through its Karachi port. For decades, Afghan traders have driven their sealed imports up to Jalalabad or Spin Buldak in southeastern Afghanistan, and then turned around some of the goods to re-enter Pakistan. In the past three years, the volume of turnaround goods has increased dramatically.The Pakistan Central Board
18155 of Revenue estimates that about 20 billion rupees ($538 million) worth of goods were smuggled into Pakistan in fiscal 1994-95 (July-June) compared to 11 billion rupees worth in 1993-94.Landmines: Ten million landmines are scattered across more than 420 square km (160 sq miles) of Afghanistan, making it one of the
18155 most heavily mined countries in the world. Landmines have killed or maimed 400,000 Afghans. The United Nations is trying to clear some 240 minefields spread over 22 sq km (13 sq miles) in Kabul alone.Modern history: The country was ruled by King Zahir Shah from 1933 until 1973 when the
18155 monarchy was overthrown in a bloodless coup. Mohammad Daoud, the king's cousin, became the country's first president, heading a moderate leftist government.Daoud was killed in a 1978 Marxist coup. Nur Mohammad Taraki became president, but was himself overthrown and killed in September 1979. Hafizullah Amin took over but was not
18155 to remain in power for long.In December 1979, Soviet troops landed in Kabul. They seized key buildings on December 27, and Babrak Karmal announced he had taken over the government. Hafizullah Amin was executed.Karmal was replaced as general secretary (leader) of the ruling People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan by Najibullah
18155 in May 1986. Karmal also resigned as president later in November, and Mohammad Tsamkani was made "caretaker" president.Najibullah became president on September 30, 1987. A traditional government-convened "Loya Jirga" (grand assembly) in Kabul on November 29-30 adopted a new constitution and elected Najibullah president for seven years.A guerrilla war pitting
18155 Soviet and Afghan government troops against Western-backed rebel forces began after the Soviet intervention. The U.N. General Assembly repeatedly voted for withdrawal of the Soviet troops, and Afghanistan was suspended from the 46-nation Islamic Conference Organisation.From June 1982, a U.N. envoy conducted indirect talks between the Afghan and Pakistani governments
18155 to seek a solution to the conflict. The U.N. envoy was required because Pakistan did not recognise the Soviet-installed Kabul government.Despite the presence of some 115,000 Soviet troops in Afghanistan, the Mujahideen rebels continued to control much of the countryside. The introduction of U.S.-made Stinger anti- aircraft missiles in 1987
18155 swung the conflict in their favour.In February 1988, Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev and Najibullah announced that Soviet troops could withdraw by February 1989 if Afghanistan and Pakistan reached a settlement at the U.N.-mediated talks in Geneva.In April 1988, Afghanistan, Pakistan, the Soviet Union and the United States signed an accord
18155 providing for Soviet withdrawal, a halt to outside help for the rebels and the return of the Afghan refugees. It also said Washington and Moscow should oversee and guarantee the plan.In April 1992, rival guerrilla groups fought for control of Kabul. President Buhanuddin Rabbani emerged a victor, but continued fighting
18155 killed 10,000 civilians in 1993.The rebel Taleban Islamic militia emerged as a new force in October 1994 and since then has taken over more than half of Afghanistan. Its latest conquest was the capture of Kabul on Friday.</

18165 Here is a profile of the Taleban Islamic militia that took over the Afghanistan capital of Kabul on Friday.The Taleban has in the past two years swept aside warring guerrilla factions, taken control of most of Afghanistan, hanged its former president from a traffic-control post, and declared it would enforce
18165 an Islamic system in the country.The Taleban movement burst onto the Afghan scene in late 1994 after it was formed by Islamic religious students led by Mullah Muhammad Omar, a former guerrilla fighter who was wounded several times in battles with Soviet soldiers in the 1980s.Little is known of the
18165 one-eyed Mohammad Omar, who according to news reports returned to religious studies after 1989, when the Soviet forces left Afghanistan. He is in his 30s.Riding a wave of revulsion against local warlords and general weariness over the country's civil war, he and other religious students formed the Taleban and battled
18165 Mujahideen guerrilla commanders who had preyed on traders at checkposts in the southern province of Kandahar.Their ranks grew rapidly, and despite military setbacks in 1995, they proved more united and better disciplined than the faction-ridden government and rival guerrilla groups.But the Taleban has remained a secretive organisation, revealing little of
18165 its structure or political ambitions, and according to news reports out of Afghanistan, its fundamentalism has not always proven popular.Banning television sets, closing down girls' schools and forcing women to cover their faces, the movement has not always gone down well in areas under its control.But for the most part,
18165 their administration apparently has been relatively efficient, free of the corruption and interference common under other factions, allowing modest commerce to be revived in the war-ravaged country.How Afghanistan as a whole would thrive under Taleban rule is less certain.Within hours of their takeover, the militia hanged President Najibullah and his
18165 brother Shahpur Ahmadzai from a concrete traffic-control post at the gates of the presidential palace.The movement also announced that an interim, six-man ruling council would now run the country.A declaration issued by Mohammad Omar and quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) news service named his deputy, Mullah Mohammad
18165 Rabbani (no relation of the president) to head the council.An earlier statement by Omar carried by AIP declared Afghanistan a "completely Islamic state" where a "complete Islamic system will be enforced.""A taleban victory in Kabul would have major implications, including a strict enforcement of Islamic law," the London-based Jane's Defence
18165 Weekly wrote in March.It said the movement did not have the power and experience to seize the whole country and maintain law and order.According to Jane's, writing last year, the movement's central leadership, or shura, is composed of eight members, of whom Mohammad Omar, Mohammad Rabbani, Borjan and Mohammad Abbas
18165 are the key players.Mohammad Rabbani was named governor of the newly captured Nangarhar earlier this month.Little is known of the others, except most appear to share the background of being born in Kandahar, fighting the Soviet occupation in the 1980s and returning to their religious studies in the wake of
18165 the Soviet withdrawal in 1989.</
18166 The Taleban militia occupying Kabul have declared an amnesty for Afghan government soldiers and officers who surrender, a commander for the triumphant rebels said."We have declared a general amnesty for all government soldiers and officers if they give up their guns. Taleban will not take revenge. We have no personal
18166 rancour. If the people find someone responsible for crimes in the past we will judge him according to Islamic law," a Taleban commander, named only Musa, told Reuters. Musa said Taleban fighters had occupied Afghan army headquarters in the northern suburb of Khairkhana, which was headquarters of government commander General
18166 Baba Jan. He said Taleban forces were heading north from the Bagram airbase they captured last night. "We know the senior government leaders escaped from Kabul to the north," he said.Musa said the Jabal-us-Seraj base further north was still held by the government's top commander Ahmad Shah Masood but Taleban
18166 fighters were heading in that direction.Musa said Taleban used loudspeakers to tell civilians in Kabul to go about their daily life as usual.He said he hoped the situation would stabilise and result in better food supplies although hundreds of thousands of civilians in Kabul would remain vulnerable, particularly in the
18166 coming winter. He added that the World Food Programme had received a convoy of 30 trucks of food from Mazar-i-Sharif, north-west of Kabul, last night.</

18168 U.N. peace envoy for Afghanistan, Norbert Holl, on Friday expressed "deep dismay" at the execution of former Afghan president Najibullah and his brother by Taleban militia and public display of their bodies.In a statement issued in Islamabad, he appealed for sparing the lives of two remaining companions of Najibullah, a
18168 bodyguard and his former chief of staff, now in Taleban hands.Holl, who heads the United Nations Special Mission to Afghanistan (USMA), said armed men abducted Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai from the USMA compound in Kabul in the early hours of Friday and later killed them.He said the abduction
18168 of the former president and his companions and the subsequent killings "without any legitimate judicial procedure" constituted a grave violation of the immunity USMA premises enjoyed under international law.These acts "also further jeopardise all the efforts which are being made to secure a peaceful settlement of the Afghanistan conflict," Holl
18168 said."USMA deeply deplores these tragic events, which cast a doubt over the willingness of those responsible to achieve reconciliation and guarantee justice in the area controlled by them," he said."USMA appeals with the utmost gravity to those responsible to spare the lives of Dr Najibullah's two remaining companions."Holl praised the
18168 former president for making "a considerable contribution" to the peaceful transfer of power to the Mujahideen guerrillas after 14 years of civil war in April 1992."In recognition of this, the secretary-general of the United Nations granted him and his companions protection in USMA's premises in Kabul for over four years,"
18168 he said."Throughout this time, and in particular in recent days, the United Nations have made strenuous efforts, for humanitarian reasons, to find a solution to the case of Dr Najibullah, with a view to enabling him to return safely to his family," Holl said.He said Najibullah had "formally abjured any
18168 political activity in the future."The bodies of Najibullah and his brother were seen by witnesses hanging from a concrete traffic-control post at the gates of the presidential palace as a crowd of more than a thousand people crowded around to watch."We killed him because he was the murderer of our
18168 people," Noor Hakmal, a Taleban commander who entered the city from Charasyab, south of Kabul, overnight, told Reuters.The Taleban entered Kabul in tanks and on foot overnight on Friday, meeting little resistance from government forces which had abandoned the city hours before.The Islamic movement announced just hours after the takeover
18168 that an interim six-man ruling council would run the country.</

18172 Afghanistan's former president Najibullah, executed in Kabul on Friday by Taleban Islamic militia after they seized the capital, was a relic of the Cold War.The man known as the "Butcher of Kabul" for his alleged proclivity for killing opponents, many by his own hand, was hanged and strung up from
18172 a traffic control post at the gates of the presidential palace.Najibullah, 49, had been a virtual prisoner at a U.N. compound in Kabul for 4-1/2 years when he was killed along with his brother, Shahpur Ahmadzai.In a visit to Kabul early this year, then-U.N. special envoy for Afghanistan Mahmoud Mestiri
18172 said he believed the former president should be allowed to go free."I hope some day things will be calm enough in this country that we could have Najibullah free again," he said. "He deserves to be free. I don't know if he was a good man, but he is a
18172 man of goodwill."But that was not to be. President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government, which had spared Najibullah's life and left a decision about his fate to the future, crumbled before the latest Taleban sweep through eastern Afghanistan.Najibullah was ousted on April 15, 1992, when the Islamic Mujahideen guerrilla forces closed in
18172 on Kabul after 14 years of civil war against a Soviet-backed communist government.The United Nations says he had offered to resign as part of a peace process to pave the way for general elections.In return, Najibullah was allowed to leave the country, but as he was driving to the airport
18172 he was stopped by Afghan army officers who had turned against him. He sought sanctuary in the U.N. compound, where officials felt obliged to take him in.It was meant to be a temporary arrangement, but he remained there as a leftover of the Cold War and something of an embarrassment
18172 for both the United Nations and the Afghan government that could not agree on what to do with him.His few visitors were from the United Nations or occasionally the Afghan government. He had not seen his wife or three daughters since his ouster, but had been making regular telephone calls
18172 to them in India, fondly hoping he would join them one day.The government said it believed it did not have the authority to release Najibullah, and that only a future government or parliament could decide his fate."This is a problem that the government has not created," then deputy foreign minister
18172 Abdur Rahim Ghafourzai said in April. "This is a problem the United Nations created, and it's up to the United Nations to find a solution to that problem."It seemed nobody was willing to take responsibility for what should happen to the man.The Rabbani government feared it could face a wave
18172 of criticism if it released Najibullah, a man whose critics say had a hand in the annihilation of hundreds of thousands during the civil war.Najibullah was elected president for seven years in 1987 by a traditional Loya Jirga (grand assembly) he had convened in Kabul. He was a diehard communist
18172 and a protege of then Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.He is credited by the United Nations for his part in the U.N.-brokered peace talks in Geneva under which Moscow pulled out more than 100,000 troops from Afghanistan in 1989 after a decade of fighting.But it is his role before and after
18172 this honeymoon period that Afghans hold against Najibullah.From late 1979 to 1985 he was head of the notorious Khad secret police that he built into a KGB-style organisation that operated by terror.Born in 1947 -- the exact date has never been made public -- Najibullah was at first hampered by
18172 his relative youth in a country where respect for the wisdom of elders is a strong tradition.Former schoolmates remember him as a devout Moslem -- Najibullah means "noble man of God" -- although he eagerly embraced the PDPA at Kabul University.For a while after taking office, Najibullah dropped the "ullah"
18172 from his name with its religious overtones, though he restored it when he became head of state.Najibullah enjoyed weightlifting, swimming, tennis and other sports in his university days. He was soft-spoken with penetrating brown eyes, but exuded dynamism and authority."He has an easy charm, but can suddenly change his manner
18172 from a relaxed pleasantness to cold, steel-like suspicion," an acquaintance once said about him.Najibullah was born into the powerful Ahmadzai clan of the Pashtun people, who make up about half Afghanistan's population. He was brought up in the Pakistani frontier city of Peshawar and in Kabul, although he regarded his
18172 family home town as Gardez, capital of the eastern province of Paktia.He attended high school in Kabul and qualified as a medical doctor in 1975 at Kabul University, where he devoted most of his student days to politics and was twice jailed.</

18173 troops launched a fresh offensive towards the town on Sunday after a lull of more than a month.The spokesman said more than 1,000 members of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) had launched two simultaneous counter-attacks from the west and the south of an army column advancing on Kilinochchi."Troops
18173 fought back valiantly, completely repulsing the attack although the terrorists used human wave tactics," he said. Suicide bombers set off blasts near the troops who fired on
18173 them."Ground troops confirmed over 450 terrorists were killed at both locations of the counter-attacks and over 300 wounded," he said. "Seventy-five army personnel including five officers were killed. Ten officers and 146 soldiers were wounded."He said troops had recovered 138 dead rebel bodies of terrorists. Most of the bodies were
18173 women.This brings the toll for LTTE dead and wounded to well over 1,000 in five days of the renewed war, according to the military. It puts the army's death toll at 146 and the number of wounded at just over 300.A military officer told Reuters on Thursday at least 100
18173 Sri Lankan soldiers were killed in a rebel pre-dawn raid but the spokesman said only 75 had been confirmed dead.It was not possible to verify conflicting claims of the warring parties as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.The ministry spokesman said the army could not advance
18173 further towards Kilinochchi at present after Thursday's fighting.The LTTE, fighting a 13-year war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, said in their daily radio broadcast on Thursday that they were engaging the troops with "increased fierceness".The government says more than 50,000
18173 people have died in the conflict since it began in 1983.The armed forces have targeted Kilinochchi since the Tigers overran the military's northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.</

18197 California Gov. Pete Wilson signed controversial legislation Friday to create a $10.5 billion publicly run authority to sell earthquake insurance to homeowners in the state.Wilson, a Republican, said the legislation should help to end California's insurance availability crisis for homeowners seeking earthquake coverage."Earthquakes will always be a fact of life
18197 in California, but homeowners no longer must risk a devastating, unrecoverable loss because they couldn't get insurance," Wilson said.The legislation will implement the so-called California Earthquake Authority. The proposal was approved by the legislature in August after months of heated debate.The privately financed, publicly managed authority will provide insurance coverage
18197 for earthquake damage to residential property owners, condominium owners, mobile-home owners and renters.The authority's earthquake policy would be limited to dwelling structures only, with a 15 percent deductible. Its policies would be written and serviced by private insurers and their agents, but the authority would issue the policy and pay
18197 the earthquake claims.California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said the authority should begin to sell policies by Dec. 1."Gov. Wilson's signature on legislation creating the California Earthquake Authority means that California's economic recovery will proceed on course -- uninterrupted by the evaporation of homeowners' insurance and the paralysing effect that would
18197 have on the state's real estate market," Quackenbush said in a statement.As a public entity, the authority will be tax-exempt, enabling it to build up enough reserves to cover major earthquake disasters.The authority will be capable of funding $10.5 billion through a combination of sources, including insurer contributions, policyholder premiums,
18197 the capital markets, and reinsurance.Quackenbush maintains that the authority would, in its first year of operation, have enough resources to pay all claims from an earthquake more than twice as destructive as the devastating 1994 Northridge quake.Wilson said mammoth natural disasters like the Northridge quake create a magnitude of loss
18197 that can plunge an insurance company into insolvency.Such disasters, coupled with California's requirement that homeowner policyholders be offered earthquake insurance, have severely restricted the availability of these policies, Wilson said.The California Department of Insurance estimated that about 99 percent of California insurers had restricted or stopped selling homeowner and earthquake
18197 insurance, making it difficult for homebuyers to obtain mortgages."The CEA will provide much-needed relief for the insurance availablility shortage," Wilson said.</

18199 Cadillac Fleetwood cars which will be phased out by the end of this year.An extended cab truck has a longer cab than the traditional pickup, and comes with a rear seat.Although the shift is viewed as a positive one for GM, it will not be for workers -- GM plans

18199 or be transferred to other plants.All workers at the plant will be placed on temporary layoff for a few months in the early part of 1997.The announcement marks the first time GM has identified the specific trucks it intends to build at the plant, which is undergoing a $260 million
18199 conversion project.Analysts said the plant ultimately will be capable of building 150,000 to 175,000 trucks a year, but shortages of components will hold the facility's production below that.However, GM faces stiff competition in the large sport/utility market, particularly from Ford Motor Co.'s new Expedition vehicle, said Michael Robinet, an automotive
18199 analyst with CSM Forecasting in Farmington Hills, Mich."I think initially the plant will be busy, but the long-term prospects could be called into question," Robinet said. 18199 third door. GM now builds extended-cab, three-door pickups only in Oshawa, Ontario.The plant also will become the sole source for a new police version of the Chevrolet Tahoe. 18199 of a long-term plan that GM has to boost truck production to more than 50 percent of its total North American capacity. For the first six months of 1996, trucks made up about 45 percent of GM's output.</

18220 London will retain its position as an important hub of the insurance industry, despite the recent difficulties experienced by Lloyds of London, the chairman of industry association LIRMA said."London is not dead, it is doing well and will continue to do so provided its constituents do not think parochially and
18220 work together to increase the size of the cake," Philip Marcell said in a speech delivered in New York.LIRMA, the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association, represents many of the international insurers and reinsurers operating in London.Marcell, who is also chairman of Unionamerica Insurance Company Ltd, was addressing a
18220 Mealey's conference on 'First Reactions to the New Reinsurance Market.' A copy of his speech was made available in London."With Lloyd's reconstruction and renewal now moving ahead, and the desire of the London market as a whole to co-operate in a way so as to produce the best framework for
18220 the production and underwriting business at the lowest cost, I see no reason why London should not continue to be a key market for wholesale insurance and reinsurance in the future," he said.Modern systems, ease of access, London's overall infrastructure and geographical concentration were the benefits offered to insurers by
18220 the London market, he added.However, Marcell said that the global market had changed and the expansion of reinsurance companies in Europe, the U.S. and particularly Bermuda could not be ignored."(Bermuda) does produce significant amounts of capacity for what I would call commodity products. We also see increased capacity in regional
18220 markets in Asia and elsewhere.""London cannot expect to be as dominant as in the past; but I do think it will continue to be dominant in speciality lines, particularly where real innovation is called for, rather than simply price cutting."Marcell said he did not expect capital markets to take over
18220 the reinsurance industry, which some observers believe will not be able to cope with increasing demand."While I accept that there might be timing gaps, the reinsurance industry has always managed to increase its capacity to cope with demand."He also said he saw a future for niche and regional reinsurers alongside
18220 the industry giants."You can survive at lower levels of capital if you are a specialist company with a history of expertise and can focus your writings accordingly."Marcell put the minimum capital requirements of a niche reinsurer at $125-$500 million, but added that regional companies in developing markets could exist with
18220 a lower capital base.-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769</

18273 work together on a case-by-case basis to get this program underway."My guess is that between now and the end of the year we will have our first cases," Wolfensohn said. Wolfensohn added, "I think we're very close to reaching a positive and productive agreement that will allow us to proceed
18273 immediately on specific cases."He said he understood that a consensus was emerging at the Paris Club of official creditors that would allow the debt initiative to proceed on a "case-by-case basis."Asked about whether the Paris Club had agreed to forgive 80 percent of its loans to specific countries, Wolfensohn said
18273 he did not know whether it was 80 percent, but he did not think it was 90 percent as the bank and IMF had been recommending.The bank has already committed a $500 million war chest to the program, and Wolfensohn repeated that he was prepared to recommend to the World
18273 Bank board that it commit a total $2 billion over the years ahead.</

18287 the committee, and Patrick Leahy, the ranking Democrat, did not address the forex issue."We'll probably have Treasury Amendment language when we reintroduce the bill in the next Congress," said Senate Agriculture Committee spokesman Andy Fischer. 18287 foreign exchange market from oversight by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.But ambiguities have arisen concerning the scope of the amendment and the Supreme Court will hear a case on the issue next term.Fischer denied a report in the Wall Street Journal on Friday that the Senators would wait until after
18287 the Supreme Court delivers a ruling on the current Treasury amendment, which is not expected to be handed down until next summer."I doubt that that is the case," Fischer said. Lugar, an Indiana Republican, and Leahy, a Vermont Democrat, had hoped to address the forex problem in the bill they
18287 introduced this year.But the CFTC and the Treasury Department were unable to reach a consensus recommendation over the summer on language for such a provision.Lugar and Leahy had asked for a recommendation by September, but officials at the two agencies recently told the committee they needed more time. 18296 The new chairwoman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said she has significant concerns about some portions of a Congressional proposal to amend U.S. commodities law.Senators Richard Lugar and Patrick Leahy introduced a bill earlier this month that would make a dozen changes in the Commodity Exchange Act, the primary
18296 U.S. law governing futures trading."We are examining the provisions," Brooksley Born said in an interview with Reuters. "There are some that cause me some significant concern and others that don't." In particular, Born raised concerns about a proposal intended to speed the approval process for new futures contracts.Under the present
18296 law, the CFTC reviews all new contracts and generally grants approval for trading within a few months.The Lugar-Leahy bill would create a legal presumption that new contracts should be approved and allow trading to begin in 10 business days unless the CFTC objects. If an objection is raised, the contract
18296 can trade in another 15 days unless the CFTC institutes proceedings to disapprove. "One provision that does cause me concern, because I think it may be unworkable from a regulatory point of view, is the provison that amends the contract designation process," Born said. "It seems quite cumbersome and perhaps
18296 unworkable."But Born said the CFTC is still evaluating the legislation and welcomed the opportunity to reassess current laws."I think it's important for regulatory agencies to review their governing statute periodically to make sure that it gives them the power that they need, that it stays up to date," said Born,
18296 an attorney at Arnold &amp; Porter before being sworn in last month as the seventh chair of the CFTC. The Senators, however, are unlikely to back down on the contract designation provision, a spokesman for the Agriculture Committee said on Friday."We have our bill and it is a well thought
18296 through position," spokesman Andy Fischer said reacting to Born's comment. "There's certainly not going to be any change in it."The bill is not expected to pass this year, but will be revived in 1997. The bill and a measure in the House of Representatives proposed by Rep. Charles Schumer would
18296 give the CFTC additional power over foreign futures contracts that accept delivery in the United States. The senate bill would grant additonal power to get information about delivery warehouses, while the Schumer bill would subject foreign contracts to U.S. rules in some cases. Most of Sumitomo Corp's trading was done
18296 on the London Metal Exchange but copper was kept at a U.S. warehouse.Born signaled that the CFTC might ask for additional information gathering power."One point that is raised by both bills os whether we have sufficient information gathering powers from U.S. warehouses of foreign exchanges in a situation where we
18296 don't have an ongoing formal investigation," Born said. In such cases, the CFTC lacks subponea power, Born noted. "That is an area we have been looking at and we'll try to determine whether we have sufficient regulatory powers."Of allegations that the LME was not forthcoming with the CFTC last year,
18296 Born said she was not familiar with the "day to day requests" made of the LME. But by "late last year, we became very pleased with the amount of information sharing."At that time, information from the LME was forwarded to the CFTC from United Kingdom securities regulators, she said. The
18296 CFTC is "pleased with the level of cooperation since then," she said.--Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312</

18314 A.H. Belo Corp 's acquisition of Providence Journal Co will give it a better geographical and network balance in broadcasting and a firm spot in the strong Seattle market, Chief Financial Officer Michael Perry said.Perry said the acqusition was mainly aimed at boosting Belo's broadcast holdings and that its seven
18314 television stations fit well with the Providence Journal's nine stations. "It gives us a geographic balance in very high growth areas and also gives us a balance among the networks," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.The $1.5 billion buy-out combines Belo's seven network-affiliated stations -- three CBS, three ABC,
18314 and one UPN -- with Providence Journal's portfolio of five NBC affiliates, two Fox, one ABC and one CBS.Belo's audience reach, which will grow from 8 percent to 12.3 percent, will be equally balanced among the big three networks, Perry said, adding that other buyouts were possible. "We have been
18314 looking for more stations and would not rule out that possibility. On a proforma basis, the company still has a pretty strong balance sheet and has capacity for further acquisitions."Of Providence Journal's stations, Belo is most excited about KING-TV, the NBC affiliate in Seattle. "In terms of demographics and growth
18314 profile, it is a very good market with a tremendous amount of immigration to the market," Perry said.Control of KING-TV will force Belo to divest of its own KIRO-TV, a UPN affiliate, in Seattle. Perry said Belo has already received offers priced at well above what it paid for KIRO-TV
18314 but did not necessarily want a straight sale."What we'd love to do is trade that station for one of the more strategically important stations elsewhere and broaden the broadcast portfolio," he said.The Providence Journal has the right to operate another Seattle station under a local management agreement, and also owns
18314 NorthWest Cable News, a regional 24-hour cable channel available in about 1.4 million homes in the Pacific Northwest. Perry said the acquisition would probably not carry any sizeable one-off charge and that the combined company would give Belo greater bargaining power to buy news print and broadcast programming at cheaper
18314 rates.He said the acquisition will be "quite dilutive" to earnings per share primarily because of the amortization of $1.2 billion in goodwill resulting from the deal.But Perry said cash flow per share, which is "far less diluted", would be a more accurate way of tracking performance going forward. Under the
18314 acqusition deal, which must still be approved by shareholders and the Federal Communications Commission to transfer station licenses, Providence Journal shareholders would receive $12.33 in cash and 0.5333 shares of Belo series A common stock for each share of Providence Journal.Perry said he expects the deal to be approved and
18314 finalized in the first half of 1997.While the rationale behind the acquisition was focused on the broadcast side, Perry insisted the newspaper publishing side of the alliance would not be neglected."At the core of our business is the Dallas Morning News, at the core of theirs is the Providence Journal-Bulletin.
18314 And that is an important part of this merger as well," he said.</

18324 The G24 group of developing countries from Africa, Asia and Latin America will voice their objections to industrialized nations' veiled protectionist measures, according to a draft report.The report obtained by Reuters was prepared for the Friday and Saturday meetings of delegates from the G24 as part of the annual meetings
18324 of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.In the draft, the G24, which includes countries as diverse as India, Brazil and the Philippines, complained that Europe's unemployment problems are often blamed on trade liberalization, prompting pressure for protectionism. "The advocacy of protectionism was particularly harmful when it was not
18324 even presented as such, but disguised under calls for environmental security, human rights or higher labor standards in the exporting countries," it said.During the April meeting of the IMF and the World Bank the G24 voiced similar complaints after a report on the role of multilateral development banks that stressed
18324 a growing tendency to evaluate borrowers domestic policies.The developing countries acknowledged the banks' efforts to help them reduce poverty, but they balked at the idea of lenders becoming sources of policy on domestic issues such as good governance.-- IMF newsroom (202) 898-8351.</

18328 Leasing has become a major industry in emerging markets, growing from around 15 billion in 1988 to 44 billion in 1994, and is set to grow further, a report from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) said.The Washington-based IFC said leasing, whereby a lessee uses an asset and pays rental on
18328 it to a lessor who owns the asset, was a mature industry in most high-income economies. But by 1994, the latest year for which global data is available, middle and low income countries accounted for five out of the 20 largest leasing markets.The IFC said the most spectacular increase had
18328 been in South Korea, which started leasing in 1975 and by 1994 was the world's fifth largest market.Market penetration (leasing as share of private investment) more than doubled in both low and middle income countries between 1988 and 1994, the report, released this week said.Leasing arrangements now account for 11
18328 percent of the financing of capital equipment in middle income countries, up from just four percent in 1988.The IFC said cross country comparisons were difficult because of different regulatory and fiscal environments.But in 1994 Asia accounted for 28 percent of the world leasing market, having overtaken Europe in 1993, which
18328 had 25 percent of market share. Latin's America's share increased fivefold to 4.2 percent in 1994 from 0.8 percent in 1989.The IFC said Africa's share had also grown to 1.3 percent of the global total, but it was made up mainly by South Africa and Morocco, which had both been
18328 among the top 50 leasing markets every year since 1989.The IFC said it would continue to promote leasing because it benefited small and medium sized companies in developing countries and worked "even in risky countries with poor access to international capital".The arrangement had also "addressed an important unmet demand and
18328 attracted borrowers away from tradiitonal financial products such as bank loans", it said.The report said the IFC will advise governments, locate international technical partners, invest in new leasing companies, help leasing companies raise finance, promote cross-border leasing and "big-ticket" leasing for sectors such as infrastructure, among other measures.-- Caroline Allen,
18328 London newsroom +44 171 542 6414</
18329 The International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private finance wing of the World Bank, said its future work in developing countries will focus on mobilising domestic savings and promoting new fund vehicles.As part of a report on investment funds in emerging markets released this week, the Washington-based IFC said it would
18329 help promote pension funds, mutual funds and local pools for venture capital funds as a way of encouraging domestic savings."The IFC will also work closely with the World Bank to support pension reforms," the report said.It will identify technical partners and invest in private pension fund managers in order to
18329 help set high standards for pension fund management.Private equity funds and venture capital funds, particularly in new sectors and new countries would help add depth and liquidity to markets, drawing in new domestic and foreign investors, the IFC said.For "pre-emerging" markets, which have not yet benefited from foreign portfolio investment,
18329 the IFC will help set up portfolio funds to attract capital. The IFC said Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Cambodia were immediate targets. More sophisticated investors who want access to emerging markets returns but a lower risk profile have been attracted by index funds, and the IFC said it would
18329 continue to roll out index funds in more regions."As well as promoting specific funds, this work will involve adding new markets to its Emerging Markets Database," the report said. "Indeed, several countries are asking IFC to include them in the coverage, as this ensures automatic foreign portfolio investment from index
18329 funds."The IFC noted that as bond markets in developing countries deepen, there would be opportunities to promote funds investing in private corporate debt.But it said its efforts would "depend to a significant extent on liberalisation efforts by governments (including those not directly related to funds, such as privatisation and private

18334 The Belgian government has decided banks will have to pay a 0.06 percent tax on the total amount outstanding in savings book accounts, a government source said on Friday.It added that banks would be allowed to book the tax -- like all indirect taxes -- as a cost. The measures
18334 is part of the 1997 budget. Earlier, another government source said there would be a 0.6 percent tax on savings book turnover."It is a tax of 0.06 percent and it will be due on the full amount of savings books accounts as shown on the liabilities side of banks' balance
18334 sheets," said the second source, who was involved in drafting the measure.A Belgian Banking Association report showed that in 1995 the sector had 2,832 billion francs worth of savings books.At 0.06 percent, this would represent a gross cost of 1.69 billion francs for the sector. Considering that it would be
18334 deducted as a cost and given the 40.2 percent corporate tax rate, the net cost to the sector would just over one billion francs.The Belgian banking sector made a 49.1 billion franc total net profit in 1994, the most recent date for which sector data are available. In that year,
18334 the seven top banks earned a total of 34.4 billion francs.Savings books are one of Belgium's most popular savings instrument. The first 50,000 francs of interest income earned on them is exempt from withholding tax.The exemption is limited to one account per person, but many Belgians open several savings book
18334 accounts and fail to declare this to the taxman.The second government source said that measures would be taken to ensure that banks did not pass on the tax to their customers by lowering the interest rates on savings books, but he declined to be more specific.Belgian media have said that
18334 the banking sector would have to contribute five billion francs to the 1997 budget.This could indicate that a planned 0.3 percent tax on physical delivery of securities -- to be paid by investors -- would cost more than the savings book tax.-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287

18335 The Belgian government on Friday reached agreement on a 1997 budget which should pave the way to European economic and monetary union without damaging consumer confidence.A government source told Reuters on Friday that an 80 billion franc austerity package will cut Belgium's state deficit to 2.9 percent in 1997 from
18335 an estimated 3.0 percent in 1996."There is a full agreement on the budget. We will reach the 2.9 percent target without hurting the average consumer too much," the source said.Cabinet aides will hammer out the final details of the package over the weekend, after which a full cabinet session of
18335 the centre-left government is set to approve it on Monday.Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will present the full text of the 1997 budget to the Belgian parliament on Tuesday at 1500 local (1300 GMT).Dehaene has shied away from raising the already record-high taxes on labour income and from a radical
18335 reform of the country's general social security system.On the taxation side, the 1997 budget hits hard at unhealthy habits -- such as smoking, drinking and driving a car.On the spending side, Dehaene has made a first stab a reforming Belgium's pension system, which -- in light of the rapid ageing
18335 of the population -- is a time bomb under the country's already troubled state finances.Taxes -- mainly indirect -- will rise by 30 billion francs.Taxes on petrol will be raised by one franc per litre in October and another franc in January. Taxes on beer will rise by one franc
18335 per 25-centilitre bottle, on spirits by 12 francs per 75-centilitre bottle, the source said.The full council of ministers on Friday morning approved the higher excise duties by executive decree. Most will take effect as of October.The investment world will also have to contribute.Retail investors will have to pay a 0.3
18335 percent tax on physical delivery of securities by banks and brokerages."A small price for anonymity," one analyst said. For tax reasons, many Belgians avoid holding registered securities and prefer holding bearer stocks and bonds in their safes.The banks would have to pay a 0.06 percent tax on the amount outstanding
18335 in savings books accounts, the tax-free regulated savings accounts which are Belgium's most popular savings instrument.It was not immediately clear how turnover will be defined, but Belgian media estimated the total cost to the Belgian banking sector at five billion francs.The source also said that 50 billion francs of spending
18335 cuts had been decided in the social security sector.The most visible measure is a gradual increase of women's retirement age to 65 years from 60 over a 13-year period, although this will have little impact on the 1997 budget.The government has also decided on a two percent tax on all
18335 early retirement pensions.Most other measures in the social security sector are highly technical. They include a reduction of family allowances for teenagers, a reduction in unemployment benefits for older people and some targetted measures in the health sector.-- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710</
18336 The recent fall in interest rates puts pressure on pension contributions to rise, Kari Puro, CEO of pension insurer Ilmarinen said on Friday.In funding pensions, the ratio between contributions and investment return is determined by a minimum required rate of return set by the ministy of social and health affairs
18336 and next year, this will have to be lowered from the current 6.00 percent due to the fall in interest rates, Puro said."Sometime next year this level can't be supported anymore," Puro told Reuters in an interview."But exactly when and by how much, I can't say yet," he added.Of the
18336 six percent return required to fund the system, five percentage points worth of revenue is added to cover future liabilities and one percentage point is paid to today's pensioners, so if the rate were lowered to 5.00 percent, current contributions would rise correspondingly."That would mean a 1.2 percentage point increase
18336 in the rate of contributions," Puro said, adding that this would by law be split equally between employers and employees.So while the government on one side is cutting income taxes next year by about two percentage points, the pension system may up the tax wedge on the other side by
18336 1.2 percentage points, about half of which would be paid by wage-earners.The total annual wage sum in Finland is about 240 billion markka. A 0.6 percentage point increase in taxpayers pension contribution would reduce disposable income by 1.4 billion markka.Although the required rate of return is set by the ministry
18336 at the pension funds' requests, it follows an agreement between the pension insurers and the labour market organisations, which always oppose lowering it since that ups contributions, Puro said.However, the protests become meaningless if returns on near risk-free financial instruments do not meet the requirement.Necessity will ultimately rule since, by
18336 law, insurers must meet the minimun rate requirement."Say the (labour market) organisations what they will, the companies must apply for a rate they can fulfil," he said.On the other hand, pension insurers can't boost returns by choosing riskier instruments since their working capital provides an insufficient buffer against more volatile
18336 asset values, Puro said.The system was created in the 1960s when real interest rates were about or below zero and the bulk of pension funds were invested in fully collateralised loans back to the companies at set interest rates. In that environment no buffers were needed.Puro chairs a committe appointed
18336 by the ministry of social and health affairs last year to find ways to adapt the system to the new environment where risk is an ever-present element in investment.This is not easy, Puro said."The problems are that lending back is not competitive with interest rates, and with the required full
18336 collateralisation, government bonds are now the only possible instrument ... and we lack working capital to invest in shares," he said.He noted that the only sources for more working capital as a buffer for risks are in the system itself -- the funds and the contributors.Unless, of course, investment income
18336 could rise, but this would again increase risks which would require more capital which would require higher investment income which would ...Puro said that any hopes for a massive flow of funds to the stockmarket from pension funds are in vain."In the best possible outcome, if we could find a
18336 way to increase working capital ... the amount of shares which is currently six billion to seven billion markka could double in ten years," he said.Compared to the total market capitalisation of shares on the Helsinki Stock Exchange -- 242.9 billion markka at end-August -- that would be marginal, he
18336 said.-- Helsinki Newsroom +358 - 0 - 680 50 242</

18341 Recognising the power that speculators have to create currency turmoil, European Union authorities are looking at how to minimise the risks in the run-up to the launch of a common currency.Past currency upheavals, such as in September 1992 when Britain and Italy were forced out of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism,
18341 have focused attention on how to smooth the transition towards economic and monetary union (EMU).At issue is the critical period between early 1998, when the EU will decide which countries qualify for EMU, and January 1, 1999 when the common euro currency is launched. Then the currencies of EMU members
18341 will become "irrevocably" fixed.Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of Europe's future central bank -- the European Monetary Institute -- has tried to defuse market speculation about conversion rates by arguing they should fixed by averaging past rates between EMU currencies. The length of the averaging process -- six months, a year, or
18341 two years -- would still have to be decided.It is an idea which is gaining ground among EU officials.As one EU monetary official put it: "If they know in advance what the calculation will be, it's more likely that speculation would be constructive ... converging rather than diverging."The averaging technique
18341 could be announced to financial markets when EMU members are chosen.While the Maastricht Treaty that governs the single currency process allows rates to be fixed only on January 1, 1999 -- announcing the method would dispel market uncertainty.The issue was informally discussed by some of those attending a meeting of
18341 EU finance ministers in Dublin last weekend.Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt told reporters that Lamfalussy had proposed announcing an averaging approach at the same time as a decision is taken on EMU participants.While the matter is not currently under discussion by either the European Commission or the EU's Monetary Committee,
18341 some officials predict it will win support."Our own thinking is that there is not substantial opposition," said one official, adding that the only ones who might object are countries which might want to engage in a "last-minute devaluation" ahead of the start of EMU.While the plan could go a long
18341 way towards reducing speculative activity on the foreign exchange markets, some say an announcement could signal that central banks of EMU nations were less than prepared to defend a given set of parity rates.Christopher Taylor, an economist at the National Institute of Economic Research in London, said there were basically
18341 two options for dealing with the key period before the single currency is launched."The issue is between a pre-announcement of the fixed set of rates and some sort of formula," Taylor said.A third option, the one laid out in the treaty, would be to accept market rates on January 1,
18341 1999. Few, however, seem prepared to go that route.Under the first approach, EMU members would announce the central parity rates between currencies they were ready to defend, creating a sort of de facto monetary union.Assuming a close degree of convergence, the parity rates might be very near to those which
18341 currently exist.This would be a bold step, and some say it would put the German Bundesbank in a very uncomfortable spot. Essentially, the central bank would have to be prepared to engage in unlimited intervention.An alternative would be Lamfalussy's plan, which Taylor says lets governments off the hook a bit
18341 but might also signal to markets that something could go wrong."The question is still what if there is some unforeseen event," he added. "I think it boils down to whether there would be some exogenous occurence."A sharp rise in U.S. interest rates, a war, or some other form of external
18341 shock would put EU monetary authorities on the defensive. An averaging technique could make management of a crisis a bit easier, say analysts.</

18352 The leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) said on Friday that an independent Scotland could become the economic "tiger" of Europe and cited the growth rates now seen in Ireland.SNP chief Alex Salmond, who was delivering a keynote speech to the party's annual conference in Inverness later on Friday,
18352 said Ireland would in three years' time be more prosperous per head of population than England."On current growth levels, Ireland will become more prosperous than the UK and Scotland by the year 2000. They have already overtaken the Welsh," Salmond said in a statement."But compared to Scotland, Ireland has next
18352 to no resources. They have used their imagination and human resources in order to drive their economy forward."With the freedom of independence, Scotland could combine our own talents with the nation's abundant resources, and make Scotland the 'tiger economy' of Europe," Salmond said.Salmond based his forecast on research carried out
18352 for the party by the House of Commons library in London.This concluded that Irish gross domestic product per head was projected "to have exceeded that of Wales in 1995 and will exceed that of Scotland, and the UK as a whole, by the year 2000", provided Ireland maintained its recent
18352 high growth rates.The SNP maintains that an independent Scotland would be the 21st richest country in the world. Some economists think Salmond's forecasts for the Irish economy are several years too optimistic.The SNP, holding its last annual conference before a general election that must be held by next May, are
18352 enjoying strong support of 29 percent at the polls, largely due to a series of Scottish policy gaffes by Labour, their main rivals.But the party was still struggling to contain the crisis that erupted after a senior party figure compared the opposition Labour party's Scottish affairs spokesman to a World
18352 War Two Nazi collaborator.SNP deputy policy chief Alex Neil used a podium speech to liken Labour's Scottish spokesman George Robertson to Lord Haw Haw, the Nazi broadcaster who was hanged for treason in 1946.Labour called for Neil to resign, and under pressure from the SNP leadership he apologised for any
18352 personal slight to Robertson.Margaret Ewing, an SNP member of the British parliament, sought to play down the gaffe, accusing the media of looking for splits in party ranks. She described Neil's remarks as "a joke that maybe misfired".</

18356 on Friday could topple bond prices and dent the dollar."The risk is that if we do get strong numbers it is going to leave the Treasury market vulnerable," said Huw Roberts."And if the Treasuries get a jolt, that could well feed back into European markets," said Roberts, a European bond
18356 strategist at NatWest Capital markets in London.Analysts polled by Reuters are forecasting that 192,000 jobs will have been added in September versus 250,000 in August, but as ever the predictions span a wide range.Patrick Mange, head of research at Deutsche Bank in Paris said he expected a lower number --
18356 around 175,000 -- but said the key figure would be the unemployment rate. "We are forecasting that will be slightly higher at 5.3 percent," he said. Reuters' poll has a forecast of 5.2 percent versus 5.1 percent in August.Earlier in the week, the NAPM index will set the tone for
18356 the U.S. until the payroll takes over. 18357 The number of petrol stations in Britain is set to fall by about a third in the next five years in the face of fierce price competition but the decline will be far slower than previously expected, a senior oil company official said on Friday."There were about 15,900 last year...I
18357 think we'll come down to about 10,000 in the next four to five years," said Steve Theede, managing director and chief executive officer of Conoco Ltd, a unit of U.S. oil major Conoco Inc.Conoco is itself a unit of Dupont Co."But the rate of these closures will not be nearly
18357 as fast as most people had previously forecast... We will have the same number of closures at the end of the day but it's a question of pace," he told Reuters in an interview at the inauguration of a new waste-water treatment plant at Conoco's Humber refinery.Many petrol retailers and
18357 oil companies in Britain have been hit in the pockets since the launch by Esso last year of its PriceWatch campaign, a move many observers said was intended to shake a lot of the smaller operators out of the market."The agreements most of these small operators have with their suppliers
18357 give some kind of a guideline margin," Theede said."The suppliers seem to be taking more of a hit in order to allow these small operators to continue to work...Some suppliers are concerned about losing more volume and more market share."I think the question is how long the suppliers are prepared
18357 to take this disproportionate hit on margins," he added.Conoco's 170,000 barrels per day Humber refinery, which Theede said was already ranked by finance house Salomon Bros as the most profitable refinery in Europe recently completed upgrading work to improve its margins further.An 85 million stg vacuum unit started up a
18357 few weeks ago at the refinery which will allow one crude unit, responsible for around one third of the refinery's total feedstock throughput, to process North Sea high acidity crudes.It is the only unit in Europe which can handle a diet of 100 percent high acidity crude, which trades at
18357 a discount of around $1.50 to Brent."We enjoy around 65 to 75 percent of that $1.50 in terms of margins," Theede said.But he declined to be precise as to how much Conoco's margins had improved overall as a result of this year's upgrading work which included changes to the refinery's
18357 distillate output to comply with tighter EU requirements on sulphur content.Theede did not foresee any significant changes in the next few years to the British demand pattern for his refinery's product."I don't see any significant changes in the next few years but we might see the recent decline in gasoline
18357 demand come to a halt and the astronomical diesel demand growth of the last five years begin to moderate a bit," he said."We have seen something of an uptick in terms of demand for gasoline, something like 0.6 percent, compared with the four percent that we've been going down in
18357 the last two years."This may be the result of conversion to diesel cars slowing down firstly because the UK government equalised duty between diesel and unleaded petrol in the Budget two years ago and secondly because over the last year the whole impression that diesel is more environmentally friendly than
18357 petrol has been severely challenged," he told Reuters.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930</

18360 The European currency unit caught the crest of this week's tidal wave of optimism about a punctual start for European monetary union and rode to its highest level in almost two years against a sinking mark.Profit-taking emerged to sweep the Ecu off these highs earlier today but interest in the
18360 unit's potential remains high.The Ecu's breather was also related to talk of European cental bank sales of Ecu for marks, which may be aimed at preventing an undesirable wipeout of the German currency.However, while the Ecu's high watermark may have been set for now, a clearing of the mist surrounding
18360 the Ecu's legal status still makes it one of the more attractive so-called "convergence trades" left to play, said analysts."The Ecu/mark move has been an interesting trade this week and has outperformed most of the currencies on the EMU story," said Andrew Chaveriat, analyst at Banque Paribas.The Ecu/mark rate rose
18360 two percent since early August to a peak of 1.9125 marks on Thursday, its highest level since October 1994. At 1330 GMT, it was at 1.9070/75."If you buy in the convergence trade idea, many rates were already quite expensive," said Chaveriat. "Rather than pick a horse that's already run too
18360 quickly, the Ecu looked better value."Analysts said a renewed scramble for convergence has intensified the hunt for best-value buys, based on the increasingly entrenched belief in a 1999 start for EMU.Convergence trades bet on locking into relatively high, but falling, yields in times of reduced currency risk.The Ecu, which originated
18360 as a basket of the 12 original European Union currencies and was for years proposed as the eventual single currency, has also been given added buoyancy of its own in recent weeks.It now looks almost certain that there will be a legal guarantee to exchange existing Ecus for the new
18360 single currency, or euro, on a one-for-one basis, analysts said.European finance ministers meeting in Dublin last weekend agreed that clarification of legal issues relating to the single currency, such as the guarantee of one-for-one conversion of the existing Ecu contracts with the new euro, should be a priority.As a result,
18360 they said Article 235 of the Maastricht Treaty will allow such urgent legal decisions, which cannot wait until the EMU launch to be clarified, to be dealt with providing there is unanimity among the 15 EU states. The European Commission is due to put forward a paper on the issue
18360 in mid-October for formal adoption at the EU summit in December.Growing optimism about EMU and the rising hopes for a prompt legal clarification of the Ecu's status lowered the discount with which market-traded Ecu trades to its theoretical value, derived from the 12 constituent units. 18391 Australian and Canadian government bonds, revelling in steady U.S. interest rates, have further to gain against Treasuries, analysts said on Friday.But with the recent rally in both markets looking strained, investors will have to move fast, particularly if U.S. economic growth decelerates in the second half of 1996 as the
18391 Federal Reserve predicts, they said."The Australian market may have a little bit further to go, partly because there's more yield enhancement there," said Stephen Hannah, head of research at IBJ in London."There also seems to be a fair degree of stability in the currency despite it having failed to push
18391 through the US$0.80 mark," he said.Australian and Canadian bonds have outstripped their dollar bloc cousin all summer as the central banks in each country sliced interest rates while the Fed held fast.The spread between the yields on 10-year Australian and U.S. bonds has shrunk to around 117 basis points from
18391 260 at the beginning of April. The Canada/U.S. gap has crunched to around 50 basis point from about 120 in the same time.Hannah said while wage pressures may begin to surface in Australia, the underlying inflation picture remains benign. Third quarter inflation data due at the end of October could
18391 provide the trigger for a 50 basis point cut from the 7.00 percent cash rate, he said."I think the spread may well test the 100 basis point level...in the next one to three months," Hannah said. "It's possible it could go below that if there are signs of exchange rate
18391 stability," he said.The Australian dollar has failed to break decisively through US$0.80 cents in three attempts in May, June and early September but it has not recoiled. It was quoted at US$0.79 at 1122 GMT.Hannah was not as positive for Canadian bonds, simply because they have hurtled ahead so far
18391 so fast."I would very much doubt whether it would trade much below 50 basis points despite the absence of a Fed move and continued speculation about a further cut in Canada," he said.Michael Burke, bond strategist at Citibank in London, took the opposite view, favouring Canadian over Australian bonds.He said
18391 the Canadian central bank could cut interest rates further, flaunting its renewed independence with monetary policy against a steadfast U.S. The call rate currently stands at 3.75-4.25 percent.Buffering a bright spread outlook was Canada's sparkling export performance which will allow it to continue in its rigorous deficit cutting programme, Burke
18391 said. Canada shipped a record C$22.51 billion worth of goods to the world in July, helped by a surge in lumber and auto part exports to the United States."Market investors are very bullish partly for reasons of external accounts and I think that's justified," said Burke.He said the Canada/U.S. spread
18391 could get as narrow as 35 basis points in the short term but if the U.S. economy begins to slow, Canadian exports will slow as well.It is this scenario that Stephen Lewis, director of research at London Bond Broking, favours. He said beyond the next month, Treasuries will begin to
18391 win back ground."I think we are going to see some deceleration of growth coming through in the second half data," he said. Australian and Canadian data was likely to show a pickup."These markets which have been at the extreme favourable end of their trading ranges relative to U.S. Treasuries, are
18391 probably going to revert to a more normal relationship," he said. Lewis expects the Canada/T-note spread to spring to 75 basis points by the end of October and the Australin/T-note spread to 140 by the end of the year.-- International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176</
