18409 Gilt futures shot higher on Friday, reversing sessions of underperformance while core European bonds could post only modest gains, dealers said.The December gilt future was trading at 108-31 at 0930 GMT, up 16/32 on the day and just below a 109-02 contract high set earlier in the session.The gilt/Bund spread
18409 shot in to 171 basis points from 177 late on Thursday. At times this week, it has widened beyond 180."Gilts have underperformed over the past couple of weeks and are playing catch-up," said Jonathan York, futures broker at Cater Allen. "There's quite a bit of upside here."At the short end
18409 of the market, short sterling futures also found a new lease of life.The December contract gained three basis points to 94.04, the March future rose four to 93.90 and the June contract leapt seven basis points to 93.66.Looking further out, 1998 and 1999 contracts leapt by 14 or 15 basis
18409 points. But analysts said this did not reflect a long-term reappraisal of British interest rate prospects."Short sterling has purely been dragged up by the gilt," said Peter Osler, economist at GNI. "I think it has gone a bit too far."Economists said gilts had suffered in the aftermath of last weekend's
18409 meeting of European Union leaders in Ireland.EU officials said agreement on a stability pact and a new exchange rate mechanism meant European Economic and Monetary Union was bang on target for its intended start date in January 1999.That prompted a wave of convergence trades by Europe's more peripheral bond markets
18409 over Bunds. But the UK's opt-out clause from a single currency left gilts outside the convergence plays prompted by pro-EMU sentiment.Convergence trades aim to profit from the narrowing of the differences between currencies as EMU approaches.Analysts said Friday's gilt rally showed investors are saying enough is enough and reappraising the
18409 fundamental value the gilt market offers. "It's about time," said Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Kleinwort Benson."There was always going to be support for gilts above 180. The intraday peak of 183 earlier this week probably lured buyers back in," Scott said.The relative moves by the Swedish and Spanish bond
18409 markets had prompted investors to re-evaluate, he said."There's probably another 10 basis points of narrowing for gilts (over Bunds) in the medium-term."</

18412 IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Friday it had lowered Belgium's Caisse Nationale de Credit Professionnel (CNCP) short-term rating to A1 from A2.IBCA also said it had cut CNCP's individual rating to C from B/C."The legal rating of 2 remains," IBCA said in a statement. IBCA said this reflected
18412 the uncertainty surrounding the future structure and direction of the CNCP group."The agency is maintaning its legal rating due to the state's continued involvement in the ownership -- currently 75 percent -- of the bank and CNCP's role in lending to small and medium-sized businesses in Belgium," IBCA said.IBCA said
18412 CNCP was the central bank to a network of mutual institutions providing credit and guarantee services in Belgium. "Its management had hoped that the credit unions would acquire most of the bank's capital upon privatisation and that the group would be able to develop a cross guarantee scheme similar to
18412 that used by cooperative groups elsewhere in Europe. However, this proved impossible to achieve," the agency said."Hence, the privatisation process and the group's structure are likely to take a different form from that envisaged by management and will take some time to finalise," IBCA said.IBCA said under a Royal Decree
18412 recently approved by the Belgian Parliament, various structural changes were being set in motion. CNCP would change its legal status from a public credit institution to a limited company and its name would be amended to Credit Professionnel, IBCA said."Also, CNCP will lose its previous legal supervisory powers for its
18412 network of local banks and will be obliged to negotiate service contracts with them. Although a solidarity fund, to which all the local credit unions will be obliged to contribute, is being established, its size has not been finalised," IBCA said.--International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041</

18415 Crisis-struck Bulgaria, bracing itself for a period of painful IMF austerity, on Friday won renewed support from the EBRD which is backing its speeded-up privatisation plans with a special fund.Starved for cash as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) delayed a second $115 million loan, Sofia gritted its teeth this week
18415 and vowed to accelerate the privatisation of 15 major state firms.In response the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has renewed its commitment to the former communist country, vowing to have its 45 million ecu ($56.54 million) "post-privatisation fund" for Bulgaria in place by early next year."We are making progress
18415 with the post-privatisation fund... we plan to have it set up by the end of the first quarter next year," said Olivier Descamps, director of the EBRD's country team for Bulgaria, adding the bank would select a fund manager within the next month.Providing 30 million ecu for debt and equity
18415 assistance, the EBRD plans to raise another 15 million for the fund from investors abroad."We have seen more interest from foreign strategic investors than ever before," he said, adding this had increased sharply since mid-year."We are getting calls from very serious people looking at helping Bulgaria complete the transition," he
18415 added. "It's crisis time, therefore it's an opportunity."The EBRD announced plans for the fund in April. It is designed to take equity stakes in newly privatised companies, and can provide loans for strategic investors with muscle -- the only ones who can take a long-term view and who have the
18415 resources to buy a sizeable stake.The sense of crisis deepened last week amid the on-going delays. Bulgarian debt hit a 12-month low in a market that setting all-time highs. Holders of Bulgarian Bradys thought they were staring default in the face in the absence of IMF cash.But the fears receded
18415 and prices revived after Bulgaria's central bank posted a 200 percent interest rate rise and Sofia stepped up plans to sell of banks and industrial firms.Market players are now growing confident that the IMF will release the loan after it meets in Washington next week."There is a feeling that they
18415 are making progress and will be rewarded," said Neil Lockwood, emerging market economist at ANZ Grindlays in London, adding Brady prices have further to climb after news they can be used in the privatisation process.Descamps said foreign investors were heartened by the good take up of privatisation vouchers domestically, and
18415 word that some 15 companies, in the chemical, steel, shipping, and engineering sectors, would reach the privatisation block by year-end.But he stressed that big problems remain."It's a very sensitive moment -- the leadership are very much aware of the situation and they're trying to do the right thing, but there
18415 is no quick fix," he said."The more you postpone the corrective action, the more painful your way out will be."($1=.7958 Ecu)</

18419 the 12 months to June 30.Figures published on Friday showed it made a pretax profit of 2.9 milllion stg, after losses of 7.0 million a year earlier, despite a doubling of research and development costs. Sales leapt 244 percent to 21.0 million stg."It is a beautiful scenario for the full
18419 year," chief executive Rolf Stahel told Reuters in a telephone interview.Shire is unusual in acquiring compounds after basic research has been done, developing them further and then seeking powerful marketing partners for its late-stage products.It has 36 products already on the market, centred on calcium supplements and oestrogen replacement therapy.
18419 Stahel said the turnaround in performance was due to three key factors -- a sharp rise in sales due to increased marketing, the acquisition of product development and licensing business SPC and royalty payments from Johnson &amp; Johnson for Shire's Alzheimer's disease drug Galanthamine. 18419 28 percent to 7.3 million stg, grew "three times faster than market growth in the U.K."He said the group's calcium products performed particularly strongly, stealing market share from majors like Sanofi and Sandoz AG. 18419 sales force to 32 during the year, a progression Stahel said would continue as long as it was self-financing. "I don't want to make massive investments in marketing at the same time as R&amp;D, that makes us like a biotech company and I don't want to be that," said Stahel.
18419 Stahel said Shire, which floated on the stock exchange earlier this year and raised 20 million stg, will be run on a "broadly cash-neutral basis". 18419 The compound, derived from daffodil bulbs, is in Phase III trials for Alzheimer's, the fatal condition that causes dementia, and Phase II trials for chronic fatigue, or ME, where it has no competition.Analysts beleive the compound could be on sale for Alzheimer's by 2000. 18465 Tens of thousands of illegal immigrants are scrambling to get on planes and boats out of the United Arab Emirates, four days before a tough new labour law comes into force, diplomats said on Friday.But thousands will likely be stranded in the Gulf state to face strict penalties when the
18465 law takes effect next Tuesday, as airlines and shipping companies struggle to cope with the mass exodus of illegal aliens.Many expatriates without valid work papers have already left in a two-month amnesty period that expires on September 30.But they are just the tip of the iceberg. Diplomats expect some 200,000
18465 illegal aliens -- mostly from the subcontinent but also from Southeast Asian countries -- will try to go home before the law catches up with them. Embassies say they have issued only about 100,000 exit permits so far."There are at least another 30,000 Indian nationals who still have to get
18465 out," Indian Consul-General in Dubai Prabhu Dayal told Reuters."If you divide that number by 250 for every aircraft needed to get them out, you'll need 120 airplanes. I don't know if that's possible in four days," he said, adding he expected a total of about 50,000 Indian nationals to leave.Flights
18465 to destinations like New Delhi, Bombay and Manila have been booked solid until the deadline for over a week, travel agents said. Tickets for a 2,000-passenger ship due to leave the UAE on September 30 were sold out within hours.An airport official in Dubai said the flood of foreigners leaving
18465 the country was so severe that sometimes travellers at the airport had to climb on each other's shoulders to move.Immigrants make up 75 percent of the population in the Gulf oil state. Many came to the UAE legally, obtaining a work permit stipulating they have to work for their sponsor.But
18465 large numbers break the law by overstaying their welcome, or absconding from their sponsors for what they say is better treatment or pay with other employers. The practices have always been illegal, but the new law imposes stricter punishment for offenders.The UAE government says it is implementing the legislation to
18465 curb the spiralling number of illegal aliens, who it says pose a security threat to the country."In the past there have been cases of embezzlement by employees who were not sponsored by their employer," said an Interior Ministry official quoted in the daily Gulf News on Friday. "Others have stolen
18465 cash and fled."The official said government studies had shown the new law was in the interest of all parties."These studies showed there were many cases of sexual and physical abuse against housemaids working illegally for other employers that went unreported because the housemaids knew they had violated the law," the
18465 newspaper reported.But many of the immigrants say they do not have enough time to prepare for their voyage home. Local newspapers report widespread complaints by the illegal aliens that employers are refusing to pay their due wages. Others say they do not have enough money to afford a flight or
18465 boat out."It's very apparent that all these people cannot make an orderly exit in four days," Dayal said. "Grace time is needed. What is so sacrosanct about the 30th of September? So many people have been harassed, there has been so much chaos. Extend the deadline."</
18466 Palestinians are venting months of frustration over slow-moving peace talks in clashes with Israelis, but the spark was an Israeli-dug tunnel near a holy Moslem shrine.The violence, which has killed 44 Palestinians and 11 Israelis since Wednesday, is a bloody reminder that Jerusalem's holy sites remain at the heart of
18466 the explosive struggle between Moslem and Jew in the Holy Land.The 488-metre (yard) tunnel is adjacent to the Temple Mount, once home to ancient Jewish Temples and now the site of the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.It snakes beneath the walled Old City along an ancient water tunnel and
18466 excavated parts of the Wailing Wall, the sole remnant of the Temple complex and a retaining wall for the mosque compound known as Haram al-Sharif, Arabic for "the holy sanctuary".Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called the opening of the tunnel a "crime" and an attempt to "Judaise" the city. Moslem officials
18466 at al-Aqsa charge Israel with trying to undermine the integrity of Islamic holy sites."The digging has caused some Islamic Waqf (Trust) buildings near al-Aqsa to crack and we had to renovate them. We are worried that this would lead to the collapse of these holy sites," Jerusalem Mufti Sheikh Ikrima
18466 Sabri told Reuters.Jerusalem's Israeli Mayor Ehud Olmert rejected the charge, telling reporters: "All this rhetoric and misinformation about the danger to the infrastructure of the Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem is sheer nonsense.""The tunnel is so far away from all the Moslem holy sites in the Temple Mount," Olmert said.The
18466 tunnel, a window to the ancient history of Jerusalem and a point of reverence for religious Jews, has been open for some time with only one entry and exit point in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City.Israel this week made a new opening to the tunnel on the Via
18466 Dolorosa in the Old City's Moslem Quarter, sparking widespread violence that threatens to crush what is left of the peace process."We didn't harm the freedom of religion. We didn't harm anyone here in his ability to pray anywhere. We simply opened an entrance to an existing tunnel," Israeli Public Security
18466 Minister Avigdor Kahalani told reporters in the tunnel.Israel hopes the second entrance will increase the number of tourists who visit the site from 70,000 to 400,000 a year.Waqf officials said the digging near al-Aqsa mosque was done without the knowledge or approval of the Islamic Trust, on Moslem property."The digging
18466 of the tunnel was done on Islamic Waqf property and is a violation of the holiness of Moslem and Christian rights," Sabri told Reuters."The new entrance leads to the Mujahideen path used by Moslems to reach al-Aqsa and used by Christians to go to their churches."The struggle between Moslem and
18466 Jew has exploded several times on the Temple Mount. In October 1990 Israeli police shot dead 17 Palestinians during a clash when thousands of Arabs stoned thousands of Jews praying at the Wailing Wall.During a Jewish festival in 1986 a grenade attack by Islamic fundamentalists killed one Israeli and wounded
18466 69 at an army ceremony below the Temple Mount.On Easter Sunday in 1982 a Jewish-American gunman shot up the Temple Mount, killing one person in a rampage that ignited weeks of Palestinian unrest in which four Arabs were killed.In September 1969 a mentally disturbed visitor from Australia entered al-Aqsa mosque

18490 U.S. and European Union trade chiefs said on Thursday they hoped to settle differences over an information technology deal both sides want approved at the World Trade Organisation ministers' meeting in December.Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who last week accused Europe of backing away from an agreement to eliminate
18490 tariffs on a wide range of electronic products, and European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said they made some progress at a meeting late on Thursday."We haven't resolved it yet," Brittan told reporters following the one-on-one session with Barshefsky. "We're quite happy to negotiate to drop tariffs, but there have
18490 to be other things in the agreement as well."Barshefsky and Brittan were in Seattle to attend a meeting of Quadrilateral trade ministers which also includes Canada's Arthur Eggleton and Japan's Shunpei Tsukahara. Barshefsky said Quad leadership on a technology deal was needed to win a global agreement at the first
18490 meeting of World Trade Organisation ministers to be held in Singapore in December.She said "good progress" was made at Thursday's meeting with Brittan and she hoped their differences could be resolved by the time the four trade chiefs leave Seattle on Saturday.Barshefsky said early on Thursday the main stumbling block
18490 was a lack of agreement among the members of the EU."Clearly Europe has to come to a rapid decision on this issue. We will not be able to move forward on this initiative ... without Europe because we will not let Europe free ride on our tariff reductions," she said.The
18490 Information Technology Agreement (ITA) would eliminate tariffs on a wide range of information products including computer chips, software and telecommunications equipment."We want the ITA to be agreed to in Singapore," said a European Union spokesman.Brittan said the main obstacle to reaching accord on the global technology agreement was the U.S.-Japan
18490 semiconductor arrangement, which excludes Europe."We are not prepared to see the U.S., Japan discriminating agreement go ahead unconditionally," Brittan said.Earlier this week, the EU wrote a letter to Barshefsky suggesting that work on the ITA could begin if the "discriminatory aspects" of the U.S.-Japan chip alliance, which was renewed this
18490 summer, were not applied until after the ITA was finalised, according to officials in Brussels.But Barshefsky has said the semiconductor issue can be easily resolved and that Europe appears to be backing away from the ITA because it does not have full agreement among its members. Brittan has denied that

18491 By Rich Miller, Economics CorrespondentTreasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday urged rich creditor countries to do more to help debt-ridden poor nations get back on their feet.Speaking to reporters ahead of the semi-annual IMF/World Bank meeting here, Rubin said Washington backs expanding the scope of debt relief provided by the
18491 "Paris Club" of creditors to as much as 80 percent from the 67 percent ceiling now."The Paris Club reduction should be up to 80 percent," he said.Representatives of the creditors' club, which includes the United States, are meeting this week in Paris to discuss how they can participate in a
18491 multi-billion dollar initiative to provide expanded debt relief to the world's poor.The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have already pledged to do their part and have called on the Paris Club to expand the size of its debt relief to cover 90 percent of outstanding loans.World Bank President
18491 James Wolfensohn warned last week that some debt-ridden poor nations would not be able to put their economies back on track if the Paris Club opts to provide only 80 percent debt relief.Oxfam International, a private environmental and development group, singled out the Paris Club as the biggest obstacle now
18491 to the multi-billion debt relief initiative.It warned on Thursday that failure to act could cost the lives of 21 million children in Africa.It remains unclear though just how much the Paris Club will be willing to do. Although major creditors such as the United States seem to be lining up
18491 behind providing 80 percent debt relief, the stance of others is still uncertain.In a Sept. 12 letter to the Fund, Paris Club head Christian Noyer said creditor nations would determine how much to expand their debt relief on a case-by-case basis, "taking account of the largest possible contributions of the
18491 World Bank and the IMF."The IMF last week promised to find the financing necessary for it to take part in the debt relief initiative, but stopped short of spelling out where the money would come from.Rubin told reporters on Thursday that the United States still believed that the Fund will
18491 have to sell off some of its nearly 104 million ounces of gold to do that.But Germany and a few other industrial nations oppose gold sales and instead want the IMF to use bilateral contributions from member nations to aid the world's poor.Rubin told reporters on Thursday that the United
18491 States would be willing to consult with Congress about possibly making such a contribution, but only if the IMF first agreed to sell some of its gold.He suggested though that a decision on gold sales may not need to be made for some years, as the IMF currently has enough
18491 money in its kitty to last until around the year 2000.</
18492 A.H. Belo Corp. said Thursday it agreed to buy newspaper and television company The Providence Journal Co. in a $1.5 billion cash-and-stock deal forming one of the largest U.S. media companies.Dallas-based Belo, which publishes the Dallas Morning News, would acquire the Providence Journal-Bulletin, the leading paper in Rhode Island and
18492 southeastern Massachusetts, as well as a slew of television stations around the country.The deal will make Belo the nation's eighth largest television group measured by revenues and the 10th largest in audience reach with the addition of Providence Journal's nine owned-and-operated TV stations, including five NBC affiliates and affiliates of
18492 ABC, CBS and Fox.Belo currently owns seven network-affiliated stations: three CBS, three ABC and one affiliate of the new UPN network.They give Belo access to eight percent of U.S. households but that will rise to 12.3 percent once the acquisition is completed following approval from federal regulators.Belo and Providence Journal
18492 had combined revenues of $1.1 billion for the 12 months ended June 30, 1996."This combination of broadcast assets creates one of the finest network-affiliated station groups in the country," Belo Chairman Robert Decherd said in a statement.Belo executives said they were determined to jump on the buy-out bandwagon which is
18492 running through the broadcast industry rather than get left behind."The industry is consolidating and in order to achieve the economies of scale that are available, and perhaps even to stay in the business, one needs to consolidate along with it," Chief Financial Officer Michael Perry said in an interview.He said
18492 Belo had been interested in strategic broadcast growth for several years and that a hefty stock offer earlier this year strengthened its balance sheet ahead of the acquisition.He also said Belo is looking out for further targets. "The company still has a pretty strong balance sheet and has capacity for
18492 further acquisitions."Belo's current broadcast stations include WFAA-TV in Dallas, KHOU-TV in Houston, WWL-TV in New Orleans and KOTV in Tulsa, Okla. Providence Journal's stations include KING-TV in Seattle, KGW-TV in Portland, Ore., KHNL-TV in Honolulu and KMSB-TV in Tucson, Ariz.Perry said that, of all Providence Journal's stations, KING-TV in Seattle,
18492 an NBC affiliate, was "the one that is really of interest to us" because of the city's strong demographics and growth profile.Providence, R.I.-based Providence Journal's cable TV businesses include a 46 percent stake in the Television Food Network and a 65 percent stake in America's Health Network. It also owns
18492 NorthWest Cable News, a regional cable channel in the Pacific Northwest."In this consolidating environment, The Providence Journal Co. could not find a better partner with whom to entrust its people and franchises to than Belo," said Providence Journal Chairman Stephen Hamblett.Under the deal Providence Journal shareholders would receive $12.33 in
18492 cash and 0.5333 shares of Belo series A common stock for each share of Providence Journal.Providence Journal will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Belo, and four directors from Providence Journal will join Belo's board, the companies said.The deal would increase the number of Belo's total shares outstanding from 44.3 million
18492 to 69.7 million and the payment of $587 million in cash to Providence Journal holders, the companies said.Belo also publishes the Owensboro (Ky.) Messenger-Inquirer, The Bryan-College Station (Texas) Eagle and the Arlington (Texas) Morning News.Perry said the merger would give Belo greater bargaining power to buy news print and broadcast
18492 programming at cheaper rates.He said the deal must still be approved by the Federal Communications Commission to transfer station licenses but that it should be completed in the first half of 1997.</

18494 continued victimisation of my family."California Gov. Pete Wilson praised the judge and jury for rendering justice. 18494 kidnap, robbery, assault and other crimes in June and the jury recommended in August he receive the death penalty.Hastings rejected a defence motion on Thursday for a retrial based on allegations of jury misconduct and he also denied a motion for the death penalty recommendation to be lowered to life
18494 in prison without possibility of parole.Hastings also rejected defence arguments that Davis's harsh upbringing helped mitigate his crimes."I cannot find that some alleged deprivation in your lifestyle caused you to brutally stalk, kidnap and murder Polly Klaas with the intent to sexually assault her," he told Davis.In his statement, Davis
18494 said that "for what it's worth" he offered his "sincere apology" to Klaas's mother, Eve Nichol, and to "certain members of the Klaas family."But the gray-haired Davis made a number of complaints about the way his case was handled, saying police should have provided him with a lawyer when they
18494 first interviewed him after his arrest.Addressing the court before sentencing, Marc Klaas told Davis: "When you get where you're going, say hello to Hitler, say hello to (serial killer Jeffrey) Dahmer and say hello to (serial killer Ted) Bundy and good riddance and the sooner you get there, the better
18494 off we all are."Davis had also caused an uproar after his conviction in June when he made an obscene gesture toward television cameras and the Klaas family in court.Public outrage over Klaas's murder spurred California's drive to pass a "three strikes, and you're out law" mandating tough sentences for repeat

18496 Jury selection in O.J. Simpson's wrongful-death civil trial moved at a snail's pace Thursday, with lengthy questioning by lawyers trying even the judge's patience.In five-and-a-half hours Thursday, only 16 potential jurors were questioned, of which 10 were accepted into the pool from which 12 jurors and eight alternates will be
18496 selected.So far, in four days of questioning potential jurors about their attitudes, only 39 have been selected for the pool -- 20 whites, 15 blacks and four from other ethnic groups.The panel will hear the civil case brought by the families of Simpson's ex-wife Nicole Brown and a friend Ronald
18496 Goldman, who were murdered on June 12, 1994. Simpson was acquitted of the murders last October.Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, who at one point appeared to be leaning back in his seat on the bench with his eyes closed, was clearly annoyed by some of the pedantic questioning by attorneys.At one point,
18496 the no-nonsense jurist who this week complained of the "snail's pace" of the proceedings and has banned TV cameras and barred a sketch artist from his courtroom, admonished Brown family lawyer John Kelly, who repeatedly asked one black juror if he had an opinion about ex-detective Mark Fuhrman.When the man
18496 repeatedly replied "no", Fujisaki snapped at Kelly: "He's already given you the answer, now move on or sit down."On Wednesday, Fujisaki had shown his patience was wearing thin with one of Simpson's lawyers, Daniel Leonard."I don't want to get short with you, but I will get short with you if
18496 you keep wandering around," the stern Japanese- American judge told the lawyer during questioning of another potential juror.Simpson, an ex-football star and movie actor, was absent for a second day from the courtroom and aides were reported as saying it was because of his frustration with the media coverage of
18496 his legal battle against the Brown family for custody of the two children he had with his ex-wife Nicole.The jury selection process is expected to last at least another week, according to Judge Fujisaki, who told one potential juror he could probably attend a job interview on Oct. 4 since
18496 the panel would probably not be seated before then.In the so-called "publicity voir-dire" phase of the selection process, potential jurors are being asked about their knowledge and opinions of the Simpson criminal trial and whether they feel they can put aside their prejudices or biases, to fairly consider the civil
18496 case. They were questioned specifically on their answers to a questionnaire that included such questions as whether they thought Simpson was a victim of racial discrimination or a police conspiracy.During Thursday's morning session, Simpson's lead attorney Robert Baker once again complained that the lawyers for the plaintiffs were singling out
18496 black jurors for more detailed questioning."Your honour, this is the 15th challenge of African-American jurors," he told the judge after another black candidate was challenged by Goldman attorney Daniel Petrocelli.Petrocelli shot back that the race issue had nothing to do with it and Judge Fujisaki excused the potential juror "for
18496 cause", commenting "This juror questioning reinforced his racial bias."The racial makeup of the jury could be crucial since unlike the predominantly black jury that acquitted Simpson in the criminal trial in downtown Los Angeles, the civil trial is being held in predominiantly white Santa Monica.Also, in a civil trial, a
18496 jury may reach a verdict on a 9-3 majority and may find on the basis of "a preponderance of evidence" as opposed to the more stringent guidelines of "beyond a reasonable doubt" used in criminal cases.If he is found responsible for the deaths of Nicole Brown and Goldman, Simpson could
18496 be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.</

18516 Computer forecasting models were in disagreement on whether freezing temperatures would reach the U.S. Midwest early next week, meteorologists said."Next week we have a whole bunch of question marks," said Weather Services Corp's Joel Burgio. "If you believe the European model, there's a very strong cold air mass coming down"
18516 across the Midwest Tuesday and Wednesday.The American model showed the cold air staying north.Burgio said he compromised and forecast freezing temperatures for areas of Wisconsin, Minnesota and northern Iowa Tuesday morning. "This particular forecaster is going with the American model," said Weather Express Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser.Over the weekend, meteorologists
18516 agreed temperatures would turn colder Saturday morning with lows in the 30s degrees Farenheit to the northwest with 40s F elsewhere.Gesser said scattered frost was possible in central Nebraska and northwest Iowa Saturday morning. Showers were expected to continue in Ohio Saturday.Sunday should be warmer and mostly dry with a
18516 few scattered showers possible, they said. Longer-range forecasts were inconsistent as the American and European models suggested different patterns. Gesser said the American model showed another wet pattern next weekend."The American model has the potential for wetness next weekend in the western corn belt," he said.That could further delay harvest
18516 in Nebraska, he said.--Emily Kaiser 312-408-8749</

18523 Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers called Friday for bolstering banking and financial systems in emerging economies, saying that international capital markets depend on their strength."We have an obvious interest in minimizing the potential for weak financial regimes to trigger financial collapse, since the official community is often drawn in to
18523 absorb some of the cost," Summers said in remarks prepared for delivery at the Inter-American Development Bank.He warned that global markets make it more likely that financial disruptions in one nation will spill across borders. In the aftermath of the 1994 Mexican financial crisis, the Group of Seven industrialised nations
18523 called for averting future crises through such measures as tougher disclosure standards and beefed up surveillance by the IMF.Earlier this year at a G-7 Summit in France, leaders put forth "key elements of what we believe should be the next phase of the agenda," Summers said. The G-7 plan centered
18523 on devising a global push to shore up emerging market systems."It is essential that the (IMF) take a more active role in helping to address the financial system vulnerabilities that can contribute to macroeconomic instability," Summers said. Summers stressed that the international financial community "has a considerable stake" in domestic
18523 financial systems, saying that their strength helps to spread prosperity across borders through economic development.He called for strict entry and reporting requirements, lending limits and other standards. And he warned that those rules must be enforced by a bank examination system, backed up by an independent authority with the ability
18523 to enforce compliance."Adopting a banking regime that looks good on paper won't head off the next crisis," he said. The World Bank and regional development banks also have a role, Summers said, in assisting with the development of financial institutions that can keep up with the rapid growth of global
18523 markets.He said the entire process would take years, predicting that it is "not one that will be competed a year or even a decade from now.""As we have learned painfully from experience, making financial systems and the international financial systems less prone to major crisis is probably the dominant financial
18523 challenge of our time," he said.</

18525 Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from up 0.300 cent a lb to off 0.100 while pork bellies were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent higher, livestock analysts said.Most analyts expect renewed demand in hog futures after Thursday's late profit taking. Another round of higher cash markets Friday morning and
18525 rising wholesale pork values should boost futures prices, analysts said.Pork cutout values rose $1.91 to $1.82 per cwt Thursday and moved up to highest levels since August 21.Larger packer kill capacity is driving live prices higher especially with cash pork prices rising, they said.However, some analysts again look for a
18525 mixed trend ahead of Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report, especially after posting new contract highs in October and December Thursday and then easing. Much of the report is already in the market but trade may still be uneven at times, they said.Average indications on Friday's report point to
18525 all hogs as of September 1 at 96.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 97.5 percent. Kept for breeding estimates averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94 to 99 and kept for market estimates averaged 96.5 and ranged 95 to 98 percent of last
18525 year. But farrowing intentions for September/November and December/February averaged near 100 percent and the high end of expectations ranged from 102 to 105 percent. A figure of 100 percent or more would signal a return to increasing hog production by the large producers, analysts said.Pork belly futures look higher following
18525 another advance in cash belly prices despite fairly active slaughter.Rising cash shows very good demand for product, they said.USDA estimated week to date slaughter through Thursday at 1,451,000 head, above 1,420,000 a week ago in the same period and also above 1,432,000 a year ago.Despite the greater amount of pork

18530 Miami has a $38.9 million deficit for fiscal 1997, but will not seek a property tax increases, city commissioners decided.The deficit figure, disclosed by acting City Manager Merrett Stierheim at a Thursday night commission meeting, represents about 14 percent of the city's $275 million operating budget.Stierheim proposed leaving the property
18530 tax rate at $11.7055 per $1,000 of assessed value, and compensating for the deficit by raising service charges and fees, cutting expenses, using short-term loans, and transferring or laying off some employees.The City Commission unanimously accepted Stierheim's recommendation, though details still must be worked out before a final budget is
18530 adopted for the fiscal year beginning Oct 1.Stierheim described the fiscal problems as "manageable" and said he expected no credit impact."There should be no concern over bond default or that bondholders are at risk," he said.Stierheim said the city would carry over a $19.4 million deficit from fiscal 1996, which
18530 ends Sept 30. The remaining $19.5 million of the decifit was due to overbudgeted revenue and underbudgeted expenses.Stierheim blamed the problems on inadequate checks and balances in the city's finance department but did not blame anyone by name.The budget shortfall was discovered after the resignation of City Manager Cesar Odio,
18530 who was charged by federal prosecutors earlier this month with conspiring to solicit bribes in relation to city contracats.City Commissioner Miller Dawkins was also charged in the bribery case, and prosecutors said former City Finance Director Manohar Surana had agreed to plead guilty on related charges.Surana resigned in August, shortly
18530 before federal prosecutors revealed he had worn a hidden wire to record conversations implicating the others.--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013</

18545 Lehman analyst Peter Wade said he expects ITT Hartford Group Inc to announce third quarter charges to boost its reserves for asbestos and environmental losses and for losses on investment contracts.Wade said he expects the company to announce a $440 million after-tax charge, or about $3.75 a share, when it
18545 announces third quarter earnings on October 18.Wade said he raised his 1997 earnings estimate for ITT Hartford to $6.40 a share from $5.30, saying the charges would reduce the drag on earnings.ITT Hartford shares rose 3/8 to 58-1/4.ITT Hartford declined immediate comment on the matter.In August, ITT Hartford said it
18545 had launched a study of its asbestos and environmental liabilities, which it expected to complete by the end of the year.ITT Hartford at that time said it was too early to know whether it would boost its $1.3 billion in reserves for pollution claims as a result of the study.The
18545 company earlier Thursday announced it expected losses from Hurricane Fran to total about $35 million after tax for the third quarter, or about $0.30 a share.Wade said his 1997 estimate includes increased financing costs of just over $0.05 a share.He said he expects the company to raise non-dilutive capital to
18545 offset the impacts of the reserve charges. He said he expects the company to issue about $500 million of equity-like capital.Wade also said he repeated his buy recommendation on ITT Hartford and has a June 1997 price target of $70 a share.Earnings of $6.40 a share in 1997 would allow
18545 ITT Hartford to generate 17 percent return on investment, he said.Wade said he was confident that ITT Hartford will take both the environmental and investment contract charges in 1996, most likely in the third quarter.He said his confidence stems from the company's decision to push up the date for the
18545 release of its earnings to October 18 from November 1.In addition, he cited Standard &amp; Poor's downgrade Wednesday of ITT Hartford units' claims-paying ability ratings and ITT Hartford's announcement Wednesday of a shelf offering of up to $1.25 billion.S&amp;P's downgrade "may indicate that the rating agency is aware of a
18545 reserve charge, meaning the charge can not be far off," Wade said in a report to the sales force.In addition, Wade said, he believes the company's new management will want to start 1997 with a clean slate and the old management will want to leave the new management unencumbered by
18545 past liabilities.ITT Hartford last week said it named Ramani Ayer to succeed Donald Frahm as chairman, president and chief executive, effective February 1, 1997.ITT Hartford also said Lon Smith would become vice chairman of The Hartford unit on February 1. He would also maintain his current responsibilities as president and
18545 chief operating officer of worldwide life insurance operations.Wade also said he believes ITT Hartford over the medium-term may examine splitting its property-casualty and life insurance operations, a move that could boost the value of ITT Hartford shares to $80 from fair value of about $65.Smith, who runs the life insurance
18545 operations, would likely play a key role in determining the feasibility of such a move and would likely run the life insurance business if it should become a separate entity, Wade said.-- Patricia Vowinkel 212-859-1716</

18562 If the credo of mainstream media is "if it bleeds, it leads," then publisher John Groom is here to say there is "good news every day."That is the idea behind Groom's Web site Positive Press, run from his nonprofit organisation, The Athens Institute in Alexandria, Virginia. Positive Press was founded
18562 on the World Wide Web in July "to counteract the tendency of the mainstream media to focus on the negative," its mission statement says.Within four days of its appearance, Positive Press was selected by online service Yahoo as a pick of the week, Pacific Bell has made it an educational
18562 link and it has logged 200,000 hits to date.On a typical day, his research team of two ploughs through the Internet and culls this good news: from the Detroit News, Chrysler has donated $2 million to the Detroit Symphony Orchestra; from the Arizona Star, chocolate may be the next health
18562 food; from Reuters, Shannon Lucid comes home from the shuttle after logging the most time in space for a woman; and from CNN, Dan, a springer spaniel that had taken a water rescue class, is credited with saving the life of a toddler.The Hartford Courant has the story of a
18562 man who found some 40-year-old dynamite, still explosive, in his garage. "If he had dragged, rather than carried, that package, this would not be a Positive Press story," the group crows.A "historical perspective section" gives the long view on the accomplishments of humankind. This week's antidote to tragedy: Travel by
18562 plane is safer than it was a generation ago; in the last nine years, the odds of perishing in a commercial airliner have been one in 1.3 million.In his online statement of philosophy, Groom cites Plutarch. And a thought of the day is from Emerson: "Go with mean people, and
18562 you think life is mean."Groom, 35, was a real estate developer when boom turned to bust. "I kept trying to think, 'Things are not really that bad. You've got to keep perspective,'" he said."I would look around for upbeat news. By the time I had found something like that, I
18562 would have to have read eight stories about a gang shooting or a hurricane in China or a volcanic eruption where 20 people had been killed -- the very negative things that the media tend to cover because people have a perverse attraction to those things," he said."I kept thinking,
18562 'Wouldn't it be good if there was some place you could go to that would be an inspirational news source, where you could read the good news?' A lot of sites on the Web have a positive inclination but it's kind of in the flower child way, like 'We're all
18562 beautiful. Let's all be nice to each other.'"Groom not only did not want to be silly, he did not want to be religious. "It's non-controversial, non-sectarian, secular," he said of his news service. He chooses bounce-back stories, stories of quiet heroism, stories about children, news about medical breakthroughs and bullish
18562 economic items."If you read polls, people view the world as getting worse, crime is getting worse. I don't think that's true," he said. "The world's really a lot safer than it has been in the past. It's a lot cleaner than it has been in the past. People live longer.
18562 They receive better medical care."There are problems in the world. No one denies this. My attitude is ... let's take a hard, cold ruthless look at reality and if you do take a hard, cold ruthless look you'll see lots of good. You don't have to be a cynic to
18562 be a realist."Groom said he has done "zero promotions" and "zero advertising" for his site. He pays for it with his own time and money. What is in it for him? Not much, except the hope he has found an untapped market for positive press and the satisfaction of getting
18562 happy news, he said."I tell you when I feel especially good is when I come across a particularly good story," he said. "Like the three-year-old who fell into the gorilla's cage and the gorilla carried it to safety. That was perfect for us."Positive Press is located at http://www.positivepress.com.</

18578 European Union ministers on Friday agreed a key part of their plan to liberalise EU telecommunications markets, a regime for licensing companies once state monopolies are ended.They also agreed to coordinate the regulation of satellite systems that will begin to offer mobile phone and data-transmission services by the end of
18578 the decade.Both initiatives must be approved by the European Parliament before final adoption.The telecoms licensing plan requires governments to use open and objective procedures and establishes a "one-stop shopping" system for companies wanting to operate in more than one EU state.A final sticking point was over when to oblige operators
18578 to apply for individual licences and when to allow them to fall under a "general authorisation" scheme requiring no prior approval.The European Commission wanted to restrict the use of individual licences to cases where governments needed to allocate radio frequencies or numbers, grant access to land or impose public service
18578 obligations.But the ministers decided EU states should be allowed to require individual licences as well for all providers of voice telephone services or public telecommunications networks, EU officials said.They also agreed that governments should be able to limit the number of operators in a given sector only if needed to
18578 ensure the efficient use of radio frequencies or, on a temporary basis, because of a shortage of telephone numbers.That responded to a request from Spain, which said it needed more time to reorganise its numbering system as required under previous EU legislation.The text says governments must in principle decide on
18578 applications for individual licences within six weeks, although that could be extended up to eight months in cases of competitive bidding.On satellite personal communications services, the ministers agreed a watered-down plan that would give primary responsibility to the inter-governmental European Conference for Postal and Telecommunications Administrations (CEPT).The European Commission had
18578 hoped to set up a single EU system for selecting and authorising the satellite systems that will begin by the end of the decade to offer mobile phone and data communications services.However, EU member states in earlier discussions resisted the plan because it would have allowed the Commission to draw
18578 up criteria for licensing operators and to play a major role in selecting them.EU officials said the ministers endorsed a new text that asks CEPT to take a series of actions by mid-1997, including harmonising the use of frequency bands and the procedures for authorising the new systems.The legislation also
18578 asks the Commission and CEPT to set up a "one-, stop-shopping" system to make it easier for operators to get authorised in more than one EU state at the same time.The ultimate decision on whether to allow a communications system to operate from national territory -- that is, to set
18578 up a satellite uplink -- rests with individual EU states.The text asks EU states to coordinate their decisions, however, if the number of systems must be limited because of a shortage of frequencies.It also says the EU can step in if the Commission or a member state consider that CEPT's
18578 work is not progressing satisfactorily. The decision would be taken by a licensing committee composed of the Commission and national representatives that will be set up under separate legislation on telecoms licences.EU states would be required to implement the telecommunications licensing regime by December 31, 1997, just in time for
18578 the January 1, 1998 EU deadline for liberalising all telecoms sectors in most countries.The satellite plan would take force 20 days after it is published in the EU's Official Journal.</

18582 Germany's upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, voted on Friday to join the government and lower house when they move to Berlin, the capital of unified Germany, in 1999.Thirteen of Germany's 16 regional states represented in the Bundesrat backed the proposal to move to Berlin, reversing a narrow decision made
18582 five years ago to remain in the sleepy Rhineside city of Bonn.But regional leaders from around Bonn said moving the Bundesrat to Berlin would betray the spirit of German federalism, the system that helped rebuild post-war Germany into a democratic state."There is no country where the two legislative bodies are
18582 separated," Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber told German ZDF television. "If you look at Rome or Paris or any other important capital city and you see both chambers are in the same place."Even though Bavaria had been strongly opposed to the government and lower house moving to Berlin when parliament voted
18582 Berlin five years ago, Stoiber said that the states would only be hurting themselves now if they stayed in Bonn."The federal character of Germany is clearly demonstrated by the fact we have 16 (regional state) capitals," Stoiber said, brushing aside criticism that too much power will be concentrated in Berlin."The
18582 political music plays in Berlin. If we stayed in Bonn we would become second rate."The Bundesrat must approve about half of all legislation the lower house passes.Bonn's mayor Baerbel Dieckmann, fighting to maintain a high profile for the city, said she was "extremely disappointed" and complained that 1,000 jobs would
18582 be lost.Ironically, five years ago when the Bundesrat first voted to stay in Bonn, local city leaders -- still stunned by the lower house's vote to leave -- said that only 300 jobs were dependent on the Bundesrat staying in Bonn.Johannes Rau, the premier of Germany's most populous state, North
18582 Rhine-Westphalia which includes Bonn, accused Bundesrat members of reneging on their promise to stay."Once you have given your word, you can't just go back on it," Rau said, warning the costs of moving the 672-member lower house, several government ministries and the Bundesrat 600 km (375 miles) east to Berlin
18582 could spiral out of control.But others argue it would also be a waste of money if officials had to shuttle between the two legislative chambers hundreds of miles (km) apart.In its resolution, the Bundesrat said if it stayed behind in Bonn it would lose its influence.Berlin city planners, who have
18582 long hoped that the Bundesrat would someday elect to join the lower house in moving to Berlin, have already set aside the Prussian House of Lords building that is just a few hundred metres (yards) south of the Reichstag where the lower house will meet.Even Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has
18582 supported efforts to keep some federal ministries in Bonn, had called the Bundesrat's 1991 decision to stay behind after the rest of the government moves to Berlin absurd.The government plans to move from Bonn, a quiet town of 300,000 that was West Germany's provisional capital between 1949 and 1990, to
18582 Berlin, a city of 3.4 million, in 1999 in time for presidential elections.Despite the exodus to Berlin, seven of the government's 16 ministries, including defence and health, will stay in Bonn to help cushion the economic blow for the city.About 18,500 government officials, mostly in the upper levels of the
18582 bureaucracy, will be moving to Berlin. The Bundesrat meets once a month and has a staff of 200.</

18597 Two German men were detained by police on Friday after one confessed he planted a camera at the test track of carmaker Volkswagen AG and sold photographs to car industry publications, a prosecutor said.The men, who were 39 and 44 years old, were not employed by Volkswagen or a rival,
18597 public prosecutor Eckehard Niestroj said in announcing the breakthrough in one of Germany's most spectacular cases of industrial espionage.Police said the men were discovered after a resident of southern Germany tipped police off to a man in Starnberg who had expertise with high-tech photographic equipment and was known to visit
18597 the test tracks of German car manufacturers.The 44-year-old man admitted that he had confessed to installing the camera and to taking covert pictures of the VW prototypes while the other has declined comment, Niestroj said.The names of the men, whose residences in Starnberg and the state of Saarland in southwest
18597 Germany have been searched by police, were not made public.Both of the men turned themselves into police once the investigation was launched and were being held in jail to prevent them from tampering with evidence, police said.VW, which declined on Friday comment on the investigation, announced in August that it
18597 had discovered the sophisticated camera at its Ehra-Lessin test track.The device apparently used heat sensors and sent photographs by means of radio or satellite technology to the home of one of the suspects, police said.Four unauthorised photographs of VW prototypes appeared in car magazines in recent months, leading the carmaker
18597 to suspect that its security system had been penetrated.The photographs were of VW's new Golf, Passat and the EA-420 model under development.Premature publication of such photographs can cost a carmaker millions of marks in lost sales because innovative body styling can be copied or preempted by rivals before the introduction
18597 of a new vehicle.Pictures of new models and prototypes are highly valued by specialist motoring magazines, and some photographers go to considerable lengths to get them.VW has said it was spending a three-digit-million mark sum to develop a new car model, of which 30 percent is to be spent on
18597 design and body styling.VW management board chairman Ferdinand Piech has said he believed the carmaker, the largest in Europe, has been under surveillance for about eight years and suspected news photographers were not behind the pictures.After discovering the cameras, VW hired organised crime expert Dieter Langendoerfer as its new security
18597 chief. Langendoerfer is scheduled to begin work at VW next week.</

18612 Commission and CEPT to set up a "one-stop-shopping" system to make it easier for operators to get authorised in more than one EU state at the same time.The ultimate decision on whether to allow a communications system to operate from national territory -- that is, to set up a satellite
18612 uplink -- rests with individual EU states, however.The text asks EU states to coordinate their decisions, however, if the number of systems must be limited because of a shortage of frequencies.It also says the EU can step in if the Commission or a member state consider that CEPT's work is
18612 not progressing satisfactorily. 18618 European Union justice ministers on Friday signed a convention aimed at tightening cooperation on extradition to prevent people suspected of terrorism in one EU member state walking scott free in another."The new instrument considerably increases the number of situations likely to give rise to extradition. The extradition threshold will be
18618 lowered," Irish Justice Minister Nora Owen told a news conference after the ministerial signing ceremony.The convention, seen as essential to creating the security necessary to allow EU citizens to travel freely within the 15-nation bloc's borders, was rushed through after a diplomatic row between Belgium and Spain over extradition in
18618 February.The convention, which must now be ratified, means that an EU country will not be able to refuse extradition of a suspected criminal on the grounds that the offence was a political one.They will also be unable to refuse extradition of their own nationals, although Germany and Portugal, who will
18618 have to amend their constitutions to come into line with that provision, will have five years to come into line.Under the convention, for example, a person suspected of conspiring with the Mafia, or taking part in terrorism or drug trafficking could be extradited.The convention also breaks new ground in providing
18618 for extradition for tax offences, Owen said."This is the first time that this particular crime will be allowed under extradition -- this is a new departure and I welcome it," said Owen, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.The extradition convention was able to be signed after Spain and Belgium
18618 earlier this week finally put an end to their row over a Belgian court's refusal earlier this year to extradite two alleged Basque separatist activists.At the time Spain broke off judicial relations with Belgium.ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) have killed some 800 people since 1968, when they started a violent
18618 drive for Basque independence.The two countries said in a joint statement on Tuesday they hoped their accord would allow them to re-start full cooperation on extradition requests in the "shortest time possible", even before ratification of the EU convention.The extradition treaty also facilitates the so-called Schengen agreement, an ambitious border
18618 free exercise fully implemented at the moment by seven EU countries, which was nearly wrecked by the Belgo-Spanish row.The accord, linking Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Spain and Portugal, is seen as a possible model for a future passport control free zone in the EU as a whole.</

18650 European Union justice ministers on Friday signed a convention aimed at tightening cooperation on extradition to prevent people suspected of terrorism in one EU member state walking scott free in another."The new instrument considerably increases the number of situations likely to give rise to extradition. The extradition threshold will be
18650 lowered," Irish Justice Minister Nora Owen told a news conference after the ministerial signing ceremony.The convention, seen as essential to creating the security necessary to allow EU citizens to travel freely within the 15-nation bloc's borders, was rushed through after a diplomatic row between Belgium and Spain over extradition in
18650 February.The convention, which must now be ratified, means that an EU country will not be able to refuse extradition of a suspected criminal on the grounds that the offence was a political one.They will also be unable to refuse extradition of their own nationals, although Germany and Portugal, who will
18650 have to amend their constitutions to come into line with that provision, will have five years to come into line.Under the convention, for example, a person suspected of conspiring with the Mafia, or taking part in terrorism or drug trafficking could be extradited.The convention also breaks new ground in providing
18650 for extradition for tax offences, Owen said."This is the first time that this particular crime will be allowed under extradition -- this is a new departure and I welcome it," said Owen, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.The extradition convention was able to be signed after Spain and Belgium
18650 earlier this week finally put an end to their row over a Belgian court's refusal earlier this year to extradite two alleged Basque separatist activists.At the time Spain broke off judicial relations with Belgium.ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) have killed some 800 people since 1968, when they started a violent
18650 drive for Basque independence.The two countries said in a joint statement on Tuesday they hoped their accord would allow them to re-start full cooperation on extradition requests in the "shortest time possible", even before ratification of the EU convention.The extradition treaty also facilitates the so-called Schengen agreement, an ambitious border
18650 free exercise fully implemented at the moment by seven EU countries, which was nearly wrecked by the Belgo-Spanish row.The accord, linking Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Spain and Portugal, is seen as a possible model for a future passport control free zone in the EU as a whole.</

18660 policy of curbing domestic grain costs.But a stronger reason for not moving now, officials said, is an arcane dispute over malt exports, with high stakes for Japanese and other brewers as well as European malt firms.Malt export refunds are usually linked to the last two barley export refunds each month.
18660 The malt export licences have a long validity of the current month plus a further 11 months.Granting higher refunds for barley on Thursday would have reduced the incentive to bid for the existing malt programme by putting upward pressure on the special malt subsidies, officials said. 18660 clamouring for such a rise.The crunch may come when the Commission looks at bids for malt exports in coming days. And according to some officials, it is ready to wave a stick to get its malt programme moving."The Commission is waiting for the trade to bid for 1.0 to 1.4
18660 million tonnes of malt on Friday and Monday, profiting from the October increment, and we have to make clear this (malt refund) is an operational level," the EU export source said.Some officials have begun talking privately of a "negative" brewing premium. This, they implied, would snatch back part of the
18660 refund if traders continued to keep the Commission waiting.The malt refund is an average of recent barley refunds, plus a malting premium (currently zero), then monthly increments of 1.1 Ecus a month where applicable. 18666 EU system for selecting and authorising the satellite systems that will begin by the end of the decade to offer mobile phone and data communications services.However, EU member states in earlier discussions resisted the plan because it would have allowed the Commission to draw up criteria for licensing operators and

18685 The European Court of Justice said national courts must evaluate all the circumstances surrounding an individual case when determining if the hiring out of vehicles is economic activity under the Sixth VAT directive.A German taxpayer purchased a motor caravan ostensibly for the purpose of hiring it out to earn an
18685 income. After two years, she had hired the car out primarily to her husband's business. She rented the caravan out to third parties a total of four times in two years, according to court documents.The court reviewed the method for characterizing "economic activity" under the Sixth VAT directive and said
18685 such activity does not include those carried out on an occasional basis.In order for the hiring out of property to be considered "exploitation of property" under the directive, and hence an economic activity, it must be done on a continuing basis.The burden of establishing eligibility for VAT deduction rests with
18685 the taxpayer, the court said. Judicial authorities should review evidence to see whether or not the purpose of the activity is to obtain income, not whether the tax payer acutally was successful.The court said the nature of the property may be considered, as well as how it is used, when
18685 analyzing if the taxpayer sought to obtain income from it."If by reason of its nature, property is capable of being used for both economic and private purposes, all the circumstances in which it is used will have to be examined in order to determine whether it is actually used for
18685 the pupose of obtaining income on a regular basis," the court said.The court suggested comparing the actual use of the property to a standard use to ascertain if the activity was in fact one carried out for obtaining income on a continuing basis. Additionally, the actual length of time the
18685 property is hired, the number of customers and the earnings received should be considered.***EXCERPTS FROM THE COURT(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)"Sixth VAT directive - Definition of economic activity - Taxable amount"In Case C-230/9426 September 1996Reference by the Bundesfinanzhof for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings
18685 pending before that court betweenRenate EnklerandFinanzamt Homburgon the interpretation of article 4(1) and (2), 6(2)(a) and 11A(1)(c) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 onthe harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of
18685 assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)---THE COURT hereby rules1. The hiring of tangible property constitutes exploitation of such property which must be classified as an "economic activity" within the meaing of article 4(2) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 onthe harmonization of the laws of
18685 the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment, if it is done for the purpose of obtaining income therefrom ona continuing basis.2. In order to determine whether the hiring out of tangible property such as a motor caravan is carried
18685 on with a view to obtaining income on a continuing basis, within the meaning of the second sentence of article 4(2) of the Sixth directive, it is for the national court to evaluate all the circumstances of the particular case.3. Article 11A(1)(c) of the Sixth Council directive is to be
18685 interpreted as meaning that the taxable amount for turnover tax on transactions treated as supplies of services under Article 6(2)(a) of the directive must include expenses which are incurred during a period in which the goods are at the taxable person's disposal in a way that he can actually use
18685 them at any time for non-business purposes and which related to the goods themselves or which the taxable person is entitled to deduct for VAT purposes. The portion of the expenses to be included must be proportionate to the ration between the total duration of actual use of the goods
18685 and the duration of actual use for non-business purposes.</

18686 Thursday in Paris.On assignments with the French news agency, the fearless reporter covered the 1979 Iranian revolution and hostage crisis, the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon and fighting in Afghanistan, Chad and Ethiopia.After joining Le Monde in 1987, he helped cover the Palestinian uprising and the Balkans, where he was

18686 and warm-hearted with us in the air raid shelters, because he knew that we were condemned to stay here when he went back to Paris."He leaves a wife and two children.</

18687 was a "French political solution" that made little sense industrially."What possible logic is there other than to keep Valeo French in what is one of the most global industries? This is a car parts company. It's not critical to the defence of France," he said. "This sends a clear message

18712 Norway and the United States formally ended a Cold War military assistance programme on Friday with Oslo paying Washington a token $1.8 million for equipment worth many times more.The termination agreement was signed by Norwegian Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo and U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry the day after an annual
18712 NATO meeting in Bergen."Today we mark the end of nearly 50 years of military assistance cooperation between Norway and the United States," Perry said at a news conference.Kosmo said NATO member Norway would never have been able to build up a strong defence had it not been for the assistance
18712 programme under which the country borrowed military equipment from the United States."The amount now paid back is just a symbolic sum," he said.Officials said Norway was paying the scrap value of the equipment received in gaining the right to its residual value.The hardware included 8,000 combat and transport vehicles, 500
18712 pieces of artillery, 170,000 small arms, dozens of warships and more than 600 planes and helicopters.Norwegian defence monthly Forsvarets Forum said the equipment was worth more than $12 billion in today's money.The shipments ran from 1950 to 1971, but the bureaucracy involved in administering the borrowed material in the end
18712 proved a burden to both countries. For example, U.S. consent was necessary for the scrapping or selling of material received.Perry and Kosmo agreed that both sides had benefited from the defence capabilities of Norway, which shares a border with Russia on what used to be the strategically-important Northern Flank.U.S. Ambassador
18712 to Norway Thomas Loftus said Norway was the first country to settle its arms assistance bill with the United States, which had similar programmes in support of the defences of all NATO countries plus Japan, Thailand and the Philippines."Norway has set the standard," he said. "Now we must finish with
18712 the Cold War and the arms assistance programmes, so that we really can look to the future."Perry said the termination of the agreement did not affect U.S. military equipment pre-positioned in mid-Norway in the 1980s for a possible Northern Flank conflict.</

18735 companies wanting to operate in more than one EU state.One of the final sticking points was over when to oblige operators to apply for individual licences and when to allow them to fall under a "general authorisation" scheme requiring no prior approval.The European Commission wanted to restrict the use of
18735 individual licences to cases where governments needed to allocate radio frequencies or numbers, grant access to land or impose public service obligations.But the ministers decided EU states should be allowed to require individual licences as well for all providers of voice telephone services or public telecommunications networks, EU officials said.They

18741 Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it was leaving unchanged its Aaa rating on the senior unsecured debt of German bank Dresdner Bank AG but has negative long-term and financial strength ratings.Moody's said the existing rating was based on Dresdner's "superior creditworthiness"."We continue to view Dresdner as a very strong
18741 and financially stable banking group both by German and international standards," Moody's said in a statement.But it added, "The outlook for the long-term and financial strength ratings are negative." Moody's said the outlook incorporated the belief that the European banking market will put Dresdner's traditional revenue source, mainly net lending
18741 margins, "under continuous downward pressure, thus challenging the group's earnings power".The report noted that the European market was currently characterised by low loan demand, tighter margins, increasing product commoditisation and gradual savings disintermediation.To offset the trend, Moody's said Dresdner was pursuing a strategy of diversifying its earnings sources, both domestically
18741 and internationally, through fees and commissions and also through trading income (not from proprietary trading).The report also said the integration of U.K. investment bank Kleinworth Benson was going on but that Dresdner faced stiff competition."Dresdner is also making sustained efforts to improve the efficiency of its domestic network, but the
18741 overall cost structure remains a financial burden," the report said.Moody's also said disclosed solvency was not very high at Dresdner by international standards but that Dresdner's economic capitalisation was boosted by hidden reserves.--Frankfurt Newsroom. +49 69 756525</

18745 Corporations and advertising agencies are frantically trying to figure out how best to reach Europe's growing number of Internet users, ignoring the few who continue to question its value as an advertising medium.Speakers at a European advertising conference in Rome said the Internet -- which basically enables anyone with a
18745 computer, telephone and modem to reach consumers around the world -- would reshape the marketing business."The number of Europe's Internet users is growing," Paolo Guadagni, marketing director for Microsoft in Italy, said.Until recently, users in the United States accounted for 80 percent of the world's 48 million Internet users, but
18745 that has shrunk to 73.4 percent, while 10.8 percent are now in Europe and 8.4 percent are in Canada and MexicoGuadagni told the annual conference of the European Association of Advertising Agencies (EAAA) which ended on Thursday that the number of Internet users was doubling each year. It now included
18745 30 million people who used the World Wide Web, the graphics-linked part of the Internet, he added.Guadagni said $45 million had been spent on advertising on the Web -- a small amount compared with television and print advertising, but one that represented rapid growth since the first ad in cyberspace
18745 in 1994.The Web's top 10 advertisers account for 27 percent of all ads on the new medium and are predominantly computer software companies, he said.A mere 10 Websites are now getting 63.6 percent of all advertising expenditure on the Web, he said. These include Infoseek, Lycos, Yahoo! and Netscape, software
18745 companies that all help users navigate around the Web.But many other kinds of companies are testing out marketing their goods and services on the Internet, including carmakers.Generals Motors, Ford, Mercedes and some Japanese manufacturers are investing a lot of money in advertising on the Internet, Guadagni told the conference, which
18745 grouped advertising agencies and trade bodies from 24 countries.Mercedes launched a Website four months ago that allows users, through graphics and virtual reality, to enter and "look around" the inside of the latest car model.But executives from Italian media groups urged delegates at the EAAA conference to keep spending money
18745 on television advertising, rather than get excited about the still largely untried world of the Internet."I do not believe it (the Internet) is the Holy Grail," Robert Hersov, managing director of Telepiu, the Italian pay-TV group, said.He said Telepiu, which now has three analogue terrestrial channels, expected -- by moving
18745 to digital satellite delivery -- to have 60 to 80 channels by September 1997."This IS the Holy Grail" for advertisers, Hersov said.Carlo Momigliano, vice director general of Publitalia, said past forecasts for the growth of Internet users had proven over optimistic.Publitalia is the "media seller" -- or company that sells
18745 advertising space -- for Mediaset, the Italian commercial television group controlled by former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.Momigliano told the conference advertisers were also better off reaching consumers through television ads since the average TV viewer was older and had more money than the mostly young people who use the
18745 Internet.Bernardo Notarangelo, special events manager at SIPRA, the media seller for RAI, Italy's state-owned television network, said the Internet was awkward for advertisers because no-one knew how much money was being spent on ads, Websites or Web-based consumer purchases."It's mumbo-jumbo economics," he said.</

18759 and other leisure time travel can be regarded as a distinct reason for the increase in the use of motor petroleum," the association said.In the 12-month period to end-August, motor petroleum sales fell 1.3 percent year-on-year to 1.87 million tonnes. 18767 a statement, the group attacked "the detention and imprisonment of opposition politicians, human rights and pro-democracy activists, trade unionists and journalists, as well as restrictions on freeedom of expression...and movement".The eight-nation Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) meets in New York this weekend to decide whether to impose sanctions on Nigeria
18767 in a bid to propel the government toward democracy.The Commonwealth, a grouping of Britain and its former colonies and protectorates, suspended oil-rich Nigeria last November after the execution of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other minority-rights activists.CMAG agreed on the sanctions -- including a ban on sporting links and arms
18767 sales -- in April but later decided to freeze them until this weekend's New York meeting to give Nigeria a further chance for talks."Human Rights Watch calls specially on CMAG...to urge the Commonwealth member states to implement the sanctions recommended by CMAG in April, and also to adopt an asset
18767 freeze and arms embargo," the group urged."Human Right Watch calls for international pressure to be maintained and intensified to ensure the Nigerian government takes meaningful steps to improve the human rights situation.The rights group dismissed recent reforms by the government of General Sani Abacha as cosmetic. Last year he set
18767 out a plan to restore civilian rule by October 1998, but CMAG says this is too long.CMAG comprises Malaysia, Zimbabwe, Jamaica, Ghana, Britain, New Zealand, South Africa and Canada.</
