18771 IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Friday it affirmed the long-term foreign currency rating of Tunisia at BBB minus.IBCA also affirmed Tunisia's short-term A3 rating. "Tunisia maintains a good track record for sound fiscal and monetary policy which has tamed public finances and inflation and resulted in a stable
18771 currency," IBCA said in a statement."Combined with reforms, good macro-economic management helped diversify the economy and increase its resilience to shocks," it said.The agency said that despite a protracted drought from 1993 to 1995 -- which put pressure on prices, imports and government finances -- the economy still posted positive
18771 growth. "Tunisia has shown further commitment to reform, which was started in 1986, by signing an Association agreement with the EU, IBCA said."The agreement involves the gradual removal of the remaining barriers to trade and is expected to lead to a free trade area in twelve years time. Businesses, under
18771 government leadership, are preparing for the challenge."But IBCA said Tunsia's trade deficit was still high relative to GDP and its financing relied heavily on tourism receipts and workers' remittances, both of which are very sensitive to external political developments. IBCA said that while Tunisia's debt service record was "impeccable", political
18771 risk was holding the country's rating down."The past year has been marked by increased intolerance of political dissent. Yet, internal political risk is mitigated by the near eradication of the Islamist threat and by social programmes which have ensured rising prosperity, thus pre-empting social unrest," it said."However, the recent political
18771 developments have raised the stakes -- should the economy falter, political unrest may surface," IBCA said.-- Kate Kelland, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682</

18782 by lawyers working on a no-win, no-fee basis. "These are cases which must and should be brought within the British legal system. It would be an outrage if because of the refusal of legal aid that these people couldn't bring their case to court," solicitor Martyn Day told BBC radio.
18782 The cancer sufferers say Imperial Tobacco, being demerged from conglomerate Hanson Plc and Gallaher, a unit of American Brands of the United States, should have reduced levels of tar in cigarettes after it became clear 40 years ago that it was causing cancer.The tobacco companies argue there is no proof
18782 that these people would not have suffered from cancer if the tar levels in the cigarettes had been reduced.The lawyers will receive no fee if the cancer victims lose the case but could earn an estimated three million stg in fees and a similar amount from the plantiffs if they
18782 are successful. The cancer victims were denied a petition for legal aid in July on the grounds that the case was unlikely to succeed."In the last 40 years, hundreds of such cases have been brought against tobacco companies worldwide and none of them have resulted in any tobacco company paying
18782 any damages at all," a spokesman for Imperial Tobacco said.Jeff Jeffery, a spokesman for Gallaher, said: "The company's policy is not to comment on matters of litigation whether current or pending." The first step in the legal action is expected within the next few weeks and the case could reach
18782 court within two years. ($1=.6416 Pound)</

18795 UK heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc said on Friday its sights are set firmly on further expansion in eastern Europe and China as it seeks growth through new markets and new products.In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive John Carter said Hepworth is in advanced talks about
18795 a number of projects in China, where it is already building two factories to make gas boilers and mains water pipes."We are at the detailed planning stages on a number of initiatives and that it all I can say," Carter said following the publication of better than expected interim results.
18795 Although Hepworth reported a drop in first-half pre-tax profit to 35.5 million stg from 37.5 million stg a year before, the results beat analysts' forecasts and bucked the sharply weaker trend seen in the rest of the building materials sector."Markets have been quite tough," Carter said, attributing Hepworth's relatively "robust"
18795 performance to the impact of efficiency gains and a focus on international markets. 18795 up 24 percent to 66 million stg. Hepworth is particularly keen to expand its pipes business in China, with its system of flexible, plastic plumbing products high on the list. "The infrastructure demand in China continues developing at a very strong pace and we want to introduce all our new,
18795 innovative technology in China," he said.Hepworth is also interested in moving into other parts of south-east Asia. 18795 our spearhead project," he said. 18795 fell to 15.6 percent in the first half from 22.3 percent a year before, "does give us the opportunity to fulfil more of our ambitions."Carter said the group will continue to review its dividend policy regularly. 18795 the dividend we paid to be appropriate for the group in its current position," he added.-- Jonathan Birt, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717</

18806 Big gold producers on Thursday said the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) plan to sell gold reserves was helping depress the price of gold bullion."There is uncertainty hanging over the market right now as to what the IMF will do," said Sam Jonah, Chief Executive of Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd."Hopefully when
18806 the IMF uncertainty is removed, we would hope the fundamentals would take over and see an upturn in the gold prices," Jonah told Reuters at a gold conference sponsored by RBC Dominion Securities Inc.Gold prices slumped on Thursday afternoon after news that the IMF had the necessary majority to sell
18806 five million ounces of gold from its reserves of approximately 104 million ounces.The market has been increasingly nervous in recent weeks about the prospect of the sales being approved, even though analysts say the volume would be easily absorbed by the market.Peter Munk, chairman of the world's third-largest gold mining
18806 house, Barrick Gold Corp, said the "overhang" of gold held by institutions such as the IMF and central banks was creating pessimism in the gold market.Sales by central banks and other institutions have filled the so-called "gap" between supply and demand. Some 130,000 tonnes of gold, including jewellery and gold
18806 bars, are estimated to make up the world's stock of mined gold.But Munk and the other directors and chairman of some of the world's biggest gold mining houses at the conference, agreed that in the long term, gold prices would head higher.Growing demand from India and China, as the economies
18806 of those countries continued to grow, was cited as a major potential increase in demand."The gap can be filled at the odd time by central bank sales and demand can be depressed temporarily, but the market has to respond to increased demand against supply," Munk said.But John Willson, president and
18806 chief executive officer of Placer Dome Inc, sounded a note of caution."The problem is all this overhang. There are 120,000 tonnes of gold out there and what are they going to do with it? That to me is a real problem," Willson said.--Lida Poletz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2936</
18807 Dairy farmer Phil Hook has been raising cattle all his life and would normally sell 20 cows at auction every week.But Hook no longer bothers taking his cattle to market. The mad cow crisis has all but finished him.It is six months since the British government admitted that eating beef
18807 could give people the fatal brain disease CJD (Creuzfeldt-Jacob Disease) and it has been a time of painful change for the beef industry.The impact of a worldwide ban on beef exports imposed by the European Union on March 27 can be plainly seen at the livestock market in Hailsham, 50
18807 miles (80 km) south of London.On a normal day 145 cattle used to be sold. But Hailsham's daily average is now around 95 as fewer traders and retailers come to the auction because of the slump in demand."I'm having a real cash flow problem. I have to feed cattle I
18807 can't sell," Hook said. Next week he will go to his local bank manager and ask for an increase in his overdraft."It's terribly frustrating. British beef is the safest and the best in the world but it's all about politics not science," said Peter Saunders, a beef exporter and owner
18807 of one of southern England's largest abattoirs.Saunders believes European politicians are using the BSE crisis as a political lever to force the British government to toe the line on closer European monetary integration."If we agreed to join the common currency with Germany and France the ban would be lifted within
18807 a week," he said before bidding 1.00 pound ($1.55) a kg (2.2 lb) for a prime Sussex steer.Saunders, who used to pay 1.40 pound a kg before the scare, has seen his meat export business plunge by 90 percent since March. He has managed to survive only through a government
18807 compensation scheme and with money earned by his participation in the cull of cattle over the age of 30 months.But the cull, aimed to revive consumer confidence in beef, has hit serious problems, both political and structural.Last week, the British government put on hold a separate cull of up to
18807 147,000 younger cattle most at risk from bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) because of new evidence from researchers that the disease would die out in five years.The European Union (EU) said the decision to suspend the additional cull ruled out for now the lifting of their ban.Saunders, whose abattoir deals with
18807 500 cattle a week, said the government had little choice but to suspend the additional cull because of the huge buildup of cattle from the rolling programme."There is a serious backlog of older cattle. I think there are a lot more cattle than even the government realises."Abattoirs could process twice
18807 as many cattle but the renderers who dispose of the carcasses cannot cope, Saunders said. He expects the backlog to increase when abattoirs and renderers start processing sheep in the autumn.Around 550,000 older cattle have been slaughtered since the cull began, according to the Intervention Board for Agricultural Produce (IBAP),
18807 the government agency coordinating the operation.Over the next three years IBAP expects to kill three million cattle at a cost to the taxpayer of around 1.65 billion pounds ($2.56 billion). The EU has promised to reimburse Britain 70 percent of the cost but that still leaves the Treasury with a
18807 large shortfall.Prime Minister John Major said in June that the total cost to the British taxpayer was expected to be around two billion pounds ($3.1 billion) over the next three years.The cull has been criticised by right-wing "Euro-sceptic" members of Major's ruling Conservative party who already believe the EU has
18807 too much influence on British domestic policies.Major has a majority of just one in parliament and the ban on British beef has made the task of keeping his government from unravelling ahead of the next election -- due by May next year -- all the more difficult."In the light of
18807 the government's problems here with its own party, they had to be sure that Europe were going to properly look at all of the scientific evidence," said Sir David Naish, president of the National Farmers Union.Political posturing "has not been helpful" according to Hook, who like most dairy and cattle
18807 farmers, grazes his herd on grass in summer but must buy costly feed for the coming winter."Small tenant farmers like myself all across the country just cannot afford to keep going on indefinitely. Politicians need to stop talking and sort this problem out," he said.British beef is still being sold
18807 in Britain but trade is well below their pre-crisis levels. Alex Mofitt, who owns two local butchers' shops, would normally buy six beasts a week at Hailsham but now only bids on one."Beef sales in my shops are down by 80 percent. I can't give away mince or stewing steak,"
18807 Mofitt said. He has had to lay off staff because of the downturn. " People will come back to beef but it will take time -- a long time."Time is something that many beef farmers across Britain do not have, according to the auctioneer at Hailsham market, Roger Waters. "At
18807 the moment we are not like the French. It's just not cricket to go and block the roads so we have been very English -- keeping a stiff upper lip," said Waters.But he believes this could change as farmers like Hook are forced to buy expensive feed for cattle that
18807 cannot be culled because of a growing backlog. 18815 Friends and family of the first man to die under Australia's unique voluntary euthanasia law packed a tin-shed Buddhist temple on Friday to bid farewell to a man described as brave and devoted to helping others.About 200 people, all barefoot, knelt or sat cross-legged while monks chanted prayers and friends
18815 praised 66-year-old carpenter and one-time Christian missionary Bob Dent.They included Philip Nitschke, the local doctor who helped Dent die under the Northern Territory's assisted-suicide law.Dent, terminally-ill with prostate cancer, died on Sunday from a computer-delivered lethal injection, becoming the first person to use the law since it came into effect
18815 in this outback region in July.His death has renewed debate in Australia and beyond on the issue of "mercy killings".The architect of the law, former Northern Territory government chief Marshall Perron, urged Australians on Friday to lobby their national parliamentarians to reject calls to overturn the territory legislation.A conservative backbencher,
18815 backed by Prime Minister John Howard, has launched a private bid in the federal parliament to have Canberra use its constitutional powers to quash the law.The law faces a separate threat in the High Court, Australia's highest court, where a coalition of doctors, church and Aboriginal leaders is seeking to
18815 have it declared unconstitutional.Media were barred from Dent's 30-minute funeral service and reporters, photographers and television crews looked on through a wire-mesh fence topped by barbed wire.Dent turned to Buddhism after he was diagnosed with prostate cancer five years ago. He went on to become a leading figure in the
18815 local Buddhist community."Today, we farewell a gentleman, a craftsman and a very generous individual," said an unidentified man heard by reporters over a loudspeaker system from the temple."This gentleman devoted most of his time to helping other people. His acceptance and lack of fear of the inevitable should be a
18815 good example and inspiration to us all."Another mourner told the crowd: "By such acts we perform today, we all wish him happiness and peace."After the service, Dent's coffin was placed before a seven metre-high gold Buddhist spire he had built while dying, as the crowd stood for three minutes' silence
18815 in sweltering heat.Nitschke walked in front of the coffin carrying a photo of Dent in the procession from the temple to the spire, or stupa.Dent's coffin was taken to a nearby crematorium, where more Buddhist blessings followed. However, family, friends and crematorium officials refused to say whether Dent had been
18815 cremated.Local government sources said earlier that a legal glitch might delay his cremation. Under local law, people can only be cremated if they have died of natural causes, unless a coroner gives a special authorisation.</

18824 By Russell Barton (ABC TV Political Editor)John Howard rushed back from Tokyo overnight last Friday - half a day early - to honour a speaking engagement at the Liberal Party's Queensland state conference, an appropriate venue, he thought, to dally with the Pauline Hanson issue.It must be quickly pointed out
18824 that her name was never mentioned.But it may as well have been flashing lights so palpable was her aura on the gathering.She would have been there had she not made one of her controversial statements before the last election which earned her immediate expulsion from the Liberal Party.It's now history,
18824 of course, that she continued to stand for the seat of Oxley, centred on the Queensland city of Ipswich, winning it handsomely as an independent.Then a little over two weeks ago Hanson took her place in the spotlight with the now famous/notorious maiden speech.Politicians of all colours have been running
18824 from it ever since, like Dracula from the stake.The reason is not hard to fathom.The content of the speech was long on ignorance, unreality and -- this is the dangerous part -- populism.Talk-back radio is still dominated by views for and against (mostly for) and the letters pages of the
18824 newspapers have at least two or three a day, although the Hanson letters are still rolling in at a rate sufficient to fill these pages on any given day.Kim Beazley has struggled to a position.This week Beazley said: "I mean she's an independent member, she's just arrived.""The question for us
18824 in political parties is how you devise a policy that ensures the health and survival of the nation," Beazley said."And she's not exactly in that debate," he said.But the prime minister is more cagey.His strategy was not to confront it until public opinion was clearer.Then in the Queensland speech to
18824 deal with it in the abstract.Hence the 'freedom of expression' speech; the claims that the yoke of political correctness had been lifted in the six months since he took office; that people now felt free to speak their minds.Neither stands up to much serious scrutiny.His rider that this new freedom
18824 brought with it the responsibility to use it wisely and fairly was widely interpreted as a shot at Hanson.Wrong, said Howard."That speech had nothing to do with Pauline Hanson," he said.On Channel Nine's Current Affair programme Howard was boasting about the tolerance of the Liberal Party.Interviewer Ray Martin shot back:
18824 "The Liberal Party wasn't so tolerant of Pauline Hanson before the election. Did you agree with kicking her out?"Answer: "Yes."Question: "Would you have her back in the party now with what she said?"Answer: "Well, she's not interested in coming back and I don't think the issue arises."It was all a
18824 bit hesitant, in contrast to the more forceful tone he used earlier when discussing his meeting with the Dalai Lama.It was also clear that no-one really believes this speech wasn't about Pauline Hanson, at least on the periphery.But it should also have become clear to the prime minister and his
18824 advisers that this sort of thing is tantamount to playing with fire.Political leaders have long realised that you can't just put a toe in the water of the debate over race and multiculturalism and then retreat to higher ground.But Howard never really got over the furore and the aftermath which
18824 erupted around his 1988 comments suggesting Asian immigration should be cut back.Although bound up with other leadership issues, the immigration comment was the catalyst which led to a deeper questioning of Howard's leadership of the Opposition at that point.Victorian Liberals, in particular, used it as a rallying point to begin
18824 a destabilisation in favour of Victoria's favourite Liberal, Andrew Peacock.Howard later apologised for the 1988 remarks but the whole issue has burned within ever since.It's now re-emerging in his regular comments against so-called political correctness and now his view about the new freedom of expression abroad in the land.But almost
18824 immediately came the backlash, first in the form of a rash of newspaper features and editorials disputing his claim and then in more practical terms with the announcement by the eccentric British historian David Irving that he would now reapply for a visa to visit Australia to promote his views
18824 questioning the holocaust.Irving has been knocked back under the former government, with support from the then Opposition.There's no record of Howard having supported his previous applications.Howard denounced the Irving announcement as gimmickry and will doubtless avoid serious controversy by allowing the application to be dealt with under the current law
18824 and regulations which is almost certain to once again rule him out.Gimmick or not, Irving's action was a warning to all politicians of the dangers of trying to catch the occasional wave of public opinion.They can turn into dumpers.(Views are those of the author, not those of Reuters)-- Reuters Canberra

18828 The long-running legal dispute over ownership of one of Australia's most sought after gold mining tenements on Friday moved a step closer to being finally resolved when the Western Australian Supreme Court ordered that a ballot be held to resolve who has priority.The Full Court of Western Australia also ordered
18828 that only two of the four parties disputing ownership of the tenement - over a 15 km patch of ground directly opposite the rich Bronzewing gold mine - be eligible to take part in the ballot. However, legal sources stressed the ballot may still not finally resolve the dispute because
18828 of the over-riding discretionary powers of the Minister for Mines which entitle him to have the final say.The 2-1 majority decision of the Full Court of the Supreme Court is the latest chapter in a dispute dating back to 15 October, 1992.On that day four parties lodged a total of
18828 eight applications for an exploration licence over the land, at the Leonora Mining Registry within 51 seconds of the Registry opening for business. Subsequently the Mining Warden determined that, for the purposes of the Mining Act 1978, the four applicants had complied with the requirements of the Act "at the
18828 same time" and a ballot should held to resolve who had priority.Two of the applicants appealed the ballot decision but the Supreme Court decided, in a judgement handed down in 1994, that it didn't have jurisdiction to intervene.This decision was overturned, however, on appeal to the High Court. 18828 was referred back to the Supreme Court for hearing and its decision was handed down on Friday. The two parties that the Supreme Court determined would now take part in the ballot are prospector Mark Creasy and a private company - Hot Holdings Pty Ltd - which has an agreement

18829 Energy Resources of Australia Ltd is studying options for increasing sales of uranium to France following endorsement by Paris of a ban on tests of nuclear weapons, ERA managing director Phil Shirvington said on Friday.Shirvington welcomed France's inclusion in the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty this week, saying it would clear
18829 the way for the Australian government to lift its restrictions on exports of uranium to the lucrative French market.Shirvington said ERA had the capacity to more than triple its sales to France, estimated at 300 tonnes last year. Signing of the ban helped boost ERA shares 25 cents to A$6.25
18829 on Friday, the highest close since June 1995."We could increase sales under existing contracts or we could extend the existing contract which expires in 2001," Shirvington told Reuters in an interview.The market for uranium should be strong for the next three or four years before leveling off, providing a window
18829 for growth, Shirvington said.Uranium currently fetches about US$16.00 a pound, up from less than $12.00 last year on the spot market. Analysts believe prices have further to go on the upside despite more supply coming on stream."There is room for all the major new contracts that are on the drawing
18829 board now without crowding out the market," Shirvington said.ERA produced about 3,500 tonnes of uranium oxide at its Ranger operation in the Northern Territory last year but expects to lift output to 5,000 tonnes by next July when the Orebody Three deposit is developed, Shirvington said. Rival WMC Ltd also
18829 hopes to raise uranium output from its Olympic Dam mine in South Australia to around 3,700 tonnes from 1,500 currently.RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd also is readying its Kintyre deposit in Western Australia for development.Production would start about two years from final approval.Market prices should continue to improve as nuclear power
18829 gains wider acceptance, Shirvington said."We're expecting prices to plateau off around 1999 or 2000," he said. "But the next few years is very good time to be writing new long-term business, which would extend out for the next 10 to 15 years," he said.At present, in Australia only ERA is
18829 permitted to export uranium to France, although government constraints imposed in protest of French nuclear bomb tests in the South Pacific, limit shipments to a small fraction of the country's requirements.Asia and the U.S. represent the largest markets for ERA, but France is also an important destination, Shirvington said. France
18829 has emerged as one of the world's biggest markets for uranium after the country embraced nuclear power generation following the oil shocks of the 1970s.Electricite de France, the national power company, is the world's single largest buyer of uranium, Shirvington said.ERA is 68.4 percent-owned by Australian mining company North Ltd.--

18833 The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Board will meet next Tuesday, October 1.It will be the first meeting with Ian Macfarlane as Governor, following the retirement of Bernie Fraser in September.Ahead of the board meeting, Reuters surveyed 32 economists on their interest rates outlook, asking three questions.1) Will there be
18833 a rate change following the October board meeting? Yes - 2 50/50 - 4 40/60 - 4 No - 21One economist preferred not to answer the question.2)What direction will the next move in interest rates most likely be? Up - 4 Down - 23 Unchanged/down - 3 Unchanged for forseeable
18833 future - 1 50/50 - 13) When will the next rate move take place? Rise Down mid 97 - 1 Oct 96 - 2 Q3 97 - 1 Oct/Nov 96 - 7 Sep 97 - 1 Nov 96 - 7 Q4 97 - 1 Nov/Dec 96 - 1 Dec 96
18833 - 1 Q4 96 - 5A fourth quarter reduction in official cash rates cut remains economists' most favoured option.Ten economists saw an October move as likely or a definite possibility. This move was seen most likely to happen either after the labour force data on October 10, or the release
18833 of third quarter inflation and wages data on October 23 and 24 respectively.As such, the RBA Board will give Macfarlane the authority to lower rates if the data falls the right way - weak employment and a high unemployment rate, and continued moderation in both inflation and wages, so a
18833 cut next Wednesday is still seen as unlikely.If the cut doesn't occur in October, then based on what information available at the moment, a November rate cut is the market's most favoured outcome.However, if employment shows strength, and the inflation and wages data disappoint, the outlook could change to rates
18833 on hold until the middle of next year, economists said.Recently retired RBA Governor Bernie Fraser's description of the July rate cut as insurance is behind some expectations of another cut, with even those expecting a hike as the next move acknowledging the possibility of another cut in 1997.Economists said it
18833 was not clear if insurance meant one cut of 50 basis points as a means to spark the labour market and activity, or whether it meant a total of 100 basis points had been approved, with 50 delivered and 50 held in reserve in case the economy needed a further
18833 boost.If a cut has not happened by the end of the year, the odds will start to favour a rise in rates from the middle of next year, they said.OFFICIAL AUSTRALIAN INTEREST RATES - October Most likely Timing of rate move next move next moveABN Amro 50/50 Down Oct/Nov 96AMP

18869 New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said Treasury's upbeat growth forecasts were validated by GDP data released on Friday, just 15 days before a general election.However, opposition Labour party finance spokesman Michael Cullen called the GDP figures "poor", pointing to slowing growth in two sectors vital to New Zealand's economic
18869 wellbeing -- manufacturing and agriculture.Earlier, Statistics New Zealand said production-based GDP grew an actual 2.6 percent in the June year, against economists' expectations of a 2.3 percent rise."The 2.6 percent annual growth shown in today's results will improve public confidence in the ability of the economy to move forward successfully
18869 next year into further improved non-inflationary growth," Birch said.Treasury's growth forecasts, released earlier this month, were higher than Reserve Bank of New Zealand and private sector forecasts. They predicted growth climbing again to 3.7 percent in 1997/98, 3.0 percent in 1998/99 and 3.5 percent in 1999/2000.Labour's Cullen said the annual
18869 growth rate had been falling for eight quarters, and the 0.3 percent rise in production based GDP in the June quarter was the lowest quarterly rate since September 1992.He said manufacturing activity had fallen on an annual basis in each of the past two quarters, and the farm sector had
18869 seen a decline in five of the last eight quarters."The fact they are in decline is a worrying signal, even to Bill Birch and his advisors, that all is not well in the New Zealand economy," Cullen said.He said there were clear signs that the economic slowdown was impacting on
18869 jobs, and the governing National Party was going into a general election on October 12 with unemployment rising and economic activity falling.Bancorp executive director Roger Kerr said while the data confirmed to some extent the slowdown in the economy, the election outcome would determine whether that trend was continued or
18869 reversed."An election result which would see no major changes to the fundamental economic direction of the country could see merry December optimism filtering through to the beginning of next year, and the resulting GDP growth pushing above 2.0 percent once again and on its way to 3.0 percent by the
18869 end of 1997."Conversely, the prospects of a centre-left government would see optimism plunging deeper and taking growth with it," he wrote in a commentary.Recent opinion polls suggest a centre-left coalition is the most likely outcome of the election, New Zealand's first under a proportional voting system.Other economists agreed the data
18869 showed a slowing economy, and said although this would please the Reserve Bank in its fight to keep underlying inflation between zero and two percent, it did not alter prospects for an easing in monetary conditions."(It is) still a reasonable rate of growth -- the economy is not collapsing," said
18869 ANZ chief economist Paul Stewart.Bankers Trust chief economist David Plank said monetary policy would be driven more by house prices, wages, and any developments in fiscal policy after the election.</

18873 More than half of Tabcorp Holdings Ltd's commissioned betting agencies in the state of Victoria might close over the next year if the company is unable to avoid a 164 percent price increase for the Sky Channel service, an agents' association official said on Friday."It we don't pay it (the
18873 annual fee hike), half the network at least closes, if we do pay it half the network closes. We're in a no-win situation," senior vice president of the Victorian TAB Agents' Association Evelyn Bakken told Reuters. Sky, owned equally by businessman Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's
18873 News Corp Ltd, has demanded the fee hike for the channel in order for Tabcorp to renew its contract which ran out in June this year, Tabcorp said in a letter to agents this week."The heavy handed position adoped by Sky will likely accelerate the closure of agencies to a
18873 much greater degree than ever contemplated by Tabcorp or agents," the company said. But Sky, which holds a virtual monopoly on direct television broadcasts of greyhound, thoroughbred and harness racing in Australia, said it would not budge on the fee hike as it was necessary to recoup the cost of
18873 broadcasting rights in Victoria."We're standing by that increase because it equates to the money it costs us to pay for that product from Victoria. My board is resolute in its decision to stand by its...fee increase," Sky managing director Bill North told Reuters.Tabcorp, which operates in Victoria only, said that
18873 under the lapsed contract it paid annual fees of A$3 million for Sky. Half of those fees were then charged to agencies on a sliding scale pegged to turnover figures.TAB's Bakken said the Sky service was vital for attracting punters but many small agencies would not be able to absorb
18873 the fee increase."(Agencies) will cease to exist without the Sky channel picture," she said.Tabcorp spokeswoman Jill Hollingworth told Reuters that negotiations with Sky were continuing but would not comment on the possible impact on revenues if the agency network was rationalised heavily. In the year to June 30, 1996 Tabcorp's
18873 net profit was A$63.4 million on turnover of A$557 million, 48 percent of which came from TAB agencies.At 0250 GMT (12.50 p.m.) Tabcorp shares were up 11 cents to A$6.32.-- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435</

18884 New Zealand's first general election under proportional representaton is fraught with unknowns, but a sure bet is a looser fiscal stance, economists said on Friday."In our view, one of the safe bets to make about the post election environment is that fiscal policy will be loosened," said Bankers Trust NZ
18884 chief economist David Plank.However, even worst case scenarios are far from bleak as New Zealand is one of the few countries in the world running budget surpluses and these are forecast to swell with no policy change. "You are going to have to see something pretty drastic to see those
18884 surpluses completely wiped out," said Bain &amp; Co economist Jill Patterson.Treasury, in an assessment of the economy ahead of the October 12 election, forecast this year's surplus at NZ$2.9 billion, 3.1 percent of GDP. It saw this rising to $6.4 billion, 5.9 percent of GDP, in 1999/2000.The Reserve Bank, in
18884 its September forecasts, was less optimistic, mainly because it projects a growth rate of 2.0 percent in the March 1997 year and 2.4 percent in 1998, against Treasury's 2.5 and 3.7 percent. It projects a surplus of $2.25 billion in 1996-97 and $1.89 billion the following year.BTNZ estimates that even
18884 a government formed by the ruling conservative National Party government would raise spending by at least $750 million in 1997/98.The new proportional system means coalition and minority governments are likely. Polls are indecisive, but suggest a left-of-centre government is more probable.Private forecaster Infometrics, in a recent assessment of parties' fiscal
18884 policies, said all will produce surpluses, with left of centre Labour having the smallest at $1.66 billion in 1997/98. It said all parties would increase spending, with the left-wing Alliance the biggest spender at $4.8 billion above current estimates for 1997/98.However, the Alliance will, by raising taxes, produce the largest
18884 surplus in that year, at $3.7 billion.The economic nationalist New Zealand First party would increase spending by $1.7 billion to produce a surplus of $3.0 billion.Bain &amp; Co's Patterson said that from a financial markets perspective there were two main issues -- whether the fiscal "slippage" was inflationary, and what
18884 implications increased spending would have for the bond market programme. On neither front does she predict strongly bearish outcomes."A lot of people say it would be a bit of a disaster, but we take the line it would depend very much how those spending initiatives are undertaken," she said of
18884 the fiscal slippage.Plans by a left of centre government to spend more on health and education could be less inflationary than the second round of tax cuts announced by National for next year and already allowed for in monetary settings by the Reserve Bank, she said.Under a Labour-led government with
18884 the more bearish Reserve Bank economic projections, bond issuance would be moderate at about $3 billion annually. "Even under a Labour-led government we are still going to be looking at a contracting bond market (using RB fiscal projections) to the extent that the amount of bonds on issue will fall
18884 from $21 billion at June 1996 down to $16 billion by June 1999," she said.Foreign investors are likely to welcome greater supply. Under the Treasury scenario with a National government, bonds on issue shrink from $21 billion to $12.4 billion by June 1999 "The fact that the bond market is
18884 contracting so significantly under a National-led government... that would be quite a worry, as some offshore investors might say they don't want to play the market because it is so small.""A programme of between $3-4 billion is not by historical standards going to create a nightmare for the markets.""You could
18884 run the argument that if supply is very limited then yields could go up. In some ways a bit of fiscal slippage as far as the bond market is concerned...from an offshore perspective, that probably isn't such a bad thing," she said.-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746</
18885 Two weeks before a general election, New Zealand's biggest company Telecom Corp is nervously awaiting an outcome that could wind back one of the most deregulated telecommunications markets in the world.On current polling, the three main opposition parties will have the numbers to end six years of conservative National Party
18885 government when the country goes to the polls on October 12 -- and all three have expressed varying reservations about the existing "light-handed" telecoms regulations.A symptom of Telecom's nervousness was chairman Peter Shirtcliffe's speech last week to an Australian business forum when he warned Australians that their $20 billion investment
18885 in New Zealand could be under threat if populist politicians -- shorthand for opposition parties New Zealand First and the Alliance -- win power proposing "short-sighted controls on economic activity".He said the left-wing Alliance and economic nationalist New Zealand First wanted to see "the heavy hand of State controlling the
18885 affairs of business".Both parties want to place limits of 24.9 percent on certain foreign shareholdings, although their criteria differ. Neither would force the sale of existing shareholdings, but both have pledged to reverse the government's August sale of Forestry Corporation for $1.6 billion to a consortium led by Fletcher Forest.OPPOSITION
18885 HAS RESERVATIONS ABOUT TELECOM REGIMEMore significantly for Telecom, the Alliance, and to a lesser extent New Zealand First and the main opposition Labour Party, have misgivings about the effectiveness of the existing light-handed telecommunications regime.This uses the Commerce Act and anti-trust Commerce Commission to control monopolistic practice. There are no
18885 industry-specific watchdogs.Communications Minister Maurice Williamson is fond of waving a blank piece of paper in front of industry groups to demonstrate the country's lack of entry barriers to the telecommunications industry.But the Alliance has used former state-owned Telecom's level of profits and market dominance as a campaign theme, saying it
18885 exploits a lack of competition.Alliance leader Jim Anderton has a personal stake in bringing Telecom to heel. He resigned from Labour in 1989 over its sale of Telecom to a consortium led by U.S companies Ameritech Corp and Bell Atlantic, each of which owns a quarter of the company.Anderton has
18885 promised to cut Telecom's residential line charges by 30 percent and remove its control of the telephone numbering system if his party wins office.His most recent spat with Shirtcliffe took the rhetoric between the two to new heights, with Anderton saying Shirtcliffe was "right to be afraid -- very, very
18885 afraid" of the Alliance.Anderton has allies for some of his complaints.New entrants to the market Clear Communications, BellSouth NZ and Australia's Telstra, and even some in government, are not convinced a hands-off approach has delivered true competition over the whole range of services.A joint Treasury-Commerce Ministry paper on the rules
18885 governing vertically-integrated monopolies, released in 1995 (prompted by a long running dispute about access for Clear to Telecom's network) was equivocal about the need for change, while pointing to Telecom's high returns.After 10 months consideration of the options raised by the report -- including industry-specific rules and arbitration mechanisms --
18885 Williamson chose to stay with the status quo.But Clear, which says there is still no effective competition for residential users, expressed its disappointment with the government's hands-off approach to the report.Clear wants industry-specific rules developed through the Telecommunications Act."There can be no true competition when one incumbent controls access, the
18885 price of access, and the contractual terms of access," Clear corporate communications manager Janiene Bayliss told Reuters."We are looking for intervention as opposed to regulation."TELECOME FAVOURS STATUS QUONot surprisingly, Telecom favours the status quo and points to Clear's profitability and a 95 percent penetration of telephones into residential houses as
18885 proof of consumer satisfaction.Williamson has promised action on a couple of the major bones of contention -- telephone number portability and the cost of interconnection to Telecom's system -- if negotiations are not carried out in good faith.He would also consider legislation barring the application of the so-called Baumol-Willig rule,
18885 approved by the Privy Council in a court case between Clear and Telecom, that allows monopolies to recover lost opportunity costs when a competitor enters the market.Given Williamson's free-market leanings, industry players see little likelihood of his threats being carried out.But Clear's Bayliss sees change as inevitable afer the election.
18885 "I don't think things will ever be the way they were in the past. There will be change regardless of the government. Parliament in general is aware the consumer is not happy."She is not concerned about the changes, however, and says even the Alliance's position is often misunderstood."They are quoted
18885 more on intervention but they are...saying if competition is not delivering benefits across the market they will regulate in the interests of getting competition."The other major opposition party, Labour, wants to establish a universal service obligation requiring telecommunications providers to ensure reasonable access for all households. But in general it,
18885 too, favours effective competition over regulation.Together Labour, the Alliance and New Zealand First are drawing 50 percent support in recent polls against 38.5 percent for the ruling National Party. National's likely coalition partners are struggling to attract enough support to win seats.New Zealand First has just under 20 percent support
18885 in recent polls while the Alliance has 14 percent, ensuring them considerable influence in any centre-left government.</
18886 A Buddhist funeral service will be held on Friday for the first man to die under Australia's world-first voluntary euthanasia law.But the funeral of Bob Dent, whose death has renewed international debate over mercy killings, has also sparked a fresh controversy over whether he can be cremated or will have
18886 to be buried.Dent, terminally ill with prostate cancer, died on Sunday after a computer-delivered lethal injection at his home in this sleepy tropical city, capital of Australia's Northern Territory.The 66-year-old former carpenter and pilot became a Buddhist after he was diagnosed with cancer five years ago, turning to meditation and
18886 traditional Chinese treatment, locals said.But a fresh controversy has erupted over whether he can be cremated in line with his wishes. Documents for the cremation require a doctor to say if the person died naturally.Dent's paperwork shows he died under the Territory's world-first assisted suicide law.A local government source told
18886 Reuters it was unclear if this would prevent Dent being cremated."We don't know if he can be cremated, like he and his wife wanted, or if he'll have to be buried," the source said.Three local councils in charge of the crematorium will consult local Buddhist leaders to decide if Dent
18886 can be cremated. Dent's widow, Judy, was not available for comment.His death has sparked a bitter and emotional debate, with opponents warning of legalised murder and moral decay and supporters describing assisted suicide as "beautiful" and a victory for personal choice.Dent, in an emotional open letter written on the eve
18886 of his death, pleaded with Australia's national parliament not to overturn the law."What right has anyone because of their own religious faith, to which I don't subscribe, to demand that I behave according to their rules and endure unnecessary intractable pain," Dent wrote in an open letter penned on the
18886 eve of his death.A backbencher in Prime Minister John Howard's conservative government has launched a private action in parliament, with Howard's support, which would see Canberra use its constitutional powers to wipe out the territory law.The assisted suicide law has sparked widespread condemnation from Australia's political leaders, medical, church and
18886 aboriginal groups and the Vatican.But opinion polls show overwhelming backing for the law among ordinary Australians, with some polls showing up to 80 percent support.Dent's doctor, euthanasia crusader Philip Nitschke, told Reuters on Friday that Dent's death had paved the way for more assisted suicides.Nitschke, who has already watched one
18886 patient die in agony while legal and political wrangles prevented use of the euthanasia law, said he had another five terminally-ill patients who wanted to die under the legislation.The Territory's law, which took effect from July, allows dying people to kill themselves with a lethal injection or pills, if three
18886 doctors support their bid.The euthanasia issue has split Australian public opinion.The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper came out strongly against the euthanasia law in an editorial on Friday but its sister newspaper, The Age, in Melbourne voiced support."The first legally assisted suicide in Australia is a triumph of the dangerous belief
18886 that everything in life, even the moment of death, can be improved by suitable legislation," the Herald said under the headline "Mercy Death Splits Nation."However, The Age's editorial supported the Territory's law and argued that federal parliament should not strike it down."...We believe that it is preferable to bring consensual
18886 mercy killing into the open under stringent conditions that hold those who exercise it accountable for their decisions," the newspaper said in an editorial headlined "Let the Quality of Mercy not be Restrained".</

18891 Burmese police detained pro-democracy politicians and blocked all roads leading to democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's house on Friday to stop a congress of her party taking place, a government official said.The Nobel Peace laureate had not been rearrested.The official told Reuters the ruling State Law and Order Restoration
18891 Council (SLORC) had decided to prevent Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) from holding a meeting because it did not have government permission for the gathering."The reason for preventing the meeting from taking place is because they invited more than 200 representatives, and a congress of this size needs
18891 prior consent of the authorities and they failed to do this," the official said in an interview.He claimed the NLD was joining forces with foreign governments like the United States to hold the congress in an effort to undermine Burma's peace and stability.The NLD said on Thursday it was holding
18891 the meeting to celebrate its eighth anniversary.The party, born amid unprecedented protests against military rule in 1988, won a landslide victory in 1990 general elections which was never recognised by SLORC.Suu Kyi, daughter of Burma's revered independence leader, Aung San, was under house arrest at the time.The military government had
18891 detained many NLD delegates on Friday afternoon, the official said. He did not know how many had been brought in for questioning so far because some were still travelling to Rangoon to attend the party congress.But he said all those who planned to attend the meeting would be picked up
18891 and brought to local "guest houses" for questioning."It is hard to say how long they will be questioned. It will probably be like last time and they will be released when everything is quieted down," he said.In May, the goverment detained more than 260 party delegates due to attend a
18891 similar NLD congress. The SLORC released most of them after about 10 days, but several dozen were charged and given long prison terms.The government also blocked University Avenue, the road Suu Kyi's house is on, to prevent anyone from going to her house."For three days, September 27, 28 and 29,
18891 nobody is allowed to go to...Suu Kyi's residence," security police Captain Aung Aung, who was manning a checkpoint on University Avenue, told Reuters."She can go and come as she pleases, we don't restrict her. We only need to stop people from going to her house," he said.Suu Kyi, who was
18891 released from six years of house arrest in July 1995, could not be reached for comment. Repeated attempts to telephone her house were unsuccessful, but the senior official said she had not be re-arrested.Police set up roadblocks and checkpoints and stopped vehicles from travelling on several blocks of University Avenue.Heavily
18891 armed security police and military intelligence officers stopped a Reuters correspondent on the street about 400 metres (yards) from Suu Kyi's lakeside home, saying no one was allowed to get near her house.Several hundred officers had manned the streets since early on Friday morning, witnesses said.Although the blockage of University
18891 Avenue, one of Rangoon's main streets, caused traffic snarls for several miles (km), the rest of the city was calm and there was no sign of military presence.The party congress, which was due to have begun on Friday, was to have been the first time Suu Kyi would meet the
18891 elected representatives of the NLD as a group.</

18893 Japan says it is at a loss as to how to defuse a growing diplomatic crisis over disputed islands in the East China Sea."Do you have any suggestions? We're racking our brains," chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters on Thursday.Pressure on Tokyo to calm anti-Japanese sentiment in regions claiming
18893 sovereignty over the islands -- known as the Senkakus in Japan and Diaoyus in Chinese -- escalated after the death of Hong Kong activist leader David Chan on Thursday, when he dived off a ship in a protest against Japanese control.His death was the first in almost two months of
18893 protests in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau since Japanese right-wing extremists erected a lighthouse on the islands as a symbol of Japanese sovereignty.Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday that he was not optimistic that there would be no diplomatic impact from Chan's death.Nozomu Akizuki, a professor at
18893 Tokai University near Tokyo, said Japan is in a dilemma because if it concedes to demands to remove the lighthouse it would also contradict its previous claims.Akizuki also said it is difficult to calm what he called an "ethnic outrage" with foreign diplomacy. "There is no real solution. A rash
18893 action would merely add fuel to the flames. The best thing to do is to remain silent," Akizuki said.On Friday, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda refused on Friday to say whether he had promised Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen in a meeting in New York at the weekend that Japan would
18893 take action against the right-wingers.But he said he told Qian that Japan would "carefully deal with the acts of the private group based on the common understanding that this issue must not jeopardise overall relations between the two countries".Qian asked Ikeda in New York that Japan take "concrete action", but
18893 Ikeda urged China in turn to approach the situation reasonably and not let it interfere with relations between the two countries.Senior Japanese Foreign Ministry officials said the government was not involved in activities of a private group and could only urge involved parties to "approach the matter calmly"."The government is
18893 in no way involved in actions of the rightist group nor do we support their activities," Foreign Ministry spokesman Ken Shimanouchi told a news conference."The structure is on private property and it is our understanding that the owner hasn't expressed objection," he said. "Japan has the rule of law... There
18893 is a limit to what Japan can do."Tokyo's claim to the islands dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.The Taiwan government also claims ownership of the islands. The Hong Kong activists had vowed to reclaim
18893 the islands, saying they would remove the lighthouse and raise the red flag of the People's Republic of China.</
18894 Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday dissolved parliament and set October 20 as the date for general elections expected to bring about political realignment but no major policy changes.The prospect of elections for the 500-seat Lower House, the first since July 1993 polls ended 38 years of unbroken rule
18894 by the Liberal Democratic Party and ushered in an era of coalition government, has so far failed to excite an apathetic public.Most analysts expect a record-low turnout for a heated but issue-free contest as weeks of wrangling between Hashimoto's LDP and two smaller coalition partners over timing of the polls
18894 gives way to an LDP search for post-election partners.One point of focus is whether the LDP, which regained the reins of power in 1994 in a coalition with the Social Democratic Party and New Party Sakigake, can capture a simple majority or will be forced to shop for new coalition
18894 partners.Hashimoto, who is also LDP president, urged his party to fight to give him a second term unfettered by the need to compromise with coalition partners."Although the LDP has been the biggest party over the last three years, we still don't have a simple majority," he said.Hashimoto is expected to
18894 pin his bid for a second term on an improving economy and his handling of a bitter dispute with the southern prefecture of Okinawa over U.S. military bases.The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), headed by former LDP powerbroker Ichiro Ozawa, plans to attack the government over an unpopular sales tax
18894 rise due in April.Shinshinto, made of components of the reformist government that ruled briefly in 1993-94, will also offer a plan for a drastic tax-system overhaul and to cut bureaucratic red tape.To Shinshinto's chagrin -- and widespread public scepticism -- the LDP has also adopted administrative reform as its poll
18894 platform, making it hard for voters to compare platforms.Marketwatchers said the elections would be a mere sideshow to more critical economic factors, but did not rule out bursts of hopeful anticipation."In the days leading to the election, there will be many optimistic promises of change with the aim of wooing
18894 voters and that could nourish the stock market," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.But Hashimoto's pep talk to the LDP on Friday offered a hint that he stands more for continuity than drastic change."We are heading for a storm of reform, and our politics, administration and social system
18894 must weather it," he told LDP legislators.Analysts say the LDP will fall some 20-30 seats short of a simple majority, forcing it to forge a coalition with a smaller party with reformist credentials.The Democratic Party, a new 40-strong group of defectors from the Social Democrats and Sakigake which boasts maverick
18894 Health Minister Naoto Kan as one of its members, fits the bill, analysts say.Kan, who aims to make the Democrats a vehicle to attract urban voters disappointed with established parties, achieved hero status this year when he revealed health ministry complicity in a decades-old scandal in which the AIDS virus
18894 was spread through untreated blood products."Stagnation would come if the LDP gets a simple majority," said John Neuffer, a political analyst at Mitsui Marine Research Institute. "The economy would like a strong plurality for the LDP, with Kan and the Democrats there to hold Hashimoto's feet to the fire on
18894 reform."The polls will be the first under reforms enacted in 1994 to correct a gerrymandered system which heavily favoured rural districts over urban areas and was seen as one reason for the long domination of Japanese politics by the LDP.Under the new system, candidates will contest 300 seats in single-seat
18894 constituencies, with the other 200 seats decided through proportional representation.</

18935 Hong Kong's securities regulator said on Friday it has publicly reprimanded Crosby Capital Markets (Asia) Ltd in connection with a placement of Giordano International Ltd shares. 18935 Chee Ying.The trade went through on the same day that Giordano announced "there was currently no definite proposal for such placing," and that Lai had not sought Crosby's consent for disposal of his shares, the regulator said."The SFC is of the view that a person reading the announcement would reasonably
18935 infer that Mr. Lai would not, at least not on the very same day of the announcement, dispose of his shares in Giordano," the regulator said in a statement. The SFC also criticised Crosby for failing to inform the market of the impending trade, or correct the perception created by
18935 the announcement."(Crosby) failed in its duty to act in the best interest of the integrity of the market and had, in so doing, prejudiced the interests of members of the investing public," the SFC said.The trade represented a 27-percent stake in Giordano, which had 708,078,000 shares outstanding at the end
18935 of the 1995 calendar year. Lai, who now owns the successful newspaper Apple Daily sold his last remaining Giordano shares at HK$7.60 each, or HK$1.54 billion. Michael Wu, acting chairman of the SFC, said the regulator is committed to upholding the integrity of the Hong Kong market and takes a
18935 serious view of the need for registered intermediaries to act in the best interest of the market while servicing their clients."We expect intermediaries to contribute actively towards a fair and orderly market and to conduct their business in a manner which ensures that the market is not misled by carefully
18935 crafted announcements intended to create an impression inconsistent with the true intentions of the players," Wu said."The investing public has the right to rely on the good faith of announcements made by listed companies at face value."In a statement, Crosby said: "At the time of Giordano's statement on behalf of
18935 Mr Lai, (Crosby) was of the impression that there was no placement forthcoming and accepted this information in good faith. (Crosby) believed at the time it was acting appropriately. (Crosby) subsequently co-operated fully with the SFC."-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441</

18953 The following is a brief chronology of the period of short-lived governments and chronic political instability in Japanese politics since 1987. Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday dissolved Japan's parliament and called general elections for October 20.November 1987 - Outgoing prime minister Yasuhiro Nakasone, in office since 1982, picks Noboru
18953 Takeshita to succeed him. Takeshita confirmed as prime minister as the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) commands a majority in parliament.June 1988 - In Recruit "shares-for-favours" scandal Takeshita and other ministers are named as recipients of pre-listed shares of the publishing firm in a shady deal.December 1988 - Finance minister Kiichi
18953 Miyazawa resigns over Recruit. Takeshita pushes through parliament a bill to introduce a politically sensitive sales tax.June 1989 - Takeshita resigns over Recruit and sales tax. Sosuke Uno succeeds him, but immediately becomes embroiled in scandal over his messy affair with a geisha.July 1989 - LDP loses majority in Upper
18953 House after polls. Uno resigns.August 1989 - Toshiki Kaifu, dubbed "Mr Clean", is chosen as prime minister because LDP still retains majority in Lower House, the more powerful of parliament's two chambers.February 1990 - Kaifu wins Lower House general elections.November 1991 - Kaifu resigns after his party, led by strongman
18953 Ichiro Ozawa, scraps his political reform bills. Former finance minister Kiichi Miyazawa takes over as premier.January 1992 - Prosecutors arrest a Miyazawa ally for allegedly accepting bribes from a property developer.May 1992 - Former Kumamoto governor Morihiro Hosokawa forms anti-corruption Japan New Party.June 1992 - Parliament enacts U.N. peacekeeping cooperation
18953 bill, allowing for dispatch of Japan's military overseas. Socialists resist, first by silent filibuster, the "ox walk", then by resigning from their seats in parliament, to no avail.October 1992 - Shin Kanemaru, LDP kingmaker and Ozawa's mentor, retires from politics after acknowledging he received illegal funds from a trucking firm.December
18953 1992 - Ichiro Ozawa and Tsutomu Hata form their own faction in the LDP, splitting from the Takeshita faction.June 1993 - Ozawa-Hata group and group led by Masayoshi Takemura quit the LDP, and no-confidence vote against Miyazawa is passed. Miyazawa dissolves Lower House for general elections.July 1993 - The LDP
18953 loses Lower House majority in polls. Seven opposition parties agree on a coalition government and name Hosokawa as premier. Yohei Kono is elected LDP president.January 1994 - Hosokawa pushes political reform bills through parliament.April 1994 - Hosokawa resigns after opposition LDP targets his shady links to a trucking firm. Tsutomu
18953 Hata, an ally of Ozawa, becomes prime minister but Socialists, biggest party in coalition, walk out of the bloc because of moves to freeze them out of decision-making process. Hata heads minority government.June 1994 - Hata resigns after LDP and Socialists threaten him with no-confidence motion. Parliament elects Tomiichi Murayama
18953 as prime minister at head of a formerly unthinkable LDP-Socialist alliance. Takemura's Sakigake party joins in.July 1994 - Murayama abandons Socialist Party's leftist tenets, including opposition to military and to U.S.-Japan Security Treaty.December 1994 - Remnants of Hosokawa-Hata coalition form opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), now led by Kaifu, who
18953 had defected from LDP in June 1994. Party comes under effective control of Ozawa.July 1995 - Socialists do badly in Upper House election. Murayama refuses to call Lower House elections.August 1995 - Ryutaro Hashimoto, trade minister under Murayama, wins election as LDP president. Kono does not run.December 1995 - Ozawa
18953 wins opposition Shinshinto leadership election against his old ally, ex-premier Hata.January 5, 1996 - Murayama resigns to hand power to Hashimoto and LDP. Murayama refuses to call general elections.January 11, 1996 - Hashimoto is named prime minister.April 16, 1996 - U.S. President Bill Clinton arrives in Tokyo for a state
18953 visit. During his three-day stay, Clinton announces base consolidation in Okinawa that will cut area U.S. military occupies by about 20 percent.June 20, 1996 - Parliament passes controversial bill to wind up ailing "jusen" housing loan firms using 685 billion yen ($6.22 billion) in taxpayers' money.September 8, 1996 - In
18953 a referendum, Okinawans vote overwhelmingly to reduce U.S. military presence on the island.September 13, 1996 - Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota agrees to take steps to renew leases for U.S. military bases on the island, ending a bitter standoff with the central government.September 27, 1996 - Hashimoto dissolves the Lower House
18953 of parliament and sets October 20 as date for general elections.</

18961 quoted at $380.60/$381.10 an ounce in Hong Kong around midday on Friday, down slightly from the previous New York close of $380.90/$381.40, but above Thursday afternoon's London fix at $380.45 -- the lowest since September 5, 1995.The slump followed comments by Camdessus that the IMF had garnered enough votes from
18961 its members to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves to relieve the debts of impoverished nations.Analysts and gold traders said the IMF sale would be carefully conducted over a long period of time and speculators had simply been taking a last minute punt on the metal."Gold has
18961 gone down because dealers are looking for $377-$378, and it is still very bearish. We're looking for a rally, but I don't think the worst is over yet," said a gold source at an international bank's Hong Kong office.Hong Kong traders said they were more concerned about tightening gold lease
18961 rates than IMF sales."There is a lot of physical demand at these levels, which means that there's extra demand on physical supply which puts pressure on lease rates," one said.One month implied gold lease rates ended around 1.59 percent on Thursday in New York, after moving up sharply from around

18961 market feared a repetition of the situation at the end of 1995, when huge amounts of borrowing squeezed the market, sending borrowing rates soaring."There's been some producer selling and we see borrowing interest in the short term period, especially overnight," said a gold dealer at a European bank's Hong Kong

18987 Key December Japanese government bond futures lost half a point on Friday, due to a media report which said the Bank of Japan is concerned about any excessive decline in long-term interest rates.A BOJ spokesman told Reuters that the central bank would not comment on the media report."The BOJ is
18987 worried that long-term interest rates are falling excessively," Jiji news agency reported.Jiji did not provide a source for its report.The December fell sharply to end at 121.45, compared to 121.95 on Thursday. "When the report about the BOJ's comment on long-term interest rates came out, the December was sold suddenly,
18987 falling to as low as 121.34," said a brokerage trader.The December had fluttered near 121.80 for much of the day before dropping sharply on the media report.The key futures contract moved within a range of 121.34 to 122.07 during the day.Turnover was 46,934 contracts.Earlier, traders said market sentiment had been
18987 dampened by selling of cash JGBs which took place the previous day. "The market is carrying over the weak sentiment from Thursday. When the December tried and failed to stay above 122.00 in the morning, it became a seller's market," said a trader for another brokerage.Selling of cash JGBs was
18987 detected on Friday as well, as types such as those in the 160 range were sold, traders said."Traders seem to be staying away from cash JGBs in the 160 and 170 range, since they seem expensive compared to other cash JGBs," said a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate.
18987 Demand for municipal and government-guaranteed bonds was weak, traders said. 18987 as of 0716 GMT, up from Thursday's 2.850 percent.The dissolution of the Lower House of parliament has had little impact on the market so far, traders said.-- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3748)</

18999 China has shut down thousands of small but heavily polluting mills and factories in a drive to curb rampant environmental damage, the China Daily said on Friday."These factories not only lag far behind in manufacturing techniques, equipment and technology, they have also wasted resources and energy," the newspaper quoted a
18999 State Environmental Protection Bureau circular as saying.Such factories had "caused incalculable harm to the environment and human health", the order said.Earlier this month the bureau issued a circular ordering heavily polluting small-scale factories in 15 industries to close by September 30.Officials in the central province of Hebei had closed more
18999 than 1,500 factories by mid-September and would shut down more than 9,000 by the end of the month, the newspaper said.Similar closures were taking place in other parts of China, it said but gave no further details.Under the campaign, authorities would close paper mills with an output of less than
18999 5,000 tonnes a year, tanneries that made less than 30,000 leather items a year and dye factories with an output of less than 500 tonnes, it said.The bureau has also vowed to close small-scale oil refineries, pesticide plants and producers of radioactive materials.China has hundreds of thousands of factories that
18999 operate with little or no waste control facilities.Other official media warned that pollution in China's offshore waters was a serious problem, with industrial and domestic waste pouring into the ocean and damage from oil already grave.China had discharged up to 8.6 billion tonnes of waste into the ocean last year,

19005 Many politicians from the National League for Democracy (NLD) party were detained by Burma's military government on Friday to prevent a party congress from taking place, a senior government official told Reuters.The official said the government would bring NLD activists who planned to attend the congress in for questioning, but
19005 said they were only being detained and not arrested. He said they would be released after the situation calms down. More than 200 NLD politicians had been invited to Aung San Suu Kyi's house to attend the congress which was meant to celebrate the eighth anniversary of the party's founding,
19005 but police blocked the street outside Suu Kyi's house on Friday to prevent the meeting from taking place.The official said the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) decided to prevent the meeting from taking place because the NLD never obtained permission for the gathering, and because the party
19005 was trying to create unrest with the meeting."For this reason the delegates who are coming to attend have been prevented from doing so. They were called in for questioning in local guest houses. After that they will be sent home," said the official, adding that Suu Kyi remained in her
19005 house and was not detained.In May the goverment detained more than 260 party delegates due to attend a similar NLD congress. The SLORC released most of them after about 10 days, but several dozen were charged and sentenced to long prison terms.</
19006 Hong Kong newspapers on Friday pointed fingers of blame in all directions for the death at sea of an activist protesting Japan's claims of sovereignty to a disputed group of islands.Protest leader David Chan was killed on Thursday when he jumped off a ship in the storm-whipped East China Sea
19006 to press China's claim to the islands, known in Japanese as the Senkakus and in China and Taiwan as the Diaoyus.Fifty protesters gathered outside Japan's consulate here shouting "down with Japanese militarism".They handed over petitions to consular staff urging Japan to quit the islands where Japanese rightwingers have built a
19006 lighthosue and raised the Japanese flag.The words "shock" and "tragedy" screamed from headlines of the major Chinese and English language newspapers which blamed all governments embroiled in the territorial quarrel, Taipei, Beijing and Tokyo, as well as those involved in the protest.Experts were also quoted as saying the tragedy could
19006 whip up a frenzy of anti-Japanese sentiment in this British colony which reverts to Chinese rule next year."The recovery of the Diaoyu Islands, now under Japanese occupation, is a cause worth dying for," the English-language Hong Kong Standard said in its editorial. "It was a brave gesture, if not a
19006 properly thought out one."But it also ran results of a street poll which showed many members of the public disagreed with that view."Naturally people are extremely upset...there will be a lot of pressure because sentiments of Chinese people around the region reached extremes and this tragedy could well channel them
19006 towards destructive actions," China watcher Li Pang-kwong of Lingnan college was quoted by the Standard as saying."What makes the outcome doubly tragic is that it was all so unnecessary," said the South China Morning Post. "The whole escalating dispute over the Diaoyu Islands has been allowed to get progressively out
19006 of hand."It said Japan could have eased tensions by removing symbols of Japan's sovereignty from the islands but "Tokyo failed to make that gesture and now a man is dead".The Chinese-language Sing Pao said Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei should all shoulder responsibility for the tragedy.If Japanese warships had not surrounded
19006 the freighter, and the Chinese and Taiwan governments had been willing to provide protection, the incident might have been avoided.The Hong Kong Economic Times said the Chinese and Taiwan governments had been too weak to stand up to Japan."How many more Chinese have to die before the Chinese government will
19006 take concrete action?"The mass-circulation Oriental Daily put the blame on Japan. It said if Tokyo had not laid claim to the Diaoyu Islands, Chan would not have organised the protest trip and been killed.The Beijing-funded daily Wen Wei Po defended China's restrained position on the dispute, saying that Beijing was
19006 doing its best to sort out the problem with Japan through diplomatic channels. It also praised Chan for his patriotism.The China-controlled Ta Kung Pao said the determination of the Chinese people to protect the Diaoyus would not be undermined.But it urged those carrying on the fight to keep cool heads
19006 and consider the big picture in working for the good of Hong Kong and the motherland.</

19063 A fad for cocoa drinks among young Japanese shows no sign of fading, and confectioners expect profits to stay at lipsmacking levels.The sweet spot will likely be this winter, after a hot cocoa boom last winter that is thought to have lifted cocoa imports to record levels, traders say."Japan's manufacturers,
19063 anticipating good sales, have aggressively launched new cocoa products," one trade house source said. "Cocoa consumption could peak in January and February, when students prepare for entrance exams," he said.Media reports in Japan late last year saying cocoa is high in fibre and helps relieve stress helped spark a hot
19063 cocoa boom that emptied supermarket shelves.The boom motivated Japanese cocoa manufacturers to boost imports of both cocoa powder and beans, and to expand their domestic production capacity, including grinding facilities.Japan's cocoa powder imports in the first seven months of calendar 1996 rose to 8,358 tonnes from 3,380 tonnes in the
19063 same period a year earlier, while cocoa bean imports rose to 32,753 tonnes from 24,661 tonnes, according to the latest Finance Ministry data.Masahisa Uchino, director-general of the Chocolate &amp; Cocoa Association of Japan, said he expected domestic output of cocoa powder, which is produced from beans, to at least double
19063 in calendar 1996 from last year's 2,568 tonnes.A spokeswoman for Morinaga and Co Ltd, which holds more than a 50 percent share of Japan's cocoa drink market, said: "Even though sales of cocoa (for hot drinks) slowed in the summer off-season, our cocoa shipments this summer were believed to be
19063 three to four times those in summer 1995."Morinaga has launched a new cocoa product for this winter season which it says dissolves more easily in hot water than existing products. It is also only mildly sweet, allowing consumers to add sugar to taste.Some traders said Japan's retail sales of hot
19063 cocoa drinks could rise to around 35 billion yen ($318 million) this year from about 20.0 billion yen ($181 million) in 1995 and about 10.0 billion yen ($90.9 million) in 1994.Looking to next year, although traders doubt the pace of last winter's boom can be sustained, they said there is
19063 still substantial room for growth as Japan's chocolate and hot cocoa consumption lags far behind other industrialised countries."Japan's retail hot cocoa sales are currently only about one-fifth those of instant coffee," the Morinaga spokeswoman said.She added that sales this autumn and winter would be the key to whether hot cocoa
19063 would become an established part of everyday life for Japanese or whether it was really just a fad.Traders also said that despite the sudden surge in hot cocoa's popularity, growth in chocolate consumption had remained sluggish, due partly to a spreading diet boom especially among young women.
