19071 Asia's booming growth is leaving an unpleasant stamp on its cities as unchecked construction leads to urban sprawls blind to the character of their pasts, major architects in the region say.Architects from 15 countries across Asia meeting in Jakarta this week warned that rapid growth in the region's urban centres
19071 threatened to make them unliveable."City with a soul", the name chosen by the Asian Congress of Architects for its seventh biannual meeting, is a warning to governments and developers to think of more than just profit margins, said congress chairman Michael Sumarijanto."Developers are thinking piecemeal," Sumarijanto told Reuters. "First the
19071 new development is built, and the infrastructure comes later."Sumarijanto said the problem faced by Indonesia was similar to those in many fast-growing Asian economies. With average economic growth of eight percent a year, developers put a premium on size and speed of construction, disregarding any overall cohesive plan."The regulations which
19071 govern development cannot keep pace with development itself," Sumarijanto said. "Unless the super (apartment) blocks are controlled by very clear urban guidelines, then each will become enclosed on its own."Tay Kheng Soon, a Singaporean architect, said Asian cities were in danger of losing their cultural heritage because of the burgeoning
19071 trend toward mass construction."Calls for respect for tradition lack any compelling force," he told the congress. "Asian cities and architecture are increasingly characterised by dramatic imported architectural statements, mainly from the United States."Asian architects are, however, beginning to promote their own cultural values in urban development.Malaysian architect Ken Yeang was
19071 awarded the Architects Regional Council Asia Award (ARCASIA) on Tuesday for combining a Kuala Lumpur office block with elements of a tropical landscape."The question is now whether developers are able to understand this," Sumarijanto said.Developers led by market forces were often unwilling to incur extra costs because of experimentation by
19071 the architect, he said.Those developers invited to join in the debate were adamant that the population pressure on Asian cities meant society had to be pragmatic."In Indonesia, more than one million units of houses are needed every year. As for now, the supply is only around 100,000 to 150,000 units
19071 a year," Ciputra (Eds: one name), founder of Indonesian property giant PT Ciputra, said.Ciputra said that because of overpopulation in Asian cities, constructors were now being forced to build self-contained satellite developments on the city boundaries.Whilst realising that new development was crucial, Sumarijanto said this kind of development could lead
19071 to a city losing its character."If you lose the soul of a city, you lose the city itself," he said.</

19073 Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday dissolved Japan's parliament and set October 20 as the date for general elections.The elections for the 500-seat Lower House, the first since July 1993 polls ended 38 years of unbroken rule by the Liberal Democratic Party and ushered in an era of coalition government,
19073 have so far failed to excite an apathetic public.Most analysts expect a record-low turnout for a heated but issue-free contest after weeks of wrangling between the LDP -- which Hashimoto now heads -- and its two smaller coalition partners over timing of the polls.The focus is on whether the LDP,
19073 which regained the reins of power in 1994 in a coalition with the Social Democratic Party and New Party Sakigake, can capture a simple majority or will be forced to shop for new coalition partners.Hashimoto urged his party to fight to give him a second term unfettered by the need
19073 to compromise with coalition partners."Although the LDP has been the biggest party over the last three years, we still don't have a simple majority," Hashimoto told a party gathering after he dissolved parliament.Hashimoto is expected to pin his bid for a second term on an improving economy and his handling
19073 of a bitter dispute with the southern prefecture of Okinawa over U.S. military bases.The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), headed by former LDP powerbroker Ichiro Ozawa, plans to attack the government for imposing an unpopular sales tax rise scheduled for next April.Shinshinto, made of components of the reformist government that
19073 ruled briefly in 1993-94 before being tripped up by the LDP, will also offer a plan for a drastic overhaul of the tax system and to cut bureaucratic red tape.To Shinshinto's chagrin -- and widespread public scepticism -- the LDP has adopted administrative reform as its election platform, making it
19073 hard for voters to compare platforms.But Hashimoto's pep talk to the LDP on Friday offered a hint that he stands more for continuity than drastic change."We are heading for a storm of reform, and our politics, administration and social system must weather it," he told LDP legislators.Analysts say the most
19073 likely way for the LDP, to survive in government -- given that it is unlikely to capture a simple majority -- is to forge a coalition with a smaller party with reformist credentials.The Democratic Party, a new 40-strong group of defectors from the Social Democrats and Sakigake, which boasts maverick
19073 Health Minister Naoto Kan as one of its members, fits the bill, analysts say."Stagnation would come if the LDP gets a simple majority," said John Neuffer, a political analyst at Mitsui Marine Research. "The economy would like a strong plurality for the LDP, with Kan and the Democrats there to
19073 hold Hashimoto's feet to the fire on reform."The polls will be the first under reforms enacted in 1994 to correct a gerrymandered system so as to make campaigning less costly and reduce dependence on political donations.Under the new system, candidates will contest 300 seats in single-seat constituencies, with the other
19073 200 seats decided through proportional representation.</
19074 Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto pledged after dissolving the Lower House of parliament on Friday that he would fight elections believing in the victory of his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP)."I will strive to fight elections believing in the victory of the LDP," the prime minister told a group of legislators
19074 of his party, the biggest in the three-party coalition.Hashimoto said he had done his best in the eight months since he took office to find a way to tackle the problems of bad loans held by mortgage firms and rebuild trust with the people of Okinawa. "We will come under
19074 storms of major reforms, and politics, society and the administration need to survive. I have decided to dissolve (the Lower House) believing that now is the only time for the people to consider the nation's future and set the direction for it," Hashimoto said.Earlier, Hashimoto's cabinet formally set October 20
19074 as the date for general elections. The polls will be the first under a system designed to make campaigning less costly and reduce graft. In place of the old multi-seat system, 300 seats will be decided on a first-past-the-post basis, with the other 200 selected by proportional representation.Hashimoto's LDP favoured
19074 going before voters as early as possible before April, when an unpopular sales tax will be raised to five percent from the current three percent.Hashimoto is expected to pin his hopes for a second term in office on an improving economy and his handling of a bitter dispute with Okinawa
19074 over U.S. military bases there.The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) plans to attack the government for imposing the sales tax rise and offer its own plan for a drastic overhaul of the tax system and to cut bureaucratic red tape.</

19106 A group of Japan's 71 biggest companies, facing a potential financial squeeze from poorly performing employee pension funds, has urged the government to reform the nation's corporate pension system, an official from the group said on Friday."It is possible the credit ratings of Japanese companies will decline if the shortage
19106 of pension funds is stated on the companies' balance sheets," the official said.Japan's rigid pension system should be reformed to help maintain Japanese companies' international competitiveness, he said. Japan's Welfare Ministry has decided to introduce market value accounting for pension funds' assets from March 1998 to more accurately gauge the
19106 financial state of the funds. At present, book value is used to calculate the assets, which does not immediately show losses caused by market price falls.The official said the 71 firms, including Nippon Steel Corp and Hitachi Ltd, also called for relaxing specified yields to variable yields on pension funds.Employers
19106 participating in the corporate pension system are required to maintain specified yields, currently at 5.5 percent a year, to guarantee predetermined benefits. However, the actual return on investments is now about three percent as a result of Japan's record low interest rates and weak economic recovery, industry sources said. Many
19106 corporate pension funds are facing a shortage of funds to pay benefits to pensioners in the future, they said.To boost returns on investment, the 71 firms called for the abolition of ceilings setting the maximum level of pension assets that can be invested in different financial instruments.The official said the
19106 group also urged the government to allow them to introduce a defined contribution pension plan, which is popular in the United States, as an option. In Japan, the benefits that an employee will receive on retirement are set beforehand. Under a defined contribution plan, benefits would depend on how much
19106 the employee saved and how well the money had been invested.Separately, the securities industry has been calling for the introduction of a defined contribution plan, which if it came into effect, would likely see a rise in stock investments through mutual funds such as it is done in the United
19107 Burmese police on Friday blocked the main road leading to the residence of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Friday where her National League for Democracy had planned to hold a congress, witnesses said."They are trying to prevent our congress from taking place," said an NLD party member, who
19107 was standing near a roadblock erected along University Avenue where Suu Kyi's house is located.Police refused to let people or vehicles gather in the vicinity of her home and diverted traffic to other roads, witnesses added.NLD party sources told Reuters they had heard that police planned to prevent anyone from
19107 gathering near Suu Kyi's home where a congress of about 200 of the NLD's key members had been planned from Friday to Sunday.A plan to hold a similar gathering in May spurred the arrest of some 260 democracy activists by the military government.The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council
19107 (SLORC) later released the detainees.So far, this time, the SLORC had not arrested any NLD supporters, NLD sources said.The scene at Suu Kyi's house was quiet with nobody gathering outside her home, although some NLD members were inside, witnesses added.There were many NLD party flags flying prominently around the compound
19107 in Suu Kyi's lakeside home to mark the congress.Repeated attempts to reach Suu Kyi's home by telephone to obtain comments from her or senior party officials failed.The NLD, which won a landslide victory in a 1990 general election that was never recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration
19107 Council (SLORC), tried to hold its first-ever gathering of elected representatives in late May.One diplomat said the upcoming party meeting would be a test of how serious the SLORC was in its desire to gag Suu Kyi who has continued to push for more democracy in Burma.He said the planned
19107 congress would clearly be seen as a challenge to the SLORC but government reaction had been muted so far.</
19108 Singapore will continue to grow in importance as a centre for foreign exchange trading despite the rising cost of doing business in the city-state, the head of Southeast Asia's fifth largest bank said on Friday.Overseas Union Bank Ltd's president and chief executive officer, Peter Seah, said Singapore had all the
19108 essential ingredients for a successful foreign exchange market. "If you remove the dollar-yen trading volume from the numbers, then Singapore is the third largest foreign exchange trading centre in the world. Certainly it is a market with bigger depth and volume than Tokyo," Seah told Reuters in an interview."You are
19108 looking at a very vibrant foreign exchange market and I see that as a major growth area for Singapore," he said."It's also an area which receives a lot of encouragement and support from the government." OUB is the fifth largest bank in ASEAN after the other three Singapore banks --
19108 The Development Bank of Singapore Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and United Overseas Bank Ltd -- and Thailand's Bangkok Bank, Seah said.The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.The bank has a large treasury operation which accounts for about 10 percent of
19108 its income, which includes active dealings in foreign exchange and other currency-based derivatives. Seah said Singapore was a far more "internationally orientated" market than Tokyo."In terms of depth of services available and instruments that are traded here, we are already ahead. For the moment we see overselves as complementing Tokyo,"
19108 he said."In the longer term we don't know. Tokyo will certainly always remain a major threat to Singapore in terms of its ability to service the region." Seah said the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX), which trades a range of currency-based derivatives, had recovered quickly from the "little blip" over
19108 the collapse of British merchant bank Barings.Losses run up by Barings Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson in Nikkei futures traded on SIMEX broke Barings in 1995."But the Barings case came and went very quickly and our markets here have gone from strength to strength," Seah said."We see that continuing and we
19108 see Singapore playing a major role also in the development of regional currency trading." Seah said he expected Singapore's foreign exchange market over the longer term to be the main market servicing Southeast Asia and the wider region to give corporations a place to trade and to hedge their foreign
19108 currency positions."Rising cost is an area of concern in Singapore but look at London," he said. "London today continues to be the dominant financial centre despite the high cost of doing business.""(Cost) is an important consideration, but what is more important is the facilities that are available, the infrastructure, the
19108 ease of communications, the language capabilities, the people, the skills available, the critical mass of financial institutions that are available here," he said."All these add up, together with the very singular trust and support by the government, to ensure that financial institutions here receive the right perks, are supported by
19108 the right laws and guided by the right type of regulations to be able to operate effectively and efficiently.""If you put all that together and look at the level of productivity that you can get out of operating in Singapore, the cost of doing business here becomes secondary for the
19108 financial institution that wants to locate in Singapore," he said.</
19109 The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan (LTCB) is aggressively trying to improve the quality of its assets and distinguish itself from its numerous rivals amid fierce competition in the Japanese market, company officials say."Japanese banks currently have similar faces," Kazuhiko Oiwa, director and general manager at LTCB's corporate planning division,
19109 told Reuters in a recent interview. "We want to make it clear what our strategy is as a wholesale bank."Oiwa said his bank would maintain its status as a wholesale lender and at the same time strengthen its investment banking business. LTCB also plans to establish a trust banking unit
19109 in the latter half of the current business year ending March 1997.LTCB, ranked as the world's 20th biggest bank in terms of assets, provides long-term funds to corporations and currently has about 8,000 corporate customers.It raises funds mainly through debentures rather than by taking deposits from individuals. Thus it has
19109 only a small network of domestic branches -- less than one-tenth of the more than 300 branches which other big commercial banks can boast.Analysts say LTCB has been aggressive in restructuring its operations and boosting its competitiveness in special fields such as derivatives and consulting.The bank said earlier this year
19109 that under its restructuring plan, it would cut its assets by 1.3 trillion yen ($11.7 billion) in the next two years.It plans to achieve this by cutting less profitable loan assets by one trillion yen ($9.0 billion) by March 31, 1997 and selling shareholdings worth 300 billion yen ($2.70 billion)
19109 by March 31, 1998. As of the end of March, its assets totalled 29.52 trillion yen ($265 billion).Earlier this year, it sold its Belgian unit LTCB (Europe) to Banque Paribas Belgique, closed its representative offices in Milan and Melbourne, and announced it would sell its U.S. securities business unit to
19109 Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc."We are meeting the challenge of cutting our assets, which have swollen too much," Oiwa said.In 1995/96 ended March 31, it posted a parent current loss of 110.48 billion yen ($995 million) as it disposed of problem loans of 650 billion yen ($5.85 billion), including those
19109 to failed housing loan firms. In 1996/97, it expects parent current profit of 20 billion yen ($180 million) while disposing of problem loans of more than 100 billion yen ($900 million).Analysts said it may be another few years before LTCB can reduce problem loans to manageable levels from the 1.2
19109 trillion yen ($10.8 billion) of such loans it had as of end-March.Oiwa said the bank's restructuring plan is contributing to its earnings for the current year to some extent. It is aiming to improve profits by 30 billion yen ($270 million) each year through the restructuring programme.An analyst at a
19109 foreign brokerage said: "Considering its strength in derivatives and strong business ties with big- and medium-sized corporations, I expect it will go along as a bank with special features."However, he said there was some doubt about opportunities for growth in light of mounting competition in domestic markets amid the ongoing
19109 financial deregulation.Asked about the possibility of a merger with another bank in the future, Oiwa did not deny such a possibility but said: "We are not considering merging with another bank now and will not think about that for the time being... We are busy becoming slimmer and more attractive

19111 China's Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin moved on Friday to tighten the communists' grip on the state media and to strengthen his position with a blaze of publicity before a party plenum.He used a visit to the Beijing offices of the People's Daily, the party mouthpiece, to deliver a hardline
19111 speech on the importance of maintaining communist control of all media, the newspaper reported, splashing the news and three photographs of Jiang across its front page.Diplomats said the speech by Jiang was aimed at bringing back into line Chinese writers and more daring media organisations that have tried to push
19111 the limits of propaganda restrictions over the past two years.State television devoted most of its main evening news broadcast on Thursday to showing Jiang's People's Daily tour, his third highly publicised appearance this week, and diplomats said the party chief and designated heir to paramount leader Deng Xiaoping appeared to
19111 be trying to shore up his position.The party is expected to hold its annual plenum early next month. Jiang will need to muster all his political forces to demonstrate he is in control and to fight off opposition to his leadership and policies from within the highly secretive Politburo and
19111 Central Committee."The leadership of the media should be in the firm grip of people loyal to Marxism, loyal to the party and loyal to the people," the People's Daily quoted Jiang as saying.Jiang followed the lead of late Chairman Mao Zedong by underlining the importance of the state-controlled propaganda machine
19111 to continued Communist Party rule in China."Media work can be said to be ideological work," Jiang said. "It is related to the future and the fate of the party and the state. Party news organisations are a part of the very life of the party."He reminded Chinese media that their
19111 role was to provide ideological underpinning for Communist Party rule and to stir up the people in support of the party."Historical experience has proved repeatedly that whether guidance of news is right or wrong has to do with the party growing strong ... the solidarity of the people and the
19111 prosperity of the nation," Jiang said."If the direction of ideology is correct, this is a blessing for the party and the people, but if the direction of ideology is incorrect, this is a disaster for the party and the people."Diplomats said Jiang's speech was the latest sign of a freeze
19111 across China's cultural world. China's propaganda tsars have asserted their authority in recent weeks by removing the president of the most outspoken newspaper in China's capital. It had reported a poisoning case that was alleged to have caused a plunge in sales of a state-owned beverage manufacturer.Cui Enqing was sacked
19111 as president of the the Beijing Youth Daily and replaced by Chen Xing, a deputy editor-in-chief of the rival and conservative Beijing Daily, on September 17.The Beijing Youth Daily had become the city's most popular newspaper, on sale at most streetside stalls. It had unusually open coverage of disasters and
19111 a sensational approach to news compared with the stultifying diet of good news and party propaganda offered up by other newspapers.</

19114 North Korea warned on Friday that it would exercise its "right to retaliate" if South Korea fails to return a submarine and its surviving and dead crew members who landed in the South last week."Our retaliation may be hundredfold or thousandfold. No matter what kind of retaliation we may make,
19114 the South Korean puppets will be wholly to blame," said a statement carried by Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and monitored in Tokyo.It was the second straight day of warnings from Pyongyang's official media over the submarine incident. On Thursday, North Korea said without elaborating that it would
19114 take strong measures against South Korea over the deaths of some of the North Koreans.Seoul estimates 26 North Koreans went ashore in South Korea from the submarine on Wednesday last week. Nine have since been killed by South Korean security forces, 11 were found shot dead -- possibly murdered by
19114 their own colleagues -- and one was captured. South Korean authorities have been searching for the others.Thousands of South Korean troops backed by helicopters have been engaged in a massive manhunt in an effort to end what has been one of the deadliest North-South clashes since early in the Cold
19114 War."The South Korean authorities must immediately stop their ill-intentioned campaign over our wrecked boat and return our submarine and surviving and dead crewmen immediately and unconditionally," the KCNA statement said."As victims, we have the right to retaliate on the offenders," said the statement, which reiterated Pyongyang's assertion that the submarine
19114 accidentally drifted into the South's waters.Seoul has dismissed North Korea's explanation for the incursion as "not worthy of consideration".South and North Korea have been technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended only with an armistice agreement.</

19120 a final decision would be made on October 23.The current ceiling on the benzene content of gasoline is five percent.MITI is also planning to stiffen guidelines on the sulphur content in gas oil, which is mainly used by buses and trucks, to below 0.05 percent from October 1997, the official
19120 said.Current standards allow up to 0.2 percent of sulphur."An agreement on the sulphur content standards has not yet been reached among all parties involved," he said.A conclusion is expected in a month's time, he said.The oil industry has been preparing for the stricter quality guidelines on oil products by upgrading

19130 Overseas Union Bank Ltd's treasury operations, such as trading in currencies, derivatives and commodities on the bank's own account, are growing, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.He told Reuters in an interview he expected treasury operations to become an increasingly important part of the activities of
19130 Singapore financial institutions but banks had to position themselves well to take advantage of the trend."For us, our treasury operations have been growing and it is a significant percentage of our total bottom line," Seah said. "Our treasury income (now) contributes more than 10 percent of our total income," Seah

19154 Japan's monetary authorities, claiming that the worst is over for the nation's financial crisis, is still propping up the fragile banking system discreetly to keep global concerns from flaring up again.The Ministry of Finance (MOF) appears to be parking a substantial volume of dollar-denominated deposits, using cash raised through dollar
19154 buying intervention, at commercial banks.This helps banks to operate in international financial markets without problems by ensuring ample dollar cash in hand, banking sources said.A year ago, a series of fiascoes at Japanese financial institutions, including Daiwa Bank's huge losses in unauthorised bond trading in New York, raised global concerns
19154 about the Japanese financial system.This resulted in a "Japan premium" which Japanese banks are asked to pay as an additional cost in borrowing funds overseas, making it virtually impossible for some banks to raise funds in the offshore markets.The premium has been around 10 basis points for major Japanese banks
19154 recently after being pushed up to 50 basis or The sources said the continuing aid from the MOF in the form of dollar deposits is helping to cap possible rises in the Japan premium, which might otherwise resurface."MOF deposits are still running, although the overall volume may be declining," said
19154 one bank official.A MOF official said he was aware of the deposits, which had existed for some time, but declined to comment on whether they were designed to help deal with fund-raising problems at specific banks."We are aware of it merely as a means to diversify management of external assets
19154 (of the Government)," he said.Japan's external reserves, the world's largest, have increased sharply in the past year and a half. They stood at $214.03 billion at end-August from $125.94 billion at end-February 1995.Banking sources said the rise in foreign assets was largely due to a heavy volume of currency intervention
19154 last year to stem the yen's sharp rise, which sent the dollar down to a post-war record low of 79.75 yen in April.The sources said the MOF does not directly channel funds to troubled banks but does it through banks with high credit ratings, to make transactions in the money
19154 market look natural to those not involved in the deals.A halt in support by the MOF could cause problems to many banks in which a failure of one bank may risk spilling over into the overall banking system, analysts said."The situation surrounding the banking system in Japan does not warrant
19154 a quick withdrawl of deposits from commercial banks," said Testufumi Yamakawa, vice president and director of Japan economic research at Goldman Sachs (Japan) Ltd."Given negative views by overseas operators and risks that their concerns flare up again, it would be safe to maintain ample liquidities (at some banks)," he added.Shinano
19154 Morita, a director at Standard &amp; Poor's in Tokyo said: "Without support by the government (in various aspects), it may not be strange if the Japan premium resumes rising".She said the banking system is still vulnerable despite steps taken by banks and the government in the past year, with no
19154 quick improvement in sight.In June, parliament passed bills to clean up the nation's bad loan mess and deal with bank failures, coupled with a scheme to wind up failed mortgage firms using taxpayers' money. Japan's 21 largest banks' disposed of about 10.7 trillion yen of loan losses at the end
19154 of March.Anlaysts and economists said the presence of Japanese banks in the international markets is likely to fall.Unlike Western banks, many Japanese banks customarily raise short-term funds on offshore markets to make long-term lending to corporations.But rises in funding costs on short-term borrowing and the Japan premium make it difficult
19154 to reap profits in their international lending business."Japanese banks' behaviour, different from international standards, is now in the process of being rectified," said Masayuki Kichikawa, an economist at Nomura Research Institute.Taisuke Tanaka, market strategist at Credit Suisse in Tokyo, said the MOF's deposits might be aimed at allowing some ailing
19154 banks to gradually withdraw from their international business without serious damage.</

19161 South Korea and Taiwan are among Asian nations most damaged by a downturn in U.S. demand for electronics, but experts say their outlooks differ sharply."They were both affected badly by the slowdown in global demand for electronic products, particularly from the United States," said Kevin Chan, economist at Salomon Brothers
19161 in Hong Kong.Electronics account for the majority of exports from both nations, but Korea had been particularly vulnerable to sinking Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) prices and this would hinder near-term recovery, analysts said."In Korea's case, (the trouble) is just starting," Graham Courtenay, an economist with SBC Warburg, said.Semiconductors and
19161 other electronic components account for at least 35 percent of Korea's exports, which crashed in response to slowing global demand, ING Barings said.Currency fluctuations worsened the situation, making Korean exports more expensive than competing Japanese products.The won has depreciated by only seven percent against the dollar in the last year,
19161 compared to a 30 percent decline in the Japanese yen.Courtenay said there had been plenty of warning signals to the DRAM price decline, but Korea failed to respond and cut back production."The price plummeted essentially because Korea was making too many," he said. "Korea has more or less destroyed the
19161 price... We all knew the price of DRAMs remained much higher than a normal cycle would suggest but Korea continued to expand capacity like no tomorrow, and all of a sudden tomorrow came."But growth in Korean exports, which are restricted to relatively few products -- electronics, machinery, automobiles and steel
19161 -- fell across the board, worsening a trade deficit to an estimated US$14.2 billion this year from US$4.7 billion last year.ING Barings estimates Korea's exports growth at 7.5 percent this year from a stellar 30.3 percent last year. Sluggish recovery to 9.0 percent is forecast next year.Taiwan, by comparison, is
19161 already showing signs of recovery, with Salomon Brothers noting a 37.4 percent rise in computer orders in the first half this year."The total exports decline appears to have bottomed," Salomon said in a recent report. "Export orders received by Taiwanese companies up to the first seven months this year were
19161 growing by an average of 7.3 percent, while total exports grew by 4.3 percent over the same period."Even so, declining demand is expected to push Taiwan's export growth down to five percent this year from 21 percent last year. Recovery is forecast next year to about 11 percent.Falling semiconductor prices
19161 actually buffered Taiwan from some of the damage this year, ING Barings said. Cheaper components fuelled demand for personal computers and notebooks, which make up most of Taiwan's electronics exports.Courtenay said Taiwan was also in a better position when the electronics price slide occurred thanks to a domestic inventory adjustment
19161 that started over a year ago."Taiwan's inventory build-up started fairly rapidly last summer and since then she's been adjusting them, which is one reason growth has been so low. She's been running down inventories," he said.In addition, Taiwan will reap increasing rewards from growing trade links with China, and from
19161 its development of high value-added industries, experts said."The share of Taiwan exports bound for the China market is increasing very rapidly," ING Barings said. "Secondly, the composition of Taiwanese exports is increasingly high value-added and tethered to some of the fastest growing industries in the world."-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852)

19194 Across the stream from the glitzy skyline of Dubai, Ram collapsed at the Indian consulate after hours in the blazing heat waiting for a permit to leave the country he had helped build.Two storeys higher, Jeleel cowered in a corridor of the consulate, clutching her emergency travel papers with one
19194 hand as she wiped away tears with the other.Ram and Jeleel are illegal guest workers in the United Arab Emirates, a Gulf oil state where immigrants make up 75 percent of the population.But faced with a new law cracking down on illegal labour, they are now among an estimated 200,000
19194 immigrants rushing to leave the country during a two-month amnesty period for illegal workers that expires on September 30.The law, which takes effect on October 1, imposes stiff penalties on illegal aliens, foreigners without valid travel documents, and workers who violate labour laws.The government vows it will rigorously enforce the
19194 law, and many immigrants -- mostly from the subcontinent but also from the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries -- are scrambling to get out before it's too late."Most of these people came to the country legally, but they absconded from their official employers for various reasons, primarily ill-treatment," said
19194 Prabhu Dayal, India's consul-general in Dubai."Secondly, they absconded because their wages were not paid for some time. They were forced to abscond."Many of the immigrants also obtain legal papers stipulating they have to work for their sponsor, but break the law by leaving to work for several employers on a
19194 part-time basis, which they say pays more than sticking to one job.The UAE government says it is implementing the law to cope with a spiralling number of illegal immigrants, who it says pose a security threat to the country."You don't know how, when and why the illegal immigrants came, so
19194 we have to clamp down on them to achieve safety for our own society," Mohammed Rashid al-Abdooli, director of the inspections department at the Labour and Social Affairs ministry, told the daily Emirates News.The government also said the law would help combat the "visa mafia" which has made huge profits
19194 by illegally selling entry visas and work permits for up to $2,000.Like many illegal workers, Ram and Jeleel came to the wealthy emirates from impoverished villages in India, filled with high hopes of big money.They paid an Indian "agent" about 20,000 rupees ($550) to find them a job with a
19194 UAE sponsor -- a prerequisite for working in the country -- who would give them good pay, room and board."But when I arrived, the horror started," said Jeleel, who left her husband and three young children behind in a town near Madras to work as a housemaid in Dubai."They took
19194 my passport so I couldn't run away. I had to work days and nights cleaning, cooking, working but I never got paid. They told me 'later'. I still don't have a single dirham."Allegations by Asian housemaids in the Gulf of abuse are hard to prove and are often discounted by
19194 governments as fabricated or exaggerated.Ram, who worked as a construction labourer, stood in line outside the consulate with thousands of others, shielding himself from the scorching sun with a piece of cardboard. When he finally reached the counter to apply for his exit permit, he fainted."It's a story of human
19194 suffering. It's not merely numbers," said an Indian diplomat.When the workers return home, many will be deep in debt and face the same hardship they tried to escape by coming to the Gulf, diplomats say.No figures for departures were available, but embassies said about 100,000 emergency papers had been issued.
19194 Many expect a rush for permits as the deadline nears.The consul-general of Pakistan in Dubai, Sajjad Ashraf, said some families who applied to leave had come to the UAE over 30 years ago, before the seven emirates unified as one country and declared their independence from Britain."They came when there
19194 were no border controls," Ashraf said. "They just arrived on launches and started working."Diplomats and travel agents say thousands of immigrants will be stranded in the UAE beyond the September 30 deadline because airlines cannot cope with the exodus.Flights to destinations such as New Delhi, Bombay and Manila until the
19194 end of the amnesty have been booked for over a week. Tickets for a 2,000-passenger boat scheduled to leave Dubai on September 28 were sold out within hours.Jeleel and many like her do not even have the money to pay for a flight or boat back to India. She huddled
19194 with other penniless immigrants in the consulate corridor, nervously waiting to hear if a donor could pay for her to go home.</

19196 Bonn, while the 672-member lower house moved to the seat of government in Berlin of Berlin, 600 km (375 miles) to the east.Many argue it would also be a waste of money if officials had to shuttle between the two legislative chambers hundreds of miles (km) apart."The lower house and

19201 A major human rights report to be released on Friday chronicles a catalogue of alleged murder, torture and sustained oppression in Nigeria and calls on the international community to isolate the West African country.The 52-page report, compiled by Human Rights Watch, accuses the military government headed by General Sani Abacha
19201 of having no intention of ever relinquishing power.Human Rights Watch is an international non-governmental organisation founded in 1978 to press for and monitor internationally accepted standards of free society.The report, released in Belgium, the United States, the Netherlands and Britain, says international outrage at human rights abuses has been dulled
19201 by economic considerations.It warns that a failure to press for change will entrench the government and lead to further abuse.A spokesman for the Nigerian embassy in Brussels said he was not aware of the report and reserved comment until after he had seen it.Abacha's government, which seized power in 1993,
19201 has been repeatedly criticised by the United Nations, Organisation of African Unity, the Commonwealth and the European Union for human rights abuse.Abacha nullified elections -- held to choose a civilian government to replace years of military rule by General Ibrahim Babangida -- and jailed Chief Mahsood Abiola, who was popularly
19201 believed to have been the winner.International outrage at Abacha's government reached a high point last November following the execution of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other members of the Movement for Survival of Ogoni Peoples who had been convicted by a military-appointed court of the murder of four Ogoni chiefs.In
19201 New York on Thursday, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy accused some fellow Commonwealth members of being "appeasers", saying they were allowing the Nigerian government "to get away with" executing Saro-Wiwa.The Human Rights Watch report says hundreds of opposition activists arrested under the guise of a "crime crackdown" are being held
19201 without trial throughout the country.It says that nearly half of 45,000 people in Nigeria's jails are awaiting trial and conditions are so bad that over 4,000 prisoners die in custody each year.It names dozens of people -- including children -- it says have been tortured by Nigerian authorities and lists
19201 examples of forced resettlement, evictions and expulsions the government is carrying out to quash opposition.The report is also critical of the Royal Dutch Petroleum Company, which controls the Shell Group, for not doing more to pressure the Nigerian government into change.Shell, which is responsible for the production of about 40
19201 percent of Nigeria's oil extracts, has faced a consumer boycott in recent years because of its links to Nigeria.A Shell spokesman in London declined to comment on the report until management had had time to study it.</
19202 World airports on Friday reported a seven per cent rise in passenger traffic and five per cent in cargo in the first half of 1996, backing forecasts of strong growth for the airline industry to the end of the century.Figures released by the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) also showed
19202 that U.S. hubs held the top four places in the global league for the busiest passenger and cargo airports between January and June.ACI, whose report was based on returns from 458 member airports around the globe, said 1.2 billion travellers passed through them in the first half of the year
19202 -- 73 million more than in the January-June period last year.Chicago's O'Hare was the world's busiest passenger airport, seeing 33.5 million people pass through, followed by Atlanta whose share during the first six months was boosted 16.2 per cent to 32.4 million due to the Olympic Games.In third position was
19202 Los Angeles with 27.9 million passengers, followed by Dallas/Fort Worth with 27 million, London's Heathrow with 26,5 and Tokyo's Haneda, Japan's main domestic hub, with 21,9 million.Cargo moved totalled 23.3 million tonnes, one million tonnes more than last year, while aircraft movements were up two per cent to 23.3 million.ACI
19202 director-general Otis Dunham said the figures "lend support to recent airline forecasts of over seven per cent annual growth in passenger trafic through to the year 2000."This is very healthy growth, and all parties in the air transport industry must redouble their efforts to get more capacity out of the
19202 system."This would imply "more efficient passenger and cargo processing, and the maximum use of new technologies both on the ground and in the air."The largest percentage passenger growth this year, although from a low base, was recorded by ACI's Africa region which saw traffic climb by 7.7 per cent to
19202 a total of 12.9 million.But North America, boosted by travel to the Olympic Games in Atlanta, saw growth of 7.1 per cent for a total of 608.8 million. Asia/Pacific airports saw 6.9 per cent more people passing through for a total of 168.7 million.European region passengers were up 6.2 per
19202 cent to a total of 330.3 million, while in the Middle East they totalled 21.7 million, an increase of 5.9 per cent. Growth in Latin America and the Caribbean was only 1.7 per cent to 36.5 million.In cargo, 12.5 million tonnes were moved by North American airports, an increase of
19202 5.5 per cent over January-June 1995. But the biggest percentage rise -- 18.4 -- was returned by the Middle East for a total of 778,951 tonnes.Asia/Pacific airport cargo moved grew four per cent to 4.4 million tonnes, while Europe saw a 3.8 per cent increase to 4.87 million.Africa, which moves
19202 relatively little cargo by air, saw a 1.1 per cent drop to 189,544 tonnes, and Latin America and the Caribbean saw an even steeper decline of 9.8 per cent to a total of only 505,399 tonnes.Top six cargo airports were Memphis, Tennessee, which moved 915,057 tonnes, Los Angeles with 821,149
19202 tonnes, Miami with 815,585, New York's Kennedy with 779,544, Tokyo's Narita with 771,045 and Germany's Frankfurt with 722,451 tonnes moved.</

19207 Italian unemployment dipped to 11.7 percent of the labour force at the end of July from 12.3 percent at the end of April, but the disparity between the north and south remained vast, the statistics office Istat said on Friday.Istat added that the fall was due almost entirely to seasonal
19207 factors as the tourist season moved into top gear, creating short-term jobs across the country."Year-on-year employment rose only in the service sector, while the performance of the agricultural sector remained negative and there was a fresh contraction in the industrial sector," Istat said.While the jobless total eased slightly throughout Italy,
19207 the underdeveloped south still bore the brunt of unemployment, with 21.4 percent of people there looking for work.By contrast only 6.2 percent of the labour force in the north and 9.7 percent of people in the centre of Italy were unemployed, Istat said.Italy's centre-left government has put the fight against
19207 unemployment at the top of its political agenda and on Tuesday signed a wide-ranging labour pact with unions and employers in a bid to stimulate the job market.The long-awaited accord included a reduction in the working week, incentives for people starting up their own businesses, tax breaks on research and
19207 encouragement for training schemes.Prime Minister Romano Prodi promised to provide 15 trillion lire ($9.9 billion) of government funds over the next three years to help finance various projects.Some 3.5 trillion lire of this is expected to be raised in the 1997 budget, which Prodi was due to unveil later on
19207 Friday.Istat, which releases employment data every three months, said the total number of people in work in Italy at the end of July was 20.3 million, up 1.2 percent on April's total and up 0.3 percent on July 1995.The army of unemployed eased to 2.69 million, down 4.5 percent on
19207 April's level. However the number of people who have been looking for work for more than a year continued to grow and accounted for 68.9 percent of the overall jobless total.Youth unemployment was also a major problem, with 32.9 percent of all people aged between 15 and 24 without work.
19207 In the south, this figure soared to 54.9 percent.As part of the labour pact, the government said it would raise the age at which people could leave school to 16 from the present 14 and promised to provide further education for anyone up to the age of 18.Analysts said the
19207 move should lead to a noticeable fall in the unemployment rate.The government is hoping to chop a further 50,000 off the jobless queue with the relaunch of a major infrastructure programme, which ground to a halt in the wake of the widespread corruption scandals of the early 1990s.Work on long-awaited
19207 motorway links in the centre and south of Italy is due to begin by the end of the year, along with an ambitious extension of the high speed railway network.</

19213 present-day reminders of the city's origins as a refreshment station for 17th century Dutch mariners bound for the spice islands of the Indies.Links between the Dutch and their former colonists were particularly close in the late 1890s when the Dutch rallied behind the Afrikaaners during the Boer Wars against the
19213 British.The then Queen, Wilhelmina, dispatched a Dutch warship to the Transvaal to fetch defeated Boer leader Paul Kruger, who arrived in the Netherlands to a hero's welcome.But in more recent times both countries chose to ignore rather than embrace their common heritage, driven apart by the policy of legally enforced
19213 segregation imposed by South Africa's ruling Nationalist Party in 1948.Queen Beatrix's German-born father Prince Bernhard publicly spoke out against apartheid during an informal trade visit to South Africa in 1954. 19239 Countries aspiring to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would do well to take note of the Netherlands, economists say.Dutch policy makers know how to operate in an EMU environment. The guilder has been tightly pegged to the mark for 15 years, and as its 1997 budget showed,
19239 the Netherlands has economic credentials which are the envy of Europe, they say.The key to the textbook Dutch economic performance -- 2.5 percent GDP growth, inflation of 2.25 percent, and falling unemployment -- is the unrelenting drive to stay competitive.With its quasi-fixed exchange rate policy, the option of tinkering with
19239 the value of the guilder to achieve international competitiveness has long been ruled out. So policymakers rely on low wage inflation and productivity improvements.Economists say the Dutch case highlights that real improvements in competiveness are an essential partner to fixed exchange rates."It's very important to realise that just fixing exchange
19239 rates is not enough," said Wike Groenenberg of Salomon Brothers in London. "The fact it's worked in the Dutch case...is because of the internal policies to ensure the link is maintained."Christer Lindholm, economist at J.P. Morgan, agreed. "Regardless of whether Germany is your main trading partner, most European countries --
19239 France in particular is suffering from some competitiveness problems at present -- can take lessons from (the Dutch experience)," he said.The guilder was last devalued against the mark in 1983. At present it may officially move within a 2.25 percent band around the German currency, but in practice, the link
19239 is far stronger.The consensus wage bargaining tradition of the Netherlands is key to its low wage inflation, as is its flexible work force.Union acceptance of a jobs over pay principle and laws which make hiring part-time and temporary workers easy have kept wages in check and put more people back
19239 to work, thus driving down the government deficit and reducing pressure on the welfare system.As the Dutch prepare to take over the presidency of the European Union in January, they do so with almost 15 years of competitive improvements behind them. The results were evident in the 1997 Dutch budget,
19239 presented to parliament last week.The government's Central Planning Bureau forecast an inflation rate of 2.5 percent in 1997, just 25 basis points above the EU average and so comfortably within EMU criteria.The deficit was forecast at 2.25 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), within the 3.0 percent EMU limit and
19239 well below the 3.5 percent EU average.Economic growth was expected to reach 2.75 percent in 1997, private consumption was seen growing by 1.75 percent and unemployment falling to 5.25 percent from 6.0 percent in 1996.So as European neighbours slash debt and muzzle inflation in a race to meet stringent EMU
19239 standards can they expect to match the Netherlands' economic success and social harmony?Paribas economist Stefan Schneider said the Dutch success story is explained in part by close economic ties with Germany which absorbs a third of Dutch exports but also by its staunchly independent central bank, something else it shares
19239 with Germany."The ultimate reason is that both countries have central banks that have earned their credibility," he added.This has insulated the guilder from speculative attacks that have shaken less solid European currencies.Schneider questioned whether other European countries had the social consensus necessary to implement sweeping labour reforms and mirror the
19239 Dutch experience.Lindholm warned that adopting the Dutch approach to competitiveness improvements would not prove a quick fix but could deliver in the longer term."This kind of policy doesn't produce immediate benefits... But beyond 1999 it would definitely be sensible (for EMU countries) to try to achieve something like this."</

19246 Austria's leading research institute WIFO on Friday reiterated that it expected economic growth to accelerate next year but cautioned the recovery would be fragile, pointing to slack domestic consumption.In its quarterly economic report, WIFO stuck to earlier forecasts that GDP growth would slow to 0.7 percent this year from 1.8
19246 percent in 1995, then rebound to 1.0 percent in 1997."Although economic growth should accelerate in the course of 1997, it still will not match levels seen in the middle of 1995," wrote the institute, whose figures form the basis of government policy.Bouyant exports would contribute to the upswing next year,
19246 WIFO said, noting that exporters were benefitting from relatively stable foreign currency markets and strong demand from central and eastern Europe. 19246 would increase one percent this year and just 0.3 percent in 1997, down from 1.9 percent in 1995."As a result some branches of industry -- textiles, clothing, leather, construction, furniture and other consumer durables -- will see declining production," WIFO said.It traced the drop to the effects of government savings
19246 and a higher tax burden from the beginning of 1997. 19246 6.6 percent in 1995. In 1997 the figure would reach 7.5 percent, WIFO said.Consumer price inflation would remain at a modest 1.7 percent this year and next, compared with 2.2 percent in 1995. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254</

19256 The number of people out of work in France hit a record high in August of 12.6 percent, official figures released on Friday showed.The Labour Ministry figures showed the number of people unemployed in August, adjusted for seasonal variations, rose 39,500 to 3,085,100. The jobless rate, based on International Labour
19256 Organisation (ILO) criteria, which exclude jobseekers who did any work, hit a record 12.6 percent, up from 12.5 percent. Unemployment had fallen in July by 20,000 but economists had called the drop an aberration due to seasonal factors and predicted it would rise in face of continued sluggish economic conditions.The
19256 longer jobless lines were bad news for Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government which has made tackling unemployment one of its top priorities. Juppe has called a confidence vote in Parliament on the government's economic policy for Tuesday.But the government received some cheer on the export front with preliminary figures
19256 showing France's trade surplus had jumped to 11.10 billion francs from a revised surplus of 9.78 billion in June.The customs office had originally reported a surplus in June of 9.75 billion francs.</

19275 Britain and China reached agreement on Thursday on arrangements for a handover ceremony in Hong Kong around midnight next June 30, when the colony reverts to Chinese rule, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said.He also told a news conference after a long meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen that
19275 Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing would visit Britain in November and that agreement had been reached on the establishment of a large British consulate-general in Hong Kong after the Chinese takeover.The joint handover ceremony would take place in the ground foyer of the new extension to the Hong Kong Convention and
19275 Exhibition Centre, which has a capacity of over 4,000 people, in the presence of high-level guests including representatives of overseas governments and international organisations."This will be a very important occasion, both as a symbol but also representing the joint will of the British and Chinese governments with regard to smooth
19275 and successful transition and one which will meet the aspirations of the people of Hong Kong," he added.The ambassadors of a joint British-Chinese liaison group would sign a document in Hong Kong on Friday detailing the arrangements."It is automatic that the governor (Chris Patten) would be part of the ceremony,"
19275 Rifkind said, though that was not discussed with Qian.It was not yet known who would be coming from Britain "but you can certainly assume that the level of British representation will correspond to the importance of the occasion," he added.He also informed Qian that Britain would stage a purely British
19275 ceremony at sunset on June 30 on Hong Kong's central waterfront."We envisage a dignified ceremony incorporating both civilian and military elements. Hong Kong and Britain are part of each other's history and it's right therefore to commemorate that fact in this important way," he added.The consulate general in Hong Kong,
19275 with a staff of about 180, would be the largest British consulate general anywhere in the world and larger than many embassies.This would emphasise "the massive interest and commitment of the United Kingdom to Hong Kong in the years to come," the foreign secretary said.Rifkind and Qian, during their nearly
19275 two-hour meeting, reiterated their opposing views about China's intention to establish a provisional legislature as a stop-gap measure until new elections are held in Hong Kong."I emphasised our continuing belief that the establishment of such a provisional legislature was both unnecessary and undesirable. The Chinese side responded on the basis
19275 of their known positions," Rifkind said.On other issues, he said he raised with Qian the question of a number of Hong Kong residents detained in China and handed over an updated list."We have urged that the Chinese should deal with these matters in a sensitive way and one that respects
19275 proper legal obligations."Rifkind told a questioner the question of Tibet was not raised though he noted he met the Dalai Lama when he visited Britain some weeks ago.</
19276 Singapore said on Thursday that the United Nations had less influence now than during the Cold War, with major powers turning the Security Council into a political theatre to soothe domestic concerns.Yet Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar, in a hard-hitting speech to the U.N. General Assembly, said that nations big and
19276 small wasted hours on U.N. reforms in debates that "served to conceal and not clarify basic issues."Efficiency, the need to spend less money, were proper concerns but did not deal with the key question of "efficiency to do what?""The sad truth is that today the United Nations plays little or
19276 no practical role in the management of the most important political, strategic and economic questions of our times," he said.On Bosnia, he said the Security Council conducted a "political theatre to assauge the domestic concerns of some of its principle members."And on economic issues, he said the U.N. "Agenda for
19276 Development," was mired in theological arguments on issues that were not so complicated."What the least developed most urgently need is not intellectual sophistry but help to build the institutions and formulate the policies that will allow them to plug into the global economy," Jayakumarhe said.At a time when national decisions
19276 cannot be made in isolation, states are choosing other multinational forums outside of the United Nations.Yet, he said, the big Second World War powers were hanging on to their domination of the U.N. Security Council. Any expansion of the council, under discussion for two years, would probably not extend the
19276 veto power to developing states."It is expecially difficult to imagine major powers allowing developing countries the veto over their policies."At minimum, he said members should allow allow small states to join their closed-door consultations when issues concerned them."All the most important decisions of the Security Council are today made informally
19276 by the permanent members" -- the United States, Britain, China, Russia and France, with participation of other states merely symbolic."Formal session are clearly only a choreographed ritual to set the final seal of approval," he said.On finances, he said that arguments made by some states, presumably Washington and to a
19276 lesser extent Moscow, about reducing their financial burdens, did not apply when they were called on to share power."There has never been any suggestion by any of the big powers that their control over critical U.N. expenditure decisions, in particular peacekeeping expenditures, should be proportionately diffused among the majority of
19276 small countries who are expected to take up the financial slack that they want to discard," he said.</
19277 Publishers hoping to find a new star author in the networking mayhem of next week's Frankfurt Book Fair can be reasonably sure of one thing -- he or she will not be German.Although Germany's publishing industry ranks third in the world after Britain and China -- with more than 74,000
19277 new titles produced last year -- German writers don't come close to dislodging Anglo-American blockbusters from bestseller lists, even on their home turf.The latest German bestseller rankings, published weekly in the Spiegel magazine, show U.S. novelist John Grisham topping the list with a translation of "The Rainmaker"Anglo-American, Spanish and Scandinavian
19277 titles crowd the rest of the top ten, with Norwegian author Jostein Gaarder occupying fifth and sixth place, while the lone German-language representative, Johannes Mario Simmel, comes in tenth.As many as 2,500 German publishers are expected to join the 6,661 exhibitors turning up for the Frankfurt Book Fair this year,
19277 which runs from October 2-7.The Fair, the central theme of which this year is Ireland, is the industry's premier annual event. Organisers say that a majority of the world's book deals are discussed, if not finalised, here each year.But German publishers have to accept that, apart from Guenter Grass, the
19277 country's best known living writer, the only German novelist to achieve global success in recent years was Patrick Sueskind with his acclaimed novel "Perfume" (1985).The problem has become a focus for debate in Germany, where publishers say they are keen as ever to promote German fiction but concede that most
19277 German novels -- often criticised as pompous and introspective -- lack popular appeal in a crowded English-language-dominated market."They write for their peers rather than the public, as though they were producing scientific tracts," said one publishing source, who spoke on condition of anonymity."No publisher is going to subsidise them if
19277 they can get a really sure bet elsewhere," the source added.Munich-based publishing group Carl Hanser Verlag, operating in the "literary" end of the fiction market and sole German publisher of Ireland's Nobel prizewinning poet Seamus Heaney, is bringing a small retinue of German writers to the Fair along with its
19277 established stars."Of course we are hoping for some exciting buys from abroad but we are very concerned to promote our German writers as well," said spokeswoman Susanne John.John, along with other publishing executives, noted that much contemporary German writing was too sombre and its language too complex to be easily
19277 marketable abroad.Many German writers, including Grass, are prone to reflections on abstractions, usually on the complex phenomenon of "Germany" in the late 20th century.Overshadowed by weighty predecessors like Heinrich Boell and Thomas Mann, German writing also lacks the straight narrative tradition that has freed their U.S. and British peers to
19277 be more playful and contemporary."I think the joy in free narrative, simple story telling is much easier to find in the U.S. for example, than it is here," said John.The young Sofia-born novelist Ilia Troyanov, published in German but translated into English, is viewed as an exception and will be
19277 among Hanser's "stars" for the Fair but experience has taught the group not to set its targets too high.Norwegian bestseller "Sophie's World", originally discovered by Carl Hanser, has sold over a million copies in Germany, for example. "But with a German, if it's not Guenter Grass, to be honest we
19277 are happy with 10,000 (in sales)," John said."Without our big names, we could not get involved with young talent at all."The German book traders' association is making a strong push this year to promote German writing and is to link up with the British Translators' Association to produce a newsletter
19277 for British publishers to alert them to new German titles.German exports of book titles are estimated at a paltry 3.2 billion marks ($2.10 billion) annually -- and most of this is generated in German-speaking Switzerland and Austria -- compared with overall German book sales of 16.5 billion marks ($10.85 billion)
19277 in 1995."The problem we face is a linguistic one predominantly," said association spokesman Eugen Emmerling. "Plus the English speaking world already covers so many exotic themes and places that it is hard to find room for other things."Every seventh book sold in Germany is a translation and threequarters of these
19277 are of U.S. or British origin, which shows that the Anglo-American influence on popular German tastes is "getting disproportionate," Emmerling said."The German public is simply very much impressed by things like Hollywood films and other aspects of U.S. culture and of course these big international firms also have a better
19277 marketing position," Emmerling said.But Emmerling added that Germany's taste for international fiction revealed an open-mindedness not often seen in foreign markets. "It's a positive thing," he said. ($1=1.5206 Mark)</
19278 Born as a squat 25 years ago and later dubbed a social experiment, the "free town" of Christiania is today a virtual institution and a tourist site drawing a million visitors every year.The disused military citadel was occupied by a handful of hippies on September 26, 1971 and they were
19278 soon joined by hundreds more, pledged to build a new society of tolerance, democracy and environmental awareness."Within three or four months there were so many people it was too late for the government to do anything about it," said one of the original squatters, who uses the name "Asterix".The anniversary
19278 is being marked by three days of music, theatre and exhibitions.The Danish state, with a tradition of tolerance and a strong distaste for confrontation, never forcibly evicted the interlopers and over the years the Christiania community has won a large degree of public acceptance.Organised within a system of house, area
19278 and general committees, the approximately 700 adults and 200 children govern themselves by consensus on everything from community finances to disputes between neighbours.Christiania does not recognise Danish law and much public and official opposition to the commune stems from the open use and sale of marijuana there.Stalls on both sides
19278 of "Pusher Street" display a range of the drug's many varieties, sold by weight or in ready-rolled cigarettes at between 10 and 40 crowns ($2-$8) apiece.Some things are forbidden, however, even in Christiania.There are bans on the use or sale of "hard" drugs, the carrying of weapons, violence, the trading
19278 of buildings or dwellings and the wearing of "colours", the identifying emblems stitched to the jackets of motorcycle gang members.The community was invaded during the late 1970s by hard drugs dealers and prostitutes controlled by violent motorcycle gangs but in 1980 it fought back."The junkies were offered withdrawal treatment and
19278 the dealers thrown out," says the collective's guide booklet.Today there is an uneasy truce between the visionaries of Christiania and the hash dealers, most of them from outside the commune and some still connected to the bike gangs.Apart from the hard-drugs ban they are not allowed to operate near the
19278 children's play areas but Asterix says he and his fellows fight a constant battle to keep the dealers in line and he would rather they all left."There's lot of money being made and some heavy people involved, it's a big worry and we spend so much energy on this problem
19278 when we could be doing other things," he said.Police leave the illegal traffic alone for most of the time but stage largely symbolic raids once in a while.Many of the 3,000 visitors who throng Christiania on an average day come to buy drugs or use the cut-price bars, Asterix says,
19278 adding that the huge numbers of outsiders compared to the 900 residents detracts from the community atmosphere.Despite problems, Christiania still functions after a quarter of a century and claims credit for some pioneering schemes.The sorting of refuse into different recycling groups such as paper, glass, metal and organic waste for
19278 conversion to fertiliser was adopted in the collective long before the city of Copenhagen introduced the practice, said a veteran resident.The principle of allowing marijuana sale or use within a specified area was also a concept being considered by cities elsewhere in Europe, she added.Christiania itself, built some 300 years
19278 ago to strengthen Copenhagen's defences during a period of constant warring with nearby Sweden, covers some 35 hectares (86.5 acres) between a moat and a sea inlet, just east of the capital's centre.Along its fringes wooden cottages nestle among trees and bushes and along waterside footpaths, giving the air of
19278 a village deep in the countryside.At its heart are a former barracks and administration buildings which now house music venues, a children's theatre, restaurants, craft workshops, a radio station and a community newspaper.There is a business restoring antique stoves and furniture and another building the distinctive Christiania Bike, actually a
19278 tricycle with a large carrier mounted over the two front wheels which can transport goods, children, or a wheelchair.Among other enterprises, collectively run, are a vegetable market, blacksmith, printing press, carpenters, candlemaker and grocer. There is also a bakery, shoemaker, and a hairdresser.Services include a health centre offering traditional and
19278 alternative medicine, a workshop teaching Yoga, Shamanism, Shiatzu and other spiritual techniques, social counselling, childcare facilities and an ecological advice centre.Each resident pays a monthly fee of 880 crowns ($152) for electricity and water, communal services, maintenance and other collective outgoings.Asterix seemed unsure if he would still be a Christianite
19278 in 25 years' time but thought that the community would still exist, a belief shared by Ulla, a professional guide to Christiania."We certainly intend to be here for another 25 years," she said.And Christianites may still be negotiating with the government in an effort to decide the waterfront settlement's official
19278 status and future, as they have since 1971. ($1=5.788 Danish Crown)</
19279 Maverick Marin Karmitz, the French film producer who champions European and Third World cinema against the U.S. film industry, is yet again bucking the trend.He opened a new cinema this month in Paris's poorest arrondissement, the 19th, the only of the capital's 20 districts where all movie theatres had closed
19279 down."It's going to work," said the Romanian-born former rebel of the May 1968 Paris student riots as reports of good ticket sales landed in his office on the opening day.The 35 million franc ($7 million) investment is risky, and Karmitz confessed to being as tense as when any of the
19279 52 films he has produced, many of them award-winning, hit the screens.Besides his money, 58-year-old Karmitz puts his heart in his cinema chain, which he named "14 Juillet" (July 14) after the date of the 1789 Revolution, perhaps to illustrate his ongoing rebellion against the domineering trend of blockbuster films
19279 that he calls the rich man's cinema.His cinemas, which have captured 10 percent of the Paris market, show quality films in their original, sub-titled version. There is no certainty that the residents of the neglected, heavily-immigrant 19th district in northeast Paris will go for them.Karmitz said he fell in love
19279 at first sight with the 120-year-old, Belle Epoque-style pavillion housing a canteen for employees of the Paris Canals Authority and decided to turn it into a six-theatre cinema without even bothering to order a market survey.The result is an elegant glass and concrete building on the bank of a canal,
19279 its walls decorated with one-liners from famous films. Its restaurant boasts a wine list chosen by film director Claude Chabrol, who manned the May 68 barricades with Karmitz.Karmitz opened the first of his 34 screens 12 years ago near Paris's Bastille square, in a popular district that was being taken
19279 over by property developpers. "People told me I was crazy," he said.The cinema prospered against all odds and helped to instil new life in the district. A grateful Karmitz has kept the headquarters of his production and distribution group MK2 in a backyard near Bastille, well away from rival companies
19279 in the chic Champs Elysees district.Karmitz is fighting the growing, U.S.-inspired trend of taking cinemas to suburban shopping malls, which he says break down the social fabric and turn town centres into deserts."A cinema must be like a local cafe, a cinema is life," said the soft-spoken, white-haired former film
19279 director.Karmitz, who backed European Union moves to keep the audio-visual industry out of the GATT world trade pact, said big suburban cinemas also boosted the U.S. film industry, the only one producing enough popular films to keep feeding the screens, at the expense of its ailing European competitor.He said the
19279 European film industry, unable to play to large audiences on the U.S. market because of language differences, was moribund, with the exception of the French industry.Forty percent of films shown in Paris in the first half of this year were French, against 32 percent from the United States and 17
19279 percent from other European countries. Sixty-four percent of films playing in the 14 Juillet chain were European."The world is going to be divided between the rich man's and the poor man's cinema," Karmitz said.The fight was between filmmakers who master technology and can afford costly special effects and virtual images,
19279 and those who, for lack of funds, must keep inventing stories."They will substitute imagination for money. This is what I want to fight for because that is how cinema will survive," he said.Karmitz has produced such award-winning successes as Louis Malle's "Farewell Children", and the late Krysztof Kielsowski's "Three Colours"
19279 trilogy of Blue, Red and White.A resolute foe of violence on the screen, he said films like U.S. director Quentin Tarantino's 1995 Cannes Golden Palm winner "Pulp Fiction" showed absolute contempt for the human body."People laugh as they blow up brains, without facing any punishment. This is intolerable," he said.He
19279 refused to distribute Pulp Fiction although he knew that it would be a box office hit."I did it knowingly. This is my freedom," he said.Karmitz said he was aware that he was treading a fine line and refusing to show films could be akin to censorship, but "I am not
19279 selling washing powder, I have a responsibility."I have fought all forms of censorship, but that does not mean I cannot have rigorous moral standards. I can afford to do what I want. I am independent. This is my own money," he said."We are living through barbarian times. I am not
19279 sure that I will see the end of the tunnel, but I hope my children will."His latest project, unveiled this month, is a "City of Image and Sound", a communication complex to open within two years alongside Paris's giant new library, the last of the late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand's
19279 architectural works.Karmitz's project will comprise more 14 Juillet screens, studios for three new television channels dedicated to knowledge, health and justice, and halls for debates."People feel a real need to speak up," he said. "Their speech has been confiscated by politicians who speak in their name."</
