19281 By Nicholas Doughty, Diplomatic CorrespondentThe U.N. Security Council, urged on by Arab states, agreed on Thursday to hold a formal debate on the Israeli-Palestinian crisis as fears grew that the Middle East peace process is about to collapse.The 15-nation Security Council met for private consultations on Thursday and agreed, despite
19281 U.S. reluctance, to convene a formal meeting on Friday at 1100 EDT (1500 GMT). Foreign ministers from some countries are expected to attend.More than 50 people, mostly Palestinians, have been killed in clashes in Gaza and the West Bank, leading to widespread Arab and European criticism of Israel's right-wing government
19281 and accusations that it is reneging on peace.Council President Alfredo Lopes Cabral of Guinea-Bissau announced the meeting, to which the United States -- Israel's chief ally -- agreed only reluctantly, saying there was little point in "rhetorical debate" when practical steps were needed.The Palestinian Authority, Saudi Arabia and Egypt had
19281 all requested a formal meeting of the Security Council. Egypt is the only current Arab member of the council.Egypt's U.N. ambassador, Nabil Elaraby, told reporters Arab nations would draft a resolution for Friday's meeting. "The situation is quite explosive," he said.Arab sources said the resolution would seek the closing of
19281 an Israeli-excavated archaeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem, near Islamic and Jewish holy places, which sparked Palestinian protest demonstrations.The group also wants the council to demand that Israel resume the Middle East peace process and abide by agreements already concluded with the Palestinian Authority by Israel's previous Labour
19281 government."We are not hoping for debate only, but for action," said Nasser al-Kidwa, the Palestinians' U.N. observer.The chances of Friday's council meeting endorsing strong criticism of Israel are slim, since the United States has the power to block any condemnation with its veto.In Washington, President Bill Clinton urged Israelis and
19281 Palestinians to end the bloodshed as his top officials engaged in frantic diplomatic efforts to salvage the peace process.Clinton made clear that the U.S. government saw Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in east Jerusalem as an irritant.Secretary of State Warren Christopher, in a telephone conversation
19281 with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu asked that the tunnel be closed, diplomatic sources said.But Netanyahu responded that shutting the tunnel down was not a viable political option and argued such action would be seen as rewarding violence, the sources said.Islamic and European nations, gathered in New York for the
19281 annual U.N. General Assembly, warned on Thursday that the crisis posed a grave threat to the whole peace process and criticised Israel, saying Netanyahu's Likud government would have to show it was committed to peace.Arab anger at Netanyahu's failure to extend self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza boiled over
19281 after his government opened the tunnel near the al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock mosques.British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said there was danger the peace process could be on the verge of collapse.U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali appealed for calm and said previous peace agreements should be implemented.Irish Foreign Minister Dick
19281 Spring, who speaks for the 15-nation European Union as his country currently holds the EU presidency, said he had conveyed to Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy "our deepest concern"."We emphasised very strongly and affirmatively the concern of the European Union that it was necessary for Israel to show ... a
19281 renewed commitment to the process. ... Signals need to be given by the Israeli government," he said.Islamic nations also met to discuss the crisis and issued a statement afterwards criticising Israel, calling on it to honour previous agreements and condemning the opening of the tunnel as "an illegal act".</

19289 Bookmakers were left running for cover on Saturday as Frankie Dettori rode seven winners from seven rides and made two punters half-millionaires.On one of the most astonishing days in British racing history, the cumulative odds on Dettori's winners amounted to 25,095-1, sending shudders down the oddsmakers' spines.One lucky backer in
19289 northern England staked just over 60 pounds ($93) in a special combination bet with bookmakers William Hill on all Dettori's mounts and ended the day over 500,000 pounds ($780,600) richer.Another punter won a similar amount with a Ladbrokes shop in London after staking an each way accumulator costing 10 pounds
19289 ($15.6).William Hill spokesman David Hood said: "It is the worse day in bookmaking history. Our managers will be settling bets until midnight."The fifth winner was expensive, the sixth dismal and after the seventh it was time to put the lights out."Another Hill spokesman, Graham Sharpe, echoed: "Frankie's seven winners have
19289 made this the blackest day in British bookmaking history."I shudder to think how much it's cost us. It's a disaster. We don't expect any sympathy but it's the worst day's business we've done since Lester Piggott was in his heyday and winning the Derby every year."It will cost us millions.
19289 We will tot up the damage when everybody's back at work."Dettori's last three winners were all favourites, forced down to much shorter prices than forecast by the sheer weight of money running up from earlier bets, such as doubles and trebles.Dettori joked with racegoers after his historic seventh win: "I'm
19289 just warming up, is there any more racing? This is everybody's dream. God was on my side."After the sixth win, I felt it was almost impossible to do seven and I told the trainer Michael Stoute that I would blame him if I lost!"I noticed when I came out the
19289 horse, who was 12-1 in the paper, was 2-1 favourite so I am sure you all had a pound on it. Go and collect your money."Thousands stayed behind to salute Dettori's feat, which included four winners for the Godolphin team trained by Saeed bin Suroor.He threw his goggles into the
19289 crowd and then sprayed onlookers with the champagne.Mike Dillon of bookmakers Ladbrokes said: "When the most popular jockey riding wins all the races, you lose. But I have to say this is tremendous day for the racing industry."The two-day Ascot festival ends on Sunday with another seven-race card. Dettori has
19289 mounts in each and the first three are favourites.On such sparkling form he might even fancy a tilt at a record set in August 1933 by Sir Gordon Richards who rode 12 winners in succession.The first came in the last race at Nottingham, followed by all six the next day
19289 at Chepstow and the first five the next day at the same track.Another Ladbrokes spokesman, Ian Wassell, said: "Tomorrow is another day to try to get some of our money back. It's the Ascot festival again. He's in all seven again tomorrow and we hope he won't repeat the dose!"I'm
19289 sure we'll have floods of people looking to do the same bet again tomorrow."</

19298 The president of the International Amateur Athletic Federation said on Saturday he intended to ban competitions which conflicted with IAAF-organised events.Speaking before Sunday's world half-marathon here, Primo Nebiolo said: "From next year we will protect our events much more strongly. This is the last time there will be competitions on
19298 the same day as an IAAF world championship. "All competitions must have special permits and the IAAF will not give any permit to any event in competition with our events." The announcement is likely to upset organisers of some well-known independent city marathons, but Nebiolo added:"We have the strength to
19298 control the sport and will disqualify any athletes taking part in other events. We will put a window three or four days before and afterwards when there cannot be any events. We can do what we want because we are the governing body." Nebiolo's comments were prompted by the fact
19298 that many of the world's top road runners have decided to stay away from Sunday's world half-marathon. Kenya's Paul Tergat, the holder of the world best for the half marathon, will compete over the same distance in Luxembourg while the Berlin Marathon has attracted the likes of Spain's Abel Anton
19298 and Kenya's Sammy Lelei. The IAAF road running commission and the Association of International Marathons are due to meet in Dublin on October 10 but Saturday's announcement will increase the strain between the bodies. The 1997 World Half Marathon Championships are scheduled for October 4 in Kosice, Poland.</

19306 English referee Paul Danson sparked off a new row over match officials on Saturday when he sent off two Sunderland players for relatively minor offences and reduced the match against Arsenal to a farce.With Sunderland having had the best of the opening spell and the game being played in a
19306 sporting spirit, Danson booked Sunderland striker Paul Stewart for a deliberate handball.In only the 15th minute, he then booked Sunderland defender Martin Scott for a hard tackle on Arsenal's Lee Dixon.Six minutes later he booked Scott and sent him off for a late tackle on Dixon, which looked clumsy but
19306 not malicious.Then he had a stand-up row with Sunderland manager Peter Reid and sent him out of the dugout.With half-time still six minutes away, he booked Stewart for a second handball and sent him off.The match was effectively over as a contest. Sunderland played with their remaining nine men back
19306 in defence for the rest of the game before losing 2-0 to two late goals.Reid was furious and could hardly find words to describe his feelings. Police protected Danson's dressing room door and Sunderland's fans went away feeling they had lost as much to the referee as to Arsenal.Reid, who
19306 admitted he called the referee "a disgrace" added: "All we want from decisions is a bit of common sense. I didn't see a bad tackle in the game."Will I try to apologise to him? I think I'll have a beer instead. That referee is off my Christmas card list for
19306 a start. But I have to apologise for my actions. I was out of order and completely unprofessional. But you get carried away in an emotional game."I have tried to go into the referee's room and talk to him but the police are guarding the door and won't let me
19306 in."Arsenal's caretaker-manager Pat Rice, who hands over to new boss Arsene Wenger on Monday, said he had every sympathy for Reid and Stewart.Rice said: "I told Peter I thought the game had been spoiled by his two guys being sent off."If Paul Stewart had been my player I would have
19306 been very disappointed to see him sent off for handball."It is a shame and I felt the referee could have allowed him a bit of leeway. He could have said, `Do that again and you are off,' instead of showing the red card."It is not the first time this season
19306 Danson has been involved in controversy. He reported Coventry manager Ron Atkinson for his behaviour after Atkinson told him he had missed a clear handball offence before Chelsea scored a goal against Coventry at Stamford Bridge three weeks ago.Atkinson has since been charged with bringing the game into disrepute.Two years
19306 ago Danson sent off Alvin Martin, then playing for West Ham, but the English Football Association later decided he was wrong to do so after examining video evidence.The match followed a plea from referee David Elleray, who sent off Everton's Duncan Ferguson last week, for the soccer public to show
19306 greater understanding of referees' problems.The officials are following strict orders from the governing bodies to apply discipline but have attracted criticism that some referees are following the edicts too closely.Elleray wrote in Saturday's Daily Express: "We are prepared to hold our hands up and say we were mistaken. The general
19306 feeling is that this has been a tough start to the season and if we are brutally honest, we've not always got it right."Last week in London, at a UEFA Round Table panel, leading referee Serge Muhmenthaler of Switzerland claimed: "Referees rarely make mistakes because they only make decisions when
19306 they are 100 per cent sure of themselves."I also don't think we need any help from technology or two referees to officiate one half of the pitch each."Two referees ? At the moment the game seems to be having enough trouble with just the one.</

19315 two minutes from time.But the real drama came in the first half when Sunderland manager Peter Reid was ordered from the dug-out as his side had two men sent off in 18 minutes by referee Paul Danson.Defender Martin Scott and striker Paul Stewart were both shown the red card for
19315 relatively minor offences.Scott was sent off after 21 minutes for a second foul on Arsenal defender Lee Dixon while Stewart was booked for a deliberate handball early in the match and was booked again and sent off after 39 minutes for appearing to handle the ball a second time.Reid had
19315 a shouting match with the referee after Scott's dismissal and was then banished from the dug-out.Wimbledon, who started the season with three straight league defeats, chalked up their fifth successive league win with a 2-0 victory at Derby with Robbie Earle (49th) and Marcus Gayle (70th) scoring. 19320 with the Orioles vying for the wild card,and then came through with the big blow off his first pitch from reliever Paul Spoljaric.After the game, Alomar had to explain both his heroics and his spat with Hirschbeck."I am not happy about what happened, but we are just human and we

19323 South Africa have banned their players from carrying commercial sponsors' logos on their bats because it could gain more prominence than the main match sponsors, national cricket chief Ali Bacher said on Saturday.The decision runs counter to a ruling by the International Cricket Council (ICC) which introduced a rule change
19323 in July allowing players to "rent" out the top nine inches on the front and the whole of the rear of their bats."We feel a bat logo could have a greater impact on a viewer than an event or a team sponsor logo on a shirt. We cannot allow this,"
19323 said Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa.Bacher said the UCB had faxed the ICC expressing the their concern over the issue.</

19333 possibility of adding a test against England to the Wallabies' eight-week, 13-match tour of Europe which starts in Italy on October 19.The ARU on Friday described as "preposterous" an offer by Home Union Tour Committee (HUTC) chairman Bob Weighhill of the mid-week dates of December 3 or 4 for the
19333 England test.The Wallabies had earlier suggested either November 2 or 16 for the England test and said they would consider cancelling the December 1 test against Wales at Cardiff, which had been added to their original itinerary, if those dates were rejected."Their offer is just a sham," ARU chief executive
19333 John O'Neill was quoted as saying in The Australian newspaper on Saturday."We've got a multi-million dollar Wallaby team that will be travelling around the backblocks of Scotland, yet they can't play England."I told (Weighhill) we would now be looking at the option of cancelling the Welsh test," he said.Weighhill said
19333 on Friday the threat to drop the Wales test could have "serious repercussions", which in turn brought a stern response from O'Neill."The whole thing is just ridiculous," O'Neill told The Australian."This Four Home Unions Tours Committee is an anachronism. 19333 not easy to change arrangements which had been in place for up to six months."For many of those people this is a rugby event of a lifetime," he said."I can understand Australia's frustration but they should appreciate our problems. They also have to realise the game is in absolute turmoil
19333 over here with the dispute between the unions and professional clubs," Weighhill said.Australia are scheduled to play Italy, Ireland, Scotland and Wales and hoped to add an England test so they could play their first "Grand Slam" of Home Unions matches since 1984.</

19352 after just two minutes when he left Deportivo keeper Jacques Songo'o standing with a superbly curled free-kick.But after a strong start Betis seemed to relax and the game became scrappy with the referee failing to clamp down on some heavy challenges.With former Ajax man Finidi George in fine form down
19352 the right wing, Betis had most of the play in the the second half.But sloppy marking let in Frenchman Mickael Madar to set up Brazilian forward Rivaldo for a simple equaliser 20 minutes from time and the visitors went home with three points after Madar was allowed a free header
19352 10 minutes later.In other games played on Saturday, Espanyol followed up their midweek UEFA Cup victory by winning 5-1 at home to first division new boys Extremadura, a side without a single point in five games. 19361 Paul Broadhurst, chasing his first win since last year's French Open, surprised even himself when he fired a 68 to share the lead with Italian Costantino Rocca in the European Open on Saturday.The Briton, one stroke behind Rocca at the halfway stage, was far from optimistic when he began the
19361 third round."I hit the ball so badly on the range before I went out I didn't know what to expect. I was cutting it, then I would pull one. It was just a mixed bag, I don't think I hit two shots the same," he said.But once on the course,
19361 everything went right and his four under par 68 took him level on 206 with Rocca who had a 69."I suppose that's golf. Probably tomorrow I'll hit it well on the range and play badly," Broadhurst said.He almost had two eagles. His 75-yard pitch to the par five first stopped
19361 only inches away and on the 413-yard 11th his nine iron approach did the same.Rocca, joint halfway leader with Jim Payne, jumped into a two-shot lead with three birdies in his first four holes but allowed the chasing pack to catch him with bogeys at the fifth and eighth.Sweden's Per-Ulrik
19361 Johansson moved into third place only a shot behind with a 66, while Scotland's Andrew Coltart was alone in fourth on eight under after a 69.Payne managed only a 72 to drop into a share of fifth spot with Ireland's Padraig Harrington, Spaniard Miguel Angel Martin and Briton Derrick Cooper.Colin
19361 Montgomerie, although 11 off the pace after a 70, still moved closer to winning his fourth European Order of Merit. Fellow Briton and closest rival Ian Woosnam fell even further back with a 74 which left him four over par and three behind Montgomerie.</

19366 U.S Open champion Pete Sampras gained a measure of revenge for his defeat by eventual winner Yevgeny Kafelnikov in the French Open with a 7-6 6-3 win over the Russian in the Swiss indoor championship on Saturday.While Sampras had won four of the six meetings between the pair, Kafelnikov had
19366 taken the last two, including a straight sets semifinal win at the French Open earlier this year to deny the American a shot at the only grand slam title to elude him.Sampras will meet Germany's Hendrik Dreekman in Sunday's final.Dreekmann, looking for first career title, breezed into his second final
19366 of the season with a 7-5 6-4 win over the Czech Republic's Jiri Novak. Sampras will be going after the 43rd title of his career.Playing in his first tournament since winning a fourth U.S. Open, the 25-year-old American will also be looking to keep his 100 per cent record intact,
19366 having won all six finals he has appeared in this year.Sampras said later the key to reaching his seventh final was surviving the a tense first set which he won in a tie-break 7-4.Kafelnikov, the third seed and world number five, took early control as he broke Sampras to go
19366 in to a 3-0 lead.But Sampras broke back and held serve to pull even at 4-4, the set going to the tie-break when Kafelnikov failed to convert a match point at 6-5.Sampras had the only break in the second set to go ahead 3-1 and never gave the Russian an
19366 opportunity to break back, wrapping up the match in one hour 13 minutes."It wasn't easy, it could have gone either way," said Sampras, the first number one to play in the Swiss indoors since Bjorn Borg in 1980. "He had set point once and he could have won the first
19366 set just as easily."He got off to a good start but you have to keep on plugging away and hope to get a break, which I did."The second set I saw him hang his head a little and I took advantage of it."Timely back-to-back breaks were also the key to
19366 Dreekmann's semifinal win over Novak, who had upset Australian Open champion Boris Becker in the second round on Thursday.Dreekmann, ranked 49th in the world, broke late in the first set to go up 6-5 and then serve out for the set.The German began the second set with another break and
19366 then held serve to win the first meeting between the two promising 21-year-olds."He's obviously got to this stage by playing good tennis," said Sampras. "He's had a good run but hopefully it will end tomorrow."</

19368 Midfielder Andreas Herzog took sweet revenge on his former team mates at Bayern Munich on Saturday, scoring twice in Werder Bremen's 3-0 win to knock the 13 times champions off the top of the German league.Challengers VfB Stuttgart seized their chance to go first with alacrity, returning to their stylish
19368 winning ways with a 5-2 away win over Bayern's local rivals 1860 Munich featuring two goals from Brazilian Giovane Elber.For Bayern, the stinging defeat came on top of a midweek defeat to Valencia in the first round of the UEFA Cup and a bout of public wrangling over the form
19368 of striker Juergen Klinsmann.Austrian international Herzog opened the scoring with a 23rd minute penalty and struck his second two minutes after the interval. Another Bayern reject, Bruno Labbadia, made it three 20 minutes from time.Herzog felt he had been badly treated in Munich, where he spent just one unhappy season
19368 before returning to Bremen in a swap for Mario Basler, and warned his former team mates before the match that he had "saved a little bit of anger for Bayern". Herzog was jubilant after handing Bayern their first defeat of the season and pushing them down to third place."I showed
19368 them I can still play football," he said.The result was especially galling for Basler, who told Bremen coach Dixie Doerner before the match: "I can only laugh when I hear that Bremen don't miss me... If I were still there, you'd be challenging at the top and playing for the
19368 title."In the event Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni pulled Basler off at half time along with the out-of-sorts Klinsmann.But Klinsmann at least could take consolation from national trainer Berti Vogts, who told the daily Bild:"He's not out of form, he's just going through what all strikers go through...If (Bayern president) Franz
19368 Beckenbauer starts thinking out loud about resting him, I say, he needs confidence, and he won't get that on the bench...If he said he wanted to go, 20 clubs would be queueing up for him."Meanwhile, Stuttgart set out to prove that they could still turn on the style now that
19368 young stand-in coach Joachim Loew has been given a full-time contract.Last week Fortuna Duesseldorf spoiled Loew's party by handing the 1992 champions their first defeat of the season, and 1860 Munich looked like doing the same when Bernhard Winkler stabbed in a rebound from an Abedi Pele shot in the
19368 11th minute.But this time the southerners regained their composure as Elber and Matthias Hagner scored twice in two minutes.In the 58th minute, Elber notched his fifth goal of the season, using the outside of his foot to sweep an unstoppable long-range shot past goalkeeper Rainer Berg.Croatian international Zvonimir Soldo made
19368 it four in the 63rd minute and Fredi Bobic, last season's leading scorer, completed the rout six minutes later.Ghana's Pele scored his first goal for 1860 Munich one minute from time to make the score 5-2.Early-season pacesetters Bayer Leverkusen moved into second place on 18 points, one behind Stuttgart and
19368 one ahead of Bayern, with a 2-1 win at Schalke.Last season's champions Borussia Dortmund are seventh with 13 points, but entertain lowly St Pauli on Sunday.In the day's other matches, Freiburg recorded their first win of the season by beating Hansa Rostock 1-0.Hamburg and Duisburg drew 1-1, and Borussia Moenchengladbach
19368 came back down to earth after putting Arsenal out of the UEFA Cup, losing 1-0 at local rivals Duesseldorf.</

19371 where he was given a neck brace for mild whiplash. It was not immediately clear for how long he would have to wear the brace.Midfielder Davids was unhurt and took part in the warm-up for the Italian champions' match against Perugia on Sunday.It was the third car accident involving a
19371 Milan player in less than a year.Last February, George Weah and French defender Patrick Vieira escaped virtually unharmed when the Liberian striker's car hit a guard rail in northern Italy.Speedy striker Marco Simone was also fortunate when he suffered only minor injuries after a crash last summer.</

19374 the constitutional text and the NP delegation described its viewpoints regarding those issues referred back by the constitutional court."Earlier this month the court ruled that some aspects of the new constitution did not comply with principles laid down in multi-party talks and had to be redrafted.This raised the possibility that
19374 Inkatha, which boycotted the constitution-making process in protest at the African National Congress having reneged on an agreement for international mediation, might return to the constitutional assembly to contribute to drafting amendments."The NP delegation strongly encouraged the IFP to rejoin the proceedings of the constitutional assembly as soon as possible,"
19374 the statement said."The IFP will now prepare specific proposals especially regarding the constitutional position and role of traditional authorities, whereafter the parties will meet again."The statement said those at the meeting included Roelf Meyer and Sam de Beer from the NP and Walter Felgate and Ben Ngubane from Inkatha.Inkatha held

19375 Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medyyessy said on Saturday that the country needed strict 1997 budget and he was not satisfied with the pace of the social security reforms."If we 'soften', we will need a supplementary budget in 1997, which could have the worst message ahead of elections," he told the
19375 daily Nepszabadsag."I am not satisfied with the pace of the advancement of reforms, mainly what concerns the health care system," he said.He added the Finance Ministry's calculations about the potential directions of reforms have not been completed yet, adding that social resistance to the reforms is strong."This can also make
19375 politics uncertain," he added.The ministry expects Hungary's social security deficit to run as high as 53 billion forints this year, compared with a target of 17.8 billion forints.The draft 1997 budget, which is to be submitted to Parliament on Monday, would widen the field of revenues upon which social security
19375 contributions are paid, and slash the expenditures of state agencies and local municipalities.Medgyessy said the government should tighten its control on the social security funds and it should have a veto right in certain decisions of the funds, which work as self-governments directed by elected bodies.He added Hungary needed strict
19375 1997 budget, otherwise the government could become unpopular ahead of the 1998 elections."Politicians should recognise that the success of the 1998 elections does not depend on how much surplus money we put into pockets," he said.Medgyessy said Hungary's economic stabilisation programme, which began in March 1995 should be continued to
19375 lay the foundations of sustainable growth.He added he hoped that the first modests benefits of the stabilisation course would be felt by Hungarians already next year.The stabilisation programme, aimed at reining in Hungary's soaring budget and current account deficits, caused real wages to slump by some 10 percent in 1995,
19375 and Medgyessy acknowledged they could drop by further four to five percent this year, compared with the two percent government target.Medgyessy said Hungary will keep the system of pre-announced crawling peg forint devaluations next year, but its has not been decided yet whether the current monthly 1.2 percent rate could
19375 be reduced next year."I have a debate with the central bank's president on when we could reduce the monthly (devaluation) rate," he said.Hungary expects inflation to drop to 18 percent next year from the forecast of 22 to 24 percent for this year.He added Hungary will continue to abolish its
19375 seven percent customs surcharge next year, taking import figures and competitiveness into account when deciding about the pace of abolishing the surcharge.-- Sandor Peto, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040</

19377 Hurricane Isidore weakened but remained a strong storm on Saturday as it churned north in the distant Atlantic far from land, the National Hurricane Center said.At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Isidore's center was about 1,200 miles (1,925 km) west of Africa's Cape Verde Islands, at latitude 19.7 north and
19377 longitude 43.3 west, moving north near 13 mph (20 kph).National Hurricane Center forecasters said that motion was expected to continue for the next 24 hours. The storm was not expected to threaten the islands of the Caribbean Sea and the U.S. east coast, said Miles Lawrence, a hurricane specialist at
19377 the center.Isidore's track also seemed likely to keep the storm away from Bermuda, the British island territory that lies well east of the North Carolina coast in the Atlantic."Bermuda has a very low chance of being threatened, certainly not in the next few days," Lawrence said.Maximum sustained winds had dropped

19424 The world's major coffee growers decided on Saturday to maintain a tight grip on exports to prevent an oversupply.The 14-member Association of Coffee Producing Countries, meeting in London, made no policy changes and said it would limit coffee exports for the year to June 1997 to the 53.5 million 60-kg
19424 bags agreed on in May.Exports for the year ended last June were 44 million bags, slightly below the 45.8 million bag limit it set in the first year of the new programme, the ACPC said."There was a shortfall of 2.19 percent of the target and this is seen as positive
19424 by the member countries," ACPC president Rubens Antonio Barbosa of Brazil told reporters.ACPC officials said no new initiatives were in the pipeline."The idea is just to continue with the second export programme...there are no new proposals," ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliviera Silva, also of Brazil, said.But Oliviera said he did not
19424 discount the possibility of revising supply controls if prices continue to tumble.Coffee prices are hovering at $1,500 a tonne, down from nearly $2,000 in May. 19424 fabric of the coffee culture"."We are very concerned about the proposed changes. We maintain that the origin of coffee is where it is produced," one producer delegate said.</

19426 processed beyond a certain degree in any given EU importing country would be labelled as originating there and not in the growing country."Origin is one of the most important factors for the determination of the organoleptic characteristics of coffee," the ACPC statement said."The lack of recognition of origin (where coffee
19426 is actually planted, grown and harvested) will lead to general confusion...and could be a factor to undermine the very fabric of coffee culture," it said."Producing countries unanimously oppose all kinds of proposals which might lead to give coffee as a final product (green, roasted, roasted and ground, decaffeinated, soluble coffees,
19426 extracts, etc) a different origin from the one that is attributed by the place where it is produced," it added.Producer delegates have said they were upset by the proposals and wary of them being implemented."We are very concerned about the proposed changes," one delegate told Reuters on Friday, adding that

19522 management and financial disorder in futures brokerages, disregard for professional standards, inadequate control of risk, and frequent litigation because of disputes, the newspaper said.In the notice, the CSRC re-affirmed that futures brokerages or authorised firms doing futures business must not entrust individuals or other companies to trade futures on their
19522 behalf. All such contracts must be cancelled within 30 days of the CSRC order on September 24, the notice said.All futures companies must conduct an internal audit within 30 days of the issue of the notice and must report the results of the audit to the CSRC, it said.As from
19522 the fourth quarter of 1996, all the firms must conduct internal audits every three months and report the results to local securities bodies, as well as the CSRC, within 15 days of the end of each quarter.The notice re-affirmed that only authorised futures brokerages could conduct futures business and these
19522 brokerages must apply to the CSRC if they want to open new branches.Violators would be fined and those guilty of serious offences would have their futures licences revoked, the notice said.Those who committed crimes would have their cases referred to the public security and judicial departments, it said.</

19533 The United Arab Emirates on Saturday extended an amnesty for illegal immigrants, giving tens of thousands of people from the Indian subcontinent and southeast Asia another month to legalise their stay or leave.Floods of illegal immigrant workers have been scrambling to get out of the oil-rich Gulf Arab state by
19533 plane and boat to avoid tough new penalties when the amnesty expires and a new law cracking down on illegal labour comes into force.The previous amnesty was due to expire on October 1, and with airlines and shipping companies unable to cope with the mass exodus, diplomats feared thousands would
19533 be stranded in the UAE after the deadline."It has been decided that the amnesty period is extended one more month until October 31, 1996 to enable those remaining offenders to benefit from this temporary exemption," an Interior Ministry statement said."The ministry hopes that this matter will be taken very seriously
19533 without any delay in order not to find it necessary to take the strict legal procedures...," it added.Jamal Sanad al-Suwaidi, the secretary-general of the committee for the demographic structure of the UAE which is in charge of the amnesty, said he expected some 140,000 illegal workers to leave the country."By
19533 Monday I expect around 70,000 people will leave the country and for the following month I think it will be a similar number and most of those people are illegal in the UAE," he told Reuters Television in an interview.He added that the move was prompted by political, economic and
19533 security factors."With this huge number of illegal workers in fact what they are doing is they are creating an illegal labour market and creating at the same time economic hardships for themselves and for other workers in the country," al-Suwaidi said."So I think it's an important decision and its about
19533 time that the decision was executed. It's a normal trend all over the world," he said.The UAE government says the new law will help curb the spiralling number of illegal aliens, who it says pose a security threat to the country.But many of the immigrants complained the amnesty period was
19533 too short and did not give them enough time to prepare for the voyage, purchase tickets and collect outstanding wages.Diplomats expect some 200,000 illegal aliens to try to leave the country before the new deadline expires at the end of October. 19533 exit permits thus far. 19533 have taken out passes or emergency certificates... 19533 work as labourers, housemaids or in the service sector. 19551 Egypt reopened one of its best endowed pyramid sites to the public on Saturday, 40 years after the Egyptian military turned the area into an army base and sealed it off from the outside world.The group of five large pyramids, at Dahshour 40 km (25 miles) south of Cairo, are
19551 second only to the famous trio at Giza and have the advantage of lying in largely unspoiled desert, away from the traffic and high-rise buildings of Giza.They also include the world's first true pyramid and the only rhomboidal or "bent" pyramid -- both built by the pharaoh Snerefu at a
19551 time of architectural experimentation.Sneferu, who ruled Egypt in about 2600 BC, was the father of Cheops, the man who built the Great Pyramid at Giza."These make it one of the most important archaeogolical sites in the ancient world," said Ali Hassan, secretary general of Egypt's Supreme Council for Antiquities."It is
19551 also one of the places which you can smell the history of Egypt. The desert is virgin, there is no invasion of modern building and no pollution. And you can see pyramids from both the Old Kingdom amd the Middle Kingdom," he added.The Bent Pyramid, the shape of which no
19551 one has ever explained to the satisfaction of all, contains cedarwood beams imported by ship from Lebanon and still in good condition more than 4,000 years later, he said.A trickle of foreign tourists came to the site on opening day and were delighted by what they saw."I used to come
19551 around and look from afar. I always hoped that this day would come, to let people who enjoy pyramids and antiquities come and visit them," said an Italian visitor."This is how we imagined Giza -- pyramids in the middle of nowhere. It's very, very impressive," said an Englishwoman.Culture Minister Farouk
19551 Hosni, who formally opened the area, said that after long talks the antiquities department persuaded the army to evacuate the site two years ago and had spent the time since then preparing the area for visitors."No buildings will be allowed for a good distance all around. We have agreed that
19551 with the military," he added.In the case of Giza, the antiquities department has fought a running battle with developers to protect the site from encroachment. Last year the government eventually abandoned plans to build a ring road right across the Giza plateau.But perhaps the biggest gain will be to archaeologists,
19551 who have hardly touched the site."Almost nothing has been done since (British Egyptologists) Perring and Vyse came in the 1830s," said Hassan.A new wave of achaeologists will want to find out why there is no burial chamber and no trace of a burial or a mortuary temple in Snerefu's true
19551 pyramid, he added."A door has been opened for scholars to come and work. The elements of this pyramid have not yet been completely found. We need excavations to explain the unknown. There is work here for years and years to come," he said.Dieter Arnold, the curator of Egyptian art at
19551 the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, told reporters he would be interested in the three Middle Kingdom pyramids at Dahshour, built by the Pharaohs Senusert III, Amenemhat II and Amenemhat III about 800 years after Sneferu.He said he believed the ruined mortuary temples at these pyramids may have
19551 been the prototype for the giant temples which stand intact on the west bank of the Nile near the southern town of Luxor, capital of Egypt another 300 years later.Visitors will eventually be able to enter almost all the Dahshour pyramids, once they are clear of the damage caused by
19551 grave robbers and by time.</

19575 The Group of Seven richest industrial nations delivered an upbeat outlook for the world economy on Saturday, saying inflation was low and forecasting faster growth into 1997.Top finance officials from the seven powerful nations also discussed ways of spreading the better times they see ahead to poorer countries by easing
19575 their debt burden.In a statement issued after a nearly six-hour meeting, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the Group of Seven welcomed recent movements in currency markets."We welcomed developments in exchange markets over the recent period," Rubin, who acted as chairman of the meeting, said in his statement. "And we
19575 reaffirmed our standing commitment to reduce (trade) imbalances and to cooperate closely in the exchange markets."The dollar has been buoyant in recent days, although currency rates have been broadly stable for some time.Rubin said the G7 finance ministers and central bankers, gathered during the IMF and World bank annual meetings,
19575 believed the world economy had improved since they last met in April and looked forward to even better times ahead."The general sense around the table was that the outlook had improved since our last meeting and that conditions appear to be in place for a strengthening and broadening of the
19575 expansion of the world economy into 1997," Rubin said.He said the G7 would seek to reduce government budget deficits in the medium term, pursue anti-inflationary policies and strengthen economic reforms."Throughout the G7 countries, inflation remains at low levels, efforts are underway to reduce fiscal deficits and external imbalances have receded,"
19575 the Treasury chief said.The G7 is comprised of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.With discussions freed of the acrimony that has sometimes characterised talks in the past, the G7 officials were able to focus on how to aid the world's poorest debtor nations.Rubin said the Paris
19575 Club of creditor nations would sharply increase the amount of help they are prepared to offer the world's poorest debtor nations. Under the new initiative, up to 80 percent of their debts would be forgiven, compared with a 67 percent ceiling now.The debt-relief initiative -- involving actions by the Paris
19575 Club of creditor countries, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank -- is aimed at putting debt-ridden poor nations, many of them in Africa, back on their feet."I hope we will be able to have the first countries to benefit from (the debt initiative)...before the end of the year,"
19575 Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told reporters after the G7 meeting.</
19576 President Bill Clinton on Saturday hailed a budget compromise with the Republican-controlled Congress that avoids another government shutdown, saying it showed "what happens when you abandon extremism."Discussing the budget breakthrough hammered out by congressional leaders and White House negotiators, Clinton told a campaign rally that "It is good for America."With

19576 over the current federal budget, Clinton was able to shape spending priorities more to his liking by threatening to use his veto power."In the last three months, as the American people have made it clear that they have no intention of seeing our country torn apart and divided by a
19576 radical agenda, we have restored a measure of bipartisanship and working together in Washington," Clinton said."Look what happens when you abandon extremism in favour of working together," Clinton told an outdoor rally in the heart of downtown Providence.White House officials said it was "no coincidence" that Clinton's reference to improved
19576 working relations with Congress over the last three months coincides with the point when Republican rival Bob Dole stepped down as Senate majority leader.Clinton told the crowd the budget accord was reached because "it reflects your priorities, and you have been speaking loud and clear."The last budget battle with Congress
19576 wound up benefitting Clinton, who cast himself as a stalwart against extreme Republican ideas and the defender of funding for popular programmes like Medicare and Medicaid for the poor and elderly.Clinton, who began his day in Texas, later appeared before a large and enthusiastic turnout in Fall River, Mass., at

19576 to withhold federal payments from someone owing support."No area cries out for greater personal responsibility than the quiet crisis of child support," Clinton said in his weekly radio address. 19576 refusing to support your family."Although the federal government currently is withholding income tax refunds to offset child support debts, Clinton's action broadly expands the practice to other payments, including worker's compensation and military retirement and disability.</
19577 (Corrects 2nd graf to make clear compromise gives president what he asked for, not more than what he asked for)By Jackie FrankAfter an all-night bargaining session, the White House and Congress reached a budget agreement early on Saturday that President Bill Clinton hailed as bipartisan progress towards a balanced budget.The
19577 compromise grants the president the extra $6.5 billion that he requested for domestic spending with $4 billion of that going to education.Speaking at a political rally in Providence, R.I., Clinton hailed the accord and praised Republicans for working in a bipartisan fashion. "It is good for America because it continues
19577 to move us toward a balanced budget while protecting, not violating, our values," he said.Republican congressional leaders, who last year pushed the government to shut down twice rather than accept the administration's budget, stressed that the bipartisan accord ensured the government would stay open next week.But Senate Democrats said they
19577 remained skeptical about what they said was the Republicans' "midnight conversion" and wanted to comb the as-yet-unprinted bill carefully.Senate Minority Leader Tom Dachle, D-South Dakota, said they would not hold it up unnecessarily. Amendments they might offer include one to guarantee physicians the right to inform patients and to remove
19577 abortion restrictions on aid to international family planning agencies.The massive $450 billion spending bill also includes banking regulatory reform, bolsters savings and loan reserves, sells broadcast airwaves, clamps down on illegal immigration and expands anti-terrorism efforts.The House of Representatives scheduled a vote on the compromise in a rare Saturday session
19577 while the Senate will debate through the weekend and send it to the White House before Monday's midnight deadline. The new fiscal year starts Tuesday, Oct. 1 and without passage of this bill, federal agencies would be forced to close.The administration had wanted the defense department's budget of $245 billion
19577 cut by $3 billion and had asked for $10 billion in extra domestic spending.Republicans were in a rush to adjourn so they could begin campaigning. Asked if that meant they gave in to Clinton, House Speaker Newt Gingrich said that wasn't the case but that compromises were made."One of the
19577 lessons we learned is that you have got to find a way to work together to get things through the Senate. You have got to find a way to get the signature of the president if you want to get it done," Gingrich, R-Georgia, said of the compromises they made
19577 this year.Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, R-Mississippi, added, "If we had the White House, it (the budget) would be different."A middle-of-night compromise on legislation to impose strict controls on immigration and crack down on illegal aliens cleared the way for agreement on the massive spending bill which funds the largest
19577 agencies in the government.The extra $6.5 billion granted Clinton's request for $4 billion more money for Head Start and other education programs and raises college student Pell grants to the largest amount in history.It allows $1.1 billion to fight terrorism, $650 million for fighting fires in Western states, $400 million
19577 to aid in recovery from Hurricane Fran, $123 million for troop redeployment in Saudi Arabia and $8.8 billion for the war on illegal drugs.The extra spending will be paid for with $2.9 billion raised from the sale of cellular communications airwaves, $3.1 billion in higher bank reserves needed to clean-up
19577 the last of the savings and loan crisis, and $1 billion from defense.The more than 2,000 page spending bill -- which likely will not be printed before the House votes -- pays for the Pentagon, the national parks, education, jobs programs, environmental protection, law enforcement including Clinton's plan to put
19577 100,000 police on the street by 2000, the White House, foreign aid, health research and a host of other activities.Congress had approved separately seven of the 13 regular spending bills worth about $150 billion covering housing, energy, water projects, Congress, agriculture, and some other agencies.Sen. Mark Hatfield, the retiring Republican
19577 chairman of the Appropriations Committee, stressed the bipartisan nature of the negotiations. "It has been truly the most bipartisan in my memory," the Oregon senator told reporters.</

19579 Republican leaders, bowing to White House demands, agreed on Saturday to remove the most controversial provisions from a bill clamping down on illegal immigration, paving the way for congressional approval.A deal reached in negotiations that stretched through the night stripped out language that would make even legal immigrants liable for
19579 deportation if they used any of dozens of government relief programmes for one year out of their first seven in the country.It also eased proposed income standards required of Americans seeking to sponsor entry of close family members.President Bill Clinton hailed the accord during a trip to Rhode Island, saying
19579 it combated illegal immigration "without hurting innocent children or punishing legal immigrants."The revised immigration measure was to be included in a huge bill funding much of the government for the 1997 fiscal year. (Corrects to make clear that the funding is for the 1997 fiscal year.)The House of Representatives was
19579 to vote on the package on Saturday and the Senate planned a vote on Monday.Many Democrats had called the provisions in parts of a section called Title 5, targeting legal immigrants, "mean-spirited" and the White House refused to accept them.Representative Howard Berman, a California Democrat and one of the bill's
19579 critics who has served on the congressional negotiating team, said: "Basically all the worst provisions of Title 5 are out."White House spokesman Mike McCurry said of the agreement: "We're satisfied we have immigration measures that will continue to protect America's borders while setting the right kind of standards for legal
19579 immigration."The agreement also removed a ban on government-paid treatment for AIDS for legal and illegal aliens.House Speaker Newt Gingrich told a news conference Republicans had yielded to the White House on some issues "in order to get everything done."He said the administration had been adamant on allowing an illegal immigrant
19579 to have government-paid treatment for AIDS as well as emergency medical services."We frankly receded to them on what most people would not think is a very good policy... an illegal immigrant not only gets emergency medical services but can in fact be treated for AIDS at the cost of $119,000
19579 to the taxpayer," Gingrich said.The immigration bill approved by the House earlier this week would have required a sponsor of an immigrant to have an income of 140 percent of poverty level to sponsor immigration of a spouse or minor child or 200 percent to sponsor other close family members.Under
19579 the accord a sponsor would need an income of 125 percent of poverty level and greater flexibility is allowed.The idea is to make sure the immigrant does not become a public charge. But critics had said millions of Americans would have been denied the right to petition for family members
19579 to enter the Unites States.But Gingrich said: "I don't believe you can explain to most Americans where somebody who is already drawing food stamps ought to be a sponsor for somebody to come. But they (the White House) insisted on that."The House author of the bill, Texas Republican Representative Lamar
19579 Smith, said all provisions aimed at stemming illegal immigration were retained. These included:- Doubling the number of border control agents with 1,000 a year added for five years.- Extra fences along the U.S.-Mexico border near San Diego.- Increased criminal penalties for alien smuggling and document fraud and wiretap authority in
19579 such cases and a streamlined exclusion and deportation process.- New rules for asylum procedures, including an entitlement to a judicial hearing within seven days.</

19585 BIF refers to the Bank Insurance Fund (BIF), which insures deposits at banks. BIF/SAIF refers to the proposal to bolster the thrift deposit insurance fund.Thrifts currently pay premiums of 23 basis points, or $0.23, per $100 of deposits. Banks pay no premiums due to a well capitalized BIF.Banks had previously
19585 opposed the measure to bolster the undercapitalized SAIF because in earlier versions it would have cost them about $12 billion over 20 years. "Due to certain revisions, the cost to banks has been somewhat reduced and opposition is softening," said Charlotte Birch, a spokeswoman for the American Bankers Association."This is
19585 not a bill that bankers will enthusiastically cheer, but it's a significant improvement over originally proposed BIF/SAIF legislation," she said.The ultimate aim is to have banks and thrifts pay the same modest premiums.Thrifts would have to pay an initial $4.7 billion to build up the SAIF, while banks would pick
19585 up part of the tab on bonds issued to pay for the previous savings and loan bailout. "Clearly, there has been a tremendous amount of momentum on the SAIF/BIF front," said Lou Nevins, president of the Western League of Savings Institutions, a trade group for West Coast thrifts. "We have
19585 a basic package that both banks and thrifts are in agreement on."Thrifts have faced several setbacks in the past, such as in April when the SAIF rescue plan was stripped from the federal budget.Nevertheless, analysts and industry sources feel the legislation will eventually succeed.Analysts says that once it goes through,
19585 most thrift analysts would revise upward their operating earnings estimates for thrifts because SAIF premiums would go down.In a recent interview, Tad Lowrey, chief executive officer of Pasadena-based CENFED Bank, said that if the issue were resolved, CENFED's annual earnings could be boosted by $0.28 a share. CENFED reported 1995
19585 profits of $1.57 a share.</

19588 Mexico hopes to pay back to the United States ahead of time more of the funds it borrowed to stem its 1995 financial meltdown, the head of the Mexican central bank said on Saturday.Miguel Mancera, governor of the Bank of Mexico, said his country intended to repay the U.S. Treasury
19588 Department and the International Monetary Fund ahead of schedule for loans that were part of a nearly $40-billion rescue package."It is something that is likely," Mancera told reporters. "I cannot give you a specific date or amount, but it is something that we would like to do if possible."In July,
19588 Mexico gave Washington a check for $7 billion, cutting to $3.5 billion its outstanding debt to the U.S. Treasury.The Clinton administration, which patched together the international loan bailout after Congress balked at ponying up the funds, welcomed the July payment and said that Mexico was on the right track.The crisis
19588 in Mexico began in December 1994 when the government botched an attempt to devalue its peso and sparked international investor panic that sent Mexican stock and bond markets plummeting and sapped international reserves.With the help of the U.S.-sponsored bailout, Mexico has recovered from its worst recession in decades, and the
19588 peso has displayed remarkable strength through 1996.Mancera, in Washington for the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings, said the peso's recent strength was due to market forces and that the government has not intervened this year to support its currency."We are in a floating exchange rate regime so
19588 the exchange rate is market-determined," Mancera said. "We have not intervened the whole year, except since August in order to buy dollars acording to a programme that we announced."In August, Mexico implemented a programme to build dollar reserves that would not affect the market value of the peso.Mancera said that
19588 international reserves, which dropped to dangerously low levels before the rescue package, were sufficient at $15.5 billion to meet Mexico's debt requirements and imports.Mexican reserves have grown by about $4 billion because of government borrowings abroad and revenues from the state oil company Pemex, which have increased as the price
19588 of oil has risen, Mancera said.At the height of the peso crisis, policymakers had worried that, with reserves steadily falling, the country did not have cash to repay its obligations without a rescue plan.The Mexican economy has shown signs of improvement in recent months, and Mancera predicted better days ahead,
19588 forecasting the economy to grow by four to five percent next year and inflation easing to about half 1996 levels.</

19601 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentRich industrial countries were poised on Saturday to sharply increase the amount of help they are prepared to offer debt-ridden poor nations under a multibillion-dollar international initiative.A senior Canadian official said he expected the Group of Seven (G7) to endorse an expansion of the debt
19601 relief they and other creditor countries were willing to provide. Under the new plan, 80 percent of poor nations' debts would be forgiven, compared with 67 percent now."It looks as though we should be able to secure that today," the official, who declined to be named, told reporters ahead of
19601 Saturday's meeting of the G7.That should pave the way for the formal launch of the multilateral debt relief plan during the current annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank that winds up on October 3.Saturday's gathering of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 -- Britain,
19601 Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- was taking place on the fringes of the annual meeting. It was scheduled to start over lunch and finish after 5:00 p.m. (2100 GMT).Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin separately told reporters that he was "optimistic" that an agreement could be
19601 reached among creditor countries to provide up to 80 percent debt relief to poor nations. But he declined to say whether that would come at Saturday's G7 meeting.The three-pronged debt-relief initiative -- involving actions by the Paris Club of creditor countries, the IMF and the World Bank -- is aimed
19601 at putting debt-ridden poor nations, many of them in Africa, back on their feet.Uganda is expected to be the first country to benefit from the plan.Both the World Bank and the IMF had urged the Paris Club of creditor nations to expand their debt relief to cover up to 90
19601 percent of their loans to eligible poor nations. But the G7, which forms the backbone of the Club, baulked.According to some estimates, about four or five countries would not be able to put their economies back on even keel and achieve so-called debt sustainability if the Paris Club only extends
19601 80 percent debt relief.The Canadian official said that the IMF and World Bank would need to make up the difference to ensure that did not happen. "The balance of resources will need to be made up by the two institutions," he said.That balance at issue amounts to some $1.2 billion.The
19601 World Bank has already pledged $2 billion to the initiative. It should not have all that much trouble in kicking in some more from the profits it makes on its loans to developing countries.But the IMF is another matter. As a monetary institution, it does not make profits on its
19601 loans.The IMF board last week pledged to come up with the necessary financing to take part in the debt relief plan, but left open the question of where the money would come from.The Canadian official said that the IMF would eventually have to sell some of its nearly 104 million
19601 ounces of gold to finance its participation in the programme. But he said that a decision on that controversial proposal may not have to be made until 1998 or beyond.The majority of the G7 back IMF gold sales. But Italy, and especially Germany, are opposed and instead want the IMF
19601 to rely on bilateral contributions from its member nations to finance stepped-up aid to poor countries.</

19637 bodies on the Baltic Sea floor where it lies, have left relatives of victims not knowing what, or who, was to blame for the accident.The ship went down about 100 km (60 miles) off the Finnish coast on its way from Estonia to Sweden after heavy seas tore the ship's
19637 bow door off and water flooded the cavernous car deck, causing the vessel to list and sink in a few minutes.More than 500 of the victims were Swedes, trapped on board as the ferry wallowed through a vicious autumn squall. Estonians made up the second largest group."Of course it's a
19637 concern to the government that we are not ready," said Olof Forssberg, the Swedish chairman of the international commission set up to investigate the accident."We are three countries without a common language," Forssberg said about the committee, which has representatives from Sweden, Finland and Estonia."New details that we have to
19637 investigate have emerged. We now have enough information to establish a cause for the accident," Forssberg said, adding he hoped the much delayed final report would be completed by the end of the year.The commission has been in disarray in recent months following the resignation of Estonian chairman Andi Meister
19637 amid allegations of cover-ups over a video of the wreck which was said to reveal who was on the bridge when the accident occurred.One of the 137 survivors, Kent Harstedt, has called for an investigation into how Swedish authorities handled the disaster.Harstedt made headlines at the time of the calamity
19637 after making a pact with a woman as the ship was sinking that if they survived they would have dinner together. The woman also lived."Two years after the accident we have no accident report and no national memorial," he said."Many countries are looking to see how Sweden, which is good
19637 at helping out with catastrophes in developing countries, copes with its own disaster," Harstedt said.A panel of experts hired by the ship's German builder Meyer Werft earlier this month accused the ship's operator, Estline of Tallinn, of poor vessel maintenance and sloppy repair work.Estline has denied any fault.Other investigations into
19637 the disaster have unearthed a series of errors which contributed to the fatalities, including weaknesses in the basic design of roll-on, roll-off ferries.Relatives of victims of the disaster filed a legal action in Paris this month against the ship's German builder and French and Swedish inspectors to try to pinpoint
19637 blame for the accident, rather than for financial compensation, they said.The Swedish government has shelved plans to encase the sunken wreck, which lies 55-88 metres (180-270 feet) down on the Baltic seabed, in a concrete shell in order to protect it from graveyard plundering.Relatives have complained the entombment would deny
19637 victims a decent burial and have called for the wreck to be salvaged, a project which would cost around 1.5 billion crowns ($230 million)."The Swedish government is the only one that has declared the site of a catastrophe a burial place," said Orjan Norlin, who lost his wife in the
19637 accident."The TWA plane outside New York was salvaged within a few weeks, but not the Estonia," Norlin said."I don't know for example where my wife is. Is she inside the Estonia, or was she, and now she's been washed away?" said Norlin, a police officer whose wife was part of

There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.Taleban earlier said it believed Rabbani and his aides fled to Jabal-us-Seraj before the militia captured the national capital Kabul and set up its own government there on Friday.Rabbani said in a statement on Friday his administration had shifted
19655 from Kabul to Parwan and the adjoining Kapisa province and was "carrying out, among other tasks, security and defence affairs" from there.AIP quoted Taleban sources as saying at least 18 pro-Rabbani fighters were killed and several captured in the Charikar fighting, compared to only five Taleban men killed.Taleban's self-declared government
19655 said it had hanged two more "accomplices" of executed former president Najibullah on Friday evening, naming them as his bodyguard, General Jafsar, and his aide Tokhi.Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai were themselves executed soon after the Taleban entered Kabul on Friday.All four had been housed at a U.N. compound
19655 in Kabul since Najibullah was ousted in April 1992.The fly-blown bodies of Najibullah and Shahpur were still hanging on Saturday from a concrete traffic post outside the presidential palace. There was no sign of the bodies of Jafsar and Tokhi.The ousted government on Friday called on the world not to
19655 recognise the fundamentalist Islamic regime decreed by the Taleban militia, which moved quickly to bar women workers from offices and promised death for adulterers and drinkers.The official Kabul Radio broadcast a message from Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar that said his movement wanted good relations with all peace-loving countries.In
19655 other developments, the United States expressed hope that the Taleban would move toward reconciliation and held out the possibility of establishing full diplomatic ties.China voiced concern on Saturday about the fighting and said it hoped for peace and reconciliation. However, Beijing stopped short of recognising the Taleban administration.In New Delhi,
19655 Amnesty International's Indian unit criticised the killing of Najibullah and called on governments to stop human rights abuses in Afganistan.Kabul Radio urged those who had fled the capital fearing bloodshed to return and said government employees should report for work. 19656 appealed for international recognition of its government.</

19659 CAPTURE KABUL, INDIA CLOSES MISSIONThe Afghan capital fell to Pakistan-backed Talebans who after gaining control executed former president Najjibullah and set up an interim Islamic government. President Burhanuddin Rabbani and Prime Minister Gulbaddin Hkmatyaar fled to escape. Najjibullah, 50, who had taken shelter at the UN office in Kabul since
19659 April 1992 when the rebels ousted his soviet-backed government after a 14-year war, was dragged to the street and hanged from a lamp-post in the heart of the city. Najjibullah's brother Shahpur Ahmedi, too suffered the same fate. Meanwhile, India closed its deplomatic mission in Kabul and watched the developments
19659 without committing any steps.----Financial ExpressFOREIGN INVESTORS MAY GET ACCESS TO GOVERNMENT BONDSThe government may soon allow full convertibility of rupee on the capital account. The government is also considering demands to throw open government bonds along with other bonds to foreign investors, said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. On his way
19659 to the annual World Bank meeting in Washington, the minister told foreign investors and non-resident Indian businessmen that decisions on opening the insurance sector to multinational and foreign companies was likely to be taken by March next year.----INDUSTRY MINISTER'S PROPOSAL ON COAL, LIGNITE SHOT DOWNThe Industry Minister's proposal to open
19659 the coal and lignite sector to multinational companies (MNCs) was shot down by the Coal Ministry. In the hope of attracting more foreign direct investment, the Industry Ministry had wanted provisions in the amended Mines (nationalisation) Act changed to allow private sector entry in coal mining and development. To this,
19659 the Coal Ministry objected, questioning legal validity of allotting captive mining blocks to private parties and opening the sector to MNCs.----BOURSE REGULATOR'S MOVE TO CURB VOLATILITY OF SCRIPSThe bourse regulator has decided on 25 percent weekly price band for restraining the volatility of scrips quoted above par. This forms part
19659 of a multi-pronged strategy to improve the vigilance systems of the bourses to check default and illegal transactions by brokers. The bourse regulator also recommends on-line segregation of client and broker transactions, keeping records of brokers and setting up of clearing corporations by stock exchanges. Other suggestions include introduction of
19659 a stock-watch mechanism, daily reporting to the bourse regulator on price and volume fluctuations in scrips.----CUSTODIAL SERVICES TO BE SET UP FOR GOVERNMENT PAPERSThe Securities Trading Corp of India (STCI) is set to enter into custodial services exclusively for government securities to widen its role in government bond trading. The
19659 custodial services is expected to be operational by fiscal 1997/98, said STCI. This would be a unique product as no other institution is providing such a facility, sources said. The services would enable STCI to create a retail market for government scrips.----The Economic TimesTRADING OF UNLISTED SCRIPS RECOMMENDED ON OTC

It has recommended trading in unlisted scrips as an initial step to add life to OTCEI. The committee pulled
19659 up OTCEI's promoters, the financial institutions, for not supporting OTCEI. 19659 public issue. The BPCL board plans to come up with the issue once the market situation improved. This is despite the fact that the issue was fully underwritten. 19659 projected for the June to September period. The slowdown led to a growing inventory with primary steel producers. 19663 Afghanistan's victorious Taleban Islamic militia paused in its pursuit of forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani who were apparently regrouping in the Panjsher Valley north of the capital Kabul.Taleban instead concentrated on consolidating its hold over Kabul, where it set up a strict fundamentalist Moslem government after capturing the
19663 city against little resistance last Friday at the climax of a sweep through eastern Afghanistan.A Pakistan-based private Afghan news service said Taleban had seized Charikar, capital of Parwan province north of Kabul, and were heading further north towards the Jabal-us-Seraj base of pro-Rabbani forces.But reporters visiting the area said Rabbani's
19663 forces still controlled Charikar and Taleban fighters were making no attempt to advance from the Bagram military air base, 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul.Four tanks flying Taleban's plain white flag guarded the edge of the militia's territory at Bagram. A score of Rabbani fighters manned a checkpoint just
19663 south of Charikar about 10 km (six miles) further north.Taleban said earlier it believed Rabbani and his aides, abandoning Kabul, fled to Jabal-us-Seraj just before the militia's fighters took control of the capital.A pro-Rabbani commander told reporters that Rabbani, his top military commander Ahmad Shah Masood, prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
19663 and Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf, leader of a pro-Rabbani faction, were now all in the Panjsher Valley in Kapisa province.Masood's mainly ethnic Tajik forces, based in the Panjsher, were in the forefront of the guerrilla war against the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan in 1980s.Rabbani had said in a statement on Friday
19663 his administration had moved from Kabul to Parwan and Kapisa and was controlling security and defence affairs from there.He called on the world not to recognise the Islamic government decreed by Taleban, which has barred women from working in offices and promised death for adulterers and drinkers.Pakistan has indicated that
19663 it may recognise the Taleban government but other countries, including the United States and China, took a more cautious line and appealed for reconciliation and an end to fighting.Taleban fighters patrolled Kabul in pick-up trucks but there were no signs of tensions as the city resumed normal life after the
19663 Friday weekend.A Taleban preacher at a mosque in Kabul's diplomatic Wazir Akbar Khan district said all men should wear either traditional skull caps or turbans to conform with strict Islamic tenets.Official Kabul Radio urged those who had fled the capital fearing bloodshed to return and said government employees should report
19663 for work.The radio also broadcast a message from Taleban's supreme leader, Mullah Mohammad Omar, saying his movement wanted good relations with all peace-loving countries.United Nations special peace envoy Norbert Holl told Taleban officials in the southern town of Kandahar that he wanted to have good relations with the Islamic movement,
19663 the Afghan Islamic Press service quoted a Taleban spokesman as saying.Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati urged groups in Afghanistan to share power and avoid outside interference in the country's affairs."No (Afghan) group could push out the other groups...All should learn to live side-by-side," Velayati told Iranian Television in a

19664 Kashmir, that the camps were closed after Taleban captured Khost province in eastern Afghanistan this month.There was no confirmation from Taleban, which seized the capital Kabul from the forces of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani on Friday after sweeping through vast areas of the east of the country earlier this month.Turabi
19664 said his party set up two camps at Khost in early 1989 to give military training to militants fighting Indian rule over two-thirds of Kashmir. Pakistan rules the remaining third.He accused Taleban of arresting more than 100 people at the camps in a move which he said also involved Pakistani
19664 intelligence agencies. 19664 people have been killed since the present revolt erupted there in January 1990.</
19665 Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto appeared to have reached a truce with President Farooq Leghari on Saturday as the two met for more than six hours after weeks of simmering differences between them.Both "expressed satisfaction over the meeting and decided to continue such meetings as before", an official statement said
19665 afterwards.The prime minister, still reeling from the shock of the death of her estranged younger brother Murtaza Bhutto in a shootout with police last week, met the president amid growing speculation that he might sack her government and order fresh elections because of opposition charges of official corruption.The statement said
19665 the two leaders would meet next after Bhutto returns from a visit to the United States, a decision that appeared to signal a temporary peace between them.The prime minister leaves for New York on Sunday, primarily to address the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.The statement said Bhutto "agreed with
19665 the spirit" of a suggestion from Leghari that parliamentary committees be formed to fight corruption.Leghari sent a rare message to parliament on Monday urging the government and the opposition parties to cooperate in setting up parliamentary committees to tackle corruption. 19665 also proposed several changes to the existing laws dealing with corruption and suggested an amendment to bar those found guilty of misconduct from public office for seven years.Bhutto, speaking at a mourning meeting for her brother on Thursday, made an apparent reference to the president's actions, alleging that there was
19665 a conspiracy against her government being implemented "under a timetable".Leghari retorted on Friday by asking unspecified holders of public office to refrain from making "unwarranted and irresponsible" statements.The indirect exchanges were the first of the type between the two leaders since they were both elected to their offices in 1993
19665 as members of the Pakistan People's Party led by Bhutto.A week ago Leghari openly aired his differences with Bhutto over the issue of judicial appointments by officially asking the Supreme Court for a delineation of his powers in the matter.This was done only a day after the shootout in the
