19670 Pakistan, accused of interference in the Afghan conflict, expects more of business than political gains from the latest twist of the turmoil there.Pakistan seemed to have these gains in mind when it became the first country to signal recognition of the new Taleban government in Afghanistan on Friday, hours after
19670 the Islamic militia stormed into the capital Kabul, analysts said.President Burhanuddin Rabbani's ousted government had been an obstacle to Islamabad's dream of opening overland trade routes to Central Asia via Afghanistan, while neighbouring Iran had already built a rail link to serve as a bridge between Central Asia and Europe.Kabul
19670 blocked once-agreed Pakistani plans early this year to repair the war-damaged road and lay a railway line through the Taleban-controlled western Afghanistan to link up with the former Soviet Central Asian republics.Proposals to use the route through the Rabbani-controlled parts of eastern and northern Afghanistan remained stalled by procedural disputes
19670 or factional fighting there.But with a Taleban government in Kabul, Pakistan can hope to realise its trade dreams soon, according to traders."If peace is restored in Afghanistan...Pakistan will get a very big market in Afghanistan and Central Asia, the head of Pakistan's national organisation of traders said.Ilyas Ahmad Bilour, president
19670 of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) said he did not expect peace there in the near future, however. "If peace is restored, Pakistan will get the market with trade in local currency, which will be helpful to our country."One of Pakistan's major economic plans held
19670 up by the Afghan conflict is to build gas and oil pipelines with the the Central Asian republic of Turkmenistan through Afghanistan.Taleban's birth two years ago as a movement of Islamic theology students is linked with trade, which it wanted to promote despite its apparent preoccupation with the avowed aim
19670 of enforcing what it regards as a strict Islamic order.The movement burst into prominence when it launched a campaign in southern Afghanistan in October 1994 to remove checkpoints set up by various factions on roads primarily to extort toll from traders.The first suspicions of Pakistan's links with the Taleban were
19670 voiced when the militia rescued a Pakistani trail-blazing 30-truck trade convoy to Central Asia in November the same year, four days after it was blocked by two guerrilla warlords, and then went on to score its major victory by capturing the former royal capital of Kandahar.Many of Taleban's members have
19670 studied in Pakistani religious madrassahs, or schools, run by fundamentalist Islamic groups.One of Kabul's most vociferous protests about the alleged Pakistani involvement came in September last year when the Taleban took the main pro-government western town of Herat, capital of the province of the same name bordering Iran.Pakistan has not
19670 reopened its embassy in Afghanistan since a mob expressed its anger over Herat's fall by burning Islamabad's mission in Kabul, killing an embassy employee and beating up the ambassador and other staff.Pakistan said on Friday it would deal with the new government and would immediately send a delegation to establish
19670 contact with it.Islamabad's move contrasted with general concern expressed elsewhere against the Taleban's summary execution of former Afghan president Najibullah, his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai and two aides after dragging them out of a United Nations compound where they had lived for protection four and a half years."The assassination would give
19670 an insight into the type of governance that could be expected from a faction which came into prominence only two years ago, and little is known of its political background," Pakistani newspaper The News commented on Saturday.Many Pakistanis also fear Taleban's rule in Afghanistan could encourage fundamentalist groups in Pakistan,
19670 which have often engaged in violence -- either in fighting between rival sects or mounting political protests.Pakistan says it has no favourites among the Afghan factions, some of whom it helped during their guerrilla war against Soviet occupation of their country in the 1980s.Former Pakistan army chief Mirza Aslam Beg
19670 said Islamabad was never behind the Taleban, and added: "If they succeed in bringing a lasting peace to Afghanistan, it would bring prosperity to Pakistan as it would give us safe and shortest passage to Central Asia."</

19691 U.S. and European Union trade chiefs on Saturday removed a major roadblock to an agreement to scrap tariffs on information technology -- potentially freeing up billions of dollars worth of trade for themselves, Japan and Canada.The two sides hope to launch the agreement at a high level meeting of World
19691 Trade Organisation members later this year.A deal addressing EU concerns about a U.S.-Japan computer chip arrangement, which was renewed in July, clears the way for negotiations to begin next week on a wider information technology agreement (ITA).The ITA would eliminate duties on a number of electronic products, including computers, software,
19691 computer chips and telecommunications equipment by 2000.Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan resolved their differences on the issue during a two-day meeting of so-called Quadrilateral (Quad) ministers which also included Shunpei Tsukahara of Japan and Arthur Eggleton of Canada."This (ITA) is a market
19691 access agreement worth tens of billions of dollars to the Quad countries alone," Barshefsky said at a news conference at the conclusion of the meeting.The deal postpones a January meeting of a U.S.-Japan semiconductor industry group until March to allow time for countries to agree to the wider technology pact.
19691 EU trade officials have expressed concern that the U.S.-Japan council would block European access to Japan's computer chip market."We are now able to go forward with negotiation of the ITA," Brittan said. "I believe this Quad can be described as the logjam-breaking Quad," he added.Barshefsky and Brittan also said they
19691 decided to try to break another logjam on negotiations for a global deal to open telecommunications markets by improving their offers. The hope is to reach global agreement by February 15.U.S. officials have said the ITA and the global telecommunications market accord would be two tangible outcomes of the WTO
19691 trade ministers meeting in Singapore in December that could demonstrate to average Americans the effectiveness of the global trading body in opening markets.One U.S. trade official said the ITA agreement would set a precedent for eliminating tariffs in other business sectors.The trade ministers also agreed to try to resume stalled
19691 global negotiations on financial services in early 1997.</

19694 plane and boat to avoid tough new penalties when the amnesty expires and a new law cracking down on illegal labour comes into force.The previous amnesty was due to expire on October 1, and with airlines and shipping companies unable to cope with the mass exodus, diplomats feared thousands would

19694 immigrants complained the amnesty period was too short and did not give them enough time to prepare for the voyage, purchase tickets and collect outstanding wages.Diplomats expect some 200,000 illegal aliens to try to leave the country before the new deadline expires at the end of October. But embassies said
19694 they had only issued about 100,000 exit permits thus far. 19694 previous deadline.Foreigners make up 75 percent of the population in the UAE, where many work as labourers, housemaids or in the service sector. Diplomats say most come to the country legally with a work permit stipulating they have to work for their sponsor.But large numbers break the law by overstaying
19694 their welcome or absconding from their sponsors for what they say is better treatment or pay with other employers.The practices have always been illegal, but the new law imposes stricter punishment for offenders, including fines, jail terms and deportation.For over a week, all flights to destinations such as New Delhi,
19694 Bombay and Manila have been booked solid past the previous deadline.Amnesty-seekers crowded around travel agencies and the Indian consulate in Dubai where airlines built makeshift counters to process tickets. 19694 ship to India, which is due to leave on September 30 carrying 2,300 passengers, were sold out in hours. The Indian Association in Dubai, which organised the ship, said on Saturday it had arranged for a converted cargo ship to depart on the same day to take 2,000 other illegal
19694 workers home.In addition, two launches were set to sail from Dubai for India on Saturday, despite widespread concern that the vessels were not safe enough for the four-day journey. 19694 the trip."There is no other cheap mode of transportation to go back," said Sunil Bhatia, who works at the privately-funded Indian Association. "And even if someone can afford the 750 dirhams for a plane ticket, there just aren't enough places left."</

19697 By Rich Miller, U.S. Economics CorrespondentRich industrial countries were poised on Saturday to sharply increase the amount of help they are prepared to offer debt-ridden poor nations under a multibillion-dollar international initiative.A senior Canadian official said he expected the Group of Seven (G7) to endorse an expansion of the debt
19697 relief they and other creditor countries were willing to provide. Under the new plan, 80 percent of poor nations' debts would be forgiven, compared with 67 percent now."It looks as though we should be able to secure that today," the official, who declined to be named, told reporters ahead of
19697 Saturday's meeting of the G7.That should pave the way for the formal launch of the multilateral debt relief plan during the current annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank that winds up on October 3.Saturday's gathering of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 -- Britain,
19697 Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- was taking place on the fringes of the annual meeting. It was scheduled to start over lunch and finish after 5:00 p.m. (2100 GMT).Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin separately told reporters that he was "optimistic" that an agreement could be
19697 reached among creditor countries to provide up to 80 percent debt relief to poor nations. But he declined to say whether that would come at Saturday's G7 meeting.The three-pronged debt-relief initiative -- involving actions by the Paris Club of creditor countries, the IMF and the World Bank -- is aimed
19697 at putting debt-ridden poor nations, many of them in Africa, back on their feet.Uganda is expected to be the first country to benefit from the plan.Both the World Bank and the IMF had urged the Paris Club of creditor nations to expand their debt relief to cover up to 90
19697 percent of their loans to eligible poor nations. But the G7, which forms the backbone of the Club, baulked.According to some estimates, about four or five countries would not be able to put their economies back on even keel and achieve so-called debt sustainability if the Paris Club only extends
19697 80 percent debt relief.The Canadian official said that the IMF and World Bank would need to make up the difference to ensure that did not happen. "The balance of resources will need to be made up by the two institutions," he said.That balance at issue amounts to some $1.2 billion.The
19697 World Bank has already pledged $2 billion to the initiative. It should not have all that much trouble in kicking in some more from the profits it makes on its loans to developing countries.But the IMF is another matter. As a monetary institution, it does not make profits on its
19697 loans.The IMF board last week pledged to come up with the necessary financing to take part in the debt relief plan, but left open the question of where the money would come from.The Canadian official said that the IMF would eventually have to sell some of its nearly 104 million
19697 ounces of gold to finance its participation in the programme. But he said that a decision on that controversial proposal may not have to be made until 1998 or beyond.The majority of the G7 back IMF gold sales. But Italy, and especially Germany, are opposed and instead want the IMF
19697 to rely on bilateral contributions from its member nations to finance stepped-up aid to poor countries.</

19700 Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates is the richest person in America for the third year in a row, according to Forbes magazine.In its issue reporting on the 400 wealthiest Americans, Forbes said the net worth of the 40-year-old billionaire has jumped to a staggering $18.5 billion, up almost $4 billion
19700 in just the last year.The stock market's bull run had much to do with the big gain in the fortunes of those who made the Forbes list. "That was a big part of it," said magazine spokesman Ray Healey. "A lot of them have huge stock fortunes." A prime example
19700 is Warren Buffett, 66, the famed Nebraska investor who came in second with a net worth of $15 billion. Third place was taken by another Microsoft billionaire, Paul Allen, 43, who helped Gates start the company 11 years ago and is worth $7.5 billion, according to Forbes.To gain admission to
19700 this exclusive club, one needed a net worth of at least $415 million this year, up $75 million from 1995. And thanks in part to the strong stock market, the average net worth of those on the list exceeded $1 billion for the first time.What can aspiring billionaires learn from
19700 this group? "Start a fabulous company -- and make sure you retain a hefty portion of the stock," said Healey.Stock was a big reason the number of billionaires on the list this year grew to 135 (corrects from 121). The wealth of all 400 on the list totalled $477 billion,
19700 (corrects combined net worth).Interestingly, the magazine pointed out that ideas now lead to great fortune, where in years past wealth was made through owning hard assets such as land, steel or oil.In the last decade the number of fortunes made in heavy industry has dropped from 103 to just 35.
19700 This year eight of the new members of the list made their fortunes in computer software, and 20 who made the list got wealthy in that industry.The financial field remains the top area where the wealthy made their money, with 51 members. The second field was gas or oil, with
19700 29 of the wealthiest in the energy industry. Real estate was third, with 28 people making their money in land, followed by 20 people in software and 18 in retailing.In the entertainment field, Star Wars producer George Lucas led with a net worth of $2 billion, followed by Steven Speilberg
19700 who is worth $1 billion, according to Forbes. The wealthiest woman in entertainment is talk-show queen Oprah Winfrey, who is worth $415 million.Like Oprah, more than half of those who made the list were not born wealthy -- 217 were self-made millionaires, Forbes said. One of them was Pamela Lopker,
19700 now worth $425 million, who made her fortune by starting a private software company and was the wealthiest self-made woman in the group.The magazine found that 30 of its 400 richest Americans never attended college. And the 63 people on the list who did not have a college degree had
19700 a much higher average net worth than the college graduates on the list. The two basic qualifications were U.S. citizenship, and a net worth -- assets minus liabilities -- of at least $415 million, up from the $340 million minimum for 1995.</

19721 Frankie Dettori's historic winning run came to an end in the first race at Ascot on Sunday as bookmakers heaved a mass sigh of relief.In an astonishing and unprecedented display on Saturday, Dettori won all seven races on a high-class card at cumulative odds of over 25,000-1.It thrilled the punters

19721 chance Kahal, ridden by Richard Hills.The defeat ended Dettori's chance of chasing a record set in August 1933 by Sir Gordon Richards who rode 12 winners in succession, spread over three days.Another defeat followed for Dettori in the second race, fifth of eight on Medaaly behind Benny The Dip, the
19721 mount of Walter Swinburn.Victory looked a distinct possibility in the third on Hal's Pal, the 6-1 favourite, but the Italian-born jockey was denied in the closing stages by 33-1 chance Amrak Ajeeb as bookmakers retrieved a little of Saturday's losses.Winning jockey Mark Rimmer said: "I could see Frankie in front

19727 As exuberant Italian jockey Frankie Dettori made racing history at Ascot, the world's most powerful racehorse owner paid him the ultimate tribute."He is the best jockey I have ever seen," Dubai's Sheikh Mohammed said of the rider whose talent and ebullience have transformed the staid world of British horse racing.Bookmakers
19727 lost an estimated 18 million pounds ($28 million) and 30 of their shops face possible closure after Dettori went through the card at Ascot's fiercely competitive festival of racing on Saturday to land all seven races at cumulative odds of over 25,000-1It was an extraordinary feat that surpassed the triumphs
19727 of racing legends Lester Piggott and Sir Gordon Richards.The champion jockey went wild after his magnificent seven. Ignoring requests from the Ascot stewards on safety grounds, he leapt off big race winners with the famous flying dismount he copied from U.S. ace Angel Cordero.He kissed a woman TV commentator and
19727 sprayed the crowd with champagne. "Don't touch me, I'm on fire," the supercharged 25-year-old joked as everyone patted him on the back. For the Prince of Pzazz, this was a racing coronation.Dettori, the son of 13-times Italian champion Gianfranco, rode his first winner in Turin 10 years ago.His compatriot, Luca
19727 Cumani, took the raw young apprentice under his wing in Newmarket, headquarters of British racing.Dettori's rise to fame was more gradual than meteoric in his first few difficult seasons.But by 1990, his natural talent was shining through. He became the first teenager since Piggott to ride 100 winners in a
19727 season. Since then he has won five British classics and twice been champion jockey.This season has been an emotional roller-coaster for Dettori.He landed the 2,000 Guineas by the narrowest of margins on Mark of Esteem but faced fines and suspension for excessive use of the whip and leaping from the
19727 saddle before he had reached the unsaddling enclosure.Then in June he broke his arm in an accident that put paid to his chances of landing the jockeys' title again. Since then he has suffered three more bans. He only just returned from the latest suspension on Friday.But nothing can wipe
19727 away the widest grin in British racing and Dettori is unrepentant."Some people don't like me leaping off, but for me it's just a natural reaction. I feel great and I want to show it," said the showman from Milan."I'm Italian and I like to show my feelings unlike a lot
19727 of people from this country who are more reserved."</

19751 Co-world number one Monica Seles fought off a determined Arantxa Sanchez Vicario on Sunday to end the six-year U.S. Fed Cup title drought.Seles battled Spain's great Fed Cup veteran for nearly two hours, claiming a 3-6 6-3 6-1 victory that gave the United States an insurmountable 3-0 lead in the
19751 best-of-five championship.The victory ended Spain's domination of the women's team event and gave the United States its 15th Fed Cup title, but its first since 1990.The Spanish team of Sanchez and Conchita Martinez was playing its sixth consecutive final and had won the Cup the last three years, beating the
19751 Americans in 1994 and 1995.But Seles, who became an American citizen in 1994 and joined the U.S. team this year in the semifinals, altered the balance of power.Seles easily beat Martinez in Saturday's opening singles and Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport downed Sanchez to give Seles a chance to clinch the
19751 tie early.But Sanchez never goes down without a fight and the match with Seles was filled with big-hitting Grand Slam final calibre tennis.When it was over, however, Seles had belted twice as many winner as Sanchez (42-19) and raised her career record against the fleet-footed Spaniard to 13-1."I was very
19751 nervous. I wasn't sure if I was going to be able to turn around but I hung in there," said Seles, who admitted to being far more nervous than she had ever been when playing just for herself -- even in the Grand Slams."All my teammates were behind me and
19751 I just hung in there," she said.Said U.S. captain Billie Jean King: "I couldn't ask for a better team. They've been just fantastic, everyone just pulled together. "It's been a tremendous effort on everyone's part."</

19757 The U.S. Fed Cup team had been counting on wildly enthusiastic home support on Saturday.As it turned out, they did not need it, but the embarrassingly sparse attendance was a huge disappointment."I really was very surprised today when we walked in -- whoa!, said Monica Seles of the sight of
19757 completely empty sections throughout the Atlantic City Convention Centre.Organisers would not give attendance figures, but fewer than 2,000 turned out at the centre which could have held some 9,000.Thanks to wins by Seles and Lindsay Davenport over Conchita Martinez and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, the Americans took a 2-0 lead in
19757 the best-of-five event even without the kind of support their opponents routinely receive as Fed Cup hosts."When we played in Nagoya we had 12,000 screaming fans, 11,000 were all against us, so it's a much different atmosphere here," Seles said of the July semifinal tie in Japan.Before the final, the
19757 players and U.S. Captain Billie Jean King often spoke in anticipation of a packed partisan crowd.After Saturday's play, the talk was of a thorough lack of Fed Cup awareness and the failure to properly promote the event in this gambling city, where the slot machine section of any casino had
19757 far more filled seats than the historic old Convention Centre."We wish more people would come out. I don't know if there are enough tennis fans in the city," lamented Seles."When you come to Atlantic City you don't come for tennis," she surmised."So few people know what's going on that when
19757 I would be walking at the hotel people would be saying 'Why are you here?' And I would be the one telling people why we were here."I don't think that's ever happened," she said.Officials from Caesars Hotel, which promoted the event, said obscure International Tennis Federation rules had forbidden them
19757 from using the names of the players until only recently, when the teams were announced.And posters that say only "Fed Cup, U.S. vs Spain" without marquee names like Seles, Sanchez Vicario, Davenport and Martinez just do not sell the event."It feels quiet. You know we had 6,000 people packed in
19757 in Valencia," said King, comparing Saturday's showing to last year's final in Spain."People in the United States don't know what Fed Cup is. I think we need more exposure. I think we have a lot more promoting to do."The difference was not lost on the Spanish stars, who are regularly
19757 supported by thousands of extremely vocal, flag-waving fans."There's not much people here," noted Martinez. "The atmosphere is really different because when we played in Valencia everybody was rooting for us."There was a lot more people in Valencia than over here."Davenport tried hard to find a silver lining."I was disappointed there
19757 weren't more people here," she said. "But they did seem to really understand what was happening."Added Seles a bit wistfully: "Hopefully tomorrow we'll get</

19764 over the 1995 European Cup Winners' Cup champions.Zaragoza went in 2-1 up at half-time thanks to well-taken goals from Gustavo Lopez and Gustavo Poyet and then went further ahead when Lopez scored his second.Barcelona, whose Portuguese star Luis Figo had netted with a superb first-time strike in the first half,
19764 pulled back to 3-2 after Ronaldo pounced on to a Figo through-pass.But the game took a dramatic twist midway through the second half when a linesman alerted the referee to an infringement in the Zaragoza penalty area.After a lengthy debate the referee sent off Zaragoza's Xavier Aguado, apparently for striking
19764 a Barcelona player, and awarded a penalty, from which Gheorghe Popescu equalised.With Zaragoza down to ten men, Luis Enrique Martinez broke through on the right to put his side ahead with a blistering shot and, shortly afterwards, Ronaldo strolled through the defence to score his fifth goal of the league
19764 season.With 13 points from five games, Barcelona are two ahead of Deportivo Coruna, 2-1 winners over Real Betis on Saturday, and Real Madrid, who clocked up their first away win in the 3-2 victory at Oviedo.Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello decided to move striker Raul back into midfield for the
19764 game at Oviedo.The move worked. 19780 earned himself the 125,000 pounds jackpot by holing a 10-foot putt on the 17th and two-putting the par five 18th from 35 feet.It gave the 29-year-old a final-round 70 and an 11-under-par total of 277 at the K Club outside Dublin, enough to edge out Rocca who could only par
19780 the last five holes.England's Roger Chapman and Scot Andrew Coltart shared third place a stroke further back.Johansson, whose best performance this year was eighth in last month's US PGA championship, said: "I've played really bad all year except for the PGA and I came here not really expecting to make

19792 all seven finals he has appeared in this year.The match unravelled quickly for the 21-year-old German after Sampras broke him at 6-5 to take the first set.Sampras then opened the second with another break, bolting to 3-0 lead to take control of the set and match.It was the same scenario
19792 in the third as Sampras simply overwhelmed Dreekmann, shutting out the nervous German to wrap up the match in one hour 22 minutes. "I didn't have a chance," said Dreekmann. "He was serving so well and if you can't return his serve you can't break him."Sampras collected $137,000 in his
19792 first appearance since he won the U.S. Open earlier this month. His prize money for the the season rose to more than $1.7 million.Sampras blasted 19 aces past the stunned Dreekmann. "I played well today, I served big," said the American."After the first set I saw him hang his head

19799 Thousands of Romanians attended the funeral of Nicu Ceausescu, youngest son of late communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, who was buried near the graves of his parents in a Bucharest cemetery on Sunday.Relatives and friends gathered to pay their last respects to Nicu, seen as his father's political heir before Ceausescu
19799 and his wife Elena were ousted and shot in a December 1989 revolt which ended their ruthless 24-year rule.Nicu, 45, a hard-drinking playboy, died in a Vienna hospital on Thursday from acute liver disease and friends flew his body back home one day later for burial.Several thousand curious crowds thronged
19799 the northwest Ghencea cemetery on Sunday for a glimpse of Nicu's coffin, wrapped in Romania's red-yellow-and-blue national flag.Members of the once powerful Ceausescu clan surrounded Nicu's elder brother Valentin and his sister Zoe as Orthodox priests held the two-hour funeral service.Nicu was buried 100 yards (metres) away from the tombs
19799 of his parents, who were shot by firing squad on Christmas 1989.Many Romanians harbour ambivalent feelings about the Ceausescu era and their fall."God rest his soul. His biggest sin was that he was his father's son," said one weeping woman, while dozens of security guards tried to keep the crowd
19799 under control.Adrian Paunescu, a former Ceausescu court poet, recited an ode to "Prince" Nicu. Paunescu runs for president for the Socialist Labour Party, heir to the former Communist Party, in November 3 polls, which coincide with parliamentary elections."Where has Romanian industry gone, where's our daily bread...where's justice the people?" ran
19799 a dirge sung near Nicu's grave by a group of musicians led by Paunescu.Living standards are lower and many say the true story of the 1989 revolt, seen by many as a coup by former communists who have held power ever since, has yet to be told.Political analysts say former
19799 communists around Paunescu are trying to capitalise ahead of November's polls on popular discontent with growing poverty and corruption which have marked Romania's painful transition towards a free market.Since the revolution, the Ceausescu family have kept a low profile and stayed away from politics.Nicu was arrested during the revolution and
19799 convicted to 20 years in jail for ordering the repression of protests in the Transylvanian city of Sibiu where he was communist party boss.Nicu always protested his innocence, saying he had left town before troops shot dead 91 people and wounded about 200.He was paroled in 1992, after courts quashed
19799 his initial conviction. He served out a lesser sentence for illegal gun possession.People in Sibiu remember Nicu for trying to oppose his father's belt-tightening policies. Some in his own generation see him as a liberal who snubbed hardliners around his father.</

19802 A top European Commission official on Sunday forecast better times ahead for Europe and said an increasing number of nations were likely to take part in the upcoming launch of a single currency."I think a significant number will be ready in 1997. When I see the present efforts I am
19802 optimistic," European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy told reporters.The single currency, to be called the euro, is being launched in 1999, but countries that wish to participate must meet tough budget targets next year.Speaking during the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, de Silguy said the improved
19802 credibility of European Monetary Union, lower long-term interest rates and a more balanced policy mix had set the stage for a rebound in economic growth in Europe."There are now increasing signs that a moderate recovery to a more healthy pace of expansion may be underway," he said.De Silguy warned, though,
19802 that the expected growth would not be enough to have any visible impact on high unemployment.He reaffirmed that the European Commission expected growth of two to 2.5 percent next year on average for the European Union as a whole. A long-awaited pick-up is needed to ensure the success of European
19802 plans for a single currency.International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus also forecast a faster pace of growth in Europe next year that would help the drive to launch a single currency."The recent rebound in the German economy is particularly encouraging," Camdessus told the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee."Economic activity seems
19802 likely to be stronger in 1997... in Europe," Camdessus said. "This will help the process toward monetary unification."De Silguy said an increasing number of European countries may be ready to meet criteria for joining EMU after a big effort to cut their budget deficits."Probably with more effort in the way
19802 of consolidation, I am sure there will be a significant number -- perhaps an increasing number," he added.Italy and Spain last week unveiled budgets designed to bring their deficits to or below three percent of Gross Domestic Product next year, the crucial year for deciding which countries will join a
19802 single currency."Italy has made a huge effort to meet the conditions to be able to switch to the euro at the end of 1997," he said.He said, however, there was no question of softening Maastricht Treaty standards for entry to monetary union.De Silguy had said before the European governments announced
19802 their cost-cutting budgets this September that around seven countries would be ready for monetary union.At a Saturday meeting of Group of Seven industrial nations, European ministers outlined agreements reached last weekend in Dublin that are designed to ensure currency and fiscal stability after the launch of the euro."The others are
19802 interested in the fact that when the mark disappears, its successor currency should be able to take exactly the role of the mark," Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said."Otherwise there could be flight into the dollar which would have consequences in the currency markets. No one is interested in that happening,"
19802 he said."They are asking questions about what the changes will mean for financial markets and currencies," Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters.French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said the euro would reflect the economies of the countries in monetary union -- which will include the strongest economies that have
19802 passed the test of fiscal and monetary credibility laid out in the Maastricht Treaty. "I have no wories about the (euro) exchange rate," he said.</

19805 The colors of fall foliage have again arrived in the most heavily wooded state in the nation, but voters are being asked if the historic forest is on the verge of destruction.The emotional battle over a logging practice known as clear-cutting has forged unusual political alliances and largely obscured debate
19805 over whom Maine will support for Congress and the White House."If we win here, it will be tremendous for forest in the rest of the country and the globe," said Jonathan Carter, who helped draft a proposal to ban clear-cutting in Maine's North Woods and tighten other logging rules.Carter and
19805 other environmentalists associated with the state's fledgling Green Party stunned political leaders and the powerful paper industry by collecting 58,000 signatures to force a referendum vote on their proposal.Voters now face campaigns for three competing referendums, including a compromise plan that would limit clear-cuts but not ban them and a
19805 "none of the above" measure that would leave current forestry rules unchanged.Several polls have shown the compromise measure leading, but pollsters caution that voters are still confused about their choices and supporters of the "none of the above" option have just launched their campaign.The forests of spruce, fir and hardwood
19805 trees have been central to Maine's economy since the first European settlers arrived. Forest-product manufacturing is the state's largest industry, employing 32,000 people in the woods and paper mills.With 90 percent of its acreage considered woodlands, Maine is the most forested state. Most commercial forest is privately owned and located
19805 in northern Maine, where unpopulated "towns" like Township 1, Range 6, are named for their map coordinates.Supporters of a clear-cut ban contend that clear-cutting -- in which all trees are removed from a large area -- inflicts long-term damage to the soil and health of the tree supply, but the
19805 industry maintains it is an important forest management tool.Ban opponents cite a state report predicting 15,000 jobs will be lost if the measure is approved, but ban supporters contend the economy will be strengthened, because selective logging requires more workers and the forest resource will be protected.Whatever the economic and
19805 environmental arguments, logging industry officials acknowledge privately that clear-cuts are difficult to defend politically, because the practice leaves ugly scars on the landscape.Under pressure from Gov. Angus King, the forest products industry negotiated an agreement with some of its traditional political enemies in the environmental community to tighten the rules
19805 for clear-cutting but not ban it."It was the right idea at the right time under the right circumstances and being supported by the right people," King told reporters Sept. 8, when the state legislature voted to place the compromise referendum on the ballot.But in agreeing to put a "competing measure"
19805 on the ballot, lawmakers were also required to give voters a choice of "none of the above." Landowner rights activists who oppose any logging restrictions have rallied behind that proposal.The forestry debate has overshadowed the campaigns for the White House and the seat being vacated by Sen. William Cohen, and
19805 some political analysts say those and other races will be influenced by the battle between the referendums."The forestry referenda are going to be one of the major stimuli of turnout in this election, because they involve issues on which voters have very strong opinions," Tony Corrado, a political scientist at
19805 Colby College, said.Corrado said increased turnout by more conservative voters in northern Maine could help Republican senate candidate Susan Collins. Democrat Joe Brennan has moved to counter that with a large voter-turnout effort in his southern Maine base. Brennan and Collins both support the compromise measure.</

19807 Germans must become more open to change if their economy is to hold its own in an increasingly competitive world and cut its high unemployment, Commerzbank chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said on Sunday."It is the great weakness of the German economy that, in political circles and in society generally, structural
19807 change is considered a threat," Kohlhaussen said."What we need is a positive attitude to change and adjustment if we want to be successful in a globalised economy and intend to achieve an adequate level of employment again." Kohlhaussen called for increased deregulation in the German market, adding that this would
19807 help to draw investment into the country.He welcomed such changes as the recent legislation to lengthen the country's highly restricted shop opening hours, but said such decisions took too long and were thus only implemented after great delays."It is high time that deregulation measures were implemented and greater flexibility was
19807 introduced in the business sector, as has long been promised," he said. "If it takes Germany 10 years to extend shop opening times by 1-1/2 hours a day, we cannot expect foreign investors to take the country seriously when they are choosing a business location," he added.Issues such as workers'
19807 worries that they would be forced to work longer hours if stores were open longer -- and even consumer concern that plans for variable opening hours would lead to uncertainty about which store was open when -- played a part in delaying the decision to extend shop hours.Even the stores
19807 themselves resisted change for years, arguing that longer hours simply meant higher costs, with no guarantee of increased turnover.But Kohlhaussen said there were signs that Germany was beginning to show a greater awareness of the need for change to keep up with rival economies, adding that this could give grounds
19807 for optimism that more flexibility was on the way."I think there will be more to come," he said.--Janet Northcote, Washington Newsroom +1 202 898 8300</

19810 Nations should make banking sector stability a primary goal of their macroeconomic and structural policies, IMF experts said Sunday in a study of "significant banking sector problems" suffered by more than 130 of the 181 IMF member countries since 1980."We argue that the presence of an unsound banking system is
19810 a very major constraint on macroeconomic policy management and that banking system soundness should be viewed as an objective itself of policy," said Carl-Johan Lindgren, chief of the Banking and Supervision division at the IMF's Monetary and Exchange Affairs Department. The publication, authored by Lindgren, Gillian Garcia and Matthew Saal,
19810 and titled "Banking Soundness and Macroeconomic Policy," was presented Sunday during the annual meeting of the World Bank and IMF.Among the study's recommendations, was the need to act swiftly in the event of banking collapse."One thing that we do say is make sure there is a strong exit policy...that when
19810 banks go bad, which happens in all banking markets, you deal with it early and forcefully," said Lindgren. "Banks should exit the market the moment they come close to insolvency," he added, noting that banks often become insolvent -- unable to pay debts as they fall due -- long before
19810 they become illiquid -- short of cash.The authors said that financial deregulation has added to the risks banking systems face, although deregulation should not be viewed as a cause of banking problems.They said fraud is frequently a problem in banking, but noted that their findings found fraud was responsible for
19810 only about 10 percent of losses in the U.S. Savings and Loan Crisis.When asked whether France had gone too far in using taxpayer money to bail out troubled Credit Lyonnais, presenter Manuel Guitian, director of the IMF's Monetary and Exchange Affairs Department, suggested banking sector stability should be among a
19810 government's first priorities."When a government decides to intervene in a particular banking case because it feels that its necessary for the system at large ... then it's money well spent," said Guitian.-- Noah Barkin, Washington Newsroom, 202-898-8300</

19816 After years of downsizing, corporate computing executives are placing performance and prospects for creating revenues ahead of cost cutting as their top priorities, according to a new study.The study to be released on Monday, prepared by Find/SVP's Strategic Research Division, also finds that a high percentage of respondends are concerned
19816 they are creating high volumes of data which are not being properly managed. A vast majority, some 93 percent of those surveyed in the U.S., are concerned about performance and response time, up nine percent from a survey a year ago, while concern over data security has diminished by seven
19816 percent to 86 percent.Greater concern over performance comes as many companies are incorporating Internet technologies into their computing environments, and some using public networks fear congestion will turn the World Wide Web into the "World Wide Wait". In a sign managers of corporate 'glass house' data centers expect to gain
19816 a central role in the growth of distributed computing, executives project 35 percent growth over the next two years in the number of servers under their control.Janice Porell, vice president of strategic marketing at EMC Corp, which commissioned the study, said it was a sign that downsizing as a trend,
19816 especially in the United States, now appears to be losing momentum. "It looks to us like information is becoming more critical to the organization," she said in an interview, adding that rather than simply being viewed as a cost, this trend "supports the notion of providing a competitive edge."Large-scale organizations
19816 are thus looking to information officers to play far more of an entrepreneurial role, using information processing to provide market leadership."Once you're ahead, everyone else is in catch-up mode," said Porell, noting companies are increasingly looking to retain their most highly valued computing services in-house. Illustrating this trend, nearly 70
19816 percent of U.S. respondents said they have already or are currently organizing their computing strategies around information rather than around technology, as they had in the past.Noting more than three-quarters of respondents have or are planning to use Internet technology, the survey said there was "a strong indication that IT
19816 strategies are increasingly focused on using information to reach business goals." Existing and new online applications are viewed as the main sources of the exploition of information technology, with database applications mentioned by 89 percent of U.S. respondents as the major contributor to growth.Unsurprisingly, given increased effort to access and
19816 utilize corporate data, respondents also identified information bottlenecks as the next unsolved critical problem for managers.In the U.S., 71 percent said business productivity is hurt by poor file server performance, and 66 percent said customer service is degraded, while at least 60 percent noted adverse impact on time-to-market and competitiveness.
19816 Significant for EMC, the top-ranking open systems supplier of storage devices, is that 92 percent of U.S. participants said they would consider a storage-based file server solution attached directly to the network to address the bottleneck.Tranferring data in differing formats between different systems is named as another major source of
19816 information bottlenecks, and 90 percent of respondents said they would consider using storage to ease the problem where possible.Three quarters of managers said open enterprise computing is generating a rapid or very rapid rise in the need for storage and retrieval capabilities, the survey found. Four out of five U.S.
19816 organizations are bringing open servers under the central control of the data center, with benefits ranging from improved backup and storage to better use of computing staff.Nevertheless, 37 percent of those polled said that 10 times the amount of critical data remains outside the data center and unavailable to the
19816 organization.Even higher levels of concern about ability to manage business-critical information in open computing environments exists in Europe and Japan, with similar levels of concern over business objectives jeopardized by computing problems. The survey is based on interviews with information technology executives and managers in 700 organizations, including 300 in
19816 the United States, 300 in six European countries -- Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Neatherlands, and Britain -- and 100 in Japan.The survey was based on an eligible universe of 33,909 organizations with at least 1,000 employees in the United States and 18,268 organizations with 500 or more employees in
19816 the European countries. REUTER SGP</

19834 Germany agreed to comply with standards set by the International Monetary Fund for release of economic data at a meeting on Sunday, but details have still to be worked out, German officials said.Finance Minister Theo Waigel said after a meeting of the International Monetary Fund's interim committee, "I said we
19834 would comply with the IMF data standard."Germany is the last of the Group of Seven countries to join the scheme which is aimed at gathering sound economic data to improve surveillance.The Group of Seven comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.Germany's objection to the scheme lay
19834 in the fact that countries meeting the IMF's standards are required to state in advance when their statistics will be published.Germany currently does not announce specific dates and times for the release of economic data in advance. Usually only a few minutes warning is given, even for highly market-sensitive data
19834 such as M3 money supply. Asked specifically whether Germany had agreed to join the scheme only if this condition was waived, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer told the briefing, "We have said we want to join but the technical details must still be cleared up."Germany objects to setting precise times for
19834 publication of its data on grounds that an ambitious early release date could lead to publication of incomplete or inaccurate figures.On the other hand, they argue, a later date which builds in a safety margin builds in a possible problem of privileged insider knowledge held by those who have access
19834 to and prepare the data.Asked whether it would be positive or negative for financial markets to know in advance when figures were coming, Tietmeyer said, "I cannot say whether it would be positive or negative for markets to give a precise date, it is just our statistical culture."--Janet Northcote, Washington

19862 Britain on Sunday demanded a change in International Monetary Fund rules so that developing countries would be forced to open up their economies to foreign capital."I firmly believe that the (IMF's) articles need revision," Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told the IMF Interim Committee meeting. "The present articles in
19862 fact permit -- and in some cases even encourage -- countries to impose controls on capital account transactions. In today's world that must be wrong," Clarke said.He argued that changes were crucial in a world where where free international flows of capital were seen as a good thing."It lets capital
19862 go where it produces the greatest return. It sharpens the incentives to save and invest...ultimately, free international flows of capital help to maximise world world growth. Everyone stands to benefit," Clarke said. "In a world of large-scale private capital flows, all the international institutions will need to respond with new
19862 rules to encourgae confidence amongst investors."The issue has sparked heated debate among developing countries. While many of them welcome the promise of greater private investment, they are also deeply worried the money could leave just as quickly, scarring their economies.Mexico's near collapse in late 1994 after its peso devaluation and
19862 a surge of money leaving the country has been taken as a warning by a number of developing countries of the dangers that investors bring. Clarke said he realised that the international community needed to help emerging economies deal with the consequences of capital flows."As (they)...liberalise capital transactions, they need
19862 to strengthen bank supervision and financial regulation," he said, acknowledging that without the right polices, such inflows could fuel inflation and worsen current account deficits.Domestic financial systems must be well-supervised, inflows should not be allowed to spark too much domestic demand and fiscal policy may have to be tightened. The
19862 funds coming in from abroad should not act as a substitute for domestic savings and exchange rate policies had to be realistic.However, for the less developed economies, some sort of controls could help prevent a rush of money leaving but should be only short-term."In the longer term, capital controls cannot
19862 substitute for sound macro-economic management and structural reform," Clarke added.</

19867 cornerstone of the banking legislation is a provision to beef up the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) with a one-time charge totaling $4.7 billion to put the SAIF at its required level. SAIF insures deposits at thrifts. Then banks would share in the thirfts' $793 million annual interest payments on
19867 Financing Corp. (FICO) bonds issued as part of the savings and loan bailout. 19867 intention is for the Bank Insurance Fund, which insures deposits at banks, to eventually merge with the SAIF and for banks and thrifts to ultimately have one charter. 19867 the bill was less extensive than he would have liked but provides increased security for SAIF and forms that baiss for long-term banking modernization.Rep. 19887 Northern Ireland peace talks resume on Monday against a bleak backdrop of mounting sectarian attacks and warnings that guerrilla violence will erupt again unless swift political progress is made.The United States, a key player in attempts to reconcile feuding Protestants and Catholics, has expressed alarm at the steadily deteriorating political
19887 and social climate since sectarian violence flared over the summer.Jean Kennedy Smith, U.S. ambassador to the Republic of Ireland, said in a speech that ordinary people were living in fear since communal violence erupted over a Protestant Orange Order march at the small town of Drumcree in July."We have been
19887 aghast and shaken at the naked sectarianism that has risen from the ashes of Drumcree, by the senseless discrimination that fragments already struggling communities, by the childish and cruel protests against families as they headed to church to worship," she said.She was referring to a wave of incidents in which
19887 churches have been attacked by extremists, businesses boycotted by both communities and worshippers picketed on their way to a Catholic church.The grass-roots sectarianism has its extreme expression in the actions of the self-styled guardian armies of the two communities, Catholic-backed Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas fighting to end British rule
19887 of the province and Protestant Loyalists battling to maintain it.The IRA has not struck targets in Northern Ireland since it broke a 17-month ceasefire last February -- limiting itself to bomb attacks on the British mainland -- and its Protestant Loyalist rivals have stuck to an uneasy truce of their
19887 own.But police say any IRA attack in Northern Ireland itself would unleash a wave of Loyalist reprisals that would return the province to a 25-year war which killed 3,200 and consign the faltering peace process to oblivion.The discovery of an IRA bomb factory in London last week has underlined the
19887 absence at the multi-party Belfast peace talks of the guerrillas' political wing, Sinn Fein.Sinn Fein is excluded from the talks by the British and Irish governments until there is a new IRA ceasefire, but the guerrillas refuses to lay down their arms for fear that their Protestant rivals will use
19887 the negotiations to try to force a wholesale surrender of weapons.The talks group Protestant Unionist parties, which are committed to British rule, and the moderate Catholic-backed Social Democratic and Labour party.The negotiations have been mired in procedural issues since opening in June and have failed to hold one plenary session
19887 devoted to discussion of substantive issues.The IRA's resumptiopn of bomb attacks on British targets has been aimed at getting Britain to drop its insistence that the guerrillas "decomission" weapons as the talks proceed."The current protracted vacuum is extremely dangerous and needs to be filled as a matter of urgency with
19887 real talks. All sensible people know that preconditions prevent this," Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams said at the weekend.At the same time sources close to the Loyalists say they are close to ending a truce which has been in effect since 1994 because of the renewed IRA violence and the
19887 failure of the British government to free jailed activists from either side.</

19890 Tony Blair, poised to lead the British Labour Party out of the political wilderness after 17 years in opposition, could face a tough battle against traditionalists at the last party conference before a general election.The centrist leader, a moderniser who has battled to attract the middle classes to Labour, said
19890 at the start of what could be a crucial week on the road to power: "We have undergone a huge process of change and it has been a hard, bumpy ride."Labour now holds 20-point opinion poll lead over Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservative Party and Blair told The Observer
19890 newspaper: "If we were not New Labour, forget it. We would not be in business as a political party."But, as delegates gathered for the party conference in the northern English seaside resort of Blackpool, two of his closest cohorts said the party's working-class roots should not be spurned in the
19890 rush to reform.Labour's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, warned Blair not to neglect the poor while wooing the middle class voters needed to return the party to power for the first time since 1979."It's very important as we reach out to these new voters, we also remember that the coalition
19890 on which we're building a Labour victory includes the dispossessed," Cook told The Sunday Times.Deputy Labour leader John Prescott also fired a warning shot across Blair's reformist bows. "Sometimes you can go too fast. It will hit the bloody wall, the buffers. The more you pile on the change, the
19890 more and more people feel a little uneasy," he said.Major must call a general election within the next eight months and, with the Conservatives split by divisions over Europe, unity at the Labour conference could prove a vital vote winner.But Labour left-wingers are spoiling for a fight over such issues
19890 as pension rights, child benefit payments and worker rights.Pensions threatened to be an emotive battleground with Lady Barbara Castle, a former Labour cabinet minister, demanding that a Labour government must restore a link between pensions and average earnings.Party officials were trying to find a compromise to avert a conference showdown
19890 between modernisers and traditionalists.Finance spokesman Gordon Brown, eager to avoid open-ended spending commitments, agreed to the setting up of a standing commission to review pensions policy.If he wins the next election, Blair's toughest choice may be to decide if Britain should join the single European currency due to be launched
19890 in January 1999. The issue has sparked party mutinies among the badly-divided Conservatives.Blair told The Observer: "My judgement is that it would be very unwise to say it is not going to happen when virtually the entire German political class is saying that it will."Reiterating Labour's position, he said "in
19890 principle a single currency has benefits" but he insisted that economic convergence was essential if the currency was to realise them.</

19894 Cary Grant introduced American drugs guru Timothy Leary to LSD and may have been a British spy in Hollywood during World War Two.These are just two juicy titbits in the publicity sheet accompanying a new biography of Hollywood's quintessential English gentleman.But readers in search of a secret rebel beneath Grant's
19894 debonair image are likely to be disappointed.Graham McCann, author of "Cary Grant, A Class Apart," says that Grant took LSD more than 100 times in the late 1950s as a therapy for emotional problems. The drug was not made illegal in the United States until 1965.The actor, then at the
19894 peak of his career, took the drug under the supervision of a Los Angeles therapist. He would block his ears with cotton wool and spin himself in circles on the couch, believing he was unscrewing himself."I wanted to rid myself of all my hypocrisies. I wanted to work through the
19894 events of my childhood, my relationship with my parents and my former wives," Grant said once in a rare moment of openness.Grant, who died in 1986, had a troubled history to unravel.He was born Archie Leach to a working class family in the western English city of Bristol in 1904.
19894 When he was nine, Grant's mother was sent to a lunatic asylum by his father who set up home with another woman.The young Leach believed his mother had abandoned him and he did not see her again until she was released, apparently in perfect mental health, 21 years later.The actor,
19894 who usually played gallant, sweet-natured men, married five times in real life and when his fourth wife Dyan Cannon divorced him she accused him of hitting her.These spare facts are well-known and the fiercely private Grant rarely discussed his personal life, leaving a hard task for his biographers.But McCann has
19894 little taste for delving into the actor's turbulent private history.The author, a Cambridge University professor, is scathing about "louche" biographies which have delved into the murkier aspects of the life of one of Hollywood's best-loved actors.In his final chaper, McCann launches a vitriolic attack on the stars of modern Hollywood."Today
19894 we have stars inviting us into their homes, revealing to us their remodelled breasts, recounting their struggles to "become' their roles, reading to us from their diaries and confiding to us all the intimate details of their "private' drink and drug hell," says a disgusted McCann."Today we have stars whose
19894 crass deportment makes Cary Grant's discreet courteousness seem positively noble by comparison."McCann's biography is a scholarly and reverent tribute to Grant and an attempt to refute the more scandalous allegations against him.On the claim that Grant initiated Leary in the use of LSD, McCann is much more vague than his
19894 publicist:"Leary claimed that Grant was one of the people who "converted' him to the positive potential of the drug," he says in the book's only reference to the man who urged young Americans in the 1960s to "turn on, tune in and drop out."McCann's claim that Grant was a spy
19894 is made in defence of suggestions that the actor sat out World War Two in the safety of Hollywood while his compatriates were at the battlefront or being bombed in their homes.But again there is little evidence that Grant spied on fellow actors suspected of having Nazi sympathies, as McCann
19894 suggests. His evidence is no more than the view of "some sources" who "thought it "seemed possible" Grant was a spy.McCann also bridles at rumours that Grant was bisexual. These dated from the 1940s when Grant shared a home for 10 years with fellow actor Randolph Scott, defying Hollywood's homophobic
19894 gossip columnists.The beach home of Grant and Scott was "a bachelor's paradise with girls running in and out of there like a subway station," McCann quotes William Randolph Hearst Junior as saying.He cites Grant's five marriages and the string of affairs he was said to have had with leading actresses,
19894 including Sophia Loren, as evidence of his unwavering heterosexuality.As his final proof, McCann triumphantly reveals that Grant once told a former Miss Denmark that she had "the sexiest-looking body he had ever seen."Even the most famous anecdote about Grant is sacrificed to McCann's scruples.According to the tale, a newspaper editor
19894 wanting to know the actor's age wired his agent asking; "How old Cary Grant?" Grant intercepted the message and replied; "Old Cary Grant fine. How you?"McCann says Grant never sent the message.But "it really ought to have been true: it captured his distinctive melange of edgy evasiveness and easy charm
19894 very neatly," says the ever-loyal author.</
19895 By Neil Winton, Science and Technology CorrespondentTwo airline pilots are peering complacently out of the cockpit on yet another uneventful flight through the clouds.One pilot spots an animal and says calmly: "I didn't know mountain goats lived in clouds".Frank Gens, senior vice-president of International Data Corp, uses this scenario in
19895 a speech to illustrate that unexpected disasters can suddenly loom up and destroy companies in the fast moving world of information technology.And, according to Gens, there are shocks in store for anyone who feels that recent upheavals mean they can now relax and familiarise themselves with the new ways at
19895 their leisure.Apparently, you ain't seen nothing yet."The Internet is triggering revolution, not evolution in the IT marketplace," Gens told a conference in Paris sponsored by IDC, the U.S. information technology consultancy and publisher.And new technologies will be triggered by consumers in the coming mass market for devices that will pave
19895 the way to the information society."The business IT market will be transformed by the massive scale of the consumer market," Gens said.IDC says that so far computers have succeeded in two stages.In the 1970s, company back-offices were automated, mainly with mainframe computers. The second phase, from the 80s until now,
19895 saw the computerisation of front-offices, with point-of-sale equipment and mobile lap-top personal computers.In the third phase, computing devices will enter every home leading to an explosion of high street buying. The information society will have arrived.According to IDC, by 2000 there will be 160 million people surfing the Internet, the
19895 worldwide network of computers linked across telephone lines. In 1996 there are about 35 million Internet users, more than double the previous year's 16 million.By the end of the century, computers will have ceased to be opaque, unreliable and expensive. Like the telephone, they will be turned off and on
19895 instinctively. Households will use enormous computing power without realising it."I think it (the computer) is going to be a typical household appliance. All over the house things will be connected. It will make people's home lives much more efficient and easy," said computing guru Esther Dyson.Dyson was speaking by telephone
19895 while on a trip to Prague."You will use E (electronic) mail to do business and for your personal life. You will find out what's on sale at Harrods, what's for lunch at the local restaurant; it doesn't seem revolutionary, it may seem trivial, but it adds up to what people
19895 control," said Dyson, who publishes the U.S. based "Esther Dyson's Monthly Report".This belief that the mass market is dawning has set up a desperate race among the world's high technology companies.They want to be the winners in the struggle to provide cheap and easy-to-use gadgets. Some see a chance to
19895 knock over current winners in the personal computer world, like Microsoft, the aggressive U.S.-based software giant.Not all industry experts are convinced that ordinary consumers will be beating a path to the computer store."People who work with computers, they've taken them into their home lives. But those not exposed to the
19895 technology, even if they've got the money are not likely to want to get involved," said Graham Taylor, senior vice-president at high technology consultancy Inteco.But people could find themselves surfing the net without realising. Televisions will effectively become personal computers by linking them to set-top boxes, or incorporating microprocessors into
19895 their design."For example, a mobile phone with a little processor inside would let you automatically dial up the cricket scores, share prices, your bank balance. Data would be coming from a web site, but you wouldn't know this," said Taylor.The struggle to find the fast lane to the information superhighway
19895 is widening to include television, telephone, as well as information technology companies.Satellite television's BSkyB, 40 percent owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, has said it will offer Internet connections when it starts a digital television service next year.But currently the inside track is held by the so-called network computer.Proselytiser-in-chief for
19895 the Network Computer is serial Microsoft baiter Larry Ellison, chairman and chief executive officer of database leader Oracle of the U.S.Oracle's Network Computer is a stripped down version of the personal computer. Costing about $500 compared with upwards of $2,000 for a PC, the Network Computer dials up processing power
19895 every time it is used.Ellison has said that the PC is ridiculously over-powered and over priced. Why pay for power and storage space you are never going to use, when you can dial up just the required brawn and brain power for each use?Oracle is only just beginning to sell
19895 these devices, initially aimed at businesses which are more likely to have the required high-quality telephone lines.Microsoft has made wrong turns before and come storming back to mangle the competition."(Microsoft chairman) Mr (Bill) Gates is not going to lie still and let the Network Computer happen. They will be major
19895 players in all this," said Inteco's Taylor.But all these devices, however clever, and even if given away, will not succeed unless the services offered are exciting."Content will be a big driver in all of these services. If there's stuff people want they will seek it out. But if it is
19895 just a mish-mash without any particular context, that will limit the appeal to the mass market," said David Tee, senior industry analyst at consultants SRI International.</

19899 Zealand fullback Matthew Ridge to play on after being apparently tackled by St George hooker Nathan Brown.Menzies scored from the next ruck and St George players argued with Manson as they left the field at halftime.Manly's first try came after just five minutes when centre Craig Innes grounded a short
19899 kick by captain Geoff Toovey. Winger Danny Moore put the match beyond doubt when he scored his side's third try after a St George error 13 minutes into the second half.Winger Nick Zisti crossed for St George 20 minutes from fulltime as his side played increasingly desperate football."We had a
19899 tough game on our hands and it's even better to win when they are the circumstances," Fulton told reporters.St George had been rated 100-1 outsiders at the start of the year after losing two coaches and several key players during the ARL's battle for control of the game with media
19899 tycoon Rupert Murdoch's banned breakaway Super League.The 75-year-old club also narrowly avoided a merger with Sydney City at the start of the year over financial problems caused by the Super League war.St George finished seventh at the end of regular season matches but compiled a list of stirring victories during
19899 the play-off series, beating higher-ranked sides Canberra, Sydney City and North Sydney to reach the grand final."We didn't save our best game till last, unfortunately," St George coach David Waite told reporters.The grand final was the last match for former Australia players David Gillespie and Des Hasler, who had announced
19899 they would retire at the end of this season.Hasler played in Manly's previous premiership winning side in 1987 and in the side beaten by Sydney Bulldogs in last year's grand final.-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

19903 With little more than three days before a strike deadline, General Motors Corp. and the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union remained at odds over work by outside contractors and other issues, union officials said.The union chose G.M. Canada on Monday as its second negotiating target after reaching agreement with Chrysler
19903 Canada earlier this month. The Chrysler pact, ratified last weekend, halts plant sales and closings during the three-year agreement and commits Chrysler to replace any union jobs lost due to work done by outside contractors, known as outsourcing.But GM, the world's largest automaker, has shown little interest in accepting the
19903 terms the union bargained with Chrysler Corp.'s Canadian subisidiary. The union has set a strike deadline of 11:59 P.M. EDT on Wednesday (3:59 A.M. GMT Thursday morning).Talks continued at a Toronto hotel on Sunday and the union planned to hold a news conference on Monday to discuss the status of
19903 negotiations, a union official said.G.M. Canada president Maureen Kempston-Darkes wrote in a letter to her employees last week that the other North American and Japanese automakers in Canada had an advantage over G.M. because they contracted out more production."GM now needs to take the steps already set in place by
19903 Ford (Motor Co.) and Chrysler to become more competitive -- we need to go further to become as productive and competitive as the Japanese transplants here in Canada and the U.S."At the heart of the disagreement is the CAW's determination to restrict outsourcing and reverse G.M. Canada's intentions to sell
19903 two plants and contract out about 5,500 union jobs.CAW President Buzz Hargrove told reporters on Friday that he had agreed to G.M.'s insistence that he meet with a secret prospective buyer for the automaker's Oshawa and Windsor, Ontario, parts plants."I told him you can buy if you want, you buy
19903 us, but you also buy the CAW-GM master collective agreement," he said.Hargove said the union has approved an escalating strike strategy that would close a few G.M. plants at a time until all of its operations were shut down."Our union has unanimously approved a selective and escalating strike strategy," he
19903 said.If no agreement is reached by the deadline, Hargrove said the union will shut down G.M. operations in Oshawa and St. Therese, Quebec. He said members will walk out of G.M.'s St. Catharines plant on October 6 and close down remaining plants in London and Windsor, also in Ontario, on
19903 October 9.Analysts said a strike could cost General Motors as much as $150 million a week, halt production of some vehicle models and interrupt U.S. operations."A long strike might get to the point where it would be reducing G.M.'s profits by maybe $100 million to $150 million a week," said
19903 Dave Healy, analyst at Burnham Securities Inc. "It could spread south of the (Canada/U.S.) border as well."But he said a Canadian strike would not reach the same proportions as an earlier strike at G.M. this year when United Auto Workers union members at a Dayton, Ohio, brake plant walked off
19903 the job over outsourcing. The strike lasted 17 days, shut virtually all GM's North American operations and cost the carmaker $900 million over 17 days.The CAW's $36.7 million strike fund may make it tough to carry out a long-term strike and pay strike benefits to 28,000 members at GM. But
19903 Hargrove said last week that the union had called a special strike dues convention for the entire 210,000-member union on October 18 as a contingency.The union leader said that if no agreement is reached, it would be the first time that a company had failed to accept a so-called pattern
19903 agreement. Traditionally the union sets the pattern with one company and applies that agreement to other automakers.</

19906 July 23, two days before he was overthrown in a coup by the Tutsi-dominated army."We expect Mr Wolpe to meet the president (Buyoya) on Monday," Major Buyoya's spokesman, Jean-Luc Ndizeye, told Reuters.Ndizeye said the military regime expected Wolpe to insist on immediate talks with Hutu rebel groups and specifically with
19906 Leonard Nyangoma, head of the largest armed faction."But we can't do that. Buyoya can't just go and shake Nyangoma's hand tomorrow," Ndizeye said.Regional countries, including all of landlocked Burundi's neighbours, imposed a total economic and trade embargo on July 31 in protest against the army coup. The sanctions are biting
19906 hard, blocking coffee exports and sending the price of basic commodities and oil rocketing.The regional leaders demanded that Buyoya meet three main conditions before sanctions are eased. He has agreed to restore the national assembly and has unbanned political parties but has so far failed to meet Nyangoma or other
19906 exiled rebel leaders from Burundi's Hutu majority.The military regime says the rebels must first renounce the "ideology of genocide" and stop killing civilians. "But we are not saying they must surrender their arms as a pre-condition," Ndizeye said.He linked Wolpe's visit to U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's first African
19906 tour between October 7-15. Christopher will not come to Burundi but will meet leaders of key pro-sanctions nations in Arusha, Tanzania.Ndizeye said he expected Buyoya to be invited to a regional summit on Burundi which he thought would be held in Arusha on October 12. Regional leaders have so far
19906 refused to see Buyoya at summit level but their sanctions committee recommended last week that he be "invited to be available" at their next summit.About 150,000 people have been killed in the past three years of ethnic war in Burundi. There is no accurate figure for current losses because insecurity
19906 in the tiny country of six million people prevents aid workers from moving freely.Wolpe was appointed by President Bill Clinton before the coup to underline U.S. concern over Burundi's dangerous drift, two years after the genocide of up to one million people in neighbouring Rwanda.Wolpe met Ntibantunganya for lunch on
19906 Sunday at the residence. "It was a small, informal affair," one of the guests said.Buyoya's regime will allow the ex-president to go abroad but insists he must first leave the embassy and go to his private residence."We will not accept that he leaves Burundi straight from the U.S. embassy residence,"
