19908 Gambia's president-elect, Yahya Jammeh, is the latest African soldier to make the transition from coupmaker to civilian president after elections that critics say were tailored to ensure victory.Jammeh, at 31 a retired colonel and Africa's youngest elected leader, won 56 percent of votes cast in the tiny West African tourist
19908 haven's election on Thursday against 36 percent for his main rival, lawyer Ousainou Darboe.But Darboe, who has taken refuge in Senegal's embassy in Banjul, denounced what he called the "hostile electioneering environment and unlevel nature of the political field" for the poll to end two years of army rule.Although Thursday's
19908 vote was orderly and apparently transparent, democracy campaigners say Jammeh basically assured the outcome by moves such as banning established politicians from standing."The military will always be military, it's not the uniform that matters, it's the attitude," said third-placed Amath Bah.Bah praised organisation of Gambia's vote as "absolutely fair and
19908 clear" but, like Jammeh's two other civilian rivals, he says bitterly they were denied a fair hearing.Jammeh, who toppled independence president Sir Dawda Jawara in 1994, banned established politicians from standing. He cited their links with Jawara whom he accused of corruption.Critics abroad, particularly the Commonwealth of Britain and its
19908 former colonies, dismissed the poll in advance saying that it was set up to ensure Jammeh's victory.Opposition parties were legally recognised two weeks before polling, had 10 days to campaign and were virtually denied access to state radio and television with their national reach."The military knew what they were doing.
19908 They didn't want the people to hear about their corruption," Bah said.A Commonwealth ministerial monitoring group described the process as "obviously flawed" and "likely to lead to the consolidation of military rule in another form".Jammeh, whose coup alienated Gambia's traditional Western partners, resigned from the army to contest the poll
19908 and on Saturday dissolved the hitherto ruling military council -- the Armed Forces Provisional Ruling Council (AFPRC).But he formed his new party, the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction (APRC), with fellow army officers and throughout the campaign, Darboe and his supporters accused the military of taking sides and harassing
19908 them."It's all the more frustrating for those Africans who spent their energies fighting the monster of one-party rule," one veteran Western diplomat in West Africa commented.Soldiers or former military men are well entrenched across West Africa -- from Ghana, where two-time coup leader Jerry Rawlings seeks a final term in
19908 December, to Togo and Guinea.This year alone, former military rulers transformed themselves to civilian presidents through the ballot box in Chad and Niger, stoking political tension in both countries.In Niger, military strongman Ibrahim Bare Mainassara toppled an elected government in January then responded to international outcry by offering a quick
19908 end to military rule.He offered himself for election but also set the rules. In the middle of voting he sacked the independent electoral commission and appointed another that declared him winner.In Chad, President Idriss Deby, who seized power in 1990, won multi-party elections in July after segments of the opposition
19908 cried foul.Critics of military men turned politicians say they have a poor democratic record, often citing veterans such as Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire or Gnassingbe Eyadema of Togo.All eyes are now on regional giant Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, and military ruler Sani Abacha's intentions in 1998, the deadline
19908 for his promised democratic transition.Nigeria has been ruled by the military for most of its nearly 36 years of independence. Many Nigerians blame their political crisis on attempts by military rulers to hang on to power as civilians.</
19909 The slow start of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, two years after the genocide of up to a million people, has fuelled fires lit by its critics.In an unfinished Arusha courtroom with no witnesses set to testify and no Rwandan journalists present to see justice done, it last week
19909 postponed its first two trials for a second time.The prosecution, defence and the tribunal were simply not ready, despite the three judges firing a public warning shot by initially threatening to resume Jean Paul Akayesu's trial on Monday before agreeing to put it off until the end of October.Georges Rutaganda,
19909 one of four Rwandan Hutu accused held in Arusha, never even appeared in court as he is seriously ill and in a hospital. He secured a postponement until March next year.Only the two defence lawyers, those accused of genocide and crimes against humanity in three months of mass slaughter in
19909 Rwanda and those still evading arrest had reason to be pleased.It was a sorry conclusion, reinforcing worries that U.N. bureaucracy and the difficulties of operating from Tanzania would defeat the tribunal's ground-breaking moral mission that no one should be free to escape being judged for their crimes.The new delays added
19909 to the immense frustration felt by Rwanda's government and relatives of the dead -- and fears that yet another U.N. operation in Africa was going horribly wrong.But in their defence the tribunal judges, aware of the poor impression, are growing increasingly impatient and are staking their reputations on real progress
19909 being just round the corner.They say the Rwanda tribunal was built from the ground up in this northern Tanzanian farming town and still worked faster than its sister tribunal on the former Yugoslavia in The Hague.Asked what he could say to the still grieving relatives of the dead from the
19909 1994 genocide who argued that justice delayed was no justice, Swedish Judge Lennart Aspegren told Reuters:"I would like to say to them that they should know there are serious international efforts to have justice done. And this is something which is absolutely unique for Africa."It should be unique because the
19909 genocide in Rwanda as far as I know was the worst genocide we have ever heard about if you take into consideration it took place in a very few months.""It is a slow and shaky start," conceded Judge Navanethem Pillay of South Africa, noting even judges complained about waiting for
19909 a year before being put on full-time duty with salaries."Everybody has legitimate complaints -- but this is a mammoth task and entirely new for Africa," she added."If you take a court system in a national state, everything is there: rules, buildings, experienced staff and equipment. But this thing had to
19909 be brought to Arusha and set up."Not a single journalist from Rwanda was in court last week to tell Rwanda and the estimated 1.7 million Rwandan Hutu refugees outside the country the tribunal was even in session.Officials said Rwandan journalists did not have the money to reach Arusha and transmit
19909 their stories or film and promised the tribunal would make more efforts to help them cover trials."It is highly relevant emotionally, psychologically for people inside Rwanda to know about the progress of the tribunal so they can begin the process of rebuilding their nation."Rwandan Vice-President Paul Kagame, whose Tutsi-led rebels
19909 seized power in July 1994, and Zimbabwe's defence minister on Thursday accused the United Nations of racial bias, saying it was moving faster to bring Bosnian war criminals to justice.Such accusations are patently untrue, Rwanda tribunal officials said, noting the former Yugoslavia tribunal had taken three years to bring its
19909 only suspect in custody to trial.The Rwanda tribunal, with a budget of $36 million for 1996 which was only approved by the U.N. in June, has indicted 21 suspects of whom 11 are in custody, including four in Arusha.Aspegren said the tribunal hit all kinds of problems imaginable, especially communications.
19909 In addition there are many problems peculiar to Rwanda, where potential witnesses are being attacked and threatened.Because of insecurity, no tribunal investigator for the prosecution has visited Zaire, with 1.1 million Rwandan Hutus.The tribunal last week ruled the identities of witnesses would be kept from the public and the media
19909 to protect them.Witnesses will testify by camera from a room outside the courtroom. Only the judges will be able to see their faces."You can never of course have 100 percent security," admitted Aspegren. "(But) we are breaking new legal ground."</

19911 Tanzania's annual rate of inflation eased to 18 percent during August -- from 18.2 per cent in July -- while the country registered a reduced trade deficit for the month, a Bank of Tanzania (BOT) report said.In its monthly economic review for September, the BOT said the August inflation rate
19911 represented an improvement of 9.3 percentage points over the 27.3 percent recorded in August 1995.The fall in inflation results from tight monetary and fiscal measures, while a satisfactory food supply situation also contributed to the decline, the report said.However, the central bank cautioned that inflation may rise in September following
19911 a recent increase in fuel prices.Tanzania's terms of trade in August saw a deficit of $66 million compared to $73.8 million for the same period last year.Export earnings increased by 22 percent to $52.94 million during August compared to August 1995. Imports remained almost static, registering a small increase of
19911 1.42 percent to $118.94 million compared to $117.28 for corresponding month in 1995.Despite a decline in prices, Tanzania's traditional export mainstays, coffee, cotton and tea, brought higher earnings due to increased sales volume. These traditional exports, worth $29.92 million, were up by 25.1 per cent compared to August 1995. Export
19911 earnings from cashew nuts declined by 13.8 percent to $1.63 million compared to the same period last year.The BOT forcast an improvement in coffee prices in the near future due to tight supply conditions and reduced global production.In a move likely to be welcomed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF),
19911 the government's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has recommended the government "refrain from borrowing from the Bank of Tanzania" to further curb inflation, the report reveals.Of the total amount of disbursed outstanding debt, ($6.5 billion) the government is the largest borrower accounting for 93.9 percent. Total private sector debt stood at
19911 2.7 percent.The BOT said the government's budgetary performance in August was encouraging with higher than expected collections in customs duty, sales tax, excise duty and non-tax revenue. On a monthly basis, collections for July and August were 36.2 billion shillings and 43.8 billion shillings respectively.In August, the BOT purchased $26.3
19911 million on the interbank foreign exchange market and paid off external debts worth $26.1 million. Tanzania's total debt at the end of August stood at $7.8 billion.The shilling appreciated 0.6 percent in August with the exchange rate moving from 601.34 to the dollar in July to 597.6 in August --
19911 due mainly to an increase in the supply of foreign exchange from pre-export earnings and a slackening in import demand.On Tanzania's food security, the BOT said total food availability for 1996/1997 stood at 7.5 million tonnes against the recommended level of 7.1 million tonnes. However, the government's food security department
19911 is expected to purchase 90,000 tonnes of maize for the strategic grain reserve. (1$=590Tsh)</

19912 denied the charge.Coetzee, de Kock's predecessor at the police murder unit, stirred the pot further on Saturday when he said Palme was killed by a former special forces soldier in the then white-run Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) who was a member of Long Reach.Williamson, in a telephone interview from Luanda on
19912 Sunday, dismissed the charge, which Coetzee admitted was hearsay."All I can do is reiterate what I've said before, that I know absolutely nothing about the Palme killing. 19912 Long Reach, which Williamson described as a company he set up in the late 1980s to conduct political risk analysis for businesses and other clients."Long Reach employed former military intelligence agents, and some of them used it as a front for other activities. 19912 throwing stones in the water and seeing where the ripples reach."The prosecutor in de Kock's trial took a similar attitude, asking the former police colonel if he also knew the truth about the John F. Kennedy assassination.All three agents have applied to the truth commission chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu
19912 for amnesty for crimes committed in defence of apartheid.The Afrikaans-language Sunday newspaper Rapport said de Kock's testimony was the start of a "gloves-off" battle between former agents of the secret police. De Kock has accused former presidents P.W. Botha and F.W. de Klerk of knowing about the dirty tricks and
19912 said he always acted on orders.</
19913 U.N. aid officials will meet in in Geneva on Monday to decide whether Rwandan refugees in Zaire and Tanzania can continue to be treated as legitimate refugees, a senior U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees official said.Assistant High Commissioner Sergio Vieira de Mello left the Rwandan capital Kigali for Geneva after
19913 a round of meetings aimed at finding solutions to the problems posed by the presence of over 1.7 million refugees in neighbouring Zaire and Tanzania.The refugees, mostly Hutus, fled Rwanda in 1994 after the Hutu-led government was ousted by rebels of the Tutsi minority. Many refugees were involved in the
19913 government-led genocide of one million Rwandans, mostly Tutsis, and refuse to go home for fear of reprisals. Some 80,000 Hutus await trial in Rwanda.De Mello said late on Saturday he had been asked by High Commissioner Sadako Ogata to assess the situation in Rwanda. After meeting Rwandan ministers, he said:
19913 "We all agree the non-resolution of the refugee problem is a major factor in the instability of the region."We need to take a different approach to the problem... implementation of the Cessation Clause is a possibility."The Cessation Clause can be invoked if the U.N. agency considers that it is no
19913 longer necessary to accord refugee status to a group of people because the conditions which led to their exile have since stabilised in their country of origin."My own assessment is that a return to Rwanda would be safe," de Mello said. "But the problem of intimidation (in the refugee camps
19913 in Zaire) is huge."Hutu hardliners hoping one day to regain power in Rwanda intimidate refugees in the camps to force them to stay in Zaire.De Mello said an attempt to carry out a census of the refugees in the camps in Zaire recently had been frustrated by "violent sabotage"."This is
19913 a challenge to our mandate," he added.In Kigali, de Mello met diplomats whose governments control much of the donor aid given to the UNHCR.Zairean Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda and Defence Minister Admiral Mavua Mudima are due to meet UNHCR officials in Geneva this week. Zaire has repeatedly called for
19913 the Rwandan refugees to return home, saying they have caused instability in eastern Zaire.Rwandan Rehabilitation Minister Patrick Mazimhaka recently told Reuters that he believed many of the Rwandans in Zaire did not qualify as refugees. "They are criminals who committed genocide," he said.The Rwanda government criticises the international community for
19913 funding the refugee camps which it says house the perpetrators of the 1994 genocide.The funds spent on the refugee camps far exceed the aid provided to Rwanda itself, it says.</

19922 Scattered across the vastness of the Kalahari desert, a handful of Bushmen survive who can read the tracks of reptile, lion or antelope with the ease of a Western teenager surfing the Internet.Now South African Louis Liebenberg is harnessing the ancient skills of hunter-gatherers to state-of-the-art computers in a plan
19922 that he says can help the survival of both the Bushmen and the world's wildlife.He has started a pilot project in one of South Africa's national parks for trackers on the park staff to carry hand-held computers into which they enter data on the animal signs they see during patrols."It's
19922 a pen-based computer, and we've developed an interface that illiterate trackers can use based on little pictures and icons. The tracker just touches the screen with a pen," Liebenberg said in an interview.The theory is that the computers will allow trackers to record information that would otherwise be quickly lost
19922 but now can be used by wildlife managers to combat poachers and assess the health of plant and animal populations."The computer covers a full range of species, down to different mongoose species," Liebenberg said."You can count the number of adults, of females, of juveniles. The computer is connected to a
19922 GPS (global positioning system) which automatically pinpoints the position and time and the date."So it's a very specific observation which at the end of the day, when you've gathered vast amounts of data, you can analyse statistically."Liebenberg said skilled trackers could identify individual black rhinos from the pattern of cracks
19922 on the underside of their feet. "It's like a fingerprint."The tracker can follow the trail of a rhino, noting the animal's activities along the way, such as how much it ate and what kind of vegetation."This has management implications in the sense that you can do the same with, for
19922 example, kudu (antelope), and determine what is the competition for food between rhino and kudu," Liebenberg said."You get a much better idea of whether there are too many rhino or if you've got space for more."He said the system would for the first time provide accurate data on nocturnal species
19922 which were seldom picked up by current wildlife surveys conducted from aircraft."There's an enormous amount of new information that becomes available. It could form the very basis of conservation management and for the cost of 10 hours of helicopter flying time you can employ a tracker for a whole year
19922 in the field..."If it works here, I think it could revolutionise wildlife management throughout the world."Liebenberg said the value of the system depended on the skills of the trackers using it, but he estimated that possibly no more than 100 highly skilled Bushmen trackers still survived in southern Africa."There's a
19922 level of refinement that you find among traditional hunter-gatherers that you simply don't find elsewhere," he said."You're looking at tracking as a tradition that goes back hundreds of thousands of years, and you're reaching a point where your last bow and arrow hunters are disappearing very rapidly."He believes his system
19922 could give the art of tracking a new importance and respectability that would help those who practise it."You're creating jobs for members of the local community using indigenous African skills that can also be important for tourism, because if you know where the animals are, you know where to take
19922 the tourists."Liebenberg hopes the computer project will provide evidence to support a theory he developed, while a student of physics and philosophy, that stone age tracking was the origin of modern science."It's always been assumed that science as we know it today was developed by the classical Greeks...But tracking involved
19922 the same hypothetico-deductive reasoning that is required in physics and mathematics."Liebenberg compares a physicist making deductions about invisible particles from the signs they leave with a tracker forming theories about animal behaviour from the tracks of an antelope."There's a sort of cultural prejudice against people who are illiterate...But with a
19922 system like this, a tracker can make a significant scientific contribution in his own right."My big dream is, I want to see if I can get an illiterate tracker to submit a thesis to university."</

19926 Asima Moravac is one of many thousands of grieving Moslem mothers in Bosnia. The body of her son Bernard returned from war decapitated, minus its left arm and its ribcage crushed by an enemy's boot.The twist to her terrible story is that Bernard was a Serb.Nobody but the killers of
19926 24-year-old Bernard knows exactly what happened after he was captured near the northwest Bosnian village of Kulen Vakuf on September 14 last year.But Moravac, a mother of eight, is convinced he was taken alive and killed in captivity after Bosnia's warring factions signed the Dayton peace accord on December 14."I
19926 feel so bitter I could finish off the whole world, not just the man who killed my son," said 45-year-old Moravac, who married a Serb in one of the many mixed marriages of pre-war Bosnia.Serb atrocities during the four year war have been widely reported and the sufferings of the
19926 Moslems -- for most of the conflict the losers -- are well documented.But rarely do bereaved families speak out in the Bosnian Serb Republic, where often foreign journalists are treated with suspicion or accused of pro-Moslem bias.Moravac tells the story of 11 agonising months of uncertainty, which ended when she
19926 identified Bernard's body on August 16, with a quiet dignity."I appeal to all sides to release the missing, the living and the dead, so the agony of (their families) can be ended," she said. "There is nothing worse than being kept in suspense."Bernard, from the hardline Serb stronghold of Prijedor,
19926 was captured when Moslem and Croatian forces were advancing into Serb territory as the tide turned in the last months of war.His platoon stumbled into an ambush, although his mother does not know whether it was set by Moslems or Croatians.That day, September 14, was exactly one year before Western-supervised
19926 Bosnian elections which were aimed at helping heal the wounds of war.Of the eight Serb soldiers, two returned alive while one escaped and hid in nearby woods about 150 metres (yards) away.He returned to Prijedor weeks later, saying he had heard no shots or screams from the ambush. This, says
19926 Moravac, proves that Bernard was taken alive.He and four others caught in the ambush returned from Moslem territory as corpses bearing signs of torture.Moravac, dressed in black to mark the first anniversary of Bernard's capture, listed the wounds on each of the four other soldiers: beatings, bullets in the neck
19926 and the forehead.Pausing as tears welled in her eyes, she said: "My son was decapitated, his left arm was severed and the right side of his chest was smashed, probably by a military boot."She identified her son by his jogging pants and underwear. He was buried in a Prijedor Orthodox
19926 cemetery on August 21.Moravac, who spoke in her suburban apartment after returning from Bernard's graveside, said a Serb doctor who conducted the autopsy put the date of death as early January this year -- after the Dayton agreement was signed in Paris.It was not clear how the doctor could determine
19926 such an accurate date of death. Bernard's body was buried for several months in the Moslem-held exclave of Bihac before it was returned in an exchange of prisoners, dead and alive.Moravac believes that Bernard and his comrades were executed because of where they came from. Serbs are alleged to have
19926 killed, tortured and raped Moslems at prison camps in the Prijedor region."These boys were never anywhere near these camps and were in no way involved in these things," she said.Bernard, who studied electrical engineering and spoke good English, was a tall, quiet young man interested in Western rock music. 19926 to his fate, she said: "In a similar situation he would have never even thought of doing such a thing."Moravac, a former seamstress who now sells kitchenware, set up a self-help group with other parents of Serbs missing in action. 19926 to the presidents of the United States, Russia and France. 19926 have hidden him from them."Unfortunately, during the war all sides hid prisoners," said the ICRC's Marco Sassoli, who chairs a committee including all three factions on missing persons.Moravac said she did not know whether detailed reports of atrocities by the Serb side were true. 19959 President Fidel Castro said on Saturday that while Cuba was recovering from the worst of its economic crisis, citizens should not think the way ahead would be easy.Paying tribute to neighbourhood groups called the Comittees for the Defence of the Revolution (CDRs), Castro was also adamant that whatever the pressures
19959 from the United States, Cuba would not permit the collapse of its communist system."The enemy knows that the (Cuban) people would prefer death one thousand times more than going back to the past (before the 1959 revolution)," Castro told a rally in the central city of Sancti Spiritus to mark
19959 the 36th anniversary of the forming of the CDRs.On the country's emergence from an economic crisis caused by the collapse of its old ally the former Soviet Union, Castro said Cuba would continue to recover but that this could take some time."We should feel satisfied at how we are recovering,
19959 but we must at the same time be on alert against any tendency to think that the way ahead of us will be a bed of roses," added Castro in a speech broadcast on state radio.Cuban authorities have predicted economic growth of about five percent this year, measured in terms
19959 of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), following GDP growth of 2.5 percent last year and a sharp contraction in the years 1989-1993.Despite modest improvement, living standards for most Cubans remain way below what they were in the 1980s.The Cuban leader said the island would not be budged by pressure from the
19959 United States, including its recent Helms-Burton law that tightens the longstanding embargo against Havana."They still want to swallow us up, they still want to annex us ... but the people say no, they won't succeed."On the role of CDRs -- the largest of Cuba's mass organisations with membership encompassing some
19959 90 percent of the adult population -- Castro said the groups still had important work to do defending the revolution, helping with political education and fighting crime.Despite the continued high theoretical membership, Cubans widely agree the CDRs have declined as a force in society in recent years.In the early years
19959 of the revolution, the groups were supposed to be a grass-roots defence against people trying to sabotage the system. For some people they acquired an image of being a means of spying on neighbours.Nowadays many people, especially the young, do not bother going to CDR meetings. But the groups still
19959 organise blood donations, gather recyclable waste material, persuade people to vote in elections and run street cleaning sessions.</

19963 Fletcher Building to Fletcher Forests will be effective retrospectively from July 1. 19963 estimated the net replacement cost of the Tasman Lumber and HT Plywood mill for Fletcher Forests at between $111 million and $139 million.The broker, however, was unable to determine whether the alternative action of buying other existing processing plants would result in more or less value being generated for Fletcher
19963 Forests than from buying the processing assets. But the report noted that control of processing capacity was considered by Fletcher Forests to be imperative to the implementation of its resource-to-customer chain strategy."In Fletcher Forests' view, it will result in incremental value in excess of the $93 million cost of purchasing
19963 the processing assets."First New Zealand Capital also found the transaction fair to Fletcher Building. "We estimate the total value of the processing asset to Fletcher Building under its management and on an autonomous going concern basis to be in the range of $18 million and $71 million," it said.Furthermore, the
19963 value likely to be realised from closing the processing plants and liquidating the processing assets was estimated to be between $38 million and $43 million."We consider Fletcher Forests is the party that is most likely to extract the highest expected value from the processing assets and hence, on the basis
19963 of being a willing buyer, Fletcher Forest should be prepared to pay the highest price for the processing assets."We would expect there to be a very limited buyer audience that could justify paying a comparable price to that to be paid by Fletcher Forests," the report said.-- Wellington newsroom 64

19966 ** BIRTHDAYS **French financier JACQUES NECKER, who was imprisoned in The Bastille for suggesting that the aristocracy pay taxes, was born in 1732. The people of Paris agreed with him, and later stormed the building and freed him.English sportsman JOHN MYTTON, who kept two-thousand dogs, 50 cats and a pet
19966 bear, was born in 1796. He was quite an individual, and had a habit of drinking a bottle of port every morning, while shaving. He also had an unusual cure for hiccups - He would set his nightshirt on fire with a candle to give himself the required fright, to
19966 scare off the hiccups !South Australian editor of the 'Adelaide Observer' JOHN STEPHENS, who once claimed that "certain moral felonies were punishable only through the press", was born in 1806.German author of "Sodom's End", HERMANN SUDERMANN, was born in 1857.Australian cricketer ERNEST "Jonah" JONES was born in 1869. He was
19966 our first fast-bowler, and put a ball through W.C.GRACE's beard in his 1896 debut international game. 19966 born in 1942. He died on the 28th of February, 1968 of a drug overdose.American drummer DEWEY MARTIN, who played with the group 'Buffalo Springfield', was born in 1942.American singer MARILYN McCOO, who sang with the 'Fifth Dimension', was born in 1943. She had hits with "Up, Up And Away"
19966 (1967), "Aquarius/Let The Sunshine In" (1969) and "I Didn't Get To Sleep" (1972). She married BILLY DAVIS JNR from the group in 1969, and recorded the million- seller duet "You Don't Have To Be A Star (To Be In My Show) in 1976. MARILYN later became the hostess of the

19970 Australia's media and telecommunications laws are preventing new and diverse operators from investing in the industry, according to a report released on Monday.The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT) Media and Telecommunications Group report said this was happening as a result of the multiple layers of regulation and opportunities for
19970 political interference.In addition, the rapid changes in technology and new media were outpacing law-making, the report said. "Freedom of communication is endangered whenever politicians or bureau have power, as they do at present, to decide who should own the media," group director Mark Armstrong said."Better laws would give more encouragement
19970 for investment in media and freedom of speech," he said."Free speech requires prosperous, stable Australian media without political control or monopolisation," he said.Armstrong said the regulatory system needed to be replaced with rules which were legislated, in black and white, by parliament. "The current laws are ageing rapidly," he said.
19970 "Australian media is likely to flourish if old and new media know in advance what the rules of the game will be," he said.The RMIT report was published following a round-table seminar involving senior media and telecommunications industry executives and policy experts.The Australian government is currently considering a review of
19970 the media industry, which could lead to changes to ownership rules and regulation.The telecommunications industry will be de-regulated in July next year in order to allow new players to enter the market.-- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730</

19973 Concern that the United States will retaliate against a decision by the European Union (EU) to sell subsidised wheat is overshadowing the Australian market.Closely-watched January 1997 wheat ended last week 50 cents lower at A$163.00 a tonne on modest volume, attributed to book squaring ahead of USDA quarterly wheat stock
19973 figures due out on later on Monday.Price flucuations last week were attributed to spread trading the nearby months, with the Australian Wheat Board cutting its pool price estimate A$10.00 to A$195.00 a tonne FOB. As a result, nearby contracts by Friday had all settled lower on the week.A breakout of
19973 a U.S.-EU subsidy war would probably firm up prices between the combatants, while making Australian wheat less attractive in price to such key buyers as China.The North Dakota Wheat Commission said on Thursday the United States needed Export Enhancement Program (EEP) subsidies to counter the European Union's Actions.But whether the
19973 U.S. would actually impose its own subsidies -- more than likely in the form of EEP -- is debatable given that U.S. wheat is running above export parity. Fearful that such a scenario may unfold, however, some brokers are encouraging Australian growers to take out put options, as the U.S.
19973 and Australian markets would probably move in opposite directions."The U.S. is keeping its EEP budget and could retaliate, basically shooting EEP bullets at Europe, and Australia will get caught in the cross-fire," said a grains analyst.The last time the U.S. imposed EEP subisides was nearly two years ago at the
19973 height of the last trade war. But there may be less reason for the U.S. to react this time around. "U.S. supply-demand is fairly tight, so there will be a significantly smaller quantity of U.S. wheat going into the export market this year," said a grains trader. "Domestic U.S. wheat
19973 prices are reflecting that tightness."-- Sydney Newsroom 61-92 373-1800</

19984 Flagship industrial metal copper powered higher on Friday as speculators capitalised on a short-term supply shortage to push the metal to a three-week peak.At the height of the morning buying spree on the London Metal Exchange (LME), copper for delivery in three months was going for $1,990 a tonne, $46
19984 more than at Thursday's close.But gains were pared in the afternoon as some investors cashed in profits.Copper ended the week on the London Metal Exchange (LME) at $1,957, up $13 from Thursday and compared to an opening price of $1,880 on Monday.The rally boosted sentiment, which was dented early this
19984 week when many industrial metals sagged to new recent lows."We expect the screws to tighten further," one LME floor trader said, referring to continuing healthy falls in inventories held in LME warehouses after a decline of 9,300 tonnes on Friday.Tighter nearby supplies have led to cash copper demanding a premium
19984 over future material for the first time since September 13.Traders on Friday were offering up to $8 a tonne more for copper for immediate delivery than for the benchmark three months material.A week ago the situation was the opposite -- three months metal was up to $13 more expensive than
19984 cash copper.But among other industrial metals, nickel tumbled lower during afternoon ring and kerb trading, against a background of Canadian producer Inco reaching a tentative pay agreement with workers at its Manitoba facilities which could end a two-week lock-out.Meanwhile, nickel stocks continue to climb, with LME inventories rising another 624
19984 tonnes today. 19985 Q4 96 - 5A fourth quarter reduction in official cash rates cut remains economists' most favoured option.Ten economists saw an October move as likely or a definite possibility. This move was seen most likely to happen either after the labour force data on October 10, or the release of third
19985 quarter inflation and wages data on October 23 and 24 respectively.As such, the RBA Board will give Macfarlane the authority to lower rates if the data falls the right way - weak employment and a high unemployment rate, and continued moderation in both inflation and wages, so a cut next
19985 Wednesday is still seen as unlikely.If the cut doesn't occur in October, then based on what information available at the moment, a November rate cut is the market's most favoured outcome.However, if employment shows strength, and the inflation and wages data disappoint, the outlook could change to rates on hold
19985 until the middle of next year, economists said.Recently retired RBA Governor Bernie Fraser's description of the July rate cut as insurance is behind some expectations of another cut, with even those expecting a hike as the next move acknowledging the possibility of another cut in 1997. Economists said it was
19985 not clear if insurance meant one cut of 50 basis points as a means to spark the labour market and activity, or whether it meant a total of 100 basis points had been approved, with 50 delivered and 50 held in reserve in case the economy needed a further boost.If
19985 a cut has not happened by the end of the year, the odds will start to favour a rise in rates from the middle of next year, they said.OFFICIAL AUSTRALIAN INTEREST RATES - October Most likely Timing of rate move next move next moveABN Amro 50/50 Down Oct/Nov 96AMP Yes

19990 The zinc and lead markets are in for a number of tough trading years, with prices for both metals seen falling in 1997, an industry study said on Monday.Zinc and lead industries faced major restructuring over the next 10 years as producers react cautiously to changes in demand fundamentals, the
19990 report, by AME Mineral Economics Proprietary Ltd, said.The accelerating impact globally of environmental legislation aimed at reducing risks from hazardous chemicals and abating air contamination threatens to encourage end users of the metals to find replacement materials, AME said. Zinc prices should fall marginally to around US$0.47 a pound in
19990 1997, before remaining flat for the next 10 years, AME figures showed.Buoyancy in prices for lead, resulting from a surprise rise in battery replacement demand, would be short-lived, AME said.That pressure would come to an end soon, leaving lead to trade at an average 34 cents a pound in 1997,
19990 five percent below the 1996 forecast of 36.3 cents.By 2005, lead price would have fallen to an average 33.6 cents a pound. Meanwhile, efforts by zinc and lead miners to reduce costs have had mixed result.In the last four years, zinc prodcution costs have fallen 25 percent, although lead costs
19990 rose 4.6 percent, AME said.AME sees prices deteriorationg despite predicting zinc and lead markets would remain in balance throughout this period.By 1998, inventories of zinc would only represent around eight weeks worth of consumption and lead would be down to six weeks.Zinc demand was dependent on the construction market, particularly
19990 roads and motor vehicles, AME said. Demand for zinc from the important construction markets would be flat among developed countries, although it should rise in the developing regions of Asia and Latin America, AME said.By 2000, zinc demand in developing countries should reach three million tonnes a year, advancing to
19990 3.5 million in 2005, it said.Environmental regulations were set to dictate constraints on both supply and demand, AME said.Regulatory action would affect the use of lead in batteries and also restrict international trade in both recycled lead and zinc, which might be defined as hazardous chemiclas, AME said. By 2000,
19990 1.5 million tonnes of new zinc mine capcity would come on stream, AME said.Smelting capacity over the same period would grow by 1.3 million tonne, it said.-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800</

19993 If upward momentum in New Zealand business confidence can be sustained over the next few months it may signal an end to the trough in economic activity, the National Bank of New Zealand said on Monday.A NBNZ survey shows business confidence rose for the third consective month in September, with
19993 a net 21 percent of respondents seeing better business conditions over the next year."In Spring things blossom; flowers, trees, romance and business confidence," the bank said. In August, a net six percent of respondents expected business conditions to improve over the next year and in July, while confidence rebounded, net
19993 confidence remained firmly negative with 16 percent expecting a deterioration in business conditions.NBNZ said the September results were enormously encouraging, adding: "If the rise is sustained over the next few months then the trough in economic activity can genuinely be declared over." The September gain was across all groups, with
19993 the service sector leading the charge. The largest turnaround came from the agricultural sector, from a net 25 percent expecting a downturn last month, to balance this month.NBNZ said that last month it lamented the torrid time exporters had been undergoing, and had also commented that the domestic economy continued
19993 to slow."The only thing that has changed this month is that respondents are more confident, leaving us in search of the x-factor." Possible explanations included encouraging signs from the global economy and positive sales and profit growth in the manufacturing sector.NBNZ said a key to the relative optimism was the
19993 net 42 percent of respondents anticipating lower interest rates -- a significant swing from the net 40 percent expecting an increase as recently as June.However, the bank noted, its survey was taken before the Reserve Bank's September economic projections, which firmly crushed any hope of immediate interest rate relief. "They
19993 (the RB) have left the door open though for lower rates in the new year, and fixed rate mortgages have already edged downward," the bank observed.A net 30 percent of respondents anticipated an increase in their own business activity. This was reflected in expected gains in profits, exports, investment and
19993 employment, but inflation expectations remain unchanged at 2.6 percent.NBNZ said the Reserve Bank could continue to bask in the subdued outlook for residential construction over the next year. 19993 the optimists should keep the champagne corks in for a while yet as several hurdles had yet to be cleared, including an election.New Zealand goes to the polls on October 12 for a general election under a new proportional voting system which favours a minority or coalition government."Ongoing confidence appears

19997 in second place on 18 percent, up two.New Zealand will hold its first election under proportional representation on October 12, and National and its potential coalition partners are looking to win at least half the vote to form a stable majority government.One possible partner, the radical free-market ACT New Zealand,
19997 scored five percent in the TV1 poll. 19997 of the 120 seats if the poll's results held through election night.Labour, economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance would have 61.National, in power since 1990, has presided over a strong economic recovery and cut taxes in July, while still running budget surpluses and paying off national debt.Its
19997 opponents say government policies are widening the gap between rich and poor. 19999 MIM Holdings Ltd said on Sunday it expected production costs from its A$290 million Enterprise copper mine extension at Mount Isa to average less than US$0.60 a pound by about 1999."It's high grade, it's deep, but with the technology we have we think we can achieve a very satisfactory cost
19999 position at Isa, which I think reflects the quality of that ore body," MIM's managing director Nick Stump told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.MIM typically keeps its production costs a secret, although analysts have estimated they are running at about US$0.71 a pound at the current deposit being mined
19999 at Mount Isa.This compares with costs of US$0.40 a pound or less among some of the lowest-cost producers.Asked if Mount Isa was making losses, Stump said the mine was operating "about break even at this time," but added "it was really hard to tell", due to copper prices and the
19999 Australian dollar exchange rate.In August, MIM reported a net profit after abnormals for the year to June 30 of A$170.6 million, but said the Mount Isa operations recorded a loss in June.The stronger the local currency, the less funds MIM can repatriate from U.S. dollar-denominated export sales, while each one
19999 U.S. cent change in the copper price on a per pound basis means A$3.77 million to the company's bottom line."Last week we had a US$0.85 (per pound) copper price and a US$0.80 exchange rate," Stump said."Pretty tough, but of course this is new territory because the price has fallen faster
19999 and further than anybody expected because of the Sumitomo fiasco," Stump added.Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp in mid-June revealed some US$1.8 billion in losses from rogue copper trades, sending the international metal price into a tailspin.Citing last week's sale of most of the company's oil and gas interests to Santos
19999 Ltd for A$45.1 million, Stump said a diposal programme of non-core assets was "well advanced".Stump also said he expected development of the George Fisher zinc prospect near Mount Isa to proceed.MIM is currently studying the feasibility of bringing the prospect on stream as zinc production at Mount Isa nears an
19999 end."I'm sure George Fisher will be mined," Stump said.</
